review: Got an estimate but went with another plumber as this was the highest quote of the 3 plumbers we interviewed for the job. Very prompt communication though.  Will re-consider for future jobs.  Seems reliable (and often you get what you pay for!)

I like the Neuvo-Latino-Americano grub here.  The place has moved locations and is now a bit larger.  Chips & Salsa are always fresh 7 tasty, too.  I wish I could give a more substanital review but I ate here so long ago - and at the old location - so I'd better just keep my mouth shut.

Went for a casual happy hour and thoroughly enjoyed my $8 (normally $12) cocktail. $3.25 for a club soda.  Ouch.  Also loved the seared tuna appetizer with - get this - portabello "fries" - so tasty.  Excellent food, service and one-of-a-kind atmosphere.  Perfect for a date or romantic dinner for two. Great for a proposal or special occaision. Expense-account-worthy.  Boy can they throw down!  N.B. - I can't get any cell phone service up here.  Oh well - with that view, who cares.
Wow - an overwhelming selection of products. They are coming out for an estimate and I will update after that time.  So far, I am liking it!

We come to this Joann's when we can't get what we need at Michael's or AC Moore - and, as you'd expect, this store is more fabric-focused so we were able to get the adhesive and embellishments my 13 year old needed for a project.  No issues.
Better cookies!!!  Try the Chinese "Jewish Deli" cookies. Very good cakes - but priced a bit high.  Need 48 hours notice for large cakes.  A good place to know about for sure!

Our 7 year old is a crafting wiz - albeit I am inept at such things.  We visited Jo-Ann on a surprisingly busy Sunday evening.  4 people working in the IMMENSE store (understaffed) but still, friendly and efficient service.  Amber (??) who was running the show, cutting fabric, re-stocking bolts and cashiering was great.  They honored all 3 of our 50% off (single item) coupons. We got alot of needed fabric, notions, needles and supplies.  LOVE IT.

This is the City Nails in Penn Center - the yelp map is incorrect.  Meanwhile some of the City Nails are good and others are disgusting.  This one is in-between.  The Guy who runs the place is very nice.  They still use sub-par base & top coats and will try to pass them off as Essie or OPI.    Come during a non-peak time and get better service.  My daughter loves it here - but she's 6.  Meanwhile they have always been very kind and generous to her.
I love TJ's and this location is no exception. The parking lot is always packed if you come Monday - Friday over lunch though.  Excellent products especially frozen foods.

This is the location in the Pennsport Shopping Plaza - right next to SuperFresh.  I actually have had great luck in here - and especially during the semi-annual sale events.  Candles for $5.00, old packaging designs for body wah & lotion for $2 or $3.  The sales associates greeted me and were friendly and helpful.  Sometimes the store is very crowded and other times absolutely dead.  I like to shop when it's not crowded - so I like that.  Glad to have one that's not in a mall. (Especially since the one on 17 & Walnut closed).

So glad that Angela and the gang are still going strong after 2 years, delivering wings, ribs, corn dogs and FABULOUS fried shrimp to Drexel/Hahnemann students and others.  Wednesday is 1/2 price boneless wings and Monday is the Shrimp deal.  Love to take my 6 year old here - as I, probably should not even contemplate eating this.  It's an OCCAISIONAL treat only.  And we get celery in lieu of fries - and I get a salad - so I feel a little less guilty.  Bring on the fried shrimp! And corn dogs. (Big and slightly sweet batter.)  Umm!

Saget's has been picking up and dropping off my dry-cleaning and this service is pricey - but so worth it as a timesaver for me.  John (the Manager) is terrific and custoimer service has been gresat - they bill me monthly and charge it right to my card.  Best of all the cleaning is expertly done and my clothes look great.

A McDonald's seems so out of place here amogst the shi-shi shops on Walnut Street.  That and it is a haven for local down & outs seeking a $1 McChicken and a coke or coffee.  I rarely ever set foot in here. (But admittedly I have once or twice.)  Yick!
We had such a great time.  Our host was a great guy and we (12 of us) escaped from the "Speakeasy" with seconds to spare.  I would recommend trying this for sure.

It's hotel food - and usually I might give a place like this 2 stars - but I am giving 3 due to VERY nice service and we lingered a very, very long time.  The main dining room was nearly empty (but the bar was hoping for happy hour) on the week night we went.  A good friend of mine who is vegetarian got the pasta with goat cheese which looked very good.  The female server was superb!  Very attentive and brought us apples and nuts (with a nut cracker) to snack on.  While there are far better choices nearby - this was a warm safe place to kill a few hours on a bitterly cold afternoon.

So upset I do not know where to begin. I will call the store later today and try to get my issues resolved, but basically they wanted to do $1300 - $1400 worth of (according to my dealer) un-needed repairs and they did a shoddy job on my oil change.  I would up paying for a 2nd oil change and a completely different roster of repairs at the dealership.  I am very hesitant to ever come back here.

Once again, Eyesite and Gene have gotten me a WINNER!!!  I am in love, love, LOVE with my new glasses. They are from Belgium and very unique looking. They make me feel like a butterfly when I wear them. They are so light and comfortable - and GORGEOUS.  I absolutely love to shop for eyewear - and I go to lots of higher-end shops, but EYESITE is where I purchase my frames and lenses.  Simply the best.

Most choices were really great (avoid the chickenparm - awful.) like my crab-stuffed ravioli, over broccoli rabe.  St. Louis Ribs were fall-off-the bone tender.  There is a slight "SYSCO" pre-fab element to the food - but for the most part we love a nice weekend lunch here.  Burgers (patty melts, southwest style) are a solid choice.  Upgrading to Sweet potato fries is a good idea!

I jokingly call this place Oh So Mediocre - but really it is pretty good.  The Korean lady who runs the place is very, very nice and always asks about my daughter.  The hot & cold food bar is fairly clean with a wide variety of choices, some of which are actually healthy.  (Be careful - many of the hot foods are loaded with oil/fat).  If you really want something good here, though - skip the "pig bar" and head to the back for a fresh grilled turkey burger.  You'll have to be prepared to wait several long minutes - but it is worth it.  Cheap and tasty - not at all dry.  I got my T-burger with Ketchup, tomato and lettuce.  3.75.  What a deal. Oh So Good.

Now that I am working in this area, I must confess that I am frequenting Qdoba far too often - however the Craft 2 menu allows me to eat one, save one - and thus not consume the requisite 750 cal minimum.  (Beans plus rice plus any meat choice = about 660 alone).  Also the "new" whole wheat tortilla is 270 cals (not 330). Additionally, they introduced a slightly spicy brown rice (a few calories less per serving than the white) in February 2013.  I don;t like it though, so I still get the bad-for-you-white rice.  Still, a cheap, calorie-bomb on the go. Oh - and I have to give a shout-out to Antoine - the cute (nearly looks like L'il Wayne!) cashier who is super cool and friendly.

My husband had a minor surgical procedure at Rothman's Surgi-Center on the 4th Floor and he was well cared for - but there was a long wait (we arrived at 8 AM and he was prepped right away but not seen by the doctor until close to 11:30 AM.  Eek.)  We got outta there just after 1 PM.  Follow-up care and administrative staff seemed good also.

What a remarkable gem in South Philly - and a perfect event space for the MANNA PA fist annual Guac-off.  Friendly staff at reception, clean restrooms, small kitchenette.  Good stuff!  You can even have a wedding here.
So far so good - I was a Commerce Bank client and now bank at TD Bank by default.  Jury's still out as I discovered an erroneous charge and need to have it investigated.

There are some great little gems tucked away in this part of town. The Clay Studio, The Wood Turning Studio - there's a bunch of artsy studios, a few BYOs scattered about and yes, tha Park-o-minium and other parking facilities.  Easy walk to Old(e) City - let's not start THAT debate again,  (Whether or not Old City has an "e" on the end of Old.  What ehvs.  Anyhow, I like this area just fine.
Thought this was outta biz?  Is it back?

This is a great place to go if you live in the city and have kids. The wait-list is waaaaaay too long though, so we usually go as guests of friends of ours who belong.  You also can't bring food in - so know that, too.

I'm sorry - but ANJOU is WEAK!!!  From the outside it looks appealing.  The menu sounds like it's gonna be good - if a bit pricey.  MEH.  MEH. MEH.  Sorry.  Nothing special here.  Go to Pizzicato, Mizu, Uzu or some other nearby place.  There are oodles of them to choose from.
3-4 stars rating for EVENTS & Ballrooms (we did not stay at the hotel).  The space is lovely and events are well planned and well run here.  And the location is sooooo convenient.

Great cappuccino and other espresso based drinks.  Plus good salads, hummus and snack-y foods.  Free wifi and comfy, homey seating.  Cute barristas (male & female) and well poured shots of eeeeeeeeeee.  Comfortable homey environment.  Beats the hell outta fourbucks.  I'm a fan!

On the scale of Chuck E. Cheese's this is a solid 2 stars -maybe 3.  We attended a friend of our child's birthday party here and it was typical chaos. Many of the games were broken and the place was clearly understand.  However, the staff that was there was very attentive and the lady who helped our party was great/  Very patient with the kids and the birthday girl got the "1000 ticket" ticket in the ticket blaster.   I generally loathe Chuck E. Cheese - but my kid loves it - and we did have a good time.

OK, This review is based on my U-haul rental in February...  wait for it... 1993.  I was a student at Penn and moved out (one way) to San Francisco.  (Wow - I can't believe I came back!)  The entire experience was a miserable wreck - literally and firguatively. The truck was filthy and had a governor (speed max) on it so we could not go above 55 - which on cross-country 60 mph roads (where most travel at 70-80) was downright dangerous.  NEVER AGAIN!

Went there again tonight - and while the decor sure ain't 5 star - the food absolutely is!!!  Shrimp Scampi . The world's BEST baba. Simple grilled veggies with chunks of feta.  So cheap (cash only at this location) and so tasty.  Killer waitresses - they attack - beware!

Needed Urgent Care (ER/ true emergency) for our 11 year old and had 5 star treatment from all staff, however we arrived on a Monday night at 6:10 PM and although triaged right away were not seen until around 9:20 PM by a resident.  (over 3 hours waiting and waiting.)  Once seen treatment, diagnosis and medications arrived quickly. Mikey (female) the respiratory therapist was truly exceptional and a wonderful care giver. Laura, patient liasion, was terfic and the Doctor - Dr. M. W. Attia is terrific.  I hope we don;t need to come back but if we ever do, we'll be coming to Dupont!  Beautiful facility.

A nice surprice on Walnut Street - a deli with some healthier choices, like fresh cut veggies (carrot, celery, cucumber, green and yellow bell peppers and a few grape tomatoes) with dip for $3.19.  Sandwiches, coffee and grocery items, too.

I can not say enough good things about Gene and the staff at eyesite. They are the ONLY place I get glasses now.  I have 4 pairs and 1 pair of sunglasses and 2 clips (one was custom made).  Excellent!

This small outpost of Manhattan Bagel is relatively well-run and offers the same choices as other Manhattan Bagels' and decent coffee for $1.59 for a small.  Not my favorite - but OK for a quick morning bagel or coffee run.

We bought our 2007 Hyundai Sonata from Fred Beans.  Over the years my family and my husband's family have each bought many different cars - new and pre-owned - of different makes from Fred Beans.  Between them and Foster & Kardane (and we were friendly with the Kardane clan back in the '80's) they pretty much OWN the D-town automotive scene.  Competitive prices and salespeople who don't make you feel like a target.  Good repair work, too.  I'm sorry to hear that Sub S. had a bad experience.  Ours has been fine - and we still have and love our car 4 years later.

I had not been to a benihana on over 20 years - and back then ist was teppanyaki only (no real sushi). Ah, the '80's - and we all owe a debt to Rocky Ayoki.  The sushi selections have improved a bit - although fish selections are limited and the Hamachi Hand Roll I had was sub-par.  (Tamago was froze - for $2.75 a piece).  Prices were too high for that sort of mediocrity.  Service was harried - we were seated on a rainy Sunday at 7 PM in the bar area, albeit with our picky 7 year old who did not care for her $3.90 Strawberry Lemonade.  (She had water instead.)  Edamame was boiled within an inch of its life.  My MIL had a tasty steak teriyaki - surprisingly yhe best of the lot. Oh and for $4.00 a single round blob of chocolate Hagen Daaz was unceremoniously plopped in a dished and thrown at my child.  Not in a hurry to return.

Xo-Cheat on your diet!  It's Xo-worth it and Xo-great to come here.  I love the Oaxacan cuisine and kick-y cocktails with real tropical fruits used in making them.  I have been here twice already and, although pricey - and sometimes unbearably crowded, I will be back again and again.  It's Xo-Good!  The Aussie Bartender is muy, muy caliente! Try a couple of Dona Florinda cocktails with fresh prickly pear cactus fruit.  Super Yum!

OMG I practially live here. (And not just as a commuter rushing thru every day.)  Every 2 weeks I have a 1-2 hour wait here to pick up my little girl.  It's always iffy as to exactly when her deadbeat dad will return her safely home - so I know every cop in the place.  (Alas, they are rarely there when you need them.)   I also know the Amtrak red caps Rich & Rich (the cigar smoking one is our fave) who work weekends.  We also know the nice Korean lady who owns the flower stand with her husband.  They give my little girl flowers every so often.   And the lady who chops the fruit at the Smoothie stand is nice too.  Oh, and Susan with the hairy upper lip who man's (or wo-man's) the Hertz rent-a-car booth is a godsend.  She allowed my daugheter to play with the (broken) yellow hertz phone and "call" people.  There is good and bad in every situation and I sure am making lemonade out of a BIG Honkin' Meyer Lemon that life handed to me.

Yes, it's expensive. No, you can;t do your "regular" shopping here but it is terrific for taking kids.  We came for the "No Kid Hungry" cupcake event (for $3 kids could decorate a chocolate or vanilla cupcake) and the kids (both age 9) loved it.  My daughter loves to shop the bulk candy department and there are some unique holiday gift ideas here also.  Look into their cosmetics (Pacifica for CHEAP!) and chocolate bar sections.  No, it's not cheap - but there are some unique items here that I can't get at Whole Foods (aka Whole Paycheck) nor Trader Joe's.

I confess, I am a Sephora and Ulta shopper - I price compare on ebay, also and it pains mne to pay retail after spending YEARS in the spa industry.  Meanwhile, I stock up on Tweezerman, NARS, Lorac, MUFE (Makeup Forever) and other staples at this Center City location.  The ever-changing line up of staff (usually young overly-made up MUAs) is friendly and usually pretty knowledgable about makeup.  Skin care?  Not as much.  Meanwhile, I love Sephora - and have since its creation. It continues to evolve.
Needed mass quantities of Guac, Pico 'n Chips for a picnic stat. Qdoba to the rescue - for $21 and change we had plenty for all.

Service was excellent from manager (owner?) Melinda and our server Ledesha. Food was just OK. (But I am pretty spoiled from NYC and Philly.)  The sashimi platter I had ($26) had some winners (fluke and sea bass) and losers (paler, poorly cut tuna, odd tasting salmon and cheap escolar "white" tuna).  DH ordered a specialty roll (called the "Thank You" roll) for $18.  Oy vey.  Strange "crunchy" fishy topping that we did not like.  Lots of fruit -mango and strawberries.  That said, we will be back - but try more affordable, conventional maki next time. There is no way I would get sashimi here again.  High prices (2 roll lunch combo is $12, 3 roll is $15.  I pay $12 for a 3 roll combo at Vic's in Philly.).  I am not sure how I feel yet - so 3 stars for now - and hopefully it will go up - not down.

Upon my teen daughter's pleading request, I caved and picked up 2 take out items at the now-dreaded Qdoba in Springfield.  What'd'ya know?  Everything was fresh and great again.  It helped that there was a new (at least new to my eyes) manager and that we cam at 11:50 AM on a Thursday before the lunch hordes had descended.  Steak burrito and Steak burrito bowl (both with Guac) were both great.  I truly hope the "badness" of the past is in the past. Management and team makes all the difference.  The female team lead (front counter) is friendly and good!  Give her a raise!

I have been to this Starbucks many times - right across the stress from CVS - and close to my former job.  No issues - very busy during morning rush (as is expected).  Good service and consistent beverage quality.  $5 coffees.  Whoo-hoo!

Standard Starbuck - mid-size location (Not huge and not tiny). Decent service - youngish staff of disinterested baristas just "doing their job".  Efficient but not warm nor friendly.  Drinks were fine - I got my kid a decaf frappucino so she was in 11 year old heaven. Ice tea was fine.  No big whoop. Glad it's here to get our four-bucks fix.

Had dinner here last night and it was just OK. Greek salad that came with dinner was good but lettuce was overly wet.  (Odd.)  Chicken Francese was swimming (drowning) in a heavy buttery sauce.  The chicken itself (I pulled it out of the sauce and put it on another plate) was good though.  Not a holy grail, but a much needed place in a culinary wasteland.

I received help over the phone and it was fine - I signed up for a 2 year membership for myself and my husband.  We got the cheaper one with 3 miles of towing.  There is also a more expensive membership with up to 100 miles of towing.  We shall see what happens if we need these services over the next 2 years.

Now that I work right near this Target, I can't help but run in from time to time for household goods, frozen entrees for lunch on the cheap and of course, a latte from Starbucks.  Lunch hour can get busy - but if you go at 10 - 11 AM (sure, my boss will love that!) it's ded in there.  Weekends?  Another story.  Parking lot is big but gets full and a bit of a cluster getting in and out.  Bonus:  I can stop at Petsmart, too.  And Trader Joes' is walking distance.  Lots of shopping in a compact area.

The desserts OTHER than ice cream are so yummy here.  The gargantuan slices of pecan or apple pie (topped with yummy ice cream, if you wish) are so great.  The sandwiches and soups are good too - but defintiely save room for dessert.  That is what  this place is famous for.  In the old days we'd get cream of broccoli soup here - so good - so rich and a slice of warm pecan pie with ice cream on top.  Mmmn mmmn!
Fresh local produce - and a summer must for corn and 'maters. They even accept credit cards - a big plus these days.  Love it!

Selection and location 4 stars, Surly/Bitchy customer service - 1 star. Price 3 stars.  I stopped in here looking for leotards (hopefully something sparkly or USA themed - they had none of that) for my 8 year old's recent gymnastics obsession.  Now, part of this was my own damned fault as I was talking on my cell phone (engrossed actually) as I entered the store and basically waved at the woman and pointed to my phone.  I tried to wrap up the conversationbut the person went on and on and I dd eventually hang up.  By then the woman had wrttenme off - which kinda sucked, because I did end up finding 2 "close-out sale" short sleeved, solid-color, basic leotards at VERY inexpensive prices (and thus non-returnable).  This place is Kickin' it old-skool - literally. Leos, skirts, ballet shoes, tap shoes, costumey things. A dancers paradise - save for the surly service. Glad they are still around - as this type of place is a dying breed.  Do not multi task in this store!!!

This corner gas station has been many types or gas station over the 35 years I have known it.  It was a Shell, a BP and even a Sunoco for a while.  Now, it's LukOIl and prices are great.  Usually well below the local average price.

I really love Angela - the owner of the new Wings to Go on the Corner of Vine & 15th.  So, I ordered a bunch of party platters (boneless wings & buffalo shrimp) for a party I had.  Everything was piping hot, fresh and perfect.  I really want people to support this much needed busines on an otherwise "dead" block.  Need wings?  Catfish?  Shrimp?  Corndogs?  Come here to get them.

I received a flaming email from someone at this restaurant immediately after I posted my review.  My review stands and I stand by what I experienced.  I had a horrible time at Mixx and now, after being harassed online there is no way i will ever return here.

Not sure why so many raves. The place is so dingy and needs a good cleaning. They do offer many authentic dishes like Duck Tongue and Frog, but we were not interested.  We got the ($32) Peking Duck and the meat was dry. Eggplant with garlic sauce (the best dish of the night) was so hot we could barely eat it.  Food is very spicy - even dishes marked mild (but that is also part of the Szechuan experience).  Compared to Han Dynasty in Philly - this place is awful.  Not coming back any time soon.

This is the same as the "Falafel Cart" reviews - same guy on 20 & Market. Line down the block.  You get what you get - and it's usually good - but I like Mama's better, Meanwhile, people LOVE this cart.

Came in for my 5-6 month prophy and saw Kara - who is a new hygenist and TERRIFIC.  She took text-book perfect bitewings (digital, baby!) and Dr. D is great as always. Plus I love LeeAnn (sp??) - the office manager.  Such a well-run place!  Plus I got strawberry prophy paste.  Wheeeeeee!

Went back to see Ruth, RDH for my 4-5 month prophy and it was a dreamy, easy-breezy $85 experience as usual.  The staff is very nice and appointments are confirmed in advance.  I LOVE THIS PRACTICE!!!!

This remains our go-to Rita's and the young teen staff is friendly and polite - in the summer (evenings) the lines can get longer.  We enjoy an occasional custard or "wooder" ice treat here.  Tip:  Ask for the kiddie size to save calories and money.  Benches and tables to sit at outdoors.

We have been here Twice over the past 18 months that we have lived in the area.  Our 8 year old loves Friendlys - but my husband and I are not big fans.  This location is relatively clean - but the service is sooooooo slow.  I mean bordering on ridiculously slow.  We came last night for a late dinner - around 8 PM and did not get our food until 8:40.  Kiddo was getting a little shiny by then - but finally it came out.  Meanwhile my husband's salad was "blah" and my "build your own" burger was actually pretty good.  Not a holy grail by any means - but with kids in tow it's a safe option.  Just don;t come here f you're in a hurry.

I have been taking classes at Fuel House (I buy packs of ten classes for $80) for 2 months now and I have lost over 5 lbs.  I am seriously considering the Unlimited Monthly membership.  There are a few classes that are NOT Zumba - like "Boot Camp" and Tabata (a high intensity interval training 30 minute workout).  There are also a few "easier" classes - which I like since my fitness level is low.  If you are a serious athlete - this is probably not the place for you, but if you are a middle-aged suburban mom with pounds to lose - come on by!!!  It's perfect for me.

I am a huge proponent of food co-ops, locavores, slow foodism, sustainable agriculture and the like - so I was thrilled to visit the medium-sized - very crowded Weaver's Way.  We have very few of these types of food coops in Philly - but when I lived in NYC there were many - in Brooklyn and Manhattan - where you could both shop and participate as a member.  Even though it's not flawless - there is a big space issue - I am so happy to have them here and I will continue to buy my brown eggs, brown rice, and brown bread here when I am in the nabe!  Oh - and they sell locally farmed Christmas trees and greens during the holiday season.  Go Weaver's!!!

A great place to get a salad, pizza or (rich and tasty) pasta for lunch.  Kinda pricey - but the portions (of pasta anyhow) are big.  I can eat half for lunch and the rest later. (dinner!!!)  I have been there now a bunch of times - many for lunch (and it is usually hoppin') and another time for a quick dinner. (They close at 7 PM.)  Both times I had pasta dishes - but my husband had pizza (he said it was good but not great.) and a friend had a salad that he LOVED.  I really enjoyed my fresh fettuccine dish and a was able to substitute marinara for the usual rich cream sauce.  The cashier was freiendly even though she was slammed with customers, and my order was processed relatively quickly.  I'll return.

Philadelphia's Chinatown may not be the largest - but it has many wonderful things to explore.  Of course, the wonderful food - restaurants, tea houses, pastry & bake shops and grocery stores.  Also Chinese culture - and gifts galore.  Much fun to come here during the Chinese New Year - but to me it is even better to come here when it is NOT a celebration - just a "normal" day - like on a Tuesday or Wednesday in the spring or fall and stroll the streets and have a leisurely lunch.  Must explore Chinatown!

Not good, Temaki. I am sorry to report that our last visit (albeit it was "Dining Under the Stars" aka "Chaos out in the Heat") the service and food quality both were Just "Meh".  Mike tried hard to please us but after receiving 2 warm and watery diet cokes (they were, thankfully, removed from the bill) and cold, soggy sweet potato tempura rolls - I am not a fan.  Also, this is now the 2nd time the salmon tasted "fishy".  Fresh raw salmon should not taste this way.  Unfortunately for me, my 8 year old ADORES the place - especially the tasty shrimp shumai (served with a saffron cream sauce and fresh sweet corn kernels) and california rolls.  We'll be back - and pray you won't take it out on us, but food and beverage quality needs to improve.  The female manager is very sweet. I think the guy hates me.  (He might really hate me now.)    :(

I am giving 5 stars not so much to the coffee shop (which is about 3.5 stars) but to the FABULOUS customer service we got from Nicolas Capes at the MAIN site of La Colombe.  You see, we wanted to have individually wrapped foil pouches of coffee as wedding favors for our June 2008 nuptuals.  DiBruno Brother's couldn;t help us.  Neither could Dunkin Donuts, nor Cappriccio (though the manager tried).  The coffee favors available on "wedding" websites as favors is sub-par pre-bagged swill.  We wanted QUALITY - and with La Colombe - our guests got it - for reasonable coin, too.  We ordered a case (96 pouches) of the house blend and bagged each pouch in a cute little tulle bag, and added a Yankee Candle "buttercream" votive.  Between the coffe and the cream - our closet smelled heavenly.  The coffee favors were a huge hit and La Colombe is the ONLY Philly coffee place to come through for us.

Nope. After I wrote my last (negative) review of my once-loved Qdoba, we went again. I needed a catering size Pico and a catering size Guac and chips.  Every time I do this (and I have now done it 3 times) I get charged a different price. This time the manager (who was running the register also) tried to charged me $8 for a catering size bag of chips (enormous) which is not what I wanted or needed.  I forked over the $10, took my guac, pico and chips and left.  Not happy.  Twice in a row now.  Not coming back. So sad. My 12 year old loves it here and I used to like it, too, but no longer.

Every summer my little daughter (who's now 5) and I "play tourist".  Even though we live in Philly - we had never tried the duck boats - and she really wanted to.  We reserved for a Wednesday tour at 4 PM.  It lasted lust over 70 minutes and was GREAT fun.  Our Captain (Crash) was funny and the tour woulda been great for a tourist or someone unfamiliar with Philly.  There were tourists from Brazil, Arizona, Iowa and Florida on our boat. And since it was not packed we each got our own seat.  Yes, it's pricey, kitschy, touristy and those quackers can me MOST irritating - but if you have little kids this is a fun way to show them the city.  That said - my kid also loved the Double-Decker bus tour.

OK, so Jones Group (As in Jones NY) who owns 9West, Enzo Angolini and many other brands, decided to rip out the 9 West in Liberty Place and replace it with "Shoe Woo" - the new concept that allows a variety of Jones brands to live together all in one store.  Decor is cutesy and brand new - with a few rotating turntables that showcase lots of mid-priced platform heels, seasonal boots and others.  My 6 year old thinks it's paradise.  Boy do they start early!  Sale shoes range from $30 - $100 - not bad if you can find your size in a sale style you like.

Yum, artery clogging, yum.   Fried Chicken. Mac and Cheeeeese.  The decor is straight outta the designer's "retro" wish list.   I can see Marsha Brady.  Great for some nap inducing corporate catering, too.  I'll write more later and elaborate.

This is a nice store - though a bit cramped.  It is not as good as Penzey's though - I bought granulated garlic at both and Penzey's was fresher and cheaper.  The salt-free lemon pepper blend from Spice corner looks promising and the service was excellent.  Nice staff working there.  Glad to see them in business.

This is a BEAUTIFUL pet store - but it is also pricey.  I guess we are helping them pay the rent in pricey Glen Eagle Square?  Right near the Whole Foods - so for me it is convenient - but I can get the Eukeneuba my rescue-mutt likes for much cheaper in Newtown Square at Delchester feed.  For toys and gifts?  this place is great! Plus they help adopt out cats and kittens.  There is also a clean-looking grooming salon in the back but you pay them to wash your own dog.  (It's like a self-service car wash for dogs.)  I don't see the point in this unless you have a big and very messy dog?  I bathe my mutt at home, so I will not use this service.  I'd rather pay for someone else to take care of the entire bathing process, or else save $$ and do it at home myself.  Nice selection of treats, too.

Absolutely delicious and perfectly cooked burgers that are not too big.  A little more expensive than 5 guys - but much better.  A great place for a haute-fast-food burger fix.  I got mine "Classic" with Cheddar.  No fries, no shake for me.  The burger was just enuf.

What a find!  What a lucky break! My 11 year old recently enrolled in dance lessons and needed shoes, tights, leotards - the works!  DanceLine and their terrific staff saved the day. They even have "Foot Undies" -  like little underwear for feet -used in lyrical dancing.  We'll be back!

Single surface ice facility for USFSA (Figure Skating) plus a few public skate times each week - call first to be sure.   No real seating.  A few minor level competitions per year.  They have a 1/2 day skating camp in the summer.  Locker room is very old, Training room is small. We are spoiled by Iceworks.  Very nice lady runs the skating program.  Apparently, Scott Hamilton trained here for a while, decades ago.
Big Target with groceries and all "the usual" Target-y stuff. No issues.  Parking lot, although enormous, is packed on weekend.  Surburbia-typical.

OMG I echo Emily A.  I just discovered the Italian Market (I know, I know -what took me so long) and I went to Claudio's for home-made ricotta (so creamy, fresh and good - and CHEAP - $2.99 a lb.) and mozzarella.  Can't weait to pre-order a Burrate for later this month.  Burrata is Mozzarella with a creamy-buttery cream in the middle - so decadent.  I have FOUND my source for mozzarella.  Hooray!
Just OK as Saladworks goes - could be fresher in the lettuce department. Meanwhile, I love Saladworks and have visited a few locations.  This one is fairly large. Gets crowded during the lunch rush.

My bad.  My mistake.  I shoulda known better. I stopped in for a "squagel" (whole grain with cream cheese). I was given a number (73) and told to wait. I waited about 3-4 minutes. Not worth it.  Sat like LEAD inside my stomach.  I did it before a few years ago, and I guess I forgot. Now I remember.  I will not be back to Cosi.

Better.  The new server/hostess Brianna (sp?) is lovely and we were warmly welcomed at 8:50 PM on a Tuesday.  (Our first choice was CLOSED.  Ouch.  Again, I ask - don;t suburban folk eat dinner?)  The secret?  Order cooked items.  The sweet potato roll and Shrimp Tempura roll were absolutely fine.  I stay away from sashimi, nigiri etc. here.  Been burned too many times. Meanwhile my 10 year old gobbles up the shrimp shumai (frozen, I think) in a delectable saffron cream sauce with fresh corn.

Tara, the manager, is a sweetie and we ordered alot of customized wedding gifts from Papyrus - and Tara took our orderes.  We also get Thank-you notes and birthday cards there.  Papyrus has upscale cards, stationary and gifts.  The store is small - but still navigable.  Although I wound up getting my wedding invitations done at Details (who rock - by the way.) I would certainly shop here (we did - but found a similar design for a bit less money at Details.) for custom wedding and party invitations.  When you shop around - come here - they will have what you need.

We had a fine experience here with our (then) 3 year old - but it was about a year ago so maybe since then it has gone downhill?  We had burgers and chicken sandwiches and my daughter's kiddie meal came in a paper car.  She loved it.  We had a nice lunch here and would go back.

Ok, I came here on the advice of co-workers who basically said "Don't eat at Long River" - which is across the street from my office.  So I trudged over the 2-3 blocks to Golden Chopstick, stood in a pretty long line and ordered a Chicken & Stringbean lunch special with brown rice to go. "Light on the sauce", I implored.  Service was friendly and the order took about 6-8 minutes to come out (not bad considering there were 7 people ahead of me.)  Walked the take-out grub back to my desk and voila.  Tasteless - abut thankfully not greasy due to the lack of sauce.  Beans were the best part - crisp.  Chicken (thankfully white meat) was bone dry and flavorless.  Not sure If I'd ever come back.  Now I am really in fear of Long River.  This is supposed to be the "good" Chinese place near my office.  Oh well.

OK, I bit the bullet and joined as an Unlimited Member for $50 per month.  My 9 year old kids loves it here too (but refuses to take the kiddie classes - she wants to take the ones I take - including Piloxing - a cross between boxing and Pilates - which is a terrific class.  I love the instructors here and many of the ladies who go here (there are a handful of men -it's mostly women) have become casual acquaintences.  I have nothing but great things to say about Fuel House. Try the Zumba - but also try the non-Zumba offerings.  Jodi, Stephanie & the team are terrific!

OMG!  A bar where you can smoke (and smoke, and smoke).  And they have a cigarette machine ($9 a pack).  A real honest-to-goodness cigarette machine.  And super friendly bartenders (like Mark on Wednesday nights) and patrons.  Classic rock on the "juke box".  Cheap-ass drinks served in plastic cups.  Fun, smoke-filled, drunken debauchery. A real working-man's bar!

I have passed this place many times over the years but it always looked creepy to me so I never ventured in.  Well, today I HAD to get breakfast stat - and decided to go inside.  Good food (solid diner fare) to go, nice ladies at the counter.  I'll be back for a lunch soon!
Fine. Had the Thai Wonton Bowl and the broth was way too salty but the veggies were great. No issues.
A great place to attend interesting college type and post-collegiate events.  A horrendous place to live.  ICK.  The dorms are in dire need of a makeover.  (And extermination for bugs.)

Well, it's 6 years later and Tokyo Sushi is still here and seems to be larger than I remember it.  I picked up a 3 roll combo from the pre-made case at $12 which have 4 pieces each of tuna (fine), salmon (fine) and Yellowtail (surprisingly very good) with scallions - all in brown rice and rather large pieces.  I am pleased and Shall return now that I am back in this area again.  Seems more like a "real" sushi place now and less like "supermarket" sushi.  Next time I will order some nigiri to order.  My only complaint?  $7 - $9.5 for a sinlge handroll (They call theirs a demaki vs. temaki)??? Way too high.    All in all very pleased and will return - and soon!

Three cheers for the kielbasi boys (one of them was smokin' hot!) and their CHEESESTAK filled pierogies.  They gave our group of 11 a tour of the smokehouse - and we got to sample the turkey kielbasi, and several other varieties.  You gotta check this place out!  This is the real deal.    $8.00 a dozen. Cash only.

Chaotic to shop here - but good values on crafting, art and school supplies.  We come here and Michael's and depending on what 'specials' or coupons are offered you can really do well here.  Back to school time (Late August/Early Sept) is madness.  Holiday season is pretty busy, too.  Not always a "floor" person when you need one - but generally we can wander around and find what we need,  Glad they exist.

While we still prefer Fellini's in downtown Media (not sure if they are the same owner or not - but the menus are very similar) we had a good experience - especially with Jessica, our helpful, friendly server.  Fellini's offers solid Italian (and lots of pasta) dishes.  Salads and Antipasto are also good here.  Crowded as heck on weekends - we squeaked in at 6:45 PM on a Saturday and somehow lucked out - there was a line to get in minutes later.  Love the Chicken with Eggplant in Aurora sauce (rich and fattening - but so tasty.) Decaf cappuccino for dessert was spot-on!  As said before - BYOB - can get noisy from drunk and happy customers. Carbo-load!

You're kidding?  I am so sorry to hear about the bad reviews below.  We rented a HUGE pole tent, tables, chairs and LARGE fans for a summer anniversary party for my parent's surprise 40th anniversary in 2006.  We dealt with Mary Beth Brilman (and also got quotes from 2-3 other vendors).  They did a site visit to make sure the tent ewould work, delivered and picked up the items exactly as ordered.  It's a shame that laura and april had botched events.  Mine was smooth as silk.

The Doylestown Farmers Market runs from late spring through mid-autumn in the parking lot at Oakland & Hamilton Streets.  There is a good selection of produce, meat, dairy, egg & beauty product vendors.    I love coming here early in the morning when they are first setting up (don;t come too late or many of the goodies are sold out) and getting whatever looks freshest - Berries in June, Greens & Beans, and goat cheeses.  Great for kids & dogs.  Support your local farmers and farmers markets! Bring cash - but a few places accept plastic.

Odd. Tacos & Donuts???    I did not have any donuts but they looked good. I got a Chopped Salad with overcooked (but tasty - great spice on it) steak.  Would have been great if the meat were at least pink.  (It was well, well, well done.)  $8.47 for a cheap lunch.  Not rushing back though.

This is more of a friend-with-an-expense account place.  The faux shi-shi atmosphere is really getting played out.  I enjoyed my meal - the tiger shrimp were flavorful, but I would have prefered the heads to have been removed.  I also thought the prices were not worth it for the quality and quantity of the food.  Pearl is nice - not bad, really, but there are much finer dining experiences to be had.

Went here today for lunch with an old, old friend who I haven't seen for about 15-18 years.  (Really.)  We both had lunch specials - He got a 3 roll for $13 and I got a 2 roll for $10.  Both came with a choice of soup or salad and we both had a good (albeit generic) fresh salad with tasty dressing.  The Ginza roll was excellent - cooked salmon, mayo, oinion and tempura flakes.  Crunchy and very Americanized - but good.  My yellowtail roll was just OK.  I can tell the quality of this place is not high end - but for a cheap sushi lunch I would, in fact, go back.  Service was unassuming and prompt - the large dining area was not even close to busy - maybe 4 tables occupied.  I would never waste my money on all-you-can-eat sushi (or all-you-can-eat anything for that matter) since I don't go for quantity - I need quality.  This place is OK - but no holy grail.

I rather like Ruby's.  It has a "Johnny Rocket's" faux-retro feel to it and you can get the healthy veggie burger and nopt eat all that fried food.  It's inexpensive and a nice place to take a break from the hectic mall.  It's good for lunch or an afternoon snack and you can brin g the kids without fear.  The burgers (I get the veggie kind) are flavorful, too.
It's a chain and it has what I need.  It's reasonably convenient. Not yuppified at all.  Service is minimal but I am usually able to find the dog-related supplies I need right away.

I had a very pleasant 4 star experience an Nooddi - but it is really a 3 star kinda place (needs a makeover!).  But - I happened to get there before 6 PM and got the early dinner special which is a great value.  A cup of Tom Kha soup. 2 steamed crab dumplings (delish!) and a generous portion of Chicken or Tofu Pad-See-Yu.  Loved every bite. And my wallet thanked me.  Great service - place was empty on a Thursday at 5:40 PM.  No, it's not the best Thai ever - but it'll do and I will be back - and likely soon.

Yes, they are high-end and expensive - but the frames are gorgeous.  (My French frames from face a face were 420 alone - plus 200 for the lenses and 150 for the sunglass clip which was custom made.)  Gene the Owner and Ala the optician were very easy to work with and the glasses were ready quickly.  (Just got  the matching custom sunglass clip.)  Ok that's $770 for 1 pair of glasses.  Egads! (Do NOT tell my parents who would FLIP out.)  I spent way more than I could afford - but they offered to charge my credit card in 2 installments - so that helped me out a wee bit.  I look great and am so happy.  Alain Mikli - eat your heart out. I am so lovin' this place.  I will be back for sure!!!!

Never had a problem with a quick slice from Spatola's years ago. Not a wholt lot of choices around here - but there are better (and worse) places to grab some garlic knots and a slice or two.  No issues from me.

This ain't my bag, baby. The free one hour of "build your own" martinis was great - for FREE - and then it was $5.00 apiece after 9 PM.  My husband got completely hammered by downing 3 of the candy garnished concoctions is 55 minutes.  It was just way too frat-boy in there - and the lack of waitress servce made it impossible for us to even order food.  (Thus we were both pretty trashed while drinking on an empty stomach.)  The cute bartender-boy made me a very tasty cosmo - but I was just as happy with my cranberry, vodka & lime.  If it were not for the "free" ploy marketing - we'd never have gone in.  And unless there's another freebie - we won't return.
Adorable gifts and toys for children - especially young girls.  Cute stuff - but pricey.  We love it there.

3.5 - 4 stars - a very nice Acme as Acme's go. I run in here on occaision for fried chicken (or grilled) - when it is fresh, and milk and other things.  Convenient location - and I can stop at Gentile's before or afterward.

We really enjoyed our 3-4 visits to Ly Michael's.  We've had lunches and dinners there.  The thai-inspried dishes are really tasty as are the Chinese choices. The Duck Dumplings (Appetizer) are so yummy.  We also loved our (medium rare) lamb chop entree.  Even our 4 year old (who then was 2 or 3 liked the food.  Service was great - because the place was nearly empty every time we were there.  I hope they get enough business to survive.  A welcome choice near the convention center. Oh - great specialty martnini's too.  The cheesecake martini tasted almost like the real thing.  (Just boozier.)

Went back again - this time with the fam because i thought my 10 year old would love it here. Sadly, she did not.  She had buffalo chicken tacos and did not like them.  She would up eating my enchilada and she did enjoy that.    Nobody liked the donuts.  It was 8:30 PM on a weeknight and they had been sitting out all day and thus were stale - as i had thought they might be.  We bought them anyway.  Bad move on our part. (I warned my husband not to get any - but he and my kid could not resist.)  Waste of good money!  The donuts sound so great, in theory.  Maybe if you get them the minute they come out?  In the mean time - PLEASE put the lemon cream sauce back on the menu - it covers a multitude of sins.  I wish i could love it here - but in it's present incarnation, I just can't/don't.  Incidentally, the ladies (2) at the front register were friendly and lovely.   there is no true waiter service - you order & pay up front and then sit and wait at a table.

My 8 year old just LOVES it here - from musical instruments to jewelry to hand bags, everything is giftable and comes from a fair-trade community.  It's great fun - but a bit pricey - and nothing here is a neccesity - but if you gotta buy gifts, at least here they are unique and helping another community.  We love it!

Dropped off our car without an appointment (our bad) on a Friday AM for state inspection but did not get the car back until 4:30 PM on Sunday.  Youch.  Meanwhile they made all the minor repairs we needed and charged an OK price (Not great, not horrible).  Wish they were more timely.
Menta's Sunoco is where I've been getting gas these days - as it is right on my way to the Elwyn train station.  Friendly service - full serve and self (full includes a window wash).  I'll be back.

3.5 - maybe even 4 stars.  This is the Tokyo Sushi stand in the Riverfront Market. Today I had a roll combo - 4 pieces each of Salmon, Tuna and Yellowtail - for $9.95.    I also have an order of microwave-heated gyoza for $3.50.  (Your standard frozen gyoza - tasty but in no way mindblowing).  Fish was fresh and tasty, but cut unevenly (the nigiri were a MESS!).  Reminds me of supermarket sushi - but a hair better because the fish is, indeed, fresh.  Just amateurishly presented.  But hey - It's Wilmington, DE in a market.  For that you might give it 5 stars!!!

I had to stop in and see what all the fuss was about - and the folks at Ryan's are very nice.  The service was easily 5 star - but the day I came there was only frozen Italian entrees - nothing fresh or hot.  (I wanna come back for the Veal Scallopine).  From a cold cuts perspective it's more like 4 stars. - A great selection of hoagie makings - Hatfield Liverwurst (our pug liked that) and Milk, Sodas, Eggs and Butter.  I want to return and support this local business.  I vacillate between 3 & 4 stars. Butchers/Delis of this kind are a dying breed, which saddens me.  The world needs more places like this.  Low prices - call in advance for a custom freezer-pack.

My jury is still out on the "new" Comcast Center food court.  I have gotten juices twice at the new juice bar.  DiBruno's is there and a fancy fish market called Under the "C".  I have had juices at Squeeze, the new juice bar (very good and fresh) and Lunch one time at La Scalla - where I got a delicious fettucine in a heavy rosa sauce which made me wish for a post-lunch nap.  I also tried the over-priced sushi from Tokyo Sushi.  Not great but not bad.  I am hopeful that the quality will stay high. The crowds at lunch are pretty large - so it's best to go before 11:50 AM or afetr 2:10 PM

I have now had lunch here twice (both times I had fresh delicious salads) and I am a fan.  Good service, clean comfortable booths and tables, and a large bar.  French onion soup was a tad too salty for my taste and pasta dishes (at lunch) are close to $20 so I will pass on those - but for salads and burgers (my dad had an amazingly good patty melt) we will be back again and again.

OK, I am now officially over my brief infatuation with TFM.  It has changed so much over the past few years that now it's Wegman's, Whole Foods or Trader Joe's for me before I come here.  My kid does not like their sushi (she also hates Trader Joe's sushi), as she is partial to the pricey whole-paycheck Genji Sushi (or going out for "real" sushi).  I miss the old days with the personal care section and bulk candies. Meanwhile, the produce is gorgeous here and the meat department has good deals on selected days - Like Cheap Chicken or Cheap Chuck.  But you have to know when to come for that and I do not shop here regularly any more.  (Wegman's must be killing them and also putting a dent in the Glen Mill's Whole Foods.)  So happy to have options, but if TFM doesn't step up their game, they will not be here 5 years from now.

Pick your own Strawberries in season has given me and now my little one spring after late spring of red-stained -face bliss.  None Such has great, fresh, farm-raised, seasonal produce.  (That means berry bliss in May/June and Corn late summer.)  We love it.  The same family has owned and run None-such for years!

I returned to Slainte today for a business lunch with about 10-12 collegues - and I have to say my opinion has improved.  For "bar food" my lunch was surprisingly fresh and wonderful.  Our server was lovely, friendly, courteous and very efficient.  (Having my firm pick up the tab never hurts!)  I ordered the grilled salmon salad ($12.99) and they added extra cucumbers upon my request,  The fish was delicious and grilled to perfection - not to overdone nor dry.  The apps we shared included the aforementioned greasy-heavy-cheesesteak springrolls - that the guys seemed to love (I am not a big fan, I guess) and very tasty Chicken Quesadillas.  Plus a generous Hummus plate.  Good job, Slainte!  A welcome addition to this nabe!  P.S.  My colleagues ordered the French Onion and "Loaded Baked Potato" soups and both looked excellent.

I am reviewing the Le Scala offshoot in the COMCAST center.  I have been there now twice - once for lunch (and it was hoppin') and another time for a quick dinner. (They close at 7 or 8 PM.)  Both times I had pasta dishes - but my husband had pizza (he said it was good but not great.) and a friend had a salad that he LOVED.  I really enjoyed my fresh fettuccine dish and a was able to substitute marinara for the usual rich cream sauce.  The cashier was freiendly even though she was slammed with customers, and my order was processed relatively quickly both times.  I'll return.
Such a shame - years ago this was THE place and had shopping and a great food court.  Now it is so dead here. And too many t-shirt/key chain vendors.  Sigh...

McCall is a smaller, private golf club - primarily used by PECO employees and clients.  they have a large "ball room" that can accomodate over 100 (maybe over 150??) for a seated affair.  We had a huge business meeting here that included a catered breakfast and lunch - both were very good.  Service is friendly.  Locker rooms are "old school" in feel and the look is a bit dated.  It's an old-school country club feel that is not too snooty. The small cafe/grill is nice for breakfast or lunch as well.

Without Whole Foods and Trader Joe's I'd be sunk. So, Whole Foods - I am be-whole-den to you.  High prices and all - what choice do I have?  My child must have chemical-free, persticide-free, herbicide-free non Genetically Modified organisms on which to feed.  And so I present - An Ode to WHOLE FOODS:  That meat case is impressive!  As are the baked desserts.  The juice bar is a saviour - and sushi never hurts!  O, Whole Foods - how I love thee - though parking really sucks. A least they'll validate the lot and save me a few bux.

I recently discovered the Italian Market (I know, I know -what took me so long?) and I went to Claudio's for home-made ricotta (so creamy, fresh and good - and CHEAP - $2.99 a lb.) and mozzarella.  Can't weait to pre-order a Burrata for later this month.  Burrata is Mozzarella with a creamy-buttery cream in the middle - so decadent.  I have FOUND my source for mozzarella.  Hooray!

Dr. Barry Dubin is the MAN!!!  He is a kind, compassionate dentist who does GREAT work and is up to date on all the latest dental techniques and technologies.  His hygienist, Ruth, is terrific (she's basically who I see - 3 times a year for cleanings.).  The office is well run and well managed.  Plus Dr. Dubin provides great marketing campaigns and incentives for referrals - like Dubin-Dollars.  He even sells gift cards!  What a great idea.  I love going to see Dr. D!!!!

OK - It's realy a 3 star place but our food and service were so nice on a frigid January night that I will round up to 4 stars.  The place is, indeed, a "hut" - you have to walk around outside to get to the bathrooms and the decor is sparse - but Nikita - our server/cashier - saved the day with her congenial manner.  To top it off my friend and I both loved our huge platters of Oxtail Stews in a rich brown saucewith plantains (not dry - very nice) and rice - fragrant with allspice and studded with beans.  A $5 (ouch) side of roti bread was the perfect accompaniment.  I loved my meal - and will return.

Honestly, this place's sorbettos and gelatos rival Capogiro in Philly and any of the joints in NYC.  The Biscotti, Vanilla, Irish Whiskey (tastes like Bailey's) and Banana varieties rocked my world.  I had a first-class affogato with a delicious espresso pulled just for me.  EVERYthing is home-made - cakes, novelties - even Pizzelle.  Can't wait to return and so glad a local chick turned me on to this place. Cheaper than Rita's.  No comparison.  JUST GO!!!!

Believe it or not we had an excellent time at cracker barrel  with our party of 5.on a not-to-busy Friday night (5-7 minute wait for a table).  The little one loved her food (fried shrimp) and she and my MIL shopped in the gift shop and bought "Mad Libs" and an old-style box of Cracker Jack.  (The little one had never had cracker jack before and wondered about the prize.)  After a carb and fat loaded meal (not good for the diet at all) we relxzed on rocking chairs out front (for sale) and played checkers.  The staff especially Judi (trainer) in the gift shop and Justin or server were all terrific.  Is this my favorite place?  No way.  But it beats Denny's or Perkins any day and you can get pancakes for dinner!

COnveniently located in RTM, this is a great place to grab inexpensive cut flowers.  The staff is friendly and very helpful.  Note:  The also give a discount to PHS (Pennsylvania Horticulture Society) members and often run deals during the flower show.

A solid 3 stars, maybe even 4  - food is very basic (possibly a little bland) but the spring rolls and bun were tasty and the traditional Vietnamese Coffee hit the spot on a cold day.  grilled Lamb over bun was succulent and tasty - albeit a small portion and $12.95.  Quick service got me in & out even on a busy Thursday lunch rush. Nearly every table was full - and this after years of being open is a great sign.  Prices are higher than in Philly (Chinatown, Vietnam,m Vietnam Palace, Pho Cali) but considering where we are - I am beyond thrilled to have a non-pizza lunch alternative.  Can't wait to go back and try the sumer rolls.

This is our go-to Rita's - for it's spacious parking lot, clean picnic tables and benches, and sweet teen-aged girls running to show.  Our 8 year old and I both get kiddie sized (ASK)  water ice or custards - and the kiddie portion is PLENTY in my opinion.  I love the coffee custard but is is GONE (forever??) now - so I get chocolate or swirl.  DD often gets lemon, blue raspberry or swedish fish flavored "wooder" ice.  The blendini is fun, too. And now they have sundaes (unlimited toppings like hot fudge, "jimmies"/Sprinkles, whipped cream and a cherry).  ASK for the kiddie size - it's cheaper, smaller and just as satisfying.  Indulgent and a diet breaker for sure - but a summertime must in PA!

Nope.  Now we go tot he Giant in Aston which is far better - albeit more crowded.  This Giant has out of date dairy products (have seen that twice now - so READ THE DATES!!!) and a picked-over produce department.  Step up your game, Giant in Brookhaven!

After not coming to the Aston diner in years, our party of 6 had a very nice lunch (specials are a good value and come with soup and dessert) for under $70.  Service by "Barb" was great and we enjoyed the food.  Burgers, grilled cheese, Chicken Caesar salad, Cobb Salad with shrimp (instead of chicken) [$14.95] with mammoth portions (took some home).  Glad things have improved. We'll return,

Good, greasy, basic pizza - a little expensive for what it is. Plus they sell gelato, subs & salads.   I had a single slice with spinach (very good spinach topping by the way) for $3.25 to go.  BIG parking lot and a large bar.

Tacos al Pastor - I dream of you...  They are slowly improving the dining area - but still needs work. meanwhile, for $2.50 a pop I get tacos al pastor - the REAL DEAL and a luscious side of guac (also $2.50).  Pico de gallo here is fresh - but super spicy with jalapeno chunks and raw onion - so bring breath mints.  Horchata is also great.  LOVE IT HERE.  Please open one in Media/Aston!!!

I have to agree.  Carrie, our "minder" Jen and the staff of Monster Minders are, indeed, pros.  Sure, they cost more than having your neighbor do it, but they walked our 14 year old pug every morning for about 6 months prior to our move to the burbs.  I am very thankful to Monster Minders for being there when we needed them.  Being able to book online is great, too. And automated billing to your credit card is super-easy!  Thank you, Monster Minders!  Woof Woof!

Meh.  2.15 for a bottle of Dasani?  I shoulda gotten a latte for $2.19 instead.  Mediocrity at its best.  I am so NOT a fan of Cosi.  After eating in them in NYC in the early 2000's when this chain emerged - it seemed cool at first.  And - if the bread is fresh and hot (before it solidifies into cold cardboard) it actually tastes pretty good.  The hungrier you are the better it'll taste.  Meanwhile - the overpriced sandwich fillings are mediocre at best. There are better places to waste (I mean spend) $9 bux.  Sorry.  Not a big fan.

When I went to Penn, this was THE Wawa - complete with the welcoming comittee of "usual" homeless guys - the same ones day after day.  They do alot of business at this well-travelled location.  \Smokes, coffee, junk food, sandwiches, ice cream - everything a college kid might need at the last minute.

OK - I haven't actually gotten to EAT the food here just yet. Today my friends and I stopped in to Mr. Pasta.  The place was dead-empty (no dine-in people at all) and just one guy in front of us who had ordered some cheese ravioli - which he says he gets all the time and LOVES.  My friend and I looked at the cases of fresh home-made "to go" pastas.  Alas, they are cash only so we had to leave and come back another day. But we WILL be back.  And soon.

We needed an oil change - stat  - and poor planning had us arrive at Pep Boys 40 minutes before closing.  They took us right away and had us in and out for $26.95 plus tax.  No issues.  Oh - and Klaus (manger from the Wilmington location) is now up here and is very knowledgeable about parts.
It's big - it's (relatively) new, it's fairly clean.  Pretty nice as major stadium venues go.  As always, wish there were more ladies bathrooms (and cleaner) and healthier food choices.

I had a lovely first-ever experience at Fresh Market. All 4 staffers I spoke with were friendly and helpful.  They carry Stonewall Kitchen Jams and Sauces - so I snagged a $7 jar of swanky peach jam.  I love stonewall - and if I buy it here I don't have to pay shipping.  They also had HINT water on sale for $1 a bottle - so I got 8 bottles. I also picked up 3 bottles of Australian Water infused with flower essences.  I am a Bach Flower Essences Practitioner so I am curious to see what it tastes like (should just taste like plain water) and if it works.    They also carry Vosges chocolate bars and other high end goodies. Produce looked great - albeit pricey and meat case looked good but I doubt I wll buy any.  I liked it here alot and will be back. It's a little pricey - but it's closer to my house than Whole Paycheck (aka Whole Foods).

Carrabas is Carrabas - and as chain Faux-talian goes it's fine.  Mid priced (dinner for 2 with one beer each and no dessert no app was about $45.  They also have promotions all the time - the one they offered when we were there was a $13 deal for a soup or salad and 2 (yes 2) plates of pasta (one for now and one for home.  Whatever,  My friend had the soup which he enjoyed and I had a very boring "house salad" with iceberg, a few shreds of carrot and 2 pieces of celery and 3 olives. No cuke, no tomato.  Just BORING.  Hot bread (good for white bread) and herbed olive oil followed.  The pasta plates are enormous.  Carbo loading at its finest.  Not gourmet - but in the Spingfield Mall - this is the best you'll get (There's a Ruby Tuesday and a Sbarro) for a sit-down meal.  Oh - and the place was FULL of kids on the Thursday night we went.

I went to Slainte (after passing it a gazillion times) yesterday when I had an hour to kill waiting for a bus.  I just so happened to arrive during happy hour (Mon - Fri 5-7 PM) and got the $5.00 bar snack - Cheesesteak Eggroll.  It was very salty - but fried crispy and most folks porbably would have loved it.  Meanwhile the regular menu was not cheap - but I was impressed by the selection of desserts and half & half 20 oz "Irish Style" pours.  (Black 'n Blue, Stoudt 'n Ale, etc.)  As I am not a drinker, a good pub is wasted on me - but Slainte is a nice environment - Eamon my server was a doll -  and I would come back here again - but next time - a green salad!  Clean bathrooms too - which is more than I can say for 30th Street Station.

Gorgeous - but it's a shame that there are just so many homeless around - and dogs pee in it.  Meanwhile, it's a treasure - and now that PHS (PA Horticultural Society) is re-planting the elm trees (they died), it will be even more special.  A Philadelphia landmark.

We bought our 2007 Hyundai Sonata from Fred Beans.  Over the years my family and my husband's family have each bought many different cars - new and pre-owned - of different makes from Fred Beans.  Between them and Foster & Kardane (and we were friendly with the Kardane clan back in the '80's) they pretty much OWN the D-town automotive scene.  Competitive prices and salespeople who don't make you feel like a target.  Good repair work, too.  I'm a fan.

OMG!!!!  I can't even believe I am the first person to Yelp this.  Do I dare tell you all how really, really, really great this place is?  It's crowded enough as it is - if I tell you I'll never get a table.  OK, I'll tell you a little bit. It's a no-decor, little atmosphere place run by a genuinely NICE family (the hostess/daughter is marrying the pizza chef in August 2008 in Brooklyn).  They make their own mozzarella, and bake fresh brick-oven pizza on a thin - but not-too-thin crust.  The shrimp scampi is ENORMOUS - they give you over a dozen shrimp. It is garlicky & oily - so if you order it light on the garlic 'n oil it's even better (IMHO).  The Veal Parm is a flam-family (that's FLAMILY) staple and my mom & I can easily split it.  (Comes with a side of pasta.)  Fresh (onion-y) bruschetta arrives on the table nearly as soon as you are seated.  Cappucino is light and frothy.  (mmmn, mmmn good.)  A great place for families and kids.  I LOVE IT HERE!!  So much!

Average CVS - we stopped in for passport photos but had to wait a really long time to get them because only 1 person know how to take them.  Meanwhile it had everything we needed and its own parking lot - which helps in downtown Media.

After attempting to come here 3 other times (the crowds are crazy - especially on weekend mornings because this is a NEW place in an underserved area) our party of 4 got in for brunch on Sunday 3/17 (St. Paddy's Day).  In addition to the full diner menu they had corned beef & cabbage and corned beef omelettes on the menu.  Angela, our over-worked server, was friendly and terrific.  She got all of our orders right and got us in and out in short order.  (The longest part was the wait for a table.)  Aston needs more restaurants, and I surely hope the Aston Diner succeeds. The booths however (as Jamal P. states) are meant for huge fat people.  I weas sitting miles away from the table and you can't move the booths nor the table.  Next time I want to be seated NOT at a booth.  I ordered the $7.95 Aston Special - a breakfast platter with one (big) pancake, 1 slice of french toast (great), 2 sausages and 2 strips of crisp bacon (a little hard).  Very fresh tasting food.  I am pleased and will return. But I'm coming on a Tuesday and not sitting in a booth.

Pho, summer rolls, iced coffee, vermicelli, broken rice plates, all the staples in a quick-service format. Mid-priced and great for lunch. Come right when they open at 11:30 to beat the lunch rush.  New digs with a clean restroom. For now.

My faith has been restored in Bistro St. Tropez - or maybe it just tastes better when somebody else is paying??   We attended a corporate luncheon (small group - 7 people) here and had great, attentive service - and best yet - much improved food.  Although they do now charge ($3.00) for the delicious hot rolls and pesto, the salade Hache (a chopped salad with chicken and shrimp - a tad over cooked) was fresh and tasty.  The classic Soupe a'l'oignon was rich in flavor, not too salty and had crisp crouton on top.  Mmmn!  The desserts were best of all (and I have NEVER had room for dessert here before, but somehow today I managed it) - ice-cream filled profiteroles and a chocolate mousse cake were shared by all.  Two leaves & a bud tea capped off a hearty lunch.  How we all need a nap, now! Off to the conference room...

I am honestly much, much happier than I ever thought I would be. I braced myself for the worst when my husband, 7 year old and I had a desparation lunch here after marathon shopping at Tar-jay and Christmas Tree Shops.  The little one had chicken fingers and fries ("safe"), DH had a chicken sandwich. I had rib tips and mac and cheese (Calorie hell.)  The rib tips were pretty awful (dried out and then barely re-succitated with a spicy-sweet sauce) .  Won;t get it again.  Here's the surprise - a very decent crock of mac 'n cheese.  The sauce was white and creamy (kinda-cheesy) and topped with yellow and white shreds of melted cheese.  The kid loved it.  Service (believe it or not) was great. We had a spill (my fault) and they hurried to clean things up and replaced our french fries quickly and for free.  Female server (can't remember her name) brought extra napkins without having to ask.  Very nice! It was not crowded (2:30 PM on a Sunday). Bathrooms were decently clean, too.  I've had better - but I've had Soooooo much worse.  I might even come back!

Mandarin Garden has been here For Eh Ver!  And the good food (not the needs-a-makeover decor) is why.  Consistently good "classic" Chinese American mid-priced food.  A local landmark - and right near the train.

Went here today for cake & ice cream with my 4 year old and we had a grand time with great service (sometimes service here is flaky but today it was not).  She had birthday cake ice cream, and adored it.  We split a GI-NORMOUS slice of chocolate layer cake - or shall I say we split 1/2 of the slice and took the other half home - it was THAT huge - and for $4.75 a slice it should be.  Not only was it huge, the loist rich cocoa-rich cake had a delicious chocolate buttercream icing that was finger lickin' good.  A great snack on a sweet summer day.

My faith has been restored. Stopped in solo tonight out of sheer craving for sushi.  I sat, alone, at the bar and chatted with Alan, Don (sp??) and my lovely server Amanda.  FANTASTIC service - and very good, fresh fish.  I am more of a purist and do not care for gloppy sauces - but the Tuna Tartare (with a bit of chopped mango, avocado and fried shallots mixed in) was perfect.  Fresh tuna - chopped - not minced.  The plate was garnished with at least 4 sauces though.  (All delicious - miso, cilantro oil, mayo, red wine reduction)  3 pieces of yellowtail sashimi (one order) and one temaki (hand roll) and I was stuffed.  I shall return - happily, now!

Lots of fun and nature's beauty for the whole family.  We take the kids here for a 'feeding the ducks" play date and mini hike (2-5 year olds) and they just love it.  Especially in good weather (not too hot or humid or raining).  Don't miss it!

Well, I got dragged back to "the pube" for a free event for a charity that I support.  While I love the charity and am thankful to the Public House for sponsoring the event, the food and beverage service here is sub par. Mediocre chicken wrap (with an odd mayo-ish sauce) was inedible.  Hummus and veggies were safe - but blah.  It's still not my thing.
This is a big Target with everything you need.  They even have a small Starbucks up front.

Do not get the "new" Shrimp!  Ick!!!  We came in at a time when almost every item on the hot bar was running low.  I tried the Surf & Turf bowl for the first time the the shrimp were old and rubbery.  There was hardly any steak left so the lady scraped out the "required" amount of dried out beef cubes.  The black beans were also old but then they brought more and she plopped a scoop of "new" beans over the dried out old ones.  I thought about asking her to re-make the dish but did not.  I should have!    Awful!!!!   Waste of $8.40 plus tax.  Cold items (Salsa, etc. were fine).  So sad because I often really enjoy Qdoba - for those fast food times in my life.
A generous co-worker bought a huge Mocha cake with rich, delicious buttercream frosting on it and we each had a slice.  HEAVENLY.

Absolutely wonderful and a real lesson for our 8 year old about "how the other half lives".  The show, fairgrounds, food (tea sandwiches an crustless white bread) and staff or volunteers are wonderful and the horses are magnificent.  We enjoyed the carriage event and seeing ladies in crazy hats.

Meh.  The place needs an interior overhaul.  SHAB-BY!  And the restrooms are up a creaky set of stairs and really need re-painted.  Oh - but the food.  It's just OK.  We have been twice - one lunch and one brunch - and I never need to go back.  The "Oatmeal Brulee" was really weird.  A gloppy pile of oatmeal surrounded by a "creme anglaise" of sorts garnished with berries.  Sounded better on paper than it was IRL.  The burgers and pastas for lunch were better and are a safer choice.  They were very accomodating to our large group with 3 small children and the bartender mixed a TASTY bloody Mary - but hauling kids upstairs to "go potty" while half-drunk is a feat in and of itself.  No need to return...  Unless you re-model.

Love these guys!  The name-sake ravioli is delicious and affordable - usually frozen and many varietys.  Great tortellini, too - meat or cheese (I love the meat).  Take it home and cook it up!   The real deal - straight from sou-philly.  Oh - and they support the Mummers - so go to P&S!

The beauty uber-store.  I really miss the flagship location in New York (it closed) but tnow there are Sephora's popping up all over.  Believe it or not, Sephora has really streamlined their brand selections over the years.  They used to carry TOO MANY brands.  Now it's just about right.  Since I am in the beauty bix and hate paying retail - I usually browse and try products here - but buy elsewhere.  However, I will say that in a pinch I run here for things I really need now - like Caudalie, MUFE (Make Up For Ever) and Ojon Hair Care.  This is like the grocery store for me.  Can't survive without it.
Somewhere between Meh and A-OK. Ye Olde Theatre.  I also hear they may rip it down and move the theatre into the Granite Run Mall itself.

Sorry - but i have had way, way, way better Afghan food.  I love Afghan food - the bread is usually sooooo good.  Sansom's was dry and re-heated in a toaster oven.  The rice (reheated as well) was good, but not great.  The salad - scooped out of a tupperware - obviously pre-prepped way in advance was wilted and over dressed.  The Chalaw Kadu (Normally a fave) was so greasy I had to pick out the chunks of pumkpin from the sauce and discard it.  I was the ONLY person in here on a Thursday night - and finally another single diner came in.  The place was dead - and I bet I know why. Get it together, folks.  I'm sticking with Kabul. (And oh, how I miss Pamir - now closed - in NYC)

3 or 4 max, for mediocre "typical" pizza joint food (wings, mozz. sticks, salads with iceberg lettuce, chicken parm) and often super crowded.  People just LOVE it here and it has been a Media, PA institution.  Plus they have a ton of beer - so thus, the crowds.  It is the best ever?  No.  But it is a solid choice for couples, singles and families with kids (and yes, there are alot of those) to grab a mid-priced pizza-joint meal.  The pizza itself is fine.  Not a holy grail and not bad - the Sicilian is great if you are willing to wait for it. Do not be in a rush and then order a Sicilian pie.

I am not a big CB fan - but the Blackberry Pancakes (when they have them seasonally) are great and our kid loves that gift shop.  We were headed home after an exhausting day and stopped in on a Saturdy night at about 7:15 PM and were thankfully seated right away.  I had the pecan crusted catfish off the "lighter options"menu with (frozen) steamed brocolli and (slightly watery) cheese grits.  The fish itself was tasty.  Kiddo loved her mac 'n cheese and chicken tenders. DH was less than thrilled with the gluey chicken 'n dumplings.  But dinner for 3 was $30 - so cheap. Carbo-loaded and OK. But NOT gourmet.

This Wawa location is right on Baltimore pike.  (No gas station - I am assuming it's a fairly old location).  Wawa is the quintessential coffee/beverages/gis/snacks place along with hoagies and prepared foods.  A truly convenient convenience store and very PA!

It's a shame the majestic Elm Trees had to be chopped down due to Dutch Elm disease - but the PHC (Penn. Horticultural Sociaty) is replanting Logan circle.  I only wish they could depose the homeless people in a humane way.  A gorgeous fountian - but people literally bathe in it.  Yick! I gotta be careful when my kid & I play here.
I think you mean Dimitri's.  See my other review on this small, cash-only Greek staple with terrific baba ganoush.

We had mediocre service from the "internet car" guy (there are 2 people dedicated to web-based pricing) and test drove a Ford Fusion.  Nice car - but we wound up purchasing a Hyundai instead.  Not a great dealership. Not overly impressed.

The food tastes fine - and the cafeteria style of "design your own" burritos, tacos and quesadillas is catching on fast -but don't be fooled.  It's still fast food - and it is super-duper HIGH in calories.  A typical burrito has 1100 - 1600 calories.  (Naked will reduce it by 330 - as the PLAIN TORTILLA is 330 whopping calories alone.)  That said - I do enjoy the Naked Chicked Burrito, no cheese, small (70 cal) taco-sized torilla on the side.  It's just too hard for me to "hold the guac" and save 220 calories.  That guac - for fast food guac tastes muy bien to me.  By the way - I think Jack-in-the-box owns Qdoba - I know Chipotle is owned by McDonalds.  FAST FOOD - people. Eat under a health advisory.

5 stars for the food!  What a fabulous find in a Girard Ave. location. We enjoyed our dinner here very much!  I had a Pineapple Strawberry Daiquiri (BYO Booze) and some amazingly good ceviche - shrimp and tillapia.  My husband's chicken enpanadas were so good, too (I got a bite!).  For entrees he had a tender and flavorful shredded pork with super-fresh corn tortilla black refried beans and rice. He liked it alot.  I really loved the Eggplant Tower - a great vegetarian (NOT VEGAN - it's overloaded with 2 kinds of cheese) choice served over white rice and a home-made tomato & onion sauce.  Desserts are very well done here, too at $6-$6.50 each we tried the banana crepes and cheesecake bunuelos.  Delicioso! We can't wait to come back (The crab & shrimp enchiladas and Carne Azada are calling to me.)! They also do weekend brunch - which sounds marvelous.  Service by our sweet cambodian server (He's a doll!) was attentive and great.  And a big thanks to Eversave (the groupon knock-off) without whom I never would have tried this place.  A super-great find!

A must-see tourist (and local) attraction - but not for small kids - way too boring. You can get through the Museum itself in 2-3 hours, if you take a tour of Wyeth's studio ($8 extra charge) allow another 75 minutes.  Cute cafe inside but no cpecialty coffee drinks - just coffee, tea and very good food.  (Shrimp & Grits and Kombucha were both available.  Interesting.  An older crowd, for sure.

Barb-Lin Carpets has been a core Doyltestown business for years 7 years.  They offer all sorts of flooring options - not just carpet - and will install it, too.  A good local source for carpetting and floors.

OMG!  Dr. Dubin moved into a gorgeous new office at the Medical Tower at 16 & Walnut.  His staff is wonderful - and they even threw a lovely dinner party tonight for his patients who have referred people.  (And next week there is a cocktail party for all of the patients at large.  Who ever hears of a dentist doing these thing?  Dr. Dubin is a great dentist (first and foremost) and also a lovely person.  My next cleaning is in November - and (believe it or not) I can't wait!

I am not a huge Indian Food lover but I do like Makhni (Butter!) Chicken.  The lamb was just OK.  Tofu was the best choice to me.  I got a rice bowl but you can also get a wrap or salad.  For whatever reason it ran me $9.80.  For that price I'd rather eat at Chipotle.  (No beverage)  Price is too high for fast food Indian.

On its literal last legs - everything is in disrepair/neglect due to the impending closure.  Good news?  Cheap ticket prices and no crowds. Bad news?  Don't eat any of the stale old food and do not use the rest room if you can avoid it.  Ick!  It's like viewing a movie in an abandoned, decaying theater.  Sad, sad, sad. Depressing.
Medium size post office with a lobby with an automated self-serve machine (thank goodness) and slow moving lines at mid-day on week days.   Glad they are here.  Wish they had later (evening) hours.
