I like that they have the list of singers on screen so you know how long you have until your turn and the people running the whole operation couldn't be nicer.   When I came here last I was just drinking water, and I really liked that they have two canteens filled with ice water so that you can just help yourself. I think more bars should do this because I'm sure that bartenders do get tired of people asking for water. It takes up their time when they could be getting other patrons real drinks.

I was craving Mexican when we stopped into this place for a quick lunch.  We were here at about 3, so there was really no one here which was fine with me. The waitress dropped off some complimentary chips and salsa, which was surprisingly good. We also got some queso which was just incredible. In fact, I might go so far as to say that it might be in the running for the best queso in NOLA.  For my entree, I got the a la carte burrito and flauta. The burrito was HUGE and came packed with carnitas and topped with queso. The flauta also had carnitas in it, but it was disappointing. It wasn't that packed with meat and the meat fell out when I took a bite. The burrito was more than enough for a lunch and for $7 you really can't beat it.  I liked this place so much that I found myself wishing I lived closer to it. It was a great lunch and I'll be back.

This is another awesome addition to the New Orleans beer scene.  The location itself is no frills: it's basically in a warehouse. The cool thing about the place is that there is a lot of wide open space and the "family style" tables allow you to get to know your fellow beer lovers. My one tiny complaint about the location is that I know it is gonna be really hot in there once summer hits. They have a few big fans going, but I can imagine you are going to have to come ready to sweat once the heat kicks up.  I've had a few beers here. The two times I've been I've gravitated towards the Charming Wit, only because it's not super heavy and it's nice to sip on a warm day. I am eager to go back and try the fruit based beers as both of my visits here were brief.

Some friends and I stopped in here one night because they were in the mood for some good pizza.  I had been here years ago, but not so much lately.  For an appetizer, we decided on the hummus and pita.  It wasn't as good as you would get a place like Byblos, but it definitely hit the spot and got the job done.  My friends got a sausage pizza, which looked great and I got a muffaletta that was also really good.  The service was excellent and the staff was friendly.  I would definitely stop in here when I was looking for a quick bite..

I really like this place! Not only do they serve sandwiches and things like that, but they have a full sushi bar, too.  When you are in this restaurant you really feel like you are in another world. I guess part of that is because it's in a hotel. This place is super "trendy" with fancy big screens and a "modern" kind of layout.  For my meal I decided that I wanted a Philly roll for my appetizer and a pressed burger for my meal. Weird, huh? Well, unfortunately the roll and the burger ended up coming out together, so I basically had a hamburger with sushi on the side. No biggie. The burger was okay, but not overly great. The sushi roll was super fresh and tasty.  If I go back, I'm sticking with the sushi.

Stopped in here for a quick bite after a long afternoon. We ordered a pepperoni pizza. It was okay. I mean, what can you really do to a pepperoni pizza to make it stand out? It came quickly when we ordered and the waiter was nice and friendly.

A nice little gallery located in old Gretna.  Reasonably priced framing and a really nice staff.  They carry the prints of a lot of local artists, such as Terrance Osborne, that make fantastic gifts.  They frequently have sales around the holidays.

A nice sized bar that is a pretty good place to watch a game. They have a lot of pool tables, and serve food if you are hungry. Nothing fancy as far as drinks go, but they do have bucket specials. Smoking is allowed, but their smoke eaters do a good job of keep up with all of it, so it's not too much of a problem.

Wendy's has actually been adding a lot of good things to their menu lately. I just had the pretzel bacon burger which was incredible. It's a bacon cheeseburger on a pretzel-like bun. It was REALLY good for fast food and I never really think that fast food burgers are good. I usually just eat them because I'm starving or something.  The drive thru here is pretty fast and I never have to wait in line too long.

Although this isn't my "go to" dry cleaner, this is a nice little place. The owner is really nice and they do a good job on your clothes. I don't usually pick my dry cleaning up in an hour, after dropping it off here, but it's always done the next day.with no issues. I haven't really had to bring anything in here that has been super stained, but for a little "fresh up", they are great.

I love when I can just walk into a place, tell the person working what I need and I have it in my hand and head out the door within minutes. That was my experience at Auto Zone today.  I was looking for some car cleaner stuff (technical name) and after describing it to the guy working, I was all set. Everything here is organized nicely and easy to find, and the product I needed was well priced. This isn't my usual Auto Zone, but I won't hesitate to return in the future.

Great place if you are looking for gorgeous lingerie.  They sell lingerie by actual designers, not just random underthings spread around.  I think that this is the closest thing that New Orleans has to an "Agent Provocateur".  They sell bras, panties, corsets, garter belts, stockings, teddies and more.  The items here aren't cheap, but they are definitely worth the extra splurge.  When you want something a little nicer than what Victoria's Secret has to offer or you want a pretty matching underwear set, this is the place to go.

Knocking them down two stars, because they've gone down hill.  The now only have chocolate donuts on the weekends and not during the week. I've never heard of such a thing. Even the donuts they do have really aren't all that great. I think I'm going to be going to Terrytown Donuts from here on out. Sorry, boo.

This is a lovely place full of masks of all types from big ones with feathers to smaller ones that just go over your eyes. They also have a nice selection of mask magnets and ornaments.  I just happened to wander in here and we were immediately greeted by the owner, who was very nice even though I was pretty much just looking around at all of the nice offerings. The masks here are beautiful, and while I wasn't in the market for one, I did notice that they were all fairly priced.  I did buy a mask magnet that was decorated with beautiful ribbons and Mardi Gras fabric, for a friend of mine, because she loves things like that. This is a great spot for gifts for locals and tourists alike.

I was here looking around to see if there was anything I wanted to buy during their semi-annual sale. I saw a lot of things that I liked, but I didn't make any purchases on this particular day. The reason for my review is to commend the man working that day, King. King was extremely friendly and helpful. He told me all about the sale and he helped me find a particular bag that I was looking for. I am sometimes overwhelmed in stores like this, mainly because I feel as if I am kind of left "on my own" to figure things out for myself, but King was more than happy to help me and make small talk. He's a great asset to the Coach company, and when I am ready to make a purchase, I will return to this Coach location.

What a cute shop!  As soon as I walked in, I was greeted by a French bulldog who I assume is the proprietor of the store. Oh, New Orleans!  They have a lot of really cute, well priced clothing. A lot of the things they offer look designer I was impressed by the unique look of everything that was for sale. The woman working there was really friendly and was quick to tell me about the sales that were going on as well as some of the jeans that I had been looking at.  Honestly, a lot of the clothing here is particularly my style, but it's a nice place that is worth checking out.

This is a cool little place to see live music.  Some friends and I saw a band here a few weeks ago.  The stage area is small, but the sound quality is good, which can be tough in a smaller place.  I really like the atmosphere of the place and the way it's decorated with a "kitschy" New Orleans feel.  My only complaint is the bar.  It's a really long bar, the place gets packed, and there was only one bartender working on a Friday night.  It took forever to get served and the poor bartender looked super frazzled (and I couldn't blame him, at all.  He was just swamped with customers.).  My suggestion would be to add another bartender on Friday nights.  Maybe this was a rare night with only one server.  Anyway, I would definitely go back, especially since they have Taceaux Loceaux being served in the kitchen.

Yum! I love a good bowl of Pho and this place does it right!  I met a friend here for lunch and was excited to add another place to my "NOLA Pho" list. We started with a plate of the pork tacos. The pork was tender, tasty and delicious. It was cooked in a typical Vietnamese fashion and it was quite tasty.  I also decided to the "combo" pho which comes packed with New York strip, brisket and meatballs. WOW. This was such a delectable bowl! They were not stingy with the meat at all and the entire serving was huge! The broth held a lot of flavor and didn't leave the meat to do all of the "flavor" work (as it sometimes does).  The atmosphere here is pretty casual. We stopped in late on a Saturday afternoon and there were only a few other people in the place. Unlike some other Vietnamese places, Mint serves alcohol and even has a happy hour Tuesday through Saturday.  I will definitely return to Mint for a tasty bowl and some apps!

Ok, just to be clear this place is getting three stars because it has air hockey and air hockey is awesome.  My ex used to live in mid city, so he and his roomies called his their "home" bar  Ok, I'll be honest.  The place isn't the worst bar I've ever set foot in.  In fact, if you take it out of the shady neighborhood that it's in, it would actually be a neat little place.  This place has a history.  If you do enough searching, you will discover what I mean.  I'm not going to go into that here.  I will say that the bartenders are really nice and the people seem nice, as well.  I wouldn't go alone, I'd go with a big group of people.

I am so excited about this place.  My family and I got take out from this restaurant for Mother's Day.  No one had ever tried this place before, so it was sort of an experiment.  We looked over the menu online and it sounded good, so we gave it a try.  Let me tell you, we were not disappointed.  I got the catfish platter which came with fries and a side salad.  Let me tell you... they give you SO MUCH catfish that I got about 2 and a half meals out of it.  No kidding!  It is so worth the money.  The pieces are big and juicy and they don't hold back on the food at all.  This is such a better deal that a place like New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood.  I definitely want to go back and try their other faire.  The shrimp platter and the oyster platter sound just divine.  I love discovering local places like this.

I was at this venue for New Orleans Fashion Week.  This is a gorgeous place. It was hard to get a feel of the room because there was a big runway in the middle of it, but even with the runway where was a lot of space to move around and room for people to sit. The highlight for me was the outside: a beautiful patio'd courtyard with a nice garden adds to the "upscale" feel and makes you feel like you are at an exquisite manor.  Parking is a pain, and I ended up having to park a few blocks away for the event that I attended, but that is the only minor drawback of the space and pretty typical for the area.

This place was okay. We were here on a Friday night for dinner after they had been open for a little over a month.  We were here early evening, so there was no crowd. You decide want you want and then go down the line and they get it together for you. On the day we were here, the staff seemed a little overwhelmed and confused with what was going on and got me and David's orders mixed up a few times. Also, they were out of fries which was just strange.  The food was okay. I had a pulled pork sandwich, creamed spinach and potato salad. The pulled pork was really tender and had a lot of flavor, the creamed spinach was good and the potato salad was okay, but nothing spectacular. David had a sausage sandwich, and that looked really good too.  The few issues I have with the place are easy to fix, so I'll probably be back, especially since Westbank barbecue options are fairly limited.

Stopped in here in an effort to soak up a bit of the "atmosphere" before it "ain't dere no more".  On a Sunday afternoon after the Irish-Italian parade it was pretty dead except for a few customers. We were quickly served by a nice woman. Ordered a couple of coffees. They were okay, but had an odd aftertaste and left a weird residue inside the cup. Maybe the coffee was old? Maybe the milk was old? I don't know, but something was off.  Probably wouldn't return. I can understand the charm of the old place, but I don't think that this Morning Call has the same pizzazz that it once held.

This place is amazing! I had such a good time.  So, I was wondering exactly what "boutique bowling" is. Apparently it's fancy pants bowling complete with a waitress who will regularly check to make sure that you have everything that you need, food and drink wise. Pretty cool.  Me and a friend played for an hour and we had a great time. The bowling was a lot of fun (I was on my third game when I discovered that I work best with the 8 lb ball) and the wait staff was super attentive in making sure that we had everything that we needed.  So, what did I score in my first ever game here? Um...geez. What's with the questions? I haven't bowled in ages, so why don't you just chill out and mind your business? It's not all about winning, you know. Jeesh!  Bonus points for fancy sliders and extra fancy beers. Also, every bowler seemed to be in a really good mood. All in all, this place is a win...or a 300, if you will.

I stopped in here with a friend for a quick dinner on a Thursday night.  There was a good crowd and some folks were singing karaoke, so that's always a good time. I decided to get three of the chicken flautas. As good as they were, they really were "no frills". I got three flautas topped with lettuce, tomato, sour cream and guac on a tiny plate- and that's it. It would have been nice to have some rice or beans on the side, but oh well. The flautas were pretty good, but didn't blow me away to any real extent.  I'm going to give them another shot, mainly because of all of the raves of the other reviewers. Next time I think I'm going to make it a point to get a full-on dinner plate.

I love the Howlin Wolf.  They put on fantastic shows from Burlesque to brass bands and everything in between.  It's a great atmosphere and always a good time.  The staff is always nice and friendly and I always end up having a good time here.  The Howlin Wolf den is also located right next to the main Howlin Wolf.  In this dimly lit bar, you can get a drink before you check out your favorite show, you can order food, or you can even see one of the shows that play regularly in the back of the den.  The last time I was at the Den, I had a cuban sandwich with fried pickles.  It was so good!  Way better than your average bar food.  My recommendation would be to check this place out for the "must see" events that they have here, get some food at the den and have a good time.

This is a review of take out.  Having tried the Mellow Mushroom in Metairie before, I knew what type of pizza to expect from this location. We were in the area and decided that we wanted to get some pizza "to go" during a working week day. We ordered online and our pizza was ready nice and fast in the time that they said it would be.  We ordered a medium "mighty meaty" pizza which was perfectly topped with mozzarella, pepperoni, sausage, ground beef, ham and applewood smoked bacon. This pie was piled so high with toppings that I was full after just once slice. Service was fast and friendly and ordering online and picking it up was a breeze. I would get take out here again.

I can't say much about this place, other than their coffee is a life saver. Their iced coffee is delicious and full of flavor and the space itself is perfect if you want to get some work done, or just relax during a fun day in the Quarter. The staff is friendly and helpful and, although I didn't have any food on this stop, I will be returning to try some of their delicious offerings. I guess a place like this might be seen as a "tourist trap", but I think locals will enjoy it too.

The only reason I ever go to this place is for two things and two things only: mini "castleburger" type burgers and super warm and soft donut holes.  This is the only place, that I'm aware of, that has the mini hamburgers, on the Westbank.  You can get them with or without cheese and they are made to order.  They are so good and SUPER cheap.  I also love the donut holes here.  They are never hard, like they are at other places and they are always super sweet, warm and soft.   The only donut I have ever gotten here was a chocolate with sprinkles (my fave) and it was delicious.  If I still ate donuts, I would definitely get them from here.  You can keep Krispy Kreme.  I am never let down by this place.

This is pretty much just a review of their beer selection.  We stopped in here on our way to a Chalmette-style bbq and I wanted to pick up my own beer because I don't like being a beer-mooch in these situations. Thankfully, Winn Dixie was close by and had just what I was looking for. I was pretty impressed with their beer selection as a whole, but I really liked that they had a wide selection of local beers including Port Orleans, Second Line and Urban South. They also had some Ghost in the Machine, if that's your thing. The beers were reasonably priced and around the same price as I've seen at other grocery stores, so this is a good place to visit if you're in the market for good brews.

Typical dive bar with a good beer selection.  This is a great place to watch a game, but be warned:  the ceilings are low and the place gets really smoky.  It's a neighborhood place and the patrons are friendly and nice.  The staff is pretty awesome, too.

Ha.  My friend said that this bar was located in "sketch ville".   I had never been before tonight.  Maybe I had, but I sure don't remember it.    Cool bar, from what I could tell.  I got a beer and headed to the back.  Nice and dark back there.  Private, just how I like it.  It's nice to know a place like this is uptown.  I'd definitely go back.  The people seem nice and I like the atmosphere.  One of the places where you can just be left alone if you want.

While it can't compare to the gloriousness that is IHOP, I still love some Waffle House, and not just because watching someone fry an egg while they're smoking reminds me of my dad (thanks, Jim Gaffigan!).  My favorite has got to be the hash browns.  I'm not even sure if they are really made out of potato, but they are really good and made with a TON of butter.    I don't think I have actually ever had waffles here.  I usually get a cheeseburger or something.  This is one of those places that can best be described as, "it is what it is".  Do you want greasy food that isn't good for you?  Are you out late and have lowered inhibitions?  Then Waffle House is the place for you!

Established by the Firemen's Charitable & Benevolent Association in 1852, Greenwood is a gorgeous, historical cemetery which was the first above ground cemetery to be built without walls.  The points of the cemetery worth seeing are the Confederate monument, the Firemen's monument, the giant Elk,  and the creepy, rusted iron tombs that are located throughout the grounds.

This gorgeous bridge is a Mid City landmark and is a nice place to take in the view while you are out on the Bayou. The bridge itself isn't anything overly fancy, in fact it's a little rusty, but it adds a nice personality to the area.  My one bridge story is this: years ago I had a friend who lived in Mid City on the Bayou, so of course he had a kayak. We used to like to kayak around the Bayou on nice days. When you go under this bridge, you have to lie down in your kayak, because it's low. If you have never seen the underside of this bridge, let me tell you- birds and spiders in a dark place is kind of jarring when you first experience it. Apparently, this is where every pigeon in Mid City camps out when they aren't flying around. After a while I got used to the spooky underside of the bridge, but it took a few tries.

I used to come to this place years and years ago when it was a dive bar that played Soulja Boy every single time you set foot in that place. I swear, that dude was that place's mascot. Anyway, Evangeline II is A LOT better than that.  Evangeline has a nice cozy feel to it, and although it's small, it still has an area for a band to perform. The night we came there was a pretty cool cover band on stage. They have a really good beer selection and I was happy that there was a lot of seating at the bar. The bartender seemed really friendly and laid back and was really good about being prompt with our order.  I definitely like this place as a laid back place to catch a band on the Avenue. It has a good atmosphere and a friendly vibe.

I am so excited about the ever expanding brewery scene in this town.  What do you get when you cross a converted theater and craft beer? You get Wayward Owl Brewing with their assortment of tasty brews in a fantastic atmosphere. I love the laid back feel of this place- lots of room, a cool vibe and, of course delicious beer. Wayward is new, but they are doing a great job at producing quality beer that I really enjoyed. On the day I was here, I was able to sample a few of the beers and I think my favorite was the IPA. I'm a huge IPA fan and theirs is hoppy without being too overwhelming.  Staff is friendly and, on the day I was here, there was a food truck outside feeding hungry drinkers. I can't wait to see what else Wayward has in store for us.

Um...yeah.  Not gonna really be able to say what hasn't already been said.   Awesome place.  Absinthe, if you want it.  Good priced beer, which is always a plus (I'm probably a rarity, since I don't drink hard liquor).  Good crowd.  Great atmosphere.  Go if you just want a drink.  Go if you want to make friends.  A win either way.  They have an awesome patio out back that is dark and secluded and a great place to sit and chat when the weather is nice.  This place appeals to me because it's one of the more low key places on Decatur.

I've never actually eaten here, but I have gotten multiple sandwich trays from this location, and they are always fantastic and on point!  My favorite thing that I have gotten here is the sandwich wraps. They are turkey and cheese wrapped in a tortilla-type wrap with mustard and sometimes avocado. I love these wraps and they are nicely sized and very tasty. They also offer half turkey and swiss sandwiches on a croissant, if you are in the mood for something a little "fancier".  The food is always really fresh here and the trays are easy to order for a quick pickup.

Well, we went here with good intentions.  I love my fried pickles and I was having a craving when a friend of mine and I decided to stop in here and score some. I had never been, but I knew that they had them on the menu. So, we go in and order, they give us our number, we sit down and we wait. And wait. And wait. Over 30 minutes of waiting, to be exact. Finally someone came over and informed us that out order had been over looked and there were getting on the issue immediately. They gave us a $5 coupon to make up for it, but when you are in a hurry to get somewhere, it's too little too late.  Two stars because after all that the fried pickles were really good and fresh and, of course, fresh out of the fryer. I'm going to go back and try a burger here, I just hope that it doesn't take me over 30 minutes to get my food.

I had to switch vets recently because as nice as my other vet was, they just couldn't get a handle on my older cat's intestinal issues. I have a 12 year old cat that suffers from digestive issues and after a lot of trial and error that resulted in no real change, I decided to switch vets.  I took my cat over to Quality Pet Care and they immediately diagnosed the issue and prescribed a special food and a daily medicine. Ever since starting this regime, my cat has been noticeably feeling better and has been gaining weight. I was so relieved because I was getting to a point of desperation and didn't know what else I could do.  The staff here is friendly and helpful and the doctors are great. Prices are pretty much "on par" with what I've been paying at other vets and they are happy to do any follow ups that your pet might need.

Anyone who knows me knows that I am a freak for Pho. It's probably the most perfect food ever and Pho Orchid is one of the few Pho places I had never been until recently.  Pho Orchid is a pretty laid back place and I was excited to see what they had to offer. I got my usual pork spring rolls appetizer and eye round steak and brisket Pho. The spring rolls were really good. The pork was flavorful and the rolls were a good size. The Pho was okay- it was nothing overly spectacular but I definitely enjoyed it enough to return next time I am looking for lunch in the area.  I think this spot is probably best for "to go" food pick up, because the tables are pretty small and I felt a little cramped. It wasn't a huge issue, just an observation.

Danon suggested this spot, and it's right up the road from me, so I decided to check it out for lunch.  Stackers has a lot of "hot" offerings such as hamburger steak, pork chops, red beans and rice and other things like that. This place is pretty simple: order at the counter and wait for them to bring your food out. On this particular day, I was in the mood for a cheeseburger and fries, so that's what I got.  The food was cooked to order and came out quickly. I was delighted that the burger was huge and there was a ton of fries- I had plenty enough to take home for later. Drinks are "serve yourself" and there was a tv on showing the game.  Stackers isn't the fanciest lunch place in the area, but the food is good and it gets the job done. They also serve breakfast, if you are heading into work and need a quick bite.

I'm kind of shocked by all of the awful reviews. I was actually kind of impressed. Those are 3 "fast food" stars, by the way.  We ordered takeout online and went it picked it up with no issues. The order was perfect. In fact, David orders from here all the time and he never has issues. Anyway, we got a thin crust pizza and cheese bread. The thin crust pizza was okay. I feel like I'm a bad judge of thin crust because it all tastes the same to me and it never really knocks my socks off. However, the cheese bread was excellent! It was packed with cheese that you could actually see spilling out of the bread.  There are always coupons on the site, so you're sure to get a deal. It's not as good as one of the more upscale pizza places, but it's good for a quick fix.

Really nice Metairie hotel. Nice size room that isn't overly big, but gets the job done.  The downstairs area is really nice. There's a bar area and an "office" area with some working computers if you have to do internet work. The best part of this hotel is probably the conference room. I attended an event here and the room is huge and perfect for entertaining. There is plenty of parking right across the street in a huge garage. Just make sure that you have cash (and exact change), as they only have a machine to pay for your parking and the machine only takes cash.

Well, my experience here was great! I was looking for some jeans, so I headed over to their "denim bar" and began the task of trying on different pairs of jeans (isn't that everyone's favorite thing to do?). One thing I like about the jeans here is that they have a little bit of stretch to them, so they fit well, where they are supposed to fit. In other words- I didn't have to compromise fit for style or vice versa. The woman working was helpful in helping me find exactly what I was looking for and I walked out with a pair of nice jeans that I am quite happy with. The jeans here aren't what you would call inexpensive, but hopefully they will last a while.

I'm always on the hunt for cool things on the Westbank and I finally tracked down this cool snowball stand. They have all the usual snowball flavors. I got my usual, bubblegum. I know. I am super predictable and boring but I like what I like. Besides snowballs, this place also has hot dogs and other non sweet treats, making it a great place to bring kids if you want to get them out of the house.  My favorite part of the whole operation is probably the fact that it has a drive thru. Super convenient on hot days when you don't want to leave the comfort of the car's air conditioning.

I love a locally owned grocery store. There's just something more personal about the entire experience.  The produce is always fresh and they have a nice sized liquor section. A friend and I were in the area and she need to stop in to pick up a certain type of liquor that apparently only this store sells. It was vodka, and of course they had it.  They seem to have a lot of local unique items as well. Someone mentioned that they have a New Orleans "souvenir" section and during MardI Gras it's packed with all kinds of different beads, koozies and trinkets.  One thing that I like about this store is, although there are a lot of people in here at any given time the people checking you out are super fast and efficient and don't leave you waiting in line for very long.

Not bad at all. Located a few doors down from the Royal Sonesta, this hotel is in the heart of the French Quarter and puts you within walking distance of all of the "action".  This is one of the nicer hotels in the quarter, but not all that expensive considering the location. The best thing about this hotel is the hotel bar. The Bombay Club is a fantastic supper club type bar that serves food, high end cocktails and has entertainment regularly. You get to experience a taste of New Orleans without having to leave the comfort of the building.

I loved Babe!  This fashionable new boutique on Freret has everything you could want for a night out from the outfit and jewelry to the shoes. The clothing is just gorgeous and you can tell that the owner took the time to curate exactly what type of looks she wanted to offer in her store. Yes, some of it is on the more expensive end (at least for me), but on the day I was here there were quite a few items on sale.  I love the way the store itself is laid out with certain clothing items in their own little lit up, framed spaces and everything is organized nicely and easy to find. You will find a little bit of everything here including tops, skirts, dresses, jeans and leggings. While I didn't buy anything on my latest trip, I am definitely adding Babe to my list of places to check out when I need an outfit for a special occasion or when I want to be a little stylish and fancy.

Man oh man.  This has to be one of the neatest spots in New Orleans.  I got to check this place out, thanks to a friend who is "in the know".  This is basically an exclusive club type place that is located right above the House of Blues.  It's dimly lit, sofas are everywhere, they are cozy corners with tables that you can sneak off to and it's decorated like only a super secret hideout can be, with cloth on the walls and interesting art everywhere.  I totally "get" why membership to this place is so expensive ($1,000/year for just the "Bronze" package).  This is one of those places where the New Orleans elite come to relax without fear of being bothered or harrassed.  Also, there is naturally no photography allowed inside.  I didn't get to experience any of the food...maybe one day.  It's just neat that I can say that I have actually been inside this "inner sanctum".

I'm not sure if it was specifically The Fudgery, but when I was a kid me and my parents used to come to The Riverwalk and they would buy me fudge as a treat.  When I saw this fudge shop I was really excited to get a slice of rocky road fudge and relive my childhood. The fudge is just as I remember it: nice and thick with pieces of marshmallow and nuts in it. A slice costs around $10, but I do feel like that's a deal for the amount you get. I like to cut off a piece and enjoy it with my coffee, so it lasts longer. They have a lot of different flavors to choose from and they have ice cream at this location as well.  I don't know if it's a regular thing, but when we bought one slice they offered us a free slice with the purchase of a second slice. We didn't take them up on the offer, but that seems like a deal if you want a few different flavors.

Before I discovered the 24 hour breakfast spot  that is IHOP, Coffee & was my "go to" for late night food or doughnut craving.  It's a typical doughnut shop, they serve all types along with coffee, juice, milk...the basics.  The also serve regular breakfast such as bacon, sausage, eggs, grits, toast.  They have a nice "lunch" selection of sandwiches and fries.  My favorite is the club sandwich with sweet potato fries and a chocolate milk.  Service is pretty fast, depending on the time of night, which is good, considering the place is always packed.  This is a JPSO cop hangout, so I never feel weird going in here with friends, even if it's late.  You can order in or get food to go.  If you want a more personal experience than IHOP or Shoney's for breakfast, than this is definitely a good stop.

I love when a business owner greets his customer with a smile and Chef Johnson did just that. I got to try Chef Johnson's at the Terrytown Food Truck fest and I am so glad they rolled over there. My boyfriend and I split the crawfish and grits and it was out of this world good. Not only was there A LOT of crawfish, but the grits were perfect and creamy and the dish was nice and rich. They really knocked it out of the park with this one. Also on the menu is a mac and cheese burger that looks outstanding and a grilled cheese that I am eager to try. Service is fast and friendly and I will be eating here again.

This is the MAC store I frequent the most. The staff is friendly and fairly knowledgeable and the service is always really good.  I was here recently to pick up some lipsticks and a couple of other things. I prefer to come to this store, rather than the MAC counter at Dillard's, because although getting here is a bit of a drive for me, I am usually guaranteed that they will have what I want. Also, this store doesn't sell out of the limited edition sets that they sell. When the Wonder Woman collection came out a while back, the MAC store at Dillard's sold out immediately, but this one had everything still in stock a week later, so I didn't have to rush over to get what I wanted.  My one complaint about this store is that some of the staff isn't as great at matching makeup foundation to your skin tone as others, so be sure to check it out for yourself when they help you, or you might end up buying a foundation that is a little too dark for your complexion.

Add this to the "places I will shop, when I'm rich" list.  I had a Maple St. shopping day so I popped in here to look around. The woman working was extremely friendly and greeted me when I walked in, and I headed over to the racks to see what was what. They carry a lot of cute dresses and tops here, but they definitely aren't cheap. They had a linen t shirt for $100. Seriously. No shade, but this stuff is just a little out of my price range.  They had a few things for sale, so I picked some things out to try on. Nothing really "worked" for me, but I can appreciate the quality of the clothing here and I am sure that it is worth the money and will likely last you years.  If you are looking for higher end clothing, this is the place for you.

This gallery is so great and is filled with cute and quirky art.  I am sure that I had definitely seen the art of Matt Rinard before I set foot into his gallery. His painting, in a "cartoony" style and mainly of animals in funny situations is sure to make anyone happy and bring a smile to your face. Here you can buy originals and prints, and the art makes the perfect gift for someone with a sense of humor. Postcards and small prints are also available.  The gallery also has photography prints and art prints from various other artists. I like that the gallery is wide open with a lot of space and the woman working was sure to ask us if we were looking for anything in particular. Even if you aren't in the market for any art, this gallery is worth checking out.

I was brought here and I was blown away by how nice this market actually is.  First of all, usually when I hear the word "Wal Mart", I go into a little bit of a panic, so when my boyfriend told me that this was actually a "nice" one, I didn't know what to think.  In a way, I would almost say it's the Westbank's answer to Whole Foods.  Not really, of course, but they carry a lot of stuff that you probably wouldn't find in you everyday grocery store.    They have a great fresh veggie selection and they have snacks that you wouldn't expect to find like pretzel chips and dried fruit snacks.  Everything is low priced, just as it is at a regular Wal Mart.    One star is lost, because the lines are always ridiculously long.

Such a CUTE store! It's basically a Forever 21 type store that is focused more on jewelry and accessories than clothes, although they did have some cute tops.  I like that everything in the store is arranged by color. There was jewelry that was grouped by: orange, green, pink, clear, etc. They had a really cool sale section that was "buy one get one free" and some of the stuff was super cheap ($8 or less!). I didn't buy anything this time, but I will definitely be back next time I am in the market for some jewelry that has a little "flash" to it.  My favorite section was probably the tiaras! Yes, I will definitely be picking one up when my birthday rolls around. Heck, it might not even take that long! Sometimes a girl just needs to wear a tiara, you know? They also carry a nice selection of evening "clutch" style bags.  It's nice that the Westbank finally has a cute accessories store.

We stopped in here for my dad's birthday. This is now the only Rotolo's on the Westbank and although I had been here a few times before, this was my first time dining in.  I love Rotolo's because their pizza is always consistently good and the service is pretty great at every location. On this visit, we decided to get a medium pizza with sausage, mushrooms and peppers. Because the pizza is made to order it takes a little longer, but it's worth it. The pizza was delicious and we had leftovers to take home.  Our waitress was super nice and after she saw the name on the credit card, she revealed that she has relatives of the same name. Typical New Orleans experience: go to lunch and discover that you are related to the waitress. I will return for another good lunch.

Bourbon Bandstand used to be Bourbon Street Blues Company and it's the same type of place.  Places like this are touristy, but they serve a purpose. On the night I was here there was a band playing and a few people in the place. The band was pretty good, but sadly we came in at the end of their set. After the band there was just a woman onstage who was singing along to the radio and dancing awkwardly. Does she work there? What is happening here? Also, there was an area where you could go get a cold beer out of ice (for a price, of course) and the bartender girl was go go dancing on top of where the beer was in the ice. Like...right on the edge of the cooler. It was awkward and a bit weird. I'm sure they tell her to do that, but I really didn't get the point, especially since there were only a few people in there drinking and hanging out.  This isn't one of the better "tourist trap" type places, so I would skip it on your next Bourbon adventure.

I really like the space. It's in a nice part of the city and when there is nothing going on here, it makes for a great place to relax and take in the world around you.  I have attended a few events here and event organizers really need to analyze the space/crowd size before they consider having another big event here. During Wednesday at the Square, it's perfect. The crowd isn't too big and there is space to move around. During other events or festivals it gets SUPER packed to the point where you are hot and uncomfortable and can't move around without bumping into people. On top of that, there is zero organization, so the area quickly becomes a mad house.  Check out this spot if it's a quiet afternoon with nothing going on. Avoid it if there is a festival that half the city shows interest in attending.

This is a cute little book shop that I've visited a few times, now. I really have no idea how they stay in business because I have never seen another shopper in the place, but considering they have been around since 1978, they must do well.  They have a nice selection of different books. A lot of John Grisham and Nora Roberts, if that's your thing. The books are broken up into different categories and they are clearly labeled. Many of the books show serious wear, but that's to be expected at a used book store. You definitely get some good deals here.  They will give you store credit, if you bring in books that they can use, so that would be good for anyone who is an avid reader.

The fly is a great little spot here in New Orleans.  It's perfect for relaxing when the weather starts to warm up in the Spring. A lot of people have crawfish boils and picnics here or they just go and hang out with friends. You have a nice view of the river and you feel as if you are in another world when you are relaxing here.

Every time I go to this place, I feel like I'm going to get stabbed (and I'm pretty adventurous).  I went here a lot before Katrina, so last summer when a friend's band was playing here, I jumped at the chance to check it out.  The place is smoky and gross.  A complete "guy" place, complete with pool tables.  Horrible for bands now.  The sound system just sucks.  I saw bands here all the time, Pre-K, now something is just off.    There was only one bartender for the whole place full of people, so you had to wait forever to get service.    I know people will say that places like this are what make NOLA unique.  Uh uh.  Places like "Lafitte's" make NOLA unique.  This is just a scummy hole in the wall.  Trust me, I am NOT a prissy snob who can't have a good time in a dive.  This place is just BEYOND.  I just thank goodness I didn't have to go to the bathroom while I was here, or I might not have made it out with my sanity.  ;)

Tucked away in a little strip mall on Gretna Blvd is this little treasure.  I rarely have to get things altered, but recently I had to bring in two tops and a pair of jeans that were way too big on me.  The shop is very small and has two or three people working at a time.  The woman who took care of me was extremely knowledgeable and knew exactly what I needed done, without me having to explain.  As soon as I put the tops and the jeans on, she had them pinned and ready to go.  I got the clothes back today and the results were just as expected and exactly what I had hoped for.  My tops were altered perfectly, and the jeans that were way too big on me, are now perfectly tailored to fit me.    The alterations just took a week. The tops were about $4.50 each and the jeans were $20, because they had to be totally redone to fit.  I will definitely be returning to the Alteration Center for any future needs.

An upscale hotel bar located in the heart of the CBD.  Great atmosphere and crowd.  A great place to stop in after work for a drink.  I dated a guy who worked in this area a while ago, and we would get together to enjoy a happy hour together after work on Fridays.  The have nice sofas by the windows, where you can sit with a group.  The bar is completely smoke free and the crowd is a little older, so it's a good place to go if you want to get away from the youngsters and their hangouts.

Gogo booth is so fun and it's a really cool twist on the photo booth idea.  I got to experience this at a bridal show I went to recently. It's a big mirror, so you get to see yourself as it takes your picture, then you get to write messages on it with your finger that print on the photos and the photos also upload to their website, which is really cool. I like that it's similar to other booths in that they have a lot of props for your to play with and I enjoyed writing messages on the mirror and interacting with it. It also makes cool sounds as you are posing for the pictures. Pictures are high quality and the experience is fun!

Since the Gretna Breaux Mart has decided to close up shop, this is now going to be my regular grocery stop.  I love this Rouses. It's a better "fresher" than the Belle Chasse Hwy. location, they have great stock of items, and the place is clean and organized. I was here most recently for one of the cheap $7 king cakes they have and I was not left disappointed. They have a whole variety from plain to filled and they're a good size for the price. Look, not every king cake can be a $25 king cake, especially when the season lasts two months. Rouses king cake will satisfy any king cake craving you might have.  I also like that Rouses has a large deli selection, a really nice beer selection and they even have a place where you can "build your own" poke bowl. That's convenient, since poke is the new super-cool thing and there are no places dedicated to the stuff anywhere on the Westbank.  The lines here always move quickly and the staff is great.

I just loved this cozy little bar tucked away in the French Quarter.  David and I stopped in here on our anniversary night and the first thing I noticed was their menu. Sure, it's a bar, but they have some seriously good sounding food and I ALMOST wished that I hadn't eaten before I got here.  The feel of the bar is meant to be like an old library with booze, and I'm all about that. The place is pretty dimly lit, which adds to a nice cozy vibe and I loved that they had a pretty good beer selection. They have a few comfy chairs to sit in, but we just hung out at the bar and took it all in. The patrons seem to be neighborhood regulars and we enjoyed just sipping our drinks and people watching.  The bartender was amazingly nice and welcoming and made our evening just perfect.

This review is written from the standpoint of someone selling to Magpie.  Right now I am going through the process of sorting through my grandmother's things and deciding what I want to keep and what I want to sell.  When I found myself with a surplus of vintage jewelry, a quick search of "New Orleans vintage jewelry buyer" introduced me to Magpie. The owner, Sarah, was nice enough to drive to my grandmother's house on the Westbank and look through her jewelry to find pieces that she would like to buy and resell. She was extremely nice and thorough. She took her time looking through TONS of jewelry, and was able to give me a fair price for a few select pieces. Sarah also mentioned that she buys certain vintage clothes and handbags.  If you are looking to sell estate jewelry, Magpie should be your first call. Sarah was personable and nice and I would happily do business with her again.

This shop is really neat and has a little bit of everything: jewelry, furniture, costumes, prints, art, and more.  We ended up here while we were just strolling around the Quarter and I love everything here! This is the type of place I would shop if money wasn't an object and I had an old mansion to decorate. I think my favorite of the offerings was the old furniture- some of it needed some work, but some of it was in really good shape. They also have a nice selection of old and unique vintage jewelry.  This is a good place to shop if you are looking for a gift, for that special someone, that's a little bit "different". Whatever you end up getting here is sure to make an impression.

WHOA! Okay, so this place is a dream spot who anyone who enjoys a nip and also enjoys saving a few bucks. It's basically CostCo for liquor of all types.  I had heard the hype about this place, so I took a field trip to Metairie to see what it was all about. WOW. Total Wine has it all. I know that it's a chain, but that doesn't seem to put people off. The booze is cheap and plentiful and they are bound to have whatever you're looking for.  I'm a beer person and their craft beer selection can't be beat. They have a ton of local brews as well as national brands and they are all well priced.  Every section is packed with everything you can imagine and they even have snacks like beer nuts and cheese poofs. The staff is super helpful and they have a whole section for "sampling", if that's your thing.  If you need alcohol for a party or just a Saturday night, this should be your first (and likely only) stop.

We have another case of a mysterious disappearing review on our hands.  I have been coming to Pho Cam Ly for years and it is always consistent and good. I get the pho with brisket and it's perfect. The broth isn't overwhelming and everything is balanced nicely.

This is a really cool shop that seems to sell a lot of local wines and other liquors. They have a wide selection of all types of wines as well as some flavored rums. There's a bar in the back, if you are in the mood to do some sampling. The only two issues I have with the place are: the bottles aren't marked with prices and you have to ask how much they are. This just seems inconvenient if you just feel like browsing. Also, it is very loud in here. There was a group sampling when we were here and they were talking at a fairly normal level, but it sounded like they were shouting. That might be a weird complaint, but I found it distracting.  This place is worth checking out if you are in the mall, but not worth going out of your way.

What a fantastic work space!  I had no idea this spot even existed until I was invited to check it out on one of their "Freelance Fridays". On Freelance Fridays you can stop in, without a membership, and see what the space has to offer.   First of all, the whole area is gorgeous. There are wide open spaces and tables for meetings, sofas for lounging and working and individual "pods" where you can set up your work station and work in peace. There's a kitchen area filled with coffee, water, other drinks, snacks and even beer. If you use a dish, please wash it and replace it when you're finished- keeping this place neat is a team effort.  I don't really have any need to become a full time member, but I can definitely see myself stopping in on another "Freelance Friday" so that I can work in a different kind of space. The Shop is what I imagine any modern work space to be and I really liked it and I would absolutely recommend it to anyone who needs a nice, quiet place to work.

Man, it's been ages since I ate here. I think it was back in my pre-Yelp days, even.  I stopped in here with a hankering for a burrito (pretty commonplace for me). I first started with some chips and queso and the restaurant's own bean dip and salsa. It was all perfect.  For my entree, I got the Burrito Gigante with shredded chicken and cheese sauce. It was incredible and, of course, I had plenty left over. It definitely satisfied my burrito craving.

Really cute antique shop among all of the other antique shops in this area.  This store feels like you are going through one of your grandmother's closets. They have a little of everything here, from vintage salt and pepper shakers to different hats, clothing, books and records. Everything is fairly well priced and would be good to give as a gift that is a little "different".

Superior Grill is one of the places you go to because someone brings you.  The margaritas are great, but the food is just mediocre.    If you are a fan of good Mexican food, you will leave disappointed because this place is nothing special.  I know this might sound weird, but I would describe it as "Mexican food geared towards white people", only because the few times I have eaten here the food has lacked flavor.  I think they are more concerned with keeping their uptown St. Charles Ave. clientele happy than spicing up the meals.  The margaritas are fantastic!  I usually like to go and hang out on the patio with friends and just have a few drinks and maybe an app.  It's nice to sit outside during the nice months when the weather is pretty.  BUT, it's not really worth fighting the crowds for this one experience.

This was my FAVORITE gallery on Dirty Linen Night.  For starters, I LOVE any type of art that has a spooky twist. It has nothing to do with Halloween: I'm a year round, spooky decor type of person. The art here is right up my alley: leafless trees silhouetted against a dark, or dimly lit sky, moss hanging off of cypress trees in the shadows. The paintings make you feel as if you're looking out of a window onto a swampy scene at midnight.   There was one piece that I particularly loved of shadowy trees against a red background. The forest seemed to call for you to come explore. In a perfect world I would have endless walls on which to hang all of the art that I covet. Until then, I'll have to make due with admiring these lovely works at Tanner Gallery.

This TJ Maxx is okay, if you're in the area.  I was here just to look around, mainly at purses and they have a decent selection, but nothing overly great. A lot of the items seemed outdated and there was no real organization. The clothing was a little better and there was a fairly big selection of items, if you're willing to look through the racks.

Don't let the fact that this spot is located in a small strip mall deter you. It's some of the best pizza and Italian food you will ever have. I had lunch here a few days ago and it was delicious.   I enjoyed the margherita pizza, the white pizza, boudin egg rolls, Mount Vesuvius shrimp, meatballs, and spinach dip. Yeah, it was a lot! Thankfully, I was sharing with a few people.   The pizza here is authentic New York style pizza with that perfect thin crust and cheese and sauce that speaks for itself. The place is family owned and the service is super friendly. It's a small spot, so give the crew some heads up if you plan on being in a big group. Otherwise, take out is a great option. I love the food here and I will absolutely be back.

If you are anything like me, you are pretty faithful when it comes to your hair stylist. I have been with my same stylist, Jeff, for 14 years. When he told me that he was moving his operation over to Salon Elle, of course I followed.  I stopped in yesterday for a later appointment and Jeff took me right away. He did a fantastic job as always and when I left, my way too long hair was trimmed to a manageable and stylish length for the summer.  I love Salon Elle. It's an old house that has been converted into a salon and the layout is just gorgeous. There is plenty of natural light that flows into the place and everything is clean and well organized. I look forward to coming here and seeing Jeff for many years to come.

Am I seriously admitting to eating one of these things in a public forum? Ugh, I guess so. Admitting to eating street meat is one of those things that is usually followed by some explanation. Something like "...but it was after a long night." or "...I was super hungry after saving those kids from that burning building!" There really is no other excuse for eating a Lucky Dog.   With that being said, my only real excuse for eating one was that I had honestly never had one (and prided myself on that fact) and one evening curiosity got the best of me. Now, I'm not going to sit here and admit to you that I got any enjoyment out of this thing, but I will confess that it wasn't nearly as bad as I thought it would be and the good news is that it didn't make me sick or kill me, so that's a plus.  Would I go out of my way to have another one? Probably not unless I was starving to death, but for what it is, it isn't horrible.

I had wanted to visit this bar for ages and I finally made it over.  What a cute spot! I love the laid back vibe, the dimmed lighting and, of course, the fancy drinks. They have a fairly extensive menu, and a few of their drinks are a bit different from that other tiki bar a few doors down. I enjoyed everything I had here and I dug the atmosphere.   This is really one of those spots where time really flies, because it's pretty dark. I liked that there was a lot of cool seating and all of the decor really made you feel as if you were in an island paradise.

This was a really cool little parade. It's more of a walking parade and there aren't a lot of big floats, but it's still a really cool idea.  Although the title is inspired by Star Wars, Chewbacchus covers everything from Star Trek to zombie movies and everything in between. It's really cool because people make their own costumes and get really into it. This isn't one of those parades that you come to expecting to get a lot of throws. You really come just to have a good time and admire the costumes and all of the work that people put into their different themes.  I think that next year I will do two things differently: I will stand in a better spot. I think that I was at the beginning of the parade and the group was kind of just getting used to the walk. And I will go to the Chewbacchanal after, because I think that would add to the experience.

This is it. Today was the day that I gave Starbucks one more chance and they failed me. I really never buy iced coffee anymore. David gave me a very nice coffee maker, so I can make iced coffee at home, but I was in a pinch today so I thought I would stop in here and grab a quick cup. Big mistake. Huge.   Time and time again they fill the entire cup with big chunks of ice and then put in the coffee. The result is a cup of coffee that I finish before the ice even melts. My grande was probably a quarter cup of actual coffee. Last time I asked them not to do this and they did it anyway. This time I totally forgot to mention it, but I feel as if it's common sense.   Just for the record: I don't blame the employees- I know they are only doing as instructed. I blame Starbucks HQ for being stingy with their coffee. As much as they are charging, they should be willing to be a little more accommodating.

This truck was a welcome addition to the Gretna Food Truck Fest. She had iced coffee ready to go for the warm afternoon. The owner of the truck is really cool, and although I knew what I wanted, she didn't mind taking a few seconds to explain to other customers exactly what she offered.  The iced coffee I got here was delicious, full of flavor and well priced. I can't help but wonder if this truck will eventually end up being a brick and mortar store. It would certainly be a nice addition to the area, but I'm sure it does well wheeling around the streets of New Orleans.

This is a fancy little place with a speakeasy feel.  I was here for an afternoon cocktail and I immediately dug the vibe: a classic cocktail bar that makes you feel as if you have stepped back in time- except for the tvs (can we PLEASE have some cocktail bars that don't feel the need to have big screens on the wall?). I got the Frenchy which was a tasty vodka and champagne concoction, which I enjoyed. They have music practically every night, but sadly I arrived too early and I wasn't able to catch the band.  This seems like the perfect place to start an evening and I will return.

I like it here. I have no idea why the main picture for the place is a picture of the men's room, but okay.  I attended my first ever Pelican's game here, as you do, and I really liked the place. There's a nice gift shop where you can pick up all of the Pelican's fan gear that you could ever want. Upstairs, there are plenty of food and drink stations, that will keep you hydrated and well fed during the game, or any other event that you may be attending here.   One thing I noticed was that there is staff EVERYWHERE and they are very friendly and help you find your seat or anything else that you might need. We were high in the seats for the game, but had no problem seeing all of the action and had a really good time.

Apparently where we're going we don't need roads. When I walked into this place the first time, it was as if Doc Brown had fired up the Delorean and kicked this baby all the way to October 21st, 2015 and took every kid from Rocco's with it.  In other words, this place went from being a college kid bar to being an old man bar in the matter of maybe a week. Trippy, man.   In all seriousness, this bar wasn't too bad. Before, it was a not so great college bar and now it's a "finding it's sea legs" older person bar (which is right up my alley). Yes, I am afraid I have finally become one of those people who prefers to sit and have a drink rather than dance all night to club music. It was bound to happen, so here we are. We're old. Join me, won't you?

I like this Little Tokyo a lot because it has a very upscale feel.  The dining room is very nice and the huge window let in a lot of natural light on nice days.  When I went here with a friend we were feeling experimental, so among other things, we decided to try the tofu steak appetizer.  It's 3 blocks of grilled tofu topped with eel sauce.  It was actually pretty good!  The tofu soaks up the taste of the sauce and gives it really good flavor.  It was interesting to try, although I probably wouldn't go out of my way to get it again.    We also got some rolls. The mid city, uptown, Philly and spicy salmon rolls were all really good and very well made.   This would be a great place to bring a date due to the nice atmosphere and upscale feel.

So, you know that thing where you had something all the time as a kid and then it went away? And then all of your memories are of how amazing this certain thing was and "if only" it was still around life would be so great? That's how I am with Krystal Burger, or at least I was.  I went in here for lunch and...well, I was left disappointed. I had always remembered Krystal being so good and the expectation didn't meet the reality. I got combo #1, which is 4 Krystal burgers, fries and a drink. First of all, the fries really had no flavor and they were definitely underwhelming. The burgers were good, but they were more bread than meat. You can't have a small patty of meat with a super fluffy bun. I mean...it was good, but it wasn't great.  Would I go back? Uh...maybe, but I wouldn't go out of my way. It IS nice, however, to have more fast food options on the Westbank for lunch.

My boyfriend turned me onto this place, as I am a Taco Bell fan, and he said that this is a step up.  He was right.  I have only ever had the burrito, but it is HUGE and I can never finish the whole dang thing!  Great prices, although it is in a sketchy area.  I have and would never go by myself.  My boyfriend has had pretty much everything on the menu and has said it is good.  It's cheap, so it's worth trying.  It's not restaurant quality Mexican, but it's better than the Bell.

Such a great shop!  Whenever I passed Blue Frog, I always kind of assumed that it was just a "do it yourself/build your own box" type of chocolate shop. While you can pick and choose chocolates from the case, they also have an assortment of all kinds of chocolates that you can give as gifts or just enjoy yourself. My faves that I saw were the chocolate musical instruments, chocolate water meters, chocolate streetcar tokens and chocolate gators. A definite "must" for anyone who is visiting NOLA and wants a "different" kind of souvenir to bring home.  They have a TON of cute gift ideas and I could never go through them all, but I will say that I thought that the chocolate gavel geared towards someone who just graduated law school was SUPER cute.  Stop in here and look around. You are sure to find something that you like. I can't wait to see if they get anything special in for Halloween!

During my formative high school years, I spent a lot of time at this library usually doing research for a project. I know what you are thinking: "why didn't you just go online?" Well kiddies, back in my day (the late 90's, early 00's) the internet wasn't what it is today. It was still fairly new, as far as research went, and the teachers at my school decided (in their infinite wisdom) that they would require 4 different sources to be cited on a paper or project. Out of those 4, only ONE could be an internet source. So, I had to go to the library and look information up in books. Oh yeah, it was a lot of fun.  Anyway, this is a really nice library and really big. I like that they have little study "nooks" that you can go into if you need to be totally alone to study or do research or work. They have special reading events for kids and other fun things for them to do.

Becky is a self made artist who is naturally talented and fantastic at painting and she adds her own unique twist to all of her work. Not only does she paint one of a kind pieces, but she offers prints at a reasonable price and she does commissioned work. If you are short on wall space, you can wear Becky's art on your body via one of the shirts she sells with her prints on it.  Positioned right on Magazine St., I like that the gallery walk-able from other little galleries and shops on the block and makes for a fantastic addition to the neighborhood. Gallery B Fos is set up perfectly with nice flow and wide open space, so that you can view all of her artwork and the staff working here was super helpful in making sure that I was being taken care of.   Gallery director Felice helps with the art consumer's needs and answers questions when the artist is off site and soon Gallery B Fos will be offering jewelry inspired by Becky's work, so stay tuned for greatness.

City Park is a fantastic "getaway" in the city, especially when the weather is really nice.  It is really gorgeous and has come a long way since Katrina with the help of local and visiting volunteers.  The shady oaks are huge and are perfect for a picnic or for just going somewhere nice to read or enjoy the day.  Throughout the park are covered areas with tables and chairs, if you are in the mood for a barbecue or a crawfish boil.   The park is close to the museum, so you can visit after a nice lunch.  There is also a tennis court, Storyland for the kids, and the botanical gardens.  A definite must for locals and tourists alike.

Fancy cocktail place that is WAY less pretentious than Cure.  One of my major complaints about Uptown is that there really aren't any cocktail bars. Well, this is pretty much as close as you are going to get. Nice place that caters to a somewhat older crowd. Smart and capable bartenders that are happy to help you figure out exactly what suits your tastes.  I do agree with Joi when she said that people here are casually dressed, considering the atmosphere. It really feels more like one of those places that you would dress up and make a night out of, but maybe that's just me.  I definitely want to go back and try some of their delicious (looking) food.

Katie wasn't lying, this store really is dangerous.  I have been here a few times now and I never made it out the door without having bought at least one thing. I know that this is a chain, and I usually prefer shopping local, but this is a good place to start if you are looking for stylish home decor. You will find it all here: pillows, bedding, candles, kitchen ware and the list goes on.  I stopped in here because I have had my eye on a big pink wool pillow. I need this pillow. It will be mine. While I was pricing it, of course they were having a 20% off sale on other bedroom items so I broke down and got myself a throw. Hey, winter is coming. No matter what your style, you are bound to find something here that will fit your personality and they are always having sales, so keep an eye out.

Someone told me the other day that my Yelp reviews are "too nice". I'll admit that unless service is horrible and I really hate the food, I will be pretty generous with my ratings. However, my four stars for Juan's were totally well earned.  Juan's is a New Orleans classic for Mexican food. I headed over here for dinner, and since I was in a "burrito" mood, I got the "wet burrito". This is a burrito packed with beans, rice, lettuce and salsa and topped with red chile sauce, melted cheese, sour cream and jalapeños. The burrito is HUGE and was so good. I was going to snap a picture, but before I could, that burrito got ate.  The service was friendly and I like that the restaurant itself is dim and kind of cozy. Juan's is small, so there is going to be a bit of a wait for a table, if you go during busy lunch and dinner hours, but I waited less than 10 minutes at 8:00.

Aaah! Another cute new boutique on Magazine St! And it JUST opened! I happened to just stumble into this place because I had never seen it before and then I realized that today was their opening day.  Lucy Rose has a lot of cute clothes for all body types. I think I would call them "happy" clothes: a lot of skirts, dresses and tops in a lot of bright colors. I was only able to quickly stop in here today, but I will definitely be back. Lucy Rose will definitely make a nice addition to Magazine St.

If jazz fest is for tourists, then the French Quarter fest is for the locals.  Tons of local bands playing music for free!  What could be better than that?  Food?  Oh yeah, there is plenty of it here.  All the food you could possibly want.  The best thing to do is go out there with a blanket, get some food, set up a picnic and enjoy the musical sounds of the city.  One of the best times you can have in New Orleans.

Guess who just discovered the "festivals" category.  This chick!  I love the poboy fest!  My boyfriend and I went to the last one with some friends and had a great time.  Be sure to get there early, because the place fills up fast and gets packed with a capital "P"..err...Packed!  By the time we decided to leave, it took us about a half hour to get from one end of Oak to the other and that was before the afternoon crowd really hit.  But you don't want to hear about that.  You want to hear about how awesome the food is.  Well, that goes without saying.  Restaurants from all over town set up booths and sell small samples of their best po boys.  Now, here's a hint.  You're gonna wanna eye up what the po boy looks like before you drop your money.  Some of them just have one ingredient like shrimp, but some of piles of stuff like sausage and yummy dressing on it.  Those are the ones you want, if you want to get your bucks worth.  No matter what you choose, it's all good and you won't be disappointed.

NOW SMOKE FREE!!  DBA is one of my favorite places to enjoy live music.  They have a fantastic beer selection and the atmosphere is great.  You can either sit in the window that faces Frenchmen and watch the world go by, or you can enjoy the live music in the stage area.  There is also a nice little "lounge" area upstairs, if you want to get away from the crowd.

I can say with complete honesty that Cane's is the ONLY fast food place that I have ever been to that has NEVER screwed up my order!  I have been going here since this place opened.  It is what it is:Chicken fingers.  They are hot and delicious and fantastic.  I LOVE their sweet tea and whenver I order a large with "easy ice", I actually get it with just a little ice!!  I have always been satisfied with Cane's and have never had reason to complain.  The way all fast food place should be.

Such a lovely little shop on so many levels!  I stopped in here because I have had this place bookmarked for a while and I finally found myself in the area, so I decided to visit. The shop itself is set up in such a lovely manner. There are glass cases full of pretty little trinkets, vintage and new alike, and everything is so sparkly and inviting under the lights.  I've found things extremely well priced here, and if you are in the market for vintage costume jewelry or accessories, you are sure to find a bauble that suits your fancy. On the day that I stopped in, a sweet woman named Eleanor was working and she engaged me in lovely conversation about old New Orleans, how much things have changed since she was a girl and the differences in dialect from one area of the city to another. I was having a pretty laid back day, so I was happy to get to know her a little better.  I will definitely return to this fantastic little treasure chest, if not for the jewelry, than for the conversation.

I am normally not really a fan of Academy. I find A LOT of their pro team related things over priced ($60 for a "licensed" Saints shirt?? No thanks.), but I do realize that the place serves a purpose.  Well, this place saved my life recently when I ended up here on the hunt for a birthday gift for my favorite Saints fan. Do you know how HARD it is to find anything "football team" related during the off season? It's real hard, y'all. It's darn near impossible. I was SAVED when I stopped in and found an awesome gift that is sure to be treasured forever (one can hope!). Needless to say, I was a happy camper.  I looked over some of the team jerseys that they had for women and I was a little less than impressed with the selection. I think once the season gets underway, they will be packing the store with goodies.

Fantastic new music venue on Frenchmen St.   Came in on opening night and the staff was friendly and welcoming. They have a nice size stage for performances, plenty of seating and they serve food! The place is beautifully done with murals on the walls and an entirely renovated space. The band was on a break for most of the time that we were here, but I will definitely be back to check out everything that this new venue has to offer.

Um yeah. I have now eaten here and I can say with full certainty that this place sucks. We ordered the burger medium and naturally it came medium well. This is irritating mainly because I only eat red meat once a week, so this was my one shot and it  was terrible.  Before the burger, we got the egg roll appetizer. It was okay. I mean, it was as decent as deep fried frozen egg rolls can be. The beer? The beer was a "no" and had ZERO flavor. To refer to this place as a "brewery" is a joke. All of the beer tastes the same and just makes me sad.

"Good not great" would be an accurate description.  Had dinner here on the advice of a friend. I had NO CLUE this place even existed, but hey, Magazine St. is a long street! I really like the atmosphere of the restaurant. We were seated by a window so that we could look out as we ate and that was nice.   I ordered the taco salad with chicken. It was okay. I liked that there were huge hunks of chicken in it, but there wasn't nearly enough of it. The salad also came with lettuce, black olives, cheese, sour cream and guacamole. Honestly, the shell was kind of stale but it wasn't terrible. I hear that the tacos are amazing, so I will be getting those if I go back.  All in all, not as great as my beloved Felipe's, but still a valid spot if you are looking for quick Mexican food.

I am updating and bumping up to five stars because this thrift store has become my first stop whenever I am looking for something from clothing to cheap electronics.  Over the past year I have found multiple working, great condition Polaroid cameras for a photographer friend of mine for $4 a piece. These cameras can be resold online for good bucks- score! I have found multiple dresses brand new with tags that I was able to snag for less than $10. I have found collectible gifts for next to nothing that cost WAY more online and that friends will cherish for a lifetime. Just today a found a practically brand new denim jacket for $6. If you aren't a regular thrift store shopper, I know you are rolling your eyes, but trust me- you will be surprised what you find here.  I constantly see brand new items for men and women that are selling at a steal. I wouldn't go so far as to buy swimsuits or shoes here (that's where I draw the line), but when I need a new dress for a casual event, this spot is always my first (and usually only) stop.

I recently had a "20's" inspired photo shoot with Make Me Up, and they sent me here (right next door to Make Me Up) to get my hair done all fancy.  They decided that they wanted to put a finger wave in my hair, which is apparently pretty complicated. It consists of putting a "wet set" in the hair, forming the waves with your fingers, setting it with hair gel and then sitting under a hair dryer for over an hour while it sets and dries. Even though the style was hard, my stylist Madeline did a fantastic job. She worked quickly and efficiently to get the waves perfect. The hardest part really was just sitting under that dryer for a really long time while it dried and set.  She did such a good job, that my hair didn't go anywhere for the rest of the day, and I'm convinced that I probably could have slept on it and wore it the entire next day without it looking any worse for wear.  If you are looking for a "different" or somewhat "complicated" hairstyle, Albert Brown is the place to go.

Well, here's a part of town I really wish I lived in. The Garden District seems to have it all: gorgeous houses, great restaurants and good shopping.  This is one of those classic New Orleans neighborhoods that is perfectly walkable and as picturesque as a postcard. It's nice to imagine living in one of these gorgeous homes and sipping coffee on the front porch, whilst looking through the newspaper. You really aren't going to see homes like this anywhere else. Well, maybe in Natchez or a place like that, but the Garden District really is the epitome of Southern charm.

The CAC is a great place for local events and parties.  I have been here for Bourbon and Burlesque. I love how wide open everything is. There are different levels and there is a lot of space for entertaining. They always have different exhibits and events happening here as well as performances in the theater area.  Although the theater is pretty small, by theater standards, it's still a really nice place to see a performance. I watched a Burlesque performance here and had a really good time.

Thanks to the magic of Yelp, I got to experience my first ever Pelicans game and it was a great one! The Pelicans set a franchise record with their score of 139 points in one game and the game itself was non stop action.  I loved that there was constant entertainment throughout the game: people running around with signs, the dancers getting the crowd pumped and even a fun game of Simon says at half time.
