Thanks to social media we were able to participate in little activities with the jumbo tron and the crowd had a great time.  I can't wait to go back and see another game!

Blue Plate Mayonnaise is THE mayonnaise that is used on most of the Po Boys in the New Orleans area. Po Boy experts will tell you that no other mayo will do.   Blue Plate is a staple throughout the South, but is "stationed" in New Orleans. It's as classic as any other product that is manufactured here and every true New Orleanian has a jar of the stuff in their fridge at all times.

Shoe-nami never disappoints, especially when you are in a pinch.  I needed some shoes for a ball, and since I was in Metairie today, I stopped in here. I have been shopping at this store for at least 15 years and I have bought countless shoes here. Right now the store is 90% boots, but I lucked out and found the perfect pair of sparkly pumps for my special night.  They always have items on sale and they even have a "buy one get one half off" deal going on pretty regularly. The shoes are on the cheaper side, but I like that. I really tend to beat up my shoes, so I'm not interested in spending more than $40 anyway.

I don't know what has come over me, but I have been LOVING Forever 21 lately.  It seems that the styles are a lot different than they used to be, and the stuff isn't geared just towards teens and the early 20s set these days.  They have been stocking really cute print dresses and tops.  I am a sucker for polka dots (they remind me of a vintagey kind of look) and Forever 21 has had a lot of polka dots the last few times I have been in there.  If you haven't checked out Forever 21 in a while, stop in and see if you see something that appeals to you.    This store is especially good because it is HUGE and packed with stuff.  You can easily spend a lot of time shopping around and checking everything out.

This place isn't really anything super special, but it's a great place to check out if you are heading out for a night out in the warehouse district.  They have really good pizza and the place has a nice "party" atmosphere on weekends and even has a dj.  It's open pretty late, especially on game days and during special events, so if you get hungry after a night of celebrating, then it's a good place to check out.

Only 3 stars??  What?!  I love this place!  Whenever I go I always get the Oyster platter that comes with fries and hush puppies and cole slaw.  The inside of the place has a "nautical" theme, so you are made to feel like you are eating in a fisherman's cabin.  They have an oyster bar, so if you are in the mood for raw oysters this is a great place to go.  This is also a good place for all kinds of seafood.  I have never had anything here that I didn't really enjoy.  The food here tends to be a little on the spicy side, so if you are a person who likes their food on the bland side, you might want to avoid this one.  The restaurant is a little on the expensive side, at least for the Westbank, so if you are on a budget you may want to go somewhere else.

As soon as I walked in and saw the big screens playing pop music videos, I knew I would love this place.  This bar is SO FUN! David and I came here to try Fauboirg Bistro, but ended up hanging out after we ate and watched a bit of the LSU game.They have an amazing happy hour special on Saturdays- 2 for 1 doubles and $3 draft beer (and it's good beer!). They are very generous with the pours and they also have wine on tap, if that's what your into.  There's a definite party vibe in here and I can see this place being a lot of fun as the evening wears on. Everyone i met was so sweet and friendly and happy to chat. I'll review the food in another post, but if you are coming for drinks you are going to have a great time.

Are you ever in the mood for a really big, messy burrito? I recently had that kind of craving, so David and I headed over to El Gato Negro, home of one of my favorite burritos.  We were here somewhat early (7 ish) on a Friday night and the crowd was non-existent, but we were greeted with a friendly "hello" and shown to our table right away. Joseph was our waiter and he was great- super friendly and attentive and full of personality. We started with an order of queso and I got my carnitas burrito smothered in their delicious tomato sauce. As always, the burrito was perfect and packed with goodies. I was pretty pleased. I also had a tasty frozen margarita that was a great "cool down" on a warm summer night.  The atmosphere of this place is pretty laid back and I imagine that they do a good lunch crowd and I'm sure that business picks up when there is a show at Howlin Wolf or Republic, so plan accordingly. I will definitely go back for more of their deliciousness.

Did you know that this is outside? Like, in nature and stuff? I know! I was shocked too!  I am not what you would call an "outdoorsy" person. A guy that I am seeing was recently shocked when I told him that I occasionally do venture outdoors and have even been known to enjoy an outdoor festival.  Anyway, I hadn't been here for years when a photographer suggested that we explore this place for a photo shoot. Okay, I'm down. The part of the preserve we ventured into was basically a mud trail next to a swamp. I could tell that it was pretty well traveled as it was pretty worn down and there was some trash (coke cans) left behind. Unfortunately, on the day we went it was muggy and hot and the bugs were everywhere. If I had brought bug spray, I would have actually loved exploring this area.  I'm giving it 5 stars because it is well taken care of and patrolled regularly, so I felt pretty safe. I will probably return when it cools down a little and the insects head South for the winter.

I am SO glad that I waited for Origami to get settled in before I tried it.  On the night that we went it wasn't crowded at all and the service was great! We were seated at a booth and after looking over the menu, we decided to order the salmon sashimi, the tiger roll and the margarita roll.  The salmon sashimi was really fresh and cut thick. This might sound silly, but I liked that it was cut into an even number of pieces so that each person gets their fair share. The margarita roll was excellent was reminiscent of the margarita rolls I had had at other sushi places. By far the star of the meal was the tiger roll. I can't find a menu, so I can't find the exact ingredients, but it was SO GOOD.  Like... so good I might order two the next time I go. I could have eaten the entire thing on my own!  Origami is a little more expensive than other sushi places, but the atmosphere and service was great and the food was excellent. I will definitely be back!

I've waited a long time to review the Roosevelt. While I have never stayed here, I have been here many times for various reasons. I have made it my yearly Christmas tradition to stop in here at least once and admire the gorgeous decorations and lights. There is just something magical about this place. I almost feel as if I'm in New York city and seeking sanctuary from the cold city snow in this hotel's lobby.  When you walk in, you are embraced by gorgeous chandeliers and classic decor. You feel as if you are stepping back in time to the 50's, when ladies wore fancy dresses and men wore hats. You can stop into the Sazerac bar for a cocktail with someone special and sit at the bar and people watch. Having a drink at the Sazerac is a giddy affair that someone must do at least once (or twice) when visiting New Orleans.  Even if you don't end up staying here, admiring this lovely hotel will be an experience in itself.

I have always had no problem finding whatever I need here. I usually just get stuff that will keep my car clean and shiny. I have known a few people who have gotten car maintenance done here with no real issue. The staff here is knowledgeable and friendly and should be able to help you with whatever you may need.

My 500th review!  After passing Guy's time and time again and hearing how great it is, I finally got to stop in and experience the deliciousness for myself.  I went in around 3 in the afternoon on a Saturday. It wasn't packed at all and I was able to quickly order and find a seat. They have an extensive menu, but unfortunately they don't have oyster po boys. Oh well. I decided on a fried shrimp, dressed, instead.  After about 10 minutes, I had my sandwich. I have to say that Guy's was well worth the wait. It was amazing. The bread was fresh and perfect and it was overflowing with shrimp. I ordered a regular size and couldn't even finish it all (of course I did, later). My friend got a roast beef po boy and that looked incredible too! When I go back (and I will be back), I will absolutely have to try it.

Although considered kind of "touristy" this is my favorite place to see live jazz.  I've seen Charmaine Neville play here multiple times, as well as some of the Marsalis'.  If you go early, you can enjoy dinner or drinks before the show.  They used to have free shows on Friday nights at Midnight, but I'm not sure if they still do.  The food is a little pricey, but I like it a lot.  When I went, I had a filet with fried calamari for an appetizer.  Yum!

It is completely unacceptable that it has taken me this long review this New Orleans music institution and for that I apologize.  Tipitina's is world known.  You know that.  The famous, the not so famous and the infamous have played here.  If they were worth listening to, they probably played here at some point.  I'm not telling you anything you don't already know.  The venue is huge and legendary.  Most times it will cost you a few bucks to get in the door, but it is always worth it.  Stories have been told here and history has been made here. If you are looking for good music, this place is a must, end of story.    What's one the best parts?  It's smoke free!

I recently attended a fundraiser here and this is such a gorgeous place!  Houses like this are what make New Orleans so unique. The entire house is decorated like any mansion should be decorated that was built in 1865- gorgeous antique furniture and art is everywhere and the wide open space makes it perfect for hosting a party.  The house and all of it's furnishings and art was actually donated to the Opera Guild in 1965.   The event I attended here was lovely. The Opera Guild staff did a good job of keeping everyone fed and entertained. I like that the house has a lot of space, so if there is a big crowd there is good flow and no one feels bunched up.  They are actually giving tours of the home every Monday until May 16th, 2016 so you don't have to wait for a fancy event to see the house for yourself.

Talk about a fantastic gift shop! I am redoing my kitchen- trust me you will be hearing more about this. Anyway, I stopped in here to find some kitchen goods and I seriously hit the jackpot. Not only did I find some fantastic shellacked oysters, but I found a really cool bottle opener that mounts on a wall. Give me all the things!  I know they have actual cooking classes, so I think I am going to come back and check that out.

This is a cool spot. There are a lot of nice and friendly people here and it was easy to find space at the bar.  The reason for this review is the awesome juke box. I was in the mood to play an "old fashioned" juke box (that means not an internet jukebox) and a friend suggested this place. The juke is pretty inexpensive and has a lot of good songs on it. I chose to play a lot of Louis Prima because it was just that kind of night.  A regular here mentioned to me that this is the place to be for Saints games, so I will have to come back and check the place out when the season starts.

Whoa. I don't understand all of the low reviews for this TJ Maxx!  This is a fairly new store- I think they built this new one at the same time that they built the new TJ Maxx on the Westbank. I stopped in here with a friend who was looking for some luggage that wouldn't break the bank. She ended up finding a nice piece of luggage that was perfect and well priced.  I browsed the women's clothing and housewares, but didn't find anything that I absolutely needed, but I found that they had a nice selection of seasonal clothing and a lot of good deals. We went in the middle of a weekday, so there weren't a lot of people in the store and the check out was easy. The cashiers were nice and we had no issues.  I'd return if I found myself in the area and in the need of a deal.

Lee Circle monument to Robert E. Lee, the Confederate General and is one of those classic New Orleans landmarks that locals probably pass all the time and don't even think about.  I didn't even realize you could review it! I have been looking up at this monument since I was a kid and there's just something about it that makes me proud to live in this city.  I don't know if there is much to say about it, other than that it's there and it's worth checking out, if you are visiting.

Well, I would tell you how this place is, but I have no idea.  We stopped in hoping to get a drink and a bite to eat (it's attached to New York pizza). There was no bartender and when someone came in from the connected restaurant to make a drink, he explained that he wasn't the bartender and couldn't serve us. Uh...ok.  We waited and waited and nothing happened, so we left. Swing and a miss. Maybe next time, but I doubt there will be a next time.

I like Best Buy. I really like Best Buy when they are having a huge sale.   They have a large selection of cell phones and other electronics, but what I usually get here are CDs and DVDs. Yes, I still listen to CDs. Does that mean I'm old? Whatever. They have sales all the time on CDs and DVDs and if you know what to look for, you can get some pretty cool deals.  I also like that during the holiday season, they have all of their holiday CDs and DVDs right in the front where you can find them.

So, it's a college bar. At least that's what the bartender told us. She said that most of the college kids were studying for finals (don't miss that) so that's why there weren't a lot of college kids when we stopped in.  I really dig this place. Nice little beer selection and a good crowd. Not too divey but not too fancy either. We stopped in here because my date had been bragging about his skee ball skills and this place has one of those old school skee ball games, which you can play for free. Not to brag, but I totally dominated at this game. Yep, all those years of training at Chuck E. Cheese (I went when it was called Showbiz Pizza) really paid off.  I'll be back for the skee ball alone. No smoking, which is always a win in this gal's book.

This is, by far, one of my favorite parades!  Fantastic throws and gorgeous floats.  I have collected so many of the little  Krewe D'Etat light up skulls over the years.  One of my favorite parts of Carnival.

What's not to love about Dollar Tree? As the name suggests- everything here is a dollar. I shop here a lot. I have purchased candy, cards, snacks, holiday decorations, arts and crafts, small gifts, fake flowers, gardening supplies, wrapping paper, not-so-great lotion, wine glasses and much more at this very store. What I like most about this store is the fact that most of the time all of the cash registers are open and the staff is fast and friendly about getting people through the lines. Also, there are always staff members walking around making sure that everything is neat, especially during the busy holiday season.  Pro tip: if possible, go in the middle of the day on a weekday because that's when the store is pretty much dead and you can get in and out in less than 10 minutes, if you know what you're looking for.

I really like this place! Checked out the Brassaholics here and although it was crowded, it was a lot of fun.  There was no cover or anything to get in. This place gets packed, so if you are going to see a band, you might want to go early.

It's been three years since I first tried HiVolt Coffee. As I was doing some Black Friday shopping in the area, I stumbled upon HiVolt Bakery- same coffee and this spot serves breakfast sandwiches and other noms.  I gotta say- my experience here was a lot better than my last at the other location. I stopped in to grab an iced coffee to go. The woman working was very nice and completed my order quickly. This shop is a bit small, but I like the ambiance and it doesn't feel as "sterile" as the other location.  The coffee was pretty good and I liked that I didn't have to add anything to it and I could just enjoy the coffee flavor minus the milk. I didn't get anything to eat this time, but HiVolt is now on my radar as a cute place for coffee and lunch.

This a such a cute shop! It's the perfect place to pick up a casual summer outfit and I found a nice long dress that was flowy and cool enough for summer.   When I was here, I met the owner Meghan and was impressed by everything this place has to offer. I love the long flowy skirts and the crop tops! I would say that the clothes here are great for a more relaxed look, when you don't want to wear jeans. They also have a nice collection of swimsuits with knitting on them, which I really liked. This is a great addition to this newly developed area in the city.

Pretty good PJ's with nice booths and free WiFi if you have work to do. I stopped in here to get my usual iced coffee and it was the usual good PJ's coffee that I really like.   My one complaint about the place is they wouldn't honor a coupon I had. They explained that the coupon could only be honored at certain locations, but there was nothing on the coupon that said that- it just said I could use it at any PJ's location. Anyway, I went to my regular PJ's a few days later and they not only honored the coupon, but they told me that it can be honored at any PJ's and the folks at this place screwed up. Long story short: the staff here didn't know what was going on. Other than that, the place is okay.

Third stop on the Metry bar crawl. Pretty cool place. Super friendly patrons.  The music was...interesting. Elvis mashed up with Eminem. Amy Winehouse mashed up with Queen. I gotta say, I didn't quite "get it", but eventually the horrible mash up music stopped and karaoke started. Everyone in our group had a really good time cheering on Joel, Dann, and John. They had some regulars who took the mic and they were really good. I could tell that the people here are all friends, which is awesome.  This was my final stop on the Metry bar crawl, and I would probably come back to this place if I were in the area.

I like this place a lot! I have seen more than one band here and have danced quite a few times upstairs to the DJ that plays.  The people here are always nice and friendly and it's a good crowd. One of the better music clubs on Frenchmen St.

I came here for lunch and I was pleasantly surprised by the entire experience.  We decided to get an order of shrimp and pork spring rolls and I got a vermicelli bowl with pork, since it was too warm for Pho. The spring rolls were tasty and got us off to a good start. My vermicelli bowl was PACKED- this is one of those places that is really generous with their bowls. The bowl was really good and the pork was cooked perfectly and had a lot of flavor.  We were in and out in about 30 minutes or so, so this is a really good place for a quick lunch.

This is a perfect little gift shop that I must have missed on past Magazine St. excursions.  Pop City offers a little bit of everything from NOLA inspired shirts to jewelry, sunglasses and other collectibles. I treated myself to a pair of earrings during my visit here that I can't wait to wear on an upcoming vacation. In the back, they have a nice selection of art for sale that was done by a local artist. The shop is very quaint and the woman working was quite nice and helped me explore the shop and find exactly what I was looking for.

Oh, Danny and Clydes, how I miss thee.  They FINALLY rebuilt in this spot, last year, after Hurricane Katrina killed the other gas station/convenience store that was here.  I love how shiny and new it is and the gas pumps actually work!  The gas is super cheap, because they are competing with the Race Trac on Lafayette (they are always the same price or 1 cent less).  The inside is nice, clean and big and they have a great selection of beer and snacks.  A good crowd goes in here, too.  I actually feel safe going here at night to fill up.  I admit that, yes, I have gotten chicken from Brothers.  It's cheap and good.  No, it's not Popeyes, and it can't compare to what Danny and Clydes once offered, but I'll take what I can get.    Thank you for rebuilding in this spot!!

Such a cute shop with a super friendly staff!  I was wandering Magazine when I came across this adorable stationary/card/all things paper store. The woman working explained to me that all of the designs are done by the owner and they are all so adorable. If you're looking for a Christmas or birthday card that's a little different or some stationary or thank you cards that have a little kick, than this is the place for you.  Everything is organized beautifully and it's all easy to find. They even have not so fancy necessities like sketch pads and graph paper and things of that nature. The woman working (I wish I had gotten her name, she was so friendly) told me that they will also have designed wrapping paper for the holidays, so I will be going back soon to see what they have and pick some up.  I felt so welcome when I was here and I will be purchasing some things from them soon. If you're stuck trying to figure out what to get someone for Christmas, head over here because you are bound to find something that will inspire you.

Only one other review that's over 3 years old? Uncalled for!  This is such a cute little jewelry shop. They carry all kinds of handmade jewelry like bracelet cuffs and necklaces.  The stuff they carry is extremely unique and I could see how a lot of this stuff would make great gifts.  Jen L. was right when she said that there is something for everyone here. They have cute little post earrings that would be perfect for a little girl who just got her ears pierced. They also have pretty little rings that any girl would love.
Flashing Gargoyles are always awesome.  The skulls didn't disappoint, either.  Another very generous crewe.  Catch of the night:  flashing gargoyles

This is a pretty basic sushi and Chinese place that serves it's purpose.  The decor is really no frills and is mainly set up as a take out joint, but that's fine. I grabbed a booth and picked a couple of rolls. I got the Naruto roll which was raw fish wrapped in cucumber and the New Orleans roll which was tuna, salmon and cream cheese topped with crab. The rolls were okay, but nothing spectacular. I was kind of annoyed because they kept falling apart has soon as I picked them up with my chopsticks- they weren't rolled tightly at all. The staff was super sweet and they were good about taking my order and getting the food out to me in a timely manner.  I'd probably order take out/delivery from here if I lived closer, but it's not worth a special trip.

I've never eaten here, but I did go here with friends to watch a Saints game and we had a pretty good time. They have a nice beer selection and although I didn't eat, the food does look pretty amazing. The place gets PACKED during Saints games with a good crowd that likes to have a good time. Because it is technically a restaurant, there is no smoking, so that's enough to make me want to hang out to watch Saints games while having a beer.  This isn't an authentic New Orleans experience, but it isn't bad for what it is.

It had been years since I had been here when I ended up here the other night.  Not much has changed, except on this particular night the place had a bit of a "club" vibe. I think the ownership has changed because what used to be a hole in the wall where you could grab a cheap burger is now a dark dance club type place. It is DEFINITELY different from the bar that Eddie described.  On this particular night, me and a friend were just in the mood to hang out somewhere and have a beer. The staff here is friendly and the bar is pretty nice. There are pool tables and a nice area with sofas if you aren't in the mood to hang at the bar. The crowd seems a bit younger than a typical Westbank place and the beer selection is decent.

Yes! I have been wanting to try this spot for the longest time and I finally made it in!  I have been making an effort to drink something green every day- my fridge is filled with green juice. I got the Amazing Greens smoothie, which is packed with greens, bananas, peaches and a whole lot of other goodies. It came out a really rich and bright green color and it tasted delightful. It had a bit of a tart flavor, but I could definitely taste the sweet of the fruits more than the veggies. I got a medium, but when I return, I will definitely get a small because it takes a while to sip and it warmed up because I was taking my time with it. There was a lot stuffed into this cup and it constituted a meal for me.  The store itself is really nice with a comfy seating area in the back with chairs and sofas. They made my smoothie quickly with barely a wait at all. I'm really glad I don't live close to this Jamba, because I would surely be broke within a month.

I wanted to update, because since I last reviewed I have gotten both mashed potatoes and red beans and rice here.  The mashed potatoes are good and they come with gravy.  I'm sure they are "instant", but who cares?  Other fast food places serve instant potatoes.  It's a convenience store and it's just as good as Popeyes, especially if you take them home and add some Crystal to them.  And yes, Brother's has red beans and rice!  Who knew?  I was really surprised at how good it was!  I'm actually going to "go there" and say that I prefer them over Popeyes!  They are more like actual homemade red beans and not the canned stuff that Popeyes is serving up these days.  Like I said before, pick some up and spice to flavor with some Crystal sauce and you are good to go.  When I get food here, I get the two piece white with a small mashed potato and it costs about $4.75, which is cheap and on top of that, they are open late.  Just sayin...  ;)

Decent fast food pizza.  Not as good as an actual pizza place like Rotolo's or even Papa John's, but it gets the job done.  The best thing about this place is the large pepperoni pizza for $5 and the really cheap bread sticks.  Not worth going out of your way for, but worth checking out, if you are in the mood for a quick bite.

I'm not a huge cook, so I don't make it here nearly as often as some people do. HKM has a nice assortment of Asian goodies of all types, including different fancy noodles, soy sauces, meat and fish. If you are looking to make anything Asian from pho to sushi, this is going to be your one stop shop.  I really liked that they sell fresh Spring rolls. You can get four really good sized ones for about $3, which can't be beat. On the day I went, they had pork and shrimp.  I'll definitely be back, HKM is an interesting place and you are bound to find something here that you will enjoy.

This is a review of the iced coffee.  This is a cute little restaurant that just opened and they serve various sandwiches and soups. In addition to the food they have an extensive juice and coffee menu. Because I love Vietnamese coffee, but I feel weird going into most places and just asking for it "to go", this seemed like the perfect place for me because "to go" is one of their specialties. I got an iced coffee and it was 12 ounces for $4. At first I thought that this was a bit overpriced, but the coffee was really rich and I enjoyed it. I think next time I am going to ask for less ice only because they packed the cup and I hate when I finish a drink and I still have a full cup of ice.  The place itself is small with a few booths and there is seating outside, if you happen to be there on a cooler day. I am eager to return and try the food and will post a review update when I do.

Awesome!  A fantastic thrift store close to home.  I stopped by here today, because the sign had been up awhile and I was anxiously awaiting it's opening.  The store is HUGE (as are all Red White and Blue thrift stores) and it was nice because it's new and everything is neat and clean.  There also weren't a TON of people, because not a lot of people know about it yet.  I guess that's about to change.  Ha.    They are cash only, and if I had more cash on me today, I would have definitely left the store with a lot of stuff.  I was most impressed that none of the stuff looked raggedy or used.  A lot of the things here still had tags and some of the dresses were the same style that I would find at upper hand consignment stores.  I saw a cute dress, that still had tags on it, that was marked as $5.95 and it was originally $20 at a retail store!  You can't beat that.  Don't be put off that this is a "thrift" store.  Go in and look around, and I think you'll be surprised at what you see.

I love Bunny Bread Warehouse, and not just because it's pretty much right down the street from where I live.  This store is pretty "no frills" and it's fairly small, but it's packed with goodies. I usually stop in here to get hamburger buns or Italian bread, because it's really fresh and it's a little bit cheaper than what you can get at the grocery store. When I come I usually like to pick up some of the small snack pies they have- I really like to get the individually wrapped pumpkin pies and pecan pies that make for a perfect dessert when you don't want to buy a whole pie. I'll occasionally pick up one of those "snoball" treats that come wrapped. Whenever I have been here the people working are usually teenagers, but they do their best to help you if you are looking for something specific.

I was on the hunt for some gifts for a Harry Potter loving friend of mine when I was told that this place was worth checking out.  Nestled in a converted house on N. Carrollton Avenue, this cute book shop seems to have a little something for everyone. They have a nice selection of really cute magnets and toys all relating to book characters. I loved the Jane Austen action figures and temporary tattoos- that is such a cute way to get kids interested in reading!   As promised, they had a nice selection of Harry Potter toys and other fun little things. I ended up getting a massive book about the Harry Potter houses as well as a couple of little toys that my friend is sure to like.  Things that I really liked about this shop: the small, but effective "local books" section that had a nice selection of local interest books, the really cool floating book shelf (how did they do that?), a whole upstairs section of children's books and a reading area for kids.  Basically, this little shop is everything you want a book shop to be and I will return.

This is a review of an art show.  I think I came on a good night, because I attended an art show here. I feel that this is what this space is best suited for. I really can't imagine it being much else. Anyway, the art was all spread out and there was a lot of space for mingling with others. The bartenders did well keeping up with the crowd, and I enjoyed my house cabernet. There was nice performance art here and I liked that there was plenty of seating right next to the stage,  I really can't imagine anything but an art show happening here. I feel like it's too small for any kind of club, unless they move a lot of stuff. I probably wouldn't go back for a "club" night, but I'd be happy to come back for another art show!

I was able to check out this Rotolo's as soon as it opened.  Having been a fan of Rotolo's for years, I was excited to see that one was opening so close to where I live.  I got my usual: a medium pepperoni pizza with extra cheese, and of course it was fantastic.  It was big enough to split with my friend and we were both satisfied.  My friend also decided to try a bowl of their tomato basil soup.  While I was unable to try it, my friend told me that it was really good, so I will be sure to get it the next time I go back.

Well, no one likes having to bring their car to the shop and the dealership can be an extra pain because they always seem to take a little longer.  I had to bring my car in because GMC had a recall so I had to get my key worked on. It's a whole thing. Anyway, I dropped the car off in the morning and they told me it would be a few hours. About an hour after the drop off, I got a call from the dealership. It seems they went nosing around under my hood and found that my belt and brake pads needed to be replaced. Well, how dare they go looking for trouble in some odd effort to keep me safe!  Anyway, they quoted a price and after giving the "go ahead" they told me my car would be ready after lunch. Then the craziest thing happened: my car was ready after lunch! They actually stuck to their word and got the job done in a timely manner. Car issues can be stressful, so it's nice that Don Bohn made the experience as painless and fast as possible.

This gorgeous shop is any glamour girls dream!  What caught my eye and got me into this shop were the lovely tiaras in the window. Honestly, I really want one, but I sometimes wonder if that's a level of "the most" that I'm not ready to approach just yet. Walking in, there are all kinds of high end sparklies that any woman would love. This is really high end costume jewelry, not the cheapo stuff that you might find at the mall (not that I have any issue with the cheapo stuff).  They have an entire table full of different rhinestone tiaras and another table full of rhinestone masks. If you're looking for something for a ball or a costume party, this is definitely the place. They even have a case full of rhinestone crowns, if you are really feeling regal and want to add some fancy head gear to your collection.  The shop owner was very sweet and asked if I needed help and informed me of the items that were for sale. I didn't purchase anything this time, but I do really want a fancy tiara, so I will eventually be back.

Today I popped in here for the first time since my last review, which was 4 years ago, so I figured it was time for an update.  We got there and the woman working the front was so nice and friendly. She immediately asked us if we wanted to sit at her favorite spot in the restaurant. We said "sure", and she lead us to a nice and cozy corner booth. It was delightful.  We weren't super hungry, so we got the vegetarian special and a rainbow roll. The vegetarian special comes with three vegetarian rolls, one of which is an avocado roll, so I was a happy camper. The rainbow roll was super good and between the veg special and the rainbow roll we had more than enough for lunch.  The waiter was very attentive and friendly throughout  the entire meal and all in all we had a perfect lunch.

I love little coffee shops like this one. This is one of those little New Orleans coffee shops that really makes the space their own by adding art and different posters to the walls. It makes the place a little bit more unique and cozy and creates a good vibe.  I stopped in here for my usual iced coffee to go. The barista was super friendly and helpful and the coffee was tasty with a lot of flavor. There are table and chairs so that you can sit and do work or just waste time. Ask the barista for the wifi password- it changes daily.

This is a super convenient Rouses right off of Poydras.  If you live in the area, and want to stock up for goods for a Saints game, it's the "go to" spot.  There is always plenty of parking and it's never overly packed with people, so you can check out pretty fast.  Just like any other Rouses there is a huge selection of goods and hard to find items.

Whoa. I finally remembered to check into this Walgreens, even though I go here all the time (seriously. I'm here at least once a week!).   This is my favorite Walgreens in my area. They seem to always have exactly what I'm looking for. The usual stuff I get here is makeup or something along those lines. They always have a nice selection of "holiday" oriented items. When I went yesterday, they had a whole aisle full of cool Valentine's Day goodies! They also have a neat little "gift" aisle full of toys for kids. I'm always pretty satisfied with what I find here.

This shop has some gorgeous jewelry. It makes me wish I had money to burn on diamond fleur de lis pendants.  This is a small shop, but it packs a lot in. Beautiful diamonds glisten in the lights and you imagine yourself being draped in luxury while attending some fancy event at someplace interesting. They have a good deal of New Orleans themed jewelry- gators and fleur de lis in every fashion, but they also have a nice selection of vintage jewelry and charms. I loved the selection of antique charms for charm bracelets, and they had so many that I'm tempted to start my own charm collection.  The owner of the shop was very nice and offered to take anything out of a case, so that we might have a closer look. For the average shopper, many of the items here will be out of price range, but they have a few items that you might like for a special occasion.

Woo hoo! Another great Magazine St. find!  I loved this store as soon as I walked in. First of all, I knew I was in a good place because when I walked in and looked to my right, I saw a "$30" rack and a "$40" rack. Now you know me, I am a fashionista on a budget. You don't have to spend a lot to look good. They have so many cute things here for great prices. The owner told me that she likes to keep most things between $20 and $60 dollars. You can't beat that and that makes this the perfect place to pick up a cute dress for a party or just hanging around town.  What's best about this place is that if you "like" them on facebook you can stay up to date with everything they have in the store because the owner posts pictures of clothes as they come in. Amazing!

I thought I had seen every type of Ulta there is, but this is a super fancy Ulta with a salon in the store! Oooh fancy!  I have mentioned in past Ulta reviews how much I love this store because some of the things they sell are better priced than what you would find at a drug store and everything is neatly organized by brand. On this particular day, I was in the market for a curling iron and I knew that Ulta would have a large selection, so that I could find what I needed. I ended up getting the perfect 1 1/2 inch barrel curler that I was looking for for a little under $40.  While this Ulta isn't necessarily worth going out of my way, it's great for beauty needs if you are in the area.

There's really not much you can say about a Metairie dive bar. I guess I'm spoiled since the NOLA smoking ban but yeah, this place is pretty smoky. I didn't have any of the food but one thing I can report is that they have Lagunitas IPA on tap, so that made me happy. On the night I was here, the crowd was pretty mellow and service was prompt. I wouldn't go out of my way to come here, but it's a decent choice if you're in the area.

Accessories is really the name of the game here. I was hopping down Maple Street when I came across this cute boutique. They have really cute clothes, but the jewelry and sunglasses were out of this world! With the help of the awesome employees, I was able to find the perfect gift for a friend- a pair of mirrored sunglasses that are both stylish and useful. The clothes here are light and perfect for the impending warmer weather and they come in lots of bright colors. Prices are a little steep, but the sunglasses I found were reasonable and seemed worth the money.

Good not great. "A-OK pretty much sums it up.  Stopped in here for lunch around 1 pm. The place wasn't packed at all. We got our menus, decided what we wanted pretty quickly and then waited. And waited. And waited. About 35 minutes later our food finally came out. Now, before you go thinking that I must have ordered something complicated, let me break it down. I ordered a croissant club sandwich with a side salad and my lunch companion ordered a wrap with fries. Nothing about either one of those things takes 35 minutes.  After the wait, the food wasn't too bad. I ate half of my sandwich and took the other half to go. My side salad was basically lettuce and cheese, but that's not too bad I guess.  I would probably go back if I wasn't in any type of hurry, but if I had to be somewhere by a certain time I would probably choose another lunch spot.

I've parked in this lot a bunch and I've never had an issue. One of the better priced lots in the area at 3 hours for $11. The attendant is always around and easily accessible, if you need help with something. I dealt with a malfunctioning machine once and the attendant was quick to help me. Keep an eye on your time because the meter maid ticket people come around every ten minutes.

After years of lamenting that the only decent coffee place on the Westbank is PJ's and after quite a few people told me about J'aime Le Cafe', I finally decided to give this place a shot.  Whoa. Okay, I don't know what they put in their coffee but I think that I'm already addicted. I got the 16oz iced latte and I seriously drank it so quickly that I wanted to turn around and go back and grab another one. It was packed with flavor, super tasty and just perfect for the warm day.  I do love that J'aime Le Cafe' has a drive thru and, even though there were a couple of cars in front of me, the line moved quickly. I will absolutely return.

FINALLY!  After years of hearing about how fantastic Yo Mama's food is, I got to check it out for myself!    I was super hungry when I checked out what Yo Mama's had to offer.  I kept it simple and ordered the "Yo Mama" burger with a side salad (yes, a salad.  Shutty!).  It was incredible and I finished it in about ten minutes.  It was easily one of the best burgers I have had in the city.    My only complaint was that I ordered it medium and it was cooked medium well.  That's not a huge thing.  I still ate it and it was still good.  Also, be prepared, this place tends to get really packed and you may be waiting about 30 minutes for food, but that's a small price to pay for such a good burger.  I want to go back and try their famed "peanut butter" burger.  I just wanted to try something basic my first time in there.

Home decor galore!  This would be the first place I would stop if I had one of those trendy Garden District shotguns and I had the money to decorate it however I wanted. All of the items here seem to be vintage inspired, and that's right up my alley. I love the bright colors and I love that the first room you see when you walk in is decorated to look like a cozy living room- it really gives you an idea of what YOUR space could look like.  My favorites were the gorgeous antique chairs that were finished with beautiful pops of color. They also have smaller items, just in case you don't have the nerve to pull the trigger on a large piece of furniture. The woman working was very friendly and I liked that there was a lot packed into the space.

My favorite Metairie sushi place!  I love to sit at the sushi bar and chat with the personable staff.  I usually get sashimi and a few rolls.  Kind of small, but I like the cozy atmosphere.  My favorite thing about this place is that it's open late on the weekends (12:30), so if you find yourself in Metairie late, for some reason, there is another option other than just fast food.

Since it has been nearly 6 whole years since I last reviewed this LC, I figured it was time for a re-review.  I still stand by the fact that the pizza here is "decent". We stopped in the other night and got one of the $5 pepperoni hot 'n ready pizzas. First of all, I'm pretty impressed that after 6 years, the price is still $5. Second of all, the pizza was really good and satisfied my pepperoni pizza craving perfectly. I also have to add that while $5 pizza is still not as good as Rotolo's, it is better than Papa John's, in my opinion. This isn't the place to say it, but I gave up on PJ's a long time ago, because quality has just gone down hill. I blame Peyton Manning.  Anyway, if you have a pepperoni pizza craving, this place will nip it in the bud.

Coyote Ugly is not only a downtown bar, it's a chain bar and that might be the worst of the worst.  Look, I get it, a place like this isn't interested in appealing to the local crowd. They are just hoping to attract enough tourist foot traffic to keep the doors open. I totally get it. The people who work here are super nice and welcoming. If you think your experience here is going to be anything like the movie that shares it's name, you are going to be sorely disappointed.  Not once did anyone say to me, "Hell no, H2O!" Pfft!

Ugh.  Is there anything appealing about the Gold Mine once you leave the cloud of college?    First of all, why is there a cover?  Why are they charging 3 bucks to go into a bar that is a smidge larger than a one bedroom apartment, hot as I don't know what, in the summer and has an actual line to get their signature drink...a flaming dr. pepper, is it?  Uhh...yeah.  I can't remember the last time I set foot in this joint, but what I always tell people is that it's not that type of place you set out to go to, it's the kind of place at which you just end up, for whatever reason.  If you are in college or out at 2 am in the quarter, go for it.  Otherwise, just cut your losses and call it a night.  This is a rare "unlisted" review.  It doesn't even deserve one of my cool lists!!

Maïs Arepas was so amazing! Possibly the perfect lunch spot.  I had actually never had an arepas before. It's basically a sandwich on a type of flat bread. I had the cerda with plantain chips which was basically a pork sandwich with freshly cooked plantains on it. It was delicious! It was packed with flavor and made for a fantastic sandwich.  Maïs Arepas also has a "juice of the day". I decided to try the strawberry limeade which was out of this world and super fresh and full of flavor.  I like the atmosphere here and it seems like this would be a really good place for groups. I can't wait to go back!

I've been putting off reviewing TJ's for a long time now. Too long, I suppose. I guess my whole issue is; I never know what to rate this place. I could give it 5 stars for what it is: a divey college bar with drinks that are pretty cheap. Or I could give it 1 star because of some of the people who tend to hang out here and the "vibe" you get when you walk in.  Finally, I decided to give it a middle of the road 3 stars. TJ's (it won't be called The Annex for much longer) is a cool place that recently went under a much needed renovation. A lot of people think it lost something, but those are probably the people living in the past. It still has a pool table and it's the same as it used to be, just a bit cleaner. The staff is always really nice and the crowd is young, but not terrible.  This isn't a place that I would go out of my way to visit, unless there is something drawing me here, but it is not yet on my "avoid at all costs" list.

Stopped in with a coworker friend of mine to look around for a birthday gift for her son. This comics shop is pretty expansive with books and toys galore. On the day that we were here, my friend was looking for something specific, and although they didn't have what she was looking for in store, they offered to order it for her.  Of course, they have some rare books that you can buy as well as some collectors items. I'm not really into comic books, but the woman working was super friendly and helpful and showed me around a bit and gave me an idea of what they have. I want to go back and bring David because he loves comic books and I know that he'd appreciate this spot.

This is the perfect shop for the fashionista in you, especially if you're looking for a dress or outfit for a special occasion.   This shop has cute little party dresses that sparkle and shine and fancier long gowns, if you need something for a wedding or party. The long gowns that they have here are out-of-this-world and look like they belong on a red carpet somewhere. They seriously look like couture designer gowns. The staff is extremely helpful and, as I looked around, I didn't feel pressured at all to purchase anything- they just let me look and ask questions, if necessary.  I didn't purchase anything on this trip, but I will definitely be back at the end of the year, and hopefully I will have an excuse (or a fancy New Year's Eve party) to wear one of these beautiful dresses.

It seems that everywhere I go, I see some work by Simon. These are nifty art pieces and signs with cute little sayings on them with a New Orleans twist. I actually stumbled into this place on accident one day after stopping into District Donuts. I had no idea that Simon even had a studio! Something else I didn't know- you can actually commission a custom piece! If you are looking for a unique "New Orleans" style gift or even if you just want something artsy to hang over your front door, this is the place for you.  Simon definitely adds a little something to the culture and magic of New Orleans.

This is a pretty good Goodwill that is packed with everything you can imagine. It's organized pretty well, by size and style of clothing. A lot of what they have here is out of date- very out of date, but I guess that's to be expected because they have a lot of things for sale. Aisles are narrow and can be hard to navigate when it's busy.  You are going to find things for really cheap here ($1 and $2 t shirts), but it's not as good of quality as you will find at other thrift stores. Much of what they have here has been well worn.
This is a really great and generous parade.  It's a great precursor to Bacchus and really gets the crowd going.  The riders seemed to be having a good time and made the experience fun for everyone.

Fantastic!  This place is amazing! Not only do they have comic books and graphic novels (I stopped in to see what they had to offer- Walking Dead wise) but they have tons of comic book related action figures, toys and gifts. The store is set up in such a way that everything is extremely easy to find. The staff was friendly and asked immediately upon my arrival if I needed help with anything.  Whatever you are in the mood for, you are bound to find it here. I will definitely return.

I don't know what it is about this PJs.  Whenever I'm in mid city (which is pretty rare these days) I usually find myself here and I am usually left disappointed.  It seems as if they are consistently out of 2% and whole milk (shouldn't whole milk be a staple in a coffee shop?  Kinda like...cups?) and they only offer half and half or soy milk, instead.  Soy milk?  In iced coffee?  Yeah, I'll take your word for it.  I get the half and half, and it usually dilutes the whole flavor of the coffee, even if I just get a little.  I do like the croissants, as they are usually pretty fresh, but compared to other PJs, the iced coffee here just isn't to my liking.

When it comes to Drago's, I really feel that it's one of those Oyster places you check out for the ambiance and the experience.  Honestly, you can get oysters a lot of places and they are probably just as good, but there is something about Drago's. It's one of those places where you dress a little nicer and have a nice night out downtown.  Their charbroiled oysters are fantastic and they aren't super expensive, considering you are in downtown New Orleans. They have a lot of other good seafood, too but I think that I've only ever had the oysters when I have been.

Gorgeous! A visit to the Lakefront Airport is like stepping back in time- I only wish I had been wearing my favorite vintage dress on the day I visited.  My dad and I had lunch at Messina's, so we decided to walk around after looking at all of the renovations at the airport. If you walk up the stone stairs, you get to see the murals that are being restored. They look so perfect that it's hard to believe that they were painted so many years ago. The Walnut Room is huge, if you are looking for a place to hold an elegant reception and there is even a flight school here. Here's a secret: I have always wanted to learn to fly, but I've never had the guts to look into lessons. Now that I know that there is a flight school at this airport, I might just have to give it some real thought.  Be sure to look down at the floor to see how many miles away from New Orleans different cities are (this will make more sense when you see it in person). The Lakefront Airport is a must visit for everyone.

If you read my review for the Westbank Panera location, than you already know that I'm a Panera fan.  I met a friend here for lunch and I was impressed- the employees were getting people quickly through the line on a busy Saturday and we were taken care of immediately. I ordered the half and half with a half of a roasted turkey and avocado sandwich and a cup of the broccoli cheddar soup (my favorite). They scanned my Panera card, I went into the dining room with my buzzer and after a minimal wait my food was ready  The roasted turkey and avocado sandwich was great! I had never had it before and I was happy to see that the turkey was freshly sliced and the avocado was perfect and ripe. Of course, the broccoli and cheddar soup was perfect as always and came with bread on the side, in case you want to dip.  As far as I can tell, this Panera doesn't have a drive thru like the Westbank location does, so if you are in a hurry you might want to call and order ahead for pick up.

Woo hoo! A Bud's Broiler on the Westbank!  What's not to love about Bud's? Flame broiled burgers that are cooked to order with thick layers of cheese and onions. Sure, they serve chicken sandwiches too, but you have to go for the classic when you are eating here.  This Bud's is pretty much like all the rest of them. I think if you have been in one of these places, you have been in all of them.

Bro, in the year of our Lord 2019, there is ZERO reason to allow smoking in a place that serves food. That's just gross.  We were here to see a band on a Saturday night and naturally the place was packed. They have a kitchen area, a stage area and a decent tap list. They also allow smoking. Not only do they allow smoking but the place reeks of cigarette smoke. I think everyone was smoking when we were here- even the bartender was smoking while she was working. Good Lord. That's not even the craziest part. The craziest part is the cigarette machine at the door, so you can buy cigarettes to smoke! It was insane.  We were here maybe 45 minutes and left stinking of smoke, so I doubt I'll be back. Jefferson Parish smoking ban soon come.

What's that smell? Oh, it's Kirkland's.  Okay, so as others have mentioned there is a very STRONG scent of candles and perfumes in this place. I won't lie- I liked it for the first few minutes. Then I hated it. Then I didn't notice it.  Aside from the smell, Kirkland's is pretty awesome! I don't even think I have set foot in a Kirkland's since there was one at Oakwood mall in the pre-Katrina days. This store is packed with all kinds of decor for the home from lamps to wall hangs and really cool stuff for the kitchen. They had these really cute measuring cups (see my photo) with cupcakes on the handle! That stuff is right up my alley and in my wheelhouse.  Fair warning: being in this place will make you want to redecorate asap. I want a portrait of a French cafe on MY wall, is all I'm going to say. I found a really cute hand painted tea cup that is large enough for a lot of green tea for about $7, so I was more than happy to pick that up.  I liked it here and I'll be back.

The few times I've been here, I've been left wondering how the place really stays in business. I mean, it's not a bad place, but there is never really anyone in here. The staff is nice enough and there are always one or two "regulars" at the bar, but you would expect more on a Friday or Saturday night.  While I wouldn't go out of my way to visit this place, it's not bad if you are looking for a quiet place to have a beer and hang out.

From start to finish, saffron was a class act. I stopped in here on a Friday night on a work venture. I didn't have reservations, so the hostess kindly asked me if I would be okay it's sitting at the bar and I was more than okay with that. I sat at the bar and the bartender was friendly and jovial. He gave me my menu and I looked it over with the light. I started with the gumbo and I had the pork vindaloo, as my entree.  I also treated myself to some coffee and dessert. All of the food and service was out of this world. I had such a wonderful time, that I actually wished that I lived in the neighborhood so that this restaurant would be within walking distance.   I had always wanted to visit saffron when it was in Gretna, but I never had the opportunity. Everything here was picture perfect and I couldn't have been happier. I will definitely return. This is perfect for a date night or just the night out with friends.  I made a guide to Indian food! Check it out here https://nola.verylocal.com/heres-your-guide-to-indian-food-in-new-orleans/188741/

We stopped in here after another New Year's Eve party was kind of dull and we were happy to find a good crowd, a good beer selection and generous seating.  This is more a sports bar than an Irish pub, but the folks are really friendly and they have some of my favorite beers on tap, so I was happy. There are plenty of tvs, so it would be a good place to watch a game and the drinks are reasonably priced, considering the location. The bartender was nice and the place is pretty clean.

If you're in the mood for soul food this is the PLACE!  Look, I had already heard about the long lines at Chicken's, so I stopped in as soon as they opened on a Monday. You know I had to hook it up with some red beans and rice and fried chicken.  The food here is served hot, fresh off the line. They have daily specials, so be sure to check the website to see what is being offered. The red beans and rice I had was perfect and the fried chicken was juicy and packed with flavor.  The staff here was super friendly and helped me figure out exactly what I wanted. Even though I was here early, the crowd was starting to build as I ate, so if you're on a time restriction, get here early!

This is a review of the bar area.  While I have yet to experience the food here, I have been through for a Bloody Mary quite a few times, and I have to say that they make one of the best I have ever had. This place has a nice casual local vibe and I think most of the people who stop in here are locals. Staff is friendly and they pour generously.

Delicious pastries and Mojo coffee on the westbank! Yes, please. The owner of this spot makes all of her pastries by hand such as croissants, cheesecake, and scones. Not to mention mojo coffee, which is one of my favorites. I'm so excited to have it right down the street.  The cafe itself is super cozy and welcoming, and the prices are really good, especially considering everything is handmade. I'm really excited that we have another coffee and pastry option here on the West Bank, that isn't Starbucks or PJ's.  I wrote about this spot for Big Easy Magazine. Read all about it here: https://www.bigeasymagazine.com/2021/05/02/local-pastry-chef-serves-up-delicious-treats-at-newly-opened-le-cafe-eblouir-coffee-pastry-boutique/

I completely fell in love with this whimsical little gallery.  The art here looks like something you would find in a child's bedroom, but it has that grown-up feel that let's you know that there's no shame in enjoying the art here, no matter your age. Whimsical fairy tale characters, New Orleans and Mardi Gras themed art and painting of animals of all types is what you'll see here.   They have small prints which are extremely affordable and really, the only reason I didn't buy something when I was here was because I couldn't decide exactly what I wanted. I know what I do want: a print of the kittens in the king cake, for obvious reasons.  The artist is very talented and I love the "carefree" feel of her work.

It's pretty surprising that I had never been here, since I have lived on the Westbank my entire life.  I think I may have gone one other time when I was a kid, but I remembered nothing about the place.  A friend and I had lunch here, and after I figured out exactly how to get to the place (it's located at the edge of Narnia), I went in and enjoyed a really good meal.  I got the catfish and white beans, which was the lunch special and one of my favorites.  It was amazing and so good!  It was a generous serving and cooked perfectly.  The atmosphere of this place is really nice and I could see myself going here on a dinner date.  It has an "upscale" feel. but I didn't feel underdressed in my jeans and sweater.  I definitely want to go back and try some other things on the menu.

I'm going to just lay it on the line: the bar is cool, but the drinks are overpriced. Way overpriced. $8 for a beer you can get for $5 elsewhere overpriced. Look, I'm not a dope. It's the Quarter. You're gonna charge what dumb tourists are gonna pay. Can I show you my Louisiana ID and get a discount? Even if it's just a buck off? Seriously, we are on the same team here. We're all friends. $15 for two beers is a little much. It's water and barley...don't get arrogant.  Other than that, this place is cool. Cool people and cool staff. Just don't rob me.

Well, I didn't even know this lake had a name, much less that it was reviewable.  This is a beautiful spot located right by the New Orleans Museum of Art at City Park. It's a spot where people come to relax and take in the scenery or paddle around on a kayak. I most recently found myself here when I came to check out the tulips, which are planted annually next to the lake. You can sit on the side and enjoy and a nice day and watch people boat around in the water and watch the ducks waddle back and forth.

We got some catering from this place and it was delicious!  We ordered big trays of pasta, jambalaya, salad, finger sandwiches and brownies. I personally tried the pasta, salad and finger sandwiches. The pasta was penne pasta that was nice and cheesy and had tons of flavor. My favorite was definitely the salad because it was packed with goodies- it had spinach, avocado, walnuts, feta, dried cranberries and it was topped with a yummy vinaigrette. It was one of the best salads I have ever had and it made me want to go to Cafe Royale and have more. The finger sandwiches were pretty good, but didn't really blow me away and I've had better elsewhere.  If you need something catered, I would chose Cafe Royale because I was more than pleased with the food.

This CVS earns bonus points because it was open on Christmas! I think they are all open on Christmas, but this was is convenient for me, because it's near me.  This CVS is WAY better organized than other ones that I have been to and everything is really easy to find. The staff was super friendly, even though they were working on Christmas and I was able to get in, find what I needed and get out in a timely manner.

I was so glad that I found myself in the neighborhood since I had heard that this is one of the better Ideal Markets.  This is a small market, but they have the good stuff- namely sweet breads made fresh. After looking around, I got a sweet bread (it had a fancy name in Spanish, but I forgot to make a note of it) and it was delightful! I could tell that it was made in store and I enjoyed it later that evening.  If you're in the mood for something hot, they have a hot bar where they are serving up delicious looking authentic food, that must be good because there was a pretty sizable line for it. The staff is always working to keep everything fresh, and when I was here they were adding fresh pastries to the pasty case, so you can bet that no matter what time you get here you're sure to enjoy something that is tasty and fresh.  Like any convenience store, they have basic groceries and a nice selection of cheeses, fruits and other produce so you should be able to find whatever you might be looking for as far as that goes.

This Taco Bell is pretty good. I just wish that it was closer to my house.  Taco Bell is pretty much the only fast food I eat, since I eat fast food so rarely. I stopped in here and I was happy that the line was not only short, but it moved quickly. I ordered a nacho supreme, which is my "usual" and is basically chips with cheese sauce, meat, and sour cream. I have found that some Taco Bells kind of haphazardly throw all of the ingredients together and call it a day. Not only did this Taco Bell actually make the nachos correctly, but they were generous with the "fixings". Hey, I know it sounds silly, but it's a Taco Bell review, so that's what you get.  In conclusion: pretty much as good as you can expect from a Taco Bell. Oh, and when I ask for "a lot" of sauce packets, they actually give me a lot of sauce packets.

While ice cream will always have a place in my heart, there's just something special about gelato- ice cream's lighter cousin.  David and I were having a dessert craving, and this place had been on my list for a while, so we popped in. It was pretty busy for after 8 on a Saturday night, but we were served quickly. I had the raspberry gelato and it was delicious with lots of flavor and the lightness that I expect from gelato. If it hadn't been so late, I probably would have tried some of the coffee, so that's a good excuse to go back.  Aside from gelato, they have a great selection of sweet and savory crepes and with plenty of seating inside and outside, it's the perfect place for a bite to eat any time of day.

This Ulta is okay, but it's not the best one in the area.   The staff has always been really friendly. My complaint about this store is that it's pretty small compared to other Ultas I've been to and there is a limited selection of products. The samples that they have for people to swatch the more high end products are DISGUSTING and look old and like kids (or messy adults) have slammed their fingers into them. I would never put my hands anywhere near that stuff. Also, they should have tissue next to the samples so that if I do decide to swatch it on my hand, I can wipe it off when I'm done.  I do like that they have a pretty extensive designer perfume selection, as well as a wide variety of hair products. I go to this Ulta pretty regularly out of necessity, but it's not worth an extra trip.

I could have sworn that I had reviewed Wit's Inn, but here we are. Anyway, I love this place! Not only is it a fantastic place to watch a Saints game, but they make delicious bloody Marys and have fantastic pizza.  The crowd is more of a neighborhood krewe, but I have always found people here super friendly and fun. Whenever I go I usually sit at the bar, but they have plenty of tables and chairs if that isn't your thing. The crowd gets rowdy during Saints games, so come with your game face on.

I had never had Pho before (believe it or not), when my b/f decided that we had to go here for lunch.  I was hesitant at first and it was all really different, but I was in for a treat.  The serving of the noodles and broth was HUGE and delicious.  I wasn't feeling too adventurous, so I just got the kind with beef in it.  It all sounded so good that I know I will be back.

Wanted to update my review, adding a star.  When I first came here, I had never had Pho before. Now that I consider myself pretty seasoned on the stuff, I have come to appreciate how fantastic Tan Dinh's Pho is. I got the Pho Tai Nam, which is rare flank and brisket and an order of pork Spring rolls. It was all amazing. The broth had a ton of flavor and I love that you get a HUGE serving of it. The rolls were delicious as well.

I just discovered this place by chance and apparently it's only been open a month or two. Unless you're familiar with the area, you're going to have trouble finding Pho 99. Pro tip: it's in the strip mall near Auto Zone.  I was in the mood for something quick and cheap, so I stopped in here for lunch. They have a really extensive menu of all of the Vietnamese faves, but as always, I was in the mood for Pho. I got the large #10 with rare steak and brisket. The portion was HUGE and I was hoping that it was all as good as it looked. Lucky me, it was delicious. The meat was perfect and the broth was full of flavor without being overpowering. I'll admit that I don't have most sophisticated palate when it comes to Pho, but I know when a bowl is bland and this one definitely wasn't.  Take it from someone who actually ate here- this is a good bowl and if you're in the mood for Pho you won't be disappointed. I'll be back!

Rue is one of my favorite places for coffee, and since the one on Magazine is now closed (boo) this is the one you gotta go to.  I'll be honest, I'm not the biggest fan of this location.  Oak in general tends to be kind of a mess, and I'm the type who doesn't like to drive around looking for a place to park.  Enough with the complaints!  I love the coffee here.  This place has huge windows and has a great light, and the cool thing about this Rue is the fact that it has an upstairs, so if you have to study and get away from the crowd, you can sneak up there and get some work done.  I'll probably re-review after I visit a few times and let the shop grow on me.

I don't get to Old Point very often.  Although it's conveniently located on the Westbank, it's just a place I find myself in very often.  When I do find myself here, it's a really cool experience.   Unless you live in the area, there's no real reason to go here, unless there is a band playing.  The venue is small, but they have bands playing here regularly and it's a cool place to have a drink and check out some local favorites.  I've never been here for a Saints game, but they have tvs, so I assume it's a good place to check one out.  I'll have to swing by next football season.  Fun fact: Scenes from the movie "Ray" were filmed here.  Wifi password: 1234567890

Let me start by saying that I am not a huge BBQ expert, so take this review for what it's worth.  While this place does have the moniker of "saloon", it is pretty big and spacious and has plenty of tables and chairs for dining. I stopped in here with a friend for lunch not really knowing what to expect. Looking over the menu, it seemed like typical faire. I had a pulled pork sandwich with potato salad. It was good, but it was lacking a good amount of sauce and I found it somewhat dry.  I didn't try any of the beer or spirits whilst I was here, so I can't comment on that, but they seemed to have a good number of local beers on tap.

This is a really nice bar with super friendly people.  We stopped in here after hanging out at Mimi's for a while. The bartender couldn't have been friendlier and the patrons were happy to chat. It's obviously a neighborhood bar full of regulars, but everyone was nice and inclusive.  The atmosphere is pretty dark and murky- it seems like a good place to go if you want to get lost for a few hours.

I have had the opportunity to go to the Ogden a lot lately.  We have seen films and exhibits here and it was fabulous on White Linen Night in August.  A great place to check out on a Sunday afternoon when you want to look at lovely art and just "get away" for a bit.  There is always something going on and memberships aren't expensive at all.  Go go go!

It's definitely time for a re-review, especially because the store has moved since my last review.  Retro Active is a great shop and I love the place on Oak. It's SO much bigger than the place on Magazine was and everything is setup perfectly. Here you will find a lovely collection of everything from vintage hats to bags to dresses to jewelry and even some men's pieces (which are located upstairs).  If you aren't really familiar with vintage clothing or if you aren't sure what you are looking for or what will look good on you, Leslie will be happy to help. She owns the store and is an EXPERT in all things vintage. You can seriously show her anything from any era and she will be able to tell you all about it. That's exactly what you want when you are vintage shopping.  All of the items are super reasonably priced and this isn't one of those stores where everything will be out of your price range. While you will find more expensive items here, you are sure to find some gorgeous affordable pieces as well. All items are fairly priced and in good, clean condition.

Ross!  I went into the store today to check on your progress since my last review!  I was shocked to discover that you have actually learned something!  I walked in, and I immediately noticed that the clothing was more organized on the racks, there were no messes or clothes on the floor and things were grouped together by size!  The second thing I noticed was 4 (count 'em) FOUR registers were open, as opposed to the previous count of one total open register!  There was still a line, but it moved quickly and there wasn't a long wait to check out.  It was fantastic!  I rewarded your efforts today, by not only purchasing a dress (I was able to find it easily, because the racks were organized by size and the fast moving line gave me no excuse to not get it), but by coming on here and boosting you up a star.  Why not a boost of 2 stars?  I want to make sure that this isn't a fluke, Ross.  Don't get lazy as the summer goes on.  Keep up the good work and that fourth star will be yours, and I will visit your place more often.

Kinda mediocre.  I usually find myself here when I am heading somewhere else on Magazine and I get hungry.  The margaritas aren't bad, but the food is nothing great.  One plus is that you can sit outside on nice days.

It feels weird to review a "chain" bookstore in New Orleans, when there are so many awesome "homegrown" bookstores in the city, but this is the one I go to, so there it is.  I find myself in B&N at least once or twice a month.  They are always having fantastic sales and the staff has always been incredibly friendly and eager to help me find anything I may be looking for.  I like that they have a lot of art books (and some really obscure ones) and they have a huge section dedicated to books by local authors and about the city.   I would love for a local bookstore to pop up in my neck of the woods, but until that happens, I am happy to call this place a favorite.
Got a couple of po boys here a few weeks ago.  Really good, and the oyster po boy is as expensive as you would expect.  ;) I'd go back.

This is a delightful spot right in the middle of the avenue. They have pastries, fruits, smoothies, coffee drinks, tea and the like.  On the night I stopped in, it was kind of late and I was craving some carrot and beet juice (who doesn't?!) and I was majorly bummed when the woman behind the counter told me that they had just begun breaking down the juice machine. Really made me blue, especially since they were an hour from closing. I decided to get an iced green tea. It was okay, and I really have no complaints. It didn't knock my socks off, but it's tea.  I like the atmosphere here. A lot of tables and chairs for people to study (many were) and a lot of space to spread out. There's a nice seating area by the window, so you can look out onto the avenue as you enjoy your breakfast, lunch or coffee.  I definitely want to return and actually try their fruit juice. I'll be happy to re-review upon a future visit.

I don't know.  On a scale of "Sucky" to "Awesome", I think that I would rate this place a solid "Meh".  First, let me start by saying that I'm not a HUGE fan of Greek food and gyros, so if you are, you may be a better judge then me.  This place pegs itself as a coffee shop that also serves food.  I went and I got some pita and hummus as an app and a chicken gyro as my dinner.  It was ok.  Nothing special.  The hummus wasn't bad, but it's hard to screw that stuff up.  I would try it again, only because I like to try a place twice before I declare that I hate it.  Decent enough if you are on the Westbank and want a gyro.  If you have the time, just head over to Byblos.

Whenever I have sushi on the Westbank, I go to Tennou.  I know what I like, and that's it.  So when some friends suggested that we try Sakura, I was skeptical.  First of all, I walked in, and the place smelled like fish.  Now, yes, I know they serve fish, but is a place supposed to reek of it?  We got regular sushi (not the Hibachi) and I wasn't impressed at all.  There wasn't anything overly terrible about it, it just didn't blow me away.  Best described: it was what it was.  I guess I would go back for the Hibachi, since I don't know of any other Hibachi places in the area, but if I just wanted regular sushi, I would head down the street to Tennou.

This is my favorite beauty supply store and I have been going here for years.  They sell the best of the best at low prices.  I was able to find my now "signature" red nail polish here, "Ruby Pumps" by China Glaze.  They also carry an excellent array of liquid eyeliners in various colors including black and even dark blue.  This is also the only place that I will buy bobby pins.  I have really thick hair, so the cheapo "Goody" brand can't stay in place.  They have heavy duty pins that stay put in my hair all day and night.  Their selection of hair care products is out of this world and it is where I discovered what I call my "magic wand", my Helen of Troy hot air brush, that gives my hair a pretty wave, without having to roll it.  Join the Sally Club for discounts and specials!

Wonderful flower shop with a wonderful owner. Pamela went out of her way to accommodate our needs over a difficult two weeks. She went in early and made special trips to complete our order and make sure that everything was perfect and delivered on time. Such a sweet woman and such a nice shop.

WOW. For such a small shop, this place sure does pack a lot into it.  I don't think I had ever even heard of this shop before I spotted it on Magazine St. the other day. They have so many cool things. Miss Claudia's carries a lot of vintage things from suits to gloves to costumes. Not only that but they have all kinds of different hats and wigs and shoes. I seriously wish that I hadn't been in a rush on the day I stopped in, because I really can see myself spending an hour or two here just going through everything that they have.  They have a perfect selection of sparkly things for Mardi Gras and I will definitely be going here the next time that I need stockings for a specific outfit or costume. Miss Claudia's had a ton of them!  I will definitely be back and I will be ready to spend more of my time here.

I recently was able to attend the Saints vs. Falcons game at the new Mercedes Benz Superdome.  I can't remember the last time I had been in the dome, but I had such an amazing time.  The dome has been beautifully redone and it's just a great venue.  They have everything here that a sports fan could want, as far as food an drinks go.  The people who work here are professional and helpful and go out of there way to make sure you have a good experience here.  If you have the opportunity to see a Saints game here, don't skip it.  It will be one of the best times you will ever have.

I really like this Mojo. I'm happy to see Freret St. expanding a little more all the time.  The atmosphere in here is cozy and the coffee is good.
