It's pretty much exactly like the Mojo on Magazine St. It was a little crowded on the day that I went, but I suppose that's probably because it's new. I just got an iced coffee to go, so I didn't stay long, but I can see how this could me a neat little place to study or do a little work.

I'm giving this Walgreens 5 stars because they actually saved me some money and they didn't have to.  I was in the area, so I stopped in because I had to pick up some nail polish and Walgreens is the only one that carries it. I got the name brand nail polish and the Walgreens brand clear coat. When I went to pay,  the beauty counter lady told me that the name brand nail polish was 2 for1. So, I was able to get the name brand clear polish instead of the Walgreens brand. Yeah, not a huge deal, but she didn't have to point it out to me.  Tip: don't park in the parking lot overnight. You will probably be towed.

I was in the mood for quick Chinese food and Wok to Go hit the spot.  I'm not overly picky when it comes to Chinese food: I really never expect it to be really great, all I expect is for it to taste somewhat like what I'm expecting. Wok to Go fit the bill. I stopped in and I got pork fried rice, an order of spring rolls and an order of dumplings. The pork fried rice was great with a lot of flavor and nice pieces of pork. The spring rolls were pretty good as well. They were veggie spring rolls and I enjoyed them. The dumplings were a deal for as many as I got for the price, but sadly they had a "plastic" after taste. I know that this stuff comes from a bag and isn't hand made, but two dumplings in and I was done.  I would probably go back and just get the fried rice- it was cooked to order and delicious.

What can I say about a place that hasn't been said in 353 reviews before this one?  Commander's is the best of the best.  It's where you want to go when you have a little extra money to spend and you want to not just have dinner, but have an EXPERIENCE.  Here the gourmet food is prepared by Chef's who were trained in their craft.  The waitstaff does this as a career, and isn't just a bunch of 20-somethings working their way through college.  This is a place where memories are made, laughs are had, and friends come together.  Engagements happen here.  Birthdays, graduations and promotions are celebrated here.  You are treated as if you are royalty, because from the time you walk into the door to the time you leave, that's exactly what you are, at this restaurant.  Sure, the place would be considered pricey by most standards but  you aren't just paying for the food.  You are paying for the privilege of dining here.

As promised, I am bumping Second Line up star because they now have working bathrooms and they are pouring into glass!  I stopped by on a Sunday afternoon, just to check the place out again and see if anything had changed since my last visit. Sure enough, they are now pouring their beers into glass and they have added a few more brews since my last visit. I loved the Chocolate Spice Stout that had just enough "kick" to it, without being too overwhelming. I also tried the Trans-Siberian Coconut which definitely had that coconut flavor. It almost reminded me of a "Mounds" bar.  There was a decent crowd for a Sunday and the bartenders were nice and helpful. I'm excited to come back and try more of their beer. I heard they are going to start bottling and canning after Mardi Gras, so that'll be a cool expansion for the company. I'll be eagerly awaiting what the future holds for this brewery.

Let me start by saying that I didn't do Fiorella's, probably the way it's supposed to be done.  In other words, I didn't get the fried chicken, or a main entree.  With that said, I ordered the chicken caesar salad and a side order of baked macaroni (mac and cheese).  It was good, not great.  The salad was huge, and was definitely big enough for a meal.  The lettuce was kind of mushy, but the chicken was tender and juicy.  The mac and cheese was ok.  It wasn't overly creamy or anything.  It was more mac and cheese with just a hint of cheese.  It wasn't terrible, but it wasn't the best, either.  The place is known for their famous fried chicken, so I would probably go back and give that a try.  The atmosphere was really nice, with kind of a "diner" feel.  The waitress couldn't have been sweeter, and was even nice enough to recommend some music acts that we should check out.

I'm going to start by saying that this is NOT the same as Buffalo Exchange.  While Buffalo Exchange has some high end stuff, Plato's closet is geared more towards teenagers and girls in their early 20's (20-22 or so).    A LOT of tshirts, short shorts and baby doll dresses.  I went in hoping to find a cheap pair of jeans just to hang around in for the summer.  If you were wondering what ever happened to low rise jeans, it turns out that every pair that was ever made, worn, and tossed aside, ended up here.    It's a good place if you have a teenager and want to pick up some tshirts or cute dresses.  If you have a more sophisticated taste, stick to Buffalo Exchange.

I love Sucre and I have been going since it opened.  When I go, I usually get the cookies and cream gelato, but the last time I went, I was talked into getting one of their small chocolate cake "treats" and it was amazing!  The small cakes tend to be a little on the expensive side, but it's good for a special occasion or a treat.

I am no fan of parking anywhere downtown. With that being said, this parking lot isn't too bad. You pay at a machine but be warned, the lot is really small. I was lucky to get a parking spot in the middle of the day when some friends and I decided to do some shopping. I managed to make it in and out the lot without my car sustaining any mystery dings, dents or scratches, so I consider the whole parking event a victory.

This Pho Bang is good. Really good. As much as I liked this one, I really miss the one on Manhattan, but I digress.  I went in and got my usual beef brisket and rare flank Pho. It was really good and had a lot of flavor. Honestly, if you read my review for the other Pho Bang, it was pretty much exactly like that. Oh! And I also really love their pork Spring rolls!  For whatever reason, this Pho Bang was really packed when I went in and it took a little while for me to be seated. That's not a huge deal, as I wasn't in any kind of major rush. I am hoping that the Pho Bang on Manhattan reopens soon (their sign says that they are TEMPORARILY closed),  but in the meantime this one will have to do.

While I'm sure that Glue would appeal to some people, it's just not one of the "nicer" vintage stores in the city.  A lot of the stuff in this store I wouldn't even consider vintage.  I mean, sure, I like a ratty looking AC/DC shirt as much as the next gal, but I doubt that I would rush out to buy one for 30 bucks and call it vintage.  The place is packed with what I guess some people would call "hipster" clothes (I HATE that term, btw.) but if you are looking for something a little fancier, you would probably be better off going next door to On the Other Hand.

I recently shot with a photographer from Texas who wanted to capture the "essence" of New Orleans, so of course he wanted to shoot at Cafe Du Monde.  Cafe Du Monde is more than cafe au lait and those beignets we all love so much, it's a New Orleans "must".  It's one of the first things people want to go when they are visiting the city and rightfully so.    When I go, I personally like to sit inside, but I know that most people prefer the experience of the patio.  The patio gets extremely packed, especially at night when tourists are walking around, but it is still worh the experience.  I think that one of my favorites is their frozen Cafe Au Lait.  I love it so much, I'll even go to the Cafe Du Monde located at the mall just to get my hands on it.  It's soo good.

While wandering around the area, we happened to stumble upon this quaint little bar.  It wasn't too late, but we were the only people in the place. That was fine by me- there were some extra credits on the jukebox so I requested a few songs and we sat and had a few drinks. The feel of the place is divey and laid back and the bartender was super nice and friendly. I'm normally not a fan of places with internet jukeboxes, but it worked well here, maybe because it was only my songs playing. Ha.  We weren't here long, but it was an enjoyable evening and I would come back for another visit.

Yay! I got to try another food truck.  I was STARVING when I ran into this truck outside of Rendezvous on Magazine. I'm always excited to try new things, so I walked up and looked over the menu. I decided to get the lechon (braised pork) in a white corn tortilla with chipotle crema and avocado. It didn't take long before my food was ready, even though there were a good number of people there.  I would say the food here is good if you have nothing to compare it to. I compared it to taceaux loceaux, which is my usual "go to" food truck for Mexican food. The pork had a lot of flavor, but the meal itself was missing something. I did enjoy it, and I would go back, but taceaux loceaux is still my first choice.

As good as other places in the city that serve gelato are, there is no topping Brocato's.  Brocato's is a classic Italian dessert place.  They serve gelato, Italian cookies, Cannolis, and more.  You can go in after a nice dinner and get a sweet treat with some coffee on the side.  I have never been in this place where it hasn't had a nice crowd.  This is a New Orleans institution and the people who go here are serious about it.  Really.  I've met people who have gone to this place their entire lives and are now bringing their grandchildren.  A definite New Orleans "don't miss".

Ugh.  What it has: A pool table that is used more for dancing on than actual pool. An upstairs that you probably didn't know about. A patio that you probably didn't know about (other than the name of the place). A hiding place under the stairs. Cheese fries that taste better after a long night. College kids  What it doesn't have: A clean bathroom A real reason for anyone over 25 to rightfully go here A sense of decor "Mr/Mrs Right" A proper dance floor  I would like to state, that in the last 5 years I have never gone here on my own volition. I have always been BROUGHT here.

I've decided to update this review because my view of the Old Point has changed considerably.  I was wrong when I said that unless you live in the area there is no reason to go here. There are a lot of reasons to go here, not the least of which is seeing a variety of different bands and enjoying the New Orleans atmosphere at a neighborhood bar just outside of New Orleans proper.  The staff is always friendly and the crowd is a bit older and respectful. My only complaint is the cigarette smoke. I don't know if it's a ventilation issue or what, but even if just one person is smoking in there, the entire place fills with smoke. I would love it if they went smoke free or installed some better smoke eaters.

Hmmm... why is Hubig's marked as closed? Down but not out, people! Hubig's is coming back!  If you grew up in New Orleans then you grew up on Hubig's. Those yummy little fried iced pies that you know are terrible for you but you didn't care because they were AMAZING.  When I was a kid, I remember enjoying mine at Kmart of all places. Trust me, I have no idea why I had them I Kmart. Maybe they were by the register? I don't know. Anyway, I think that my favorites are apple and lemon.  I know that non-locals will insist that Hubig's aren't as great as we make them out to be, but Adam Richman (host of Man vs. Food on Travel Channel) RAVED about them when he was down here, so there's that.

As far as Taco Bells go, this one is okay.  A few things you measure a fast food place on: speed of getting customers through, order "correctness" and quality of food. We stopped in here at around 10 on a Saturday, and of course there was a line. Despite this, the staff did get us through pretty quickly. It didn't feel like there were any major delays that could have been handled on their end. Once we ordered, the food order was right and it was pretty good. I'm glad we didn't have to deal with any of the issues that past reviewers had to deal with.   This isn't my "go to" Taco Bell, but it's just as good as any of the other ones I've been to.

I was really impressed with Los Panchos. I eat at my fair share of Mexican restaurants and Los Panchos was up there with some of the best.  I ordered a chicken burrito that came topped with cheese sauce. It was amazing and so good. It was really big and I took my leftovers home and got a second meal out of it. Also, it's worth noting that the free chips and salsa are also really good. The salsa here has flavor and a little bit of spice, which makes it delicious. I have found that other places have salsa that is really bland. I guess they are afraid to give you the spicy stuff, because not everyone likes it, but Los Panchos didn't hold back. They also have yummy Mexican coke with real sugar. It can't be beat!  I will definitely go back! Their food is good, the prices are reasonable and they have a ton of different dishes to try.

I love a really cute shop with well priced jewelry.  I just happened to find this place while I was out and about and it's wonderful! They have earrings, necklaces and other pieces of costume jewelry and most are priced around $20. They have a board in the back of items that are 75% off and I was able to get two pairs of cute earrings for $10 total! They also have other "girly" type accessories, that you or the lady in your life are sure to love.  This is a great place to pick up a stocking-stuffer for the holidays or treat yourself to a little something special.

Really nice PJ's, It almost feels like it belongs Uptown. It's really big with sofas and a few tables for sitting. I did however, find it a bit dark, There wasn't a lot of light coming in and the lights were kind of dim. That's awesome if you are looking for place with mood lighting, but if you are trying to get some work done it might be a bit difficult,  The coffee was typical PJ's coffee. I kind of wish this PJ's was closer to me because I really dig how big it is, even if it is a little dim in here.

We decided to get a drink here while we waited for our reservation at a place across the street.  This is a neat little bar that mainly attracts foot traffic off the street- I don't know if anyone really sets out to spend an evening here. I had a tap beer and my friend had a vodka and cranberry. My beer was good, but my friend's vodka and cran was pretty weak. The main focus here is "drunk food"- they are open late and serve pizza, burgers and the like, and I am sure that's how they get most of their business. The bar was pretty dead at 7 on a Saturday, but we enjoyed hanging out here and chatting while other patrons started their evening.

This seems to be one of those New Orleans staples that I had always wanted to try, but never had the opportunity.  A friend and I stopped in here one night for a bite to eat.  I had never been, but had always wondered about the place.  First of all, I was really impressed by the diverse menu.  Not only do they serve burgers and salad, but they serve breakfast food AND one of my faves, spinach artichoke dip!  We got an order of dip and I had two eggs over easy with bacon and hash browns (which were pretty much just sliced up potatoes).  The food was really good and the eggs were perfectly cooked.  The dip wasn't the best I had ever had, but it did the job and it was served with chips.  I would definitely go back here.  I am a huge fan of any place that serves breakfast food all day (IHOP, Waffle House), so it's always nice to know where to go, if I'm ever in the mood for that kind of thing.

This is a pretty good spot, if you are in the mood for some quick Mexican-ish food.  I came here for lunch at around 1 and it was pretty empty. After looking over the menu, I decided to get the burrito lunch special with pork. This is a pretty basic burrito packed with pork, rice, beans and cheese and a side of "fixins"- sour cream, guacamole, lettuce and tomato. The burrito was pretty good, but nothing earth shattering. It was somewhat bland, so I added some of the salsa from the complimentary chips and salsa and that added a little kick to it.  It's had to really judge a place on a simple lunch, so I will return and get a full dinner and re-review, if appropriate.

I was pretty disappointed in this stop on the Westbank snowball tour.  First of all, like Jess mentioned, they are really slow. You order at one window and they give you your snowball at another window. We only had two people ahead of us and there was still a bit of a wait to get our snowballs.  I got the pink bubblegum. There wasn't a lot of "juice" in it at all and I think you can even tell in my picture that the ice wasn't really soaked. The flavor was weird and tasted like medicine with a weird aftertaste. David tasted mine and he said the same thing. They do have a wide selection of hamburgers and poboys, if you aren't in the mood for a snowball, but you want to munch on something. I probably won't be back.

I used to come to this Walgreens fairly regularly back when I had friends who lived near it. I recently visited this Walgreens for the first time in a long time.  This is a pretty typical Walgreens- they carry all of the usual Walgreens stuff. The staff at this location was pretty friendly when I dropped in and helped me find what I was looking for. I happened to be looking for a certain kind of vitamin for joint pain (not for me, btw) and the pharmacist pointed me in the right direction right away. Also, on the day I was here, they were having a pretty nice little sale on some makeup products, so I stocked up.  The store and the pharmacy here are both open 24/7, so make note of that if you are in need in the late night/early morning hours.

Such a cute shop! This place is a candy lovers dream and offers all types of yummy candy gifts such as giant Reese's cups, giant Hershey bars, extra long Twizzlers, giant gummy bears and pocky along with tons more.  The shop is small and they do have some candy that you can pile into bags and buy, but the main attraction here is all of the unique candy themed gifts and things like that. Some really cute things that I had to resist purchasing was the plush ketchup and french fries that had smiley faces, a plush ice cream cone and pillows that were made to look like candy. One thing I loved was the assortment of candy scented candles that I will definitely be going back to get.  Since we are in the Halloween season there is a nice assortment of Halloween themed treats, so be sure to stock up if that's your thing.

I had always seen Dr. Bob's art all over New Orleans, but it wasn't until a friend and I did a post lunch pop in, that I knew that he had an actual studio.  If you are looking for New Orleans folk art, Dr. Bob is pretty much the "go to". In this small studio you can find paintings and signs of all types. In fact, until Simon came along, you would see Dr. Bob's art in every restaurant and bar in the area.  You can find art for pretty cheap here (under $50) and he has bigger, more expensive pieces, if you are looking for something like that. He also does custom work, so if there is something that you have in mind, sit down with him and he will be happy to collaborate with you.  Dr. Bob also works Jazz Fest every year and sells his work there, if you don't want to venture to Chartres.

I am so excited!  Owners Lindsay and Scott have been working SO HARD on opening their own brewery and tap room. The day has finally come and I am so excited that I got to be a part of it!  First of all, the brewery is small, but it's gorgeous. There are 12 taps  of all different types of beer that are all reasonably priced and Russell is the fantastic bartender who is serving them to you.  Not only are they going to be serving "visiting" beers, but they are also going to be brewing and serving their own beer, which is beyond exciting. This city doesn't have enough breweries serving up really good craft beer. Courtyard Brewery is helping to solve that problem.   When you are hanging out here, you really feel as if you are among friends. I met a bunch of people that I had never met before and we all got along great because we are all beer lovers.  Courtyard Brewery is a welcome addition to the New Orleans beer scene. I am so excited to experience it and I am so excited to go back!

Hansen's is a New Orleans institution and who doesn't love a snowball on a hot day?  I stopped here on a not-too-hot day and was intimidated by the line out the door, onto the sidewalk and nearly into the street. Luckily, the line moved at a steady pace and before I knew it, I was inside placing my order.  They have the basic flavors here and don't really have anything super exotic. I decided on a bubblegum snowball (one of my faves). I liked that the ice was really finely shaved giving it a velvet like consistency. They were super generous with the syrup and the snowball itself was delicious.  I can't wait to go back to Hansen's.

If you ever travel from New Orleans to Slidell, chances are you're familiar with Fisherman's Castle on the Irish Bayou. When I was a kid I was convinced that real royalty lived here after being banished from their kingdom for reasons unknown.  It was originally built over 30 years ago for the World's Fair and thanks to new ownership, it has undergone a complete renovation which is easy to tell from the outside.  We are talking full renovation- from what I've heard they gutted the entire place and completely restored it.   I have no idea if they hold events here or not, but I do know that it's a private residence so I would discourage anyone from knocking on the door and asking for a tour. According to Facebook, the owners are restoring the grounds and will be opening the space up for photo shoots, so I guess we'll see. I would love to get a look at the inside, if it's at all possible. This is one of the most noted landmarks on the NOLA to Slidell drive, and is worth looking out for as it's something a bit different on the landscape.

A nice little "blink and you'll miss it" wine shop in the middle of the Bywater.  I am rarely in the Bywater and I passed this place a few times and just assumed it was nothing more than a wine shop. It wasn't until I was brought here on a date that I realized that not only is it a wine shop, you can also sample wine by the glass here as well. Walking in, the place is packed with wines of all types that you can buy by the bottle and take with you or drink on premises. I decided to try a nice glass of $5 red wine. I'm no wine connoisseur, so this was perfect for me. There are seats where you can sit and chat and they have a tapas menu, if you want something to munch on.  I really liked the atmosphere, and while I wouldn't call it the most romantic place in the world, it's a nice spot to sit and sample wine, if that's your thing.

I'm not usually a Starbucks fan at all but, after hoofing it around the Quarter for French Quarter Fest, I decided to stop in here for an iced coffee to get my energy up. It worked like a charm and I went from dozing to having a pep in my step in no time.  The set up of this store is nice enough and they woman who made my coffee for me was good at her job, in the sense that she didn't mess up my order. Other than that, yeah it's a Starbucks.

This is a cool place to check out, if you want to get off of the beaten path of Bourbon Street.  There is always a good crowd in here and the staff is really nice.  The bar is decorated with old New Orleans memorabilia and has a kind of "old, gritty" New Orleans feel.  They do serve food, although I've never eaten here and the food looks a little shady and boring.  The bar has a back area, but I'm not experienced enough with the place to vouch for all that.

Although this isn't the best Popeyes in the area, this is the one I go to most often. Their drive thru is always fast and they actually fill the mashed potato and red beans and rice containers up to the top. Also, the staff has always been friendly. So, while it's still fast food and it take A LOT for me to give fast food more than three stars, this is a decent stop for some chicken and sides.

Baker's Dozen donuts seem to be everywhere lately, and that is definitely not a complaint!  These delicious donuts are fluffy, light and delicious and whenever I go to a party or event and see that they are serving Baker's Dozen donuts, I know that I am definitely in for a treat. Yes, their store is located all the way out in Jefferson, but it is definitely worth the trip. Not only are the donuts delicious but the staff is amazingly friendly. Brandi, one of the owners, is super personable and is always open to a chat.  I look forward to another delicious bite of Baker's Dozen.

I don't know.  Maybe I'm a snob when it comes to oysters and seafood in general, but I was left underwhelmed by my experience here.  My friends ordered a dozen oysters; half raw and half char broiled.  I ordered the seafood etouffee.  I tried the oysters, but I immediately noticed that they weren't very big.  The char broiled oysters were good and had a nice buttery flavor.  My etouffee was ok, but not really anything special.  The prices here seem a little bit steep for what seems to be just a casual dining place.  I will say that one of my friends ordered the seafood platter, which came with fried crab, catfish, oysters and fries.  It was huge, looked really good, and can definitely be split between two people.  The service was good and we were seated quickly, with only about a ten minute wait.  Given the choice, I would probably go somewhere else for my oyster needs.  I'd be more inclined to support a small local business, rather than this chain.

This is a really nice bohemian-chic kind of spot.  They have a nice selection of long flowy dresses and coverups, jumpsuits, lounge pants and tops that are probably meant to be worn without a bra. Real free living type of clothes.  The woman working when I came in was really friendly and I did find a few things that I was interested in trying on. I like the style of some of the things here, but I did find some things to be a little pricey. For example: there was a long, blue thin material "kaftan" (as it was labeled) that was over $200. Basically this store is great if you want to live the free beach life and you don't mind spending a few bucks.  I'm giving four stars because the staff was beyond helpful and I do like some of the clothing here. I just wish it was a bit more affordable for the every day boho queen.

I am so confused by the mixed reviews of this place, I really liked it.  When I stopped in on a Tuesday night I was the only one in here and the DNC was on- perfect. I sat at a nice little table in the back and I enjoyed the solitude as I looked over the menu. I started with my usual- noodle salad and got the tuna roll, Philly roll and a rainbow roll. The noodle salad was perfection, as were the rolls. Everything tasted really fresh and tasted the way I expected it to taste, so I was pleased.  I love the atmosphere of this restaurant. The inside feels like a restaurant you would find Uptown and it's actually pretty "fancy" for a Westbank place. The waitress was attentive, probably because I was the only customer, but she was good about getting everything to me in a timely manner.  I liked everything here and I'll be back.

Les Bon Temps is a cool place to check out live shows or just go and hang out with friends.  It's a small place, so if you want access to the pool table, you have to get there early.  Brass bands and other bands put on shows in the back, which is always a lot of fun.    Be aware: the floor in the back is brick and uneven, which makes dancing difficult, especially if you are in heels.

I love this shop! Walking in, you immediately discover that Idea Factory is going to bring you back to simpler times. The times before modern technology when toys were built to last.  Everything here is hand made out of wood, and it's a sight to behold. Tops, puzzles, train whistles, secret boxes and much more are on display and available for purchase for the kid (or big kid) in your life. They have a fantastic selection of unique gifts that are sure to capture the imagination. The staff is very friendly and is more than happy to explain how everything works and you are sure to find something that you'll enjoy. I want to go back and buy one of the slide boxes to keep my rings in, so I'm sure I'll be making a trip back to this delightful spot.

Pretty good, but don't expect anything spectacular.  We popped in here pretty late and I'm pretty sure it's the only late night diner type place in the area. I ordered 2 eggs over easy, grits, toast, and bacon- you know this by now. Well, the eggs were definitely over medium, but that wasn't earth shattering. Two things that put me off were the slice of American cheese on the grits and the "butter" that didn't soak into my toast. I don't mind the cheese thing so much, it just would have been nice if they had mixed it in. Other than that, the grits were pretty good, As for the toast- I took a bite and couldn't bring myself to eat any more of it; something just wasn't right.   The staff is nice enough and the food came quickly. It's a good spot for greasy spoon type food if you have a hankering.

I guess I am pretty lucky. I have only caught the Lapalco Bridge when it's been up a few times in my life, and I've traveled on it a lot. I think it's cool that when they do construction on it, they are pretty fast about it. Although, last summer it was a closed for 4 or 5 days and it took me forever to get from Marrero to Gretna, but whatever. That wasn't a huge deal.

This place was a nice little surprise while we were out and about looking for some Halloween fun that wasn't too crazy.  We were here for a few drinks at the upstairs bar. I love the view from the balcony area and the nice breeze coming off of the river was really pleasant. I couldn't stay out there long because, even though it was a warm-ish night, the breeze from the river made it quite cool.  They have a pretty decent selection of local beers on draft. I didn't see anything that really blew me away or anything that was that unusual or hard to come by at other spots, but I appreciated that they had so many local taps. There are a few big screens, which makes me think that this is probably a hot spot during football games.  This place feels a lot like Happy's with a more local vibe. I didn't have any food, but they have a full menu of sandwiches and other hot dishes.

I had been wracking my brain for DAYS trying to remember what this place was called, when someone reviewed it, I finally remembered...McHardy's!  The first time I ever went to this place, I had just wrapped a photo shoot  and the photographer asked me if I wanted to have lunch.  When he mentioned that we were going to take a ride and get McHardy's, I had no idea what he was talking about.  Let me tell you, I LOVE me some Popeyes, but if I had to choose, I would definitely choose McHardy's.  I think that it's probably the closest you can get to homemade chicken without making chicken at home.  It's crispy, juicy and spicy.  It's delicious.  Also, this place has any other chicken place beat, as far as the price goes.  You can get a whole dinner for a super reasonable price.  There used to be a McHardy's on the Westbank, but I never made it to that one.  It might still be there, so be sure you check that out, if you are on the Westbank.

Not a bad little bar.  They have their signature drink: the hand grenade.  Word of advice: don't chug those things and don't have more than one.  They are stronger than you think.    Tropical Isle is one of those typical touristy kind of spots.  They have bands every now and then. If you are visiting, go just to say you went, but seek out nicer places once you try the drinks here.

Whee!  This is always a fun and unique way to see the city and get from point A to point B.  I have never lived near the streetcar, so I have never actually used the it for it's designated purpose (actual transportation).  I've only hopped on with friends for a ride on a nice day.   Actually, that's not true!  A guy I dated a few years back lived within walking distance of the line and I remember we rode the streetcar down Canal to downtown on the 4th of July, in order to see the fireworks.  I remember it being really packed and hot, but hey, it was a huge Summer holiday, so I can't fault anyone for that.  Anyway, the streetcar is definitely one of the most "New Orleans" parts of the city and something you have to do at least once, even if it's just for a fun, cheap ride.

This was my first time ever at the track for Thanksgiving!  Since I had never been here, I really had no idea what to expect. Now I am about sound a little childish, but here we go. I don't gamble. I'm not good at it, I always lose, and I prefer to spend my money on clothes or yummy food than try my luck. With that said, YAY HORSIES! I really liked getting to watch the horses race and get to see them line up and all that. I'm sure there is a more technical term than that, but I'm new at all this.  It was cold. Luckily the area where you place bets/get snack and drinks is enclosed, so that made for a nice place to stay warm. It gets boring in between races, so don't be shy about chatting it up with other people who are waiting for the race to start. Everyone seemed pretty friendly.  I want to go back and watch the ostrich races one of these days!

Ooh! This is another local favorite of mine!  Although Aunt Sally's sells all different types of pralines (triple chocolate, cafe du lait, bananas foster) my absolute favorite go to is the original creamy. Now, what is a praline? Well, it's basically cream and sugar mixed with nuts and made into a delicious candy. The original creamy melts in your mouth and is so sweet and good. They are perfect as a desert or even in the morning with a nice cup of coffee.  Here at Aunt Sally's you can buy them in boxes or 6 or 12, so they are extremely easy to take back home with you or even give as gifts. They also have a nice assortment of different gift baskets that are perfect for any occasion.

This seems to be a popular little gas station because it's located right off of an exit. I stopped in to load up on some snacks for a mini road trip. The store is small and the selection of goodies is somewhat limited. They have a lot of "Golden Flake" brand chips and jerky and stuff, but nothing really beyond that.  I found it strange that they don't sell sunglasses. I had forgotten my sunglasses, so I had planned to just pick up a cheap pair and nope, they don't sell them. I found it pretty odd, because I'm sure a lot of people stop in for little things like that. Oh well.  They have a nice selection of Mad Dog 2020 and malt liquor, if that's your thing.

This cute little shop is located in one of the best parts of Mid City- the American Can, not far from the bayou. Here you will not only find a nice selection of wines, but I was delighted to discover that they have a really great beer selection as well. They have wine tastings on Thursdays and Fridays, as well as other little events throughout the month. I enjoyed a Friday tasting and the staff is happy to tell you a little bit about the wine and find a wine that you would enjoy.  I love the little seating area right inside, so you can buy a bottle on wine and sit and sip with friends on a nice afternoon. Everything here is well priced and the staff is eager to help you find whatever you may be looking for.

Not a terrible bar. I only go here because some friends of mine live about 2 minutes from the place.  Okay crowd, but it gets super packed with young people who are just there to get ripped. Ridiculously smokey and since I am being drawn more and more to places that lack smoke completely, this is a turn off.  They do have a few little bar games here that are pretty fun. Like Morgan mentioned, the skee ball is one of the selling points. All in all not a bad place if you are in the area, but not worth the trip if you aren't.

I can't believe I have never reviewed this place!  No trip to mid city is complete without a trip to Parkway.  In my opinion, they make some of the most perfect po boys in the city.  Whenever I go, I usually get a shrimp po boy, fully dressed.  I usually eat at the bar, when I go, because I find the service to be faster.  Or, I will order at the bar and take my food outside when I get it.  Also a great place to get a good poboy, a beer, and watch the game.

I'm always appreciative of any reason to have lunch at St. Roch Market, because it's always an excuse to try something I've never had before or revisit an old fave.  Good Bird has been on my list for a while, mainly because I love any kind of chicken sandwich, so I was eager to see what they had to offer. Upon a friend's suggestion I got the Larry Bird. With chicken, lettuce, tomato, avocado, and bacon all on ciabatta bread, it's hard to go wrong. The sandwich didn't disappoint- it's really big and served wrapped in paper with a side of their homemade chips. The chicken is nice and juicy and the avocado and bacon was the perfect touch. This sandwich was delicious! It was go-out-of-your-way good.  They have a pretty vast menu of other chicken sandwiches, but honestly I would just stick with the Larry Bird because, bacon. They also have wraps available, if you're not in the mood for a lot of bread. They have a Freret location that I'm eager to check out, mainly because it's closer to me than St. Roch.  Good Bird isn't just good; it's great! I'll be back.

I'm always such a huge fan of Bath & Body Works aka "The Works" and this one is no different.  We stopped in here while we were doing some gift shopping and we were immediately greeted by Allison. She was super nice and helpful, told us about some specials that they were having and even hooked us up with some coupons. Right now The Works is having a "buy 2, get one free" sale, so while that's not on the same level as the Semi-annual sale, it's still worth checking out if you're in the market for some fall scents.  They're always having cool sales and great deals, so keep an eye out if candles, body sprays, shower gels and lotions are your thing.

This is a typical Party City. They have a lot of party decorations and things like that. During the Halloween season they have a really good selection of costumes. During the off season, you can find some costume pieces like wigs and gloves and stuff, but if you really need a costume worth something, you are going to have to look elsewhere.  I really like the huge candy section that they have now. You can go in and fill up a bag. Every 15 pieces of wrapped candy is a dollar, so it's a really good deal and can be a lot of fun to bring the kids for a treat.

I have to update this review because I'm addicted to Sucre cupcakes. I totally blame David.  If you have never had the cupcakes here, you need to know that you're going to get addicted. My faves are the strawberry ones and the vanilla ones. You get a HUGE cupcake that is soft and moist (sorry...damp? Is that better? Not dry.) and then you top it with the lightest, fluffiest icing that has even been created. I'm not even an icing person, but I could eat this icing by the tub.  Last time we were here I got a confetti cake gelato and a strawberry cupcake to go, because sometimes you want to eat a cupcake with glitter icing in bed and that's okay. They also have a wide assortment of chocolates and other fancy desserts and yums.  You're not going to be disappointed with anything you get here and all of it is well worth the price.

Wow.  This place has majorly improved in the year since my last review.  I have been here a few more times since I last reviewed and I have pretty much enjoyed it every single time.  I usually get a burrito, which comes with a side of chips.  I like the queso, but if you want just salsa, they will charge you for it.  Chips and salsa are not free here as they are at other places.    This is a pretty good place to eat on major holidays.  I remember eating here on the 4th of July when other places were packed and I had a really good time.  While Nacho Mama's will never rank as high as "Felipe's" in my book, I would definitely not hesitate to eat here if I was in the area.

No go cups and rude staff makes for a sad Marielle.   Seriously the muscle men at this place were gross and the staff was beyond rude. I asked for a go cup and I was told that they weren't allowed on this block. This is the same block as Lucy's and Vic's. I can't take my drink to go? Come on.    The music is what I would I imagine my suicide soundtrack would be. Seriously. It's boom boom boom with no end. Good Lawd.  If I had to pick an afterlife torture for my enemies, it would be Ohm. In conclusion, this place sucks and the people know it because I told them. I said, "Hey, do you know what Yelp is?" The dude at the door said, "Yep!" and I smiled. Here's the review you deserve.   Good morning. Good afternoon. And Good Night! Oy.

This is always a fun parade, if not a little slow moving. I have to agree with Bobby, there are always huge gaps in the parade where you feel like it's over.  Honestly, for me the best part of Barkus isn't really Barkus at all. I like going down to the Quarter on the day of and walking around and seeing all of the people out there with their dogs. On this day, everywhere in the Quarter is "dog friendly", people dress up their dogs and it's a lot of fun to see.  I do always enjoy seeing the parade dogs in their various costumes- some are very extravagant.

I loved this neat little vintage store.  It seems that they have a little bit of everything from clothing to jewelry to picture frames. Oh, and I loved the hats! I saw a cute little travel box with all kinds of goodies in it and I guess I should have asked if it was for sale. Now I'm kicking myself. Oh well.  I was admiring a rack of dresses when I noticed a lovely stuffed dog curled up on the sofa. Well, I admired it until it opened it's eyes and curiously looked at me. I asked him for some assistance but he explained that I was interrupting his nap, so I went about shopping on my own.  I was wondering if they buy vintage things. I couldn't really figure out if the owner herself is a collector and just finds things online to sell, or if she would be open to buying from someone off the street.  I will definitely go back whenever I have vintage needs. I agree with Joi. The smell of this shop is really nice and it's quiet. You feel like you are in an elder's old home full of antiques.

This should definitely be your first stop if you're looking for some art that's a little "different". There's a lot of different things here, but all of it has a spooky edge, that I just love.  I was here for Dirty Linen Night and I was able to walk around and really get a feel of the work here. The art is gorgeous and ranges from the strange to the macabre. There was even a diorama of a creepy murder scene, in case that's something that you might want to add to your collection. Anything that you end up purchasing here is sure to be a conversation starter. There is a sweetness to some of the more creepy works, which I can really appreciate.  I'm not sure if I'll be purchasing any of the works here for my own home, but I do like what they have going here.

This seems to be the new food truck on the block and ooh baby is it a good one!  Ok, so I'm going to admit that I was one of people saying "$7 for a banh mi? Seriously?" But after tasting it's deliciousness, I was put it my place. This banh mi was PACKED with pork and provided a culinary experience that was out of this world. It had so much flavor that I enjoyed every bite and I was excited to share the experience with my insta-foodies.  While I'm being totally honest, I'm going to admit that the Cajun Spring Rolls were less than spectacular on my end. I think that they could use a bit more spice. Hey, add a little kick to those rolls and I will be all over them!  Saigon Slim's is going to go far and I am so excited that I was able to experience them tonight. I can't wait to try the rest of their faire!

I have been here a couple of times and have had a really good time here.  This is a neighborhood place and while it's not in the best area, if you are familiar with your surroundings or if you visit here with friends, you should be fine. I was here this past weekend for a dance party. The crowd was small, but it was still a lot of fun.    The bar is cash only and pretty basic when it comes to beer. A really chill place to hang out and unwind after a long day.

Everybody knows the main story behind the Make it Right project: Brad Pitt and a lot of other awesome people put their time and money into making sure the people of the lower 9th ward got the good hurricane proof housing that they deserve for an affordable price.  I recently was able to pass through and see for myself the work that has been done here. It's amazing. The houses are beautifully made and the lower 9th ward is more gorgeous than ever. The houses almost look like works of art. The houses are raised up and most of them have an area under the house for parking cars. A lot of the houses have solar panels on the roof in an effort to keep everything as "green" as possible.  I think that Make it Right is an amazing foundation and the work that they have done is to be admired. The people who took the time and money to do this for this community should be commended. It is my hope that other flood prone communities follow the lead of Make it Right and work to provide safe housing for their residents.

Full disclosure: although I'm an adventurous eater, I'm not super familiar with Middle Eastern food. In fact, I have only been to Lebanon's Cafe once and Byblos a few times. So, when the boyfriend/man I'm seeing suggested Cleopatra's, I was down. He goes here a lot and tells me how good it is, so I figured it was worth a shot.  We went on a weeknight and walking in, I was kind of nervous. There was hardly anyone here for dinner, but then again, it is the Westbank on a Wednesday. For my drink I decided to try the Lebanese iced tea. It was pretty good and I would liken it to fruit punch more than tea, but I enjoyed it. For my entree I decided on the beef (it might be called 'gourmet') shwarma. It came with a side of rice, hummus and salad. It was all really good. I found the meat tender and full of flavor. The hummus was super good as was the salad. The rice was a little bland, but it wasn't terrible.  I would definitely go back! Because there wasn't a crowd, we were served fairly quickly and we didn't feel rushed.

I stopped in here with a minor issue on my new (to me) road bike and the staff was super nice and helpful and fixed the issue quickly. I had been in here before when I had issues with another bike and their advice was always solid and "did the trick".  Atmosphere is comfortable and the place isn't run by "bike snobs".

The Westbank has an Ulta! Fantastic!   Michelle was the first person to tell me that Ulta was coming to Oakwood, and I couldn't have been more excited. I got word that it finally opened, so I was eager to check it out.   For those of you not in the "know", Ulta is basically a huge beauty supply store. They have everything from drugstore brands to more upscale stuff. I saw on their website that they carry by favorite facial moisturizer so I headed down to check it out. They have EVERYTHING here. Not only did they have my moisturizer, but I also found some OPI nail polish that I really liked. They also carry designer perfume, hair styling stuff and pretty much anything else you could need beauty wise. I get the feeling I will be spending a lot of time and money here.

Such a cute little pastry shop!  I didn't even know this place was here, until I was driving down Terry Parkway and noticed the sign. I made note of the name and did some research. I liked what I saw, so I decided to pop in and check it out for myself.  Upon entering, I was greeted immediately by the owner. It was a little later in the day, so a lot of the goodies had been snatched up, but there was a chocolate strawberry cake that caught my eye. After I got it home, I was delighted at how tasty and fresh it was. Yes, the strawberries were super fresh and the cake was light and melted in my mouth.  They have a nice selection of pastries here and, when I go back, I'm going to have to try some of their macaroons. I also saw some posts about a doberge cake that looks really good, so I'm eager to try that as well.  They serve different coffees, if you want some coffee with your dessert and, for the summer, they are also serving flavored teas. It sounds like the perfect way to beat the heat!

This is such a great little spot! While it isn't the fanciest place in the world, it's a really nice place to stop in, listen to some music and have a drink or two.  The place was pretty dead when we stopped in on Friday night, but the bartender was friendly and the band was good. The setup of the place is very odd- the band is located right next to the door, there is a small seating area across the from the band and then there's the bar. Everything is kind of squeezed in, but for what it is, it's a pretty good place.  This bar does serve Lucid "absinthe" and a few basic beers like High Life and stuff like that. There's a weird, dark seating area in the back that is kind of away from everything. I think vampires have their meetings back there or something.  All in all this place is a good time, and while it's not as "hopping" as some other music venues, it's worth checking out if you are in the neighborhood.

I was pretty shocked that the cemetery had zero reviews. It's pretty nice, located in the middle of a neighborhood. I stopped in here to take a few photos from my personal use. I was astonished at how many of the graves were older, some of the last burials in them took place in the 30s and 40s.   For the most part, the graves are well kempt in the number one cemetery, but in the number two cemetery, it's a different story. In the number two cemetery, graves are falling into disrepair, just because a lot of time has passed and the families have likely died off. That's not to say anything bad about New Orleans Catholic cemeteries, which maintains the properties. I enjoyed walking through both spaces, and I enjoyed the quiet of all of it.

It's time for an update and I am declaring Cleopatra the best lunch spot in town!  I know those are some big words, but I stand by them. Cleopatra consistently offers delicious, fresh and fast lunch at a price that's almost criminal. They have an entire lunch menu of options, but I usually get the beef shawarma plate which comes with hummus, rice, pita, a good size salad and pickled vegetables, all for $10 before tip. This sounds like a lot of food, because it is. These are generous "dinner sized" portions of delicious, fresh food and you can't beat the price.  I also like this spot because they know that if you're here for lunch on a weekday, you have to get back to work, so you get the food fast. You'd think quality would suffer, but it doesn't at all. It comes out hot and delicious.   This is a family owned place and service is always excellent and the owners take pride in their restaurant and it shows. I love the food here and I really need to make of eating here more often.

This is a gorgeous fancy shop for people who still hand write letters and appreciate the finer things.  We stopped in here just to look around and WOW- they have gorgeous things here. I loved the ink pens that you have to actually fill with ink. They have ink wells containing inks of all different colors: different shades of blue, greens and coppers really blew me away.  They also sell a large assortment of fancy magnifying glasses with beautiful silver handles and gorgeous wrapping paper and stationary. If you are looking for a unique gift for a writer in your life, Papier Plume should be your first and last stop.  The store owner was extremely welcoming and asked where we were from and if we needed help with anything. I also heard her telling other people to "enjoy the city", which I love from any store proprietor, especially one in the French Quarter.

Can't really say much about this place because I popped in and out so quickly that I didn't even have a chance to order a drink.  So, why am I bothering to review it? Well, we stopped in to see what's what and pretty much use the restroom. Although we weren't paying for anything the staff was super friendly and nice and the people hanging out here seemed nice too.  I'm sure I'll be back at some point.

This is SUCH a cool store.  More Fun is a must visit for any comic book fan or collector.  They have anything you could want and they take subscriptions, if you want your comics to arrive in perfect condition.  They carry everything from DVDs to action figures and everything in between.  If it's something comic book or collectable you are looking for, then this should definitely be your first (and probably only) stop.    Bonus points from me because I was able to find really cool books about pinups here!

I'm updating this review mainly because I MUST remember to stop coming here when Wok to Go is closed. I don't know what has happened, but the food is just awful- it has no flavor and the only good thing about it is that it's cheap. I used to get take out from this spot all the time, but the last few times I did, I couldn't even finish what I was eating.  Tonight I got the Moo Goo Gai Pan and I took a few bites and I was done. It comes with shrimp fried rice and an egg roll- both of those were decent, but the rest of the dish was inedible. I can usually power through something, even if it's not that good, but I didn't even want to bother wasting the calories by eating it all. I had some of the rice and the egg roll and that was that.  I get that it's a hole in the wall place and most, if not all, of their food comes from a bag, but this was just bad. Never again.

I've been to the Convention Center many times over the years. It's a great space: large enough to accommodate a full Mardi Gras parade and it's revelers, if that gives you any idea.  Most recently I attended NOLA Christmas Fest here and I just loved the way it was all laid out, even though we parked in the lot way at the other end and had to walk to where we were going. The staff at the Convention Center is always helpful and they're good at telling you where you need to be and when.   My only complaint is that I wish there was more parking around the convention center. You have a few choices: park in the big lot by the Riverwalk or park across Tchoupitoulas in the lot they have over there. It can't be helped, but that's the only drawback of this otherwise great space.

I'm updating because if you are going to go here, you are gonna want to get the speciality rolls.  Now I know.  I've had the playboy roll, Buddha belly roll and the St Charles roll.  All three were fantastic and about $15 each, but they are really big and enough for two people.  So, yeah this place is pretty awesome.

I hit the drive thru today to grab a strawberry margarita. I got the Big Kahuna 44oz for $8.  You can't beat it- pour what you want in a cup and freeze the rest.   We're in Covid-mode and the drive thru window had a safety screen and the woman who served me put on fresh gloves to do so. I was impressed.   Drink was great and just what I was in the mood for. Great spot!

Being an Entergy customer is like being in an abusive relationship.  Entergy totally mistreats you.  The power will go out for no reason and for 5 hours at a time.    I'm sorry, Entergy.  Is it something I said?  I won't make you mad again.  I promise.  But you can't leave Entergy because there's no one else out there.  So, you settle and decide that this is life now.  Losing power willy nilly and for no reason.  Just go limp and accept it.  One star because Entergy is a step up from candlelight and another star because I'm typing this on a computer powered by electricity that Entergy is providing.

There are probably some "pros" to parking in this lot, but I'm at a loss.  So, they got rid of the parking lot workers, but also raised the prices. In other words, you have to pay MORE to use a machine to park. I hate using a machine to park because that means my time in the lot is limited. I would rather just park and come back and pay a human for however long I was in there. With that being said- I parked for 3 hours and came back after 3 hours and wasn't ticketed or bothered. I guess I win.

I don't know if I could anything about this place that hasn't already been said.  It's not such a bad place, but it seems a little out of place on Bourbon St. I feel as if it's trying to be a little more upscale, and that's hard to pull off when you are surrounded by strip clubs and souvenir shops.   I think that the first thing I noticed about S&S is that the inside of it looks like a brothel. There's red velvet everywhere and it has a "peep show" kind of feel. Oddly enough, I kind of got the feeling that they modeled some of the decor after One Eyed Jack's, but maybe I'm insane. There wasn't anything overly great about the service, but the staff was really friendly, nice and accomodating and went above in beyond in making us feel welcome.  I might go back if I were in the area, but that's not really likely.

The sculpture garden at the New Orleans Museum of Art is one of New Orleans' hidden treasures.  Located behind the museum, near City Park, the garden is free to visit and the sculptures are ever changing and when you visit you almost feel as if you are in another world.  There is a body of water that goes through the garden and you can actually go on a gondola ride!  This is a great place to just come and relax and reflect and enjoy the scenery.  It's very quiet and peaceful and I think it would be fantastic to come here after a long day and just walk around or even on a date.  I have been to a few events in the Sculpture Garden over the years and it's a lovely place to have a party. A few years ago I was fortunate enough to see a live production of "A Midsummer Night's Dream" and the garden provided the perfect back drop for this particular production. Because this spot is free, it's a great place to enjoy a nice afternoon and just relax.

This is a review of the beer/bar area and not the food.  We stopped in here on Mardi Gras, just to check it out and try out the beer. The downstairs area was pretty crowded, so we headed upstairs and snagged a seat at the bar. I would say that Crescent City Brewhouse is more of a restaurant than a brewhouse- they only offer four beers, but nonetheless, i was eager to try what they had. I decided to try the Red Stallion and the Imperial Pilsner. Both were pretty good. They didn't knock my socks off, but they were enjoyable.  The bartender was really nice and worked fast to take our order. The menu looked good, so I might try the food if I make it back.

Cucos is a chain, and when you go with a chain you are gonna get chain food.  Nothing here is overly spectacular.  When I go, I get the chicken nachos which aren't too bad.  The chips and salsa are also pretty good, but when it's free, it's hard to rate a restaurant on that.  I've also gotten the taco salad here which was underwhelming.  I don't know.  I guess I'm a snob when it comes to Mexican food.  I like it to be more on the authentic side.    If you want run of the mill "Mexican" food, then this is your place.  If you are looking for something a little more authentic, check out La Fiesta on Stumpf.

40 Arpent is a fantastic little brewery quickly adding to the landscape of the Louisiana beer scene.  Set in Arabi,  this family owned brewery has really taken off in the last few months. It's still a small operation, compared to other breweries, but I can see them going places. I think my two favorite beers from 40 Arpent are the Creole Red Bean and Rice Ale, which tastes a lot better than it sounds and the Copasaw Wheat which is packs a lot of flavor.    I'm really excited to see what 40 Arpent does next.

Such a nice theater! We ended up seeing a sketch comedy show here in which the players performed a short skit about all 50 states. It was great! I am a huge comedy fan and I absolutely love improv and sketch comedy, so I know that I will make more of a point to see shows here.  The space itself is pretty small, but I actually like the intimate feel and there was plenty of seating and space for everyone. A man working mentioned that they are adding a bar area soon, so I'm sure that will be a draw for some people. I look forward to seeing more shows at TNM and having a good laugh.

Phillips is definitely one of the nicer places on Maple St.  When you go in, you feel as if you are in a high end place.  I have never been in here when it has been packed and it isn't packed with college kids like the other places.  There is a nice older crowd here and although the drinks are a little more expensive, it's worth it if you don't have to deal with a huge crowd.  Phillips also has pool tables and nice seating areas for groups, if you don't want to sit at the bar.  The lighting is dim and cozy and the music isn't super loud, so you can have a conversation.

Besides the fact that it's my dream to one day be married here, St Louis Cathedral is one of the most recognized landmarks in the City of New Orleans.  This gorgeous church is located near Jackson Square, and is a symbol and the center, of New Orleans' predominantly Catholic faith.  No matter your religion, you should have no trouble recognizing the beauty of this iconic structure.  Who could forget the poignant moment, after Hurricane Katrina, when President George W. Bush addressed our nation in front of the Cathedral?  The hands on the church's clock face were frozen in place at the very time the city lost power and the lives of it's people were forever changed.  That is one of the moments that I don't think I will ever forget.  Whether you are Catholic or not, a local or a visitor, next time you are in the area, stop into the Cathedral and light a candle.  Maybe say a prayer.  You might be a little better for it.

I'm not sure how long this shop has been here, but since I'm always in the market to shop at new (to me) lingerie shops, I was happy to discover this spot on a recent outing.  Basics is anything but basic- they have a lovely selection of "every day" bras and underwear as well as things that are a little fancier for the times when you want to mix it up. I happened to be in the market for a strapless bra, and Basics had a lot of options. The staff was helpful and friendly, and although I haven't purchased anything yet, I will be back when I am ready to make my move.  In the adjoining room they have a fantastic selection of swim and workout wear that is sure to make anyone feel fancy on their next trip to the gym. One thing that I especially liked about this shop is the attention to personal details- they had lotions and body sprays along with clothing and I like that for times when you want to pamper yourself all the way.

A new pho place popped up on my radar, so you know I had to check it out.  Pho Kang is located in the same building that used to house Pho Orchid. Someone said that they thought it was the same place, with a different name, but I'm not sure. I stopped in for lunch and there was no one else in here. I started with an order of grilled pork spring rolls and Vietnamese coffee and I got a regular bowl of rare beef and brisket pho for my entree.  The spring rolls were excellent- packed with fresh ingredients and the pork didn't have a weird grill after taste that I've noticed that it has elsewhere. The pho was great! The regular bowl was small and the perfect size for lunch and the meat was generous and the broth was flavorful. I really enjoyed it and it's one of the better "new" bowls that I have tried lately.  Service is fast and friendly, making this a great lunch stop.

I've been sitting on this review for a week and I think that I am going to go with 3.25 stars.  I really like this place. It has a cool atmosphere and the staff is super attentive and friendly. I went in and I was told to just seat myself. It's an "informal" kind of atmosphere; the menus are in a bucket on the table along with the forks and knives, which was oddly off putting..   I wasn't super hungry, so I just decided on a bowl of mac and cheese which was $5. It was really good, and if I go back that is probably what I will get. Looking over the menu, the sandwiches just seem kind of expensive to me., I caught a glimpse of other people's and they didn't look like anything overly special. I know I have to actually try one for myself. Maybe I am really missing out, but I was happy with my mac and cheese and that was that.

Yay! This place is so cool. I love the whole setup of it. The bar itself does turn and that's a little weird, but it turns slowly and you get used to it after a few minutes. There is a huge sitting area where you can watch a live band. I think that there was a jazz singer the night that I went.  The bartenders are super fast and work really well with the moving bar. I guess they have to in order to work there. I had a "fancy" drink, which was a Ramos gin fizz. It was really good and kind of tasted like cake. I'm usually not big on drinks with hard liquor in them, but this one impressed me.  I wish I could have stayed longer, but it's a hotel bar and it's not open super late. I will definitely go earlier next time so that I can get a more extensive experience.

I love a fancy house that has been converted into a hotel! There is just something so cozy about a place like that and when you step into the Cornstalk you feel as if you are stepping into a castle in a far away land.  We occupied a room downstairs and it was small, but gorgeous. The room was complete with gorgeous wall paper, an antique style phone and old books. The decor of the entire hotel is just lovely and has a beautiful antique feel. We were bouncing around the entire hotel taking pictures and exploring, and the staff was really nice and accommodating. My only complaint is that there was some kind of construction being done right outside the window of our room and it was a little loud.  My favorite spot in the entire place was upstairs. There is a nice balcony space where you can step out and look over the garden area and it's just lovely. I would recommend anyone on vacation (or stay-cation) give this place a shot.

I'm always a fan of art that's a little different and Frenchy fits that category in the best way.  I had the opportunity to stop in here and meet the artist and I was blown away by all of his different types of art work. Full of color and open to interpretation, I like that his work is in a different style than a "typical" New Orleans artist and you can tell that he pulls his inspiration from the city, but it's art that anyone can relate to, no matter where they are from. His gallery itself has a warehouse feel but is splashed with paintings from the more abstract to gorgeous portraits of NOLA musicians Dr John, Allen Toussaint and James Booker. I like that his portraits swirl with color and that Frenchy is not afraid to "paint outside the lines".  Frenchy himself was very friendly and open and happy to talk about his art. Maybe someday I will own an original.

Meh.  This used to be a cute little low key hang out, but during the school year it's a full blown college bar packed with college kids (of course).  They do have drink specials, but the drinks shrink with the specials.  For $2.50 you will get a little more than a thimble full of beer.  I really wish I had taken a picture.  It's a joke.  There are way better places on Maple St.  Go there.

Elizabeth is an amazing photographer and so fun to work with! She brings her professionalism and her dedication to every shoot. She works with you to create a vision that you will cherish for years to come. I love how her photos have an "retro" feel to them and a little bit of edge. The images she and I created looked as if they were straight out of the 50's. You won't be disappointed.

I finally made it to this New Orleans institution and I couldn't be more pleased with my experience.  We went at around 1 and by then the lunch crowd had died down, so we were quickly seated. Everything on the menu looked so good and you can get an assortment of things like poboys, seafood platters and spaghetti.  I decided to start with the turtle soup. While it wasn't bad, it's not on the level of a place like Commander's Palace. It had good flavor, but they kind of went easy on the turtle, if that makes any kind of sense. For my entree, I got the fried oyster platter and that came with fries. I LOVE fried oysters and any place that offers a fried oyster platter is good in my book. The oysters were AMAZING. I actually loved that they were a little smaller, which allowed me to eat the whole thing in one bite and not cut it in half.  I will definitely return to Mandina's and will be adding it to my list of recommended places to visit when living in/visiting New Orleans.

This place has a little bit of everything. It feels like you are sorting through someone's garage with the way things are organized, but I like that there is a lot to look at and it's well priced. You'll find a little bit of everything here: candlesticks, lamps, old salt and pepper shakers, furniture, clocks, art, etc. Anything you can imagine when you hear the word "knick knack" is for sale at this place. I was happy to see that the prices are reasonable, compared to other shops.   The basic idea of this store is to come and get things that you can maybe repurpose into something you can use. Don't come expecting the items to be in "perfect" condition, although I did find the furniture to be in great shape.

Finally got to try this place after my boyfriend had been raving about it.  Talk about fantastic!  The place is small, but it has an upscale "diner" feel.  I ordered the "Cubano", which was their take on a Cuban sandwich.  My boyfriend got a pastrami sandwich that looked delicious!  We had table service, which my boyfriend told me was new.  We went kind of late (around 10) and the place only had a few people in it, as it closes at 11.  We will definitely be going back!

Wow.  I had no idea that I ate so much Mexican food, but this is my like my fifth Mexican restaurant review.  Anyway...La Fiesta isn't a place that looks like much from the outside.  Ok, it doesn't look like much inside, either.  I'm pretty sure that this is a house that has been converted to a restaurant.  But, don't let looks fool you.    The food here is awesome.  I would brand this as close to "authentic" Mexican food as it gets (correct me if I'm wrong).  My favorite is either a burrito or a chorta (I think...the thing with the cheese and meat sauce).  Everything I have eaten here has been awesome and prices are reasonable.    A definite "must try" if you find yourself on the Westbank.

This store is okay, but a lot of the clothing seems like it's a "throwback" to about 8 years ago when Affliction and short shorts were all the rage.  The women's clothing selection at this store is pretty thin, especially for summer. As I said, short shorts seem to be the big thing. They also have tank tops and a small swimsuit selection. The men's selection isn't much better with a wide selection of Affliction shirts and other dated "graphic" tees. On the day that we were here they had some men's jeans on sale and the styles are nice and this is pretty much the only thing I would consider purchasing here.

What can I say? It's a Starbucks and if you've been to one, you've been to them all.  My "go to's" for Starbucks are always the peppermint mocha frappucino or the pumpkin spice frapp, when it's in season. I stop in here when I am looking for a dessert type of drink and I don't think I have ever actually had real coffee here, now that I think about it.  This is a nice location that usually has people coming and going all day, since it's located on a busy part of Manhattan.

I couldn't wait to review this exquisite gallery.  We were wandering on Royal when the beautiful art in the window caught our eye. We walked in and were greeted by a delightful woman who was more than happy to chat with us and show us around. The art here is beautiful, and is mostly French artists.  One of the exceptions is an artist named Matthew Peck. David and I were taken aback by his unique style and his paintings that look like photographs and that actually glow when the lights are dimmed. His work is spectacular, and just the fact that we were able to discover this artist is enough for me to give this gallery 5 stars. Obtaining a print of his work has jumped to the top of our "to do" list.  There are gorgeous works by many artists in this gallery, so if you're in the area don't hesitate to stop in.

It's a Burger King.  How do you review a Burger King?  They are all the same.    Well, it's number 3 for a reason.  The food is "meh", even when it's the best it's ever been.  Whoppers aren't big anymore and the fries can't compare to McD's.  They do a good breakfast and I do come here to get my favorite: a croissanwich with the little bite size hash browns.

Out of all of the AMC theaters, this one is probably my favorite.  First of all, I love that it's located in a mall, so that you can go window shopping, if you are waiting for your showtime to come up.  Also, the upstairs (where the theaters are) is huge.  They have a huge concession area where you can sit and talk and eat your snacks before or after the movie.  The seats themselves are the most comfortable of all three AMC theaters (the AMC on the Westbank has the worst ones, in my opinion).  The theaters always seem clean and they manage crowds well (if you are going to a popular movie, they put you in a line while you wait for seating to start.  I've found that this prevents chaos.

I miss the Saenger so much and can't wait for it to reopen!  I have seen so many different shows here since I was a child.  They used to have a ballet every year that I can remember going to see on  field trips.  I also saw "Grease" here (starring Frankie Avalon, himself) when it was traveling around the country.  I think that my favorite show was, by far, when Alanis Morissette acoustic show I saw here about 2 months before Katrina.  She was touring her "Jagged Little Pill" acoustic album.  The show was really nice, because only the bottom part of the theatre was filled.  This was done on purpose so that the show had a more intimate feel.   The theatre itself is lovely, and from what I have heard will be absolutely gorgeous after the renovations are complete.  I can't wait to once again enjoy a show at the Saenger.

I'm usually against re reviewing unless my experience has changed drastically, but I'm updating anyway. This place has been a solid "meh" for the 3 years since my last review.  Look, here's the deal, when I am in the mood for cheap Mexican that ISN'T Taco Bell, I usually just go here. Seeing as how it's the 4th of July and America is a melting pot, I decided to check this place out today for lunch. I ordered the flauta combo with the beans and rice. It's all microwaved. All of it. They know it. I know it. Let's not pretend this is in any way authentic or fresh but hey, my lunch was $8 before tax and tip, so maybe I decided to look the other way and just enjoy it for what it is.  Long story short: don't go here for authentic Mexican. Go here because it's better than Taco Bell and still has the same decor it's had since it opened in 1981.

Here's another sushi place that I wouldn't go out of my way to go to, but the food wasn't too bad.  I've kind of made it my mission to try a new sushi place whenever I can.  When I went to this place, what immediately leaped out to me was how friendly the staff was.  We went kind of late, and they were about 30 minutes from closing, but they didn't shoot us away or rush us.  The food was good...typical sushi.  The one thing that kind of gave me pause...I ordered a roll that is normally served kind of cool.  Well, they had just finished making the rice for it, so when I popped it into my mouth it was warm...and I was expecting it to be cold.  I don't know, I just remember that as being as jarring experience.  LOL.    I'd definitely go back.

When this place fell off the planet a few years ago, I was really bummed.  There used to be one right by my house and I loved going there when I was in the mood for inexpensive pasta that wasn't the Olive Garden.  When I heard that there was one at Clearview Mall, I couldn't wait to check it out.  Of course, you know when I went, I just had to get my favorite which is the muffaletta pasta.  Yummy penne pasta with strips of ham and salami topped with olive salad, mozzarella, and olive oil.  Sure, it's not the healthiest thing on the menu, but it is definitely my favorite.  After Katrina, they had taken it off of their menu, for whatever reason, and I was so bummed.  Well, it was fabulous and it was just as I had remembered.  The chicken quesadilla pasta is also really good, if you are in the mood for something a little spicier.  Sure, it's a mall restaurant, but give it a chance.  The food is good, not too expensive and the service is great!  I will definitely be going back!

I spent the better part of the Saints 2009 season in this place watching the Saints on the road to the Super Bowl.  This is a great neighborhood bar full of awesome locals.  It's a fabulous place to watch games because they have a huge projector screen and the place gets PACKED for not only football games, but futbol games as well!  Also, I LOVE how "into it" the fans here get.   On Saints game days, you can bring a dish in the theme of whoever the Saints are playing (ie: Saints vs Falcons="dirty bird" stew).  They also serve traditional Irish faire (the owners are Irish...as in FROM Ireland) and they have game nights.  It's just a great place all around, and whether you are local or a tourist, you will definitely be made to feel welcome here.  Fun fact: on the facebook page for this place, they let you know that it's time to come watch the game with the simple phrase, "the biscuits are in the oven!"

This is a review coming from someone who doesn't smoke or vape. I basically stopped in because we were sight seeing along Canal Street and I always wondered what this shop was about.  Well, mystery solved: it's a head shop. Here you can find a wide selection of pretty glass pipes, vape stuff, incense, and other things you can inhale/inhale things out of. The pipes they sell are actually really pretty and I got a nice picture of some of the ones they had in the display case.  Along with all of that, they sell long flowy flower and tie dye dresses, t shirts, hats, bags and other accessories. Even though I am sure me and my boyfriend looked like a couple of square fish out of water, the woman working greeted us with a smile and told us to let her know if we needed anything.  If you are into clothing that is tie dyed or a little different or if you are in the need of vape/tobacco products, this is the place for you.
