The Smoothie King Center isn't so big that you feel as if you're miles away from the action and, although I watched most of the game on the big screens, I had no problem seeing all of the action on the court.  The staff was excellent and we found our seats with no issues. The only hiccup came when we were leaving getting out of the garage took and while was a bit of a pain, but that's to be expected at a place like this.

This is one of my favorite places to check out live music on Frenchmen street.  Although it's not as fancy as Snug Harbor or even dba, it has a certain "New Orleans" charm about it and there are always cool bands playing here.  Spotted Cat doesn't seem to have become as overrun with "Treme" fans as other Frenchmen street places and the crowd is more local.  The staff is always friendly, even when the place is packed.  A definite "must" for any local or visitor.

Just wanted to update this to say that I have been LOVING their rainbow roll as of late!  You can get a half order, so you don't have to worry about having to eat 8 really big roll pieces.  Also, I have taken to getting their iced green tea with my meals, which is fabulous and refreshing, especially on hot summer days.  I really wish I could bottle the stuff, because it has more flavor than the iced green tea I've had at other places.  Just a note: others have complained about the service, but I've never had any issue and I've been here A LOT for both lunch and dinner.

Yikes. It's a split here between really good and really bad.  The really good: they were having a big sale on home decor, which I happened to be in the market for. They also had my hair products that i buy here because they are super cheap salon-like brands and I get to save a lot of money.  The really bad- disorganization, this place is a mess. I couldn't find anyone to help me get something specific that was on a high shelf, so they lost out on a $40 sale. Once I went to check out, the price of some hair products I bought rang up more than what it was marked. The cashier went to go check it out and came back and told me it had been labeled wrong and the higher price was the correct one. At that point i just bought it, because I had been in line for at least 10 minutes. I know I should have walked out, but I didn't want to think I had completely wasted my time.   All in all this frustrating experience guaranteed that I will shop elsewhere next time.

I just got a fancy new Samsung Galaxy smart phone (subtle brag) and the folks at T Mobile were more then helpful in helping me figure out exactly what would work best for me and getting me all set up.  They helped me take my old, sad smart phone and transfer all of my info to my fancy new phone, with no trouble at all. Service was fast and there was zero wait, even though there were a few other people in the store.

No, you're eyes aren't deceiving you. Ruby Red's is BACK in their original location!!  It's been two long years (maybe more), but today I was able to have one of Ruby's delicious steak cheddar burgers that I missed so much. Now, they have only been open for about 5 days and they are currently only serving burgers, so if you are craving a chicken sandwich, you might have to wait a week before you are able to sink your teeth into one.  Walking in, it was as if nothing had changed. The peanuts were on the floor, the checkered table cloths were in place and I was a happy camper. I got my burger medium rare and it came with steak fries. It was all as good as I remembered.  I can't wait to go back again and again. FINALLY a good burger place on the Westbank!

This is a nice little bar off of Bourbon St. It's not so bad, as it has a nice mix of locals and tourists. I've always found that the bartenders here are nice and friendly.  There is a really nice patio in the back where you can socialize on nice days. You can also host private parties on the patio, as I have been to a couple. I have always had a good time here and I would return.

I stopped in here because I found myself in the 'hood and I needed to stock up on some Mardi Gras supplies. This place was STOCKED for Mardi Gras and I was so excited to get some holiday stuff here.  I got a few tshirts and a king cake scented candle (yum!). This is a cool shop and while I don't think it has as much as other Fleurty Girl shops, they have a nice selection here. The girls working here did a good job at managing the customers and helping with whatever was needed. As always, FG is a great gift shop and a great place to pick up a cute top or gift for your favorite NOLA lover.

This TJ Maxx won my heart immediately for the simple fact that their shoe section is organized and not all over the floor.  I found some cute pumps that were on sale for $5 and fit me perfectly. They also had a nice selection of flats, although I was not really in the market for them on the day I was here. The checkout went fast and the staff is friendly enough. Honestly, I knew what I was looking for, so I didn't venture into the rest of the store, but I was happy with what I found.

The oyster fest is nice mainly because it's one of the smaller fests in the area.  There are all kinds of awesome oyster based foods from all around the city. My favorite, the oyster po boy, never disappoints. There are also bands and live music so you can have a good time while you eat. The fest is held at Woldenberg park, so you can watch the river as you eat and relax.  The only complaint is that it happens right at the cusp of Spring and Summer, so the heat can be pretty intense. Don't forget your sunscreen!

I like Parasol's although admittedly, I don't go here as nearly often as I used to since Tracey's moved in and I really never eat here.   This is a nice little neighborhood joint that serves up a good poboy. I'll usually stop in with friends at the end of the night to get a beer. It's on a dimly lit corner, so I would never go by myself and the place itself is really small, so it's not the first place I seek out when I am looking for a place to hang out. It serves it's purpose, but as I said before, I prefer Tracey's.

Yay! I feel like this little spot on Decatur has finally found the bar that it's supposed to be. Other bars that have moved into 1135 Decatur haven't seemed to last, but I love Spitfire.  First of all, the bar itself is really cool. There's a propeller behind the bar that actually spins! Second of all, the staff is friendly and the music is good, with various tunes from the 80's and 90's. It doesn't have the "dirty" feel that other bars on Decatur seem to have, and although it's dark, you don't feel like you are going to run into a bad element here. There are pool tables in the back, if that's your thing and you are bound to have a good time.
Reviewing this one, since it's the one I go to.    The best iced coffee anywhere.  Better prices than Starbucks.  Why go anywhere else?

This is a neat shop that has a lot of fun little treats.  As the name suggests, they have pralines. I didn't try any, so I can't vouch for them, but I've discovered that if you've had one praline you've had them all. They also carry a variety of cooking supplies such as utensils as well as spices and hot sauces and things like that. The woman working was sure to ask if I needed any help or if I was looking for anything specific. This was nice, especially considering I had stopped in on a pretty busy night.  Magnolia probably isn't worth going out of your way, but if you find yourself in the area, it's worth a look.

I'm giving this Cafe Du Monde 4 stars, for the main reason that it's convenient for me.  It's a Cafe Du Monde just like any other.  You're gonna get cafe au lait and beignets.  When I go to this one, I usually just get a frozen cafe au lait, which is just fabulous!  This location is in the mall, so it's never packed.  They also have their classic little green tables and chairs for sitting.  Nice view of the mall fountain from the seats.

Yvonne Lafleur is known as the poster woman for fashion in the New Orleans area.  Not only is this shop located in one of my FAVORITE parts of uptown, but it carries some of the most gorgeous dresses I have ever laid eyes on.  If you need a dress for a special occasion (and you have a few bucks) this should be the first place you look.  Now that it's the season for Carnival balls, their window is dressed with gorgeous sparkly treats that I can only dream of being able to afford and having somewhere special enough to wear.  They also carry lingerie, which I would call "special occasion" lingerie for a honeymoon or anniversary.

I have since gone back a few times since my last review and I really love this place.  Not only are the cookies fantastic, but the mega-fours (extra large petit fours) are AMAZING! They are almost like slices of wedding cake. They also have regular sized petit fours as well as slices of cake and cake balls. I also like that they decorate the sugar cookies according to the season. Also, the woman working here is always super nice and friendly and will help with whatever you may need.  Check out the picture of my festive Christmas cookies!

Oh my God! I am way overdue for an Avenue Pub update!  Since my last review, I have become a bit of a beer connoisseur and I know a good beer when I taste one. Not only does Ave Pub have revolving taps, but the owner Polly  is always sure to have an abundance of delicious brews in bottles for her patrons to sample. I love the Pub because the bartenders are always super friendly, even if you are a beer novice and you need a little help figuring out what you like.  I love this place not only for the beer, but the balcony and the fact that it is open 24 hours. It also doesn't hurt that one of my bestest friends, Liam works the graveyard shift a lot of nights. If you are service industry, head in here after work and you will be treated right.  Oh and it helps that Ave Pub has a kitchen. Not sure what time it closes, so you might want to do your research before you plan on munching here. Just a note: the dump truck fries are legendary.  Will I go back? Uh...yeah. Always.

I had always passed this place, whilst driving down St. Charles and would think to myself "eek, what a dive!"  So, when my boyfriend suggested that we meet his friend and her husband here, one afternoon for a beer, I was less than thrilled.  Whatever, I'll give it a shot.  So, I went and it really wasn't that bad.  They have a huge beer selection, which is a huge plus.  This place didn't really start to grow on me, until a few months later when we celebrated a friend's birthday here.  We went to the upstairs area and sat in a big group on the balcony.  You have a great view of St. Charles Ave and the atmosphere is nice and not too loud.  They also serve food.  This night, we got a few snacks.  We also went back and got burgers, which were really good.  I took off one star because it's really smoky, so sitting inside isn't as nice as sitting outside.  Despite that, I would definitely go back.

Now, I'm sure that some would consider this Asian food, but I would respectfully call it "Asian light".  I don't think I've ever eaten anything overly Thai here.  Not unless putting a sauce on a piece of salmon is Thai food.  Not that I'm complaining.  I have never had anything here that I didn't like.  In fact, I like this place a lot.  Whenever I go I feel like I'm eating dinner in the middle of a nightclub.  They have many delicious signature drinks.  I had one, but I can't remember what it was called.  I think it was some kind of daiquiri.    They have a lot of social events here, and I can see this being a cool little "after work" place to stop and get a drink.

This is a SUPER cute gift shop in Metairie.  The sell New Orleans "centric" gifts, jewelry and home decor that is in the same vein as Fleurty Girl. I stopped in here looking for a New Orleans charm bracelet and I was excited to discover that MJ'S carries them and has plenty of really cute New Orleans charms for under $15 each. Some of my favorites included a shot gun house, Roman candy cart, K&B sign and the Rosenberg's girl. Really unique stuff that any local is sure to love.  They also sell a lot of things to do with the Saints and pretty much Fleur de Lis anything. If you are looking for a cute gift, this is a fabulous place to start.

I was here when I was having my Roux Carre adventure and after hearing raves, I knew Splendid Pig was going to be my lunch choice.  I got the Pork-a-mein, which is their version of Yakamein. This is hot a dish with an egg, noodles, and meat all served in a broth. The pork was flavorful and the egg was a nice touch. It was cooked over easy, so it oozed into the rest of the dish, which I liked. While it wasn't the greatest version of this dish I have had in my life, I enjoyed it and I wouldn't hesitate to order again (although, I really want to try their Banh Mi).

Honestly, it's a daiquiri shop on Bourbon and all that entails.  We stopped in here one night during/after French Quarter fest and it was pretty dead, all things considered. The bartender was really nice and I think that we just had beer or something.  They do, of course, have their famous frozen daiquiris, if that's your thing. Of course this is the type of place that caters to 90% tourists, so it is what it is.

Judge me all you want, but I had a really good time here.  This is a cute little piano bar that does a good job of getting the crowd going. We stopped in here after the Yelp awards looking for some good music and to have fun. There was a "washboard" player who pulled me on stage so I could dance around like a dope and play his washboard. They play a lot of classic piano type songs like Billy Joel and some music you can dance to as well. I know that this place is more of a tourist hang, but I had a blast here and I wouldn't hesitate to return if I was in the mood for something a little bit different. I almost prefer it over Pat O's piano bar because this spot encourages dancing.

Actually not terrible for fast food in the middle of a casino.  We were in Harrah's enjoying the sights and the smoke free air, when we decided that we could definitely eat. Where else but Fudrucker's, open 24/7? I got a bacon cheeseburger and onion rings and maybe I was just hungry, but I found it to be really good for fast food! The service was super fast (and yes, there was a line!)   If I was hungry at the casino, I would definitely swoop into this place again. At least it's not a buffet!

I recently needed two tires replaced on my car and the first place I decided to go to get them was firestone.  They are always extremely helpful and friendly.  Not only were my tires replaced with ease, but they gave me a warranty on them, in case I get a flat or have a blowout and need a tire replacement.  They make the stressful situation of needing new tires a lot less stressful with their knowledge and the ease of which everything is handled.  Highly recommended and I would definitely return for future help.

This neat market has always been a favorite of mine, especially since it is open on weekend evenings and is only a few steps from the best music clubs on the block.It's the perfect spot for local artists and designers to sell their wares and I have known quite a few people who have had sale tables here.  The vendors here sell all types of things from jewelry to hair accessories to housewares. About a year ago, I was excited to find a small handmade hat here that is a perfect costume accessory once parades and festivals roll around.  Please note: a lot of the vendors do not want pictures of their wares taken, so be sure to ask if you want to send a picture to someone with a gift idea. I spotted some hand painted coasters here, that I thought a friend would like, but the vendor didn't want me taking pictures. Totally understood and worth noting.

Really good lunch specials. I usually get the fried chicken and corn grits. The serving is usually way more than a lunch portion and I always have left overs. Although Zea is a chain, it's still a good place to stop for lunch.  I feel bad for writing such a short review, but there really is nothing more to say about the place!

I have been a Fleurty shopper for years and I am always impressed with the products and service at this shop.  I was recently in the market to pick up some NOLA themed gifts for an out of town friend, so of course Fleurty Girl was my first stop. I wasn't in the market for t shirts, because buying clothes for other people can sometimes be tricky, so the girl working helped me on finding some other gifts that my friend would like. I got a few New Orleans themed candles, a tumbler and some stationary that my friend is sure to love. I was able to construct an entire New Orleans gift basket with the goodies I found here.  Fleurty Girl is your "one stop shop" for all things New Orleans and you are sure to find something that the New Orleans lover in your life will like.

"Some girl came in here and now we're on Yelp!"  That's what the bartender said to me when I told her that I had recently heard about this dive through a friend of mine. That friend and the girl who put Pete's on Yelp are one in the same. I have Holly G. to thank for this latest discovery.  What an awesome place! Totally unassuming bar located in the middle of a neighborhood. So unassuming, in fact, that one of the people I went with once lived 2 blocks away on the same street and had no idea it was there. It's like a secret clubhouse! It doesn't even have a sign!  Really cool people and the bartender is really nice and friendly. Loved the jukebox. Got in there and played a little Beatles and Elvis. Yeah, it was that kind of night. There weren't a lot of people in there and it wasn't super smoky so that's also a big plus.  Hours vary depending on the crowd. The bartender said sometimes they will close at midnight and sometimes they will close later depending on how many people are in there. I will definitely be back!

I had a date here once!  Sorry Scott S.  But, seriously!  I danced and everything!  This place is amazing.  How is it I had forgotten about it until now?  It's along the lines of Irvin Mayfield's as far as music and ambiance goes.  Never been there?  Allow me to explain.  The atmosphere is fantastic.  Really upscale and nice. Comfy seats, a good crowd and good music. You don't feel out of place in nice jeans, but trust me, dress up.    Jeremy Davenport plays here every Thursday, Friday and Saturday.  His shows start at 5:30 on Thursdays and 9 on Fridays and Saturdays and it's always a good time.  Sure, the drinks aren't cheap, but it's almost as if they were it would bring the place down, you know?  Like... if you take a girl out to dinner and she orders a salad, it's almost like, "What's the point?".  Ok, I'm rambling.  Do you like cool music, like The Rat Pack and big band stuff?  Do you like to dance?  Well, then get to the Davenport!

I do not make it to this fantastic music hot spot nearly enough. That's a real crime considering that I have never had a bad time here.  Most of the time there is a cover because there is an awesome band playing, but this is one of the few places where I actually don't mind paying a cover. The drinks are pretty cheap and the crowd is so fun. When I was in here there was a band playing that was a nice mix of all kinds of characters. The crowd had a good time dancing along to the music and the atmosphere was just happy.   I can't wait to go back!

I mean...ok. Yeah. Um...sure.  Miracle on Fulton doesn't really do it for me. Am I missing something? It's basically Celebration in the Oaks with a lot less celebrating. It's free, so that's good but it's nothing overly special. It's nice for what it is, but a little cheesy. I'm not a "fake snow/colored tree" kinda girl. This is Louisiana. Give me a fake green tree with zero snow and that' fine. It's a nice place to visit, but if you have seen this attraction one year, you have basically seen it every year.

The crazy thing is that I come to this Winn Dixie fairly regularly, but I always forget to check in! Hence my belated review.  This store is okay. It's not really my first choice when I am looking for something  grocery wise in the area. Some of the stuff here can be a bit overpriced and they often don't have what I am looking for. If you are looking for fancy beer or cheese, skip this place and head over to Rouses.  I have found the staff pretty friendly, but during the day they don't keep a ton of registers open during the day because the crowd that comes in is smaller.

Time for an update and I'm bumping them up a star.  The place is still packed, but it's not OVERLY packed as I remember. Everything is neatly organized and I loved the extensive selection of vintage hats in the back. The staff is super friendly and nice and very welcoming. Here you will find dresses and clothes from every era- 40's and 50's to 90's. You are sure to find something that will suit you here.  Be sure to check in the back for wedding and prom dresses.

Compared to some of the other cemeteries in the area, this cemetery seems pretty "low key" and unassuming. It doesn't have a lot of fancy monuments. It doesn't have tourists walking through and taking pictures to bring home. It's just a nice cemetery to walk through and admire on a nice day.  The one or two times I have been here the big gate hasn't been open and you have to work your way in through a small rusted gate that's on the side. A lot of the graves here are pretty old and while some are falling apart, a lot of them are kept up nicely.  It's not a "destination" spot, but it's definitely worth a look.

I've driven across this bridge by accident a few times. I'm not super familiar with the area and I figure my intended destination is on the other side of this bridge and it rarely is.  On the occasions that I have crossed this bridge on purpose, it hasn't been all that bad, even though sometimes people drive like maniacs and I'm convinced that I am going to go off the side, even though that's impossible. The bridge definitely does need some work. Teneha hit the nail on the head when she called it "rickety" and whenever I cross it, I half expect the whole thing to come tumbling down. I mean- if there is a big truck on the bridge, the whole structure shakes and shifts. Yikes!  This isn't a bad bridge, but I'm glad I don't have to cross it regularly.

This was the perfect place for a quick iced coffee stop when I was running around in the area and in need of caffeine.  The shop is small and located behind New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood and can be tricky to find if it's your first time. The barista was friendly and the coffee was really good. A large cost a little over $3, which is a good price point for the area. I'm not usually a big beignet person, but chocolate beignets intrigue me, so I will probably be back.

H&M is really nothing special. It's cheap clothing at a cheap price. I don't know why so many locals got so excited about this place. I guess it's just because it's new. Meanwhile, if you wanted to, you could just go shopping on the H&M website. But uh...I guess people didn't realize that.  H&M is located in a prime spot in downtown New Orleans, and to me, it just seems out of place. If I was a tourist, I wouldn't want to waste my time shopping at a huge national chain store, but I guess that's me.  The clothing style is basically modern casual tops, bottoms and dresses for girls. They have stuff for men and kids, but I honestly didn't check that stuff out when I went. Honestly, you can find clothing that is just as nice or nicer at one of the little shops on Magazine St., and by shopping there you are supporting local business.

I like this Tuesday Morning a lot. It's big and they offer the typical home decor type of stuff.  On this day, I was here looking for a housewarming gift for a relative and the woman working was able to help me locate some bar stools that will be perfect for the new place. I like that everything here is neatly organized- it made it very simple to find what I want. Also, because we are heading into the fall season, they have a nice selection of fall items and even some stuff out for Christmas. I will definitely return to pick up some more house stuff, especially when my kitchen remodeling is done.

I love Baskin Robbins when I want a specific treat.  I don't really go for the ice cream, itself.  Honestly, it's a smidge overpriced and blue bell is just as good and cheaper.  I love to get the cappuccino drinks here.  Get them without the whipped cream, if you are interested in cutting out a few calories.  That's just a good life rule...always go "no whip".  Anyway, they also have awesome ice cream cakes.  I had one for my birthday (chocolate chip) and it was great!  If you sign up for the birthday club, you get a free scoop of ice cream on your birthday and a discount on an ice cream cake for your birthday, too!  I've been a member since I was a kid.

I seem to always pass this place on weekends and hear fantastic music flowing from this bar but it is usually so packed (lucky them!) that fighting a crowd just doesn't appeal to me when there are so many other options.  I was able to stop in here when a friend and I decided we were in the mood for sake. I really liked it here. There was a small band (a singer and her accompaniment) playing when we sat down and looked over the drink menu. They have a HUGE selection of cold sake. I'm not usually a fan, but I tried one that was a little sweet and fruity and I was pleasantly surprised by it. They have such an extensive collection of sake and Japanese beer that you are bound to find something to enjoy, no matter what your tastes.

This place takes the headache out of banking. Always in and out really quickly. Knowledgeable staff will take care of whatever you need. When making transactions, I've never had to wait in line longer than 5 minutes.

Storyland is a really cool addition to City Park.  It's all of the fairy tales comes to life! There is a pirate ship, Cinderella's carriage, a princess castle and much more. I loved going here as a kid and I still have my special "key" that I was given so that I could hear the story of each special character.   Be sure to call ahead and see if they are open before you go, because the hours seem to be odd and I think that on certain days they close earlier than on other days and they close for inclement weather, etc.

Uh...ordering drinks took forever because the two bartenders can't handle the crowd and someone's dog peed on the floor RIGHT IN FRONT OF ME.  The owner of the dog made no move to clean it up.  Disgusting.  If you are going to bring your dog out, please make sure the thing is properly trained.

Suzette's calls itself a "romantic boutique" and you will definitely find all that that phrase would entail here.  This is a great place that sells everything a woman would need to feel her best and sexiest.  They carry lingerie, including fantastic honeymoon lingerie (white robes, slips and nighties).  They also carry various "fun" outfits, stockings, makeup and the like.    I was amazed by the amount of Halloween costumes this place has!  Everything from the "sexy" looks to the more elaborate.  They carry all sizes and they have a fantastic selection.  The staff is really helpful with anything you may need, and will help with fittings, if you would like a second opinion on a certain outfit.  They also carry what I will refer to as "personal" items.  Just head to the back and go behind the curtain.

This isn't a bad place.  They serve salads, burgers and cheese fries.  It's pretty much a few steps up from bar food, but that's not a bad thing.  The staff is very efficient and attentive.  When I went, I got a burger.  It wasn't anything overly special, but I liked it.  This would be a good place to come before you head out for a night out, as the place is right next to a bar (and also HAS a bar) and the food is well priced.

Oh my God! I had seriously forgotten about my experience with American Taxi until John's review!  During YSB we decided to take a cab to the event on St. Claude in order to be safe. Well, driving might have been a better idea. The driver we had was INSANE! He was speeding and running red lights and swerving in and out of lanes. It was seriously scary. They are getting two stars because I made it to my destination in one unharmed piece.  From now on, I will ONLY cab with United. Every other cab company I have ever experienced has been sub par.

First of all, I want to start by saying I don't know why I do this to myself. I once again ended up at a bar on Bourbon St. Gee, I wonder how it went.  Well, it sucked. It was Razzoo's without the charm. The music was pretty good and the shot girl was super nice, but the guy on stage who was pumping up the crowd needs to work on his act. It wasn't really entertaining. Of course, in places like this, you gotta take what you can get.  So, why the two stars?? Uh... $6.75 for a beer is the reason. It was Abita Amber, not some fancy import. I know it's the quarter, but come on.

Stopped in here for a bit during French Quarter Fest. The bartender was really nice and I liked that all of the doors were open letting fresh air into the place.  I didn't stay long, but they do seem to have a nice selection of absinthe and the bartender sounded like she knew what she was talking about when someone asked about them. The decor is a little grimy, but it's not terrible for a FQ spot.

This is such a cool hangout for beer lovers.  Not only can you get delicious beer that is super fresh, but you can get NOLA brews that are only available in the tap room. It's a great excuse to spend an evening "taste testing" some of the best beers around.  The staff is super friendly and knowledgeable, and although the tap room itself it small, there are plenty of seats at picnic style tables. When I stopped in on Friday I tried the Pineapple Habanero IPA, which is a beer with a little spice to it (and a tap room exclusive) and I also had the Prytania Porter, which was dark and delicious.  The beers are constantly rotating, so I will definitely be back to see what they are going to brew next.

I guess I'm old fashioned when it comes to banking, but I like to deal with humans. I am not a fan of dealing with a machine when I have to make a deposit. I know, I'm weird and I'm living in the stone age.  As a result, I rate banks on how fast the lines move and how quickly and I can get in and out of the bank. The lines here move quickly and the tellers are great. I was here on an weekday afternoon and there weren't a lot of people in line and the two tellers who were working did a great job at getting everyone through in a timely manner. I was just here to make a deposit, so I wasn't doing anything earth shattering, but my needs were handled with ease and I can't ask for much better than that.

This was more of a 3.5 star experience.  A friend and I stopped in here 2 days after Christmas for a quick lunch. The place was dead, except for one or two other tables. We were here for the sushi, so we looked over things as we waited on our drinks. That's one strange thing about this restaurant: they serve burgers and sandwiches and they serve sushi. It's like the owners weren't sure what they wanted the place to be.  Anyway, we ordered the Philly roll, the Metry roll and the Rainbow roll. After we ordered we had to wait a really long time. Normally this wouldn't be a big deal, but there was no one here and we felt that the wait was way too long considering the place was dead. When the food finally came, it was pretty good. My favorite was the Metry roll because it had a bit of spice to it which gave it a nice kick. The other two rolls were pretty good, but nothing spectacular.  I might come back, but I am going to skip the sushi next time. There are better places in Metairie with more sushi selection and tastier rolls.

I'm not sure how to feel about this place. On one hand, the clothing is gorgeous. On the other hand, I felt less than welcome when I shopped here.  I was in here looking around and hoping to find some new clothes for my New Year wardrobe. I was dressed down, having spent the entire day running errands and finishing Christmas shopping. Upon walking in, the woman working kind of looked me over and didn't say "hi" or anything. However, I did notice that she greeted other customers. I didn't think much of it and I just looked around as I normally do, but I did find it kind of weird.  The clothing here is lovely and they have a wide selection of things from casual to dressy. I saw a lovely red dress that I am actually considering purchasing just so I have it for any fancy event that might come up. The clothes are a little pricier, but I can tell that they're worth it because the quality is outstanding.  Because they're located in old Metairie, I would recommend dressing up a little when shopping here. Otherwise, you're on your own as far as help is concerned.

I stopped in here while doing some last minute Christmas shopping and I just love the vibe!  This is a shop that features gifts by local artists. A lot of it has a "New Orleans" theme, but nothing is gaudy or tacky like some other shops. While browsing, I happened to find some oysters and a voodoo doll toothpick holder made by Yelp's very own Re! It's always cool finding her art out in the world. Although I didn't buy anything on this go round, I did see a lot of things that will make fantastic gifts and I will be returning to spend my money. The owner was really friendly and asked if I needed help finding anything, which I always appreciate.

Who doesn't love a little bling?  This place is heaven for anyone who loves something shiny and loves to match their necklace to their top. As others have said, everything here is organized by color and while they have purses and clothing, I always go for the jewelry. One of my favorite spots for costume jewelry is So Good, but Charming Charlie is a close second.  I stopped in here with the intention of just looking around, but of course that never happens and I ended up getting some cute pink earrings that will go great with any summer ensemble. Another thing I love about CC is you can get hair accessories here as well- they have a nice little selection of tiaras for your wedding or everyday tiara needs.  True, the jewelry isn't the greatest quality in the world, but if it falls apart or you lose something you won't feel terrible about it, because it's all pretty cheap.

We were in the area when we decided to stop in here and grab a bite to eat. The setup here is pretty simple: you order what you want at the counter and you wait at a table. I like that they have dishes to choose from or you can just build your own, if you desire. I decided to keep it simple and I got a salad that was big and packed with olives, cucumbers, tomatoes, feta and onions. It was great and was filling without being heavy and I especially liked the vinaigrette that it was topped with. David had the spaghetti and meatballs, which he said was delicious.  This restaurant also has a really nice beer selection, so I was pleased that I was able to enjoy a nice IPA with my meal. The dishes are well priced, the food is good and the staff is friendly. I'll be back.

We stopped in here to see one of the cover bands that frequently play the Metairie bar scene. It's not a bad place. Legends is pretty big and gets pretty packed when a band is playing. The bartenders are quick to get drinks distributed, even with a large crowd. The sound for the music isn't all that wonderful, but for a bar it's pretty good.  I wouldn't mind checking this place out on a "slower" kind of night.

What do you get when you cross a bike shop with an art gallery? Apparently you get Lil Deb's Snow World.  I had zero clue that this place existed until David's aunt suggested we check it out. It's literally located in the back of a bike shop/art gallery right on Lafayette. We walked through and ordered, which was easy enough. I got the strawberry cheesecake snowball, just to mix it up a bit. I really liked it- the ice was nice and fine and they were really generous with the juice.  There are a few seats inside and there is a picnic table outside, so that you can eat your treat on site. They also have other snowball stand basics such as nachos, pickles and things like that.

I walked by this place tonight and I remembered that it's been my "to review" pile for awhile now. Famous Door is pretty cool- they have nicely priced drinks, they usually have a band playing and the majority of the place is well-behaved tourists. The few times I've been in here I've gotten the house drink which is a sugary concoction of which I can't remember the name. I do remember that there is plenty of seating near the door if you want to people watch or make a quick escape. I would hang out here again.

I usually don't review parking lots, because if you've been to one you've been to all of them. I'm reviewing this one mainly to say that if you park here and you are going to GW Fins (and other surrounding "nice" restaurants, I'm sure) you can get your parking validated and park here for free.  The staff here was all women on the night that I went, and I thought that was pretty cool. They were extremely fast and efficient, and while it wasn't the busiest night of the week, I appreciated it because I have been in situations where I feel like I am waiting forever for them to get my car for me and there is no one else there.  The lot is in an area that is relatively safe and it wasn't a far walk from the lot to GW Fins.

It's a Wal Mart, so if you've been in one, you've been in most.  I don't "do" Wal Mart. I can take the crowd. I can't take the chaos. There is too much going on all at once and it gives me anxiety. But alas, sometimes you must venture into the deepest depths of the scariest places on earth to get something that you need to live.  They have good deals on groceries and they have just about anything you could ever want here. The only drawback in the super long lines and the slow cashiers. I mean, seriously. Wasn't there a time where cashiers put a little hustle into the checkout? Oh well.

I didn't even know that this spot was check in-able until I saw someone review it. I guess I should have known.  I have spent so much time at Latrobe Park and I find it to be one of the hidden gems in the city. Located right outside the French Market, it's the perfect spot to sit and enjoy a nice day or munch on beignets. I like the the area is "sunken" (for lack of a better term), so you are kind of hidden away when you are sitting on the benches under the trees.  I kind of think the term "park" is generous when describing this little spot. It's more of a sanctuary where you can sit and enjoy the day away from the rest of the crowd of the Quarter.

Good Lord. Parking in this area on a Saturday is a beast!  Pretty cool little place. The large ice coffee is really large. I like that they have a "bar" area where you can sit and hang out. The only real con about this place is it's SUPER busy and the line is pretty long when you are waiting to get coffee. They do have a lot of beverage and pastry choices, so that makes up for it.

Oh my gaaaaah! Talk about retro dress heaven!!  I stopped in here with a friend, after he mentioned that this place is a "must" for any retro lover. They carry a wide selection of "Stop Staring!" dresses, which are all  amazing. If you are into the whole 50's retro look, this is the place for you.   There is a wide selection of retro dresses in a lot of different sizes. They vary from what I would call casual swing dresses to fancier form fitting wiggle dresses, in both solids and prints. I am only knocking off a star because the dresses are a little steep, though I understand this is the dress manufacturer price.  I kind of wonder if past reviewers. went into the store, or just went by what they saw in the window, because if you are a guy, they also carry a wide selection of suits of all kinds at very good prices. In fact, I would say that they have more men's suits than ladies dresses! You are sure to find something amazing.  Bonus points: they are open late every night of the week (close at 11pm!).

The Kingpin is a cool place to catch the Saints game, or catch a band when they have one.  They have an extensive beer selection and the crowd is always nice and friendly.  The place does tend to get crowded on weekends.  One huge complaint: the smoke in this place is insane, even if there aren't a lot of people in here.

I'm actually kind of honored to be the first to review this awesome store! In a world of Home Depots and Lowes, this nice family owned store will make you feel good about shopping local.  I recently had to stop in here because my dad was working on something that he needed a certain part for. We have always gone here for our hardware needs, so he called ahead and had them set it aside, so I just had to go and pick it up. The owner is always sure to give me a really personal experience whenever I go in and he will usually ask what I'm working on or what I have planned for the part I'm buying.  The store itself is nicely organized and the prices here are just as good, if not better than the big name stores. Also, this is where I go whenever I need a brake tag. Just pull your car around to the side and you will be in and out in no time. I have never had to wait in any kind of long line and I have never had any problems getting a tag here.

Smoothie King is a must. It's now a national chain but did you know that it all started in Kenner, of all places? Pretty neat piece of trivia.  My favorite thing to get here is the angel food. I swear, I have been getting these things since I was a kid and I don't think I have ever gotten anything else. It's a yummy blend of strawberries, bananas and other fruits. It's super sweet and makes for a great treat every now and then.  Smoothie King also has assorted supplements, power bars and drink mixes for all of you health freaks out there.

This was such a fantastic parade!  First of all, they are super generous with throws and the floats are GORGEOUS.  The highlight this year for me was definitely seeing Harry Connick Jr. and Cindy Lauper.  I was also excited to catch beads from the mayor himself: Mitch Landrieu!  I think I was more excited to see him than the actual "celebrities".  Ha.  I guess I'm a nerd.  Orpheus is definitely joining Muses, Tucks, and d'Etat as my "must see" parades of the season.

After passing this place for years, I FINALLY decided to stop in and check the place out. One Smart Cookie is a small bakery that sells different sugar cookies, petit fours and cakes. I just stopped in to look around and decided on one of the sugar cookies. It was really good with a lot of flavor and kind of reminded me of wedding cake, flavor wise (I think it was the almond).  I think that you can order specific cookies and cakes for special occasions. I'll definitely be back.

Metairie cemetery is probably the most beautiful of it's kind in the city.  There are gorgeous statues and structures and the graves themselves are really works of art.  A description just won't do it justice.  You must see it for yourself.  The cemetery is extremely well kempt and almost looks like a park with beautiful statues when you are visiting.  I encourage everyone to visit and see it in person.

When it's early morning (11am) and you are about to get into a full day of festing, you are gonna need a jump start. Enter Starbucks. We grabbed some coffee here on the way to French Quarter fest, and even though they were busy, the staff got our coffee to us quickly- and with a smile! The iced coffee is as good as any Starbucks. This spot is pretty small, and we were in and out so fast I didn't notice if there are places to sit, but if you are downtown for festing or shopping, this is a good place to get some brew.

I'm gonna be frank.  The only real reason to ever go to Vinnie's is if you want a burger, because they are actually really good.  I'd say it's probably a step up from usual bar food quality.  The burgers are always really big and cooked to order.  They actually serve a few different sandwiches, but in a place like this, a burger is probably your best bet.  I came here years ago and actually "hung out", but as of late, I only get take out from here, so I can't really speak to the quality of the place itself.  I do remember that they have a few pool tables, as well as tables and chairs, if you want to sit down and eat something.  Not a bad place to check out, if you are in the mood for some late night grub on the Westbank.

Over the years, I've had a few dealings with Ochsner Medical Center.  Things usually go smoothly (all things considered) and the staff and nurses are really nice and do their best to make your comfortable and make your stay enjoyable. Years ago I had to go to the ER with stomach issues and then my dad had to go with a cut and the wait wasn't long either time. They do their best to get to you as quickly as possible and make your stay as enjoyable as they can, under the circumstances.

This is a pretty good Wal Mart. You might be asking yourself "what qualifies a pretty good Wal Mart?" Well, for me it's a few things: I find what I need quickly and easily, the check out lines move fast and...that's about it.  This Wal Mart met all of my Wal Mart expectations. I stopped in on an afternoon that I happened to be passing by and needed some stuff. Walking through this place I realized that this Wal Mart is way bigger than the one in Harvey, which means they have more stuff to choose from. I didn't need much on this trip, just some basic makeup and some ear buds. I found both without hassle and without having to deal with too many other people (don't you hate when people block an entire aisle with their cart?). Believe it or not, I was in and out in less than 10 minutes. I was even super impressed when the check out woman in my line had to go price check something for another customer and another worker saw me waiting, waved me over to her line and checked me out WITHOUT PROMPTING. Pretty good, Wal Mart.

I'm going to keep this pretty short and sweet, because it's a delicate thing to review, yet I need people to know what kind of place this is.  My grandmother recently passed away at 95 years and she had made all of her arrangements through Lake Lawn, thanks to a long standing relationship with them. Thanks to those arrangements and our funeral director, this whole process was made much easier than it could have been. Jean (sp?) was SO sweet and wonderful throughout the entire thing and she made sure that all of our needs were met. The priest (Fr. Meyer) who performed my grandmother's funeral mass was perfect and we couldn't have asked for anyone better during this difficult time.  Lake Lawn made a really unfortunate process a lot more comfortable through their professionalism and gentility. We couldn't have asked for anything better and I would recommend them to anyone faced with a sudden (or not so sudden) death.

I've been back to Pho Tau Bay many times since my last review.  I've also tried other pho places.  Pho Tau Bay is definitely the best I have been to.  I can look past the lackluster decor and focus on the food and it really is amazing.   When I first reviewed, I was completely inexperienced when it came to pho.  I now realize that Pho Tau Bay is pretty fantastic and you really do get  A LOT for the (little) money you spend.  There is a reason that people will travel across that big scary bridge to get a taste of this wonderful food.

I was doing some work at the Jung Hotel over the course of two days, and I hit this coffee shop, located therein, 3 times.  I like this place, even if the coffee is a bit pricey. I can't complain as I know why it's pricey: 1) It's a coffee shop located in a brand new hotel. 2) It's located on Canal street and the foot traffic is off the walls.  The staff here is really great and they have all the fancy stuff as well as teas and I think they also have smoothies. Like any good coffee shop they have a nice variety of pastries and sandwiches and they have Abita Amber in their cold case, if you're looking to party.  I got their iced coffee which was VERY good- it was nice and rich and it had a lot of flavor. The space is small, but there are plenty of tables if you want to work and the nice big windows give you a good view of the world passing by outside.  If you're in the area this is a good place to stop for your caffeine fix.

This is a cool place, but WHY do you allow smoking??   I was told that I had to try the barbecue here, so we decided to stop in so I could get a taste. We sat at the bar, looked over the menu and started with some yummy fried pickles. I decided to get the pulled pork sandwich and mac and cheese (my barbecue favorites). Full disclosure: they did screw up my order at first, bringing out a brisket sandwich, but they quickly corrected the problem and I was well on my way.  The sandwich was really good- the pork was tender and smoky and had a lot of flavor without needing sauce. The mac and cheese was out of this world! It might be some of the best mac and cheese I have ever had; it's definitely up there.  Honestly, I wouldn't dine in again mainly because of the cigarette smoke. There weren't a lot of people in here, but it was a little overwhelming and took away from the entire experience for me. I wouldn't hesitate to drop in and get an order to go, however.

If you're looking for a quick Mexican lunch, and you don't feel like fighting the crowd at Juan's, than La Carreta is the place for you.  I stopped in here for lunch mid-day on a weekday and the place was pretty empty. Free chips and salsa was dropped on the table and I looked over the menu. I was in a burrito kind of mood so I decided to get the build-it-yourself burrito with carnitas. It also comes with your choice of salad or tortilla soup, so I got the soup.  First of all, the soup was fantastic. I never think to order soup at Mexican restaurants, but this one didn't disappoint. The burrito was great as well, it was packed with carnitas and other things and it had a nice kick to it. I also had it topped with a green sauce that has just enough spice. The burrito and soup came to $12 and I took half of the burrito home, so I consider this a complete lunch success!  This spot is great and satisfies the Mexican craving. It's not super authentic, but if you're looking for a burrito fix, this is the spot.

I've been a fan of the original outdoor art market on Frenchmen for a long time and they now have a second location on Decatur.  Packed with tons of local art, this is the perfect place to pass through if you are looking for a unique gift or art piece and you want to support a local artist. I really like that the artists are personally there with their booth so you can ask them questions about their art or see the process of it actually being made.

Not so much a "club" as it is a fancy casino bar.  I don't know what goes on during the week, but on Friday and Saturday night at 10, they turn the music up and have gogo dancers.  They also have a VIP section, which is just a little quartered off section of the club.  There's really no where to dance, so I think that calling this place a "club" is being generous, but it isn't a bad place to hang out if you have some friends in the casino and you just want to get a drink.

If you are into art that's a little strange, interesting, and different, than look no further than Funeral Gallery and, more specifically, Vinsantos' hand made art dolls.  There's a lot of different art by different artists here, but Vinsantos' dolls caught my eye. Like something out of a Tim Burton fantasy and completely hand made, these dolls are molded with big eyes, beautiful colors, gorgeous clothes and reside in a handmade case for display. The dolls aren't cheap, but the detail that has clearly gone into them really is something to behold. If you aren't ready to commit to an actual doll, they have small prints of different dolls that are available for $20 each.  Other art goes along with the "Halloween all year" type feel of the place. There are large portraits of Frankenstein, The Bride of Frankenstein, and Vampira among others. All of the art here is very different from other galleries and appeals to a certain type of person, namely the type of person who wishes to adorn their home with conversation pieces rather than the same old "picture on a wall".

Santos is the newest incarnation at this spot at 1135 Decatur. It seems there have been A LOT of different bars here over the years, but since this bar is owned and operated by the same people who run The Saint on St. Mary, hopefully it will stick.  We were here semi-early on a Saturday night and it was pretty quiet. I do like the vibe here- it's a little spooky and cool and there's a nice dance floor where I assume they will have music. They have some good local beers on tap, which is always a plus for me and the bartender was friendly. The bar seems a lot nicer than when other businesses were here- I'm not sure if they have done a full on renovation, but I like what they've done with the place. I'm excited to see what type of events they host here in the future.

I have a mission this year: track down all of the snow ball stands on the Westbank and try/review them. I'm no hero and you don't have to thank me. I'm doing the Lord's work.  Snow World was my first stop and this is a cute little stand that used to be called "Van's Snowballs" when I was a kid. We came around 7 and there was a nice little line. I ordered a 12oz strawberry cheesecake for a little over dollar. The ice was finely shaved like any good snowball and there was plenty of juice. The flavor itself wasn't overly strong with the "cheesecake" part of the flavor, but it was very sweet and I enjoyed it. Even though there was a long line and multiple orders, the folks in the stand got everyone through pretty quickly.  Bonus points: they have a "clear" bubblegum flavor for those of you who like bubblegum, but don't want to turn your teeth blue.

Ahh. Being in this place brought back a lot of memories. This used to be where the Westbank Bennigan's location was and I came here all the time as a kid. Oddly enough, not much has changed on the inside. Sure, all of the Bennigan's knick knacks are gone and replaced with Mexican decor, but the layout is exactly the same.  I have discovered that I am pretty easy to please when it comes to Tex-Mex type food: basically as long as it's cooked well and has cheese on it, I'm happy. I was here on a night that I happened to be craving a serious burrito, so that's what I got. The burrito platter comes with a good sized burrito topped with tomato sauce and cheese with rice and lettuce, tomato, guacamole and sour cream on the side. I was really impressed, especially considering this platter is under $10. Everything had a lot of flavor and although the rice could have been cooked a little longer, I still enjoyed it.  The staff was friendly enough and everything came out pretty quickly, especially considering we were here during the dinner rush. I will definitely be dining here again.

Time for a review update! Wisp has worked their magic yet again! My laptop (the same one from the last review) was having charging issues again and, sure enough, it needed a new charge port. Also, I had had a cracked screen for well over a year and had them fix that as well, just as long as they were going to be doing things with it. Well, in a day they fixed the port and the screen and my computer is back to work! Yay! They always do such a good job here and I would never bring my computer anywhere else. I use my laptop for my job, so downtime is a "no go" for me. Thankfully, they work fast at Wisp!  The staff is friendly, the work is exceptional and the prices are fair.

NOLA is a fantastic local brewery run by kind people who know their way around the hops. Really nice facility with a room full of all of the NOLA beer taps so that you can treat yourself to free samples every Friday at 2 during the brewery tour.

It's a bookstore. It gets the job done, doesn't it?  I really like B&N because they always seem to have whatever I am looking for, no matter how obscure it is. Really. You can be looking for a book that hasn't been in print since the 80's and it's very likely that this place will have at least one copy of it.   They also have a really big selection of magazines here. I was able to find Burlesque Bible, a magazine that is on the more expensive end and that I hadn't been able to locate anywhere else in town. I thought I was going to have to order it online and pay shipping when I spotted it here. Fantastic!  If you are looking for something specific, in the reading material department, this should definitely be your first stop.

It was a gorgeous Sunday when David suggested we take the ferry to the French Quarter, have lunch and sight see. It was the day of the Barkus parade and we knew there would be a lot of people out and about. I love this ferry. I don't utilize it all that much, but it's a great way to see the city and take some pictures (if that's your thing). On a clear day you can see St. Louis Cathedral as you ride across. As others have said, it costs $2 per person each way and they don't give change which is a bit shady. I get that it would take time to give everyone change, but it's still a little weird.  On a nice breezy day, a ferry ride is a great way to get to and from the city and you don't have to worry about driving, which is always a plus.

This is a really cute shop and if you're into the "old timey" kind of decor like I am, you are sure to love it.  Think back to the days of old metal signs, small gas stations, corner stores and soda shops and you will understand exactly what this store is all about. They offer a wide variety of "not so modern"-day items that are good conversation pieces and fun things to add to any collection. One thing that caught my eye was the hot air balloon mobile. I have no need for one, but I was tempted to get it just to add it to my home.  A few things are a little bit ridiculous and out there. I had to roll my eyes at the portraits of different generations of presidents playing poker- not exactly something I would want in my study. Other things are cool: they have some unique decanters, wall art, compasses, jewelry and much more.  If you're into things from "yesterday", this is a great place to visit.

I might have found my new uptown coffee house!    I was disappointed when Rue de la Course, on Magazine, closed and I was trying to figure out where I was supposed to get good coffee in the Uptown area, without having to drive all the way over to the Rue on Oak.  I found a new home at Mojo!  Not only does Mojo have a nice and cozy atmosphere, but their iced coffee is amazing.  I got a large and finished it in no time.  I wanted another, but I decided that I didn't want to be so caffeinated  that I could fly, so I opted against a second cup.  I will definitely be going back for this delicious coffee next time I am in the area.

Great place for window shopping, especially if you are trying to waste a little time waiting for a movie to start at the theater. Fantastic stores that are really nice with an upscale feel. There are a little expensive, but not too bad.   One complaint-man oh man do I hate the parking garage attached to this place. It is super narrow and has one of those "roundabouts" that get you from one floor to the next. I am always so scared that I'm going to hit the wall. So yeah, I'm a chicken, so I just end up parking in the lot right across the street in order to save my sanity.

What a fantastic company!  Recently, I needed my 16 year old sofa partially reupholstered and I also needed the reclining function fixed on one side. The owner came to the house, looked at the sofa, assessed what needed to be done and made the arrangements for the sofa to be picked up so that they could work their "magic".  After a little over a week, my sofa was ready and in excellent, like-new condition! Not only did they reupholster two cushions and fix the recliner, but they also added necessary padding to certain cushions as well as the arm rest. The sofa has never looked better and I couldn't be happier with the results!  I would highly recommend this company for their great communication, excellent service and good pricing.

I just started going to Dr. Connell after my other dentist retired. t Dr. Connell and his staff are fantastic.  Extremely friendly and personable.  The dental assistant who worked on me was very nice and was quick to explain things to me.

Ooh tasty!  I had had Chez Pierre pastries before at bridal shows I've worked, so they were definitely on my list of places to visit. David brought me here when we were in the mood for something sweet and the spot didn't disappoint.  I got a strawberry Napoleon and David got a huge piece of red velvet cake. My Napoleon was delicious with thick cream inside and big piece of strawberry. It wasn't overly sweet and it satisfied my sweet tooth nicely. I only wish that the crust on top had been a little flakier and easier to pierce with my fork- I ended up having to pick it off and eat it like a cracker. David's cake was big and easily big enough for two people, if you're looking to share.  They also have a full menu of Vietnamese food here, so you can get lunch along with your dessert, if you wish.

I can't believe that I have never reviewed this quaint little Magazine St. bakery. I believe the ownership changed hands a while ago, but I've always loved this place.  I was here today for quick work meeting and every meeting is better with yummy iced coffee and croissants. La Boulangerie has both along with cake, pastries, sandwiches, soups and much more.   There was a decent crowd for a Thursday lunch hour, but it wasn't terrible and everyone was masked up (pandemic-era review). My only complaint was that it was a bit warm inside, but I know how a.cs have trouble keeping up with the intense NOLA summers, so that wasn't a big deal.

New Orleans is full of different burlesque shows, troupes and acts.  In a sea of traditional burlesque, the Dirty Dime Peepshow stands out. Bella Blue is the producer and she never disappoints.    Edgy and fun, the Dirty Dime features seasoned performers, as well as new talent.  It is so much fun, and if you are a Burlesque "virgin", you will definitely cut your teeth quickly here.

During the Yelp event at Pearl, I decided to duck into this neat little Farmer's Market and see what they had to offer. What I found was one more reason why Mid City is so great. This small market offers a whole variety of things such as fresh fruits and vegetables and fresh caught seafood. The woman working the seafood table mentioned that the shrimp and crabs she had were caught the day before- it doesn't get much better than that.  I didn't get anything this time, but I this is definitely a neat little addition to the area, especially when the weather is nice and you are headed to a wine tasting at Pearl on a Thursday. All of the vendors are local, so you are supporting local businesses by shopping here and I found them all to be friendly.

I was super impressed by this PJ's! I just stopped in for a quick coffee and a croissant, but considering it's in the Quarter, I was happy that it was only $6. Don't you hate places that upcharge, due to location?  This shop was following all proper Covid precautions and Julie (I think that was her name) was super nice. Stop in, if you're in the area!

This is easily one of the best Dollar Trees in the area.  I stop in here regularly to get cheap flowers for my mom's grave, which is right around the corner (the grave is outside, so super-nice silk flowers would be a waste). They always seem to have the cutest accessories for sale and the last time I was here I got some St. Patrick's Day socks (on sale the first week of January) and a gaudy Shamrock thing to stick on my Irish mother's grave, which I'm sure she appreciated.  The staff is always nice and I always find whatever I need. Big win!

Well, this place just came out of nowhere!  We were waiting to get lunch at Blue Giant, so we popped in here for some coffee while waiting to be called. This is such a cute shop in a nice developed part of Magazine St.  The space is bright with big windows and there is plenty of space outside for sitting. The shop is right next door to a work out studio and right across from Claret, so you are going to have a lot of people to mingle with.  The coffee I had was great and I was delighted to see that they offer a full menu of snacks and sandwiches, that are sure to keep you satisfied. They also offer free wifi, if you're looking to get some work done.

Yakuza House is putting a twist on what you think sushi is. You aren't going to find typical rolls here. You're going to get hand rolls that are made right in front of you, sandos, and other delicious food made fresh by the chef.   The place is small, so you're going to need reservations, but it's definitely worth it. I sat at the bar, so that I could watch Chef work his magic. I had salmon belly nigiri, a sando, and the Nibbles hand roll set, which came with three kinds of hand rolls--salmon, bay scallop and blue crab, which were served fresh when I was ready for them.   If you sit at the bar, the chef will keep an eye on your plate and serve you the hand rolls as you need them. There are only four tables in the entire restaurant, so don't expect a huge place.   I really think Yakuza House is going to be the next hot restaurant on the scene, so get in while you can.  I wrote about this spot for Offbeat Magazine's Offbeat Eats column. Check it out here: https://www.offbeat.com/articles/dining-out-yakuza-house/

Really, how can you give Jackson Square anything less than 5 stars?  When you talk Jackson Square, you are talking classic New Orleans. The majesty of St. Louis Cathedral and the statue of Andrew Jackson that are synonymous with New Orleans and the magic of the city. The artists selling their masterpieces, street musicians putting on a show and fortune tellers that will tell you what your future holds.   You know, when you get right down to it, the best parts of this city really are free. I love that you can just walk around and take it all in. Jackson Square is as good as it gets. It's the second thing that people think of when they think of New Orleans and we wouldn't have it any other way.

Bayou Beer Garden is a good place to go see some live music or comedy.  I agree with Shannon's comment that the main draw is the huge patio.  The bar itself is basically an old house that has been converted and the whole "backyard area" is where the deck and patio is.  This is where bands perform.  It's well lit and has Christmas style lights for atmosphere.  Admittedly, I haven't been here in a really long time, but the last time I was here, the inside was really smoky.  This probably isn't a place I would go unless a band I really wanted to see was playing.

Take out only, and they have some outdoor seating, but unless you want to sit in the hot sun, your best bet is probably just taking it to go.   On the day I was here, they had a boudin special, so that's what I got. I got it with a side of potato salad and mustard greens. The boudin was really good, although I think I would have enjoyed it more if it was a little spicier. I always like my boudin to be on the spicier side.   The potato salad and mustard greens were perfect and balance out the sausage well. The process is pretty easy, you go to the window and order, and the food comes out pretty quickly. All of my food cost $11, so I'm not complaining. I will definitely be back; the food was great.  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here: https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

Long overdue update!!  Since my last review, smoking has been "outlawed" in bars, so that isn't an issue. The outdoor patio has its own bar with TONS of beer on tap- local and otherwise.   The vibe is fun and I love that there's a lot of space out there. There are big TVs that are great for game watching and the staff is friendly and fun. There's still the indoor area if that's more your thing, but the draw is that awesome patio/bar situation.  This spot is a Mid-City gem and I will definitely be visiting more often.

Thanks to Dennis G, who reviewed the Metairie location for reminding me that I owe this place a review.  Wow.  I can't believe I have never reviewed this place!  I seriously eat here probably once a month.  Now, Piccadilly isn't one of those places that you go to for a fancy dining experience, but the food is like home cooking to me, probably because I have been coming here since I was a kid.  I always get the dilly plate, which is an entree', two sides and a piece of bread for under 8 bucks.  You really can't beat that.  I usually get the fried catfish, mashed potatoes and gravy and broccoli with a soft roll.  It's always good and fresh and it always leaves me satisfied.  Also, I don't often get dessert, but when I do I get the chocolate pudding.  This place is pretty awesome.  I know there are people who have never been and would never want to try it, but this place reminds me of my childhood when I would go with my grandmother to lunch.  They also have take out, if you don't want to sit down and eat!

WOW. Why would anyone ever go to Acme?  Stopped in here for lunch on a Sunday afternoon. The restaurant was pretty empty, and we were seated and served quickly. We started out with an order of a dozen raw oysters. OUT OF THIS WORLD. Fat and fresh. Amazing and soo good. I probably could have gotten another dozen and called it a day.  For my entree, I got a hot sausage po boy. This came topped with blue cheese cole slaw and had thin cut french fries on the side. I really liked that the sausage was "pattie style". It made it way easier to eat and handle. It was delicious and full of flavor. We also decided to split an order of onion rings. Not only did they bring out a lot of rings, but they were huge and perfectly fried.  So, seriously. Why would you wait in line at Acme when Felix's has everything you need? Mine is just one more positive review to add to the pile.

I grabbed some post-Yelp event drinks here with Steve, and although the place was on the slower side on this particular night, I had a good time. The bartender was really friendly and I was happy to see that they offer Not Your Father's Root Beer, which I happily sipped on. I like that the bar is a little dark and somewhat tucked away just enough to make it feel like a hide out. I want to come back on a night that there are a few more people here and I would love to see a drag show.

Went tonight for "industrial" night at my friend Travis' suggestion.  Good bar.  Good crowd.  Good music.  I have seen a burlesque show here in the past, and the place was packed.  From what I hear, it is a lot how "Krystal" and "Dervish" used to be.  I can't speak to that, it was before my time.  I went and had a good time.

Morbid curiosity is what brought me here. I had passed this place tons of times and constantly wondered what it was all about. I had definitely asked myself more than once, "Why would a bar choose to have a toilet theme?" Well, I still don't know the answer to that question, but I finally made it here.  The place is a lot bigger than I expected and on this particular night the place was packed. Even though there were a ton of people here, the bartender was fast and friendly. There's a large space so there were people dancing and others just sitting at the bar chatting.  This is a cool little chill spot. I don't know if I'll be back. I feel like my question has been answered about this place, but I'm glad that I went once.

This is a fancy little bar located in the Windsor Court. A friend and I stopped in here to get a drink before heading out to dinner. I really like the nice upscale decor. It feels as if you are in someone's really nice home. They have a whole array of fancy cocktails, but instead of a cocktail, I just decided to get a beer. I really liked that there was a pianist playing "background music" as we chatted on one of the many sofas.  I would definitely love to go back here on a date, as I think it would be the perfect spot to start a romantic evening.

This is such a great rentable space with lots of light and big windows and mirrors. Most people rent this spot to practice dancing, but I recently had a photo shoot here it was the perfect area to convert into a quick studio.  They let you rent the rooms by the hour and I love the open area of the room, the abundance of natural light and all of the space we had to work with. The staff here has always been nothing but kind to me whenever I have found myself here. There is a small kitchen space downstairs with a few snacks and coffee, if you plan on being here for a while.

Probably closer to a 3.5.  I really like that this is a nice neighborhood coffee shop with outside seating. I was shocked at how packed it was at 11am. Really. It took me about 15 minutes from the time I ordered to the time I finally got my drink. It was nuts.  I ordered a mocha chip Mochassippi, which is basically their version of a frappuccino (which everyone knows, I'm sure). It was okay. Not as sweet as I was expecting, but all in all not bad.  The place is pretty loud inside, especially when there are a lot of people around, but you can reserve private rooms in the back for designated periods of time.  I'd go back, but probably after the morning rush.

Wow Carreta's, I'm actually kind of impressed.  We stopped into Carreta's on a Saturday for lunch and the crowd was pretty thin. The waitress took our drink order immediately and within just a few minutes of ordering our food (about 10 minutes) we had it in front of us. My first thought was, "Uh oh, we have a reheat situation on our hands.", but it wasn't reheated at all (at least from what I could tell.).  I decided to do the "create your own" with the shredded chicken quesadilla and the shredded chicken flautas (two per order). For a grand total of 8.20, this is probably one of the best lunch deals in the city. The quesadilla was perfect- plenty of cheese mixed in with the juicy chicken and seasoned perfectly. The flautas were out of this world. They were hot and fresh and I really enjoyed them and the shell had just enough crunch to it. The combination of both the quesadilla and the flautas made for the perfect lunch.  I would absolutely return and try more of what Carreta's has on the menu. I am eager to try their burrito plate!

You guys. This place. Wow.  Where did this restaurant come from? Was this always here? Why am I just now discovering it?!  This restaurant is incredible and completely New Orleans. There is an AMAZING view of the river and delicious food. We were just here for appetizers and the view and this place didn't disappoint in either department. We ordered the fried calamari and the bacon wrapped olives. The calamari was amazing and the serving was huge, plenty enough for two people. The bacon wrapped olives were different and good.  My only tiny complaint was that it took a while for a waiter to acknowledge us, but as soon as he did, he was quite attentive. This would be a fabulous place for a date night and I will definitely be back.

The Elks trucks parade is a classic and it's the perfect end to Mardi Gras. The crowds are always a lot more laid back at this parade than at other parades, the riders are always really generous with the throws, and while the "floats" aren't anything overly fancy, they get the job done.  I pretty much grew up on truck parades. The sounds of a truck's horn and the smell of exhaust will probably remind me of Mardi Gras for the rest of my life. For this particular parade, I like to just sit back and relax somewhere on St. Charles Avenue and just watch it pass as I enjoy the day.  The best part of this parade is that it seems to go on and on almost without end. It's really entertaining and it's one of the few parades where people aren't chomping at the bit to get some fancy throw- they just enjoy it for what it is.

I'm gonna start by saying that I am NOT crafty at all, so I can't really give a review from a "crafters" point of view.  Michaels is a really cool store that has everything (or close to it) that a creative type could ever want.  Paints, beads, markers, crayons, and clay are just a few things you can get here.  What I really like about this store is, if you have a kid, you could take them in here and let them pick out a fun activity for them to do.  They sell things that you can paint and decorate, like wooden cutouts.  They have coloring books and crafts of all types.  If you get a child started with this kind of thing early, they will be creative for life.  It's also a good idea to pick up colors and crafts for a kids party or rainy days when a child needs something to do.  Michael's also carries frames and things like that.  Like I said, I'm not a person who is really into crafts, but if I were, this would be my spot.

Wow, fancy!  This place is HUGE and is located right before the Causeway Bridge. Seriously. Don't accidentally cross the bridge.  I came here for a photo shoot and at first I was a little confused. I mean, the building itself isn't hard to miss, but there are a bunch of different parking garages and I wasn't sure which one to park in. I pretty much just picked one at random. It turned out that parking is super cheap (mine was free) so it all worked out.  The lobby is huge when you first walk in and you feel like you are in an expensive New Orleans hotel and not out in the 'burbs somewhere. It was pretty impressive. The room is small, but gets the job done. Nothing overly special, but clean and efficient.

What a gorgeous bar!  As soon as I walked into Vive, I knew it was high class.  The bar is beautifully lit with Vive's signature purple.  The bartenders were very friendly, as well.  I love that there is a nice lounge area on the inside part of the bar.  It would be a great place to enjoy happy hour.  Outside is lovely.  It's a hotel, so there is a small pool, as well as a patio with plenty of seating.  There is a beautiful garden surrounding the pool area that makes you feel as if you are on vacation in another city.  WIth the open patio you can enjoy the sun, or admire the night, after the sun goes down.  Vive is located just a few doors down from one of my favorite restaurants, Oceana, so I can definitely see myself getting a cocktail here before heading to dinner, one night.  A definite gem in the Quarter.

I hadn't been to this theater in years when I decided to stop in to see The Amazing Spiderman.  It was just as I had remembered with one major difference: the seats are now made out of a fancy fake leather (or maybe real leather?  I couldn't tell.  It was dark,) instead of the typical cloth.  At first I thought it would be pretty nice to have seats like that, but I had worn shorts on this particular day, and after a while my thighs began to stick to the seat.  I had to keep shifting because it was pretty uncomfortable.  Also, I know it's summer, but the theater was FREEZING.  It was a good 65 degrees in there and maybe even colder!
