Another reason I wish I hadn't worn shorts!  So, in conclusion, not a bad place to see a movie, if you are wearing pants.

This place is obviously family owned, which is fantastic.  The pizza isn't bad and they have beer on tap.  The staff is very attentive and eager to please.  My only complaint would be the prices.  I KNOW that it's a small place, so they have to make some profit, but the prices are a little steep and you feel like you are getting ripped off, unless you are ordering a large.   Definitely go, but know that you will be paying a little more for pizza than usual.

The same owners as the old Parasols.  HUGE place, delicious food and awesome atmosphere.  Great place to go see a game, because they have a huge projector screen.  I have only been twice, but both times I got a wonderful roast beef po boy.  You can even eat outside!   One star knocked off for not taking credit cards (although, I get why they don't...one less thing to worry about.).  I will definitely be going back!

I had never been to this place when my boyfriend took me to celebrate my birthday.  First of all, the atmosphere is wonderful and romantic.  The lighting isn't too bright or too dim, it's perfect for dates.  The food was exquisite.  I had no idea what to expect, but I got the salmon and I was blown away at how wonderful it was.  The wait staff was extremely attentive and helpful.  I would definitely love to go back someday.  The place isn't cheap, but it's worth spoiling yourself on a special occasion.

There are two things I love when it comes to coffee: PJ's iced coffee and not having to get out of my vehicle to obtain said iced coffee. This PJ's has both of those magical qualities.  So there I am, driving through the Da Metrys, when I decide that I could use a caffeine fix. Not only is there a shiny PJ's over yonder, but I drive up and discover that they have a drive thru. Bing! Oh, and it's 2 in the afternoon, so there's no line. Bing, again!  Not only does this PJ's serve up an icy cool treat on a warm day, but the staff is quick with your order AND bonus points because this PJ's has 2% milk. Who needs Starbucks?

Victory wasn't too bad, but after waiting a while to check this place out, I was left unimpressed.  Victory is really small and is really a bit of a dive in nice clothing.  I can picture coming here on a nice night out, but on the night I was here, it just felt like your average run of the mill bar.  When we received our drinks, the order was messed up not once but twice.  I understand that it was our waitresses first time ever waiting tables (that's what she told us), but on a busy Friday night, the wait staff should really know what they are doing and management should maybe not put the new girl on the floor.  Would I go back?  Yeah, if I was in the area, but I wouldn't really go out of my way.

This is a typical "greasy spoon" type of breakfast place.  The quality of the food here really depends on who happens to be working in the back when you get here. I usually get two eggs over easy, toast, bacon and hash browns. More often than not the eggs are cooked correctly, but there have been a few times where they have been under cooked and I've had to send them back to the kitchen.  They also have donuts and a few other pastries, but if you want them fresh you better get there in the morning.

We used this service Saturday night because the Uber app was being a pain and not working right. This is the exact same idea as Uber: tell them where you are and where you're going and they'll come get you. The wait is a bit longer because there aren't as many Lyft drivers in the city as Uber drivers, but the service is identical and you can tip on the app. Our driver was really nice and chatty, which made the ride through traffic from our hotel to our dinner destination a breeze. I would probably still opt for Uber, if given a choice, but Lyft is a good alternative.

This Reginelli's is conveniently located in the "social hub" (as I've begun calling it) of Poydras, where there is a nice selection of bars and different restaurants to choose from and the proximity to the Superdome can't be beat.  Some friends and I just wanted a quick snack, so we ordered a small pepperoni pizza (6) slices and it cost $9.33.  What I didn't understand was that a large pizza, which is 8 slices cost about $14.  A little over $4 for two more slices?  Seems odd, even if the slices are bigger than normal, but I digress.  The pizza was really good and the crust had a lot of flavor.  I will definitely be going back and trying some of their many specialty pizzas.

Last summer was the first time that I was able to make it back to Houston's since I had first eaten there, about a month before Katrina.  I was delighted to discover that it was better than ever.  When I first got there, I was told that there would be a 45 minute wait.  Instead, I ate with a friend at the bar and the mood was great.  Because we were sitting at the bar, we were served quickly and I already had my food when I was told that I could move to a table, if I wanted.  I went on a Friday night, and apparently this is a night that they have live music.  Or maybe it's every night.  My only complaint would be that the music was super loud for such a small place, so it was hard to talk.  Other than that, I would definitely go back.

I'll admit it.  I am a total bargain junkie/thrift store enthusiast.    This place is HUGE and packed with great deals.  Great place for new moms, because a lot of the baby clothes are brand new with tags (probably given as gifts and the baby outgrew them quickly).  I have found dresses, blouses, and tshirts here.    There is nothing wrong with shopping thrift, if you know what to look for.  The people who just see it as "second hand junk" don't have the "eye", as I like to call it.  I have found many awesome treasures here.

I think that this spot would have made more of an impression on me if I was more of a cocktail person.  We decided to grab a quick bite before heading over to a show. We sat at the bar and got a couple of drinks. We ordered the meat and cheese board to split. It was pretty good, but it didn't really do it for me. I think it was too simple, if that makes sense.  I think if I were to go back I would probably focus more on trying some fancy cocktails, rather than the food. The atmosphere is nice and the staff is friendly. I can see how it would be a cool spot to start the evening.

Mid City Yacht Club is a real gem of a place.  I had never been when a friend invited me here to check out the Mayweather fight.  I am so glad I discovered this place!  The people are really nice and it's a great sports bar.  They have 5 tv's behind the bar that are always showing 5 different games, whether it's football, baseball, or anything else you could possibly think of.  There is a big projection screen in the back of the place with plenty of seats and there is free food (meatballs, hotdogs, chips) on game days.  There is also a tv outside, if you don't feel like dealing with the smoke or huge crowds that like to gather here on game days.  I have to be honest, this is one of the friendliest places I've ever been to in the city.  I had never been here before and people seemed eager to introduce themselves and make me feel welcome.  A really great place to make friends and watch a Saints or LSU game.  WiFi password: yachtclub

The first time I went here, I was less than impressed.  It was packed, I couldn't find a seat and the people were kind of rude.    When my boyfriend suggested a few months ago that we check it out, I was hesitant.  It was kind of early, so we gave it a try.  We got to sit at the bar, which was a huge plus.  Then, it was time to order "munchies".  We got a yummy cheese plate and the "pomme fritas" (I think that's the spelling) with some Chimay from the tap.  It was fantastic!  I would definitely suggest going a little early, if you aren't into the crowded "bar" scene.  It's a really great little date place and a good place to start the night.

This is a dream store for anyone who is decorating their house or yard. They have a little bit of everything from chairs to sofas to fountains for the yard and lawn furniture. They have adorable mid-century couches that make me want to re-decorate immediately.  When I stopped in, I was on the hunt for a new patio umbrella. They have a great selection of colorful umbrellas for a good price. The biggest that I found was a large umbrella for $79, which I found to be a pretty good deal. Something else I like is that they have two kinds: the stand alone umbrellas and the ones that go in the table.  Everything here is well organized and staff is everywhere on the floor, in case you need help with something. You can also visit their website and see what the store has in stock which makes it convenient, if you don't want to make the drive to Kenner.
If this place really closed, that makes me sad.  They had a great patio and their Cinco de Mayo parties were always fantastic.

Balcony Bar has improved greatly since my last review. The crowd is MUCH improved thanks to an awesome door guy. The place gets a good crowd without being TOO crowded. There is no smoking (I know that there is no smoking in every bar now, but Balcony Bar has been no smoking for two years). And the best part is the beer- the owners have really made an effort to add a lot of local beer on tap which I am always a fan of. As a result of there being better beer, the place isn't as "fratty" anymore and you can actually sit down and have a conversation and not feel weird.  While Balcony Bar still isn't my first stop if I am looking for a good time, it's not a bar that I avoid as I once did.

I thought I had reviewed WWOZ!  I love this station and I have found myself listening to it more and more as of late. It just seems like there is nothing else good on non-satellite radio! They are always playing good music, local and otherwise and the live wire music calendar is a must.  If you aren't in NOLA, don't fret, you can listen to WWOZ on their iPod and Android app! They play a lot of good stuff during Mardi Gras, too and that is probably my favorite time of year to tune in.

A friend and I got some take out from this place last night.  We got a couple of crunchy rolls, a Philly roll and a tuna and avocado roll.  The rolls were good, but not great, and the Philly roll had a distinct "fish" taste.  Not a fresh fish taste, but an overwhelming "not so fresh" fish taste.  Also, the rolls were super small.  You would think that 4 rolls would be plenty of food for two people, but we were both still hungry at the end of the meal.  I doubt I would go back here.  If I was in Metairie and wanted sushi take out, I would spend a few extra bucks and go to Little Tokyo which is always fantastic.

I had actually never eaten here when my boyfriend brought me to this place a few months back.  I got some kind of calzone that was really salty and cheesy.  The cheese wasn't bad, but it was a little too salty for my liking.  Also, we went on a Saturday night, and although they weren't insanely packed, it took them forever to get us our order.  I would go back again (my rule is to try a place twice, unless the food is horrible), but I would be more careful about what I order (when they call something "meaty", they mean it!).

Madame John's is a self guided tour through a classic French home that really isn't anything overly great. It's a gorgeous spot and the tour is free, so you really can't complain and it's worth checking out, as long as you aren't expecting anything over the top. Move from room to room and read about the history of the house and the pottery therein.   I really liked the space itself, but I'll be honest when I say that I found the "tour" kind of boring. There was no one there so I could ask questions and the building was basically a ghost town. I was happy to stop in and I did appreciate the history of the home, but I would have liked to have been able to ask a few questions.

Come on baby... Kick them daisies Look at them girls with the Daisy dukes on I want ya to Look at them girls with the Daisy dukes on Everybody Look at them girls with the Daisy dukes on  Anyone remember that song? Just me? Fair enough.  I stopped in here to sample the Bloody Mary because of Yelp's Bloody Mary challenge. I really love the Bloody here and I have since I first tried one at a Yelp event a few years ago. I love that this drink comes in a big glass mug and is garnished with lemon, lime, olives, a celery stalk and a crawfish. No, it's not crawfish season. No, I do not want to know where this single crawfish came from. Their Bloody is pretty classic with just enough spice and more tomato flavor than booze flavor (I don't like it when the ratio is off).  I didn't try the food on this stop, but people around me did and it looked fantastic, so I will definitely be back to try a yummy breakfast or burger!

Dang Algiers Rouses, you fancy!  This Rouses feels a lot like the Rouses on Tchoupitoulas: a bit upscale and sophisticated with a lot to offer. Also, being in this Rouses makes me realize how much the one on Belle Chasse Highway needs an update. I don't even know if the one on Belle Chasse Highway can even be called a real Rouses because it lacks a lot of cool things that other Rouses have.  Anyway, Algiers Rouses has it all: a neat salad bar, an impressive seafood selection, sushi, a hot bar and a decent beer selection- all of my "go tos". Everything is organized nicely and the staff is really friendly and greeted me as soon as I walked in.  I like that they had multiple registers open, even though the place wasn't super busy, so I was in and out in no time. I might start going to this Rouses more often, mainly because it's nicer and it seems to have more of the "good stuff".

Here comes another parking lot review.  I won't bore you with repeating that I'm not really a fan of the "pay ahead" lots they have downtown now, but this isn't a bad one. I have parked here a few times on my way to catch an event at House of Blues, or have dinner in that general area. The cost for 3 hours of parking is $18, which is a little steep, but it's still better than risking your car's integrity by parking on the street. There is always a lot of space in this lot and it's fairly easy to find a spot closer to the street and under the lights, which I like.  Pro tip: set an alarm on your phone and get back to your car before your time is up because they won't hesitate to boot/tow you. I see the truck out there just waiting for people to forget to come back.

Woo wee.  I love this place!  They have so many neat things, from furniture to beer (different departments ;)).  This is the place to go to if you are looking for Warsteiner Dunkel.  You know... that yummy German beer that you can only find once in a blue moon at a bar?  Well, they actually have it here!  In fact, they have a pretty awesome and diverse beer and wine selection.  Also, if you are adventurous, they have a pretty eclectic amount of international foods.  A lot of different pastas and things that would be great for side dishes.  If there is something that you always wanted to try that is kind of different, and you would prefer to try it at home and not in a restaurant, chances are that this place has it.

Generations Hall is a really cool venue for hosting events. I went to a fundraiser here and I was struck by how well everything was organized.  The staff was on point and were taking care of people quickly with no long lines. There was plenty of food that was organized into neat little stations. There were even a few silent auctions going on that went off without a hitch. I had never been to Generations Hall when it wasn't "Metro", but seeing how everything was done, I would definitely suggest this venue to anyone who is looking to host an event.

How can you go wrong with a place with huge pictures of "old time" movie stars on the wall?  An offshoot of the World War 2 museum, my boyfriend and I ate here before going to the Ogden (it's right across the street).  We didn't have a lot of time, so we decided to just get an app.  We ended up splitting the mini cheeseburgers and they were DELICIOUS.  I mean, the place IS a John Besh restaurant, so it's only the best.  We were also given flavored pickle spears, which sounds odd, but they were really good.  I could definitely see going back to this place for a night out with friends.  They also have a nightly show called the "Stage Door Canteen" that is set in the time of the 40's, during the war.  I haven't seen it yet, but it is definitely on my "to do" list!

There's a reason why this is called the "best" of all the Popeyes in the city and why Eastbankers will travel all the way to the Westside, in order to come to this one.  The chicken here is always consistently fresh and hot.  I wouldn't say that it's cooked to order, but it's darn close.  The chicken just seems crispier here, than at other Popeyes.

90.7 FM on the dial!  Definitely my favorite radio station for really good old (and new) music.  I love the variety of music that they play from jazz to blues to funk.  This is the station that introduced me to Rebirth Brass Band years ago!  They play some old music on vinyl records, which I really enjoy.  This station is a "must" for any local or visitor trying to get into the "spirit" of the city.  Also a great listen for those who miss WBYU.  Not quite the same, but the closest thing to it on air in the city.

I ended up here on my quest for live music. I actually found it here but dang, why is y'all's ac not pumping in the middle of a New Orleans August?  We were loving the music and loving the cocktails, but we couldn't hang out for very long because I was starting to puddle and that's not a good look. It was HOT. I love the layout of this spot- it's obviously an old house that has been converted and I love that the front room has a nice bar and the performer(s) while the back rooms are more relaxed and social.   Four stars because the atmosphere won me over and I can see myself coming back when the weather is a little cooler.

Clever clever...  The idea of this place is that they will put all of this cool stuff up for sale right next to bars and other tourist traps so you will definitely want to buy something. Here you can find special candles and incense and books. I swear, I was thisclose to buying some candles. I doubt any of the things sold here are legit voodoo things, but it's a cool place for someone to stop in for the novelty and fun of it.

This is the type of bar I think of when I think of divey New Orleans bars- it's dark and secluded and has a good crowd.  We stopped in here after dinner one night and even though it was semi early in the evening, the night was already well under way for a lot of folks. I like that the bar is a bit cozy and mysterious and they are generous with the pours. My friend was really digging the video poker machines in the back, and they seemed to be paying well on this particular night.  We had fun picking out songs on the jukebox and sitting at the bar and chatting with our fellow patrons as we let the night drift by. The bartender was friendly and welcoming and we had a great time.

You can keep Port of Call.  In my opinion, this is the best burger place in the city.  They serve a lot of other things, including hot dogs, but if you want good food order a burger with everything, including cheese and onions.  It's my favorite.  I usually get a huge root beer and fries on the side.  Definitely not health food, but if you are a looking for a good local burger, this is the place to be.

Whenever someone asks if we can go to Lucy's, I always ask if we can go across the street to Tommy's instead.  This is one of the nicest and coziest spots in the city.  I have memories of coming here on Friday's in the late afternoon.  Me and some friends would look at the wine list and pick something that we had never heard of before.  Then we would just hang out and talk and catch up.  Day would turn into night and a woman would start singing with piano accompaniment, as the after dinner crowd started to file in.  Older men in untied ties would sit at the bar and have a glass or two and discuss their day.  There's just something amazingly "old school" about it.  You feel a little out of place, but not in a bad way.     I would suggest Tommy's to anyone who is looking for a different bar experience.  Anyone who is looking for something a little more classic that your average watering hole.

I don't know if you can really call this a legitimate mall. It has a Target, an AMC theater and a few shops here and there, but it's really nothing spectacular. I don't even think that anyone would go out of their way to go to this mall. It's more of a nice place to walk around while you are waiting for your movie to start. Sorry for all of the "hate", but there are a lot of other way better malls out there. Lakeside is  minutes away.

Hmm...I guess I'll write a review, since I checked in here.  They have a nice selection of beer and snacks and their gas is always pretty cheap.  I've actually gotten sandwiches from here before, and they are pretty good!  They also sell Yellow Tail wine, which is a classic.  The staff is really nice and when I went in on my birthday, the guy who checked out my items wished me "Happy Birthday".  Did I just admit to spending my birthday at Race Trac?  You bet your sweet bow tie I did.  I hear the iced coffee is good and cheap, but I can't speak to that.  They do, however, have different colored frozen drinks, which is probably the sugary equivalent to the "squishee" on The Simpsons.

I am so excited that there is finally a yummy cupcake shop on the Westbank!  I have only had one cupcake from here, because I wanted to test the place out.  I got the "Wedding cake" cupcake (one of my favorite flavors) and it was delicous!  It was soft and well made and topped with a mound of delicious icing.  At $3.23, these specialty cupcakes are reasonably priced.  Gigi's has a lot of cupcake choices from red velvet to chocolate.  I could definitely see stopping in here and picking up a dozen for a birthday party or special occasion.  I will be going back and trying their other flavors very soon.
Just had to update and mention that WWOZ has an iphone/android app with the channel streaming, so if you aren't in town, you can still listen to awesome music.  Yes, I just discovered this.

Pretty much one of the best places to get all of the "fixin's" for a crawfish boil or cookout.  They have all of the fresh seafood that you could ever want or need. Yes, they only do take out, but keep in mind the fact that post people who frequent this place live in the area and are usually picking up stuff for crawfish/crab boils and things like that. The staff is really friendly and will be more than happy to help you with whatever you need.  They also have sausages and things like that, but I have never gotten that stuff here.

I like Bar Redux. I really like Bar Redux.  This place makes you feel like you are hanging out in a friend's basement. I said that same thing about Dos Jefes, but the difference here is that the basement belongs to a cool friend and not your parents. The bar is on the divier side, but the staff is friendly and eager to please. It's definitely a neighborhood place and that patrons are more than happy to make a bit of chit chat.  On this particular night the patio was closed, because there was no band, so I didn't really get to get a feel of that part of the place. It was also really hot out, so I wasn't complaining. I've also heard that they have amazing food, so I will have to see what the kitchen has to offer when I return.
Awwesome parade with a lot to give.  Very generous krewe.  Catch of the night: tons of doubloons and blinky medallions.

This store is okay. The place had just possibly been robbed when we got here (lots of cops and confused workers), so maybe I'm leaning a little more towards the negative.   Honestly, we just stopped in here for a wine and liquor run, so this review is going to be short and sweet. They were having a sale on Barefoot wine, so we got that and it turned out to be pretty good. They have a pretty good beer selection- nothing too crafty, but the more "mainstream" stuff is well stocked and there are a lot of choices. Aisles are wide to prevent crowding, which is awesome and we checked out with ease. We even saved $4 for using a Winn Dixie card.

Things it is: a dive a cool place to see a band a place to get two types of 40 Arpent beer on tap a place to get tamales a cool local hangout  Things it isn't: an uppity hang out a smoke free bar a place that you will probably want to spend a lot of time smoke free a place with an extensive beer list a place with signage   Old Arabi Bar is a straight up dive if ever there was one. I had a good time here watching a band that I had never heard of and enjoying a local beer. The tamales were exceptional and although there was no sign, you shouldn't be scared of this bar that is basically a hole in the middle of a neighborhood.

One of the great things about French Quarter Fest is that you end up wandering into places you might not have stumbled into otherwise. Enter Naghi's.  What drew me in were the life size sculptures, which I assume are meant for a gorgeous mansion or yard. These things are beautiful and one day, when I have my dream home, I will own many of them. They also had a golden Buddha statue just hanging out on the counter that cost $3000 and a huge portrait of Prince. Yeah, this shop was randomly awesome. They had a display case full of gorgeous jewelry and the man who was working was very nice and greeted me and told me to let him know if I need any help.  I'm not sure if I will ever have the financial means, but when the day comes and I have a mid-life crisis, I'm skipping the sports car and getting that Buddha.

I've been to this place a few times now and it's more than a bar, it's a really nice place to relax with friends.  Sure, it's an older crowd, but on Fridays they have Phil Melancon on the piano and you can't resist having a good time as he sings classics from Nat King Cole and others from that classic era.  The hotel and the bar have an old Hollywood history.  Celebrities such as Tennessee Williams, Frank Sinatra, Walt Disney, Truman Capote and many others have stayed (and drank) here when they were in New Orleans.  The Bayou Bar definitely has an old, classic feel and it's one of those New Orleans bars that makes you appreciate what the city has to offer.

I love this new little consignment shop on Magazine! I think they just opened, because they were in the process of hiring someone when I went in.  They have a great variety of things here. If you are looking for something super fancy and want to pay a little more, they have what you need. If you aren't looking to spend a lot, they have something that will suit your style at a reasonable price. This shop is really cute and my dinky little pictures don't do it justice.  They have everything from skirt and tops to dresses to vintage style purses and jewelry. I will definitely be back when I am looking for something with a little flair.

Oh, Dat Dog.  I had only heard rumors of your awesomeness.  Then I got to experience it for myself.  Dat Dog isn't your daddy's hot dog.  Leave those franks at the ball park.  With such options as bratwaurst and crawfish sausage, you can't miss.  You can get your hot dog topped with your choice of toppings from onions to cheese and much much more.  They also serve fries that you can get topped with chilli and cheese.    I had a fantastic alligator sausage hot dog with cheese and mustard on it (I'm a purist).  It was WONDERFUL (see my pic)!  Also, there is something about the buns that just makes the whole experience great.  Warm, soft and a little bit...sweet?  I will definitely be going back and I'm eager to try all of the sausages that they offer.  Yum!

Super generous Krewe. The gentlemen love the Mar. I got beads, blinky beads, a blinky bracelet and a blinky headband. Was I blinkyed out? Negatory. Hermes proved, once again, that they are the most generous of the Thursday night krewes.

This must be one of those places that you have to visit a few times to enjoy. I really wasn't impressed. The patrons didn't seem friendly and they had a dj for some reason. Keep in mind, there were about 6 people in this place when we went.   It's a 24 hour bar. I can only imagine the type of people that hit this place up at 8,9, or 10 in the morning. Good God. I guess it's more of a neighborhood hangout, but I just don't get it.

After a Yelp event, I was craving some iced coffee, so I popped in here because it was close and it looked like they had what I needed.  I kept my order simple and just got an iced coffee, even though all of their sweet treats looked amazing! My coffee was okay- I could tell that it was "no frills" coffee (that's okay, they aren't really a coffee shop) that had some ice added to it. Also, I didn't ask for cream and sugar, but for whatever reason they just decided to add it- not a huge deal, but that's worth noting if you have dietary concerns.  Decent coffee if you're in a pinch, if you're looking for the "good stuff", go elsewhere.

I tried this place a while ago, after so many people had raved about it.  This was during the time that Oak St. was being worked on, so it was kind of a challenge getting there in the first place.  Anyway, I went and I wasn't really blown away by the food here.  I got my usual: salmon sashimi and a couple of rolls.  They were good, but not good enough for me to go out of my way to get here.    I will, however, comend them on their atmosphere.  The place is quite large, well lit, and I liked the modern feel.  Also, for dessert I got some green tea ice cream and I was blown away at how yummy and refreshing it was.

I have been back here a bunch of times since my first review and I feel as if I have gotten a feel for the place.  When I go, I usually get the "daily", which is the cocktail of the day (you can sample it, before you order) or I just let the bartender mix me up something that he thinks I will like. I also really like the wine selection that they have. Although there are sofas in the back and tables, I usually sit at the bar and chat with other patrons.  The place never really gets overly packed.  It's one of those places where people stop in for a drink or two and move on, so there is good crowd flow.

This is such a welcoming place! We were having Sunday Funday in the Quarter when we passed this spot. The doors were wide open and the musicians told us to "come in!", so we did.  This is a small bar, but I found it cozy. It was packed with what seemed like neighborhood regulars and everyone was enjoying themselves. As the name of the bar promises, there was a jazz band holding court in the corner playing some classic tunes. I can't vouch for the food, but the drinks are well priced especially considering you are in the middle of a "touristy" area.

Tutti Frutti  offers delicious frozen yogurt at reasonable price. The way it is done here is you go in and you are given a cup. You then fill the cup with as much yogurt and toppings as you would like, your cup is then weighed and you are charged according to how much your cup weighs. Really simple, especially on those days that you aren't in the mood for a lot or you are in the mood for a little more. Tutti Frutti offers a nice selection of flavors including pecan praline, raspberry pomegranate, death by chocolate and almond. Keep in mind that you can mix and match flavors, so the possibilities are endless.   The best part about Tutti Frutti is the toppings. Not only do they offer fruit toppings such as fresh strawberries and kiwi, but they also have a nice selection of nuts and candies, for those days that you are in the mood to really indulge. Also, don't worry if you aren't sure what flavors suit your tastes;   Tutti Frutti is more than happy to let you sample all that they have to offer.

This is a decent space. Me and some friends came here to see some music and we had a pretty good time. The area we were in was pretty small and dark. I'm not sure if the entire place is like this, but once the space started filling up it was pretty tight. Cover wasn't horrible- $10 at the door, and the bar had a decent beer selection.  Parts of the show sounded like it was a bit too loud for the space. I don't even know if this is a legitimate complaint, or maybe I'm just old. It's a nice enough place that I would return for future events, but it would have to be something that I really want to see.

Monkey Hill is one of those bars that you want to check out during the week, and avoid like the plague on the weekends.  Definitely a more upscale bar, Monkey Hill is located by river road.  It's a good size place with a nice bar area and a nice sitting area with sofas and chairs, where you can sit with a big group or get to know new people.  My only complaint is, on the weekends, this place gets packed with college age regulars who are dressed like they are going to watch a tennis match.  That's not necessarily a bad thing, but I have always preferred to go during the week.    Worth checking out, if you are looking for a nicer uptown experience.

I've been here a few times, but I have yet to eat here.  Some friends and I usually just hang out in the bar area, because we don't feel like dealing with the smoke at another place.  The staff is always super friendly and eager to please.  So, why three stars you ask?  Well, I guess it's because this place isn't anything overly special and the drinks are over priced.  I know, you're going to call me cheap, but I think $5.75 for a Stella is a little steep.  It's not a bad price if you're on a date and having a fancy night, but just for a random night out, it can add up.  I would go back if I had a reason to, but I wouldn't go out of my way to spend an evening here.  I do want to try the food though!  Ok, I'll go back and try the food and re-review.  Deal?

Whoa! This PetSmart is really huge and way bigger than the one on the Westbank.  My cat has been having stomach issues, so I stopped in here to talk to a pro about maybe switching up her food. He pointed me in the direction of some "nature based" food that is more plants than meat because apparently meat can irritate older cats stomachs. It's a whole thing! While I didn't purchase the food, the guy I talked to was quite knowledgeable and he definitely knew what he was talking about.  This store has a great selection of toys, food and all the other good pet stuff you could want. They have cats up for adoption in the front, and in the back they have fish, reptiles and small furry creatures. There was one bearded dragon who kept eye contact with me the entire time and I think he wanted me to take him home. Fun fact: I used to have a pet iguana and I would love to have a bearded dragon, but today was not the day.  Anyway, I love the new and nice store. I am thankful for the helpful staff and cat food education.

It's late night. I can't sleep. I'm reviewing a Taco Bell. What has happened to my life?  Okay, so actually this Taco Bell is pretty decent as far as Taco Bells go. They have never messed my order up and they are generous when I ask for extra sauce. My problem with this location is the line is often way too long and they are slow getting people through and I have been told, more than once, that they are in the middle of a shift change when I think that they just don't feel like being bothered with taking and preparing an order because the store is dead in the middle of the afternoon.  I know fast food is pretty limited in this area, so I guess you can just take what you can get.

Whoo hoo!  I got to try Barrel Proof and I loved it! Did you know that our very own Elite yelper Davis J., LIVES at this bar? Ok not really, but he is here a lot and when someone has a bunch of check ins to a place, in a short period of time, I bookmark it and file it under "must try".  I finally found myself at Barrel Proof and it didn't disappoint. Formerly Bridge Lounge, Barrel Proof is a fancy cocktail bar without the pretension of a fancy cocktail bar. The staff is friendly, the crowd is rowdy and the drinks are good. You can't ask for more than that. They have totally redone the inside of the place and the only thing that remains of Bridge Lounge is the cozy, dark atmosphere (minus the dogs and loud music). The bartenders are happy to mix you up a fancy cocktail or just pour you a beer, if that's more your speed.  I will definitely be back to make more memories and have some more good times.

I love Celebration in the Oaks!  This is always fun, because the whole family can do it.  On paper it seems so simple: Christmas lights in a bunch of trees,  but it's so much more than that.  The park is transformed into a twinkling magical Christmas land.  I know some people might not be into that type of thing, but I always enjoy it.  This is always a popular place to bring the kids, a good place for teens to hang out for a little while and the perfect place to propose during the holiday season (ok, I'll admit, I think that a proposal here is a little cheeseball.  I mean, I'm not the type of girl who wants to get engaged among screaming kids, but hey, judge not lest ye be, right?).  There's a train that you can bring the kids on and a carousel and other fun little things for kids to do.  Popcorn, hot chocolate and other little snacks are provided.

*This is a review of the consignment part of the store*  With all of the stuff we had to clear and get rid of during a recent "clean out" we knew that trying to sell things on our own wouldn't be out only option. After doing some research, Heirloom Furnishings seemed like a good place to sell some things that we had no need for.  I personally sold jewelry here. The owner went through every piece and picked out what she thought would sell, priced it and before I knew it it had been sold and she had a check for me. While some pieces took a few months to sell, others sold pretty quickly and I was pleased with the way that she decided to price things. Of course, because it's consignment, the owner does take a percentage, but it's a small price to pay considering it would take longer for you to sell the stuff on your own.

At the end of a long night out in Da Metry's, you might find yourself hungry. In which case, make your way over to City Diner to get something good before you head home.  We stopped in here after a pretty long night. It's all a bit fuzzy, but I do know that a delicious breakfast with eggs, grits and bacon was involved. The classic breakfast wasn't the star of the show. This place is known for their HUGE pancakes, so of course we had to try them. I'll admit it- by the time the pancakes came out I was pretty full. I cut myself a slice of the pancakes (like it was cake) and I do remember it being delicious.   City Diner is one of the better choices for a late night meal in this area. I'm not a huge IHOP person these days, so I'm happy to support this spot and I'll return.

This is a nice spot off the "beaten path" for those of us who don't want to go deep into the heart of the French Quarter, but still want to hang out downtown for a little while.  The people here have always been really nice and the drinks are well priced. The place is kind of small, but I actually do like the fact that there aren't any tvs here (or if there are, I didn't notice because they weren't on), so that there aren't any distractions if you are trying to have a conversation.

This place is fantastic. They serve delicious daiquiris and food if you are looking for something to munch.  We stopped in a little later on a Saturday night and I was tired of drinking beer, so I got a margarita daiquiri. It was really good and actually tasted closer to a margarita than other shops that just taste like a mix. I know that this was from a mix too, but it had more flavor than other spots. The bartender was friendly and made us feel welcome. I'm sure smoking is allowed since it's JP, but I didn't notice a smokey smell in the place, which puts it at the top of my "cool" list.

Salvo's is AMAZING. Don't be put off that it is "all the way" in Belle Chasse. It is most definitely worth the trip.  This is a pretty basic restaurant. You walk in and order whatever you want at the counter and then you sit at one of the picnic style tables. It's no frills, but the food is delicious. I always get the oyster po boy and I am never disappointed. The oysters are always fat and juicy and really good.  Other than po boys, Salvo's has other fried seafood, platters and boiled seafood. The staff is super nice and will make you feel right at home.

I don't know if Spanish Plaza (Plaza de España) has been restored or renovated since some of the previous reviews, but I found it to be lovely. David and I wandered over here after we were done with Fried Chicken Fest and after a quick stroll through the Riverwalk Mall. The fountain was on and it was nice and clear water flowing through. The fountain and the surrounding structures are in good shape and it was lovely enjoying the afternoon next to this iconic New Orleans landmark.  As Nicole said, the restaurants in the Plaza are few and far between. I don't know what a "Crazy Lobster" is, but they got one.   I guess there's not much to say that hasn't previously been said about the Spanish Plaza. It's not necessarily worth seeking out if you visiting from out of town, but it's worth a look if you find yourself in the area.  Spanish Plaza aka Plaza de España, I like you.

This cute little shop was unexpected on our walk down Decatur during French Quarter Fest.  We stepped in and we were delighted to see all kinds of tasty treats for sale from unusual candies to just about every soda and soda flavored product you could think of. We picked up some salt water taffy, because I had never had any and my friend insisted I try it. Yep, it was a total win and I loved the melt-in-your mouth goodness of the treat.  This is the perfect shop if you are looking for something a bit different to give the kids (or someone else you love) for a fun occasion such as Easter or Christmas.

I'll be the first to admit that I am not the biggest fan of king cake. I mean, I like it, but I have been known to go an entire Carnival season without having a single slice.  After seeing a lot of people posting photos of their delicious cakes online, I decided to go out and get one of my own. After a bit of research, I found myself at Antoine's. For $18, you get a really large king cake. I opted for the plain, just so I could make a fair judgement on the taste. Well, it was out of this world delicious. I like that it was soft and sweet without being overwhelmingly sweet. Some king cakes overdo it on the sugar and it's too much to handle, but Antoine's did theirs right.  The staff was friendly, and they had king cakes galore into the late afternoon, so I didn't have to worry about rushing in to get one early in the morning.

Yet another one of the delicious gems located inside St. Roch Market.  I stopped in for lunch and I already knew what I was getting. I had seen pictures of The Munch on the internets and I knew that I had to make this pulled pork and mac and cheese sandwich mine. My hopes were pretty high, but they were definitely met as soon as I was presented with this plate of goodness. The combination of pulled pork and mac and cheese sounds decadent, because it is. I only ate half of the sandwich and took the rest to go, I swear!  My friend got a crepe, which looked fantastic and I will be trying one of those next time. I like that Dirty Dishes has a nice selection of different things that are sure to suit any mood you're in. The fact that this is a family owned business makes coming here even better. I will be back.

My boyfriend and I got lunch here a few months ago, after a trip to the zoo, and we were both majorly underwhelmed.  First of all, I ordered a ham and cheese sandwich with a side of mac and cheese.  When I got it, there was no cheese on my ham and cheese.  I probably should have complained, but I was super hungry, so I just decided to eat it.  It wasn't anything special.  It was pretty much a ham sandwich that I could have made at home, yet it was 8 bucks.  My mac and cheese was watery and flavorless.  I can't remember what my boyfriend got, but he wasn't overly impressed, either.  I had never been there before, but he had and said that the quality of food had gone down considerably.

This hotel is one of the best kept secrets in the Garden District.  Prytania Park is in a perfect location- within walking distance of a lot of cool bars and restaurants. It's in a safe area, check in is easy, there's a nice big lot so you don't have to park on the street, downtown NOLA is just an Uber away and the rates are pretty reasonable.  With my experience here the rooms have always been clean and everything has been well looked after. The rooms on the actual inside of the building are quiet and safe and far enough away from the street that I don't have to worry about noisy foot traffic. The tvs are small, so if you plan on watching a lot of tv (for some reason), be aware of that.

Ahh! Finally! I feel like I've been waiting forever for this location to open, especially since David and I are such a fan of the French Quarter location.  We stopped in tonight for a quick bite and this spot didn't disappoint. They don't have a full menu yet, but we got an order of the 5 cheese mac and cheese and it was WONDERFUL. We loved the atmosphere of the place, there is a full bar with music videos playing, and the bartender just couldn't have been nicer. They have a whole selection of burgers and I will definitely be back to get an order of their pizza mac and cheese, which is one of my faves.  This is going to be a hot late night spot among the local college crowd and I'm so happy to have a place like this uptown without having to fight quarter traffic.

Goodness gracious! What a charming little find!  I have been up and down this street tons of times and I never noticed this little spot until a friend brought me here. I had just had a huge lunch, so I didn't partake in the amazing looking pastries. I am talking about HUGE danish that looked incredible. I just decided to get an iced coffee that was delicious and flavorful.  I also noticed that they have an array of sandwiches on the menu, so I will have to stop in one day for lunch and really see what this place is all about.

This is pretty cool neighborhood bar. I never would have even known it was here, if I wasn't looking for it- the front of it kind of blends into everything else on the street. The bartender was nice and the people drinking here were as well. It has a lot more space inside than you would ever imagine- if you head to the back there is a whole lounge area with a pool tables and sofas. There's also another sofa right outside the lounge area, which I enjoyed and that was actually clean. Not worth going out of your way, but nice if you are in the area.

It's always weird to review a bridge, because there's really nothing much to say about it, unless it's in terrible disrepair.  I passed over this bridge and I didn't even realize it was a bridge until I saw the sign. It's in good shape and doesn't seem like it's going to collapse and take me down with it, so that's a plus. I only ever cross this bridge when I'm heading to the Lakefront Airport, which is a rarity considering I don't own my own private plane, yet. I think I might have crossed this bridge a lot, back when I was going to UNO, but I'm not sure.  As others have said, the views of the lake are great, but eyes on the road unless you're the passenger.

Such a cute boutique!  When House of Lounge closed, there was definitely a need for another "upscale" lingerie shop on Magazine St. Bonjour filled that need.  I stopped in here to browse around and I was immediately impressed. First of all, they carry a huge range of bra sizes, even for the bigger busted gals, and the bras are gorgeous. They have a nice selection of corsets and ruffle panties as well. I like that the boutique has a lot of space, so that you don't feel cramped as you are searching through all of their amazing merchandise. The whole place has a very fancy and Parisian feel and this would be a great place to shop either for yourself or a gift for a bride or girlfriend.

Really cute store with "rockabilly" and "retro" kind of styles.  I do agree that it's a little pricey, but for the French Quarter it really isn't that bad. Here you will find all kinds of "swing" dresses as well as different looks for men who are into the retro kind of look. They also have a wide assortment of cowboy boots, and if steam punk is your thing, they sell a few accessories in order to complete your costume.  The store is small, but has a really wide selection of clothing and shoes to choose from. Don't forget to look in the back for the shoe selection!

Full disclosure: I prefer CVS over Walgreens all day. CVS is never really packed and the service is always fast and friendly.  I was here today looking for my favorite hair serum, after not being able to find it at another CVS location. I found it here quickly and painlessly. While I was here I also picked up some Olay products, that were cheaper than I've seen at other places and some travel size mouthwash and hairspray. Checkout was simple and fast and I joined the CVS discount club to save money on future purchases. Win!

This is a divey little spot and, although it calls itself the Roosevelt Hotel Bar, it has nothing to do with the Roosevelt Hotel. I guess there's a history behind why they named it that.  There are only a few seats at the bar and the drinks are cheap. This is a nifty after dinner spot if you want a good cocktail, but don't expect anything fancy. The staff is friendly enough (although, when I was here they were experiencing post-Mardi Gras burn out) and they have a few decent beers.   I probably wouldn't choose this spot over The Sazerac Bar, in the Roosevelt Hotel, but it gets the job done.

My experience here couldn't have been any easier.  I was in the Quarter for a meeting and, lucky me, this shop was just a few doors down. Their counter is facing the street, so I ordered as soon as I walked in. My iced coffee came fast and it was perfect- definitely what I needed to deal with people in the French Quarter driving like dopes.

Anyone who knows anything about me knows I'm a Fleurty Girl fan and FG is always my go to for any gift giving occasion.  It's hard to believe what started out as just a t shirt shop has expanded into an entire empire of the coolest gifts in New Orleans. I stopped into this location to look around for a birthday gift. There was a wide assortment of all things New Orleans related such as ornaments, cups, mugs, shirts and things of that nature as well as a lot of other home decor.  The woman working was setting up for Christmas, but she took the time to show me a few of the new things that they had in store. I didn't find anything that really fit the bill for my friend's birthday, but I love that they always have new and unique items in the FG stores and I loved the plentiful parking at this shop. I know I'll be back, I always am.

Fantastic sweets, especially pralines!  I sampled some of Old Town's offerings at a recent event and I was blown away by how good their classic pralines are, as well as their chocolate pralines! Both were really fresh and tasted like homemade. I like that their classic praline is a little thicker than some others I've had. I also had some chocolates and candied nuts, which were tasty as well.  Their actual brick and mortar store is no more, but you can still order their products online and arrange a pick up. You can order sweets for them for yourself or for an event.

I've been a fan of Dirty Coast long before they had an actual store and they were just operating online and selling their wares at odd little venues around the city.  The shirts are definitely unique and if you are "NOLA-centric", as I am, you will quickly become a fan of these quirky tees.  I have a few of the "original" ones, that are kind of worn out from over wear, but I still rock with pride. "New Orleans: It sticks to you" and "NOLA: Made with soul" are personal favorites.    There are a lot of great t-shirt shops in the city (that I am also a fan of), but there is something special about Dirty Coast.  All you have to do is attend one of their fashion shows in order to see it.
A very generous krewe, especially to kids.  A lot of themed throws.  I got a lot of beads with "Hermes" on them.   Catch of the night:  Blinky winged shoe beads

Since my usual "go to" sushi place, Tennou, is doing take out only, I ended up here for the dine-in sushi experience.  I got the New Orleans roll, the salmon roll, the tuna roll and a Philly roll. All of the food was great. I've been here a few times and the service is pretty good and, although I wish the staff was better about wearing masks, I felt safe because the tables were distant from each other.  The restaurant itself is huge and gorgeous, and has been totally renovated from when it was Parrot Pete's. I'm not sure if this would be my first pick for Westbank sushi, but it did the job. I'd like to return and try their ramen!

I would definitely give Gambino's a solid three stars.  My main complaint is that if you want anything good, you have to go pretty early because they sell out of pastries quickly, and they won't get anymore in until the next morning.  When I get something here, it's usually a king cake.  Not a bad place to go, if you are in the area, but not worth going out of your way for.

I have seriously never reviewed THE Wally World?  Wow. Well, I've been here maybe twice. Once I was looking for a bathroom, so I don't know if you want to count that. They have everything that a regular Wal Mart has but it's quite...colorful. You might see someone get cursed out. You might see a baby draw a weapon. Anything can happen at this Wal Mart.  In all honesty, Wal Mart DOES serve a purpose and it's really a necessary evil. They have super cheap stuff that you need and you know you are going to end up here at least once in your life. Just go limp and let it happen. Wait. What?  Anyway, 1 million hits can't be wrong! This is THE Wally World. You better recanize! http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WF0tkdhtIDA

Moe's might be a chain, but this spot gets a nod for being super affordable. With a menu that includes well-priced sandwiches, platters, a kid's menu and catering options, there's no reason why Moe's shouldn't be an option when looking for something tasty and smoky. The fact that it won't cost you and arm and a leg is a huge bonus here.  I had the pulled pork sandwich with mac and cheese and potato salad ($9).  I'm a firm believer that good barbecue doesn't need sauce and Moe's proves that. The delicious pork speaks for itself, but I added some sauce, just for a little more "zing".  The mac and cheese and potato salad were perfection and I am happy to report that I left Moe's feeling more than satisfied. I especially loved how friendly the staff here was and how fast the food came out; when I'm hungry, I don't want to wait!  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here: https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

Wow. I was in the area and searching for a lunch place when I just happened to walk past this spot. Apparently, it was one of their first days doing dine-in, so I popped right in and had a seat (after signing in).  This restaurant actually used to be a record store and I love the open vibe of the place. I got an order of the ramen, some lumpia and the dumplings. The way it works is your order at the counter and pay and they bring you your food, when it's ready.    The lumpia and the dumplings were incredible. The dumplings came in a tasty sauce that was just a perfect compliment and added even more flavor. The lumpia was delicate and tasty.  The ramen was great! It was packed with pork and the broth was flavorful. Of course, I picked an unseasonably warm October day to get ramen, but it was totally worth it. I loved every bite.  I really admire that this restaurant opened during the pandemic and the hard work really shows in the delicious food. This was a great spot for lunch and I'll be back.

Not my usual "go to" Brothers, but it gets the job done. This place is as reasonably priced as the other convenience stores in the area, but this one definitely isn't as clean and it has a certain "sketch" factor to it. There are always people just lurking around in the parking lot not really doing anything. I've never gotten hot food here (and I wouldn't), but their drink selection is as good as any other spot.

Hmmm...okay, here's the situation: this would be a pretty great place if it wasn't on Bourbon St.   We ended up here one night after a day of hanging out in the Quarter and we were pretty surprised- the staff is friendly, drinks aren't crazy expensive and there was a live band rocking out and actually playing listenable music and not TOP 40. The main problem is the crowd. Of course, you're on Bourbon, so everyone is rowdy and loud and drunk. The place is fairly small and it was crowded, so people were pushing each other out of the way to get to the bar. There are tables and chairs throughout the venue, that are almost in the way when there are a lot of people and a band is playing.  I think if this bar was a little more "off the beaten path" it would be more stars, but I'm sure the owners are making their money, so what do I know? Stop in to see a band, but brace for a Bourbon crowd.

Super cute spot, especially if you want a tasty treat and you're tired of the same old snowball.  Big O's pushes their pops all over town, but right now you can get one at the popsicle doorbell at 3510 Royal St. Just ring the bell most days between 2 pm and 8 pm and the awesome owner Jesse will take your order and bring your wrapped popsicle to you promptly. Pay with Venmo for a completely touch-free experience.  I got the blueberry mango cream and the watermelon basil lemonade. The cream pop was smooth and rich just like yummy ice cream and the watermelon basil lemonade was crisp and tasty. All of the pops are made with fresh ingredients and the taste proves it.  I'll definitely be visiting again soon!

This is a cute little shop that carries a nice mix and casual and "fancier" clothing. The prices are pretty reasonable and right now they have a nice selection of light cotton clothing for the warmer weather.   When I was here I was greeted by the owner and her sweet dog, Gus. They have a good selection of cotton dresses, but on this day I was on the hunt for some comfy shorts that I could wear all day and that were a little different from what I usually go for. I found some cute pink cotton shorts that are thin and perfect for the summer and will be great to wear to festivals.  This is a good place to shop if you are looking for something a little nicer than you would be able to find at a mall.

Oh here we go. Good 'ol Cleopatra used to be a Westbank parade, until it decided to switch to the Uptown route. Well, for all intents and purposes it is still a Westbank parade. All of the Westbank high schools are represented as well as the Gretna police and the fact that people with "Westbank is the Bestbank" signs get a lot of beads, should tell you that this is a Westbank parade at it's finest. In fact, everything about this parade is Westbank, except for it's route.  Pretty decent throws to be had and the Krewe is generous. This years keepers were a Cleopatra koozie, a few light up throws and a bottle opener key chain with a light on it.

This has become one of my favorite places in the city.  Since my review over 2 years ago, I have tried much of the food, a lot of the wine and some of the beer. Delachaise is the perfect little bistro when you want to enjoy a night out, but you don't want to get overly fancy.  My favorites on the food menu are the gourmet grilled cheese and the cheese plate. I have tried many cheeses on the cheese plate and I've always been delighted by my choices. The gourmet grilled cheese is to die for. It's so rich that you can pretty much split it with a friend.  I really like the seating area by the window, and it's always a perfect night when I am lucky enough to grab this limited spot. Sitting on the patio is perfect for early evening as the sun begins to set and the night winds down.  There is an extensive wine selection so you are sure to find something that suits your tastes.

Rouses is a pretty great market.  They are always having specials and have a great selection of deli items such as assorted cheeses and sandwiches.  You can go in and get a mini platter of finger sandwiches for around 5 bucks!  Who wouldn't like that?  They also have sushi rolls that are made fresh daily.  Don't be scared.  It's nothing too exotic.  They usually have crunchy rolls, rolls made with faux crab and veggie rolls.  I don't think any of them actually contain real raw fish and they are actually pretty good, if you want to pick one up for lunch.

I hate to give one of the few parks/green spaces in this area a paltry three stars, bit I feel like it's deserved.  This park is plagued with a few issues: not the least of it is there really isn't much going on here and there isn't much to look at. The grass is frequently overgrown, drainage isn't great, it's a mess after it rains, people litter and it isn't picked up regularly, and sometimes the place can be a bit of a mess. One of the few things this park has going for it is there are a few nice cypress trees and there is a lot of space. I used to come here frequently when I was a kid and fly my kite and it was perfect for that because there is room to run.  I have never been to the observatory, but I do think that that's a cool addition and I wouldn't mind checking that out.

Mr. Tequila on Freret Street is a Mexican restaurant that has tasty food and cocktails to satisfy your craving.  Some popular menu favorites include Traditional Fajitas ($11.50), a savory blend of grilled bell peppers, onions, and a choice of rice, refried beans, sour cream, lettuce, pico de gallo, guacamole, and tortillas; Freret Burrito ($14.25), a steak or grilled chicken burrito filled with rice, beans, pico de gallo, and guacamole with a side of fries; and Nacho Fries ($10.95) topped with steak, cheese, pico de gallo, guacamole and sour cream.  On my visit, I had the Black and Gold Burrito ($12.25), which the menu describes as a burrito filled with ground beef or shredded chicken, rice, beans, topped with chile con carne and white cheese dip. I got mine with shredded chicken and chile con carne on the side. It was a great size for the price; the chili con carne and cheese dip were the perfect touch.  With great food and great service, I will definitely be back!  I wrote about this spot for Uptown Messenger. Check it out here: https://uptownmessenger.com/2021/08/gonzalez-brothers-offer-authentic-mexican-flavors-at-mr-tequila/

I was expecting more.  I'm a beer lover, so when I heard that a beer bar was opening on the Westbank (where I live), I was excited. When I walked in, my excitement faded fast.  For starters, it's Jefferson Parish, so they allow smoking. I just can't "do" smoking bars anymore. My sinuses have aged, I guess, and being around cig smoke leads to two days worth of congestion that I don't want to deal with. Why they don't have machines sucking out the smoke, I couldn't tell you, but it was so thick that it left a haze across the bar.  On top of that, they only have 6 beers on tap and the rest are bottles. Come on. You're going to call yourself a beer bar and not have a decent tap selection? Even Vinnie's has a respectable selection of beers on tap.   Between the smoke and the limited taps, I'll just head over to Avenue Pub on St. Charles for my craft beer fix. Maybe I'm a snob. If you want a big selection of bottled and canned beer, this is the spot.

This is a cute little shop with a little bit of everything. The name is quite appropriate because you do feel as if you are looking through your grandmother's old collectibles.  Grandmother's Buttons has a nice mix of everything from jewelry and house decor to Christmas decorations and clothes. This place is a few steps above your typical thrift store. On the day I was here, I found a pair of earrings that were perfect for a coworkers birthday and she just loved them. This is a nice spot to check out if you are looking for something a little different and unique or if you are looking for a gift for someone special.

This is a review for the patio/bar/outside area.  We were wandering around the Saturday before Halloween kind of just looking for something to do, and after not finding much, when we found ourselves here. The place had a good crowd and there was a band and a place to sit, so we were all about it. The patio area is really nice, there's a lot of space and the bar is right there so you can get some drinks with no hassle and without having to push your way through the crowd. They do have a few local beers on tap, so I enjoyed that while we listened to the band and took in the space.  This seems like a cool place to just hang out, so we'll be back.

This is an Old Metairie classic that was pretty packed on the night I was here, but thankfully the line moved fast.  This seems to be the "teenage hangout" and I think I was the oldest person here (who wasn't a parent) on the night that I stopped in. I decided to get the rainbow flavor, because I've been on a rainbow kick lately and rainbow is different at every stand. At this particular stand, the rainbow flavor was really good and tasted like melted ice cream. Their prices are a little more steep than Westbank stands, but by "steep" I mean 50 cents more...so not horrible. The ice isn't as fine as some other places, but I found it smooth and the syrup pour was generous.  Along with snowballs, they have an assortment of ice cream cones. The people in front of me got some swirl cones that looked delicious! I will be back if I find myself in the area.

This is an adorable bed and breakfast on Esplanade. The staff is super nice and helpful with any of your needs. I did a photo shoot here and the man working that day was extremely helpful and accommodating. He was really nice about letting us use one of the rooms as well as the living room for the shoot.  One of the best features of the room was the claw foot tub. It gave the room an extremely romantic feel and would be perfect for a weekend "away", even if you are a local. The entire house has that "old New Orleans" type of feel and the house has antique furniture throughout. This bed and breakfast would make a cozy getaway for tourists and locals alike.

Some places are probably best left as a part of a song. Margaritaville, for example. I spent the entire time I was here looking for my lost shaker of salt and never found it. That's a metaphor for something. I have no idea what, but I'll figure it out.  Honestly, it's not a bad place for a tourist to stop and get a cocktail, but this local girl just couldn't enjoy the place. The front bar (or is it the back bar?) had a band playing that was way too loud for the room. The lead singer must have thought he was playing Jackson Square or something. We seriously had to relocate to get away from it. It was that bad.  Margaritas aren't terrible, but tons of alcohol doesn't necessarily make a good drink. Their mixologist needs to know that. I didn't try the food, but I'm sure it's typical chain faire. Go in if you are in the neighborhood and need sustenance, but there are a lot of better places in the area.  Some people say that there's a woman to blame. I'm that woman. I went here and it was my own damn fault.

This is a really cool, upscale bar in the quarter. With it's cozy atmosphere and waiters in full attire you are made to feel special as soon as you walk in. I sat on a sofa and perused the list of fancy cocktails. Since I am not a big liquor drinker, I decided on a simple glass of red wine. It was, of course, delicious.  This is also a cigar bar, and although I don't smoke, they seemed to have a wide selection of stogies to choose from.

This is a cute little shop that carries tshirts with a New Orleans and Louisiana theme in a city that seems to be full of shops that carry tshirts with a Louisiana theme.  Like Jen mentioned, they are from Laffy, so a lot of their shirts are Acadania-centric, but they have a good selection of NOLA themed shirts that are sure to satisfy anyone with local pride. Aside from shirts, they have baby onesies as well as themed coasters, magnets and post cards.  Their prices are fair and are shirts are only a few dollars more than certain shirts at other shops. Also, their shirts are unique- they don't "recycle" themes from other shirt shops and I appreciated that because it would be really easy to take a "known" phrase and put a new design to it.

This isn't a bad little place, if you happen to be on the Westbank and need some sports equipment.  They sell everything that you could probably need, from football pads to golf clubs.  My only complaint was that their "tailgate" selection of Saints and LSU shirts/jerseys etc was really kind of sad.  There wasn't a big selection at all and there were a limited number of sizes.  I don't know if it was just this particular location, or if I should be looking for game day gear at a specialty shop instead.  I would go here if I need sports equipment, but for other stuff I would go elsewhere.

I think that I am quickly becoming a big fan of the coffee here.  I was in Metairie and in the mood for coffee when I spotted this place. Having first tried N.O.C&B for the first time just a few weeks ago, I was all about adding another iced coffee to my frequent buyer card. I got a "large" and it was as tasty as the coffee at the St. Charles location. This spot gets a few extra points because it has a drive thru, making it really convenient, since I was in a bit of a rush.  I do think that $4.10 is a little steep for a large iced coffee, but it has a lot of flavor and you get a lot of it. I wouldn't go out of my way to visit this particular location, but it was good in a pinch.
I stop in here once a week.  No crowd.  Good beer and wine selection.  Fresh produce and bread, always!

Stopped in here on a Friday night after a movie. It was about 10pm, so I was happy to see that they were open. There was really no one else in here, so we sat down, looked over the menu and decided to order the Smokin' Chicken pizza which is chicken breast,  onions, pancetta and green onions.  I was pretty impressed by the pizza. It had a lot of favor and I am not usually the type of person to put chicken on a pizza. Usually if I'm eating pizza I like pepperoni and sausage on there, because if I'm gonna be bad I'm going to do it right. Anyway, a medium ended up being the perfect size for two people and we had no problem finishing it.  I would definitely return, if I found myself in the area. I think it's the perfect place to eat before or after a movie, since it's so close to the theater.

I was in the area, and in the mood for coffee, so The Bean Gallery was a natural pick.  Parking was easy on this particular day- plenty of street parking, and there was a good crowd in the place. I like the atmosphere here and there are plenty of tables and sofas where people can spread out and do work. WiFi is free with a password.  The man working was really nice. I got my usual large iced coffee and I found the coffee here to be good, without being too strong. While I would say the coffee should definitely be sipped, I didn't find it overwhelming at all.  There are some tables and chairs, if you want to sit outside on a nice day and they also serve an assortment of sandwiches if you want to stop in for lunch.

A downtown bar with an uptown feel.  I'm not giving it 5 stars, mainly because it IS downtown (not my scene) and parking is a nightmare.    But I digress...  I went to this place not knowing what to expect.  Tonique is small, cozy and intimate.  The people are friendly and they have a huge choice of cocktails.  Now, let me start by reiterating that I am not a liquor drinker, however, when in Rome...  I started with a "True Kick" which is Gin based.  It was smooth and really easy to drink.  A real "sip" kind of drink, which is always ok with me.  The next drink I tried was a "St Claude" which had a rum base and a cherry under taste.  I liked it a lot and although it wasn't as smooth as my first drink, it was definitely a good one.  The place didn't get too crowded and the people there were really nice.  I would LOVE if this place were smoke free, only because it's so small that the smoke gets thick really fast.  I would definitely go back to this place, maybe on a date.

Great food and they actually carry Kroenenbourg!  Can you believe it??  I have never had a dish here that I didn't like.  I usually get the muffaletta calzone!  Mmmm....so good!  The "Sweep the floor" breadsticks are another fave.  This location is HUGE, so if you have a big group, they can accomodate you and it is walking distance from good Quarter bars.

I went on a date here a while back and I loved this place!  They have a nice patio area, so my date and I decided to sit outside (it was summer).  We both had the salmon and we loved it.  It was perfectly prepared and it was served with a delicious sauce that was incredible.  We decided against wine, but they have a really impressive wine list.  I haven't been back yet, but I have to make that a priority, as I was extremely happy with the service, the food and the place itself.

Yay! I had always wanted to check out Grand Theater and I got my chance when we came to see Batman vs. Superman here. I love the comfy reclining seats that make you feel like you are basically at home in your living room (with a bunch of strangers, in the dark). Everything was clean and there wasn't popcorn or old candy wrappers strewn about, so that's a "W" in my book.   I'm usually not one to mention bathrooms in a review, but the ones here were perfect! Everything was neat, clean and well taken care of. This theater is definitely worth the drive if you are looking for an experience that is a little more special than your usual movie night.

I've been to the Big Top a few times, mainly for Burlesque shows. In all honesty, I usually forget about it because it's tucked into a street right off of St. Charles Ave away from the hustle and bustle of the city.  This is a cool little place. It is pretty small and tends to get really packed whenever there is any kind of show. The cash bar is tucked away in a corner, making it somewhat difficult to get a drink if there is a big crowd. I have always enjoyed looking at the art here (when it is bright enough to see it) and for the most part this is a cool little place. I really wish the bathrooms weren't combined, but I guess that's the only option when a place is super small.

Oh my goooooooosh. This is a great store!  So, anyone familiar with my "style" know that I love dresses with a little bit of a vintage/retro/pinup flair. I just happened to stumble into this fabulous shop which carries dresses in the style of "Trashy Diva", "Bettie Page Clothing" and other favorites.  I was in kind of a rush, so I didn't have time to try anything on, but I definitely need to have some kind of shopping spree here soon. I just wish I had discovered this place before the holidays. I would have sent EVERYONE here to purchase my gift.  The dresses here are amazing and you really can't go wrong with anything you find here. Even if you think it's not really your "style", just stop in and check them out. You are bound to find something you will like.

To look at this place you would never guess that it actually has really good food!  I stopped in here with a friend of mine because we were in the mood for hamburgers.  I got the 8oz dressed burger which came with a cheesy potato.  I ordered it medium, but it was closer to well done.  It was still really good and juicy.  I was surprised as I would never expect good food from a little dive such as this.  We didn't stay for longer than we had time to eat, but from the sports paraphernalia on the walls, I can tell that it's a good place to catch a game and hang out with friends.  I will definitely be going back here to hang out with friends and try some of the other food they have to offer.

You know I had to be one of the first to check out the first Dairy Queen on the Westbank.  I had been looking forward to checking this place out, since since I had heard that DQ was finally coming to my area.  I went expecting a crowd, and I wasn't disappointed.   I mean, they had to have the JPSO out there directing traffic!  Despite the crowd, it was all very organized and the drive thru line moved quickly.  And I must say that the staff was super nice, even though they were swamped.  I ordered a turkey club sandwich, which came on a panini type of bread and, of course, a strawberry cheesequake blizzard.  Both were so good.  The sandwich was excellent and deli style, even though it was just fast food.  The blizzard was wonderful and left me wanting to try all of them.  Needless to say, I will definitely go back.  There is so much I want to try!

Me and the man were craving meat, and when our first option didn't pan out, we found ourselves here.  We came on a weeknight and there were a few people here, but it wasn't packed or anything. The first thing that struck me was that the inside looked as if it hadn't been updated since the place was built in the 80's, but that's no big deal. Pretty typical.   We decided on the burger with cheddar and that came with fries. The burger was cooked to perfection, but the only complaint was that it was a bit greasy. Like, to the point that the grease was coating my mouth. I feel like this is an easy fix, but about halfway through the burger, it got to be a little off putting. Other than that, it was really good, which sounds weird after the "grease" complaint, but here we are. The fries were super good and I did like the kind of "down home" feel of the whole place.  I would probably go back, mainly because the Westbank doesn't have a lot of other burger options, so I'll take what I can get.

Mmm..home cookin', when you don't feel like cookin'!  I have never been disappointed when getting food from here.  My favorite is the fried catfish, although that is pretty hard to screw up.  They have a lot of menu items from chicken to pork chops and the prices aren't too bad.  We mostly get take out, but the one time we ate there, the staff was great.  Good size portions and yummy sides (try the cole slaw!).

This is a divey little neighborhood bar, but it hosts a good crowd. On the night that we were here a few streets in the area were without power, so there were a good number of people enjoying the ac and having a few drinks.  The drinks are cheap and thankfully there is a smoking ban in place, so I was able to enjoy my cocktails without worrying about reeking of cigarettes. The bartender was a real character, had a lot of personality and loved to chat.
