I want to go back and play some tunes on the jukebox- there was a line when I was here and I am anxious to see the kind of music selection they have.

What a cool spot!  I had passed this place a few times on my way to Delachaise and always wondered what it was like. It looked small and cozy, so I was eager to check it out.  I walked in and I felt welcome immediately. The bar was filled with local "regulars", and although the place is pretty small, I had no issues finding a seat on the side away from the bar itself. They have a few beers on tap and I'm sure more in bottles. I just stuck to getting Bass on tap.  My only real complaint was that the place was a bit smoky, because it's small, but if you stay a little while it really isn't that bad.

I was pretty bummed when TJ Maxx moved from it's previous location near my house, alllll the way to Algiers. It takes me 10 whole minutes to get there!  Since I found myself in the area, I decided to stop in and check out the fancy new digs. The store is located in an entirely new complex and everything is fresh, new and organized perfectly. The store is HUGE, so I can't really blame them for the location change. TJ Maxx has everything from clothing to purses, jewelry and housewares. Since it was nearing the end of October when I stopped in, naturally all of the Christmas stuff was on full display- from wrapping paper to holiday scented candles.  I've always liked TJ Maxx because the items here are well priced and actually nice and not of cheap quality. The staff was also super friendly and were sure to ask if I needed help, which was extremely appreciated. Although I didn't buy anything, the check out lines weren't too long and all registers were open.

Whenever I think of this place, I think of the phrase "A great place to visit, but I wouldn't want to live there."  Twelve Mile Limit is a cozy little cocktail bar, but I have to agree with Tiff D when she said that it is a dive. It's pretty much a dive bar that tries to fancy itself up by serving cocktails. It's not in the greatest of neighborhoods (because of this, I have only been here once) and I think it's more of a neighborhood place than a place that someone would seek out. There are so many nice cocktail bars in the city. Going out of your way to come here for a drink seems like a waste.

This is the "original" NOLA area Macy's and it's not that great.    Like others have said, it is extremely lacking. I was in the area and decided to stop in and check out the handbags and the selection was just pathetic. Things are disorganized and out of place and there are no employees around to help. It's sad because I came ready to spend my money and left empty handed.  I passed through the shoe department on my way out, and it looked as if it had been hit by a tornado. Shoes thrown everywhere and some not matching and I couldn't even begin to find something that I would want to purchase. You would think that the manager would take more pride in his/her store. I think I'll stick to the Lakeside location.

I really like this cute little shop!  Located on Freret, this place has two things that I really like: good coffee and quiet. It seems that the new trend is to blast obnoxious music in coffee shops. There's none of that here.  I got an iced coffee and it was really good. It didn't taste like the "same old" that you find at other shops. In the front, there is a nice seating area with big chairs and there are tables and chairs in the back, Local art adorns the walls, giving the place a nice, quaint feel. Also, it's a huge plus that the coffee isn't SO strong that it makes me want to run 25 miles without stopping. Sometimes I think that some of these places are in a competition to see whose coffee can make someone drop dead, first.   Anyway... I like this place and I shall return.

I was here for the Summer of Sustainability dinner that I was lucky enough to get tickets to through Yelp.  The space itself is lovely. The clubhouse has a Southern mansion type feel from the light fixtures to the bar area. When you walk out on the back deck, you are surrounded by large trees that canopy the green space that leads out onto the golf course. I would really just enjoy sitting out here on a nice day, sipping a cocktail.  For the dinner I attended, everything was organized beautifully. There were 6 courses total and each course had it's own fork set in place, as well as it's own wine glass. The staff here was great about refilling drinks in a timely manner, clearing plates as I was finished and the courses came out quickly. The bartender here is extremely knowledgeable, and when I first got here, he helped me pick a wine that I would like since I'm not really that much of a wine drinker.  Now that they are open to the public for lunch and dinner, I will be returning to get the full clubhouse experience soon.

While not one of the more extraordinary cemeteries in New Orleans, Lafayette Cemetery #1 is worth a walk through, if you're in the area. I happened to be in the neighborhood and I realized I hadn't been here in a while, so I decided to take a few minutes and duck in. The cemetery was pretty quiet except for a tour guide telling a few folks about the space.   One thing I find a bit off putting about this cemetery is: although there are a few entrances, they are all locked off except for the main entrance. In other words, you are kind of trapped if you walk all the way to the back and decide to want to make a quick exit. Also, there are a lot of rows of graves that are ill-kempt and there is a lot of mud and muck in certain places. On my way out someone approached me from behind to ask me for money- he was a homeless veteran. I was glad I was with my coworker, because he scared the hell out of me. Security in here would be nice, at least at the entrance.

The National World War II Museum is a "must visit" when you come to New Orleans.  I have been here 3 times and it's always the first place I suggest to anyone who is visiting from out of town.  This place is full of all of the History of the war and really cool artifacts and interviews with people who went to war, as well as those who stayed behind.  I haven't been able to get back to see the film "Beyond all Boundaries", but I hope to soon, as I have heard that it's excellent.  Be sure to set aside an entire afternoon for the museum, because it is quite large and there is a lot to see and read.  You want to be able to take your time, so that you can get the full experience.

Such a great little place! After seeing a few folks check in here, we decided to head over and see what it was all about. I just love tiki bars- fruity drinks in fun cups and glasses with a tropic atmosphere. What's not to love?  This bar is tucked into the middle of a neighborhood, so it might be a bit hard to find at first. Fortunately, it's positioned nicely under a street light, so it's not too hard to miss. I decided to get their house punch, which was fruity, really good and served in a cute tiki cup complete with umbrella and mermaid. If tiki drinks aren't your thing, they have a full bar and a nice selection of local beers. They also serve food, if you're hungry. I only tried one drink on the day I was here, but I'm eager to stop back in and try more. They have a nice stage area, so I think that they might be planning on hosting bands in the future. I can't wait to go back!

I've been back to Oak a few times since my previous review and I think it's only appropriate that I bump them up a star.  Maybe when I first came here, I came on an "off" night, but the times I have been here since have been delightful.  The venue wasn't packed at all and not everyone was dressed up (dressing up isn't bad, mind you, the last time I think I had caught the place when they were having an after party for a Christmas thing).    This actually is a great place to see live jazz and I love that a place like this exists uptown.  I love seeing live shows, but don't always want to deal with the hassle of driving to and parking somewhere on Frenchmen.  Oak is in a really nice and safe area and street parking is plentiful close to the venue.    The staff is extremely nice and helpful and attentive.  I will definitely be going back a few times over and keeping my eye on their music calendar.

This cool little snowball stand not only serves snowballs, they serve a whole menu of poboys and fries. Since I am on a Westbank snowball adventure, I just got a snowball.  I decided to get a rainbow flavor (a new favorite). You walk up to the window, ring the bell and let them know what you are interested in ordering. One thing about this place is they give you a choice of "coned" or "flattened" at the top. Well, why wouldn't you get the cone?  The ice was okay, but not really as fine as I like and the juice was definitely lacking. The flavors they used blended together decently, but after a while the whole thing just tasted like a lime snowball. One plus about this stand is that they do have tables and chairs, if you want to sit outside. The stand isn't in the best neighborhood, and you are eating on a highway, but the only other option is eating in your car.  Good for what it is, but I won't be back.

My boyfriend (I start a lot of reviews like this, but we go out to eat a lot, ok? ;)) and I were both in the mood for a cheeseburger when we went here.  For some reason, I thought a New Orleans hamburger and seafood co. was located here, but I digress.  Anyway, we went in and ordered our burgers medium.  Well, they ended up coming well done, but they weren't bad, and we didn't bother to waste time complaining.    The service was good and the food came fast.  The only complaint my b/f had was that they calculated a 15% gratuity into the check, for a party of only two people.  It seemed odd, because he had planned on tipping a little bit more than that.  Of course, I explained that for every person who tips 18%, there is that person who doesn't tip at all.  They have obviously had some kind of issue in the past, so they felt the need to do that.  I would go back, but I would stress that I would like my burger medium and not well done.

I love having a drink on the porch of this gorgeous house turned hotel and pretend I am sipping a mint julep in the old South.  This is one of my favorite spots to hang Uptown and definitely a great place whether you want to get a drink on date, or with a group of friends.  If the weather is a little too hot for your liking, you can always sit inside, just be aware that it fills up fast.  Also, they do have wait service, but most of the time you are better off getting your own drink at the bar, if you are in any kind of hurry.  Also, I was actually lucky enough to know someone who was staying here years ago, so I got to take a look at one of the rooms.  It was huge and gorgeous and had a real "old" New Orleans feel.  I do some modeling and I would love to do a shoot there someday, but I digress.  This would be a great place to stay if you are traveling to the city on your honeymoon or just on a vacation.

I love pizza and when I saw that this place had Chicago deep dish, I was in. I had never had deep dish before, but the pictures had me sold.  We stopped in on a late Saturday afternoon and lucky us, it was happy hour. Happy hour means $3 draft beer and half off of apps. Sweet! They have a nice selection of local beers and we got an order of mozzarella sticks, just to start us off.  Now, the deep dish pizza takes 45 minutes to cook, so keep that in mind when you are visiting. We got the supreme deep dish which is pepperoni, sausage, green peppers, onions, and black olives all layered into cheesy goodness. I can't even describe how good this was. There was cheese galore and layer after layer of meat and sauce. The crust was perfection and the whole thing was unlike anything I had ever had. We got the 7" pie and that was more than enough for two people and we even had leftovers.  The food was good and service was friendly. and I will definitely be back, especially for happy hour.

This place is great! Not only can you go in and get your makeup done by a pro for a special occasion (or just a night out) but they sell makeup here too. The entire staff is really knowledgeable and can help you figure out what works for you (and what doesn't).  They also do spray tanning and you and your friends can have a makeup party for a birthday or bachelorette party. It's a really cool idea for something different.

This a nice little neighborhood bar. The bartender was really friendly and they have good beer like Fat Tire and LA 31. It was pretty slow on the night that we came, so we chatted with the bartender and the one other patron that was in the place. I can see how this is probably a popular hang out earlier in the evening. I got the vibe that it's a "pre game" type of bar. I'd love to come back on a night where there are more people. Like others have said the place is cash only.

This shop is incredible! First of all, they have a lot of cute clothing and the owner was awesome. Second of all, it's all really well priced stuff! On the day I was here everything was $19! That's almost unheard of for a store on Magazine St.  Here you'll find a nice selection of casual-style dresses and other outfits. They also have a nice selection of accessories. I wished I had come to this store first because I had just left another store where I splurged and bought a few things and I think my money would have been a tad better spent here. I'm definitely going to be coming back to do some post-Christmas shopping and I can't wait to stock up on nice, inexpensive clothes.

I really need to rave about this place for a minute.  I love how cozy the house itself is- there are rooms in the back area and there is a nice colorful patio. We were in one of the back rooms that is right off of the street and it was nice and quiet and we weren't bothered at all. The room is small, but if you are looking for a great "crash pad" during Mardi Gras, or any other time that you are visiting, this is the place for you.  I love this neighborhood, and there are a lot of bars and restaurants in the area that are walkable and the streetcar is just a few blocks over. The staff is as nice as can be- the first time I dealt with a man and the second time I dealt with a woman. I think they are both owners and they were helpful in getting us cabs so that we could zip around town.  Creole Gardens has a complimentary breakfast for customers- one at 7am and one at 9am. You order at the kitchen and they bring your food to you in the dining room.

I don't know why I bother with fast food at all, especially Sonic.  The service at this Sonic is always super slow, more than once the food has been...let's just say "not really hot" and I always seem to leave unimpressed. The only saving grace is the happy hour, where you can get discount drinks, but even those are pretty disappointing.   There are better choices for fast food. Avoid this place.

I don't have much occasion to frequent Office Depot, but whenever I have been here I have had no issue finding what I needed. They have all of the basic office supplies that you would expect to need and find and they even have fancy office furniture!  About a year ago I bought a box of envelopes (for some reason). I used two of them before I realized that I didn't need a whole box. I brought them back and explained the situation and they took them back and gave me a refund with no issue.

Kind of sketch-ville. Of course I was passing through Algiers when my "low fuel" light came on. Naturally, I started freaking out (inside) and hit up my smart phone to find the nearest gas station and this is where it lead me. There were random men just lurking outside with no real purpose. There were people giving me weird looks as I was filling up. Yep, this gas station had it all! With that said, the gas wasn't too pricey at $2.05/gallon. I wouldn't seek this place out, but it got the job done so mission accomplished.

Wow.  I had completely forgotten about this place and I haven't been in about a year!  First of all, believe it or not, I have never gotten the pizza here.  Yeah, I know.  My favorite is the Pasta Jambalaya and I get it everytime I go.  It's basically jambalaya served over penne pasta...delicious!  Now just a fair warning, all of the LA pizza kitchens are independently owned and they all have different menus.  When I went to the uptown location, not only was I surprised to see that they didn't carry my favorite, but the dish I ordered (I can't even remember what it was) wasn't good at all.

I just loved this unique gallery!  I was lucky enough to be able to pass through here on Dirty Linen night and I was delighted by the type of art that Chris Roberts-Antieau has created here. The art here is really unique because the "paintings" are really all hand stitched. It's like someone created different art work quilts that tell a story and convey a mood. It's very unique and very interesting.  Some of the art stands alone, and some of it tells a whole story like a quilted comic strip, of sorts. It's such an interesting way of creating art that the process itself must be fascinating.

I think I have found my new Uptown coffee house hang out.  Ever since Rue De La Course on Magazine closed, I have been searching for a new Uptown coffee place to call home. Sometimes you just want to go somewhere and sip coffee and take it all in. I think I have finally found my new place.  Reservoir Cafe is really neat. In a lot of ways, it reminds me of that other LGD fave Mojo. Not only is the coffee really good, but there is plenty of seating (they even have booths!) and the place is small enough to feel cozy and nice. They serve sandwiches for breakfast and lunch and have all of the other basic things that you would expect from a coffee place. I like that they have a big window in the front, so that you can watch the world go by. There is plenty of outside seating, too for the nice days that you want to get some fresh air.

Oh my gosh! This is SUCH a cute shop!!  I never even knew this place existed, until I happened to be driving down Magazine St. one day and it caught my eye.  This place is amazing and carries every type of umbrella you could ever imagine. I love that they have unique, pretty umbrellas, and in a rainy city like New Orleans, it almost makes you wonder why there aren't more umbrella shops in town.  I didn't buy anything this time, but I have my eye on a gorgeous red lace parasol. They have umbrellas for second lines for weddings as well, so if you are looking for that type of thing, be sure to check this place out. They even have umbrellas that are perfect for kids!  I will say that the umbrellas are not on the cheap side at all, but for as unique as they are, I think that they are absolutely worth the money.

Ha. We actually ended up here accidentally. We had just finished dinner at Gautreau's when I had the idea to see some live music. I knew that a band was probably playing at Les Bon Temps on Magazine, so we hopped into a cab and told the cabbie that's where we wanted to go.  Well, he misunderstood and we weren't paying attention (too much chatting) and next thing you know, he pulls up in front of Bon Ton Cafe. Deciding to make the best of an unplanned situation, we decided to hop out and check the place out.  Well, it's a full on restaurant, but they do have a bar, so we sat and enjoyed some beer for a little while. The staff seemed happy to have us and enjoyed our little story about going down the wrong path.  After hanging out for a while, they called us a cab and we eventually ended up at the correct Les Bon Temp. Naturally, this is the one day a week that a band wasn't playing. You win some, you lose some.  I'll be back at Bon Ton soon to actually eat.

This coffee was a lifesaver when I stopped in here after checking out during my Pontchartrain stay. The cafe itself is pretty small with basic tables and chairs and you let them know if you are dining in or getting something to go, as soon as you walk in. The staff is super nice and although I didn't eat here, I can say that the iced coffee is particularly good and while it's not the *best* coffee I have ever had, I found it flavorful and enjoyable.

This isn't one of the biggest or fanciest parades, but it's a good little kick off to the Mardi Gras parade season.  They don't have any really special throws, but I did get a cup to add to my "collection".  Suzanne pretty much hit the nail on the head with this one.

Bellocq is one of the fancy cocktail bars the New Orleans is known for. I am not really a huge cocktail person, but I can appreciate a well crafted drink.  Bellocq has an extensive menu of drinks that they can make for you, that are sure to appeal to all tastes.  Oddly enough, I think that the best thing about this place is the atmosphere. It's really dimly lit, which I love. I really dig cozy places like this. It also has a lot of sofas and benches for group sitting, which adds to the tranquility of the entire place.   If you are in the mood for a little something to eat, they have a small menu of little tapas that you can munch on.  I knocked off a two stars because the staff seemed overwhelmed by the large crowd and there was limited seating at 9 pm.

Okay hotel located in what I would call "sketch ville".  A friend of mine was staying here on his visit to the city. The room wasn't too bad. It had an area for sleeping with a good size tv and there was an attached "sitting" room with a seating area and a desk and a view of Canal Street. One thing that would get really old is the ridiculously small bathroom. You have to squeeze yourself against the wall in order to get the door to close!  The thing that struck me about this place was the lobby. There seemed to be people who weren't staying here milling about and the staff seemed pretty indifferent. Even though my friend was just a few blocks from Bourbon, I encouraged him to get a cab and not walk because the area isn't good at all.

This is a pretty "okay" gas station. I always like to get gas at Brothers because it's definitely cheaper than other stations. Inside they have some food offerings like fried chicken, fish, po boys, fries and things like that. The store seems pretty clean and I've never had an issue with service here. The one or two times I've gotten food here, it's been pretty good even though this isn't my usual go to Brothers.  This spot can get a little sketchy at night, so keep your wits about you.

This is an interesting little hole in the wall where the selling point is cheap drinks. You will also see some unique characters here. Cheap drinks or not, this isn't really my type of place and I would never go out of my way to come here. With that said, it serves a purpose and the "regulars" seem to like it.

This is for a review of the pool/bar area.  I was here for a private party. I really liked the pool area. I didn't get to swim, but I can see how during the summer this would be a cool hang out spot for those of us who don't have a pool or want to sneak into a hotel pool to swim (ha). The pool is a good size and there is a nice outdoor bar and seating area/cabana area. Really nice for a party or something.  The inside bar area is nice too. There is a pretty decent beer selection and the bartender was friendly and nice. The seating is somewhat uncomfortable and left a little something to be desired, but besides that I really enjoyed it here.  I would love to go back and actually try the food and get the full experience.

Really fun spot that always has a cool band on stage and a lot of people dancing.  Cafe Negril isn't as big as some of the other music venues on Frenchmen St, but it's still really cool. It gets full pretty quick, so a lot of the time you just end up dancing with a bunch of strangers and it's a lot of fun. They have a lot of reggae bands that play here. I don't think that's all that plays here, but it's what has been on stage the last few times I have been here.  I'd go back. Worth checking out, but probably not worth going out of your way.

I've been coming to this Baskin Robbins forever. I really like that it is a little smaller than other BRs. To me that adds something to it.  I came here the other day for a strawberry and banana smoothie and it was so good! I had never tried any of the smoothies here, but now that I know how tasty they are, I will definitely be getting them more often.
Awesome glass beads, bracelets, and luggage tags this year!  Another all star performance!

With a name like "Who Dat" it's gotta be good, right?  This is a neat little Marigny coffee shop and cafe. When I pulled up to this place, I didn't expect much. It looked SUPER small and nothing really special on the outside. When I went inside, I was pleasantly surprised to find a super cozy set up. First of all, it was a rainy day, so that added to the cozy atmosphere. Second of all, I liked that there were small tables and a little "dining" area in the back and on the other side there was a room complete with sofas. It felt like I was at someone's house.  I ordered an ice coffee, which was delicious and I decided to sit outside with a friend and talk and watch the rain. Really nice. I didn't get to try the food but looking over the menu, they offer what sounds like super yummy sandwiches that I will definitely have to go back and try. I also want to try their breakfast selections.  Extra points for super easy street parking. I got a spot right in front and there were plenty to spare!

I am pretty excited for this car wash. Usually, I have to travel all the way to Marrero to get my car cleaned the way I like, but this spot is closer to home so I thought I would give it a shot.  I just did the drive thru wash on the day I came. Like Eddie said, it is a "touch" car wash, so there are brushes and stuff scrubbing the dirt off. They don't have a "pre wash", which is usually a guy with a soapy brush who loosens up the dirt on your car before your drive into the wash. It had been a while since I had my car washed, and while this car wash did get a lot of dirt off, there was still a lot of dirt left on my car after I was done- a bummer to say the least.  I'm not complaining- the wash I chose was only $5 and I know that if I had done a "pre scrub" like Eddie suggests, it would have done the job. I'll probably be back.

I have been here once and I will probably never be back. The place isn't bad and the staff is super nice, but I HATE bars where I have to get buzzed in.   I know it's supposed to make me feel safe, but the buzzer has the opposite effect on me. I get buzzed in and then the questions start popping into my head. "Why do they need a buzzer?" "What happened that the manager finally said 'We need to start buzzing people in'"? "What is the criteria for NOT buzzing someone in?" "THAT dude looks a little suspicious. How did HE get in?"  It's just a whole lot in my head when I am trying to just relax with friends. No thanks. There are too many nice bars in the city. Ok, now I'm sounding like a snob. In conclusion, good place that would be better if I wasn't worried about the buzzer.

I had completely forgotten that we had gotten take out from here!  I got an alligator poboy from this place that was out of this world delicious!  I tend to be a pretty adventurous eater, so if you are too, then you have to try it.  I've only gotten take out and I haven't been to the actual place, so I can't really review the atmosphere or anything.  I'll be sure to update when I go back!

Really fun and we had a perfect spot right near Canal Place!  This is a pretty short parade, and as long as you aren't going into it expecting a big Mardi Gras style parade, you are going to have a good time. I liked the themed floats that had a local flavor (Pat O'Brien's, PJ's coffee) and the highlight was definitely the bands and the marching groups.  I wish that there had been a few more "spooky" throws, but I was happy that I got a whole bunch of Krewe of Boo cups, a Pat O's hat, PJ's coffee and Aunt Sally's pralines. Whenever food is involved, I'm a happy camper- if only I had gotten my hands on a bag of Chee Wees! I do wish they would throw beads with Halloween themes such a skeletons and pumpkins and things like that and maybe a signature Krewe of Boo bead- the regular plain Mardi Gras beads seemed like a waste and lot of people didn't even bother trying to catch them.  All in all I had a good time and I'll attend in the future.

After passing Rag Doll over and over when it was closed, I finally made it here during business hours. I was not left disappointed.  First of all, they have all kinds of cute dresses that are great for everyday wear or a special occasion. My favorite was probably the rack of handmade dresses using vintage patterns. Super cute idea! New vintage! They also have an assortment of vintage clothing and jewelry, which is really reasonably priced (less than $30).  With so many "vintage" shops on Magazine street, I found that this is one of the best of the bunch, as far as prices go. You can step in here and choose from a lot of cute things for well under $100. My kind of place! I will definitely be back.

I can't believe I forgot to review this place!  I went here when some friends and I went to a Saints game a few weeks ago.  This is a great place to hang out before or after a  Saints game, mainly because it's really close to the Superdome and they serve beer and food.  When we went the bar was extremely packed (of course), but in spite of that, we were able to order food and we were served pretty quickly.  We sat at the bar, since it was the only "free" spot, so I didn't get to try out the fancy beer taps that are on the tables.  This is a wonderful place to go if you are tailgating for a Saints game, or if you just find yourself in the area and want something a little different.  I will definitely go back, next time I find myself in that neck of the woods.

I'm kind of worried about this place. It just opened (they have grand opening signs everywhere) and yet, the place was totally dead when I stopped in.  I had received some "incentive" coupons in the mail from this Dunkin' Donuts, in order to encourage new customers. I needed no real encouragement, as this DD is pretty close to my house and I am a sucker for cheap, not so great, but it has caffeine in it, coffee.  I stopped in to get a discount iced coffee with my magic coupon and the place was pretty dead. The girl behind the counter was super nice and accommodating and I felt bad that I wasn't more in the mood for a donut or something, but I was kind of in a rush and needed an iced coffee STAT.  I've pretty much made it my personal mission to keep this place open. This spot has been cursed ever since the Pizza Hut closed, so I'm gonna stop in a couple times a week for coffee and a sandwich or something.

This Sun Ray is a weird mix of cooked plates and sushi.  They have things you would probably expect from a place like this such as chicken and shrimp and even nachos and quesadillas.  Oddly, I have never had any of that.  The two times I have been here, I had the sushi.  Now, this isn't what you think of when you think of a typical sushi place.  I got a few rolls and the sashimi, and the fact is, it was just ok.  It's definitely a good place to get sushi, if you are in the mood for it while you are with people who don't eat the stuff, or are in the mood for cooked food.  Would I seek this place out for just sushi?  No.  Sun Ray wouldn't even make it into my top 5 for that, but it's not terrible.

Some friends and I checked Oak out for a bite to eat at a place that's a little different.  It wasn't great, but it wasn't terrible either.  First, I definitely have to agree with people who say that this place is loud.  It's really loud, and although they have live music, I don't think that this place was built for that kind of thing.  If you want to see a band here, don't expect to have any kind of conversation.  Also, Oak is really brightly lit and I wish that there were more places to sit.  It was pretty packed and seats were at a premium.  Heads up: if you go here, dress up, because everyone does.  My friends and I were in jeans and we felt a bit out of place.  Not a bad place to start your night, but once it gets packed, it's no fun.

Du Mois was kind enough to host the first Yelp Elite event of 2011.  I had heard about the opening of this gallery, but hadn't had the chance to check it out, before I attended the event.  I was really impressed.    The place itself is small, but nice with three main rooms and a large room in the back.  I was surprised to see some photographs of an old acquaintance of mine on the walls.  I knew she was a photographer, but I had no idea she was so accomplished.  I like that the gallery is brightly lit with a lot of open space.  A great addition to uptown.

I feel like this is one of those places when you want to feel like one of the "special" people.  The place is definitely fancy and the atmosphere fits well into it's Uptown location.  The thing about this place is I never really leave FULL.  You know how other sushi places leave you feeling like you won't have to eat for a week?  This place makes me feel like I'm just "munching".  Maybe I'm not ordering enough or just eating with too large a group.  Ha.  The food is good, but nothing spectacular.  I would call it overpriced, only because you can get the same thing somewhere else for a lot less.  But, as in a lot of these cases, you are paying for not only the food, but the experience.  My boyfriend's friend just started working here, so maybe I will make it back.  I'll be sure to update, if my opinion changes.

This is every mother's dream, especially if you are a mother who is looking to go the "natural" parenting route. No, I'm not a mother, but I stopped in here with a friend who was looking to pick up some things for her future niece or nephew.   Not only will you find baby toys and furniture here, but you will find a vast array of natural products such as baby washes and even cloth diapers. And if you have no idea where to begin with cloth diapers, the staff is expert at it and will tell you everything you need to know from what kind of diapers you need to how many times to change them and how to wash them.  Mom isn't left out, Zuka offers a wide variety of nursing bras, maternity fashion, skin products, breast pumps and nursing pillows. Basically, everything you need to care for your little one before and after he/she has arrived.

Admittedly, I am not what you think of when you think "country", but for the past few years I have been on the hunt for red cowboy (girl) boots. Why? Well, because I think they are pretty cool and an all purpose kind of shoe. And red is just snazzy.   I had looked online, but I hadn't ever had the chance to look for boots in an actual store. I was super excited when I saw that not only did Cavender's have the boots that I sought, but they were priced well! I didn't buy them yet, but I will probably be back to get them after a little more shopping around.  If boots aren't your thing, Cavender's also has a nice selection of "country" inspired clothing and jewelry. A lot of the clothes are overly "stereotypical" of what you think of when you think of Western wear, so don't be afraid to stop in and look around. You might find something that suits you.

I am pretty torn about this place. I came for breakfast and got two eggs over easy, grits, bacon and toast. The eggs were VERY under cooked to the point that I couldn't finish them, a few pieces of bacon were pretty much burnt and the grits were...odd. The grits were almost soupy because I think they put too much cream in them or something- I could barely eat them with a fork.  The staff here was nice and I do like the atmosphere of the place. I didn't partake, but they have a "build your own" Bloody Mary bar for Sunday brunch. Maybe this was an off day, so I would probably give them another shot.

Muses is one of the parades that I (and many others) look forward to every year.  The entire crew is made up of women.  They floats are fantastic, huge, and wonderfully lit (since it's a night parade).  I think that my favorite float of theirs is probably their big shoe float.  Shoes are definitely the ongoing "theme" of this crew.  Shoe beads, shoe bracelets, and even custom decorated shoes are just some of their awesome throws.  In past years I have also caught fluffy zebra print spears, scarves,and light up necklaces.  Marchers with the group include the Camel toe lady steppers and the Muff-a-Lottas.  This is a definite "must" on the Uptown parade route.  Catch of the night: decorated shoes.  Anything with a shoe on it (not hard to come by!).

If White Linen is snooty and pretentious, then I would call Dirty Linen it's more fun cousin. The cousin you want to hang out with because she knows all the cool people and all of the cool places to go and she'll sneak you beer before you hit 21.  Dirty Linen is so much better than White Linen. Yes, it's still hot, but it's not nearly as "uppity". Most of the crowd seems a bit younger than White Linen and the whole atmosphere is more laid back and relaxed. The galleries on Royal are fantastic and everyone just goes and has a good time and seems to be in a good mood.

This is a great place to see a band.  The place is really big and has great accoustics.  I saw the Molly Ringwalds here about a year ago and had a really great time.  The venue has three separate bars, so you're covered if you need a drink.  The best part is probably the parking lot, so you don't have to worry about street parking.  I would recommend checking the website before going to a show, because depending on who's playing, the cover can be kind of high.

I just stopped in for iced coffee, so this review is going to be short and sweet.  I was in the area and had heard this place was pretty good, so I decided to check it out. To my delight, they have a drive thru BUT it is an extremely sharp turn around the building and a little tight, so be careful if you are driving a big body type of vehicle.  The coffee itself was good. I was happy to see that their version of "large" is actually a really good size. The coffee had a lot of flavor and I enjoyed it.

Royal Street is to the Quarter what Magazine Street is to the Garden District- you can find it all on Royal Street.  Royal Street is my favorite street in the Quarter for a few reasons: it's not packed with bars like other streets, there are a lot of gorgeous galleries to pop into and take in the lovely art, antique stores don't get any better than on Royal and the street performers and buskers add a certain charm that you would be hard pressed to find anywhere else. There is nothing better than walking down Royal Street on a nice afternoon and taking in the vibe of the city and maybe stopping into some shops along the way to do some browsing.  Royal seems to be in the center of it all, and when you find yourself here you can guarantee that you aren't too far from a good time. If you spend enough time on this street, you will absolutely be able to catch a second line or two.

I'm bumping them down a star. While Muses is still an awesome parade, I think that they could be a little more generous with the throws and, yes, that includes the shoes. I have been going to this parade for years and years and I have never caught a shoe on my own. Shoes not withstanding, I feel that if you are in the middle of the parade route, you just aren't going to get a lot. We were standing with a big group of kids who had trouble getting throws, so it wasn't just because I'm a grown woman. I was pretty pleased with what I did catch this year: my rubber ducky light up pen and the silver block letter Muses necklace are two of my favorites. There were plenty of bands and dance groups, which is always fun and the ladies seemed to be having a good time.  While I think that this parade is still a "don't miss", some improvements can be made as far as consistency goes.

Storyville is such a cool place for locals and tourists alike to go and pick up some really cute New Orleans themed tshirts and favors.  This is the place where I got my infamous "Brad Pitt for Mayor" tshirt that always seems to get a chuckle whenever I wear it.  Storyville is located right across the street from another New Orleans tshirt shop: Fleurty Girl, so between both stores you should be covered for anything you may need.

For my 100th Yelp review for the Yelp 100 challenge, I decided to review Joan of Arc.  I absolutely love this statue. One of the many nods to France in our great city. She sits majestically on her horse on Decatur St.. She has become such a fixture in our city, that it's hard to believe she has only been here since 1959 when Charles de Gaulle came here and presented her to New Orleans on a state visit.   I know it's probably a little hokey, but I like then there is a big Saints game and someone takes the liberty of attaching a Saints flag to her pole.

I stopped in for a quick lunch on a rushed afternoon.  I liked that the green tea I ordered came bottled and not from a mix. I don't really mind the mix I get at other places, but the bottle is always better in my opinion. I got a Godzilla roll (special roll), which came packed with snow crab, salmon, tuna, yellowtail, avocado, asparagus, cucumber and cream cheese and wrapped in green soy paper. It was a huge roll and well worth the $15. I usually don't pay this much for a special roll, but this is the only one on the menu that appealed to me and I really liked it. I also got the two roll special of a tuna roll and a Philly roll. The two roll special came with a pretty basic salad that was okay, but nothing really incredible. The tuna and Philly rolls were good.  Akira is good, but a little more expensive than I'm used to. I can usually get a tuna roll for about $3 and it was $5 here. All of the food was fresh and I enjoyed it.

We've parked here twice while we went to Broussard's and we didn't have an issue either time. The only times we have used this lot have been during the day, so I can't speak to what it's like at night, but in the daylight hours it feels pretty safe. Prices are pretty typical, although maybe not quite as expensive as some of the bigger lots.
Well, I drove up and ordered and they gave me the food in a timely manner. It doesn't get much better than that, right?

I love the peristyle! Not only is it probably one of the most well known landmarks at City Park, but there is always something going on.  Most recently, the peristyle hosted "Swingin' in the Oaks", which featured an orchestra playing all kinds of classic songs. The thing that I like most about the peristyle is the wide open space where you can just go and sit and relax on a nice day. One of my favorite things to do is get an iced coffee from Morning Call, and sit on the steps next to the lion statues and just relax and watch the goings on in the rest of the park.  Weddings and other fancy events are held in the peristyle as well and I have done my fair share of photo shoots in between the gorgeous pillars.

It's hard to find anything negative to say about this historic park and preserve. Okay, maybe one negative thing- during the summer it gets really hot and humid and the bug situation is insane, since you are in a swamp and all.  This park has some great man made trails, so that you can walk through and observe nature from the safety of some slightly raised wood. I wasn't exaggerating when I said that you are completely surrounded by swamp when you're here and although I have never seen a gator myself, I'm sure they are wandering around. Like, I doubt they say to themselves, "Hey, those people are trying to enjoy a nice nature walk, let's not spook them with our little eyes that float just above the water."  You are going to see spiders and other crawlies but you will also see gorgeous plants and flowers and you will hear birds chirping and get to experience the glory of nature first hand. This is a nice quiet place if you want to relax and a great place to spend some time during the cooler months.

Nice, quaint hotel.  Super easy to find and plenty of available street parking is always a plus with me. The rooms itself was nice. It had a nice sleep area with a small attached sitting area. There was a bar right by the door complete with a sink so that you could mix drinks and entertain if you want to stay in the room. I like that the hotel is far enough away from the madness of the French Quarter so that you can still walk around the area and not feel too much like a tourist.  I had a photo shoot here and the photographer mentioned that he got a really good deal on the room through one of those hotel discount sites, so be on the lookout for that kind of thing.

I have been a fan of Dirty Coast for the better part of 10 years or so. I wear their t shirts all the time and I love that they offer New Orleans themed goodies that aren't cheesy.  When I stopped in here I was on a mission: I was looking for pins. They offer the cutest New Orleans pins and I just had to stock up on a few. I got four and they were having a sale, so they came to $30 total. I got a gumbo with french bread, an oyster poboy, a snowball and a bloody Mary. I am SO excited to add these cute pins to my collection. I will definitely be back to get some more to give as Christmas gifts.

Although I didn't buy a mattress set from this place, they are getting 4 stars because of their huge selection and helpful employee.  I stopped in here the day before the 4th of July to check out what sales they had going on. I'm in the market for a new mattress set, and I decided to start my search here. The man working was extremely helpful and friendly and helped me decipher what kind of mattress I wanted, since there are so many choices these days (firm, plush, soft, pillow top, gel foam, etc.).  I won't say that they have the best deals in town, but they did have a lot of mattresses on clearance for around $300 and $400. While they really didn't fit what I was looking for, this would be a good place to start if you are looking for a discounted mattress for a college kid, a first apartment or a guest room.

This is pretty much the perfect gift shop for the "girly girl" in your life.  Not only does this shop have adorable clothing, but they have gifts that are perfect for a new bride (they have a cat themed glass that says "I'm getting Meowied"), anyone graduating, or pretty much anyone who likes wine. Their "I don't give a sip" glasses are pretty cute. I love the dainty jewelry they have here and I can never come here without buying at least one bracelet.  On my last trip in, I got myself a necklace, a bracelet and a cute top because they happened to be having an end of season sale. The better sale items are always on the back wall and the ladies working are always helpful in finding whatever you may be looking for. While this store isn't quite as big as the one at Oakwood, it's packed with a lot of good stuff.

This is a review of their king cake.  I'm always on the hunt for really good king cake. I'm not a huge king cake connoisseur, but I know what I like: traditional, "plain" with a nice icing/sugar combo.  I had heard the king cake here at Coffee & was good, so I picked one up. First of all, the cake here is HUGE and costs $15- well worth the money in my opinion. It was nice and soft and had that nice cinnamon taste that I enjoy in a king cake. The icing/sugar combo was perfect and overall I enjoyed it and would purchase another one.  In addition to king cake, this diner has traditional donuts and diner food, including $6 shrimp and grits. I'm tempted to try it, but I'm also scared. I think I'll just stick to the king cake.

Bacchus is one of my favorite parades. This Super Krewe is made up of huge, gorgeous floats and is always generous with the throws. I usually like to catch it on St. Charles Avenue, because I can't be bothered with barricades on the downtown part of the route.

Hey kids!  Do you want your teeth vibrated out of your head by music that is super loud?  Do you want to dance in near darkness with sweaty strangers on drugs to repetitive, pulsating beats?  Do you want to over pay for a weak vodka drink?  Do you want to be hit on by a 50-something year old man who is just too cool to stay out of the club on a Saturday night (he is SO HIP!)?  Do you just have nothing else to do come 4 in the morning and you want to make one more bad decision?  Then Ampersand or "Amps" is the place for you!  Ugh.  Seriously.  It's New Orleans.  Why are you in a horrible nightclub that wishes it was in Las Vegas?  Go see some jazz, for goodness sake.  I haven't been here in over two years.  I will never go back.  You can't make me.

Mardi Gras fountain is a landmark that I didn't even know was check in-able! I think it was built to honor all of New Orleans' Mardi Gras krewes. It really is a gorgeous landmark, now that it's been redone, albeit a bit out of the way.

I'm going to start off with a really basic assessment: World of Beer is great for those of you who live in Metairie, want some decent beer and maybe have yet to discover Lager's.  Maybe I went at the wrong time. I went on a Saturday night and there was the usual crowd of people in there who were looking for a party. My friend and I sat at the bar and looked over the menu. Nothing really jumped out at me and everything you can find here you can find at Avenue Pub.  The vibe here is just weird. It's a beer bar and we were sitting at the bar and the bartender was non stop with making mixed drinks. Who comes to a beer bar and gets mixed drinks? And then there was a singer there that just felt unnecessary, out of place and odd.  If you want food they have such faire as the "beer pretzel". God only knows what that is. I'm sure it's a pretzel with a beer sauce or something.  There are way better places for beer all over the city. I won't be returning to WoB.

This place isn't as terrible as some other clubs (*cough* Amps *cough*), but it's still not really my scene. It is a big space with three different bars downstairs and the staff does seem to do pretty well in handling a big crowd. The music is horrible and way too loud. Yeah, I know, it's a nightclub. I guess I'm old. Whatever. When my teeth are vibrating in my head, I'm not having fun.  They have different theme parties that they go all out for. I haven't been to one in years, but I remember them being a pretty good time.

I think I may have new favorite Quarter bar!  This is a really cozy spot, I love the atmosphere and the whole place just feels "old New Orleans/Europe" to me. On the night we were here we sat at the bar and had some champagne. The vibe here is very laid back and relaxed, and on this particular night, it was a thin crowd and Patrick was walking around talking to customers and having a good time.  There's an outside patio area that I am eager to check out when the weather gets a little cooler. The best part about the place is that it's close to Bourbon for those who want to be near the "action", but not in it, but it has yet to be over run with obnoxious tourists (I love tourists, but not the ones who only come to New Orleans to get wasted).  I can't wait to go back.

Three cheers for Gator 1! We got to ride this around town for the Brews Cruise and our lovely CM Morgan gave us special permission to review this one of a kind party transport system.  As others have described, the Gator 1 is a party bus that has been magically transformed from a fire truck. If that's not cool enough, you are in a covered but open vehicle where you are standing (and holding onto the safety bar) as you are driven from spot to spot (complete with sirens and honking).   Don (the captain of Gator 1) was awesome and kept the tunes pumping and he helped us maneuver getting in and out of the truck safely. This is probably the most fun party bus type thing that I have ever been on. Don is a very safe driver and drives slowly so that everyone is safe on the ride.  I had such a great time and I wouldn't hesitate to hire Don and Gator 1 for any type of party or bar crawl.

This is a review of the bar only.  We stopped in here for some post-event cocktails and I immediately loved the laid back vibe of the place; it was really cozy and hip. The bartenders were really sweet and I was impressed with Revel's beer selection.   I'm always looking for nice bars that cater to the "chat and drink" crowd more than the "party" crowd and Revel definitely fits the bill. They seem to have quite the selection of cocktails that I will have to try the next time I'm in the area.

5 years later and I just bought a mattress from here, so I'm re-reviewing!  I actually bought the mattress a few months ago, but I wanted time to "break it in" to make sure I liked it. I ended up getting a nice new Sealy at a fair price. My advice: always wait for sales to purchase a mattress- they happen multiple times a year and you will save a ton.  Anyway, the staff was very helpful when I stopped in to look at mattresses and I ended up finding a foam mattress that I love! It's been a few months and I have no complaints. The delivery folks took my old mattress when they delivered the new one, so the process couldn't have been any easier.

Kind of a weird way to describe it, but I would almost label this place "Vietnamese fast food".  It's a small place located right inside the Hong Kong market. There's a counter where you can order and a couple of tables and chairs.  I stopped in because I heard through the grape vine that they have an avocado smoothie here and avocado smoothies are my new obsession. Went right in and ordered. I like that you have the option of getting your drink without the tapioca balls (my choice). The smoothie was a really good size for $4.75 and full of flavor. You could tell that it was really fresh. Pro tip: I noticed that as the drink warmed to room temperature the avocado taste was a lot more rich, so don't be so quick to gulp it all down in the first few minutes.  They also serve small banh mi sandwiches, which are a steal at $3 each. That's why I labeled it "fast food", because you can get a quick little bite for cheap.  I'll definitely be back and I'll probably get some sandwiches when I return.

This is a lovely photo gallery located right in the heart of Jackson Square.  The work of Louis Sahuc is featured throughout the gallery, Louis has been a photographer since 1972, and here you can buy originals and prints of his work in all sizes. His lovely art varies from pictures of New Orleans during a hard rainstorm, to St. Louis Cathedral in the fog and the people of New Orleans.  What I like about Louis Sahuc's work is that it isn't typical New Orleans photography. Yes, there are pictures of the architecture of the city, but his work seems to contain more heart than some of the other work I've seen. I feel like his pictures are meant not only to appeal to tourists, but to find homes with locals as well.  If you are in the area, be sure to stop in and check it out.

Crazy good!  We stopped in here for dinner one night and even though it was a Friday, it wasn't crowded at all. I had never been here before, but I knew what I was in the mood for so ordering was a breeze. I started with a frozen margarita with salt and chips and queso. The margarita was perfect, and although it was probably from a mix, I liked it. The chips and queso were a perfect start- the chips were nice and thin and not too salty.  For my entree I got the pork burrito and I got an order of rice and beans on the side. This burrito was HUGE! I loved that it was topped with sour cream and taco sauce and it was jam packed with huge pieces of pork, rice, beans, sour cream, cheese and guacamole. This would have been easily split between two people. The rice and beans were okay, but I found the rice to be a bit dry.  Service was spot on our waitress didn't leave us waiting for the check or the box. I will return.

I want to start by saying the salesman was great and I have zero issues with him.  I stopped in here while getting some prices for a new mattress. Believe it or not, it's been 5 years since I bought a new mattress and it was already sagging, but that's another story. I found a mattress that I really liked at another store, so I was shopping around trying to find the best price. Well, first of all, spoiler alert- Mattress Direct has some of the highest prices I encountered, despite their catchy, "The best rest for less" slogan. Also, the mattress I was interested in was the only one that didn't have a box spring and was basically sitting on the machinery that was used to move it into the store, so if this had been my first stop, I wouldn't have even bothered trying the mattress I really wanted.  The salesman did his best to explain pricing and everything, but at the end of the day, it was "no" from me. There are better prices out there, so shop around before you buy from here.

If you're looking for a cute spot for a reasonably priced dessert, look no further than The Cupcake Collection. Here you will find the sweetest treats at the best prices. Flavors like chocolate, vanilla, strawberry, and they're famed sweet potato are must try.   Everyone who works here is always so sweet and welcoming and the cupcakes are simple, but delicious. They are still taking covid precautions, so for best service, I would suggest ordering your cupcakes ahead of time on their website. But, if you just drop in, they'll take care of you.  I wrote about the history of this spot for Big Easy Magazine. Check it out here: https://www.bigeasymagazine.com/2021/06/23/1new-orleans-native-mignon-francois-discusses-the-origin-of-the-cupcake-collective-and-how-she-built-the-wildly-successful-empire-from-scratch/

Why review a tunnel?  The same reason you climb Mt. Everest: because it's there.  There aren't a lot of reasons to travel to the Westbank.  Not that the Harvey Tunnel is a reason, I was just saying.  It is definitely a faster route than the expressway and if you want you can hold your breath when you go in and see if you can hold it the entire time until you drive out of it.  Only do that if you are a passenger, though.  I don't know what your breath holding capacity is and I don't want to be blamed for someone passing out and wrecking their car.  Umm... I guess that's about it.  Oh yeah, I kinda wanna see this tunnel and the Belle Chasse tunnel fight it out for "official tunnel of the Metro New Orleans" area.

I had been trying to decide what review #2200 would be and I had a spot in mind, but decided that it should be Ruby Slipper instead.  This is the last place I dined before the "stay at home" order from the mayor due to the covid-19 panic. We were already on edge when we ate here, but the bartender was AMAZING. He was funny and light-hearted and kept us laughing throughout our visit. He really took our minds of our worries, all while sanitizing everything and handling multiple customers at once with kindness. I'm kicking myself for not getting his name, but he had brown hair and a beard. He was wonderful.  For my meal I got my regular- Chicken St. Charles, which is a fried chicken Benedict on top of a biscuit. I also got a side of grits and bacon. It was all delicious and, considering the circumstances, it was perfectly cooked and served with a smile.  This experience is one of the reasons I love Ruby Slipper and I'll always return. They really make you feel like family. Please give that bartender a raise- he went above and beyond.

Water ice is a tasty dessert that's big in the east, especially in Philadelphia. The finely granulated concoction is blended with flavor throughout and scoops and eats like ice cream. It melts slowly and makes for the perfect treat on a hot day.   There are 20 flavors to try including blueberry, lemon, strawberry lemonade, cotton candy and cherry.  I tried the cherry flavor and, as someone who had never had anything like this before, I was immediately hooked. It's so much different than a New Orleans snowball. The flavor is evenly blended throughout the dessert and the taste is refreshing- I was a fan after my first bite. I like that it doesn't melt quickly and get all soupy, like some other ice desserts.  If you want something other than dessert, Tapeh's provides lunch items such as chicken and waffles, sandwiches, nachos, fries and Philly cheesesteak.  I wrote about this spot for Very Local New Orleans, read the whole article here: https://nola.verylocal.com/tapehs-water-ice-brings-a-tasty-east-coast-treat-to-algiers/161674/

Grit's isn't as bad as it's next door neighbor, F&M's. The crowd tends to be a little bit older and the music is more tolerable.  I stopped in on a week night for drinks with a few friends and I realized that it's actually a decent establishment. The drinks are well priced and the bar is a "hang out" for friendly neighborhood folks who are happy to make conversation. I remember this place before the smoking ban, and I can only imagine that the ban worked in Grit's favor. The bartender was friendly and was happy to make small talk and I would return on another week night.

Really big PJ's and open pretty late (we stopped in around 9 after we had sushi next door), so that's pretty cool.  Lot's of tables and free WiFi for anyone who wants to do some work. Definitely one of the "sit and stay" PJ's, rather than a "order and go" store. The iced coffee I ordered was really good and priced the same as other PJ's.  I'll be back when I find myself in the area.

The food here is a reflection on what you would find in any Colombian kitchen; the servings are large and the dishes don't hold back on the flavor. The experience feels as if you are eating in a friend's home rather than a restaurant.  Some of the menu's specialties are Empandas ($2.50), a traditional corn patty filled with beef or chicken; Bandeja Paisa ($22), white rice, red beans, grilled steak, pork belly fried egg, avocado, sweet plantain, Colombian chorizo and arepa; Patacón Gloria ($18-$22), fried green plantain with lettuce and cheese with choice of pork, steak and chicken, or shrimp; and Pescado Frito ($25), a grilled stuffed fish served with rice, vegetables, fried green plantains and salad.  Everything was fantastic and the owners are so nice. They now have outdoor seating which is perfect for nice days.  I wrote about this spot for Uptown Messenger. Check it out here: https://uptownmessenger.com/2021/05/golden-gate-bistro/

We wandered into Brick Oven, one night, after Gendusa's was packed. This was right after the election, so I assume people were just happy to be out of the house and eating cheap.  We got here and the place was pretty dead and we were seated quickly.  For our appetizer we got cheese bread and for my entree I got shrimp and crawfish pasta and I got a meatball on top, for funsies. The cheese bread was delicious- it's super hard to mess that up. The shrimp and crawfish pasta was excellent, as well. The meatball was a little over cooked, but that's not the end of the world.  I used to go to Brick Oven more often than I do now, but I think I'm going to add it to the rotation.

David and I were here on my birthday because it was the only bar that wasn't crazy packed, because there was a big event going on downtown.  I like this place- the vibe is relaxed and the big selling point is their awesome beer selection. You don't expect to find a good craft beer bar in the middle of Bourbon St., but this spot fit the bill nicely, so I was happy that we just happened to find this spot. They had a band when we first got there, but they were on their last song as soon as we sat down.   This is a place worth checking out, if you're trying to get away from the crowds.

Honestly, I'm not a SUPER huge fan of Indian food. I'm a firm believer that within every type of food there is something that a person can at least tolerate but I find it difficult to find something tolerable about food with curry.  When I came here, a friend of mine and I split an order of chicken tikka masala. It was basically chicken in a cream sauce served with rice. It wasn't bad, but it's probably not something I would go out of my way to order again.  I really don't know if I'll be back. I try to stay open minded, but this type of food just really doesn't ring my bells.

Considering all of the lots in the Quarter are now "pay ahead", the garages are really becoming the only option, if you don't want to pay for more time than you need.  This is a pretty typical parking garage. You pull in, hand your keys over to the valet and you pay and get your car when you return. This is a good place to pay and park if you're going out in the Bourbon area and you want to be close and get there and back quickly. We parked here when we were going to Mr. B's and when we returned we handed over our ticket with no problem. There was a little oddness while we were waiting for our car. Turns out the person we handed our ticket to didn't pass it off to a valet, so we waited longer than we had to.  All in all, this was a pretty good experience and definitely beats parking in one of those drafty lots, especially when the weather is cool.

I'll tell you what. I was here on a Saturday morning for a quick coffee and this place was BUSTLING!   Apparently, they do a good brunch here and people were knocking back the cocktails at 10:00 a.m. This is a cute place to hang out if you want drinks and something to munch on, especially around breakfast or lunch. It's casual but has a good vibe.  I've never had anything other than coffee here, but the flavored beignets are tempting, so I might try them when I find myself here again.

Alma is such a fantastic cafe for brunch and lunch! If you're a fan of coffee and delicious Hondura food, this is the place for you.  All-day breakfast includes highlights such as the Alma Breakfast: two eggs, refried beans, sweet plantains, avocado, queso fresco, and homemade crema; Louisa Toast: Louisiana lump blue crab, soft scrambled eggs, mushrooms, and herbs served on white rustic bread with chive cream cheese; Breakfast Tacos: three homemade corn tortillas, scrambled eggs, roasted poblano, pepper jack cheese, crispy potatoes, and avocado served with salsa; and Corned Beef Hash: Homemade corned beef hash, home potatoes served with two sunny-side-up eggs.  The lunch menu is sure to delight with Enchiladas Hondureñas: two enchiladas made with local Louisiana ground beef, green cabbage, sliced boiled egg, homemade red sauce, and queso cotija; Carne Asada: Louisiana-raised Wagyu ribeye, torched cherry tomatoes and encurtido served with four homemade corn tortillas; and Camarones a la Diabla: grilled local Louisiana jumbo shrimp topped with Calabrian chile butter and Japanese panko breadcrumbs.  I wrote about this spot for Offbeat. Read more here: https://www.offbeat.com/articles/dining-out-alma-cafe/

I have been to this place twice and both times it was fantastic.  The first time I went I got the pig ears (yeah...) and I think I got some kind of sandwich.  That was pretty good.  BUT, the second time I went I got the rabbit and dumplings.  Oh my gosh!  It was one of the most fantastic dishes I have ever eaten.  I had never had rabbit before, so I was hesitant, but it was so rich and delicious, I couldn't get enough.  Be sure to make reservations (if possible) or get there early in order to avoid the dinner rush, because the place does get crowded and getting a table can be a challenge.  Also, they are also the only place that I know that serves actual moonshine.  Do with that what you will.  ;)

I don't understand why the French Market has such a low rating.    Sure, it's always packed with cheap stuff like sunglasses and lighters and purses, but there is something about it I love.  On a nice day, I like to take a trip down to the french market and go "treasure hunting".  There is no denying that it's a great place to find that perfect souvenir for an out of town friend.  I would much rather patronize this market rather than the dinky little souvenir shops that litter the downtown area and carry tshirts that say things like "I got Bourbon faced on S**t St." (although, that is a classic).  This place carries everything from purses to sunglasses to lighters and everything else in between.  They only accept cash, so be sure to hit the ATM before you go.

While this isn't my "go to" salon, I recently had a fancy pants photo shoot and I was sent here to have my "up do" and makeup done.  First, Ms. Jan took care of me and started on my hair. She worked with me to determine what kind of look I wanted, and then she went to work. You can tell that she is a pro, because she had me in a gorgeous up do in no time!  Next, it was time to get my make up done. I went over to Meg and she gave me a "natural" look for the bridal photo shoot that I had planned. Honestly, I don't wear makeup a lot, but when I do I like to put a little more on than she did. I guess when you are doing a bridal shoot, you want subtlety. All in all, I was satisfied with the look I was given.  I can't say I would go back to Salon Couvie, only because they are no where near me, but I will say that if you are in the area and you need hair or makeup done, the Salon Couvie staff does a great job.

It's so cheesy that you appreciate how cheesy it is after a couple of cocktails.  Yeah, this is a super small *blink and you'll miss it* bar in Pirate's Alley. Yeah, the female bartenders are trussed up like wenches. Yeah, they serve Absinthe. Yeah. the whole place has a pretty "toursity" feel, but by the time you venture into this place none of that is going to bother you.  The place is small and cozy and tends to get packed, but there is seating outside, so what are you complaining about? They serve Absinthe and it comes with a whole fancy story that is intended for tourists but if you're a local, I'm sure you will appreciate it as well. I like it here because it feels like a secret hideout, since it's in alley. Cash only, sucka.

Ahh! My sweetie was nice enough to surprise me with some goodies from Sucré and I couldn't have been more delighted. There's just something about a man who knows you have a thing for fancy cupcakes. We each had a vanilla cupcake and red velvet cupcake. The cupcakes are HUGE, soft and tasty. I preferred the vanilla one slightly more that the red velvet because it was a little more moist and it had GLITTER ICING! Who doesn't love edible glitter? It might be the best thing ever. These cupcakes are probably worth whatever you have to pay in order to get your hands on them- they are delicious and decadent and reminiscent of pieces of wedding cake. I can't wait to have more.

Raucous, rowdy and irreverent are all words I would use to describe Krewe Du Vieux.  Classically, the first parade of Carnival season, Krewe Du Vieux is always a good time.  The themes are very "adult" themed, so mom, leave little Timmy at home.  The throws vary from the usual (someone gave me a ceramic mask one year) to the ridiculous (condoms and tequila shots).  This parade is always a good time and is best enjoyed with a cold beer and a good group of friends.  Another Mardi Gras "must".

Yes!  This place is fantastic.  They have wonderful sandwiches and pastas.  One of my faves to get is actually the "vegetarian" sandwich, which is basically a veggie pizza between two pieces of flat bread, but it's really good.  I've also had their chicken pasta which was absolutely fantastic.  This place does great take out, if you are just in the mood to place an order and pick it up.

Pretty good, but I wasn't overly blown away. The iced coffee wasn't too bad but it really wasn't anything special. It was as good as PJ's (and about the same price) but if I'm going to a local coffee shop, I want something a little more special.  The place itself is small. Very small. And it seemed to be lacking something. It didn't feel very "warm" to me and the atmosphere seemed off. The porch was super nice and if it had been a cooler day I would have enjoyed my coffee there.  I would go back for the coffee, but I wouldn't stay.

I was introduced to this by my boyfriend.   I'm pretty picky when it comes to Chinese food, but this place is great.  My faves are the steamed dumplings, crab rangoon and fried rice.  Food is ready fast and it's always good!

Didn't actually step into this place, but we did order delivery from here.  We had the grilled chicken pizza and it was so good. It's a veggie pizza topped with chunks of chicken. The best part is the HUGE pieces of roasted garlic. I LOVE garlic, so it was awesome finding yummy pieces of garlic buried under mounds of cheese and other toppings. Speaking of cheese, there was tons of it. Magazine Pizza does not skimp at all. I will definitely be trying other pies from this place!

Goorin Bros. is one of those places where I would definitely splurge on a regular basis, if I had the money and if I had the occasion to wear a lot of different fancy hats.  We stopped in here during French Quarter Fest and I think I was secretly hoping that I would stumble across the perfect sun hat, because I was baking in the sun. Alas, it wasn't meant to be, but they do have a nice selection of different fancy hats for special occasions. The selection of women's hats seems to be a bit more generous than other hat shops I've visited, and the staff seems to be pretty cool with people coming in and trying on hats to see what works best for them. Hats aren't cheap, but you can tell that they are made to last.  Goorin Bros. does frequently have sales, so I think the next time they have one of their sample sales I will have to treat myself.

The Rusty Nail is okay. I don't know if I understand the obsession that some people have with that place. They serve decent drinks and the staff is nice and friendly.  The real selling point of "The Nail" is the patio. It's large and gorgeous and on a nice night you can sit out there with friends and have a really nice evening under the stars.  There's pretty much nothing else for me to add that hasn't been said already. I'll return to The Rusty Nail, but I won't go out of my way.

If you're going on vacation, renting a car is the way to go.  David and I decided that renting a car would be the best idea for our trip to Pensacola and we were right. David booked a 4 door car on booking.com, made all the arrangements and the car was ready for pickup at 8am on the day of our trip. The car was the perfect size, super comfortable and had plenty of room for luggage and room to spread out. The car didn't have any funky smells and it was clean and ready to go when we picked it up. Not only that, but the car got fabulous gas mileage and got us safely to and from Pensacola with no issues at all.  You have to put down a $250 fee, with the regular fee, when you rent the car but you get that back when you return the car. We are definitely going to be renting from Enterprise again.

Like everyone else, I'm going to go ahead and call this store really cute. They have a great selection of shoes and they were even having a really nice sale when I was here. Whether you are looking for "night on the town" type shoes or just casual shoes, you will find some good deals here.  When I was here I was looking for some shoes to go with my Halloween costume. The woman working was very helpful and although I didn't find exactly what I was looking for, I saw enough to know that I will be returning whenever I am in the need for some stylish pumps. They also carry a nice selection of New Orleans themed t shirts that are made out of a really soft cotton, so check that out if it's your thing.

What kind of weirdo goes to a Jamaican food truck and gets a veggie burger? Um...I do!  I guess I really wasn't in the mood for jerk chicken when I decided to mosey up to this truck for a bite to eat. The veggie burger wasn't bad. It certainly got the job done. I was starving when I noticed this truck! I would try it again and I would probably get the jerk chicken and not the veggie burger.

One word: Tomato Basil Soup  Really, that's all you need to know.  The soup...it is to die for.  Everything I have gotten here has been fabulous.  They have great desserts and bread, but that soup...WOW.  Let's just say this...they sell it by the jar.  That's how awesome it is.  Great prices and great food.  Who can hate that?

My boyfriend and I's favorite breakfast spot.  He usually gets the french toast, which looks delicious.  We have also gotten the big breakfast and the breakfast sandwich they have there.  The food is always awesome and if you like bacon, they don't "stiff" you on it.  Coffee isn't fabulous, but you can eat outside with your dog, if you want.  Great on Saturdays after the Gretna Farmers Market, which is just a few steps away.

It's easy to see why they call it Burger King. This place is truly tops when it comes to a good burger. The burgers are flame broiled, so you can really taste the difference. Is it real meat? Who knows and who cares? When something tastes this good, you just want to eat it. I really like how the slice of American cheese that was haphazardly slapped onto my double cheeseburger was clearly done so with love. Was the cheese melted onto the burger? Of course it wasn't! It was still cold from the fridge, just how you like it. The bun was perfectly warmed to slightly above room temperature which added a nice touch to this meal that I scarfed down in my car, in under 3 minutes, while at a red light.  I actually was impressed that no one was here in the mid afternoon and I was served quickly without any fuss. Brava.

I really loved this bar. On a night where we were trying to avoid a huge crowd, it was a life saver. They have a jukebox in the back and it's nice and dark. I love a dark bar! A few street performers filtered in and out for drinks and it just seems like a really fun spot. The bartender was really friendly and welcoming and the beer was good.

Surprisingly, things are pretty well organized here. I've never been confused or gotten lost when I was trying to figure out where to go. Parking is fairly plentiful. People working here taking care of tickets are really nice and helpful.

A large gallery of bodypainted works located in the French Quarter.  Craig is a true artist and paints everything on the human body from landscapes to animal prints.  It's such a unique art.  You can buy pictures of his work at his gallery.  Craig takes his work very seriously and travels the world attending different body painting conventions and events.  He is known for bodypainting large groups on White Linen Night and Halloween night and sending them off to hypnotize all the people who are out and about for these events.  If you want, you can even contact Craig about possibly being a living canvas for his gorgeous work.

I can't really give a review of a "full on" dinner experience here, but we did stop in on the tail end of happy hour and sat at the bar and ate.  The bartender was friendly and took our order and brought our food out fairly quickly. I had the Caesar salad with chicken, which was nothing overly spectacular, but it hit the spot at the time.  I think their happy hour starts at some insane time like noon and goes until 7, so if you are looking for an early drink, this might be a good place to start.
