I have been on the hunt for organic soap for a while now, so when someone suggest I check out the Herb Import company, I was a bit confused. I thought this place only sold incense and essential oils. I had no idea that there is so much more to this shop!  Not only was I able to find my amazing organic soap, but they had it in all kinds of yummy scents and it didn't break the bank. This shop also carries a wide variety of things such as Saints you can display in your car (holy Saints, not NFL Saints), assorted vitamins and supplements, organic teas, "good luck" candles and interesting gifts that are perfect for the more spiritual person in your life. Of course, they do also sell incense and essential oils, but you should go in knowing that they sell a little bit of everything.  Bonus points: this shop smells so good!

We had a major craving for crawfish when we we decided to check this place out. They have crawfish at $5/lb, so the prices aren't terrible right now.  This is a pretty basic place: they have a bar area, you sit at a table and you order whatever you want. We decided to get a few pounds of crawfish, potatoes and two big pieces of sausage. The crawfish was pretty good, and although I like it when it's a bit spicier, I enjoyed them. It's early in the season, so they were small and some were mealy, but that's not the fault of Perino's. The potatoes were delicious and the sausage was perfect.  Aside from crawfish, they have crabs, shrimp and oysters so they will satisfy any seafood desire that you just so happen to have.

It's a bar!  It's a theatre! One Eyed Jack's has everything.  This place has regular burlesque shows as well as comedy shows and live music.  They have 80's night on Thursdays starting at 10 and the it is by far one of the most popular weekly events in the city and the place gets packed.    The drinks are pretty cheap, by quarter standards, and the people here are always nice.  Great place to hang out if you are an "artsy" type, as you are sure to meet someone here that you have something in common with.

This is a cute cafe located in the Roosevelt hotel and is a pretty perfect spot for lunch  This was a tough call, as far as a rating goes. On one hand, the Cuban sandwich I had wasn't the best I've ever had but I was starving when I ate it and it really hit the spot. The truffle fries were amazing. They came with aioli for dipping and I couldn't get enough. I could have had an entire meal of fries. They have a really cute case that is full of little chocolates to choose from and they also have coffee drinks.  They have a few sandwich and salad options here and while it isn't the cheapest lunch in the city, you get a good amount for what you pay for.  I'm marking the place three stars, but would probably lean more towards 3.5 stars, if this were Star Search.

I was excited to try Fellini's today because I had noticed that a lot of yelpers check in here and it sounded like a good location for lunch.    So, I went today for lunch and the place was pretty empty.  I ordered the ham and cheese sandwich which came with a side of pasta salad.  Ok, so the sandwich wasn't anything amazing and I've had better pasta salad, but for lunch it wasn't bad.  I'm giving this place four stars for a few other reasons.  There is outdoor seating on a lovely patio.  It seems like a great place to have lunch with girlfriends, sip wine and watch the world go by.  Another good thing about it, although the place is small, there is a nice size parking lot.  One of my biggest pet peeves of other "cafe" type places is lack of parking or super small lots.  Yeah, service was slow, but that's not a huge deal.  I sat at my table and read the latest issue of the "New Orleans Levee".

Question: why is the hot new trend things that are knitted? Dresses that are knitted. Shorts that are knitted. I don't get it, but if you like knitted things, H & M has tons of it!  I can't figure out how I feel about H & M. On one hand they have some cute things at good prices, on the other hand I feel like most of their clothes are geared towards 21 year old girls living in California. However, I am glad that this huge new store opened at Oakwood.  This store is pretty big and they have clothes for men, women and kids. They have a large selection of mainly casual clothes and they have a decent shoe and lingerie section. The shoes don't look like they would last that long, but they are only about $10, so it's still a deal.  When I visited this store, I was happy to see that the line was super long, so they seem to be doing good business already. The staff seemed capable and were getting people in and out fairly quickly.

Sometimes a girl needs something sexy- either for her own thrill, or the thrill of another. Enter Trashy Diva.  Don't let the name fool you- there is nothing "trashy" about this spot. Here you will find the best of the best when it comes to lingerie and other underthings. I scooped up a bra (and a few other frills) for a keen price and the staff was more than willing to help me figure out exactly what I needed.  If you are looking for a little bit of satin and lace to make you feel special, then this is the spot for you. Don't be shy about asking the staff for some help, they are here to make sure you find exactly what you are looking for.  I had NO IDEA you could hold events here and thanks to Emily M., I will be making a note of this and will probably have a party here in the future. What a brilliant idea!

This is a pretty good PJ's with a friendly staff. I love the fact that it's big and the windows let in a lot of natural light. I ordered my regular large iced coffee and it was good, but I think that the half and half I added to it was off. It had an odd taste, so I blame the add-in.  There are plenty of big tables so that you can sit and do work and, of course, the wi-fi is free. This wouldn't be my first choice for a NOLA PJ's, mainly because there's a sketchy gas station across the street, but it gets the job done if you're in the area.

Stopped in here during French Quarter Fest to take a break from the heat and get a bite to eat. Considering it was a busy day, we were seated and served quickly.  We got to sit in a small table in the corner, which I really liked. It was nice to be away from the crowd for a while. We decided to order the muffaletta and split it. It was a little on the bready side, but after a long day on my feet it was delicious and hit the spot.  I loved the atmosphere of this place. All of the doors were open and people were sitting outside and inside eating and talking and enjoying each other and the nice day. It gave the afternoon a very quaint feel and I really appreciated it.  I'l definitely be back and I'm excited to try the other food that they offer.

To the locals, the Gambit might not be much, but I think it's an excellent resource for out of town visitors.  Available at many venues through the city, the Gambit offers information on events that are going on in the city such as live shows, fests and gallery showings.  The Gambit offers reviews of restaurants and has articles about little historic things that are going on the city.  For example, in the Mardi Gras issue, there was an article about the history of Rex.  It's not one of the greatest free publications in the city, but considering that it is probably geared more towards tourists, it gets the job done.

This is a neat little grocery store. It reminded me a little of Whole Foods, but not as snobby.  I came here looking for something specific and was helped right away. The staff is friendly and everything is really easy to find.

Two new sushi places in a week!  Lucky me!  I had never been to Sushi Brothers, and I'm always eager to try new sushi places.  Seriously.  I think I want to review every single one in the city.  Anyway, we weren't super hungry when we ate here, so we only ended getting three rolls.  We got a crunchy dynamite roll, a cucumber roll and a special roll, the black and gold roll.  I won't bore you with the details of the crunchy dynamite and cucumber rolls.  They were good, and let's face it, that stuff is hard to screw up.  The black and gold roll was fantastic!  I can't remember what was in, except that it had cream cheese and it was topped with avocado and mango.  They said that it is their most popular specialty roll, and I can see why.  It is fantastic!  Don't be scared of the cream cheese, fish combo...it's really good!  I would definitely go back here.  I like that it has a more casual feel than a lot of other sushi places around town.

Maybe it makes me a weirdo, but I was super-duper ridiculously excited when I discovered that we were finally getting a Reginelli's on the Westbank. It's my favorite local pizza place and the new location isn't far from my house: score!  I stopped in for lunch at around 2 on a Wednesday. First of all, this place is huge- perfect for groups and lots of space. I wasn't in the mood for pizza, so I decided to get the Downtowner sandwich which is turkey, salami, tomatoes, cheese and some other goodies on toasted garlic bread. The sandwich was fantastic and I really enjoyed it and it the perfect thing for lunch.  I'm also excited about this place because they have free delivery, so I will be taking advantage of that soon.

While I'm not as outraged as Charles H., I gotta be honest: the iced coffee here is sub par. I drink a lot of iced coffee around town and the brew here is two things I can't stand: super bitter with a tart under taste and so packed with caffeine that it made me feel jittery and weird.  I got the iced coffee with 2% milk, but I guess that wasn't enough to dilute the weird, bitter flavor of it. It just wasn't good. I got a large, took 2 sips and really wanted to throw the rest away. I forced myself to drink it, so as not to have totally wasted my money, and I was left a shaky, over-caffeinated mess by the time I finished the cup.  They are getting three stars because the woman in front of me ordered 4 or 5 cups of coffee and a ton of pastries and they were fast about it, so I didn't have to wait long to get my order in and get out of there. The atmosphere seems nice and would be a quiet place to do work or chat, but the coffee just wasn't for me.

I'm a longtime fan of La Madeline and, although I usually frequent the one on St. Charles, this is a good location as well.  I stopped in for my usual- a bowl of their delicious tomato basil soup which, paired with bread, is pretty much the perfect meal. It was as good as ever and I lucked out because there wasn't much of a crowd on the evening I was here.  My one complaint about this location is that the parking lot is awful. There is one way in and one way out, and if you miss your chance to turn in, you are pretty much screwed. In fact, all of the parking lots in this little area are bad, but I digress. Just have your wits about you, when you get here because if you miss your turn, you're done.

I don't know, but Puccino's really thinks a lot of themselves.  I passed through, and I was just in the mood for an iced coffee. A medium iced coffee costs a bit over $3 and a large costs over $4. Uhh...what? I know that they peg it as "Italian" coffee, but it's not good enough to be charging these kind of prices. I didn't eat here, but they have a pretty extensive lunch menu with sandwiches and salads. I do like the atmosphere with the booths and little coffee things packed into every corner. There are too many coffee places in this area to waste your money here.

I went to Murphy's for the first time years ago.  I think I was on a date.  Considering it's a Westbank bar, it's really not a bad place.  They have a pretty diverse beer selection on tap, pool tables and dart boards.  They also have a really cool internet juke box, so you can play any kind of song that you like.  The bartenders are always friendly and the atmosphere is laid back.  My only complaint is that the smoke in here is out of this world, so it's not a place that I would frequent, because of that.

Some might say my first mistake was getting fish at a chicken joint.  Well, who asked?  So, I went and I was in the mood for catfish.  I got the catfish, and well...there was a good amount of it and the pieces were nice and thick.  The problem was...well...see, it's a chicken place.  They fry their chicken in the oil and then they fry their fish in the oil.  Then the fish tastes like chicken.  I guess if they called it "chicken fried fish" I would have given them three stars.  This is what I get for being adventurous.

Yeah. yeah.  I know.  Most people go here for breakfast.  Hey, I was one of those people too.  I always got the "quick two egg breakfast" whenever I happened to be here, no matter what time.  Getting anything else but pancakes or eggs at a place with "pancakes" in the title just seems...wrong.  Well, one day I was there for lunch  My boyfriend got his usual french toast, but I wanted something else.  I wanted to try actual lunch food.  So, I decided to try the pot roast melt, and oh, what the heck, I'll have some onion rings on the side.  Oh. My. Gah.  It was soooo good.  I haven't ordered anything else since I had this.  There is no going back for me.  I have even turned my boyfriend into a pot roast sandwich fan.  They are FANTASTIC!

Ah, newspaper, the dying medium.  My family has been a faithful subscriber to the Times Picayune for as long as I can remember.  Some may say that it's "bias", but really, what newspaper isn't?  Wherever you go, the newspaper is going to lean one way or the other and that's just the way it is.  I'll be honest.  Since I am a part of the "younger" generation, I do get most of my news online at nola.com (which is the same as the TP). because I find it more convenient to read throughout the day.  You get good info from this paper and I really think that it has a lot to offer.  My favorite part of the paper is probably the more local, bi weekly "break off"; Gretna Picayune, Marrero Picayune, etc.  It's full of local information about what is going on in the area and little local events.  Sure, this paper has flaws, but who doesn't save the first page when something significant happens in this town (Katrina, Super Bowl).

This is such a fabulous addition to this little area right off of Magazine St.!  I'll admit that I'm not huge in the crafts or sewing departments, but this store has a friendly staff that will show you around and help you with whatever you need. If you are the sewing type they do sell a lot of different fabrics for your to turn into something amazing.  I was most blown away by their embroidery. I got a beach bag embroidered with my name on it and it was lovely. It's the perfect thing to get me ready for the beach. They do embroidery on anything you like, so don't be shy about bringing something in for the staff to work on. They also offer sewing classes for kids, if you are looking to get them into a neat and useful hobby.

I used to go to this bar "back in the day" when it was called "Snooks".  I liked it then, and I like it even more now.  There are a few reasons to like this place.  First of all, it's at the end of Bourbon St. that is away from most of the drunken crowd.  Sure, you get some of it, because Tropical Isle is right across the street, but it's far enough away from the hip hop clubs to still be enjoyable.    Second of all, it's a hotel bar.  That means that you not only have access to a clean bathroom (on Bourbon St!), but the place is never going to get super, annoyingly packed and you're gonna be able to sit and have a conversation while enjoying a cocktail.  All in all, if I HAD to go Bourbon, I would probably try to stick to just going to this place, since it is nice for a Bourbon bar and the crowd isn't too rowdy.

The sculpture garden at the New Orleans Museum of Art is one of New Orleans' hidden treasures.  Located behind the museum, near city park, the garden is free to visit and the sculptures are ever changing and when you visit you almost feel as if you are in another world.  There is a body of water that goes through the garden and you can actually go on a gondola ride!  This is a great place to just come and relax and reflect and enjoy the scenery.  It's very quiet and peaceful and I think it would be fantastic to come here after a long day and just walk around or even on a date.

This is a good size Victoria's Secret with a really friendly staff.  Whenever I go here, I really can't walk from the entrance to the register without being asked if I need a bra fitting.  That's not a bad thing at all.  I don't need one, but they don't know that.  They have a nice selection of gorgeous lingerie, as well as perfumes, lotions, stockings and makeup.  There are obviously better places where you can buy higher quality lingerie, but if you are on the Westbank, don't hesitate to stop in.

Precision Movers is fantastic! I needed movers and I had zero experience with this type of thing, so naturally I was a bit nervous. I didn't know the process and I was worried about my antiques getting scratched.  Well, first of all, Precision Movers showed up a bit early (after calling to confirm that we were ready for them) and quickly got to work. Everything was wrapped up in padding so that nothing would be damaged and everything was moved, loaded and unloaded with care.  The two men that came were extremely nice and friendly and more than capable of handling the job in front of them. Everything that I needed moved was moved in about 2 and a half hours (they were scheduled for three hours).  I was beyond pleased and happy with the entire experience and I would DEFINITELY call on Precision Movers again. Also, I called them about a week before I needed them and they had no problem scheduling me in.

Popeyes doin' WORK!  If you read my last review, then you will understand why I hadn't returned to this Popeyes until tonight. I didn't feel like driving very far for dinner, so I thought I'd give this Popeyes another chance. After all, I was only ordering a couple of sides, so if they screw it up it's not a huge loss.  I popped in and I decided to just go inside rather than wait in the long drive through line. First of all, I was greeted immediately upon walking in. Then I gave my order- one large red beans and rice and one large mac and cheese. Service was fast and efficient and there was no wait. Here's the big news: they filled the sides all the way to the TOP, y'all! They topped them off! I'm talking a full container! Look, this is HUGE. Popeyes is always trying to hold back on the goods, but not tonight. TOPPED. OFF.   Maybe it was a fluke, but I'm kicking them up two stars for fast friendly service and delivering on the sides.

I've been to both this location and the uptown location.  Since the uptown one has nearly 100 reviews, I'll review this one.  Out of the two Juan's locations, this one is my definite favorite.  I have never had a to wait for a table here and the service is always fast and friendly.  I've found that at the other one, unless you sit at the bar you are in for a long wait for a table and then your food.  That's fine, if you aren't in a rush, but if you have places to be, then that doesn't work.  I go to the one in mid city and the staff is always friendly.  I get usually get the super burrito and end up taking half of it home.  I don't have to tell you how good the margaritas are.  They are excellent.  A good priced place with good food.  You can't go wrong.

I don't make it out to Lager's often, but when I find myself in Metairie, and the group I'm with wants something other than the same old, I usually suggest this place.  Not only does Lager's have a fantastic beer selection (in that sense, it is basically Metairie's answer to The Bulldog.  They even have some beer on tap that The Bulldog doesn't offer) but they have really good food.  I have gone here for dinner more than once and I would definitely call it a step up from typical "bar" food.  I like the "old pub" feel of the place.  They have a big screen for games days, but the place is small.  If you are planning on checking out your favorite team here, you might want to arrive early.

Maple Street Book Shop is a New Orleans institution and I am SO embarrassed that I am only just now stopping in here.  For such a small shop, Maple Street Books has quite the selection of everything from new and used to fiction, non fiction and local selections. As I walked up the quaint porch there was a rack of used books with a decent selection that I flipped through. After I made my way inside, I found myself in the "New Orleans" section that was full of books about the city we love. I picked up a copy of "Cast of Characters", a book about the different personalities that make New Orleans so unique.  There aren't enough book shops like this anymore and it feels like the "big names" have taken over, so it was nice to patronize this locally owned shop for a change. If I lived in the area, I would make it a point to come here more regularly.

Not my first choice for gas, but my gas light was on and I found myself here. This isn't a bad neighborhood station, but it's a little scary if you're here by yourself (especially if you're a woman pumping gas alone). Lots of folks will want to engage in small talk and the parking lot gets packed with lurkers. Pumps are slow to...well...pump, so you're going to be stuck standing there forever as people lurk around and look you over wondering who you are and if you live "around here".  Keep your head on a swivel, and you'll be fine.

THIS is what I'm talking about!  The snowballs here are the kind that made the snowball famous- the ice is super fine like velvet and each bite melts in your mouth. I decided to get a rainbow snowball, which is a mix of 4 flavors I couldn't name, but it was delicious. They also have a nice selection of shakes, malts, funnel cakes and other sweet treats. For some reason they don't take cards, so be sure to have some cash on hand.
It's a Sonic. What can you say? I pulled in, ordered a cherry limeade and got a cherry limeade. Service was fast and it was happy hour so I got a large for a little over a dollar. Win.

Im giving the Dungeon four stars on music alone.  They have really "heavy" stuff, that you don't hear in a typical bar.  Slated as an "underground" bar, the Dungeon has been around forever.  In the light of day, the gargoyles on the wall and the "spooky" decorations would look cheesy, but for some reason, it works here.    I went recently and was kind of disappointed that the long haired metal heads, that usually work the place, are gone.  In their place now is typical bouncer looking guys, who look out of place, except for their black tshirts.  The place is now, for all intents and purposes, a tourist trap, as is every other bar in the quarter.  In other words, if you are going to go expecting to see leather clad women hanging from the ceilings and "head bangers" rocking out to the latest NIN release, then prepare to be disappointed. If you are in the mood to listen to some good metal, then you will have a good time.

I hope your have your fancy pants ready, because you will definitely want to have them on when you drop into Mélange.  Not that the place is overly fancy or snooty, but it feels like one of those bars where it is most appropriate to dress up.   A friend and I dropped in here one night to see what this place was all about and what we found was a delightful speakeasy.  The atmosphere is wonderful and the bartender will be happy to make you a fancy cocktail for you to sip as you watch the foot traffic on Frenchmen go by.

This is a great dog park on the corner of Barracks and Dauphine St. in the French Quarter.  It's really big and takes up about half of a city block.    There is a large grass field for dogs to play in and get to know each other.  There are is also a cement spot where baby pools are filled with water, if your dog wants to take a dip on hot days.  There is also a fountain for water.  We brought a boxer here, and the other dog owners were really nice, even though he is a big dog that always wants to play.  The people seemed friendly, and there were nice shady spots to sit and escape from the heat as the dog wore himself out making new friends.

Heyyyy Heyyyyyy.  Ok, so first of all: I am starting to think that all of these New Orleans coffee shops get their coffee from the same place and the joke is on all of us for paying different prices.  I stopped in to grab an iced coffee. Yeah, I know that I'm boring and predictable. Whatever, I like what I like. The coffee was good and pretty cheap blah blah blah.  I really like the atmosphere of this place. It's right next door to Ms. Mae's which gives the places a bit of a "gritty" feel. It's small, but cozy with people doing work at the tables within. The door was open and I liked the welcome feel.  They have a lot of sandwiches and baked goods here, so it's a great place to stop in for a snack. It actually feels a lot like Mojo with the food and setup. I like it. I'll be back.

This isn't a bad little bar. I like the "Australian" kind of theme. There is usually soccer or some international sport playing on one of the tvs. It isn't the biggest place in the world, but a lot of days it sure beats whatever is going on across the street at Lucy's, which tends to get overly packed.  I probably wouldn't go out of my way to hang out here, but it's a cool spot if I find myself in the area.

Lakeview is a quaint little New Orleans suburb. I think it's really nice because it is basically right on the lake, there are a good number of decent restaurants and it's a good place to raise the kids. It's the perfect neighborhood for people who want to live in New Orleans, but not really.  Before Katrina, a good amount of the people who lived in Lakeview were older and mainly retired. Since the rebuilding, more and more younger people and their families have moved in and have contributed to the revitalization of the area.   Lakeview is a great area to live in for the days that you just want to go out to the lakefront and hang out and relax. If you are looking for a quiet neighborhood to live, this is the place. Just pack up the family, move into a lakefront mansion and pray that the levee doesn't snap (again).

This is a friendly neighborhood place that has probably became a lot more friendly since it was featured on a T.V. show that I won't name.  On the night I came there was no band (I know!) and there were just some neighborhood folks sitting around and have a good time. The bartender had a lot of personality, and even though it was late, he didn't "shoo" us out of the bar when we stopped in. I liked the atmosphere and I do want to come back when they actually have a band playing.

I feel weird writing a review of this place, because all we had here are appetizers, but here we are.  Me and a friend went here just because we were in the mood for some appetizers and we had both heard a lot of good things about this place.  We sat in the bar area and decided to order the pork tacos.  They were small, but really good.  The atmosphere of this place is nice.  It's a Susan Spicer restaurant, so you know it's going to be good quality dining.  I didn't get a look at the actual menu, but I would love to go back and check this place out for an actual dinner.  Just an amusing note.  You can tell that this is one of those places that is "see and be seen".  It's located in Lakeview and between all of the tanned, blonde women, I felt like I was watching a live version of "The Real Housewives of New Orleans".  I literally overheard a woman talking about how her kids are away at camp for the summer.  I just thought that was a neat little observation.  :)

Oh, Fridays, why did you mess with a good thing, when you changed your Caesar salad dressing?  I LOVED the old dressing.  What the heck is this new Caesar vinaigrette dressing you have now??  It's no where near as good as the old creamy Caesar dressing was.  I FINALLY found a Caesar dressing that I LOVED and you change it!  I'm so let down.  I understand that you might want to offer a healthier option, when it comes to dressing, but could you offer both the vinaigrette and the creamy one?  When all I'm having for lunch is a salad and soup, I'm really not counting calories.  4 stars, still, because I do like the food and it is really super cheap.

This is a fantastic little bar to hang out in, if you aren't really in the mood for the hustle and bustle of the Sazerac Bar. The vibe here is extremely laid back and on the nights I have been, there has been a jazz band playing. Food is served here and they have an assortment of specialty cocktails. I enjoy the Bayou Swizzle, which is a yummy rum drink with juice.  For a really romantic feel: sit in one of the corner booths. It's the perfect spot to sit and enjoy the music and atmosphere with a date.

I love The Grocery!  I just wish they were open later.  I guess with food this good, you can close when you darn well please.  I have a friend who lives within walking distance of The Grocery, and when we are hanging at his house for the Uptown parades, The Grocery is a must.  They have the best pressed sandwiches ever and my favorite is the pressed ham.  There is always a line during parade season, so be patient.  I have never been inside, I have always just ordered at the window and taken out.  I will have to try eating there the next time I go.

A little bit of Italy in our own backyard!   I didn't even know this place existed until a few years ago when a photographer suggested that we do a photo shoot here. I was blown away that something so cool was right in the middle of our city.  I love the different fountains and water scapes and at night it is just gorgeous when it is all lit up.  Taking pictures here is always fun, because someone will inevitably ask where the photo was taken and express shock when you tell them that it is right here in New Orleans.

The iced coffee proved to be a life saver during a particularly hot walk through the Quarter. The girl who took my order was nice and helpful and there wasn't a long line. I like that this location has two registers in order to keep up with any potential crowd, as I can imagine that in the morning this is extremely necessary. The coffee was tasty, cheap ($3 for a 24 oz) and definitely hit the spot.  They have an assortment of pastries and a nice area for seating. Everything is clean is well kempt, even after a busy French Quarter morning. The bathroom is also really clean and nicely taken care of.

NOMA is such a gorgeous museum.  This used to be one of my favorite places to go as a child.    First of all, NOMA is huge and has a lot of different works of art.  They always have "touring" exhibits.  I remember seeing a lot of different ones here, but I think my favorite was the Monet exhibit when I was about 12.  One of my favorite parts of NOMA is the sculpture garden, which is located just behind the museum itself.  It's a surreal garden with different sculptures that are always changing and it is just overall nice and relaxing.  When the weather is nice, NOMA also puts on plays in the sculpture garden and in the museum itself, so be sure to keep an eye out for that.

Here's another one of those "starter" parades that kind of get you ready for the bigger parades.  It's nice, but short and really not all that memorable.  I had a good time watching it, but I probably wouldn't go out of my way to see it, as I might for some other Krewes.

How does one go about reviewing a Home Depot? I mean, it's a huge hardware outlet. They sell everything from ceiling fans (have you ever just stood in that section on a hot summer day? Refreshing!) to all kinds of rope and everything in between. On the rare occasion that I have found myself here, I have been able to find whatever it is that I was looking for.

This review is for the bar area.   I would tell you how the service was here, but we were never served.  The people seemed nice.  The atmosphere was fancy-esque (although there was a game of some sort on the t.v.).  But we never got any food or drinks here.  We waited, but it took forever for the waiter/bartender to notice us.  Even when he did, we were left with zilch.  And there you have it.

The Green Bridge connects Chalmette to the rest of the world. Depending on how you feel about Chalmette, this could either be seen as a good or bad thing.  This bridge kind of feels like it leads off into nowhere and David mentioned that he doesn't feel like it's in the best condition. I don't think it's going to crash down or anything, but I wouldn't want to drive on it during a major storm or other weather event. As Chris mentioned, it doesn't have any lights, so I wouldn't want to drive on it at night.  This rusty old bridge to Chalmette is a perfect metaphor for being in Chalmette itself: it's not quite as good as what you'd find in New Orleans and you're going to have to deal with some things that make you uneasy so just hit the gas and get through it as quickly as possible.

This store is AWESOME!  Have you ever gotten one of those gift catalogs in the mail full of little odds and ends and stuff you really don't need, but you really want?  Well, Funrock'n has that stuff and more.  When you first walk in, don't be overwhelmed by the huge selection of goods.  There is so much stuff to look over, it will take you a while to absorb everything.  They have a huge selection of "retro inspired" items, such as Bettie Page and Marilyn Monroe lunchboxes, magnets coffee mugs, playing cards and other assorted gifts.  They also have cute little gift like hand held noise machines, and at Christmas I was tempted to get the stocking that was in the shape of the "major award" from "A Christmas Story" (they also had the night lite!).  Another thing I love about this place is the assortment of quirky greeting cards and magnets with nifty little sayings on them.  This is definitely a fantastic place to check out, if you are looking for a gift for someone in your life who is maybe a little quirky, fun, and has a sense of humor.

This is just a review of the bar.  We stopped in here on my birthday night because everywhere else in the area was pretty packed (one of the downsides of having a birthday that falls in that weird purgatory between Thanksgiving and Christmas). This is a pretty nice hotel bar and it was pretty quiet for a Saturday night. In fact, it was so quiet that David and I were the only couple in the place.  The bartender was really nice and they have a few decent beers on tap, for a reasonable price, so I had no complaints. The seating is really comfortable there are lots of sofas and chairs for lounging if that's your thing. Honestly, if you are having a night out in the Quarter, and you want to go a bit off of the beaten path, this is definitely the place for you. It still has the "New Orleans vibe" without the hassle of loud and obnoxious crowds.   It's a nice place to unwind at the end of a night out and I'd visit again.

This is a really cool spot that I had no idea even existed!  This is basically different spaces that you can rent for whatever your needs, whether it be dance or photography. The space that we were in was $30 for an hour, which is really perfect if you are giving a quick dance lesson or if you need space for a photo shoot. The studio we used had really big windows that let in a lot of light and make the area perfect for photography. It also had a huge mirror that was fun to play around with.  So many artists in this town are looking for open spaces in which to work, and I think that Nola Spaces is perfect for just that. The staff is friendly and accommodating and will put you in the space that best fits your needs.

There was a time when Bourbon St. was a host to glittery Burlesque shows and jazz bands and culture.  Those days are long gone.    Now Bourbon St. is nothing more than tacky souvenir shops, strip clubs and cheap drink bars.  It's basically where any kind of New Orleans culture goes to die and end up slapped on a tshirt.  It gets way too packed with people who are just there for cheap beer specials and terrible cover bands.  I guess this is a "must" for any New Orleans first timer, but go during the day and only go once.  There is really nothing redeeming about the place.  Oh, and whenever you see moisture on the street, ask yourself, "Did it rain today?".

Decided on an oyster po boy for dinner on Ash Wednesday. It was AMAZING!   The thing I liked most about it (aside from the juicy oysters) was the bread. It was nice and soft. Now don't get me wrong, I like crunchy and crumby French bread on a po boy as much as the next person, but every once in a while you want to taste more of the goodies in the sandwich than the bread. I feel that some places have a weird bread:sandwich filling ratio and a lot of times the bread over powers the whole thing. That didn't happen here.  I also got some fries on the side, but they were just okay. The place is pretty well priced. I don't know what Steven S. was talking about because the foot long stuffed crab is only $8.49, but I digress. Along with the usual seafood po boys, they also have roast beef, sausage and more. I definitely have to go back and try their alligator sausage po boy. They also have different platters that come with fries.  I'm always happy to find a good place for a seafood po boy on the Westbank.

I stopped in here for lunch since I was in the area and I was eager to see the new place since the expansion. It was pretty packed at lunch, so me and a coworker had no choice but to order at the counter and sit/eat outside.  I got the original cheesesteak half with a side of fries. The sandwich itself was great- the meat was tender and the fries were really good too. The meat on my sandwich had really good flavor, the cheese went nicely with it and the "half" was the perfect portion for lunch. It was a fairly hot day so I was wishing that there was a bit of shade outside- an awning, an umbrella on the table, something. Other than the heat, my experience here was good.  Service is pretty fast, so I would probably come back again for lunch.

How do you review a bridge?  How do you rate a bridge?  5 stars because it's always done a good job of not collapsing whilst I was driving on it!  It is pretty cool to drive over, because it IS so long.  You get a nice view of the lake and I can imagine that driving over it at night can be a bit of an adventure.

This is a really cool little shop on Oak.  I had been wanting to check this place out for a while, after hearing raves about it and earlier this week, I finally had the chance.  I would classify the clothing here as "casual chic".  There were a lot of nice dresses, tank tops and thin tops for summer, which is perfect for the New Orleans climate.  The clothes here we colorful, modern and really fun. I was also impressed by the prices, as everything was really affordable without looking cheap.

Stopped in here while out with friends and we decided we needed a bite to eat. I probably never would have even know about this place if my friends hadn't been regulars here.  I got a big slice of pizza with chicken on it. It was really good, especially considering this is basically just one of those places and you order pizza and it's already made. The chicken had a lot of flavor and the slices are really big.   They are open late and this place is definitely a better choice than a lot of the other "fast food" options in the area.

This is basically the same idea as Pure Yogurt Culture, except it's located on the Westbank.  It has way more flavors than Pure (like red velvet cake and strawberry lemonade) and it goes by the same "self serve and pay by the ounce" system.  When I went, the place was packed, but the line moved quickly.  The girl took about 30 seconds to ring each person up.  I was pretty impressed.  The yogurt was really good and I got a good amount for the $3.43 that I spent.  Excited that there is a place like this on the Westbank.  A good, semi-healthy alternative to the same old thing.

Not too bad for what it is.  This is the new Christmas tradition that has happened at the Convention Center for the past few years. It's pretty neat- you walk in and there are all kinds of differently decorated Christmas trees, there are rides, little snacks, an ice skating rink and inflatable things for kids to jump around on.  David and I liked walking through taking it all in. It's definitely geared more towards kids, but there's some cool stuff for adults to do. I really liked the carousel. David went on the snow mizer ride, which I avoided because it spins you around and I can't get down with that. The ice skating rink was really small and the line to ice skate was insane, so we decided to skip that. If we go again, we're going to go when they first open so that we can get on the ice when it's fresh and avoid standing in a long line.  I had a good time and going definitely put me in the Christmas spirit, so I think it was worth the time to go.

I stopped in here for an oil change the day after the 4th of July, which was probably my first mistake. I figured there wouldn't be a big crowd and I was very wrong.  Tom was the man who took care of me and he was very nice. Nothing that happened was his fault, but a lot of people "called in" because it was the day after a holiday and they were understaffed. My simple oil change and tire rotation took over two hours. Again, Tom was lovely and very apologetic and the job was down well, so in the end, the length of time was my only main complaint.  I like that you can make your appointment online and they do take you car as soon as you come in. Next time, I plan on being the first appointment of the day.

This seafood place is owned by the same folks who own Big EZ seafood, so if you have been there, you won't be disappointed by the quality of food here.  I got my usual 12 inch shrimp poboy and it didn't disappoint. For $10 you get a poboy PACKED with large shrimp that are falling out of the bread. They are fried to perfection and delicious and you get a lot of "bang" for your buck, which is why I'm a big fan of this place. Just like Big EZ, they have boiled seafood, other types of poboys and platters and I have always been beyond pleased with what these owners have to offer. I am so glad to see them expanding and plan on adding Mr. Crabhouse to my regular seafood rotation.

I found an amazing dress for New Year's Eve here! Yes, I already got my New Year's Eve dress- I don't like waiting until the last minute.  Yes, the dresses here are a little fancier and more expensive than the average "run of the mill" dresses you might find at Dillard's, but they are better quality and for special occasions. I came in just thinking that I would look around and "window shop", but then I found an amazing dress for a pretty good price that I just had to have.  I was specifically looking for something with a little sparkle and pizzazz and the woman working here was quick to find me something that worked for me and in my price range. I would absolutely recommend this store to anyone looking for a fancy dress for a special evening or a night out on the town.

We're getting into the warmer season here in New Orleans, so you know that it's time for snowballs. What's better than a regular old snowball? A designer snowball! A designer snowball is a creation by stand owner Stricen Carter and it's topped with candy cookies cheesecake and basically any goodies you can imagine. These Instagram worthy treats will have you coming back for more.  When I stopped in here, I got a strawberry cheesecake snowball that came complete with a wedge of cheesecake inside of it. It was outstanding! I love how fine the ice is here and as the snowball melted the cheesecake mixed in to make it a perfect treat. There's a lot of sugar here, so be sure to pace yourself. If you're looking for a unique dessert fit for Instagram, this is the spot.  I wrote about this spot for Very Local New Orleans. Read that article here: https://nola.verylocal.com/sweet-thangs-update-stricen-carters-designer-snoballs/180480/

I like Stein Mart. They have a little mix of everything at different prices and they seem to always be having some sort of sale.  I was here looking for a few vacation items and, as usual, I headed right to the sale section. Why pay full price when you can pay a sale price, says I. They had a great selection of sale stuff and I found a cute top that is great for summer. If sales aren't really your thing, they have a nice selection of "fancier" items that range from $100 to $200+, depending on what you are looking for. They also have a wide selection of work out clothes, which I wasn't in the market for, but I will be returning when I am looking for that type of thing.  This is a pretty typical department store that has a little bit of everything and you are bound to find something that suits you.

Whoa! When did the Westbank get a Hardee's?  Dustin told me about this hidden "gem" in Marrero, so I decided to swing through and check it out. I'm not crazy adventurous so I just decided to get a burger and fries. I know, this place has burritos and tacos and stuff, but I wasn't in the mood for that. Well, the burger and fries were fine (better than McD's, not as good as Wendy's), but somehow they forgot to put my order in, so I had to pull up in the line and wait 10 extra minutes for my food. How does someone forget to put an order in?  I want to go back and try some of their breakfast stuff, as I hear it's pretty amazing.

As far as bars on Bourbon Street go, this one wasn't too bad. The place is actually called "Prohibition: Huge Ass Beers", so make a note of that if you're looking for the place, for some reason.  Just like any bar like this, it's going to be a tourist trap and there were plenty on the night we were here. We were hanging out waiting for the Krewe of Boo parade to start and we decided to sit at the bar, have a few drinks and watch the LSU game. There was a band playing that was pretty good and the staff was friendly and fast. They have a "2 for 1" deal that basically applies to all of the crappy beer, so I skipped it and got myself a regular priced Lagunitas IPA that I was happy with.  I wouldn't plan an evening around hanging out here, but it isn't a bad choice if you're in the area.

When someone texted me and asked me if I was opening a chicken place I had no idea what they were talking about. No, Nola Chick is not my new chicken joint, even though it's been my online handle for years. But I love fried chicken, so I knew I had to check this spot out.  When I stopped in, I had the Hot Chick on a bun. It had the perfect level of tang from the chili sauce. I tried the Parish Chick on a biscuit, and the spicy-sweet honey complemented the tender chicken, and would make a perfect (late) breakfast sandwich. I especially loved the way the honey and juice from the chicken soaked into the biscuit.  I also had chicken tenders, which were tasty, and with choices of sticky Thai chili, satsuma barbecue, Cajun honey or ranch dipping sauce, you can't go wrong with mixing and matching your flavors. In my opinion, these juicy tenders give another popular chicken tender spot a run for their money.  I wrote about this spot for Mid City Messenger. Read more here: https://midcitymessenger.com/2021/02/12/nola-chick-drive-thru-opens-at-tulane-and-carrollton/

For some reason, I'm obnoxiously picky about Chinese food. Where do I get off? I can't cook it, but I consider myself the Guy Fieri of the stuff. Okay, not quite, but I know what I like when it comes to pretend Chinese cuisine.  I got Panda King takeout because I got a flyer in the mail, with the menu, and I realize I'd never been. I got a takeout of sweet and sour shrimp, veggie fried rice and it came with an egg roll and two crab rangoons.  The sweet and sour shrimp was okay, it was a little heavy on the batter, but I do like that the sauce came on the side. The veggie rice was flavorless and I had to add soy sauce to make it edible. The egg rolls and the crab rangoons were great! I'd probably order these on their own- I guess you can never go wrong with fried stuff.  Would I go back? Eh, maybe to dine in or to do dim sum. For takeout, there are better places around here.

Not bad for what is basically fast food pizza.  They have regular specials, so you can always find some kind of deal depending on what day you decide to go. The pizza itself is just "okay" but better than most other pizza chains. I find it a little "bready", if that makes any sense. My first choice is always something a little more "upscale", but if you need something in a pinch, don't hesitate to come here.

I have zero experience with casinos.  I don't gamble and I've only been to two casinos in my entire life.  Harrah's is one of them.  Really big and geared towards tourists with Fleur de Lis on everything and a brass band that does a second line through the casino every few hours.  There's a restaurant in the casino and I'm pretty sure it's a buffet.  I've never tried it, but it must be pretty good because there are always people in there.  The best section of the casino is probably the poker room.  It's huge and there's usually a waiting list to sit at one of the tables.  It's one of the regular locations for the "World Series of Poker", so everything in the poker room is top notch.  The cocktail waitresses are super attentive and the section has it's own bar, if you want to get your own drink.  I agree with Jeremy S, in that the restrooms are always super clean, and I don't think that I have ever been in there when there wasn't an attendant keeping things neat and tidy..

Fat Harry's isn't a bad little place.  We stopped in here on Lundi Gras after parades. They recently had a fire and redid the entire place, although it really doesn't look all that different to me. By the time we got here, it was pretty empty. I guess the usual crowd had better things to do after the parade. I did have a good time dancing around to the music that was playing.  This probably isn't a place I would seek out. From what I remember from years ago it's mostly a college hang out and these days I am just too old to hang out with people under 23 (hair flip). I do hear that their grill is reopening soon, so maybe I will stop in just to see what they offer.

When I saw the new kid on the block moving into this prime spot on Gretna Blvd., I knew I had to get over there and taste test it for myself. It's a hard job, but someone has to do it.  It was lunchtime and I was starving, so I was happy to be seated immediately and presented with chips and salsa, which was delicious. They have a really big menu with ever Mexican-inspired dish you could imagine, but I decided to get a Burrito Supreme with chicken off of the lunch menu.  The burrito supreme is a calorie explosion that comes topped with lettuce, tomatoes, tomato salsa, guacamole and sour cream. The dish also comes with a side of rice. It was probably the perfect portion for lunch, even though I like when I have some leftovers to bring home. At $10 I thought it was a little small, especially compared to the burrito at El Patron for the same price, but I enjoyed it.  Staff was friendly and attentive and I like the vibe of this spot, so I would have lunch here again.

Not the worst, but they definitely need to work on some things.   This Starbucks is already located in a Target store, so I feel like it should lose points for that. I don't like having to wade through a sea of middle-aged, oblivious moms in yoga pants who would rather chit chat than let you get your coffee (this actually happened, I'm not stereotyping).   There was one woman working when I was here and she was being run ragged. She was hustling getting coffee, food and everything else that the MAMs were demanding of her. I seriously think she was thrilled when I just ordered a large iced coffee.  At other stores such a simple order comes out right away, but because there was only one person working, it took a while. Seriously Target, get that girl some help. The coffee was mediocre, as expected, and I only stopped here in the first place because someone gave me a gift card for Christmas because they obviously hate me or something.  Anyway, if you need coffee during your Target trip, then this is the spot. Otherwise, you should probably avoid.

Cooter Brown's is fantastic.  Not only is it a great place to watch a game (the place is huge, has two bars with a HUGE beer selection and lots of tvs) but they have FANTASTIC oysters.    Whenever I go here my friend and I usually split a dozen raw oysters and some fries.  The oysters are really BIG and juicy and full of flavor.  I've found at places like Acme, the oysters tend to be on the smaller side, but that wasn't an issue here.  The fries we ordered were topped with chili and cheese and we ate them with a fork.  So good!  If oysters aren't your thing, Cooter's also serves different kinds of sandwiches, burgers and po boys.  They also have different types of hot dogs and side orders such as chicken fingers and mozzarella sticks.   Whether you are stopping in for the game, a beer with friends or dinner, you are sure to find what you are looking for here.  Please note: the online menu is not up to date AT ALL, so be sure to look the bar menu over, before ordering.

This is a wonderful book shop, especially if you're looking for the local goods.  I ended up here for a book signing and I fell in love! I like that it's located at the Rink, which is a cool little center and I like the New Orleans and Louisiana representation on the shelves. They have autographed copies of books, if that's your thing, and if you're looking for a rare book, GDBS will help you track it down.  The shop is regularly holding cute events, so you can stop in, get a book and maybe a cocktail. You can't go wrong!

I'm usually not a liquor drinker at all. Beer and wine (sometimes) is more my thing, but my friend had his birthday party here, so it was the perfect opportunity to check the place out.  Seven Three has all of your liquor bases covered: they make vodka, gin, whiskey and even moonshine. They have an extensive cocktail menu, or you can just get them to whip you up one of your favorites. I had the Gentilly Gin Punch. I haven't had a lot of gin, but the punch went down really smoothly and I could barely taste the alcohol. I know this might not be everyone's thing, but I liked it.  The distillery and bar itself is huge, and was perfect for the event I was attending. There was a big room in the front with a bar and another bar in the back with plenty of seating, including booths, if you don't want to sit at the actual bar. My only small complaint was that the place doesn't have a lot of windows (it's basically a converted warehouse), so I imagine there isn't a lot of natural light coming in during the day.

This is a pretty laid back neighborhood bar. Like other bars in this area, everyone seems to know each other and the place is friendly. There are pool tables, if you like to play and there's a fairly decent beer selection. On the day I was here I was just grabbing a quick drink with some friends and we sat at the bar and chatted with the bartender for a bit. The service was good, but it wasn't really packed when I was here, so I don't know how service is when there's a crowd.

A lot of fluff for what is basically a typical hotel bar.  The only really redeeming quality of the place was the view of the city.  Drinks were overpriced and the over all attitude of the place wasn't very welcoming. The only reason to go here would be if you are a man who wants a beer while you wait for your date to finish getting ready up in the room.    I would have no reason to ever go back here.  If you're visiting New Orleans, venture out and go see the more friendly places that our city has to offer.

Fair warning: I was in starvation nation when I found myself here, so keep that in mind when you are reading this.  OH MY GOD THIS MIGHT BE THE BEST PIZZA I HAVE EVER EATEN!!!!!!  Okay, now that I got that out of my system- we stopped into this neighborhood convenience store on the hunt for a snack. This place has a little bit of everything, like others have said. It's a spot where you can "make groceries", if you are in a pinch.  They have a pretty good selection of fresh pizza and I decided to get the feta and spinach one, because it looked really good. You get a huge slice of pizza and mine was so big that I had to actually fold it and eat it sandwich style. It's not the very best pizza I have ever had, but it had been a long evening and I was thankful for it. It did have a lot of flavor and was really good, especially considering that this place is basically just a hole in the wall.  Would I return? Sure, why not?

This is one of the dark little bars that is located at the end of Lower Decatur.  Abbey isn't one of my favorite spots, but it's a nice haunt where you can stop and grab a beer or a mixed drink for pretty cheap. One thing I really do like about this spot are the booths where you can sit and chat away from the hustle and bustle of the bar itself. They have a jukebox with some pretty interesting tunes, and I like that's it not one of those internet jukeboxes so many places have these days.  In general, the crowd is friendly here, but I have encountered a few salty types once or twice. The bartender I have dealt with the last two times I've visited was really funny with a great personality and was open to providing some good conversation.  I wouldn't go out of my way to return, but I'd gladly duck in, if I find myself in the area.

Uh...well. Let's just say this: they are fast to show up, but you really better know how to get where you are going, because you are going to have to give your cabbie directions. At least, that was my experience.  A friend and I were going from Tchoupitoulas to Oak Street. I thought it was an easy enough job. Well, the cabbie had no idea where Oak Street was and we had to give him turn by turn directions: "left here, right here". I guess that's no big deal, but if I didn't know the exact way myself, I would have been up a creek without a paddle. Why would a cab company hire someone who doesn't know their way around?  Also, it was eerily quiet in the cab. Aside from us giving the guy directions, it was silent. No radio, no nothing.  I will avoid this company from here on out.

Yeah, this is the kind of place that I will shop one day when I am a multi-millionaire.  Everything here is incredible and gorgeous. Not only that, but I happen to know the person who photographs all of this good stuff for the sale catalog, so I get to see all these wonderful things up close on instagram every now and then.  This is a fantastic antique shop that sells fancy, intricate clocks, gorgeous furniture and even statues. All of it looks like it belongs in one of those mansions on St. Charles Avenue.   Even if the stuff is out of your price range, it's worth stopping in and seeing what they have because everything here is just gorgeous and perfect.

Oooh. I had yummy croissants from here this morning. So good. Nice and fresh and I like how there is an outer thick "crust" with the soft inside. They are so delicious, no butter or anything else needed. They also sell danish and other pastries. Perfect little neighborhood breakfast spot, if you are looking to pick up something that isn't a doughnut or a bagel.

David and I decided to check out this new beer bar and we enjoyed it, even though the place was pretty dead and their beer was limited.  The space is lovely and they have their own parking lot, which is immediate bonus points. I sampled a couple of their ciders and enjoyed them- the Broad Street Belle stood out to me. When I went, they mainly had guest taps and cans that you can find just about anywhere. No complaints as I was happy to sip on my Founders All Day IPA which was only $3.  I'll definitely be back to sample more of their own offerings.

I adore this place on so many levels! They pull you in with their pink decor, zebra carpet bright lights and shiny sparkly jewelry. It's the ultimate girl trap.  I love anything that glitters in the light and this place has it by the truckload: There is shiny everything from earrings and bracelets to necklaces and keychains. Some of it is big and obnoxious (in a good way) and some of it is subtle and dainty. I swear, I would show you but you really aren't allowed to take pictures here, probably because it ruins the magic.  I wanted some "statement" rhinestone earrings, and fortunately I was in the area, so I found myself in So Good. I found exactly what I was looking for immediately. Staff will follow you around the store, especially if you come later in the evening. Don't take it personally, I am sure they have people trying to steal all the time.  This is your one stop shop for anyone who wants their costume jewelry to make a statement and get them noticed.

I went here for the first time with some fellow yelpers to enjoy happy hour.  We all decided on cheese fondue and chocolate fondue.  It was good, but not great, but a nice little something to munch on while sipping wine and enjoying conversation with friends.  A couple of people that we were with decided to eat dinner here.  That was an adventure.  You basically cook your own food.  Do you like cooking your own food?  Awesome!  So, why are you going to go to a restaurant and pay to cook your own food?  I don't know.    I would go back for the fondue and maybe a salad, but the idea of cooking my food at the table just isn't appealing to me.  But hey, some people might love that.

This is a really nice Walgreens in a good location. I was actually in Mid City and craving lemonade, of all things, so I stopped in here to pick one up. There weren't any long lines and the staff seemed efficient.  It's basically the same as any other Walgreens.

Musician's Village is another example of the good that is being since Hurricane Katrina.  This provides an area for the musician's of New Orleans to live. These are the people that contribute to the culture of our city and many of them were left homeless after the storm. Harry Connick Jr. and Branford Marsalis have lent their time to helping get this endeavor off the ground and funded.

Stopped in here, and if I'm being totally honest, I was left a bit disappointed. Let me explain. I had heard that although Elio's mainly deals in wine, they also have a pretty good beer selection. While the beer selection isn't anything out of this world, I will say that it's decent. The only problem is A LOT of the beers are old. Like, 6 months old. I understand that most people who come here are looking for wine, so that is the main focus, but if you are going to offer something, I feel that it should be pretty fresh.   I was able to pick up a couple of bottles, but I probably would have picked up a few more if there were more fresh selections. For my buck, I think that next time I'm going to skip this place when looking for beer, and just come for the wine.

There are two things that I love: a deal and a good cause. You will find both at the No Fleas Market.  No Fleas is a thrift store with a twist. Not only are you going to find clothing, housewares and books here, but all of the proceeds of anything purchased here go directly to help animals!  They have a huge selection of clothing here. In fact, it's mostly clothing and a wide variety of it. The clothes are in good condition and are well priced, so you are sure to easily find something here that you will like. They also sell basic housewares such as glasses, household decorations and the like and they have a large book selection.  When I stopped in. I saw a gorgeous sequin black dress and if I had had an excuse to wear it, I would have snapped it up on the spot. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable and will help you find anything that you may be specifically looking for.

Hmmm this bar used to be a place. The bartender said "Round Up", but that didn't sound familiar to me. What was this place??  ANYWAY. We came here because I was in search of music and this bar...didn't have music. Womp. Oh well. They DID have All Day IPA, so I was pretty happy. You can sit at the bar or you can sit outside on the PATIO! Yeah, that's right, this place has a patio complete with a light up tree, tons of seating and a blow up pool. Did I get in the pool? NAH. But I did dig the patio and the vibe out there was fantastic. I just wish that it was a smidge cooler so that I can really hang out and soak up the atmosphere. This is definitely going to be a destination once fall arrives.

I have been a long time fan of the Pop City on Magazine and I recently stopped into the downtown location looking for some gifts.  This is a really cute store that has different types of gifts for people who appreciate things that are a little different. One thing I was looking for were some Elvis and Marilyn Monroe themed gifts and this places delivered in the form of coffee mugs, lunchboxes, figurines and other cool things to choose from.   They also carry any array of non-cheesy New Orleans souvenirs as well as t shirts and other fun gifts. I almost want to say think of it as a New Orleans version of Spencer's and you have Pop City, except that Pop City is better because it's locally owned.

What is going on in this strip mall? All of the stores here are terrible. Get it together, Algiers.  Okay, so this Ross is a mess. This Ross has the same issue that the Ross on Manhattan had before they got their stuff together. Nothing is organized, everything is thrown around and the shoe section looks like a bomb went off.  All I wanted was some cute flats at a low price. Did Ross have them? Maybe. Who's to say, considering nothing is organized by size and there are shoes missing their mate? It's sad, because I came in ready to spend money, but I was left frustrated that I couldn't figure out what was what.  I won't be back and I'll just stick to the more organized Ross in Harvey.

So this is what the Dungeon is now and I am not a fan.  The old dungeon had a certain appeal to it. Yeah, it was cheesy with the gargoyles and stuff, but there was a certain mysterious charm. Now it's just like any other tourist trap in the Quarter. The last time I went I was blown away by how different it is now. All of the kitschy decorations are gone and in it's place is a whole lot of nothing.   Also, there once was a time where taking a picture inside the Dungeon was grounds for immediate banishment into the streets. Now you are encouraged to take a souvenir picture in a stand up coffin that they have leaning against the wall. I took a picture in it to show how bad it is. And of course, the bookcase and all of the cages are gone, so really what are you even doing here?

I had a meeting at this CC's recently and it turned out to be the perfect place to grab a coffee and have a chat. The coffee is typical Community Coffee, so I'll spare you my thoughts on that. This review is for the space.  This CC's is huge with plenty of tables and chairs and plenty of natural light flowing in through the windows that look out onto Magazine St. I love the whole "New Orleans" vibe of the place, right down to the New Orleans brass band music that was playing over the radio.  There's a nice selection of sweet treats, if you're in the mood and the staff was really friendly and service was fast, even though there was a bit of a line.

After a busy day of Quarter hopping, my companion and I had to make a stop for some iced coffee. Lucky for us, this spot was right on our route.  First of all, what a cute place! It almost has a casual walk in diner type of feel. They not only offer coffee but they have beignets, obviously, as well as a few other cookies, tarts and sweet goodies as well as omelets and other savory yums. There was a bit of a line, but the staff here is great at getting peoples orders and moving folks through the line quickly. I had an iced coffee in my hand in no time and only for a little over $3- talk about great prices (considering you are in the Qwatas).  We took a seat at the table on the side and sipped our coffee for a bit. There's also a nice little outdoor seating area, if you would like some fresh air.

I know that I must have been to Vaso before, but maybe not.  Some friends and I were wandering down Frenchmen St. just looking for a place to listen to music where there was no cover. For some reason Apple Barrel was packed and charging a $5 cover. No thanks.  We saw that this place was way less crowded and a bress band was on stage, so we decided to stop in. I think that this place was the Hookah bar years and years ago. Anyway, I really liked the atmosphere in here. It was cozy and laid back with plenty of seating so that we could enjoy the show. The band was awesome and it was a really good time.  I'm excited to add this to the list of my "regular" music hang outs.

This is a nice part of the city and some green space in the middle of the concrete jungle of the French Quarter area.  I've attended a few events here, the most recent being the NOLA Mac and Cheese fest and it's always a good space for events and I always have a good time. The park is home to famed Congo Square, ponds, and sculptures honoring those who have helped make New Orleans great.  If you have the opportunity to attend a festival here, be sure to do so because it's a nice space worth spending some time in.

I love the Bulldog, because of their vast beer selection and pretty good food.  The Bulldog mid city is not my regular "home base", but it does have it's high points.  It's bigger than the Uptown location, which I know that some people would prefer.  It's much better for bigger groups, because if you have a big group at the other Bulldog, you pretty much have to either get there early and get a table or sit on the patio.  This Bulldog has a really nice patio area.  I like the way it's decorated with the lanterns and the lights.  This venue has more of a "lounge" feel to it.  It's definitely a different vibe than the other one.  I'm giving it 4 stars, only because my personal preference is a place that is a little more intimate, but that's just personal opinion.

I stopped into this new little clothing store on Magazine St after noticing the cute dresses in the store window.  Bella & Harlow has really cute vintage inspired dresses. When I was here, I was wishing that I had a few more dollars to spend. There is nothing cheap about the clothing here, that's for sure. I think I saw a dress here that was over $300. That's fine if it's going toward a fancy gown or something,  but I can't see spending that on a little day dress. I know what you're going to say... I have cheap taste. Ok, whatever you say!  But hey, they do have really cute dresses here and I would absolutely shop here and spend the money if I saw something I really liked.

Although Dimartino's serves a variety of sandwiches, I have only every gotten the muffalettas here.  It helps that this is the only place that I have ever found a muffaletta that I like (on the Westbank).  I usually get the "large" muffaletta, and although it's not as big as it used to be (back in the day, it was the size of a dinner plate, and half was plenty for a dinner!), they are still fantastic.  I like to get mine to go, bring it home, and put a little extra olive oil on it.  Mmm!  Also, did you know that you can order mini muffalettas for parties?  It's true!  They are as good as the big ones, just in a smaller form.  My family usually orders a bunch for New Year's Eve, and they are always a hit.  And they freeze really well, if you want to save a few for later.

Okay, so I don't even know if you can really consider this a Sephora. This is like the MAC store at Dillard's- it's a much smaller version, and while you will be able to find a few things you like, you need to go elsewhere to get the full experience.  I was here looking for some foundation- it seems that I always have to switch up my foundations because my skin gets irritated. The girl working here was helpful, but she wasn't successful in finding a foundation that matched my skin tone to my satisfaction.  They offer other makeup things here, but if you are looking for a big selection, you'll be better off going to the big store at Lakeside.

A friend of mine eats here all the time and he told me they had a good Cuban, so I had to check it out.  Holly's is a convenience store with a kitchen in the back. The store itself just sells basic things- snack items and soft drinks, and the place isn't big at all. You order at the counter and then you wait as they make your food.  I decided to get the Cuban sandwich with a side of plantains. The sandwich was really good. I don't know if it's as a good as the one at El Libre, but it's pressed nicely, really cheesy and the bread is nice and crispy. The plantains were really good too and you get a good amount of them for about $3.  I'm going to go back and order ahead next time, because there is a bit of a wait while they make your food for you.

I got my braces from Dr. Devereux back in '99.  I remember that he PROMISED that they would be off in time for my senior prom and graduation and they were (2 years total)!  He totally made it happen!  Now I have a fabulous straight smile that I am always getting complimented on and I couldn't be happier with his work.  Dr. Devereux was always fabulous and really nice and efficient.  I would highly recommend him!

So first things first, yeah this cemetery is located in a pretty sketchy part of town so you have to be careful when you go. With that said, it really should be counted among the historic cemeteries of New Orleans.  It is not PERFECTLY well kept, so a lot of the tombs are falling apart, while others are in pretty good condition. This isn't as nice one of the fancier cemeteries like Metairie cemetery or something, but it still has it's own charm nonetheless.

Talk about your lifesavers, I am giving 4 stars mainly because they serve the caffeine that I so craved. I like the atmosphere of this place- it's located in a hotel. There is seating right by the windows, so people watching is breeze.   The reason I am giving four stars and not five stars is because of the bathroom. So, I go in the bathroom of the hotel lobby, which is also the PJ's bathroom and both toilets are clogged up. On top of that, the automatic sink didn't recognize me as a person. It wouldn't work. Am I a ghost? I am waving my hand in front of both faucets and nothing is happening. All in all it was a pretty gross experience. I guess it was a weird fluke, but for a bathroom to not work in the lobby of busy hotel is pretty odd.

I checked this truck out at Gretna Food Truck Fest and I am so glad I did!  First of all, the owners of this truck are beyond sweet and have a great personality, which is always a delight. I stepped up and decided to get the Southern Chicken. This is their version of the Chic-Fil-A sandwich (I'm saying that, not them)- a nice cut of fried chicken, topped with a pickle on a buttery bun. There are two sliders to an order and they are pretty big, so don't be afraid to share.   The slider is out of this world! The chicken is juicy and perfectly fried with a lot of flavor. They have mustard on the truck, if you want to add it, which I did. The mustard added the perfect kick to this tasty delight that was served fresh out of the fryer. I will definitely have to seek this truck out again. I think I'm addicted to that chicken!

Here's another one of those cool music clubs near Frenchmen street.  It seems that whenever I pass this place there is some wonderful music coming from it.  It seems that there is always some kind of fantastic band playing here.   The other night some friends and I stopped in here and there was an eclectic band playing some amazing music.  I don't know how to describe it, but the band consisted of a sax, a trumpet, a bass, a guitar, a drummer, a keyboard and the leader of the pack was a rapper/hype man.  It was a combination of hip hop and jazz and it was really amazing and unlike anything I had ever heard.  They did a good job at getting the crowd up and dancing and we had a fantastic time.  All kinds of musicians are welcome to play here, as the Balcony hosts an array of artists.  No matter when you stop in, you are bound to hear something that you will like.

I came to this Home Depot after my usual Home Depot in Gretna didn't have the industrial cleaning supplies I needed. A quick search showed that this HD had what I sought, so I headed this way.  I had trouble finding what I was looking for, but a sales person quickly pointed me in the right direction and turned out to be a major lifesaver. I have also done some shopping here for under cabinet lights that I am considering once my new kitchen is built. They have a nice selection of rope lights and "puck" lights that are surprisingly easy to install and priced well.  Home Depot is pretty good about having seasonal sales, so keep an eye out if you are looking for something specific.

Finally! A sports supply store other than Academy on the Westbank!  This store is HUGE and has everything you could possibly want. I came in to check out what they had as far as Saints apparel, and they had a ton of options. OTHER stores see fit with only offering a couple of pink jerseys and cutesy t shirts to their female football fans, but Dick's offers actual league apparel, which is nice.  They have anything sports related to could want here. They even have fancy frisbees for frisbee golf. I have no idea what frisbee golf even is, but you can get whatever size/weight frisbee you want for it here, so go nuts.  Anything you could need in the sports related field is here, so check this place out.

I've never gotten more than an appetizer here, but I really like the place.  It has an "old school" Westbank feel and could probably stand to be updated, but the staff is nice and it's a nice place to hang out if you just want an appetizer or a drink.    The front has more of a "loungey" feel with a jukebox, bar area, and video poker, but the back is huge and gorgeous.  I can definitely see having a party here or going here on a night out with friends.  The staff was really nice and attentive and made sure that we were taken care of and had everything that we needed.  I would definitely go back, maybe for lunch.

If you are from the Westbank, this is the streetcar that you can hop on and travel to Mid City. Or, if you are in Mid City, this streetcar will take you downtown.  I don't have a ton of experience when it comes to riding the rails, but this streetcar line has always served me well. Of course, it gets packed on busier days- a few years back riding from Mid City to downtown on Halloween was cramped, to say the least. It usually runs on time with few delays and the cars are in good shape.  I like that the cars have ac, so you're not sweating to death on hotter days and it's a dependable alternative if you want to travel throughout the city and not have to worry about parking.

YAY! I never go on the ferry (because I honestly never have any reason to), but this was a really cool experience.   I went on the ferry to go from Algiers to downtown for the French Quarter Fest.  It wasn't overly packed, it was a great view and it was super convenient, because it dropped us off right where the fest was.  I can definitely see why people would use the ferry to travel, especially if they are on a bike.
