I had never bought a "real" bike before...just ones that you could pick up at K-Mart.  The bike that they sold me has held up the NOLA city streets just like they said it would.  I haven't had any service work done so I can't really speak to that service.

I needed a bunch of small gifts (both in cost and size) and remembered this lovely shop... Zoomed over and was in and out pretty quickly. They had pralines packaged in various sizes from a single praline in a sealed bag to multiples in other packaging. Perfect!  The staff was friendly and helpful. The space is roomy with an assortment of other gift type items to catch your eye.  The pralines were delicious and the perfect small gift that I needed.

Sometimes you just need the cheapest gas. And this was my go to spot for most of the 80s when it was Tenneco and my parents had given me a gas card. Yep dating myself with all the old-timey references.  It's a pretty sketchy location and mostly the guys hanging outside are just interested in drinking and don't cause any trouble...it is JP afterall.   Gas is cheap. It is not well lit and I only stop during daylight hours.

One of two subcontracts for city trash removal. If their number is on your city issued trashcan then they're your contract.  The garbageman takes all of our cans (and sometimes we have a lot) and don't leave trash in the street...such an improvement post-K.  And the one time they missed our entire block, I called and trash was picked up the next morning.

I was a little apprehensive about fruit in my poke bowl. But I was wrong. The kiwi, pineapple and orange with my ahi tuna was delicious. Plus I added cucumbers to my bowl and I'm glad I did; the bowl needed the crunch.  The counter folks were great. The food was tasty and fresh. And, of course, all the spots at AM are super clean and spiffy.   While I love the fishes, I'll probably check out the smoked tofu bowl because I love that too. Definitely a great option while you're in Auction House.

Finally made it to Café Adelaide for a Christmas lunch a couple of weeks ago, and the food was delicious.  The soup of the day was a butternut squash that was creamy & deeply satisfying.  My dining companions had the turtle soup & the gumbo and they both said they were excellent.  And being ladies at lunch we all had salads; two of us had the strawberry salad which was nicely balanced with all its various elements. Our third had the shrimp boil salad which (despite missing some punctuation on the menu and causing us to be confused) was boiled shrimp and boiled potatoes in a salad form.  She said it was super tasty & spicy.  The service was attentive without being officious.  And did I mention the 25 cent martinis?

+1 star for the fabulous outdoor setting.  -1 star for indifferent plating.  And by that I mean ending up with bits of someone else's meal on my plate.  They have a bunch of vegetarian selections.  And cover the gamut of salads, burgers, and hot dishes.  Maybe's it's just that they are trying to do too much to do any of it really well.

Vincent's would be a good place to bring a date...maybe not a first date, too much pressure. Maybe like a third or fourth when you really want to wow them.  The food is rich and tasty...and garlicy (maybe you and your date will cancel each other out?)  The decor is kitschy Italian bistro but still cute.  The lighting is low and romantic to the point of my MiL pulling out a flashlight to read her menu.  (I didn't say I was on a date.)  The restaurant is small so reservations are a good idea.  I've never had a bad meal here even when we've come with a group over 10.  The corn & crab soup in the bread bowl is delish.  And last time I had the mirltons stuffed with shrimp, super tasty and way more garlicy than my grandmother made them.

Pretty sure this is the original Mona's location. And it was closed for a few years after it caught on fire.  The renovations post-fire are pretty fancy...for Mona's.  But don't worry the prices are still ridiculously low.   Since I have a Mona's a half  mile from my house, I don't make it to the mid-city location to often.  But I came by on Mother's Day with the family before a concert in City Park.  The parents have always been big fans of middle eastern food (I remember going to a restaraunt called House of Mesopotamia with them in the late 70s/early 80s).  The menu is the same as the other locations.  And we all enjoyed the food, as a group we had lamb, beef, chicken, and veggie options.

Housed in a beautifully renovated craftsman shotgun, this neighborhood art gallery drew quite a packed house for their art opening tonight. How could I resist a show entitled, Whimsy?  Of course I found a piece that I really want & may have to come back after considering the piece a bit.  The crowd for the opening was substantial for such a small space...I thought all the parking was being taken up by folks at Happy Hour at Cure (almost next door) but I was wrong.  ALL of them were for the gallery, a great party scene but it made it a little difficult to view the art.  I'm going to have go back and check the pieces when it's a bit more subdued.
Really fresh seafood for sale and sandwiches too.  Good stuff.  No dine in service though.

I'd been to JE previously for HH (2-5 weekdays) which offers well priced drinks and pasta specials...HHs that end at 5 are normally just terrible for me. Besides a less than friendly bartender, I had a nice time.  FF to this week and I actually sat down in the restaurant and revisited one of those pasta dishes. I wolfed down an order of the canestri cacio e pepe, so little basket pasta with cheese and pepper. And OMG did it hit the spot. Just what I needed and then some.   Service was great and the server was on the spot with water refills and the bill so we could be on our way. Will definitely come back for a pasta fix.

Makings of a fun evening?  *Good bourbon selection - yep *Hanging out w/ childhood friends - yep *in a bar where you can actually hear each other speak - yep super low key & fun.  Glad my friend Dave lives around the corner. Although I do think it's cheating for him to pick a bar 30 feet from his house.

This location is smaller than the Lakeview store and I'm not sure if carries the same merchandise or not but it does have some really cute locally themed gifts and kids stuff. It definitely has less women's clothing.  The staff was busy (it was the Saturday before Christmas) but I was offered assistance and everyone was nice.  The parking lot is bit frightening since you have to back out onto Metairie Road AND I was parked between 2 monster SUVs...luckily one of them wanted might spot. Phew.

Did you know that if you go to Dirty Coast wearing a Dirty Coast t-shirt that they give you 10% off? That's what I was told over the weekend at this location. So remember that if you're ready to purchase some gifts...  I usually shop at the uptown location but this is a great spot for local t's and gifts in the FQ. Love the decor that they use inside including items from parades and what not.  I forget how hyperlocal some of their stuff is until I'm explaining to a visitor what some of the items mean/are.  Great locally owned shop to find souvenirs and gifts and maybe something for yourself!

My review is for lunch only. While I was seated near the stage area, no music was happening on the weekday afternoon while I was there. And since I was in town visiting with one of my besties, I was really glad that we could chatter at each other rather than listening to what I'm sure is awesome music.   We chose a variety of small plates and gobble up everything with only a few leftovers for her family to sample. We ate the pimento cheese balls, skillet cornbread, grilled pear pizza, brussels sprouts, Gray's salad....and maybe a special. Everything was delicious. And our server was great. The cocktail menu looked amazing but we were behaving ourselves so next time.  The building is gorgeous. Love all the exposed brick and woodbeams. We were seated upstairs and it was very cozy.

Newcomb art museum is a small free museum on the Tulane Campus. If you're there during the day, make sure to park in visitor spots. Luckily my last visit was for a show opening, so parking was not an issue.  The museum has a variety of galleries in the same building as the art school. Some of these galleries are not well signed so if you don't know where you're going, you have to ask...or like we did last night for the opening, follow the noise.  I think there are special 4 exhibits happening at the moment in different rooms. And the permanent collection is not always on view. It's a good spot to check out a small installation or collection. Call before you go if you wish to see something specific.

The menu is interesting and has some items I haven't seen on other local menus. And I like how they've dressed up the decor...but left the doors from when it was Doors. Odd.  We had a variety of rolls, sushi, appetizers, and udon in my group. Everything was fine. BUT on the Sunday afternoon that I went, the whole place smelled like spoiling seafood.  I will try it again but the locale will not replace my regular sushi haunts.

One of my favorite memories of the Peristyle was dancing across it, just spinning and spinning...of course I was just a tot when I did that, although yes I would do that again...as soon as it gets a little cooler. Yesterday when I passed by the entire pavilion was full of tables and chairs as caterers were setting up for some sort of to do.   When it was built, in 1907 it was designed for open air dances with a band on one side and a dance floor on the other. I love the neo-classical colonnade and I miss the melty faced lions. Who knew our weather would be so brutal on their faces but those were "renovated" in 2012 and look more lion-y now.   You can rent the space for your event from City Park, hence the catered event yesterday, but if it's not booked you can have your own dance party/photo session/impromptu soiree in it's environs and backed by beautiful Bayou Metairie.

Went in October and the french bread tasted like freezer.  And they were out of 1/2 of their entrees.  I know times are tough, but c'mon.  The food they did have was pretty good.  But freezer burned bread?  You get a 2.

In relation to the reupholstery of our vintage chair, this is where we bought the fabulous retro fabric.  Fabrixx specializes in upholstery and curtain fabric; this is not where you will find cloth to whip up a dress, unless you are Scarlet O'Hara and want a green velvet drapery dress.  Finding someone to actually help you can be a challenge, but when you do they usually have good advice.  I believe the store offers some services (like making curtains, etc.) but I have never used those.  They really do have fabric for almost every taste + great sales on remnants.

Took the 7 year old niece shopping today for her birthday and checked out Swap for Kids.  The store is small but well stocked...if you're looking more for baby/toddler clothes.  My niece who is 7 but wears a size 12 (what are they feeding kids these days?) had a more limited selection.  But we still found her a skirt, dress, and jacket...all for under $30.  And if her Mom doesn't approve any one piece? I'm not so concerned since they were under $10 each.

I decided that I needed a photo of a cemetery for a professional poster that I presented at a meeting.  (Yes this seemed an excellent idea to me at the time...it was sort of zombie/Halloween themed.)  And I was looking for the perfect cemetery to use as my shadow on the title.    After taking photos various places in my fair cities of the dead, I decided that I needed to try Lafayette no.1.  Really it was silly that I had used them earlier since they were a lot closer to my house than others.  I guess I just feel like this cemetery is overexposed. Anne Rice used to use it to make grand entrances to book signings at the independent bookseller nearby (even being carried out in a coffin once).  And then it was featured in a local novel (Ruined by Paula Morris which is pretty good so don't let the YA designation dissuade you).  ANYWAY.  I found the perfect shot, so yay Lafayette no.1
Good, fast work.  I haven't had anything complicated done here though.  Only hems in pants and sleeves.

Wow. Can I say the chef who runs this small spot in the Catahoula hotel is HUSTLING. He cooks in a tiny space and seems to do it all by himself! Kudos,sir.  The menu is small and vegan but the food is really flavorful and tasty. I had the chinese greens (these were OK and a little difficult to eat with plastic utensils...solution eat with your hands), the bao (tofu was super tasty) and the scallion pancake (the star). Everything was tasty & quick!   Ordering and payment was at the bar of the hotel (Pisco Bar) so that was easy. There is some space inside the hotel/bar to eat but we enjoyed the lovely courtyard which was somehow cool enough (after an earlier rain) on a Saturday night in August!  Will definitely be back to sample as the menu changes with the season.

I'm not sure how it happened that I haven't been to this spot since it reopened, post-K. But away a group of us went a couple of weeks ago. We knew it gets busy for lunch no matter what the day, so we arrived early to get a large table for the 5 of us. Most of us ordered off the regular menu and one person got the buffet.   My stuffed shrimp were delicious! And while pricey at $18 for a lunch, the portion was dinner sized and I had the leftovers for dinner. My coworkers had the shrimp clemenceau and the stewed chicken as well. We all really enjoyed our food. And service was great. They even separated our checks, whew.  I love the renovated dining room and the various rooms of the restaurant. I remember it being much darker 15 years ago. And it was very convenient for us that it has a parking lot.  Definitely will not wait so long to be back.

This is a large lot on Rampart and it is well lit. There is not an attendant on duty but be assured they have folks who circle looking for expired parking.  There is an app to pay for parking but I usually just add cash to the machine on site or swipe  a credit card. I've parked here pretty often without a problem.  Rate do vary depending on day of the week, time of day, time of year, etc. They do offer monthly contract parking if you live/work nearby. http://www2.premiumparking.com/park/locations-nola/420-n-rampart-st-338/  So my big issues are mostly with other users of this lot. Usually they cannot figure out the machine or park their gigantor vehicles too close to the lines and try to ding my car. Hmph

The first itme I stopped in was for lunch on a work day and Revel had just opened. My salad was delicious but with only one server working the restaurant portion and no drinking for me, it may not have been the quickest choice.  Finally made it back for a Happy Hour last week. Loved the wine and cocktail selection at HH and that they were supporting a charity that day. My sparkling wine was tasty and the snacks people got looked delicious.  Next stop...to actually eat dinner here.

While waiting for traffic so I could cross the street, I looked up a the golden shininess of this statue. It used to be located on the street between Harrah's and the river but was moved when Harrah's went under construction. She was a gift from France in the 1970s and is a replica of a statue in Paris.  She was moved to her current location in the tiny pocket park where N.Peters and Decatur split off in 1999ish. I like to think she's guarding the French Market against incursions from national retailers.  The Joan of Arc parade honors her on Epiphany which is also her birthday (and the start of the carnival season). Her feast day is May 20th and the day she was burned at the stake... maybe something should start happening in her honor then.

Y'know I used to love Bacchus with the BacchaGator and the BacchaWhopper and the Kong family (all are annual floats).  But this year the themed floats were LAME.  I think Bacchus is showing the age of it's krewe. C'mon "Saluting our WWII Veterans" may be a fine & noble theme, but it doesn't lend itself to exciting floats.  Yawn.  Props for the Bacchus foam football that looks like grapes.

I was surprised when I checked in here earlier today to see that the flag shop had such low score (2.5 stars) and now I see why...only 2 reviews.    I think this shop is a hoot.  The owners are very sweet and helpful.  The selection is huge.  I'm not a super home-decoratey person, but they carry such a variety here, that there truly is something for everyone.  We've purchased Saints & Jazz Fest flags here.  Today it was gifts for my Mom to give various folks.  She bought 3 different New Orleans themed flags and was very pleased with the prices.  Yes, walking into the shop is an experience as you are walking with flags brushing your shoulders (even short me).  If you're claustrophobic, it could be a problem.  Also the owners have a pet parrot in the store; I enjoyed talking to the bird, but my Mom is a bit phobic so she just pretended that it didn't exist.  You can't miss the store when it's open since they put so much of the stock on the street and it's really fun to see all the flags, windsocks and whirlygigs blowing in the wind.

I stopped in for an early Saturday morning breakfast with a friend.... And while it was good, it wasn't really what I was expecting. It's more a grab and go sort of place.  You order at the counter and folks were a mix of fancy coffee drinks and food. They seemed to be short staffed the day we were there, but that's just the way it is these days.  I got a breakfast biscuit with bacon on the side and an iced tea. My friend got the avocado toast and a coffee. My biscuit was good but the cheese was skimpy. My friend really enjoyed her toast.  The big plus is that if you want to have an adult beverage at 7am that's possible here.   It's in a big space with well spaced tables and outdoor dining so those are all pluses.

My only mistake at WINO was running an open tab on my card.  And after hitting the fun wine vending machines (it was like I was a little kid with unlimited change to hit the gumball machines), I quickly ran up a tab double what I thought I would.  Oh well, that's what happens when you taste lots & lots of wine.    I'm envious that @Seale P has eaten there a few times.  The night I went and wanted to eat, they were out of almost everything and my companion is gluten intolerant so that severely limited the few choices left.    I would happily go again...and give myself a credit limit the next time.

On a rainy Saturday we stopped in here because we were starving. I knew there wasn't too much on the menu for me (non-meat eater) but my friends eat all the meaty things so no big.  I had the caprese panini and my friends has a burger and a philly cheesesteak. They both really enjoyed their sandwiches and mine was fine but a little skimpy on the fillings. The crisps and fries were aces though. DELICOUS. They have coffee and tea and then a cooler of drinks. So there's a good selection for your beverage needs and a water area near the front.  Of course then we got ice cream and we all enjoyed our scoops. I had the hummingbird flavor (no actual birds, more the southern cake) and I can't remember what my friends had. Again delicious.  Staff was great and the space is really fun but with limited seating. I think most folks take their sammiches to go.

Please note that I have not used Zeus' Place for boarding or grooming as my big girl isn't with me anymore. BUT I have donated towels to their rescue efforts and occasionally played with their animals up for adoption through their rescue efforts.  Everyone is so nice and very into the welfare of the animals in their charge. And I love how committed they are to rescuing animals. Good job!

I stopped into Jaegers recently and picked up some to go plates for my parents and my dinner. It had been a while since I'd been over here.   Placing my order while sitting at the bar was super easy and the staff was friendly. And everything was well priced for the quality and the quantity. But let me tell you... my Dad's face when he saw those stuffed crabs, in the real shell not a little metal tin. He LOVED it. The friend shrimp were great and my Mom said the shrimp pasta was good too.   I wish the menu was a little more informative as to what is on a plate so I wouldn't have to ask so many questions.

Jaeger's was an institution on the lakefront until Katrina.  And I've always thought it was OK.  The advantage to the Lakefront location was that you ordered & paid at the counter and then a server brought your food.  This was ideal for large groups (no bill politics at the end).  The new location on Clearview is a basic NOLA seafood restaurant, lots of boiled (in season) and fried.  Good but not great.

Slowest Sonic ever. All I want is my strawberry limeade as a reward for running my errands. And it takes over 10 minutes to even take my order? Ridic...and not exactly fast food.  Otherwise food/drinks are the same as all Sonics.

Pandemic Review: I guess it's been a very long time since I've been in this shop if I don't have a review for it.   I am working on my house float and needed some exterior paint quarts to make it happen. SW was actually cheaper than other locations for some really basic paint. I walked in (masked of course) and they had hand sanitizer ready for me.  The sales associate was great to work with and she helped me find the least expensive options, knowing that I need the boards that I'm painting to last from Jan. 6 to Feb. 16.   The paint worked great and my project is looking wonderful.   Staff was all masked. There are plexi barriers at checkout. Hand sanitizer is supplied and there are clear social distancing markers on the floor.

Another solid Mr. Ed's. Y'know this local chain isn't fancy but is really solid, especially for fried foods. Like every location, the food was good and plentiful. The staff was great. The menu is the same as the other locations with the daily specials. I feel like the bar might be a little better. My old fashioned was perfect. And since fried shrimp has been my go to since I was a tyke... they do it right.   The location on St Charles is lovely and if you get a front window like we did you can watch the streetcar pass by. The bathroom is a bit of a wander so prepare for that.

I was hunting for an accessible lunch spot on a Saturday with the parents. Someplace that did plate lunches and not just sandwiches and this place was a great homey choice.  There is a ramp into the restaurant so it was easy for my seniors to access. The menu had enough variety to keep us all happy. Mom had the cochon de lait cuban and loved it. Dad had the hamburger steak and I had the fried shrimp plate. Our food was all tasty and well-prepared. The portion size was good and we had leftovers for them.   The server was great and she checked on us a couple of times and was very helpful. A good choice if you're in the area.

Once upon a time, I got a large portion of my wardrobe at the old UAL that was located on Vets. That store (and the shopping mall where it was located) is long gone but I remember it fondly when I pop into the FQ location.  This store is jammed with clothing...overly jammed. It's hard to move around and hard to get the clothes off the racks. So you have to have the energy to dig... The sizing is all over the map so definitely plan to try everything on. The staff is varied, but you sometimes find someone actually helpful.   I've mostly been successful with accessories in the last few years. Maybe because I no longer have the energy (after wandering the FQ) to do that much digging through the racks.

My review is for facial services. I have chased my favorite facialist around various locations in the GNO for the last decade. And now Nikki is affiliated with this salon. The location is new (and beautiful!) but the salon has been around for a bit (formerly located on Lapalco).  Nikki was running a special on infusion mini-facials for their grand opening. And while it wasn't relaxing as what she normally does, I definitely could see the difference in my skin. She is happy to consult with clients on whatever their skin needs are.   The facial room is very relaxing and well decorated with a very comfy bed and low lights. The whole salon is beautifully renovated. There is parking in back but you enter through the front door...unless you need to use the ramp.   Will definitely be back soon for Nikki's care.

This is such a lovely space and has been a variety of businesses over the last few years. I hope this iteration of the Tasting Room makes it!  My most recent visit was to a HH event planned by a friend on a Wednesday night in early January. There were $5 wines and $5 HH boards. They also have cocktails. But I was only doing club soda that evening but still had a great time.  The space is lovely and very conducive to intimate conversations or even some silliness with your friends. The bartender was friendly and the kitchen was quick.   In better weather there is a closed courtyard in back that is really pretty. I'll definitely have to stop back when I'm actually imbibing.

Pandemic Review: I was pretty sure I had previously reviewed this spot...  But since things have changed this year, I'll take another go. Most important thing to remember is that they are closed on Saturdays!  Right now, your minimum order is 4 cupcakes, so plan to either share or be a cupcake piggie. I split the difference by eating 2 and then giving the other 2 to my Mom.   One person inside the small shop at a time. You stand behind a table and everything is handled distantly; you can also call in an order and use one of several apps to have them delivered. And they even have shipping!  First choice: the blackout cupcake, just like the old McKenzie's cake but better. I also tasted the strawberry cupcake (the fruit flavors are delish) and the chocolate cupcake. My Mom raved about the sweet potato. Previously I've tried the lemon blueberry (seasonal flavor I think) and it was amazing too.  Putting on my GBBS hat, the sponge is light and moist and the icing is fluffy and not too sweet. Fillings are tasty too.
They sell pre-made Mardi Gras ladders, but you have to trick them out yourself.  Decent selection, incredibly helpful staff.

Pandemic update: Eleven years later (wow this was an FtR for me in 2009), this is still a solid choice for a neighborhood hardware store. I need various items for my housefloat and stopped in here while I was in the neighborhood to see what they had.  While one item was sold out, the others were available and at good prices. The workers are generally helpful and happy to give you ideas for your projects.  Everyone was masked and they had hand sanitizer so yay!

I loved the auction house that used to be in this location. But this fancy food court is a great addition to the area. It's perfect for when you cannot agree with your friends on a type of food.   The renovation of the space is beautiful and it's bright and airy. The food booths are interesting and tasty. The private room is a great space, roomy enough to move around and still intimate.   Love that in addition to the yummy food there is also a bar in case you need a grown up beverage. I haven't tried all the booths, but I've eaten at about half.

I decided that I deserved a biscuit early Sunday morning after running around and taking care of some business for my family. I consulted my app to see who was open at 8am and had good biscuits. So I ended up at Blue Line.   So early on a Sunday there was plenty of seating choices but since I was alone, I sat at the bar. Order at the counter and boom my food was out quick-quick. I ordered the blue line breakfast with grits and a biscuit. They allowed me to sub avocado for the meat. (See my pic).   Staff was super friendly. Food was good and way too much so I took some home. Biscuit was just what I needed and their homemade jam was yummy.

I attended a family wedding at this old school reception hall in Elmwood. The hall is divided into 2 sections and we were actually in both. The wedding happened on one side and they set up a very nice space for the ceremony and then we proceeded to the other side (after second lining in the parking lot) for the reception.   The staff was uniformly great and very helpful. Like most receptions the food was a mixed bag. Some items were delicious and others were meh. However the passed pastries at the end of the event were delish and I was sad that I was almost full. The bartenders were hard working and kept up with the thirsty crowd.  The dance floor was spacious and the dj played a variety of music so that even my 70+ parents got up and danced.  Yes the area is more industrial but there are a couple of reception halls in the area. The parking is abundant.

My go-to-bar for when I have out of town guests.  If they have a teenager, you can sit outside.  If you have a member of the senior generation, they still love the locale.  Great ambiance, good drinks, amazing people-watching

Wow! My last review of this spot is from 8 years ago... when I was looking for spot to have a boozy brunch for Jenn B!  So many years so many checkins. I miss bar hangs so much!  I stopped by just before 12 Mile was shutdown for MG weekend and got some batched to go cocktails. My 12 Mile Limit was delicious as was my to go old fashioned. You can always count on an excellent drink from the bartenders.  When I went it was to go orders only, at the front door with a plexi guard between me and the bartender + masks. Easy peasy.   They are serving on their patio at the moment (I think). And food is definitely available. High marks to the management for doing everything they can to keep their people (employees and patrons) safe.

Saints Football re-starts on Sunday so I guess it's about time that I get around to reviewing this event space. On game days, it's a "private lounge" to get a drink before the game. I've been inside on those days, but I don't remember how or why... was I on a list? Did I just wander in and no one stopped me? Who knows?  I've also been here for a variety of charitable events and it's a nice large space so there's plenty of room to move around. The food has always been good (from the mashed potato bar to sushi to salad bar to carving stations) and the bartenders are top notch.  If you're paying for drinks they can be a bit pricey but consider the locale. Random thought... I think this used to be the lower level of the Macy's that was once in this location, so I think I've bought housewares in the same space. Maybe.

Are you in dire need of Saints/Pelicans/LSU/Tulane gear? Then this is the shop for you.  It's no frills but has shirts, hats, homegoods, whatever you might need. I've mostly been here for Saints stuff and they have a wide variety of items.  Staff is helpful and the store is full. The parking lot though... it can get very full and is very narrow.

Yum to the tasty drinks and the awesome mac-n-cheese.  Love hanging out on the veranda in gorgeous weather.  And then there's the pool. Yes, there are lots of naked people. Yes, everyone looks, but don't be a douche and stare.   Things I like about the pool area:  * spacious * tab can be run at both bars at once (genius!) * hot tub * lots of chairs * secret tattoos on the patrons  Things I don't like: * bare asses on the chairs  * rented towels are pretty chintzy (bring your own) * mosquitos  All and all a fun way to spend the late afternoon....

When I first noticed these coffee shops popping up around town, I thought they were a national chain. Upon stepping into this location on Sunday morning, I realized nope; this is definitely local. Wow that's a lot of stuff everywhere.  I met some family members and we had a variety of items. I liked that I could ask for my hot tea in ceramic and not in their go-cups. I think hot tea changes taste when served in those synthetic-y cups. My nieces got hot chocolate and it was OK. The one person who got iced coffee was happy.  The food was hit or miss. The grits were gummy and the cheese grits had unmelted squares of cheese on top. One of the croissant sandwiches was sort of burnt, but my biscuit sandwich was good but really small.  Definitely will do a in a pinch but not my first choice.

Had a mini-shopping-palooza today and hit a few of the clothing consignment shops (Prima Donna, Swap, Encore, and On the Other Hand) uptown in search of a formal gown that would fit my short, curvy self.  So I feel confident in my comparisons.  Prima Donna's Closet is located in the Garden District right on the streetcar line.  It is very organized and has a good selection of shoes (green patent leather Jimmy Choo boots - thank goodness they weren't my size), accessories and a variety of women's clothing.  Several of the gowns I tried on were actually new, so I didn't have to examine them as closely for stains or damage.  The quality of the merchandise is good, but the prices reflect that.  There is a clearance room in the back but you have push past the enormous wedding gowns.    Not sure why Plus sizes is in the name. They carried from size 2 to 3x.

I hadn't been in Vic's in years when I stopped in the other night. And while it's a huge open space with lots of tvs and seats, it's still not going to be on regular rotation because of the cigarette smoke. As Vicky said, even if you don't seen anyone smoking the place just smells.   The drinks are cheap. So maybe dash in to order, then sit outside in front of the bar if the weather is OK.  The regulars are generally welcoming. But the bathrooms are odd. The stalls do not have doors instead they have curtains...which seems really unhygienic.

Shh! Don't tell my dentist that I go in here OK.  This is the store that you wished were next to your house when you were 10 years old.  Seriously.  It has a variety of candy to fit every need...or want...or whatever.

Yum Brunch! My poached eggs St Louis were totally delish.  My friends got the poboy benedict...although the ham was in chunks not shaved like the menu said and a catfish poboy which was huge.  All the food was tasty; service was a bit odd.  It felt like maybe our server was in training and the floor manager kept asking us weird questions about her service, with her standing next to him. She was doing a fine job but still weird & uncomfortable.  My friend also hit up the bloody mary bar...which had the strangest selection that day. No spicy beans, no celery, no okra. Weird.  I went with a sangria that was really tasty.

This is not your standard shopping mall, instead it's a former factory converted into a variety of arty stores and restaurants.    My friend loves the antique mall here. And it's a nice space to wander in on a rainy day.    There is also a giant rocking chair which seems to be a photo op destination.

Hmmm....what is there for the non-meater? Surprisingly a choice of grilled cheese sandwiches, including one made with cheese wiz.  But what gives this joint the 4th star? The boil fries!  They were OMG delicious and spicy!  Plus the staff was working their tails off to make sure everyone was happy and fed. Good job!

OMG! They have Flatsies here...OK they aren't the ones from my youth, but one of the modern incarnations, but still cool.  The selection was really interesting and different. This would definitely be on my list for gift giving for the children in my life.  The store was also really well laid out and well lit.

As far as I can remember this was the first Rouse's in the greater New Orleans area. It's small and a bit rundown at this point, but it has a good selection of location items.  The staff was pleasant and helpful. But boy does the parking lot need work.

HUGE warehouse out near the Lakefront airport. Wow there was so much stuff in there, much of it dusty so dress accordingly.  I was given the heads up that they had a bunch of surplus wheelchairs in their warehouse so I called to verify and got a price of $50 and showed up on a Saturday morning. We made our way through the rabbit warren of furniture and lamps and housewares and stuff to the wheelchair graveyard. They only had a few left, so I picked the best of the lot and was able to pay with my credit card.   As I tried to get the wheelchair in my car, it wouldn't fold but one of the workers realized that it had an anti-theft bar on it and took some tools out of his vehicle and removed it for me.   Yay! The wheelchair rolls well and isn't the prettiest but it served my Mom well yesterday at parades, even though "she doesn't really need it."

Maybe I'm justing missing the Blue Bird, but I thought the menu at Coulis was a little sparse.  I almost never eat breakfast out so was looking for something....but whatever it was wasn't on the menu.  Which is more a personal problem, I know.  So I ordered the breakfast sandwich and I think they scrambled up 3 eggs to go on it which was bit much for the croissant.  And we had a service bobble (the server didn't think E had ordered anything), but it was remedied with appropriate apologies.   Maybe I'll try again for lunch...

I was surprised to see that I gave this go to spot 3 stars over 3 years ago, as I eat here pretty regularly.   I love their fried shrimp banh mi also their tofu banh mi which isn't on the menu but they'll totally make you one. Speaking of not on the menu, they've also made me a grilled shrimp banh mi when I just couldn't do fried.  I also like their bun and the curry (which states is a shrimp broth). The spring rolls are solid as well.  I do a lot of takeout since this is near work. But if I dine in, I always prefer the patio. The parking lot can be a bit of a disaster around lunchtime but you can usually find parking on the street nearby, especially now that street construction is wrapping up.

Fun neighborhood bar in the warehouse district; good selection of scotches (which I don't drink).    About 4 times a year, they host Opera on Tap which is a fabulous way to check out some highbrow stuff in a lowbrow setting.

This is a nice spacious location with a patio (yay outdoors, boo smokers) They had a good variety of pastries the last time I was in.  And the ginger peach iced tea hit the spot.  The staff was courteous and quick. A solid local choice.  BUT I hate the parking lot at this strip mall with a vengeance...it's weirdly layed out and then add old ladies in giant cars. Yipes!

Interesting place. It's not really a traditional sushi restaurant.  But more of an Asian restaurant that also sells sushi.  Very important items to note it has INARI which is really hard to comeby in NOLA and I love it.  It also has a vegetarian sushi or sashimi plate which is again rare.   We had the specialty strawberry something roll and while I was hesitant, it was delicious. Another standout was the dessert tempura blueberry something. So tasty  The specialty cocktail menu was interesting and they had a good selection of high end sakes.  The service is still uneven but it's a new restaurant. I did feel the staff was trying...just confused.

I came here with a group of 6 coworkers for lunch last month. And the space is amazing! So light and airy and as is only right filled with art.  The food was great. I loved my mushroom and gouda grilled cheese. Others had the frittata, the apple melt, and the pulled pork. Everyone loved their food and that mac-n-cheese was divine. No time for dessert but I look forward to having a more leisurely meal in the future.  When I know I'm going to a place that is training HS age students, I have more patience with service bobbles and really our only one was that no one was sure who was our server, but that was quickly handled. The iced tea and water refills were plentiful so Yay for that.

This is the original location of the Pho Orchid empire...ok maybe it's not an empire, but  it does have a couple of locations and at least one express location.  The atmosphere is fancy asian and the staff is efficient and polite. It was *freezing* during my supper so I was definitely glad I brought a sweater.  The food was good but the menu isn't as veggie friendly as some other Vietnamese places, but maybe that doesn't sell in the Metrys. For instance when I asked if the vegetarian pho came with veggie broth, I was told no. So that would be not a vegetarian dish.  I got a shrimp dish and it was really tasty as were the spring rolls. My friend, who is a regular, enjoyed her more meaty dish.  It is a spacious restaurant with a couple of 8 tops so this would be a good choice for a larger group.

Obviously, I did not attend school here...but my Dad did...back when it was where you sent your son to get him to behave.  Add in an uncle, a bunch of cousins and now my nephew and I guess I do have a good family connection.    My reviews are for the chapel and the theater space...where I've spent the most time. The chapel is BEAUTIFUL. Love the domed stained glass...and I was sure I had a photo of it to post. Maybe later.  The theater space is good and really state of the art in many ways. The a/c can be spotty so if you're always hot, sit towards the outside walls and if you're usually cold than stay towards the middle.

I was on a quest for something very specific which is a terrible thing to look for in thrift shops, but y'know I'm stubborn.  This shop is really clean and well laid out. BUT if you're looking for clothes this may not be your best bet as it half the store is devoted to furniture. And the furniture is again in decent shape and clean. Some of the stuff looks new so I wonder if they get items from stores sometimes.  The parking lot is also clean and easy in and out from Jefferson Highway. I didn't find what I was looking for but it was clear that lots of other people were.

The best thing about this tiny little gas station? The price.  They consistently have cheaper gas prices then most of the stations around them (with the possible exception of the Discount Zone).    The worst thing? It is tiny so there is often a line for the pumps and it's ill planned in a corner of the Walmart parking lot, almost too close to the Highway.    Also, I feel bad for the person who has to work inside the tiny cube. Maybe it's secretly a government experiment?

As bright & shiny as the original on Magazine, but y'know in a strip mall. The staff was helpful and knew their product.  And the desserts were as delicious as ever. I do love the sense of playfulness that Chef Tariq brings to his dishes.    Minus 1 star for the disaster that is that corner of the Lakeside parking lot. Jeez.

You can sit out on the porch and pretend to be super fancy while admiring the Victorian/Queen Anne architecture of this lovely building.  Solid iced tea selection with normally 3 options...many more for hot. A very tasty and filling chocolate chip cookie is generally available as well as muffins and bagels.  The staff is usually pleasant and the indoor rooms are very cozy.

So mostly I just ditch shoes when they wear out, but I recently blew out both heel caps on a pair of vintage suede boots that I love.  So off to Joe's Cobbler.  The repairs are always stellar and the woman who works there (Josephine? or perhaps Joe's daughter?) has always been very helpful and kind.    Plus I love stores with shop dogs.  Hers is well trained and does not come down the stair into the store front without permission.

I am not a huge donut person, but when I stop by Freret to bring donuts to work? I am the hero.  These are tasty donuts, the glazed, chocolate glazed and the cake (which are considered fancy and cost a bit more).  I have not had a plate lunch here yet, but E did stop by to grab a breakfast sandwich to go.  Since he didn't want meat on his egg & cheese biscuit, the staff was a bit confused.  They didn't want him to pay the extra 25 cents (or whatever) for meat he didn't get.  Good folks.

Last night Midway was my perfect stop. I had been shopping all day, was cranky, and wanted seafood AND cheese. Lo & behold the King Creole pizza...  Seriously, this pie was a marvel. Plumb juicy beautiful shrimp that were clearly fresh  on top of a white sauce but then dabbled with a tomato basil bits  and, of course, lots of yummy cheese made for a lovely and delicious pizza.   I ordered my takeout at the bar and the lovely bartender made me an old fashioned while I waited. She even warned me that she had made it "a little strong." Clearly she recognized a road weary shopping warrior when she saw one.   The wait time was just enough for me to enjoy some of my cocktail and take a few deep breaths. Yay for go cups in NOLA (as always but it needs to be said).   I also had the tasty fresh house salad, but the pizza was the star of this show. 5 stars for being exactly what I needed.

If you're in the French Quarter and you need a New Orleans themed Christmas ornament in August, then this should be your destination.    Honestly the Christmas all year round freaks me out a bit.  C'mon let's keep the seasons in perspective.  However, my oldest brother helped renovate this place when it 1st opened. I think it was his first job (outside of working for family) when he was a teen...so maybe 1977?  I thought he was supercool to be working on a shop in the French Quarter.

Great little coffee and snack joint inside the Roosevelt Hotel. It's where the gingerbread houses are displayed in December.  It has a pretty dessert selection and PJs coffees & teas. Since I'm a fan of PJs teas, this is good for me They can also make a yummy hot chocolate.   It's convenient and affordable (especially considering the surroundings). The staff has always been pleasant and patient and the place is clean and beautiful.

Y'know when I've gone to this strip mall before, I've only had eyes for Hi Do bakery, so I never even noticed the bar down the way.  If it hadn't been for Joi & John and the Party Bus Wank tour, I would never have stopped here. But y'know it was a pretty cool place. The regulars were funny and tolerant of our nonsense. The bartender makes a good drink and was very nice.  Definitely worth a stop if you're in the area and looking for a homey (if your home is somewhere in the timewarp 70s) experience.

So I randomly ran into my aunt and uncle (and their friends) on Halloween as they were heading to one of my uncle's favorite bars in the FQ. Of course, they couldn't miss me as I was the one in the enormous Mad Hatter hat.  Who knew my Ohio (but Louisiana born) uncle loved this place? And why? Because he likes their absinthe service...which was a bit off (plastic cups) on Halloween night but still. I have no idea what sort of absinthe was served as I am not a fan. But if you're looking to drink the formerly forbidden drink in the shadow of the cathedral than this is the place for you.   It's a great location and off the beaten path a bit. Sitting outside and watching and commenting on everyone's costumes was a great end to my Halloween festivities. My favorite costume? A girl who was the travel gnome and her costume was mostly yarn and posterboard. Supercreative.  I think the last time I stopped in a this place, it was more of a restaurant...or maybe that was because it was during the day. Sometimes FQ memories can be a bit hazy, y'know.

I hadn't been to this spot in forever when we stopped in for a quick meal on a Saturday night. We must have missed the early dinner rush since the place was emptying by the time we were seated just before 8.   I ordered a salad with grilled shrimp and it was all soooo salty that i must have guzzled 2 or 3 iced teas.  My friend enjoyed her meal more than I did, but for the life of me I can't remember what it was.   The staff was attentive and friendly.  We were in the overflow room and our service didn't suffer but  think I would choose the main dining room on lighting alone.

What a great independent coffee shop. My iced tea was excellent which is great because so many coffee shops in town do tea poorly.   Shake sugary baked goods, my slice of morning glory bread was super tasty.   Views are great as are the outdoor seating area. Owners/staff are lovely.   Will definitely need to stop back in.

This is the big Lowe's..especially when compared to my little Jefferson Highway version anyday. Maybe it's because I was here on a Sunday evening, but while folks answered my questions (mostly about where stuff was located), no one was really helpful.   I stopped in this location because I thought there might be a better selection of certain items (closet storage and lamps) and while there was more overall stock, it still wasn't what I was looking for.  Oh well.  The hunt continues.  Pro tip: they shut down the air 30 minutes before the store closes, but don't actually make an announcement, until they start turning out the lights at 5 minutes till closing..or at least that's what happened at 8 pm on a Sunday.
Went last week for my birthday dinner (on a Monday!).  The menu is focused and delicious.  I had a fish special that included beets & jerusalem artichokes.  Highly recommended.

Painted Alive specializes in paintings on skin.  Don't be scared, no people or animals were flayed in the name of art.  The pieces that are for sale are photographs of the original artwork that was painted directly onto human flesh.  Some pieces celebrate the human form, where others are more in a trump d'oeil style so that you have to hunt to realize that you're actually looking at a person.  The gallery covers several body painting artists, but the majority of pieces are by the owner Craig Tracy.  (My disclaimer for the day - Craig & I grew up together.)

Not much to eat if you're with a vegetarian, but a very cute place.  The wait staff seemed way overworked the night I was there, like they weren't completely prepared for as many diners as were there that night.

I was on a Sunday afternoon bar crawl in the Quarters and was fading and there it was my caffeine godsend. Seriously, I'm not a coffee drinker but that go cup of iced tea saved my life.  The staff was helpful and polite. The space was clean  and there was space to move around. And my iced tea did not taste like coffee! So I was a happy girl. Oh and the chocolate chip cookie that I bought was life saving to another member of the group who was starving.   Of course, when I left the store, I had lost my group and had to go find them over on Bourbon. But totally worth the detour.

I was convinced I had already reviewed Performance...but clearly I was confused.  More confusing? While the shop is still open (and still called Performance), it is no longer a Subaru dealership.  I've used them for warranty work (now will have to go out to Bryan Subaru...oh wait, my car is out of warranty) and for general repairs.  The staff has been fine and the repairs have held.  But c'mon the car's a Subaru which means it's a tank (I give Subaru 5 stars btw)

Ummm... I've been here a bunch and never reviewed? Weird. Y'all know I love pizza so I'm all about the local pizza places. This spot has some interesting specialty pizzas that are tasty with fresh toppings. The crust is medium thickness but not too chewy. Love the grilled shrimp and the spinach artichoke. I'm also a big fan of the mango-cado salad.   I've always picked up my pizzas... I may be outside of their delivery area.... or maybe not. I figure if I'm getting a pizza at least I can go fetch it myself. The staff in the shop is personable but not necessarily your standard service industry interaction. I once got into a totally ridiculous (and fun) argument with the counter staff about Madonna... because a song of hers was playing. Good times.  The dine in portion of the restaurant is small but serviceable.   Great now I want pizza at 9:30am.

Y'know I like Krewe du Vieux and have attended most years that it's rolled.  (Shout to 1990 & King Al Scramuzza - My Mom & I sang his commercial to him when he stopped in front of us. Classy)  Since this parade is made up of subkrewes who are essentially independent, the parade seems a bit disjointed.  One group will have amazing costume or a great satirical theme and the next boring surprise pizza boxes. (I'm sorry I'm just over it after seeing them for the last decade.)    I do love the brass bands.  So points for fun satirical themes and keeping it old school in the French Quarter, minus points for some dude molesting me (on my back thank you) with a..."personal massager" and right after he did the same thing to my mother.  Sketch.

Sorry, Ryan, I'm going to disagree with you on this one.  I think Bourbon street is entertaining.  You get to watch tourists from all over the world have massive freak outs / bouts of complete drunkeness / whatever.  Yes it's filled with tourist nonsense, but that doesn't mean it can't be fun.

I went to Midway on their opening night, despite TS Lee.  They seemed a bit overwhelmed (but grateful) for the crowd that turned up.  Despite it being opening night, the staff seemed to be working well together with only minor issues.  We ended up eating at the bar.  We had a 2 salads & 2 small pizzas, but we should have split a single pizza. The crust is thick and very filling.  I really liked the flavor and the texture but E wasn't as enthused.  I think he's just a thin-crust person.  I liked it because it was different.  The toppings were good and his veggie pizza had really fresh big pieces.  The salads were tasty and the local beer selection was good.  I hope their menu expands a bit beyond just pizza & salads in the future.

Even in college, I never hung out at FH. Sure I'd stop in when other folks wanted to but it wasn't my regular spot.  But I have to give it to the owners. They are survivors.   The joint burns? They rebuild. The construction next door causes them damage? They fix it.  They're like the energizer bunny of bars. They just keep going.   To me the best time to stop by is for happy hour on a pretty day and sit outside with a beverage and some cheese fries.    +1 star for coming back from their latest setback and opening (bar only) in time for the carnival season.

As I was leaving City Hall on Saturday morning, I discovered this brand new car wash on Earhart. So new that they were offering all washes for $2. All the bells and whistles (normally $14) for that price? Yes please.  The wash did a great job on my car. And liked the blinking lights and multicolored  swirls for foam that poured over my car...very rave like. And the vacuum section was good and spacious and the brand new vacuums have major suckage...so much so that one tried to eat my sweater.   They don't offer a vending machine to purchase a shammy or other cleaning supplies which I've noticed at other car washes. And there was no floor mat machine. I'm not sure if this is because they are so new or they don't plan to get those.   The space was super clean and the staff was really nice. They do offer unlimited washes for $10 per month which is a really great deal if you're organized.   Will definitely stop back in.

I'm not a coffee drinker but my SO is & he stops by Village Coffee daily. Prices are good; coffee is tasty and staff is friendly.  Definitely better than the abandoned bank building that once brought down this corner.

I swore I wrote a review of this little park, but it seems to have disappeared.   This is a great park to play on a swingset or a slide. Yes those are mostly for kids, but I tried to convince E that we should try the swings out while we were walking by this week...and then I realized what Jean-Paul put in his review...all the non-toddler swings are gone, which is sad.  There still open green space at the back of the park so that's something.

Solid (this is my adjective of the month, I guess) diner type spot.  I did not have the coffee since I don't drink the stuff but the iced tea was good and the breakfasts were all really tasty. They even added extra strawberries to the fruit cup for the nieces.  Good prices, courteous service, good choice in Old Gretna for diner food.

My review is for the weekend Dim Sum only. I've not eaten at the buffet next door.  Until Vicky brought me over to the dim sum world, I had only read about this lovely tradition or seen it on TV. And I can see why folk are fans.  You order beaucoup small plates of delicious and spin them to each other on a lazy susan. What's not to love?  Service is different and you sometimes have to ask for things, but all the servers have been polite and helpful. If you know about a dim sum dish that is usually offered, don't hesitate to ask. You may have missed it on a cart or it may not have been offered to you yet.  Standouts for me are the steamed dumplings, the Chinese broccoli, the noodle dishes (which are veggie), the gyoza, and the egg & rice cake dish that looked like hashbrowns.  Tip:  Leave the teapot lid open if you want another pot of tea...

Honestly they had me at fried okra when I read the online menu. I needed a spot closer to the airport that was open on a week night.  Once I saw that Steve I was a fan. I knew it would all be good. My aunt and cousins enjoyed their food thoroughly. One of my cousins DEMOLISHED some boiled crabs and we all enjoyed boiled crawfish (this was a couple of months ago). The plate dinners were good to OK. Don't try to go healthy here, just go ahead and get the fried food rather than the grilled. My stuffed crab wasn't my favorite but it was fine. The fried okra did not disappoint, but I would probably tell them to leave the whisper of grated parmesan off next time.  Service was great. Our server made sure our water glasses were full and that the beers were restocked at appropriate intervals. The decor is old school seafood joint so that was perfect.  My aunt was so impressed with the seafood that she bought a few pounds of boiled crawfish to bring  home to my parents.  Great spot if you're in the neighborhood.
Great full service book shop.  Lots of signed editions.  Great local selection.

My Mom and I got crepes for dinner from the truck while at the sculpture garden at City Park. They were slammed with orders but were hustling to get everyone's orders out.  I had the crepe Italian with mozzarella, tomatoes and basil. Tomatoes could have been riper but it was very satisfying. Mom had the SBT, spinach, bacon and tomato and gobbled it up so she must have been happy.  I couldn't find a separate listing for the crepe truck vs. the bricks and mortar. The big difference is obviously location and the truck has only a small selection of the full menu.

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. So while we were in our Black Friday shopping extravaganza, we stopped for lunch with friends at Slice.  AND I love the Garden District location.  But this one really needs to work on their service, it took over 90 minutes from start to finish which is ridiculous.  Multiple tables came in after us and were finished way before us, because it took so long for our food to come out.    I will give this location another chance if I'm in the area, but will stick with the original for now.

A friend recommended their veggie burger...which I had never seen on their menu so I asked the next time they were parked by work, as again it wasn't on the menu. And yes they had some!   Their veggie burger is beet based so it was a pretty purple and it was nicely spicy with a nutty crunch so definitely a tasty version. The burgers come with lettuce (nicely crisp), slice of tomato (really ripe) and homemade pickles (delish) then you can finish dressing with mayo, yellow mustard and ketchup at the counter. The bun was soft and not seeded (my preference).   I wish I knew consistently if they had the veg burger before I sought them out. Also since I ordered off their regular menu I had no idea of the cost beforehand ($8).

Was craving some soup but they don't have the vegetarian tofu soup on the menu with the new name and new menu.  I opted for tofu spring rolls and grilled shrimp bun. The rolls were fine just a bit heavy on the noodles and not so much with  the rest of the ingredients. The bun was huge! And there were lots of veggies in addition to the shrimp. Very very tasty.  The space is lovely and the service was spot on.
Great neighborhood pizza joint.  And they have pellet ice.

Still the same cute stuff with good selection of seasonal shoes and handbags. But across the street, from the original location. They are now located at 4122 Magazine Street which is stated on their FB page, but not on the website...yet.  It seems like they've eliminated some of the secondary merchandise but maybe I'm still confused by the new layout. It's gonna take me awhile to get used to it.  Their stock was a tad bit diminished today but that's because they had HUGE sales prior to moving. Smart girls.

Outstanding atmosphere, yummy cocktails and great snacks.  But then again, I have a special affinity for Napoleon House.    In the 1930s there were apartments on the upper floors (the 1st floor was a grocery not a bar).  My grandparents lived on the 3rd floor when they were 1st married.  And if you give my mother a few sips of an adult beverage, she will giggle that she was conceived there.  It's her only dirty joke.

What? I don't have a review of this joint? Craziness  So, yeah, you can buy your throws here (beads, stuffed animals, spears, etc), but the real reason to hunt this joint down in a mixed residental/industrial area is for the costume supplies.  Gaudy satins, sparkly trim, appliques, tulle (for homemade tutus), hats, feathers, feathers, feathers. All of it is here. Caveats: check for cleanliness. Since this is all stored in a warehouse, the bottom of the pile fabrics can be dusty/dirty. Also make sure the checkout folks treat your feathers gently.   You can also buy tiaras, scepters and other royal accouterments here. I mean who doesn't need a Mother of the Queen pin?
Delicious fresh baked goods and my boyfriend (the coffee drinker) says they have his favorite coffee in town.  And you can buy king cake by the slice most days, during the season.

My meal was fine (I had the veggie quesadillas); the crawfish bruschetta were good. Two of my friends seemed to enjoy their meals (daily fish special and a salad), but our fourth said his pasta and seafood dish was inedible. That plus the extremely long wait for our entrees rates only 3 stars.  And it's a shame because it's a cute little restaurant in an interesting neighborhood.  Also, they had to find us a table that wasn't super wobbly.

Really cute boutique store in downtown Franklin.  They had a nice variety of accessories. The clothes were a good mix of special pieces and basics. I was lucky enough to hit up their sale rack and get some nice discounts.  My teen niece was in love with a couple of the purses here.  The sales clerk was helpful and not intrusive.

Another solid King Cake bakery.  I haven't been to the actual store. Their cakes are at various locations around the city.  A coworker brought this one today.  We had the pecan praline version which was more of a topping then a filling.  The pecan praline was tasty without being too sweet (emphasis on pecan rather than praline which I appreciated).  I did have to dump off some of the icing.  That was a little too sweet for me first thing in the morning.  Tasty.

Updating my review after a lovely father's day meal... I was expecting their standard brunch menu (which is good) but instead we were treated to a really extensive father's day menu (the same one they also used for mother's day).  We ordered the sampler appetizer tray for the table and it was quickly gobbled up: veggie eggrolls, yucca, softshell crab, shrimp, chicken croquets, and plantains.  It was definitely the way to go for our group of 5.  My parents split paella valencia  for 2 and proclaimed it delicious. The variety of seafood was really amazing and my Mom was impressed that the chicken wasn't the primary protein.  One brother ordered the breakfast burrito (which was huge) and the other brother ordered ropa viejas which he loved.  I had the scrambled eggs with seafood which was tasty but probably a little safe. I wish I had gotten something a bit more exotic.  We split a flan and a tres leches cake for dessert which were both excellent.  Round that out with some tasty sangria.  And it was a good day.

NOMA is a great regional art museum with good collections in Asian and African art.  They also have scored some excellent traveling exhibits.  I will always love NOMA because as a child, it really opened my eyes to art.  I climbed on their lipanzzer modern art sculpture.  And fell in love with a Georgia O'Keefe landscape.

Yum! Cake donuts for days. I love cake style donuts and they are hard to find.  Blue Dot has a multitude of flavors...an embarrassment of riches even.  Some were perfect, a couple were a bit too sweet, but I'm sure that's personal taste.  Staff was friendly & efficient.    Thank goodness I don't live too close.

hmmm...I forgot to review this place last summer. But maybe that's because I had a totally forgettable meal.  I think I enjoyed one of my tapas items...something with watermelon, can't remember.  Maybe if I knew I was heading to a bar scene with food, I wouldn't have minded. The place was loud, loud, loud (or lively in Open Table parlance) and that made it hard to chat with my friends visiting from out of town.

Oh my, another overlooked gem that I haven't reviewed yet.  If you need a hat (OK maybe not a befeathered 1890s lady's confection), this is the ONLY place to go. I know there are national upstarts in town, but you know you want to shop at a locally owned store that is staffed by a multi-generational family.  My uncle replaces his straw Panama hat here every few years (and invariably tells me the same Panama hat joke). I still have my grandfather's stetson (with his initials embossed inside) that he wore into the mid 70s. You can buy a safari helmet from them or a kangol or Greek fisherman's cap ...most anything.   My next purchase from them will be a top hat because y'know...I need one of those.  Stalker tip: Follow them on FB to see what celebrity has stopped in.

Not my usual cup of tea... When the Red Eye opened it was more of a diner, right? Or am I hallucinating that? And then it became a throw back dance club bar where you should NEVER where your good shoes since some drunky is going to pour a drink on you anyway.  My youngest brother told me tonight that you shouldn't even try to go here if you're over 30. Oops...messed that one up.  So the drinks are basic and the floor is sticky, but there was some awesome people watching. And I got to see a drunk girl try to pick a fight with a bouncer so that was amusing.    I guess if it's what you're into then wooooo!

As our only "alternative" paper (and I do use that term loosely), the Gambit offers a needed counterpoint to the mainstream Times Picayune.  And importantly, it is locally owned.  As others have noted, it is free and used to be the go to place for apartment classifieds...but I guess Craig's List has all that business now.  The writers go in-depth on local issues each and every week, with occasional breaks for highlighting important local happenings, Hello Jazz Fest issue!  They also host one of my favorite local news blogs, Blog of New Orleans (http://www.bestofneworleans.com/blogs/blogofneworleans/). The once a week twitter round up, on Mondays, is hysterical.
My least favorite of the local bookstores.  If you're not a regular don't expect good service.

First time I wandered into this gallery, I just couldn't help but laugh. Mostly because the little boy I grew up with has made good! Love his aesthetic and his creativity. His path to this gallery has been quite twisty & turny but that all influences his art.   He sells both original works, prints, limited editions and does commissions. His trompe l'oeil style is fascinating and is the most beautiful camouflage you've ever seen.   The gallery space is lovely and there are usually videos playing that demonstrate his process.   Definitely a must stop while you're wandering the quarter.

So maybe this just isn't my sort of place...although with the cheap prices for premium liquor, you would think it would be.  And it was good for people watching.  But with the booming sound system (my throat was hoarse the next day from yelling over it), the pervasive cigarette smoke (Yuck), and the subzero a/c (brrrr), I was not too comfortable.    Maybe if friends wanted to go back on a less crowded/smoky/noisy night, I would try again. Or maybe I'll just convince friends to try someplace else.

As I have small feet, I appreciate that they carry a wider variety of sizes.  Yes, some MawMaw (that's your grandma) shoes, but lots of cute and classic stuff too.  Recently scored cute Cole Haan orange casual shoes for $25.

Hmmmm... another review that disappeared. I'm still not sure why that happens.  Very delicious iced tea and I liked the frozen lemonade drink that they have here. I've found the pastries to be fine. They have them delivered from other local establishments and I remember them being labeled as such. Great for locals who have an affinity for certain bakeries. Love the shopping kiosk in the center and I've definitely bought fun little gifts here.   The line can be confusing if it's busy since many folks are first timers/tourists grabbing a beverage before their tour (that meets in the lobby of the Rink).  The outside deck is great and relaxing. And, of course, I love the Rink, the building that houses Still Perkin'. BTW the name refers to the fact that this independent coffee shop was once a franchise of a local change. When that relationship ended, they kept on going. Good for them!

It's hard for me to believe that this beautiful opened up space used to be the old Sazerac restaurant. It only makes sense to expand to another lounge...especially one that serves food. The space is spacious and airy although it does get loud depending on the crowd.  The evening I was there, the service was slow but they were slammed. My old fashioned was OK but not great. Next time I'll get a straight pour here and same the fancier drinks for the Sazerac Bar.  Benefit of this space...since it serves food, it is not exclusively 21 and over if you have younger family members with you.

The Theater of the Performing Arts was your typical 1970s era venue...until the Katrina floods.  It had its gala reopening last month (January 2009).  During the time it was closed it was entirely refurbished with all new sound and lighting systems.  I can't wait for the opera to return to the Theater in March.  And I'm off to see a symphony concert there tomorrow night.

Wait, what?! A chocolate shop that I didn't know about in the heart of the FQ? Where have I been?  But honestly it would be very easy to overlook this tiny little shop.   Yes, the space is small. And there were actually 2 staff members working (one for chocolate and one for gelato) in an area the size of a small living room. I was a bit stunned by the prices but the quality was good. I had a couple of chocolates and a sample of the king cake gelato that was on special.  I would probably stop in again, especially for the gelato. The prices would force me to have some portion control.

Again, I don't know how I haven't reviewed the Dungeon yet.  I used to spend a LOT of time here.  Almost got kicked out once with a friend b/c of our wild dancing.  Ha!  Has anyone mentioned that you can dance in a cage on the 2nd floor?  Or your friends can make out with supposedly gay boys in there?  A great place to people watch and just have a ridiculously silly good time.

Late on a Sunday night, I was hungry for sushi and several of my regular spots were either closed or I wasn't in the mood. And even though Sushi Bros has been in this location forever, I'd never tried it. So here's a run down of some of what we ate.  The good: the yellowtail roll was delicious and well balanced. The geisha girl roll was huge and really grew on me (but we asked for it without the eel sauce; I'm really not a fan of drowned in sauce.)  The OK; the Louisiana roll needed more pickled okra.  The bad: poorly cut red snapper sushi. Seriously how do you make red snapper that tough?  Pricing was good so I might go back but I would stick with rolls and not sushi in the future.  The staff was attentive and refilled our water/iced tea glasses several times. The ambiance is attractive.

I had lunch at Maya's last weekend and they were using their brunch menu.  I suspect that my entree is on their regular menu though I got the curried shrimp which was very tasty but maybe a little heavy on the cream sauce for a hot midday.  My friend got the breakfast sandwich on DELICIOUS coconut bread.  Really amazing.  There were also cocktails specials, so that definitely influences up to 4 stars for delish sangria & bloody marys for $5.  (Mimosas too but I didn't have one of those).   Definitely plan on going back.

My biggest problem with this location? It never seems too clean...the floors, the tables. Let's just hope the kitchen is OK.    I like their salads and love the tomato basil soup and their savory pastries are usually OK.  Yes the sweet pastries are tasty, but honestly I'd rather patronize a non-chain.  But that's just me being snobby (or shop locally or whatever).    This is a solid choice for quick (but not fast, y'know) lunch especially if you're alone.

I need to try this spot again...maybe earlier in the day. My food was yummy...but they had run out of ice for my tea. So I ended up with mostly warmish iced tea.  The baked goods were really tasty and my boxed biscuit was good...but I had to tell the counter clerk 3 times to leave off the bacon which she never wrote down. When she turned my order in to the back, I called out to the line chef that I needed the bacon left off. He looked at the ticket again and said thanks for letting him know since it wasn't written down. They did offer me extra fruit since I didn't want bacon. Now that's an awesome trade off for me.  The preserves were outstanding and homemade so that's a definite bonus.

I went for brunch and was so not impressed. The drinks were hit or miss. The food was OK, but not great. And it was crowded and super hot.  I did enjoy the 80s DJ and the videos projected on the wall.  I went back for lunch a week  or two later because it's someone's favorite lunch place and I wanted to give the lunch menu a shot.  And my experience was really much better.  The lunch items were tasty and well prepared. And while the place was still not well air conditioned, it was not nearly so warm.  But the problem for is that it's still inside the super sketchy St. Vincent's. And I don't know that I'm ever going to be comfortable wandering into that place.

Low key coffee shop but with fancy coffee...except I don't drink coffee.  So they have a nice selection of pellogrino here as well as other non-fancy canned drinks. They also have quality iced tea that does not taste like coffee.  Although the space is long and narrow, it's usually not packed and so you can find a space to stop and chat with friends. The one table out front affords excellent people watching. And the courtyard out back is very restful.  The staff has been uniformly polite and sometimes really friendly.

I'm not really sure how I don't have a review of this store; I think Yelp likes to keep me on my toes by gobbling up some reviews.   This store is chockablock full of novelty items. They do custom t-shirts; have gift items for whatever is the hip tv show of the moment...or classic show that people love (Dr. Who or I Love Lucy or Family Guy, etc, etc, etc).   Things I bought last week, a handsaw for cutting cakes, cat key caps, a batgirl keychain, novelty ice tray.   The staff can vary from out of it, to superhelpful, to hating life, so that's always a fun spin of the wheel. I will say the staff has always been really nice to my older Mom who asks way too many questions when she shops here.

This is the main post office for the City of New Orleans so it's usually crowded but it stays open later and usually has a bunch of windows open.  I've mostly gotten cranky but helpful employees. (I think if you're too cheerful or pleasant that you get delegated to other tasks.) But I've also seen them go out of their way for an honestly befuddled senior.   The vending machines for stamps and whatnot have always worked and there is plenty of parking.  They have longer hours than most branches, so it's all good.

I mean c'mon the name is awesome so my friend and I decided to stop in and check it out. They had some great furniture including a sideboard that might work in my friend's dining room. Lots of fun decor items.  The staff was helpful but left us to wander ...and the store is much larger on the inside than you would think. The prices were good for both the large furniture items and the smaller decor pieces.  Definitely a fun shop. Next time I had to Nashville, maybe I'll have to drive.

Cute converted corner store that makes a lovely intimate theater space. I saw a moody multi-media theater piece here and the only distraction was that during the quieter spaces I could really hear the traffic on St. Claude.  The box office space was furnished like an eccentric aunt's living room (and I mean that as a compliment) and was a comfortable space to wait for the show to go on.  The seating in the theater was comfortable and felt sturdy. (That seems a weird thing to state until I mention that the last venue where I saw this theater company my chair lost a leg in the middle of the performance.)  And the staff was all really nice.
Where to start?  I've never had the correct order of food delivered.  Last time I was there my cousin's bill was 4x the amount it should have been and took over an hour to straighten out.   O

I've been to Mondo a couple of times and my food has always been delicious and the service has been fine. But I've hesitated to review because I feel like a crankypants, the place is just so darn loud, especially at night.  The food is inventive and interesting and it's difficult to pick what to order because it all sounds so good. PLUS it has items that even tempt the less adventurous eater so you can bring the picky folks along with you.  My faves: the deviled egg plate (I will not share next time) and the fish tacos. One of my dining companions was raving about the pimento & andouille grilled cheese.  So my problem is the volume. I've been here at night where I cannot hear my dinner companion who is speaking at a normal volume. C'mon it's a restaurant not a night club...not that the problem is music. It's the other patrons. The place is popular and jammed many evenings so the volume you hear is everyone having a good time.  And I'm still crankypants.  So 4 stars because all they really need is some sound deadening and I would be a much happier camper.
Yummy Hippie pizza tonight.  But what is up with parents bringing their kids to restaurants to let them run amok.  Made me want to trip the little angels.  Tonight was also $10 bottle of wine night.

Obviously the best thing about going out to eat with Vicky is her awesome company. But another advantage is that when we go to Chinese restaurants, they immediately offer her the traditional menu rather than the American one.  We had the seafood and bean curd soup (which may normally have meat in it too but  they customized it) and while the texture was really different for me, it was really delicious.
