While I will always prefer the real French pastries found on every corner in even the smallest ville in France, at least this particular Paris Baguette has the touch and feel of a real old fashioned Boulanger. Wooden floors and display shelves, mural of the Tour Eifel, and decent cakes, breads, tarts and coffee, make this a pleasant stop and relaxation spot.  This is the third PB I have visited, and it is by far the most comfortable on a human scale.  The others have either been too big and cold (Edison), or too small and subterranean (Elkins Park).  This one does it well.   Glad they got it right this time.

I liked my breakfast at Hampton House Waffles & Eatery.   The dining room was nicer than expected, and service was outspokenly friendly and accommodating. I sat at the short counter where I was attended to by several people.  Coffee arrived promptly, and my order was taken with interest.  The server wanted to be sure that I knew what I was getting with the Gus' Special Omelet. He described in detail that it was a pancake type egg dish, with the home fries, as well as the feta, onions and green peppers inside the egg shell.  No problem. That was exactly what I wanted.   It arrived about ten minutes later, filling the entire plate from rim to rim.  The rye toast arrived a few moments later, lathered in butter. A few shakes of the pepper shaker and I was good to go.   It was a solid, filling meal.  Plenty of ingredients to load it up, with each element identifiable on the tongue. Maybe, a little more feta would have been helpful. The toast was also worthy of special recognition, as it was very hot from the toaster, and had a great crunch.   Next time, have to try the namesake waffles.

This Dunkin Donuts on Bustleton Avenue in the far Northeast Philadelphia, is about average for this species of fried round dough outlets. Small footprint, but with a corner lounge with worn out leatherette sofa and easy chair, and slate accent wall.   Nice touches, but it comes down to the quality of their bread and butter - their coffee and sweet dough. In this they cannot complete with the new wave of cafes, bakeries and donut specialty houses that are working harder for my dollar. In the last two weeks I have tasted far better java, and munched on way more luxurious cakes and dough fry around town and the burbs, than sampled last night. Maybe a little more money, but the difference in quality is patent. Too, they don't sweep the floor around you while sitting down to enjoy their wares. No one likes dust and dirt flying around their food. No one wants to feel swept out.   DD. Too much of a no longer great thing. Becoming stale; much like day old donuts.

This Giant on West Trenton Avenue in Morrisville is the same size as its sisters in Lower Makefield and Langhorne (Newtown), and has more or less the same inventory, but it does feel more dark and dingy than those other stores.  When I shop there, the lack of adequate lighting makes it a bit oppressive to spend much time.  The absence of the smaller, modern, carts available elsewhere, makes it necessary to use the larger, older and rustier pushers that often have gimpy wheels.    While it wouldn't take much to upgrade this commercial space into a more pleasant facility, the company seems to have decided to leave it as it is.  Perhaps, their lease is coming to an end, or the revenue from this location does not justify the expenditure.  Regardless, aside from the convenience of stopping in here occasionally, I would avoid it and frequent the newer and easier to navigate markets just to the north for the same prices.

It's about time to bestow the fifth star to Newtown Bagel. It is awarded for consistency of effort, sincere and friendly service, long term partnership with the community and excellence in breakfast sandwiches. Their success is shown by the opening of a second shop, Yardley Bagel Co. in Lower Makefield, which produces the same quality baked rounders as Newtown, in a more expansive and comfortable space. Can a third be far behind?   While I still have a small issue with the texture of the bagel skin which is softer (less crisp) than I prefer, I can't deny that the pliable nature when fresh from the oven creates a perfect platform for a hot steaming sandwich. My just eaten sausage, egg & cheese on untoasted onion bagel was wonderfully delicious from first bite through last. The chew blended ingredients well and gave full voice to the harmonics exploding in my mouth. Alas, my tastes have matured to appreciate the pleasure of the different texture. There is a place in life for more than one variety of bagel.   Bagel Wisdom attained by hard experience and exhaustive bagel research cannot be denied.

When the sign on the front door says, "DO NOT ENTER WITH HOODIE OR MASK...IF SO YOU ARE NOW TRESPASSING," you know there is a fundamental problem being expressed by management.  This isn't the best neighborhood in the Capital City, in fact, it is one of the worst. I wouldn't be found here at night, but for a quick lunch with parking right out front, and Trenton's finest stopping in for take out, I felt pretty safe as I dined on my Eggplant Parm Sandwich.    The loaf was fresh, mildly crunchy and had a good mild yeasty flavor.  The Eggplant had been sautéed in a frying pan with extra virgin olive oil before being finished in the pizza oven to melt the cheese and seal the final product.  It was a good sandwich, even if not the lunch of the gods.   Service was friendly, if a little jumpy.  Only four booths for eating in.  Same ownership for 23 years.    I guess they have seen the hood change during that time.  How many holdups before the sign went up?    No doubt, one was enough.

State Street Kitchen is NO LONGER open Friday nights for dinner.    The menu leaned toward Korean cuisine, complete with stainless steel bowls, chop sticks, and special hot sauces to heat your pallet and warm the soul.  The crowd is quite different than who you see at breakfast and lunch.  It seems like many of Micha's friends come down to hang out with her.  They bring wine or harder stuff for all to share, and often pick up a mix of desserts to pass around.  Sort of like a pot luck.   This is a great direction for this small house.  With the right people working the kitchen, expanding to other nights would be a boon to nighttime State Street.

Read Whitney A. from Holland review (12/2/12), which mirrors my own.  The staff is very friendly and fast, the price is reasonable, and the coffee decent. All good things. But, the bagels are not close to being the right texture nor taste. They could be so much better with a little tinkering.  It's not that they are bad, it's just that they miss the target of being really satisfying.  With so many bagelphiles adrift at the loss of Bagel Junction, Newtown Bagel could become our Shangri-la, and garner our undying devotion and business with a few adjustments.

Keystone is still the reliable discount tire house on Street Road, Bensalem, Pa. They offer a broad inventory of competitive tires, and provide honest assessments of which is best for your car and driving style.    Just came down to replace two all season touring hard rubbers, and had several to choose from, and others that could be on site within 24 hours.  They suggested which would most likely suit my needs, and it was on the low end of the price range.  65,000 miles rode wear guarantee.  They also showed me where my existing tires were worn unevenly, and strongly recommended an alignment at my earliest opportunity.  They didn't push.  They just pointed out the problems I had been having and would continue to experience if this was not addressed.   I drove away with a new set of shoes and a far smoother ride.

Whoomzie's is named for an owner's mother's nickname, according to the counter person who made my onion bagel, butter & Swiss sandwich this morning. In all respects but the new name, this bagel house is unchanged from its days as Jersey Girl Cafe. There is a small lounge area with TV, table and loveseat, as well as a sunny dining area with seven tables. Orders are taken toward the rear of the shop.   My morning repast was good, although I found the bagel denser than I prefer. Still a good taste with fresh butter and cheese. It was a very decent chew. Having I Love Lucy reruns playing in the background made for a relaxing and reminiscing moment. Those gags never get old.   Oh, I just realized that something else has changed. They reversed the entry/exit doors to improve traffic flow within the store. Too, the door latch hardware still sticks without paying proper attention to turning the knob.

Classic German American bakery in Bensalem, Bucks County.  This two store chain produces some of the best sweet dough around.  Their Cinnamon Rolls are big, light and covered in excellent icing.  Eat 'em while they're hot for maximum load mind blowing experience. They react well out of the microwave, too.  Butter Cake is more dense, moist and uber sweet for those of us who love a mouth full of Domino delight. Heat it up and it becomes sweet butter soup. The large cookie, brownie, cannoli trays looked great, but will await another day.   This shop is well lit, allowing we gawkers to have close up looks at all the amazing goodies.  The staff is friendly and seems to enjoy all the customers drooling over their wares.    The coffee isn't bad, either.

The status of Duke must mean that I like the place enough to return more often than any other Yelper.  It has sought of snuck up on me that I have become Newtown Bagel Company royalty, but it does reflect reality.    I have grown accustomed to their bagels, and more particularly the warm friendly way they greet me and know what I want before I order it.  Yes. They are making a safe assumption for someone who is a creature of habit when it comes to bagels.    They informed me that they have a punch card and since acquiring it I have scored a couple of free cups of coffee.  Nice touch.   I have become a fan based on the above, and it is time for my reviews to reflect this.

The layout is the mirror image of The Home Depot I visit most often, but it only required a second to figure that out.  The orange aprons were friendly and helpful.  We found what we needed, and after reading a few of the labels, made a choice in remote garage openers (serious shit, I know!). After we got it home and read the fine print inside the packaging, I realized that my machines are antiques and several generations behind contemporary technology.  Seems 1993 was the cut off date for the latest radio frequency devices, while mine are a few years older.  How can such things that still work well be obsolete?   So, had to return it today to my local THD, and go with the Genie brand, which, after all, were the ones I installed originally.  Only they make the expensive key to maintain their own stuff.   Should have the code mastered soon, and have two functioning remote door openers to allow for ease of access and egress for both old and new(er) vehicles.   Now I know more than I ever wanted to know about remote garage door openers.    Ah, wisdom!

We weren't sure where to go for a good haircut/shaping for her thick black Chinese hair, but waiting longer for a visit home was finally off the table. She decided to walk around Chinatown and check out a few salons and talk with the cutters to see what they recommended. Our third stop was Famous Hair Salon on Cherry Street between 10th & 11th. Not sure how the decision was made, but she took a seat in front of the mirror and the manager/stylist went to work. I sat on a bench and nodded out.  She looked great and seemed very pleased with the result. Happy she. Happy me!   The prices were reasonable, although it is a cash only shop.

If you are into old world bakery pastries like you used to munch when grannie took you shopping, then Eet Gud Bakery is the place that will fill your nostalgic sweet tooth.   Large format Danish, donuts, cakes, cookies and loaves of Euro-style breads overflow the display cases and back shelves.  The copious icing on the top only hints at the abundance of cream filling within.  Like Glazed Donuts?  Look no further.  Cream-filled sticks?  Glazed Sour Cream rounders?    This is your Shangri-La!  All this caloric glory provided courtesy of the women behind the counter who have been packing bags and boxes of these incredible delights for the past 40+ years.    Once you bite into their cruller or cherry-cheese Danish there is no going back.  The addiction is instantaneous and dream-evoking.    Go after a particular bad day when you need a sugar fix.  This place will do ya!

Just returned for another round of Chengdu Heat.   The Diced Chicken with Dry Hot Pepper was impeccable, with tender chicken coated in a hot spice dusting and lightly fried, all stirred with a variety of peppers. The more I ate the more comfortable my palate was with the heat.  We had a Fish Fillet dish on the Specials Menu.  It was likewise tender, moist, and more of a blast furnace due to the red sesame oils it was simmered in.  This one never cooled down.   If you are unaccustomed to unadulterated Szechuanese 5 alarm cuisine, this may not be your cup of tea. Han Dynasty doesn't approach this degree of conflagration. But, if you are into it, you will find your experience here quite fulfilling.  This guy is on fire!

Solid new Casa Mexicana on Markley Street, right in front of El Primo Mercado and Cafe. Limited parking in front, with much more behind. Bright and colorful with a limited menu of their greatest hits. Friendly, efficient service from the lovely woman working the floor.   I ordered their Cemita Poblano Torta, a supersized fresh sesame seeded roll full of spicy ground beef, queso fresca, lettuce, red salsa, al pastor style. It was a huge work of edible art. Hot bites and I could only manage to consume half while sitting at a high top table. Took the rest home.   They did bring two bowls of red/green salsa to me, but the chips never arrived. On the other hand their horchata was a chill, refreshing and cinnamon flavored liter of strong slurp. At $2 for the "small" size, it was the bargain of the day.    Given a choice between this "Mexico City Woman" restaurant and El Primo about 100 feet away, I would go with El Primo based on more choices and stronger kitchen talent, although the former rice drink was more flavorful than the later.   Norristown and environs continues to impress with its broad array of comidas Latina Americanas.

This newest Trenton McDonald's is located on Chambers Street, catty corner from St. Francis Medical Center and across the street from Trenton Central High School.  Pretty good location.   It is one of the newer designed, small footprint stores, with wrap around, two lane, drive thru.  They really expect most of their business to stay outside.  They are friendly and efficient at what they do. But, if you are a pedestrian, be careful approaching the front door as there will be traffic bearing down on you, with drivers not necessarily paying attention to your presence.    The food is standard Mickey fare.  I am more fond of their breakfast sandwiches than the burgers.  I grabbed a sausage, egg & cheese biscuit and large coffee on my way to the office.  Priced at just over $5., it was a reasonable deal.  The meal was freshly made, with tender, buttery biscuit and still hot patty.  The coffee has been pretty good lately, and the one price of any size is a clever marketing tool.    Breakfast @ desk is not my favorite way to eat, but some days it can be like that.    Everything was satisfactory.

Below average wings at best. Ours were cooked to order, but overstayed their welcome in the deep fryer making them dry and way more chewy than should be. More like chicken jerky. Too, the fries were limp and dying by the time the styro packaging was opened. At least the Fanta Orange was as expected.   Definitely a one and done experience. There are just too many quality wings available in almost every restaurant in  the country to be satisfied with such a poor effort.

Very glad to report that nothing much has changed at Bagel Delight since my last report. Still baking very good Bagels, providing friendly service & above average Java. The regulars appear to be the same, too. Understandable. If I lived in Lambertville I would be one of them.

Just added two new dishes to the excellent heat profile provided by Szechuan House.  The Chongqing Chicken is a first cousin to the Spicy Chicken Dry Pot Style I have had in the past. High burn with every crunchy morsel. Just below numb on the volcanic scale, perhaps not reaching conflagration due to the meager presence of Szechuan black peppercorns and reliance on red chillies to cover for their absence, but still excellent.   The Crispy Fish Fillets Sweet & Sour was a large deep platter full of lightly fried fish and loads of orangey thick sauce. More Cantonese, but a strong interpretation. Really liked it in the face of all the other flames.   The few other plates were good, but not worth taking up more space here in light of all the other fireball delights found in this still surprisingly authentic Chengdu palace.

Of the limited Chinese options in the Newtown area, this place is by far the worst.  Strictly take out unless you want to sit at one of the two odd sized tables covered with newspapers.  Several Guangzhou brothers operate this relocated tiny shop.  The kitchen is in full view, and it is not always pleasant to watch how the food prep is done.  As someone else suggested, this is a place to go only when all the alternatives are blown away by a storm.

This warehouse of a shoe store is to feet what The Home Depot is to home improvement. It offers more than you could possibly need to do the job, but intoxicates with choices. Depending on your interest, you can wander around either one mesmerized by all the possibilities.  I needed a pair of dress browns to wear with business suits. The far left wall had at least 50. Wing tip, two tone, light, medium or dark umber. Contrasting laces, loafers. Traditional or light weight. American, English or Italian. Get the picture?   Eenie, meenie, miinie, mo...  The psychology is to force abandonment of rational decisions and lead you to the conclusion that it makes sense to buy more than one pair to get you past indecisiveness. Don't worry. You are saving money, too.   I fought off the urge to splurge and went with Aldo wingtips. Good fit. The cashier approved.  Will need to find the right color shoe cream to keep them looking spiffy.   Very proud that I didn't succumb to the pressure to buy them all (Yet).

Is it the best diner in New Jersey, Land of Diner Enchantment? Maybe not, but it certainly has history and local color going for it. Oh, and a great breakfast if you fancy overflowing plates, unlimited coffee, and a Greek Omelet that is a wonder of the world.   What is it about feta cheese and eggs that moves me so?  Don't know, but when mixed with sausage, potato, onion, peppers, all wrapped up in an fresh egg case, they become an amazing sensory explosion.   Trenton may have seen better days (we have been waiting for its resurgence since it was "Americas Town" in the 60's), but Pat's carries on. Diners are only partially about the food, and the rest about the concept, design, and lustful loyalty they inspire.  Pat's is a worthy contender for the Urban Diner List on Yelp* (If there is one).  Give it a try.  Sit at the counter and watch professionals do their thing. Sit at a window and see a worldview that captures the past-its-prime city, the capital of the Garden State, remind you that... We Are Still Here.

There are two entries for this supermarket, the other being, "McCaffery's Supermarket."   Same store. Same experience.   Slightly upscale compared to the nearest competition, Acme and Giant, but not up to the quality and gestalt of the Wegman's, Whole Foods, and Trader Joe's of the world. Have to wonder what would happen if one of those retailers came to Ntown, which has been discussed, but not yet evolved into a real plan.     This shop has the mandatory Starbucks, and a pretty good produce department.  The rest is the same as everyone else. Close your eyes and open them again, and you could be in any generic supermarket in the USA.  No better. No worse. At least you know where everything is.   Definitely, middle of the road grocery experience.

As the old saying goes, " Anything worth doing is worth overdoing." This perfectly sums up Redberry in Village of Newtown Shopping Center.  There are many franchises out there, and all are about the same, with only slight differences in flavors, textures, and toppings.  Here, the flavors seem tamped down.  The Country Vanilla was weak, and the Pumpkin more like nutmeg and Cinnamon, than real pumpkin.  The toppings are all sugary and add too many calories to be healthy.   The environment is very bright and bare bones.  No comfortable place to sit other than plastic chairs and small tables. Take out is certainly the message here.  It would be interesting to compare the calories here with the real ice cream places nearby.  For my taste buds, and someone who loves yogurt, Redberry is an underwhelming experience, although my young son likes it . At approximately $5. per serving with toppings, it is not a cheap treat.

I have returned to McC's a few times since my last review in January, 2013, and have noticed a general improvement in the offerings, marketing, and prices.  While still tending to the more expensive side compared to the competition, it is now possible to find items on sale of more than a nickel off the normal retail price, and the staff seems to have grown into their new surroundings in Newtown, and are more friendly, courteous and knowledgeable.    It is still not my first choice for groceries (have to go to Trader Joe's and Wegman's in Lawrenceville, New Jersey for that), but I am willing to visit here for the things the family needs without gritting my teeth with self loathing.  Still wish they carried Finlandia Swiss and a few other non-Boars Head deli products, but I am learning to live with that, as it seems the others supermarkets in Newtown have cut the same deal with that company.    Time for a raise.  Three Stars.
Sunday Brunch UYE Review -  Sorry folks. You'll have to read the other reviews of this Am-azie-ing brunch venue.  I need to take a nap first.

This GNC has been in the Village of Newtown for 15 years.  It is a good place to pick up nutritional supplements to assist your healthy lifestyle remain that way.  While diet is a key determinant of health, sometimes an assist from a quality vitamin, mineral, or herbal mix can enhance the constitution.    For me, several health professionals, both traditional, allopathic and alternative have recommended Grape Seed Extract, Ginseng, Ginko Biloba and a good multi-vitamin be added on a daily basis. After more than 20 years of using them they seem to have made a difference.  Skeptics can doubt, but I am a believer.    GNC offers high end products, and when I don't want to boil herbs to make health teas, I use their supplements based on confidence that they are high quality and subject to decent quality control.  Sometimes the higher price disturbs me when I find another good manufacturer at better price (I do shop around), but absent that, GNC has my loyalty.

Old Style pizza joint with a broader menu to attract more diners into their cozy dining room.    Problem is that while the Tomato Pie and the other spinning disks are very good, the same cannot be said for the rest of the in house cuisine.  This was my first visit to Palermo's III after visiting the others in Hamilton and Bordentown.    The Tomato Pie is thin, crisp and nicely spiced here, but if forced to compare with its former siblings, it would come behind the Bordentown establishment for quality pies.  We also ordered a family sized Caesar Salad and Sautéed Spinach as a side dish to get in our veggies for the day.    The Salad was just okay with nice Romaine, Shaved Carrots, Onion and Croutons.  However, the dressing came in a small plastic container and was mass produced and lacking in true Caesar flavor (no anchovy taste).  The Spinach was definitely from the freezer and was a watery tasteless waste to eat.  Very disappointing, and not worth the $6, by half.   Lesson learned. Stick to the pizza and tomato pies, and leave the rest to those who don't know better.

McCaffery Supermarkets recently opened another store at the site of the former Genuardis Supermarket. They have upgraded it considerably, and it is a very pleasant environment for food shopping. However, the prices have gone up and they are not really competitive with the Acme in the same shopping area, nor the new Giant that replaced Clemens last year. I went through it a few months ago, and realized that all the things I normally purchase were more expensive there than the other two venues.  I don't go there any longer, as any of the specialty items they carry that are not in the others markets, can be found in abundance at Whole Foods with more variety and an even nicer experience.

Pleasant environment for a first lunch at Vietnam Restaurant on 11th Street.  Dark wood tones, extensive menu, and apparently, a good bar.    My lunch was simple; Pho Tai.  The bowl was smaller than at other VN locales, but tasty and well presented with a full plate of accessories (spouts, lime, jalapenos,basil leaves).  The flank steak was thin and lean.  The broth as doctored at the table, spicy and engaging.  The noodles, soft and of adequate volume.  At $6.95, it was exactly what I wanted for a light lunch.  The Vietnamese coffee was also very satisfying.    I need to visit a few more times and try more on the menu before coming to a final opinion on this pleasant fixture on the edge of Chinatown.

Richard Thorton was the original owner of this historic structure on the corner of State and Centre in the heart of Newtown Borough. While he would be proud that his home still stands sentinel after more than 250 years, his allegiance now would be to the nation he witnessed being born and to the Black Horse Tavern that occupies the premises and warms his ghost as he sits at the bar after hours, enjoying the many tales his compatriots tell as the town sleeps.

Young man wanted a haircut that was long in front and crew in back.  He is old enough to make such momentous decisions on his own, but needed a ride and paymaster. You get what I mean?   Great Clips in The Village of Newtown Shopping Center was open on Friday night and wasn't busy. They took him right away. I stood back and permitted the stylista and Young Man to negotiate alone. They reached accord and the clippers started buzzing and scissors started cutting.   Ten minutes later the job was done. YM was satisfied with the rad results, and I was pleased with the $15 prix.   He didn't look bad, and I can get used to the blond streaks (I hope).   The shop is in the midst of major renovation. Be careful where you step. It should look great when completed.

Lovely to look at, but impossible to love.   The setting alongside Lake Afton is as pretty as a postcard, but the 3 car parking lot is ridiculously inadequate. It makes a difficult traffic location that much worse, forcing people to focus on parking rather than driving.  Double and illegal parking happen every day, creating a dangerous condition. Amazing that the Yardley government permitted Star$$$ to do this.    The coffee is the same as everywhere else, which to me is poor to average for the basics, but decent if you fall prey to the insidious upsell pressure to go latte or capp in order to be able to imbibe the burnt tasting brew.   The facility is pleasant once inside, with windows facing Main Street or the lake. It is also a front row seat to the near miss accidents that routinely happen there.

Love the location in the heart of Newtown, and very happy they appear to be doing well.  However, this variably topped flatbread is just not pizza. Many love it and are fans or more. I have eaten there a dozen or more times and find it curious, interesting, and mostly satisfying as a healthy alternative meal. Still, when I want real pizza I do not think of Jules.  It does not satisfy me the way a true tomato pie does.  It lacks the cultural affect, the aroma, the bite and crunch, and finally, the taste of traditional Italian pizza.  Too, no one speaks Italian behind the counter.    These are part of the pizza experience that are every bit as important as the actual slice, folded and ready for the big first bite.   Cent Anni!

Brooklyn Bagels is an open and spacious shop just off County Line Road at the intersection with 2nd Street Pike at the border between Southampton and Huntingdon Valley. It offers a wide variety of traditional and more modern twists on the bagel genre.    The bagels are large.  They have the right mildly crunchy exterior, but an interior that is a little too dense for me. That just means that it is kneaded too long before boiling, removing the air pockets that create a lighter product.  Sometimes the only way to know if the density is wrong is to wait to see what happens in its digestion.  When I get indigestion and a lingering aftertaste, I know it was not quite right.   Still, they use extra large baked onion chips on their bagels, and apply them evenly on both sides. All good.    I am sure that these rounders hold up very well clamping down on a heavy sandwich, and they certainly have their fans.  But for me, a lighter chew is preferable.  In my bagel quest throughout Bucks County, Bagel Train in Yardley comes closest to my desired Golden Fleece.

Stopped in mid-afternoon last Saturday.  Really liked what they've done with the place.  The core bar and dining area remains untouched, but there is a large outdoor canvassed patio out back that really expands the possibilities.  This day, a band was tuning up for an early set while a cadre of heavy metal thunder Harleys chilled and waited.   The people working the bar and floor were cool and sweet and handled everyone with grace and humor.  The food (Burger and Roast Pork Sandwiches) were very good.  My Yeungling Draft was cold and thirst quenching.   Haven't met Ralphie yet, but the dude got something going on!   Will be back pronto. Left something with our pleasing server that I really want back.

I was cruising down Maple Avenue, Langhorne, in need for a caffeine break.  Up ahead was what looked to be a fairly new Dunkin Donuts. I parked, went in, and ordered hot java.   To my surprise, the coffee was above average for a DD, and the staff friendly and efficient. They must be hooked up to a good water company for the coffee to be that smooth.
Can't speak to the rest of the menu this cold and rainy Friday morning, but this place certainly has hot decent coffee at a great price ($1. for any size joe).   Service for the drive thru was fine.

Getting back to basics, all I wanted was the original double patty Elevation Burger, straight up with ketchup, jalapenos, and hot pepper relish. No fries. No shake. No sweet drinks.   That was exactly what was delivered to my high top several minutes later. It came neatly wrapped in a plain brown paper sleeve. Upon opening, there was copious grease dripping from the wrapper. The chef must have added that after grilling, because the burger itself was no overly wet.   It tasted great. There must be something to that organic, hormone free, free range cattle from whence the beef puck comes. The texture was soft, and the flavor, excellent. Definitely a step above 5 Dudes, and on par with Shake Shack at a lower price point. Reminded of Burgatory, one of my faves in the Pittsburgh, PA area. Priced right at around $7 for the sandwich.   Fries started at $3.50, and shakes, $5. Add those and pretty soon you have an expensive lunch on your hands. Without, the burger justifies itself every time.

That's quite a lot of braggadocio for a tiny Chinese takeout shop on the bad side of Brunswick Avenue in Trenton, NJ. Actually, there is no good side in that part of town. Of course, it is just advertising; meaning that none of that name is true.   This chop shop is state of the art dumpy and depressing. The woman at the order station is friendly enough, but the kitchen help spends a lot of time staring out at the customers. Just a little weird. Whether eating in or taking away, the food is served in the same closed take out containers. Plastic and styro all the way. Chinese tea? Bring yours from home.   It's not that the grub is bad, it is about average for a joint that doesn't much care about you, and assumes you know nothing about Chinese/American food. The wonton soup, pork egg foo young and fried rice were recognizable by sight and taste. Yellow dye chicken stock, thick skinned dumplings, day old yellow chunky rice - just the way they taught them in mail order cooking school.    Edible, but forgettable.

Staples is a cornucopia of office supplies.   Much like Home Depot for home repairs, or Cabella's for all things outdoors, this warehouse provides multiple alternatives for anything you need to run your office, prepare your kids for school, and even large colorful tins of Danish butter cookies for your office kitchen.   While not always the most competitive in price compared to the catalogue and online outfits, when a shop like Staples is in your town, and you can eyeball and touch the things you need before you take them home or to the office, there is an obvious advantage to the consumer that makes the cost differential worthwhile.  It is the only place I buy my calendar for the new year, and I admit to being amazed and amused by the variety of paperclips available.   If there is a shortcoming (and the basis for not shouting, "Woohoo!") it is that the staffing is meager and there are seldom enough workers on the floor to help out finding things.    Still, I am very happy to have Staples in Newtown.

I rarely get to this part of Levittown, but I had a date with Levittown Printing just down Haines Road and decided to look for a breakfast place where I could hang out until they opened.  Yelp led me to Violetwood Café, yet another of those quiet gardens hidden from plain sight in a strip commercial center that has seen far better days.  The café is brightly painted and staffed by a cadre of black T- shirted servers who have a very positive attitude about their restaurant and seem to enjoy their jobs.  I sat down in a booth toward the back and had a mug of coffee in front of me within a minute. It was fine. The menu had both the popular usual suspects for breakfast, plus a few permanent house specials as well as a daily black board.    My Sausage Scramble (I think that was it) was a large mountain of Egg, Italian Sweet Sausage, Onion, Peppers, topped with Provolone.  It was moist, and chunky and fun to eat.  The Rye Toast was a real loaf complete with Caraway Seeds.    Violetwood Café is a 4 Star performer, and could easily move up.

Mr. China in the Pennington Road Shopping Center, Trenton, NJ, actually surprised me with its cleanliness and decent lunch offerings. The space while primarily for takeout, also has eight booths for people like me who prefer to eat in in relative comfort when the food is hot.   Service was friendly and smiling.  The house mother took orders, worked the cash register and delivered my General Tso's Chicken to me.  It was actually on a ceramic plate, not a takeout container, a big plus. The meal was pretty good for a generic well known dish. There was ample chicken. The breading was not overly thick, and the sauce was freshly made with chili flakes noticeable in the dark amber covering. The fried rice was a weak point, as it was mass produced with a yellow dye and few veggies, meat or egg.    With a bottle of Snapple, it was a $7 deal.   It was A-OK!

Apparently, China Express has been at the corner of S. Olden Avenue and Liberty Street in Hamilton, NJ, for several years, but managed to eluded Yelp detection.  Those hidden days are over now, and it is time for this small primarily take out joint to come out of the shadows.    The house has a couple of booths and tables for those who prefer to dine in, but even the house sitters get their General Tso's in styro and plastic.  No concession to customers who actually eat what they cooked in front of them.    My lunch special was pretty much down the middle of what is generally offered in these places.  Massive amounts of pre-dyed yellow pork fried rice with small pieces of meat and veggies, along with heavily glooped chicken pieces; breaded, fried and doused in mostly sweet amber jacket.  Nothing new under this sun.   It was neither better nor worse than most of the others of this genre.  Edible, if not inspiring.  At under $6., plus the cost of a drink, it was what was expected.    Ownership is friendly and efficient, and they keep the house bright and clean.  Best part is the small parking lot right next door.

Liberty Two Diner (Freedom to Dine) was a good place to stop for lunch on my way north on Rt. 130 in Bordentown, NJ.  It doesn't look like much at 50 mph, but at speeds slow enough to allow for a seat at the 10 spinner counter, it had everything necessary for a solid meal.  Friendly service, large menu, Cecilware coffee maker, and small bowl of soup with every sandwich.    The Navy Bean potage was surprisingly good, loaded with white beans and well-stewed veggies in a mild tomato base.  Liked it a lot.  Followed on by a Chicken Salad Sandwich on Rye toast, which was tasty and filling.  Perhaps, not as chunky as I prefer, but still fresh, cool, and plentiful.  The side of French Fries was way over the top, but the few I sampled were hot and crisp.  Beware opening the ketchup bottle (It discharges on its own).   All this, and change for $7., plus tip.    I'll be back.

Bagel appreciation is very subjective.    One person's phantasm is another persons disappointment. So, it is important to keep that in mind when evaluating a rounder experience.   This became paramount when I stopped by Abington All Star Bagel on Rt. 611.  The shop was small and clean.  The staff, friendly and helpful.  The bagels in the display, real beauties.  I ordered my standard Onion Bagel with butter and Swiss, and took the bag to go.    Upon opening the white sack, and unfolding its wrappings, I beheld a large, lovely, heavily onion flaked top, which still carried the aroma of its freshness.  First bite confirmed its recent vintage, and also that it was quite dense and firmly chewy.  Many like this texture in their bagels, but I prefer a crunchier skin and light, airy innards.    This was not that, but I appreciated the quality of the product nonetheless.  While I would not seek out All Star for my frequent bagel fix, there are others who will find these dough tires the cat's meow.   Freedom of Choice!

This is another underheated, undercleaned, primarily takeout Chinese/American shop in the Capitol Plaza Center in Ewing, NJ. It is very cheap for those lunch combos with fried rice, and a buck more for an egg roll.   My General Tso's Chicken was okay, cut into smaller pieces and not too heavily breaded, with a decent amber sauce. On the other hand, the fried rice was a dark brown from the beef consommé in which it was made, and served hard and clumpy, with a minimum of veggies/sprouts. Had the taste of being prepared too long ago, and left sitting in the pot all day.   The woman working the counter was friendly, and brought lunch to me at the table with a smile. She trusted me enough to wait until I was finished to accept payment.   A mixed bag.   2.5 STARS.

Family run grocery that grew with the population and moved out of Trenton to this location in the burbs to keep up with their customers.    A good idea before the hypermarkets began to dominate the landscape and put immense pressure on the little guys to match either price (impossible) or performance (customer service and specialty items).  This it could do for a while, but ultimately it was not a long term solution.  Today, it struggles along as a convenience stop for those in the area.    The selection is limited, and the prices are higher than most of the competition.  The family is older and the next generation has not picked up the baton.    At least it is clean and the staff friendly for the most part.   In time, it too will pass into history.

Cleanest Friendly's I've ever visited.   Like an oasis in the middle of Gloucester Premium Outlets, it provided shelter and sustenance when I had had enough shopping and just wanted to get off my feet and quell the emerging late afternoon hunger pangs from dodging lunch.    Friendly service, and a reasonably priced patty melt with waffle fries were exactly what I needed.  The surprise free sundae put a creamy smile on my face.   Sure. I've had better, but Being There was Everything this day!

I had not been inside Giuseppe's Pizza since before my twelve year old was born.  That is a life time in pizza years.  After today's basketball game in Churchville, we stopped in for a few slices and drinks to assuage the pain of another close loss.   The pizza was as good as I remembered it.  Strong enough dough to hold its point proudly without folding like a dog's ear; minimal drip of oil from the face of the pie; and a serenely enjoyable first bite experience.  My son's first impression was equally positive.  His comment to the effect that it was not quite as good as Marco's in Newtown was well taken and subject to debate.  Regardless, Giuseppe's is in good company. We will need to explore the menu further by venturing into cheese steaks, parms, and pasta to consider moving up the star ranks.

Stopped in the other day for a late lunch.  This was a first visit since this pizza parlor changed hands, and it was immediately apparent that the entire shop had had a makeover. The kitchen was now in the back, and the dining room in front; a reversal of its original layout.  New walls and floors made the place feel more upscale than the old place. Nice use of stone, wood and paint.   We opted for cheesesteak and eggplant parm sandwiches.  Both came with fries. The steak was a full load of chopped beef mixed with onions and mushrooms on a lightly crusted roll.  Very good.  The eggplant was thin sliced, breaded, sautéed in olive oil, and then grilled again in the oven, after which it was dosed with their homemade gravy and mozza.  Again, very good. The rolls were notable for their crunch and pleasant taste. The fries were really unnecessary, and were the weakest part of the repast, as frozen crinkle cuts.    Reasonable prices.  Friendly service.   Will definitely return for the pizza and more menu items when in an Italian mood.

Well, all right!  The new and improved Acme in The Village of Newtown requires a revisit to the old review. It is no longer the boring step sister box store of yesteryear. Now, not only has Starbucks taken up residence in the front of the store, but they have installed a beer and wine aisle and a small eating area near the deli department. Will the wonders never cease?!  Even service seems to have moved up a notch. More friendly faces and helpful hands. Better trained cashiers and help desk personnel. The salad bar is definitely cleaner and better stocked than before, too.   Yes. It is still an Acme and not a Wegmans, so let's keep perspective. Yet, the new Acme is far better than the old, and they deserve an "A" for effort. Prices are still very competitive for the area. They are really working to hold on to their old customers and attract new ones.   These days I find myself thinking of stopping in their Starbucks, or grabbing a six pack rather than making a separate run to the local beer outlet. Give them credit for opening my mind to their new possibilities.

TWO SLICE LUNCH REVIEW  Despite receiving the "well done" reheat as requested, I was less than satisfied with the quality of the pizza served up at Nina's on Bridgetown Pike, Feasterville-Trevose, PA.   Most significantly, the balance of cheese to red sauce was way off. There was a ton of low grade mozzarella releasing oil and dripping on the plate, and the mass of fromage on top made the undercarriage too weak to hold the weight, causing sag from the get go. Too, the sauce, such as it was, was overwhelmed by the copious cheese, so that the only available flavor on the tongue was of salt. Not pleasant.   Service was fine and efficient. The dining room was partially open for sit down dining, with chairs on top of tables elsewhere in the room.   I didn't sample anything else on the menu, but Nina's is a No-No if looking for decent tomato pie, at least of the reheated variety.

Better known as Anthony's IV Pizza & Pasta on Bridge Street in Morrisville, Pa., which has its own Yelp page and more reviews, this old line pizza joint may not look like much, but turns out pretty good Italian sandwiches and platters at last century prices.   Only street parking available, but in the evening, the avenues of Morrisville are pretty much open and you can pull up right in front or on the side street (Washington).  Friendly faces and adequate booth and table seating.    This is another of the Mexican/Italian deals, but don't let that deter you.  The food is good and you won't really notice any Spanish accent unless you order the Mexican Pizza.  My Sweet Sausage, Pepper & Onion Sandwich was as good as most you can get across the river in the capital of New Guernsey.

Decent enough small diner on York Road in Warminster, PA, where breakfast was had this morning. My third post-vaccine meal in a restaurant as the world crawls out of its collective cave to taste life again.   The Vegetarian Omelet was a substantial plate load of 3 eggs, broccoli, onion, mushroom and spinach, with a shovel full of home fried potatoes for balance and good measure. Rye toast was a crunch and a half. Very filling, but required extra black pepper for taste on both the eggs and taters.   I was surprised and concerned that the server was not masked, when we were required to be, and the owner was covered as well. Even with two jabs I would have felt more secure had she considered the reality that she was in contact with everyone in the dining room and kitchen and close proximity with every customers' food.  There is something to be said for keeping up appearances, especially in a food service business.   Maybe management will see this review and reevaluate its policy on proper social distancing protocols even in the improving circumstance of an almost safe, nearly post Covid world.

Apparently, the Popeyes website had so much traffic recently as people went crazy looking for their new chicken sandwiches, that it broke down! What followed was the exhaustion of sandwich provisions nationally, resulting in millions of disappointed customers arriving at bright orange & red stores just to discover signs across the wall menu that said,   " WE'LL BE BACK!"   I was one of those people at their small shop in Levittown, PA. The line wasn't long, but the sense of delayed gratification was tangible. After all those YouTube vids of people sitting with stacks of regular and spicy mayo sammies wrapped in specially designed paper, and watching them munch them up, rolling their eyes in delight, and attempting to speak waxingly with mouths full, it was almost too much to bear.   So, I grudgingly went home with a 3 piece dinner to share, knowing I would have a hard time convincing anyone that I didn't eat them on the way.   Brilliant marketing, though! Always leave us wanting more.

WHOLE PIE PIZZA REVIEW -  Stopped at Giuseppe's for late lunch after a beautiful walk around at Morris Arboretum. It was about half way home. Perhaps with eyes bigger than stomach, we went with a large pie, half pepperoni, thinking a fresh baked pizza would be more satisfying than reheated slices and we could take the rest home.   It didn't quite work out as planned.   Upon delivery to our table by the friendly server, we noticed a small pool of oil sitting mid pie. We blotted up as much as we could, but it remained shiny with the excretions from the pepperoni and low grade mozza covering the crust.   The request for a "well done" finish to make the undercarriage as firm as possible wasn't honored, so each slice drooped down when lifted and continued to drip oil. The cheese layer was too thick to be supported, and there wasn't any balance with the sauce, which was a bit salty for our buds.   Just not a very strong effort. Made us rue our decision and wish we had gone with a couple of slices, or better yet, not stopped in at all.

The space was modern, yet comfortable. Black tables, wood-like floors.  A nice diner-esque counter. HD TV on the wall.  Menu full of creative alternatives in the pancake, French toast, waffle and omelet genres.    Perhaps I made a mistake in ordering a simple Short Stack of French Toast.  It seemed as soon as I gave the friendly server my order she was coming back with it already mixed, dipped, grilled and plated.  Olympic turn around time.   But, something went wrong.  The four wedges were not fully cooked.  The toast was mushy and not hot in its core. There was no crispy caramelization.  It had been rushed for no apparent reason other than inattention.  Time constraints did not permit returning it to the grill for a few extra minutes, so I ate what I could and took my leave.   With so many good reviews, mine is surely an outlier.  I will try again in a few weeks and see what I get.  But for now, I have certainly had much better French Toast at many places in the area.

I stopped in at Namaste Indian Bistro in the Davisville Center in Warrington, PA, yesterday to chow down on their weekend lunch buffet. The shop is deep and quite narrow, obviously carved out of an adjoining store to create another retail space. Maybe a dozen tables in front, with the food spread out on a table right outside the kitchen.   There was plenty to choose from made up of a mix of chicken, vegetarian and even a goat curry dish. Some were very freshly prepared, while others were past their prime from sitting out over a steam table, inevitable when dealing with buffets. Still everything I tasted was good to excellent, especially the veggie korma and custom made garlic naan. Appreciated all the beautiful yellows, reds and amber colors from all the sauces.   I enjoyed my meal. At $11.99 for AYCE, I thought it a very good deal.   Service was minimalist, but how much to expect when basically serving yourself? My water glass was refilled, the used plate removed from the table promptly and the naan brought out from the tandor oven when fully baked and steaming hot.   What's not to like?!

Surprisingly strong fried chicken down on South Broad Street by Popeye's.   The bright orange shop has been there for several years, but always seemed out of place as a drive through box in the middle of urbanity. My bad for not checking it out before now. Walked in on a very clean space staffed with friendlies and stocked with trays of golden brown clucker.   Their two piece lunch deal came with one side and a biscuit. Under $5 for a filling and tasty treat. I ordered the spicy version. While it wasn't too spicy, it was certainly hot and crisp. The inner meat in the breast burnt my fingers as I ripped it apart. Soft and juicy. Really liked it. Actually gave me two wings along with the breast. Coke machine offered a large variety of their soft drinks.   There is another excellent chicken shack further down Broad, so there is a choice of good stops to satisfy the bird lover in you.

I'm not sure how the words, "authentic" and "style" can be used in the same phrase to describe the legitimacy of anything produced far from the original source, as done by Manhattan Bagels. "Style" suggests it has a similarity to the original, but really isn't from the creative source; while, "authentic," is defined as being from the original hands. So, it really can't be both - except in the world of Madison Avenue false advertising.   Please excuse the discourse on meaning, but the truth is that regardless of name and slogans, these are decent bagels. While not quite as crisp as I like on the outside, the texture is lightly chewy with a pleasant mild maltiness within, and without skimping on the toasted onion flakes or veggie cream cheese. I would like them even if from Manhattan, Kansas.   Service was friendly and quick, and the House Blend coffee provided the requisite morning kick in the pants.   This franchise is well represented in these parts, so while not on my list of absolute favorite bagel houses, it is certainly worth a stop when the breakfast bird is hunting for its early worm. You shouldn't be disappointed.

Honey Baked Ham is the non-kosher name for a chain of primarily sandwich places where you can order a combination of sandwich, bread, drink, side and cookie for a prix fix.  You can also order a full ham. This one is in the Village of Newtown section anchored by the Pier 1 store.   The few times I have been there I have gone with Turkey Breast, Swiss Cheese with lettuce and mustard, Cole Slaw side, Snapple Ice Tea and a Peanut Butter Cookie. It comes in a cute box.  They taste good, if not outstanding.  The service has been friendly, but when I am there it seems the owner is there alone and doing all the work.  This makes for a feeling that he is rushing around, for which he has my sympathy.    I have also been a regular of another HBH in the Mercer Mall in Lawrenceville, New Jersey.  That shop seems better organized, and the food is somehow more enjoyable.   Still, when I need to eat at my desk or want to be in Tyler Park for an hour of nature, HBH offers a great solution.

Hospitals are never fun places to be. Even when just visiting a sense of dread overcomes us.   Yet, Thomas Jefferson University Hospital, and all its component parts, makes the experience as positive as possible for most of us.  From the valet service drivers through the Chief of Medicine everyone approaches people with humanity and an understanding of what is involved in going there.    I have been using TJUH for a long time for myself, my family, and friends.  I recommend it to everyone seeking world class medicine with a friendly face.  From Rothman, The Heart Institute, Cancer Center, and ER, the treatment is state of the art and first class.   Unfortunately, I have seen my share of medical centers in New York, and for my health and for those I love, Jefferson is where I find the best combination of care and caring.   Before you decide on anything serious it is wise to at least obtain a consultation with a Jeff doc.  You will be glad you did.

This is an old style Jersey diner before they started using steroids to make them bigger. The ambiance suits the architecture, and the staff is friendly and prompt.    I stopped in for a late lunch last week.  I was greeted with a warm engaging smile by Christine, who led me to my table, handed me the menu, and went over the specials.    I went with the Chicken Salad Wrap which came with a cup of Chicken Okra Soup and Fries.  The Soup was really good; making me wish I had a bowl of it.  Lots of chunky okra and chicken, with other veggies thrown in for good measure.  The Chicken Salad was wrapped tight with Lettuce, Tomato and Sweet Pepper.  I could only finish half, but it tasted freshly made.  Quite enjoyable, although I prefer my chicken salad chunkier.    I was most taken by the atmosphere here.  It captured the feel of an old time diner, and while I ate I was able to temporarily depart this contemporary mortal coil, and spend a few moments in a bygone era.  Although the interior is of recent vintage, they did an excellent job in maintaining its simplicity.   Will definitely return regularly.

Aside from being the only DD I know that has converted floor space into a fire pit leather sofa lounge, there is nothing out of the ordinary in this shop.  The coffee is hot. The donuts sweet. The service so-so.  The lounge full of Russian 20 somethings.  If any of these appeal to you, this is the place for you. Me?  Not so much.

California Tortilla has good, fresh grub in a Mexican/Tex-Mex style.  The store is large and clean, and the staff seems into its mission.  My Chicken Quesadilla was loaded with Beans, Corn, Lettuce, Fresh Jalapenos, Monterrey Jack and plenty of Doodle Do.   The Tortilla was thin and crisp from heating on the grill as its ingredients were gathered and mixed and then sealed with the melting of the cheese.  It was very nice.    Their signature is the wall of hot sauces that you can select and pour into little plastic cups in any configuration and quantity you wish.  I went with the Bee Sting Honey/Habanero and Pineapple Pizzazz (I do love fruity salsas).  The Pineapple combo was deliciously hot and played well with the quesadilla.  The Bee Sting was exactly that.  Hot, piquant, and left me to drive home with semi-numb lips.  It was great!   So, while I normally prefer my Southwestern cuisine in divey bars in Tucson or Nuevo Laredo, or even in the transformed taverns of Trenton that are now all Latin eateries, California Tortilla offers a very tasty and entertaining alternative, especially if you don't like adventure as part of your dining experience.

When a young and growing child runs through a pair of athletic shoes in a matter of months, the need for a fairly priced distribution point becomes a financial necessity.    So it is that Dick's Sporting Goods a big box store very near the Oxford Valley Mall comes into play.  It is in the rear of that warehouse of a retail outlet that all varieties of foot gear are displayed and available for purchase.  Where some of the smaller shops have a few designs in a few colors from a few manufacturers, Dick's offers the most of all.  Too, if paying attention to the flyers in the mail or email advertisements, it is possible to save substantially.  Size 12 Nike Air basketball shoes listed for sale at $85, were actually secured for $20 less with the help of those coupons and cards.  The cashier was very helpful in making sure we got the best possible price.    Knowing we will be back in about 90 days to replace the worn out Nikes with a new and likely larger pair, is a good incentive for both parties to maintain good relations.    See you then, Dick.

The cheapest gas in this part of town and right on my way home at night.   Yes. It is a busy station due to price and location (Route 29 Northbound), but I find the service to be prompt and friendly.  I never go into the store, so can't comment on the coffee, snacks nor social propositioning.    If you're looking for quality gasoline and good prices, this is a good place to consider.

I haven't tried the Wings here, but if they are anything like from their other locations, they are fine.  I stopped in for a Fried Fish Sandwich the other day for late lunch.  The Fish was light and flakey, the breading thin with a mild taste.  Most important, the oil was clean, so there was not unwanted taste from anything that had been fried before.  For comparison, the fish at JC's Fish and Soul Food  farther down Nottingham is better.   The accompanying Fries were also okay.    I wouldn't rush back to Chuck's, but I wouldn't avoid it, either.

It's hard to get excited about a car rental experience. Still, there are better and worse ones, and this interaction with Enterprise in Fairless Hills, Pa., was better than many.    My vehicle was in the body shop for repairs after a rear ender than left the rear bumper of my car looking like the loser of a boxing match.  These folks picked me up at the shop, drove me to their store to complete the necessary forms and had me on the road in less than 20 minutes.  They worked seamlessly with my auto insurance to arrange for coverage, leaving me with a small balance to pay for the reality that most car rentals cost more than $16 a day.    My Mazda 6 was decent, if not exceptional.  It was clean and handled well.  It was efficient on gas.  When I brought it back, they drove me to the body shop with a warm smile and interesting conversation.    No hesitation to use them again.
Two listings for this new smoothie shop. This one appears to be secondary. Try the other for tips and reviews.

The Café sits in the Pine Watson Shopping Plaza on North Pine just before the intersection with Maple Street in Langhorne Borough.  It is the star of an otherwise undistinguished row of shops and restos. The interior is bright and homey with  nice counters, tables and booths. The servers are friendly, courteous and have time for a short chat with all the customers.   The breakfast menu is traditional, and the coffee is Ellis through a Bunn-o-Matic. Strong, middle of the road brew.  I went with a short stack of French Toast along with the java.  It was made with Texas Toast and arrived nicely crusty with caramelized edges.  It would have been even better with real maple syrup, but then the price would have been much higher.    There are a high percentage of regulars here which adds to the attraction.  The repartee with the high energy behind the counter ladies is warm and clever.  I imagine that if this was closer to home or on my way to work, I, too, would be a regular guest.   As it is, I am a fan, and I will get here sporadically when I can.

Located in the Newtown Business Commons, Cosi offers breakfast, lunch and dinner for the businesses in the area, as well as the Homewood Suites Hotel down the street.The chain offers moderately upscale, fresh foods in a comfortable, modern environment.  We had two Cosis in Newtown, but one closed last year.  The food was consistent from both of them. Breakfast meetings are my primary reason for being there.  Their oatmeal, square bagels (freshly made), muffins, and coffee are very good.  The lunch salads, sandwiches and pizzas are fresh, creative and tasty.  Try the Signature Salad with grapes, dried cranberries, walnuts and blue cheese.  Breakfast comes in at about $7., and lunch, $10.  Certainly, not outrageous.  The staff is competent, if not always warm. Overall, a very good place to enjoy a local breakfast or lunch with friends and associates.

We walked in during a birthday party for a young child.  The store was loud with kiddos shouting and running around.  Not bad if you like that helter-skelter ambiance.  But, not the place to find a quiet corner and enjoy a fresh baked and salted mini pretzel or three.  So, we took advantage of their special of 12 minis for $5., and boogied out to the car to continue on to Philly and munch in the voiture.   The pretzels were fresh and okay, but far short of spectacular.  Chewy.  Salty. Carb City. Definitely needed a washdown to keep the pipes clear.    The hot dog pretzels did look interesting.

This adaptive reuse of the former NASA centrifuge where our astronauts were trained before heading for the Moon, is a model of excellence in concept, design and performance.  It is worth a look just to see the once state of the art space technology now sitting above your head in a large circular room, bathed in warm blues, reds and greens.  Where once science reigned supreme, now houses one of the most interesting and comfortable banquet halls imaginable.    That we just attended a wonderful event honoring terrific people who helped make our Council Rock School District one of the best in Pennsylvania, if not nationwide, is very nice, but that it was held in this amazing "space," makes the moment unforgettable.   Wonder what they could do with a great rock band here?

I am in the minority on this one, but to me the name misrepresents the products and atmosphere of the 2 Paris Baguettes that I have visited.    While the shop here is smallish and in the basement of the H Mart building, it is clean and has good service.  Yet, the selection here is not as varied as in the plant in Edison, New Jersey, and the seating arrangements not as comfortable.    Most important is that while all the baked goods I have tried are fresh and soft, they bear no relation to the boulangerie found in its namesake, Paris, France.  There, the taste and texture of each of the pastries is unique, while here they are uniform and provide little differentiation.  Yes. They are all sweet and tender, but are not anything like a French bakery.  Perhaps, I was spoiled living in France and enjoying the pleasure of great croissant and other delights on a daily basis, but as "nice" as these offerings are, they do not approach the amazing flavors and surprises found on every corner in Paris.    Paris Baguette?  C'est nes pas vrai.

New kid in town...Smoothie King in the Village of Newtown South. Near Marcos and Wendy's.  Huge selection of combo fruit drinks with nutritional additives of choice. Three sizes: large, larger and largest.  I just tried something with Orange and Mango Juices, plus Banana and some secret ingredients.  First sip came on strong, and it continued to hold my attention all the way to the bottom.    The owners of this new shop are good local folk excited to be opening a business in Newtown.    We wish them every success.

Corner Bakery Café is still a comfortable place for breakfast, lunch or dinner, and seems to have settled into its skin in the time it has been open in the Village of Newtown.    I am partial to the Steel Cut Oatmeal breakfast, and the sandwiches available for lunch. The basic Tuna Salad Sandy is tasty and filling at a reasonable price.  The option between Carrot Sticks or Chips is a good one.  The Bakery choices are very good, if perhaps a little pricey for the size of each slice, muffin or bagel.  Coffee is above average.   However, as the current Duke of this domain I am at a loss to understand why I was asked not to take a photo of the display case with all its goodies.  I thought free advertising was always a good thing.  Especially on Yelp!

I am still a breakfast regular, and an occasional lunch person here.  My Oatmeal, Squagel and Coffee still offer a good price for a good meal.  In fact, the cost seems to have gone down recently due to some combo they put into effect.    It is a convenient stop on my way to the office.  They recently moved the coffee out from behind the service counter and it is now pour your own.  This makes for a small jam, but it is manageable.   Every ten breakfasts/coffees gets a freebee if you have their card.   Good deal.

Crowded to near over capacity this New Year's Eve Day, but we managed a table, ordered, and were served within 15 minutes.    Everything (French Toast, Corned Beef Hash, and Sausage, Egg & Cheese Sandwich) were decent, solid breakfasts.  No complaints.    Service was as good as it could be given the cramped conditions.  Had to bring the bill to the cashier in the back for payment.  Unusual, but no big deal.   Aunt Judy's has its charm as a morning get together joint.  It is one of those places where who you know there is more important than what you eat.

The merger with Continental Airlines may have been good for United, but it has not been a blessing for its passengers. Where Continental offered excellent people up front and in the aisles, quality entertainment options with the self-programming movie and music system, and decent food on international flights, the "new and improved" version is anything but.  Gone are the useful menus; replaced by, "Chicken or fish," without further information.  Gone are the stopby's to see how you are doing.  Now, the flights are sterile.    It is obvious that problems with management are spilling into customer services. Even the introductory videos with Jeff Whomever seem bland and not designed to offer even a sincere gratitude for flying with them.  In fact, in the video on the plane to Beijing, he seemed gaunt and suffering a health problem.  Hope he hasn't been spending too much time inflight, because often after one of these 14 hour jobs, I feel just like he looks.

The best thing about this Starbucks on Main Street, Doylestown, is the front elevation from the street. It occupies a historic building that dominates a key intersection in the Borough.  Very attractive.   Sadly, that is where the positives end.  Inside, the layout is dreary. Dark on the brightest days, it feels like a morose ghost inhabits it, making for a sense of weariness. The coffee at all Star$$$ is universally bad, and it is no different here. It forces you to upgrade to an expensive alternative to regular coffee, a perverse upsell that seems to work everywhere. The pleasantness of the staff is helpful, but cannot overcome the down energy that is ever present.   Many better choices in town, perhaps why the shop was not overly busy while life on the streets around it was jumping.

My first visit to any Home Goods occurred yesterday when returning a gift.  After securing the store credit I walked around the space to see if I could find something of equal value while there to avoid the need for a return visit.   I couldn't, and walking around this downscale sibling of TJ Maxx was actually rather depressing.  Lots of junque. No real value.   Big brother has more useful things.  Luckily the store credit extends to all members of this retail family.
Still a great morning wake up! Strong java. Well made breakfasts. Friendly, homey, service.
Very sad to learn that Hogeland's has closed its doors for the last time.  Its food, and the warm community atmosphere it created, will be sorely missed.

TWO SLICE REVIEW   Average pizza from this small shop in a rundown commercial 3 store strip on Pennington Road, Ewing, NJ.    The crusts are thin enough, and the red sauce has a mildly salty taste on the regular pie and a basil-sweet flavor on the other one I tried, that looks something like a tomato pie. Both held up their points when picked up from the exposed crust, but both also had oil drip and a somewhat soft slice center despite asking for the reheat to be well done.   They private label their soda, and I liked the pineapple pop.    There are three tables in house, so this is primarily a takeout joint.  However, reading the complaints from customers waiting for delivery, going there to eat their stuff seemed the better course.    It was just okay. Nothing more.

Piccolo Trattoria is a local success story, and it is well deserved.  Its growth to 3 shops is testament to the hard work and persistence of its creator.  While I have only frequented the Newtown location, I hear great things about Flowers Mill and Pennington.    Take out pizza is an almost weekly order for us.  Friday or Saturday night would not be complete with a regular or Brooklyn Pie and a Spring Mix Salad.  The kitchen is a factory operation which you can watch as you wait at the register to pick up your food.  It is a beehive.   The pizza is very good and the Brooklyn Pie an excellent version of Sicilian with semi-sweet sauce, basil leaves, and copious mozzarella.  The Spring Mix is loaded with Green Apple slices, Walnuts, Feta, and first class Balsamic. The times I have eaten in house, everything has been well presented, tasty, and in abundance.  Most of the menu is traditional Italian American fare, so if you have a more adventurous palate, you may want to try Vecchia Osteria., or travel a bit farther afield to Philly or NYC.   Otherwise, you can't go wrong with Piccolo.

Way down Rt.13 in Croydon, PA, lies a new casa Mexicana run by a young entrepreneurial college student. Although bare boned at present, the large dining room, with colorful mural and carved/painted tables & chairs, already has a kitchen turning out authentic south of the border cuisine.   Last night I enjoyed an order of tacos dorado - chicken and cheese stuffed /rolled flautas (flutes), chips and salsa and tamarindo drink for less than $10. The roll ups were hot and crunchy with a top load of shredded lettuce, tomato and fresh crema dressing. I poured on the salsa from the table munchies to turn up the heat. Enjoyed it very much. The drink was tasty and sweet (perhaps, too much so), but refreshing and an effective counterpoint to the chili burn.   Service was friendly, informative and provided by the owner of the enterprise. Her pride and smooth effort was visible and a pleasure to behold.   Will be back to see what she does with the place.

A good bagel if you like the dense variety with plenty a texture and chew.   Mine was certainly fresh that morning, with those super sized onion flakes sticking resolutely to its top, and big enough to retain some moisture within and provide more flavor than the smaller chips that crunch well but fall off too easily. This was my maiden voyage to Bagelocity/Soup King, although I had liked its name since driving by the store in a strip center on Bensalem Road a few years ago.   I went with my favorite combination breakfast bagel sandwich with butter and swiss (love the interplay of nutty swiss cheese and those onion flakes on my tongue). With coffee the price was under $4, compared to a couple of bucks more for the same thing at my local place in Yardley.   The shop has been around for a while, but is still comfortable and clean. The staff I dealt with were friendly and brought the bagel to my booth when ready. Although I prefer a lighter, more airy, less kneaded round, I would certainly return to Bagelocity, especially to check out their soups and try a few more bagels.

China Dragon on Jacksonville Road, Ivyland, PA, is a fairly standard Chinese American house wokking dishes for the American palate. Their menu reflects it is from the same cooking school as every other such restaurant around the USA. The space offers a few tables for eating in, but the majority of their business appears to be takeout. They also offer sushi, Japanese and Thai platters, but I would be cautious going there if you have much appreciation for real food from those countries.   I found that the egg foo young I ordered was actually pretty good compared to many others I have tried.  The two pancakes were flash fried in the wok steel, so that the outside was light and crisp, while the inside was soft, pliant and tasty.  The ubiquitous brown sauce was made to order, and was smooth, without lumpy flour balls. The fried rice on the other hand, was mass produced at an earlier time, and tasted it. Its texture was a bit dried out, and was dyed by the food coloring in the bouillon used to cook the rice.   The net of it all was a three star moment.

Step into history with a visit to Newtown Hardware House.  This impeccably maintained old fashioned hardware store is a museum of Americana in screws, nails, tools, plumbing, electrical supplies, and even Flexible Flyer sleds and snow shovels.   The amazing and virtuous Dave C., the owner of the NHH for many years recently sold it to a local family to keep the operation open, so head in to buy the light bulbs and faucets you need for your fix-it projects.  Bring your kids so they can experience a slice of America that is almost extinct. While in the area, visit the other shops on State Street to support the community and the businesses that keep Newtown, Newtown.

After three visits Pho & Café Viet Huong gives the impression of being a Vietnamese diner.  A broad menu and very reasonable prices, but nothing all that impressive coming from the kitchen.   Last night I tried the Chicken with Rice in Lemongrass Sauce.  It was described as being spicy, but wasn't.  The Chicken was overcooked and dry, and the Lemongrass flavor weak.  The only veggies were Green Peppers and Onions cut large.  The Rice was fine, but I did not use much for sopping up the sauce as it was just not worth the calories.    In the recent past, I have tried the Pho.  It was adequate, but not the rich broth and ample meat and noodles that can be had right next door or across the parking lot.  Too, the smoothies and bubble teas are not all made with fresh fruit, but come from a can.  They are cool and sweet, but don't taste lively.    Lastly, the Vietnamese Coffee (hot) was pretty good.    This is really a place to come if you want a filling meal that doesn't break the bank. Still, the word that keeps flashing for me is, "Uninspiring."

Wang's Garden in the Village Shires Shopping Center off Buck Road in Holland, PA, is a family run Chinese/American house that has been wokking and rolling menu standards for a generation at this location. Mama runs the front of the shop, while dad is master chef. Prices are on the lower end of reasonable, reflecting the rent paid over the years.   My roast pork egg foo young was two smallish pancakes, full of pork and veggies and melded together with two eggs.  The brown sauce seemed fresh, and the accompanying fried rice was also above average, with plenty of pork, peas, shoots and more egg. A pretty decent lunch platter. The weak link was the hot & sour soup, which lacked fresh mushrooms,  had little tofu, and was dominated by its vinegar. It seemed past its prime.    Service was friendly and accommodating. They offer hot tea at no extra charge, which was appreciated.

If you are fortunate enough to remember when drug stores were primarily pharmacies where the expertise of the pharmacist and the family doctor were responsible for the health of the community, then you can appreciate Bear Apothecary in Lambertville, NJ.   Walking in is a step back in time, but where it matters - customer/medicine accountability - it is completely up to date. Mort wears the long white coat from 1960, signifying his deep roots in patient care and his long distance perspective on the evolution of drugs and illness. The generations of families that have relied on that knowledge testify to the commitment made by the owners since its founding.   True, Bear is not a contemporary super-pharmacy, but, isn't that a good thing? I really don't care if I can buy snacks, drinks or books when I need a prescription filled for my kid. Knowing that the pharmacist has seen it all before, and staked his career on the wellness of my community is paramount. Such knowledge (and wisdom) cannot be duplicated.

It was a cold, windy, city morn when we reached Washington Avenue, and I still hadn't had my first cup of java. I was trying to maintain my good mood, but it would be a losing battle without some caffeine soon.   Desperate times called for desperate measures.   I remembered there was this Bambu shop nearby, so I Yelped it and realized it was right across 6th Street from where we were. We walked over and found it in the inner corner of the shopping center. It was a small shop, with short red sofa, three cafe tables, and a few chairs along the window. The walls were covered in menus and photos of their signature Che fruity concoctions.   Colorful, but I needed something stronger and hotter. Farther down the drinks list was the coffee. I asked for Vietnamese coffee, hot. I normally drink it in VN cafes or after meals, so this was my first takeout.   It was exactly as expected. Strong, hot and sweetened by condensed milk. I missed the whole drip experience but it was great to be able to shop the market with java in hand.

Can't say that a woman's accessories boutique is a subject in my wheelhouse, but I know an attractive shop when I see one. More to the point, when they are having a sale on handbags and I can stock up for Valentine's Day on leather I think she will like, it is a very good day.   Lou Lou Boutique has shelves of sacks and over the shoulder book pockets, not to mention, costume jewelry and a few clothing racks, that make browsing an enjoyable indulgence.
