This may be primarily a take out joint, but the large dining area belays that, and a few of the other reviews reflect dining in experiences.    My light bite dinner of Wonton Soup (I ordered Hot & Sour Soup, but what the hey...?!), and Fried Dumplings was average.  Chicken Broth with standard yellow dye, thick wonton skins and a meat filling that was lacking taste.  Same for the Dumplings, with the exception of the dipping sauce which I doctored with chili sauce requested for flavor.    East China feels and looks rundown and in need of a bright facelift.  The owners seem content to do the minimum required to keep the doors open without real concern for customer satisfaction nor comfort.    There are better Chinese/American houses nearby more deserving of your appetite.

Cool Blue.  Overhead river meandering.  Clear Mushroom Soup clarifying.   Captain Roll (Spicy Crunchy Tuna, Crabmeat, Salmon, Eel & Avocado) drizzled with Chef's Special Sauce), visual, tasty pleasure.   Hot and grainy Green Tea.   Great way to reach the end of the day.

Three generations of donuts have been baked and served from this Colmar, Pa. location.  It isn't an accident that they are considered among the best sweet rounders in this quadrant of the Universe.  And, now that the Great Pumpkin has arrived, Yum Yum is baking its amazing orange squash variant in many forms.  They are all great!  While we went in just for a small sample with coffee, the counterperson advised us that buying 6 would cost the same as 5, we were easily persuaded to go with the half doz and bring home whatever we didn't consume on premises.  A couple of Pumpkin Sugar Cinnamons, a pair of classic Glazed, and a deuce of Honey Dipped, and a coupla small Joes, and we retreated to a corner table to dive in.    Each was excellent, but the Pumpkin stood out as large, authentically pumpkin tasting, and cake style.  Fresh and delicious.  The Glazed and Honey Dipped were less distinguishable from the competition, but still a sweet sticky mess.    These guys do donuts right!  How many made it home?  Just two survived the initial onslaught.

Man, has Mill Street come back to life!  I had not been down by the Delaware River for several years and was very pleasantly surprised by the return of vibrancy around there.  Kelch House was recommended by a local businessman we were visiting, and he was right on with his suggestion. The five of us had a variety of things on the menu, and all of us were happy with our choices.   I had the Apple and Feta Salad, consisting of Granny Smith slices, Romaine, Candied Walnuts, and a good amount of fresh Feta Cheese.  The Balsamic was a nice taste to wrap it all together. A good meal @ $9.  Looking at my mates I observed various stages of gluttony displayed over a Cheesesteak and French Onion Soup.  Someone mentioned the Fries were excellent.     The facility is dressed in colonial attire, with large windows bringing in wonderful light. The view of the river from our table was great on this autumn day.   Definitely worth a special visit to return to both Kelch House and Bristol.   Well done, City!

All malls are dinosaurs waiting for extinction.   Neshaminy is no different.  Aside from the entertainment value of the AMC theaters, there is little to recommend it.  After ruining Main Streets around the world with large parking fields and lots of meaningless choices, they are now suffering the same fate.   People are "Malled Out!"   We want something more integrated into our communities; part of our social fabric, not something standing alone and uninvolved.  The next generation will be synthetic villages.  Smaller shopping markets clustered together and surrounded by neighborhoods, schools, parks, hospitals,  employment opportunities, and good roads leading to the rebirthed urban centers.  It is called by many names, New Urbanism, Post-Modern Cities, Back to the Future, etc. But, it is definitely coming.   There are examples of this next utopian model around the world, and if you find one be sure to investigate.    I, for one, am excited for the chance to return to a future full of the elements that made earlier societies function efficiently, while adapting the best that technology and science have to offer.
The outpatient radiology department works well.  Can't speak to other departments or services, but there is no problem going to St. Mary for xrays, catscans, petscans or MRIs as an outpatient.

This is one of the new versions of the old theme that is Dunkin Donuts.  The space is larger, brighter, cleaner than most of its siblings, with one end of the shop furnished with easy chairs and small tables to encourage hanging out.    The coffee is average DD brew. The staff is efficient. The baked goods looked all shiny and glazed, but I did not try one this visit.    Maybe next time.

When it comes to coffee there are three main ingredients: 1. the coffee, 2. the water, and 3. the maker. At Dunkin Donuts the constant is the coffee.  The makers are all trained in the same methods and everything comes packaged for ease of use.  That makes the quality of the water the primary variable.  For some reason, the coffee at this DD tastes different (in a bad way). It is harsh and leaves a bitter aftertaste.  It must be the water, because the nearest other DD in Lower Makefield near the Hampton Inn does not have this problem, but they are serviced by a different water company. Elementary, my dear Watson...

Only in America!  Here we have a "New York Bagel" shop run by Arabic speaking guys, who seem to know how to "make the donuts..."   I was impressed.    The crew of Ewing's Finest who were there ahead of me seemed to know a good morning stop.  I felt incredibly safe.  But, the parking lot was like a DMZ.

Tan May Chinese Restaurant sits in the Shop Rite center just off Pennington Road in Ewing, NJ. While primarily a take out joint, there are six tables for sitting in, and for the owner's kids to hang out on during summer vacation. Nice to see the family together.  My lunch special was actually better than expected. The egg Foo Young was made with fresh ingredients and the ubiquitous brown sauce lighter and more flavorful than in most chop shops. Even the fried rice, though that prefab yellow cast, was at least tender and full of finely cut veggies.  Prices were ridiculously low (under $7), and there was a choice of soup, egg roll or bottled drink included. No extra charge for my Snapple.  While the place could be cleaner, and the mess in the hallway leading to the restroom organized and stored out of sight, the food makes it worthy of regular, if infrequent, visits.

As the nearest pizza joint to my office, I really have not taken advantage of its prime location. After trying Jeppy's Brooklyn Pie that oversight will soon be corrected.   Today I dealt with the man himself. Affable to the nines. He recommended slices of the 'Brooklyn' sitting in display.  Agreeing, he hand selected the best two available and put them in the oven to reheat.  The mozza was homemade, and tasted it. Mildly salty and soft. The crust, airy and cracker firm and crisp. Really superior work.   This shop is in the first floor of a converted residence with apartment above. The restroom is back in the kitchen, requiring an escort. The WC itself is unusual, in that it shows its previous adaption for family living with full shower.   Given the surprising quality of this pizza, it is definitely deserving of an upgrade to 4 Stars. That they forgot my drink keeps it from attaining top rank.

Called ahead to pick up a large pie for dinner. Half plain. Half sausage. This was my first visit to Red Star Pizza 3, and my impression was that it was attractive inside, with room to sit for dinner, and had a friendly efficient staff. The pizza was ready when I arrived, and I was back on the road in under five minutes.   Opening the box in my kitchen, it looked good and had a nice aroma. Pizza is always best eaten straight from the oven, and this one confirmed that axiom. Both slices had the right combo of sauce and cheese, but having cooled for a while, the crust was now weak and could not hold the topside weight. Still, the taste was there. The sausage crumble was strong.   We had a decent dinner from Red Star, and will get back there to mange in house as soon as possible.

This is a mini-DD that shares the building with another business, yet it has a small outdoor seating area in front of the shop if you really feel like hanging out and smelling the exhaust of the cars parked right next to you.   The coffee is what most of us expect from this ever expanding franchise.  Average coffee whose main attraction is its basic consistency across the nation.    Service here is fast and efficient, if not overly friendly nor engaging.    It is amazing how different each DD "makes the donuts," however, I did not have any here and cannot speak to their taste and quality.

International House of Pancakes (or burgers if you follow their latest campaign) is nothing if not consistent with their primary menu. The pancakes are good wherever you find the IHOP sign, the coffee always hot and served with a pitcher for refills. Breakfast is breakfast across their wide spread enterprise.   We stopped in after an appointment to grab a morning bite. The store was large and divided into sections. We were seated in the back room and approached by our server in less than a minute.   Coffee, please. And, that spicy omelet with avocado on top, while you're at it. Extra plate for sharing, too. Easily done. It arrived with second plate in a few minutes. Surprisingly good, especially the unexpected BBQ brisket sticking out both ends that added a savory chew to the otherwise soft melty dish. The three pancake side was more than enough to split after spreading on butter and a combination of table syrups. Glad we had only one platter, because we were challenged finishing it.   IHOP is an easy choice if a decent American breakfast is what you want. The jury is still out on the burgers.

Wish I didn't have to return to DP Auto Body less than a year since my previous visit, but as luck would have it, I had another rear ender.  Ugh!   Dave Miller has a great way with people.  He is able to make an unpleasant experience as comfortable as possible by his friendly demeanor, clear explanations, excellent shop, and fair prices.    And, yes.  If I need more work done in the future, I would return without hesitation.

Over the years, this basement emporium has become my last resort for ingredients that just can't be found anywhere else in the City.  That special vinegar for dumplings, the fried chili in oil with black beans, and the narrow gauge rolling pin for making dumpling skins from scratch, all reside in Asia Supermarket.  But, you might need help finding all of them from the amazing employees who have the entire layout memorized.    Speaking Mandarin or Cantonese helps, but with a smile and small kowtow, they switch to English and will even guide you to where these treasures are found.

This is the most beautiful and serene space for foot massage I have experienced in the USA. The décor is cool and quiet, despite it being a simple large space without inner separating walls. 20 large reclining chairs in 3 rows.  All visible, yet private. Choice of herbal bath for your feet to soak in, while 20 minutes is spent on solid upper body massage.   Very restful, except when my foot master dug deep into certain points and looked to see my reaction. He knew the meridians, and was able to push chi.  Green tea leaves sink to the bottom of my cup as I slip away.

For some reason, I was sitting in this DD trying to check in on my mobile phone, and was told I was too far away!  I guess that depends on what dimension of reality you are measuring from. Or maybe, this is in one of those GPS warps, where the directions get lost due to cosmic interference.   Otherwise, nothing special going on here. The coffee is only Okay (bad water?), but I have noticed a deterioration of DD coffee quality at many shops over the past few years. They really need to standardize the water variable, because without good water, the coffee beans can do little.   My son's basketball team was celebrating the end of their season here last night. The boys seemed happy with the Baskin Robbins, but I saw a dish of strawberry ice cream that was so red, I wondered what red dye farm it had visited before being consumed.   Loved the company, but will live without their goods in the future.

While I wouldn't wager on the last time the Department of Licenses and Inspections walked down the stairs into Asia Supermarket, I might take your bet that we could find a completely esoteric noodle sauce, cookie, or tea previously believed to be extinct anywhere outside of China.  This place seems to have all that stuff, and more. The prices are cheap, the aisles narrow, and the shopping carts from a bygone era.    Still, if it is something you remember eating back home, or a cooking utensil unavailable in Sears, this is the place you may find it.  Go for that reason, or for the great sense of nostalgia emanating from every shelf and refrigeration unit.    It is not every day that you can be both a consumer and an anthropologist at the same moment.  The museum-like quality of some of the dark corners makes this a multi-dimensional experience. Stock up on your packaged, canned and bottled goods at good prices as you explore its inner recesses.   Don't forget to come up for air.

Excellent burgers on South 5th Street, just where Passyunk intersects with the 5. Design your own using the three computer stations, or go to the counter to talk with the people working there. Either way you get a standard double patty complemented any way you choose. If you don't want to think that much about it, the menu offers several great combinations that are bound to make you happy.   Just the right amount of grease, potato or pretzel roll, natural sugar carbonated beverages, Bassett ice cream based shakes, and fresh fruit smoothies, all surround the ultimate comfort food for your indulgence.   Prices that won't break the bank just off the hippest street in town.   If there is something to improve upon, it is that it appears that every burger is finished to well done regardless of how you request it. Still, they are so juicy I almost didn't notice.

When my HVAC system died last year, I called around for estimates to replace the 25 year old dinosaur with a more state of the art apparatus. Not only was Christian less expensive for equivalent mechanicals, but they did not attempt to oversell me on a product that my home really could not benefit from, regardless of rebates or government programs.  Much appreciated.  They got the job done in one day, were neat and quiet, and gave me both a coupon for an additional discount and my first tune-up as part of the deal.  One year financing without interest was also a nice touch.    With all the heat and humidity this summer, I think of them almost daily as I cool down in my favorite chair with a tall glass of lemonade.    Thanks, Christian HVAC!

After exploring the canyons of The Home Depot, we walked out into the cold dark gray sky. We were a little hungry after all the hiking and saw this Burger King on the edge of this shopping zone on Bromley Road.   The store was nearly empty @ 3:00, and there was no wait to order. Whopper meal and a double cheeseburger from the value menu. Easy. Right? Except, our order taker thought we wanted a second meal when we only wanted the sandwich along with the Whopper meal. Small miscommunication that was fixed with managerial assistance after the register froze.   The burgers were typical of BK cuisine. Adequate fast food. The Freestyle sodie dispenser was still fun. So many choices at my fingertips. Absent were any condiments on this side of the counter. No ketchup pump. No salt or pepper. No plastic utensils. I'm sure they had their reasons.   This experience wouldn't have been particularly notable if I hadn't been to another BK two weeks before in Pa (Oxford Valley), where we were literally treated like fast-food royalty, in a shop that even has a fireplace lounge, and a real personal touch.  Spoiled us for future BK visits.

This is a review of Plain Pizza Slices served at lunch.  While the reheat did a good job firming/crisping the crust so that the point held up and provided a firm bite, the remainder of the experience was somewhat of a letdown.  The sauce was on the salty side, while I prefer a sweeter, more basil flavor tone.  The cheese was ample, but without much taste to contribute to overall dining pleasure.    Two slices and a soft drink came in under $7.00, but the same can be had a several other places for at least a buck less.   Reviews say that their cheesesteak is the way to go at Venezia, but when the standard tomato pie is so ordinary and uninspired, I would not elect to return to give something else a try.  There are too many better choices in the vicinity.   Venezia does not make the cut for a quality pizza slice.

MEETING ROOM SERVICES ONLY  We held a fundraiser in the Pheasant Room last night for about 70 people.  We provided all the food and drink, but the hotel management provided set up/clean up, ice and ice containers, and a "Can Do" attitude for all our requests. They were helpful, friendly and made sound suggestions.  They also assisted with creating the sound stage for our musical entertainment.   All for a very reasonable price.   As a result, the event was a smashing success.  Everyone was happy and well fed, even when during speech time when all the local pols made their pitches to Get Out the Vote. No one left early, and many remained to listen to our local musicians make merriment.   Homewood Suites is definitely a place to consider for your next meeting or event. The only downside is that it lacks a kitchen for serious catering, but once there you can have fun and even spend the night.

The choice was between Jack & Jill hard ice cream and vanilla/chocolate/orange soft serve. I went with a cup of orange vanilla swirl in styro. While waiting at the window of this renovated former fast food shell, I watched all the families sitting around enjoying a cool moment on a humid sticky evening in June.   I was more in the mood to drive home and spoon the melting combo in air conditioned comfort. Besides, I prefer drinking this elixer to licking it. I sampled it at red lights along the way.   Have to admit to being disappointed. The vanilla had little flavor and the orange while tasty, was also grainy like the orange powder had not been mixed enough to reach the smooth silkiness desired for soft serve.   There are many choices for ice cream in this part of the world, so I hope this was just a glitch in a normally high quality operation.

This Dunkin is located at the intersection of Parkway Avenue and Pennington Road in Trenton, NJ.  It is fairly new and is well maintained.  There is a drive thru option. Plenty of parking if you want to go inside.   I walked in after lunch to grab an afternoon wakemeup.  The woman behind the counter was friendly and efficient. They had a surprisingly full rack of donut and muffin options for the time of day.  A few customers sat at one of the tables discussing business. Overall, the place was attractive, with everyone doing their job professionally.    The coffee was what you expect from this franchise.  Consistent. Strong. Not overly acidic. Not particularly flavorful. Fully capable of keeping me awake for my afternoon surge toward the five o'clock world.    Right down the middle.

Ten of us showed up at Ocean Harbor late Saturday morning for dim sum. Perhaps because it was mid-August, street parking was available on Race Street, so we only had to walk a block to reach this large, bright yellow painted, high ceilinged, dining hall. Had this been a wedding, we would have been the guests of honor, because we were seated up on the stage at the rear of the room.   Wish I knew the names of everything we sampled, but it came at us so fast and furious, with multiple carts constantly dropping off dishes, that I barely had time to photograph them before they were snapped up by our crew's chopsticks. Regardless, everything was surprisingly good.   No problem with service, either. The size of our group provided all the incentive necessary to get us plenty of attention.  That most of our party spoke Mandarin probably didn't hurt.   All we ate and drank came to $100. Great deal for the quantity and quality of food consumed.   We agreed that coming back again was very likely.

Not much here unless you have a seat at one of the four tables on the patio or on the Septa train coming down the tracks. With a beautiful Saturday afternoon bringing out bikers from the nearby trail to rest and recharge, all the seats were occupied, so we could only take our latte and pour over back to the car and keep going.   No doubt an interesting use of the backroom of the bicycle shop and an attractive old stone building. The lone barista was kept busy and did a good job. Bakery products were almost exhausted. Coffee okay.   We had a nice drive home through a part of Conshohockon we had not seen before, but Riverbend is not a great place for a coffee stop under these circumstances.   The Cafe is a takeout shop right now with potential to be a lot more.

Still a fine place for lunch, particularly on an early Spring day when a walk from the office is a perfect respite from the workload of the moment.   On such days, and many others, Becky's is a fine destination for a fresh and tasty meal.

Admittedly, being objective about funeral homes is a bridge too far.    When a good friend departed this mortal coil a few days ago at an age too young, it was just a matter of hours before his family arranged for his "launch" to take place here.  One door closes. Another opens. The soft breeze in the trees is the soul waving goodbye.   The chapel was no different than any contemporary synagogue.  It was quietly dignified and naturally had us reflecting on the passing of one life to the next dimension, and our own frail mortality.    Lots of oak. Family reading poems. Rabbinic eulogy spoken personally from the memories of family and friends.    The Mourner's Kaddish. A prayer for the living. Of the greatness of the knowing Breath. For Peace. That despite profound loss, the One is to be praised.   "... and the world will carry on..."

We had a very good dinner here last week while in town for haircut and walkabout.   The floor plan is spacious, with bamboo and other strong Asian cues.  The staff was friendly and able to answer a few of my more technical questions about the dishes.  The insights provided led me to try the Hue Style Noodle Soup.  Turns out, this potage uses Egg Noodles rather than rice, and has a red cast due to the ground up Spicy Red Peppers and Hoisin mixed into the Beef Broth.  Otherwise, the same Sprouts, Thai Basil, Jalapeno Slices, and Lime Wedges were available as desired. The taste slides up the heat scale and adds another dimension to the otherwise wonderful flavors of the traditional Pho.  A lot of sliced Steak in there, too.  Very satisfying.   The Shrimp & Pork Roll app was fresh and delish with a sweet peanut sauce for dipping.   Will definitely return to try more of the menu.  Very enjoyable experience at Vietnam Palace.

COFFEE STOP REVIEW:  When the sign on the door of the nearby bagel shop said it was closed permanently, I looked for an alternative source for the caffeine fix I needed to account for my earlier than normal awakening to attend to a court matter in Mt. Holly, NJ. Luckily for me there was a Wawa right down the road.   It was an old version convenience store, sans gas pumps and large food preparation area. Still, it had 6 types of java and a fixings island. All this boy needed. The Guatemalan medium roast caught my attention, and I poured it into a 16 oz container with a milk lightener to taste.   I pulled in the first sip as I settled back in my car. Hot, strong and pleasantly robust, it was just what the doctor ordered. Had me humming and beating my fingers on the wheel in minutes. When I walked into the judge's Chambers I was fully equipped to handle whatever my adversary threw my way.

Take out only Chinese American shop on Lincoln Highway (Rt. 1), Levittown, PA. All the usual suspects, including General Tso's Chicken, my choice. The place needs a thorough cleaning, especially around the floor to near ceiling stack of soda cases around the cooler.   My combo included a heavy load of fried rice dyed dark brown from the bouillion in which it was cooked,  and a smallish egg roll that while crisp was 95% cabbage. The actual chicken was pretty good with the extra heat from a few Szechuan chilies I requested. The portion was impressive. I couldn't finish all that was stuffed into the plastic container.   Overall, if the main course is what matters most, 21 Chinese Kitchen did chicken well, with  respectable sauce. The rest of the meal was mostly empty filler, not worth consuming. If you figure out how to get just what you want without the other stuff, a satisfying meal is within your grasp.

Pop's Bagels sits in the shadow of Johnny Apple's in Holland, PA. It is a small shop with a few tables, counter and bagel bins along the walls. It is bright white, and on a sunny late September morning the room was very inviting. The folks working there were nearly as bright and cheerful. I ordered my customary onion bagel with butter and swiss, not toasted, and retreated to the side of the room to wait and watch.   Families came in for bags of rounders, and a few occupied the tables available. My coffee and bagel were called, and I grabbed and walked out again into the morning light. The parking lot is far larger than the store so there is never a shortage of spaces.   The bagel was fresh and pliant, with a mix of both savory (onion) and sweet (dough) flavors. The crust lacked any crispness and I couldn't differentiate between the skin and inner texture. Too, the meat of the bagel although light and chewy, lacked the air pockets found in traditional ones. Perhaps, more boiling or lye exposure would create that texture.   Many people prefer this style bagel, but it is not my desired finish.

Typical Chinese kitchen in DeKalb Pike, Blue Bell, PA. All the usual menu suspects with long lunch specials list @$6.95, with rice, broccoli and soft drink. Soup and egg roll not included.   My General Tso's Chicken was served in house in a takeout container and flimsy white plastic fork. The flavor of the sauce had a little heat, but was otherwise unremarkable. Same for the fried rice and the florets. The only thing that stood out from the other Chinois/American hybrid houses was the outward charm and warm interaction provided by the friendly and solicitous owner, who was very happy to meet a new customer.   Decent takeout place, but not beyond the mean of all such restaurants. Good for a fast and cheap lunch. They had a stream of people coming in for pickup while I was there, most of whom seemed to have been there before.   Doubtful I will ever be in that group.

The first review did not take into account the real centrum of Isaac's - its beer.   As my awareness and taste for craft brews evolve I am developing a richer appreciation for Isaac's Bar and Newton's Natural Laws.  I have returned often enough to realize I have become a fan.    The choices are extensive and the additions well conceived.    4 Stars for what there is.  5 Stars for what it could become.  UPDATE: December 23, 3016 - Full House this Friday night before Christmas. 30 minute wait for a table not unreasonable. Nice booth for 6 upstairs. Service good given the crowd. Mad Elf in the house.  But, my Pickleback Burger arrived feeling neglected in the kitchen. More well done than the requested medium, and the deep fried Jamison pickles very dark brown and really burnt beyond enjoyable. Burger crumbled when forked, rather than holding firm as a never frozen puck would do. Disappointing effort by the no doubt busy grillmaster.

I guess you have to possess fond memories of Pollo Campero from your childhood or hometown to fully appreciate the specialness of this place.  It is a bright and happy place, and the food gets to your table quickly with a smiling face attached.  But, after taking a big bite out of their famous Chicken the party comes to an end rather quickly.   True, the chicken is fresh and juicy, and has a citrus and chili flavor going on to tickle the taste buds.  But, after that the experience is rather flat.  The side dishes are ordinary (beans, coleslaw, taters, etc.), and the drinks are generic except for the Horacha, which was too sweet and tasted like it was from a mix.   As fast chicken goes, this is a reasonable alternative to the Colonel or Popeye's, but not as good as a Bojangles or Cluck-U. There are other Guatemalan restaurants in Trenton that make great fried chicken in a much more unique and pleasant atmosphere.  If you have the time and sense of adventure, you should try them and compare.

I haven't updated this review since Dragon of Newtown moved to Swamp Road a few years ago.  The menu hasn't changed much, but the size of the restaurant has shrunk to fit in an appropriately smaller space retained from the years as Meglio's. It appears better organized and more tidy than before. Service remains friendly and attentive, and Philomena is still the empress overseeing the operation.   Although I am occasional there for dinner, lunch is my regular beat. Their combination specials are a few bucks higher than other Chinese houses, but by comparison the quality is higher than most. The wonton soup has a pleasant consomme base stock and the wontons are thin skinned and stuffed with a good ground pork filling. I normally request Orange Beef (fried rice, broccoli, comes with). The sauce is tart with slivers of orange peel, and appears to be made to order, rather than the time stamped heavy gloop offered elsewhere. Decent tea flows freely.   For a local dine in/take out, Dragon is a way better than average option among Chinese American kitchens. They are really making an effort to appeal to the pallette as well as the wallet.

Coming back to Einstein after a hiatus of more than six months, it was shocking to see the changed conditions all around the shop. I never had strong attraction to their bagels, but the convenience and decent coffee was a sufficient draw to get me there sometimes.  This visit, while the staff was still friendly and helpful, it was impossible not to notice the amount of dirt all around.  The floors, counters, refrigerator, coffee urns, etc., all seemed to have been neglected.  I happened to see the back of a coffee sign sitting on the coffee counter, and it had not been cleaned in a long time.   These are signs of lax oversight and poor training. Either corrective steps are taken soon, or this EBB will slide into oblivion.   A downgrade is inevitable.  We have all experienced better than this.

For a state agency that deals heavily with the public, this PennDot Licensing and Photo Center does a pretty good job. It is certainly less crowded than the closest alternative in Bensalem, and the entire vibe ( such as it is), more relaxed.  We were in and out with a driver's test in under and hour, with time to go across the street to Ben & Irv's for breakfast. Sadly, the young man has to return to show more competence in parallel parking, but that gives us another opportunity for a good meal nearby.

Two Slices and a Drink review only.   I came in around 3 on Sunday afternoon and asked for their 2 slices and a drink special, which is listed on the board for $4.99.  I requested the plain pizza I saw sitting in the display be served, "well done," so that it was heated enough to remelt the cheese and bring them back to life.    The pizza arrived hot enough, but also clearly past its prime.  Although the underside was firm and held its load well, it was approaching staleness. There should be a time limit for how long a pie can sit around before it is disposed of and replaced for the next customer.  Too, I am not fond of having my fingers burned from the hot oil dripping out the back of the slice when I fold it over in order to gain a stronger grasp.    Finally, I was charged $6 and change for the snack, clearly above the listed price.  Perhaps, I was there too late, or it was not available on weekends.  The sign should have so stated if that was so.    Clean shop. But, I have experienced better pizza by the slice.

Where else but Philly can you find an authentic cheesesteak right down to the greasy last bite....in the airport? Eat at Joe's is that place in Terminal B. By the way, that isn't just the name of the joint, it's an order!

How many people love their jobs so much that they willingly pose for a Yelp photo without being asked twice?  Not so many.  But, at this Philly Soft Pretzel Factory, not only are the pretzels bagged while hot, but the workers there genuinely smile and have fun taking care of you.    We picked up 10 standard sized bowties, although we had the choice of minis, and singular chubby nubs.  During our interaction, they described how to use them as sandwich ends by slicing and even grilling before loading with our favorite contents.  Never thought to use them at home that way, but liked the idea.    I never believed a one item business would be successful in the long run, but these folks have been ongoing for more than ten years.  That is a hell of a lot of pretzels.

Now, you've heard 'bout 5 Guys. Had grease from Robin and Chee B.  Maybe even a sloppy Bobby or DQ.  But, you've never had a burger Till you've heard Buddy play the blues...  Beef ground fresh daily. Hand cut fries. Homemade sauces. Martin's Potato Bun. And, all the toppings and combos you can imagine, and then some...  The messiest burger I have enjoyed in a long time. First bite, and half the load of onions, shrooms, cheddar and Swiss slid out the back door onto my fries. Made them even better.   The mix of A-1, garlic mayo and ketchup was all over my fingers and running down my chin.   6 napkin job.  If this isn't burger heaven, it is at least an outpost along the way.

I just needed a caffeine boost to make it back to Pennsy and saw this DD on Broad Street.  It was dark and a little difficult to see the driving lanes in the parking lot.  Next thing I knew I was in the drive thru lane and couldn't get out!   I reached the order speaker, but did not understand the Hindi dialect being spoken.  I waited until it changed to English and ordered coffee and a round sweet.  Easy so far.  Of course, when I finally opened up the bag when I was back on the street, I had not been given what I ordered.    Ate it anyway. Not bad.  But, it does prove a point - Sometimes, a drive thru will not do.  There are some things that must be seen before being ordered.  For all I know, they gave me what they thought I wanted. Or maybe, it was just fate that brought me a Sour Cream Donut rather than the Glazed requested.    These things were meant to be a mystery.

Eat at Joe's...if ya know what's gud fo' ya.  You can almost forget that this is PHL when you ask for a breakfast sandwich or cheesesteak.  You can hear the sizzle, and smell the hot grease.  When the cook opens the torpedo roll and turns it upside down onto the innards of your sandwich, rather than scooping it up with the spatula and slapping it onto the bread, you almost believe you are at you corner pizza shop waiting on Carmine to drop it the wrapping paper and roll it up with tape.   Alas, that dream fades with the next announcement that your flight is overbooked and they need volunteers...But, maybe it is worth delaying your flight so you can enjoy another Eat at Joe's special?

It looks like I waited too long to stop in to Cafe Ole. The signs on the front window indicate that the shop is closed and for sale.  If you know anyone interested in operating a "bistro" and cafe in wonderful downtown Trenton, have them check it out. Looks like I missed a cool place.

If I am here often enough to be a Duke, I must be a fan!  Too, this morning I had the Raspberry Stuffed French Toast blackboard special.  Two slices of well dipped bread sandwiching homemade creamy Cream Cheese stuffing, and topped with in house Raspberry reduction topping.    Sweeeet & Tarrrt!  Filling enough for two meals.   Best thing I've eaten at Squirrels Nest.

The day the Gap arrived in Newtown I knew we had arrived.  When it expanded from the original small store on State Street and moved to the Village of Newtown, I wondered if it was possible to have too much Gap?  Apparently not. Both the large Gap and the Gap Body are successful.   If you like Gap gear this is an easy place to shop. Plenty of space. Good workers. Enough parking. Several eateries nearby when you need a break.

Golden Dawn was a disappointment on several levels.   First, sitting at the end of the counter it took overly long for someone to slip me a menu and offer me a cup of coffee.  I understand busy, but there were several staff people just walking around with their heads down.  Second, the French Toast I ordered, while thick as advertised, had not soaked long enough in the egg mix, and the center of each slice was dry.  This made for a less than enjoyable experience.  Just glad I went with a short stack.    Third, although I sat at the counter for at least 30 minutes as I waited and ate, no one came by with a pot of coffee and offered to refill my mug.  Again, servers all around trying their best to avoid eye contact with everybody.  They succeeded in making me feel invisible.   And, in making me feel an unwanted customer.    Have it your way.   Without me.

This review is only for the meeting facilities and first floor offerings of the Holiday Inn Philadelphia Stadium.   I have been here a couple of times over the years for larger meetings where people were coming in from around the country or region.  While the building is dated and can use refurbishing in the lobby and meeting rooms, the overall plant still functions fairly well.  This is a mid-range hotel designed for sports oriented guests to enjoy the professional teams coming in to play our guys.  It is far from state of the art, but serves its purpose.  If you want high end there are other places available nearby, and even better ones downtown.    So, accept it for what it is - a heads on beds, one day meeting center, where comfort, cuisine and pampering are low priorities.  And, if you need to stay a night or two and don't want to wander far afield, this place will do nicely.    Don't forget that there are fun entertainment venues, and Tony Luke's only minutes away.  Just ask the front desk or the bellman for recommendations.  They know where the action is.

Very surprised that this Mickey D's does not show up on Yelp, although it has been open at this location for several years. It stands next door to the Broad Street Car Wash, so after a shine-on-line, I dropped in for a quickie before heading back to the office.   The shop is fairly small, but clean.  The counter staff was alert and efficient.  I tried a Double Jalapeno Burger on the Dollar Menu, and a Lemonade.    Surprisingly, the burger was decent (I know...compared to what?), with both sliced, pickled pepper and crispy, lightly dusted and fried bits of the hot green meanie.   It might be a few years before I hit another one of these places, but since the last time it was obvious they were trying to improve their offerings.    The $3.50 price for this small meal had me whistling a happy (meal) tune.

After trying the sushi, Yummy remains 3 Stars.    It is true as others say that the rolls are larger than in most fish houses.  By larger, I mean in circumference and in size of the component parts.  Yet, while the fish seemed fresh, they did not offer a pronounced flavor beyond the sauce that was drizzled on top and the Soy/Wasabi/Ginger accompaniments.    Too, the Wasabi was the mass produced green variety that most offer, and the Ginger was the artificially colored orange, rather than the actual white of natural Ginger.    It was adequate and fresh, but certainly far from best of breed that is available only a short distance away.    The family is very pleasant, and the hostess friendly and helpful. Her husband does the artistry, while the kids and grandmother sit nearby, making it feel somewhat like I was eating in their dining room.    Not bad, but not exceptional.  When convenience is the primary factor, it serves its purpose well.

It was very helpful to find a Mandarin speaking doctor in this part of Bucks County.  My Chinese guest's son was not feeling well and we needed medical attention from someone who could ask questions and understand his answers.  Dr. Ellen Kim was conscientious and made her patient feel at ease as she examined him and took notes on her laptop.  The blood work she ordered was appropriate and the results decisive in how to address the problem.    A big plus was the presence of Mercy Diagnostics in the same building.  They were able to take us promptly, draw the blood and get the results to Dr. Kim within a few days.   Visiting Wrightstown Family Medicine is also a worthwhile trip for the quality of the facility built to house them on Second Street Pike.  It is beautifully constructed and decorated to suggest an 18th Century farmhouse.    This medical practice and Dr. Kim are highly recommended.

Sub Maria's scores points just for its nameplay.    This now Korean deli is packed into a small corner storefront with floor to ceiling shelves and refrigeration that provide almost everything imaginable for a good Jersey lunch.  Superior loaves of fresh bread are the heart of any worthy sandwich, and Maria's uses an excellent bakery.  Light, mildly springy, just the right yeast aftertaste.  When loaded with well made Chicken Salad, Lettuce, Tomato and Sweet Pickled Peppers, it is a pleasure to indulge.   The back glass walled drink cases are full of the favorites, except for some of the more exotic international brands, like Jarritos.  But, you can't expect a joint this small to have everything.    The aisles inventory snacks and pre-packaged sweets to complete the meal.    Now, if they figured out a place to make fresh fruit smoothies, bubble teas, and real brownies, they would be a candidate for the Jersey Deli Hall of Fame.    As it is, Sub Maria's knows how to create an awesome Submaria...ine.   A little hard to find at the ass end of Nottingham Way, it is worth pulling out the GPS to enter this special emporium.    Parking lot out back.

Bonjour Creperie Café is on the first floor of an office building at 790 Township Line Road in Lower Makefield, Pa. It seems to have been open a very short time as it is still bright and shiny.  Even the crepe cooker looks brand new.    Jean Pierre is the owner and crepemaster in this maison.  He dresses the part well, with black striped pants and white chef's jacket.  Even his very authentic French accent adds to the genuineness of the experience.  He greeted me with, "Bonjour," and seemed happy to have a short exchange in Francaise.    My breakfast Crepe of Bacon and Gruyere, topped with a smoky Vinaigrette drizzle was very good, and the accompanying Java was also a superior blend.  There is much more on the lunch and dessert menus, but they must wait for another time, when I don't have to run off to the office.    I hope Bonjour Creperie Café does well at this location.  This office complex does not offer any alternatives, and it is nice to have a quality vendor close at hand for the folks who work here. There is also an outdoor area for good weather dining.

Apparently, Ginos was a Philly thing back in the day.  Now, its reincarnation attempts to recreate that experience for the 21st century burger palate.  Not having those memories, I am left to evaluate this Street Road stop in the present.   Burgers joints are going through a differentiation process.  The McD experience has evolved into a Red Robin/Cheeburger/Hooters high end burger place, and now, a middle rung on the ladder ala Five Guys/Nifty Fifty/Johnie Rockets.  Grease seems to be the special ingredient.  Not that I have anything against grease...it is the "secret sauce" of the burger biz.   Ginos falls into the space between McD and Five Guys.  It allows more self expression in what you want in the bun, and the fries are better than average.  The patty is free form and only 2 oz.  The bun is adequate and hold together better than the white bread variety found in many lesser establishments.  Whether you like this semi-customized approach comes down to whether you can accept that grease adds flavor and texture to the dining experience.  I think it does.  That, and some friendly service, brings me back for lunch when I am in the area.

I guess I'm not a Red Carpet kind of guy because unless it is very early or very late, I prefer just to sit with everyone else, plug in and drift away.  However, on those other occasions when travel and torture seem to become confused, even a less than optimal airport "club" can be the difference between tolerable abuse and downright grouchiness.    A free drink (or two), a passable snack, and a comfortable chair, can feel like an oasis in the desert.  Although PHL's United lounge is subpar, it can still save the day.  The staff overcompensates because they know what we are all dealing with.    Just wish they brought it some genuine cheesesteaks and Yingling to remind us of what can be so redeeming about Philly.

The return visit was even better than the first.  The Pho Tam Nam Gan, was absolutely crammed with thin sliced Roundeye Steak, Well Done Brisket and Soft Tendon, in addition to the nest of thin noodles, slivers of Onion and Scallion, plus the optional Sprouts, Thai Basil, Jalapeno and Fresh Squeezed Lime.  It was impossible to push down the flat bottom spoon to slurp the beef broth without causing spillage over the rim of the bowl.    Hot. Steamy. Meaty. Delicious.   (And not a hint of MSG.)

Quest Diagnostics has been operating in the Village of Newtown for several years, but has not yet made it to Yelp.  I go their as part of my routine health maintenance; getting blood and other lab work done prior to my annual physical examination.  It is convenient for those in the community, and the technicians do their jobs efficiently and with cordiality.  My arteries are difficult to find when blood is to be drawn, and the phlebotomists often have to go hunting with a thin, flexible needle before they locate a source for my fluids to flow into a vial.  While I don't have White Coat Syndrome, I make these folks work.    It is easier to get the lab work done before seeing the doctor, and the results are obtained faster, than having the doctor's office staff get the samples and then send them out to a lab for testing and analysis.    It is not really possible to be a fan of a place like this, let alone think that it is a great experience.  3 Stars will have to do.

Lou Lou Burgers is a new house on Main Street, New Hope, PA. The inside dining room is small, but there are plenty of red umbrella-covered tables in the front yard to help out. It is run by college students, which keeps the energy level high to offset the laid back atmosphere in the woody dining room. It also means less than consistent service as sometimes they are more engaged with themselves than customers. No big deal, but you don't want to be that guy who gets impatient waiting for the bill with empty plates on the table.   My Firecracker Burger was a fresh ground half pound of round steak and brisket, finished to the requested medium on a decent bun. The taste was excellent, with a never frozen texture and true beef flavor. Liked it alot. The side of fries were likewise taters just moments before the drop into boiling oil. Crisp, lightly salted, with plenty of those little nibs to crunch.   Prices are reasonable @ between $6.50-7.50 per, but everything else costs, so it is hard to get out at less the ten bucks a person.   This is New Hope (No Hope), after all.

Bread Crumb is a nice old place just outside downtown Doylestown on Easton Road.  It sits in an older strip commercial zone and with lower rent can keep their menu costs down for the fixed income crowd, and those who enjoy a frugal breakfast on occasion.   The counter has room for about half dozen spinners, and the service from there is friendly and efficient.  The coffee was a good brew, and refills were offered several times as I sat and devoured the French Toast.  The Log Cabin syrup tasted like it might be a refill of an industrial strength brand, but the overall taste of the meal was okay, but not more.   The French Toast would have been improved with the additional of a little vanilla extract and sugar in the egg mix to bring up the flavor of the finished product and allow for the caramelization of the edges into a crispy bite.  Without them, the taste was a bit "eggy," and flat.    Still, the place has a certain sunshine charm that makes it a pleasant stop.

This Burger King sits in the neighborhood of Sesame Place and Oxford Valley Mall.  As such, it is in a premier location to attract families and shoppers for a fast bite.  Anticipating this, BKHQ designed this shop with extra space, large kiddie room, and a multitude of dining areas with different looks and feels. They even put in a fireplace lounge for those in a romantic mood. It may be the nicest Burger King I have ever seen. Almost date-worthy.  My Whopper was as good as a Whopper can be, and still fell short of much of the competition. It was hot, but the large slices of onion were not. Mayo and lettuce caused slippage, and my fingers bore witness to the consequence. Fries were decent and there were plenty of carbonated beverages, while not the excessive choice of the new fangled sodie machines.   Service was amazingly efficient for a fast food operation, with servers walking my tray over to me beyond the counter. The space was very clean.   If BK figured out how to make a first rate burger, a joint like this would be a revelation.

It's not the largest beer distributor in Newtown. It's the ONLY beer distributor in Newtown. As such, it is a convenient place to pick up a few cases of Boddington, Flying Fish, or the King of Beers, for your next shindig or to get you through the week.   Yes. It still feels like a cool, damp warehouse, mainly because it is.  Floor to ceiling cardboard encasing a cool twenty-four is bound to make everything moist.   Don't forget to go next door to the State Store, a/k/a Ten Centre Wine and Spirits, to pick up your other alcohol requirements.  This one, two punch makes for convenience.  The big parking lot out front makes it hassle-free.   Drink responsibly. Party like a maniac.

I've returned to Mil-Lee's a couple of times over the past year.  Have to say that the breakfasts have been consistently very good with overflowing plate and excellent friendly service.   The coffee has a nice bite.  The Sausage, Onion, Pepper Omelet I had today was tasty and filling. The accompanying Home Fries were too much to finish.    It is time to add the Luv-Inn to my short list of breakfast favorites on my way to court in Trenton.    I should have bounced to 4 Stars before this.

Unfortunately, Washington Crossing Coffee has departed the scene here at Capital Health. The area where it once resided is now just a seating area on the second floor of the medical center, with several high tops still in place where customers once sat. I was surprised how few people I saw inside the large building, especially considering how crowded the parking lots are all around the institution. Understandable how a small business couldn't survive in the absence of many people as potential customers and a cheap cafeteria on the lower level.   But, fear not.   Starbucks now has a micro stand inside Lori's Gift Shop on the first floor near the front door. It may not be as good as WCC, but give the youngster credit, it may ultimately succeed where the local mom and pop operation could not.   Time will tell.

First visit to a Quick Chek anywhere, and I was surprised how large this one was. It easily reminds of a rest stop along a turnpike or a Sheetz station anywhere in Pa.   They prepare hot dishes on request and have a long wall full of refrigeration units stocked with every American soft drink imaginable.    The coffee selection is broader than most 7/11s, and the adjoining snack section will remind you to take your insulin.    Fairly clean as such places go.  Good pricing, too.   I will stop into this and other Quick Cheks when the situation allows.

I don't often feel the need for a pedicure, but I admit that when my feet are beat and toe nails ragged, some TLC to the tootsies can be a true pleasure. So, after a particularly horrific week of office moving and presidential election poll working, I wandered through Morrisville one evening this week and found M & M Nail Bar Spa in the shopping plaza just off Trenton Road.    Even though it was 15 minutes to closing, and the front door was locked, the woman running the shop was happy to let me in and give me the full foot deal for $23.  Very much appreciated.  Hot soak, salts, scrub, clip, dig, sand, and massage, accompanied by my choice of alcoholic beverage, juice, tea or coffee.  Very cool way to mellow out.    Thirty minutes later my wheels felt like Fred Astaire's feet - Happy, light and content.  The glass of red wine may have had something to do with that.   Next time, how about a few apps?

Yummy Sushi has moved to newer digs just off the College of New Jersey campus, but their food hasn't changed along with it.   It had been a few years since last visit because I found everything I tried from pho to sushi rolls was average at best. Today I ordered their teriyaki salmon bento box, and must report that nothing has changed. The rolls are still on the thick side with far more rice wrap than contents. Made for an adequate chew, but lacking in much taste beyond the soy/wasabe/ginger additive. It was nice to see they were using white ginger.   If all the iceberg and cabbage were removed, there really wasn't much to the meal. Two small shumai, 2x4  grilled salmon with decent teriyaki BBQ sauce, and the six roll segments. Not complaining about the $12.95 tag, but a little more real food would have made for a better value.   Yummy is still a family place with Granny sitting in the corner and now teenage kids in the opposite corner yakking while serving customers. No problem with service otherwise.   There are still better choices nearby if higher quality dishes are your priority.

The original Jake's is here on Bustleton Pike in Richboro, PA. in a small strip center. The dining room/lunch counter is smaller than their house in Newtown, but with the addition of the extended barroom next door, the place feels more interesting. Also MaiTai brunches are always a strong addition.   I sat on a spinner and enjoyed the repartee with the ladies in black working the room. Time to chat and work on this rainy Columbus Day. They took turns serving menu, coffee and breakfast. Good teamwork. The java was from a Bunn-O-Matic; hot and strong.   The short stack french toast was good, with plenty of egg, vanilla and touch of sugar in the mix saturating to the center of each slice. Caramelized edges always please me, and I was not disappointed. Real maple syrup would have made this an almost perfect plate, but it is hard to offer that liquid amber elixir at these prices.   I sat in for a second mug of Joe to postpone walking out into the storm. I didn't mind extending my visit a little longer this wet day.
The Moo Truck is temporarily closed. Be sure to call before coming.

Divine Pizza has become a semi-regular lunch stop over the past year and a half.  Their pizza remains solid, but I have been impressed with the quality of their hot sandwiches.    From Eggplant Parm, to Italian Sweet Sausage, to Peppers and Onions, to Italian Hot Dogs, their plates are substantial, hearty and very tasty.  Their torpedo rolls are first rate, and are locally baked to produce crunchy skin and soft insides.    Definitely have become a strong fan.

Willow Grove Park Mall is not where I normally shop, but sometimes a little diversion pays unexpected dividends.  Generally, I find the latest incarnation of Macy's to be a shoppers hunting ground.  There are always sales, coupons, and additional discounts on lots of the merchandise, so at least in the clothing departments, it is possible to find quality pieces at surprisingly good prices.    This Macy's is laid out as the others in Oxford Valley or Quaker Bridge, but on this Saturday late morning/early afternoon, there were many fewer customers, and salespeople. Not sure what the story was, but I found what I needed, tried things on without interference from staff, and only found slight delay at cashiering on the way out.  It was almost like they were using an honor system.  Pick out what you want.  Try it on. Leave what you don't want. Pay for what you do.  Interact with Macy's only when you draw your credit card.  We trust you.   Saved about 60% off the original price, and left a happy man.

Newest design for DD. Not surprised as it had to do something extraordinary to get into Upper Makefield. This shop has an inside lobby with doors on 2 sides to allow for circulation of customers. Too, it has a pleasant sitting area to one side complete with a lounge by the large front window.   The coffee is standard for a DD. Service is friendly and efficient.   Nice to have a morning hangout in the Crossing.

Very decent Vietnamese house in Mt. Laurel, NJ.  Man! This part of the world is all shopping centers and highways.  What happened to rural Moorestown and Mt. Laurel?  Well, at least they had the good sense to permit Pho Xinh to open their southeast Asian restaurant. It's not just Viet cuisine, as it also has offerings from Thailand.    My lunch was the Jasmin Grill, consisting of 2 very thin pork chops, grilled and barbequed, cuke and tomato side salad/garnish, and a cup of broken rice.  For another buck I also received a small fried spring roll.  Very good service, with everyone pitching in.    Taste was fine, especially after I mixed the Hoisin and Chili Sauces together for dipping the meat, and poured the thin spring roll sauce over the rice to add more flavor.    If I find myself in the area again, I will sit down for a bowl of Pho.   Not quite Washington Avenue, Philly, but strong for this neck of the woods.

My second visit to any Quick Chek, and I admit that their approach to Convenience Store is a nice upgrade over the traditional view of the genre.    They offer hot and cold customized food, an array of coffee and snack options, and a spacious floor plan that encourages you to walk around and check it out.  Too, the staff in both places I have visited is friendly and courteous to a very noticeable degree.    These places remind of modern rest stops found along the highways and byways of America.  Finding them on the streets of our cities is a bit of an amazement.   A very enjoyable one.

I have returned three times since the review, and sampled their food each time.   Their burgers are very good.  Large patty cooked to the requested finish with loads of toppings and a steak knife piercing the sandwich like a dagger through the heart. Also ordered the cheesesteak sliders, which were basically cheesesteak encapsulated within a thin dough deep fried before presentation.  Also, good, but not the grabber that the burger was.   Beer selection is excellent for a neighborhood bar & grill, and the service remains friendly and courteous.   Work being done in the back to bring up the comfort of the dining area.  Too, the men's room is nice enough to be in someone's home.  Well done!

The United States Postal Service as embodied by the Post Office at 20 Terry Drive in Newtown has provided me and my business with a post office box address, mail and shipping services for several years.  I like having a face behind these services as it reassures that someone is taking personal and professional responsibility for making sure everything I send out gets to its destination, and that I receive everything that is sent to me.  Yes, FedEx and the others can do a lot of the same things, but there is something very American about having these guys and facilities in the community.    Let's hope they figure out a way to stay open and active as part of the American landscape.

Very nice to have a bakery café open in Chinatown late on a Saturday night.   The Vietnamese Coffee was very good.  The Dulces were varietal and fresh. And the service unhurried in a "have a long conversation" way.    Pleased to find a place to hang out for a while without high decibels, nor strutting nighthawks.    Table in the back. Stay as long as you like.

Hometown Deli in the Anchor Crossing Center doesn't look like much walking in. Small eating area to the left, a few rows of snacks and drinks coolers in the middle, and deli department to the left rear. It all seems a little worn. But, ordering a sandwich and taking possession of it quicky changed those first impressions.   My chicken salad on rye toast was delivered to my table by the deli chef. It was bigger than expected, and first bite opened my eyes in pleasant surprise. The chicken salad was chunky, creamy and had very fresh taste. Combined with a thick red tomato slice and dark green lettuce, inside real rye toast, it was very good and enjoyable. It was almost too much to finish.   Apparently, they do breakfast sandwiches just as good.   See you again soon, Hometown Deli.

Very nice facility in Bensalem, Pa. Dark tones. Square bar. Attractive, attentive service. Happy hour drink and apps menu at good prices. Outdoor patio for nice weather.   Food, however, is average to dull. Their Louie Burger looks great, but lacks fresh ground beef flavor and juiciness. Perhaps frozen. The sliders, same thing. Dry with little taste. Sauces don't bring them back to life. Their special bourbon wings were too wet. No crunch. Weak whiskey taste. Not fun to eat. Left most of them behind.   Looks like a meet up place for the after work crowd. That makes sense given the look of the place, location and happy hour discounts. But, certainly there are better places for burgers and wings.  2.5 Stars.

This is the laboratory collection location preferred by Parx Casino for prospective employees. After the initial interview at the casino, they hand over a large manila envelop with the proper Quest Diagnostics form for completion, signing, and to turn in to the Quest personnel for processing along with a urine sample.   It is not the most efficient operation, but they get you in and out as quickly as possible. There is a sign-in tablet for registering your presence, which seemed to work when we were there. The employees didn't have bubbling personalities, but they weren't rude, either. Just another day of handling blood and piss for them.   At the end, they keep the forms and samples, and send the results back to Parx within 24 hours in most cases.   If you've had illegal drugs in your system in the recent past, these tests will show them, and the job will be forfeit.

Buckingham Valley Vineyards is another beautifully laid out small acreage winery specializing is the sweeter vintages of fruit and grape based fermentations. Like some of the others in the area it is second generation family run operation with the love and care given the vines obvious to any who stop in for a self guided tour and the tasting available throughout the year.   Although I prefer drier wines, I have sampled the bottles and casks here and found them to be pretty good, but not what I want to purchase for personal consumption. Still, a relaxing afternoon overlooking the long rows of arbors sipping peach and blackberry wines and heavier port like sipping liqueurs has a very mellowing effect on the soul.   Well worth a stop on the Bucks County winery tour.

Pho Kitch'n on Ridge Pike, Eagleville, PA, is an Asian fusion restaurant with Vietnamese cuisine taking the lead and Thai/Chinese following close behind. It is in a free standing A frame building, with plenty of parking and nice size dining room.   I went with the namesake noodle soup with lean round steak and fatty flank. It was a large bowl for $8.95 and the stock was good with interesting and subtle flavors from long simmering, and a large knot of noodles beneath the surface.   Sadly, the side plate of accessories to add to the pho was disappointing, with withered Thai basil and dessicated lime wedge visible with a quick glance. Delivering them to the table was an act of disrespect and slovenliness that is impossible to dismiss as an oversight. The woman serving me certainly put the plate together in the kitchen, and just didn't give a damn, or worse.  Ironically, the pho itself was pretty good (even without the basil and lime), and would have garnered a higher score but for the passive aggressiveness served with the pho.   2 Stars

Not a bad place to stop for a cuppa joe on the way into Mt. Holly.    It's clean and the service is good.  Only 6 tables for those who want to hang for a few.  Definitely built for get and go, but lacking a drive thru window.    The seasonal Pumpkin Donut wasn't bad, either.

Not a bad place for a pie, but my experience with their Eggplant Parm Sandwich left something to be desired.   The slices of this nightshade were thick and not quite sautéed through and through, leaving parts of the meal somewhat harder than expected.  Too, they seem to have only been in the pan once after breading, rather than twice, before and after breadcrumbs were added.  When heated twice in hot olive oil the veggie is much softer and takes on the taste of the surrounding ingredients better.  No complaint with the gravy, cheese, nor roll. However, I would not order this again.   Nick's has the feel of a slice and cheesesteak joint.  It is small, but nicely appointed in a low key way.  The staff is fine, and anyone who has hands free behind the counter will bring out the platter when it is ready.    Lipton products, meaning that high corn fructose is a prime part of every bottle.  Not so good for health.  An upgrade in the drink cooler would be a big plus.

Pulled up to this Prince Fried Chicken after work one night last week.  The driveway is not on Olden Avenue, but on the side street next to the adjoining liquor store.  Miss that and you will have a job finding your way back here, especially after dark.  That being said, after trying their breasts and wings I will not likely be going back.  When I arrived home and sat down to eat my purchase, I found the coating to be overcooked and the meat a bit dry.  I had noticed that the chicken was a shade darker than richly golden, but as everything in the bin was the same color, I thought that would not be an issue.  It was, however.   The pieces were meaty and the prices very inexpensive.  If the chicken itself had been crunchy, spicy and moist, it would have been a big hit. It might have been a bad lot left in the fryer too long, or perhaps suffering freezer burn, but you only get one chance to make a first impression.    Given the alternative fried chicken shacks all around the area, I will keep searching for the perfect batch.

VITAMIN/SUPPLEMENT REVIEW ONLY  Visited the Carousel Gardens campus today, thinking Organnons Market might carry the things I needed in their vitamin supplement area. It was my first visit so I looked around the shop. Few customers on a Saturday afternoon, but the produce looked good and the canned goods were limited but interestingly esoteric. Nice selection of coffee, too.   Yet, they didn't have any of the three things I needed that are fairly standard in most health food stores. The worker was helpful, and apologized for not being able to help me out. No sweat. Drove down to Big Bear and found what I needed. Plus, they were selling Kicking Horse Coffee for $3 less per bag then Organnons.   Good to have a quality locally focused organic food outlet nearby, but given it's inherent inventory limitations and prices, it won't be a regular stop for our provisions.

I am not an expert on haunted hay rides, but I went along for the ride last night with my seventeen year old son and his two buds. At $36 per person, it was an expensive thrill, and if I had to cost it out, it came to about $10 a scare. Not really all that spooked out, but they are dealing with a mixed audience and what frightens me might cause coronaries in others. Yet, the monster in the Trump mask was so realistic I almost thought he was moonlighting.   The flatbed wagon held about a dozen people and the course went on for 20 minutes. There were plenty of ghouls and demons along the route and they never came out of character. The haunted house was very dark and foreboding, and the choreography was, again, well done. Plenty of screams.   There is a small snack area, but don't come to eat to avoid leaving it on the field.   The guys had a lot of fun and the two hours there went quickly. I probably won't do this again as the world is frightening enough without finding more ways to be scared s**tless!

Decent beer distributor in Richboro, PA.   Plenty of choice. Domestic, European, Mexican and some hard cider. I needed a case for an upcoming Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) dinner. In the absence of Tsingdao or other Asian brew, I opted for Modelo Especial, a very good Mexican lager with strong, yet balanced flavor.   The 24 count case cost $33 and change including tax. No bad, but not as reasonable as at my favorite alcohol warehouse in Jersey. Still, considering time and transportation, it was well worth it.   Happy New Year, Everybody!

While I appreciate the difference between Joe Santucci's rectangular upside down pizza with mozzarella cheese baked under the dark red sauce, and traditional east coast round pies that put the cheese on top, I can't say that after picking it up to bring home that it is significantly better. I did like the somewhat thicker crust and pasty thick tomato sauce, but not more than the quality "Jersey" style pizza from joints like DeLorenzo's in Lower Makefield, or the Burg in Falls, to name a few others.   I guess being suckled on Brooklyn and Trenton slices spoiled me for other conceptions. I just like the thinner crusted, basil flavored, chunky tomato sauced, creations, with the secrets of the dough mixed with softer water that flavors the crust with subtle cracker-like tones and texture.   To my buds, the Trenton Pie is perfection, far superior to the upside down variation Philly is famous for. It's not that I don't enjoy this style once in a while, but given the choice, the ones from Trenton win every time.

Solid 3.5 Star breakfast & lunch deli in the Glen Roc Shopping Center on Scotch Road in Ewing, NJ.    Décor is minimalist, with a few tables near the counter and kitchen and a second dining room to the right with ten more tables when the crowd arrives. The joint is clean and the service is friendly and efficient. Ordering is done at the cashier, and one of the staff brings the food to the table. There seems to be a group of regular alder cockers hanging out, but they are amusing and harmless.   My breakfast sausage, egg & cheese sandwich arrived with a small container of orange juice, a nice unexpected touch. The roll was better than average with a fresh firm crust and flakey innards. It was a good sammy with oozing American cheese and fried egg.  I would certainly have it again if nearby in the morning. The coffee was hot and middle of the road in strength.   Price was under $6 for food and beverage; a very attractive price.    If Deli-Licious Café had a bit more character and comfort, it could easily garner the fourth star.

Standard CVS drug store and food market in Newtown Borough. To my eyes they all look the same and really have little to offer other than prescription drugs. Everything else is predictable and overpriced.   I am surprised to see that the floor has industrial carpeting throughout, as it is difficult to clean. In a place frequented by sick people such flooring is not optimized for a healthy environment. I prefer hard surfaces that can be swept and washed often. Maybe this carpet is removable, but the question remains, how often?   The answer, not often enough.

If you love simple and delicious Polish food, Pierogi Factory is singing your song.    This tiny four table restaurant is in the Shops at Red Lion on Bustleton Avenue, Northeast Philly.  The menu focuses on the staples: Pierogies, Stuffed Cabbage, Potato Pancakes, Kielbasa and a few other goodies.  Service is casual and sincere.    We ordered their Combo Dinners in order to sample as many of their dishes as possible.  Combo # 1 had two potato pancakes, 3 pierogis of choice (traditional potato and farmer's cheese), and 1 Golabki (stuffed cabbage), with a little container of sour cream ($9.95).  Every element was excellently prepared with taste as good as my grandmother used to make.  The other combo swapped out the potato pancakes for a nice length of smoked (grilled) kielbasa ($10.95).  Also, fantastic.    I was full, but not stuffed, when we finished eating.  We shared a piece of apple cake ($3.00).  It was not as good as granny's, as it lacked the moisture, density and large apple slices she used to fatten up her grandchildren.    Still, a very pleasant surprise on Bustleton. Will definitely visit here again.

Friends B & G is one of the better places to hang out if beer, sports and decent (not great) food are your priorities. When we arrived Friday around 9, the place was packed, but the good people at the bar were more than willing to move down and make room for us.  Love that kind of courtesy.  We had drinks and eventually a booth cleared and we were able to sit around and have a couple of apps that were ample for the 8 of us.  The Nachos Supreme were what you would expect - piled high with chips, cheese, chopped onions and peppers; and the Hot Wings pretty good when considering there were about 20 of them.  Good prices, too.  Our group often meets there after big events (like elections), and we always find space to celebrate.  We are hoping for a good reason to party next Tuesday night.    You are all invited.  See you there.

Same great big fat donuts as the other Yum Yum shops around.  Same good coffee.  Same very reasonable prices.  Same friendly service and pride in the baker's craft.   This one lacks a public restroom, meaning if that is one of the reasons for your stop here, you should consider visiting the Wawa Service Station across the street before you go.   Easier to indulge that way!

Bagelissimo is an Italian deli of a bagel shop, showing that cross cultural alternatives can work well. The shop in a fairly new strip center on Rt. 206 North, has a decent layout for eating in or taking out. They offer a fair variety of bagels, muffins and sandwiches, although the rounders are a bit denser than I prefer.   My onion bagel, butter and swiss had good flavor, plenty of dry onion flakes, and a lot of chewability. A few air pockets here and there would have brought it completely home for me.   Service was prompt and friendly. Prices about the best I have encountered recently. My sammy went for $2. I am sure the manager saw my double take. I dropped a buck in the tip basket out of appreciation for my wallet.

REHEATED SLICE COVID TAKEOUT REVIEW:  The constant problem with ordering pizza by the slice is that they require sufficient reheating in the oven to resuscitate it into edible condition. If not requested to be "well done," they are only partially revived, while the rest tastes dead or just lacking in energy.   The same is true here. Without knowing how long it had been sitting on the cooling rack, nor the heat of the oven, the time spent could have been enough to scorch the undercarriage and bubble up the cheese, but it didn't quite make it all the way back to life. As a result it was a mediocre slice. Decent crust, almost right sauce needing more basil, and thick cheese deposit in the center that wasn't quite the volcanic lava desired.   Not bad for noshing in the car on the way back to Bucks, but not the Jersey Strong hoped for.   Oh, and the shop really needs a deep cleaning. Where's the TLC?

This Donkey Donuts is in the parking lot of Fieldcrest Center, Columbus, NJ. It has the latest style with smallish indoor sitting area and wrap around drive thru for those who don't have a moment to spare to get out of their cars and walk inside.   The coffee is pretty much standard DD, and the sweet dough fry what you expect from this outfit. Of course, the Christmas donuts are a pleasant diversion.   No problem with service, although I forgot that it was on me to pull out napkins and stuff them in the bag. Had some in the car anyway.  Maybe I've been spoiled by all the cafe/coffee house alternatives around these days, but I am finding the Donkey brew to be somewhat pedestrian. They really need to kick it up a notch if they want to succeed in the java wars.

Is it possible to be a fan or Wahoo for a shoe repair shop?   Existential inquiry, but one worth considering as long as your soul and sole relate well with each other. Mine always have.  The longer I walk, the deeper within I delve. Same for you?  Then, be sure to treat your feet well through well crafted footwear maintenance.   Newtown Shoe Repair sits in the middle of downtown Newtown Borough, in an undersized storefront shop, with walk up steps to the wood and glass doors.  Careful, if you open the door without the magic words, you are stepping into a time machine than has only one destination date - 1955.   The old machines, the smell of leather and wax, the shelves full of shoes and boots... Worth a visit, but of course the business owners would love you to take off your shoes and let them put on new heals and a shine.   It is a bit expensive for basic service - now $25. for almost any repair. So, as the other reviewer suggests, drop off your shoes and walk around Newtown for a great afternoon.  But, you might want to bring an extra pair of shoes...

Michael's is a roadside diner on Street Road, Bensalem, PA. It has a counter with spinner seats and a fairly large dining room. It serves three squares a day with professional servers who have been there for decades.   I stopped by for breakfast this week and took a stool facing the dessert cooler and ordered coffee with a Country Omelet, hash browns and rye toast. The java was industrial strength, as desired. The three egger was okay with an overload of green pepper along with onion and diced potatoes. The hash browns were a bit of overkill given their cousins in the eggs, and would have tasted better if they replaced the spuds inside the shell, as they had far more flavor and texture than those puny chunks used as filler. Overall, the opus was a tad dry, detracting from what might have been a contender had it been moister and had better balanced ingredients.   Liked the rye toast.   Service was fine. Access into the building was ADA compliant with ramp and wide front door. Didn't check the bathrooms.   Michael's was decent, but nothing to distinguish it from the other culinary attractions along this stretch of Street Road.

Perhaps it was just this particular Perkins, but it does seem that this franchise is a poor man's version of the ubiquitous IHOP.
