It was hard not to notice an immediate disappointment moving from the beautiful menu photos to the presentation on our plates. From proud to defeated, boisterously sensational to meekly fallen, the reality fell far from the mark.   Not that the french toast platter and quesadillas were without taste, but that they were not nearly as grand as advertised. The brioche thick slices absorbed the egg/sugar/vanilla mix, but not quite enough to overcome its dry core. The crisp bacon was not so, and the deflated quesadillas were so thinly filled as to believe the promised steak was little more than tender shoe leather.   True, the hall was crowded, the prices quite reasonable and the coffee topped off in a thermos pitcher on the table. Kenny's service was friendly, clever and accommodating, but could not overcome the the tools he was working with.   Perkins appeared to be an anchor of this Grant Avenue neighborhood in Northeast Philly. It should do something to assure that it does not contribute further to its distress.

Man!   You guys are so harsh on poor little DD here in Holland.  The three of you only gave it 1 Star apiece.    The coffee is standard for DD; no better, no worse.  The staff does seem disorganized and a bit comical how they step over each other and can't remember your order.   The donuts are never really good at any Dunkin, so nothing new there.    Yeah, I've had way better than everything on the board here. But, is it as bad as finding a mouse in your donut?  (Thus, the "Eek!")   I think not.

Authentic Polish/East European smoked meat emporium situated in the Trenton Farmers Market, with the touch and feel of butcher/deli of my childhood. The center of attention is the Kielbasi collection where you can order any combination of long red sausage you desire for slicing, grilling or mixing in a casserole. Also do their own stuffed cabbage quite well.   Not impressed with the pierogi which are no longer homemade, but trucked down from Brooklyn, and are thick skinned with too dry potato mash.   And, as with most of the outfits here, the prices are premium leaving little to the imagination. Definitely paying for the privilege of participating in a cultural event.

Housed in a former convenience store, Piazza's Bakery does all its work in their large workspace and ovens in the back room. A large tray of yeast glazed pretzel twist donuts was coming out, and I immediately pointed to it, saying, "I want some of those!"   Great choice, because they were terrific - light, airy, mildly yeasty and, oh, so, perfectly glazed. Very reminiscent of Crispy Kremes classics, but bigger. The brownies were just as impressive with a layer of chocolate icing above dense chewy choco base. Their croissants were also good, but not as flaky as a French boulangerie would create.   Their were plenty of cookies, fruit pies and customized celebratory cakes that looked great, but were beyond the limits of my sweet tooth. Didn't see much in the way of bread or rolls while there, but that could have been a question of timing.  Piazza's is worth another visit.

This Dairy Delite on Rt. 13 in Levittown is the twin of the ice cream stand on Woodbourne Road by the same name.    It is housed in a mid-twentieth century style all glass summer enhancing structure that is iconic for those of us who remember going to such places as children.  As was the custom then, it is staffed by lovely high schoolers who bring their innocence and enthusiasm to the job of ice cream dispensers.    When I got on the short line I saw the handmade sign for "Soft Peanut Butter," and allowed myself to be swayed by that suggestion.  No complaints, as the large cup of the dense, sweet, creamy, almost custard-like, soft serve was delicious to the last melted drop.   Under $4. for all that pleasure.  Maybe it still is 1970 at Dairy Delite!

Another state of the art burger emporium from Five Guys.   If you like your sliders fresh, hot and greasy, this is your place.  For $10. you get the standard double with or without cheese and all the toppings you can imagine, on a crushed bun, and a cuppa hot fries that spills into the bag and is easily enough for three. Another few bucks for the bottomless drinks.  When the 13 year old we were with suggested McDonald's for lunch, I Yelped for an alternative and found this 5 Dudes even closer than the golden arches.  It was his first try and though he didn't say much, he ate the whole sandwich, plenty of fries, and washed everything down with Sprite.    Win-win for all of us.

I have been back regularly since my review.  Having overcome my hesitance about the quirky advertising with cows asking humans to eat more chickens (that's another dissertation about social morality), and eaten a few other things beyond the Sausage, Egg and Cheese Biscuit (5 Stars), I achieved the realization that I was too harsh in my evaluation before.   The sandwiches are good, the shakes superior, and the playroom for kids, unique.  I don't have to agree with corporate politics to appreciate the grub.   Okay. I am a fan. I am willing to admit it.
Sweet, creamy, cold.   Orange Cream (twirl of vanilla and orange) tastes like childhood.

Sorry folks.  This strictly take out joint on S. Broad Street, Trenton, is just not very good.  The family running it is nice, but the food leaves a lot to be desired.  I guess if you can't make the trip to a reasonably authentic or even a decent Americanized Chinois place, then this is what is left.  It's a shame because there are several good places not too far away.   The dishes were plentiful with abundant fried rice and a large pile of Sesame Chicken, but the quality just was not there.  The taste was generic sweet gloop on top of too long frozen chicken, and fried rice that was made either last night or early in the morning with a large dose of brown dyed beef bouillon.  I watched as a Bento Box was prepared for someone.  The fish came out of baggies and sat on the hot prep table as it was put together.  I was glad I was not the one who was going to eat it.  I could practically see the bacteria multiplying.    There are some relatively decent Chinese Take Out places in the area, but My Kitchen is not one of them.

This Cheeburger Cheeburger franchise is right across the street from Red Robin, so there is a natural choice to make when making a burger run.  If you want a beer with that, than RR is your only option.  If great shakes are a priority, Chee Chee is the better way to go.    Here, the ambiance is all ersatz 1950's diner-esqueness.  Very similar to Nifty Fifty, Johnnie Rocket's, Jake's Wayback, and the like.  I forgive them the weak attempt at historical orientation, as the actual product is pretty good.    The burgers and fries are fresh, not frozen at the start, and the end result is a decent (not great) burger experience.  Compared to 5 Guys, it falls a little short in the taste department (not enough tasty grease), but it compensates with more menu variety (chicken, salads), and additional treats to put on the burger (banana chilies, shrooms, pickles, etc.).  The shakes are very good, and they will add malt powder for no additional charge if asked.  Really, creamy and tasty.   Bottom line - Worth the trip and money when you want a good nostalgia burger.

Before getting on the Pa Turnpike early this morning, I made a short detour onto Horizon Boulevard to get some java and a small bite for breakfast.  When Chik-Fil-A was not yet open, I drove through the take out window at Starbucks next door.    I liked the convenience and time savings of a drive thru, but it seemed like the order taker was also the barista as well as the short order cook.  So, she looked rather busy, and in need of assistance.  Still, she kept her composure and got everything right.    As usual, the coffee had a burnt and bitter taste, but the extra milk requested helped to soften the harshness.  I asked for their Sausage, Egg and Cheese Sandwich on a croissant, but was told that all these meals are pre-packaged and microwaved just before sale.  I decided to go with the English Muffin as the only option.  I don't like what microwaves do to eggs and bread, so the meal was at best, average.  Nothing I would want a second time.    Hopefully, CFA will be open next time I find myself in a similar predicament.

Great urban park with an amazing history. But, what makes it Philadelphia's gift to the world is the view from the Belmont Plateau overlooking Center City.  Go about 4 pm in Spring or Autumn when the light turns a golden hue, and it is... Simply.   Breathtaking.

Although designed primarily for take out, there are two tables in the front of the house for eating in.  Be forewarned that in cooler weather, the space is not heated, but for a small space heater that can be turned on near the tables.    Aside from that bit of discomfort, the fare from this Chinese/American shop is better than average.  My Orange Chicken, Fried Rice and Hot & Sour Soup were all superior to most of the other alternative takeaways in the Morrisville/Trenton region (except for the more authentically Chinese restos that don't fit in this category).  The chicken did not seem to have been frozen and the sauce was pleasantly thinner than the goop found in most places.  Too, it was a nice customer service to offer to make the Orange Chicken for a lunch special when it was not on the menu.    The Soup was loaded with tofu, sprouts and mushrooms, while not dosed heavily with MSG. The Fried Rice was dyed with the bouillon beef stock, but was otherwise full of veggies and chunks of pork.    The friendly, accommodating service made for an enjoyable, if chilly, meal.

Needing to paint the wood trim around my home the same color as the original, I took a chip of paint to The Paint Store in Newtown to see if they could match it.  They were able to match it as a Benjamin Moore paint called, "Steamed Spinach."  Who'd a thunk it would be that easy?   So, they mixed me a quart of it, low gloss, and I walked out a happy homeowner.  The experience was pleasant and completely no sweat.  The shop has all the material necessary for such jobs.  The prices are not as cheap as the highway box stores, but the convenience of being 5 minutes from home, and keeping our community businesses successful, is worth the small premium to me.    Now, all I need is a way to get 30 feet up to the gable to paint.

It seems all the service stations in Newtown are owned by the same extended family. Makes one wonder if that is one of the reason the price of gas in town is higher than anywhere else outside of New York City.  Maybe? Maybe not.  While I always attempt to fill up in Jersey where the prices are a good thirty cents a gallon cheaper, sometimes that is impossible.  When the good option is out of the question, I visit Kerrigan's to purchase enough fuel to get me around until I can cross the Delaware.    As Kimberly G. rightly notes, the cost here is the lowest in town. Too, Sunoco has the two grades of premium, and it is possible to go with the 90 Octane drink, rather than the 92, and save a few more shekels.   I can't speak to the mechanic's services.  I use a cousin's shop down on Sycamore for that, and find those folks totally reputable.

Nice cold morning. Quiet breakfast with my son before camping. Sausage, egg & cheese biscuit quite tasty.  I am not really a fan of Chik Fil A.  I don't get the name, nor the advertising.  The chicken sandwiches do not move me. The only things I like are the breakfast sandwiches and the shakes, which are rich and creamy.

Right on the Broad Street/Rt. 206 Circle in Hamilton, NJ, this Advance Auto Parts store used to be a Chinese Buffet back in the day.  There are similarities in the wide display of everything car/truck related being found on the aisles, the same way the multitude of chicken pieces were dressed up with many sauces, accompanied by veggie and rice alternatives.    I came in looking for a jack and lug wrench to replace the original equipment that had gone missing recently (one of the great mysteries of life).  Everything Advance had was for much heavier usage.  Even the smallest scissor jack was engineered to lift a panel truck, and much too heavy duty (and just plain heavy) for my needs.  I did remember to pick up a replacement wiper; finding myself studying the chart to determine which model and level of sophistication was required.  For $22 this better last forever.   Service was of the DIY variety, which was okay after I located the area of the shop I wanted, but no one volunteered to assist.  I guess most customers have been there before.

Newtown Jewelers is a family run jewelry store on State Street, Newtown Borough.  It is a small shop, but it has a nice selection of affordable pieces, including watches, gold and silver rings, bracelets and necklaces, as well as a few nice gemstone articles. They are well connected and can find almost anything you want, and they enjoy the challenge.   I routinely bring my watches there for repair and batteries, and find the interaction with Cheryl and Bill to be warm and often entertaining.   This is certainly a shop locally winner!

Chik Fil A in Newtown stands across the parking fields from Acme, and shares a parking lot with Appleby's.  They have both drive through and eat-in services.  I am not a fan of their chicken sandwiches and nuggets, although my young son loves them.  For me, they lack much taste and the roll and filet together are too soft for an enjoyable bite and chew. I will only eat them if I am very hungry. However, the breakfast sandwiches are superior products compared to other fast food variations.  The sausage, egg and cheese biscuit is super tasty and textured, so every bite is a pleasure.  The fresh biscuits are flakey and have a mild buttery flavor.   The best thing offered are the shakes.  They claim to be "hand spun," whatever that means.  The taste is wonderful with the right amount of sweetness and creaminess.  Their season special shakes are fun on St. Patrick's Day (green minty), late summer (peach), and fall (pumpkin).  They are a little expensive compared to the drink alternatives, but a palate pleaser.  I am not a regular here, but there is a time when it offers exactly what I want.

I am not sure I would have located a super Wawa in the center of Richboro, PA, but it is there, and takes its place as the crown jewel of this landlocked hamlet, gas islands and all.   The store itself is a good example of the new breed of roadside services that modernizes the convenience store with enlargement, attractive environment, and decent food and drink alternatives. And for the coffee crowd they have figured out that procuring better beans is a cheap way to grab the loyalty and favor of the java drinking public. Selling any size for a buck is a loss leader that everyone can appreciate, and leaves some jingle for something sweet to eat.   The gas prices are generally below the competition, and as it is self service in the Commonwealth, the efficiency pumping your own saves time and treasure.   The evolution of the reststop service oasis has come a long way in a short time. With plenty of choice in a reasonably clean cool space, there is something for almost everyone. Add a few tables for the sit and chat folks and it could become Richboro City Hall.

BREAKFAST ONLY REVIEW -  Reno's is basically a pizza take out joint on very old (and nearly decrepit) business route one in Penndel, PA. There are two small tables in front, but upon talking with the one man on duty (owner?), it was apparent that their business plan had changed to a stripped down pizza-to-go operation. Even the sign offering breakfast was misleading, as they would still grill up a morning sandwich, but lacked a means to provide hot coffee to customers. So, my idea to sit down for a quick early bite was denied by the lack of the essential beverage.   Still, the sausage, egg and cheese on Kaiser roll was pretty good, with fried egg and white American cheese. The roll was more a potato roll than the described German loaf, but was actually better than the anticipated bake would have been. Just would have preferred not to eat it in the car.   Can't speak to Reno's pizza or other Italian plates, but the sammy itself was an enjoyable chew.

I am not a Star$$$ fan.   I love coffee that tastes good at its base and does not require extra processing (read, latte, capp, etc.) to make it palatable.  So, it is always somewhat surprising to see these little coffee caves sprout up in supermarkets and box stores and do moderately well.  I admit to having been a happy stockholder for a while, but that did not change my opinion of the underlying product.    So, I was skeptical when I walked into Target a few years ago, and several times since, to see this outpost hanging its shingle within.  It is still there, but seems to be scraping along with only one person running the operation.  Some people like to sip java as they push their shopping carts around the store.  A few actually stop in only for the coffee and depart.    It would be great if there were more coffee alternatives around here.  Until then, this place and the competing Dunkin Donuts and diners of the world will duke it out for my coffee dollar.

Cold Spring has moved uptown from its original digs in an blown out old industrial building in Yardley, to this modern warehouse just south of 5 Points on Rt. 413, Wrightstown, Pa.  While the 19th Century look of the old place was cool, having an air conditioned space large enough to hold and display a vast variety of American and international suds, is an improvement.  They even have room for the mid-sized shopping carts that can hold a couple of cases while you shop and make way to the cashier.    We were in a Mexican fiesta mood, so picked up a 12 bottle case of Corona, and another of Dos Equis (XX) Sampler.  Bought a supply of Lime at Tanner Bros.   True, the price of cerveza goes up all the time, especially for the imports, but there is something to be said for comfort and convenience in brew buying.   Cold Spring opens at 9 during the week, giving it a leg up on other local distributors who open later in the morning.  Never too early for fiesta!

Enid C. has it right.   Pork Soy Sauce Noodle, Shaved.   It was textured to the bite, lots of surface area to pick up and hold the wonderful sauce; a large bowled experience with Ground Pork, mild Chili Flavor, Cilantro cooked into the mix, and enough liquid to cover every nano of the free form Noodles.   Did it change my life as suggested by Enid?  The jury is still out, but the fact that they are taking so long to decide is definitely a good thing.    I am hooked!  Just added 5 or 6 spoons of Sesame/Chili Oil from the table container, and the taste exploded in my mouth.   When a joint has over 800 reviews there is little left to distinguish one from the rest.  Short and sweet (In this case more spicy) is the way to go.

Mission BBQ on Roosevelt Boulevard in Northeast Philadephia, does pretty good BBQ ribs and chicken, especially for a joint north of the Mason-Dixon Line.  The house looks the part, with lots of dark wood, picnic-like tables and photos of first responders on the walls.   We ordered the equivalent of half racks of baby backs and regular spare ribs, and a half chicken.  All had sides of some sort, but aside from the fries and corn bread, those were not memorable. The ribs on the other hand were very good.  Pull off the bone smoked, with tender meat and nice rub and bark.  Each table had 6 bottle rockets with various sauces to be squirted on to moisten and flavor the chew.  None of them really stood out, and for the most part, the "as is" ribs were fine without anything more.    Prices were reasonable. Service was all at the order counter with no table service.   The consensus was that this was a legit BBQ joint that we would return to when the mood for pork ribs or pulled meat overcame us again.

The upper reaches of Washington Avenue are rather bleak with warehouses and abandoned buildings all around.  The only ray of light in the area of 15th Street is the corner Dunkin Donuts.  On a dark night, it is like seeing Las Vegas as you drive in from the desert.    This particular shop seems to be a hang out for a certain taxi company, where at any time of the day, the parking lot and surround curbs are parked up with off duty cabs.  The drivers stand around outside or sit within, chatting in their native tongues, and sipping the local brew.  All this adds to the color of the joint.    The coffee is pretty much standard issue DD.  Never great. Always adequate. The bakery offerings are below average, as if they are being made by people who don't really get the donut concept.  Maybe that's the way the cabbies like them.   It's hard to get excited about any Dunkin, and this one is no different.    Any caffeine in a storm.

PIZZA BY THE SLICE REVIEW  Nova Trattoria recently moved to this location, replacing the Mexican casa that was there before. It is a smallish space with a row of tables along the wall, with kitchen on the opposite side behind another wall that gives the appearance of being a very narrow dining room.   I ordered a slice of Brooklyn pie and another tradition regular triangle. The Brooklyn slice was pretty good - thin crust, Marzano sauce and dollops of mozza in a square pan. It was firm, crisp and pleasantly chewy.  The regular slice was not as good.  The crust was limp despite requesting it be reheated well done, and there was ample oil drip onto the paper plate. Just not a strong presentation.  The price was good at around $5 for the slices and bottle of water. Service was pleasant from start to finish.   There is much better pizza and tomato pie right nearby.

Decent D & D on West Trenton Avenue, Morrisville, right next to Italian Peoples Bakery.  Run by an efficient and friendly crew.   The coffee is okay, but not outstanding.  The baked goods are also right down the middle of the road.  My Everything Bagel with Light Veggie Cream Cheese filled the need to quiet my stomach until after court.   Plenty of parking at a mildly difficult intersection.

In my search for the best bagel in the Trenton/Hamilton matrix, I stumbled upon Tina's Bagel Factory.  It is attached to Tina's Italian resto; and they no doubt share their pizza oven.    While I did not expect much, it turned out to be the best bagel I have tried so far in the area.  Not too dense as most of the other purveyors are; Tina does not over knead the dough, leaving air pockets throughout to keep the heart of the bagel light and the skin crunchy. Kudos!  I will be back as time allows to see if I just got lucky or she really knows what she is doing. But, for now, Tina goes to the head of the bagel class.    Nosh on!

Lucas Plumbing and Lucas Ltd. are one in the same.   Had Brandon back to the house today to repair a balky toilet in the downstairs powder room.    Yes. He was a few hours later than originally scheduled, but that was beyond his control.  He ran into a one hour job that required four hours of work.  At least, the office called me twice with a heads up, and offer to reschedule.    Our job was truly one hour, and he was handing me the invoice in 50 minutes.  Not cheap by any stretch, but done right and with a positive attitude.    These guys have my loyalty.

The best place I stayed in Tucson.  The rooms were renovated and comfortable. They overlooked the golf course and Santa Catalina Mountains. They had a small balcony, a perfect place for first coffee as the course was being watered and the mountains glowed in the morning sun.    Because I was working during the day, the family was happy to have so many entertainment options right on campus.  The swimming area kept my young son happy. He is a young seal in the water.  The location is at the end of North Campbell and there are plenty of restaurants and shops in the vicinity.  If I was spending the day in one stone area, I would be dropped off and they had the rental car to cruise town and explore.    It all worked well from La Paloma.

This may be the largest Starbucks I have seen east of Ohio!   At least 5,000 square feet, it feels like a small theater, more than a cafe. Plenty a seating with tables, chairs and more relaxed furniture in the corner. Easily 15 foot ceiling which does impact the acoustics, but almost feels like being outside. A 50 foot wall long black and white panel that pulls the room together.   Yet, when I was there at 4:30 on a recent afternoon, the operation was being run by only 3 baristas, including drive through service. Impressive that they managed to sweep and clean up the place during their shifts.   Menu was standard for the Green Mermaid, although the display case was somewhat depleted given the time of day. I snared the final slice of lemon pound cake - my endulgance for the week. It was as tart and sweet as always.   While still not a true fan of Starbucks, this place isn't bad.

This is a new drive thru Starbucks on RT. 541 (Burlington-Mt. Holly Road), is one of their smaller designs, yet with ample comfortable seating for those who prefer to sip in or work, and a tight bar area with two cashiers and snack offerings. The staff is skilled and friendly, and keep the joint humming and clean.   I stopped in after court in Mt. Holly, in need of a caffeine jolt to keep me sharp through the rest of a dreary Thursday. My grande low fat latte did the trick as I watched the laptops burying their noses in daily labor.   Wish I liked nitro cold brew, because that was very popular with the peeps there. There must be something to it, but I just don't like the bitterness.   Regardless, in the land of Dunkin it is nice to have an upgrade available.

The Korean double fried chicken wings were excellent with their Secret Spice Sauce. Crisp, hot spicy and a little sweet. Made from scratch upon ordering so it took 20 minutes for them to be prepared. Next time I'll call ahead to save time. Great to have these near best of breed wings so close at hand, rather than having to travel to another county to get a fix.  Yet, that "Homemade Hamburger" needs to be reconsidered and hopefully reinvented. It was awful. The ground beef was a poor quality with pieces of fat and other nasties that fell apart upon biting into the sandwich. The slice of red onion was tough and bitter. Their signature burger sauce was okay, but really added nothing positive to the taste. A Sriracha mayo would have been a better option, or something like Russian dressing. The potato wedges were quite good, but it would take alot of convincing to get me to try that thing again.   So, it was the best of times and the worst of times at CHKN & BBQ. Stick with what you do well and move away from what you don't if you want to succeed.

Quintessential working person's dive bar, with a laid back atmosphere, decent kitchen, and friendly barkeeps.    Fair beer selection on tap, but not a craft beer haven. A great place for a Burger or Cheesesteak, especially on the days that they are a special low price. Open for breakfast for the early birds.  See their website for updates and events.    The outdoor patio is a great addition.  Enough TV screens to satisfy the most diverse taste in entertainment.  Last night, World Cup, Yankees, and Mexican soap opera played their unique games.  If you prefer live entertainment, it is available certain nights with local bands, or a customer acting out his comedic fantasy.  I enjoyed a guy in a Rod Stewart wig hitting on the lovely bartender with one pick up line after another, until we were all listening and shouting suggestions.  It was a kick! The dude was funny.   Puss N Boots. Definitely a great place for a hot plate, a cold brew, and a hearty laugh; all at great prices.

When you walk into a pizza joint for lunch at 2:30 and the chef is gone and nothing can be prepared, the first impression cannot be good.    So it was today when I dropped by BellItalia of Trenton (not Bella Italia according to the sign and menu), a shoe box take out dive that had absolutely nothing to offer but its menu and the advice that I could order in the future and they would deliver.    'Fraid not, gentlemen.    There is nothing "Bella", nor even "Italia" about this place.  So many better options in town it would be a shame to waste even one meal on this outfit.

Still a great cheesesteak after several more visits over the past couple of years.    The BIG STORY is the availability of a credit card processor that saves the time and expense of bringing enough cash or using the captive ATM.    The sandwiches come to ten bucks with a drink, so it pays to be ready for the splurge.

Walking over to Viet Tofu to check out their Banh Mi and Spicy Tofu, I found the storefront empty.   The sign on the front door said they were temporarily closed for renovations and would reopen soon.   I'll try again in a few months.

This site attempts to do too many things.   In addition to housing a Dunkin' Donuts, it is also a Getty Gas Station, mini-deli, and lottery dispenser.  As a result, the place feels disorganized like it has a bad case of Attention Deficit Disorder.  Parking is limited and a bit dangerous with all the different uses bringing vehicles in from all directions.    The DD coffee is average.  The Bagel with Lite Veggie spread was toasted automatically, although I prefer it not, causing a cream cheese melt and a small mess in my car.  The taste was decent for a mass produced bakery product, but these rounders will never be mistaken for quality bagels.    It will do when time is very short and an injection of caffeine and a few calories are needed to survive through the first court appearance of the morning. Other than that, this is not a shop I would select for a morning munch nor java stop.

This is a tough spot to survive for a pizza shop due to its awkward location at the intersection of Buck and Holland Roads. Too many odd angles to negotiate unless your heading south on Holland. Still, it is worth your patience and driving skills to go to Giovanni's if you want a hot lunch or dinner to bring home.   I picked up a Sweet Italian Sausage Sandwich with sauteed onions and green peppers (sauce on the side) today. I called ahead and when I arrived 15 minutes later it was being kept hot on top of the pizza oven, wrapped and ready. It was a jumbo sammy, jammed with enough for at least two people, it's contents cut into bite size pieces of sausage and smaller virginized pepper & onion. The roll was a little soft due to being housed in one sided aluminum paper which trapped all the moisture inside, but even so it was an enjoyable lunch experience.   I managed to consume half before my warning lights alerted me to reaching overfull capacity. Repackaged the rest for home delivery.   Overall, a very good submarine @ just under $10 for a zoftig belly buster.

I stopped in this Ruby Tuesday's restaurant last night in the mood for a burger and beer. I sat at the small square bar, ordered a Sam's Winter Lager, but allowed myself to be distracted by the specials menu. So, rather than a burger I went with the Shepherd's Pie @ $11.99.   Big mistake.  While it included a reasonable salad bar, the "pie" itself was smaller than its photograph on the menu. It came in a cast iron skillet, perhaps 6" in diameter at the top, and smaller at the base. It was primarily instant mashed potatoes above a ground beef gruel. I counted 5 peas. There was little beef and mostly a gravy-like substance beneath the top layer. Pathetic.   I made the best of it, and did not request a better meal. I don't like being that guy. Still, it showed that Tuby Ruesday was willing to sell overpriced garbage dishes without qualms for quality nor their reputation.   If they don't care what they offer their customers, neither will we care to find out what comes next. In this business, one strike is all you get.  Complete ripoff.

Needed a fast bite between afternoon and evening meetings and decided to hit up the McDonald's on Horizon Boulevard, Bensalem, PA. I seem to prefer Mickey D's recently when in this "no time to sit and eat" mode. Starting with their surprisingly tasty crisp fries, to their less compelling, but still decent Quarter Pounders, this oldest of national burger franchises has really upped its game in the last few years.  I enjoyed my repast, even while slumming in the car as I drove to the next destination. Hot taters, oniony beef pucks, soft bun and cold chill drink, we're just about what I wanted and needed.   Not that I want this to become a habit (bad one), but I have to admit I felt a childlike sense of happy abandon in chowing down on this almost forbidden micro pleasure.

I just checked the Village Bagel website to confirm what I had read before; "...You will not be disappointed...Stop by..."  Well, when I arrived at their shop after a 30 minute drive from home to sample their product, I followed the directions posted on their windows to call in an order. No problem. Happy to comply.   Unfortunately, the friendly sounding woman on the line advised me that they were not conducting any retail business for the day, but only filling orders for Christmas. I could not walk in, nor order a breakfast bagel (onion w garden veggie & coffee), but would have to leave empty handed. Not even explaining my long drive, nor the absence of any notice on their website, let alone, Yelp, nor sign on their front door, could persuade her to extend a humanitarian exception and slice/smear a bagel for me.   Nope. I would have to drive away without satisfaction.   Ho hum...  Merry Christmas to you, too!   There wasn't any room at the inn, either. At least I am in good company.

It's convenient to have a local parcel place to take care of shipping issues.   The shop is big for its purpose, and seems a bit sparsely inventoried.  When I worked for a big firm, our mail room looked more stacked and ready to wage a mailing barrage around the world. Still, everything here is computerized. Give them your phone number to find your account (or make one), and give them a name and city where you want to send your package, and in a second they have all the known names/addresses there, and you select the right one.    Small world and getting smaller by the minute.   The only real downside is the expense of using their services.  I just spend $70 to send a very small package to California overnight.  Makes me think I should set up an account directly with FedEx or UPS.    This charge felt like I had just been held up on the stage coach from Bisbee to Tombstone. These robbers didn't even bother to wear masks.  But, I sure felt someone's hand in my pocket.

"....with a name like Smucker's...  Couldn't resist, but the slogan does hold true.  If their food isn't good, they will hear about it in a bad way.    Fortunately, most of the salads and side dishes found in the display are very good.  The service is friendly and prompt, and you can even taste a sample of anything that interests you.  My favorites are the Baked Lima Beans, Chicken Salad, and Rice Pudding; all of which I can eat in one meal either in the tiny sitdown areas, or as take home.  Also, the jarred goods on the right hand side of the shop are worth a look for some esoteric Pennsylvania Dutch/Amish treats.  Their Corn Relish is great!   Still only open Thursday through Saturday, it is best to get there early for the freshest selection.  Eat it quickly to enjoy its peak flavors.

Slowly, but surely, Bagel Train has become my primary bagel source.  While I still miss Bagel Junction in Newtown, the B Train has found a way into my heart and stomach with regularity.  My son and I stop in once a week before school to grab a breakfast of Onion Bagel, Butter and Swiss. He goes for Yoohoo, while I pour my first coffee of the day.    The bite, texture and taste are exactly what we love (and kvell over).  This has become our routine. Bonding is a wonderful side dish with the bagels.    Given the importance it has taken on in our lives, and the high quality and exceptional taste sensations generated, a bump to 5 Stars is overdue.

A certain political party in Bucks County had its annual Jefferson Dinner at Pen Ryn Mansion last week.    The entire locale is incredibly pretty for Bensalem, Pa., but the Delaware River still has its charm, and the building and landscaping there are very nice.  There is plenty of parking and if you have time you can stroll down to the banks of the river and watch the dusk settle in and the lights of Burlington, NJ come up across the river.      The dining facility is ornate with heavy curtains and chandeliers, but although dated, it does give off an air of historical pretense.  If there is an issue it is with the HVAC.  On this relatively warm October night, the bar area was downright hot, and the large banquet room only a little more comfortable.  Of course, all the hot air from the podium may have had something to do with that.    Pen Ryn would be a nice place for a traditional wedding or other large format celebration.  This is my third of fourth visit, and it is always an attractive, if not completely comfortable place to spend the evening with a few hundred of my closest friends.

Another variation of the endless fastfood burger joints, this one a Wendy's.    Plenty of parking around the free standing building, but designed to have the only entrance door right near the drive through line.  Dangerous. Why not have them separated on opposite sides of the building to protect folks going in?    The dining room was empty at 2:30 in the afternoon.  Clean.  Plenty of tables, with seats all facing north and south.  I was looking for something easy for a late lunch and opted for the 4 for $4.  Fine print - you get a single sandwich of your choice, and must accept the 4 count chicken tenders, flies and a drink.  Want 2 burgers?  Tough luck. That's not how this deal is played.  Ridiculous!  Can't remember what I ate, other than it was hot and forgettable.  The tenders were average, and the French fries pretty good.  Large lemonade washdown.  Guess that's the point.  When the fries are the best part of the meal, there is a serious creativity problem at Chez Wendy.  Ho - hum.

Coming here directly from Farmers' Best Supermarket on Adams is probably not fair to Farmers'.  But, we needed a few things in the way of kitchenware that Kobawoo had in large amounts.  It was impossible not to notice how clean and organized this place was compared to where we had just been.  Better lighting.  Broader aisles.  Smaller space, yet nicely laid out.    Strong display of serving vessels and cooking utensils for both the home and professional kitchen.  Only thing it lacked was plastic chopsticks for restaurant use, so bamboo would not have to be wasted on a single use.    Overall, a good place for Asian cooking needs, and one to which I would gladly return.
This is where the deliciously creamy Goodnoe Ice Cream is made.  You have to go to the Goodnoe Ice Cream shop on Sycamore Street to actually buy it.  Very worth the trip.

Still a great place for lunch or dinner in Newtown.   My son loves the Buffalo Chicken Cheese Steak and it is one of the first things he wants when he returns for a visit.   I had Penne Aglio Olio with Spinach tonight, and it was very good.  The side salad needs a little work to bring it up to par, but that is a small nit in an otherwise enjoyable dinner.

First rate gelati with an abundance of fruity flavors to mix with the heavy creaminess of the custard. Darkest Cherry, or Green Apple, or Mango Tango, or something like that are all treats.   Word on the street is that this Rita's is the most successful in their national franchise. For a little barn that is closed between Thanksgiving and May Day that is quite a feat.   Come to Newtown for ice cream and other sweet creamies. So many choices in a small area, and a great town to walk around while ice creams drips from your chin.

At the intersection of Stoopville Road and Washington Crossing Road in Lower Makefield, Village Market has been dishing out good breakfast and lunch sandwiches for decades.  Their recent upgrade adds to its luster, and the newly engineered intersection makes it easier to get in and out with risk of bodily harm.  It is easy to miss the deli section in the white building next to the Exxon station, but try to stop in.  VM has a deserved reputation among locals for hearty breakfast sandys and over-stuffed burritos, way above average lunch options (especially Cheesesteaks and Chicken Salad subs and wraps, and even decent fresh coffee. It is primarily a take out joint, and the parking is adequate.  The staff moves efficiently and knows what the regulars want.    There is a bit of confusion as to who has jurisdiction over Village Market.  Although much closer to the center of Newtown, it is actually in Lower Make.  Don't let that squabble deter you from sampling their homemade menu.  But, if you have the misfortune of being pulled over for speeding on Rt. 513, the police who will be stopping you and issuing the summons are from Lower Makefield, so don't blame Newtown.

A dozen or so visits to Bagel Train has led me to the opinion that it deserves an upgrade to four stars.  Perhaps, my taste bud memories have waned, allowing me to create new images of my childhood in the City.  Maybe, I am feeling more at home standing in line and interacting with the good folks working there.  Too, it could be the realization that BT's "baagels" are less expensive than the recently departed Bagel Junction (of blessed memory).  Regardless, I now look forward to the first bite of these creations, and that deserves recognition via promotion.

The third generation of Goodnoes are now in the ice cream business, carrying on the rich and creamy family tradition. While no longer occupying the history corner restaurant (great loss), they have the same ice cream that made the name synonymous with excellent ice cream, sundaes, malts, etc.  The dairy still turns out the same delicious flavors that your grandparents loved and waited for on Saturday nights.  Newtown has an embarrassment of ice cream riches.  Sweet Pea, Owowcow, Zebra Striped Whale and Goodnoes.  All are good in different ways. But, for my ice cream dollar, Goodnoes is still first in my heart and stomach.   It is worth a visit to Newtown to try all four places and decide for yourself.

Saw the movie, About Time, last night.  This isn't a movie review site, but if you are looking for theaters it does not hurt to get an idea about what is playing.   This was a feel good movie with enough suspension of disbelief required to last for weeks.  If you enjoy time travel (who doesn't like going back in time), then this one is for you.  It is light, funny, and endearingly idiosyncratic.  Yes, it leaves many questions unanswered, but that is not the point of romantic comedies.    The acting is believable, and the London and Cornwall locales attractive.    Looking for something to do next Sunday night, check this one out if you want a movie that leaves you with a smile, rather than a grimace.  If you want dinner with that, do what we did and go to Misto Diner for an above average Chinese meal first.

Horsham Donuts just hit the big time.  It is joining up with Donut Connection, the national round hole franchiser, to take advantage of the marketing clout that name provides.    From the donut lovers perspective you gotta hope that this in no way interferes with the excellence of the current fare.  Horsham bakes up some high quality dough rings, with a broad variety that has captured the affection of the masses.    As long as their hard earned reputation for great donuts doesn't suffer, who could complain about a name change?  My last taste of their Glazed babies, Cherry, and Chocolate rounders, left me in a trance-like state.    Or was that just a wonderful sugar rush?

I don't quite get the Bubble Tea craze, but I did stop in to this one tonight to pick up something warm and stimulating for the drive north.   I took out a Bubble Green Tea, and discovered from the friendlies that the shop was under new ownership and had changed its name to, "Tea Chat."  The joint was a narrow corner store, but clean and inviting.  The prices for the various teas and smoothies were quite reasonable at between $3 and $5.    Good luck to the new enterprise.  May your Boba always snap when you chew them!

Miller's Ale House is a chain out of Florida with outlets from Nevada/Arizona, to right here in River City.  It sits on Rt. 1 (Southbound side) in Langhorne right up against Oxford Valley Mall.  It is easy to miss.    Perhaps, it should be.  It is basically a sports bar with televisions abounding, large beer offerings (the usual suspects in national brands, plus some better known smaller breweries.  The food is what we have come to expect from similar houses - lots of fried food, burgers, wings, salads, even an occasional lobster has been seen sitting at the bar.  It is all basically okay, but nothing worth going back for a second time, unless you find the bartenders or waitresses to your liking (then you are not going for the food).   Given a choice, I prefer the genuine local establishments, which in Newtown are The Clubhouse, Isaac's, Friends, and even The Green Parrot for either a comfortable place to drink and smooze, or watch the Olympics.  We all know our favorite dives.    Miller's is an adequate alternative, but never feels like home.

Still @ 4 Stars.  Returned to try a little Sushi in the form of Salmon Skin Roll.  It was well presented, tightly wrapped, and tasty.  Very happy for the low salt soy sauce option on the table.    Also ordered Chicken Pad Thai, and while amply plated with plenty of fresh ingredients, the taste was not what I expected from this Thai dish.  Wrong spice mix to my palate.   And, my pet peeve again presented itself.  Although there were only 3 tables occupied in the house, we were all seated on top of each other, disturbing the tranquility of the well crafted environment.  I just don't want to eavesdrop on what the next booth has ordered before as they show off for their guest, nor how many sushi roll orders should be eaten in vs. taken home to the kids.   Give us all a little space and we can enjoy our East Sushi in peace.

A business lunch brought 7 of us to Miller's late last week.  The house looks a lot better in daylight. Plenty of room, and large windows that open wide on beautiful days to give the feel of eating out on the spring porch.  Small choice of draft beers, but enough to keep most people happy. Service was fine, especially the fact that they have some extra large booths that fit all of us comfortably.  Most of us chose from the salad menu, but there was a burger in the group, too.  When served, although 5 different names, they all looked basically the same with each having been accessorized slightly differently. It was funny, and they were okay, but not particularly memorable. We talked more than we ate, so it didn't make much difference.  If we end up working a project together it will be all worthwhile.

La Stalla Market on Sycamore Street, Newtown, Pa, does a very good job creating a traditional Italian deli in the heart of this old town. Plenty of cheese wheels, dried sausage, breads, sweets and takeout meals for the asking; all in a small shop that smells as great as it looks.   I was there to grab a sandwich for lunch. They have a long list of choices that can be wrapped, rolled or sliced-breaded. I went with their turkey BLT on a 12" crusty roll. It was huge. Stuffed with enough ingredients for two meals and smeared with aoili mayo that pulled the various tastes and textures together. The roll was excellent, with hard crusty exterior and well aerated sourdough flavor within. Definitely, best of breed master baker. Chomp and chew required strong jaw and teeth, and boy was it a worthwhile challenge.   It was a great sandwich experience.   Ate half, and rewrapped the remainder for later consumption (son devoured it as soon as I got home). $10 for two meals makes the price very reasonable.   In a land full of mediocre pizza shops, it is so nice to have another vision of Italian cuisine so well represented.

It is hard to get too excited about a multiplex cinema unless the IMAX seats vibrate and massage me during the show.  Otherwise, "seen one ya seen 'em all."   While IMAX is an improvement over the standard movie experience, I find the 3-D versions of movies to offer little beyond the regular mode.  After a few minutes my mind adjusts to the distorted perception that things are flying at me, and I forget that I am supposed to be having a different reaction.  Too, the cockamamie glasses are always dirty, requiring me to clean them, or suffer through  smudgy vision.  Just not worth the extra couple of bucks for me.   Otherwise, Neshaminy AMC has comfortable seats and convenient drink holders, which is a plus, but aside from the old Newtown Theater, almost all movie houses have similar conveniences.    Parking is fairly good, but a short walk is needed, and the snack bar is loaded with everything a movie goer generally wants, unless something healthy is what they seek.

The Bowl inspired Grill (sic) is a relatively new entry in the luncheon wars in beautiful downtown Trenton, NJ. It is located on South Warren Street, the cobblestoned lane that manages to look good despite all the degradation around it. It is an Americanized Mexi house that does it's best to imitate Chipotle, with bowls, burritos or wraps made to order as you select the rice, beans, meat, salsa and drink of choice being constructed behind the counter. All this for around ten bucks.  We walked down last week. The room was empty, but for one table when we arrived at 1:00. The two women working the assembly line were friendly and knew their craft. I ordered a bowl with brown rice, red beans, shredded beef, corn salsa and cilantro. It felt hefty on the plastic tray.   The result was tasty and filling, but far from special. Then again, I don't frequent Chipotle for the same reason. I prefer the authentic version of Central American cuisine so prevalent and delicious around this capital city. Yet, for a downtown foodery it certainly carries it's weight and contributes some variety to the lunch scene in these parts.

The anti-Starbucks. In sight of its backdoor. Pour your own and no waiting. Decent coffee and snacks. Inferior view, but no seating required. I'm not saying 7/11 is a true alternative to the Green Mermaid, but if you strip away the atmospherics and even the pretension, and the antisocial, illegal, parking in front so some can get their daily grind going without the trouble of finding a safe place to stash their wheels, what you are left with are taste and price.  On both counts, the Lucky Numbers win - with parking to spare.

Marcos Pizzeria has reopened! The fire that closed Marcos and its neighbor put a serious dent in my pizza diet, and I can imagine others felt similarly.  It is located in the Village of Newtown Shopping Center, just behind the Wendy's. Once a week I go for a couple of slices (tomato pie and traditional eggplant), and never fail to run into someone I knew in the same frame of mind needing a pizza to brighten our day. The few times I was there for dinner, I had a parmigiana or aglio olio pasta dish. Satisfying. The downside has been that the shop is small and not comfortable enough for extended dining.  Too, in winter when the door opens, everyone is greeted with a cold blast, which chills both the patron and the food. There are other pizza options in Newtown, and I frequent most of them.  They are all decent, if not attaining the Trenton nor Brooklyn pizza pantheon. But, who can travel to those places every time you crave a T.pie?  Right now, Marcos offers me the most positive "Pizzaxperience" in town.

There are more reviews for this PennDot Licensing Center to be found on a separate page labeled, PennDot.    Not sure why two pages are needed, but perhaps it adds to the chances of being found here.    The Commonwealth is really making an effort to make these places more consumer friendly.  I was able to renew my driver's license in less than ten minutes.  However, their interworking with other agencies remains problematic.  When Social Security and Homeland Security are required to be involved in securing a new license, the process is awkward, delayed, and guaranteed to frustrate.   Can't blame the Governor for the issues raised by the Feds, but there ought to be an easier way.

Jersey hyper market comes to Bucks and shows up the local talent Acmes and Giants with huge selection and cutthroat pricing.  It has everything those other guys have, and so much more in a shelf by shelf comparison.   More labels.  More variety.  More choice.    It may not have been the wisest thing to make a first visit on a Saturday afternoon when the place was full of Sunday pushcart drivers, as the number of near misses with the granny class kept me on edge and hoping my auto insurance comprehensive would cover any property damage.  Too, the cost of things was not always clear on their price cards below the items, especially the discounted products.  A bit more clarity would be a big help.    Other than those nits, Shop Rite - Yardley is a great place to stock up.  We came in needing a few things, and walked out with a large cart full of everything else we would use in the months ahead.    Next time, a weekday evening will be explored to see if the overall experience will feel less risky.

I must confess.  I don't like malls. They seem dinosaurs in the 21st Century.   Perhaps, part of the problem are the anchor tenants; those big department stores that try to be all things to all people, and end up being quite the opposite - offering a sad retail experience that feels lifeless.  So it was when I decided to go to Sears to purchase a replacement for my dearly departed 12 year old Hoover canister. I knew I was risking a bout of depression, but throughout my life Sears was the place where appliances were plentiful.  My grandfather shopped there for refrigerators and washing machines with me in tow, and I would continue the custom with my son.   Not much to report beyond the fact that our saleswoman was knowledgeable and honest enough to point me in the right direction even when the price was lower.  Ended up with a Hoover Whirlwind in light blue. Good price.    After putting it together at home, and running it in the family room and a bedroom, I can candidly say that it sucks.  That is a good thing.

While down in this neck of the woods we decided to check out this Home Depot's garden department to pick up a few more bags of mulch. It is basically the same layout as every other HAD, with their planting inventory primarily outside, and the soil, fertilizer and mulch stacked high in the adjacent parking lot.   I went over to the cashier to pay for what we wanted, and picked up a tray of petunas on sale nearby. Receipt in hand I went back to the wagon and drove it over to the mulch. The dude with the weight lifting vest met me there and helped load the bags in back. At $3 per bag, it was the regular price. (Note: It is on sale now for $2.)  The home garden is looking good with this dress up. Will go back this afternoon for another load at the discount price. Maybe look at more annual color on the borders.   I'm still not a HD lover, but do admit that they are hard to beat on many things.

Two Slices and a Drink Review  Stopped into Peppi's Pizza & Pasta after shopping at the Giant Supermarket in the same Shoppes at Flowers Mill commercial center.  Narrow in front, with dining room in back, this is a typical pizza parlor with booths, and a vast array of pies for examination, temptation and ordering.  I asked that my two regulars be "well done," in order to reawaken the taste slumbering within after extended time under hot lamps and hungry eyes.    The slices were as requested and picking each aloft showed the crust to be firm and able to supports its load.  The tomato sauce was on the salty side, as was the mozza.  Would have preferred a sweeter bite. Still, that's just a matter of taste, and many people like it that way.   Service was friendly and prompt, and the free refill of the soft drink, a nice touch.   Certainly worthy of a pizza snack when out and about.

This US Post Office in Morrisville, PA is about par for the course for an aging government facility. Parking in front. PO boxes to the right and services to the left upon entry. Queue of patrons longer than it should be at 1:30 in the afternoon, but only one guy working the counter until another co-worker got off lunch, an no postmaster in sight to address the service shortage.   Still, when my turn, the dude was friendly and attentive. He helped me out with the request for commemorative stamps for the office mail. Even made suggestions to be sure I saw everything. All the stamps were the forever variety; a big plus. Purple Heart, military service metals, team sport balls and Janis Joplin peaked my fancy. Janis?! Somebody in the institution really appreciates rock history. Thinking of framing those.  The place needs better lighting and a way to bring help to bear when it is busy, yet no major complaints given I was in and out in under 10 minutes.

Decent enough bagel and friendly service, but it is somewhat amazing that there is so much disparity between one Manhattan Bagel shop and another; this one on Bustleton Avenue in the Russian part of Northeast Philly landing on the lower end of the spectrum.   Crust not as firm/crisp as others nearby, and far fewer roasted onion flakes attached. Still, more than adequate veggie cream cheese coverage within to help offset the shortcomings.   Their coffee is strong and holds its own for a breakfast blend. Been sipping it for several hours and it hasn't turned bitter.   Will certainly do until a real bakery shows up and turns out a Real McCoy bagel, that knows how to bathe well before baking.

Fu Wah (Happy Children) is a small Chinese shop in an old strip center on Olden Avenue Extension, Ewing, NJ. It has the advantage of 8 booths/tables for the eat in crowd, in addition to a brisk take out business. The whole family pitches in during summer. Mom took my order at the front counter. Dad woked it up in the kitchen, and young son served me with a spirited, "Enjoy your lunch."  I would have if the hot and sour soup did not have a large lump of pork fat below the surface, and the sesame chicken wasn't all dark meat with little sauce to stir into the yellow dyed fried rice.   Get the picture? Not the greatest effort by these happy children.

Bagel Train remains my favorite bagel vendor in the area.   Always a curiosity why people from Bagel City (born and raised there myself) think they know rounders better than anyone else, or that there is any uniformity among Big Apple bagels. There really isn't. I've had great ones on the Westside, and crappy ones in Soho. I've bitten into rock hard dense losers in Canarsie, and lovely light crunchers in Elmwood.   So, don't listen to anyone who says they know what's best for anyone but themselves. If you love them, that's all that matters. Even if you never spent a day of your life in the City That Never Sleeps!

Hunan Wok (identified as only, "Hunan" on the sign above the shop), is a fairly typical Chinese/American suburban restaurant in the Fairgrounds Shopping Plaza just outside downtown Mt. Holly.  The menu is what you expect to find in such places.  It is set up primarily for takeout, but offers a few tables for those who prefer to eat in, as I did.    My lunch consisted of Sesame Chicken, Fried Rice, & Wonton Soup.  It was served to me in the takeout containers, with plastic utensils.  The soup was straight up chicken bouillon and the wontons were thick skinned and of average quality.  The Chicken itself was plentiful with a mix of white and dark meat, breaded, and drowned in dark amber goopy sauce, with sesame seeds sprinkled on top.  It was not bad, but undistinguishable from most other such joints.  The rice had been prepared in the same soup mix as the wonton, and carried the same yellow color.  More than enough, but not worth carbing out on.   Service was fine.  The proprietress was engaged and efficient.  The price was under $7 with a soft drink.

Was a time Dunkin Donuts was about the best coffee/cake sweets house in the nation because of their consistency. No matter where your caffeine bug bit, there was a DD nearby that could be counted on to offer java and fried dough that was similar from place to place.   Maybe it's because there are so many coffee houses and high quality roast cafes around these days, but it has been a long while since I truly enjoyed a cuppa joe from Dunkin. Could be the quality of water has declined, or that the beans have suffered from lax quality control or increased competition from all the new java outlets, but even the sweet dough lacks the enjoyability of the old days.   Hence, I was not surprised when I stopped in to this DD/Baskin Robbins joint to give me a boost the other night, and the small coffee and sour cream rounder were both hopelessly ordinary and lacking in life energy. In a word, they sucked.   Saving grace? The shop was large and had ample seating. The people working there were pleasant and engaged well with customers.   Ho Hum.

One of those old fashioned stainless steel and glass diners from the 1950's, that is still pumping out excellent breakfast fare for road warriors. Pulled in driving my late model Zipmobile, and when I returned, it had transformed into a 1958 Packard.  Just what I always wanted!  The staff was perfect for this stage.  Friendly, gregarious, and full of "Honey."    The French Toast was very good, too.  Enough egg, soaked through and through, and a caramelized texture where the super hot range had cauterized the surface of the bread.  If they had used real maple syrup rather than the mass produced prepackaged variety, it would have attained all star (5 Star) status.  Also needed a Cecilware coffee urn, rather than the newer Bunn for the best coffee.   I don't mind cutting corners to make ends meet, but in my fantasy the syrup comes straight from a Vermont Sugar Maple to my plate.

More a cafe and less a bakery at the intersection of Holland and Buck Roads in Southampton, PA, this Eastern European house is well decorated with a large dining room and four private rooms for group breakfast and lunch. The menu is very interesting with the use of standard ingredients prepared by hands trained in formerly socialist republics.   I ordered the Tomato Feta Omelet. It was cooked in a personal sized polished steel pan and served to me still burning hot in that instrument, on an oval wooden insulating plank. The outer egg was almost a souffle texture and the taste was great. It came with two chunks of bread and a small dish of sweet butter. The bread had a crisp crust warm enough to melt the spread. It was also excellent and left me wishing for more.   The final surprise was the brewing of La Colombe coffee; strong enough to take immediate notice, and a pitcher of milk for mixing to my preferred shade of auburn. It was so good!  Service was efficient and beautifully accented.   This was a surprising and awesome meal at a very reasonable price. It was good to visit Kiev for a few minutes.

"Anything worth doing is worth overdoing." - Albert Einstein  And so it is with bubble tea shops in Philly Chinatown.  You can't cross the street without seeing bobba signs on every corner. Tapioca is definitely having an amazing resurgence. I don't get why gummy sweet goobers are so popular, but I'm obviously in the minority.   Still, I enjoy good milk tea as much as the next guy, and Vivi Bubble Tea has it's fair share of that. The space is larger than expected, with a large room with group tables in back for all your friends. Service is efficient and friendly. I had my almond milk tea in hand in under a minute. Impressive.   The tea was good and exactly what I needed to continue with my shopping list and Artiva haircut. Steamy hot, mildly sweet, sufficiently nutty. $4.   Noticed that Vivi offered fried chicken wings. Piquing my curiousity, I made a mental note to give them a try next time I needed a nosh while in Ctown.

Be Well Bakery & Cafe does it right.  Not only is the house cozy and spacious, the java very good and the bakery products excellent, but it is all wrapped into a business philosophy that promotes community, creativity, healthy living and complete genuineness.   All very noble, right? But, let's get back to their house goodies for a second. I was tempted by their lemon tart in the display case. I love lemon bars, so I figured, why not? It was awesome! Creamy tart/sweet lemon filling, thin, flakey crust, plump, cool blueberries sitting on top. An orgy in my mouth.   There are a lot of good bakeries and coffee houses these days; not as many in combination. Be Well is certainly one of the best of the genre in the region.   All this in a beautiful part of Montgomery County, just down the road from Bryn Athyn Cathedral and Historic District. Worthwhile drive with Be Well as the final destination.

As federal agencies go, USCIS sets the standard for how to treat people right.   The new facility on North 41st Street in West Philly is a vast improvement over Callowhill Avenue. Not only is the space well renovated for more comfort during the inevitable security screening and wait for your appointment, but the guards and staff are trained to treat people with respect and assistance. They patiently repeat instructions and never lose their cool.   The meetings are conducted across a counter and thick glass wall, but the interaction remains low key and humane. They intend to answer questions fully, and will make formal inquiry when they do not have a reasonable answer on their computer screen. Don't forget that most visa files are not in Philadelphia, and they cannot see everything in them.  Street parking, metered or not, is usually available if you are driving, and the subway is not far away. Too, this part of town, just beyond the universities and at the edge of Powelton Village, offers many tasty distractions before or after conducting your business.

Round sugar cakes.  Sweeter than they should be, but fresh baked white cake base is tender and moist at least for a few hours. Many choices for dipped toppings in pretty colors, but all taste more or less the same. Really a confectionery more than a bakery.   To be avoided if sugar is a health issue for you. Best suited for kids whining for a candy fix, and other folks cheating on their diets.   Their Covid protocol should be improved a bit, because they allow you to come in to order and then wait outside for a staff person to bring your order out to you in 10 or more minutes. In hot or cold weather it gets a bit uncomfortable. Perhaps, a few folding chairs set up in the shade would alleviate the problem;  outdoor umbrellas, if necessary.   If you are into Ducks, don't forget your insulin.

We just enjoyed a very satisfying Good Friday breakfast at Jake's in Newtown. Plenty to eat, tasty and quite fairly priced.   It seems time to revisit the old review and adjust the ranking to 4 stars. I've eaten here often enough to become a fan.

Copa on South Street was my mainstay for several years after tai chi classes at The Painted Bride.  Those days are only for reminiscing now, but the taste and zest of Copabanana remains a trigger to my salivary glands. I have returned on occasion, and still loved the dirty ambiance, lusty margaritas, incredible Copaburgers (extra jalapenos, please), and the earthshaking Spanish flies...er...fries.  My son, now 12, has gone with me, so another generation is preparing to take its place where Friday night legends are made (and oft forgotten by Saturday morning).   What others Yelpers say about the conditions in the joint is true, but the best Tex-Mex food is always found in the dingiest hole-in-the-wall places.  Am I right? At least you know there are no cleaning agent molecules in the air to settle on your food.  These days I try to stop in before or after a 76'er game.  Copa still possesses that "in your face" attitude that I have loved, lo these many years. May it always be so. Amen!

After an afternoon of legalized public inebriation at the Winetoberfest, I needed a cup of java to bring me back to Earth before returning to my car for the winding journey home.  After striking out at two cafes that seemed disenchanted with the day's events and were keeping a very low profile, someone suggested we check out Mal's.    It was open and almost empty, but the counter looked inviting.  We sat on a couple of old spinners and ordered the Joe large and hot.  That is what we got. Fresh and it a supersized styro take away cup.  It was what just what the doctor ordered. Helped straighten me out.  The restroom was also a big help after the amount of liquids consumed in a short time.    We sat where we could see into the kitchen and watched as a Cheesesteak was prepared and sent out.  Looked okay, but I was not tempted.    For being my personal oasis yesterday early evening, Mal's gets my undying appreciation, and 3 Stars.  The staff gets 4 because they definitely came through for me.

On the second visit I opted to eat breakfast in house, and found it enjoyable with the smell of the baking bagels in the air, and the bucolic ambiance.  The Onion Bagel was as the first one - not quite crunchy enough.  Still, it was fresh and tasty, and at a great price of under $4. for the bagel and decent Jamaican Blue Mountain style java.    Easy to become a fan of this comfy chill.

You know those infinitesimal screws that are used to put eyeglasses together? The ones the size of baby gnats?   On a few occasions one of those poppy seed screws escaped and I returned to Steve for repair and consolation.  Each time he has graciously taken the pair into his repair shop and emerged a few minutes later with everything back in working order, cleaned and readjusted.  Yesterday, when a nose cushion fell off after about 5 years of wear, he replaced both free of charge and with a smile.    I have been very happy with the Prodesign frames from Denmark, and most of all with Steve Robbins for continuing to stand behind his product.    Does it get any better than that in the optometry world?    I think not.  5 Stars!

Steven Robbins has been providing my glasses (progressives and sunglasses) for over 15 years.  He has been in business in Newtown for three decades. His current location is next to Jake's Eatery and Domino Pizza, but don't let that deter you.  The shop is first class, and he and his staff make you feel comfortable right from jump.  Most important, he has a large collection of designer frames, at reasonable prices.  His turn around time is at the longest a few days.    Take a look around by yourself, or get the relaxed guided tour from Steve.  Kuerig Coffee Maker available with snacks while your stroll around the shop.  Definitely, worth a look before or after you have exhausted the alternatives.  Steven Robbins Eyewear is a winner.
A worthy successor to the Clemons Supermarket that was here for many years. Bigger store. Better prices. Good people.

Jinrong Li, Master Massage Therapist, LMT, runs this clean, state of the art spa on the north end of State Street in Newtown Borough.  She previously was the massage master at the Newtown Athletic Club.    Jin does an excellent job relieving neck and back pain in a comfortable setting.  She is also a Skin Care Specialist, although I have never utilized those services.

The price was great, but the bagel was way below average.   There was no differentiation between the crust and the meat of the bagel.  Just tasted like decent bread, but without any zest from a firm to crunchy crust, nor air pockets within to make the innards light and airy.  Clearly, RJ's has lost the recipe and won't admit it.   I appreciated the extra cheese in the sandwich and the coffee club pricing that brought my breakfast in at a skinny $3.  But, still, if it doesn't provide the bagel experience, what am I paying for?    New York Bagel around the corner on Parkway is a much better bagel option.

Newtown Chocolatier is a venerable and sweet institution in Newtown.  They recently moved from their old digs on State Street to Newtown Richboro Road (Swamp Road).  The new location is very well designed with plenty of display area to drool over.   The chocolate remains among the best home made sweets I have ever tasted.  The prices are higher than I like for a chocoholic, but I never complain about the quality.  Their arrangement with Whole Foods testifies to their dedication to their craft.   I am crazy for their peanut butter cups (Reeces), as well as their turtles and creams. But, to save a few bucks I usually go to the half price baskets to see what they are letting go at a discount. Yesterday, it was chocolate covered pretzels, cashew in milk chocolate, and solid milks, as well as a mix of darks.  Walked out with a bag at almost $10, that will satisfy my sweet tooth for a week or so.    Newtown Chocolatier is not a place I can frequent, but every now and then when I need a lift, it becomes my oasis.

Like most of us, Crowne Plaza Philadelphia-Bucks County looked better when it was younger.  What was once smooth, soft and supple, becomes lined, cracked and brittle.  This hotel is no different.   While it is still capable of putting heads on beds as it did 20 years ago, it no longer looks the part of a beauty queen.  The hair is streaked gray, the laugh lines more pronounced, and the plumbing often in need of repair.  Feel too hot?  Too cold?    Join the club.

Just discovered this place down State Street from my office. Full menu of massage alternatives. Chinese owner/practitioner.  First deep tissue massage was excellent for a long enduring herniated disk.   Prices higher than the cities, but the convenience and absence of driving, tolls, and gasoline costs, make this quite reasonable. Very comfortable environment and dedicated owner. Will definitely go again.  8.27.13 I have been back twice since the first visit/review.  Jinrong, the Master Massage Therapist, knows where the problem lies, and her hands find the pressure and trigger points to work.  An hour of a little discomfort when she digs in, but weeks of relief when she is finished opened the facet joints and calming the nerve roots.

Happy Hour Tavern is in a small commercial strip on Veteran's Highway, and quite easy to miss. Effort should be made to find it if a friendly working man's bar is what you like.    They have a fairly broad beer list, both tap and glass. The kitchen isn't exciting, but it does a decent job with the basics.  The important aspect is the atmosphere.  It is a cozy, unassuming place, where you can sit at the bar over a good crafty, shoot the breeze with some great storytellers, and walk out with change.    Most significantly, they have one of the rare shuffle board games - complete with sawdust needed to keep the oak surface slick.  Love that game. It ought to be an Olympic sport. Way more exciting than curling.    No. I wouldn't bring a date here, but when I want a hidden place to sit, think, smooze, and feel the cool weight of shuffle disks in my hand, Happy Hour Tavern does the trick.

While the drive thru moved well, the actual meal was not worth the wait.   It had been a while since I was this hungry and rushed enough to consider a BK stop.  This was one of those rare afternoons where I would eat at my desk.   The Mushroom Swiss Burger was a tasteless and textureless mush.  No wonder you can get 2 for $5.  They want to get rid of them. And, what about the Strawberry Lemonade?  The medium was about a half gallon of overly sweet, strawberry syruped, lemon wash ice water.    The condensation puddle on my desk slowly spread as I wondered what had possessed me to go for this meal.  Hunger makes for some bad choices.

This is a typical Chinese/American shop with the standard menu and lunch specials.  The effort at offering Thai dishes really doesn't work as everyone here is Chinese.    My General's Chicken was average, with dark amber gloopy sauce, but a nice portion of bird and rice.  As always, the ubiquitous sprigs of broccoli provided contrasting colors and a third food group.  The Wonton Soup had been prepared earlier and was dyed from whatever bouillon they were using.  Similarly, the Fried Rice had become dark from the same beef coloration.  Too thick wonton skins, and very dense filling of some kind of meat-food.    The taste was lackluster, but acceptable given the known parameters of such joints. At least, the room was well decorated and provided decent seating for eat in customers.  Service was fine.
There are two listings for this supermarket, with this one containing the store number. Be sure to look for both to find all reviews.

Who am I kidding?  I just went into Newtown Chocolatier to pick up some Peanut Butter Cups and Pecan Turtles for my son to bring to his grandparents for Easter.  While I was at it I asked the kind woman behind the counter if they had any broken pieces available.  She went into the back room and came out with a box of Milk Chocolate Strips.  I took every last nibble, and just tasted a bit before writing this update.    Daaaahhhhmmmm!  So good.  Sweet, smooth, instantly addicting.   5 Aces, and should have been so all along.

Basil Leaf appears to be closed or out of business.  The blinds are drawn closed, and there is poster board covering the glass door. A business card from the Health Department attached to the door asked for a phone call.  Hopefully, this is a temporary situation. Will keep Yelp advised...

Why does Star$$$ coffee always taste burnt? This is always my problem with Green Mermaid coffee.  The house coffee, without the benefit of heavy doctoring into lattes, capps, etc., is close to awful - harsh, bitter, skin peeling.  After being reformulated into the expensive brew, they are good drinks.  But, should you have to forgo the basics and rely on alchemy to be able to drink their stuff? Just asking.  The bakery goods are very nice, and the oatmeal breakfast is way above average.   The former Rexall never looked this good.  This is a great place to meet someone, and sit for a while. The bench sitters out front may take that idea to an extreme.  So, how to rate when there is so much going on and such extreme divergence of quality and experience?  "Meh," doesn't really reflect the gestalt. "Yay!" is really going too far. "OK," is just about right.

Dessert Review  We stopped in Adonio's Diner as the last stop after foot massage and Afghani dinner. Just wanted some java and something sweet to finish the night's run. They advertise that they had a bakery, so they had to have some nice stuff. Right?  Not quite.   Perhaps, because it was a long holiday weekend, and they gave the Baker's the day off, but all they had was cheesecake and apple crumb pie, neither of which looked to be made in house.  Ordered the apple slice anyway. I have never seen a smaller excuse for a diner dessert. Where most diners go out of their way to be excessive in these situations, Adonio's fit on a small saucer, practically flat and with little apple.The taste was industrial. The accompanying cuppa joe was also small and not very good.  The dinner customers were scoring large platters of whatever, and seemed satisfied. So, this was all about apres diner offerings.
