For unknown reasons, mine sucked. My friend's rice pudding was okay, but also miniscule compared to what most diners provide.   First and last impression.

Another great night for baseball at Arm & Hammer Park!   We watched a slow game through five innings, when no one seemed capable of mounting any offense, become a slug fest for the home town Thunder, who scored ten runs in two innings to put the game away.    All this under pink sunset clouds and Dollar Dog Night!    The adversary?  The Richmond Flying Squirrels.  Hard to imagine them even wearing pants.

Even with rain delays, Double AA Minor League Baseball as personified by the Trenton Thunder and the multi-named Waterfront Park/Arm&Hammer Park/Samuel Plumeri Park, offers a great all American experience that is great for family, friends, clubs, offices, and just solitary "Field of Dreams" lovers.    So, it is with a strong sense of having a beautiful and unique cultural experience that we return regularly to this Temple of Timeless Baseball to pay our respect and appreciation for the Great American Pastime.   It was so much fun to be back again.

I admit to not understanding the word order of this dental office in Holland, PA. Holland Family Dental makes alot more sense in English, but perhaps the point is that it is the correct linguistics in other cultures. Or, it could just be a mistake.   This office is on the lower level of this professional office building, and difficult to see from parking lot level. Once inside, there is a small waiting area with 6 chairs, a reception area with 2 women managing the intake and insurance operation, and three examination/treatment rooms with three hygienists and one dentist.   The expected first visit paperwork took a long while, but once that was accomplished, the wait to see the dentist, have x-rays, be examined and have a cleaning was fairly prompt. It ended up being an almost two hour visit.   Staff was efficient, friendly and explained the process well. They were patient with my questions, and made intelligent adjustments when I realized I did not have a necessary document.   My son seemed satisfied with his dental care. Hopefully, he won't need to return until next year's maintenance.

A fun and challenging course, especially for a public facility. Reminds of the wild rough and smallish greens of the British Open courses like St. Andrews in Scotland.    Apres golf in the cozy clubhouse is also a pleasure with a small bar and room for a small dinner party.   Also can't complain that it is the club nearest home.

After a pleasant exchange of messages with the owner of Langhorne Coffee House, I learned that the eggs are bathed in Italian Sparkling Water to create the light texture I described in my earlier review. Apparently, a family secret from the Old Country (the best kind of cooking secrets).    Knowing the truth of the matter, my impression has changed for the better.  An extra star is warranted, not only for the discovery of how the meal was made, but also for the wonderful extra step that continues a family tradition to be shared with the world.

Out of town friends chose to stay at the Radisson Hotel Philadelphia Northeast for a few nights while visiting the area.  I tried to tell them in advance that the hotel was not really in Philadelphia at all, but just beyond the city limits in Bucks County.  I also described the neighborhood as groaty old Route 1, auto dealers, by the hour motels, and garish liquor stores. They didn't care. The price was right, and they wanted to shop in the surrounding malls.    I went to see them there a couple of times. Parking was easy with a big lot.  The building looked a bit dated, but still highly functional.  Nice atrium in the lobby.  Cool black and whites of historic buildings in Philly.  A decent bar and free breakfast.  Clean, comfortable rooms.  Small bathrooms.   They managed to eat at several interesting places within a short distance (Steve's Prince of Steaks, Andy's Diner, Mission BBQ, Starbucks, to name a few).  They had nothing but good things to say about the place, other than they wished they had stayed in Center City, and could just put their horses in the stable and walk around town.    Maybe next time.

When Macy's does an after-sale sale, and the prices are up to 80% off the original, I can find useful, quality merchandise in the Men's Department.  The area is clean, organized and fairly relaxed for finding a style and quality I like.    At those discounts the value is greatly enhanced and it can compete with the deep dive price warehouses like TJ Maxx and Target.   Just picked up a couple of very nice sweaters at very attractive prices.  You don't even need to bring all those coupons that arrive in the mail or online.  The cashier will willingly give every discount available as you check out.

October 15, 2015 - Finally ordered their small, personal sized tomato pie as Ingrid had suggested months ago. Boy, was she right! The super thin crisp crust was a firm delight, and the mozza, chunky tomato pieces and spices exactly what was required. Simply stated, I loved it!

Bagel Board is a tiny corner bagel shop right next to the Croyden Train Station on Bristol Pike (Rt. 13). Location for commuters is perfect coming or going.  It is family owned/operated by a nice couple who seem to handle the rush efficiently and without loss of cool.    My Onion Bagel with Butter and Cheese was solid.  Firm crisp outer crust and light insides.  Wish they had Swiss Cheese, but the American was okay.  The sandwich was ready just as I capped my coffee.  Couldn't find milk, but had the choice of half & half or powdered creamer.    There is only one small table and a bench inside, so take away is the name of the game.  Given its proximity to the choo-choo, most wouldn't want to mange in the house in any event.  Not to mention that Dog & Bull is right down the street, where you can sit at the bar and have a cool one with your round one from the neighbor.  All aboard for Bagel Board! (Couldn't resist.)

I hadn't been to the Kopper Kettle Tavern for at least twenty years, perhaps indicating that I didn't feel an urge to visit this fish oriented restaurant on Bridgetown Pike in Trevose, PA. It was as remembered - cozy, slightly past its prime, with small bar and side dining room. Lots of old Formica tables and rolled stainless steel chairs. I took a stool at the bar and ordered a domestic light draft and the flounder dinner with pepper hash and baked potato.   Everything was pretty much average. No surprises in the brew. The fish was probably frozen, nicely breaded and fried in oil clean enough to have no secondary taste. The potato was not of a baking variety and remained dry no matter how much butter was melted into it. I liked the pepper hash, which was basically a spicy slaw. I mixed the tartar and shrimp cocktail sauces together on the plate from the two table rockets given me by the friendly bartender. They made for decent dipping of the fillets.   Maybe the sandwiches are the way to go at the Kettle, because the platter was twice the price, yet far less than double the value.

I guess I picked the wrong night to see all the hubbub at the Buck Hotel.  No cougars. Not even a stray pussycat. The barroom feels like a hunting lodge with a large angular bar, large TV's and curiosities hanging on the walls. Most pronounced; a 12' nutcracker standing guard over the operation.  This was a quiet Sunday night. No complaint.   I had a Chicken Salad sandwich and a glass of red.  Both were fine, but certainly I was not in search of the sweet spots on the food nor liquor menus.  They were enough for the moment.    It had been many years since my last visit, and but for the suggestion of meeting someone there for a conversation, I would not have chosen it this time.  Still, I was curious to see what had changed, and I could not detect much alternation.    Not a bad place for a Sunday evening, but to taste the full flavor it would likely require a return on a busier night.

Quick stop for a couple of slices and a drink on the way to a meeting.   The shop was nice in a slightly dated sort of way, and the kitchen was out front where everyone could see what was happening.  The service was friendly and prompt, as I told my waitperson I had a short time to get to my destination.  She complied.   The plain pizza slices were decent, but no better than what would pass for average in my part of the world.  Crust was firm enough to hold up its weight, but not overly crisp.  The sauce and cheese were okay, but not distinct.  Certainly a reasonable place to have lunch in the Far Northeast.  The dinner menu would be worth a try if in the area.    Thanks for lunch!

This Wendy's is freestanding in the parking lot of the shopping plaza that also contains Maryanne's Homestyle Restaurant.  It has not been completely modernized yet, but it is basically clean and ready for the effort Dave Thomas' ghost is making to upgrade their facilities. They do have that super soda dispenser that allows the customer to pour their own from a multitude of options.    We ordered the basic Dave's Single and Double, French Fries, and a drink.  Not bad, but both of our burgers were only slightly above room temperature.  They had obviously been cooked at some time before serving, and taken from a warming drawer to make the sandwich without a thought to reheating, or even putting the patty back on the grill for a couple of minutes before laying on the cold lettuce, tomato, cheese and onion.  Thus, while the veggies were cool and fresh, the main attraction suffered greatly by comparison, as the meat needed more heat to make it a full player.    Edible, but why couldn't they check on the patty and serve it at optimal temperature?    The soda machine was fun, though.  We probably should have gone to Maryanne's.

Grab-N-Go Bagel & Deli sits in the same commercial strip as Le Soleil Bakery and China Boys Restaurant. It is a neighborhood convenience store with a strong deli and grill department for good breakfasts and lunches.  Their inventory includes fresh bagels, muffins, and the right breads for making a superior Boar's Head sandwich.  They also offer Eight O'clock Coffee, the old A&P brand.  I have never seen it brewed for sale before.    My simple Onion Bagel, Butter and Swiss was prepared smartly, wrapped in foil and bagged in a minute.  With medium coffee, the $3.50 price was a true bargain.  Even better, the bagel was plump and freshly crisp on the outside and softly chewy within.  Can't be sure, but they may have gotten these babies from Bagel Stop over on Hamilton Ave.  I enjoyed the sandwich and the coffee cup sits on my desk as I write this review.  Still tastes good.   While this is not primarily a bagel shop, they can be forgiven because the rounders they do have are good, and the rest of their products are first rate, as long as you like Boar's Head.   Fast, friendly service.  Management on site.  Oh, Yeah....they also sell hookahs!

Not sure how this one got passed the filters, but Broad St Car Wash and Broad Street Car Wash are one in the same.    They both do a very good job cleaning my vehicle of all the ashiness that covers the sheet metal (polymer) after snow and salt get finished turning the wheels into a ghost.   If I had to choose between one or the other, I would probably choose Street, as St implies sainthood, and I doubt that this "Shine On Line" operation is on the short list for canonization.   Although, there are times I thank the Almighty for creating this automated wonder of the world.

The best place to stop before a long drive north or south coming from Newtown, this DD is hidden in the office/hotel complex next to the Hampton Inn, right of Rt. 95.    The coffee is decent (far better than the coffee @ the other DD in Newtown), and the staff organized and efficient.  While I am not a fan of their baked goods, push come to shove, I can be found with breakfast sandy or toasted bagel in my possession.  My 13 year old goes for milk and a couple of glazed rounders.    All in all, a reasonably tasty coffee at a good price, with a smiling face.  I don't need more than that at a caffeine oasis.

Great Valley Diner on Route 30 in Malvern, PA, sits in a former fast food structure, but aside from the general boxy nature of the space, it has escaped its past, and now looks something like what it is - a kitchen for three squares a day. It has a small counter with three or four spinners, and a dining room with a dozen or so booths and tables. The menu has all the usual suspects, especially breakfast, with a full list of egg/omelet, pancake/french toast possibilities and decent coffee served in red mugs.   I went with their Italian Omelet, but subbed feta cheese for their regular provolone.  No sweat.  It was served less than ten minutes later and was quite good, with crispy home fries and rye toast.  There were plenty of sweet sausage, onion and pepper in addition to the fresh feta.  Service was provided by a family member, who was pleasant and attentive.  My red mug was refilled twice without request.   Adequate parking. Exiting from the connecting shopping plaza onto Route 30, a bit confusing.   3.5 STARS

Another great early summer night along the Mighty Delaware watching Trenton Thunder baseball.    We dined exclusively from Chickie's and Pete's this time.  Italian Sausage with Pepper and Onions, Trenton Hot Dogs (stuffed with Potato, Pepper and Pickle), and Crab Fries. I was surprised at the quality of the Sausage, and how well it was grilled just before being slapped into the fresh Italian Roll.  Even the P & O were sautéed correctly.  The Fries were dosed in Old Bay Seasoning and came with a side of Creamy Cheese Dressing for dipping.  All that for under $23.    We were all smiles despite a loss by the home team to New Hampshire.

All the usual suspects on the breakfast and lunch menu at Hatboro TNT Diner, and surprisingly good prices, too. That explains the dominance of the social security crowd. They know a good deal when they see one.   True, this is formerly a Wendy's burger house, and the outlines of the old small version franchise from the 1980s shows. Still, it is clean, well run and has a friendly serving staff capable of keeping you coffee cup full and quality small talk. This is an adaptive reuse that still works in the 21st.   My french toast was a well made two slice platter which was enough for me, decent sausage patties and a bottomless cup of java. I've had worse at twice the price.   What it lacks in local color, it makes up for in solid deliverables and stirling repartee with staff.   Thanks, Debbie.

Once upon a time, Vince's Pizza in Yardley was a regular stop on the underground pizza railway running from Bristol up to Riegelsville.   It seems that somewhere along the way Vince's recipe or his touch for making good tomato pie got lost.  Today, my slices were doughy rather than crisp, not well reheated in the oven, and had a slightly bitter taste.  Too, it failed the most crucial pizza test - when lifted off the paper plate the point sagged like an old dog ear and immediately began to drip oil.  This was not the experience I was anticipating when I stopped in to renew acquaintances with one of my old haunts.    The price for the slices and small drink was just slightly above 5 bucks, which was great, but I would have gladly paid more for quality pizza.   Oh, woe is me.  How the mighty have fallen.

For the sake of comparison, I decided to visit the Giant Supermarket in the Flowers Mill Shopping Center, Langhorne, Pa., just to see how it stacked up against my local market in Newtown/Middletown.    Not very well, I'm afraid.   While as large or larger than my local Giant, the layout was inferior, and the space felt dark from poor lighting.  It was difficult to find certain items that were not where they logically belonged (i.e., Bubba Burgers). So, I found myself wandering down aisles thinking that there was something wrong with my vision.  No. It wasn't me.    Service was fine, and the cashier very friendly.    Still, my neighborhood store retains my loyalty.

1/3/2016 - Finally made it here for dinner. The Tomato Pie (w. mushrooms) was excellent.  The Caesar Salad, not so much. Better to stick with what Palermo's does best and leave the greens to a garden master.

Standard pizzeria on Mill Creek Road, Levittown, PA. This place is in a tiny commercial strip, a double wide storefront with kitchen/counter to the right and dining room to the left. Strictly a slice, pie and steak joint. Management is friendly and clearly happy for your business.   The food is what you'd expect from a traditional northeastern Mexitalian pizza parlor. The pies are competently made and the cheesesteaks are loaded with chopped beef, cheese and whatever else you desire in terms of onions, peppers, mushrooms, etc. The roll is decent, too, but not particularly crispy. Prices are definitely on the low end of the scale, making for a good meal on a budget. My two slice lunch (mushroom and plain) were requested well done, and that was what I got. Firm points. Scorched undercarriage. Well remelted mozzarella. Quite solid with a sprinkle of crushed hot pepper.   Not sure if Luigi is in the house anymore, but as a place to grab a couple of slices and a drink for lunch, this place is worthy of consideration.

As a first timer, I was pleasantly surprised by Steam, the railroad car-looking restaurant/pub on 2nd Street Pike in Southampton, Pa.    The Friday night crowd was loud, but friendly.  The bar was long and packed.  The dining tables seemed to turn over quickly enough without a reservation.  We waited about 20 minutes for a deuce hightop mid-floor.  The service dudes were all "can do!"   My burger was very good and required knife and fork as I could never open my jaws wide enough to capture it in a bite.  My companion's sliders were also tasty.  The French Onion Soup was decent, but not the strongest entry of the evening.    Steam (suggestive of the locomotive steam engine), appears to have a successful formula.  Space, fairly priced drinks($5 margaritas, beer specials), a long happy hour, and an above average bar menu.  Live music, too.    I will likely be back.

If you are ever curious about what goes on in Roebling, NJ, the former company town owned by the steel company by that name, Kalman Bakery offers another tasty reason to satisfy your history bug.   The row houses down near the river are interesting, although this burg has definitely seen happier days. But, plan to stop at Kalman's for a sweet treat on your way out of town. This family operation bakes up very good cookies, cakes and donuts at low budget prices to meet the needs of the community. The coffee is decent, too.   When I visited last week in the late morning, I was the only customer. I was greeted by a woman behind a high refrigeration display case. She explained that everything was made there, and that Tuesday was the start of their week and all was freshly baked. The traditional Old Fashioned donut looked like a blooming flower, while the Glazed was a pillow of sweetness and light. So good with the java washdown.   Now that I know where it is hidden, I will be back to Kalman's as time and sweet tooth allow.

While Peace Valley Park is a beautiful oasis of field, forest and water, when I visited last weekend there was nary a parking space. People were packed in on the trails and along the waterfront with little concern for social distancing, nor masks. It looked so unsafe to be there despite the perfect weather, that we decided not to search for parking, but to leave the park for another less overcrowded day.   We are all feeling rammy about the too long quarantine and have chronic cabin fever, but to ignore the advice of health experts that precautions remain essential to avoid infection, is to not only risk my own life, but the lives of those I love.   The North Branch of Neshaminy Creek and the reservoir from its damming (Lake Galena) will still be there when it is safer to explore.

Pie'd Piper in the Trenton Farmers Market is a hybrid shop, equal parts traditional deli and bakery. There are sandwiches galore and plenty of kielbasi and other stuffed derma to chose from, and in the vein of filling skins, excellent jelly and cream donuts. Homemade pierogi, too.  Friendly staff filled out order, but the cost across the board took us by surprise. As with most of TFM, prices were far from the expected wholesale plus, and much more premium, take it or leave it. The bill came in at nearly $50. We shelled it out, realizing this place would have to be an acquired taste.

Before you get to the excellent restaurant in back, you pass through a small but packed with merchandise mercado general. It is worth the exploration in its own right before sitting down for almuertzo o diner. The collection of chilies alone is a botanist's wet dream.   It is not every day that you can walk through a museum quality exhibit of colorful peppers, followed by shelves full of Madonna and Child statuary, on the way to a delicious and culturally absorbing meal.   Although the market/kitchen concept is standard issue in Mexico and their outposts around the world, this one is a typical sample with outstanding chef at the back of the joint.

Gino runs his shop, Mamma Rosa's Restaurant, like he was inviting each customer into his home for a meal.  The space is a converted/expanded residence from a time before zoning made such mixed uses impossible in most places.  It is cozy, warm, and bright, sort of like a old summer home in Ortley Beach or Lavalette.   I sat at a kitchen table and ordered what Gino suggested was one of the better things on the menu, a Chicken Parm Sandwich.  It arrived about 10 minutes later; a fat breast, butterflied, with rich tomato gravy, grated cheese, on a very good oven toasted half torpedo.  It was excellent and required knife and fork to be eaten without losing the back end.    Gino introduced himself and we chatted about his bio and how he came to be a restauranteur. The entire experience was very personal, and it was easy to slip and stay in the embrace of your Italian grandfather's kitchen.

Stopped in for a late afternoon slice to hold off hunger for a few hours. Nice shop with a half dozen booths and broad Italian menu. HDTVs playing Mexican talk shows.  I asked for a slice of sausage pie "well done," from those under the display glass.   It arrived hot and steaming, and certainly what I asked for.  Sadly, all the heat had not helped rigidify the chassis. It still collapsed under its own weight. The crust was soggy from an approach that put too much on top and didn't allow enough moisture to escape in the oven. The taste was there, but the texture was AWOL.   There aren't many pizza joint in this area that understand the right balance between ingredients and strong crust that results in a pie that is crisp, tasty and light on its feet. Loading up on cheese at the expense of sauce and other toppings just misses the mark.    The secret is that when it comes to great pizza, less is more.

Time to upgrade Ms. Philly Grill after a return breakfast visit this week.   The place looks about the same as when last here several years ago. Still clean and full of red and white leatherette booths with chrome around the trim. This time staff was more attentive, bringing orders from the kitchen promptly and offering to refill the coffee mug as they passed around the dining room.   My Hercules Omelet was a three egger variant of a Greek, but with Gyro meat (beef/lamb) in place of sausage, and spinach, onion, tomato and feta. Large half plate of home fries alongside. I liked it a lot, especially with a squirt of hot sauce all around. Coffee was strong, too, with the requested milk rather than creamers.   It is quite possible that the same regulars I saw last time where still hanging out. My server looked like the woman who helped me before. She seemed to take a proprietary interest in the operation.   Glad I returned and was able to write a more positive review. It also provides me with another good joint to eat when in the vicinity.

It took some time, but I finally made it in to FedNuts today. And while I didn't partake in the donuts or chicken (both of which were tempting and delicious-looking), I did have a large cup of smooth coffee while enjoying conversation with the revolving door of industry peeps and neighborhood loyalists.  Felicia and Blake make the ordering process look seamless, even as the small space filled with eager chicken-lovin' hopefuls right before noon. Arrive well before that to enjoy counter seating and some of the non-fancy donuts, which are only available early in the day. Next time, that chicken is mine.

Tippling Place was the third cocktail bar I walked into on Saturday night around 8pm but it was the first with an available seat. I think this place flies just below the radar, which is great when all you want is a place to sit and enjoy a beverage. The bartenders are friendly and there isn't any attitude. Just a cool, comfy setting and great drinks.   The cocktail menu is pretty extensive but I was disappointed that there weren't any hot beverages listed. So I went with a different seasonal delight, which was a pumpkin egg nog of sorts. It wasn't as heavy as a traditional spiked nog though it had all the right flavors. My second drink was made with rye and it was boozy. I loved the pretty cocktail glass it was served in - very vintage.  Drink prices are steep; right in line with other cocktail bars in this city.

So far, so good. I had my first experience with ECO Cleaners a couple weeks ago. I dropped my clothes off on a Monday or Tuesday in hopes that I could have them by Friday, which was not a problem. My usual spot always takes at least a week.   On Friday morning, I received a text message from the cleaners informing me that my clothes were ready for pick-up. I haven't done an Inspector Gadget-style study of my threads but they seemed appropriately cleaned and pressed. Also, this place was a lot less expensive than my usual dry cleaner.   Today I dropped off a second batch, which will again be ready by Friday. If all continues to go well, ECO may become my go-to dry cleaner. Super happy to have this business so close and convenient to my home.

Just wanted to give a gigantic shout out to the crispy bacon & feta salad I had for lunch today. It was so damn good, I may need to go back tomorrow for another. Ants Pants is legit. Just wish they accepted cards!

I've been taking Platoon's free classes at the Comcast Center for the past four weeks and I absolutely love them. The trainers, Michelle and Malik, are awesome and inspirational.   I'll admit, I begrudgingly went to the second class dreading the various cycles we had gone through the week before. I assumed that because the classes were free, they would be exactly the same. Wrong! Every single class has been different. Each has been painful in its own special way, but for me, not knowing what's next makes it easier to push through. This has kept me going back for more week after week.   Although I already have a gym membership and pay for another boot camp in NJ, I am seriously considering looking into Platoon's programs.

Super solid delivery experience from Southgate last weekend! Though my husband and I have been to the restaurant plenty of times, it was our first time trying delivery. The restaurant did an incredible job wrapping everything securely, and the time between placing our order and receiving it was really quick!   We started with the KFC (spicy) and the pork dumplings. My husband loves dumplings and I was lucky to snag one. Southgate's were very tasty and I really liked the dipping sauce. The KFC was delicious, as always.   I stayed consistent with my main and got the Seoul hot chicken sandwich, with fries. It was delicious and definitely spicy. My husband had the pork ssam - I didn't try it but it looked great. Can't wait until we can enjoy a meal at the restaurant again but, in the meantime, I'm happy to know we can enjoy the same delicious food at home.

I was out for a long walk yesterday when I came up to Hale & True, and immediately noticed the signage outside. They are currently offering cider to-go through their window. How could I resist? The employee was friendly and informative about the different types of cider. They had two different bottled ciders, another in cans, and everything on tap was available for growler fills.   The employee put on gloves for the transaction and it was quick and easy. I went with the Lil' Sunshine, which is made with honey and orange peel. I'm saving my cider for the weekend and can't wait to pop it open for a little taste of sunshine!

I met up with a friend for lunch outside on a gorgeous afternoon a few weeks ago. There were plenty of outdoor tables which were covered by a tent that was open along one side. Because it was so sunny, it actually felt quite warm but I bet the tent would be great at blocking some wind on a chillier day.   I was happy to see some booze free options on the beverage list, and ordered a Don't Call Me Shirley, which was a simple club soda with housemade grenadine - fantastic!   We shared the arugula salad, margherita and mushroom pizzas. I specifically requested the salad first but everything was brought out at the same time. Nonetheless, every single item was delicious! So delicious, that my husband and I ordered dinner from the Pizzeria Vetri in Rittenhouse that same night.  I feel like Philadelphia has gone from pizza desert to pizza wonderland in a pretty short time. I don't always think of Vetri when I think of pizza, but it's a consistently solid spot that shouldn't be overlooked.

I ordered delivery from Poke Bowl recently and was pretty happy with my order. I got the Ahi on Fire bowl, regular size. I did ask for the sriracha aioli on the side, which was a solid decision. I'm a little picky about aioli so having the ability to control the amount was perfect.   The bowl came with sticky rice, fresh tuna, jalapeños, scallions, spicy shoyu and a couple other ingredients. I have to agree with Megan Y that there was more heat than actual flavor. Next time, I think I'll create my own bowl and add some seaweed and cucumber to enhance.   Overall, solid poke delivery and I'll be ordering again in the near future.

Thanks to the care instructions I received at Pure, my white orchid has been thriving. So well, in fact, that it grew so top-heavy with blooms that the simple base it came in could no longer anchor the plant down - even with a weight thrown in! After watching my lovely take a flying leap from the windowsill one day, I finally got the hint and off to Pure we went.   One of the florists helped me pick out an appropriate base, and then she transported the plant and added some taller stems to keep the branch upright. I am so pleased with the results and how much prettier the orchid looks in a proper flower pot.   I do not believe the orchid will attempt any more dives.

Excuse me, have you had the mac and cheese? It comes in a piping hot cup which keeps the cheese gooey until the last mouthful, and is topped with buttery breadcrumbs that provide a perfect little crunch.   I shared one side of mac with two other ladies during dinner last night, but it just wasn't enough. So I went back for a midnight feeding and ordered another... which I ate all by myself. I'll spend the day in self-loathing mode but damn that mac was good.

After closing down a nearby restaurant, it was decided that Tria was the closest spot for a drink in a quiet atmosphere.  At around midnight, the bar was surprisingly quiet for a Saturday and there were only a few tables still occupied.  I loved the dark, sexy vibe, flickering candles and the music selection, which was loud enough to hear but not so much that we had to shout over it.    Since I had already enjoyed several beverages throughout the late afternoon and evening, I asked the bartender for a light beer of his choice.  He suggested one of their newest beers, Avril, which turned out to be a refreshing Belgian Ale.  It was a lovely evening and I plan to return soon for another relaxing night, perhaps with wine and cheese next time.

There isn't too much to say that hasn't already been said.  This particular location is clean, nice-looking and always packed with fun-loving people.  Once in a while, you will run into people from the local sports scene, which is always fun.    My most recent visit was on Friday night, after the Flyers' disappointing overtime loss to the Montreal Canadiens.  When my friends and I arrived shortly after the game, Riley Cote and Arron Asham were already seated and drinking beers with a group of people.  How these guys showered and got over there so quickly remains a mystery.  Is there an underground tunnel that leads from the Flyers' locker room to Chickie's main bar?  In addition to the lively crowd and local sports figures, there were also Amstel Light girls giving out free beer.  Score!

Kermit's is overdue for an update from me. I'm there about once a week but could easily be there more because of my addiction to carbs. Fortunately, they do carry other, less carb-forward items! Soups and salads, for one. Their soups vary but I'm a fan of the potato leek. The salads are always delicious!    Obviously, my favorite items are the pizza, bagels and a few of the sweets. I'm not crazy about the icing used for the cakes (it's got that whipped cream taste - I prefer sugary frostings) but I love their brownies and cheesecake bars. They also have great hot and iced coffee and there are rumors of soft serve for the summer. That's a rumor I can get behind.

For the organizational freak in me, The Container Store fulfills my every wish. I got so excited by the potential of the merchandise on my last visit that I had to force myself to focus and stick with the tasks at hand. Which were: airtight mason jars for my flour, sugar, etc., a vertical wrapping paper container and a box for Christmas decorations.   So maybe I got a little sidetracked by all the after-holiday sales. At least I have mini cards to attach to next year's gifts!  Frugal shoppers beware, gettin' tidy comes at a price. Set limits and try not to get bamboozled by the aisles and aisles of promised structure to your chaotic life.

My first experience at Heads & Tails was on Friday, and it will not be my last. The boutique salon was recommended from a business owner friend who always looks amazing. I booked my blow out with Dana and hoped for the best.   I was a bundle of nerves when I arrived to my appointment - that night I would be hosting a large event and I wanted everything to go smoothly while simultaneously looking cute, calm and collected. Dana hooked it up with a glass of red while she got to work on my tresses. We chatted easily and my nerves started to calm.   My hair is that weird length between short and long so I wasn't sure how a blow out would look, but Dana knew exactly what she was doing. In the end, I had a great style that I felt comfortable with and that even boosted my confidence. To my utter amazement, my hair still looked great after a heavy night's sleep and I was able to rock the look for an extra day. Already looking forward to my next visit!

I've been back to Osteria twice for happy hour and both times have been solid. If you arrive early you can have your choice of seats at the bar; the crowds don't start rolling in until after 6.   Glasses of prosecco, a red wine and a white wine are all $5. Pretty solid! There is also a beer and cocktail on the happy hour list as well. I'm a fan of the prosecco.  All pizzas are half off and there is a variety of small plates - I tried the trentino and parma pizzas and both were great. The wings were also very good. They are small and cooked perfectly and have a slightly sweet glaze and some seasonings.   Pro-tip: you can get from Osteria to Distrito on the inside if you need to avoid the elements!

I've had takeout from Izumi a couple times now and I really love it. The food is always packaged very nicely and everything tastes great. I love that they label the sushi on the clear lid so you know which rolls are which! The gyoza are huge, delicious and come with an awesome cucumber salad. Probably my favorite gyoza in the city. I've still never dined in but I would love to do that sooner than later!

Sea salt honey tart, you make me want to write a country song.   Last night, I hosted my book club and one of our fabulous members brought over the sea salt honey tart from Cake Life. Hmm, Cake Life? "It's where Beyoncé got her birthday cake." 'Nuff said!   I'm not a huge dessert person but I know when a good thing's in front of me, so of course I helped myself to a sliver. Wow. The rich, sweet, buttery-goodness with just the tiniest hint of sea salt to round out the flavors was truly magic. The tart reminded me of St. Louis gooey butter cake - but better.   Waking up this morning to a leftover slice really made my day!

I only stopped by RBC for a single round with some friends but had a great time! There's a huge lot with tons of parking, and plenty of seating both indoors and outside on a patio. I was really impressed by the selection of brews and thrilled that there were a couple cider options.   Upon looking at their website, I realize now there are also some wine, cocktail and a few NA options as well. Good job, Rockwell!   I wasn't feeling beer so opted for the chile guava cider, which tasted like a typical apple cider but with a fantastic spicy kick at the end. The sweetness was just right for me. Not too dry but definitely not too sweet. I really loved this cider!   There's a small shop where you can pick up beer to go and I thought the packaging was really gorgeous. I would have loved to pick up some beer for my husband but didn't want to chance packing them in my bag before flying home. If you're hungry, there's also a food window and I saw some delish looking cheese fries - next time!

I had a very positive experience with Wilensky's. Our front door lock had been getting tougher and tougher to open over the course of a few weeks - to the point where we realized we couldn't leave the house without getting it fixed because we feared we wouldn't be able to get back in!   I found Wilensky's on Yelp, gave them a ring in the morning and spoke with a friendly guy who said he would have their locksmith give me a call as soon as he was in. I received a call maybe an hour later and the locksmith said he could be over around noon, and he was.   Turned out, something in our lock had broken and needed to be replaced. This was remedied in about fifteen or twenty minutes and now our lock works perfectly. The total charge was $140 - eighty or ninety of that was the visit alone and the rest was for the fix. Yowza. Hopefully my locks will be good to go for a long time!

After dinner at ZoT with a large crew of yelpers, several of us were in the mood for a change of scenery.  I had never been to The Irish Pol before, so had no expectations whatsoever.  This is what I encountered:  - 30 or so beers on tap, including Blanche de Bruxelles, the first beer I requested at ZoT and seemingly the only beer that they did not have  - Awesome jukebox that consistently defaulted to Beastie Boys tunes between requested songs  - My newest addiction, Photo Hunt, which apparently cannot be mastered (even with a team of five people)   - AWESOME bar food.  Does The Irish Pol cater?  They should.  My brother will be so impressed when I introduce him to this most wonderful dive bar.  It is sure to become a staple.

I love this bar. Last night was my second visit and I enjoyed it just as much as round one. The cocktails are well-balanced and delicious; the bartenders really know what they are doing.   Happy hour is a total steal, featuring a really nice red and wine selection and a handful of cocktails, plus some of the regular bar snacks at way reduced prices. I won't tell you how many orders of the puffed pork chips with wild onion sour cream dip I ordered, but it was more than one.

I am way overdue on an upgrade to Buena Onda. We order lunch or dinner from them pretty regularly, and it's rare that I receive an order that I'm not happy with, though it does occasionally happen. Thankfully, our orders are on point more often than not.  One thing Buena Onda does better than most of its competitors is packaging. Tacos arrive in grooved cardboard containers that keep the tacos from spilling all over. We enjoy the fish and shrimp tacos but have tried many of the others as well.   Recently, buena bowls have been added to the menu, and they are great! So far, I've tried one with tofu chorizo and one with shrimp. Both were excellent and kept me full all day, which is what I want out of a healthy(ish) lunch.   I have been pretty disappointed by the serving sizes of the guacamole and salsa, which come at standard restaurant prices but really small portions. Nonetheless, I love Buena Onda for quick and easy Mexican food, delivered to my front door.

I love Shibe! My husband picked up a couple gifts there for Christmas, including something I needed for a pollyanna gift for my brother in law. I was very happy with the items he picked out - the styles are cool and have a throwback look, totally different from other Philadelphia sports wear I've seen.   The shirt for my brother in law was too small, so I swung by the store one day to swap out, after calling first to confirm that there was a larger size. While there I also picked up a gift for my grandfather, a long-sleeved gray Eagles shirt made of the softest cotton. The shirt is nice enough to wear out for a casual dinner and doesn't have gigantic logos or anything too loud.   I also happened to notice the nice selection of female attire, and I have my eye on a throwback Eagles sweatshirt. Prices are very reasonable and the selection is vast for such a small store. I'm impressed!

As far as my care at this office goes, I feel pretty confident. But that's once I'm in the exam room. Everything before and after that point is why this facility gets an average rating. The receptionists are hit and miss... mostly miss. I've gotten attitude and short attention spans on almost every call I've placed to the office. God forbid you ask whether your insurance covers something and they have to open a file or place a call to find out.   The doctors are solid. I used to see Dr. Hyder but after seeing Dr. Prasad once I ended up continuing with her. She's no longer in the Cinnaminson office but on my visit last week I saw Dr. Kessler and she was great, too.

Okay, Smiths.  To be fair, your establishment is pretty swank for a sports bar and my brain did start chanting "sau-sage par-ty, sau-sage par-ty!" upon entering.  However, $26 for two slightly-dirty Ketel One martinis?  For realz?!  Not to mention, the martini I specifically requested was listed on the board as having blue-cheese stuffed olives and yet the olives in my drink, while indeed plump and delicious, were hollow and... empty inside.  Sad.    I'll be back to check out a game and some of those delicious-looking apps, but I definitely won't be hitting the hard stuff.

Starbucks in my home town! The future is now!   Like Yelper Steve P, I too was very skeptical when I saw the Starbucks sign outside of the building that once was a mom and pop pancake house way back in the day. But I was pleasantly surprised by the large, inviting space when I walked through the doors. This would be a great spot to get some work done or have a casual meeting.   I ordered an Americano and asked if they had the egg white breakfast sandwich, since I didn't see it on display. The employee at the register looked through the refrigerator but, unfortunately, they didn't have my go-to. I opted instead for the bacon, gouda and egg sandwich which was tasty if not as light as the egg white option. My Americano was HOT - I couldn't drink it for a good twenty minutes.   Overall, glad to see this new location so close to home. No more driving to Delran for my Starbucks fix!

Guys, this place is dangerous. In fact, my stomach is rumbling at the mere thought of all those rum drinks I put down during my recent trip to New Orleans.   There's some good news. While the sickeningly sweet grenade drinks are poured straight from a bar gun, there are some drinks on the menu that are a little less suspect. The Pirate's Passion is made of 151 rum, Malibu and pineapple juice. No added syrups or sugars or anything. Drink one so you can get the whole Bourbon Street thing out of your system and then switch to something lighter. Don't drink several. Trust me.   Love that they feature bands and especially love the request system, which is one of those bank tube thingies that suctions your container of requests (and your tip for the band, of course) over the bar and to the band.   Last but not least, props to the bartenders, who pour the same drinks over and over and who maintain the same high level of theatrics every time someone orders a Shark Attack.

Crazy Sushi remains my go-to for an inexpensive sushi lunch delivery during the week. Their lunch specials are great; I always get three rolls with soup and rarely deviate from that order. By the time tax and gratuity are added, my total is still less than twenty bucks! Delivery is usually super quick, often within a half hour of placing an order. I usually see the same delivery man who is always very friendly. Love this place!

What's not to love about this gorgeous example of architecture? Traveling can be hectic and sometimes stressful, but whenever I find myself inside 30th Street Station I feel calm. There's usually a pretty chill vibe about the place, which puts me in a good traveling mood. Whenever I return from a trip, I feel welcomed back by a beautiful building that reminds me I'm home.   There are plenty of coffee options for the morning, and from what I hear some of the restaurant selections aren't half bad, though I don't believe I've ever taken advantage myself. The book store is pretty decent, and there's usually somewhere to sit if necessary.

Fried. Cheese.   But not just any cheese - these curds are pressed in Wisconsin and sent straight to the folks at The Cow and The Curd, where they are prepped and served within days of arrival. Bite into one of these little nuggets and expect some of the ooziest cheese around. Definitely try them with the chipotle dipping sauce, which only makes them tastier.   I highly recommend splitting an order with a friend or two - much as you'll want that little bucket all to yourself, it's probably in your best interest to share.

This was the go-to movie theatre during my teenage and college years. And apparently, it still is since Loews' parking lot is always full and the theatre remains relatively nice. The one thing I don't love about the place is that the crowds can be unruly depending on the movie and time of day (usually a night or weekend, which is becoming less and less likely a time that I'll go to the movies nowadays). That's probably not something most movie theatres have control over but it is a reason that I'll typically opt for the former Ritz in Voorhees or the Ritz locations in the city. That said, it's the perfect theatre for a weekday flick and very convenient to the area's shopping and restaurants.

I've been here twice now, the first time for a manicure and the second for a pedicure. For a manicure, it's a very nice place and you'll certainly get your money's worth. But for pedicure services, no one can match my regular guy Thom from the salon I frequent in NJ.  The pedicure chairs are not comfortable. Basically, you are sitting on a cushioned bench against a wall. From this angle, lifting your leg for certain parts of the service feels more like exercise. For the cost of a pedi at Rescue, I want to relax and zone out, not pull a muscle trying keep from sliding off the bench as I hold my leg in a 90 degree angle.   I would certainly return to Rescue for another manicure or some of the services they are better known for, but for pedis I'll stick to my usual spot.

Every time we sit at one of the pub tables at Southwark, I admire the beautiful orchids in the windows. The thick, sturdy leaves of the plants are deceiving; they give way to long, thin branches too weak to support their own stunning flowers without assistance from supports. I'm fascinated by them.   Needless to say, I was touched when my boyfriend presented me with my own white orchid for Valentine's Day. It was one of the most thoughtful, lovely gifts I've ever received.   Since it was purchased from Pure, I decided to pop in to get some tips for how to take care of my new beauty. The store had several interesting flowers and not the typical bouquets one would expect from a flower shop.   The woman I spoke with was super helpful, and I'm so happy I stopped in. Apparently, orchids draw most of their moisture from the air, so it's really only necessary to water them about once a month with a half cup of hot water. I shudder to think what would have happened had I not known this info. Hopefully my plant will continue to thrive and flourish for many moons to come.

After getting home late from an event recently and realizing I'd skipped dinner, I opened my various delivery apps to see what was available after 10pm on a weekday. I had a craving for Chinese and Red Kings 2 was one of the very few places that was still accepting orders. So I crossed my fingers while placing an order for general tso's, fried rice and wonton soup.   Not only did Red Kings come through with some very solid eats, the window of time between my order and delivery was only about 30 minutes, give or take. The food was nicely packaged and there was plenty of it; I got several meals out of my order. Adding this one to the delivery rotation for sure!

Not awesome.   That's how I'd describe my experience at Five Guys tonight. I was so pumped for a Five Guys burger, since they are Whole30-compliant. The young lady who took our order was friendly and seemed to understand exactly what I wanted - a burger in a lettuce wrap, with grilled onions, tomato and pickles.   When our number was called, my mom and I grabbed the bag and went back to her house to dig in. I opened up my container and couldn't believe it: two grossly overcooked patties, no lettuce whatsoever, a couple slices of pale tomato, a couple pickles and a small pile of grilled onions. Where was the g-d $&*# lettuce wrap?! In that moment I was Nancy Kerrigan. Whyyyyyyyyy?   My stepdad said the Cajun fries were really good, but his burger, and my mom's, were also majorly overcooked. The fries I couldn't have, because, Whole30. Nine more days. French fries of the world, you're on notice.

I definitely like this location of Foodery more than the other. Even though it's smaller and cramped, I feel like I can find what I'm looking for quickly. The prices are still astronomical. A mixed six pack and a bag of Doritos set us back somewhere around $26 on Saturday. And before you go thinking we picked a bunch of fancy stuff, consider the following. The beers in our sixer were: Dogfish Head 60 Minute, Harpoon IPA, Ballast Point Sculpin, Victory Weizen Bock, Cerberus something or other (looks slightly fancy with a foil topper) and Great Lakes Edmund Fitzgerald. Come on.

Being in the Market & Shops at Comcast Center reminds me all too much of my former life in the corporate world. Shudder.  That said, if I did work in the Comcast Center, I'd be pleased with the options for lunch that I'd be able to take advantage of without even leaving the building. Percy Street Barbecue and DiBruno Bros., most notably.   The "Shops" would leave me wanting. There isn't much to get excited about. A lady who wants to flex some plastic on her lunch break is better off at Liberty Place or Walnut Street.

I recently noticed Giorgio on one of the apps I use regularly for delivery. My go-to pizza spots are Kermit's and Santucci's, but I was in the mood for something different and gave Giorgio Pizza a try. It's worth noting that the prices at Giorgio are a lot lower than these other spots.  We ordered a sausage pizza and some arancini. Delivery was fast and the food was just the right temp. While the sausage on the pizza was average, I found the pizza overall to be pretty solid. The arancini was cooked nicely but it was sitting in sauce so the parts facing the sauce became soggy. I'd recommend serving the sauce separately for take-out or delivery.  I would definitely consider Giorgio again for fast pizza delivery when I'm not looking for anything extra fancy.

Solid eats, Golden Triangle. And thank you, Yelpers, for the solid reviews which led to my trying this place for takeout while in the neighborhood. I placed an order through Eat24 and the food was ready fifteen minutes later.   My order was just some basic shrimp pad Thai but it was easily one of the better pad Thais I've had in Philly. My husband started with the roti, which came with a cup of potato curry soup. This four dollar starter is absolutely delicious and a must-get, if you're carbing out on a Sunday (or any day, really). His pineapple rice was nicely balanced with crunchy veggies and great flavor. The price was right as our total came to about $25.   If it weren't for the $4 delivery fee I'd probably order from here on the reg. For now, I'll stick to pick-up when I'm in the area.

Czerw's is a no-frills shop for all your Polish needs. There's a fridge filled with pierogi and a meat counter with several varieties of Polish sausage. The guy who works the counter has to be one of the nicest butchers around. He welcomed me and my fiancé like we were regulars for years. We picked up a couple pounds of kielbasa and grilled it for the game - it was a huge hit and couldn't have been easier. Five stars!

Compared with other Starbucks locations, this one seemed fairly new. There were several comfy-looking chairs and the entire place was spotless.   The staff seemed a bit amateur. I asked about the ingredients in a pumpkin latte and got a bewildered look from a staffer, like I had just asked a question about quantum physics. After I explained ("You know, is there sweetened syrup? Just spices? What exactly gives the latte it's pumpkin flavor?"), she relaxed and ran through the ingredients list, which seemed too sugary for what I wanted (and there's no sugar-free version of the pumpkin latte). I went with a regular latte and the boyfriend ordered a mocha.   There were several staffers but the process wasn't as seamless as other locations. Still, this is one of the few coffee shops in the area that I could find on my Yelp app, so it did the trick.

When my husband and I got home around midnight on a recent Friday, we realized we were hungry and had no food in the house. We were super excited to see that Oregon Steaks was still taking delivery orders, and we placed an order for a chicken cheese steak for him and a turkey hoagie for me.   The delivery was fast - maybe thirty minutes tops? Awesome. The sandwiches were huge. I thought the quality of the turkey was just okay - and I also pulled about half of it off because there was so much. My husband enjoyed his chicken cheesesteak.   Though I might not pick Oregon Steaks as my first choice when other options are available, it was more than solid for an impromptu late night meal delivered right to our door.

Spending a Saturday night at my sister's house often comes with some late night eating, and Domino's has come through for us on more than one occasion with fast, reliable delivery and accurate orders.   After trying but failing to find a local pizza shop that was still open and making deliveries around midnight, we had to default to Domino's. While I wasn't involved in the ordering process, my phone was used to download the Domino's app and place the order. Apparently, there were lots of helpful notifications about our order being received, our pizza being prepared, and at what time we could expect delivery. Just like our previous experience, delivery was surprisingly quick and our pizza was hot and actually quite tasty.   This may have been our only option for late night eating, but it wasn't a bad option at all.

My boyfriend and I popped into Rittenhouse Hardware this morning to pick up a few supplies. Compared to the home improvement giants, the store was minuscule, but every square inch of space was taken up by gadgets and tools.   As one employee worked on making us key copies, another was available to tell us exactly where to find everything on our list. Both knew the merchandise inside and out, and we received helpful tips whenever we were stuck deciding between items.   The experience was quick, painless and dare I say, fun? I absolutely plan to visit this little shop on the regular for all my household ish.

Numa has taken over one of my old favorites (Moshi Moshi) from the days when I worked in the evil world of legal marketing. I was happy to see a trendy overhaul had taken place with regards to decor, since its former self was pretty dated.   I found prices to be on the high side for lunch. My tuna set which consisted of a miso soup starter and two pieces of tuna sushi, a tuna avocado roll and a spicy tuna roll set me back $14. This is definitely higher than typical sushi roll combos at most places, but I did think the sushi was better than average. It was quite delicious, actually.   I'm happy to know that this is still are reliable spot for quality sushi and I'll likely return.

My crew returned to Smith's for happy hour on Friday night.  Both bar areas were packed with people who were happy to be out of work and starting the weekend on an unusually warm March evening.  A table opened up and we sat down to order some apps.  The boneless buffalo chicken and bacon mac and cheese* were both pretty awesome.  Our server was friendly and fairly quick, although she forgot special requests like sauce on the side, etc.  Overall, it was a solid happy hour and everyone around us seemed to share that sentiment.  *Several hours later, I returned home and tried to recreate the culinary delight that is bacon mac and cheese.  My findings?  Microwave bacon and Annie's whole wheat shells and cheddar do not a gourmet bacon mac and cheese make.

Since giving up meat and poultry for the month of February, I've often found myself lusting over memories of my meal at The Fat Ham last month. I really don't think I was cut out to be a vegetarian.   My favorite bites:  Ricotta cheese Oyster sliders Baked mac and cheese Hot chicken Chocolate chip cookie skillet  So, to sum it up: cheese, fried things, and carbs. Fantastic.   My dining companions and I had several more dishes, including the mustard greens, ham and eggs, grilled trout, shrimp and grits and Carolina gold rice, amongst others. While these didn't make it into my faves (and I'm starting to realize why - because they were not fried and were possibly healthy), it was nice to try a little bit of everything. Knowing now what Kevin and the team can do with a chicken, I'm also very much looking forward to testing out the country fried lobster tail.  On a brief second visit for drinks, delicious cocktails and a light and bright red wine on tap were enjoyed.        Anxiously awaiting my next visit.

This store has all of your costume needs covered. The best part is that it is open year round, as opposed to many of the pop-up Halloween stores that come in and out of the area. I stop by every few months to pick up props for events and they always have what I'm looking for. The prices are a little more expensive than I'd typically expect for cheaply-made, plastic doodads. But honestly, the fact that I can get in and get out with exactly what I need makes it worthwhile. Just be sure to purchase only what you want - the store does not take returns, which can be an inconvenience.

They have a wedge salad on the menu! Happy day!  Only problem is, I cut into it during this morning's brunch without realizing one of the herbs sprinkled on top is something my palette is vehemently against. The freshly diced herb served as a salad shrapnel, which unfortunately turned me off. Otherwise, this would have been one of the best wedge salads I've come across in recent memory, since all other components were perfect. Next time, I'll order without the extra greenery.

I'm not really a Starbucks fan but sometimes, it works. The employees at this location were all super friendly and engaging. You know when you have a bunch of questions about something and you can tell when the person behind the counter is losing patience? Not this crew. They were happy to answer the surprising array of questions I had about their iced teas.   Speaking of which, I ordered some type of berry concoction that was bright pink and fruity but very, very tart. Walk the extra block to Cafe Ole for their amazing raspberry iced tea if that's what you're jonesin' for (sorry, Starbucks). The only reason I didn't do that was because I had already been there just an hour earlier and didn't want to be that weirdo going back twice in an hour.

I haven't been hitting too many new businesses lately so I'm making sure to give extra love to the ones that have been getting me through this year. Every single time I'm in Old City, I figure out a way to swing by Cafe Square One. Their salads are still just as awesome as they were when I first tried them a couple years ago, and the employees are always friendly and welcoming.   One day I'll deviate from my beloved southwest salad to try one of the wraps or sandwiches... one day.

If you haven't had happy hour at Xochitl yet, you are missing out. From 5-7, get $3 drafts and $5 margs (the best in Philly, in my opinion). Late night Thursdays add half off to the bar menu. I suggest the guacamole, queso fundido, torta sliders, calamar, tacos de suadero and ceviche.  So basically, everything is awesome.

Maybe Top Tomato does some menu items right, but my turkey and cheese hoagie was pretty weak yesterday. They didn't have American cheese listed on their menu when we ordered online, so I had to get provolone. No big deal. But the turkey definitely wasn't high quality deli turkey and the tomatoes were a tad mealy. If you're going to have the word "tomato" in your name, at least get some tasty hothouse varieties.   My sandwich was sliced at a really weird angle and not all the way through, so when I tried to pull the sandwich apart the bread ended up ripping at the wrong place. I realize this is the whiniest of all complaints, and I probably sound like a total brat, but if I'm going to order a sandwich from one place over dozens of others in this city, at least try to sell me on it.   My friends seemed pretty happy with all of their selections (cheesesteaks, some type of chicken sandwich and an eggplant parm). I'll admit, there was some food envy. But I'm not sure that I'll be giving Top Tomato a second look the next time I want a sammie.

I had a hankering for Thai and Jasmine Rice was very close to where I was when said cravings occurred. After checking out the reviews and deciding to go for curry rather than a noodle dish, I placed an order for the green curry with shrimp. The food was done quickly and I was on my way.   The portion size was generous and there were five or so very large shrimp and lots of crisp, fresh veggies. The curry was flavorful, with a little heat, and not too heavy. The rice was perfectly sticky and delicious. I was very pleasantly surprised by Jasmine Rice (based on some of the reviews I read), but I will definitely think of them next time I have a curry craving.

Thanks, Jay's, for helping me out with my diet today. How did you know I don't like salmon sushi? You must have had some idea since you replaced my California roll with a spicy salmon roll in my take-out. Clearly, my eyes were bigger than my stomach (yet again) when I ordered the three roll combo instead of the two roll. However, in the future, I'd like to make that decision on my own. Because you still got me for the cost of three rolls even though I only ended up receiving two out of the three that I ordered.   Who knows what that poor guy who walked in after me ended up with. Five minutes after placing his order, he was asked for his order... again.   For average-at-best sushi, awkward service and the California/salmon roll switcheroo, I bestow two stars.

I've always been a fan of Jones, and I'm clearly not alone since this restaurant has been around for quite a while. I swung by after tonight's Yelp Elite Event for a bite and was not disappointed. The menu offers something for everyone.   Since our threesome was all in agreement that the "cheese hold the meat burger" sounded great, we decided to share it as an app. This pseudo-burger consisted of a soft and buttery roll with a giant slab of haloumi cheese, lemon aioli, lettuce and tomato. We hacked it into threes and I was instantly wishing there was more to go around. Our server told us it's a new addition to the menu, and to that I say: "Well played, Jones. Well played."  I also had the ahi tuna tacos, which were good, but not as good as the non-burger burger. Everything in the tacos is served cold; essentially ahi tuna in taco shells, with lettuce, cilantro and a spicy aioli.  I'll be back for that haloumi burger.

In one of the more random moves ever, some friends and I ended a weeknight out at Ariana. There were several tables filled with people who appeared to be regulars, and I got that fun feeling like I had stepped into a cool, secret spot. That doesn't happen often. I liked it!  I had enjoyed a peach hookah once before at another establishment and no one seemed to protest at my suggestion, so that's what we ordered. It took a few rounds to really get going but once it did - hiyooo! Some felt the buzz more than others (that would be me, the lightweight), but it was pleasant and brief, without any weird side effects.  We thought the place was open pretty late but the check was dropped at our table shortly after midnight and we got the vibe that it was time to go. Next time, I'll make sure we have enough of a time cushion to finish up before feeling like we have to split.

You know how every town has an Italian restaurant that consistently churns out awesome food and is your go-to staple?  That's Bruno's.  There are three main parts to this establishment; a BYO restaurant where you can have a nice dinner, a take-out type section where you can also enjoy a quick slice and a liquor store.    Take-out is probably my favorite option.  You can call ahead to place your order, run into the liquor store to grab the perfect bottle of red or white, then pick up your dinner.  Dinners come with a roll and a pretty large side salad, and the entrees are huge (without compromising on quality) and delicious.  I highly recommend the pasta with clams and red sauce.  The red sauce is homemade with plum tomatoes and fresh garlic.  Soooooo good!

Every time I bit into the snappy dog of my Cincinnati Skyline on Saturday, I couldn't help but think that it was the best hot dog I'd ever eaten. I probably said it at least three times. The experience reminded me of a fond hot dog memory of my childhood. Christine B was the lucky recipient of that tale, and if she was bored to death hearing the story of my favorite hot dog, she was a good sport and didn't show it.   This particular link was nestled in a soft bun which held up to the ingredients: chili, chopped onions, creamy nacho cheese and fresh diced green onions. The entire thing was delicious. Adding to the experience were the thick cut French fries. I felt they needed a tad more salt, but they were great otherwise. We opted for garlic aioli and peppercorn ranch dipping sauces, but I tried the honey mustard also and liked it best out of the three.   Not sure why it took me so long to give in to the temptations of Hot Diggity, but it definitely won't be long until my next visit.

For anyone who has been dying to know the answer to the age-old question, "How are those pretzel-dogs at Philly Soft Pretzel Factory?"  I have stepped up to the challenge of taste testing one.  The results:  Not that great.  Kind of gross, actually.    The regular pretzels are bangin', though.  Especially when they're fresh out of the oven.  In tomorrow's edition of Questions People Ponder:  Wawa chocolate milk: moo or don't?

Love La Colombe, don't necessarily love this location.   The baristas are all friendly enough, but the bustling energy makes me want to grab my cup and peace out rather than pull up a chair. I'm a much bigger fan of the location on Penn Square.

My first trip to Mac's was solid. A server set us up at a table for six right away and he was on top of his serving game for our visit. When I wasn't sure what I wanted to drink, he brought over a few different samples for me to try. Still kicking myself for not ordering the high ABV coffee IPA that was available.   A friend seemed to enjoy a hummus plate so I ordered one to snack on. I liked that there were a lot of vegetables and not just pita. For the most part the plate was okay, but the first red pepper strip I picked up was slimy, so I avoided those. The cucumber slices were good but they were layered with some sad looking tomato slices. The garlicky hummus had some random red onion slices sticking straight out of it.   Don't go to Mac's for the hummus plate. Do go for the beer and friendly service. (And maybe some french fries - those looked really good!)

I was very pleasantly surprised by my lunch at Red Owl Tavern today. I always sort of thought of the place as a tourist spot since it's located in a hotel. The lunch crowd did seem like a mix of tourists but also regulars who work in the area. I heard more than one table order the cheesesteak, and my server, Liam, said it's one of his recommendations whenever people ask what's good.   I went with the cobb salad, dressing on the side, no onions, add grilled shrimp. The salad came out just as I requested, was perfectly sized and so fresh! The shrimp were huge and there were four - I feel like this salad will actually carry me to dinner. The homemade ranch dressing was perfection. I loved everything about my lunch! I drank water and was happy that my server left the bottle on the table.   Everyone from the hostess to my server to the GM was very friendly. Great experience and I would certainly return without hesitation when in the neighborhood.

I used The Gourmet Vendor for an event and it worked out great. I found out about them from a friend who has hired them for family parties on several occasions. What's more fun than an old-school hot dog stand at your party?!    Brad, the owner of the company, was very easy to get in touch with and the cart arrived on time for set-up at my event. The guy who operated the cart was great and I saw lots of happy hot dog lovers. Definitely a great move for a party!

Wow, I had no idea Doylestown had such a shopping scene! I happened to park across from this business on Friday afternoon, and when I saw the Free People sign I had to pop in for a look.   Since I was with my husband I tried to make it quick, but I could have easily spent a half hour or more combing through everything in the store. They stock a variety of recognizable brands and I thought everything was priced fairly. I ended up with a pair of cute, lightweight pants that I can't wait to break out in warmer months!   I look forward to future Doylestown visits and more shopping at this awesome boutique!

I've hit up Village Whiskey twice in the past couple of months and it's still a great spot for a bite. Both visits were on Sundays, and we've been lucky to get seated right away both times even though the restaurant is small and seating is tight.   On the first visit, three of us shared a bunch of plates: pickled cherry tomatoes, village burger, bbq pork sammy, and duck fat fries with Sly Fox cheddar sauce. Everything was delicious! I was also happy to see a couple solid non-alcoholic options as well; the lavender fields was a hit!   Last Sunday, I tried the veggie burger and my sister had the bbq pork sammy. Again, we ordered the fries with cheddar sauce. I do think the cheddar sauce could have a bit more flavor, but the fries themselves are really great regardless.    Honestly, Village Whiskey is a spot I didn't think about much because I always just assumed it would be too crowded. Now that I've found the sweet spot, it's becoming part of my weekend rotation!

Summer has only just begun, but I've already made several trips to John's for their delicious water ice. My favorite is a pineapple and cherry combo. Both flavors are perfection and just the right amount of sweet. The prices are great; it's two bucks for a small which is perfect for an every day sort of treat. I look forward to many visits as the weather heats up!

My friend and I spent much of Bastille Day at the bar at London Grill. The bartenders were friendly and in jovial moods. There were some liquor promo girls giving out free samples of product, which was cool.   Once we decided we were hungry, I ordered a burger and my friend ordered parmesan truffle fries. The burger was curiously served on an English muffin-type roll, but it was pretty tasty. The fries that came with, along with my friend's fries, were room temp and not delish. She sent hers back but I had my burger so I was okay. A new batch came out approximately one minute later and they were definitely hotter but still just so-so.   It's not often that I'm in Fairmount so I'm not sure I would go out of my way just to hit up London Grille. But if I found myself in the area, I wouldn't be opposed to stopping by, either.

I returned to Prohibition Taproom for some pre-concert eats and drinks.  Happy hour was from 5 - 7 but since everyone in my group was drinking bottled beer, we did not benefit from the specials.  Still, the beer selection is very fairly priced.  The bartender was friendly and effortlessly handled the entire bar on her own, which was no small feat as mostly all of the stools were taken.    Between four of us, we had the hummus plate, deep fried green beans and onion rings.  There was more than enough food and we didn't even come close to finishing everything.  The hummus was very good, as were the green beans, which came with some sort of garlic dipping sauce.  I highly suggest investing in some Altoids if you plan to order either of these plates.  The onion rings were really thick-cut and almost a little too onion-y.  The dipping sauce seemed like a cross between ranch dressing and vinegar.  It was pretty potent and I'd probably lean towards ketchup in the future, but that's just me.    I shall return.

Like David B, my first introduction to Cucina Zapata was also at the Vendy Awards. Curried chicken over rice hooked me in while mini tacos with chicken and short rib sealed the deal. It was one of the few trucks that day that kept the line moving quickly and was also prepared for the crowds. Even when an L&I inspector jumped aboard in the beginning of the event, causing everything to grind to a halt, the food truck peeps kept their cool and business was back up and running in no time.   I'll definitely make a point to seek out Cucina Zapata for lunch in the near future!

SUPER BOWL LII CHAMPIONS!!!  Thank you to this incredible team of players and coaches for making the dreams of an entire region come true. What an amazing story of perseverance, hard work and camaraderie!   See you at the parade! #FlyEaglesFly

I've been wanting to try pierogi from Mom Mom's for ages and finally had the opportunity at this year's Bloktoberfest. A friend and I decided to share an order which was a good move since you get several pierogi.   I grew up on my grandmom's pierogi so I have my preferences as to what I look for and enjoy. Mom Mom's pierogi have come the closest to the bull's eye, even if they were slightly different than my Gram's version. I liked that the potato and cheese filling wasn't completely pureed - there was a little texture which makes a huge difference. I also liked that they were topped with sauteed onion and served with sour cream and chives. In my family we sauté our pierogi in some butter and call it a day but this was a nice twist.   Mom Mom may not be MY grandmom, but she's still throwing it down in the pierogi gauntlet.

After a draining experience at the Nissan service department across the street, I decided to treat myself to a little pity party lunch for one at Nordstrom Cafe. Menus are on a table just outside, so you place and pay for your order first, then choose a table. At that point, a server picks up your receipt and everything proceeds like a normal restaurant experience. The only thing I didn't like about this set-up was that you have to know exactly what you want at the time of ordering. So if you suddenly feel like dessert, I guess you'd have to go back to the front. No big.  I ordered an iced tea and chicken Caesar salad. My server was very sweet and made sure I was all set with everything I needed. She also refilled my tea, which was great. The salad was pretty good and everything I saw at other tables looked great, too. The best part of all was that I enjoyed a relatively cheap lunch in a quiet setting which was worlds above the mall food court. I'll definitely return when I need a little shopping break.

Every time I walk into the Foodery, I'm excited by the well stocked beer selection, which I am confident has been handled with care to avoid any possibility of spoiling.      Every time I walk out of the Foodery, I feel like I've been robbed in broad daylight in front of a police station.  Why did two bottles of Stillwater Ale cost almost TEN DOLLARS more at Foodery than at a competitor (ahem, Food & Friends) across town?  I get the convenience factor of the location, and the fact that Foodery started the trend, but come on.  Maybe the price gouging works on the clueless but I'll mix my six elsewhere.

There's something very cozy about La Va, and I like that in a coffee shop. Comfy chairs intermingle with standard table and chair set-ups, where people come in droves to work or study.   Lattes are served in giant mugs and the pretty barista with curly hair will even craft a design in the foam, if she's not too busy. That automatically makes her my favorite.    Weekend afternoons at La Va are a little too crowded for my liking, but weeknights are usually quiet enough to sit down and relax a bit. I expect to visit quite often once I'm in my new 'hood!

I loooooove me some Nordstrom but found this particular location to be a little less cared-for than others. Sales racks weren't very well organized and no one came up to ask if I needed help with anything, which is unusual for Nordstrom. When I helped myself to a dressing room (again, no one to be found), the open rooms had piles of clothes and the room I ended up in wasn't super clean, either (I'm talking dried spills on the tables - ick).    All that said, this location is the largest in the area and has a really great selection of clothes. The woman who rang me up was also very sweet. I am not a fan of driving out to KOP but when I am in the area for business I always make Nordstrom a stop.

Cute cafe in the Francisville/Fairmount area that provided an awesome place for me to hole up for several hours and have lunch, take a couple meetings, and get some work done.
