I was disappointed because I had been looking forward to the brunch burger, but I ended up going with the regular menu burger instead, with salad instead of fries.   The burger was okay; not super juicy and probably a bit more on the med-well side than medium. I had a couple bites of the fried clams which were awesome and the perfect summer menu item. Service was solid.   Going back to four stars for SPTR but it's still a reliable neighborhood spot.

I was pleasantly surprised by my brunch experience at The Strip Joint. Cheeky name for a steak restaurant, by the way. I like it. That said, I really hate that they took it a step further and labeled the menu with sections called "something wet" and "happy endings" - ick.   Now that I got that out of the way; four dollar bloody marys and mimosas! That's pretty sweet. For a deal like that I didn't bat an eye at my $16 brunch selection, which ended up being totally worth the price tag. The crab cake benedict is served over a risotto cake and has a large serving of breakfast potatoes. The sriracha hollandaise, which I requested on the side, was absolutely delish. My fiancé didn't seem blown away by his peppers and eggs sandwich, but the bacon on the side was pretty great. It was thick cut and perfectly cooked.   Our server was nice and helpful. The bloody marys were very tasty. I'd go back for brunch again sometime.

Wow, the AMC Marlton has changed since my last visit, eons ago! I love the reserve ahead system, the comfy chairs with plenty of cup holders, the space between rows (and your neighbor), the wide aisles!   My only two gripes, and I know one of them isn't changing: the inability to use gift passes online, and refreshments prices. I had four movie pass tickets and went to book my seats online, only to find out that I had to go in-person to redeem. Come on, AMC! Give those passes a code, update your online reservations system, and we can all avoid the unnecessary advance visit to the theater.   A small popcorn and small soda costs $11 and change?! SMH, indeed!

A very hectic day came to a slow and peaceful halt the moment I walked through Biba's doors on Saturday evening. We went with the intention of learning something during Drink. Think. but ended up staying for dinner and several more glasses of delicious red wines.   The place is darkly outfitted but has a huge window which allows for both natural light and people watching. We chose to sit at the bar, complete with always-necessary hooks for coats, purses and, on that night, umbrellas.   We learned about Old World and New World Syrah, and we paired our tasting with a crunchy cheddar, smoky speck with the most delicious honey mustard and roasted garlic scented olives. This was just enough to whet our appetite for heartier bites of a vinaigrette-dressed salad with figs, blue cheese and hazelnuts, as well as a smoked chicken panino which was super tasty but not too heavy.   As always with any Tria establishment, we ended up spending more dough than we intended, but the fact that I was able to exchange some stress for sanity was well worth the price. I look forward to my next visit!

My friend treated me to a spa day a few weeks before my wedding (I have amazing friends). We had a package that included a facial and massage. My massage was with Kim, and it was wonderful. She guaranteed that I would fall asleep by the time she was done, and I thought there was no way because I was pretty wound up with so much going on in my head. Despite this, Kim had to wake me out of a gentle sleep as she finished!   My facial was nice and I really enjoyed chatting with my facialist, who was hilarious. I do have to admit that I didn't really care for the scent of the products that were used.   I have a go-to salon in the burbs that I really love already, so it's not too likely that I'll switch. But I did really enjoy my spa day here and would recommend it to anyone looking for some relaxation in the city.

Capogiro's locations are some of my favorite places to grab a cup of coffee and get some work done. The music is always great and the employees are always pleasant. And the wifi passwords are always hilarious. Today's password was: grapefruitcampari. That made me happy.  I don't know how I turn off my attraction to their gelato on the days that I visit solely for work, but I do. Knowing I'll get a delicious latte out of the trip definitely helps. And if I ever did want a treat, there are loads of confections on the counter... and about a million flavors of said gelato.

I ordered a buffalo chicken cheesesteak and a soda from Talk of the Town for lunch today via GrubHub. The delivery was quoted at about an hour, which was accurate. The sandwich was actually pretty good, if a bit small for more than eight bucks. It was the right amount of food for lunch, just on the expensive side.   The soda arrived in a to-go cup with a lid. I thought that was kind of strange since I was expecting a can. Then I noticed that the cup itself reeked of cigarette smoke. As did the napkins and the bag that contained my sandwich. Gross. There are few things I find more offensive than a big whiff of cigarette smoke, and the last thing I want is for my lunch to be permeated with the stuff. Needless to say, I won't be ordering takeout from Talk of the Town again, though I wouldn't rule out a visit to the actual storefront.

My experience at Schlafly over the weekend was a little strange, to be honest. I sat down and ordered a club soda and some fish tacos. The tacos were brought over in less than five minutes which was a little suspect, but I was truly hungry and took my chances. They were actually edible and I was happy to have a somewhat healthy meal before flying home.   I asked for the check and my server offered to give me a refill of my club soda in a to-go cup, which was very nice. My bill came to nineteen dollars and some change; I put thirty on the table. My server came by and picked up the check and cash, said she appreciated me, and was off. I started to realize after a few minutes that she wasn't coming back. I don't mean to sound cheap, but I wasn't about to leave a fifty percent tip, either! I basically had to hunt down said server by the kitchen to ask for some change. It was awkward! Next time, I'm eating before I get to the airport.

Tiffin is not my favorite Indian, but it is far less expensive than my favorite, so it wins out when it comes to delivery.   After reviewing a previous order, I again ordered the chili chicken and garlic naan, plus chicken tikka masala and onion bhaji, a new-to-me app.   The chili chicken was completely different from what I remembered, and my fiancé and I were not fans and will not order it again. I actually loved the onion bhaji for an inexpensive and slightly guilty app (they are fried) and the chicken tikka masala was very good but contained only 7-8 pieces of chicken. For the price, it's still a good deal and I'll likely choose Tiffin next time I'm craving Indian food at home.

My friend and I found ourselves here on Sunday night in hopes that we could get seated.  As luck would have it, there were two seats available at the chef's counter.  Since neither of us was starving, we ordered 4 plates to share~ a serrano ham and fig salad, two different flatbreads and parmesan artichokes.  Everything was really nicely presented and full of flavor.  Our server was very attentive and pleasant.       The seasonal peach sangria was delicious and probably one of the best I've had.  Our only gripe was that it was SO HOT in the restaurant.  And not just where we were seated, but everywhere.  We suspected the managers were probably trying to conjure the actual temperature of Spain to provide the full experience.  As we watched the desserts being prepared in front of us, the ice cream scooped on top started melting instantly.  I felt kind of sad for the people who had ordered them.  Overall, I'd love to try Amada again, but probably not until summer is over.  I loathe melty ice cream!

I had my first and definitely not my last experience at Crème Brûlée bistro a couple weeks ago. I had no idea the place existed until a friend posted some delicious looking photos on his instagram account. I made it my mission to try the french onion soup as soon as possible.   Sadly, the soup was sold out on the day of my visit! L'horreur! Instead, I opted for a tomato, mozzarella and pesto baguette (hold the truffle oil) with a side salad. It was very satisfying but I still have my soup craving and will need to return sooner than later to satisfy it! Also looking forward to trying some of their beautiful pastries.

I had a pretty solid first experience at Poké-Man. I popped in on a Friday evening and placed an order for two poké bowls. One of the employees helped me out with the menu and some questions I had. I decided to get a bubble tea at the last minute and asked for the black tea but made less sweet. The end result was a delicious bubble tea made exactly to my request.   At home, the bowls were also as-requested. I thought some of the toppings were a little skimpy but, overall, still a pretty packed bowl that kept me full for the rest of the night. I'm looking forward to more visits and am happy they use frequent customer cards as well!

Upon hearing that some of our go-to South Philly Christmas tree locations were not operating this year, my husband got to work on finding a new spot. Not only was picking out our tree at Giordano fast and easy, we also spent less than any other year in recent memory.   I pulled up curbside on Washington Ave and nervously turned on my flashers. Yep, I was that girl, but thankfully didn't get any angry honks. Within five minutes, we selected a great-looking tree with a pleasant bluish hue (a blue spruce, I'm told). We paid just $45 plus a nice tip for the young guy who eagerly helped us out. Our tree was loaded onto the car and we were off.   The tree is absorbing water quickly and it smells fantastic. The needles are definitely sharper than other trees we've had in the past, but I don't plan on bumping into it too often! Great experience and we'll definitely consider them again next year!

A South Jersey gem! Donkey's Place makes a killer cheesesteak that's slightly different from your typical sub shop steak. They use a round, poppy seed roll, and they stack that roll with layers of meat, American cheese and perfectly fried onions. It is a heavy sandwich. And it is delicious.   Call me crazy, but I think the sandwich is even better if you let it marinate for a little while before diving right in. It also tastes great reheated in an air fryer. No matter how you like your cheesesteaks, Donkey's makes a great one!

Nomad Roman is my preferred Nomad location. Although I do think the Nomad just off of South Street is nicer, decor-wise, Nomad Roman on Locust Street has two things going for it that the other doesn't: less children and better pizza. Of course, pizza style is definitely a matter of preference. For me, the super thin and slightly charred crust at Nomad Roman is worlds better than the slightly thicker and much more chewy crust at Nomad.   The salad with mixed greens, pears, dried cranberries, blue cheese and pecans is a perfect start to a meal. Meatballs with broccoli rabe and a dusting of parmesan are also really great. You can't go wrong in the pizza department but the Trenton pie is pretty close to perfect. It's also just five bucks at their amazing happy hour, which also features five dollar glasses of house red and white.

Mummies, Roman statues, the third largest sphinx in the world: The Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology is fantastic!    I loved this museum when I first toured it almost ten years ago for a business event, and I loved it just as much on my second visit during Fair Food Philly's Brewer's Plate event. Exploring ancient history with a beer in hand is definitely an awesome experience.   The architecture of the building (especially the rotunda) is breathtaking and the grounds are lovely. This is a great museum and should not be overlooked by visitors or long-time residents.

We ordered poke bowls for delivery from Red Poke last night for the first time. The ordering platform we used (Uber Eats) required a selection of two proteins. I would have preferred to stick with just one but went with the big eye tuna and yellowtail.   The bowl was large and the ingredients were fresh, but every so often something in the bowl had a mild chemically taste. I couldn't tell if it was the cucumbers or the onion crisps but I narrowed it down to those two things, which I'd probably avoid in the future. The cucumbers were sliced a little too thick for my liking, anyway. I'd just try other toppings next time.   This wasn't my favorite poke spot but I'd be open to trying again in the future.
Grounds in my cuppa, with increasing frequency? No thank you, Grooveground.  Surprise! "Regular" had cinnamon undertones. Morning just got worse.

I had a major craving for one of those Thanksgiving sandwiches and this Primo was close to my location when said craving occurred. The store was clean and employees were all business but friendly. As I waited for my order, I perused the chips - they have every variety you could possibly want.   I wanted my sandwich hot but was informed that it might not travel well and was encouraged to opt for the cold turkey on the sandwich and a side of gravy. A generous side of gravy was provided in a separate paper bag, and I agree that this was the best option.   All of the ingredients of the sandwich were good and my craving was satisfied, but I think the Thanksgiving sandwich is better in my imagination than it is on my tastebuds. I think I'll stick with regular hoagies for the most part, but if the craving strikes once a year I'll definitely hit Primo for the fix.

Rittenhouse Square? Too crowded, too expected. Washington Square? Too far, not enough character. Fitler Square? Juuuuust right!  This unassuming little park just across from Dmitri's charmed me when I first discovered it a year or so ago, and it has remained my favorite in Philly. It's well-maintained, with a few cute animal statues, brick walkways and lots of soft green grass for picnicking. The park is never overcrowded, and there is always a bench available, even on weekends. What a perfect oasis near my home!

Definitely a huge fan of The PokéSpot! I've ordered for delivery and stopped in for takeout for the first time yesterday. I'm fairly certain I ordered the same thing each time; a rice base with one scoop of ahi tuna and one scoop of spicy tuna. I topped with seaweed salad, avocado and cucumber, though it's kind of hard to narrow down because there are so many delicious fresh options! Crispy onions add some texture and wasabi shoyu sauce on the side is perfect for an extra flavor kick.   There was a line when I visited in-person but it moved quickly and the employees were friendly. The bowls make for a hearty lunch and tide me over until dinner. Nothing but praise from this girl!

I enjoyed this cute local theater that shows only a few feature flicks at a time. Though clearly an older building, the theater was clean and comfortable. We saw Silver Linings Playbook and the picture was very clear and, just as important, the movie audience was respectful. Before the movie, an employee came in to announce a raffle the theater was running, and also talk about their upcoming Oscars party, which sounded like fun. I'd happily trek out to Ambler for dinner and a movie again.

Caffe Maida provided two much-needed espressos on a recent evening in Ambler. But let's be real. If there was any competition at all this place would probably be in a little bit of trouble. I can't give less than three stars since they seemed to be the only coffee-slinging game in town, however. Glad they had the beans when I needed them.

I'm pretty sure Lowe's was the first store I physically set foot inside since the Covid-19 pandemic took over in mid-March. Last weekend, I decided it was time to get my roofdeck summer-ready and I felt comfortable enough to visit the store while donning a mask and bringing my own Lysol wipes.   This particular location has an exit only situation coming from the garden center, with entry taking place through the main doors. Everyone there including customers had masks on which was great. I didn't see any wipes available but I also didn't look super hard. I grabbed a cart from the parking lot so I could sweep through the outdoor plants by the curb before entering the store itself.    The plants and flower selection was poppin' and I picked up a couple geraniums and a gorgeous yellow calla lily that I am hoping I can keep alive for as long as possible. I would definitely return to this Lowe's if I needed more home or garden supplies.

This Ritz is a step below the one around the corner closer to Chestnut Street. But it's still a solid spot to catch a flick.   On weekday afternoons, the cost for a movie is just $6.50, which is practically unheard of these days. Concessions are still on the pricey side - some things never change.   Bathrooms were relatively clean on my recent visit. Ever notice how Ritz bathrooms smell like orange Fruit Loops?

I'm new to the frozen yogurt game and don't have a ton of experience with what's great and what's not so great. But Kiwi was bright, clean, had plenty of choices and a friendly staff. What's not to like? To expand my frozen yogurt portfolio, I tried dollops of the red velvet flavor with graham cracker crumbles, peanut butter flavor with super mini chocolate chips and original tart flavor with Cinnamon Toast Crunch. You get your own and then pay by the ounce, which is great for trying as much or as little as you'd like. It was a nice treat, and I may just be intrigued enough to develop a habit.

Wow, Rowan has really changed since I was an undergrad. There's a full on shopping center with multiple restaurants. Back in my day, (insert long, winding speech about terrible food options and walking uphill both ways).   The Chickie's & Pete's wasn't too crowded on a Wednesday night. We were seated near a huge screen, which made hockey watching lots of fun. I cannot go to a C&P and not get crab fries, so we ordered those as soon as we sat down. I was happy this location had Heineken 0.0, since I was driving but love beer with bar food.   The fries were delish, and then we moved on to the lobster pizza, which had a lot more flavor than I expected! It was very garlicky and had loads of cheese and some really nice chunks of lobster tail.   Our server was friendly but didn't come around super often, which was really the only negative part of the experience. Overall, a solid night out before heading home!

When the winter months set in, my cravings for hot chocolate begin to skyrocket. After attending a Sixers game one cold night a few weeks ago, we decided to hit Broad Street Diner after the game. We sat at the counter and I had hot chocolate with whipped cream while my husband had a black and white milkshake. Both hit the spot, and the milkshake was huge.   Our server was sweet and overall the experience was good. This may become a tradition for post-game celebrations!

Hands down, Maple Shade Custard Stand has THE BEST soft serve in this area.  I say this as a former employee (summer job in college) and a lifelong customer.  My sister worked one or two summers there during college as well and shares my opinion.  Sundaes, milk shakes, flurries (soft ice cream blended with toppings of your choice), water ice, homemade chocolate covered bananas, chipwiches and ice cream sandwiches are just some of the things you can get every day of the week and any time of year.  I always leave happy and with exactly what I came for-- they are well prepared and well stocked for business.  Probably one of the reasons why they have been around for decades!

While I have yet to dine at this particular Le Pain Quotidien, I do have to give their staff five giant stars for helping me out the other day. I was running late to a personal training session at Platoon's new facility and I realized as I got to the corner of 8th and Walnut that I actually wasn't sure about the exact address. Panicked and without my iPhone, I popped into Le Pain Quotidien to see if, by chance, one of the employees would know where the place was located.   After explaining my predicament, the friendly young lady behind the counter popped out her smart phone and checked her Yelp app for me. I got to my appointment with a few minutes to spare and a smile of relief. I'll be sure to update once I return for a paid experience!

If you're looking for an upscale cocktail bar without the riff raff while in New Orleans, this is your place. In fact, they close at 11pm on weeknights and midnight on Fridays and Saturdays.   A group of us popped in for a nightcap after the place was recommended to me by a Yelp bud (thanks, Kyle!). Perusing the menu of tiki drinks, I went straight for the mai tai and it was absolutely delicious. So good, that my cocktail was passed around to everyone in my group for a taste. When we heard the gong (yes, gong!) signaling last call, everyone placed their order for a mai tai. Solid spot!

I checked this place out for lunch earlier this week. The menu is massive and curiously runs the gamut from traditional pizza shop offerings to Mediterranean style dishes.   I placed my order online, but when I tried to punch in the promotion code for a 10% discount, nothing happened. The ordering process was easy and even offered options for customization. I removed the onions from my chicken Caesar wrap and entered a note that I wanted the dressing served on the side.   When I arrived less than ten minutes later, my order was ready, but the dressing was mixed in the wrap. (So if you plan to order a sauce on the side, I'd recommend calling over using the online ordering process.)  The wrap was decent, but the chicken was more in the style of a chicken cheesesteak than regular grilled chicken. It was served with a bag of chips and a pickle. For less than $8, it wasn't a bad lunch option, but it's not about to become a regular in the rotation, either.

Our group of six ducked into The Corner Foodery for some pre-gaming action before the Flyers game on Saturday. The set up is half bottle shop, half sit-down eatery. You can pick out bottles to drink there and just pay as you go and enjoy the seating. There are still and bubbly water taps and several TVs scattered around. I was surprised at the ample amount of seating and even more surprised at the lack of people. I think this place is still under the radar, but I can't imagine that it will be for very long. It's not often you can go to a restaurant and drink a beer at the bottle price.     The menu is a mix of sandwiches, salads and snacks that sounds delicious. I'm eager to get back for lunch or dinner sometime soon.

Our normal sushi delivery spot wasn't open so we tried Koto on a whim, and our delivery experience was pretty great. We ordered the vegetable gyoza, which had a perfect chew and flavorful filling. For rolls, my husband had the spicy tuna and salmon avocado, while I had the spicy tuna and tuna avocado. We shared an angel roll, as well. Everything was packaged nicely and the prices were fair. I'd try them again!

My feelings about this location of Good Karma somewhat echo my feelings of the other; decent but not my fave. This particular spot is very close to where I live, so I'm sure it will go into the rotation of places to grab a cup, as I've yet to find the cafe that will become my steady.   The other day I stopped by for an impromptu latte. I was sure I would end up liking this second version of GK better than the first. The cafe was smaller than I expected, but it was bright and full of the same good vibes that fill the front part of the Pine Street shop.   I walked outside and pulled my first sip - it was warm, not even close to hot. Frustrating, since coffee comes at a premium nowadays.   I'll return, but I make no promises once I find my go-to establishment.

Cute coffee shop with excellent iced coffee and great pastries. I enjoyed a ham and cheese croissant which was flaky, buttery deliciousness.   I read something on their website about how tables can be reserved for $10/hour. Since I was meeting with one of my team members I decided to reserve a table for two hours. When I arrived on that weekday morning, the coffee shop was empty save for one or two other people. So, I most likely wouldn't formally reserve a table again unless I was going at a peak time - seemed like kind of a waste of money. Although, your reservation does get you a 20% discount on all food and drink orders. And I suppose if you really needed to guarantee a table for a work meeting, it's good to know that Rally offers this, since I can't think of a single other place that does. So there's pros and cons to that.   I am looking forward to returning!

I am a regular at the Lacquer Lounge in Queen Village but the Rittenhouse location proved to be more convenient this week so I decided to make my appointment there. The space is larger than the other location but just as cute and girly. Everyone working was laid-back and friendly, which is one of the things I have always loved about Lacquer Lounge.   Both my classic pedi with Lina and my power hour mani with Nicole were great. These gals really made my nails look fantastic. Even though the Queen Village location will always have a slight edge for me, I'm really excited about this second location which is closer to where I live and also convenient for whenever I'm running around Rittenhouse. Best of both worlds!

After staring longingly at the "Coming Soon" sign that hung in the doorway for months on end, Woksabi finally opened and I was able to check out the eats.    Yesterday being my birthday (shameless plug~ I'm a Leo, what do you expect?!), I decided it was as good a time as any to treat myself to a little take-out.  I tried the "tuna madness" roll, which the previous reviewer recommended.  It was a crunchy spicy tuna roll topped with seared tuna, scallions and tobiko.  I figured at $12, the roll would be pretty substantial, but I threw in a cucumber roll just in case.    I got home and tore into my bag-- and was a little disappointed.  The tuna madness roll was no larger than an average, run of the mill tuna roll, with small pieces of seared tuna on top.  I wondered, "Where exactly is the madness?" It was good for sure, but definitely not worth $12.    I'll be back, but next time will opt for the regular spicy tuna rolls that cost half the price.

Does someone mind explaining why the apocalypse hit this Walmart location a long time ago?   Walking in, I'm like a deer in headlights with the absence of neck tattoos, tight polyester clothing and loud, screaming children. I quickly scurry past the masses at customer service and Subway, trying to avoid eye contact while planning my attack. The faster I get to the items I need, the faster I can just get out of there already.   Problem is, the items I need never seem to be in stock, or available at all. Something as basic as plastic cups was too much to ask on my recent visit. I secured small cups but, other than the giant red Solo cups, there were no other options for something in between.   The only redeeming thing about the place is the body shop, which unfortunately means I have had to endure many an hour walking around the store while my car received an oil change. There aren't even any decent stores in the strip mall that shares the parking lot to escape to.   I do believe I made my final exit through this Walmart's doors the other day.

Recently, I wrote about the disappointing search for good pad Thai in my area.  I had surrendered my efforts and had given up hope, when I suddenly recalled seeing some random hot entrees on a take out menu from nearby Woksabi.  Thinking the chances of finding Thai items at a Japanese restaurant were slim, I quickly scanned the menu when, out of nowhere, I saw it: Pad Thai with chicken, shrimp or beef: $10.  I promptly placed my order and was told it would be ready in 20 minutes.    A half hour later, I pulled a huge container of steaming hot goodness from the brown paper bag.  The noodles did not appear oily at all, which meant the dish was created by Thailand standards as opposed to most Americanized versions which are made with oil (yeah, I looked it up- Wikipedia rocks!).  My request to 86 the tofu was honored.  Not only was the serving size large enough for two lunches, it was also light, flavorful and just all-around awesome.  Pad Thai victory!!!

Airport food is so hit or miss (mostly miss) but Balducci's is a solid option. They have a large variety of snacks including some heartier stuff that actually passes off as healthy, too.   There is a pretty solid selection of grab and go meals, including sandwiches, salads and vegetarian entrees. There is also a counter where you can get some of the sandwiches warmed up. That's where I ordered my bacon, egg and cheese on an english muffin while grabbing a caprese baguette to go. (In my opinion, caprese is the most inoffensive sandwich one can eat on a plane.)  The breakfast sandwich was actually quite tasty. Their coffee is also acceptable. But the best part of Balducci's is that you can get in and out relatively quickly. The Starbucks and La Colombe located in the main hallway outside of terminals B and C always have the longest lines! This is my new go-to.

It's been a while since I've eaten in the restaurant, but every time I have whether for dinner, brunch or a small party, it is always a great experience.    Recently, my mom ordered dinner from Due Amici for my sister's graduation party.  There was plenty of food and everything was delicious.  Even better was knowing that my mom would have one less thing to stress about so she could enjoy herself along with everyone else.

I love Career Wardrobe and everything they stand for - bettering the community by helping unemployed women to find jobs and look the part.   Donating is easy, especially at The Wardrobe Boutique location on Spring Garden. The building is located on the corner and there is a sizeable loading zone on 19th Street where you can pull up to unload. The boutique itself is cute and well-organized, and the women who work at this location are always so friendly. Tax forms are available, if you need/want them.   Great community service!

This place is so solid, I have to update my review to five stars. We order delivery from The Foodery pretty regularly, and we are always very happy with our orders. The half sandwich plus a side of soup or salad is a great deal at $11. You get the heartiness of the sandwich without feeling like you went overboard on the carbs. Favorite sandwiches are the olive oil poached tuna, the godfather, and the roasted turkey (served warm).    Sandwiches are very consistent - I know what I'm going to get every single time. Ingredients are tasty and high quality. I definitely think The Foodery is a level above other comparable sandwich shops.

I've experienced better is right. Of all Saladworks locations I've patronized, this was one of the worst. The workers were friendly but the restaurant wasn't a place I'd like to sit down and eat a meal.   The salad I did get was totally fine, but the salads on display looked sad and gross. They aren't trying very hard, and it shows.

First Person Arts is a first class organization. Their events are meaningful, well-run, well-staffed and always a great time. I attended my first Story Slam last week and it happened to be a Grand Slam - pretty much a guarantee for great narratives and funny deliveries.   Before the Slam was an optional pre-party barbecue catered by Sweet Lucy's and Victory Brewing Company. I cannot say enough great things about Sweet Lucy's and their delicious smoked meats and hearty sides. Experiencing them once again only reminded me that I need to return to the mothership soon, likely with a sixer of Victory brew.  The Slam took place in a large, air-conditioned theater with better than average folding chairs and the right amount of leg room. Every participant followed the rules and the time guidelines, and the event moved along seamlessly, with a short but necessary break for intermission.   If you haven't yet seen or participated in a Story Slam, they take place about once a month and they provide a fun, different kind of night out.

My sister and I wandered over to Falls Taproom for an after dinner drink on Friday night. The downstairs bar was packed but we grabbed two newly opened seats at the bar upstairs. I love the dark wood and old timey light bulbs. Didn't really love/understand the TVs with black and white movies, which were on silent. I say sports or nothing!   The cocktail menu is interesting and I was immediately drawn to the hot apple cider with rum. My sister opted for another boozy concoction but she switched over to the apple cider for her second round. I loved the cracked clove on top; it made the drink very fragrant. This is the perfect beverage for a chilly fall night.   Our bartender was nice and we enjoyed chatting with him. We're already talking about our next visit!

Stella Pizza is pretty darn good.  It's my second choice when I order pizza because I do prefer the pies at another Haddon Ave. establishment, but the thing about Stella is that their other items are reliable as well.  Salads are great (especially the Caesar salad and the buffalo chicken salad), and they come with a garlicky roll.    AND, Stella was my great-grandmom's name.  What's not to like about that?!

After a long car ride home from North Jersey, the last thing I wanted to do was go back out in search of dinner. We placed an order with Slice, and within 45 minutes dinner arrived. One small signature salad and one large margherita pizza came to around $25, with free delivery.   The dressing for the salad came in a side cup, which was great because there were no soggy bits. Just fresh arugula, dried cranberries, gorgonzola and pine nuts. The pie, on the other hand, was definitely soggy. Some time in the oven helped significantly, but shouldn't delivery pizza be ready to enjoy when it arrives?   Nonetheless, I do like Slice and I'll give some of their other pies a try the next time we order.

When I learned that the pastry chef who made my wedding cake was taking over a local bakery in Wayne, I immediately marked my calendar for a visit! Marqessa Gesualdi is not only extremely talented, she's also lovely to work with and truly cares about creating the best experience possible for her clients.   Alisha S and I popped into Aux Petits Delices for some morning sugar. We shared the flaky napoleon and the ultra rich delice - both were incredible! The delice put me into a near sugar coma, but the combination of dark chocolate and hazelnut were irresistible.   The bakery also sells baguettes, croissants and chocolates. They have some seating, and serve La Colombe coffee, so you can enjoy a sweet treat right in the shop. I am so happy Marqessa has landed in her very own bakery and cannot wait to commission her for a (smaller) replica of my amazing wedding cake sometime in the future!

Dig is pretty similar in concept to another nearby healthy, fast-casual concept. However, Dig's execution is much better. I'd seen tons of recent positive reviews on Yelp so I made a mental note to check them out next time I was in the area.   Fast forward to my visit, I probably looked like a deer in headlights when I got in line. Thankfully, the staff could not have been nicer and even helped me along with some suggestions to keep me moving. I opted for a rice base, salmon protein, roasted brussel sprouts, and roasted carrots (there may have been some other root veggies in there as well). An employee suggested I try the mustard sauce and she was spot on because that sauce went perfectly with this combo! Everything had so much flavor and I was really impressed with my experience overall.   I'm dying to try some of the macaroni and cheese but that will have to be on a day when I'm feeling splurgey. Otherwise, I'm super grateful for another healthy and quick to-go option in Center City!

I was craving some basic comfort food recently and decided to order a grilled cheese and tomato soup from The Foodery. The order came with a pickle slice and bag of chips. Though I did need to reheat the grilled cheese in my air fryer upon arrival, it was still great and the tomato soup was perfect (and topped with a big, cheesy crouton thing!).   I've always liked this spot and am glad to see they are still offering quality eats!

Jackass Burrito is a welcome addition to my delivery lineup. The burritos are a bit of a departure from the usual options. We ordered the K-Town (korean beef, kimchi, etc.), baja shrimp (crispy shrimp, cabbage, baja sauce, etc.) and all day breakfast burritos, plus an order of guac and the salsa trio.   The burritos were large, wrapped very well, and delivered in super cute boxes. We enjoyed all of them, though I'd consider these burritos to be more on the splurgey side of the burrito spectrum (it's possible to eat a semi-healthy burrito, I swear!). The shrimp had a distinct buffalo tang, which I loved but my husband wasn't crazy about. Of all three options, I think the breakfast burrito was my favorite. Guac and salsas were all great, too. Will definitely order again!

(said in a NeNe Leakes voice) You have done me wrrronnng, Yelp!   With a four star average, I thought I was in store for a pretty great slice of pie. Not so. The first bite of the plain slice was promising, but subsequent nibbles were dry and lacking flavor. The bbq chicken slice had an off-putting flavor from the barbecue sauce. Ick.  Perhaps a whole hot pie would work out better than a single slice from behind the counter... but it's unlikely I'll be back to find out.

I am way late in my review of Cook, which is one of Philadelphia's best offerings in the food and beverage world. Every month, a schedule of events is announced, along with a date when tickets go on sale. Tickets go very quickly, and they are pricey. But totally worth the splurge.  I've attended a dinner put together by sushi chef Hiroyuki Tanaka (of Zama restaurant), which was beautiful and incredible. Wine pairings were poured for every course. More recently, I attended a rum class by Sara Justice from Franklin Mortgage that was fun and boozy. Some small bites were served.  Seating wraps around the large kitchen island in the center, providing a great view for all and accessibility to ask questions. Looking forward to my next class!

This gorgeous store is packed to the gills with team memorabilia. Unfortunately, the selection of merch for the hometown teams is a bit limited. But if you're a fan of another team and you live in Philly, this is certainly your best bet for finding gear. But it's definitely going to cost ya. I picked up a Sixers tee for my dad today and it was not cheap. It's a very nice shirt, though, one that he'll hopefully have for many years due to the high quality.

I had a very positive experience at OCF yesterday. It had been a while since my last visit. I'm not sure why; this place is in my neighborhood and there always seems to be plenty of seating available. They have free wifi and the music is great, ranging from indie rock to jazz during my visit.   The baristas were so nice and I really enjoyed chatting with them. And these guys make an absolutely delicious (and pretty!) chai tea latte with real tea. I noticed some really tasty-looking pastries and cookies, but didn't partake. Next time! I won't wait so long before my next visit, either.

I found myself craving that baja shrimp burrito again so we placed another order with Jackass Burrito. This time, we also tried the frito pie burrito and also a more traditional al pastor burrito (I don't believe this was an option last time so it was nice to see a new menu item). We again ordered the guac and salsa trio. This was more than enough food for two meals - one very hefty dinner followed by a slightly less hefty dinner the next day.   I'm a fan!

A friend of mine (what's up, Kylie!) told me about Geisha House when we got together for coffee last week. Since it was in the area and I had some free time, I took a stroll on over to check it out for myself.   First impression: super cute shop! I started chatting with the woman working who I quickly found out was filling in for her daughter (the owner of the store) that morning. She could not have been nicer and it was really nice to chat with her as I shopped.   I wasn't looking for anything in particular but ended up trying on four different pieces. There were two that I really liked but I ultimately went for a dress for just under fifty bucks. As I was paying I also took note of the many great accessories and small gifts. I had to hold myself back from impulse purchasing several more items.   I was beyond bummed when my favorite Old City boutique recently closed, but I'm thrilled to have found a new store that I like just as much!

Welcome to the neighborhood, OCF! My first trip was fairly solid. Four styles of coffee were offered and served in a French press, yielding multiple cups for my friend (who unfortunately didn't love the brew she selected). The barista asked if I wanted my latte flat, which I can honestly say I've never been asked before in my history of ordering lattes. Apparently it has to do with the thickness of the foam.   The café has an Elixr meets Noble meets office building vibe. There is a lot of lime green, wood, funky chairs, and some more practical-looking chairs as well. I personally hope OCF will be a more mature alternative to La Va, where people will be able to have meetings or get some work done in a calmer setting. Time will tell.   Cakes, croissants and other baked goods looked delicious, and come from The Sweet Life Bakeshop. I'll be returning soon for a slice of that lemon cake to go along with my coffee.

I really love Gran Caffe L'Aquila. It's sort of become my low-key coffee meeting spot. The vibes are super relaxed in the morning - it feels more like a market in the early hours of the day than a restaurant. You can order coffee at the counter and sit anywhere.   Around lunchtime is when things start picking up and table service kicks off. Last week I had a coffee meeting around 11, but I decided to stick around a little while longer to get some work done and enjoy lunch. I had the chitarra pasta which was tossed with a bright, zesty tomato sauce, guanciale and pecorino cheese. It was perfectly sized and absolutely delicious.   The sandwiches also looked incredible and I would love to try them sometime. But first, I need to make my way through the rest of the pasta menu.

So I've never written a Sweet Lucy's review. Say whaaaa? From my first visit, after a football UYE with yelpers Jim H, Bill M, Dan C, Akshay M and Caroline L, to my experiences with their catering at First Person Arts events, one thing is for certain: Lucy is one smooth southern lady.   Pulled pork, mac and cheese, spicy collards and corn bread - that's all you need to know. If you're planning to eat at the restaurant, bring a crew, bring some brew and grab one of the picnic tables. You're guaranteed to have a great meal and a great time.

For what it is (cheap and quick), Le Chic Nails is all right.   But I'm a big girl now, and I've moved on to greener pastures, in the form of nicer salons.  Should you choose to make Le Chic Nails a part of your girly upkeep, ask for Pheng. She's a sweetheart and she does a nice job.  (FYI: Cam, the woman from my visits back in '09, no longer works there.)

This local farmers' market is a great place for flowers and fresh produce. The flower selection is vast and includes flats for planting, larger buckets for doorsteps and hanging baskets. I picked up two beautiful hanging baskets this week, one of which contained bright orangey begonias. They also carry seasonal flowers, like tulips and lilies for Easter.   The market always seems to be open during daytime from spring through the fall and prices can't be beat. Well, unless you hit a place like Produce Junction, but I'd rather spend a couple more bucks and shop local.

Gotta give some more love to one of my favorite spots for a quick sandwich and a great place to stock up on some grocery staples! Though I don't get there as often as I'd like simply due to distance from my house, Palm Tree is a must stop anytime I'm in the area.  The chicken salad is still a favorite though I've been opting for tuna lately which is always great. I love that there is always a loaf or two of fresh bread available so I can grab a pint of tuna salad to make lunches at home. Their day-old bags of rolls, bagels and croissants for half price also come in handy. I bring them home, slice them up and throw them in the freezer for whenever I need them.   The snack selection is amazing - I don't know how they manage to pack so many things into such a small store, but Palm Tree carries all of my go-tos, like Pop Chips, Smart Sweets, Tate's and more. Add in the always-friendly service, plus the recent addition of plexiglass barriers between employees and staff, and you've got a five star biz!

For a late Monday morning, this restaurant was surprisingly busy and the staff seemed very frantic. I sat at an open table which I soon realized was sticky from the previous guest and was never wiped down. There were also a lot of flies in the restaurant which was pretty annoying.   My omelet arrived quickly and was just okay - definitely not something I would go out of my way for again. I find my experiences at the other LPQ higher up on Walnut to be pretty consistently solid, and that is my preferred location for sure.

Huge Zoës Kitchen fangirl here! I used to frequent the Cherry Hill location, but now that the Moorestown location has opened it's become my new-go to as I am in the area often.   Everything at this location is just as clean, fresh and delicious as I've come to expect from Zoës. My go-to is the salmon kebabs with tzatziki, side salad and white beans. My husband loves the chicken piadina. I've often ordered the fresh fruit side and it is always a great mix of really delicious fruit. I so appreciate businesses that make it easy to eat healthy  yet heartily, and that is accomplished here.   Last but not least, the staff at this location has been great, particularly the young gent who works weeknights.

Seasons 52 has the best happy hour for a health-conscious person who wants to go up on a Tuesday (or any weekday, for that matter). My friend and I arrived shortly after 5pm and the bar was already packed - we nabbed two of the last remaining seats and promptly ordered some vinho verde. The pours are generous at Seasons 52, and this seems to be the case regardless of the location. I like it.   After trying nearly all of their happy hour bites on previous visits, I know that I'm not super crazy about any of them. So my friend and I ordered a couple flatbreads to share, which are tasty and still pretty low in cals. The pepperoni with pesto was very flavorful while the artichoke and goat cheese was nice and light but still tasty. Will return next time I want some happy hour action before a shopping trip!

Marsha Brown's was recommended by several Yelpers as a solid spot for lunch and I'm really glad we checked it out. As much as I wanted a burger, I opted for the chopped salad. I never imagined I'd crave a salad as much as I have since I finished it yesterday.   The chopped salad contained asparagus, artichoke, broccoli, olives, bacon and blue cheese. It was all mixed together and formed into a mold of sorts. I ordered it with grilled shrimp and the dressing (ranch) on the side. I don't know what made that salad so delicious but all the ingredients together were awesome. And the dressing was absolutely perfect, though I hardly needed any since the salad itself was so flavorful.   We sat at the bar since all tables were booked. The bartender was very friendly but he also had to take care of the nearby tables, so things like place settings and drink refills had to be requested. No big, though. We were taken care of and we really enjoyed ourselves. I will be making plans to return, and hopefully not too far into the future - I need that salad in my life!

Bomb Bomb is every bit the stereotypical South Philly restaurant. Ancient reservations book? Check. Loud, perhaps a-little-too-friendly service? Check. Red sauce? Check. Wine in jugs? Check check.   I passed on the jug wine but gave an enthusiastic hell yes to a lot of the food menu during my visit with friends a few months back. We ordered a bunch of stuff to share, though they were also out of some of the items we requested. Like salad. Weird, right? Nonetheless, our veggie-free meal was still delicious and there were plenty of laughs thanks to the laid back style of the servers and other patrons.   Looking forward to my next visit!

Just here to add yet another five star review to Philadelphia Distilling's Yelp listing! My husband and I stopped by for pre-concert cocktails and this place did not disappoint! It was my first time there but his millionth (or so). I need to start taking up his invites more often because I've clearly been missing out on some of the city's best spots!   The space is incredibly beautiful and we were lucky to grab the last two open seats at the bar on our visit. The bartenders really know their stuff and the woman who helped us out could not have been more on point. She asked what kind of drinks we like, flavor profiles, etc. and then mixed us up some very tasty concoctions.   Very much looking forward to my next visit!

Ugh, our Philadelphia state liquor stores, am I right? This one was close to where I spent my afternoon working, so I headed in with high hopes of a decent bubbles selection for celebrating my first wedding anniversary. To my surprise, there were several inexpensive but nice enough bottles to choose from. I went with a bottle of Chandon and also a cheap Sauvignon Blanc to go along with our dinner.  This store is one of the old, ugly ones that hasn't yet been remodeled. Where the names of countries on the walls has absolutely nothing to do with the organization of the wines underneath.   Oh, and as other reviewers have mentioned, there was a panhandler. Not outside of the store, IN the actual store. No idea how this happened as there was a security guy at the entrance when I walked in.   Good luck and godspeed.

As most probably know, I tend to dine out more than I dine in. But on the rare occasions that I do feel like holding it down in the kitch, I want to cook with the freshest ingredients possible. Headhouse Farmers Market appeals to both sides of my culinary conundrum.   On the days I want to get crafty, there are loads of fresh produce available. Some veggies I wouldn't even know what to do with. More often than not, I just want to fork over some cash for a prepared product. Luckily for me, Market Day Canele, Renaissance Sausage, Los Taquitos de Puebla and the expensive-but-delicious lemonade stand are there to satisfy. Look for me on the nearby steps, with all the others who go to the Farmers Market just to eat!

I've only been twice, but I really like Lucky 13. My first visit was several years ago for some drinks. Not sure why it took me so long to return but it was selected as our meeting place for Saturday night's shenanigans and it was just right. The bartender was friendly and fast with slinging our drinks. Several rounds ended up costing far less than I anticipated, a welcome respite in this world of fourteen dollar cocktails in which we live.   The music was on point and just loud enough. The TVs were programmed to whatever games were taking place. The bathroom was clean and I especially liked the cool throwback photos adorning the walls (Bridget Bardot - meow!). I've heard the food is surprisingly delicious and I'm looking forward to seeing for myself next time.

It was well worth the rainy drive to Turnersville to receive the kind of friendly, straightforward service that I was not afforded at another Hyundai dealer closer to where I live.  I worked with a negotiator (who I hired) to handle the details of the purchase of my new car and the trade-in of my old one. He arranged everything with Dave at Hyundai, who was very nice to work with, patiently answering all of my questions and showing me every last detail of my new car. I also received more than I expected for the trade-in of my old vehicle, which was awesome.   The paperwork was pretty straightforward and quick, and there were no surprises. I am thrilled with my new car and with my experience at Hyundai of Turnersville!

This is my new go-to nail place.  I randomly stopped in a few weeks ago on a Monday night and was able to get a pedicure without an appointment.  The employees were all very friendly and welcoming, and my nail tech, Cam, did a great job.  When my service was complete, the owner gave me a card for $5 off on my next visit.  Two weeks later, I returned for a mani and pedi, again with Cam and this time with an appointment.  She again did an excellent job and I was in an out in about an hour.  The salon itself is great because the pedicure chairs all have awesome massage functions and the manicure chairs are comfortable and have wheels (i.e., you don't have to risk ruining your nails by touching the chair).  The decor is cute and very beachy.

I was on the hunt for "saucy" traditional pizza yesterday, and a friend recommended Francoluigi's. I was pumped to see the special - two medium pies for $15 (good on Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday). I ordered the special, plus a caesar salad and a side of marinara for crust-dipping. I was able to pay by card over the phone and was told delivery would be within the hour.   True to their word, my delivery arrived about 45 minutes later. The medium pizzas are on the small side, but perfect for two people to share. While I wouldn't say the pizza was especially saucy, the extra side of marinara I ordered made up for it. If you can wait an extra ten minutes, I'd strongly suggest re-heating slices in the oven for a much-needed crisp. Props to the caesar, which was large and had the most delicious homemade dressing.   We have a second pizza on deck for tonight's dinner and I couldn't be happier about it. Francoluigi's is officially in the rotation for delivery that won't break the bank.

It's Party City, so you pretty much know what to expect walking in. Five stars for being one of the only party supplies stores in the entire city. Minus one star for the check-out process, which always seems to take far longer than it should. God forbid someone in front of you has a return. That's an all hands on deck situation.   There is a great selection of trinkets for every possible occasion or theme. They even carry those tacky cake-toppers where the bride is dragging the groom down the aisle. So there's that. For elaborate or even unique costumes, go elsewhere. Party City carries the same costumes they always have, back since the days you scoured the Halloween circular when you were 12.

Planter's House is a gem in St. Louis. My friend and I went for drinks and dinner and were not disappointed. There is a front room that has slightly more of a restaurant feel while the back room is darker and more intimate - it would be an awesome spot to bring a date.    We both started with cocktails which were made with care and heavy on the booze. I switched to wine once the food started to arrive - the bartender gave a very nice pour. We had the marinated olives and a cheese plate to start and I would highly recommend both. I opted for the cioppino for my main and it was very nice - the toast that was lathered in aioli was perfect for broth dipping. I was powerless against those carbs.   We passed on dessert though a quick look at the menu would suggest maybe that was a mistake. A homemade "twicks" bar? Someone please get that and report back.

I liked everything about this coffee shop, to be quite honest. There was plenty of available seating on a weekday morning, the ac was kicking on what was an unseasonably hot day, and I had a pretty view of 13th and Pine. The cherry on top? La Colombe is the house brew. I was quite content during my almost two hour visit.   The baristas were nice, and I was able to start a tab since I was expecting someone to meet me a bit later. They also take credit cards! Before leaving I ended up ordering a chicken salad sandwich on ciabatta to go. If that wasn't the best chicken salad I've had in a long time. It was awesome! I'll definitely add The Last Drop to my rotation for those days when I need to get out of the house to work or take a meeting.

Kraftwork is Sidecar's Northern sibling. The beer list is great, and you can see what's on deck after any particular keg is kicked. The look of the bar is industrial and a lot of the materials were salvaged and re-used, which makes for a cool space.   We stopped by for some beers and a bite on a Sunday afternoon. The bartender was nice enough to let us sample a couple different beers while we made our decisions. We shared the beer can chicken sandwich, which was pretty tasty. The bun is really big and it's easier to just eat the thing open-faced. The fries that came with were delish and especially good with the mustard dipping sauce. The parmesan truffle popcorn was a bit of a let-down. Definitely not as good as the version at Royal. But probably a lot healthier.   I wouldn't go out of my way for Kraftwork, and that's probably because I'm lucky enough to have Sidecar around the corner from my apartment. But when in Fishtown, it's a solid choice.

Very very solid Thai delivery last night via Yelp! This was our first time ordering from Ratchada and the only thing that was disappointing was the delivery itself. We received our order about a half hour after the original hour that it was promised, and only after contacting Eat24 for an update.  Aside from the long delivery wait, everything else was on point. We ordered a Thai beef salad, which was really nice. The veggies were crisp, the beef was tender and nicely seasoned, and there was a spicy kick. I ordered the pad si-ew with shrimp, which was delicious. There was enough to split into two meals! My husband had the pork jungle - great flavors, though he said the pork was a little tough. He also had a lot of leftover veggies, which I tossed into my pad si-ew leftovers for lunch today. Possibly even better on day two! We'll be ordering from Ratchada again.

While I'm keeping my rating for Misconduct at three stars, I can now say they are three very robust, shiny stars when compared with the three hesitant stars from my previous review.   After a very late night on the town, I was in need of food in my belly and a little hair of the dog action. My lunch buddy and I were ushered past Misconduct's long bar, its seats full with construction workers who looked but kept their traps shut. Clearly, lunching indoors as opposed to on a wall somewhere has a different set of decorum.   My bloody Mary served as the life raft in my hangover sea, and my grilled chicken Caesar salad was perfectly dressed, with tender, grilled chicken and a thrilling excess of croutons. It was just what I needed to right my ship.

I like Green Line Cafe so much more than I liked Lovers and Madmen (sorry, fans of L&M). The entire space looks like it had a face-lift. The café feels cleaner and updated and it's now a great place for a business meeting or just a quiet place to get some work done. There aren't too many food options so maybe don't go there hungry or expecting much variety, but the coffee does the trick.

These guys are open late for all your drunken (food) desires. After my sister's bachelorette party shenanigans, it was pretty unanimous that everyone wanted/needed something greasy to sop up the cocktails. I gave our limo driver the address for Sonny's and we were whisked to cheesesteak heaven.   We must have arrived just before the bars closed because there were only a couple other people there. I'm sure this place gets slammed at 2am. Everyone received their orders pretty quickly. Back in the limo, I immediately regretted not adding some fries to my order. I nabbed a few from my sister's friend and they were some of the hottest, crispiest, tastiest spuds around. From what I recall, my whiz wit was pretty solid as well.   We were pretty tuned up when we arrived and the guys behind the counter were so nice. They must have the patience of saints, because I can only imagine what they deal with every weekend.

Last night, I dreamt I went to a crazy, no-holds-barred, Jersey shore-themed party... only it took place in one of Philly's classiest, most heralded restaurants, Zahav. The large, bright space was cleared of its tables, and all of the staff members were transported from a late 80s Def Leppard concert, with big hair and stonewashed denim as far as the eye could see. When I glanced into the open kitchen area, I almost pinched myself (but didn't because then I would have had to wake up). There stood some of Philadelphia's most notorious chefs, elbow to elbow, preparing delicious renditions of Jersey shore staples such as juicy hamburgers, spicy pizza turnovers, garlicky fried clams and savory crab boils. To wash it all down? Miller Lite and Miller High Life pounders, sold straight out of a wheeled ice bucket, natch. The pièce de résistance? A Journey cover band that also dedicated plenty of play time to Jersey boys Jon Bon Jovi and Bruuuuuuce.   This morning, after turning off the alarm and sleepily sitting up in bed, I noticed the blue stamp on my hand. The epic party from my dreams was real!!!

The availability of solid coffee options from the adjoined Milkboy and a really nice selection of snacks are just the icing on the cake at Bryn Mawr Film Institute. What really sets the place apart from other theaters is the small, hometown vibe and interesting selections.  Last night, I attended a preview screening of Race to the Bottom of the Earth, which starred Todd Carmichael of La Colombe. The screening was presented by First Person Arts, and after the movie, there was a Q&A with Todd which brought a very personal touch to an intense documentary.   Regarding the aesthetics of the theater itself, everything appeared clean and well-maintained, but seats were ancient and a bit uncomfortable. A minor detail but one that will sneak up after two plus hours of sitting.   It isn't often that I get out to the burbs of PA, but I would definitely go out of my way to see a film at Bryn Mawr Film Institute again.

Still very much enamored with Francoluigi's. Since my last review, I've had a couple slices at the restaurant, and another delivery experience. I loved that I was able to enjoy a Peroni with my slices at the tables by the front counter. I'd like to have a meal in the dining room sometime.   Recently, I was craving baked ziti so we placed a delivery order. Again, you can't beat delivery for a dollar and the ability to pay by card over the phone, including your driver's tip in your payment.   Their caesar salad was still incredible, and I loved the garlic knots that were included. Two orders of baked ziti for two is more than enough for two meals. I stuck one of the ziti trays in the freezer for another day. Francoluigi's uses more of a rosé sauce in their ziti, while I would have preferred a more acidic red sauce. I was glad I once again asked for a side of marinara. When I heat my extra ziti, I'll be adding some tomato sauce to the top for a little more bite.

I loved swinging by this cute beer garden in Fishtown over the weekend! There were a variety of beers on tap and a couple kombuchas by Baba's Brew that were made specifically for Tired Hands. I tried the purple one and, unfortunately, found it a little too tart/vinegary for my tastebuds. I'm fairly choosy about the kombuchas I like so don't let that dissuade you if you're a fan!   There's lots of seating all around the perimeter of the garden and the space is really cute overall. The bouncer was hilarious and the staff working the beer trailer were very nice. Definitely a great summer stop if you're in the area!

Sometimes I dismiss Lord & Taylor as sort of a mom store but I have to say that they really came through for me before my recent trip to Mexico. I went to Nordstrom to check out the swimsuits and was wildly disappointed in the selection. I called my mom in despair and she told me she had seen a pretty big variety at Lord & Taylor and she offered to meet me there (Moms. They are the best!).   Before long, I had an armful of swimwear and was headed to the dressing rooms. There were also loads of cute cover-ups as well. I left the store a little poorer but a whole lot happier. Definitely going to give Lord & Taylor another look next time the occasion arises!

Stuck in jury duty and with the Flower Show in town, Reading Terminal Market was no place to be at lunch time. I hightailed it to Maggiano's, where I hoped I could grab a seat at the bar and a reasonably healthy lunch.   As luck would have it, there was one open bar stool. I ordered an iced tea and the chopped salad with chicken. In the meantime, I received a bread basket with olive oil and spices - this helped take the edge off.   My salad arrived soon after and I have to say, it really hit the spot. This salad was huge but I ate every last bite. The dressing was delicious and not too heavy-handed. The chicken was tender. My only complaint would be that the tomatoes were hard. I wish restaurants would omit tomatoes when they aren't in season because, more often than not, they're just sad.   Lunch was pretty steep at nearly $23 plus tip, but it was worth it since I avoided the insane crowds at RTM.

I saw Kevin's review and couldn't pass up the chance to throw my two cents in also.  My family has had many dinners here for special occasions such as milestone birthdays and high school and college graduations.  Despite always having a reservation, we usually have to wait a little while for our table.  Understandable, since the place is always packed on weekends.  My grandfather usually just leads everyone in a round of drinks at the bar.    Once seated, the service ranges from pretty good to great.  As mostly everyone has mentioned, the chicken parm is huge and delicious.  We always have leftovers.  Somehow, after the rounds of bread, salad and entrees, we soldier on for the best part of the meal--strawberry and vanilla ice cream crepes.  Two or three orders will easily feed a group of 10.    Georgine's definitely isn't a spot I would think to go normally, but for an affordable family dinner, it's a great choice.

We've had our eye on Alma del Mar ever since watching their story on Queer Eye a few months back. Finally made it in for a late breakfast this morning and had a great experience!   The outdoor patio is really cute and tables are very spaced out. There aren't too many places to sit and eat in the Italian Market but Alma del Mar is right in the middle of all the action, while still being tucked away from the street. There are signs at the front of the patio with all of the Covid precautions the restaurant is taking and requesting of their customers. There was hand sanitizer on our table and everyone we encountered was wearing masks properly.   After checking out our menus, my husband and I both decided on huevos rancheros. Plus a trifecta of water, coffee and OJ. The OJ was fresh squeezed and tasted great. The coffee was awesome, too.   We were presented with enormous servings of huevos rancheros and we each left about half of the dish behind. On a future visit, we'd probably order one to share plus something else from the menu. Looking forward to next time!

Did you know you can get six packs to go at David's? Well, you can. Nothing fancy, but they do have Tsingtao, which kind of works for whatever it is you're doing in Chinatown.   I haven't tried the food, but after witnessing the take-out orders and hearing the phone blow up, I'm looking forward to a visit. Of course, I'll update my review accordingly at that time.

So happy to see the former Kanella space back in action as Kanella Grill. This iteration is casual and has a short menu with kebab and shawarma pitas and platters, plus a few side items.   My friend brought a bottle of rosé, which was promptly put on ice, and we received a cup of flavorful olives. We started with the chips and tzanziki - a huge bowl of seasoned, hot and crispy fries that is an absolute steal at four bucks.   My entree was the chicken kebab platter with rice and extra tomato salad in place of pita. It was great, and I loved the little cup of tahini that was served with the dish.  We were too full for dessert but I will be partaking in the baklava at some point in the future!

After weeks of bridesmaid dieting, the day after my friend's wedding all I wanted was margaritas and nachos. Loco Pez was the perfect setting for this indulgent affair. The bar is bright and fun. The holographic Jesus picture and various random decorations are great.   Margaritas are solid and the nachos are huge and loaded with toppings. Apparently the happy hour is pretty sweet so we'll definitely return for that. Be sure to bring cash or your debit card to hit the ATM!

I am thrilled to have a large Lou Lou boutique in Philadelphia! I've been a fan since a friend introduced me to this place years ago in DC. There are several locations in that area and I am always sure to stop by at least one when I'm in town. When I saw the signage pop up right here on 13th Street a few months back, I was stoked!  My recent visit was for a specific reason, but of course I left with way more than I planned. I wanted a placeholder ring for an upcoming vacation so that I don't run the risk of losing my good bling while participating in water sports and such. Call me paranoid, but I'd rather be safe than sorry! There were several options and I am happy with the simple but classy band I purchased for a cool $18.   In addition, I grabbed novelty sunglasses, a scarf, and a cover-up/kaftan that I'm absolutely loving. It's a good thing they have a loyalty card - my purchases are going to add up quickly!

I had plans to spend the better part of a day in KOP, and I didn't have to think too long or hard about where I'd have lunch. I arrived around 1:30 and the restaurant was pretty emptied out from the lunch crowds by that point. I ordered a salad with chicken (half and half on the dressings, which were served on the side) and a side of chickpea masala, since I was extra hungry.   I had just enough time to get my beverage (love that big Coke machine because sparkling Dasani is my jam) and all the little side sauces before my order was up. The salad plus side was plenty for a super hearty lunch and kept me full until dinner. The Choolaah salad has so much going on, flavor-wise, that not much dressing is even needed. I love the unique flavors and textures; there's a ton going on in this dish! The chicken was plentiful, super tender and delicious.   For a fast casual restaurant, the food at Choolaah exceeds every expectation. Great concept and I can't wait for my next visit!

I took a chance and ordered some delivery from Mole Poblano, a restaurant unfamiliar to me until I came across it on Eat24 and saw the really high rating. Normally, Mexican food does not travel well, but I was dying for something different from my usual sushi/Mediterranean/rice bowl lineup.   I ordered the chicken enchiladas in red sauce, no cheese or sour cream (in an attempt to keep the meal semi-healthy). Since I didn't hit the minimum required for ordering, I also got some guacamole.   The delivery arrived within the promised window and by a friendly delivery guy. Not only was the food packaged well, it looked fresh and appetizing and came exactly as I requested. The portion was enormous and more than enough for one full meal and another smaller meal. Everything tasted great and not at all heavy or oily. The guac was some of the best I've had in Philly. Definitely a fan and looking forward to trying more!

I'd give them an extra half-star, but since that's not possible I tend to round down when making my final decision.  Service is hit or miss-- our guy last night rocked it out and didn't hesitate to switch my beer when I wasn't crazy about my first choice.    The food is your typical bar fare.  I've had a jerk chicken sandwich here that was the bomb, and hummus that tasted like it came out of a plastic container from Acme.     Since the jalapeno poppers don't come with a warning, heed mine: give those little bitches time to cool, or you WILL burn your mouth upon taking your first bite.  The pain will be so severe that it will likely cause uncontrollable drooling and possible God sightings.

Just thinking back on my limited experiences at this establishment gives me the creeps.  At the time, I worked at a nearby law firm and this was a favorite for support staff members and alcoholic attorneys alike (sorry for blowing up anyone's spot).  It is one of those places that you sneak off to for lunch to have a beer or four, and if you see anyone from work, you silently acknowledge them and immediately forget that you saw them there.  So I guess it's cool that this unspoken code exists.    However, the place is downright nasty.  Cobwebs hang in the corners and every surface has that sticky feel to it.  You know what I'm talking about.  Mace's Crossing is as close to a dungeon as you can possibly get in the middle of Center City.

Great experience at Pokeworks last week! I was in the area for meetings and this came as a suggestion for a healthy lunch. I selected the spicy ahi bowl but customized my order with a bunch of add-ons. The employees were so friendly and patient while I made my selections. I also received 10% off my order, I think because I was a first timer. I'd definitely return when in the area.

I was referred to this practice by a friend and had a positive experience overall during my first visit in February. The waiting room was clean and inviting, and there were plenty of current magazines.   My cleaning was very thorough and I liked the dental hygienist - I wish I could remember her name! She did a great job and my teeth felt shiny and new after she was through. She also gave me a couple tips for how to care for my sensitive teeth, which was appreciated.   The dentist was fairly quick as most dentists are, but I had a positive experience with her as well. I'm so happy to have found a new dental practice in my area that takes my insurance and makes me feel comfortable!

West Elm is responsible for furnishing and decorating several areas of my house. Even when we shop around for certain pieces, my man and I usually return to West Elm for the final purchase. We love the place so much we registered there (super pumped over that, by the way)! Setting up said registry could not have been easier; you download an app and start scanning right from your phone!    This particular location is gorgeous and I've heard it's one of their biggest showrooms. There are always a lot of employees and it's pretty easy to find someone to help when you have a question. I have also had employees go out of their way to make sure I had a good experience. I once had a discount card I wanted to apply towards an expensive rug, but I didn't read the fine print, which included some extra hoops to go through before receiving the discount. West Elm still honored the offer anyway, no hoop jumping required. Happy, loyal customer here!

I finally made it to North Bowl for a happy hour that extended well into the evening on St. Patty's Day. We hung out at the bar upstairs, which was relatively quiet until around 7 or 8pm. Our bartender was fantastic and I was an instant fan of her blackberry bourbon smash cocktail. Woooo, that was some potent sipping!   Eventually, it was time to grab some food and I loved the buffalo chicken salad, which I requested with ranch dressing instead of the balsamic and thousand island dressings that come standard. The chips with salsa and queso are a great snack, and the long tots with longhots and cheese are completely delicious.    Best of all were the vibes - kind of island-y, plus a super amazing playlist that was later replaced by a DJ who was fantastic. I also loved the local artwork, which became a topic of discussion between almost everyone seated at the bar at one point. We called it a night around 10:30 but I could have partied all night in that atmosphere. Can't wait to return (and I don't even love bowling)!

Cafe L'Aube is an excellent option for weekend (or weekday!) brunch in Graduate Hospital. On the day we went, there was absolutely no wait, and there were several tables available. Ever since L'Aube left their South Street location, I've been seriously missing their delicious lattes. I'm so glad they are back in the area and even closer to my apartment so I can have the lattes any time I want! I even think the crêpes are better at this new location. The ham, egg and cheese version I had was enormous and so delicious.   I'm overdue for another visit.

The Pickled Heron has been on my list of bookmarked restaurants for a long time, and I finally got to check it out with two girlfriends on Friday. We arrived armed with three bottles of vino. Though the restaurant was featuring some type of restaurant week deal, they still had their full menu available, which was our preference. Unfortunately, the menu didn't exactly match the one online, and my friend was disappointed to see that the scallops were no longer being offered. Luckily, there were still a handful of other seafood options.   I started with the moules frites. The mussels were served in a light, saffron-scented broth and they were fantastic. The fries were piping hot and served in a cone with a mild dipping sauce. Next up was a steak with bone marrow stuffing, mushrooms and onion. The steak was a perfect medium rare as requested.   We passed on dessert but said yes to French pressed coffee. I'm glad I finally got a chance to try The Pickled Heron and I'd be down for a return trip sometime.

Maggiano's is an Italian chain with pretty good food and fair prices.  Most times, I have eaten here with just a couple other people, so we all order our own meals and take home leftovers.  However, if food comas are more your thing, gather up some friends and go "family-style."    If your experience is anything like the one I had with a group of about 20 on Friday night, you will be seated about 30 - 45 minutes after your reservation time.  Just as you start to ponder cannibalism, massive appetizer plates and bowls of salad will be delivered.  You'll be stuffed before the main course yet you will continue eating, because by now there are huge dishes of pasta and plates of chicken.  By the time dessert comes around, you consider calling a wide-load crane instead of a taxi.  Diets, beware.

Wow~ I don't know what some of the posters from '06 are talking about, but it's definitely not the same place I've been hitting up...  I love coffee, but Grooveground's is a bit strong and takes some getting used to~ they will happily throw a shot of hot water in there if you ask though... I've since worked up a tolerance and take my fix strong the way they serve it!
