The people who work here are so friendly; many of them remember what you drink and most are always willing to chat about whatever random bullshit you talk about before you get your first cup of the day.    I've never gotten food here, but they have a nice variety for such a tiny place.  Also, there are only one or two people working at one time, but it's not normally crowded enough to warrant more.  This is a neighborhood joint~ if you don't like it, there are at least 3 other options for coffee within two blocks!

My husband and I popped into Fiore for a late lunch on Sunday afternoon. Since it was a holiday weekend, the restaurant was on the quiet side, save for a few occupied tables.  The brunch/lunch menu is pretty small but there were a few things that jumped out right away. In terms of beverages, I was very happy to see multiple non-alcoholic options available, including San Pellegrino sodas and Baba's Brew kombucha. They had Purple Rain and Flower Power, which are my two favorites.   We decided to share the chopped salad, 'nduja toast, and chorizo pizzette. Everything was fresh and tasty, though each plate was pretty small so be prepared for a tapas-style meal, at least during brunch.   Solid experience and I'd be interested in returning to try more!

This is a cute place and much-needed for the area it is in.  The beer selection is decent but the food... needs work.  The menu is very small and the way things are presented make it seem like they are trying too hard to be upscale.  The nachos in particular were a huge disappointment.  I didn't know it was possible to screw up a standard plate of bar nachos until the other night at Devil's Den.  After seeing a couple plates go by, we decided to order them.  We hadn't noticed an abundance of salsa, so we specifically asked for some on the side.  This is how the conversation went:  me: we'll have the nachos with a side of salsa server: (weird look)...okay...  two minutes later  server: we don't have salsa... is fresh pico okay? me: that would be great!  two minutes later  server: um, we can't do pico either.  How about a free side of guacamole? me: um, okay  Who serves nachos without salsa or anything resembling salsa?    Devil's Den does.  P.S.  For the record, ketchup is not really good on nachos...

From my first set of fangs to present-day maintenance, Dr. Dickey has always been my go-to guy for dentistry. His staff members are all welcoming, gentle (especially in matters concerning my sensitive gums!) and genuine.   To this day, I have never had a cavity, and I credit the many torturous minutes of flouride treatments during my childhood. The good news for kids of this generation is that the office no longer uses the tray and gel methods of yesteryear; now kids can simply swish around some rinse and be on their way!  Bonus points for current magazines and Wi-Fi!

After working up a sweat at Maha nearby, Melissa P and I decided to reward ourselves with a semi-splurge lunch at Luke's Lobster. The lobster roll combo comes with chips and a drink for $17, which is a deal when you consider the fact that you are eating lobster, just a bit pricier than I would normally spend on lunch. Totally worth it for a special treat.   The roll was pleasantly stuffed with big chunks of lobster meat, and just the right amount of butter and a bit of seasoning. If I could think of one thing that would make it even better it would be a slice of lemon to squirt on top. The pickle was great, and the chips were the delish kettle-cooked kind. I thought the seating inside was really cute and a lot more plentiful than I expected for such a small place.   I've been thinking about the lobster roll ever since I ate it nearly a week ago, so if that doesn't say five stars, I don't know what does.

We hired First Class for my sister's wedding and also the bachelorette party. Since my family had already booked them for the wedding, First Class hooked us up with discounted pricing for the bachelorette party which was great.   For both occasions, the drivers were pretty well-versed with all of the stops we wanted to make. I'm sure providing all of this info ahead of time helped. I thought the driver on the day of the wedding was particularly awesome. He not only knew each stop in two different states without needing help from anyone in the bridal party but he also handled the gigantic limo bus really well and always found a convenient place to park.   The limo bus we had for the wedding was pretty incredible. We fit sixteen people easily and could have fit more. There was tons of space, plenty of handrails and even a stripper pole. Yup. Bridal party gone wild!

It took me more than three years to hit up Palm Tree Market but, since my first visit a few weeks ago, I've returned or ordered delivery a handful of times. There is a large variety of sandwiches and lunch meat is carved fresh for each one. I love the paninis because they aren't super heavy. They are just the right amount of toasted to where the cheese is melty.   There is a small refrigerated section with dips and a few other essentials, and a nice variety of chips. They also have every type of cold beverage you could possibly want.   The store is super clean and nice-looking. The employees are friendly. Super happy I finally checked this place out!

I really have nothing bad to say about my experience at Laughlin. In fact, it was probably the easiest of all the steps in the transformation of a NJ-licensed vehicle to a PA one. I went on a weekday around noon and was in and out in a matter of ten minutes. Steve was a pretty funny guy, and he was nice enough to remove my old NJ plates and put my new plate on for me. I'd definitely recommend this place to anyone in need of title transfer, registration and plates.

I have been loving this Chipotle for healthy, fast lunches. Yep, I said healthy. Because if you forgo the wrap, cheese and heavy meats, you really can have your Chipotle and eat it too. Ask for a burrito bowl, and then use a lettuce base with just a little bit of brown rice and black beans, plus onions and peppers. I've noticed that Chipotle workers across the board are super generous with toppings, which is awesome, but also dangerous if you are trying to watch what you're eating.   I finish off my burrito bowl with pico and both of the tomato-based salsas, plus some guacamole for some rich flavor and healthy fat. Their guac is super fresh and tasty. No dressing needed!   The employees are always fast and friendly. Once their diet coke dispenser shot out clear liquid which was a bummer, but besides that, this location rocks.

If you're in the South Jersey area and looking to load up on seasonal flowers, Lowe's in Delran has you covered. I stopped by and was super impressed by the amazing array of hanging baskets and planters of all shapes and sizes. I do find them to be a little on the pricey side, but the selection was truly incredible. Hopefully I don't kill off my new buds (lolz) in record time.

I swung by LA Nail Bar on a whim to get a quick mani before the weekend. My experience was positive; I popped in before lunch and there was an opening. The woman who did my nails was nice and gentle. She worked on my nails quickly but efficiently, and they looked great when they were done. I took extra time to dry them and was given a great neck massage.   My nails looked awesome, but that only lasted for one day. By Saturday, my nails were already chipping a lot. I think some more buffing would have prevented this, and probably a better quality top coat too.   I'd consider trying LA Nail Bar again if I was in the area and in dire need of a mani, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

Finally tried Wrap Shack after hearing good things for years! I ordered a chicken caesar wrap even though they only have it on the menu as a salad option. The wrap was super dense and I ended up enjoying it for lunch on back to back days. That said, the wrap barely had any lettuce; it was mostly just chopped chicken and dressing. So I would love to see some lettuce and even tomato, but I also understand that I ordered off the menu. Would try again for sure!

Popped over to Zavino for happy hour last night and was pretty impressed. I can't believe it but that was only my second visit since they opened. I certainly won't wait so long to get back again.   I didn't eat anything (except for the garnishes in my martini) but the combination cheese and charcuterie board that my friends ordered looked beautiful and delicious. Happy hour wines are five dollars but the options were pinot noir and chardonnay. I'd rather walk on hot coals in bare feet than drink chardonnay (okay fine, I'd pick the chardonnay between the two but I wouldn't be happy about it) so I instead opted for a glass of prosecco. Nine dollars seemed reasonable and the bubbles were tasty!   Then, I spotted a martini with prosciutto-wrapped blue cheese stuffed olives on the menu. I had to have it. When I found out the house vodka is Gordon's, I had to upgrade to Grey Goose, their only other vodka. This drink was amazing. A meal in a glass!   So while I did fail miserably at the whole save money at happy hour thing, I did have a very positive experience and am looking forward to next time.

Is there really another option?   Di Bruno Bros corners the market on cheeses, cured meats, gourmet foodstuffs and prepared items to eat at home or in the bright second floor cafe. A cheese called Etorki that I tried two years ago at a lunch meeting was waiting for me to try again on a visit last week. On another trip in the same week, my boyfriend ordered a muffuletta sandwich, which I had never had the pleasure of tasting before. It was unbelievable, served alongside house-made kettle chips.   I can already see myself relying on Di Bruno's stock rather than making a trip to the grocery store. This will be great for the taste buds and bad on the wallet. Fortunately, with three more check-ins I'll get 10% off my purchase. I plan on making that trip count.

I went to the new and improved Roxy to check out The Wolf of Wall Street. I had never been to the old Roxy, so I'm not sure how things have changed. But I did notice that everything in the venue appeared to be new and clean. It seems as though some construction is still underway, however. The area where you walk in and purchase tickets and refreshments is very tight. Hopefully that will be improved.   The theater itself was completely packed. It's a really good thing we got there early and had our choice of seats; it looked like some late arrivals were split up. We sat in the second to last row and, though the screen was smaller than some of the mainstream theaters, it was clear and the sound quality was good.   The snack selection was pretty limited; I didn't notice a fresh popcorn machine and they were out of Diet Coke on the night of our visit.   Hopefully improvements will be made all around as the Roxy completes its transformation. It's cool to have a theater within walking distance to home so I'm looking forward to going back.

Riding in the car with my two guy friends, I heard one ask the other if he wanted to go to The Rail.  I sarcastically asked who the lucky lady was, and when my friends stopped laughing hysterically, they informed me that The Rail is a bar in nearby Barrington.    A few minutes later, we arrived at a pretty interesting place that I never knew existed.  The two middle aged bartenders were dressed in classy bartender uniforms-- definitely something you don't see every day at your run of the mill South Jersey bar.  I was instantly charmed.    The walls were covered in local memorabilia and a pool table was wedged into the only available space on the floor.  The upstairs loft that overlooked the bar area had some tables.  This would be a really fun place to grab some friends on a Saturday afternoon and just hang out, watch sports and play pool.

My experiences at this year's PHS Pop Up Garden so far have been wonderful! I've already been three times this season and I think it's their best year yet.   I've recently traded boozy beverages for alcohol free concoctions, and PHS is killing the game with their incredible and thoughtful collection of AF drinks. Which is just one of the many reasons why PHS will become one of my go-tos this summer.   There's plenty of seating, but even if you end up without a seat, there's lots of open space to stand until seats do become available.   Finally, the staff is awesome. I attended a meet up last night and every employee I interacted with was really cool. Loving this gem!

Where, pray tell, was I purchasing items to clothe and accessorize myself with before Nordstrom rolled into town?    Anyone?  Anyone?!  I simply adore this place.  From the unique, surprisingly affordable clothing and superior customer service to the adorably decorated dressing rooms and overall layout, my shopping experiences have never been anything but enjoyable.  Some of my favorite finds in the past year have come from Nordstrom, including a red wool coat, party dress, 60s-style earrings and more.  Every item was well under $100.    Of course, higher-end labels are available, but I tend to stay away from that side of the store in order to avoid thread envy.

We popped into the Four Seasons on a whim while in the area on Saturday. I was dying for a hot spiked beverage and I figured the Four Seasons could comply. We were surprised to see dozens of kids in costumes getting ready to perform through the Swann Lounge. The bar was packed, but many of the tables and chairs were actually situated in the hall outside the lounge. A manager assured us that we could still get service there, so we grabbed a table and commenced people-watching.   There wasn't a hot cocktail on the menu but our server said they could probably do a hot toddy. It ended up being delicious and exactly what I wanted. Of course, one drink turned into a few plus a light dinner of mussels with grilled bread and a spinach and goat cheese salad. Everything was great. I'm actually really looking forward to returning some time and trying their cheesesteak, which I thought I spotted on a previous visit and confirmed via the menu this time around. It's definitely on the pricey side but I'm sure it's damn tasty.   If the Swann Lounge added happy hour, I'd probably become a regular.

Welcome to Graduate Hospital, Neighborhood Books! This is a super cute, well laid-out, used bookstore with a lot of great titles. I picked up an international bestseller for about half off the cover price. So it's not garage sale prices but it's still cheaper than buying from one of the big box brand bookstores. I'll happily fork over a five-spot or so for a newish title from a local biz.   The owner said he won't be in the position to buy books for a couple months while he's still getting his current stock situated. No worries, I'll just hold on to Fifty Shades a little longer.

I have a hard time making decisions sometimes.  So my brain wants to self-destruct, Inspector Gadget-style, when faced with the many gelato choices at Capogiro.  Thankfully, they allow you to double up on flavors in even the small size.  Money.  As for the gelato itself?  I pity the fool who doesn't revel in its greatness.

This particular Saladworks was recently reopened by the franchisee from the Collingswood location that I used to frequent. The staff at Delran Saladworks are equally friendly and fast - a big plus since that line can get pretty long during prime lunch hours.   The cafe was bright and clean, though I took my salad to go. All of the ingredients were really fresh. My only gripe is the salad dressing part of the line. Two huge scoops of dressing is way too much for the size of the salads (which seem to get smaller as the years go by - remember the big seafoam green bowls from Saladworks of yore?). The person in charge of dressing should probably ask "one scoop or two?" Sounds silly, but she was so fast I didn't have time to ask her to stop, as I watched her dump the second onto my salad, which was swimming in italian vinaigrette when I got home.   Dressing aside, this Saladworks is better than most and I'll likely return next time I have a craving and I'm in the area.

Upgrade!   I knew after the Elite Event at Nomad back in April that they were serving up some seriously tasty pies, but I waited to return on a regular night before going for the review update. After last night's meal, I'm convinced that Nomad's pizza is legit.   We ordered a classic margherita, the spicy sausage and the spinach pies. All three were super flavorful, the ingredients bursting with goodness.   The pizzas are now served with pizza cutters, which expedites the process of getting slices distributed. Our servers even offered to cut for us.   The dessert list was expanded to include specials, though we opted for a strawberry mascarpone ice cream and a dark chocolate sorbet, both from The Bent Spoon in Princeton. The two were great on their own but even more delicious together.  I have other spots in Philly that are my favorite for pizza, but variety is the spice of life. I'm happy to switch things up every now and again; I'm kind of a pizza polygamist.

I mean this in the nicest way possible: Café Lutecia is the Doobie's of coffee shops. As cozy and lived-in as your grandparents' basement, this café is a far cry from some of the newer, trendier coffee shops.   The food smelled heavenly when I stopped in yesterday for a quick iced coffee to go. Several people appeared to be regulars, and the tables outside are always occupied whenever I pass by.  I offer up only three stars because I think the coffee is average, but I know that I'll be returning soon for lunch based on the raves of other Yelp friends. The sight of a bubbling hot, cheese-topped French bread was all I needed to make a mental note to plan my next visit.

I am such a fan of Scoop DeVille. My go-to location is at The Bourse, but my husband ordered a birthday cake for me from this location (the mint chip one - everyone loved it) in August, and I also popped in while I was in the area earlier this week.   Scoop is known for their blends but I am all about the hard ice cream. The flavors rotate all the time and they are often very Philly-centric which is so fun. I ordered a pint of dough boi and the young guy who took my order absolutely stuffed that pint to the brim!    This location didn't seem to have as much variety in terms of desserts and ice cream flavors, but perhaps it was just the timing of my visit. I did notice that they had loads of ice cream cakes ready for the taking so this is a great spot to get a gourmet ice cream cake that will beat out any grocery store option.

Very solid hoagies from Lennie's for some Sunday football watching! I placed my order for pick-up via Grubhub and the sandwiches were ready to go upon my arrival fifteen minutes later. At the store, I also purchased a bag of chips, of which they had a small variety.   My turkey and cheese was made to my exact specifications and my husband seemed pleased with his Godfather Part 1 sandwich as well. I personally prefer shredded iceberg to a single slice of romaine but I know that's being extra picky. I'd happily hit this place up for sandwiches again when in the area.

I enjoyed my brunch at Front Street Cafe a few weeks ago. I love when restaurants feature a brunch menu during the week; it's the best time to check out spots that might otherwise be too crowded on weekends.   The eggs benedict with bacon was very tasty. I love when there's a side salad and the one that came with was fresh and flavorful. I was so curious about the oven roasted potato so I ordered one on the side. It was super crispy on the outsides and fluffy in the middle. Delish.   The restaurant is quite large and features a beautiful bar as the centerpiece of two dining rooms (there is also an upstairs area and a courtyard for warmer months). It's a nice place to get some work done or meet up with a friend, especially during the week. Looking forward to my next visit.

Compared with the Home Depot across the street, Lowe's had everything we were looking for and then some. I'm not a fan of big-box stores, and my boyfriend is even less enthusiastic towards them. But in order to get our balcony ready for summer, we had to bite the bullet and just go.   Fortunately, there was a huge selection of patio furniture, all right in the center aisle (so no fruitless searching) and easily accessible. I'll even admit we had fun narrowing down our choices.   This Lowe's also boasts a really large section of indoor and outdoor plants, which will be helpful for accessorizing the balcony, provided I can keep our existing plant alive in the meantime.

After trying soup dumplings for the first time a few weeks ago, I can say I'm hooked and haven't stopped thinking about them since! We checked out Dim Sum Garden around 9pm on a Friday night and the place was packed, with a line. Somehow, our party of two was seated within ten minutes of walking through the door!   Having already consumed several cocktails, we were pretty ravenous and probably over-ordered. But I can't think of anything I would have wanted to leave out. We had: chive and pork dumplings (fried), steamed pork soup dumplings, scallion pancake, pork with sauce noodles and diced chicken with chili pepper. Everything was delicious! And so inexpensive. With tax (and before tip), the total was something like $33. Insanity!    Servers were hustling and they were all very friendly. Water glasses were refilled quickly. My only gripe was that the bottles on the table with soy, vinegar and chili oil were very sticky.   Next time, I'm grabbing a sixer and an even bigger crew!

Solid beer selection, electronic jukebox, pool, shuffle board and the best wings around. What's not to love about the Jug?   It had been years since my last visit but everything was just as it should be when I stopped by with some family members after a party. This isn't my favorite hometown bar, but then again, I tend to avoid my hometown bars, unless I'm traveling in a pack with the fam.   I ordered wings (hot and garlic) plus an order of cheese fries to go for a late night bite. We didn't have far to travel and everything tasted great - even the fries, which still had some crispness despite the cheese. Sides of blue cheese and ranch were provided as requested, along with a basket of celery.  I'll be working off my midnight meal for the rest of the week, but it was worth it.

Realizing that my previous review update was probably bringing down PATCO's overall rating, I wanted to update again to the four stars I feel they deserve.  I do recognize that my experience last winter was a freak incident (that better not happen again).  For the most part, PATCO is reliable and still the least expensive way for me to get to and from the city.  The increased security has not gone unnoticed, and I give props to the officers who are on their game when the Drunky McSkunkies and Shady McShadertons start any bullshit.  Bonus: For anyone with an iPhone, the PATCO app with train schedules is solid.

Earth Bread & Brewery is an awesome concept. I really like the beer program especially. The handful of beers on tap are always unique and you will never drink the same thing twice. That is, unless you go back while a particular keg is still available. EB&B does not repeat beers - ever. Every single recipe is different in some way. Really very cool when you think about it!   I've had the flatbreads on two different occasions. I like the variety and creative toppings, especially on the seed pizza (pumpkin seeds are so underrated). But I'm not a huge fan of the flatbreads overall. However, I do like them much more the next day after heating them up in the toaster oven. Go figure. They also serve soup and a rotating hummus/dip appetizer.   When in Mt. Airy, give this place a look. It's worth a stop.

You'd be surprised, as I was, how hard it is to find a decent cup of coffee on a Friday night. With the exception of restaurants, there aren't many places that cater to the evening coffee-drinking crowd.   As we drove down Second, the search seemed futile. And then, there Philadelphia Java Company was. It was around 8pm and we thought that perhaps we were too late, but the door opened easily and the barista greeted us warmly. My relief was palpable; I had a long night of work ahead and I needed a jump start to get going.   My large latte did just that, while half of a locally-made chocolate chip cookie brownie served as dessert. I admired the marble-topped cafe tables and large windows with a view of the April showers that had been slamming us all day. I'll definitely return.

I discovered Fantagio one evening when I stopped by my usual mani/pedi spot, Victoria's Nails in Haddonfield.  They were booked solid with people who actually had appointments (imagine that!) and I was out of luck~ until one of the nail techs mentioned their new spa around the corner, Fantagio.  This fab woman made a quick call, handed me a coupon book and sent me on my way.    The next hour and a half was spent in pure bliss and serenity.  The pedicure involved moisturizing creams, hot stones and steamy towels.  Combined with a massage chair and the latest Harper's Bazaar, this girl was one happy camper.  The manicure that followed was equally thorough, and my polish stayed on for a full week (cue oohs and aahs)!    Before leaving, the owner gave me a tour of the spa area, which was smartly designed yet comfortable.  This is a great place for a mini spa experience that will not break the bank.

I went to Roast+Chop expecting another build your own salad place, but was pleasantly surprised that the concept is so much more. There are a variety of proteins and the bowls seem like they could be quite hearty, with the plethora of hot and cold ingredients.   Since I had salad on the brain, I created a bowl based loosely on the southwest chicken bowl. The ingredients were fresh and flavorful and I enjoyed the citrus dressing. The employee who put together my bowl was so friendly and she threw in a box of housemade chips after I mentioned it was my first visit. I ended up having the chips for a snack later in the day and they were awesome!   Next time, I'd like to try a warm bowl to get a sense of some of the other flavors. There are so many combos you could come up with which keeps things interesting. I'd love a place like this close to my house in Philly; I'd grab dinner there all the time!

Noord was such a pleasant surprise on a date night during the winter! Going in, I had no idea what to expect from a Dutch restaurant. Turns out, it's just lots of seafood, plus a bunch of flavor-packed supporting ingredients like mustards, vinaigrettes and pickled vegetables.   The bread they start you out with is truly magnificent. I'm not even a huge rye bread person but I was addicted from first bite. We shared the bitterballen, the Dutch version of meatballs, and a salad with bleu cheese to start. Excellent choices which didn't leave us too full for mains (if anything it's multiple servings of that bread that will get you!). The shellfish stew was excellent and I know my husband was happy with his entree as well, though I can't remember at this point what it was.   The vibes at Noord were very European, with tables fairly close together and a nice din throughout the restaurant that seemed to suggest a fun night out was being had by all. Our server was as gregarious as he was efficient, adding to the atmosphere. Can't wait to do it again!

After another great experience, I decided I'm not going to hate just because they use little olives in their martinis.  I shouldn't be drinking martinis with pizza anyway, I should be drinking wine.  Lesson learned.  On a Saturday night when we were too exhausted to do any restaurant research, Pietro's was a no-brainer for an easy, relaxing dinner spot.  At around 9, there were plenty of open tables and minimal distractions.  Our server was attentive and friendly, and both the salad and pizza we ordered came out perfect.  In a city filled with fancy, well-acclaimed restaurants, the always dependable and wallet-friendly Pietro's remains one of my favorites.

After reading Jess D's ROTD and noticing a Yelp Deal on the Three Sirens page, I decided a return trip was in order. I purchased the deal, figuring I'd find something no matter what, and went to the shop. On my visit, I tried on a handful of cute clothes, but left empty-handed because I felt the dresses I tried were too short for my tall frame. But after a few days of nonstop thinking about one of the dresses, I decided I had to go back with a pair of tights and heels to see if maybe I'd change my mind once I saw the dress with a pair of tights underneath. Was the dress still a spot too short? Yes. Did I buy it anyway? Yes. Do I regret the decision? Not even a little.   Moral of the story: when in doubt, show those stems, ladies!

My first experience at Sprouts was great! Everything was well-stocked and, when I couldn't find the one thing I needed (asparagus), a nice employee went to the back to find some. So, the customer service was on point!   Prices seemed pretty reasonable and I definitely see myself shopping here regularly, due to its proximity to my home and free parking (can I get an amen?!).

Of the two, I like the Sweetgreen location in University City a lot more since there is indoor seating. But my experience at this location last night was a pleasant one. Employees shouted out hellos the minute my sister and I walked through the door.   There were samples of one of the beverages plus a specialty salad which was nice to have as we waited. I ordered my usual guacamole greens salad while my sister ordered the kale Caesar at my suggestion. We had a short cab ride home which was long enough for the tortilla chips in my salad to get soggy. Mental note for next time. We both enjoyed our healthy dinner - here's hoping they put a location closer to my house!

It makes me so happy that Capogiro is available any time of year to satisfy my gelato cravings. They also double as a fantastic coffee shop. On this unseasonably warm day, I enjoyed some of their rich iced coffee.   While there, I picked up some gelato for the weekend. I love that bacio (chocolate hazelnut) and stracciatella (Italian chocolate chip) are always available. The employee who helped me was so nice and even packed the gelato with ice so that it wouldn't melt on my trip across town. I can't wait for my Saturday night treat!

Four out of six people from my last visit to Tashan went back again to celebrate a birthday this week. I wasn't sure if the experience would match our previous visit, but after a few bites, it was confirmed: Tashan is a five star restaurant all the way. Our server was knowledgeable, funny and great all around. He recommended the most perfect white wine to complement my tastes and my meal.   We had several repeats from our last visit plus one or two new plates:  GOC Naan Peshawari Naan Gol-Gappa Malai Kofta Lollypops Goat Cheese Taftaans Palak Tikki Tandoori Jumbo Shrimp Naga Beef Sümi  Chicken Patanga Xacutti Pork Tenderloin Kobe Chopan Kebob  Favorites for me were the peshawari naan, stuffed with a paste of cashews and raisins among other things, the malai kofta lollypops, goat cheese taftaans, huge tandoori shrimp and the chicken patanga. I'm slowly but surely crafting my perfect meal for one.  For dessert, a shared order of custardy crème brulee, and a cup of special blend La Colombe. Now that Tashan is open for lunch, I can hardly wait for an excuse to treat myself. If you haven't been already, do yourself a favor and go.

When it comes to comfort food, Stargazy is where it's at. The traditional pie and mash just can't be beat for when you want something home cooked and soul satisfying.   When my husband decided to treat me to the Friday fish and chips last week, I knew it would be great and I wasn't wrong. When he got home from the pick-up, we unpacked massive pieces of freshly fried cod, and plenty of thick cut fries. The mushy peas were perfect. Normally, I'm not a big tartare sauce girl, but Sam's version could make me a believer.   Sam threw in some sticky toffee pudding, which was delicious. The chocolate sea salt bars we ordered were also fantastic. Five stars forever!

This teeny showroom (is showroom the manly term for boutique?) on 2nd in NoLibs is as cute - I mean, as manly - as can be and perfect for picking up a little something for the dudes in your life. I strolled in with no expectations while doing some Christmas shopping in early December and ended up leaving with two gifts - custom Phillies tees for my squeeze and my brother. The shirts I purchased were actually the work of one of the owner's friend's, but the Duke and Winston merch was all great, too. The clothes have a breezy coolness about them that doesn't come off too bro-y.   If you're still not sold, pop by to check out the adorable mascot, Duke, a big bulldog with puppy dog eyes. He'll convince you. (Psst, ladies: the owner's just as cute.)

I had a chance to check out the With Love Beer Garden at the Four Seasons last night for Philly Beer Week, and I loved every second of it. The garden was bumpin' despite the sweltering heat. Tickets for beer and food could be purchased at one table (cash only), then traded in at another.   Every weekday during Beer Week, a different brewery is featured and a nice selection of beer is available. On Wednesday night, Dock Street ruled the taps and I once again enjoyed OMG Pale Ale, Pimp My Rye and their newest brew, Saison Erbe, which we dubbed "pizza in a glass." Delicious.  The crowd was friendly, and the misters added a very nice touch on a hot day. Being able to hang out on the green grass in the middle of the city felt really special. I only hope they bring this garden back for next year's Beer Week!

I have a go-to nail salon that I love, but I can't deny that I was happy to see this new salon pop up in my neighborhood for last-minute appointments. Since I didn't have the time to get to my usual salon, I called South Street Nails on Friday and made an appointment for a 4pm pedi.  I rolled in right on time and the salon was busy. The space is pretty tight and you definitely feel really on top of your neighbors. I had to wait for a few minutes for a chair to open up, but once my service began it was all good. The chairs offer a really strong massage function which I desperately needed.   I didn't catch the name of my technician but she did a great job. I had chosen a light color and she asked if I wanted a third coat. I didn't, but I appreciated the attention to detail! When my service was complete I was led to the dryers and received an amazing shoulder and back massage! There is a 10% discount when paying in cash, which is awesome. My pedi was $27 plus tip and worth every penny.

The area surrounding Ten Stone is a little run-down, so it was a nice surprise to see that the restaurant/bar is bright and cheery inside.  When I went on Sunday afternoon, it was fairly crowded.  There was only one server and a couple food runners, but the server was very sweet and friendly despite having to take care of all the tables in the front area (in her shoes, I probably would have been a crazed beotch).  At her recommendation I got a bloody Mary, which came complete with a garnish stick containing lemon, lime, a red pepper slice, a large shrimp and an olive... the bases were pretty much covered.  My boyfriend got the turkey chili, which I couldn't stop eating when it arrived.  It was so good!  I'll definitely have to go back sometime for lunch or dinner.  What a cute place!  Update, 4/15/08: I made it back into this place last night and had to give them another star.  The bartenders were simply awesome.  There were many beers on tap that I was unfamiliar with so one of the guys happily gave me samples galore until I found something I liked.  Nice!

I'm still lovin' on Percy Street BBQ, especially after continuing my boyfriend's birthday celebration there last night.   First off, the bartenders are fantastic, friendly and fast. They are always on top of their game and seem genuinely happy to engage in conversation. I like that in my enablers!  One menu item not to be overlooked is the fries, which come loaded with melted cheese and pulled pork. While I didn't order them on my recent visit, several friends did and you know I snagged a few. It was unanimous: Percy's plate of spuds beats out Khyber's debris fries.   Extra special thanks to chef Erin O'Shea for whipping up a gorgeous red velvet cake in honor of the birthday boy. It was a lovely surprise and provided the little touch of sweetness everyone was after (although I am so returning soon to try that Best of Philly key lime pie).

Circles can count me amongst their many fans. After several deliveries and one dine-in experience, they have earned themselves a spot in my go-to Thai restaurants. I will say though, on occasion, food has been too salty. The lemongrass soup I ordered most recently was a big offender. But other than that, I'm happy with the eats.   If you can get over to the restaurant, it's actually quite nice and they do a crazy bargain-priced lunch with three courses for under ten bucks. I'm a fan of any of their noodle dishes, but I hear great things about the curries as well.

I really wanted pho, and I was really too lazy to go get it, so I gave Huong Tram another chance via Caviar. This experience definitely warranted an upgrade from my previous review.   The pho arrived perfectly packaged - the broth was in a plastic container inside a brown paper bag; the noodles and beef were in a styrofoam container, and the sprouts, lime wedges, jalapeños and sauces were all in a separate bag. I put everything together in a giant bowl of my own and enjoyed my lunch. I did think the restaurant was a little heavy handed with the onions, but aside from that, the soup hit the spot. I'd consider ordering from Huong Tram again.

Smak Parlour is a cute boutique but I never have any luck finding something that works for me. Yesterday was my second visit and I once again took an armful of clothing into the dressing room. Dress after dress was just too short and almost all of them had cinched waists which is all wrong for my body type. It was a sad shopping day.  The sales girls were sweet and were happy to run downstairs to check for other sizes when I couldn't find mine on the floor. After talking with a friend today who swears by the place, we've decided to return and focus only on tops, which will hopefully end in success. To be continued!

Joining a new gym can be a daunting task.  Luckily, my transition from old to new was not nearly as awkward as I feared.  Super Fitness is huge compared to my last gym.  An abundance of treadmills means there is (usually) no wait for me to get my run on.  There are tons of resistance machines and a very large free weight area.  Sometimes the free weight section of a gym can be a little intimidating--but I don't get that vibe here at all, which is really nice.  A full range of classes for various fitness levels are offered every day of the week, and best of all, they are included with a membership.  I'm a big fan of Sandy's boot camp class~ it's intense and painful (am I sweating or crying?!) yet totally satisfying at the same time.

I'm thrilled at all the Targets that have popped up in Philly recently! This location has parking, which is wonderful, and is convenient whenever I happen to be in the NoLibs/Fishtown areas.   While I haven't browsed through the entire store, this Target seems a lot larger than some of the other city Targets. They have a full stock of bath and beauty items and I was very pleased with the selection on my last visit.   I haven't interacted with any employees because the lines are mostly self-service, but they are around and available, if needed.

I visited this center when I met with my friend, Dr. Angela Jarvis, to consult on a detox diet I was planning to do. She showed me around the office and I was amazed at everything it had to offer: Acupuncture, chiropractic care, personal training, yoga, nutrition counseling and lots more.   Angela walked me through everything I needed to know about the detox and was always available to answer questions I had along the way. After the detox I felt lighter, healthier and more relaxed, just as she said I would. I highly recommend this center for anyone looking to improve their health.

I met George Logan at a Yelp event for business owners so I knew he was serious about his reputation and taking care of his clients. My husband and I had a handful of projects that we have been wanting to complete for some time, so I took his card and reached out via text (his preferred communication method) a few days later to set up a consultation.   After the consultation, George sent me an estimate. My husband and I  decided to remove one of the lower-priority projects from the list to cut back on the total cost, which wasn't a problem. Construction began a week or so later with the plumbing work, which lasted one day. One week after that, the drywall and surface area parts of the project were completed by a different crew.   George accepts Venmo payments (which is super convenient!), and he was onsite at the start of each day to make sure his crew was informed. Everyone was friendly and professional. I'd absolutely hire George again and would recommend his business to anyone with home improvement projects that are too big to handle by a novice!

Count me as one of the many fans of Elixr. I've now visited twice, and I can attest to the friendly and informative service. One morning, while trying not to go overboard on caffeine, I got into a conversation with one of the baristas and discovered that a regular cup of coffee actually has more caffeine than a latte. I'm sure that also depends on sizes and whatnot, but it was enlightening nonetheless.   I ordered my latte and admired the lovely fruit tarts on display. Priced at a mere $2.50 each, I'll be sure to return when my sweet tooth starts calling.  The space itself is cute, with long wooden tables for sharing and a counter along one wall with stool seating. A refrigerated case houses juices, orangina and sparkling water.   What a nice little nook of serenity in the center of the concrete jungle!

The name of this restaurant always made me think dark lodge with moose heads on the walls. Still, I wanted to check it out and I finally got my chance. It was later in the evening, when most places either stop selling food and close for the night or break out the bar menus for the night owls. We walked in and asked a server if it would be possible to get two orders of French onion soup at the bar, and after checking with the kitchen she confirmed that we could. The restaurant was cute and French and nothing like I'd imagined it would be.   There were some deliciously crunchy peanuts in glass jars across the bar, which was nice since bar snacks are hard to come by these days. Our bartender was sweet and helpful. The soup was generously portioned and had loads of cheese, but something was missing in the broth. It wasn't overly flavorful, and I probably would have sprinkled some salt, had they not already dumped their shakers for the night.   I'm glad I finally got to check Caribou Cafe out and I'd like to discover what else is on the menu.

Jim's: A good cheesesteak? Yes. The best ever? No.  Not only that, but the service was gruff and barky. "I can't hear you!" hollered the guy behind the grease-flecked window. "Whiz with fried onions!" I repeated back, slightly louder. Sheesh.  I watched as he decided to either scoop up every last bit of cooked meat on the grill or wait for the fresh meat to brown. He went with the former, although he tried to compensate with extra fried onions. I was disappointed. Fortunately, this was yet another case of my eyes being bigger than my stomach, because once I got my cheesesteak and Diet Coke (laugh all you want, I have to cut calories somewhere!) upstairs to the table seating, I was pretty content. Had there been more steak, the whiz would have been drowned out completely. Although, I would have preferred the whiz on top versus being slathered on the bun.   I housed that thing at warp speed and, while it was greasy and tasty, it was not earth-moving. I've had comparable (or better) steaks in Jersey, for less money and service with a smile.

I loved this cozy coffee shop off of Haddon Ave in Collingswood! Revolution is so close to where I used to live before I made the transition to full-time city girl. Being in Collingswood and checking out this awesome, new-ish business really gave me some nostalgia!   The coffee was great and there was a small selection of sandwiches on the blackboard. Unfortunately, they were out of sandwiches on the Friday I visited, so I stuck with just the coffee.   I made my way up the spiral staircase to grab an open table. There is office space located upstairs and the one table is located right by the door to an office. If you want to sit at this table without being in the way, you'd have to sit facing the wall, which is pretty awkward. Next time I'll try a little harder to find a spot downstairs.   My sister lives in Collingswood now and I may have scooped her on this coffee shop. I'm sure I'll be back with her sometime in the future!

While "running errands" at Nordstrom last week*, I suddenly recalled Andrea T.'s testimonial that the red velvet cupcakes from the coffee shop on the first floor were pretty fab.  Sure enough, when I walked into the cafe they were lined up behind the glass, waiting to be taken to a good home.  The cupcakes were small for $2.50 a pop but if those little suckers weren't dense...  They made for the perfect dessert, enjoyed on my couch and in my jammies with my favorite guy.    *LOVE my new top!

Guapos Tacos are served street-style, with the protein taking center stage and chopped onions and cilantro plus light sauces adding to the flavor.   My first experience was at Amis industry night last September. There I tried tacos de lengua (tongue), tacos de carnitas and veggie tacos. The standouts were the lengua and veggie. The tongue was tender like a filet and the accompanying sauce had a tangy flavor. The veggie taco had flavorful, marinated grilled veggies.   My second taste of Guapos Tacos was at the Vendy Awards. The grilled mahi mahi taco with a generous splash of hot sauce (from the selection of sauces on the ledge built into the the truck) was so delicious, I gladly waited in line again for seconds later in the day.   The truck is colorful and fun and the guys who work inside are personable and handle crowds well. Two thumbs up for this tasty taco truck!

COVID-19 update: I visited Ringpfeil for my annual skin check and felt extremely comfortable with how everything was handled during my visit. Check-in was on the first floor, as usual. After settling my co-pay, I was directed to the second floor and given a specific exam room. There were signs everywhere pointing to the numbered exam rooms, and signs inside the room with instructions.   My appointment was just as thorough as always and, as usual, I received excellent care from my dermatologist. There is always an additional staff member in the room to take notes and I felt very comfortable at all times. Everyone, including me, was masked up and my dermatologist was also wearing gloves.   Get your skin checked and don't forget your SPF daily!

Swung by the new Cambridge last night and it was bumpin'! So much so that the wait for a table was almost a half hour. Normally, this wouldn't be a problem and we'd just grab a drink and wait, but I was already well into hangry territory so we opted to grab a bite elsewhere. Afterwards, we returned and were seated at a table right away. We had several drinks and our server was great. The food at the surrounding tables looked awesome, and I was a little regretful that we hadn't just waited before. But I'm sure we'll be back in no time.   My only gripe, and I see that it is a common theme in the reviews so far, is the noise. We broke out a decibel measuring app for fun and the reading was very high. But our ears already knew that. I did enjoy the music selection, but I'm hanging on to hope that some sound muffling will take effect soon. Aside from that, the bar/restaurant is gorgeous and I'm really looking forward to hanging out there!

I was looking for a birthday gift for my brother so wandered into this store the other day.  Right away I found something he would like, which was awesome.  The store had a lot of great stuff but the prices were a bit ridic for things like basic t-shirts.  Like the previous poster said, there is definitely a hipster-type vibe here~ but nothing wins a hipster over faster than when you compliment the music selection (especially when it's coming direct from his ipod- bonus points!!!).    I'm just kidding~ the guy who worked there was super nice and even wrote down the name of the cd for me (Different Class by Pulp).  That little act of kindness made my day, and my bro loved his new hat!

This pizza place has been around for ages and is still kicking.  There is definitely a ton of nostalgic appeal for me here since I grew up in Cinnaminson; pizza in my grade school classrooms was ALWAYS from Brother's, I had my first kiss after a group dinner here, my field hockey and lacrosse teams in high school always convened here and now my sister and I hit it up for hangover food when we're so inclined.  Years have gone by but one thing remains the same-- the pizza.  And it's freaking gooooooooood.

As far as fast food restaurants go, Chick-fil-A is all right in my book.  The chicken strips and nuggets are always tender on the inside, with a crunchy, slightly salty coating of goodness on the outside.  The fries are of the waffle variety, but you won't see Aunt Jemima around this neck of the woods.  Barbecue sauce, honey mustard or ketchup will do just fine.  Yum.

What a cute little spot in the heart of Old City! A gorgeous square wood communal table is the first thing that drew my eye when I first walked into Fork Etc. late in the afternoon on Friday.   My companion and I were just swinging by for a quick beverage - bottles of Victory's Fists of Feury. We took our beers over to the super cushy and comfy banquet close to the giant window, perfect for people-watching.   I am very much looking forward to returning for lunch or a quiet meal in the evening, where I'll watch the world pass me by.

As much as I totally loathe taking my car to Cherry Hill Nissan, I will say that I always feel like it has been well taken care of after all is said and done.   Or maybe I just need to tell myself that as I part with hundreds of dollars every time my ride needs fixing. Everything is beyond expensive, and should you decide not to have an issue fixed right away (because there are other, more pressing car issues to handle first), you will still be charged a fee just because someone looked at the source of the noise, light, etc. In addition to paying whatever fee you are already paying to have other problems resolved.   Having a car while living in the city is definitely a luxury, but it's an expensive one. Regardless, I need my wheels to work like a well-oiled machine whenever I want to get out of town. After 7+ years, my car is still treating me well, and I probably have CH Nissan to thank for part of that.

I had a $20 Rum Bucks coupon from an event I went to last year that I finally put to use last Saturday. The rum list was huge, but I flipped to the cocktail section of the menu to make my decision. Right away I noticed a skinny mojito, made with Splenda syrup instead of simple syrup. Unfortunately, there was no Splenda syrup made. Did I mention it was a Saturday, just after opening? I sucked it up and went with a regular mojito instead. The drink was tasty, I even had two, but I don't see myself dropping $12/drink there regularly.   The decor feels dated but it's still a nice looking place. But the tacky pirate in the lounge area up front has got to go.   If you aren't in the mood for a fancy drink, the happy hour specials are pretty recession-friendly and are offered seven days a week. Also, the bartender was nice, which certainly isn't a given these days. I don't know that I'd go out of my way for Rum Bar, but if I were in the area and the mood hit, I wouldn't object to going back.

I'm definitely a fan of Cafe L'Aube, and I was super bummed to discover a couple weeks ago that their Washington Ave location is no longer open on weekends. But when the craving for L'Aube coffee and a crêpe strikes, you have to answer the call, even if it requires a little more distance to travel.   L'Aube's Rittenhouse location is cute and very French (or at least, how I imagine very French to be). Baguettes, pastries and juices line the counters and the short but sweet menu has something for everyone. I went with my standard order, the Complete, with Emmentaler cheese, ham and egg, in a buckwheat crêpe. Sometimes, this crêpe is perfect, and other times, it can be a bit dry. To avoid this, the Le Fromager crêpe is probably a better option because the chevre has a wonderful creaminess that pairs really well with the egg, bacon and grape tomatoes.  One of the best things about L'Aube is their coffee. It's absolutely delicious and right up there with La Colombe, my other favorite. Their lattes are better than anywhere else, and served in gigantic mugs. Je t'aime, L'Aube!

I've been living in Philly for nearly six years, but have held on to a lot of my South Jersey doctors just because I felt comfortable and had good relationships. A long drive and even longer wait times at my former dermatologist finally convinced me to search for a new one in Philly for my annual body scan. I'm so glad I found Ringpfeil Dermatology through Yelp!   Making my appointment was easy and the office is conveniently located in the Rittenhouse area. The office is clean, bright and modern, and I was seen right at my scheduled appointment time. Dr. Bird was awesome. I liked her the moment we started talking and knew I had made the right decision. She took her time with my scan and called out notations for her assistant to record on my medical file. I had a couple small biopsies which were practically painless and handled very quickly.   I feel so good about my decision to move my dermatology care to Ringpfeil and Dr. Bird and look forward to years of healthy skin with their help!

This particular Iron Hill Brewery comes as a runner up to my preferred locations in Maple Shade and West Chester. On a quiet Saturday afternoon, the place was fairly empty and yet service wasn't as on-point as it could have been.   I find some of the menu items (at all locations) to be on the high side for the quantity received. A fish taco appetizer which contained a single taco was about eight bucks. The cheesesteak egg rolls are also bling-blingin' at eleven dollars for two rolls, each cut in half. (For the record, I can get cheesesteak eggrolls that are every bit as good at Woody's for half the price.) My Mediterranean wrap was fairly priced at $9.50, with a $2.50 upcharge for sweet potato fries swapped out for regular.   I do enjoy Iron Hill Brewery and I dig their beer especially, but as far as food is concerned, there are better finds.

I have never had a bad meal here~ although I tend to order one of the same three things every time: the Mediterranean salad which has the most amazing homemade salad dressing, the pasta with vodka sauce (I usually substitute their whole wheat fettuccini for the penne that comes standard) and of course, pizza.  The food is always great; everything is homemade and very fresh.  I could probably eat here several times a week and never tire of it~ in fact, I was here on Friday night for dinner and went back again for lunch the next day.  The service was good both times this past weekend but it can get really crazy at lunch time during the week.  In my opinion though, the quality of the food and the prices are worth it!    My only gripe is that they serve their martinis with crappy little salad bar olives instead of the nice big ones~ you've gotta have the big ones for martinis!

I do declare, that Percy Street Barbecue has the best mac and cheese I have ever stuffed in my gullet.  Thick, rich, cheesy sauce and perfect noodles (not quite al dente but not the least bit soggy) are nestled under a layer of buttery breadcrumbs and served in a piping hot dish. Unreal.   Also of note is the warm German potato salad (and you KNOW I love some GPS) and the collard greens. The jalapeno cheddar corn muffin is tasty for sure, although I agree with Dan F that it leans on the too-much-butter side. Yes, that side does exist, although it's a hard one to admit.  On my recent visit I ordered pulled pork as my protein, and found it to be nicely smoked but with too many fatty bits throughout. Another BBQ spot owns my heart when it comes to pulled pork, and Percy's was good, just not as good.   The restaurant was extremely quiet during lunch hours on a weekday. Not that I'm suggesting it would be an ideal spot for corporate workers to escape Big Brother and enjoy a liquid lunch. Nope, not at all.

I have to give credit where credit is due and I can definitely say my initial feelings about Dock Street South have changed. When Covid came rolling into our lives, Dock Street started offering bake-at-home pizza kits. We ordered one in those early shelter in place days and thought the pizza was delicious. Recently, we ordered another as part of the Yelp KIT, which resulted in another great pizza night at home.   Additionally, this location has recently hired a new chef, and they were also seen rolling a pizza oven into the building recently. Happy day! I guess 2020 isn't a total bust, afterall.

I popped into Paper On Pine today to pick up a little something for my love. I ended up with little somethings for four people I love. The cards are absolutely perfect. The selection at first appears small, but when every card says exactly the right thing, you don't need aisles to choose from.   While I didn't have time to peruse the rest of the store, I have a feeling I'd love every inch of it. At check out, the (very nice) woman working there gave me a card for frequent visits. Buy ten cards and get the eleventh free. I'm already halfway there. What a great shop!

When I checked-in to PF Chang's last week, I admit that I laughed at my buddy Brian L's five star review (sorry, Bri). Admittedly, it was several years old, but five stars for a chain restaurant?  I happily ate my words after experiencing excellent service courtesy of our bartender (John) and a terrific happy hour featuring majorly discounted food and drink specials. The specials run from 3-6, an awkward happy hour time for sure, but the deals are aplenty. There's an array of discounted beer, wine and cocktails (not just one or two from each category). Food ranges from $3-7, and the portions are regular-size.   We enjoyed a couple drinks each and four happy hour plates (tuna tataki, chicken lettuce wraps, crab wontons and pork dumplings). The total was just over forty bucks. That's a mid-week dinner out that I can get behind.

I had a hankering for some sushi and always heard positive things about Fuji, so I decided to give it a try.  The restaurant is located in one of the miniature mall-type buildings on Kings Highway in Haddonfield.  The sign out front makes it relatively easy to find, and there is free parking on nights and weekends in the back.    My meal was basic, but exactly what I wanted.  Clear soup, edamame, two pieces each of yellowtail and tuna sushi plus a spicy tuna hand roll.  And a salt lick.  Just kidding.  Luckily, my salt-a-thon was followed shortly thereafter by a boot camp class.   I found some items to be a little on the pricey side when compared with other restaurants of similar caliber in the area.  Still, everything was prepared well and was of a high quality.  I would certainly recommend this restaurant to anyone in the Haddonfield area who wants great, uncomplicated sushi without having to travel very far to get it.

I purchased the Yelp KIT from Aurora Grace and it was fantastic, as expected. Included in the $25 kit is some "ball park bark" - thin, dark chocolate speckled with popcorn and peanuts - plus a pint of vanilla bean ice cream (creamy and delicious!) and, finally, an adorable Philly Phanatic bar which has so far proven to be too cute to eat.   I placed my order online for next day pick-up and received a notification that it was ready earlier than anticipated. My husband picked up the order when he was out running errands, easy peasy. I love fancy chocolates and ice cream so I'll be keeping Aurora Grace in mind for gifts for friends (or myself) in the future!

Macy's Cherry Hill is on one helluva downward spiral. It's almost like Nordstrom arrived and the whole place just gave up and waved the white flag of defeat. The only area of the store that doesn't make me want to pull my hair out is the downstairs home area.  I'm sure it's in Macy's best interest to at least keep the bed, bath and kitchen departments up to snuff - they'd be reduced to nothing without their bridal registry business.  The shoe department is always a zoo, the lingerie/pajama department is stocked with items I'd imagine could be found in a Kmart (cheap- and tacky-looking) and the women's department is a minefield littered with detonated clothes explosions: articles falling off of hangers, draped over racks or just on the floor. Dressing rooms are outdated and just kind of gross.   It would really take a miracle to get this place back on track.

My friend/colleague Cara and I enjoyed a leisurely lunch at Strangelove's this week. We arrived past the usual lunch hour and there were just a few people eating at the bar. The bartender, Jill, took care of us at a nearby table.   We started with a glass of vinho verde which was slightly effervescent and went very well with the delicious pimento cheese we ordered. Next up was a round of gazpacho, which came in an enormous bowl. We both did not finish since we had salads on the way. My arugula salad was dressed in a tangy vinaigrette with a handful of grilled shrimp and pickled veggies. It was light but high on taste; I'd order it again. Looking forward to returning for dinner!

Give it up for PATCO.  In the past year, there have been drastic improvements in areas that count.  Out with the old-school magnetic tickets and arcade-like change machines, in with paper tickets from a machine that accepts ones, fives, tens and twenties.   Gone are the days when you must brandish your mace like a deranged lunatic while waiting at the stations (many of them underground) after dark; now there are security people at every stop.  Keep that mace handy while in the train though... the freaks really do come out at night.  The trains might be reminiscent of 1980, the year they were last updated, but so what?  PATCO is still a reliable, quick and affordable way for people to travel across the bridge.

The beer menu definitely has personality but besides that?  Eh.      Chips and salsa cost 7 or 8 dollars, which is crazy considering they come standard at most Mexican restaurants.  The chips bore a strong resemblance to Tostitos Gold.  Remember them?  They were the super thick yellowy chips.  I suspect you can't find them in stores anymore because Jose Pistolas probably bought them all out.      My boyfriend had a pork and pineapple burrito, which was... different, and I had the tuna tacos which were good but not memorable.    Everything is pretty much a la carte~ so if you want rice and beans with your entree you better fork over $4.  We passed.    I would go back if I was with people who wanted to go, but probably wouldn't choose to go there again myself.

I was in the neighborhood for a meeting and swung by GSpa afterwards for a mani-pedi. The sign outside suggested that they were offering $10 off this combo but when I got inside I found out that was only for the more costly mani-pedis. I decided to stay regardless, and I'm glad I did. There were tons of OPI and Essie polishes to choose from, and I had the place all to myself which was very nice. This is definitely a much nicer salon than most nail places in the city. The decor is better (more spa-like) and there's a fountain or two with trickling water.   My pedi was so relaxing and, just as importantly, not painful. The nail tech took her time and didn't rush through any part of the process. The massage she gave was absolutely wonderful, and the products used were better quality than your average spot.   My mani was just as great and I had a blast chatting with the young woman who performed my service (if you're reading this, I didn't get a ticket!). I'm adding GSpa to my list of acceptable nail salons and I will be back.

While on my way to one of my usual spots for coffee in Rittenhouse, I took a sharp left and detoured to Saxbys, since I had never been. The first thing I noticed was the expansive menu of coffee beverages. They sounded great but I know these types of drinks usually taste too sweet for me so I went with a regular coffee and requested a single shot of chocolate syrup. For $2.05, I don't know if I got that little kick of suga' for free or if Saxbys prices are just that low. Nonetheless, it made me happy. And happy people tip better.   The fixins station was a bit of a mess and in a crowded area. I think it would be better for everyone over by the ledge near the door. The staff all seemed nice. Not bad, Saxbys.

Swinging back over to the Sprouts page to share more love. This has become my go-to grocery store and I have been placing weekly orders through Instacart since the beginning of the pandemic. We do pick-up because it's super easy; just pull in to the designated spots, let the shoppers know you're there via the app, pop your trunk and you're out of there in no time.   The best thing about Sprouts is that the products are comparable to what you'll find at Whole Foods, only better priced. Cons are that their pantry and household items are limited to a couple different brands. Some products I do like, but I often have to do a Target run for things where I have a brand preference. In terms of the basics, Sprouts covers us pretty well and I am so happy to have them nearby.

I love the Stage for its large main stage and the artists that appear on it. Also, I've heard of surprise visits by some big names which has got to be an amazing thing to see when you're just there hanging out.   The place is always pretty crowded and it's difficult to get to the bar. That would be the biggest negative about The Stage. But the quality of live music and - this is important after all those beers - the gigantic bathrooms which can accommodate lots of ladies are clutch. Definitely a must-visit while in Nashville.

Elixr is one of my favorite coffee shops for meetings and brainstorming. The energy is high, the music is pumping (which sometimes makes it hard to have a conversation so I generally keep said meetings to three people max) and the caffeine is a-kickin'. Pretty sure I'm never falling asleep tonight after two afternoon coffee drinks. Also, the baristas are friendly and they always do that cute heart thing in the latte foam. I love cute hearts in latte foam!   The turnover for tables and especially the more comfy couch seating is pretty high, or maybe I've just been lucky on my past couple of visits. The people watching is prime.

My life was made easier because of Fireball Printing. With a short time frame and limited budget, I turned to the fabulous Felicia D for a recommendation that would fit my needs. She sent me Fireball's website, which was both easy to navigate and understand. I uploaded my file, gave my contact info and received a call within a couple hours.   After discussing my options, I made my decisions and gave my credit card info over the phone. One week later, 5000 postcards were delivered to my front door at no additional charge. Not only did my cards look exactly the way I wanted, but a few Atomic FireBall candies had been thrown in to boot!

I'm pretty sure I now know the true meaning of "everybody wang chung tonight."  A limo bus packed with 20 girls on a bachelorette party was my destiny on a wintry Saturday night.  Upstairs at Risque was our first stop.  No sooner had the door of the bus opened, that a beefcake jumped aboard and got acquainted with our bachelorette.  High pitched squealing ensued.  After being escorted inside and to our table, we were waited on and entertained throughout the night.  My memory remains extremely hazy about all the goings-on, but one thing remains firmly intact in my temporal lobe: DayGlo orange banana hammock.  While I don't think any of the girls plan to start frequenting Upstairs at Risque on regular weekends, I'm sure we'll all keep it in mind while planning future bachelorette parties.  Minus one star for letting people smoke inside!

Peet's coffee with a side of financial planning? Yes, please.   If you've never been to ING Café, give it a whirl for your morning cup. The beverages are cheaper than most coffee shops, and the baristas/bankers are friendly. No one will talk your ear off about a savings account or anything. If you have a question, they're happy to help, but if you don't, just get your drink and be on your way, no hassle.

I love the drive through at this Starbucks. I realize that sentence makes me sound like the laziest person alive, but I'm typically on my way to a friend's house whenever I swing by this location and the drive through is just too convenient to pass up. Everyone who works there is super friendly from my experiences and the line moves quickly. They even plug your drinks with those little green plastic things so there's no spillage. I just wish there was a more convenient way to get out of the parking lot, instead of having to drive back through the strip mall lot.

My man brought home dinner last night, in the form of a half chicken and two sides from Rotisseur. A hot and healthy meal with no kitchen prep? Sign me up!   The chicken was super juicy, tender and very flavorful. Even the pieces well below the crackling skin. Our sides were roasted potatoes and pickled veggies. While the pickled veggies were snappy and fun, I would have preferred some collard greens, spinach, green beans or basically any type of healthy, hot vegetable option. Most of the sides currently offered are starchy and heavy, like mac and cheese and corn bread. Which is totally great, but some lighter options would be most welcome.   I'm sure it won't be long before we pick up dinner again - hopefully with a heaping side of veggies to go alongside!

The building alone is worthy of five stars. Decked out with enormous windows and incredible views of both Independence Mall and the city skyline, it's a breathtaking vantage point.  My recent visit to check out the Spies, Traitors and Saboteurs exhibition, created by the International Spy Museum, was an informative and interesting one. The exhibition chronicles deviants of American history, from when the British invaded in 1812, to the rise of the KKK in the 60s, to present-day tragedies like 9/11. Seeing a mangled sign from the 76th floor of one of the Twin Towers brought tears to my eyes.   I think Tom D sums up my feelings on the Constitution Center best in saying that it is a place "that makes you really proud to be an American."

While the Midtown Tria has always been my favorite, Rittenhouse Tria has really started to grow on me as of late.  The walking proximity to my guy's place makes it the obvious choice when we want a nice glass of wine and a little bite.    The big snowstorm of Winter 2010 is when Rittenhouse Tria really warmed the cockles of my heart.  Despite the weather, the beer, wine and cheese bar was business as usual, with an abundance of pleasant servers who were up to the task of keeping guests fed and quenched.  For $5, we enjoyed glasses of 18% Dogfish Head World Wide Stout.  If that doesn't get the blood pumping on a wintry day, nothing will.  We people watched from our high-top at the back of the bar, amazed by the fact that the nail salon across the street was open, and laughing about how funny it would be if we ran off with some poor woman's snow boots as she enjoyed her pedicure.        Gotta love snow days.

I visited this year's PHS Pop Up Garden yesterday and left a lot less impressed than I was last year. Drinks are now cash-only which is inconvenient. Also, the beer seemed to be pouring very slowly which was causing a major back-up in the line. The move from bottled beer to draft beer somehow also came with a one dollar mark-up over last year's prices.    Food is available through the Jamaican Jerk Hut and rotating food carts. I really liked the offerings from last year's Garces Catering truck - there were some healthy items available, which was great.     Unfortunately, the bathrooms were lacking both soap and paper towels on my visit.   I'm sure I'll be back at some point this summer, but with the plethora of other outdoor beer gardens this year, I'm not rushing back.

I literally just walked in the door from my coconut manicure at Tierra Mia and I feel positively blissful. As if that didn't justify my visit enough, my nails look flawless. That's no easy feat, especially when the shade is dark. And speaking of which, one of the things I love about this salon is that you are guided through the polishes and encouraged to check them out on your nail first before committing to a color. What I originally thought I wanted turned out to be too dark but a second polish was just what I was looking for.   Treat yourself, ladies.

We popped into Green Line Cafe on Sunday for a quick iced coffee to go and, I have to say, that coffee was delicious! Smooth and flavorful; it was everything I wanted in an iced coffee!   The baristas were so friendly and we were in and out quickly. I also noticed lots of good looking baked goods as well.

I was in the mood to try something new and different, so I ordered a lunch delivery from this spot yesterday. I kept it simple and went with just the lemongrass chicken entree.   My delivery arrived quickly, but as soon as I got the bag into my house I realized the sauce from the chicken had leaked out all over the inside of the bag. The food was packed in styrofoam containers which don't exactly travel well if they're being jostled around by a delivery guy on a bike. It was a mess to clean up and the chicken container didn't have much sauce left inside.   Once I got everything onto a plate, I can honestly say the food was just all right, nothing special. I did contact the delivery service about my experience and was given a credit for a future order. Unfortunately, it won't be with Huong Tram.

I can't imagine giving the PHS Pop Up Garden any less than five stars. PHS took a vacant lot and turned it into a gorgeous urban oasis. There are picnic tables everywhere and some other casual seating areas.   The food by Garces Catering Co. is limited but everyone should be able to find something they like. I had the turkey sandwich for lunch and enjoyed it so much I had it again when I found myself hungry for dinner about four hours later! Ten bucks for a turkey sandwich is a little cray, but the minced onion jam and avocado aioli took it up a notch, and the kettle chips alongside were great. Beers are five bucks and I enjoyed several icy cold Summer Loves throughout the day.   Bathrooms were better than I expected! Probably cleaner than a lot of the bars I've visited. Can't understand why I waited so long to check this place out, but I'll take advantage as much as possible for the rest of summer!

I'm definitely a fan of Lolita's new look and the switch from BYO to boozy. I love a good margarita and the bartenders there serve them up every which way - salty, spicy, skinny, sweet - the choice is yours.   Every Mexican meal should start with some guac. I'll probably skip the charred shishito for the traditional on my next visit; I wasn't really picking up much pepper and the peas weren't doing it for me. I think I'm just a traditionalist when it comes to the green stuff. The tuna tostaditas are a total win; I was far more into those than the citrus marinated shrimp and scallops.   The cholula fried chicken tacos are fun but I think the carnitas tacos have the edge. Do not miss the fried plantains. Trust me on this one. They are fantastic!   When it comes to Mexican food, I definitely prefer the savory over the sweet. On our visit there was absolutely no room to even consider dessert.   Rumor has it late night happy hour is a go. It won't be long before the tequila calls me back.

Small, quirky spot that provided a solid weekday lunch and a lot of entertainment. I went one day during the summer and the Olympics were on the TV. The owner was all over the restaurant, commenting on the Olympians, chatting with the other occupied table who seemed to be regulars, dropping off coffee, etc. We chatted for a while about pierogi and I definitely want to get in there to try her version sometime.   I had either an omelet or scramble (I forget which at this point) but I do know it was delicious and there was a ton of food on my plate. They also serve their own hot sauces from mild to very hot - nice touch! Tables are small and, as I mentioned, so is the restaurant, so go expecting a solid, hearty meal and probably some very entertaining conversation then be on your way.

After a wine-filled dinner out with two girlfriends, we decided to pass on dessert and instead continue our night with an after-dinner drink.  Someone suggested L2 since it was nearby so off we went.    It felt like fate when we walked into the bar and three front and center bar stools were available.  I proceeded to order a chocolate martini from Liz, the friendly tattooed bartender who was positively jamming to the Prince CD playing in the background.  The martini was so good and seemed perfectly matched with the Goldfish crackers that were in glass milk jugs on the bar.  The combination reminded me of my youth, which was awesome.    DISCLAIMER: Next time I want to re-create a childhood snack, I'm going to stick with good old-fashioned chocolate milk, because three chocolate milks will not cause the side-splitting headache effect that three chocolate martinis (and many glasses of wine) will the next morning.  However, if I'm ever again jonesin' for ONE really good chocolate martini, L2 is my place!

This is becoming my favorite coffee shop, even though it's not in my neighborhood. The baristas are nice, and they take credit cards. I am in love with the Earl Gray tea with some steamed milk. Also, their pressed mozzarella tomato sandwich is great! I go out of my way to work at this cafe, and I don't mind a bit.

With a trunk full of soiled linens from the recent Yelper Party, I searched Yelp to find a place to get them cleaned. Maytag came up with great reviews and weekend hours. Plus, it's in my neighborhood, so extremely convenient.  I swung by on Saturday with two huge trash bags filled with linens, and the woman who worked there weighed them and gave me a receipt, saying I could pick them up later. Same day service!
