I ended up getting them the next day, but for more than forty pounds of linens, my charge was less than $35. Crazy! After the sheets were folded up, they all fit neatly into just one of the bags. It's cash only, but such a deal. Strongly recommended.

Three stars seems appropriate for Joe's. My husband and I were out running errands all day, when we realized it was time for dinner. In the mood for seafood, we thought it might be fun and a little bit random to try Joe's Crab Shack. The restaurant was poppin' so we decided to take seats at the bar.   The bartender who was our server was friendly, but didn't check in with us very often. The other bartender actually went out of her way to make sure we had the proper utensils, napkins, etc.   I wanted something simple and healthy so I got the cedar salmon. It was indeed simple but the fish was flavorful and the portion was pretty generous. The veggies and rice alongside were boring but, again, I was going for healthy. My husband had a steam bucket with crab legs and a medley of seafood, corn and potatoes. He was happy with his choice.   Overall, I'd say our experience was fine but probably a one and done.

Love The Lodge at the RiverRink! My husband's former company threw his farewell party there, and we had a private area catered with huge trays of Chickie's crab fries. Amazing.   I was back again for a family fun night on Saturday and we had a blast. The ice was pretty crowded for the 5pm skate but not enough that you couldn't get around without knocking into people, if you can skate somewhat strategically. I did see quite a few spills.   Our crew ice skated for probably 25 minutes tops before we decided to warm up in The Lodge. I love the selection of beers, wine and hot spiked beverages. There are also food offerings from Chickie & Pete's, Garces and Franklin Fountain. We grabbed a bunch of food to share and I have to admit the cheesesteak from C&P's hit the spot.   Why not five stars? The bathroom situation is dire. It's one of those trailer bathrooms that are often just fine, but looked absolutely gross on the night we visited. I took one look and turned right back around. The bathrooms inside the rink are a much safer bet.

Pat O'Brien's was the first stop of the day on a day that quickly went downhill due to many, many rum concoctions and little food. Of course, we went to try the Hurricanes, which come to you in all their Hawaiian Punch-red glory through a serving device that fills several glasses at the same time from a seemingly endless trough. PRO TIP: There are several bars throughout the property and, if you can believe it, they all charge different prices for their drinks. The least expensive by a quarter or two can be found at the inside bars.   The outside patio area is very pretty but also very hot (because, New Orleans). We opted for the cool temps of the inside bar, which had the smells and feels of just about every old school Irish bar out there. This is when we discovered the differing price structure of the beverages. Said Hurricanes were sweet. God only knows what possessed me to order a second after finishing that first.   I think Pat O's is a one and done type of experience for me personally, but don't let that stop you from doing as the tourists do on your own trip!

Tattooed Mom has never been my favorite spot (my last visit was probably about five years ago), but I definitely get why people dig it. On my recent visit, I discovered the upstairs for the first time. Interesting. I enjoyed finding Doggystyle in the jukebox and played almost the entire album. I also played pool (terribly) alongside Vinny P, who amazingly kept me as his partner for more than one game. Speaking of my pool partner, he graciously shared his basket of tots and I found them to be quite delicious.   Until we meet again, T-Mom's.

Jury duty: sequestered at lunch edition.   If you're ever performing your civic duty in Philadelphia and lunch is brought in from Tootsie's, you are in good hands.   Though the menu is brief and pretty basic, there was something for everyone. My turkey and cheese on wheat hit the spot, came with the correct side (chips) and a decent fruit cup for dessert. There were a solid array of choices of sides and desserts.   I'm fairly certain everyone got exactly what they asked for, so this would be a good spot when you need to order lunch for a group, or are just in need of a simple, brown bag lunch.

I desperately needed a pedi, but not anything too fabulous/expensive. Just one that would get me through the two weeks before my friend's wedding when, as one of the bridesmaids, I'll be primped and prettied up and my nails will be taken care of all over again. When I read the reviews for Boutique Nails and Hair, I saw mostly positive things from some trusted Yelpy cohorts.   The woman who took care of me was sweet, and when I mentioned that I'm training for a run she was especially careful not to go overboard on the scrubbing.   It's rare that I'll give more than 3 stars to a quickie nail salon, because I'm too spoiled by nice salons at this point. The difference in quality of products, attention to detail and overall relaxation is huge. But for a walk-in spot that smoothed over the rough edges and painted my toes a shiny candy apple red, I'm pleased with my experience.

I breezed through this store for the first time on Sunday, after seeing a cute dress on a sale rack outside the front door. As I busied myself with a rack of clothing, my boyfriend came over and whispered in my ear, "Did you see who's here?" One quick glance at the back of a curly-headed man was all I needed to see: Scott Hartnell!   Turns out, even athletes don't get out of shopping with their ladies.  The merchandise was on the slimmer side, compared with some of the larger stores on the street, but there were a few interesting pieces. I tried on a couple cute dresses that ended up fitting like a potato sack and a muumuu, in that order.   I would probably swing through the store again while in the area, but I wouldn't go out of my way for it, either.

I've been to Founding Fathers three times. The first was during an Eagles game, and it was so crowded that our group left right away, knowing it would be very difficult to even get up to the bar. So, I probably won't be going back during any major sporting events, despite the plethora of large TVs on every wall.   My next two visits were for a late dinner. Bianca was our server on both occasions and she was friendly and did a great job. It seems like this bar hosts a lot of loud twenty-somethings and I'm sure that doesn't always make for an easy night.   The food is fairly average, maybe a little above, but I've also only tried some of the small plates. Flatbreads are good but could use a couple more minutes in the oven, and the chicken fingers are great but you get four for nine dollars which is crazy. The beer selection is solid. I also like that the high tops along the wall have lots of room and feel a bit further from the crowd than the high tops closer to the bar area. Overall, solid spot for a casual meal.

I was making homemade crunchwraps and needed tostadas. Harder to find than you might think, even at the giant grocery stores I occasionally visit in the 'burbs. That said, I knew exactly where I'd find them in Philly, so I sent my husband on a mission to Tortilleria San Roman, where he secured a fat stack.   The tostadas are perfectly crunchy and ideal for recipes, or breaking apart and dipping into every last queso/salsa/hot sauce you've accumulated during this crazy year. The bonus was getting to support a local business, even whilst cooking my own dinner for a change.

Just off the plane from Philly to St. Louis, I was in desperate need of some caffeine and a bite. To Kaldi's we went, where an oasis of coffee beverages and healthy food options awaited.   The baristas were friendly and funny - love that. I ordered an iced coffee and a chickpea wrap which came stuffed with quinoa and kalamata olives and came with a choice of side. I picked the chips, which were super thin, perfectly crunchy and just a little salty. The wrap was filling and delicious but didn't make me feel super weighed down.   I noticed some outdoor seating which would be great on a nice day. This is a great spot for a solo working lunch, coffee meeting or gabfest with a friend.

I've come to like honeygrow a bit more over the past year or so. The machines can still be a little finicky at times but nothing like they were when I wrote my last review. I love being able to customize my salad to my exact needs without annoying anyone in the process. The ingredients are always fresh and I love the dressing options (I usually opt for one of the vinaigrettes). This is one of my go-to spots for a healthy salad. The juices are solid as well.  I do hate the bowls they use, because if you cut your salad, the bowl will topple over and your ingredients will go flying and you will rage. You. Will. Rage. For this reason, I usually transfer my salad to a sturdier bowl at home.   Fresh. Healthy. Friendly employees. Worthy of an upgrade to four stars.

I really loved this adorable bagel shop my sister brought me to when I stayed at her house a couple weekends ago. If I lived in the area, it would undoubtedly be the place where I would set up shop a couple times a week. It's cozy, with the brick oven cooking bagels and lots of comfy seating and coffee tables. Looks like they have lunch options in addition to breakfast.  Love that they serve La Colombe, and loved even more that they had bags of beans for sale as well, since I needed to stock up. While I didn't get my own bagel that day, I did try a bite or two of my sister's, which was delicious. Can't wait to go back next time I visit and eat all the carbs.

My husband and I went out for a long stroll around the city on Labor Day, and one of our first stops was Cira Green. To be honest, I didn't really know what to expect, but I was very pleasantly surprised by the beautiful, well-maintained space. There was hardly anyone around on such a gorgeous day, so the park felt like a fun secret between the few people who were enjoying some time there.   The views of the city are absolutely beautiful. Because of the building's proximity to the Schuylkill River, you get the river views as well as the skyline views in all directions.   I hope to get back soon and I plan to bring a picnic along!

If we were voting on decor alone, I'd give the place 5 stars, hands-down.  The place is so cute inside and I did not run out of things to look at the entire 2+ hours I was there for brunch on Sunday.  The crabcake sandwich I had was really good and served with a nice fruit salad on the side.    My only gripe is that it was extremely warm in the restaurant~ I was sweating the entire time I sat at the bar while waiting for my friends.  Other than that, fantastic place and I'd be inclined to bump my review up to 5 stars if I go back and have another great, less hot-flashy, experience.

In case you haven't heard, Sidecar's upstairs bar/dining room is open for service! We swung by last night with friends to check it out and everyone agreed that the exposed brick, retro banquettes and tables and large windows with a pretty view of the skyline were on point. It's a totally different vibe and yet somehow the same old Sidecar. Great servers, awesome beer. Two thumbs up.

This is pretty much the nicest public library I've ever been to. It's enormous. More like something you'd find on a college campus. Now I know where Cherry Hill taxpayer dollars are going.   My little cousin held a film premiere (yes, really) in one of the rooms on the lower level. I think my aunt said it was around $150 to rent and it fit ~100 people. So on a meeting space standpoint, that's not too shabby.

Oops!  I was wrong in my previous review when I said that Severino pastas only come frozen or dried. Some varieties are also available fresh. I know this because I have a pound of whole wheat fettuccine packaged neatly in a little box, ready for dinner tonight.   Another thing I noticed while in the store today is that the cheese selection is no joke. I literally swooned when I saw a big block of etorki, which I previously thought was only available at DiBruno Brothers (in this area, anyway). If summer wasn't just around the corner I'd be serving a cheese course tonight as well. Le sigh.

I'm picking up what you're putting down, Bardot. The dark and sexy bar is perfect for a date or small group. And the tiny, tucked-away parlor with curtain would be perfect for a scandalous liaison.   The staff was sweet but not entirely up to speed on menu items. The buttery shrimp were served head-on, though when I asked before ordering I was told that they were served only with the tails still attached. Minor, but enough of a turnoff for me that I probably would have opted for a different plate. The octopus dish was a win amongst our table of three, and I simply could not get enough of the spaetzle with purple cauliflower. It was perfect.   Our server recommended cocktails for my friends while I tried the Côtes du Rhône Blanc, which I deeply enjoyed. I can't wait to go back for another glass, some more French pop, and that delicious-looking burger that accidentally almost made its way to our table.

I'm going to update my rating to three stars, because I enjoyed my lunch on Saturday. But, I still feel pretty strongly that some of the sides could be tweaked a bit for better taste. My German potato salad and sauerkraut were both served ice cold. I don't get it! German potato salad is delicious at room temp, and who eats sauerkraut cold?! To be honest, I order these sides because they aren't as heavy as some of the other options. I really wish a little more care was put into the way they are presented.   My quarter pound of pulled pork was smokey, full of flavor and delicious! And my husband's burnt end beans were equally awesome.   I really do like Fette Sau, but I still don't love it.

This PJs has definitely made some major improvements since my last review more than five years ago. At the time, Iron Hill had rolled in around the corner and seemed like a shinier, better option. But over time, my loyalties have remained with PJs. They definitely went through a rough patch but my handful of visits over the past few years have all been solid.   The beer program has improved from a selection of domestics to an array of craft brews for every taste. Their wings are awesome and I love that they have so many different types of buffalo-style choices like wraps, salads and sandwiches. Big fan.

Super cute boutique on Pine that I never even knew existed until Friday. I popped into Hello Home thinking they sold baby gear, and was told that only their location in Rittenhouse has a baby section. The woman working also told me that Industry just down the street stocked a small amount of baby merchandise.   I had ten minutes on my meter and no more quarters so I needed to make things snappy. It's probably a good thing, because I saw a lot of cute stuff as I rushed my way to the back of Industry. I could have easily done way more damage with some more time. The baby selection was small but there were some really cute Philly-centric onesies, which was exactly what I was hoping to find. The gentleman at the counter took off the price tag and wrapped the onesie in a cute box with a twine bow. I love when I don't have to wrap gifts! I'll definitely return, perhaps for my own perusal.

Solid experience from The Original Turkey yesterday. Options are fairly limited, which is actually great because it helps to keep the line moving. The line was maybe ten people deep when I jumped on and it moved pretty quickly.   I ordered the turkey sandwich with lettuce, tomato and choice of cheese. I opted for rye and asked for one slice of swiss - no mayo. I also asked for toasted bread. Turns out, if you want toasted, they just pop your sandwich onto a press. I like that! I also got a small side of coleslaw and some pickles. The coleslaw was a bit mayo-heavy for my liking but I did enjoy the sweet taste with the saltiness of the pickles. All together I think my order was in the neighborhood of nine dollars and I can definitely get on board with that.

My husband has been raving about Burg's forever, and I'm so glad I finally took his recommendation and tried it for dinner with a friend. The decor is super cute; think relaxed surf shack vibes. The menu of drinks and food is short but sweet. What they do in the food department, they do very well.   My friend ordered the lone cocktail on the menu, which was some sort of fresh watermelon punch, served in a fun tiki glass with a fistful of fresh mint. It was delicious! I was feeling super basic so was happy to see Coors Light among the list of much tastier yet heavier craft brews.  We ordered a bunch of plates from the menu - they are so affordable, how could you not?! We had edamame, mushroom and kimchi spring rolls, miso cod, tuna poke, cucumber salad, and also a surprise from the kitchen - mixed olives which I believe were lightly dusted with fennel pollen and served with some orange rind. Everything was delicious and light - even the spring rolls had a very thin wrapper and didn't seem greasy.   In short: I loved Burg's and can't wait to return!

This gated storage facility is clean, easy to get in and out of, and not too scary. Well, it's a little scary when the light timer runs out and you get stuck in the dark, but other than that, not too bad.   The rental fee for a very small closet is edging ever closer to $100 per month, but I have to say, I'm happy to have a place that isn't my own apartment to store all my schwag.   I also hope to one day become friends with the VitaminWater rep.

I attended a showing of the play Bachelorette with a couple friends last night. Before then, I had never heard of the Adrienne Theater, and I was surprised when we arrived to a multi-purpose building that seemed to have a lot of different theater spaces within. Bachelorette was in the Sky Box, all the way up the staircase.   The stage was small but the set was cool, and every seat in the small theater was filled. Even from my position in the last row on the end, I could still see and hear everything just fine. I'd definitely attend a show there again.

Located on what is probably one of the most beautiful, majestic streets in Philadelphia is the Rosenbach Museum & Library. I stopped by for a tour recently and was really taken by some of the beautiful pieces and the stories behind them. My docent of the day, Elyse, knew everything there was to know about each item and the museum itself. Truth be told, I felt like a royal dum dum, knowing next to nothing about art history, but I was assured that most people aren't overly familiar with many of the works. That, or Elyse was trying to make me feel better. It worked!  My favorite piece was a Thomas Sully portrait of Rebecca Gratz, a well-known Philadelphia socialite in the 1800s. The tale behind the woman is a truly fascinating one, and I was inspired enough to do my own research.   I'd encourage anyone with a little extra time to spare to go and find his or her own muse within the walls of the Rosenbach.

How I love this place! Georgetti's is the quintessential neighborhood prepared foods grocery. It's a one stop shop for a delicious meal for one or ten (or more - they cater!).   I'm honestly not a big fan of cooking, so any ally that assists in getting a delicious meal on the table is a huge plus. From fresh breads to homemade soups, dressings, pastas, sauces and more, I generally pick up anywhere from two to five meals' worth of groceries whenever I make a stop.   Georgetti's pumpkin bisque kicks off my family's Thanksgiving dinner and their lobster bisque is a staple in our annual feast of seven fishes for Christmas Eve. This business is truly one of the best and I'm so grateful it exists!

I was totally stoked to check out the Philly version of Fette Sau. Hate to say it, but I was really disappointed. The meats are smoked and not saucy; you can add your own sauce once you are at the table. We had a few different meats and they were okay but I do prefer a saucier style of BBQ.   The real disappointment was in the sides. The sauerkraut was served cold. It was crunchy. Let me repeat: crunchy, cold, sauerkraut. Who likes that? The German potato salad was also cold. GPS is often served at room temperature which is just fine, but this was refrigerator cold and lacking in any tangy, delicious flavor. It was so weak. The only side I really enjoyed was the baked beans.   Fette Sau doesn't come cheap, either. For that reason, I guess I can look at the bright side and be grateful that I'm not a fan.

After perusing the Yelp reviews on Foo Truck, I decided the green curry quinoa foo'wich sounded like a winner. The contents were secured in a perfectly folded tortilla, which looked like it had been pressed for extra measure and a little crunch. The delicious pocket stayed intact even through the last few bites -impressive!  The sandwich itself was nicely flavored with coconut milk and some serious heat. A small side of Sriracha added an extra kick, though I had to take turns guzzling water between bites. I was also able to nab a bite of the meatball 'wich, and I definitely liked the flavors there, too. I expect more visits to the Foo Truck in my future!

Damn you, Scott L. from Belmont, CA, for thinking to review Georgetti's before me!    I grew up on the pasta, sauces, soups and bread from Georgetti's.  Everything is homemade and takes very little time to prepare at home.  This is a one-stop shop for pulling together an Italian dinner for two or ten, without the hassle of actually cooking.

Despite not being able to locate a single employee during my hour+ visit on Sunday, I was definitely feeling this branch of Sweat. I walked in, took one look at that giant ramp to the second floor, and kept right on walking towards the back, thinking (hoping?) that the treadmills would be on the first floor. Nice try. I found an approachable looking dude who, between gulps of air, informed me that the cardio equipment was on level two. Up the incline I went.   It turned out to be a good thing, because I got to scope out the gym in its entirety and without much distraction, as pleasant Sunday afternoons are the deadest time in the life of a gym. The huge open areas really worked for me, and everything was new-looking. The treadmills faced a large open window, providing a nice distraction during commercials of the Phillies game, which I watched on the TV that was attached to my machine. I had an excellent workout, and I'd happily visit this location again.

A little slice of peace and tranquility right in Philadelphia! I'm so glad I got to -finally- check out Shofuso Japanese House & Garden. Shofuso is located in Fairmount Park, and there is a small parking lot onsite. You must leave your shoes on a rack before entering the house (don't forget to bring socks!).   The gardens are small but lovely, and I especially enjoyed the koi fish in the pond, which were enormous! The house is very interesting; some rooms you can walk through while others you can only look into from outside, but each room has a sheet with information so you can learn more about the function of the room. The docents were all tied up with leading other people around the house but I overheard some of the information which was quite interesting. If you can snag a docent to lead you around, do it!   The wraparound porch overlooking the pond was a great place to sit and relax after the tour. I could see myself going back on a nice day simply to enjoy a refreshing mental break. Philadelphians: add this to your summer to-do list!

I found Philly Custom DJ through a Yelp search and it was a total win! Adam responded to my message within minutes and was able to work with my budget for a two-hour event. When the party was still rocking, he had no problem adding an extra half hour (paid, of course), which I greatly appreciated.   From our first communication, Adam was always available and he even created a shared playlist doc so that we could work together on the music for my event. Working with Adam was above all else easy - I can't tell you how many times I've had difficulty getting in touch with DJs in the past. That was not the case here at all. I'm looking forward to booking Philly Custom DJ for other events in the future!

I have passed by this fairly new-to-the-neighborhood coffee shop often and have wanted to check it out.  Friday morning presented the perfect opportunity to do so as I had the day off and was running errands around town.  I stopped in for a coffee and something sweet, I wasn't sure what yet.  The friendly woman behind the counter said that the pumpkin scones had been freshly baked that morning, and I was sold.    The shop was super cute; stylish and fun but relaxed.  I prayed that the coffee would be good so I could start making this place a regular stop--it was!  I got home and tore into my scone which was filled with nuts, raisins and cranberries.  Yum.    I really hope the owners do well here and I will be doing my part to make sure they do!

Burg's was a favorite of mine, so I was pumped when Community opened up in its place. The opening menu didn't thrill me but, recently, the menu has changed quite a bit and I finally got around to trying Community for takeout this week.   I had the chicken shawarma sandwich with zataar fries. My husband had the chickpea veggie burger which was basically the same thing that I ordered but with a meatless protein (love that this is an option!). I also added on a side salad.   Everything was packaged nicely and the portions were generous. I really loved my side salad and the homemade dressing that came with - delish! The sandwich was also solid, though I would have preferred it without beets but didn't see a way to modify or make a note anywhere. Also, I would have ordered the sandwich with salad instead of fries, but there wasn't an option to swap (salad instead of fries was an option for the chickpea sandwich, however, so this may have just been an oversight or glitch).    Overall, a solid first experience and I look forward to trying more from the menu!

It's been a minute since my last visit to La Calaca Feliz. My husband happened to be in the neighborhood and I was jonesing for tacos so he suggested takeout from La Calaca. Excellent choice!   We ordered the shrimp tacos, blackened mahi mahi tacos and a side of refried beans all to share. I had some leftover guac and chips at home; otherwise, we probably would have ordered another side or app.   The tacos were absolutely delicious. There were two flour tacos in the mahi order and three, smaller corn tacos in the shrimp order. Both had entirely different toppings, which I loved. I think the shrimp tacos had a slight edge for my favorite but the mahi was great as well. The beans were solid, too.   Glad we revisited La Calaca Feliz and I'll be thinking of them for takeout more often in the future!

I've loved Vault + Vine since before I ever stepped foot in the store. My sister lives nearby and she picks up a lot of her gifts there. Most recently, a pair of earrings for my birthday in August!   Last Sunday we stopped by together and I was really impressed by the array of jewelry, candles, cards and other gifts that they are able to pack in to such a petite space. The greenery is particularly impressive, and they have a really beautiful selection. I'm in the beginning stages of making some changes to my home office and would like to incorporate a large plant. We spoke with one of the employees (Kay, I think!) who was very knowledgeable. When I'm ready to make a purchase, I'll definitely consider returning to Vault + Vine since they were already so helpful.   Also, love the cafe area and they make a great, not-too-sweet chai. What a cute spot!

Update! Café Ynez is my go-to neighborhood spot for a working breakfast. There are always seats on weekday mornings and everyone is so friendly. I love the food (the vegetarian enchiladas and breakfast burrito are my faves) but I enjoy chatting with Qamara, the manager, just as much! The prices are more than fair which gives me an excuse to go pretty regularly. One of these days I'll go for dinner with a bottle of tequila in tow so I can try their margs.

We checked out Flying Fish's tasting room on a recent Friday before heading to dinner nearby. The location isn't super desirable as it's way down 295 without much else to visit nearby, but Flying Fish may soon become a destination in itself with the addition of some outdoor elements, on deck for later this summer.  State law requires tasting room visitors to receive an education about the beer before consumption, so we quickly learned a bit about each beer style Flying Fish creates. We wanted to try all the beers available during our visit so our group of four shared a tasting of all nine on tap. I'm pretty familiar with the regulars: Hopfish, Red Fish, Extra Pale Ale and the Exit series. The NJ 350 Anniversary Ale is available now and it's awesome.   There is no food served in the tasting room (again, blame the state laws) but it's still worth a trip to try the suds. I'm looking forward to going back when the outdoor area is complete.

I owe Veda an upgrade. My husband and I went recently with my in-laws and had a really fantastic meal!   We shared a bunch of starters which were all delicious and everyone was pleased with their entrees as well. Our server (I can't remember her name but she's so sweet and I remembered her from when she worked at Sidecar) was great and very knowledgeable about the menu and the wine list. I enjoyed several glasses of crisp white along with my meal.   I've always considered Veda to be a pretty close tie with my other favorite Indian restaurant in town, but Veda might have a slight edge. I'm looking forward to my next meal, either in-house or via delivery.

We checked out this theatre to see Life of Pi late on Friday evening, and I was surprised to see that there were hardly any people there at all. There were maybe three groups in our theater which made for a quiet, relaxing viewing.   Everything from the hallways to the bathrooms was clean and well kept. I was a little disappointed in the film selection (Jack the Giant Slayer in both regular and 3D? Really?), but I ended up really enjoying Life of Pi so there were no regrets there. Would I go out of my way for this theatre? No. But if you live in the area, it's a solid option.

My favorite part of a cupcake, or any cake, for that matter, is the icing. Oddly enough, Pamcakes' cupcakes proved to me that there can be too much of a good thing. There was more icing than cake! However, the cake itself was one of the moistest I've encountered - the day after it was purchased!  Our two cupcakes were adorably packaged in a to-go box and tied with a white and red string. Just opening that box made me happy today. I'll definitely check out Pamcakes again, but I'll be crossing my fingers for just a bit more cake to even out all that icing.

If you're looking for high quality, delicious chocolates in Philadelphia, Lore's is your place. My mother-in-law has been giving us boxes of buttercreams for some time. Recently, she threw in a box of dark chocolate covered caramels sprinkled with sea salt. They are so fresh and so delicious!   The store itself has all the nostalgia of an old school candy shop. I stopped by during the Christmas season to pick up a box of chocolates for my grandmom. Lore's is now my go-to for nice chocolates!

One of my goals is to become more familiar with Chinatown this year, so I started with Chinatown Square this week. Basically, this is sort of a modern food court with a nice-sized handful of restaurants. The space was clean and had a nice, sleek appearance, plus good music pumping in the background! Some of the restaurants had counter tops only and you'd have to take your food to the seating area in the back, while others had bar seating in front and looked to serve alcoholic beverages.   I was happy to see one of my favorites, Halal Guys, as well as discover a new favorite in Philly Poké. I also can't wait to check out the new Korean restaurant upstairs, and the Mexican-Korean fusion spot towards the back. I'll be returning ASAP!

I'm with Angela J - Penguin Cleaners is ridiculously expensive. However, every item I've ever dropped off comes back looking like I just pulled it off the rack. The kind folks who own this place have restored dresses that I swore would never look the same again after accidental wine spillage.  Now that I live in the city, I am going to look for a place nearby for my regular dry cleaning needs. But when it comes to my favorite, most delicate pieces, I'll continue to travel across the bridge for reliable care.

Wow. Four plus years of living in Collingswood and I had yet to step foot into the Collingswood Ballroom until this past weekend when one of my besties got married. The main events coordinator seemed really organized and, more importantly, calm. The ceremony was set to take place outside and that's how we rehearsed it, but when rain threatened on the big day and everything had to be moved inside, no one panicked and everything went off beautifully and without a hitch.   The Ballroom itself is very pretty and fits a ton of people. I love that there is only one ballroom so your special event feels special and not like one of many as it does at a lot of wedding-focused venues. The balcony provides the perfect setting for pre-reception cocktails. Bathrooms were very clean throughout the night.   I'm not sure if you can hire your own catering or if the catering is contracted to a specific house caterer, so I'll reserve my comments on food and service. Speaking just from a venue standpoint, I was impressed and I'd recommend the Collingswood Ballroom for weddings or other large-scale events.

Last night we hit up Race Street for some brews after ice skating. The lighting was dim, the fireplace was kicking, and Radiohead was the soundtrack. It was a very comfy place to kick back for a couple hours with friends.   We ordered a few dishes and I remain skeptical of the offerings. Buffalo shrimp were a disappointment as they arrived completely naked - no batter or any sort of crunchy coating - and just sort of marinating in buffalo sauce. At least it was a healthy snack! Waters were requested but never brought over to the table, even after a server mentioned he would be back with waters after we asked.   Great spot for a beer with friends while in the area, maybe a bite if you know what to order, but probably not a destination.

I ordered delivery from Amalia's last week for the first time. When ordering Mediterranean, I usually keep it pretty simple and stick with the chicken kebabs. These were served over rice with a side of salad (several choices - I went with the classic Mediterranean) and some mezza which included olives and pickled veggies. The platter also comes with pita which I asked them to leave out since I try to avoid delicious gluten during the week.   I was bummed that there wasn't an option to add a side of hummus as part of the meal. Instead, I had to order a small side which cost five dollars for a teeny tiny portion. I was grateful that they were willing to sub fresh veggies for pita, however. All of the food was quite good!   My lunch total came out to over twenty bucks which was quite steep, but I was also paying for the convenience of delivery. I really liked Amalia's but will probably keep it as a once-in-a-while treat instead of a regular in my delivery lineup.

A friend and I set out to the Taproom one night last week for a couple drinks.  Despite living in the area for almost three years, I had never actually gone to this particular bar, which was formerly known as R Mac's.  The parking lot was completely packed, and the outdoor deck was crowded with a mix of people in all age groups.  There are two bars on the deck, the larger of which held flat screen TVs that were easy to see from all sides of the bar area.  I was pleasantly surprised that my martini was served in a real martini glass (the cute stemless kind!) as opposed to a plastic version since we were outside.   When it started to get cooler, we moved inside.  The restaurant and bar area was very nice, and looked like a great place to hang out, grab a bite or watch a game.  They also have live music on Thursday nights.    It's nice to have an alternative to PJ's, and the outdoor deck gives the Taproom an edge with the warmer months coming.

If Georgetti's ever closed, I'd be totally screwed, because I buy all of my meals for special occasions celebrated at home from this place! Please don't ever, ever close, Georgetti's!  My last review sums it up but to get into a bit more detail, my favorites are:   Soup - lobster bisque, escarole, chicken chili   Pasta - I'm a fan of either the plain white pasta or the wheat, cut into fettuccine thickness. In my opinion, it's better than any other fresh pasta you can buy in this area.  Sauce - marinara, meat sauce, pesto, alfredo  Salad dressing - traditional vinaigrette  Prepared foods - lasagna, any of the stuffed breads, chicken parmesan cutlets  These are my standard go-tos but you could get anything in that store and not go wrong. I've happily trekked over the bridge and back just to grab dinner. The people who work there are always the nicest, and there's always something different to sample while you're there. One of my favorite local businesses, and I'll go back again and again.

Really loved this pretty coffee shop in Old City. It's bright and spacious, with a nice seating area by the window up front, and plenty of tables throughout the space. I chose a table towards the back near the awesome desert mural. Props for having coat hooks prominently placed along the higher counters. Five stars to their music selection, also.  The baristas were all really nice. I opted for a basic cup of coffee which tasted great. My coffee companion went for a breakfast sandwich that looked really delicious.   Going to Menagerie just to enjoy a coffee while I work would mean going out of my way, but I can honestly see myself doing that because I liked the place so much. Looking forward to my next visit!

Love this pretty boutique in Old City! I dropped by with a friend to browse and ended up with a lacy tank perfect for layering. The tank itself was very affordable but I did notice some higher-priced items as well. Like many of the other boutiques in Old City, it's a mix which is good for everyone.   The ladies working were super friendly and it was an overall pleasant experience. I'll return next time I'm strolling the shops.

Maybe I went on an off day but I felt like So Crepe was so average. There were only a few occupied tables but it took forever to order drinks, order food, receive food, etc. It was just a slow operation.   As for the menu, I was surprised by some of the weird savory options (hot dogs?!) and lack of more classic offerings. I ordered the So French crêpe and found the crêpe itself to be rather dry, and I also wasn't crazy about the ham used in the dish.   Ever since L'Aube closed its doors I have been unable to find crêpes I enjoy as much in Philly. The quest continues.

We hit Knead Bagels a few weeks ago and I liked my breakfast very much. I always order the same thing at bagel shops - everything toasted, with veggie cream cheese, bacon, tomato and cucumber. This is what I ordered at Knead but was told they don't serve tomatoes off-season. Fair-enough! I opted for their roasted tomato cream cheese to give the flavor I wanted.   With coffee and a bottle of water, the price rang in less than what I'd spend at Spread but more than South Street Bagels, which is fine. Everything was very tasty and I'll definitely go back when I'm in the area at breakfast time again.

I've probably been watching too many episodes of Say Yes to the Dress. That must be the reason why walking into David's Bridal felt like walking into a time warp back to the 80s. The cheesy music, the terrible decor. Kleinfeld's twas not.   My visit was specifically for bridesmaid dress shopping for my friend's wedding. Our sales rep was somewhat helpful. I'm not sure if she had other appointments at the same time or what, but my friend's mom actually did a better job retrieving the correct dresses and the appropriate sizes for the bridal party.   The common area in the dressing room was a bit tight, with only one large mirrored area for everyone in the fitting room to share. The individual rooms were quite roomy, however.   I felt like the bridesmaid dress selection was a little weak, but they did have tons and tons of wedding gowns. Erin F's experience as a bride-to-be was quite positive, and I'm kind of a novice when it comes to these matters. I'm curious to see how this store would compare with others in the area.

My mom and sister always rave about Marshalls (attached to HomeGoods) but I can't ever figure out what gets them so excited. 95% of the time I go into this hybrid of a store, I'm going to the HomeGoods side. I've scored everything from white plates and a pretty wicker basket for Dîner en Blanc to luxurious Calvin Klein pillows at big markdowns. I'm always intrigued by the majorly discounted accent furniture, and I can't wait to decorate my future home with fun pieces, provided it is bigger than the tiny pad in which I currently reside. Oh yes, HomeGoods, we're going to have some fun.

Knock fills the much-needed niche of the classy gay bar in town. It seems worlds away from Woody's, Tabu and Q Lounge, which is precisely why it felt just a bit out of place as a stop along last night's Gay Bar Crawl.     No matter, the bartenders there treated us kindly with discounted drinks that were creative and enormous. In the line chart that was my drunkenness last night, I'm pretty sure this is where the line started to take a sharp descent.   It seemed like the kitchen was turning out some really awesome eats, because mostly everyone there was having dinner. Also, the Flyers game was on several TVs around the bar, which pleased me greatly.

It had been years since my last Farmicia visit, and with a friend staying at a nearby hotel I thought it would be a solid place for us to grab lunch. We started with the butternut squash soup, and it wasn't long before we both realized that there were awkward chunks of spice within the soup that were impossible to chew. I gave up on my soup about halfway through and mentioned something to our server when she stopped by to check in.   Next up for me were the steak fajitas which were fine but not very memorable. I was happy with my option to sub corn tortillas for flour, however. My friend's salad also looked fine but not very special.  For somewhere in the neighborhood of fifty bucks including tip, I expected a lot more than partly inedible soup and lackluster main courses.

Mangia Macaroni had been on my radar for a while. Their IG page always features some delicious-looking pasta or Italian side. We decided to give them a try on Saturday night for delivery.   We ordered shrimp scampi, crab ravioli and garlic bread. All of the entrees come with a side salad and a hunk of bread with garlic butter.   Presentation-wise, everything was packaged well and was intact upon arrival. The food was probably about three stars for me; the fact that the prices were great and the entrees came with side salads and bread definitely elevated the experience to four star level. This is affordable takeout perfect for a night when you don't feel like cooking.

Upgrading Race Street because my experience last night was solid. My friend and I had just finished dinner at Tuna Bar but we weren't ready to go home. I suggested hot toddies at Race Street and across the street we went.   With only a few more nights until Christmas, this place was bumpin'! We grabbed a table but just a few minutes later, every seat was taken. The servers seemed to be rotating and everyone who stopped by our table at one point or another was super friendly.   The hot toddies were delish (they also do a hot spiked cider) and didn't cost a fortune, which was nice. I also love the fireplace, which is always crackling away on a cold winter's night. It might even be time to try the food again. Hopefully I'll be back sooner than later for a revisit.

I was back again last Friday with a "buy one dinner, get one free" birthday postcard in hand.  I brought my sister since she had never been.  We started out with the guacamole, which was good but would have been better with a little jalapeno or something to give it a kick.  The pico and black bean salsa that comes standard with dinner was tasty as usual.    By the time the entrees rolled out, we were each two deep with Corona Light and feeling a little full from all the chips, salsa and guac.  We found a way to soldier on and really enjoyed our meals.  Mine was a shrimp and scallop burrito with a side of grilled veggies, and Kate's was the chicken fajita plate, which she ate less than half of before giving up.  Everything was really, really good.  Service was consistent throughout our stay and the manager was pretty entertaining and even let us keep his bottle opener on our table.  Tortilla Press, you get another star this time!

I see that I gave this store three stars on a previous visit, but I feel that was probably too generous. Yes, the employees are friendly. And yes, the store is close to where I live, but convenience doesn't make a solid wine store.   This particular branch of PA Wine & Spirits is small. There are maybe three aisles and wine accounts for about half of the store. Half of the wine is cheap crap. So in the end, you are left with about a half an aisle of drinkable vino.   It's super rare that anyone will offer assistance in selecting a bottle, but you're probably better off busting out an app or doing some Internet research as you walk through the aisles.

My first experience at honeygrow was okay. As a first timer, I wasn't sure if I needed to wait in line to use the order machines, if I could go right up to one, or what. It's a tight space with a lot of people during the lunch hour. When I got up to the machine, something was off and I had to touch the screen a hundred times every time I made a choice. The process was slow and frustrating. Maybe I just picked the wonky machine that day. I certainly hope so, otherwise I'd be a lot less likely to go through this process again.   My salad was good but I honestly would have customized it more if the machine had not been so slow. I wasn't super crazy about the soy ginger dressing; it was just like the ginger dressing you would get at a Japanese restaurant; thick and not really good for coating the ingredients. But I loved the list of fresh ingredients, and some of the other dressings sounded pretty tasty. I'll give them another shot sometime.

I am so thrilled to see Hawthornes back up and running after their fire last year. I've been back twice for brunch since they re-opened and, dare I say, I think it may be even better than before?!   There is now wine by the bottle plus Bloody Marys and mimosas! This girl is happy. On my first visit back I ordered the SOS - cream chipped beef on toast. Looks terrifying to the unfamiliar, tastes amazing to anyone who grew up eating it! The second time I ordered Juan's Big Burrito, minus the tortilla. So basically I chose my ingredients (cheddar, onions and bell peppers) and had some scrambled eggs with all of the extras from the burrito on the side (sour cream, avocado, salsa). This came with a heaping side of homefries. It was awesome!  I've checked out their dinner menu and I'm excited to give that a whirl. Welcome back!

I absolutely loved Wonderspaces! For those who are familiar with Artechouse in Washington, DC (or Miami or NYC), it's somewhat similar but, in my humble opinion, waaaaay cooler.   This is Wonderspaces' second permanent location, so new art installations will swap out every few months. That said, do not sleep on the first round of installations! I was truly impressed by so many of them, and they ranged from more traditional art pieces to interactive exhibits, including some virtual reality works (my favorite overall was one of the VRs, titled: Transition).    There's a bar in case you want to grab a drink, though you'll have to leave said drink at drop tables for many of the exhibits.   To be honest, I first thought Wonderspaces was a temporary exhibition and am thrilled that it's permanent! I will definitely plan more visits in the future and can't wait to see how the installations change over time!

I'm a little wishy washy about my feelings towards Garces Trading Company. On my first visit, I was with my mom and our cousin and we ordered a cheese plate to enjoy with a bottle of wine we purchased there. The entire time, we felt pressured to either order more food or hurry up and get out so the table would be free for people who were planning to eat a meal. It was a Friday afternoon, hours after the lunch rush.    I've also had sandwiches and some take-home meal options and just wasn't really blown away by anything. I do love the concept and the beautiful, yet pricey, grocery area with fancy spreads, cheeses and meats. I would like to return sometime for a full meal and see how it goes. I've had their brunch prix fixe bookmarked for what feels like ages, but $12 bellinis make me hesitate.

Solid ice cream shop in the Marlton area. This place is close to my sister's house and serves a large assortment of homemade ice creams and frozen custard. I had mint chocolate chip with hot fudge and it was so big I could only eat about half. Prices were reasonable and I will definitely want to hit this place again the next time I am in the neighborhood.

Though I tend to gravitate towards local shops for bath and beauty products, I still think Lush is great. You can usually find one in any major city, which works when you need something in a pinch and prefer natural products. The packaging is fun and loud, and the names and descriptions are always creative.   I find employees to be a bit pushy sometimes, however, I had an easy in and out experience this week when I recycled some old containers for a brand new face mask - brazened honey. I can't wait to try it! Because the products are natural, they often have a shelf life (some have to be refrigerated!), which is understandable but can be preventative when it comes to committing to a full-sized purchase.   Finally, some of their bath bombs have left color behind on my tub. It's always removable, but that doesn't happen with the bombs from my local spot. Nonetheless, I'm still a fan and enjoy a lot of their products!

Square Pie is still bomb as ever. We arrived at 4pm on the dot to place a takeout order to bring to my brother's house for his birthday. We started a tradition of birthday pizza parties and, let me just tell you, it's proven to be a great decision.   We ordered a pepperoni pizza and spinach pizza, and a Caesar salad. But after chatting it over with the chef and hostess, I added a second salad which was smart. One would not have been enough for four people but two was just right. Their caesar is great!   The pizzas were perfection. I don't know how they make those giant, thick slices somehow feel light but the crust is flaky, flavorful and just amazing. The toppings are just right without going overboard. I had a slice of each pie which was the perfect amount. Can't wait for the next visit or takeout order!

This place is the jam. I've never been but my boyfriend has brought home the goods on several occasions. The chips are great and stay fresh for a long time. The salsas are awesome but the red one is hotter than the blazes of hell. So get the green which brings just a hint of heat if you're sensitive to that sort of thing.

I blame my self-loathing this morning on last night's adventure to Adsum, where, despite having just housed a burrito, I was still tempted enough to try the poutine. I ordered it without the foie gras, and still found it to be delicious. The fries were perfectly crispy and salty, the gravy was spot on, and the cheese curds were just starting to melt. Delish.  I washed it down with a Dogfish Head 60 Minute IPA, followed by an old fashioned, which was made to perfection.   The tunes that played in the background could have been from my own Pandora station, so I was definitely happy there. Beakers and test tubes behind the bar made my inner science geek absolutely giddy. I'd like to venture back sometime soon, when I have a legitimate hunger going. Then I'll really do some damage.

I had a great experience with this Canal's on Saturday. I was craving 21st Amendment's Hell or High Watermelon and wasn't sure where to find it by the case. Since I was in NJ, I gave Canal's a call and they not only had it in stock, but were willing to put a case aside for me as long as I planned to stop by that day. Since there were only two cases left, this was a great favor and made my life pretty easy. Not to mention, the case was around $32 before tax, which seemed really reasonable.  I walked up and down their beer aisles while there and was surprised at the great selection. Since this place is just a few miles from my parents' house, it's safe to say there will be plenty more visits in my future.

The Capogiro on Passyunk has a distinct vibe that differs from the other locations. The front is reminiscent of an old-fashioned ice cream shop, while the back seating area feels like a fancy living room in South Philly.   There didn't seem to be as many flavors to choose from at this location, and the gelato isn't displayed in the same tantalizing way as it is elsewhere.   Regardless, I'm always happy to have a Capogiro option around for when the mood strikes.

One thing I definitely didn't have while living in the burbs? Delivery sushi. And not just sushi that defaults to acceptable because it saves me a trip off the couch. Vic Sushi is pretty decent stuff.   I did think the fancy rolls were overpriced. Paying well over ten bucks because a roll involves two types of fish and some eel sauce does not justify that cost (although the rolls with mango intrigue). Next time, I'll go for one of the three roll dealies, which comes to a much more wallet-friendly $10.95.

The first time I sat down in Sassafras a few months ago, I thought I had stumbled upon Old City's answer to Chick's Café & Wine Bar.  I had been vaguely aware of the café's existence for years yet never thought to stop in.  I was instantly charmed by the tin ceilings, tiled floors and old-timey surroundings, including the bartenders, who were dressed in starchy whites with black ties.    The cocktail menu looked promising.  Absinthe, ROOT, and other interesting spirits were listed as ingredients.  After two or three visits, however, I've found the consistency of the drinks to be staggeringly different depending on the 'tender.  I've had great drinks at Sassafras but I've also had several disappointing ones.  I once ordered a bloody Mary, a featured drink on the menu, and the result was something akin to what I can mix myself on an airplane using only two ingredients.    All things considered, I still think this bar is one of the gems of Old City, and rumor has it that the food is pretty good, too.  I'll definitely return but I'll be choosy with my beverage selection.

You guys know what to expect at Panera. This one is clean, has all the things I need and in the right places and provides an acceptable quick meal when necessary.   When I ordered my bagel the other day, I asked for it to be toasted. The girl at the counter even said, "you wanted it toasted, right?" So that was two confirmations that I wanted that bagel toasted. Guess what wasn't toasted?   The moral of this story is, don't go asking for anything above and beyond the status quo at this Panera, and you should be satisfied.

I like Panera.  It's quick, convenient and tasty.    Unfortunately, many of the items are a caloric death trap, so I tend to stay away from the following 90% of the time: sandwiches, paninis, frozen/blended drinks, breakfast selections and bakery items.  If I'm hungover, it's a different story and I'll eat anything that isn't nailed down.  For the other days of the week, there are still some viable options that won't send you straight to diet hell.  Today, the chicken and rice soup with a hunk of multi-grain baguette made me a pretty happy girl.  It remains to be seen if this will actually get me through to dinner, or if I'll be gnawing my own arm off for survival at some point later in the day.  I'm going to go with 4 p.m. on the over/under.

I got my birthday brunch on at Green Eggs last week and I was a pretty happy camper. There were so many amazing-sounding things on the menu that I had a difficult time choosing just one. Since it was a special day, we went a little crazy and started the meal with a muffin topped with walnuts and crème anglaise that was featured that morning. It was delicious, and a perfectly sweet way to start our brunch.   When I saw two gigantic griddles of the "kitchen sink" delivered to a neighboring table, I almost changed my order. But I ultimately went with the breakfast burrito, with egg whites instead of whole eggs. Because you know, it's so much healthier that way.   Stuffed with eggs, potatoes, peppers and cheese and topped with black beans, pico, avocado and sour cream, it was one hefty burrito. I was so engrossed in my own meal that I barely glanced at my boyfriend's smoked salmon benedict.   Servers were all friendly and chatty, and the café had a really pleasant, comfortable feel. I have no idea why it has taken me so long to try this place, but it's sure to become a staple.

I'm way overdue on this review, but I was scrolling through businesses and was reminded of a really great day last summer that included Dahlak. My husband and I spent a beautiful summer day bouncing around the city with family, then we all went our separate ways and he and I ended up at Dahlak to smoke some shisha. We'd never been to the restaurant before, so it took some directions from the friendly staff for us to find our way past the dining room to the back bar area.   We posted up at the bar and I had a fresh juice while my husband had a beer. And some shisha, of course. There was an electronic jukebox and we quickly bonded with another couple over our music selections. It was just one of those perfect summer Sundays.   Dahlak is closed for renovations at the moment and I'm looking forward to checking those out once we can all get out to enjoy restaurants again.

A box of six of the most delicious sticky buns you ever did taste (with nuts or raisins - your choice!) will set you back only $5.50. That's less than a dollar per sweet, sticky, gooey bun!   The donuts and cakes also looked incredible but we were on a mission for buns only. I'd definitely make the trip to deep South Philly again for more sweet treats!

On a recent cold and rainy night, I decided to go the delivery route for dinner. Yellowtail was new to me, so I checked out the reviews which were fairly positive. The delivery fee is $1 but the minimum order is just $10 so this worked out well. I ordered the three roll combo for $10.95 and my delivery arrived well within the promised time of 30-45 minutes. Probably less than that, actually.   I ordered a tuna avocado roll, tuna cucumber roll and a California roll. I loved that the rolls weren't too weighed down with rice. Each bite was the perfect size and everything tasted great. I asked for extra wasabi and received enough for a family of four. I will definitely order from Yellowtail again.

Super cute dog and cat -stuffs. My sister and I swung by one afternoon and she was very impressed with the array of merchandise. Particularly the doggie outfits, which she is always buying for her own pup. She says he likes it.   They always have a cute pooch or two up for adoption, and seeing their little faces through the window on the street melts my heart every time (and I'm not even a "dog person").   Doggie Style also offers grooming services, but I've heard mixed reviews from friends who have taken their dogs there. But for pet necessities or even items for pet-lovers, this is a great spot.

When I went to this FedEx location to pick up a shipment my colleague re-routed for me, I happened to mention to the employee looking for my box that the shipment had just been re-routed the previous night. She immediately went into auto FedEx employee mode, reciting something about how re-routed packages never arrive the next day, blah blah blah, call 1-800 blah blah blah. My colleague had guaranteed that I would be able to pick up that shipment, but I knew I wasn't going to get anywhere trying to argue my case so I left and contacted my colleague for the scoop.   A few hours later, low and behold, my packages arrived! I was helped by another employee who was really friendly and who even offered to help me out with my packages. I declined because how else am I going to get the arms of a WWE Total Diva?   So all in all, not a total fail but certainly not my favorite customer service experience.

I enjoyed my meal at Luna, but I'm going with three stars which feels accurate of my experience overall. Our server was friendly and poured us waters as soon as we sat. I ordered the buffalo chicken salad with dressing on the side.   My salad arrived and was super tasty, but I did need some more buffalo sauce because I like things saucy. There was no avocado on the salad, which had been listed on the menu. So that was a bummer. My dining partner ordered a sandwich, which she later told me was really kind of boring. Mental note for next time.   No one really checked in with us after we got our food and I had to flag a server down for more water. Our check was dropped without an ask if we needed anything else. And, as others have mentioned, it's cash only.   Again, I liked my salad a lot so would get that again if I were to return. I wouldn't go out of my way, though.

I don't know, y'all. I know the 'Vous is a staple but I'm just not that into it. I swung by for a quick beverage on a recent Saturday because my guy was there with his friends. There are specials even on Saturday, which is cool, but High Life and the other beer they were featuring on tap just did not appeal. When my girl Aaliyah P arrived, we hung around for one very quick drink and were on our way.   On a positive note, I do remember good bar food from a previous visit. I wouldn't be opposed to swinging by sometime to check that out again, but it probably wouldn't be my own suggestion.

I've found my new Chinese takeout/delivery spot! We decided to try Dim Sum House the night before Christmas Eve, when we were in the thick of gift wrapping and recipe making. I was looking for comfort food and received it in abundance.   We started with scallion pancakes (always a must) and pork soup dumplings. The scallion pancakes were perfect. Sadly, the soup dumplings were oddly placed at the bottom of the bag in a styrofoam container, which resulted in most of the dumplings arriving crushed, as pictured. However, each dumpling was in its own tiny container, so the dumplings were still somewhat intact, if less soupy than desired.   Our entrees were general tso's and dry pepper chicken. Both were generous portions and each dish was great. My only complaint with the entrees is that we received only one side of white rice, when we definitely could have used two.   Overall, the food was delicious and we were happy despite the small flaws. Definitely ordering from Dim Sum House again next time I have a Chinese food craving!

Louie is the spot in St. Louis! I've been twice - once with a group for my best girl's bachelorette dinner and again last weekend with the same friend. We loved having Jordy as our server for the group dinner but our server on Saturday, Chloe, was also awesome!   Do not sleep on the small plates as they are all delicious! I can't remember all the details from our group dinner but I do know we basically ordered the entire small plates section. On Saturday, my friend and I narrowed down to the olives, hummus, and cauliflower. Still thinking about that cauliflower two days later. It's battered (and possibly lightly pickled prior to battering?) and served with an aioli. Increds.   Because we're carb monsters, we ordered two pizzas to share: the pomodoro fresco and broccolini, ricotta and lemon. Both were delicious! My only regret was eating all of the amazing fresh bread when we first sat down because we had no room for dessert.   Love this spot and can't wait to return on my next visit to St. Louis!

This restaurant is close to where I work and the only Thai place in town so I decided to give it a shot.  Last week, I ordered the chicken pad Thai to-go at lunch time.  The dish was all right but nothing to write home about.    Why I returned for seconds after not being impressed the first time, I'm not sure.  It was kind of like one of those first dates that go okay, but the cocktails make you think you enjoyed the evening more than you really did and you agree to go out again.  You then spend the whole second date wondering why you didn't trust your instincts while simultaneously planning your exit strategy.    Such was the same with my vegetable pad Thai at lunch today.  As soon as I took my first bite I knew I just wasn't that into it.  To its credit, the veggie pad Thai spared me from corny jokes and emergency phone calls to friends from the bathroom.  I suffered through the meal in silence and when it was over, I tossed the Thai Basil phone number into the nearest trash can.

As far as state stores go, this one's not too bad. It's super close to where I live and convenience is always a factor. Also, the employees at this particular store go out of their way to be friendly, which you know is not the case for all state stores if you've been to the one around 12th and Chestnut.   I do wish the refrigerated section extended beyond a few bottles of chardonnay, pinot grigio and cheap white zinfandel. If you want anything decent and you want it cold, make sure to purchase early and refrigerate yourself.

700.   The number of course makes me think of Veteran's Stadium, which makes me think of football, which makes me think of Philadelphia sports, which makes me think of hockey, which makes me think of hockey players, which makes me think of Race Street Cafe (Flyers players are rumored to hang there), which will now make me think of my 700th review! Full circle. Don't you love it?   Think that over for a second while I tell you what I most definitely love: Race Street Cafe's garden salad with buffalo chicken. Fresh mixed greens, shredded carrots, cherry tomatoes, blue cheese and two perfectly-crunchy strips of chicken in delectable wing sauce. Skip the standard balsamic dressing that comes with in exchange for homemade ranch, which had delightful flavors of fresh herbs.   Yelp-tern Allison's special salad of the day had beets, halved hard-boiled eggs, red onion and fried goat cheese. I'm not a beet lover, but if that salad didn't look good...    There were plenty of other things on the menu that I had ruled out in favor of the salad. I can't wait to go back again and again to tick them all off my list!

It's a good thing I don't work in the Comcast Center. I'd probably spend all my money at DiBruno and eat cheese and bread for lunch every day, rendering me into one of those people who wears the matching separates that barely pass as acceptable out-of-the-house clothes. You know the ones.  While I didn't peruse the cheese and charcuterie section on my short visit yesterday, I did have a bangin' iced coffee with a shot of chocolate syrup. Delish!

Hot dayamn I'm getting my culture on lately!   Last night, I hit the Academy of Music for some more Tchaikovsky action. This time, for The Pennsylvania Ballet's performance of Swan Lake. The performance itself was beautiful, and the orchestra was fantastic, melding seamlessly into the show.   The theater was pretty in a way I would imagine old-school theaters to be, although the areas outside reminded me of a grade school building. The hallways and bathrooms were just too sterile for a structure that holds such grand events.    Seats were tiny, and there were some sections with obstructed views because of columns. I was dangerously close to one of those seats, and I would not have been happy had I been seated there. Nonetheless, we still had a pretty good view even from our location up high.   I would definitely return for another ballet or musical, but I'd probably try to get seats on a lower level.

I returned to Race Street Cafe for brunch recently and was not disappointed. Service was friendly and there were quite a few brunch selections that sounded great. In the end, I went with the feta and spinach omelet, which came with tater tots, choice of breakfast meat and toast, and a side of fruit. Everything was delicious!   Tables are packed together pretty tightly and my chair was constantly bumping against the person seated behind me. It's a tight squeeze when all the tables are seated.  I was glad we decided to check out Race Street for brunch. I don't get there too often but am always happy with my experience.

I went to Severino in hopes of finding homemade soup.  Unfortunately, there was no soup to be found but that was only a minor setback once I saw the many different pastas and homemade sauces displayed.  The pastas come frozen or dried, depending on the type, and I believe everything is made on the premises.  Pasta in every shape and variety is available.  I settled on whole wheat fettuccine, which came in a nice sized bundle.    Picking a sauce was a bit trickier.  They had every flavor imaginable, either homemade in the freezers or in gourmet bottled varieties.  The homemade red clam sauce jumped out at me so I went with it.  Meanwhile, I practically needed a straitjacket to avoid throwing any of the cheeses, breads (focaccia!!!), crackers, dips (dirty martini dip?!?!?), olives or veggies on the counter along my otherwise healthy meal.    For $11, I had at least two nights worth of said pasta and sauce (which was DELISH, by the way), plus tons of leftover dry pasta for the next time I want to get all Italian with myself.  And speaking of the next time, I'm totally planning to break down and try that dirty martini dip!

Solid experience at this FedEx location today. I walked in and was instantly welcomed by at least one employee, and a manager came over to ask what I needed help with and directed me to the right place.   I had to overnight a document and the woman who helped me was friendly and thorough - she had me double check all of the info she entered for accuracy. I was in and out in a matter of minutes and that's worthy of five stars in my book!

Admittedly, South Square has not always been my favorite grocery store, however, I am definitely a fan of how they are handling safety and sanitation during the COVID-19 pandemic. From the very beginning, this store had a sanitation station set up outside for their shopping carts. Inside, there are wipes and also barriers between customers and employees at the check-out lines. These steps are greatly appreciated!   In addition, South Square was stocked on several household items that we haven't been able to find elsewhere for weeks. We were able to secure our preferred laundry detergent, along with a large container of Lysol wipes, among a handful of other items.   I also have to admit, when I can't find a basic household item at the newer nearby grocery store, I have almost always been able to track it down at South Square. They can be pricey, and I don't love all of the departments, but this neighborhood staple definitely serves a purpose.

We swung by GTC for a quick snack on Sunday afternoon. I really love the switch to a bar in exchange for the shopping area that previously occupied the left side of the restaurant. There are lots of interesting sounding cocktails and, of course, a very solid wine list.   There are two versions of Bloody Marys - one is fairly traditional and one is made with green tomatillos and garnished with cheese-stuffed olives and a pepper. In my opinion, the traditional bloody could use a bit of salt or worcestershire or a salted rim, but it was solid. The green BM was interesting and tasty but the standard red is still my preference.   We shared a bowl of pasta e fagioli and the house made mozzarella. Both were excellent and really hit the spot. Said mozz is available for just five bucks during the weekday happy hour which runs from 4-7. My fiancé and I were in agreement that we need to get back for that happy hour ASAP.

GTC has become one of my favorite dinner destinations. The menu is reasonable enough for a weeknight meal but also a great option for a weekend dinner with friends. You can BYO wine with no corkage fee, even though there is a full bar.   As far as the menu goes, the house specialty frites is always a great choice. The butcher's steak option comes with 7 ounces of delicious, perfectly cooked steak, topped with butter and served with a choice of three sauces. Duck fat fries come standard but I haven't had any problems subbing a salad instead. The salsa verde is basically a chimichurri sauce and it is perfection.     On my most recent visit, I opted for the trout almondine, which was incredible. I only wish that it was served with a side salad since it was basically just the fish, with a whole lot of fresh parsley on top. GTC should consider adding a section of sides since many of their entrees are served a la carte, like the trout.   Of the smaller plates, you can't go wrong with the house made mozzarella or the French onion soup. I look forward to my next visit!

I'm bummed to say that my second visit to Race Street Cafe was a bust. On Saturday of Memorial Day weekend, the bar was understaffed and overwhelmed. Our server was nice but clearly spread too thin between the many occupied tables in and outside. Our food took forever and drinks were almost as long.   The food was good for bar food but there was no reason why we should have waited as long as we did. Needless to say, I won't be recommending the place on a weekend though I'm sure I'll return for lunch sometime.

Delivery via Eat24 from Hummus Grill was solid. I ordered the grilled chicken platter with rice, cucumber and tomato salad, tabbouleh and hummus. It came with a side of wheat pita, as well as some delicious homemade hot sauce.   The delivery travel caused the ingredients in the container to shift around a bit, but nothing was spilling or too messy, which I appreciated.   I skipped the pita in an effort to keep the carb count down so no comments on that. The rest of the food was definitely enough for two filling meals. Though the chicken wasn't all white meat, which I prefer, it was completely boneless and had a really nice grilled taste. All other sides complemented the chicken nicely and tasted very fresh.   Hopefully meal two out of this order will taste just as good for lunch tomorrow. Glad to have another solid delivery spot that doesn't break the bank.

Update! It has been years since my last Sidecar review! Nearly four, to be exact. Meanwhile, Sidecar is my go-to neighborhood bar, I practically know the menu by heart, I have consistently great experiences with servers and bartenders there, they always play great music... the list goes on!   Something I'm really loving that they didn't have the last time I wrote a review is the addition of a few really nicely done cocktails. I've been drinking less beer and more wine and cocktails lately, and I absolutely love the raspberry cooler, with fresh raspberry iced tea, vodka, simple syrup and fresh lemon and mint. It's a simple drink that isn't overly sweet, which is just perfect for me.    The food is consistent, whether you go for brunch or dinner, and I love that the kitchen is open late. My go-tos are the pretzel chicken bites, carnitas, salads and, when I'm feeling extra splurge-y, the Super Mario burger. Delish. Anything on their brunch menu is a hit with me. Thanks for holding it down in the 'hood, Sidecar.

Just a reminder that Frangelli's is still the South Philly bakery you want, need and deserve. I picked up cannoli donuts and sticky buns for a recent tailgate party (this was a serious tailgate party!) and they were, of course, a huge hit. The donuts were so fresh and the sticky buns were just incredible. Their prices have increased since my last visit but still remain very affordable. Totally worth that deep South Philly drive and questionable park job for sure!

This PJ's is very close to where I grew up so it's probably the one I've been to most, although I prefer the Westmont/Haddonfield location.  Maple Shade PJ's has the same good bar food and beer specials, but the service is usually slower and not as accurate.  For example, while lunching with my sister today, I asked for my salad dressing on the side.  The salad came out with the dressing on top.  It was easy to push some aside so it wasn't a big deal (it was a wedge salad, just to give you a visual image).  Had the dressing been mixed in (chopped salad style), I would have gone a little Chuck Norris because a) I hate overly dressed salads and refuse to eat a plate of dressing with some lettuce and, b) sending it back would have only added more time to my already maxed out lunch break.     Now when you have me over for salad you know what not to do.

I want to love this place.  There are definitely things I love about it~ the guacamole, the black bean and salsa dip, the decor, the churro dessert... but the experience as a whole?  Eh.    It's hit or miss.  I've been there and have ordered things that came out perfect (quesadillas, fajitas, fish tacos); and I've been there and ordered things that sound awesome in theory (honey lime scallops, chicken mole, chicken and sweet potato burrito) and they just taste bland.  An average place gets an average 3 stars.  Also, don't be the last party in there... or the remaining uncut staff will give you the hairy eyeball and you'll be lucky if they don't start turning off the lights!

These four stars are for the happy hour, which is positively awesome, especially considering the location. A handful of us had plans to meet up at one of Rittenhouse's bar/restaurants, only to discover the place was closed for a private party. We scoured our brains to come up with an appropriate Plan B, and Alma de Cuba saved the day.  Happy hour runs every weeknight from 5-7 and features six dollar sangria and two types of mojitos. Small plates are half off, which is a total bargain. Everything ordered looked delish, though I only tried the toasted hazelnut guacamole since I had plans for dinner.   While I wasn't crazy about the sweet sangria, the traditional mojito did the trick. It was boozy but light; perfect for summer sipping. It had been years since my last trip to Alma de Cuba, but they are now on the short list of happy hour spots.

Our group stopped in Reds Bar for a quick beverage while making our way down the Pacific Coast Highway in November. First thoughts: Santa Barbara is a cool town! We all would like to go back sometime. First thoughts of Reds Bar: cute, and a little divey. I dig.   We were the first patrons to arrive and the only patrons during our brief stay.
