Despite this, service was pretty laid-back. We had to walk up to the bar to order our drinks and, even though there were only four, one of the drinks was incorrect. It was mine, of course, but I went with it and the drink I received was pretty tasty. Not sure how the low-key service would fare with a larger crowd but it was fine for just our little crew. That bathroom could probably use a scrub down, though.

This is a quickie review for anyone considering Tinto for Restaurant Week. I just returned from my dinner and both my friend and I were thrilled with the food, service and price of our meal.   The Restaurant Week menu is fairly expansive and very generous - we shared eight plates plus a dessert course which was just the right size, as we were stuffed by that point. Also, I'm not drinking this month, and our server said the bartender would be able to whip something up for me. I had an alcohol-free sangria which was light and fun. Having a mocktail option really helps me get past the no-wine-for-me sads at the beginning of the meal.   Another thing that I should mention is that the pacing was perfect. We were not rushed at all and spent a leisurely two hours at dinner. If you're considering Tinto for Restaurant Week, or anytime really, just make your reservation already!

After reading Marcello D.'s very solid review of Tony's, I swung by one day last week while running errands on my lunch break.    The door was held open for me by a friendly gentleman on his way out, and I entered to hear the husband and wife duo behind the counter speaking to each other in Italian.  Swoon!  I ordered two slices to go, one plain and one veggie.  Fifteen minutes later I was back at my desk, inhaling the pizza as fast as humanly possible.  The slices were nicely sized and with a thin crust.  The toppings on the veggie pizza made me feel downright healthy about my lunch choice.  I felt like I gave into my pizza craving without going way overboard in the calorie department.  Whether or not that was true... is irrelevant at this point.  I have had better pizza, but for a quick takeout slice, Tony's wasn't a bad option.  I'll check them out again sometime soon.

Excellent experience at this Square One location this morning! I love the 13th Street shop and was surprised to discover that there is another right on JFK Blvd. The aesthetic is similar - it's a really attractive coffee shop with clear signage and nice people.   There isn't as much seating in this shop as there is on 13th Street, but I was able to grab a couple chairs at a community table, which served my purposes well since I had multiple meetings.   I'm battling a winter cold which is making me feel groggy and tired, so I really needed a pick-me-up upon arrival. Their Americano comes with four shots of espresso and you'd better believe that woke me up. The barista was super friendly and very enjoyable to chat with; he recommended that I try one of the immune booster shots that they carry in their cold case. I selected the one with turmeric, vitamin C and some other ish I can't remember. The taste wasn't super pleasant but I'm down to try anything if it will help kick this cold.   Definitely putting this Square One into the meetings rotation.

Why does Collingswood get all the cool things AFTER I move? Luckily, my sister now lives in the area so I get to visit my old stomping grounds on the reg. And Devil's Creek Brewery, conveniently located in the middle of town in the Lumberyard complex, is going to be a regular stop.   The tasting room was packed on Friday night and we even ran into friends from the city when we walked in. This place is definitely a destination. Laws prevent the brewery from serving food but you can BYO or order delivery if you're so inclined.   I really enjoyed the pilsner and also the IPA on nitro (Nitro Man). There were six or seven beers of different styles, so most likely something for everyone. The business owners and other staff were all super fun and nice and we had a great time socializing. I look forward to many more visits!

One of my close friends introduced me to Cherry St. Tavern because her fiance lives around the corner and it's their go-to spot for beer in a laid-back environment.  Something about the place reminds me of my grandparents' basement, but in a good way.  It's just a comfortable place to be.    Pitchers are available, food is basic but pretty darn good (especially while trying to soak up the alcohol), there's a juke box filled with classics and last but not least, there is a super cute bartender.  What else could a girl need?

My mom had discounted tickets for the Philly Sightseeing Tour so we took my grandmom out for a day of sightseeing. This tour can really be made or broken by the tour guide. For the first half of our day (start point at The Bourse to the Art Museum), our guide mumbled and wasn't very enthusiastic.   We decided to walk around the Art Museum for a bit, so by the time we got back on the bus, we had a new tour guide. He was friendly, enthusiastic and knew a lot about the city. I was a bit disappointed that he promoted Pat's and Geno's, however. There was one other local on the bus as well and we sort of gave each other the eye like, "Really? Really?!" Friends, there are far better cheesesteaks out there!   While I didn't learn anything new about the city, from a local's point of view, I thought the tour did a very nice job showcasing Philadelphia to visitors.

I loved my weekday brunch at The Dutch. Everything from the food to service was great. The interior is nice but there are also several tables outside, which is where we decided to dine.   The menu is short and sweet but very well-rounded. I loved that there were several options for breakfast meats. I ordered the eggs, meat, bread, potato plate and asked to sub a side salad for bread, which was not a problem. I selected the turkey bacon as my meat and it had great flavor. I loved the seasoned potatoes as well. My dining companion had the banana pancakes which looked heavenly.   Our servers kept our coffee and water glasses full and were very sweet. Great experience and I'm looking forward to my next visit.

My husband and I were in the mood for something different over the weekend so we decided to treat ourselves to delivery from Oyster House. Two entrees, plus all the associated delivery fees, came close to $70, but we enjoyed our entrees and were happy to have a night off from cooking.   I had the pan roasted flounder with broccoli, chickpeas and tahini. I wasn't crazy about the tahini and would likely ask for that on the side next time. The fish was cooked perfectly, however, and the dish was overall a nice, healthy meal. My husband had the fisherman's stew which had great flavor.   I'd love if Oyster House offered some healthy sides like roasted vegetables or baked potatoes. We weren't feeling fries or salads so we ended up making a side at home to complement our entrees. Solid experience overall, though, and we'd definitely order from them again!

Of all the Philly Fine Wine & Good Spirits stores, this one is definitely up there among the nicest and most organized. Occasionally I have had some luck with getting decent recommendations from staff members, but more often than not I have to do some iphone research from the aisles.   The woman who was sampling wines from CA on my recent visit was knowledgeable not just about the wines she was pouring but also other wines in the store. The cashiers are fast and friendly.   It's still not as good as the stores in New Jersey but it's an improvement over other FW&GS locations.

Love, love, love this gelato and coffee shop! I was headed to West Chester to host an event and decided to get there a couple hours early to beat any rush hour traffic. I had some studying to catch up on for my French class so I needed a quiet spot with wifi and great coffee. Gemelli came up in a Yelp search and it proved to be the perfect spot.   The gelato and desserts looked amazing. It was all I could do to not order something splurge-y and call it a day. Instead, I ordered a latte with fresh whipped cream. I also tried a sample of the cannoli gelato which was heaven. I immediately texted my sister to say I'd be willing to drive to West Chester anytime so she could visit her old college stomping grounds... and get gelato.   I'm sure this cafe gets packed with families and college kids in the evening, but it provided the perfect, quiet place for me to hunker down and crack the books during the afternoon. Can't wait to return for that amazing gelato!

Met a friend for lunch at Soup Kitchen and enjoyed my experience. The space was larger than expected, with plenty of tables for what is probably a light lunch crowd, given the less-busy neighborhood. While I'd love to try the meatloaf sandwich sometime, both of us opted for the shakshuka. It's basically a vegetarian chili with two over easy eggs and some feta cheese. It's spicy and delicious, served with a piece of toasted French bread.   Service was really relaxed; we had to sort of grab someone from time to time if we needed anything, but it wasn't a big deal. I will definitely come back sometime... and I may even go out of my way for another bowl of that shakshuka!

Although I've never set foot in the store, I have been the lucky recipient of some gifts from Duross & Langel. I am a huge fan of bubble baths, and while there is indeed a time and place for Mr. Bubble, a girl likes to luxuriate every now and again. D&L's vanilla bubble bath has a pleasant scent without overpowering. Just a tiny teaspoonful was more than enough to produce tons-o-suds once I turned on the jets in my tub. Best of all, after soaking for over a half hour, my skin didn't feel the least bit dry.  Also in my arsenal is a container of brand new lavender-scented relaxation bathing salts that will undoubtedly leave my bathroom smelling like a Rittenhouse day spa. Serenity is mine!

Yesterday, I attended the annual oyster shucking competition at Oyster House, where professionals and amateurs battle it out to see who can schuck the best.   The five dollar cover charge to watch the competition was completely tacky. Yes, oysters were passed around to guests after they were shucked, but they were donated to begin with. The bar was full and mostly everyone had a drink in hand; money was being made. So that's how I felt about that.  Otherwise, the crowd was great, the event was a good time, and the bloody Marys were on-point.

Since my first visit to Farmers' Cabinet last week, I've already been back twice. This review is regarding my experience at the bar only, since I've yet to eat there. When Phoebe is on the roster, you know you're in good hands. I've sampled several of the cocktails, including the beer-inspired selections, and there really is something for everyone on the list. Well, except for that guy who foolishly asked for a bloody Mary the other night. Maybe not him.   Bar snacks make a triumphant and interesting return in the form of sometimes sweet, sometimes spicy (sometimes a little of both!) popcorn and roasted barley. My digestive system thanks Farmers' Cabinet for the unexpected fiber supplement with my liquor.  The old-timey decor is stellar, and I've noticed more and more people dressing the part of Prohibition-era rebels. Best of all, though, is the band, Drew Nugent and the Midnight Society. The dapper outfits, the old-school microphone, the horns and the lead singer's Eddie Cantor-like vocals are just perfect. Even a song called "My girl's p***y" had people grinning ear to ear and singing along during a Friday night performance.   I adore this place.

Hello, new favorite food truck! I was pumped to learn of the Fry Truck's existence and its appearance at the Wheat Beer Fest in Point Breeze was serendipitous. The menu is quite extensive - several types of fry options, loads of different topping combinations - these guys thought of everything!  In the end, we decided to try the waffle fries, Vicki N' Pete style, which came with Old Bay and melted American cheese. As we waited for the order, I helped myself to a large cup of ketchup and lots of napkins from the counter.   The serving size of our order of fries was enormous! The spuds were perfectly cooked and very tasty. They were possibly a little too salty which only caused my beer to go down faster (festival problems). Later, I had a bite from a friend's order which had waffle fries (no added seasoning) and steak, and they were awesome, too. Can't wait to bump into this truck at another festival soon!

My husband and I were in the area (I recently discovered Suburban Square and let's just say I'm obsessed) and looking for something new-to-us for dinner. Biga popped up on a search for pizza and had great reviews, so the decision was easy!   We were greeted warmly by the hostesses and seated. I loved the interesting non-alcoholic beverage options and ordered a grapefruit concoction called nautical nonsense, which was reminiscent of a paloma. It was refreshing and a great cocktail substitute.   We started with the farro salad which was super tasty. I don't think my husband has ever been so into kale! Next, we shared a classic margherita and da bomb, with soppressata and chilis. The latter packed a punch in both flavor and heat. We loved both pies and they were sizable enough to enjoy several slices from each and still take a few home.   Great experience all around and I will definitely think of Biga again next time I'm in the area!

Machi Sushi is one of the few sushi restaurants that delivers during the afternoon on a weekday, so I gave it a whirl. There is a delivery minimum (but no delivery charge), and the three roll combo didn't get me there so I added on a seaweed salad. With tip, this made my lunch a little on the pricy side at $20, but it was worth it.   The delivery arrived quickly, and the sushi rolls were pretty good and just how I requested. I had a shrimp tempura roll, a spicy tuna roll and a regular tuna roll with crunchy flakes added. There were eight small-sized pieces to each roll, and I was happy with the portion size. The seaweed salad was average if a little too oily. I had a few bites but mostly stuck to the rolls. I'll probably opt for a house salad or soup to get to that minimum next time.

My mom and I got into a little happy hour action at Harvest a couple weeks ago and it was a pretty solid experience overall. The bar area is bright and sunny and the bar is quite large, with lots of tables around as well.   The happy hour deals are pretty sweet, but the best bang for your buck is in the food offerings. Flatbreads are large and offered for just five bucks. They are much more substantial than the flatbreads at a similar restaurant chain and a lot tastier, too.   The happy hour wines were a steal but the wines themselves were not great. My mom and I both switched to full price glasses after our first round. All in all, it was an inexpensive night out and I always love having healthier alternatives to happy hour snacks.

A full upgrade to five stars is long overdue for this Philly staple. I've been back time and again and, while most visits are for drinks only, I have a great time every time. Last Saturday night we stopped in twice, for pre-dinner and post-dinner drinks. Their earl grey hot toddy is perfect for a chilly night, and the wine list has something for everyone and at reasonable price points to boot. Bartenders are friendly. The music selection is always a fun mix - loved the 70s disco jams on our recent visit!   My previous review nearly nine years ago reflects the opinions of a different, must less mature person. I'm older now, I'm wiser now.

Davio's Galleria is one of the few (if not the only) coffee shops around the KOP Town Center. It's big and roomy, quiet, never crowded (I often go at random times, like mid-late afternoon), has free wifi, big tables and access to outlets. What more could a girl ask for?   Coffee. They have it.   Food. They have that, too, but they are often out of ingredients. Again, I usually pop in later in the day, so it's probably on me if certain items aren't available any longer.   I love this place for what it is and have always had a good experience.

I've recently found myself popping into Lucky more and more whenever I'm in the area. The employees at the Walnut Street location are always very friendly and helpful, which makes shopping more enjoyable. Also, they run some amazing sales! It's pretty unlikely that I will swing in and not find something to purchase. While I haven't tried their jeans in a while, the sales have been enticing me to check them out. To be continued!

Every time we decide to order Chinese, we end up spending loads of time on research, because we simply haven't come across a go-to place. Usually, one of us will enjoy their food while the other thinks theirs is just all right. Spicy Memory may have changed the game on Saturday night.  We ordered a quart of wonton soup ($8.95), a scallion pancake ($4.50) and two chicken entrees (general tso's and garlic sauce, $14.95/each). I included prices here because I do think Spicy Memory is more expensive than its competitors. However, I felt the quality was better, as was the quantity. The soup was delicious and came with 10 dumplings. Both containers of chicken were loaded and provided us with plenty of food for a second meal.   Spicy Memory, you have my attention! This is definitely my spot the next time I'm craving Chinese.

I'm so happy to see Occasionette growing with a Collingswood location! I frequent the East Passyunk shop, but my sister lives about three blocks away from the new location, so I've already stopped in a handful of times over the past month or so. Every single time, I end up with a card, gift for a friend or family member, or little present for myself. I absolutely love this store and the interesting selection!   From tea towels to candles to kitchen gadgets to spices (my husband and I are fans of the popcorn enhancers, and my sister loved the spiced wine/cider kit I tossed into her birthday gift) to jewelry to adorable cards and more, I could just go cray cray at this place (and often do). Best of all, prices are very reasonable!   Please support this amazing local shop - you'll be a fan for life just like me!

Garage lived up to its name in that it was about as hot as a garage during our visit last Saturday. It was truly sweltering. Not sure if the AC just isn't up to snuff with the size of the place, but eventually, they gave up and opened the large garage door in front. That was when we decided to move on.   But aside from the heat, I did like the place. The can selection is pretty sizable, though they did run out of my beer of choice during my visit. There are a lot of fun arcade-style games. And the bathrooms are nice and clean. The acoustics are very loud. Put money in the juke and you won't hear your songs unless you listen very closely. A bunch of people had BYO food from nearby restaurants; not sure if that policy will continue after the built-in food truck is running, but I thought it was cool nonetheless. I think I'll probably prefer Garage in the cooler months, and it's definitely a good place for groups.

This Michaels is my go-to spot whenever I need something crafty for work or life. Most recently, I hit them up for wedding supplies. I was very impressed by the range in products. I always thought of Michael's strictly for craft supplies but found entire sections of wedding necessities, including a really nice variety of bulk thank you cards.   My mom always tells me you should never buy anything at Michael's without a coupon, and she's right. All you have to do is go to their website to see their weekly coupons, and you can present them at the counter right on your phone. I had a 50% off any item coupon that I used on a box of thank you cards. My husband was in line behind me with box number two, and as he tried to pull the coupon up on his phone, the employee helping me out said he could just use the coupon that was already on my phone - excellent!   I'd rather drive across state lines to visit this store than visit the AC Moore in South Philly. It is worth the trip!

This particular Lulu location was smaller than some that I've been to, but they had a nice selection of merchandise. The ladies who were working at the changing rooms were super nice and helpful.   I ended up with a cute pair of running shorts which made their debut yesterday. They were comfortable through my run and stayed put the entire time. There's nothing worse than clothing getting in the way of a workout. That's something I never have to worry about with Lululemon's apparel. My friend got some really adorable pants that I keep thinking I may need to buy for myself. If only they had sales!

We attended a wedding at HollyHedge Estate on Saturday and it was absolutely beautiful. The estate is laid back a bit from the street, and there are several different structures on the property.   The ceremony was held outside on a very nice patio. Immediately following was a cocktail hour on the same patio. I've never seen staff move so quickly to transform a space!   The reception took place in a space that had a warm and cozy feel, but that still managed to fit somewhere in the neighborhood of 180 - 200 people, with a smallish dance floor.   The food was definitely above average compared with most weddings, and the bartenders were great. I would definitely recommend HollyHedge as a great place to host a special event.

I stopped in Society Hill Society with my partner in crime Aaliyah P on a sunny Sunday afternoon.   First off, love what you did with the place, SHS! There's still a great rustic vibe but the space has gotten a lot cozier. This bar is the ideal setting for a chilly fall or winter night.   We were only in for one quick drink and we both opted for The Mind-Killer, which involved a brûlée torch to finish it off. Fancy! Said cocktail was fun and tasty and pretty to boot!  Looking forward to my next visit and trying some of the food menu!

Everyone in my family refers to this place as "The Bread Basket," which I believe was the original name.  I'm not sure when they changed their moniker to the oh-so-creative "Bread and Bagels."   Despite the identity crisis, the little shop has been churning out the same delicious breads for years.  They have several varieties, but the pepperoni bread remains the favorite at our family gatherings.  It is especially delish when heated in the oven for a little crunch, and served with marinara.  Yum.  In addition to the stuffed breads, they also have, you guessed it, bagels!  Never had one but they look and smell delicious, as do all of their other baked goods, which include: pastries, muffins, gargantuan cupcakes, etc.  Prices are low ($6 for a loaf of pepperoni bread) and they always seem to be open whenever I need to pick something up last-minute before a party.

Upgrade! It was after 9pm and I was in the area and craving some Vietnamese takeout. Vietnam Palace still had some people dining inside, though they looked to be at the end of their night. Thankfully, the gentleman who was managing the restaurant (he may have been the owner), said that I could still place an order.   I was craving comfort food and really wanted to try a Vietnamese soup. The manager/owner recommended the beef soup which sounded good to me. Since I only had a credit card and the limit was $15, I also ordered the lemongrass shrimp entree for the following day.   I took a somewhat spastic Uber ride home but my eats were packaged up well with no spillage. The soup was indeed comforting and delicious, and enough for two light meals. The lemongrass shrimp entree was also great and enough for two small meals.   After re-reading my former review, I see that I enjoyed some lychee martinis here back in the day. I'm going to have to dine in next time. Lychee me!

Per usual, it was the eleventh hour before leaving for vacation and I still needed a pair of heels, a manicure and an eyebrow wax. I found the desired heels in record time and dashed to Nail Trix, the only nail salon in the entire mall, with about 45 minutes to closing time.   There were two employees and one was just finishing with another customer so she was ready for me when I selected my color. When I asked to have my nails trimmed, she clipped them so fast I was a little afraid she would accidentally get my nail bed, too. She flew through the manicure in record time, and I tried to remind myself that you get what you pay for and it was my own fault for waiting until the last minute. Not even 48 hours later, most of my nails are starting to chip. Glad I picked a light color.  The eyebrow wax, also quite fast, got the job done although I had to do a little extra plucking at home. I'd say two stars is actually pretty generous, all things considered. Next time, I will definitely plan ahead and go to a nicer salon.

I love Thai Square so much and am so happy they are open again for delivery and takeout. This is one of our favorite neighborhood businesses, but we also think it's some of the best Thai the city has to offer.   I almost always start my meal with the tom yum soup, which is vibrant, flavorful, and just the right punch of spicy (when you order mild or medium). Other starters we like are the golden spring rolls and chicken skewers with peanut sauce.   As for entrees, I've liked everything I've tried but the crabmeat pad thai has become a favorite, along with the pad kra pow with shrimp.   The restaurant is small but really cute and we've enjoyed dinner there with a bottle of wine on a few occasions. That said, our go-to is delivery and it's always fast and accurate.

Perhaps Dolce Carini's pizza is decent (according to my fellow Yelpers), but their wraps are not. I ordered delivery via Eat24 yesterday, and I can honestly say it was my first bad experience with that service and one of their participating restaurants. First off, someone called me to ask my address (which you confirm at the time of ordering) because the delivery guy was lost. I live on a corner in a pretty easy-to-navigate neighborhood so I don't know what the problem was. I had to wait by the door for over ten minutes as I took calls from this guy while attempting to navigate him closer to my place.   So the food arrives, and my turkey club wrap is just falling apart. It looked like the wrap was placed down, the ingredients were put inside, and the sides of the wrap folded over. The under-side was wet. I literally had to get a plate and deconstruct and then reconstruct the wrap. Doing so enabled me to remove most of the turkey, which was low-quality deli slices. Sorry to say, but that was my first and last experience with Dolce Carini.

I love Occasionette! I make it a point to make this adorable store one of my first stops every year before Christmas. It's where I find all of my husband's stocking stuffers, plus a few unique and local gifts for friends.   I was thrilled to see Sugarfina's rosé gummy bears in stock - those things were sold out with waitlists for months when they came out over the summer! My husband was stoked that I had tracked them down (#brosé #summerofbrosé).   While at the store I also bought myself the most amazing, wood wick candle called Christmas Past. At $18 this was definitely a splurge but the scent is incredible and I love the crackle sound the wick makes (#basic).   This is by far one of the best local shops for gifts in Philly.

I'm trying to think of something nice to say... At least there's a parking lot?   The woman who called and left a message about my package repeated the info three times, which I liked. Okay, so we'll go with two stars for said woman and the parking lot. The customer service I received during my brief visit was non-existent. I asked two or three questions and each was met with the same "I dunno" from the dimwitted, robotic employee.   Lesson learned: dealing with the Philly UPS employees in person is just as frustrating as when you have to call and wade your way through the automated prompts.

Three dollars for an ice pop seems a little steep. But I guess when you compare that to, say, the desserts at Franklin Fountain or Capogiro, it's a bargain. Though I do enjoy those other two quite a bit more. Perhaps I'm comparing apples to oranges?   Nonetheless, this shop is adorable, with their popsicle puzzle toys for kids, bright colors and mini trays for serving the pops. There is an extensive list of pops containing dairy or not, and all of the flavors are interesting combinations. I went with a pineapple basil which was very nice for a hot summer night.

Picking up tickets to yesterday's afternoon showing of The King's Speech left me, well, speechless. A pair of tickets were more expensive at this mall theater than at the Ritz in Old City!   Also more expensive were the concessions. A small soda (oddly enough, the same size as a small kiddie pool) cost $4.50. I realize there is a huge mark-up on food and drink at the movies, but I could get four or five 2 liters for that price!   The saving grace was the theater itself. The room was clean, floors didn't seem sticky and the quality of the film seemed flawless to my eye. This spot is miles above Loews in Cherry Hill, but not quite Voorhees status.

My husband and I have been talking about grabbing roast beef sandwiches at Cherry Street Tavern for the longest time, and we finally made it over on Sunday night with a friend. We started with a plate of nachos which didn't stand a chance. The 'chos were super basic - hearty round chips out of the bag with some cheese sauce, chili, sour cream and pickled jalapeños. They were simple yet hit the spot, which led to a lengthy conversation about the bastardization of nachos in recent times. Really enlightening stuff.   Next up were our roast beef sandwiches, which you can top with American, Swiss or Provolone. For .50 more, top your 'wich with sharp provolone and a side of hot peppers. Washed down with a couple beers, this meal hit the spot. The bartender was a friendly gent who both wrangled drinks and put together meals for everyone in the place. My next craving for a hot roast beef sandwich will have me heading straight to Cherry Street.

A boozy brunch is the perfect way to kick off a Saturday, if you ask me. And The Scottish Arms does it right, with a make-your-own Bloody Mary bar complete with several types of mixers, hot sauces and other add-ins.   Their brunch menu is filled with hearty options, and my Seamus MacBenedict (available with ham instead of salmon, if you choose) was delicious. My only little gripe, and this seems to happen often when it comes to eggs benedict, was that the egg white was not fully cooked. No worries, because I had a lovely little cast iron pot of home fries which were on point.  The French press coffee was smooth and our service was lovely. This is the kind of pub where I could easily pass a day (or night) hanging out.

These five stars go out to DiBartolo Bakery's chocolate-frosted, cream-filled donuts, with a special shout-out to the intoxicating aroma that wafts out of the corner building and into the neighborhood.  I can't speak for any of the cakes, cookies or other pastries in the store, though they are all beautiful.  When I walk into Dibartolo, there's only one thing I'm after.

Vietnam Cafe was a last minute dinner destination after spending Sunday afternoon in West Philly. My husband and I arrived feeling pretty hungry so we started off with two apps: veggie fried spring rolls and shrimp papaya salad. We also ordered the coconut drink and the Vietnamese limeade. Both were delicious but the coconut drink was extra refreshing and complementary with the food.   The starters were really great. The spring rolls were hot and perfectly crunchy while the papaya salad was light but full of flavor. These went together really well.   For mains, I tried the Mongolian beef while my husband had the lemongrass chicken. The flavors in each dish were really complex and intense. My only suggestion for the beef dish would be for the chefs to cut the meat into smaller, bite-sized pieces. Also, the servings were large enough to bring home leftovers for dinner the next night.   I can easily see this review getting upgraded to five stars if future visits continue to impress. I'll definitely try to get back sooner than later!

Yeah... no. The first thing I noticed upon arrival to Tootsie's Orchid Lounge, airport version, was the distinct and slightly unpleasant smell. The second thing I noticed upon sitting at the bar was the disgustingly dirty floor. Why did we stay? I guess the live music had something to do with it. That was the only redeeming quality about this place.   It's a shame that a place as iconic as Tootsie's would put their name on this extremely sub-par restaurant, even if it is in an airport. The rest of the airport seemed very clean and well-kept, so I'm not sure why the ball was so majorly dropped here.   Service was extremely slow and you really had to speak up to get someone's attention. The food was pretty awful. I also witnessed a bartender pouring a drink with one of those liquor measuring devices, but he would pull the bottle away before the pour was complete which amounted to spilled liquor around the drink. I would veer towards fast food or eating before the airport when given the choice again.

Very solid first experience with BLO/OUT! My hair was just two days from my regular cut and color, but I had an event to attend plus my anniversary dinner, so decided to treat myself to a blowout to ensure a good hair day. I booked my blowout, and added on a ten minute scalp massage, online.   As luck would have it, I was paired up with Alessandra, who was amazing. I don't feel like I gave very good direction on what I wanted and yet she read my mind anyway and worked out a look that was bouncy and fun. The scalp massage was relaxing and just what I needed.   I have been spoiled by my regular salon with super comfortable hair washing stations, and I found the stations at BLO/OUT to be a bit hard on the neck. I also thought the salon could use a little bit of an update, but I read in another review that this might be currently happening, so I'm interested to see how it goes. I'd be happy to see Alessandra again and will book with her for my next visit!

I checked out Acme Feed & Seed last year on a hardhat tour when construction was still underway. I couldn't wait to return on my next visit to see the finished product, and that's exactly what I did with a couple other ladies on the last day of my bachelorette trip.   On a Sunday afternoon, Acme was surprisingly not very busy. There seemed to be plenty of tables available for brunch with live music. The band was more jazz and blues than country, which was a nice change from everything else on Broadway.   The second floor has more of a lounge vibe, while the third floor is for private events. We ended up spending most of our time on the roofdeck, which had amazing views of the city plus a stellar DJ. Shoot for a shaded seat if you can because it gets super hot in the sun. A couple misting machines were placed around the deck and the occasional misty breeze was a welcome respite from the sun's rays. Moscow mules were my drink of choice and they were excellently made. I look forward to returning for more good vibes on my next visit.

I'm with Lia B - Thai Square is definitely the best and most affordable Thai in the Graduate Hospital area. Not only is it a cute, BYO restaurant right in the neighborhood, but they also have delivery for those nights when you just don't feel like leaving the house.   I've tried a lot of the menu at this point, and favorites are the vegetable spring rolls, curry chicken dumplings, chicken skewers, coconut shrimp, curry entrees, shrimp pad Thai and tom yum soup. Actually, I don't think I've had anything I didn't like from Thai Square. Also, their spice levels mean business. I generally order medium which can occasionally be almost a little too hot for me (in a good way - please don't change this, Thai Square!).   The folks who own the place are very friendly, and I'm happy to have such a solid spot so close to home.

My main squeeze surprised me with a bouquet of flowers last Wednesday, and that same bouquet is still rockin' out with its blossoms out a full week later. The flowers were wrapped nicely in paper with a straw bow, which matched the theme of the fall blooms inside.   While not a huge fan of lilies myself (I find their fragrance to be a little overpowering), anyone who does enjoy them will absolutely love the selection from Flowers & Company. They are gargantuan! Truly, I've never seen a flower so big, and especially not in a home arrangement. Give this place a shot the next time you are looking to brighten someone's day!

So glad I came across The Quick Fixx during my Yelp search for delivery on Friday night, when I was looking for something hot, healthy, and reasonably-priced. It's worth noting that The Quick Fixx has no delivery fee and only a ten dollar minimum. That's a better deal than all my other regular delivery spots.   The create-your-own option is legit. I went with whole wheat penne, broccoli, fresh mozzarella and tomato garlic sauce. And guess what? There's now a side salad option! So I got myself a side salad with lemon vinaigrette because I'm a baller like that. The total was $14 plus tip.   Imagine my surprise when my doorbell rang and I was greeted by the owner himself, Matt. This is a guy who really cares about his business, his customers and the neighborhood.   Dinner was bangin' and exactly what I wanted. I even had leftovers for lunch the next day. After perusing the website and finding out about their "Ten Spot" lunch menu, I'll be hitting those up in the near future as well.

Very cute coffee and specialty candy and gift shop in Lambertville. My husband and I stopped in for a cup of something warm on a cold night. I noticed the delicious-sounding hot chocolate sign which mentioned several spices. It sounded wonderful but I opted for a mocha latte since I was looking for some caffeine.   Our drinks were prepared and we sat at the stools by the window. My drink was absolutely delicious, but it definitely was not a mocha latte. I'm fairly certain I actually got a cup of the hot chocolate afterall, based on the description I read and the flavors I tasted. It was great, just not what I ordered. Regardless, cute spot and I would return!

Five.   Five dollar.   Five dollar footloooonnnngs!!!!   Not only is Subway convenient and diet-friendly, it's also cheap! I go through stages where I'll get a foot-long and eat half for lunch and half for dinner all week. Please tell me where else you can get two meals for $5.35 (including tax)?!   This location is great because it is conveniently located near both my office and apartment. The restaurant is always clean and the employees are friendly. In other words, they never make me feel awkward about loading my turkey and cheese with lettuce, tomatoes, onions, black olives, green peppers, sweet peppers, banana peppers, pickles and red wine vinaigrette.  I probably owe them money by the time I leave...

They definitely have the "quick" part down. Our order was delivered in about twenty minutes on a Saturday night. But as for the "fixx," I'm sort of in need of another, and I finished dinner only a half hour ago. What I mean is, the portion sizes are small. That's not to say that they aren't perfectly fine. In fact, if you're on a diet or you just like single-serving portions, this is actually a great option so you won't go crazy and eat five times the amount of pasta you should eat.   My boyfriend had the cheese ravioli with spicy red sauce, while I had a makeshift Caesar with romaine, tomatoes, grilled chicken and Caesar dressing on the side. I requested croutons, but only received two slices of grilled baguette. Not sure if that was supposed to be the actual croutons or what, but either way, I'd prefer regular croutons. Know what I mean?   Our food was tasty for sure, but for $18, we were left looking at each other and asking "what's next?" I'll definitely give them another shot but if I've got a full appetite I'll probably need salad AND pasta.

Welcome to the neighborhood, Green Aisle! I must say, I was super excited when I heard news that Green Aisle would be occupying the former Betty's Speakeasy (and short-lived ¡Juice!) space. What I didn't factor in was the additional hit to my checking account. It's true, items at this grocery are at a premium, but that's because they're of the highest quality. Specialty items are just that - special. Ya dig?   Owners Adam and Andrew are some of my favorite Philadelphians. They embody all that is great about small, local businesses - friendly service, an interest in the neighborhood and its residents, and a true passion for their products.   From homemade butterscotch sauce from Brooklyn (the best ice cream topper I have ever had outside of an old fashioned ice cream shop), to house-made pickles and preserves, to the fabulous array of cocktail accoutrements, Green Aisle has every last thing on your pantry wish list. They also have hand-dipped ice cream!

What a cute, deceivingly large, market! I ran into Sassafras for a hot second before Thursday night's Elite Event to grab some ice and was shocked at the spread in what I thought would be a tiny corner store. The place was clean, well-stocked and had a friendly staff. I wish I had a cute market like this in my neck of the woods.   Ten dollar credit card limit but you probably aren't spending less than that in a market anyway.  Also, since this is neither 100% gourmet market or grocery store, I'm going to tow the line and list it in both.

From our first visits to Frida Cantina for watching Eagles games with friends at the bar, to our recent deliveries during Covid, we remain big fans!   Delivery is always a solid experience and everything is packaged well. I've been digging the al pastor tacos and we almost always get an order of guac and chips, which is pretty substantial. The restaurant always throws in some homemade salsas - the green salsa is absolutely delicious!

I'm shocked at the bad reviews for Terminal F, which is easily my favorite terminal to fly out of at PHL. I get super excited when I find out my flight is leaving from Terminal F. The dining options and brighter space are worlds better than the other terminals.   If you're getting dropped off, you don't have to go through the main terminals and take the shuttle to F - you can just get dropped off right at F! Just check your gate before you get to the airport. It is that easy.   As for the food, I'm partial to Local, the sit-down restaurant with iPad ordering where you pay right after you order so that when you are finished you can leave at any time. For fast food there are some solid offerings, like Chipotle, Le Bus, Philly Pretzel Factory, Smashburger, etc.

I've had two really great meals at Kidari so far. Once with my girl Angela J over the summer and again with my man on Friday for lunch. Both times I had the spicy tuna tartar which is delicious. It is served with some fried potato straws and two different types of sauce. I also really enjoy their miso soup, which has a bit more flavor than some of their competitors' versions.   Normally, I'm not a fan of raw salmon but Kidari's fish is so fresh and clean tasting that I really enjoyed their spicy salmon roll. Maybe even more than my usual go-to, the spicy tuna roll. Their rolls are plump and filling; after the soup and shared app, two was more than enough.   During the summer there was an awesome half-priced sushi happy hour. Not sure if they are still offering this deal but if so, it's a total steal for some really quality sushi.

I love that there's a new Pure Fare relatively close to my neighborhood. This one is much smaller than the location on 21st, but the size is just right for the area. There are a few tables up front and a small refrigerated case with a selection of sandwiches, salads and snacks.   There are only about five sandwich and five salad choices, so go in with an open mind as to what you'd like to eat. I selected one of my faves, the turkey and cheddar sandwich with spicy honey mustard, yesterday. I also grabbed a banana cookie and coffee. Total cost was over twelve dollars, which is a bit steep, but I always appreciate knowing what is in my food and exactly how many calories it's going to cost me. I'll pay a premium for that anytime.   Since the closing of my go-to lunch spot (Healthy Bites To Go), I haven't really found a suitable replacement as far as healthy lunches are concerned. Pure Fare is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, and I'll likely become a regular fairly quickly.

Allison B and I had a delightful sushi lunch today at Machi. I had only tried them for delivery in the past, and it was apparent to me today that most of their business is of the take-out variety.  We were the only table in the small restaurant, which was just fine by us.   The lunch special comes with either soup or salad and a two or three roll combo. I had just come from spinning class so my hungry self was all about three rolls (which I of course couldn't finish). The salads were quite large with delicious ginger dressing. My sushi rolls were very tasty and the fish was very fresh. The wasabi was delightfully strong. I'll return (or order) again!

Every time I go to the P&P, I wake up the next morning enveloped in regret. I should probably stop going, huh?   It had been a long while since I set foot in the place. So long, in fact, that I was told the ground floor bar had been closed for renovations for some time and the bar action was now upstairs.   The upstairs bar area looked like part of a sad comedy club from the early 80s. The only brightness in the room came from a small television, and the creepy monitor from the video camera trained on the front door. Absolutely no music played, and I didn't see or smell any hot water dogs. Downgrade.  My three stars are for the daydreams I have, thinking about what characters have sat at the bar over the years and wondering if they shared the same melancholic feelings as me while doing so.   I hope not to return, but at some point I probably will.

19 Degrees is a solid step up from the market that was previously in this space. It still serves a similar purpose (deli/market), but the feel is much nicer. I'd be just as comfortable sitting down for a bite as I do taking my sammies to go. The counter staff is friendly and they also seem to have regulars at lunch time.   That said, my sandwich was slightly off from what I requested when I stopped in last week. It was still tasty, just lacking all the components I wanted (which I actually had to repeat while ordering). I definitely like that they use quality deli meats and everything tastes super fresh. I'll keep 19 Degrees in the rotation for quick and inexpensive lunches during the week.

Tom's is solid. We order delivery from time to time. Our orders are always accurate and fairly fast, so that's definitely a positive.   In terms of food, their soup dumplings are great and they have the best scallion pancakes around. As for entrees, my husband likes the garlic chicken while I lean towards the sesame chicken. I've really enjoyed it in the past but my order last weekend seemed overly syrupy sweet. Maybe next time I'll go with the ol' general for more of a balance.

Wow.    That was my first impression when walking into Union Trust.  Beautiful architecture, and what were probably some crazy-expensive renovations, stretched from marble floor to richly adorned ceiling.  The main level bar was still swinging after 10 on a weeknight, but there were plenty of available chairs at the upstairs bar for an after dinner cocktail.  As my mom and I sat there chatting, I had a hard time focusing on the conversation as my eyes were wandering all over the room.  For me, this restaurant instantly became the most glamorous in the city, and has shot to the top of my "places to dine" list.  Therefore, my stars are all based on my cocktail experience alone (said cocktail was a tasty gin, strawberry and basil combination made by a friendly bartender).  I hope they can be matched when I come back for dinner, so I can love on this place even more!

YUM! I loved my dinner at Agno Grill last night. My boyfriend has been bugging me to try this place and telling me that I would love it. I'm already a big fan of Pure Fare and, honestly, I might like the Agno Grill concept even more. There are so many choices for what you can put into your bowl or wrap that you could probably go twenty times and have something different each time.   Last night I opted for a (step 1) black rice bowl with (step 2) veggies, (step 3) roasted cauliflower, olives, and white bean, spinach and parmesan spread plus (step 4) tzatziki and the special sauce of the day, green peppers and olive tapenade. And no, I didn't order a single thing extra - you really get that many different toppings in your bowl or wrap! Having so many things in a bowl was kind of crazy but it was fun trying different flavor combinations. I loved every bite and will definitely be hitting up Agno again soon. The more healthy-yet-interesting options in this city, the better.

I'm smack in the middle of my French for Travelers class, and I am truly loving it. Before signing up for my course at Alliance Francaise de Philadelphie, I did some research to decide where I should take my classes. Very happy with my decision to go with the Alliance, since it's not just a place to take classes but also a community of folks who are either from France or speak French or are attempting to learn. Though I have yet to take part, there are community events each month that seem interesting and fun.   I'm a total beginner, and could not have asked for a better instructor in Yann. He moved to Philadelphia from France just four months ago and he's a wonderful teacher. He's very encouraging and patient and has a great teaching style. We learn at a pace that is challenging but not too fast. He assigns homework and sends materials that help me with at-home study.   It's going to take a long time to really understand this language, but I feel like I've found the place that will give me the tools and knowledge to do so.

Still a fan of Seasons 52 although sometimes I think their food could use a bit more... seasoning. Today I had a cup of clam and shrimp cioppino, which was light and tasty. For my main course I had fish tacos. They were presented very nicely, and the flavors were good, but the lettuce mix seemed like something that came right out of a bag. I'm pretty sure that it was, with little strips of carrots and everything. A vinegary slaw in its place would have made a huge difference, and would have kept the tacos from being a touch too dry. Nonetheless, it was a guilt-free meal and filling lunch.

I finally made it in to Eviama for a service (though I have been there several times to make purchases or host events), on New Year's Eve no less! My neck and shoulders had been feeling super tight for weeks so I finally decided to give my fiancé a break and get a professional massage. I could not believe my luck that there was an available appointment with Cooper in the early afternoon.   When I arrived, I filled out a quick form and then Cooper took me to the treatment room, where we talked about some of my problem areas. The massage was fantastic. My shoulders and upper back felt a lot less stiff and I had that euphoric feeling that only the best massages bring on when I walked outside into the cold winter air. I would definitely recommend Cooper and Eviama to anyone looking to escape the city and the craziness of life for an hour of relaxation.

Not updating this review sooner has been a complete oversight.  I've actually been back four or five times since my first visit, and Amis has become one of my favorite destinations for dining and/or drinks.  There are several things on the menu that I have come to absolutely adore, starting with the strozzaprete alla vongole, its buttery flavors I have talked up to just about anyone who will listen.  Another favorite is the bufala ricotta; rich and creamy and drizzled with olive oil, it is the perfect spread for the accompanying toasted bread.    I was once offered a bite of the turkey cutlet by a distinguished gentleman sitting next to me at the bar.  Normally, I'd pass without thinking twice, but this man insisted that the preparation changed his previous contempt for turkey to pure lust, at least, for this particular dish.  Who could pass that up?  I have to hand it to the guy, he was right on.  It sounds crazy to order something so plain-sounding, but trust Vetri and his crew to turn a plain old turkey into a Cinderella story.  A turkerella, if you will.  Make your reservations far in advance, dolls.  The tables don't come easy!

I like Lo Spiedo even though I don't get there very often due to the location. Because they are a bit off the beaten path, I appreciate that they offer free parking on-site.   My recent visit was for the Summer of Brosé happy hour. I loved the lineup of rosés, even if I didn't think their special was all that... special. Only one of the wines was discounted and it was still an eight dollar glass, which made for a pricey night when all was said and done.   The food is always great, but I was so bummed to see some of the grilled/skewered protein options removed from the menu since my last visit. The menu is now primarily composed of small plates, sandwiches, pastas and pricey entrees. I really dig the grilled chicken wings and bbq popcorn (amazing!). I'm hoping they bring the shaved pumpkin salad back in the fall, which is one of my favorite seasonal dishes, and something for which I'd go out of my way.

Thank you, Andrea F, for leading the way to Plaza Garibaldi! I'd had this spot bookmarked for a while based on Andrea's review, and I finally placed an order for delivery one night earlier this week.   I went with the chicken enchipocladas which was a tasty and hearty choice. There were three corn torillas stuffed with shredded chicken and topped with chipotle sauce, sliced avocado and a light sprinkling of queso fresco, plus a swizzle of sour cream. This was a nice, lighter alternative to enchiladas.   On the side, I received a container with pico de gallo, rice and refried beans, plus a small bag of tortilla chips and two salsas. The meal itself was only twelve bucks but delivery plus tip put the total slightly above $20. Considering I got two meals out of it, that was fine with me.   I might deviate to other menu items next time as I felt like I was missing a bit of texture. Overall, excited to have a new option for Mexican delivery!

If only I had options like the ones at Franklin's Table back when I was in college! This food hall is pretty legit. It brings together some of Philadelphia's best known restaurants and makes them a lot more accessible. Perhaps Franklin's Table is a little pricier than other food halls, but I'd argue that you're also getting really high quality food at a fraction of the regular restaurant cost.    I'd imagine this place must be pretty crazy at peak hours. I've only stopped by during random afternoon hours and have had positive experiences. Even the bathrooms are clean and nice. My main suggestion would be to add a composting bin in addition to the regular trash and recycling. So many restaurants are using compostable utensils/containers now and it's a shame to not dispose of them correctly.

Wow, the happy hour. I popped in for a drink and bite one weeknight and was pleasantly surprised. The bar features a red, a white and one cocktail for half off. They also offer a complimentary flatbread. I chose the goat cheese and artichoke flatbread and a small Greek salad. Both were awesome and substantial enough for dinner. With my glass of white, the total bill was just over eleven dollars. What a steal! And even though I was dining solo, I had live piano music to keep me company. I may need to make happy hour at Seasons a weekly thing!

Erawan deserves an upgrade from me. They are definitely in the running for my go-to Thai delivery. They aren't open on Mondays and their delivery fee via GrubHub is $3, which is kind of a bummer. But the food is solid.   I enjoy their tom yum soup and I also recently tried their version of wonton soup. It's totally different from the Chinese version, almost reminding me of a chicken noodle soup, but with light wontons instead of noodles. It was a nice alternative to the tom yum, although that's still my preference.   The chicken with pineapple sauce is always on point, though the portions can sometimes be a bit small compared with the price. The rice is sticky every single time; it even holds up in the fridge better than most rice.

While I'm definitely more skeptical than my fellow Yelpers when it comes to trying the prepared foods at this market, I will agree that the place is stocked to the brim with absolutely everything. I've never made it all the way down the aisles; the couple of visits I've made have been for milk or OJ. But it's clear that this place probably covers every household need.   Maybe I'll give the breakfast sandwiches a shot sometime. Maybe.

My girlfriends and I hit Heritage about a month or so ago for dinner and drinks. I loved everything about my experience and have been hankering to get back. The space is gorgeous. There's a very large dining room and bar area plus a lounge area and seating outside on a cute patio. We chose to sit outside for our meal which was a good call on a nice summer night.  There was a rosé from NJ that was so amazing (I know, crazy!), we ordered several bottles throughout the night! Favorite dishes were the kale salad, heirloom tomatoes, corn cakes, egg noodles and roasted chicken. Oh wow that chicken. Our least favorite dish was the mussels. They sounded nice but we should have read between the lines when our server described them as "on the large side." They were grossly large and the only thing we didn't finish!   We skipped dessert in favor of a nightcap in the lounge area. Our dinner server stuck with us for serving our drinks as well and he was awesome all night. Really excited for the next visit!

I've had two really solid experiences at Hi Kori. Tucked away at the far end of Chinatown Square, the bar is a hidden gem offering a break from the rest of bustling Chinatown.   Each visit was for drinks only. I found them to be well balanced and crafted by really friendly bartenders. Certainly a worthy place to spend your dollars and relax for a bit while in the area!

Loving this new DiBruno location in Market East. They carry a healthy array of to-go items, packaged foods and snacks, have a nice selection of cheeses and meats, and there are loads of helpful and friendly employees all over the store.   Very nice touch giving customers free flowers with a purchase the day before Thanksgiving. They were beautiful and lasted at least a week!

I absolutely love that there is a Tuesday Farmers Market that runs all afternoon and into the evening right in my neighborhood. Julian Abele is a really pretty plot of land and I really hope the market continues through the year (well, as long as possible once the weather starts getting cold - hopefully in the very distant future). It seems like there are usually only one or two vendors so there isn't a huge selection, but there is always a nice array of local produce, some canned goods and some baked items available.

Last Saturday morning, my friend and I visited the new Bruegger's for a grab and go breakfast that would remedy our stomachs from a late night out.  I ordered an everything bagel "softwich" with turkey, lettuce, tomato and pickles on the side as well as a cup of coffee.  When this rang up somewhere around the $9 mark, I was momentarily stupefied.  Talk about over-inflation.  After parting with my final skinny jeans-crumpled Hamilton, we were off.  Back at the couch, I discovered that my softwich, while slammin', was missing its side of pickles.  Bummer.  Still, this would not keep me from returning to Bruegger's in the future.  Then, I took my first sip of coffee.  It was quite possibly the worst ever, right alongside the crap they serve in the Philly airport (refer to my review for details on THAT).  Yuck.  Bad coffee just ruins the breakfast experience.    I'd come back for bagels, but who really wants to make two stops in the morning for bagels and coffee?  Madness, I tell you.

I hadn't been to this deli in quite some time, but I wanted some beer for the game last weekend so decided to swing by for a six pack. This place is weird. It appears to be owned or run by a bunch of young guys. One guy, not sure if he was part of the crew or what, was passed out at a table.   There are definitely better places to grab a sandwich or six pack in the area, and I probably won't be back.

I was shocked - SHOCKED - I tell you, when I arrived at FedEx Ship Center on the Saturday before Christmas and became just the second person in line. Had everyone really beat me at the Christmas game this year or were the employees at this location just that good at expediting packages to and from customers?   Honestly, it was probably just a fluke that I walked in to no crowd when I did. The employees didn't seem particularly speedy but I still received my package in one piece with little fuss.

Dear Friends and Family,  The holidays are fast approaching! Don't you hate it when, once the pressure is on, you suddenly forget all those great ideas you had for gifts all year long? I do, too. So I thought I'd make myself useful and remind you all of my love of Duross & Langel's bath products. I'm still obsessed with the bubble bath, and my vanilla is running dangerously low. I'm also a big fan of the eucalyptus scent. I'd also LOVE some of their soy wax candles. These items will set you back less than $25 a pop (you could actually get TWO bottles of bubble bath for less than $25!). See? One person off your Christmas list already. Always happy to help.  Love,  Michelle      PS, I'm currently loving the stress relief bubble bath, but I'm pretty well-stocked on that one.

Chick's is our date night closer bar, and I absolutely love it.   We usually swing by on Thursdays when Jesse is working (but we've experienced great cocktails under the care of George as well). Just one drink always turns into several, and how could it not with great conversation amongst staff who have become friends.   The bar is typically quiet later in the evening and there's never any trouble getting a seat. There's usually a character or two which adds to the laughs. If you haven't checked this place out, hit your bookmark button and give them a look next time you want a nightcap.

I popped into A La Mousse in hopes of a bubble tea, but was informed they only have them certain days of the week. So I decided to try one of their many hot beverages, instead. I ordered a matcha latte with almond milk and asked that it only be made a little bit sweet.   As I was waiting, I perused the desserts. They really have some gorgeous cakes and other confections. I will definitely have to return to try the matcha chocolate cake, which looked incredible.   The store was super clean and bright, a very inviting space. My drink was made to perfection and warmed me up for the rest of my walk home. I look forward to returning!

Located in an inconspicuous strip of office buildings, right across the street from Cooper River, is the best kept secret in Camden County... and it took a born-and-raised Philadelphian to tell me about it!  Moore Brothers imports wines from small distributors.  Every bottle is kept in a temperature-controlled setting.  The staff members are not only excellent at pairing wines with whatever food combination you throw at them, but they are also well-versed with menus from restaurants all over the Delaware Valley.  Last week, I was on my way to a friend's house for a dinner featuring grilled chicken, corn on the cob and Caprese salad.  The gentleman assisting me asked if I knew what marinade was being used on the chicken.  When I wasn't sure, he pulled several options for me, but he used the salad as the determining factor, which led to a pinot grigio that perfectly complemented the meal later that evening.  On every visit, I've been helped the moment I walk through the door, and I've never once been made to feel foolish asking a question about the wine.  The staff members seem to appreciate people who want to learn, and they are always happy to assist.

What's not to love about this Di Bruno Bros.? Its location in the Italian Market dates back 75 years. Though small, this may be my favorite location of all - the curated selection is top quality and allows you to get in and get out with everything you need. The cheesemongers are the best. I could walk through that store and not even look at the cheese and they will still offer a slice of whatever is being featured that day. (Note: When in Di Bruno, I always purchase cheese.)  Last year my fiancé and I took our families to Di Bruno After Hours, which is when the shop closes and you have the entire place to yourselves. You bring the wine and beer, Di Bruno hooks it up with cheese galore and various snacks. Even my stepdad, a man whose personal constitution involves something about pledging allegiance only to American cheese, found things to enjoy.   Here's to 75 more years!

While I've never stepped foot inside Pretty Sweet Bakery, I've often admired the robin's egg blue-and-white shop from the street or car.  It's probably high time I check out the store firsthand, as I've already tried their delicious chocolate chip scones, purchased at local coffee shops, as well as their cupcakes.  Oh the cupcakes!  Last week, my stepmom surprised me with cupcakes in lieu of regular cake for my birthday.  There were three different versions, but I made a beeline for one of the red velvets, my favorite.  The cake was dense and moist, the frosting whipped and sweet.      Cupcakes make me sooooo happy, and Pretty Sweet Bakery's are no exception!

We ordered some solid Thai from Erawan last night. Delivery was fast compared with other Thai spots with delivery. They definitely get some points there. We ordered fried pork dumplings which were incredibly greasy, but still tasty. On the healthier end of the spectrum, my pad broccoli with chicken was light and flavorful. The rice was perfectly sticky. My boyfriend had chicken in pineapple sauce which was lighter than I expected and had a really nice sweet but spicy flavor. Last week he ordered chicken in some sort of spicy pepper sauce which was also really great.   As far as my favorite Thai delivery goes, I still have one other place that leads the pack, but because of the fast delivery, Erawan will definitely see some repeat business from me.

I hate to downgrade a restaurant that I've really loved in the past, but my recent brunch experience at Amis was not at all worth the high price tag that came along with it.   My friend and I were seated against the wall in the upper left area. Our server was polite but possibly a bit spread thin as we often had to wait longer than usual to order drinks. Speaking of drinks: the bellini is a spiced peach version that's high on flavor but low on champs. I had nary a buzz after I finished so I switched to the spicy bloody mary which was fine but didn't seem all that different from a regular bloody mary.    For food, I opted for the san marzano tomatoes with eggs and basil. This teeny tiny portion tasted fine but, again, nothing special. The roasted potatoes were under-seasoned and Lo Spiedo's homemade smoked bacon tasted no different from store bought bacon.   After hearing so many positive things about Amis' brunch I can honestly say I was disappointed, especially since brunch for two with tip came to somewhere around $100, give or take. I'll stick with dinner at Amis from here on out.

Lots of TVs for sports fanatics?  Check.  Good bar food and decent drink specials?  Check.  Home to one of the more awkward dates of my life?  Check.  A fabulous server who knows to keep those drinks coming?  Double check.

The absolute best. While I adore all of the restaurants in Philly that are currently offering wine to-go during Covid-19, I really appreciate that I can order bottles from Moore Brothers at very reasonable prices and pick them up contact-free within a 24-hour window.  The website is easy to use and each wine has a lot of info so you could really spend some time being selective. My husband and I ordered a medley of rosés and whites, plus a couple lighter reds. We placed the order on Sunday morning and our pick-up was ready later that day. We arrived shortly before closing and called the store - the woman who answered told us to pop the trunk and they would be right out. So easy!   One of the nicest parts of the experience is that Moore Brothers packs in some slips which give details about each wine. I love that because I always try my best to pair our wines with the food we're eating. If you've never been to this great local biz, it's most certainly worth the trip!

A friend in the neighborhood told me she prefers Thai Square over another nearby Thai restaurant, so my man and I decided to check it out on Saturday night. We walked up with a six pack on ice, expecting a wait, but there was only one other seated table. After being a very loyal Healthy Bites To Go customer, I was surprised by how roomy the dining room was - I think they can seat about 20.   We started with the fried pork dumplings, chicken skewers and coconut shrimp. I thought the dumplings were a bit too doughy (I prefer the ones in a thinner wrapper) but I really liked the shrimp and chicken skewers and their accompanying sauces.   For my main, I talked it over with our server and took her suggestion to try the exotic spiced pork. I ordered a medium spice level which was borderline hot for me, which is to say it was just right. The pork was lean and tender and the veggies were crisp. My fiancé's pad kra pow with chicken was very flavorful as well. Service was very pleasant. We look forward to trying more from Thai Square.

I really enjoyed lunch at CO-OP this week. The restaurant is incredibly beautiful. My friend and I were hoping to sit outside, and when we mentioned this to the hostess, she hit a button and the walls started to fold up into the building!   There were a lot of tasty-sounding dishes available for lunch, but I wanted to keep things relatively light with a salad. I ordered the kale salad with the dressing and blue cheese on the side. I also added avocado and grilled shrimp. The salad was quite large and very pretty. There was an entire half of perfectly-ripe avocado, which I loved! I wasn't so crazy about the green goddess dressing; it didn't really have much flavor. I'd order this salad again for sure, but perhaps with a vinaigrette, instead.   I told my husband last night that I really want to return for dinner sometime. And I'd be very interested to know whether or not they offer a happy hour. That's one I'd be willing to go out of my way for, mos def.

It has long been lamented that we don't take advantage of our waterfront property, with the exception of maybe Festival Pier. The gorgeous remodeling of Pier 11 is a welcome sight. Hopefully this new addition will start a revival.   Walking towards the water on the upper level, you get the sensation that you are walking towards an edge with no barrier. On closer inspection, a row of steep steps/seats come into view, along with a smaller staircase on the left. Railings surrounding the pier are all angled, providing a comfortable place to stand and reflect.   Several benches and a few picnic tables are available, but alcohol may only be consumed with the use of a permit... so either conceal wisely or just bring some Ssips iced teas.   Very much looking forward to seeing this park in full swing during the hot summer months, and hoping it is only the beginning to a more beautiful waterfront experience.

My friend has been raving about The Couch Tomato for ages, so we met there for lunch last week. I love the various salad offerings or the option to create-your-own. We placed our order at the counter then grabbed a table outside.   I selected the salad with barbecue chicken, tomatoes, corn, black beans and cheddar. I got ranch dressing on the side. The salad was big, super-fresh, and really delicious. Since the chicken had a decent amount of sauce, I didn't need as much dressing, which I liked. My friend created his own salad but the toppings were a little skimpy, especially the quinoa - he ended up paying extra to get some more on the side.   Overall, very solid spot for a healthy lunch and I've heard the pizza is delicious as well. I'll definitely return when I'm lunching in Manayunk!

I've been loving on this store from afar for quite some time, following their Instagram and plotting my purchases. I finally made it in and picked up the perfect Christmas gift for a friend. Meanwhile, my husband was taking notes, as he got me the most beautiful pair of earrings. Seriously, I'm obsessed.   The store has a great selection of new age-y crystals and stones, tarot cards, candles, and other assorted energy enhancers. There's also a ton of really beautiful jewelry, including some incredible vintage pieces.   I've recently subscribed to the newsletter and am very excited about the store's monthly horoscope and tarot reading sessions!

My husband and I met up with our friends at Frida Cantina for a quick drink before our dinner reservations at another nearby establishment. What a gem! The decor is bright, festive and inviting. Though we weren't there for very long, I was really impressed and can't wait to go back for a meal sometime soon!   We sat at the bar and the list of cocktails looked delicious. I wasn't drinking alcohol, so asked the bartender if I could possibly get something off the menu. He didn't hesitate and within a few seconds, I had a gorgeous hibiscus drink of my own, complete with a very tasty rim!   If the food is anything like the drinks, I will be very happy. Can't wait to return soon!

You would think that in our age of advanced technology, upgrading a phone would be a piece of cake. Unfortunately, this process always seems to take hours. I'll never understand it.   The bright side to my visit to this location on Saturday was the woman who helped me through, Yezenia. She calmly explained my options and answered my questions. I also felt that she really took the time to explore what packages would be best for me personally, based on my usage history. Not only did I leave with a new phone which I had to shell out $0 to receive after my trade-in, but my bill will also be less than what I was paying before because of the new plan offerings.   While the entire process did take over an hour to complete, Yezenia made it as painless as possible. Also, I'd like to give a shout out to the gentleman who helped me when I first walked in - I don't remember his name but he came across as honest and informed, which was appreciated.

I love this place! It's dark, it's cool, it's a welcome addition to a growing list of great businesses in the area.   Both of my visits to Second District have been at the end of my night after several libations. At that point I am usually nursing a pale ale or two and several glasses of water as I go in for the bites.   The chicken sandwich is fantastic and so are all of the snacks I've tried, particularly the pork rinds, wings and pickles.   Table service has been great - I had the same friendly server on both visits. Excellent addition to the Philly food and beverage scene!

My experience at Breakaway Bikes was brief but solid. My boyfriend bought me indoor cycling shoes for my bday but they were a tad small and also needed clips installed. They were quickly exchanged for the correct size and then they were fitted appropriately with the clips. I was told that if I have any problems with my ride, I can bring the shoes back and have the clips adjusted at any time. Sweet! Employees were friendly and helpful. Solid spot.

If the La Colombe in Rittenhouse and the one by City Hall were men, I'd choose the latter without a shred of uncertainty. Polar opposites, the City Hall location is newer, cleaner, brighter, cooler.   Despite less seating, the turnover was pretty fast during my afternoon visit on Thursday. Pastries looked decadent, and their coffee is my absolute fave. A water station with cold, sparkling and room temp options with real glasses was just perfect. I may plan all my meetings there.

In all my years of drunk eating, I had never been to Lorenzo's before Saturday.  After a long night out, our crew ordered a pie which, to my shock and drunken delight, was so large it required TWO boxes!  Noticing the condiments on the counter, I opened the top box and started liberally sprinkling the pie with... something.  We discovered soon after that the something was garlic powder.  Oops!  We enjoyed a very garlicky pizza that tasted like the food of the gods at the time, if a tad potent.    Sober reflection tells me that the pizza was tasty but undercooked.  The one remaining slice in my fridge will be reheated in the oven for lunch today, providing some much-needed crunchiness.  It should be noted, this is probably the first time in history that I have ever had leftovers from late-night eating.  Lorenzo's, I salute you!

I looooove Plenty on East Passyunk Avenue, so I was absolutely stoked when their new location on Spruce Street finally opened last week. I parked the car illegally and stood watch while my partner in crime ran inside for breakfast sandwiches.   My choice was the pancetta hash, with two fried eggs, pancetta, breakfast potatoes, and fontina. We got home and tore open our packages. Mine came in a cardboard to-go box, and when I opened the lid the first thing I noticed was the pool of egg yolk covering the entire bottom of the box, leaving the whole underside of my sandwich completely soaked and really messy. Meanwhile, the roll was really tough and also very large, and it overpowered (what was left of) the ingredients in the sandwich. If you do feel compelled to order the pancetta hash to go after reading this, be sure to order it with scrambled eggs.   This was my first time ordering breakfast at Plenty; normally I have sandwiches and almost always the tasso ham panini, which is incredible. I'm looking forward to swinging by again soon, and hopefully updating my review once that happens.

Never had a sit-down dinner here, but I remember the bar food being good from a happy hour I went to a year or so ago.  Went last night and threw back a pretty delish sangria like nobody's business.  The server told me what was in it but after the second or third alcohol he mentioned, I lost track.  There was definitely burgundy wine in there somewhere and at least one type of brandy.    The upstairs bar area is super cute but tiny~ so get there early after work if you want a table near the kick-ass windows that overlook Chestnut.

I took the Yin Yoga class with Barbara on a cold Friday night in December. Yoga is one of those things I have a love/hate relationship with; I'm not very flexible, so poses don't come easily for me.
