In fact, I'm often so tight that it's hard for me to even get into or hold poses. This gentle yoga class is perfect for runners and weight lifters who need to loosen up and stretch those muscles.   The thing I loved most about this class in particular is that it is a candlelit class, so the room is dark and only lit by flickering candles. It made me feel less self conscious as I was struggling through poses. I really enjoyed how Barbara walked around and offered corrections and soothing words. Also, the studio has everything you need, from blankets to straps and blocks. I brought my own mat but it was nice to have everything else available.   Looking forward to getting back for another class when my schedule allows!

I love this place for a healthy lunch! The employees are very efficient to the point of making me feel super rushed - be sure to know exactly what you want when it's your turn in line! That said, even when the line is long you know you won't have much of a wait, so that is the plus side.   It's taken me a few visits to figure out the lay of the land, but my go-to is usually a greens and lentils bowl with chicken, topped with hummus, tzatziki, and harissa, plus an assortment of fresh veggie toppings and kalamata olives. I usually get a sauce on the side but often don't need it because everything in the bowl is flavorful enough on its own.

My grandmom has been talking up this diner for a while, so I had to take her out for lunch to see what the fuss was about. We went on a Friday and the restaurant was pretty busy.   The menu stands up to any other Jersey diner. It's several pages long and loaded with options. How do they do it? I'll never know. I decided to go basic and had a bacon, cheddar and tomato omelet with hashbrowns and toast. It was a huge plate of food and the hashbrowns were perfectly crispy! My grandmom had a turkey club which came with soup and dessert, so that was also a massive meal. She swapped onion rings for fries and they were quite delish.   My only suggestion would be for the servers to stop by the table a few minutes after food is delivered, just to make sure everything is correct, drinks are filled, etc.   Naturally, Gram had coupons so the meal total before tip was under $25. Such a steal! I think this is our new go-to for lunches out together.

I am hooked. Since my last review, not only did I lower my regular gym membership, but I actually decided to terminate my membership completely. Nothing came close the to the workouts I receive at Flywheel. The classes and instructors, quality of the bikes, wide variety of class times, and themed rides at Flywheel are unmatched.   If you had told me a year ago that I would regularly spend $20-$25 on single spin classes, I would have said you were crazy. But that was before my introduction to Flywheel. And now, for us frequent fly-ers, there's a $180/month membership option which entitles members to unlimited classes. In my first month alone, I hit twelve, which works out to $15 per class, making my membership completely worthwhile. While still pricey, I've decided that I can make some cutbacks to my other expensive habits (food, drinks, nails, shopping, etc.) in order to fit Flywheel into my life. I'm more than willing to sacrifice a few cocktails each week in exchange for a toned, fit body.

The diner-style seating and Greek grandma-ladies behind the counter kicked things off to a promising start during stop three of an Old City pizza crawl. Homemade desserts called from behind a display window, but it was the pies we were after. Pizza pies.   A slice of cheese and a slice with crumbled sausage were placed on our table, hot from the oven. This pizza had so much potential, with a nice crunch to the entire crust and the delicious crumbled sausage. Alas, the cheese had no oozy stretch. As my boyfriend later recounted to friends, "government cheese laughed at this cheese."

Yesterday I popped in to try on some jeans since I'd heard about Madewell's denim exchange program. It's a promotion going on through the end of the year where you can bring in any pair of old jeans to donate (jeans are used for housing insulation for those in need) and receive $20 off a new pair from Madewell. Their jeans are pretty pricey so I was all about this deal, especially after hearing rave reviews about Madewell's denim.   I gathered tons of clothes to try on and was helped by Sophia, who pulled other items that were similar to things I was already trying on, which I loved. She also gave honest feedback - I wasn't pressured into anything I knew was not right. I ended up with just one pair of jeans and one sale tee, but I loved both pieces. And I cleaned out five pairs of old jeans from my closet in the process, so there's that. Love this store!

Cheers to Little Fish for offering a few unique options for take out that are vastly different from a lot of other restaurants. Obviously, we're a bit limited at the moment, so trying something new and exciting was a treat. My husband and I splurged and ordered two of the hamachi rice bowls - I managed to get the last two of the day! The guy who took my order over the phone was very nice. Once I arrived to the restaurant, I called and the bag was brought out right away.   The bowls were put together nicely and everything was fresh. I think next time I might opt for one of the bento boxes for more variety.   It had been ages since my last visit to Little Fish and I look forward to going back for a full meal when possible.

Sorry, Cava, but it's time for a downgrade. I visit this location every so often and the quality has gone down over my past few stops. The food station area is always very messy. The employees, while efficient, aren't very friendly. It's clear that you are expected to do your part in ordering quickly to move things along, and yet, nothing is labeled so how would a first timer (or even an occasional customer) know what anything is without asking a hundred questions?   I often order the grilled chicken which isn't always lean and/or trimmed, which can be gross. Other than that, the other ingredients are always fresh and tasty. I also really like the option of lentils for something different, and I dig the lentil and supergreens mix as a base.   Hopefully, some improvements will be made to the customer service and also the tidiness of the food station.

Vegan chocolate frozen yogurt that tastes just like chocolate soft serve... and is 220 calories for quite a large cup. What's up.   (Skip the swirl - the vanilla cashew is really grainy. But maybe that's your thing. If so, keep on keepin' on you grainy ice cream lover, you.)

This Staples was surprisingly crowded when I stopped in for a print job last week. There was one person working the printing center and several people waiting on projects. Once I made it to the front of the line, my printing was handled quickly and I was happy with the results.   Then I moved over to the registers where two employees were handling customers very slowly. Mid-afternoon Staples runs should not be so time consuming!

Welcome to the 'hood, Tria! After the super sad news that Dmitri's would be leaving their Fitler Square home, the only thing that numbed the pain was the announcement of Tria moving in.   I've swung by twice now and both nights were poppin'. Of course, the wine program is on point and the servers are super hospitable and very well-versed in their knowledge of the grapes (and everything else).   On the food menu, I loved seeing some of my Tria favorites (warm bean dip, asparagus and white bean salad) plus some new, heartier fare thanks to the full kitchen. My bae Aaliyah P and I split the aforementioned salad and some mushroom tagliatelle and that pasta was to-die. It was actually a very nice portion to split after the salad (I could totally clean house on that pasta myself on a hungrier night, however). I can't wait to try everything else on the dinner menu!

I've been loving Bakeshop on 20th for quick and healthy breakfast delivery every now and then. I love the egg white wrap with feta, tomatoes and spinach. So tasty! I also tried the avocado toast recently, which was absolutely delish as well.   I'm not as big of a fan of going in to the shop. It's so tiny and gets super crowded. I also find them rather expensive. An avocado toast, salmon avocado toast special, and four largish pastries somehow set me back to the tune of fifty dollars last weekend (plus tip, for the super sweet gentleman working that Sunday). I'm still scratching my head over that one, and I'm clearly not over it.   I'll be sticking with the breakfast bites, but will be purchasing bulk pastries elsewhere in the future!

Okay DaMò, I see you!   This place has been on my radar for a while, but we don't order Italian for takeout super often. After a long and chilly day, I was craving comfort food. My husband suggested DaMò which sounded just right.   We each ordered small pastas (mine was the casarecce arrabbiata and his was a custom creation with tonnarelli and bolognese sauce). We also ordered the caprese salad and a piece of focaccia. The caprese was small and the tomatoes were just okay. For $14, we'll pass on this dish in the future. The focaccia, however, was fantastic. Going to have to double that order next time!   Both pastas were great and exactly what we were expecting. The small portion size was perfect for both of us; I even had a little bit left over for the next day. Adding DaMò to our takeout/delivery rotation for sure!

Walk into this bar and walk back in time to when dark lounges with kitschy decor ruled all. There wasn't enough time during my stay to take in all the fabulous sculptures, trinkets, paintings and more.  While there was a nice selection of cocktails, my crew of ladies kept things simple with a few rounds of beer. We also sampled a couple items from the menu - the mac and cheese which was unreal and the potato and celery root latkes which were very tasty as well. I ordered a chicken parm sandwich to go for my man and the takeout bag must have weighed about five pounds.   And how about that bar staff?! What a bunch of crafty, fine-looking individuals!   Franky Bradley's is about to become my spot, and I'm not the only one. Mayor Nutter and his posse rolled in during my visit and word is, that wasn't his first time, either. I look forward to my upcoming dance-off with the mayor once the upstairs opens up.

My first visit to this Sweetgreen location was just okay. The food was great - my kale Caesar salad was delicious and I have been enjoying the butternut squash soup on the fall menu. My issues were with the cleanliness of the restaurant - there were flies everywhere near the produce behind the main prep area - and the lack of basic essentials - no napkins, no salt and pepper packets or shakers, etc. They were also out of turkey, which is featured in a bunch of their fall salads.   This is a brand new Sweetgreen location. Get it together!

My crew of ladies started our Friday girls' night out at Noche.  The place was crowded (but not overly so) around 7:30.  We grabbed a booth (which are very poorly constructed, I might add--unless reclining into your neighbor's table is supposed to happen) and ordered some nachos and a pitcher of beer.  Had we arrived earlier, we would have been able to take advantage of the buy one get one pizzas and half priced apps.  Luckily, Noche's nachos were worth their regular price.  The mountain of chips (some of which were a little browned from the oven--my favorite!) with cheese, chicken, jalapenos, sour cream, black beans, salsa and guacamole was the perfect meal to kick off the weekend.  Our server kept our pitchers a-coming, and the experience as a whole was pleasant.    One thing I don't get is the pool table.  It takes up way too much real estate, and it's almost impossible to get to either the juke box or bathroom without being speared in the kidney by a pool stick.

Do you see the photo of the flowers that arrived at my apartment last weekend?! They were absolutely beautiful!   The arrangement was sent from my fabulous friend Aimee from St. Louis. She told me she sort of just picked a place and ordered. I was stunned when I realized the business didn't have any reviews on Yelp already. The flowers were just so pretty and perfect for spring and the occasion itself (my recent engagement!).   If you're looking for a Philadelphia flower delivery, give Philadelphia Flower a shout. They know how to pick some beautiful blooms.

After taking nearly fifty Flywheel classes, you'd think I would have stopped into the deli that shares the same breezeway at least once, but nope! It wasn't until last night that I decided to check them out for a quick meal to go after class.   Despite my ravenous appetite, I wanted to keep things relatively healthy. I ordered a wrap with turkey, turkey bacon, lettuce and tomato. It came with a side so I picked coleslaw, and once I got home I added it to my wrap. Delish!   I asked if there would be a pickle on the side (not leaving a deli without one!) and the cashier gave me a bag to take back to the pickle bar. YES.   The menu is pretty large and I'm especially excited by the mashed potatoes. I don't know, I just really love some taters so I'm really down with the potential to grab some to go.

I'm torn between three and four stars for my first experience with Real Food Eatery. I've been wanting to try it for a while and finally decided to place a delivery order on one of a small handful of days last week when I opted for healthy foods over carbs, cheese, more carbs and alcohol. The holidays, am I right?   I love the variety of choices for mains and sides. Don't like beets? No problem, there's about six other sides to select from. I went with salmon over brown rice, with sides of kale and mushrooms and parmesan broccoli. I also ordered a side of roasted apples.   The food arrived and I was very happy with the size of the platter. I wanted to eat healthy but I didn't want to go to bed hungry. I will say that the piece of salmon was minuscule, but perfectly cooked. The kale and mushroom side was extremely salty but was a bit more balanced when I ate it together with the rice. The apples were a perfect sweet treat with zero guilt.   I'll definitely give Real Food another try when I need something healthy but don't feel like cooking.

My husband and I were super excited to check out The Met for John Oliver's first night in Philadelphia. My husband is a born and raised Philadelphian and he never believed that he'd see the day when this majestic building would be made whole again. It's really pretty impressive how the restorations came together.   That said, I do wish some consideration would have gone into the comfort of the seating. The rows are very close together and our knees were touching the seat backs in front of us. After nearly two hours, I couldn't wait to get out of those chairs!   Staff members were hit or miss; some were friendly (ushers/bartenders) while others were super gruff (security).  The sound at our show was great and we had a great view to the stage even though we were seated in the loge area on the third level.    Very happy to see this Philly icon get a second life and I'm sure we'll be back.

I've basically become obsessed with this place. The sandwiches are all filling and delicious. So far I've tried the turkey with cheddar and honey mustard, turkey with pear and gorgonzola and the tandoori chicken. Best of all, the nutritional information is easily accessible via the website. Which means no frustrating guesstimating for those of us on a diet.   The bakery area is filled with homemade items made out of healthy ingredients. The banana cookie, though small, packs a huge punch of flavor and for only 85 calories. If I had unlimited funds, I'd probably eat at Pure Fare every single day.

I attended my first-ever class at Tria's Fermentation School earlier this month and plan to make it a regular occurrence. My guy and I attended the Spain v. Portugal Showdown, instructed by Michael McCaulley (who was appropriately just nominated for a James Beard Award). For ninety very entertaining minutes, Michael explained the nine or so wines we tasted, the characteristics of both regions and how the wines from each region compared. Audience interaction was encouraged and the classroom was a friendly, comfortable environment.   A sampling of cheeses, charcuterie, breads and accoutrements were served on little boards for each student, which was a very nice touch.   I am very much looking forward to our next class, and would highly recommend a session to anyone looking to enhance his or her knowledge while getting a good buzz on in the process.

Easily one of my favorite coffee shops in the city. I love the space - lots of seating between the picnic tables near the register, plus the stand alone tables scattered along the back wall and throughout the main floor.   Employees are always really pleasant. The last time I was there, the music was all old school stuff like Frank Sinatra - I loved it because it was so different from what you typically get at a coffee shop. The crowd is always really diverse which I like as well. You have your students but also your professional types.   I love the Americanos and the pastry selection is excellent. They have a savory pastry with goat cheese, sun dried tomatoes and spinach that is absolute perfection. I also dig that they have a cold case of to-go beverages and meal options for eating in or taking on the run. Finally, major props for the still and sparkling water station, with actual water glasses, instead of the shot glasses most coffee shops provide.   See you again soon, Parliament!

Pita Chip has quickly become one of my go-tos for fast, healthy food to go. I usually get the half and half bowl (rice and lettuce), with chicken shawarma, hummus, and a variety of fresh toppings. I love that there are so many vegetable options to choose from; everything always looks so colorful and healthy!   I'm a big fan of their vegan tahini as a sauce, but I recently tried the garlic sauce which is almost like an aioli. It would be great with fries! I haven't tried Pita Chip's fries yet, but when I do I will definitely get the garlic sauce for dipping.   My bowl rings in at eight dollars and change, which is really great for a hefty amount of food that keeps me going for hours. The employees are always friendly, and there's a loyalty card program as well as emailed coupons. Great spot for quick, healthy eats!

First time at the Fairmount location of Little Pete's! This is an old school diner all the way. I had a coffee within moments of sitting down and I saw all the usual breakfast staples on the menu. I ordered an omelet with onions, peppers and feta, and it was dropped off in no time at all.   My dining companion and I lingered for a while after breakfast and it became increasingly harder to get a coffee. But, overall, it was a very solid experience and a great option for a weekday, since it was relatively quiet.

Perhaps the "Speakeasy" part of the name rings a little too true - if my boyfriend hadn't pointed out the business, I probably would have passed it by dozens of times before realizing it. But behind the darkened windows lies a delightful little nook with great coffee, affordable bites and friendly staff members.   And cupcakes. Beautiful, perfect cupcakes... that I have yet to try! I know, I know, cupcake-queen and all that jazz. I definitely need to check those out. In the meantime, I'm loving their coffee (which unfortunately only comes in one size, although it's hella strong). I also enjoyed my breakfast sandwich yesterday, with egg whites, smoked cheddar and bacon on a crusty baguette with a lovely side of greens with pesto dressing.   This is a great neighborhood spot!

I am not a large festival type of person, but Bloktoberfest is the exception to the rule. It started off pretty small a few years ago and has since grown to a blocks-long party on South Street West. I'm a big fan of arriving early, grabbing some drink tickets and hitting up the cool craft beer tents and food trucks. After around 4pm the lines start getting pretty long and the streets are packed. That's generally when I start thinking about my next move.   The crowd is made up of mostly young professionals and families - I really enjoy that. No one seems to get out of hand (at least, during the daylight hours, from what I can tell) and they stop selling beer tickets at a certain point to help ensure that. The organizers are all about keeping the local businesses and neighbors happy and Bloktoberfest is a very well-run event overall. Can't wait for next year!

After two-plus years at my gym, I started feeling the familiar itch for change. The change of seasons felt like a great time to try something new, so I purchased a month-long pass at Tuck. They currently have a new student special for just $69 which offers a month of unlimited classes!  I had taken barre classes before and my experiences were all over the map; some classes were great, while others couldn't be over fast enough. Tuck strikes this amazing balance of a really hard workout that somehow still feels enjoyable. Also, the best part is that there are several instructors so every class feels different. Each instructor has their own style - it's really great for variety and keeps things interesting!   The studio is always bright and clean and the equipment is nice. I'm really enjoying my new workout and plan to continue through the summer, and perhaps even longer!

I have to hand it to the Dîner en Blanc organizers - they really stepped it up for year three. The location on Broad Street was amazing. So many photo ops. The party spanned from Chestnut to Pine Streets and every block was filled with beautifully decorated tables and some fine looking people.   As opposed to last year's location on the Parkway, this year provided much more space between tables, and there was a lot more foot traffic which made the event feel interactive with the city. Amazingly, the predicted rain held off, but had there been a weather catastrophe, we would have been moved to the Kimmel Center, which was on reserve as a pretty excellent back-up plan. Can't wait to see what year four brings!

The fab Alex W and I chose Pure Fare for our lunch date this week. I had tried one of their sandwiches before and was looking forward to tasting more of their goods.  The store was smaller than I expected but I loved the layout. A communal table in the center of the room provides plenty of seating for anyone wanting to eat there. A coffee and fresh juice bar is located on one of the shorter walls, while prepared items line the long wall. Some breakfast selections are featured in a display near the register.  I especially love that the calorie info is posted on every single item in clear view. I selected a spinach and artichoke frittata for only 200 calories, and I split the quinoa salad with Alex. The salad was filled with apricots, avocado, cherry tomatoes, basil and almonds. Very tasty. The frittata had a satisfying cheddar flavor without feeling heavy. I would absolutely get either item again. Alex's turkey sandwich with veggies was flavorful and had a nice crunch. All items totaled around $18, which seemed fair given the quality of the food. Looking forward to trying more!

Apologies for what may seem like haterade, but Rittenhouse Square simply is not my favorite park in the city. For me, a park should be a calming oasis where I can sit and collect my thoughts or have a quiet conversation.   Rittenhouse is like the Cherry Hill Mall of the outdoors. It's a melting pot of people from all walks of life (cool), which also includes lecherous men with lame pick-up lines and people who think nothing of chain smoking next to you as you try to eat lunch or simply breathe (not cool).   When alone, I always find myself walking through quickly and avoiding the eyes of people lined against the paths. Not exactly a feeling of serenity.   My favorite part of Rittenhouse Square Park is enjoying it from the outside, seated at one of Parc's tables, with a glass of white and a warm shrimp salad.

As I've been dabbling into meditation more and more, I've noticed Mama's Wellness Joint keeps popping up across my social feeds. Finally, the stars aligned and my schedule worked out so I was able to attend a session.   The space is lovely, with a nice reception area that has a pretty cool gift shop. Shoes have to be removed before heading into the main room, and there is plenty of space for that.   The practice room has a very soothing feel. For my session, only a few small spotlights provided some low lighting, and we made ourselves comfortable with the blankets and bolsters provided.   Mama's offers yoga, but there are a handful of meditation practices offered for all types of interests, by a variety of practitioners. I'm excited to explore more of these in the future!

Okay, I've been back twice and the counter staff could not have been nicer or the sandwiches (tasso ham and tuna - an awesome choice for something a bit lighter but still filling) more delicious. I love that they have a frequent sandwicher card so that I'll eventually earn one for free.   Once the weather warms up a bit and I become a little less lazy, I'll walk myself over there and enjoy a meal in their cute loft space.

This Starbucks left a lot to be desired on my visit this afternoon. There were only two employees working and one seemed to be training - and it was busy! We arrived when there wasn't much of a line but the queue got backed up several times while we were there.   Secondly, there is not much seating available so you really have to pounce on a table the moment it becomes unoccupied.   Third, the snack case was pretty barren and not super appealing. Perhaps this is a positive as it kept me from snacking!    Finally, the music was turned way loud. I'm certain that Starbucks has some sort of corporate policy about their music volume and this particular location was definitely not abiding to that decibel. Totally distracting.   My green tea latte was fine but the condiments station could have used a clean-up.

My sis raves about Johnny Mañanas. It's her go-to happy hour spot and she's obsessed with the margaritas and taco salads (see: Kate C's review). So we made plans to meet up last Friday so I could see what the fuss was all about.   First impression: kitschy but fun vibe, weird smell. Not like stale beer smell, but something equally not pleasant. As the place filled and the scent of cooking food took over, it got better. But still, might want to look into that.   Our server was sweet and checked in often. The margaritas were on point. The sour mix is house-made and the drinks went down easy. I was buzzing after one but totally went for round two.   The taco salad was pretty awesome. My sister said they normally come topped with shredded chicken and sauteed onions and peppers but our chicken was in strips and there were no sauteed onions and peppers to be found. Still, it was a tasty salad and huge.   I'm down for round two at this place.

I like this coffee shop. It's small, but there are three high top tables with stools that are comfortable to work from or conduct a quick meeting. I've never seen all of the seats filled so it's not a bad alternative to the always-crowded Elixr across the street.   La Colombe is on tap and the prices are pretty in line with other shops. There's a small case of pre-made sandwiches and baked goods but I haven't tried anything.   Also, I remembered my last visit being somewhat chilly but the café was nice and toasty today. So there's that, too.

I relied on Yelp reviews to lead me to a new dry cleaner, and I was not disappointed. When I brought my clothes to Master Tailor, the owner meticulously combed over my clothes looking for spots or discolorations of any kind, marking everything with red tape. She was able to have my clothes ready for pick up just two days later, and everything looks great. This is my new dry cleaner. Thank you, Yelp!

Yeah guys, I went out after dinner too.    My friend invited me to join her at Raven Lounge, where she would be meeting up with her boyfriend and some of his friends.  The words "single" and "cute" were all this hot-blooded lady needed to hear for convincing and we were off.  Solid beats, cold brews and Hungry Hungry Hippos are where it's at.  This morning, as I was fishing through my bag I noticed a stray piece of Jenga had hitched a ride to Jersey.  Don't worry, Raven Lounge peeps, I'll bring it back soon.  Maybe.

Bayard's is a local chocolate company with three locations.  Each "chocolate house" is similar, but the one I have frequented most is the Cinnaminson location.  Every time I visit I am filled with warm feelings and the reminiscence of past holidays and birthday celebrations.    In high school, a friend of mine worked at the Cinnaminson Bayard's and every time we had a sleepover, she would bring BAGS of chocolates.  I can't imagine how many calories were consumed on those nights!  Now, I stick to just a couple pieces of my very favorites.  I cannot go into a Bayard's without leaving with a chocolate covered marshmallow for myself.  Does anyone remember that Sesame Street clip with the little kid and the chocolate covered cookie?  Am I jogging memories here?  That's me with the marshmallow.  Other favorites are the dark chocolate covered orange peels, which are so different from anything you would find at other chocolate stores and so very good, and the chocolate and vanilla butter creams.

I eye up Moustaki every time I drive past but rarely find myself in the area. I've always been curious because I absolutely love Mediterranean food! Last week, I finally made Moustaki my dining destination before heading to an event at the Franklin Institute.   The menu has a lot on it and there's definitely something for everyone. I'm trying to get into a more pescetarian diet so I gravitated towards the salmon platter. In an attempt to keep it healthy-ish, I went with rice and lemon potatoes, though I was definitely eyeing up the fries.   We started with the feta dip appetizer which I wasn't crazy about. The cucumbers that came with were past their prime; they had that soft, translucent look around the edges.   Fortunately, the main dish was really solid. The salmon portion was generous and I liked the potatoes a lot (the rice was fine, nothing extraordinary).   I'd give Moustaki another shot if I happened to be in the neighborhood again.

When it comes to new-to-me places, I can be as bashful as a child, refusing to go it alone for the first time, hiding behind my mom's pant leg while I assess the situation.   Even though I've been living in the city for almost six months, it took that long for me to check out the Schuylkill River Trail. Friends promised a safe and scenic place to run outside, but I just kept going to the gym. That, or - get this - driving to Jersey where my courses were plotted and I felt comfortable with where I was going and what to expect.  Finally, my boyfriend and I decided to take a walk, and to the Trail we went. Shocked was I at how well-maintained and well-populated the area actually was. I felt like I had made this amazing discovery, and I couldn't stop talking about how glad I was that we had finally taken that walk.   Yesterday, I enjoyed my first of what will likely be many solo runs on the Trail.

Never go here if you are easily distracted or hungover.  You will circle the racks for an hour or more, try on bikinis in December and will leave feeling frustrated and empty-handed while swearing to never return.  Of course, you will be lured back by promises of designer merchandise at a fraction of the price plus 25% off in the holiday sale.  Keep your wits about you and stick to your game plan.  You just might end up with a Christmas gift for the boyfriend and a hot minidress for New Year's.

I needed a bouquet of flowers, and I needed them quickly. I vaguely remembered a bunch of last-minute-men hovering around flowers on Spruce Street at around 5pm on Valentine's Day, but I couldn't recall the exact location of where this was witnessed. I jumped in my car and did a Spruce Street drive-by. Once I spotted Spruce Food Market, it all came rushing back.   I parked in the twenty minute loading zone across the street and surveyed the impressive array of bouquets. Mostly all, if not all, were reasonably priced under $20. I grabbed a lovely assortment that included roses, carnations, big stalk thingees I don't know the name of and a mix other blossoms. Some paper was wrapped around them and I was out the door in seconds. The flowers were well-received and I have Spruce Food Market to thank. I will definitely return the next time I need flowers.

I recalled my only experience at Mama Palma's as being pretty mediocre, but I was willing to give them another shot since there are so few sit-down pizza places in the neighborhood. The boyfriend and I ordered diet cokes, and after scoping out the beer prices, we were happy. $7 for a draft Peroni? Mama, please.   To start, a shared Caesar salad that was so bland, I could only hope the pizza would save dinner. The mostly-white iceberg was dressed in watered-down dressing. Either that, or the rinsed lettuce was still wet when the dressing was tossed in. Flavorless slices of dry bread topped the lettuce. Total cost, $10.  Our pizza was significantly better, with generous crumbles of sausage, mozzarella, some peppers and a chunky tomato sauce. The crust was not memorable. When two slices remained and we were given the option of boxing, we decided to just leave them behind.   Next time, I'll trek over to Pietro's or just order up some Slice.

I would like to take this time to appeal to the folks at the Royal in a request to get the chicken frankie wrap on the lunch menu. Yesterday I had a craving, and that craving was for more chicken frankie. Sad was my heart when, after reading and re-reading the menu three times, there was no frankie or even frankfurter for that matter. I went with my backup, the grilled chicken sandwich with pears and gorgonzola, but it was a very distant second to the wrap.

Barcade is a cool spot for something different. Friends and I kicked off an afternoon of fun at the Ms. Pac-Man game, where it became depressingly obvious how far I've fallen from my youthful domination of video games.   The bartenders were friendly and willing to whip up one mean bloody mary in addition to offering helpful info during the beer selection process. The draft list is quite extensive.   I didn't eat but the food looked decent in a bar food kind of way.   Barcade isn't really a place I'd typically hang out which is probably why my feelings are so-so on the place. But if you like good beer and you love arcade games, this spot will be right up your alley.

A few of us stopped by Yellow Juice Bar on Sunday afternoon after a workout. There were two people waiting on a juice that was in-process when we arrived. We placed our order for three juices which came to slightly over $20. I got out my credit card and the juice bar employee asked me if I had cash - they were having problems with the system. I didn't think I had enough on me but just when I realized I did, the credit card went through, though I was unable to get a printed receipt or tip on my card.   The juices took a while to process and, I have to admit, the finished product didn't stack up to my favorite juice bar across town (the ingredients in the drink were almost identical to the blend I normally order at the other establishment). Nor did the experience overall with the employees. Hopefully Yellow Juice Bar was just having an off day but I'm not sure how soon I'll be back to find out.

I wish I could remember the name of the juice I sucked down on Friday, but it had apple, cucumber, kale and ginger and was recommended by the gentleman behind the counter. Pure deliciousness. And served just the right temp, with just a few ice cubes.  The store is bright and the employees were friendly during my visit. When the guy who made my juice poured my cup, he even let me drink a few sips so he could top me off with what was left in the pitcher. Nice! I also love that the calories are listed for all menu items. That's huge, and super appreciated.   So glad Philly is catching on to the juicing craze, because I've been really into juice as an in-between snack, or as a complement to a lighter lunch. Sip-N-Glo definitely doesn't come cheap; my 16oz juice was more than $7! I'm willing to pay for that deliciousness every now and then for a treat, though I'd likely have it more often if it was a little more wallet-friendly. It is still juice, and not a meal, after all.

This is when an extra half star would come in handy.  I'm only giving three because I've been spoiled by the location in Marlton which is a hundred times nicer.  The lunch specials here are decent, but any roll deviating from the 8 or so standards will cost you.  Special rolls are kind of pricey for lunch but suitable for dinner.  The sushi is good but I probably wouldn't visit this location again unless I was picking up take-out.

Props to Dae Bak for handling our fairly tipsy and hungry group last night! A bunch of us were at Hop Sing for an event and decided to cross the street for some much-needed sustenance. We were seated at a large table by the window (fun people watching!) and kept servers busy with food orders and many rounds of Korean beer.   We started with a scallion pancake which seemed to include a lot more than scallions - maybe some seafood? All I know is that it was fried, filling, and exactly what I needed at that moment in time. The fried dumplings were also really tasty.   I did a chicken dolsot bibimbap bowl for my entree and it was extra sizzly. I spread the rice all around the bowl and it reached a very desirable level of crispiness. It's been a while since I've had a dolsot bibimbap bowl that was hot enough to achieve this and I was happy that Dae Bak's version was up for the challenge! Our servers were very sweet and really on top of everything.   Next time, I'd like to venture out of my comfort zone and try some other dishes!

Loved, loved, loved my first experience at Root on Friday night. I went for an early dinner in a small group and we were able to take advantage of the happy hour specials from our table. The rum old fashioned is how we kicked things off, and then I enjoyed several glasses of the vinho verde with my meal.   To start, we snacked on the fried chickpeas, crispy potatoes and corn zeppole. I could not get enough of those taters and chickpeas! We also enjoyed a cheese and salumi selection that was very nice, and a total steal with four selections at half the normal price.   Next, we shared the kale and escarole salad, spinach and ricotta gnudi, and meatballs. Each plate was absolutely delicious and I'd order any and all of them again.   Service was on point, relaxed and friendly. I really can't wait to get back to Root for another happy hour or dinner!

The long-awaited Rival Bros. coffee bar is as cool as the names of their signature roasts. The neighborhood seems to be on board big time - there have been people in and out every time I've swung by for a cup.   Last weekend, my fiancé picked up an herb scone from the bakery display and he made the mistake of giving me a bite. This was like no scone I've ever before tasted. Bakery products come from High Street on Market so it should have been no surprise that it was incredible.   Great addition to the neighborhood.

This sunny little establishment serves up 100% fruit and veggie juices, plus frozen banana twirls and a few salad options. I've been there twice for juice, and I love that I can pick out one of the green juices and then customize it further by adding some apples to sweeten it up a bit. Can't wait to try their lemonade one hot day soon!

Sarcone's makes the rolls that set the hoagie standard in Philadelphia. So how could the sandwiches from their deli be anything less than five-star worthy?  We arrived a couple hours before the first Eagles home game of the season. The two women working the counter were efficient. One had two phones in her hand while the other rang up orders and took walk-ins.   I was trying to keep it (relatively) healthy so I went with a turkey and cheese hoagie with lettuce, tomato, onions, pickles and hot peppers. The medium was the perfect size for enjoying half before the game (lunch!) and half after (dinner!). I tried a bite of the classic Italian and man was that good. Next time I go for more of a splurge, that's what I'm getting. And probably about a half pound of those sharp provolone-stuffed olives, too.

About 20-30% of my Christmas gifts for family and friends this year came from Open House. I really could have found something for anyone in that store. Fun, unique and quirky gifts were purchased for my brother, and I found the most perfect travel book for my boyfriend's parents, who are always jetting off to another exotic locale.   The prices are definitely high, though I still felt they were fair for most items. I saw some things that could be found cheaper at a Homegoods type of store, but I wasn't really there for those types of things anyway. I wanted unique and thoughtful gifts, and that's exactly what I found. Yay for shopping local!

The closer City Fitness on South Street gets to completion, the closer I get to giving my notice at Sweat on Walnut. We've had a good year, but with the temptation of brand new equipment and clean everything, Sweat can't compete.   I generally hit the gym anywhere from two to four times a week exclusively to run on the treadmills. I choose the same machine every single day - one that's closest to the windows and without a TV, which usually guarantees that I won't have to work out on top of anyone else. So when the guy who cleans the equipment tries to squeeze through the half-foot between my machine and the wall, instead of simply walking around to the next aisle, my personal space feels a little compromised. I'm sure he's a very sweet guy; he seems to know the whole neighborhood. But even if he were a professional hockey player, I'd want him to back up off me while I'm trying to get my run on.   Mini-rant aside, the bottom line is that the machines are mega-old, the equipment is old, the locker rooms look old... you get the picture. Sweat, you are on borrowed time.

I'm going to update my review to four stars after another successful shopping trip at Madewell. A necklace I had my eye on last time was on sale, but when I attempted to pull it off the rack, a whole bunch of them got tangled in the process. One of the sales associates spent several minutes untangling them for me, which was super nice.   In the meantime, I made my way to the back of the store, where sale items were being additionally discounted another 40%. I tried on a handful of tops and decided to get two of them. Both are pretty unique and I have a feeling I'll be getting a lot of wear out of them this season.   There were several bags and shoes that also grabbed my attention, but the prices in that department are a little steep. I did score a $10 off online card with my purchase so perhaps I'll take a gander to see what's on sale.

I ordered delivery from Square on Square one day this week just before noon. Though the food delivery websites stated that the only option at the time was for pick-up, I called the restaurant and they confirmed that they could deliver. So, keep that in mind if you want delivery.   I ordered a quart of wonton soup and chicken with spicy garlic sauce. The food was very tasty, and definitely better quality than some other Chinese take-out spots, but also more expensive. The chicken portion was on the smaller side though I did still get two small meals out of it, since I also had the soup.   I'll definitely give these guys another shot the next time I'm craving Chinese - would love to try some of their other options.

A nightcap (or two) at the garden bar on a perfect summer night is about as magical as it gets in Philadelphia. After dinner in Queen Village, we decided to take a stroll and grab a drink, when we realized how close were were to Talula's. There were only a few people left at the bar when we arrived, and soon it was just the two of us.   The cocktail list is full of refreshing options for summer. I tried their take on a Moscow Mule - it was tasty, but I do wish it was served in a copper mug. Drinks are pricey, with most in the $11-$15 range. That adds up quickly! Our bartender was great, and happy to answer questions. I'm really jonesing to return for a romantic dinner on the patio. Talula's is definitely in the running for my birthday dinner later this summer!

A group of family and friends and I had a really great experience at Firebirds in Moorestown in early December. We arrived right around 4pm, the beginning of happy hour (which lasts until 7, by the way - heck yes!), and sat at some high top tables by the fire. The bartender was our server and she was great about prompt drink orders and water refills throughout our stay.   Happy hour specials are pretty solid, and we ordered several rounds of drinks and a bunch of apps to share. Favorites were the soft pretzels with beer cheese and chicken tenders with all the sauces they have available because your girl right here loves some sauce options.   We did notice that the buns for our sliders were really hard and we mentioned something to our server about it. The manager came over to chat with us and graciously sent out another plate of chicken tenders and removed the sliders from our check. Such a nice gesture and definitely gave this place points in my book. I'm sure we'll all return for another happy hour sesh in the future!

I keep getting prompted to write a review for Barcelona since I checked-in there during my Labor Day weekend trip to St. Louis. But honestly, my experience didn't go too far beyond chatting with the cute young bartenders and downing far too many shots of high-end tequila with my sister from another mister, Aimee K. The bar was a pretty lively spot on a Saturday night and the food that went by looked good, though we didn't order anything. The bathrooms were clean. Next time I'm in St. Louis, I'll return to Barcelona and I'll actually get some food to go along with my tequila.

This super cute market is located too close to me that I have only been once. I'm going to rectify that situation, especially now that I know they have a small but comprehensive selection of foodstuffs packaged to-go, veggies, coffee (I'm 99% sure it was my love, La Colombe), baked goodies and a varied menu great for lunch or dinner. There's also seating downstairs, which seemed to be a popular choice on the day of my visit.   I ordered an egg white breakfast burrito which was perfectly-sized and had a nice distribution of all ingredients. The salsa was served on the side, which saved me from any burrito mishaps. I'd probably ask for an extra side next time, since I eat everything breakfast-y laden with either salsa or ketchup. Can't wait to check out the other menu items, and pick up some of that delish-looking chicken salad to go!

I've only stopped by Tredici Enoteca for after-dinner drinks, but I can tell it's about to become one of my favorite spots. The wine selection is carefully curated and prices range from moderate to indulgent. I had a glass of the most fantastic verdicchio from the cruvinet and followed that up with some fabulous sparkling rosé.   The restaurant is larger than it appears from the outside, which I was happy to see, since I keep hearing how popular this place has become already. I really loved the sleek, upscale vibe, and I felt like I was in another city. Can't wait to return for a bite and many more glasses of wine!

Oh how I wish my pants had an elastic band.  Just finished brunch with 8 friends at Cafe Lift and it was gut-bustingly delicious.  Since they don't take reservations, I arrived early to see if I could get a table in the works for our large group.  By the time everyone arrived, we were seated without a problem and popping bottles of champagne for mimosas (it's byo, by the way).  Our server was efficient and kept the oj coming.  I ordered a fritatta with pancetta, sauteed onions, roasted red peppers and gorgonzola.  In an effort to curb calories somewhere in the meal, I asked for egg whites.  This was met with some hesitation (something about the fritatta not rising with only egg whites), so I asked for all the same ingredients in an egg white omelet.  When breakfast arrived soon after, my egg white frittata was indeed on the plate... so not sure what all the rising business was about, but it was fantastic!  Whole grain toast and potatoes were served alongside.    9 people left absolutely stuffed for under twenty bucks a person.  I will definitely be back!

I'm still going with the old A-OK for Fado. It's not a place that would become a destination on a regular night out, but when I revisited last week for Marcello's Flyers Faithful event, I had a good time. The bathrooms are still kind of scrummy and haven't been updated since my previous visit, but the rest of the place is all right. The sound system was impressively loud. Maybe a little too much, but I guess it was better to be a tad too loud than not loud enough considering we were all playing a game.   Our server stopped by regularly and split checks without even being asked, which was appreciated. I munched on fried pickles and sipped diet coke so I don't have much to say about the food, although I did like their version of fried dill chips. This bar holds a definite spot in my past but I'm okay with a return visit from time to time.

This review is for Memphis Taproom's beer garden, which is one of my favorite places to hang in the summer. I've actually never even had a beer in Memphis Taproom itself, though I've heard great things about their food so I'll have to try it sometime. But in the warm months, there's nothing that's going to separate me from that garden. Well, maybe a torrential downpour in the middle of an otherwise sunny day.   Why would you go inside when you've got lots of picnic tables (partial shade in some areas but don't forget the SPF!), cans of craft beer (with beer tab recycling program!) and awesomely creative hot dogs (veggie dogs available upon request!). The canned beer is a rotating list, which rocks. The hot dogs offer something for everyone. On my recent visit, a friend and I shared a deep fried dog with sauerkraut, onions and mustard and a grilled dog with chili, cheddar and macaroni salad. Hiyoooo!

Noble's earthy tones and woodsy decor make me feel like I'm in a treehouse. A grown-up treehouse, of course, with refined food, inventive cocktails and interesting bartenders.   I've only had dinner there once, which was delicious, but I typically find myself at Noble for the cocktail scene. First of all, Christian Gaal is on staff, so you know the libations are for serious (although every 'tender there knows how to make an excellent drink).  Most recently I enjoyed a simple drink from the menu which consisted of Bombay gin, housemade tonic and lemon. It was effervescent and clean, exactly what I wanted. Now that the weather is showing signs of warmth, I imagine I'll be back quite a bit to take advantage of the open window seating from my city treehouse.

Free People is starting to take more of my money than Madewell, and that's saying something. My past couple experiences at this location have been great, with Sara upstairs helping me with outfit suggestions.   This store is always presented really beautifully, but as a savvy shopper, I rarely spend much time up front. Free People is notoriously expensive at full price but, once things go on sale, it's a whole new ballgame. I've found some great stuff in the sale racks, though you have to be prepared to really comb through as everything is squeezed together.   Finally, I'm obsessed with the reusable bags they give for purchases. I use these all the time over other reusable bags simply because they're so pretty.

Very cool venue in an inconspicuous area of Fishtown! I attended the inaugural Cooking Up Couture event at Front & Palmer on Friday night. The venue has several different areas which makes it perfect for a party that has to transition from cocktail hour to the main event. The decor was pretty industrial and open; brick walls, wood floors, exposed ductwork, etc. The only issue that stood out to me was the acoustics; the music and announcements seemed to echo around the larger room which made it hard to understand yet still extremely loud.    Because of the location, I probably wouldn't host an event with lots of out of town guests at Front & Palmer, though I'd absolutely host some type of cool function focused on city dwellers.

I've revisited this sweetgreen location a few times and haven't had any issues since my first experience early on. Last night I ordered the harvest bowl, which was delicious. I opted for dressing on the side and tried two different ones; I liked the curry yogurt for this particular salad a lot more than the balsamic vinaigrette. The salad was a nice size and all of the ingredients were very fresh and flavorful. Dinner was healthy but hearty, a combo I can get behind!

I can't really explain why I wasn't super satisfied with my experience at Llama Tooth, I just wasn't. The outside patio is gorgeous but it was like a graveyard on a perfectly nice Saturday afternoon. Besides our group of six, there were only two other tables occupied in the large space.   Krista P and I split a carafe of sangria, which yielded about four drinks total. With no guests in the restaurant and only a few outside, it took longer than expected for our round of bevvies to appear.   We didn't try anything from the food menu, so I can't comment there. I probably need to give Llama Tooth another chance... but with so many options in the city and limited funding, I'm not sure a return trip is in the cards.

I popped into Lost & Found over the weekend and walked out with two shirts for a little over sixty bucks total. The collection of tops, bottoms and dresses is small but nicely curated, and the sizing of the pieces seemed to be more in line with women's clothing than junior's clothing, which is often an issue with boutique stores. I also noticed that mostly everything I looked at was reduced in price. Not sure if I was just there during a sale or what, but I was happy.  The dressing rooms have super breezy curtains - be cautious! The mirrors are located outside the room and on a slant. The owner promised me that no one had ever returned an item due to false advertising in the slanted mirror! I tried my shirts on as soon as I got home and liked them just as much as I had at the store, slanted mirror or not. I'll definitely stop back in the next time I'm shopping in Old City.

Because my boyfriend is wonderful (and because I look like a scary Medusa when I wake up), he offered to pick up coffee and breakfast this morning. We pondered our options and settled on Healthy Bites to Go, which was a new one for me. After perusing the online menu, I noted that many items were not in fact all that healthy, but I brushed that thought aside as I selected my bacon, egg and cheese on an everything bagel.   At $7.50, it didn't come cheap, but boy was it delicious. The bacon was peppered on the edges and the cheese was actually a local cheddar. Delish. It was a bit heavy for my usual breakfast tastes but it will make for a perfect hangover meal at some point in the (near?) future.  Also, the coffee was great. A bajillion points for that. We'll return.

I finally made it to the Royal for dinner. Our Cuban spring rolls were tasty, but my boyfriend's chicken Frankie wrap was off-the-chain. In fact, it was so fantastic, I lost interest in my Caesar salad about half way through. The polenta croutons and somewhat odd sour cream dressing did nothing for me. My sister, who ordered the same thing, shared this sentiment, though she soldiered on. Fortunately, I was able to score multiple bites of the Frankie - soft lovash stuffed with curried chicken deliciousness. The fries alongside were hot, crisp and delicious, as always.  But the real stunner of the night? Truffled parmesan popcorn. It was so good, we debated getting another order to-go for our walk to the POPE (let the record state, we did not actually do this). Best thing pocket change can buy.

Central Park Corp. should file a lawsuit against this place for insinuating that their bagels are even close to something New York would produce. These things are balls of dough, some with seasonings. A toasted bagel is indistinguishable from one that isn't toasted. But if you ask for toasted, keep an eye out, because your "bagel" will sit on the counter until you have to ask for it. Terrible. If you want a real bagel, you must drive to North Jersey. One of the few things (I will admit) they do better.

I love this place, and I wish it was in my neighborhood!   While I don't get to the Fairmount area too often, I think Bar Hygge is worth a trip. From house-made brews to a thoughtful wine list, cocktails and impressive whiskey selection, they have libations covered.   The dinner menu is filled with surprises, like the build-your-own board. A handful of cheese and charcuterie options are there, but there are also tons of interesting selections like charred octopus, calabrian chili arancini, roasted sunchokes and much more. Great idea and super unique!  The rest of the menu offers a mix of elevated bar food and a nice array of entrees. There is an impressive use of vegetables across the menu and the descriptions sound really enticing. Though I only had a few bites from a board on my recent visit, I've got Bar Hygge at the top of mind for the next time I want to try something new and different for dinner.

My sister and I popped into Healthy Garden for lunch recently. The name implies that the business would be geared entirely towards healthy foods, but the menu read more like something from a diner, only with a lot of salad, juice and smoothie options. There were quite a few fried options available, and the restaurant itself looked like it had been a pizza parlor in a former life. So there's a lack of consistency across the board.   That said, the food itself was solid. We each had salads and juices. The juices were huge and priced really well for the size. The salads were also enormous and large enough for two meals. All ingredients were very fresh, and the dressings were great.   If I were in the area, I'd be down for some takeout but I probably wouldn't dine in again.

A five dollar cover and beat service on my last visit is the reason for my downgrade.  Cover charges are for places that make Arthur Kade feel special and shore bars.    Time is never the destination, yet it can be a viable option when you find yourself in the Midtown area without a plan (just not on Saturday night - see cover charge).  That's probably not the best description to give a place, but it's accurate for Time.

I recently had a working lunch at Rose Tattoo Cafe. The last time I had been there was about thirteen years ago with my college beau. At the time, Rose Tattoo felt romantic and the menu seemed exciting. On my recent visit, I was shocked by how little the place had changed, which made it feel and look extremely dated.   The menu didn't provide many exciting options. I had a crab cake sandwich with fries that was fine but nothing memorable. Our server, while nice, was slow and had several mixups. Rose Tattoo was better as a memory.

Excellent experience with illexotics on Sunday! I'd been meaning to take my orchid there for a while for some much-needed TLC. Over the weekend, I was gifted a funky new planter, which was the sign I needed to get over to East Passyunk.   The store is so cool; gorgeous plants everywhere, plus reptiles and amphibians (and some insects that I chose to ignore). The house chameleon, Blaze Blu, is so beautiful!   I was surprised by the activity going on at the store; there were quite a few people who were in and out during my brief visits to drop off and pick up. The guys who own the shop were so knowledgeable and pleasant!   I picked out a new planter for my orchid, and was given a selection of plants that would be a good fit for my other planter. The end result was even better than I hoped for; my orchid looks so amazing since being re-potted, and my new plant is a happy addition to my home. I will be returning for all my indoor flora needs from here on out!

I've used Philadelphia Flower Co. on several occasions and have always been very happy with my orders and the service I've received.   Before my wedding, I called to order arrangements for my mom/stepdad, dad/stepmom and fiancé's parents. When I asked if they delivered to NJ (where both sets of my parents live), they initially said no, but they made an exception since they are still relatively close to the city. The delivery charge was slightly higher, but worth it since I have been so happy with Philadelphia Flower Co. in the past.   All of the flowers arrived the next day as promised. I was worried at first when my mom revealed that she had not been home all day, but there was a note in the mailbox that the flowers were left with our neighbor. All of the arrangements looked great and everyone was happy to have flowers in the house for the big weekend. I will definitely continue to call Philadelphia Flower Co. whenever the need arises!

Swung through for lunch on Friday and was quite pleased with my chicken dol sot bibimbap. It didn't take very long before my number was called and I had a large sizzling bowl in front of me, with a side of that red spicy sauce to mix in, and some kimchee for a kick.   There were loads of veggies and nothing in the bowl was greasy. In fact, I'd suggest this as a solid option for a healthy lunch.

I seriously love this place.  The menu looks like a newspaper and there are 3 pages full of items for adults and one page for kids.  There are about thirty different varieties of grilled cheese, and breakfast is served all day, every day.  The best thing about their breakfast is that the menu deviates so far from the traditional fare on diner menus.  Last Saturday I had a "Farmer's Market" egg white omelet with Swiss cheese, herbs and tons of fresh veggies.  There were about 12 other original omelets featured, as well as a "create your own" option.  The wheat toast that came with my order was thick-cut and grainy.  In other words, bangin'.     There are also loads of salads, sandwiches, soups and platters to satisfy any craving.  My sister loves the Foghorn Country Chicken salad, and it's so big that I have never seen her finish it.   Last but definitely not least, there is a HUGE ice cream menu that puts the Friendly's version from my childhood to shame.

Definitely not a bad stop for all your craft beer needs. There's a pretty decent selection for both refrigerated and non-refrigerated bottles. Prices seem to be on the more affordable side when compared with other local shops, at least for the larger-sized bottles.   The woman working the counter didn't say very much while we were in the store, if anything at all. So if you're looking to have a conversation about the suds, or if you need a recommendation, I'd probably shop elsewhere. But if you're open to adventure or you know what you're looking for, this is a great spot.

Victory Beer Hall is where I end up most every time I'm at Xfinity Live. I love the great beer selection and the food menu is pretty large and covers all bases. But service ranges from decent to abysmal.   On a busy night before a game, our party received apps before drinks, and our server was nowhere in sight for long periods of time. Food usually comes out quickly, which is good if you are trying to get to one of the stadiums; the service is what slows things down.   I've had the buffalo chicken wrap, buffalo chicken salad, and various appetizers and everything has been great. It's the perfect place for junk food, but there are salads with grilled chicken for when you want to be healthy.  I've also seen live acoustic sets, which is always fun. Xfinity Live can be hit or miss but Victory is a hit most of the time.

Thank you, P'unk Burger, for providing quality, BS-free proteins, in a plethora of ways (on a bun, as a salad, with lettuce leaves) and with an abundance of add-on options, from sauce to cheese to veggies to fried things to proteins and everything in-between.   I thoroughly enjoyed my incredibly juicy burger with tomato, caramelized onions, guacamole, pickles and mustard, wrapped in lettuce, last week. I cannot wait to try some of the fries next time - they smelled incredible!   Friendly service. Cash only (ATM on the premises).

On weekend mornings, when the craving for a leisurely brunch strikes, there is only one place on my mind as of late: Royal Tavern.   The bar has a chill vibe with servers to match. They constantly come around with water or coffee refills, which are often necessary depending on how late the previous evening lasted. Food selections are solid and range from the sweet (homemade granola with lavender honey) to the savory (cubano omelet with pickle salad and breakfast potatoes).  Easily, my favorite thing about The Royal is their bloody Mary. It has the most incredible taste with just the right kick of spice, and is garnished with a spicy pickle spear and lemon and lime wedges. The bloody is also offered with bacon vodka, although I've never tried this version.  Brunch is served starting at 10am on weekends, which is on the early side compared to most other bar/restaurants. Oddly enough, I have never visited for any reason other than brunch. I'm going to have to rectify that very soon.

I'm so happy our favorite neighborhood cantina was able to give me a night off from cooking over the weekend. I'd been craving nachos so placing my order for those wasn't even a question. My husband ordered mahi mahi tacos and I ordered the steak tacos. We placed our pick up order through Caviar.   Soon after, the restaurant called to let us know they were out of steak, so they ran through the other options and I went with chorizo tacos. Our food was ready pretty quickly and my husband ran over to pick everything up. Everything was absolutely delicious, as usual, and we even had leftovers for the following day. While he was there, my husband saw that they are also offering to-go quarts of their delish margarita mix, so we may have to grab some this week for make-at-home drinks.   Wishing the very best for one of my favorite neighborhood businesses during this trying time. If you love nachos (and tacos, and guac, etc.), definitely give Los Camaradas a look for contact free delivery or pick up!

I had never even heard of this place until the other night when a friend suggested we go for a couple drinks and some appetizers.  The bar area was not very full for a Friday night, but Nola strikes me as more of a cozy little restaurant than a bar anyway.    We had oysters stuffed with crab meat and this Cajun shrimp thing with rice that was phenomenal.  I'd like to go back for dinner sometime to check out other items on the menu.  I never thought New Orleans-type cuisine would be for me, but the Cajun shrimp at Nola has me reconsidering.

My first experience at the Troc was a few weeks ago for the Old Dominion concert. I knew from reviews that drinks are served upstairs-only when the crowd is all-ages, so my friend and I headed up the steps where we were greeted with several long lines. Luckily, the lines moved relatively quickly and we were able to have a couple beverages before heading back downstairs to use the bathroom (another long line) and then secure our spot not too far from the stage.   The band sounded incredible and the acoustics were great. I was thrilled with the show since I've been waiting for this band to come around since the second I first heard them about a year ago. I love seeing an amazing band in a venue like this because the experience is so much more intimate and special. The only downside is that general admission crowds tend to be a little pushy. But hey, I'll take the bad with the good if it means I get to be up close with the musicians!

Should have checked the Yelp app first. Tsk, tsk.  At Nail Polish, $18 (plus tip) will get you a run-of-the-mill manicure, a beating while your nails dry (which they refer to as a massage), and wide-eyed comments and titters about your height, if you are a statuesque woman like myself. I'm 5'10" before heels and have no issues with my tall-ness, but I felt kind of like a circus freak with the number of questions I had to field in front of an audience while selecting my polish.   I actually had to walk outside and catch a breath of fresh air while waiting for my friend's mani to finish up. This was probably the least relaxing manicure experience of my life.   Also, what is up with the mini-convenience store going on along the wall? Pregnancy tests and sample-sized shampoos were among the items available for purchase.

If they were to coexist on a school yard, Primo Hoagies would be the ass-kicking bully to dorky Wawa.  Blasphemous?  Perhaps, but the quality of breads, meats and cheeses are far superior at Primo to the limited selection at Wawa.    Yesterday I went in to pick up hoagies before the Phils game.  The woman at the counter offered to set them up on a tray and then she threw in three sides of extras without me even asking (pickles, banana peppers and sweet peppers).  For $35 (including a bag of chips), I fed five hungry, somewhat intoxicated adults and had leftovers for after the game.  Minus one star only because orders are occasionally messed up.  This only happened to me once but my boss refuses to go there because it happened to her a bunch of times.

I'm going to be straight with you. I am not usually a fan of frozen yogurt. It just doesn't do for me what ice cream or even water ice can do. But after several visits to The Igloo, my mind has been changed.   The Greek frozen yogurt is really, really good. I don't like plain frozen yogurt, but I like The Igloo's version. With some cookie crumbles on top, it's perfect. And something like 125 calories per serving. Just be mindful of that serving size while utilizing the single-size, serve-yourself bucket. I get the purpose of said bucket at a store that prices things out based on weight, but a single serving of fro-yo literally looks like... well, a drop in a bucket.   Another thing I like about this place is that they aren't just frozen yogurt. They also serve a couple types of gelato, and water ice is on the agenda for this summer. The owners are super friendly and really care about their customer feedback. I'm so glad this place is in my neighborhood!

I just realized that I never updated my review as I said I would after having a chance to dine in the restaurant. Well guess what? I had a meal at Los Taquitos de Puebla and if I took anything away from the experience, it was that this place is simply not for me.   The restaurant was very quick-serve, get in and get out, but that doesn't excuse trash on the floor. I'm a big believer in putting your best foot forward and that is possible even without fancy decorations or a big budget. Cleanliness is next to godliness, mis amigos.   There are still things to like: real coke in glass bottles, ridiculously spicy and flavorful salsas and the traveling tacos al pastor stand seen at farmers' markets and food truck gatherings. I dig these guys for street food but that's about it.

I took myself to the new AMC Dine-In on Monday to see Little Women. I bought my ticket online the night before, which was super easy. That said, I'm glad I arrived early, because the line for concessions was long and it didn't move very fast. My medium popcorn and drink came to sixteen dollars and change. Obnoxious.  Concessions aside, the theater was great. My seat was comfortable, and I loved the added heat feature! Also, super nice to have a little table with cup holder, so I didn't have to keep the popcorn in my lap.   I love some of the older, local theaters in the city, but they can't exactly compete with these comfy seats and large screens. AMC Fashion District has definitely earned a spot in my movie theater rotation!

A second meal at Talula's Garden was enjoyable, though I still believe four stars is appropriate. While some items soar, others leave me wanting. And at prices like Talula's, I'd hope for my socks to be knocked off. That said, the place certainly doesn't hurt for business. We saw a two top get turned away for not having reservations on a notoriously slow night. So people are clearly loving the place.   As was the case last time, the restaurant's decor was warm and comfortable, and service was perfect. We started with a fall cheese plate, which was really nicely done. The mushroom soup looked beautiful, but the creamy broth lacked the rich flavor I expected.   My skirt steak entree was very good, with vinegary cipollini onions, broccoli and crispy potatoes. One thing I will say about Talula's is that the portions are generous. I couldn't finish my entree.   For dessert, we shared the fig pudding, which is topped with butterscotch sauce and served with goat cheese ice cream. It's not the prettiest dessert, but on first taste I was absolutely hooked. One of the better desserts I've had in a while.

My wonderful boyfriend ran around town on Sunday picking up supplies for the days we'd be stuck inside because of the storm. Magpie was one of his stops. He grabbed a chorizo chili pie, some gouda and squash pie and a bag of pie fries with pumpkin dip.  The pie fries were totally addictive. What a delicious sweet and savory snack! Genius idea. The pie crust is the best part of pie, afterall.  We heated the savory pies up for lunch and both were very good. However, there was a leafy herb in the gouda/squash pie that totally overpowered the other flavors. I was not a fan of that at all but the rest of the pie was good once I pulled the herb pieces off. Still, I'd probably opt for something else next time. The chorizo chili pie was delish and came topped with corn chips and cheddar cheese. A side cup of sour cream was included for a nice touch.  I'm a fan and I'd love to try more of what they have to offer!

A friend and I hit up Jet Wine Bar for happy hour on a Wednesday. We were actively avoiding the Center City Sips establishments in hopes of bar seating and a quieter atmosphere. With only a few other people besides ourselves, we got just that.   House wines are $5 during happy hour but I'd recommend navigating to other selections for bolder flavors. Still, the house white was crisp and refreshing.   Complimentary breadsticks (baked by local coffee bar/bakery Nook, as indicated on the menu) were crunchy, slightly salty and totally satisfying. We shared a cheese and charcuterie plate which we ordered with truffled goat cheese, mimolette (on special), speck and sopressata. The plate also came with spicy cashews, apple slivers, olives, grapes, quince paste, and a few thin slices of bread. I've been spoiled after working at Sycamore so I'd love to see a spicy mustard and some honey in addition. Otherwise, the plate was lovely and we enjoyed it a lot.   After chatting with the owner and checking out the loungey area downstairs, I could easily see myself returning to hang out in either area.

Awesome: - The main floor is a piano bar. - The second floor is a dance party with great tunes. - The walls of the dance floor are mirrored (check out my bad self and these moves like MJ!).  The not so cool:  - No glasses of water, only bottles for purchase. Which leads me to... - Peeps be rip-roarin' wasted on you name it. Hence the charge for water. So try not to get dehydrated while working up that sweat, and if you do, save a few extra dollars. Why?  - Cash only.

I never intended to write a review update for my dermatologist, but when I looked up the address to confirm and saw Jon D.'s review, I reconsidered.  When I last described my experiences with Alta almost a year ago, I actually was not "kidding."  In fact, I returned yesterday for my annual and my experience was fine.  When I arrived to a crowded waiting room, everyone on the staff had a pleasant demeanor and paperwork was processed quickly.  Although the wait time was longer than expected, a TV tuned to NBC's coverage of the Phils provided a nice distraction.  Once inside an exam room, I did not have to wait long for the doctor, and he was personable yet professional as always.       I have recommended this practice to countless friends and family members and I will continue to do so because of the quality of care I receive on every visit.    One last note, the office will be moving to another building in the area sometime before the end of the year.

My family have been loyal customers to various Bobby Chez locations for years. I'm excited to have a location in Delran that's easily accessible whenever I'm in the area to visit family.   The crab cakes are pricey and they seem to get smaller and smaller as the years go by. I typically buy one each for me and my husband but it never really feels like enough, though we love pairing the crab cakes with the mashed potatoes and have tried a bunch of the other sides as well.   Some of the other entrees have been hit or miss. The chicken parm we had was very tough and we were not fans. My sister said she had the same experience with Bobby's chicken parm and no longer buys it. More recently, I tried the buffalo shrimp and those were a hit. I will for sure look for those again next time I'm in the shop.

I'm still a fan but my lunch at CTH today was lackluster. I requested a Caesar salad with grilled shrimp and was told that they no longer have shrimp. Odd but okay. I ordered chicken instead. The chicken was sliced on top of the salad and it looked nice, but after moving the pieces around, most of them had layers of fat running through them. Layers of fat running through chicken. Clearly whoever prepared the salad saw this, so I wasn't sure why it was sitting on my plate. No one eating a salad would eat a piece of fatty chicken.  Fortunately, my boyfriend's margherita pizza was pretty tasty, and they had Deschutes Mirror Pond Pale Ale on tap, which I had discovered earlier in the week. Next time I have a meal at City Tap I'm going basic and sticking with pizza or a salad without any added protein.

Philly Pretzel Factory can't have five stars, because my favorite soft pretzels of all time come from a small mom and pop in NJ. However, Philly Pretzel does serve up a tasty twist, with consistency across their locations. The fact that they were open on Thanksgiving morning until 1pm to provide my homemade beer cheese dip with a vessel (in the form of delicious, salty rivets) was a total lifesaver.

Overall, I'm a fan of Zio's. Their pizza is great and they have enormous salads that can serve multiple people or be split for two meals.   I popped in the day after Thanksgiving to grab a to-go salad - my usual, Greek with grilled chicken. I got it home and the salad looked great. And I love that they serve fresh garlic knots and bread on the side. Unfortunately, the chicken was really rubbery and I had to pick around it, which really only left me with veggies and dressing.
