Valanni, you little devil!  When did you go getting all chic to die?!  I mean, I knew you had a facelift since the last time I dined with you but I didn't know you had a full body restoration.  You look fabulous!  While we only stopped in for a drink after dinner, I was impressed.  The decor is stylish, the music was great and my mojito was delish.  Best of all, it had a rock candy garnish!!!!  I tend to get crazy excited over the little pleasures in life and this was no exception.  My girlfriends had sangria and said it was excellent.  Can't wait to come back and try the eats as well!

I'm bumping Nordstrom Rack up to four stars. During my visit last week, I looked down at my watch and realized I had already spent two full hours browsing the store and trying on clothes and shoes. Two hours of my life!  There was a lot more variety with brands than my previous visits, and I actually had to force myself to put some things back so that I wouldn't spend a fortune. I walked away with some totally hot Donald Pliner heels that I imagine will get a lot of mileage on the dance floors of Las Vegas in a few weeks.
Whole Foods: The only time cooking dinner becomes more expensive than going out to dinner.   But they have a taco bar now!

I'm bumping up to four stars as a result of friendlier service, pitchers of water and bottomless coffee. Today I met a friend for lunch and ordered a whole wheat everything bagel with veggie cream cheese, tomato and bacon, plus a cup of coffee. The total was around ten bucks, which is still pretty expensive, but since it was lunch and not breakfast I didn't mind. There are now pitchers of ice water with lemon, which I'm happy to drink over paying for a bottle of water.   My bagel sammie was absolutely delicious, and it came with slices of fresh cucumber on the side, which I then stuffed inside to add a little more crunch and flavor. Again, this isn't an every day type of place, but for a really tasty bagel and a cute place to have lunch, it's solid. Also, the wood burning oven smells like a campfire. Who doesn't love that?

There's a lot to like about Plenty. For example, the barista/server who was working while I was there this week, Michael, was really great. Friendly, helpful, didn't make me feel like I was annoying even though I was there for a while - pretty much everything you'd want in a barista.   My latte was superb. My food was... eh. I used to love sandwiches from Plenty but I just find them so lackluster now. Ingredients aren't really plentiful and I often find myself hungry again a few hours later. I do like that their chicken salad is made with minimal mayo and some mustard mixed in. I just wish there was more than two tablespoons of it on a sandwich!   Downgrading to four stars. I still love Plenty the cafe, but Plenty the restaurant isn't really wowing me.

Am I total tool for admitting that I actually like this place?  I'm not talking every night of the week, but I do have fun whenever I end up here.  Maybe it's because I'm usually half in the bag already, maybe it's because I'm reminded of my college nights in frat party basements or maybe it's because I'm just so damn relieved that the bathrooms themselves are way cleaner than the aforementioned frat party basements.  The point is, Drinker's always provides an experience that is both cheap and fun.  They also provide the Beastie's Licensed to Ill cd in their jukebox.

I had an Uber Eats credit and we were craving pizza, so decided to give LaScala's a try. I'd been to one of their other locations for a bridal shower before, and was really impressed with the food.   Our experience overall was solid, though delivery took a lot longer than the quoted time. I called the restaurant at one point after our delivery window to check on the status. They told me it was on the way and, sure enough, the pizza arrived about ten minutes later.  We ordered a caesar salad, large classic pie, and small white spinach pie. This was more than enough food for two meals plus a couple extra slices. The pizza was best after a quick reheat in the oven; I especially enjoyed the white pizza.

To be honest, I had avoided K'Far because I'd heard about long lines and I am not about the line life. One weekday morning I was out for an early walk with my husband and we ended up in K'Far's vicinity, so decided to pop over. There were only a few people waiting for orders so the timing worked out perfectly!   We ordered two egg and cheese Jerusalem bagel sandwiches, a hot coffee and a tehina chocolate chip cookie. My only wish was that I had the foresight to order more sweets to-go. The egg sandwiches were perfect! The bread was absolutely incredible, and the egg to cheese ratio was just right. The chocolate chip cookie that we shared at home later was delicious.   The good news is you can also place pick-up orders online which will soften the blow if there are any major lines happening. I'll be scheming my next visit for sure!

I love Nordstrom Rack, but I was skeptical over the new location in Center City, because I assumed that everything would be picked over by the lunch crowd. Not so, as I was pleased to discover on my visit today.   The store is still very new but I was impressed by the tidiness and selection, especially with regards to the lingerie department. While I will likely favor the Cherry Hill location, it's nice to have the option to shop the Rack in the city as well.

I finally made it to 10 Arts. Well, I made it to the lounge, anyway. It was a Thursday, later in the night and we arrived to a pretty lively scene. A DJ was situated in a corner and ladies were dolled up like it was prime time on Saturday.   Our threesome grabbed one of the only high tops available, and we perused the bar menu while ordering martinis and Manhattans. While I personally found the prices to be on the high side, we were undeterred as we had already imbibed and on empty stomachs no less. We ordered some oysters, some pretzels and a flatbread pizza.   The oysters were so perfect, so delicious, that we ordered another round. At $3 a pop, they add up quickly. The pretzels, while tasty when dunked in the spicy mustard and cheese sauces, were probably not worth their eight dollar price tag.   I will definitely return for another swanktified evening, but more likely for happy hour or the final drink of a night out.

You guys, Chick's is not playing around when it comes to breakfast sandwiches. They are $6 or $7.50, depending on whether you want meat. And hot damn these sammies are legit!   You have a choice of how you'd like your eggs, type of cheese, type of bread, and choice of breakfast meat. There are other toppings available for an additional cost.   I had scrambled eggs, American cheese and bacon on an english muffin. I ate the sandwich around 9am and wasn't hungry again until 3pm. I probably could have split it into two meals but it was so delish I polished off the whole thing! My husband, whose brilliant idea it was to get the sandwiches, was a little miffed that the english muffins weren't properly toasted and crunchy (they were warmed on a flat top). I normally would share this opinion but actually thought the muffin tasted great as-is because it was so fresh!   100% getting after these sandwiches again in the near future!

I don't know if Uber's standards for their UberX drivers and vehicles has lowered to keep up with demand in Philadelphia, but it sure seems that way. In the past few weeks alone, I've been picked up in several shoddy cars, including some that reeked of recently-extinguished cigarettes. I've also had at least one driver with questionable hygiene.   Additionally, about three in four drivers are not familiar with the city enough to forego their gps. The major problem with this is that the gps system Uber uses has lately been way off in terms of accuracy. It's super rare that I get into a car and the most direct route is used. If I'm not paying attention, I could end up several blocks past where I should have been let out or turned onto a more direct route. I thought part of the Uber experience was to sit back, relax and let the driver do the work? Now, I'm often the navigator in a dumpy car no better than one of the city's cabs, the only advantage being that UberX is still slightly cheaper. I am over it. Perhaps it's time to give Lyft a chance afterall.

We revisited Anastasi for takeout over the weekend, and I'm so glad we did! The pasta dishes were jumping out at us this time, so my husband ordered the linguini with mussels (red sauce) and I went with the lobster pasta, which came not only with a very generous portion of lobster tail, but also jumbo lump crabmeat, shrimp, and scallops, in a blush sauce.   We started with clams casino which I have to admit I'm extremely picky about. My Grandmom's recipe is my gold standard and I've yet to find a restaurant that comes close. My husband thought they were good, but I'd probably opt for something else as a starter in the future.   The pastas were priced in the twenties and thirties which I was fine with for a nicer meal on the weekend. However, the portions were sized to feed multiple people! My husband's linguini and mussels came in a small bucket while my lobster pasta arrived in a small aluminum tray, like the ones you see for catering! We enjoyed two hearty dinners plus one lunch thanks to these generous portions. Definitely looking forward to more Anastasi nights!

I was looking forward to checking out the bar at William Douglas for their 9 p.m. happy hour, which is featured on their website.  When I arrived, the scene was surprisingly dead for a Friday night.  I took a seat at the bar and inquired about the happy hour menu, and was informed that it was no longer offered and the website "had not been updated in months."  The bartender suggested that I try McCormick & Schmick's next door, which did have a 9 p.m. happy hour.  I text messaged my friends the change in plans and off I went.

Absolutely love having Bud & Marilyn's as an option when flying domestic in Philly! I popped in recently for a meal before a flight and was happy to see a wide array of options. I ordered the huevos rancheros, which came with vegetarian chorizo. I'm trying to expand my horizons with meatless meals and this seemed like a great opportunity to try something new. The dish was absolutely delicious!   Service was a little on the slow side considering the airport location, and a cup of coffee cost almost four bucks. Nonetheless, it's great to see PHL stepping up its game in the food and bev department. Fingers crossed the international terminal gets some love, too!

I've got mad love for Green Aisle. Where else can you get all the trimmings from your favorite spots around the city and suburbs? We're talking creamy hummus from Zahav and those gorgeous meringues from Fond, locally farmed meats, produce and cheese, Severino pasta and Market Day Canelé, to name a few.   And let's not forget their killer cocktail mixers. A generous friend sent us a crate full of cocktailing goodies from Green Aisle, including several types of bitters, syrups and tonics. The crate was personally delivered to my doorstep by Adam, one of the brother duo who own the place.   About those brothers. They're about as helpful, charming and fun to talk to as it gets. If you haven't been to Green Aisle yet, go check out the merch and strike up a conversation while you're at it. It's one of the best things to do on Passyunk Ave.

I've been hitting up Le Pain Quotidien fairly regularly and have grown really fond of the place. The staff are all super friendly and they know the menu well. I love that the nutritional info is listed on every menu item - it makes choosing a healthy meal much easier. The warm grains bowl with goat cheese is decent, but I really love the vegetable quiche which is served with a side salad topped with the most delicious vinaigrette.   For a quick and easy meal, cup of tea or coffee or even a glass of wine (they have a small but solid selection of beer, wine and cocktails), LPQ works.

I was super pumped to try World Wide Burrito last week as I love burritos and anything even remotely resembling Mexican food (traditional or Americanized - give it all to me)! I ordered the Aztec and it was huge and super delicious. The chicken inside was nicely seasoned and tender. I loved the ingredients of the Aztec - they all blended together perfectly. The fact that the burrito never fell apart or got too messy while I was eating it was also awesome. As for the adorable guys who run the truck? Icing on the cake.

Finding myself in the area with some time on my hands, I popped into Paper Source to pick up some cards, and came away super impressed not just by the variety of cards but also the array of small gifts. I could have spent a boatload in that store, but I held back and picked up just what I needed: a couple special occasion cards and a pack of cute thank you cards. Total was just over twenty bucks which is probably the cost of four cards at the drugstore.  I spent a few minutes chatting with one of the employees (possibly the manager?) and learned about some workshops that they host at the store. I'm considering signing up for one in the near future. I'm not super crafty but I would like to spruce up my skills a bit and this seems like a fun way to do it.

My first visit to Lovers & Madmen was quite a while back (March of 2010, actually). I loved the name and the fact that re-runs of The Muppets were playing on the TV. I didn't love the coffee, this I distinctly remember.   Fast forward a couple years and I found myself at Lovers & Madmen again for a meeting. It was super hot outside on the day of my visit, and I walked into the cafe and immediately realized that there was no AC flowing. Worse, the open windows weren't getting any breeze at all, and the huge front window seemed to serve only as a magnifying glass to the sun. With no available tables, I sat on one of the shoddy, sunken couches and felt my body heat rise.   My cup of coffee was from the end of a pot, so there were little dregs of beans floating about my cup. The barista offered to top me off before I left, since I had only received about 3/4 of a pour, but I passed. I'm not sure what type of coffee they brew, but I'm not a fan.

This might be a record for updated reviews, but RAH is my neighborhood bar and it's been a while since my last update. With the recent change in chefs, now seems like a good time.   The food going on at Resurrection right now is fantastic. I used to hate the constant menu changes but I've grown to love them because it keeps things fresh and different. The 5-7 weekday happy hour is great but even better is the 6-10 Sunday happy hour. That's a dangerous way to end the weekend.   Bar snacks are priced around $8-10 each. We ordered three on our recent visit (kale salad, cavatelli and soup) to share. We polished those off and had to check out the menu again, this time opting to share a "big plate" of mushroom risotto. The risotto was delicious but not at all what I would consider a big plate. Multiple dishes add up quickly here, so if all you really want is a snack, you're in for a delicious treat. But if you're hungry, I'd recommend selecting something from the sandwiches section or the fried chicken plate, which is plenty of food.

I'm not going to go jumping for joy over this post office or anything, but its parking lot alone makes me very happy that its our default location. How many other post offices in the city have a parking lot? Maybe they all do, I actually have no idea, but I'm thinking probably not.   The counter closes at noon on Saturdays but during the week it's open until at least 5. There's rarely a line of more than one or two people, and the woman who typically works the counter is efficient, if a little brusque. But hey, as long as I can get my stamps and packages in a timely manner, that's just fine with me.

While I probably wouldn't choose this place as a dinner destination, I did have lunch here at least once every two to three weeks when I worked nearby.  The food is definitely a big step up from your standard take-out places.  It's got more of a P.F. Chang's vibe to it (meaning, stir-fried white meat chicken rather than random chicken pieces that are battered and deep fried to disguise their true identity).  I always alternated between the cashew chicken and the garlic chicken (not recommended if you plan on getting up close and personal with anyone for the rest of the day).    The Thai stuff I've tried is pretty good as well; particularly the chicken satay with peanut sauce and cucumber salad.    Bonus, you have the option of white or brown rice with your meal!

My man went out to run some errands on Friday and came home with a box of empanadas from a Jezabel's pop-up. We received two each of four different kinds and the box came with three side sauces/pickled veggies.   We heated up half the box for lunch on Saturday, but everything was so delicious that we decided to heat the rest and go all in! My favorites were the chicken with olives and beef with raisins, but the empanada with leeks was great, too. I especially loved the chimichurri sauce - I could eat that with everything! Looking forward to more empanadas in my future!

This store is a mecca for wine lovers ranging from sorority Boone's Farm novices to sommeliers alike.  There are rows and rows of grape goodness, all laid out in idiot-proof sections.  The amount of choices might seem overwhelming, but there are tags throughout the store featuring wines of the week and employee favorites.  The friendly and knowledgeable staff members are always willing to help if you aren't sure what you are looking for or just need a great recommendation.    They also have a huge selection of beer and other liquor, as well as every mixer or add-on you could possibly imagine.  To top it off, prices are significantly better than other area stores.

This was my first time trying an Orangetheory class in a different city, and I loved it! The studio was just about to celebrate their one year anniversary and still had that brand new, clean vibe. I registered online and was happy to see that I didn't have to pay any additional fees on top of my current 4x/month membership.   As usual, the class was challenging and I felt very satisfied with my workout. The instructor was motivating and clear with explanations. I'm excited to try other studios when I travel because of this experience!

With so many great reviews, I was sure Custard & Cakes Creamery was going to be awesome. However, their frozen custard just couldn't compare with the kind I grew up with at the Maple Shade custard stand. The vanilla was super light in consistency and didn't have much flavor. However, the hard ice cream I got to try was pretty tasty. If there's a next time, that's definitely what I'll get.   Prices are more than fair and probably the lowest I've seen at any local ice cream shop.

This review is going to be short and sweet because it's all about donuts and basically everyone knows that Beiler's has some of the best around. Personally, I like to keep it simple with my sweets. So I'm partial to the chocolate-frosted, cream-filled donuts or basic glazed/frosted. If you do like different flavors and toppings, there's definitely plenty of those to choose from as well.   The donuts are perfectly sized so you can enjoy one for breakfast without feeling like you blasted through half a day's calories. An excellent treat for these trying times!

This bar is located at the end of my street and I've always eyed it suspiciously.  It has a dive-y look to it, and I never see anyone going in or out.  It wasn't until a friend in the area told me that I would have to check it out as a rite of passage for living so close by that I resolved to stop in for a drink.    A few friends and I decided to swing by after dinner on a Saturday night.  I was shocked to walk through the doors and into a pretty vibrant bar scene.  Sure, a few of the women looked like they were waiting for the Rock of Love Season 4 audition, but the overall vibe was a lot better than anticipated.  A round of four beers cost under $11, and rumor has it that the bar food is pretty decent.

I personally found this Maggiano's to be on the dank side compared to how I remembered the Philadelphia location. Granted, I haven't been to that Maggiano's in years but I always enjoyed the food, service and even the atmosphere. Cherry Hill Maggiano's was not feeling very lively on a Sunday afternoon, but I guess that shouldn't be too surprising considering the summer months and mass exodus to the shore each weekend.   My friend and I kicked things off with a glass of wine and some warm bread with olive oil. We shared the mussels in white sauce, the Maggiano's salad and a special salad with avocado, shrimp and crab. The mussels were pretty good, but I felt both salads were overdressed. Ask for dressing on the side if you're sensitive to that sort of thing. Despite this, both salads were crisp, fresh, and with just the right amount of toppings (although the shrimp and crab salad probably could have used more lettuce).   This isn't a bad option while at the Cherry Hill Mall, but I wouldn't go out of my way, either.

I'm in love with a bar.  There's a waiting area with a shoe shine.   There are candelabra with tall red candles.   There's a Lee in a perfectly fitted cranberry velvet suit.   Original prescriptions for alcohol during the Prohibition Era are framed and mounted to the walls.   Delicious cocktails that taste far more complex than their basic ingredients would indicate are creative and certainly make for fun conversation (new favorite drink: tequila with strawberry).  Bartenders are stylishly dressed, with excellent manners and service to match.  Yep, it's love all right.

This location of OCF is huge and perfect for a meeting or just a hard core work sesh. The employees are friendly (especially the tall guy with the beard who also had to clean up our unfortunate water spill - sorry again and thank you for being so sweet about it!).    I ordered some eggs scrambled with veggies, which came with some potatoes and toast. This is exactly the type of healthy but filling breakfast I like to eat and I was happy to see this option on the menu. The menu here is definitely much larger than some of the smaller OCF locations.   Coffee was great; it's $1 to refill your cup. I can't think of anything I didn't like about my experience so I'm going with five stars for OCF!

Went to dinner here on a double date.  My friend and I are total food snobs and love going out to eat together.  We selected this restaurant because it was part of the Dining out For Life program, in which a good percentage of the check is donated towards AIDS research.  We might not have gone here otherwise, with so many other options in the city.  BUT, thanks to the program, I'm so glad we did!  Everything from the staff, the drinks, the bar, the decor and most importantly, the food was absolutely awesome.  We will definitely be back!

The best thing about this Starbucks is seeing the line of cars wrapped around the building as you walk inside to no line. The worst part? Waiting because everyone working is handling all the requests from the drive-thru.   Other than that, it's an average Starbucks with the usual offerings.

Ultimo now has sandwiches from American Sardine Bar. You could get the popular turkey sandwich... but you should really go rogue and get the vegan potato salad sandwich, which is far superior. Take it home, pop it in the toaster oven to warm it up, and it's even better.

My family has this weird tradition.  Every year on the day after Thanksgiving, we go to Bertucci's for lunch.  Forget the 50 lbs. of leftovers in the fridge, we want pizza!  So off we went, this time to the Mt. Laurel location.    Our server brought out piping hot rolls, which were really good, and plenty of oil for dipping.  The salad bowl had only enough salad for about two people, but we asked for another and rationed it out.    Our pizzas, the silano and shrimp bella napoli, came out soon after.  I didn't have any of the silano because I remembered the chicken being questionable from previous visits, but the shrimp bella napoli was really good.  Spicy red sauce with mozzarella and tons of shrimp on top made for a really good pizza.  Two carafes of sangiovese topped off the lunch.    I don't think I'd ever give Bertucci's five stars, but I always enjoy my visits.  I know what I like and what to stay away from, so I'm never disappointed.

YUM!  This spot has the best pizza by far in the Collingswood/Westmont/Haddonfield area.  I'm a big fan of their Sicilian style pizza~ and even my parents agree with me on this (they are very picky when it comes to good pizza)!   I give Finizio's 4 stars and not 5 because I'm not crazy about some of the other stuff on their menu, particularly anything with chicken.  They use the stuff that tastes like it's been frozen for 5 years and came out of a high school cafeteria... yuck.  The pizza will rock your world though, trust me!

One time, my adorable grandparents had us over to celebrate a birthday.  My grandfather excitedly announced that he had picked up a cake from ACME with buttercream frosting.  Mmm, buttercream frosting!  We sang, cut the cake and doled out the slices, but I eyed my piece suspiciously.  The frosting looked very much like that glorified Cool Whip ACME so loves to use in their bakery.    We all dug in but the confused reaction was instantaneous.  The frosting WAS the glorified Cool Whip kind! That's when someone picked up the box and read the made-up word, "bettercream."  My grandfather and his eyesight were had by ACME!    Flying Monkey's cupcakes are lovely to look at.  Unfortunately, they are too dry, and the frosting tastes like bettercream.

I was at a meeting nearby and needed an afternoon pick-me-up. I spotted the sign on the corner pointing to Gryphon Cafe so I ran across the street to check it out. The space is open and industrial-looking - a fun place for a meeting or to get some work done.   I had the cold brew and have to say I wasn't crazy about it. It could just be that it was my third coffee of the day so my body was trying to tell me something. It wouldn't stop me from going again to try another beverage. The baked goods looked amazing and the barista said they stock them from Machine Shop. The everything seasoning-topped bagels and breads looked delish.   There was also a big bowl of fresh fruit by the counter so I picked up a couple pieces for home. Solid coffee shop and I'd love to get back for another visit sometime.

I just walked out of lunch at Vicia and it was so great I had to jump on Yelp to talk about it. The restaurant is very attractive, with plenty of tables inside as well as on a covered patio (with space heaters). There is a smartly curated lunch menu which currently features a sandwich, a couple salads, a tartine and soup. You can pick two for $12 or three for $15. Such a great deal!   I opted for the ham sandwich and kale salad, plus a chamomile ginger spritz. Both of my selections were excellent! My husband had the sandwich and sweet potato soup, which was delicious as well.   My only regret is not having more time while we're in town to try dinner. Vicia is a gem!

Honeygrow is a local business that has really grown on me over the years. This particular location is one of the few healthy, fast-casual restaurants in the KOP Town Center, and I was grateful to spot it while in the area recently.   I ordered my usual salad, customized the way I like it. While I waited I saw several people swing in to pick up to-go orders. My salad was ready fairly quickly and I brought it over to the counter to grab some utensils. I noticed that the salt and pepper shakers were empty, which was weird since the restaurant was also empty at the time. One of the workers noticed me shaking away at an empty pepper shaker and he graciously offered to get more for me.   My salad was delicious, per usual. They have the best white balsamic vinaigrette! My only complaint is that I hate the bowls they use! I like to cut my salads and I can't do this in their bowls without toppling the whole thing. A minor gripe but it's something I notice every single time! Other than that, keep doing you, Honeygrow. I love having a healthy, local option!

This is my least favorite PJ's location.  Although it is the largest, and definitely the most popular, something about the vibe is just off for me.  Saturday nights always have a cover charge.  It's only $5, and I suppose this pays for the band, but I'd rather NOT see most of the bands they feature anyway.  Fortunately, the beer specials are consistent through all the PJ's locations, and $2.75 Blue Moon makes for a cheap night out.      An overcrowding of tables and chairs makes getting from one area to another quite challenging.  The bathrooms aren't the cleanest, despite an attendant, and the lines start to get long later in the night.   In closing, I'm a little cranky that I wasted a perfectly good Saturday night here.

Welcome to Philly, Halal Guys! I only sampled the eats from this super popular, NYC born-and-bred business for the first time at the October Yelper Party. I knew then that I'd be seeking them out once their Chinatown location opened, so imagine my excitement when they popped up on one of my delivery apps tonight!   I ordered the half chicken half gyro platter which came with lettuce, tomatoes, rice and pita, plus some of the hot and white sauce packets on the side. I also ordered a side of hummus for just a couple dollars more.   The food arrived and it was a gigantic portion and everything tasted delicious. I made the mistake of pouring the red sauce all over my food before trying it. Big mistake! That sauce is super hot and I ended up having to pull some of the sauce-covered pieces out of the bowl! Next time, I'll use this sauce sparingly and keep it to the side. My fault, for sure. The hummus was also delicious and there was an extra warm pita included as well. This will definitely become one of my go-to delivery spots.

After reading some awesome reviews and hearing so many great things after Yelp's Backstage Pass Party, I knew I had to cross town and check out Rybread. With our day off today, it was the perfect opportunity for me and the boy to check the place out for lunch.   The chalkboard of choices was extensive. Everything sounded so great but I was pretty committed to the Charlotte. Sadly, I made the unwise decision to switch to multigrain bread. This was sad because the bread got a little soggy with the pickles, honey mustard and tomatoes. My own fault, of course. Next time, I'll stick with the recommended bread option. The ingredients were all fresh and delicious; the price was right. Their counter staff was also very friendly.  The strawberry iced tea was delightful and I also got to take a coffee home after redeeming my check-in offer. I'll be returning soon to check another sammie off the list!

I was at The Prince Theater twice this week for Philadelphia Film Festival movies. Prior to this week, I had never set foot in the theater, so it was nice checking out something new (to me) in the city.   The multi-use theater is huge and offers stadium seating. Unless you were stuck in one of the very front rows for a movie, I don't think there is a bad seat in the house. Seating is definitely old school - don't expect luxurious accommodations - but it's fine for a movie or show.   My husband had popcorn on both visits and the bites I tried were good. He mentioned that they also sell wine, which is always a plus. I hope I have the opportunity to return to The Prince for future events!

Two stars because they have the drugs.  Three missing stars because once I started getting "the pill," I also started getting dirty looks from the pre-historic staff every time I picked them up.  Walgreens and I have been going steady ever since!

Did I REALLY just house an 830 calorie burrito?   According to Baja Fresh's website, yes I did.  Fuuuuuuuuuuuucccccckkkkkkkkk.  Not that I thought a pork burrito that weighed about the same as a newborn baby was going to be healthy, but the only toppings were pico and guac, so I thought I was still in reasonably safe territory.  Isn't pork called "the other white meat" because it's supposed to be good for you?  I'm clearly in some sort of holiday denial.    On the plus side, the burrito was pretty tasty so I'm bumping to two stars.  However, I'm not sure it was worth all the extra cardio it will take to burn that puppy off.  I should have re-read my first review before making such a poor hunger-based decision.

My girl Michelle and I had brunch here during our recent trip to Nashville (yep, Michelle squared - double trouble!). The bloody marys were great. We ordered a few oysters as well and our server did a great job describing them - they were on point. The only thing that bugged me is they arrived just after our mains. I hate when you try to course things out but then everything arrives at the same time!   My friend had "The Highway" - fried chicken on waffles. It looked great but she said the crispy breading kept coming off of the chicken. I pulled some random maneuver out of left field and played things safe with the "Southern Fried Egg Sandwich." It was good but not super memorable.   The restaurant is really pretty and definitely a classy brunch locale. There was live music (which I quickly learned is par for the course in Nashville) so that was a plus, too. All in all, The Southern Steak & Oyster is a solid spot!

Melissa P and I decided to check out Cafe Chismosa for a casual lunch/brunch on Saturday afternoon. With an outdoor table available in the sun, we were sold right away. The inside of the cafe is also super cute - bright and airy.   The menu is focused on Latin-inspired lunch and brunch items. I opted to keep my choices on the healthy side and was greatly rewarded with fresh, clean, flavorful food. To start, we shared the shrimp ceviche which was absolutely gorgeous and had loads of bright, tasty ingredients.   Next, I tried a smoked scallop salad with avocado and quinoa. Wow. I haven't stopped thinking about this salad since I had it, and I can't wait to go back and get it again ASAP. I'd never had smoked scallops before but they were perfect on this salad and the perfect match for creamy avocado.   I will happily go out of my way to patronize this wonderful business again.

Love my Photobot 3000 peeps! I've hired them for several large-scale events and they have always been great to work with - quick to respond to emails leading up and going above and beyond expectations at the events.   One of the things I like most about Photobot in particular is that they have the ability to customize the background screen for the photos. They have incorporated artwork that I used to promote my events and the end result was unique and festive.   Theresa and Scott are lovely to work with and I'd recommend them for any special event!

A friend and I swung by BSBH for a drink last week. We arrived during happy hour and requested outside seating from the friendly host. Draft beers were discounted for the happy hour special so we each ordered a brew. Our server asked if we'd like water and though we said yes, we never actually received it. No big as we were only there for one drink.   We also ordered the fried pickles which were okay, but didn't have much flavor. They tasted more like fried cucumbers than fried pickles; the briny taste of a pickle was not really detectable.   Based on this experience I'm going with three stars but I definitely want to get back at some point to experience more.

I must be missing something, because my first experience at Royal Izakaya was just okay. We went for dinner with friends recently and I wasn't blown away by anything I tried.   This is one of those restaurants where items come out of the kitchen as they are prepared. Great if everyone is on board with sharing, not so great when everyone has an idea of what they want to eat and it's all different. I waited a while before any of the dishes I ordered made it to the table.   I had some gyoza, wings, fried scallops (a special), tuna avocado roll and spicy tuna roll. Everything was okay but I wasn't overly impressed. In fact, I downright disliked the spicy tuna roll, which tasted really fishy to me - not the clean, fresh way tuna usually tastes.   I really liked the vibe of the bar area and am definitely up for another visit to see if maybe I was there on an off night for the kitchen.

Whoa, Fountain Porter, I owed you this review update! Since that very first experience six years ago, we've kept the tradition alive and hit Fountain Porter every year after purchasing our Christmas tree. This year was no exception, even if we had to get our burgers to-go.   This spot is easily one of Philly's best deals. Six bucks gets you a perfect cheeseburger. It's not fancy, but it is delicious. And three dollars for a hefty order of crispy fries? Sign. Me. Up. Don't forget to throw in a side of pickles, because Fountain Porter's are addictive and you'll want more than the two that already come with your burger.  Dinner for two, plus a nice tip, came to under thirty bucks. Can't beat it. Looking forward to our next pick-up!

Yum.  This diner is very close to where I live and was recommended to me ages ago by a friend in my town.  I went there for the first time this past weekend and will definitely be making return appearances.  Service was friendly and quick, which is exactly what one would expect at a good diner.  I was pretty particular about my egg white omelet and was so happy when it came out spot-on with my requests.  It was awesome.  The standard diner cake display had me practically drooling when I walked by... I'll definitely be back to hit that up one night when my self control is waning and I feel like being a fat kid.

Me 'N" Mo provided me and a friend with a very pleasant lunch experience last week. The menu is simple. It's a whole lotta meatballs served a whole lotta ways. Get them with pasta, on bread, or in a Sarcone's roll. Choose your type (beef, pork, veggie, and a couple other options), your sauce (again, several choices) and the way you want them served.   I opted to keep things traditional and went with the beef meatballs with marinara sauce on a roll with provolone cheese. Extra sauce on the side 'cause I like to get saucy. My sandwich was absolutely delicious and was served with a nice arugula salad alongside. Looking forward to my next visit!

Last week, I got takeout from Loco Pez for the first time since they opened in my neighborhood. I had the shrimp burrito and my husband got the vegan chorizo burrito. We also ordered chips and salsa.   When we arrived, everything was packaged and sitting on a table by the front door, so it was an easy, virtually contactless transaction. The burritos were delicious and I really loved the fresh pico de gallo, for which they provided a generous amount of chips. Also, they included three different types of salsas which was awesome. I'd happily order from Loco Pez again!

I resisted updating my review after my last experience at Villa Barone's Collingswood location, and wrote off my so-so meal as a fluke.  After lunch there today, I have come to the conclusion that the food is either not as good as it used to be or not as good as I thought it was.    Service has always been great, so there is absolutely no problem there.  My downgrade in stars comes simply from the food.  The last time I had dinner with some girlfriends, my chicken saltimbocca arrived with prosciutto that looked and tasted more like deli ham.  Additionally, I distinctly recall that the dish had a gray palor, which is neither inspiring or appetizing.   Today, while lunching with a friend, my gnocchi pomodoro tasted like bloated potato puffballs that had been floating around the pot for too long.  Even the zesty pomodoro sauce couldn't mask the dull flavor.  I feel like my downgrade to three stars is actually being generous, as my past two meals were hovering closer to two.  The fresh baked bread and kind service keeps me from going lower.    Villa Barone, get it together or I'm going down the street.  You know where.

This particular Taco Bell/KFC was clean and decorated for the holidays on my recent, random visit. I did think the service was much slower than most Taco Bell locations, however. Also, it was clear that whoever constructed my soft taco supreme did not care about the placement of the sour cream. It was sloppily located close to the edges of the taco shell - a taco faux pas. Still, for cleanliness and holiday spirit, I say three stars are in order.

I have to give a little review update shout out to the staff at Drinker's Pub. On my sister's wedding day, our entire bridal party rolled in unannounced to grab a round and several photos (my sister and her now-husband actually met at Drinker's, believe it or not!). The bartenders were cool, and the patrons didn't mind letting us take over the bar for a minute (literally - my sister and her husband posed on the bar with the rest of us around them).   It should also be mentioned that the drinks are CHEAP. I ordered a round of four or five drinks and handed the bartender a twenty before running to pose for a picture. I came back with another twenty to settle whatever I owed and the bartender gave me change. Amazing.

I love Philadelphia Theatre Company! I've seen a handful of shows over the past couple of years and really enjoy the varied programming. One show is never indicative of the next show. The acting is always great and I find it fairly easy to get wrapped up in a production in a matter of minutes.   The theatre is comfortable and every seat offers a nice view. I also love the sets! My favorite show so far has been Small Mouth Sounds. The set was so simple but perfect, and I loved that they incorporated scent into the atmosphere - it really enhanced the experience! I don't want to give anything away, but if you're considering seeing this show, you need to just buy a ticket already. It was hilarious, heartwarming, and fun.

I dig El Vez.  Their guacamole is kick-ass and the blood orange margarita is as yummy as the previous reviews indicate.  Also, an old school photo booth that actually works?!  Yippee!  Lounge-y background music and glittery decorations make for a fun atmosphere.  It's been a while since I've had dinner there, but hanging at the bar for drinks the other night made me want to plan another night out as soon as possible.

I ordered a salad from Matt & Marie's for delivery today at lunch. This was my first experience with the business. The reviews about their salads were fairly positive, and the photos looked great.   My order was for the La Scala, which comes with roasted red peppers, tomatoes and fresh mozzarella. I added on carved turkey and croutons, at an additional cost. My total order came to nearly $18, but I was paying a premium for delivery on a day full of conference calls.    My salad arrived looking tasty, but the croutons were missing. Sadness! I enjoyed the salad dressing and the ingredients were fresh, but I really wanted the croutons for some much-needed crunch.   I would love to see a build-your-own salad option like they have for sandwiches. I'd rather create my own than choose from a set list, since I often like to make modifications.

Applebee's is my least favorite sit-down chain, but this particular location gets three stars from me for three reasons.  One, the food is decent provided you don't choose anything off of the Weight Watchers menu.* Two, it is the only casual restaurant with a liquor license in the same lot as the movie theatre.  Three, this location is also in very close proximity to the Flyers Skate Zone, where practices are held.  Anything that heightens my chances of a run-in with a Flyer is a-ok with me.     Footnotes: *I have much love for WW and their invaluable points system (that helped this girl and countless others lose the freshman you-know-what), but the point-friendly Applebee's items are gross.  I whip up more flavorful and healthy recipes in my own kitchen, which is approximately two by four feet.

Odd decor aside, I truly love what FUEL is trying to - and does - accomplish. I need go-to places for healthy meals and I can probably count on one hand the spots that I rely on regularly. FUEL is one of them.   I love their salads, and seeing the nutritional info makes me that much more confident that I'm making the right choices. I am wary about most of the sandwiches since breads aren't included in the counts and they sound too delicious to be legitimately diet-friendly. But I would like to give them a try sometime.   The Passyunk location is far easier for me to get to than the one in center city, and I think the employees are friendlier, too. I dig it.

I revisited The Southern three times during my recent Nashville visit, and had a pretty great experience each time. The hot chicken salad was calling my name during the first visit, and it's what I ended up ordering on my second trip as well because I liked it so much. A heaping portion of field greens topped with the most awesome hot chicken, plus chopped pickles, slices of celery and carrot and finally a mixture of both ranch and blue cheese dressings is what makes up this salad of awesome.   On trip three I tried a cup of the gumbo (delish) plus the burger, which is topped with pimento cheese and bacon. This massive burger was served alongside a heaping pile of delicious sweet potato fries. Wow, I'm feeling guilty all over again! Totally worth it. Until my next trip south, I'll be craving that hot chicken salad on the reg.

Really loved my experience at No. 308. The bar is worlds away from the honky tonk bars in downtown Nashville. This is a laid back spot with cool decor, informative bartenders and great cocktails. I stuck with a ginger and bourbon selection but my colleague had a drink in a Coke bottle that had peanuts in it. Peanuts! I'm truly regretful that I didn't try one for myself but I am looking forward to attempting to make this creation at home. I'd probably make an effort to swing by again next time I'm in town.

Hands down, the best empanadas I've ever had. Empanada Mama bakes theirs, but nothing about the empanada was dry, which is usually my issue with baked empanadas. Instead, the crust was flaky and flavorful, the way a great pastry should be; the fillings were unique and interesting.   We got a box of six which included two traditional beef, barbecue chicken, sausage and peppers, cauliflower and corn. I expected to have a clear ranking of my favorites but was surprised to find that I liked them all almost equally.   My husband loves empanadas so I'm glad we stumbled across this place. We arrived just before noon to only one person in line, but the line behind us quickly grew. Definitely a spot to revisit the next time we're in Doylestown!

I agree with m. k.  The bartenders are awesome and make great drinks.  I get the Mediterranean plate (warm pita triangles, olives, feta and two kinds of hummus) every time I'm here and it's reaaalllly good.  Even my sister who was previously afraid of hummus (we lived a sheltered childhood, food-wise) enjoyed it.

Solid! My fiancé suggested tacking a five dollar burger date on to our annual tradition of Christmas tree shopping in South Philly, so I happily agreed. Last night was my first visit to Fountain Porter. It's a cozy neighborhood bar with lots of stools in the bar area and some seat-yourself tables in the back.   The menu is small and direct: five dollar cheeseburger, three dollar fries, assorted pickled vegetables and some cheese and charcuterie. We both went for the burger, fries and a side of dill pickles. A pint of Kenzinger was a very reasonable three bucks, and the rest of the beer list was very well rounded with something for everyone.  The burger tasted great and was nicely sized - not too huge but large enough to satisfy. The fries were perfectly crisp, and the pickles were tangy and spiced just right. Also, the bartenders were really on top of things and they were both nice guys. I see a return trip in my future.

I have a very love/hate relationship with this park. The center boasts an enormous hill. Perfect for sledding... or torturing your body into summer-ready shape.   For the past few years, I've been taking bootcamp classes on and off with Michele Held, a certified fitness instructor, roughly once a week on average. Michelle is 50 years old, has four kids, and is in better physical shape than any other woman I personally know. Each spring through early fall, Michele holds bootcamp classes at Laurel Acres. It's an hour of nonstop cardio and weight-training, including (of course) the hill, which she affectionately refers to as "the mountain."   The hill itself is steep and unforgiving. There is a long staircase on the left side as you face the hill - perfect for running, lunges and other torture. There are benches at the top of the hill that provide a lovely view of the park - also great for squats and tricep dips.   There are also running trails, a lake, playgrounds and other traditional park fixtures. I mostly think of the park with feelings of dread, but it's actually a very pretty place when bootcamp doesn't come into play.

Today was my second visit to Rittenhouse Dentists and I feel like this will be my go-to dental practice for years to come. My hygienist was Elise and I cannot say enough about her gentle touch and friendly banter! Seriously, these are the qualities you look for during those 20-or-so minutes of twice-a-year cleanings.   The waiting area is modern and comfortable, and they get you in and out as quickly as possible. I love that they apply lip balm so your lips remain plump and pouty. It's the little things, friends.   If you're looking to upgrade your dental game, this is the spot to do it.

I've had it with Capital. They used to be so reliable about a year ago but lately, not so much. It seems like every time I call for a cab, I end up waiting outside as the minutes tick by, growing more and more anxious as I realize I may be late to whatever meeting, appointment, etc. I may have.   This morning was no different. I called at 8:37 for a cab to 30th Street Station. Twenty minutes later, still no cab, we started walking towards busier streets so that we could simply hail one. While in transit, I received a call from Capital that my cab had arrived. It was 9:04. Thanks. In the past I would have called to cancel, but this has happened so many times that I have come to expect that a cab may not show up in a timely manner, or at all. Bottom line, if there's a delay, people need to be notified. I will not call Capital again.

I was lucky enough to be invited to Mercato for lunch by their lovely PR lady, Kate. As you can see from my previous reviews, Mercato has long been a favorite of mine and I'm happy to report that my feelings remain the same after my lunch visit. The boyfriend and I enjoyed a leisurely pre-Memorial Day weekend meal with a bottle of white and our experience could not have been better.   We started with a lentil salad, which was perfect for the season. Next up was the grilled artichoke, a personal favorite, with sea salt and the most delicious aioli for dipping. A salmon tartare was delicious, and though I usually prefer tuna to salmon, this version was a nice change.   By the time our main course arrived (orecchiette with sausage and plum tomato sauce), I was pretty stuffed. I thought I'd only take a few bites but it was so delicious that I ate the entire thing. Fortunately, I would not be spending time on the beach that weekend.   It had been too long since my last visit to this restaurant but I'm so pleased that the food is just as good as ever. Mercato is consistently awesome.

Although I haven't stayed at this hotel, I did experience the five star service the Four Seasons is known for during my two visits to the With Love Beer Garden this week. The garden was prepped and lovely both times, and every single employee I encountered was helpful and polite.   The guys working the food area were great, and it was fun chatting with them while waiting for my kielbasa sandwich. Said sammie contained three nice slices of meat on a perfect little roll, topped with sauteed onions and spicy mustard. It was a delicious treat and a steal for only $5.50. Later, I tried the grilled shrimp taco with pickled cabbage, guacamole and sour cream and it was a very close second to the kielbasa.  I'm very grateful for the opportunity to hang at the posh courtyard, while chatting up interesting hotel guests who were all too happy to walk out the door and into a Philly Beer Week event. I only hope the hotel will consider doing more events like this throughout the summer.

Fuzhou House isn't the best Chinese take-out I've had, but it's far from the worst. For about ten bucks, I got at least two meals out of my General Tso's chicken entree, which came with a pint of white rice. The chicken was even better straight out of the fridge the next afternoon.   The employees are friendly, the place is clean and I just found out they also deliver for free.

I've been hitting up Plenty a bit more regularly and I'm a huge fan. Ever since they changed up the space a bit and added more tables, there is a cozy, cafe type of feel. There's wifi so you can get some work done, great coffee and delicious sandwiches. There are even breakfast options.   My favorite sandwich remains the tasso ham but I also order the turkey and the tuna pretty often. Careful with the turkey if you're watching your waistline - they sneak mayo on there to keep it from being too dry, but the last time I was there, mayo wasn't listed as one of the ingredients even though it was on the sandwich.   The guy who has been working the counter most often during my visits has always been super pleasant. The giant jug of complimentary water flavored with fruit is a really nice touch. I just love this place. Check it out if you haven't already!

Wow, I must have really been holding a grudge about that white tuna from back in the day, because it took more than ten years to give 1225Raw (formerly just Raw, I think?) another shot. Originally, we planned to order from another restaurant that we love, but the wait time was nearly three hours long for delivery on a Saturday night! We looked at other options and decided to give 1225Raw a try. I'm so glad we did, because we had a really solid experience.   We ordered: pork gyoza, shrimp robatayaki, bulgogi robatayaki, spicy tuna roll, yellowtail jalapeño roll, shrimp tempura roll and cali katsu roll. I thought the robatayaki was a little skimpy, however, it was delicious. Next time, we'll probably go with two per person.   The rolls were all really delish. Super fresh and lots of flavor. I would definitely order all of these again. There was plenty of ginger and super spicy wasabi packed alongside, too.   Happy to have this spot back on my radar and will definitely think of them again for sushi. In fact, since I first drafted this review last week, we've already ordered again and had another great experience!

Crystal Lake, we need to talk.   The last couple times I chalked it up to a bad day, a full moon, what have you.  Today was the last straw.  Lately I've developed feelings of anger and resentment towards you.  I'm angry because my omelets are never as good as they used to be and resentful because I know you are holding out, or worse, giving your best to someone else.  It's because of this that I am going to start seeing other diners.    Ssshh, don't get upset.  I'll definitely be back for a quickie between the hours of 2 and 4 a.m. some night when I'm drunk and nothing else is open.

I don't find myself in the Fairmount area too often, but I ended up at Le Pain Quotidien semi-recently for a quick bite before an event nearby. The cafe has large windows, making for a nice, bright environment. Our server was super friendly and made the experience more enjoyable.   In my opinion, the food at Le Pain Quotidien (regardless of location) is pretty simple and straightforward. My mind has never been blown by any dish but some are better than others. The coffee is usually pretty good. I appreciate that I can always get something healthy and nutritional info is available.

I much prefer the quiet peacefulness of Washington Square Park to our other famous Philly park. It's sprawling, with plenty of grass for a picnic, lots of trees for shade, and gorgeous scenery in every direction.   You also can't beat being so close to Talula's Daily, in case you need a quick and easy lunch to go, or even just an afternoon pick-me-up in the form of a coffee or treat.

I typically go to the Cherry Hill DSW location, but this one was close by when I was running errands so I swung in with high hopes of finding a pair of shoes at the last minute on the day of an event. This DSW was enormous and well-stocked. I often see shoes I love and then get super bummed when my size isn't available. Not here! Almost every pair I liked came in my size and I ended up with the most amazing pair of open-toed black booties.   Staff members were friendly and the store was clean and well-organized. Love.

Welcome to the neighborhood, Ultimo! I was thrilled when I found out something new was coming to Graduate Hospital, and though the wait was a long one, it's wonderful to see a bustling new business in the 'hood.   I'll be honest. Ultimo doesn't brew my favorite beans, but the taste is one I could get used to as an alternate to my long time fave (La Colombe). The space is naturally bright and I'm betting I could be pretty productive with a constant supply of coffee and something from the pastry case. I couldn't tell if there was anything more substantial to eat, but I'll be looking for that option on future visits. In the meantime, I'm just so happy to see a gorgeous new coffee bar in an area that desperately needed one.  PS, Open until 8pm on weeknights and 9pm on weekends? Huzzah!

Last night, my mom and I chose New Deck as the meeting place for drinks and a bite after her conference nearby. The menu was exactly what we were looking for; a decent happy hour and a few small plates. I had French onion soup and we shared a Mediterranean plate and some chicken fingers. The beers were super fresh and delicious; Guinness for Mom and Harp for me.   New Deck has a nice pub environment and it was clean and pretty bustling considering the Monday night. However, New Deck has a problem, and it's pretty clearly outlined in other recent reviews. It's the service. We sat at the bar and the bartender was surlier than Mr. Carson in Downton Abbey, and not in an endearing way. An Irish accent only gets you so far. It was very hard to get this bartender's attention on multiple occasions, and we actually felt like we were bothering him when we needed something. This is the guy you stick behind the bar on a college campus?   New Deck filled all of our requirements for a night out except for the good service part. We'll be choosing another destination next time.

Where's the love, y'all? Golden Dawn has been one of my favorite diners since I was a little kid. We go way back. My Nana and Pop-Pop ordered dinner from there every single night. When I stayed over, my go-to was always the turkey dinner with mashed potatoes and string beans. The mashed potatoes were deliciously unique - I think they used sour cream in them.   Now I dig the egg white omelets, which are enormous and come loaded and with a large side of perfectly crispy hashbrowns. I never once had to ask for a refill of coffee or water on my last visit. This is a Jersey diner at its finest.

Friends, some things are better left in the past:  Ex-boyfriends. ck one. College pizza.  The one that rings truest to me is the pizza. Things have changed drastically since I've left my old stomping grounds. Or maybe I was just used to accepting mediocrity on my budget at the time. Regardless, I revisited my college pizza fave while passing through town yesterday, and I'd like my six bucks back.   The pizza still looked decent (see pic - deceiving, no?). They had all my old varieties: chicken romano, cheesesteak, bruschetta, etc. I selected a slice of white with spinach and tomatoes and a piece of the bruschetta Sicilian. After five minutes in the oven, the pizza was ready to go and I got to it.   Disappointing. Both pies were beyond dry and nearly flavorless. I ate out of hunger, but not with gusto. Life beyond college is so much better.

A gigantic turkey and cheese hoagie for only five bucks? Can't beat it! Although it wasn't as tasty as the offerings at some of our more famous sandwich shops, it did the trick on a hungry-verging-on-hangry stomach. There's still a half left for a future meal.   A credit card minimum of ten bucks was a minor inconvenience, but I managed to hit ten and change with the addition of a Diet Snapple and a bottle of corn and black bean salsa. Hope it's good...  Probably my favorite discovery about May's was the hand dipped ice cream counter. Breyer's is tops in my book and I will definitely return the next time I'm craving a sweet treat in my 'hood.

Glen Foerd Mansion is a beautiful venue with lots of history and character.  I've been to several parties here and everything is always perfect.  The staff is the best and they always do everything possible to make you comfortable.    There are so many unique areas to check out if you find yourself at an event here.  Make sure to see the art gallery upstairs and the old-fashioned cellar.  Both have some interesting things to look at, especially after you've had a few drinks.  I'm updating my pics so you can see what I mean!

When I swung by Total Wine on my lunch break today, I knew exactly what I wanted for an upcoming byo dinner: Marraso Vineyards Malbec, which I fell in love with on a recent trip to San Francisco.  Unfortunately, things didn't go according to plan.  I grabbed a wine rep for assistance (there are always several on the floor so you don't have to go far) and he did not recognize the producer.  A quick search on the computer confirmed that the wine was not carried in the store.  Now for the bright side: the rep not only gave me some recommendations for another Malbec, he also offered to special order the wine I had requested originally.  In about one to two weeks, I will be getting a call from Total Wine to let me know that I can pick up my bottles.  Happy day!

This review is solely for the concretes, of which I indulged on Saturday night. I perused the list of mix-ins and had a plan in action (vanilla custard with caramel, fudge and marshmallow, sort of like a take on B&J's Phish Food), when the gentleman behind the counter suggested that I opt for the flavor of the day, salted caramel custard. Sold! I ordered a half concrete with chocolate and marshmallow. Meanwhile, despite having just come from dinner, the scent of the burgers was intoxicating. Next time.   Our concretes were ready in no time and we enjoyed them at the counter seating along the window. Yum. A half was the perfect size, too. Can't wait to go back and try the regular menu!

It's been a while since my last review for On Point when they first popped up in Point Breeze. Since that time, they've become one of my go-to delivery spots, typically for breakfast/brunch. Their omelettes are simply fantastic; I wish I knew how to make eggs like that! The huevos rancheros dish is great as well; there is so much flavor and the restaurant puts sauce on the side when you get delivery which is really helpful.   Before the pandemic, I met a friend for lunch and tried the falafel pita - it was awesome and I've been wanting to get it again ever since!   My only suggestion would be to add more options to the create-your-own omelet when ordering delivery. I would love to see pico de gallo and beans as an add-in, since they already have them in other dishes on the menu. Or maybe even a new, Mexican-style omelet option? Either way, love this spot and will continue to support them from afar until it's safe to dine in again!

13th Street Pizza is definitely better when you can heat it up a bit. Otherwise, it's quickly-made doughy crust with greasy cheese conglomerating on top. So, perfect for when you're drunk and don't care what you're eating, but much better after it's been heated and the crust crisps up and the cheese is somewhat melty.   I probably would not ever eat this pizza while sober, however.

Like Linda Blair in The Exorcist, the power of Christ compels me to write a review of this God-awful place.   I'd passed by Buca di Beppo (both the location in Cherry Hill and the one in center city) several times. Always with a little shudder and the hope that I would never set foot in the restaurant. I can't really explain it, but the tacky sign and other adornments gave me the creeps... and that was just the exterior of the building.   When a group of us decided to go out for a pasta dinner before several friends were set to run the Philly marathon, I thought we were all set for a night of Maggiano's or some other reasonably priced chain with lots of carbs on the menu. Not so. Every Italian restaurant in the city was booked-- with the exception of Buca.   While I can't remember all the various items we ordered, I do remember that the portion sizes were gluttonous and I left feeling nauseous. If ever you find yourself wandering down 15th street on a dark and hungry night, avert your eyes and continue on until you reach a safe haven!

I found this Chinese restaurant to be pretty average. Chinese pizza tasted the same as it always does, and the chicken entree we ordered had a little too much sweet sauce. Nothing new there.   Normally, wonton soup is pretty consistent regardless of where it is ordered, but I actually liked Szechuan Hunan's a little bit less. It tasted faintly of nutmeg or cinnamon, which didn't work for me.   The search for cheap but above average Chinese continues.

Bowling is not my favorite sport. I'm a pretty athletic person but I just don't have the skills or the desire to conquer the activity. So when I find myself at one to two bowling parties per year (give or take), I typically either avoid playing in favor of mingling or suck it up and accept the many gutter balls to come in the next two-hour window of my future.   PEP Bowl is great for parties because you can rent the entire place out and bring your own food and booze. This obviously makes for an inexpensive party option and gives your party peoples a fun activity to bond over.   I do wish the staff would ask smokers to step away from the open door. I've noticed prominent cigarette smoke wafting in each time I've been to PEP Bowl, which is a big-time personal annoyance.

Here's the thing about Target.  No matter what you think you are going in there for, you are always going to come out with a bunch of random stuff you didn't even realize you needed.    Take last night.  My mom and I walk in and see the bargain stuff on our right.  Suddenly, it is imperative that I own a large black plastic bowl.  Only 99 cents!   Next up, jewelry section.  I really need new earrings.  Sold, for $4.99!  What's that?  Clearance picture frames?  Well I DID just order all those pics from Kodak Gallery.  Cha-ching!  Wait, what did I come here for?  Oh yes, mascara and razors.  (I especially love that since this Target is in a pretty nice neighborhood, the razors aren't kept on lockdown with built-in alarm systems.  Just grab and go!)    $50 later, we left the store.    P.S. I can't wait to try my Archer Farms stone ground crackers later!

Solid first experience with Merkaz. As a lover of Middle Eastern cuisine, this place has been on my radar for a while. Yesterday I decided to place a delivery order for lunch. There are two chicken options - schnitzel (fried) or chicken salad. Honestly, I would have preferred a simple grilled chicken, but I went with the chicken salad. It was tasty, and I loved the addition of some crunched up potato chips, but I felt like something was missing. The pickle on the side, adorably wrapped in a tiny paper bag, was a great add-on, however.  I also ordered a side of hummus because, a) never miss an opportunity to get some of Solomonov's hummus and, b) it was only five bucks for an eight ounce container!   Looking forward to trying more of the menu.

This was probably the most disorganized, unfriendly and questionably clean Shake Shack location I've visited. We popped in on Sunday night for dessert and the cashier seemed bothered to help us.   We received a buzzer after placing our order and stood near the staircase to wait. In that time, I took in the surroundings and was unimpressed by the cleanliness of the counters, floors and other surfaces. Meanwhile, an employee who was collecting metal trays clanged them together loudly as he walked around the restaurant.   Our desserts were the only saving grace, though the employees could probably use a refresher. My ice cream cone was a bit wonky (but delicious, nonetheless) and my husband's shake was paltry; the cup was only about 2/3 full which was kind of lame.   We were in the area which is why we visited this location, but I would pick another Shake Shack location in the future.

I get downright bitter when something I hold dear is taken away from me. Maybe that's why I've been disappointed in past visits to Resurrection, when the infamous twice fried chicken was not available. Thankfully, they've decided to show mercy and the bird I love is back on the menu. While I'm not so foolish to think that this will last forever, I will remain hopeful.   A newly adjusted happy hour (5-7 instead of the previous 4-6) and the return of the chicken are certainly reason enough for a review upgrade.

As soon as I walked into the building that houses Sweat's Arch Street location, I could smell fresh juice. I had no idea that the same building is also home to RC Juice Club, and I was happy to come across the biz. After sweating it out in a class next door, I happily rewarded myself and a friend with some fresh juice. Both juices tasted amazing - like healthy, delicious lemonades. The employees were super friendly, also. Great spot!

The boyfriend usually swears by Olde City Taxi, but these guys sucked it big time when we called for a ride to 30th Street Station last week. I don't know why, but every time we call a cab (from any company) specifically for 30th Street, they never seem to show. For now on, Uber will be my go-to when it comes to time-sensitive rides.   Back to Olde City Taxi: we waited for thirty minutes and even logged a follow up call during that time to ensure that someone was on their way. Ultimately, we trudged down the street with our rolly bags to hunt down a cab the old-fashioned way.   Another Philly cab company on my do not call list.

We returned for another pizza date over the weekend. The Crispin cider on tap was delish. I couldn't stop stealing sips of it from across the table, despite my nice glass of malbec.   We once again ordered a gabagool pizza, which was great, and a clams casino pizza, a special. That one was okay. The pancetta on top was cut too large and was particularly fatty. I would have loved it pan seared in smaller bits then put on top. I also wish the pizzas arrived with salt, pepper and hot red peppers. Other than that, I'm a fan and I can't wait to work my way through the rest of Birra's offerings.

When the salmon dinner I attempted to cook went horribly awry, my quick-thinking beau suggested takeout from Seafood Unlimited. We're currently on a detox, so we needed very plain fish prepared only with olive oil or spices. No butter, no alternate ingredients, etc. I called to place an order and asked about a million questions along the way.   Once the goods were home, we hungrily dug in. The cost for tilapia or flounder with two sides is just under twenty bucks, which isn't too bad. Everything was prepared the way we asked (as far as I could tell!) and packaged nicely. I would order takeout from them again but I'm also interested in checking out the restaurant itself, which was recently renovated.

Cork is around the corner from my house yet I've only been a handful of times.  Not sure why, because the food is good and they have excellent happy hour specials.  Take Monday nights for example.  Half-priced bottles of wine until 7 p.m.  HALF PRICE!  You can't get two glasses for less than that and now you are getting, what, four?  Mama like.  My friend and I were in the mood for white and couldn't decide, so the Martin Codax Albarino was recommended.  I had never tried this type of wine before, but it ended up being one of the best I've ever tasted.  I love discoveries!    For dinner we had a huge Mediterranean plate which was also half-priced, as well as a grilled shrimp, pesto, fontinella and arugula "mini pizza" that was actually big enough to leave us with leftovers.  What a great, not-overly-expensive way to start off the week!  I can't wait to go back!

Two summers ago, my husband surprised me with window boxes from Enliven for my birthday. It is truly the gift that keeps on giving! We have an annual subscription, so when the seasons change, Enliven comes out to remove old plants and refresh with brand new ones.   I honestly couldn't choose which season is my favorite; the flowers and plants are always just so spot on! I really loved this year's spring planters with colorful pastel blooms and light green plants with big, fuzzy leaves. Summer planters require a lot of water; how I wish we had a hose in the front of our house!   You might think the winter boxes would be somewhat dull, but they are anything but; they are always filled with gorgeous greenery and, my personal favorite, lots of eucalyptus. The scent hits me every time I pass them by and our home always looks so festive for the holiday season!   These planters bring me joy every single day, and there's nothing like the surprise of a fresh batch when the seasons change. If you're thinking of upping your city garden game, I highly recommend Enliven!

I really loved Brewery ARS on my first visit a month or so ago. My brother and SIL were in town so we did a family/friends night out and there was a group of about ten of us bouncing around. ARS was our second stop and I think we spent more time there than anywhere else.   The beers were fresh and crisp. I don't drink craft beer very often anymore, but when I do I like west coast style pale ales and IPAs. So if you dig that style, you'll probably really enjoy much of the selection here.    The tasting room is definitely small but we lucked out during our Saturday night visit. We had mostly standing room to begin but by the time we closed the place down there were plenty of open tables. I'd recommend going during an off time if you want to grab a seat and relax. Otherwise, grab a brew and make some friends!

Now that I know Woody's has some of the best bar snacks in Midtown, an extra star is warranted. The first stop of our Gay Bar Crawl on Tuesday met us with Austin, the hunky and personable bartender, and Tommy D, the friendly house chef. Tommy hooked us up with four huge plates of food to try, including house-made potato chips, delicious chicken tenders, four different types of spring rolls (each with a tasty dipping sauce) and calamari.   The bites gave us the fuel we needed to power through a four bar crawl. Word is, Woody's serves a mean brunch and bloody Mary, so you know I'll be back. The cheesesteak spring rolls are calling my name!

Ugh, Hallmark.  They lure me in with stores a-plenty and Gold Crown Rewards coupons.  Still, every time a holiday rolls around and I inevitably end up in the store, I want to scream.  Instead, I stare at the same cards for twenty minutes until I pick out something so generic, it could be sent to my dentist.     Then, I take my cards up to the counter, where one of four women is smiling maniacally and asks if I found everything I was looking for.  Instead of responding with, "No I didn't, because it's not 1965 and not everyone has parents who are still happily married to each other.  Oh yeah, and my stepdad is not my 'mom's special loved one,' he's my stepdad!"  I simply say yes, pay for my cards and leave, hoping a new card store will roll into town.

For a girl and her boyfriend who were eating nothing but cruciferous veggies, apples and pears for three days straight, the prospect of avocado and cucumber rolls made with brown rice was about as exciting as a steak-lover eating gratis at Barclay Prime.   While we loved that we were eating something new after three days of darkness, the rolls were just okay. The rice wasn't as sticky as I've come to expect from sushi rice. Pieces were on the small side, though each roll came with 12 (priced accordingly).   Service was lackluster. I immediately received a water when I arrived but we had to ask for one for my boyfriend. Also, we sat around for a while before our order was taken, even though we were the only people there at that point.   We chose Mizu because of the seating and option of brown rice, but I'll stick with one of my other spots for sushi in Rittenhouse now that my crazy detox diet is over!

I've been spending a whole lot of time in coffee shops lately and I've been especially charmed by L'Aube. My skim latte last Monday morning was absolutely dreamy. I can only imagine how amazing the crepes are - the smell was intoxicating!   Next time I'm in the mood for a little French rendezvous, I know exactly the place to go. Wonder if I can convince anyone to sing The Beatles' "Michelle" to me?

I loved my first visit to the Independence Beer Garden! It was pretty crowded at dinnertime on a Sunday evening. Luckily, my fiancé and his friends had already locked down a table. The Watermelon Wheat pitchers were flowing but I quickly switched to the gin, cucumber and elderflower drink at the suggestion of our server.   Speaking of whom, she was the sweetest, most soft spoken, lovely woman (blonde with pink hair, I can't remember her name)! Always right on top of anything we needed and knew the menu front to back.   I was super hungry and feeling indulgent so I ordered the cheeseburger and pickle chips. The burger was good; I've had better but it did the trick. The pickle chips were awesome; I see more of these in my future. Can't wait for many more warm spring and summer nights at the IBG!

The Industry has eased its way on to my short list of favorite bars in the city. I truly love this place. It's great for drinks, dinner, and brunch - sometimes all three if you hang out long enough (it happens). The service is always friendly and fantastic.   In my humble opinion, the food has been getting better and better over time. There's always a great selection for dinner ranging from salads and sandwiches to entrees. For brunch, I always go savory but would highly recommend sharing something sweet. I once had a few bites of their baked pancake special and it was phenomenal.  Super solid spot.

Okay, so I know I only wrote my first review of Porco's a couple weeks ago, however, I had to swing on back for a review update because I finally tried one of the pork sandwiches over the weekend.   Mind. Blowing.   Honestly, the cubano sandwich was one of the best things I've eaten all year. The pork was super tender and so flavorful.
