There were some crunchy bits that added great texture and pops of flavor. The pickled veggies and mustard aioli really brightened up the whole sandwich. The freshly baked bread held everything together and did not fall apart.   My husband and I have become weekday pescetarians and have been eating meat only on weekends. This sandwich basically confirmed that I could never go full-vegetarian. Unreal. I look forward to revisiting the cubano next weekend.

I ordered a salad from Torch-Wood Market for delivery and was very happy with my order! The salad was super fresh and had a nice amount of toppings. The dressing was served on the side, per my request. Best of all, I think the salad set me back something like eight bucks. I never get away with spending less than ten bucks for lunch so that was a true joy. Looking forward to many more happy memories with Torch-Wood!

Vernick Coffee Bar seems to be the it place right now! I went for a working lunch last week and brought my laptop so that I could stay and get some work done. Who knew I'd run into so many familiar faces that I'd actually get less done than if I were at my own house with all the usual distractions?!   Lunch was great. Our server was really sweet and knew the menu very well. I went with the chilled shrimp soba noodle salad and it was absolutely delicious. Super fresh and perfect for a light lunch!   Later on while seated by the coffee bar, I splurged on a salted caramel cookie which was, sadly, not nearly as tasty as it looked (didn't stop me from eating it, though). I'll have to try one of the other pastries next time, and there are plenty from which to choose. Looking forward to my next visit!

I love you, Insomnia Cookies. Since you've expanded your delivery territory to cover Graduate Hospital, we've ordered twice in the past month. Danger Zone, population: me.   My only (minor) complaint is that the presentation is a bit sloppy. Our recent order of six cookies arrived in a pizza box type thing and they were kind of all over the place, but still intact. The deliciousness of the slightly-crunchy, slightly-soft cookies was not impacted by the seemingly bumpy trip to our doorstep.   The chocolate chunk and double chocolate chunk are great. We even scored three of our cookies for free because of some sort of March Madness promotion that was on the Insomnia website. I love that they do stuff like that.   Also appreciated is the ice cream option, which always arrives still frozen. Flavors rotate but I can personally attest to the coffee and mint chocolate chip ice creams being a very good partner to the cookies.

I ordered delivery from Al Zaytouna based on the many reviews by friends who had also ordered, and enjoyed, delivery. My experience was no different. My order arrived fairly quickly and everything was intact and kept separate by a divided container.   The pita was a bit on the tough side but I didn't really mind. I liked the thinness of it; perfect for wrapping everything up into rolled sandwiches. The chicken from my kebabs was a little bit dry, but with some hummus and veggies, it still tasted good. There was so much food that I actually had some leftovers, which I promptly tore up after a night on the town later that evening. I'll definitely hit up Al Zaytouna again for future delivery.

After reading Stephen H's ROTD for Stir last week, I checked out the other reviews and realized I needed to get in on the action as soon as possible. Little did I know how soon I'd be partaking - just days later I found myself walking down Chancellor with a bevy of yelp buds.   For some reason, what I pictured Stir to look like and what it actually looked like were two very different things. I had imagined a wall of dark brick and a long chestnut bar with little space to maneuver. What I got was a square bar in the center of a cozy room, plus another bar with more space in the back, and very tasteful décor all around. Added to that was a 'tender who knew how to make a martini just as well as he made every one of us Stir newbs feel welcome.   Thanks to Sue for letting me tickle her pickle. I quite liked it, actually.

It's a double review day, because I couldn't give love to Small Oven and not Porco's! For those who don't know, Porco's and Small Oven are two concepts running out of the same space. Porco's is all about the meats, but they also serve some fantastic meaty substitutes!   Though they are known for their porchetta, I opted for a meatball sandwich the first time I tried Porco's. The sandwich was stuffed with pork and beef blend meatballs and the house-made mozz took the sandwich over the top.   I've also tried their vegetarian sandwich, which was loaded with layers of veggies and felt super hearty but also healthy.   Porco's is still slinging sandwiches despite these trying times, so be sure to call ahead for pick up at their take-out window, or order delivery straight to your front door!

Yeah, it's true.  I'm that girl who never got excited about a trip to Monk's. My first experience was so-so and one subsequent trip for a quick beer during last winter's snowpocalypse didn't win me over, either.   For me, Monk's was a Philly fixture that blended with the urban landscape.  Why I heard myself suggesting the place as a lunch option the other day is still a mystery. Divine intervention? Perhaps. Because the pot of Ghent mussels, bathing in a Saison Dupont broth filled with bacon, leeks and blue cheese, were life-changing.  Also, it appears my previous gripe is null and void. Burgers are now served with a choice of greens or - wait for it - frites. Reunited and it feels so gooooood!

A friend/fellow yelper and I met for a drunken brunch to celebrate Labor Day.  We started our meal with bloody marys, which were just okay (but not bad enough to stop us from ordering a second round later in the meal).  Next time, I'll probably opt for one of Mixto's many other signature drinks instead.  We started with the platanitos; plantain chips and guacamole.  I like my chips salted, but the plantain chips were nakey so we just threw some salt on top of the guac.  No complaints though.  I order this starter often so I knew what to expect.  For my breakfast, I had huevos rancheros.  My dining companion and I gave a shout out to Monica S. at this point, the resident expert on this dish.  I was given my choice of breakfast meat and I went with chorizo, which ended up being pretty awesome.  Refried beans and some homemade tortilla chips completed the meal.  Shout out to our server, Louis, who was efficient and pleasant, despite our many questions and special requests.

I was so pleasantly surprised by my brunch at Cafe La Maude a couple months ago. There were a few tables set up outside but it was a warm day so we decided to eat inside. Fortunately, we snagged the last available table, but even if there had been a wait, it seemed like turnover was pretty quick. Still, the place was bumpin' on a Sunday morning!    The menu was much larger than I expected for a cafe, and they also had some specials. I went super basic with scrambled eggs and cheddar on a croissant, but it was delicious. The coffee was great, too. My friend raved about her salad. The staff was very friendly and one of the owners/managers swung by each table to make sure people were enjoying themselves. I can't wait to go back!

I had a great experience placing a wine delivery with Fishtown Social a few weeks ago. The full list of offerings is available on their website, with some notes about each bottle. I ordered two whites (including a dry riesling from local winery Wayvine - I love this wine!) and a bottle of bubbles.   Deliveries take place on Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. I placed my order through email on a Thursday night, received confirmation and paid on Friday morning, and received the delivery that afternoon.   There's really something for everyone on Fishtown Social's wine list, so give them a look next time you're stocking up on wine.

Martha, you are the jam. The menu situation is genius. Don't know what I'm talking about? Well, just pull out your phone and check out martha.menu - there, you will find an updated list of all menu items. No specials, no 86 this and that, just the bites and beverages available for purchase at any given time, straight up.   The bar itself is funky and chill, the backyard garden even better. It's like being in someone's backyard with its low-key, cute vibe. And, there's bocce ball. Love.   The hoagies are increds, the pickles are the best I've had in this city (seriously), and the warm spiced nuts are deliciously perfect.   Way to keep it cool and local, Martha. You're tops in my book.

Walking into Bloom on Sunday, I had no idea what to expect, but I was surprised to find that the tiny shop was stuffed with clothes, accessories, soaps, candles and other little trinkets. I saw about a million great stocking stuffers during my short visit. I'm still thinking about the sequined business card holder I saw and wishing there was someone on my Christmas list who could use it.   I didn't end up purchasing anything, but I did walk away impressed by the selection. I will definitely stop by again the next time I need a cute gift for a friend or my sister.

I stumbled into Chipotle around 8 pm on Thursday night, straight out of a boot camp class. I can't imagine what I must have looked like. Hungry - no, starving, I told the guy behind the counter that I had never been to a Chipotle and asked if he could just run through the options. I decided to go with a burrito, since it would be traveling with me back to Philly and it seemed like the least messy choice. At that moment, he yelled "free burrito!" and nods were shared between the workers.   I don't know if it was because they were frightened of my sweaty self and wanted me out as fast as possible, or if it was because I was an eager Chipotle newbie, but I was so surprised and extremely grateful nonetheless. Back at my apartment, my burrito tasted like food of the gods, with two sides of salsas and some Mexican crema. I will undoubtedly return, hopefully not resembling the female Hulk next time.

I won't lie. I was a little surprised when I found out that Krispy Kreme would be going in smack between McMillan's and DiBartolo, two bakeries that I believe to be the creme de la creme of doughnut purveyors in South Jersey. I even voiced my suspicions on a Talk thread (and later got totally called out on it by a Krispy Kreme higher-up. Oops! Sorry, Braden.).   HOWEVER, I went to the Collingswood Krispy Kreme pre-opening party and have to say that the selection is pretty baller. I scored a mini doughnut and a sample of one of the legit sticky buns covered in frosting, but there was so much more that beckoned from the squeaky clean cases. The coffee was also pretty good. There was plenty of seating and rumor has it that there will even be a lounge area. This, along with a drive-thru lane, certainly sets KK apart from the other bakeries. Also, they'll be open until 11pm, which may take care of some evening munchies.   Am I giving up my old bakeries? Hells no. But is there room in town for another? I don't see why not.

There aren't many sit-down breakfast options in Midtown during the week, so Green Eggs fills that need quite nicely. It isn't my favorite brunch spot, but on weekdays when there's no wait, it's a solid option. On weekends, expect lines on lines. It's one of those brunch factory-type places, with huge portions that people go crazy over. I get that people dig that, but it's not really my scene.   I recently enjoyed an eggs benedict with a healthy side of breakfast potatoes (on a weekday, naturally). You get a choice of a couple different potato styles, and I chose the one with peppers and onions, which I liked a lot. The coffee is La Colombe, which I love, but it tasted burnt.   The restaurant is cash only, which is not convenient, though there is an ATM on site. I'll be back if in the area and craving breakfast, but if I have extra time and other options I'd likely choose elsewhere.

It's kind of a hike for me to get to this Shop Rite, but the money I save from my shopper card is totally worth it ($14+ on my last visit!). There's certainly no shopping incentive at Whole Foods, other than the free parking, which you always get at Shop Rite stores. I've also found that most Shop Rites have very similar layouts, making grocery runs so much easier.   I've never had issues with the quality of any item, from produce to meats to dairy. I'm also happy with a lot of the store brand products.   Jerry F points out in his review that the check-out staff is friendly AND competent, and I have to agree. There are always a decent amount of lanes open and no added frustration during the check-out process.

Popped into Vedge on a whim on Thursday for a nightcap. We were fortunate enough to enjoy the front lounge to ourselves for the entire time we were there, making for a really fun and romantic night out. The wine list was great, with some really interesting selections including a sparkling shiraz that was totally unexpected and completely awesome. Both of the mixed olives bowls provided for a very nice accompaniment. I may even be convinced to try dinner next time.
You know what boyfriends like for Valentine's Day? Lingerie and Han Dynasty take-out. Served separately, of course.

Loved my first experience at a.bar. This dark and sexy corner bar is prime real estate for people-watching. Somehow, the shades on the windows kept people from really looking in, but were still perfect for looking out. No fishbowl effect.  The menu looks really awesome, but I didn't have anything to eat since we had dinner reservations at a.kitchen. But I did try the Pamplemousse Spritz, which was a perfect summer cocktail. Drinks are pricey, but considering the location I think that's to be expected. Said libations pack a punch so I have no complaints.   Really looking forward to my next rendezvous on the corner of 18th and Walnut.

You know what? I don't even care if their ice cream is overpriced. It's homemade and delicious and just better than anything else out there. The mint chip has those thin slices of dark chocolate that melt on contact, rather than chew up all waxy-like. And the mint is so refreshingly delicious. My only problem is trying to catch every last drop before it drips off the cone. That's not a bad problem to have.

Last night, I found a new happy hour spot for my rotation. My two friends and I randomly decided to check out The Coffee Bar, and I'm so glad we did. The two baristas/bartenders were very friendly and knew a lot about beer, which is always a great sign. I opted for a glass of red while my cohorts selected their brews.  While checking-in on my Yelp app, I noticed a special offer on the business listing: "$10 beer & lunch, Monday through Friday. Choose any sandwich, wrap or salad" and enjoy a "beer of the day." NICE!   Already planning my return visit, we grabbed the check as last call was made. I was confused to see that my $9 glass of wine was listed as something around $5 on the bill; my friends' beers were also nicely discounted. Then we found out that happy hour runs from 6-8, every weekday night. The three of us left in very good spirits and we all plan to return.

It's the first time you are making dinner for your:  a. lover  b. family  c. domesticated friends d. Yikes, all of the above!  Why chance it by making something from scratch when you can guarantee a great meal from the good people at Bobby Chez!  They have jumbo lump crab cakes (fried and broiled), chicken parm (awesome), chicken pot pie and at least one or two other daily specials.  Side dishes include the always amazing lobster mash, garlic mash, grilled veggies and many others.  Everything is partially cooked so all you have to do is throw the goods in the oven for the recommended cook time listed on the handy little sheet they give you with every order.    And hey, you can always pull a Mrs. Doubtfire and toss all the containers and bag in the outside trash.  Go ahead, tell them you slaved all day.  Chances are they won't believe you, but at least everyone will enjoy their meal!

I wanted to send a friend flowers for a special occasion, but considering she lives nearly 1,000 miles away, I had to turn to Yelp for guidance. Petals by Irene was one of the first results and, since they work with Yelp's delivery platform, my life was made easier as my info was already stored as part of my profile.   In just a few minutes, I selected a pretty, modern arrangement, crafted a personal message, paid for the flowers and moved on with my day. Delivery was $25 which is STEEP, but I really loved the arrangement and was willing to pay for convenience rather than spend more time shopping around.   After placing the order, I received a confirmation. On delivery day, I received a photo of the flowers! This was such a nice surprise that made me feel confident with my purchase. My friend received the flowers as scheduled and said they were beautiful. Very pleased with my experience and would recommend Petals by Irene to anyone ordering from out of town (or in town!).

It only occurred to me today, as I was walking out of this particular Wells Fargo location after another very pleasant experience, that I should probably write them a review. Without fail, every single time I conduct any sort of business at this branch, I receive a friendly greeting and a genuine "How are you doing today?" I've probably told the tellers here more than they need to know about my day/life just because they are so darn friendly.   My new husband and I had a particularly great experience last Saturday when we were depositing checks and cash from our wedding. The name of the gentleman who helped us is escaping me (I'm so sorry!) but he was so wonderful - setting us up in a private area so we could endorse our checks, and handling all of the transactions with a smile.   Maybe I just go at off hours but I never notice too much of a wait, either. Definitely the best Wells Fargo in the area, as far as I'm concerned.

Admittedly, I've never actually been to El Zarape, but I've now had their tacos al pastor on two occasions: Flavors of the Avenue and the Flavors preview party. The tacos are delicious. The meat is perfect; lightly seared to a crunch but not burnt or too dry. The chopped onions and cilantro meld with some homemade sauces into a medley of Mexican love. These are the best traditional tacos I've had outside of Mexico, but the advantage goes to El Zarape for not throwing me a side of Montezuma's Revenge.
A full service gas station in Philadelphia???   *puts away hand sanitizer*  This Jersey expat is one happy camper. I'm never going to the stations on Broad ever again.

The Living Room is a newish spot for coffee, quick bites, solid background music, wifi, and a nice environment to get some work done. I swung by with some time to kill for a cup of coffee and to get a few emails out. The woman working the counter was super friendly and came around to refill cups since there were only a couple of us in at the time. I enjoyed my coffee and will have to swing back next time I'm in the neighborhood to try the food.

I was thrilled to see Bacchus open on Christmas Eve as I was walking home from the gym and needed a grab-and-go lunch to tide me over before my annual feast of fishes. A blackboard special grabbed my attention: turkey, cooper sharp, bacon and some sort of delicious aioli. These ingredients were served on a toasted multigrain roll that was large enough to share with my husband. The sandwich was delicious!   I noticed loads of people popping in to pick up catering items, and made a mental note for the future. All of the employees were wearing festive hats and were so friendly. I've only picked up a sandwich from Bacchus maybe one other time but this experience definitely put them back on my radar!

If excellent cocktails, toe-tapping tunes from the 50s and beautiful portraits of gorgeous, naked women are not things you enjoy, head elsewhere.  Otherwise, join me at one of the booths along the fabulous vintage red-and-black-velvet wallpaper, and order yourself the bartender's choice. You'll be asked a series of questions regarding how you like your drinks, and a few minutes later you'll be presented with a potion that was tailored to suit your palate.  When the wind is howling and the summer sun seems like a dream, ask about the hot beverages, which aren't listed individually but are certainly offered. Raise that toddy to your lips and let it warm you from the inside out... as if that gorgeous brunette on the far wall didn't get you hot under the collar already!

A toasted whole wheat everything bagel with low-fat vegetable cream cheese and a large cup of L'Aube coffee? The perfect start to my Sunday morning and the fuel I needed to make it through a workout I really wasn't in the mood to start in the first place.   Decent bagels are so few and far between in Philly that South Street Bagels are automatically elevated to four star territory. There are better bagels to be had, but you'll have to travel to Jersey to get them. In the city, this spot corners the market.

I was initially bummed when APO closed its doors, but happy to discover that The Corner remains mostly the same, only with better cocktails and a food menu.   While I haven't tried any of the snacks, I have had several drinks including classic old fashioneds and martinis, plus one or two selections from the specialty cocktails menu. The Mother's Little Helper is like an old fashioned with a pumpkin twist. Pretty delicious.   My family also was quite pleased with the libations on a recent visit, when we all pre-gamed before going to see the Philadelphia Orchestra. The family that cocktails together gets cultured together, I suppose. We'll be back!

My sister and I made our maiden pilgrimage to the POPE on Saturday night after having dinner nearby. First impression? Nicest bar staff in the city. Also, cool dungeon!  From the moment we sat down to the moment we left, every bartender was happy to offer a suggestion, give a taste, have a chat, or whatever else was needed at the moment.   My sister is a light beer swilling girl, but in an attempt to break her out of that repressed world, I asked the bartender to recommend something easy-drinking for her to try. He pulled not one but two tastes, both of which she liked.   The following day, I ran into a friend who told me the POPE has some of the best fried chicken in the city. And since you know your girl loves some fried chicken, I'll be sure to return with the quickness.

I was part of a large group dinner at Spice 28 on Wednesday, and we had a great time. It's hard not to compare a lot of the menu items to the other king of Sichuan in Philadelphia, but Spice 28 is a very close second. And if it's ambiance you're looking for, Spice has the edge.   The great thing about this place is the variety of the menu. Creative selections like wontons with guacamole and tempura lobster add an extra layer to your main dish.   Speaking of the main dishes, the two I tried (dry pepper chicken and hot pot chicken) were so spicy that they bordered on unenjoyable. I could taste no difference in the degree of heat between spice levels two and three; both were hard on my pansy palate. That said, both were executed well, so I'll just opt for the lowest spice level next time. And there will be a next time.   The price was right and I've got a 10% off check-in offer that I plan on utilizing soon. Looking forward to my next round of tastebud ass-kicking.

I found Gene through a search for window cleaning and Yelp did not steer me wrong! I sent a message through the Request a Quote feature and heard back on the same day. Gene and I talked a couple times to figure out the best day for him to come out. He was always easy to get in touch with - something I definitely do not take for granted!   Within a week, Gene was at my house, giving my windows the thorough scrub down they so desperately needed. Insides, outsides, screens and windowsills - everything is spotless. My rooms are noticeably brighter and my house feels so ready for spring! It's also worth mentioning that Gene was courteous and professional - someone I would absolutely recommend to friends and neighbors looking for window cleaning (or power washing and carpet cleaning, since he does those, too). The price was very reasonable as well.   I'm extremely happy with my experience and look forward to calling on Gene again in the future!

I stopped by Bonejour on a whim on Sunday afternoon when I realized I still needed a gift for my sister's dog, Chubbs. The fluffy-haired kitty in the window knew how to work it when we walked in - she immediately started meowing at us and brushing up against her cage in a very cute way. How someone hasn't taken her home already, I have no idea. She almost had me convinced!   Once I broke my gaze I was able to focus on the many toys, treats, outfits (Chubbs has many) and other accessories. I grabbed a couple holiday items and braced myself for the total, which turned out to be very reasonable. The woman working was very helpful in answering questions about whether the things I selected would be appropriate for a small dog. I was even able to get everything gift wrapped in a bag with really cute paw-print tissue paper. One more check on my Christmas list!

I've been to this Crate & Barrel twice and experienced excellent customer service, both times by the same woman (Felecia).   On my recent visit, I picked up a pair of herb scissors (an amazing pair of scissors with about four sets of blades slightly spaced out so you can quickly dice up fresh basil, cilantro, etc. - genius!) as part of my mother's birthday gift. Naturally, I had left my card, bag and tissue paper on the couch at home, and when I mentioned this to Felecia, she promptly wrapped the shears in a nice bag with pretty tissue paper and gave me a little card. She saved me a trip and some money, and I was a happy camper.

Not that I've been to loads and loads of them in my life, but Woody's seems to be a gay bar with training wheels. It's got the tee-hee factor with the name, plus dance parties several nights a week with hordes of young, sweaty twenty-somethings grindin' up on the dance floor to Lady Gaga's latest and greatest.   Personally, I have to be feeling pretty good to not mind being closely surrounded on all sides while in a bar. That is absolutely unavoidable at Woody's on a busy night, so if you're squeamish about tight crowds like me, plan to drink heavily. Drinks are a bit pricey for the size but they're strong so they get points there.   Go in a group, have some fun, dance it up, but don't expect to be blown away. Well, maybe.

I ordered delivery from Al Zaytouna yesterday and went with my usual Mediterranean pick of chicken kebabs. I opted for grilled veggies instead of rice for $2 more. Unfortunately, as I have noticed in the past with orders from this restaurant, my chicken was once again super dry and actually difficult to cut with a knife. All other components of the platter were great. I'm downgrading to three stars since there are other Mediterranean spots that I like a bit more.

I can't believe I'm the first person to write a review for the new Grubhouse at The Bourse! My husband and I dropped by for breakfast. Grubhouse is known for their belly busting breakfast creations, but I like to stick to the lighter side, especially during the week. Still, my breakfast sandwich with turkey bacon, egg and cheese felt like a splurge. It was delicious! The brioche bun was super soft and flavorful and the single slice of American cheese was just right.    My husband had the sausage and pepper hash with egg which was sizeable and very tasty. It should be noted that breakfast at Grubhouse is also a bargain, with the sandwich costing six bucks and the breakfast bowl ringing in at only eight. Coffee is hot and served in a large to-go cup.   I look forward to many more breakfasts here! Pro-tip: They are one of the only vendors in the new Bourse Food Hall that is starting out with Sunday hours.

Eat-A-Pita has been on my to-try list for lunch ever since I attended their event for Yelp's In It To Thin It in the spring. So after a meeting nearby this morning, I popped over to grab a pita to go. My wheat pita, stuffed with carved turkey, avocado, lettuce, tomato and sprouts was absolutely delicious. All of the ingredients were plentiful and terrific. The parmesan peppercorn dressing I received on the side was probably the most tasty sandwich topping ever.   I noticed a sign with a list of soups above the register. I'll have to try some next time. Contrary to what I originally thought, Eat-A-Pita is a local establishment, not a big national chain or franchise. Everything is made in-house.   My only regret is that I don't live closer to this awesome lunch option. I'll probably just start creating excuses to visit Midtown Village around lunchtime more often.

I love Martha! While I'm sad we can't take advantage of their adorable outdoor patio right now, I'm very happy we can still swing by for takeout. While running errands in the neighborhood last week, we placed an order for a couple sandwiches, the olives, and some beer to-go. There were several other people picking up orders around the same time, which is always good to see.   The ordering process was easy and included options like sauce on the side, etc. I tried the Al's Toona and it was great! I opted for the sauce on the side and received a dressing, olive tapenade and sliced fresh jalapeños in small containers. This was especially appreciated as I saved half of my sandwich for the next day. The chips and pickles that came along with the sandwich were awesome! My husband got the Gladys, which he enjoyed. The olives were great as well and we enjoyed them as a snack.   Hopefully we'll be able to dine in again sooner than later but it's great to have Martha to-go in the meantime!

Peanuts roasted in-house, four different ways (but no option for salted, darnit).  Pistachios, cashews, jordan almonds, caramel popcorn, trail mix, dried fruits, animal crackers, chocolate and chocolate covered treats, those minty pastel-colored nonpareil thingers and pretty much everything else you can think of from your childhood five and ten can be found in this store.    Nuts to You is the PERFECT place to stop before a baseball game.    And now I want a snack.

A mix of old meets new, Sugarcube is a dream for fashionistas and frugal shoppers alike, male or female. Every item is hand selected by the dedicated staff, and the owners are passionate about their customers just as they are about their business. Anyone searching for a unique piece that no one else will have should consider this store.   In the fall, I coveted an 80s-inspired silky black and white blouse with billowy sleeves and slender, buttoned wrists; the back was cut in a sexy but flattering v-shape. Much to my chagrin, the piece was one of the new items and therefore, out of my price range. I'm still a little tormented by the memory of feeling like a stone cold fox in that top. Next time I have a little extra green to shell out on something special, I'm going back.

I stopped by Bodhi for the first time yesterday afternoon and I have to say, my feelings are inconclusive.   What I loved:  The quaint shop, with bright colors and a country feel.   Cupcakes are from Betty's Speakeasy (which is located in my neighborhood and is a place I frequent).  The barista was friendly and engaging.  In addition to the indoor seating there were a couple tables and chairs outside, where I happily sipped my iced coffee, even if I was on a major angle.  What I'm unsure about:   The coffee. Which is kind of the point here. Something about the taste was just off to me, and yet strangely addictive at the same time.   More visits are required for me to really decide my feelings, so until then, three stars.

Just got back from my first experience at Birra and I'll definitely be returning. It smelled like heaven when we walked through the doors around 4:30. The large bar takes up most of the space but tables along the outskirts provide additional seating.   Large plates aren't available until after 5pm but we were there for salad and pizza. The Caesar salad was large enough to share and came tossed in a delicious homemade dressing with a large parmesan crisp. We ordered the Gabagool pizza, with capocollo and arugula. The sauce was on the sweeter side and the meat wasn't as spicy as I was expecting. The toppings were generous and the pizza came straight from the oven. I'd probably switch it up on my next visit and try another type of pie. Looking forward to my next visit!

I met up with a friend at B2 recently and it was my first-ever visit. Really enjoyed the casual vibe and the extra large tables. I could definitely see myself getting some serious work done in that environment.   The coffee tasted great and it was strong. I was caffeine-buzzing all day long off of my large cup. I didn't have any food and I think the menu is pretty basic, but a toasting everything bagel smelled terrific, and the current main photo of the cucumber and goat cheese sandwich looks great. I'll be making a return trip soon.

After a meeting in the area, Maggie L and I decided to hit Pod for lunch. We started with the chicken lettuce wraps, which were really great and also very filling for two people. I wanted a martini but considered my workload and ordered an unsweetened iced tea, instead. It was super flavorful and served with a slice of orange - very nice!   Next up were: the jumbo lump California roll, a spicy tuna roll topped with rock shrimp, and a spicy yellowtail roll with fresh jalapeño slices (my favorite of the three for its lightness and extra heat!). I was very happy that all of the rolls were well balanced (not overly sauced) and easy to eat (not too big, not falling apart). This was the perfect amount of food for two fairly hungry people. If you're not feeling as hungry, the lettuce wraps and two rolls could suffice.   Our server was friendly and helpful yet a little slow for lunch. But I enjoyed my experience so much that I definitely wanted to bump up my rating to a more appropriate four stars!

As far as Panera locations go, I thought this one was okay. I didn't like it as much as the location I frequent most in Delran. I did the You Pick Two combo with French onion soup (I really like their version because it's not too heavy but still delicious) and the roasted turkey and avocado BLT which was super boring. The tomato was flavorless and the applewood smoked bacon was very reminiscent of microwave bacon. But it was one of the healthier options on the menu, without the mayo.   I do really love the Panera card because I seem to rack up rewards pretty quickly. As far as chain breakfast/lunch spots go, I'm a fan.

In my experience, the city version of a national store is usually lacking. I'll pick the 'burbs versions of Target, Lowe's, etc. any day. But I have to give it up to the Philadelphia Pier 1, because it's not half bad.   From small pieces of accent furniture to summer patio necessities, I've done my fair share of credit card swiping at this location. I especially love that you can see online if an item is available for pickup at the store. You can often have items shipped in for store pick-up for no extra charge, as well.   Check out the sales racks near the register, where there are often really cute stationery options and other office items for a steal!

My girlfriends and I ordered dinner from Luigi's one weeknight last week. They ordered a portabella mushroom pizza with whole wheat crust and a salad, and I went with a grilled chicken Caesar salad with tomatoes and dressing on the side. Everything arrived as requested, with extra pieces of grilled garlic bread for everyone.   Delivery was very fast. If I find out that they deliver to my neighborhood I'd definitely give them a try again.

I enjoyed my first Nom Nom Bowl experience! This is an order-by-screen situation so it's probably wise to consult the menu first. I ordered the goma tuna poke bowl and thought everything about it was delicious. I loved all the ingredients (even if I wasn't totally sure what all of them were) and the slightly spicy kick was a pleasant surprise.   I do think a build-your-own bowl option would be a nice addition to the menu, since I sometimes like to customize my own. Regardless, I definitely see myself enjoying many more bowls in the future!

I've been a Moorestown Mall shopper since my allowance days. This was the mall of choice during my grade school years, when Spencers, Time Out, the food court and movie theater were the only things that mattered.  As an adult, the variety of stores is limited, but less crowds makes for better parking and getting in and out and on your way quickly. This isn't the mall I'd choose if I were doing a major shopping trip, but if I just needed a basic top or pair of shoes or something in a cinch, it would do the trick. I'm a fan of Lord and Taylor for those items. And after all these years, the food court is still pretty decent.

I am one lucky lady with all the men in my life giving me flowers lately! Recently, I was gifted with a lovely arrangement from my friend, Dan F. Almost a full week later, the blooms are still sprightly and holding it down on my windowsill (see pic, aerial view).   I'm sure all the other sills in the 'hood are jealous, and they should be. Not all of them are fortunate enough to hold fresh, herbal greenery mixed with blossoms boasting the most amazingly accented petals.   Well. The secret's out now that the array is from Poppy. So all those green-eyed sills can just go get their own pretty mix. After all, imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

Fergie's is a great Irish pub that I only end up at every once in a while, but every time I do, I'm happy. Recently, I went for a meet-the-brewer event. The subject brew was Allagash, and every style I tried tasted super fresh and went down like water.   Now that the kitchen is being run by Mark Coates of Bebe's BBQ, I'm anxious to go back for dinner one night. I was lucky enough to sample a few bites of brisket, and the smoke flavor was off the charts. I can't wait to return with a full appetite and unleash my inner carnivore.

While I feel really bad about removing a couple stars from 11th Street, it has to be done. The guys who work there are the sweetest, and I don't doubt that they know their way around cars, but on my recent visit, I was told that my check engine light was on for something really minor and it was turned off and I went on my merry way.   When the light came back on a few weeks later, I took the car to my dealership and found out that my catalytic converter needed replacing. This is no cheap affair, but had it not been replaced, the engine could have blown, which would have been a catalytic catastrophe on my savings.  The guys at 11th Street were spot on about the heater's issues, so I'll give them that, although the temporary fix they finagled still left me on the receiving end of cold air after a day or so.   As much as I hate shelling my hard-earned money over to the dealership, at least I know my car is safe and the issues were addressed appropriately.

We had such a great experience at Birra last night that I just wanted to give a little update. After being seated at a nearby pizza restaurant and being ignored for a solid five minutes or so, we decided to cut our losses and head to Birra. I am so glad we did! Our server was totally great from the second we sat down.   We ordered the meatball appetizer and were told it would take about fifteen minutes to prepare. It ended up being a little longer, which wasn't a huge deal, but our server said that she took care of a round of our drinks to make up for it. What a pleasant surprise! I thought the meatballs were well worth the wait, but this was a nice gesture all the same. And as for those glasses of wine, if you order two of the same, they will bring over a half carafe, which easily provides for about three glasses total. I am a fan.

This is just like South Philly Paesano's, only a little rougher around the edges. Everything is delicious... As if there was any question. Call ahead if you want to skip the borderline risqué chatter from the cooks.

A friend and I met for lunch at Tria Taproom recently and I was shocked to find the place totally empty. So if, like me, you've had trouble getting in there on a Saturday night because of the crowds, check them out for lunch if you can!   I started with a glass of iced tea (definitely looking to getting back there for wine, however) and it was really delicious. Fresh-brewed and with some flavor. My friend and I ordered several plates to share. The octopus was tender and tasted great and the cobb salad was awesome. Plenty of thick-cut bacon and gorgonzola. I had the three cheese flatbread as well and really enjoyed it. There were nice slices of tomato on top that added just the right amount of acidity.   Really looking forward to more visits at Tria Taproom!

In terms of honeygrow experiences, this one was just okay. The ordering process was straightforward and easy as always, and there was a lot of seating in this particular location. I was in the mood for something different from my usual salad order. I had tried the red coconut curry before at an event so decided to go with that.   It took a while for the order to come up but since I was getting something hot instead of a salad, that was fine. When my name was called, I had to ask for a cup and the extra slice of bread that I ordered. I feel like this happens a lot at honeygrow; something often tends to be missing from the final order (occasionally, it's the salad dressing, which is super annoying when you get it all the way home!).   My noodles were so lightly dressed there was barely any flavor. I was glad I added on crunchy onions at the last minute, otherwise there woudn't have been much taste at all.   I really like honeygrow overall and especially their mission to use high-quality ingredients, but the experiences can be hit or miss.

Van saved my eyebrows from extreme unibrow territory when I blew through the doors of 4 Sisters yesterday afternoon. After a struggle with the meter outside, which wouldn't take my singles OR credit cards (what else is new, PPA?), I plopped in two quarters and had fifteen minutes to get in and get out.   The salon was clean and cute - I was surprised that I had never been there before. Van introduced herself and brought me to the private room, where in less than five minutes, my brows were shaped and looking good.   I'll definitely give 4 Sisters a look the next time I need a quickie mani or pedi as well.

I'm starting to realize I've got a thing for locally-owned neighborhood grocery stores. Walking into Riverwinds Produce over the weekend, I realized my ideal neighborhood grocery exists, even if it's located on the opposite side of the city from where I live!   This place has everything! From a nice selection of fresh produce to nearly every Philly-made baked good, snack, or beverage. We stopped in to stock up on Movement Labs' Yerba Maté, after learning it's no longer in production (wah!). We ended up finding several other items to get us through the week ahead, plus a friendly staff who were all happy to help. I'll be back the next time, and probably every time, I'm in Fishtown!

I absolutely loved Paperdolls Boutique! It was so much larger than most boutique shops and had a great array of clothing, from casual to dressy. I tried on an armful of items and found several pieces that I could have taken home. In the end, I went with a long skirt and a cute top. Neither piece was on sale but I liked them both so much that I didn't care.   The shop gals were friendly and helpful. There are also tons of accessories and small gift items. Great place to shop in St. Louis!

I popped into this Snap Kitchen location yesterday to stock up on meals for the week. The layout is exactly like the one in Old City, and there were friendly employees ready to answer any questions I had.   From this round of goods I've so far tried the curried chicken salad (very flavorful and perfect for a healthy, high-protein snack), the goat cheese and tomato tart, which was excellent, and the chimichurri beef. After trying several of the medium-sized entrees, the beef was easily the heartiest and most filling.   Snap might seem pricey, but when I compare it to the amount of ordering out I generally do during the week, it all evens out. I definitely feel like my meals are way healthier when I buy in advance for the week, instead of waiting until 2pm day-of and making terrible choices because I'm too hungry to think straight.  Snap, I am picking up what you're putting down.

I appreciate local businesses and water ice is a very welcome seasonal treat born out of Philadelphia. However, I wasn't super impressed by my experience at Pop's. The young woman working the window was a little curt and my order was incorrect. When I realized this and went back over to the window, I was given a brand new full-size replacement, no questions asked. That was nice.   The water ice itself was extra watery and the flavor was kind of bland (I had cherry and lemon). Maybe we stopped by on an off day. I'd give it another shot if I was in the area. Also, they sell soft pretzels and there's nothing like a water ice and soft pretzel combo!

I don't understand the obsession with this place.  Yes, they have a great beer selection.  So do many other establishments in the city.  The food is okay but is it worth having to wait an hour and change in the overcrowded aisle next to the bar for a table at 10 p.m. on a Friday?  Hell to the no.    The duck spring rolls are bland compared to others I've tasted in the city (Pearl and XIX) and the Monk's Burger is like a red-headed stepchild next to the Good Dog's Good Dog Burger.  Speaking of which, who orders a burger and thinks, "what I really want on the side is a nice, dainty pile of spring mix salad?!"  It's like they trick you into ordering the fries because who really eats a burger without fries?  Infuriating.  I'd go back if I were outnumbered in a group of Monk's devotees, but not by my own free will.

What an adorable old-timey ice cream shop! How my very first visit occurred just two nights ago, after the majority of my adulthood has been spent hanging out in the city, I don't know.  My small dish of coffee ice cream topped with homemade hot fudge was one of the best experiences in ice cream I've ever known. I had no idea what real hot fudge was before tasting it at Franklin Fountain. Smooth, buttery, chocolate - that's what.   The prices are steep but the quality was so high that I'd gladly fork over my hard-earned cash. This could seriously become an addiction.

Decent local bar, good for catching the game and some snacks. The kitchen is open late every day, which is something that isn't always easy to find. The beer selection is pretty solid.   Friends and I stopped in on Thursday night for some beers and snacks. We ordered cheese fries, cheesesteak egg rolls and a chicken quesadilla. The food was good enough for late night munchies, but I probably wouldn't seek out New Wave for a regular meal. That said, I'd be fine with popping in while in the neighborhood to view a game and enjoy a cold one.

Cute coffee shop which would serve as an excellent place to read a book, have a meeting or get some work done. I opted for a cup of the cold brew on nitro which was smooth and delicious and required less cream than I'd normally put in my coffee.   My meeting took place on one of the comfortable couches. Afterwards, I moved myself to a table in an effort to get some work done. Unfortunately, the wifi was down so I ended up having to leave for another spot, but I'm looking forward to returning for either a meeting or just a quiet, cool place to work.

McMillan's is probably the greatest bakery ever.  A friend of mine is so obsessed with their cakes that he will use any and every excuse to make a stop.  Rumors of the infamous cream donuts at McMillan's made their way to me when my coworkers discovered my weakness.  I didn't believe the hype, opting to stick with my old standby, Dunkin Donuts' kreme-filled chocolate-frosted (occasionally with sprinkles) donut, on the rare occasion that I started my day with such an indulgence.  One day, a visitor to our office brought in a huge bakery box filled with deliciousness from McMillan's.  There were several cream-filled donuts and I think I visualized my name written in the powdered sugar on one of them.  It was love at first bite.    I still have love for ya, Dunkin Donuts, but I hope you don't mind being the side piece for now on.

Nick's is a South Philly dive with cheap domestics and ultra delicious roast beef sandwiches and delightfully greasy, crispy fries. Sports play on the TVs over the bar.    Don't expect coddling of any kind from the servers; they are rushing around and their only mission is to deliver the goods and get you out of those seats as quickly as possible. On a recent visit, our group stood awkwardly by the door for ages without being acknowledged by anyone. Eventually, we made our way to the bar and took over a couple high top tables. In the bar area, you can order food and drinks directly from the bartender, which was just fine with us.  Everyone in our crew was in agreement that the sandwiches hit the spot. We shared a couple orders of the gravy fries which were sinfully fantastic. Paul R hit the nail on the head when he said it's a great spot to bring friends from out of town. I can't wait to go back for another visit, myself.

This movie theater and I go way back. It used to be part of the Ritz group and it always had a very arty, coffee house vibe.   Now, it's part of the AMC fam so the feel has changed a bit. While the concessions are solid, the rest of the theater is not on par with other area AMCs that have been upgraded.   Still, this is one of the better options in South Jersey for catching a flick, and one of my preferred theaters if I'm rolling solo. Fingers crossed for some upgrades!

This is one of my favorite Wawas, because I generally walk in looking like a swamp creature after my bootcamp class and no one even bats an eye. In fact, the employees go out of their way to be friendly and conversational.   The store is well stocked and there are always fresh cut mangoes in the cold case. Two thumbs up.

I never think to make Omoi a destination, but visits tend to happen whenever I find myself walking by. Last Saturday, a friend and I were walking past and she said, "What is that place?" Stunned, I dragged her into the store. I thought everyone knew about this cute little shop with Japanese flair!   There are so many fun little gifts and trinkets to peruse. I immediately spotted a suede magenta bag that I could envision as my pop of color while wearing a black dress. It was forty bucks. I'm still thinking of going back to grab it. I bet I'd use it all the time.   Instead, I ended up picking up a card from their wall of terribly amusing creations. There's a little section for every imaginable scenario. And I feel pretty confident that my recipient won't have already come across said card in every single drug store across town.

MOD is a great fast casual option for customizable pizzas and salads. That said, it is not your standard pizza parlor pie, but more of an upgraded make-at-home version. I love that you can select from some tried and true combos or simply design your own. The pizzas are ready in minutes, so that's definitely a plus.   Last week, I stopped in for a pizza and salad to go. The guy who took my order was nice and patient. I was bringing everything back over the bridge so my husband got the oven started so we could reheat the pizza once I arrived; definitely a good call as the crust is so thin that the pizza cools quickly. I knew one pizza for two people would be stretching it which is why I also got a salad. The Italian dressing was great!   I'd probably lean towards dining in for the future because the food is best when served right away.

In my opinion, this is by far the best restaurant on Haddon Ave.  The martini list is a mile long, the newly renovated bar is really classy, service is always wonderful and the food is consistently fantastic.    I've probably gotten crab cakes 90% of the time I have eaten here, and they are always fresh and made with big chunks of crab meat.  Portion sizes are on the very large side.  You will never leave here hungry, and if you do, I would suggest a Lap-Band.  Seriously.      All desserts are homemade and brought around on a large tray so you have to physically look at them before you decide.  It kind of breaks my heart a little on the days that I pass and just have a coffee instead, because my head is screaming "GIVE ME THOSE THREE ON THE UPPER RIGHT!!!!!!!"  However, if I'm here for a special occasion, I'm always down for splitting something sweet!

I'm pretty much loving this place. I've landed at Boot & Saddle as my closer bar on three occasions now. Our servers have been great despite the crowds, and we've somehow scored seats pretty quickly each time. I love the dim lighting and the original artwork and wall decor from the bar's previous incarnation.  The draft list is pretty solid and rotates often. I was thrilled to see Pliny the Elder during a recent visit but it was gone just one week later. Glad I got to partake while they had it. If you don't fancy any of the drafts, the bottle list should have what you're after.   The food menu is small but solid. While I wasn't crazy about the roasted pumpkin and kale soup (I was expecting creamy but it was broth-based), I did love the grilled cheese and hash browns with spicy cheese sauce.   Really, the only thing I don't love is the cocktails. I've made my way through most of the offerings and they just aren't doing it for me. Stick with beer or drink your whiskey straight for best results.

I had been told repeatedly by a friend before my trip to Nashville that I had to visit Las Paletas while there. The place reminded me a lot of Philly's Little Pop Shop, with interesting flavors and pops starting at $2.50. I wanted something light and fruity so I chose the cantaloupe flavor. It tasted like biting into a fresh cantaloupe, only as a popsicle! It was awesome. My friend enjoyed her chocolate with banana chunks pop. Definitely worth a visit on a hot day!

I had been to Champps once before and didn't remember being all that impressed, but my sister insisted that they have the best nachos ever and that they would feed all three girls in our group who were jonesin' for some junk food.  We enter the restaurant which appears to be in decent shape and we head to the table.  Appearances can be deceiving!  The floor was littered with straw wrappers, food and other random debris.  It looked like a toddler convention had taken place in the dining area.  Once seated, I kicked the chicken chunks out from under my chair and announced that I was heading to the restrooms.  Of 5 toilets, only one of the three that remained unoccupied was not flushed.  You know you are in a crappy place when the patrons can't be bothered to flush the toilet.  Pun intended.  Back at the table, my appetite still miraculously intact, we dove into a nacho plate that was good, and definitely huge, but not good enough to ever get me back in this place.  I'm giving two stars because the food wasn't bad and our server was awesome.

This was the closest liquor store to my apartment when I lived in Collingswood, so it got some pretty decent business out of me during my 4+ years there. Cook's has an okay selection of craft beer for such a small store, and the prices aren't too bad. Wine options are solid and fairly priced. Now that I live in Philly where even a bottle of Ecco Domani will cost you, I can appreciate the place even more. I also like that there is always a nice selection of chilled whites ready for BYO-ing. And the staff has always been great. I miss regular Jersey liquor stores!

I fell in love with this adorable store on Passyunk when I first stopped in around the holidays. At that point, my shopping was complete but there were so many cute gift ideas that I knew it was only a matter of time before I would return.   In need of a baby gift and recalling the locally-made and locally-inspired onesies, I returned to find something cute for my best guy friend's adorable baby girl. This time, most of the onesie designs were super hipster. This would be great for some of my friends but totally lost on this particular couple. Fortunately, I spotted some handmade baby blankets. So soft and with gently colored patterns, it was immediately evident that this was the perfect gift. And the price was more than fair. The woman working wrapped the blanket in pink tissue paper and placed it into a simple brown shopper with the store's name. Easy peasy! Next time I need a gift that doesn't break the bank, I'm checking out Nice Things first.

Bar Ferdinand had long been on my "to try" list. Our party of four plus a dog arrived on a Sunday evening and we were fortunate enough to get a table outside right away. We took some time discussing the menu and came up with a pretty extensive list.   Highlights for me were the surtido de carnes (charcuterie board consisting of four delicious cured meats), patatas bravas (fried potatoes in a tasty aioli), datiles rellenos (stuffed dates), queso de cabra cocinado (baked goat cheese with pine nuts) and the almejas (steamed clams). These items would all make my list on a return visit.   Items that left me less impressed were the empanadas, which had so much potential but ended up tasting kind of bland. Same with the stuffed peppers, which had little flavor other than the peppers themselves. The hits were far greater than the misses, and I'm looking forward to seeing how the menu changes with Ansill's reign.

My fiance proposed in April with a ring from Barsky. I couldn't have done better if I had picked out the ring myself - it was exactly what I wanted!   Fast forward several months. The ring has always been loose, but over the winter it has been looser than ever so I knew I had to get it resized, and quickly. I brought the ring to Barsky the day before Valentine's Day, because I like to torture people. Kidding, but I happened to be in the area so I made a stop, knowing I would most likely have to leave the ring for several days. I was told it would take about a week. When I mentioned that I had an event to attend on the following Wednesday, the gentleman helping me said he would get it done in time.  I called on Wednesday and sure enough, my ring was ready for pick-up. The end result was stunning. Not only does the ring fit perfectly but it looks like it is back to its original condition - all sparkly and shiny! We'll be heading back to look at wedding bands and I'm looking forward to that experience as well.

I had frozen yogurt for the first time in my adult life at Yogorino last night. Turns out, it's changed a lot since I was little and isn't at all like the stuff found in the freezer section at the grocery store. Creamy, slightly tart but still just sweet enough, I took one look at the plastic jugs of fake syrup toppings and instead opted for some fresh chopped nectarines.   As a few others have pointed out, it is hard to distinguish what each topping is just from the sign on the wall. Meringue pieces looked like mochi, the sauces were unidentifiable from each other, etc.  The price points were fair, and I left satisfied but not too full from a small cup.

I am embarrassed at how many times I have walked by this little boutique and haven't walked in to shop. Thank goodness, I discovered them at their outside booth during the Lafayette Holiday House tour.   My cousin and are the family shoppers and after browsing the items at the outdoor booth, we headed up the street to check out the store. We weren't the only ones with this brilliant idea, the store was packed. After finding several gifts for different people on our Santa list, we opted to return later to make our purchases and avoid the crowd.   Without giving away details, because a recipient may be reading this review. We found several unique and STL themed gifts for local sports fans and bar items for the boozers. We do not discriminate, we shop for the naughty and nice.   The staff was friendly and very helpful with our selections. This little shop will now be one of my go to stores for unique gifts and I'll be shopping local.   Will I return? - YES!  When: December 10, 2017 Why: Naughty or Nice List

I thought when I went to the Early Bird Special today I'd be joining a bunch of diners my age and older. To our surprise, we were the oldest ones in the dining room. It was all young professionals taking advantage of the $9.95 dinner special.   Both of us enjoyed the 8 oz Ribeye which came with a salad and a side dish of your choice. I choose my favorite vegetable, asparagus as mine. It was five stalks, that were prepared perfectly. They were tender with just enough snap. My dining partner went with their pasta with red sauce. He said the penne noodles were done al dente and the sauce was a traditional marinara.   The Ribeye's were tender and we both had them done medium rare. 8 oz may seem small to some, but it was the perfect size for a lite dinner. Our Early Bird Dinner also included a dinner salad, making this a very fulfilling meal.   If you're on a budget or just want to save a few bucks, eat early (3PM - 6PM Monday-Thursday) at Joey B's and you'll enjoy a great meal.

I am happy to say, Cassy the owner and executive chef at HWK has contacted me and was in shock that I had the experience that I did. She assured me that was not their policy and was going to use this situation as a teaching moment with her front of the house staff.   I appreciated her outreach and will attempt to dine at HWK again. Once I do, hopefully you'll see another increase in stars.

Wow, this is the best Marshalls I have ever shopped. It was clean, well organized and had stuff I actually wanted to buy. The other day I went shopping at The Rack, looking for a short sleeved linen shirt and had no luck. I found it here and for only $20. What a deal. I hope they can keep it up. If they can, I will be a repeat offender. I mean, I will be a repeat shopper.   I only shopped the Men's Dept., but the shoe selection looked huge as did the home area.   Deer Creek Plaza has been totally redone, I'm looking forward to shopping the other new stores as they open.

This is a pretty amazing bar, it has the feeling of a true neighborhood bar, and like Kelly B. said, "that happens to be downtown." If I lived downtown, I'd have a name plate on one of the bar-stools.  I would never drink at home alone, I would be here with all my friends. This is the "Cheers" of St. Louis.   The drinks here are cheap and with the free pour that the bartenders do here, they are worth every cent. Some of their rail liquor is what some bars offer as "call brands".   The party room downstairs is a great place for a friends gathering to celebrate special occasions. I only got to sample a few food offerings the night I visited,  from a small buffet. What I did sample was good bar grub, but I want to go back and taste what I here is, "the best cheeseburger".   Jack I'm giving you fair warning, I'm going to be back.

It's Sunday night and the Cards are in the playoffs, we're not cooking or going out for dinner. We didn't want pizza, Chinese or any type of fast food. We were at a a loss for ideas. I was searching Yelp for ideas and checked to see if Joey B's did carry- out and to my surprise they did.  We checked the menu and made the call.   We ordered two of their Blue Plate Specials; Country Fried Chicken and Homemade Meatloaf. Both came with mashed potatoes and gravy and corn on the cob. The meatloaf also came with a side salad that was humongous, it was big enough for both of us to share. My Homemade Meatloaf  with a brown gravy truly had to down home taste. It is way better then other "Blue Plate Specials" near and on "The Hill". My SO enjoyed his Country Fried Chicken and its white gravy topping. Their great taste surprised us coming from a sports bar which is known for burgers and pizza.   I think Joey B's will be getting some more carryout orders from us.  They're close, the prices are right and the food is good.

If you've ordered pizza from Bono's you know it's the real deal. However, this review I was to highlight their Chicken Wings. Many local pizza joints and chains offer chicken wings, but none of them compare to those at Bono's. They have the best wings of all the pizza delivery places in my hood.   Bono's wings are good size, meaty, juicy and well coated in their house sauce. I've been know to order a double order for a night of movies at home. To make it a true meal, I add a Caesar Salad. Or I just add an order of Cheese Garlic Bread and let the movie roll.   Great pizza, but I love their wings too.

If you haven't heard, the Tuesday Blue Plate Special is now Tacos and it is a sure fire way to get a good Mex-Fix.  You'll have three tacos; a chorizo, a carnitas, and a mixed-vegetable, along with rice and beans. As usual you'll get the flavorful house salad and a glass of iced tea. ( I love their salad dressing, wish it was available bottled.) Now let's talk about the new blue plate itself. I'd be hard pressed to select which taco I thought was best, each was in a class of it's own.  I was surprised that I actually liked the vegetable taco. The broccoli had a crisp snap and the red pepper and onion added extra flavor. The beans were just okay, need something to give it  a bang. Ask for their hot sauce, add it to the rice and you've got a great side to your tacos.  This place is still the best value for lunch.

Is the Egg White Delight McMuffin, delightfully delicious? Yes, if you add Frank's Hot Sauce.   When you break down the nutrition facts and compare the new Egg White to the Regular McMuffin, there really isn't that much of a difference. You save 50 calories and 5 grams of fat ordering the EW. Ordering the regular Egg McMuffin you lose 1 gram of fiber and get 20 mg less of Sodium. If you count points on the Weight Watchers program, a regular McMuffin is 8 points and the new Egg White is 7. One point is not that big of a savings. The egg whites and white cheddar is not exclusive to the McMuffin, you can try it on any egg & cheese sandwich. Which means, you can have it your way. Oh wait, that is another burger joints phrase.   Normally I am not a fan of McDonalds, but this one is close to work and surprisingly is better then any of the ones near my home in Saint Louis. When I am in need of a quick breakfast, this is a great place to stop. The staff is friendly and awake when I stop by at 5:30 AM.

Ben (chef/owner)  from Salume Beddu and Andrey (General Manager)  from 33 Wine Shop have taken an old 1930's gas station and turned it into a trendy little wine bar. The bar area is compact, cozy and all the windows give it a felling  of being larger then it really is.   Great wine by the glass, tasting flights measured to perfection and an impressive selection of liquor as well. I went craving a red wine, but when I saw they offered Tito's Vodka my favorite I was swayed away.   We enjoyed a sampling of artisan cured meats and hard cheese served with fresh bread and oil.   A great place for Happy Hour or after theater drinks.

Before my last visit I quick tipped this business as a great asset to our neighborhood, I may have jumped the gun. It has a long way to go, but they are still fairly new, so I am sure they are suffering from growing pains.  First thing that we found distracting is the big cooler in the lounge area. Find it a new home, it ruins the ambiance that you have created and it is a good feeling. Secondly, don't down grade yourself with the Robert Mondavi - Woodbridge table tents. Your serving quality wines, and everyone knows Woodbridge does not fall into that category.   The staff is friendly and provides good service, but while we were there they seemed to be over staffed and falling over each other.  They've decorated well for the holidays and I love the heated front patio and the fire pit in the back patio.   I'll revisit and I am sure they'll pull it together so I can upgrade my # of stars.

Reading some of these other Yelp reviews, I figure someone got spanked at this store and most likely got spanked hard. The reason I say this is, every time I have shopped here the customer service is has been the quality of a high end retailer and we're shopping for office supplies here. They now know the importance of good CS.   There is an OM closer to my home, but when I am in need of office stuff, I drive the extra distance to this OF. One reason I like this Office Depot, is that I can get certain supplies such as: paper clips, rubber bands, binder clips, etc. in the color orange. Orange is my favorite color and kinda my signature color, so it seems appropriate to have these daily work items in orange. Oh, who am I kidding - the reason I buy these things in orange is so I know when some one has "stolen" my desk stuff.  Great store. Clean, well organized, good selection and as mentioned above - very good customer service.   Feels kind of weird giving an office supply store a 4, but they deserve it.

Drizzle, Drazzle, Drozzle, Drone. Time a this one to have a frozen custard.   One of the rewards of shopping at Garden Heights Nursery on Big Bend is being able to enjoy a treat from Mr. Wizard. I have recently had enough sweet treats, that I am now in a position to agree with Stephanie S.. Ted Drews can only wish he could be as good as Mr. Wizard.   The custard at Mr. Wizard is richer, creamier and more flavorful then TD's. It is so good, I can even enjoy his custard plain with no toppings. When I do, they add just the right amount of topping to the concrete. They even have me expanding my choices in flavors. My most recent choice was Nestle Crunch.   I am thankful that I do not live close to Mr. Wizard. If I did, I would find some reason to reward myself with a custard treat almost everyday and I'd most likely end up being  the same size as the governor of New Jersey.

Yawn! Boring. Nothing special. Chocolate Covered Cherry use to be my go to order, but tonight it fell flat. My taste buds felt no excitement while I ate my, concrete.   What happened to you Mr. Wizard? I use to love you, but you were totally bland tonight. To be honest, there was absolutely no flavor to your custard tonight. I also am doubting if your staff got my order right. I think they actually served me yogurt instead of custard.   Product wise, I'd give you 2 Stars, but the friendly and professional young lady working the window got you the extra star.   When: July 19, 2016 Why: Ice Cream/Custard Sweet Treat

I live right in the middle of Colors of Springs and another nursery. I will be honest and say, I support both of them. However, I will say when it comes to trees, bushes and roses, I buy them at Colors of Spring.  I am amazed at how healthy and beautiful their selections are, and how they have flourished in my yard. I've bought 4 trees, 5 bushes and 3 roses and love'm all.  Their staff came to my house and assisted us in the placement of our new landscaping. Not being versed in planting, I paid for their services to plant our new landscaping. We've gotten so many complements on our yard thanks to Colors of Spring.

I had to raise my rating to 5 Stars after Friday nights dinner at Farmhaus. Everything we had was totally off the charts. We had a blast sharing comments about our feast with the table of ladies next to us.  Our table started out with Butternut Squash Soup, Roasted Mushroom Salad and Fish Chowder. I wish the bowl of Fish Chowder was bottomless, it was that amazing. The seared Tuna Steak Floating in the bowl was the best Tuna I have ever experienced.  Our entree's were the Escolar and the Bacon Wrapped Meatloaf. Both melted in your mouth, with the Escolar getting the highest marks. I wanted to try the Blackened North Carolina Amberjack, but having a guest from Texas I wanted him to experience the "famous" meatloaf. The desserts, let me just say I'll be doing extra laps around Tilles Park.  Service at Farmhaus is incredible, they always friendly and make me feel special. If you haven't gone to Farmhaus  I have only one question for you. What are you waiting for? When you go I recommend reservations, it's that popular.

Attention: I hope my 5 Star Rating draws attention to their need for DONATIONS. My recent visit found thin and boring retail racks. Please donate, especially men's clothing.   What a major disappointment. I had heard such great things about this shop, so I thought I'd give it a visit. I was shocked at the small and poor variety of items. I hate to admit it, but I have more clothes at home in my closets and off season racks in the basement then they did in their entire mens department. I felt so bad for them, that it inspired me to go home and clean out my closets to make a donation. Which I will be dropping off next week.   This charitable organization does such great work in our community. Their work alone deserves 5 Stars. The Scholarship Foundation of St. Louis is a nonprofit organization providing access to higher education throughout our community. They provide interest-free, fee-free loans and grants to over 600 area students. That's something our government doesn't even do.   Please, donate and shop the ScholarShop.   When: June 28, 2016 Why: Checking it out.

I've tried to come back to you this year Ted, but it just isn't working for me anymore.  Your custard isn't as thick and creamy as it once was and your staff is developing attitude.   You are no longer the only custard in town, you now have competition and they are all serving up a better product. Even Andy the new boy in town is providing a superior cup or cone of custard.   I know I am giving a big thumbs down to a St. Louis institution, but it really isn't that good, guys and gals.

If you need a gadget or gizmo for cooking or baking, chances are you'll find it here at Kitchen Conservatory. KC is like a Williams-Sonoma, Sur LaTable and the kitchen department at Bed, Bath and Beyond on steroids.  Instead of shopping a chain, you can shop local and buy your gadgets and gizmos here. You'll pay substantially more, but it is worth it because you are supporting a local business. Also, it is common sense that the knowledge from the staff is worth the extra cents.   I've heard their cooking classes are some of the best in the city, so I'll be checking them out so I can hopefully bump them up a star or two.

This is not my usual Lowe's, but next time I need to shop the "Big Box" I will think of this one. During a recent rain and wind storm, I lost one of my favorite ceramic pots. My banana plat survived, but I was left with a "cracked pot" and it was orange my favorite color.   I went on a mission shopping, trying to find a replacement. I wasn't even looking for another orange pot, I just wanted a style and size that could accommodate my plant. Being the end of September, my selection of pots was limited. Or at least pots that meet my standards. This Lowe's was my fifth store, yes I was that obsessed with finding the right pot.  As I entered their garden area, it was love at first sight. It was the right size, not breakable, on sale and it was orange. I could not have been happier.   My usual Lowe's is Kirkwood or Loughborough, but now that Maplewood has won my heart, I'll be back. Funny thing, the Maplewood location is closer to my home. I guess Dorothy is right, "there is no place like home".

Everywhere we go, people want to know, who we are...... We are the birds, the mighty, mighty birds.......  That is part of an old high school cheer. I'm a graduate of Southwestern High School and the Piasa Bird was our mascot. So the Piasa Bird has a special place in my heart. Growing up in the area, I remember another location of the bird being painted on the bluffs. It was sit back further from the road, so this present day location is more tourist friendly.   When visiting the Alton and Grafton area, it is worth a stop to view the painting and to read the legend of the mighty, mighty Piasa Bird.

We've expanded our Bono experience and tried their Calzone and am glad we did. It was awesome, a nice change from doing pizza and wings.   Calzone & salad a perfect lunch for when stuck at home alone.

Great little new pet shop, that is off the beaten path. If it is near your neighborhood, it is well worth searching out. It is just east on Elchelberger off Hampton.   They have a good selection of premium pet foods, toys and collar & leashes. What also makes this place stand out is the friendly staff and customer service. I also liked the area where you can wash your own four legged friend for a minimal fee.   We're all taking the Yelp pledge to shop local and this would be a great place to shop for you fur-babies.

Walking here and back home, helps me justify the calories. (Round trip is about 5 miles) My favorite concrete is M & M's, for some reason - I just keep ordering it time again and again. I also like raspberry. However, every year my first order is always just a dish of the custard plain - to experience the best frozen custard in the Midwest. Whatever your favorite is, it will make a great concrete or sundae. You'll also enjoy checking out all the celebrity autographs in the window

Safe and Secure, that is how I feel with ADT Security Services. I originally started out with Brinks Home Security when I had a system installed in my home. Then with mergers and buy-outs, I am now with ADT and in my opinion it is for the best.   When I wanted to get rid of my landline, ADT made it so easy for me to transfer everything over to a cellular program. Most recently, ADT notified me of changes to the cellular program and sent a tech out to my home to make the necessary changes to my equipment. This visit was at not cost to me. That makes me a happy loyal customer.   On occasion I have had to call the customer service department for various reasons and have never had a long wait period. My calls and questions have all been dealt with in a minimum amount of time. I believe that since they are dealing with, "security" that they respond quickly.  If you are looking for a home or business security system - I recommend ADT.

If you're from STL, you know JBD is the place to go for your Halloween costume needs and Mardi Gras Beads. I recently learned it is also the place to go for Elf and Santa Costumes, too.   My cousin told me she was searching for Elf accessories that she could wear when volunteering at the USO's Christmas event. I told her I'd swing by Johnnie's and see what I could find. It was like I found the pot of gold. They had a huge variety of all types of accessories to create a whimsical elf outfit. I was also amazed at the huge selection of tradition style Santa suits in a wide range of prices.   Other departments I noticed on this shopping expedition, was theatrical make-up and crowns. They had an amazing selection of rhinestone tiaras for Homecoming Queens or beauty pageant winners.   The store is huge, well kept and the staff can give you creative ideas to get you started.
