Patience is a virtue and it is one I do not have. Sometimes when I want something, I don't want to wait. I want it and I want it NOW. I'm starting a low-carb diet and was wanting the New Atkins book and cookbook. Sure, I could have gotten on the internet and ordered it from Amazon at a cheaper price and waited a week for its' arrival. However today, I was able to walk in to B&NB, get both books, not pay shipping and start reading tonight.  The store is easy to navigate. If you know the type of book and category it would be located in, it should be an easy find. I found my books with ease. My cashier was friendly and tried to sell me their frequent shopper/readers card. It offers some nice perks, but for me the $25 annual fee wasn't worth it. If you're a true bookworm, it would be a bargain.

When: March 6 Why: Shopping for area rug  Thought this was suppose to be a "Super Target", with a larger and better selection then the others. If so, I was not impressed. My usual Target had the same selections.   I found this store to be poorly organized, cluttered and just on the other side of dirty. It did not make for a pleasant shopping experience. The clerks we dealt with, were too busy doing task work then providing customer service and closing a sale.   Enough has been said about the parking, after all it is The Promenade and it is always a pain.

The boss treated to lunch today, and part of our order came from Papa John's. We had some team members who appreciate a more traditional crust over the St. Louis thin crust, so their choice was Papa.   Papa may be in the house, but his pizza just doesn't make the cut.  I will admit the topping were plentiful and there was plenty of cheese, but it was tuff and chewy.   Delivery girl was just so-so, nothing to write about. When you deliver to me, I want to see some gratitude, make me want to order from you again.   I am done with larger pizza chains, I am learning that the privately owned and those who only have a shop or two are the ones who are truly mastering the art of pizza.   The next time the boss treats to lunch, I taking charge and driving outside the city limits and exposing my co-workers to a true pizza experience.

Great Maplewood location, providing a larger space to produce more of those great chocolates and brittle. The bacon brittle and sea salt caramels are my favorites.   Same great friendly customer service.   Now I have one close to work and one close to home. I am a happy chocoholic.

I am sad to say, I am subtracting a star and removing Porter's from my Crispy Chicken List. Our last two dinners were lackluster and if either of them were my first experience at Porter's I never would have had the love affair I did with them. They seem to have lost their focus on both customer service and frying up crispy chicken.

Cupcakes are the perfect size cake in my opinion. They provide portion control and satisfy the desire for something sweet.   The presentation here at The Cup, is fantastic. They decorate each cupcake as if it were a full sized cake. Making them a perfect treat or for celebrating a special event. Their staff is polite and engaging, making you want to return time and time again.   My favorite is by far the Red Velvet. It is always moist and rich in flavor.  Another one that I favor is Raspberry Truffle, yummy yummy.   I know they do a fine business here, I just wish they were on the main drag of Maryland instead of being hidden in the "rear". I think more people would notice them and it would bring in more new biz. I myself forget about them when I'm in the Plaza. Out of sight , out of mind and these cupcakes are too good to miss out on.   My next party or celebration,  desserts are coming from The Cup.

OMG! Who knew? I didn't know until my friend Norma, took me here on a shopping outing. She had a coupon she wanted to redeem and as we browsed the store I was in total amazement. I was totally blown away by the selection and prices.   It's a big box like Lowe's and Home Depot minus all the bullshit. By that I mean, there is no lumber, garden shop or appliances. They totally focus on tools and hardware. I saw things I have always wanted at lower prices and discovered new gadgets that I never knew I wanted or needed.   If you go, by all means sign up for their mailings and e-mails. You'll receive coupons that will get you discounts on their already low prices. If your a handyman or handywoman, you owe it to yourself to check Harbor Freight Tools out.

Dados is a fairly new little cafe in the St. Louis Hills neighborhood. For me it's a great place to grab a quick lunch. It's conveniently located on Hampton Avenue near Eichelberger.   I stopped by one day during the holidays, when I needed to rejuvenate myself after some power shopping. The menu is simple and my eyes were immediately drawn to the Mile High BLT. I can tell you, there is no comparison with the one you get at Crown Candy Kitchen. Dados does it way better. They toasted the bread perfectly, just enough mayo, crisp lettuce, fresh tomato and of course crisp and crunchy bacon. I was glad to see that the fries they offered as a side, were the thick cut Steak fries. They're my favorite. I would have liked them to have been fried a little more crisper, but my BLT was so good I didn't mind.   I plan to stop by again to try some of their Greek dishes like the salad and gyro. Also, a burger with those big steak fries would be a nice lunch, too.   When: December 11, 2015 Why: Lunch

I've been back to this TB a couple of times since my initial visit and have decided to lower their overall rating to 3 stars.  The ambiance and customer service are still 4 star worthy, but the food has dropped to 3 stars. It has become your typical TB fast food. Good for a quick cheap lunch or a post bar late night treat.   Today's visit was to experience the highly promoted "Dorito Taco" that is being chatted up and down on our local Yelp talk thread. It wasn't that bad, the shell really tasted like a dorito chip.  Would I want my taco shell to taste like a dorito all the time? Hell no, but this one time was okay. I do give extra credit points to TB for serving the dorito shell in a cardboard sleeve.  It prevented me from getting "orange" fingers.   Overall, I still say this is one of the best Taco Bells I have visited. As for the Dorito Taco I can at least say, "been there, ate that".

Have you ever wondered what the test kitchen looks like for Hardee's?  I am confident that it is clean and has some of the coolest kitchen gadgets and appliances. What I am curious to know is what the staff who creates their new menu items look like. They can not look like the sexy actors & models who appear in Hardee's commercials. Their high fat and calorie loaded menu items have to be created by little Pillsbury Dough boys and girls.   Being a fan of bacon, when I saw the new commercials for the Bacon Bacon Biscuit, I knew I'd be visiting soon. How can I resist a flaky buttery biscuit, filled with crispy bacon strips, Canadian bacon, cheddar cheese and a fluffy egg. I heard my arteries closing up as I ate my breakfast treat. Hardee's biscuits are by far the best fast food biscuits. I'd even say, they can beat some of the diners in quality. It is obvious they are made by hand and not frozen.   Now that I have tried the BBB, my next adventure will be their Jalapeno Burger. I'll be doing extra reps or time on the treadmill to burn those extra calories.

Meet several friends here for lunch, and I must admit I was pleasantly surprised. Being closely bonded with these friends, we shared our entree experiences. I had the Stuffed & Grilled Portabella Sandwich - FANTASTIC! (the favorite of all) I loved the combination of red pepper, asparagus, and avocado was amazing and the waffle fries were better then a steak cut french fry. My friends had the Fried Chicken Salad and the Red Lion Soft Cheddar Burger, and both were very good. The combination of beef, pork and lamb in the RL Burger adds a kick of flavor that will take you by surprise. The Fried Chicken Salad, is a huge salad with Chicken Tenders on top. I have said it before, this is not for a dieter. The staff was friendly and made our lunch a fun experience.

Warning: Do Not and I repeat Do Not order the Maple Sausage,  Egg and Cheese Biscuit.  In one simple word it is, "nasty".   When I saw the combinations of the two words, sausage and maple I thought Hardee's had created another tasty unique breakfast biscuit. I was wrong, this creation is a total miss. The three link sausages resting on top of the neatly folded scrambled egg did not do the biscuit justice. The maple flavoring tasted artificial and left an aftertaste in my mouth. Thankful I keep a toothbrush and paste in my locker at work.   This location is the midpoint between home and work, so it is a good place to refill my travel  mug with coffee if need be and to grab a morning biscuit if I didn't eat breakfast at home. The staff is always perky and friendly at 5:20 AM which is impressive.   I will still rely on this Hardee's  on certain mornings, but I will not order the Maple Sausage Biscuit again.  It is still haunting me 3 hours later.

I'm not a shopper, I'm a dropper. I drop off donations to help change lives within my community.   The donation process is very easy. Just follow the signs that will lead to the back side of the store. There you'll find a loading dock for unloading all your goodies. One of their friendly workers will come out and help you unload your donation. Be patient, they may not come out immediately, but they're fairly quick. They'll also give you a signed and dated form for your charitable donation. The IRS likes them signed.   It is so easy to donate, you have no excuse to not clean out that closet or basement of all those things you no longer wear or need.   Will I return? - I "drop" by again real soon.   When: December 27, 2017 Why: Year End Donation

Fashion Forward and Classic frames at very reasonable prices. Customer service was great. I visited a couple of times and each time they took time to assist me in frame selection and to figure my out of pocket after insurance.   I'll be honest, I ended up ordering my new glasses from another optical store, that saved me more out of pocket $'s.  However, I still want to give SEE Eyewear 4 Stars for selection and service. My SO who does have insurance used a Groupon and got a great pair of glasses. I highly recommend SEE and will check them out again when it is time for new glasses.

Why buy your Halloween candy at the local drug store or warehouse club, when you have a local candy company in your hometown? If you haven't been to GCC, you've got to go and take a trip down memory lane. You'll find candies that you have forgotten about and they'll be at prices that will be easy on your wallet.   I pick up my Halloween candy here and am able to offer my little ghost and goblins full size instead of those midgets or fun size the other houses will be giving. This is also the place I stock up for the candy dishes at work. Yes, I said the plural word candies, not singular candy. We have issues.   This candy warehouse is a very well kept secret in STL and it shouldn't be.  Go support a local business and satisfy your sweet tooth.   Will I return? - When the candy dish is empty and every Halloween.   When: To embarrassed to tell Why: It's Halloween time

Bob primarily sells to the wholesale market, but they've got their very own little retail store to serve us lovers of seafood. The staff is well knowledge and helpful in selecting your purchase. They assure you everything is fresh and encourage you to smell it before you buy it. The sniff test does works when buying seafood.   We stopped by today and picked up some farm raised Atlantic Mussels and a half dozen huge Atlantic caught sea scallops. You know I love mussels and sea scallops, since I have a list dedicated to them here on Yelp. Our purchase today was so fresh and cost friendly, I'm adding Bob's Seafood to both list. We may have done the cooking ourselves, but it's the same seafood we would have eaten at a restaurant. So it is so worthy of a place on my special list.

My Christmas goodies bag are once again going to have treats from Kakao. This year each bag is going to have a box of 5 Sea Salt Caramels, containing 3 milk and 2 dark chocolates.  These caramels are truly orgasmic. Some of the bags will also have chocolate scented pencils, Kakao Chap stick, Cocoa Grilling Rub and a chocolate Santa.  They have "Happy Holidays" box available but I choose the traditional brown box. The friendly staff also offered me holiday ribbon, but again I choose the traditional Kakao orange ribbon. One of the ladies asked me if I was sure, I guess she thought being a guy a needed help with my wrapping. I quickly explained to her that orange is my signature color and everyone would know it was from me having an orange ribbon. Her coworker giggled and said, you must be comfortable here with all our orange.   If you need stocking stuffers you should be shopping here. They've got it all in a chocolate theme. Just to give you some ideas of other items I bought; body scrub, hot coco mix, truffles and that previously mentioned chap stick that rivals our Yelp Stick.

I have owned three Hondas and all three of them came from St Louis Honda. The Service Department is excellent, I get everything done for my CRV here; check-ups, oil changes and anything else.  The service dept. staff is professional and it shows in their customer service.  I usually wait for my car, the waiting room is small but has WiFi which makes the time pass quickly.  Have a Honda or need a Honda, this is the place.

I cannot believe I haven't updated my review in over eight years. That is just wrong and I apologize. If you are organized to the point of being just this side of OCD, this is the store for you. It will have you organized in a flash.   I have used products from here to organize my kitchen drawers and today I organized my spice cabinet. Penzeys Spices would be so proud of my newly organized shelves.   While I was redoing my spice cabinet, I also grabbed a new standing drying rack for the laundry room. We all have those favorite items, that just cannot go into that dryer. It's compact, rust-free and made in the USA.   Earlier this year I also, bought a small five drawer rolling rack for my personal stuff at work. My new work location does not offer lockers, so this little jewel keeps all my personal items neat and tidy.   Love this store!   I'll be back? - I just said, "I love this store!"  When: April 19, 2019 and an earlier date that I can't remember Why: Spice Cabinet make-over

I can not sing the praises loud enough about this amazing place. They are all saints in my eyes, they saved my precious Peaches. Peaches got extremely ill on the 4th of July, seriously she was bout to cross the Rainbow Bridge. As Sarah and Chip have stated,  they give you a low & high estimate and explain in details the options. They help you make the right call for your pet. The staff is compassionate and true animal lovers.  Peaches had to stay in ICU for three days and our bill was $1200.00,  and worth every penny. She is back to her ole-self  at being a spoiled diva.  If you ever have a pet emergency, I recommend VVS.

Neveria La Vallesana has won my heart, or at least my tummy. I will admit, when we were first greeted and seated, I was grumbling. No chips and salsa brought to the table and no liquor license, which meant no Margarita. How do they expect me to eat Mexican food without chips and liquid refreshment? To my surprise I enjoyed my street tacos much more, because I had not filled myself up with countless chips and a boozy drink.   The SO was in the mood to make his "world famous" tamales so we made a trip down  to Cherokee for his special ingredients.  We knew not to grocery shop on an empty stomach, so we stopped in Neveria La Vallesana. We each had three street tacos and a side of beans. I choose, shredded pork, chicken and grilled steak.  All three were flavorful, but next time and there will be a next time I will be ordering all three chicken. Yes, the chicken was that flavorful.   The service was friendly and with the good food, this will be one of my regular haunts for Mexican food. Can't wait for them to get a liquor license.

Dado's loses a star with me. I stopped by for the Sunday Brunch and they did not impress me. I found the food on the buffet not to be up to the standards of their regular offerings. I felt the food was rather bland and flavorless.   It would have been nice if they offered an omelet bar or a carving station and charged a little more. Some fresh fruits also would have been a nice touch.   I'll be back to try the Prime Rib special, I've heard great things about it.  Hopefully, after a good piece of prime rib I'll be able to bump them back up to at least 4 Stars.   I'll be back? - Yes, to try the Prime Rib  When: November 4, 2018 Why: Sunday Brunch

Let's be honest with ourselves. What would you prefer to have, 6" or 8"? I don't know about you, but I'll take 8" over 6" any day. Seriously, there is no comparison between Subway and Jimmy John's. The 8" sandwiches at Jimmy John's are better.   My personal favorite is the #9 ITALIAN NIGHT CLUB. It is real genoa salami, Italian capicola, smoked ham, and provolone cheese all topped with lettuce, tomato, onion, mayo, and Jimmy John's homemade Italian vinaigrette. As the menu says, you have to order hot peppers on it. They just add that extra kick to the flavor. As a side I enjoy their Jalapeño Chips.   Depending how hungry I am, I can devour the entire sandwich or cut it in half and have lunch the next day. If it is a work day the next day, I almost always cut it in half.   The staff is always freaky fast with a side of friendly.

Oh, what a beautiful morning. Oh, what a beautiful day. I just had a delicious breakfast at, Morning Glory Diner.   Yes, I just participated in the first round of, "Meet the Diner". It's a new monthly CYE, that is going to expose us all to the fabulous and delicious diners within our great city of STL. Best of all, you get to do experience them with fellow Yelpers aka foodies just like yourself.   David one one of the co-owners was the perfect host. You could hear his passion as he explained each item on his breakfast menu to our group of Yelpers/foodies. He shared which were his personal favorites and which contained house-made items/ingredients. Seriously, whatever you selecte, would be the right choice. Nobody was disappointed with their choice and everyone cleaned their plates.   Max, this was a fun CYE. I am looking forward to the next diner, and personally, I am hoping to make it to each and everyone on the diner tour.

Macy's and Department stores in general aren't what they use to be. I recently shopped the Men's department before an appointment at the Apple store and was majorly disappointed.   The only associates I saw were at the fragrance counter and in the Ralph Lauren area. I did find a shirt in the Ralph area, but there was no assistance. It basically was self-serve, as if I were at the outlet store. The one associate was so busy ringing shoppers out and processing returns, she couldn't get out and truly "sell" the brand.   I think in a few years department stores and malls, are going to go the way of dinosaurs.   When: August 5, 2021 Why: Killing time & shopping RL

Was running errands in West County and needed a few items for dinner that evening. Traffic was already getting bad on Olive, so I stopped by Schnucks in Bellerive Plaza. As usual, the county Schnucks was bigger and had a larger selection then the city stores that I am use to.   What really blew my mind was the produce section. It was HUGE! It was so impressive, that if this were my regular Schnucks, I'd probably become a vegetarian. Yeah, it was that amazing.

I love the VIP Sale at Macy's. Who wouldn't love shopping your favorite departments and getting 20% off regular prices, sale and clearance prices too. Normally my favorite department is excluded from these promotional sales, but not this time. This time the Ralph Lauren department was included and I took advantage. I got shirts, shorts, socks and hats all at a huge savings. Sale goes till Sunday and there's some leather goods that may be calling my name.   The ladies of this department were so helpful in assisting me in finding my sizes and recommending items I had not noticed myself (which is rare, I know that dept. well). Part of my purchase was done as a pre-sale the day before the sale actually started. They then hold it till the actual sale day and you go back to the store with no worries of your wish list being sold to someone else.   Some of these ladies know exactly what is hanging in my closet and that scares me. Or is that good

My county and Illinois friends now have another reason to come to downtown Saint Louis, besides a Cardinal or Rams game. Taze is a creative new twist on Mediterranean food, it is high-end fast food at an affordable price. It is build your own, with fresh, quality ingredients.   Think Chipotle or Qudoba, or even Subway. You first pick your type of pita, I choose whole wheat. Then you select your meat and all the fresh toppings you want. Then you select a side; mine was fries. As if that isn't enough food, they offer you a scoop of humus as well. My meat was beef & lamb, which was tender as tender could be. The fries were skin on Russet potatoes, that were gourmet burger joint quality. Being a fan of Jalapeños, I couldn't resist their Jalapeño humus and it left me speechless.   Enjoy before or after a game. Or make a special trip downtown and enjoy Taze. It is well worth risking your life and making the trip to downtown Saint Louis.   When: June 28, 2015 Why: International Supper Club Meeting

Needed an extra key for work, so I stopped by Krause since it is in my hood.  I could not be happier with the service I received. I was greeted by a friendly associate, he made my key and I was out the door in under 5 minutes and that was with small talk.   If and when I need more keys made, I'll keep my business local and come back to Krause.

I absolutely love the lay out of this store. My hometown Target is in the midst of a remodel and I can only hope it looks like this one when they are done. The flow of the aisles and staggering of the different departments, makes for a pleasant shopping experience.   The store is always super clean and well merchandised. I do believe they even have some more upscaled items that are not available at the Alton store. Today I was shopping for a baby shower gift and found a fabulous Aveeno mommy & baby gift basket. It was perfect, a little something for the momma as well as the new baby.   The check out process took some time, but that was okay. It was obvious they were training new cashiers. We all need to have patience. Remember, it is a virtue.   Many of my favorite places to shop in E-ville are near this Target, so it makes it easy for me to stop by whenever I am in town.   When: October 20, 2021 Why: Baby Shower Shopping

What do you do when you literally have eaten everything on the menu? You check and see if there's an off the menu special of the night. That's what I had to do the other night and the kitchen at PS knocked it out of the park with their special.   The special was a Ribeye and they did it equally as well as any steakhouse in the city. They prepared it to my requested medium-rare and served it with Fingerling Potatoes and Green Beans. It all was delicious and as always my Manhattan was a perfect pairing.   PS never disappoints me, with food, cocktails or service. I cannot wait to see what they do with The Bellwether. I'll have two great places to frequent.   I'll be back? - PS is my go to in STL.   When: February 27, 2019 Why: Late Dinner

If you are a smart shopper, you will never pay retail at Macy's. They are always having a sale, coupon or have a clearance rack tucked away somewhere. My favorite are those clearance racks. I shop them like you'd shop the racks at TJ Max or Marshall's and I always find something in my size. In my opinion it's better quality and more current to fashion trends.  I'll give up my secret, my favorite rack is the Ralph Lauren.   My other favorite departments are:  Men's Shoes - They have Cole Hahn and the men who work the dept. are always helpful and knowledgeable.   Men's Suits - When my job required my attire to be "suits", Macy's put places like Mens Wearhouse to shame in both selection and pricing.   Housewares - Watch for sales when needing to add new pots and pans to your kitchen.  Bed & Bath - The Hotel Collection is equal to Pottery Barn and a much better price and larger color selection.  It's a department store where you can find many of your needs at a good sale price.

Running errands and in need of a quick lunch, so I stopped by the Atomic Cowboy. It was late lunchtime, closer to 1then 12. I picked a stool at my favorite place to dine, the bar.   I started out with one of the neighbors down the street craft beers, UCBC Forest Park Pils. It's always one of my favorites, I order it all the time when I'm at UCBC. As I studied the menu, Poutinelicious jumped out at me. I wasn't that hungry, but wanted to satisfy the hunger pains. The menu described it as crispy fries topped with, smoked chicken, cheese curds, burnt onions and chicken love. I will say the toppings were correct and they did add flavor to the fries. However, I thought the fries were limp before the toppings were added. Should have gone with the Swordfish Tacos.   Service was a little lack luster. The staff seemed more pre-occupied with doing prep work and getting prepared for the evening business.   Will I return? - Yeah, I'll give them another try.   When: February 27, 2017 Why: Lunch

It's been awhile, so it is time to update my SCG review and give them an extra star that is well deserved.   Reasons they deserved an the extra star:  1) They open at 6:30 AM. I'm an early riser so this works perfect with my daily itinerary.   2) You can order just "One" Biscuit and Gravy. Biscuits are big & fluffy and the gravy would make a farmers wife proud.   3) Greek Omelet is one of my favorites.  4) Weekday Scrambler is an affordable and filling breakfast.   5) Great dark roast coffee. It's self serve, so you never have to wait for a server to fill your cup.   6) Works of local artist adorn the walls. Best of all, it's for sale.   Will I return? - Silly, question. What do you, think?  When: November 29, 2017  Why: Breakfast, duh.

Fast food fast, that doesn't taste like fast food made quickly.  We were in the mood for hamburgers, but not in the mood to cook, so off to Sonic I drove. When I returned home, we were pleased our meal was still warm.  Our cheeseburgers were meaty and had the perfect amount of toppings. One of us had tots, they were crispy and a good change from the typical french fries. However, I had the french fries  and was totally pleased. In my book, Tater Tots are for breakfast. We shared an order of Onion Rings which were sit down restaurant quality. In closing, I'll tell you the Banana and Caramel shakes were just, "Yummy"!  Can't imagine eating in my car, but as carry-out - I'll be back to Sonic.

Was in the area and thought I do a flash back to when I worked and hung out in the grove area before it was, "The Grove".  To drive down the street and get a bag of "belly bombers" at the end of a night  was a good way to cut the booze.   A White Castle is only good when you have enough liquor in your system to counter re-act. However, I will say the french fries and chocolate shakes are good.   Now I remember why I only crave these once every blue moon.

I don't get this OfficeMax, it just feels weird. It also seems to be a lot smaller then your typical OfficeMax. Staff isn't as friendly and helpful as other OfficeMax stores.  However, when shopping at the Schnucks next door it is a convenient location to quickly pick some needed office supplies. I got what I needed and got out.

Splish, Splash, my car took a bath.   I use to be a fan and regular of the Hampton Car Wash. When it closed last month I wondered if my car would ever be clean again. So, I was on a search to find a new car spa for Carlos my CRV. I had no idea I was going to hit a gold mine on my first visit to a new car wash. No disrespect to the now shuttered HCW, but wow is there a difference in service and staff. Why did I stay with you so long?   This Waterway is kept as clean as the cars they are detailing. The staff is friendly and professional. In fact, they look as if they were recruited right of a private prep school or a J Crew catalog.   The prices are a little higher then what I have paid in the past, but the quality of work is better. So paying more $'s to have Carlos look his best, is well worth it.  The staff at WGW make him scrubby dutch clean.

This store must have been born again. I shopped this store before reading any reviews on Yelp and was totally pleased. The Shoe Carnival near my home on Watson Road closed and this is the next closest, so it was logical I'd give it a try. Is it in the greatest neighborhood? Not really, but it is still a safe one.  This staff was extremely helpful and friendly. I truly believe each and every associate in the store (5) spoke or had some type of interaction with us while shopping. I was impressed with cleanliness and how well organized the store was presented. I was also surprised to see that they offered various brands. I had no idea SC carried Ralph Lauren. However, I did know they are one of the better places to get affordable Nikes.   Those that know me, know that I have an obsession with colorful socks and shoelaces . I may have found my favorite selection of shoelaces at this SC, they had colors that I have been searching for to complete my wardrobe.   Give this Shoe Carnival a try!

It is still a four star experience, but I am not a fan of their Stuffed pizzas.   This visit we tried the Chicago Style, Stuffed pizza. It was truly stuffed to the edges with toppings, or should I say fillings. However, for our personal taste it was way to much dough. The way they create their stuffed pizza is simple, they just make a regular pizza and then top it with another pizza shell on top. They then add a minimal more toppings to complete the Stuffed Pizza. Like any Papa Murphy's pizza you take it home and bake. Only exception is, this pizza is baked at 375.   I agree with Tom C., beware of the size of pizzas. The large is way to large for two. You'll either have leftovers for breakfast or lunch the next day. Next time we're going to try cutting it in half. We will then prepare one half and freeze the other half for another day.   Great staff, they are always friendly and professional. They were extremely busy on a Sunday night close to closing and it was amazing how clean they kept their prep area.

A fabulous pet store in Soulard. It is room after room of everything you'd ever need to spoil your dog or cat. At first you'd think it looks like a hoarders house, because they make use of every space imaginable. What makes them not like a hoarder, is it all is merchandised well and they know where everything is.   They have a large variety of quality pet foods and the staff we spoke with were very knowledgeable about their ingredients and difference. They also hooked us up with some new biodegradable scoop bags. Gotta be Eco friendly when walking the K-9's.   Friendly staff and endless goodies makes Pets in the City.

I love this store. Every time I shop here I ask myself, "why don't you make this your regular grocery store". I have to drive a little further to get here, but the short distance is well worth it.  The produce section amazes me, the presentation is as if they were getting ready for a photo shoot. (I'll take a picture next time). Also, the vegetables are fresher then the other grocer I usually shop. Plus the fact that there always seems to be a produce clerk there to assist and answer your questions. The prepared foods section is amazing, great place to pick-up lunches for work or those lazy nights when you just don't want to cook. No need to stop at the butcher shop for those special cuts, they're here. I can go on and on, we had so much shopping here this morning getting ready for holiday baking.  The staff was helping us find things and laughing with us about our craziness. At least I hope it was with and "not at us".  This is now my grocer of choice.

We look forward to each new issue of Sauce. At times we pick up two copies so we don't have to wait for the other to finish reading.  It provides good information about events, new openings and still highlights restaurants that have been here awhile as St. Louis favorites. Another reviewer didn't  think they gave honest criticism, I do. I just want the facts, I'll decide if it is to my liking. I don't trust movie critics, so why should I trust restaurant critic.   Keep up the good work Sauce, your doing a great job on educating the public and encouraging them to expand their experiences in food.  Sauce is free, it is worth my time and once you've read it I'm sure you'll be looking for the next issue.

Going to The Cup today, I discovered a new fashion boutique that gives me a reason to shop local. The shop offers women's and men's fashions. They also have a fabulous selection of watches, purses, messenger bags and shoes.   I was impressed with their selection of sweaters and hoodies. The sweaters ranged in price from $169 - $89 which I found to be very reasonable. One of their hoodies was by a San Francisco artist who is originally from STL and sold for a mere $60. Many of the shirts were also unique in design. It is so much fun wearing something that is so different then the "mall" fashions that people ask, "where did you get that" and that is what you'll hear when you shop 10denza.   Next time you are in the CWE drinking or eating on Maryland, I suggest you stop by 10denza and discover for yourself what I discovered today.

Citygarden is another beautiful Saint Louis park. It is filled beautiful sculptures, beautiful landscaping and beautiful fountains. What makes it even more beautiful, is you get to enjoy it for free.   It's a great place to go and escape the stresses of our crazy lives. A quite stroll through the park will have you feeling completely relaxed and refreshed. As an added bonus, you can enjoy breakfast or lunch on the patio at Death In The Afternoon which is located on the Chestnut side of the park.   I highly recommend a visit to our city residents and tourist. I also encourage our county residents to come down and experience the beauty and peacefulness of Citygarden.   In closing, I will say it one more time, this is a beautiful park.

Good old fashion Italian deli. We went today for lunch, it was my partners first time. We loved it. We had a Hot Salami and Italian Trio.  The line was long when we entered, we took our number and were amazed at how fast the line moved. The ladies of Gioia's know how to give good customer service and make a quality sandwich fast.  They've got Billy Goat Chips, which are a perfect side to a huge deli sandwich.

Sometimes it is scary walking into a store and all the sales professionals know your name...LOL. What makes the customer service so great here is that they take the time to know and listen to their customers.  Even with all the SP's on duty today being with other customers, they each wished me a  happy holiday season as we passed.   The new item that I wanted today had not arrived yet, and they assured me I'd be called when it did arrive.

Was on jury duty and this restaurant was convenient for our lunch break. I live close to both Chris' Pancake and Bartolino's Osteria, so I thought this would be a good choice. It was just, okay.   I'm a big fan of the Bartolino's Salad. I've had it at the Osteria and also at their South location, so when I saw it on the menu here, I wanted it for lunch. What they served me, was no where near the Bartolino salad that I love. It wasn't even a good salad. I would have better off ordering breakfast for lunch, because Chris always does breakfast right.   Will I return? - If I get called back for Jury duty in 2 years  When: May 3, 2017 Why: Lunch at Jury Duty

I miss the Original Spicer's. It use to be one of my favorite stores. When it closed, I was so sad, but took advantage of it's Going Out of Business sales.   When this new Spicer's reopened with a very similar format, I was happy again. I once again, had a fun place to shop for unique children's gifts and even for adults who had a child trapped within.   Now I'm sad again, my last visit was a total disappointment. The shelves were sparsely stocked, merchandising looked haphazard and the variety of quality merchandise was lacking. Which made me wonder if we may be seeing another going out of business sale soon.  I was greeted by the lone employee, but beyond a "hello" there was no customer service. This visit was so disappointing, that I may never return and I love to shop and give gifts.   Times have changed, times are a changing, but I want my original Spicer's back.  It truly was a trip over the rainbow.

A mom and pop diner offering decent food at an affordable price. It has zero ambiance. In a long shot gun type dining room, the decor is plain and simple. Their servers are graduates of the Flo's School of Waitressing and I am fairly certain, Mel is in the kitchen cooking.   Breakfast is the best deal, but they turn out a good Angus burger for lunch too. You get what you pay for, so you'll leave satisfied.

One of the main reasons I like Yelp is that it exposes me to new experiences. It guides me out of my box and my comfort zone.   With that being stated, I would have never experienced this totally cool neighborhood bar in Soulard. As Jenny P stated it is small and divey, but in my opinon that is what gave it all it's warmth and charm. The regulars were welcoming of new patrons and engaged conversation.   They've just opened a new game room that  offers a good variety of bar amusements. To make it easier for you to get your drink on while you get your game on, they have a second bar located in the new addition.  The staff is friendly, and the bartenders make a good drink. I was totally amazed at the quality of food from a dive bar. The crab cakes could win a blue ribbon at a county fair and the chicken strips put other bars to shame. My new Yelp friend Matt C., is right the thin crust pizza is "really good". I didn't take a menu home, but wish they delievered on The Hill.   Next time I'm in Soulard, I'll stop by 1860.

Great neighborhood bar for awesome burgers. I bounce back-n-forth between two for my visits; The Royale (Wagyu Kobe) or Bison (MO raised).  Keep in mind both of these type of burgers can not be cooked over medium. I get mine done medium rare and they are just perfect.  Your burger comes with one side, and french fries are not available. I just love it when a restaurant gets creative and doesn't offer them.  I'm a big fan of our home town Billy Goat Chips, but when at The Royale, you've got to experience their house made Sweet Potato Chips. As a child I hated sweet potato's, now I can't get enough.  Sometimes when I/we visit it's for their taco's. We'll order two each of their Smoked Brisket and Fish then share. These are the only fish taco's that I like. Save room, and I do mean room for dessert. You've gotta have "The Boozy-Q". Devil's food cake, Irish cream, Chambord whipped cream...... plus more chocolate toppings. Don't ask about the calories.
After 50 years of serving the Lindenwood neighborhood, this IHOP has closed its doors. They were a great inexpensive place for week day breakfast. They'll be missed by many.

Was craving Pumpkin Pancakes so we visited Sunday morning. This place is small and they cram as many booths and tables in as they can. With this being the case, the noise level is loud.  Our food was very good breakfast fare, our bacon was crisp, sausage seared well and the eggs done to order.  We ordered the same special so we had a good chuckle, my plate had more bacon and sausage then my "SO". I guess math skills are not really required to cook at IHOP.

Why can't my local Schnucks have a produce department like this one? I know, they gotta cater to the neighborhood the store is located, but we're talking fruits and vegetables. It's not like I'm asking for cuts of meat or other high end services. I just want my veggies and fruits to be as fresh and plentiful as this location.   This produce department is "almost" on par with Whole Foods. WF of course has more "organic", but this is still an excellent selection and variety.   I guess I'm just going to have to drive out of city into Clayton, to shop this Schnucks in the future. Which scares me to a small degree. As stated in other reviews, this is not the safest parking lot. It's not hoodlums you need to worry about, it is other drivers. However, I will take the risk to create a masterful meal at home.

Love this place, I have multiple pieces and enjoy them all. The quality is excellent - worth the price. Treat yourself - you'll be glad you did. The sales professionals are top-notch, they are friendly and make a pleasant shopping experience. I agree with one of the other reviewers, I wish St. Louis would get more of the latest releases.  However,  you can always have it shipped to the St Louis store.

They've added a nice addition to their deli and prepared food, Bob's Signature Smokehouse BBQ. It may not be Pappy's or Bogart's, but it is damn good for quick meal. They've got Baby Back Ribs, Beef Brisket, Pulled Pork or Chicken, and Turkey Breast. You can also get Smoked Salmon and a Whole or Half Chicken.   We've tried the 1/2 Rack Baby Back Ribs and Beef Brisket. The meat fell off the bones  and the brisket will have me going back for more. They offer eight different signature sides, but we made our own at home.   You can see the smoker as you enter the store, it sits right out in the parking lot. If you don't notice it, chances are you'll smell the apple and cherry wood that they are slowly smoking the meat over.

I love the OfficeMax Brown Bag 20% Sale, that they have this time of year. For those who are not familiar with this sale, it is when everything that you can fit into a traditional paper grocery bag is 20% off. The bag you need to use is sent out in the Sunday paper and it is a fun way to shop. I can pack that bag tight and save a bundle. It is how I stock up on home office supplies for the year.   This location has improved on its' customer service since my last visit. They finally are taking the lead of their major competitor on greeting and serving. I just wish they offered more variety like the other office big box store.

This place is awesome. When I was prepping for a Florida vacation, I checked out a couple local tanning salons before selecting this one for my pre-trip tan. The facility is extremely clean and the staff is friendly and professional. My trip was over a year ago and I still visit Tan Co. it helps keep my tan dark and I feel like I just got back from the beach. I also, like their Mystic Tan, it covers the body well and does not look like some lower quality spray tans. I'm a big fan!!!

Congratulations, Bobby. I'm bumping you up to 5 well deserved stars. I am so in love with your frozen custard. It's so rich and creamy. The popular custard stands in St. Louis cannot compare to the quality of product and customer service that you provide. I am a fan and you are so worth the drive. I stop by every time I have dinner in Edwardsville.   On my way to a dinner, I stopped and bought Carmel Apples for the other guest and of course, one for me. While at dinner, I made sure to leave room for a mini concrete on the way home. The Yummy Drummy, satisfied my sweet tooth, before I drove back to STL.   I'll be back? - You betcha.   When: October 14, 2018 Why: Carmel Apples and Best Frozen Custard

Love to entertain at home? Then this is the store for you, it will make your entertaining so easy and impressive.  I like their selection of housewares, stemware and oh, hell I like every department. Parts of my house could be an C&B Outlet store.  I hate to admit it, but when I walk in to The Boulevard store, it is like Norm walking into Cheers. Everyone knows my name.  Perfect place for the housewarming gift, or Bridal Registry.

A delightful lunch. We started out with Toasted Ravioli's, (which I normally don't order) and they were actually very good. We ordered, Veal Parmesan and Tuto Mari with red sauce. The veal was tender and flavorful and the seafood was abundant in the pasta. The house salad was a great beginning to the fabulous entrees. Fresh bread, butter and oil were readily available. The entire staff were friendly and provided 4 star service. Can't wait for my next visit.

Not impressed with this new location. I never visited the one across the street, so I cannot compare the two, but this one disappointed me. Yes, it is ultra modern, but it stark and modular. It is cold in design and the staff is cold as well.   The quality of food and beverage still meet the high standards I expect from SLBC. I also, liked what I'd call the Progress Board, which allows you to watch the status of your order. If you watch the board, you'll know your order is ready before they call your name out.   Unlike Kay, I am so glad they did not put a drive-thru at this location. I am anti drive-thru at any business. So when I see a new one that opts out of that service, I am a happy customer and in this case a happy stockholder.   I'll be back and hopefully the staff will be adjusted to the new digs and have a better attitude.

I am not a DIY type guy, but I will say out of the Hobby Lobby stores I have shopped when I need to, this one in Kirkwood is the best.   Today I wasn't even shopping, I was only here to meet up with my favorite cousin to have lunch in downtown Kirkwood. With that being said, I walked out of the store with a bulging bag of gift boxes and gift tissue. It was all 50% off and the holiday season hasn't even begun.   My gift wrapping is going to be so easy this year. All I need to do is make fabulous bows and having worked at Tiffany's, I can make a mean bow.   I'll be back? - Not often, but when the need arrives I'll return.   When: November 19, 2017 Why: Mindless Shopping

If it were not for Aaron B. I would have never discovered the Bon Bons here at Serendipity. He is so right, they are the BOMB BOMB. They're the perfect ice cream treat. They're the famously flavorful Serendipity ice cream dipped in chocolate which forms a hard shell. They're bite size and you can't just stop at one.   I love that Serendipity is expanding their brand beyond their parlor in Webster Groves. Recently I enjoyed a mini cone at Five Star Burgers and I always ask at local restaurants who does their ice cream before ordering. Serendipity always closes the deal. While at a recent Yelp event at SHIC, Beckie announced to us that her ice cream will be available at Field Foods.   If Serendipity keeps expanding their brand, my waist will expand too. Who needs Ben & Jerry when you have Serendipity in our hometown.

Great place to buy those hostess gifts this holiday season. Not everything is monogrammed and you can seriously find something for everyone.  They have gifts for the young city girl, things a grandmother would enjoy and everyone in between.   I entered the store at the same time as  a lady close to my age and we both went about our shopping. The young lady working asked the woman if see needed help and assisted her. As the sales girl was going to the stockroom, she stopped and asked me if I was with the lady. When I responded, "No.", she immediately apologized for not asking me earlier if I needed help. She said they were not use to men coming in the store. I grinned and said, "Men shop, too".   I found a couple of holiday gifts and a birthday gift as well. I mailed the birthday gift on Friday and got a call this morning from the recipient raving how much they loved it.   Like Aimee, I may not shop here often, but now that I now what they have I will be back for those special little gifts. Who knows, I may just get something monogrammed next time.

It's a Starbucks. What makes this one different from all the other Starbucks, is that they are slow as molasses that has been kept in the ice box. I don't even get complicated drinks. I order cold brew, black and it still takes forever. However, they do provide me with a laugh. They can't spell my name right. I could understand if they spelled it with a ph instead of the v, but here they spell it with a b. The last poor barista who tried to call my name out had no idea how to pronounce Steben.  I give him credit, he politely asked how to pronounce it. Since the v & b are next to each other on the keyboard, I just smiled and told him it was a typo.   This Starbucks is in my hood, so I'll continue to support them. I'll just take a deep breath before walking in and make sure my patience switch is flipped to the on position.

Yum-Yum!   So many forget that Serendipity was the trend setter for homemade ice cream in the St. Louis area. They blazed the trail for those newer ice cream shoppes that have popped up in the last couple of years.   Being in Webster Grove's for  a YEE at The Frisco, a group of stopped by afterwards for a sweet little treat. Some of my friends went whole hog and got huge cones or house made ice cream sandwiches. I was already fairly full and opted for a kid's cone. I like the fact that they let adults order the kids cone, some of the other parlor don't.   I'm a sucker for any ice cream that has, "cake" in it's name, so my flavor of the night was, "Birthday Cake". It was so tasty, I'll be going back for more in a few days, when it truly is my birthday.   The staff is typical ice cream parlor staff, high school kids. They work quickly, are courteous and friendly. May be young, but they're doing a great job.   I'll be back? - Yep, for more, Birthday Cake Ice Cream  When: October 30, 2018 Why: Sweet Treat

A fantastic neighborhood bar. It's actually a well hidden gem. Babe's is located on Ivanhoe, across the street from Vinnie's and down the street from Pizza-A-Go-Go. Making this a popular area on Ivanhoe.   The reason I mentioned the nearby restaurants, is because Babe's has no food. However, you're welcome to enjoy a Gyro or a pizza from one of  these nearby venues.   The outside patio is spacious and comfortable. It's a great place to enjoy a cocktail or beer with friends. Especially now during this post-pandemic time.    The cocktails are cheaper than most popular bars and the cordial bartenders make them strong.  Which makes Babe's a perfect place for day drinking.   Will I return? - Yes. It's in my hood.   When: July 2, 2020 Why: Day Drinking in our Post-Pandemic World

When I tell people I went to Wash U, it isn't as prestigious as it sounds. The Wash U I went to is a laundromat.   I have a washer and dryer at home, but there times when size does matter and you just need something bigger. Those larger capacity washers and dryers come in handy when you need to wash quilts, comforters or rugs.  Why put rough wear and tear on your own when you can use a commercial size down the street. In addition to 3 stars, I also give Wash U 3 C's for convenience, cleanliness  and cheap.   So the next time someone tells you they went to "Wash U", you can ask them do you mean the university or laundromat?

It's a QT, enough said. They're all pretty much the same.   This one has an amazing location. It's probably one of the most busiest corners in the city. Which can cause some craziness in the parking lot. Just be alert to when you are backing out of a space or pulling away from a pump.  Also, be alert to the fact that not all entrances, allow you to exit. For that simple reason, I'll put this QuikTrip in my Parking Lot Derby Collection.   The inside of this QT is kept clean, including the restrooms which is important during this pandemic. Their customer service staff is also very hospitable, making it a pleasant shopping experience.   Again, it's a gas station and convenience store rolled into one. It has the QT Kitchen which is a bonus. So, this QT beats most 7-11's and Circle K's by a long shot.   When: December 3, 2020 Why: Gas and liquid refreshment

I agree with Chris Z , this location is FAST, efficient and unfriendly. I do not need them to be my new BFF, get me in and out as fast as possible.   I was prepared to wait like I normally do at the South Kingshighway location, but I was in and out in 5 minute. No need to have my iPad for entertainment.   Highly recommend for those who have no patience or are in a hurry.

TSA is quickly becoming one of my favorite places to go.   Warning to "Pork" themed restaurants, The Scottish Arms has a Pork Burger that is the "bomb". It is full of flavor and when paired with an ice cold draft beer (Whale from Six Row Brewing Co.) it makes a refreshing summer meal. Enjoying it on the Scottish Arms patio makes it perfect.   In addition to the Pork Burger we enjoyed their classic Fish -n - Chips.  I dare anyone to find and introduce me better F-n-C's, here in STL, then those served at TSA. I'll be surprised if you do.   The service here always amazes me, it is top notch. Their staff is always friendly and very accommodating. To give you an example, the night we were there a young lady on the patio was chilled. It was one of those recent cool nights we just experienced. To make her comfortable, the server gave her an extra table cloth to wrap around herself like a shawl.  That is a step beyond the norm.

Nice! The ambiance is simple and rustic. Making for a very comfortable atmosphere to relax and enjoy craft brews from Bluewood and some of their guest taps.   The bartenders of course are very knowledgeable on the beers on tap. If you're not sure what you'll like, tell them what your preferences are and they'll guide you. Today I didn't take advantage of their flights, but they do offer them. So many of our local breweries don't offer flights, so I'm happy to see Bluewood is on board with offering them. It's a great way to experience multiple brews, to find out which one is your new favorite.   A BIG plus for BB is having Mac's Local Eats sharing their space. The combination of the two makes for a fun filled experience. Beer and Burgers, what more could you want.   I'll be back? - Hell, YES!  When: September 18, 2019 Why: Grand Opening with Mac's Local Eats

I am a fan of Old Bakery Beer. I love supporting a local business that gives back to their community and that is what OBB does. On the third Monday of every month OBB sponsors, Drink For A Cause. Between 4 and 9 PM 25% of their beer sales are donated to a local charity. So go have a beer to support a local brewery and you'll also be helping a local charity.   I've never been disappointed with any of the food at Old Bakery, but I'll tell you my favorite is the Caesar Salad with White Anchovy's. The salad is huge and has the perfect combination of Parmesan and croutons. I always add anchovy's and they are not stingy with those salty little fishies. They also toss the salad with just the right amount of dressing.   Staff is hipster, which is perfect for a craft brewery.   Will I go back? - Gotta support local charities.   When: Multiple times Why: Supporting local charity or meeting up with family.

I am so proud of, The Grove. I use to bartend in the area before it was actually called, "The Grove". Yes, I am that old. Back in those days, there were a lot of boarded up building between the bars that were open and setting the trend for the future.   Now, it is thriving STL community that supports many popular restaurants, breweries, coffee shops and alternative nightclubs. What makes me proudest, is that the residential community is growing as well. The Grove, is a thriving STL neighborhood that is growing by leaps and bounds.   I hope they keep up the development. I smile every time I drive through or visit one of the businesses. It is a neighborhood, that shows the diversity and love of each other in St. Louis, that sometimes gets over-looked.

I need a support group. A support group for shopaholics who are addicted to Crate and Barrel. I shop here at least once a month, when I come to get my haircut at James Mitchell. As I browse through the store, I can easily find something I cannot live without. Or at least I think, I cannot live without it.  Either way, I love this store.   I am a kitchen gadget junkie and I can always find some new gizmo here. Another thing that I like at C&B is their selection of dinnerware and stemware. It is so vast, I can find the perfect items for entertaining at home, or a gift for any occasion.   When shopping for new furniture, I usually start here, too. It's high quality and soundly constructed.   Shopping at Crate and Barrel makes me happy. Can't believe I hadn't updated my review in the last 8 years. Well, I got that corrected today.   I'll be back? - I addicted.   When: April 3, 2019 Why: It's a monthly thing.

Bubbles and Burgers, what a delightful combination.   Once restaurants got to open up with patio sitting, I was ready for bubbles. POP had a coupon in the EXP, so I had some redeeming to do before they all expired. I enjoyed a nice glass of Brut on their back patio, it was very relaxing and refreshing to finally be out and a bout.   Normally I like a beer with a burger, but having the glass of bubbly was a nice twist. When you think burgers, POP may not pop into your mind, but it should. Their Smash Burger is damn good. It's two patties that is topped with roasted onions, liquid cheddar and pickles. The bun is a sesame challah and it comes with a side of fries. I've always been a fan of serving ketchup in a little cup and was glad to see them serving theirs that way. Honestly, I don't know if that is the regular way, or it it's the new pandemic way. Either way, it makes me happy.   The customer service was attentive and it was obvious they were following CDC protocols to keep everyone safe.   When: August 13, 2020 Why: EXP Coupon

I'm going to let you in on a "dirty" little secret. The "dirty" chicken wings at SOHA are phenomenal. The wings themselves are huge, meaty and juicy. They have just enough, spicy kick, to be the perfect accompaniment to a cold beer.  These wings are so incredibly good, I am placing them in the #1 spot on my Wings, Wings and more Wings  list.   SOHA with it's amazing wings, enormous variety of beers and multiple TV's, is the perfect place to watch your favorite sports games. Or, you can just stop by for a cold icy beer and an appetizer before going home after a hard day at work.

I can munch on snacks and sip 4 oz samplings of beer all afternoon or night at Bridge Tap House. It's a great way to experience a wide variety of craft beers locally and from all across the country.  My go to snack is the Tortilla Chips with an IPA Cheddar dip. The chips are actually better then some of the local Mexican restaurants. Until Ian Froeb recommended the Smoked Paprika and Sea Salt popcorn on his STL 100 List, I would have never tried it. I never imagined bar popcorn would taste this good. I should have know better, since it is a David Bailey establishment. I'm not sure want is the perfect accompaniment, the popcorn or the craft beer. Either way, they both go together extremely well.   Will I return? Just try to stop me and see what happens.   When: September 11, 2016 Why: Craft Beer Sampling & STL 100 List

Wing Stop's catch phrase is, "The Wing Experts". I don't think so. They were not "bad", I've just had better. In fact I've had better from a pizza joint or a pub and I was hoping for better.  The fries, were limp and tasted as if they were prepared in old oil. Another big disappointment, after reading Shelly D's glowing review.   My co-workers get carry-out frequently from here, so I'll re-visit too in hopes of a better experience. Perhaps they were just having an off night.
So long, farewell, auf wiedersehn, goodbye.   I loved Borders much more then Barnes & Nobel. Who am I to judge, I am just a Yelper in St. Louis.

I gotta admit, I only shop here with their coupons. If you don't have a coupon the prices are not that much different then any where else.  Today we went and got a digital scale for the kitchen, it is time for holiday baking.  We researched on line before shopping and were pleased they had the one we wanted in stock. We also needed a bread spatula, no luck with that item.  Normally when I shop here the staff is average to below average at best, but today they were above average. They were friendly, out-going and actually helpful. We chuckled as we observed, it looked as if they had gone to "The Grove" and recruited their holiday staff. Which was a good thing, for their customer service.

I'm loving my new hometown Target. The layout is a lot different from my old big city Target, but I'm adjusting to the flow. The staff here is also more down to earth and friendly. Just walking through the store, whenever I pass an associate, they all speak and ask if I am finding everything I am looking for or need. It is obvious, the management here is focused on customer service and has trained their staff well.   As others have commented, this store is always clean and well organized. Having just moved into a new house, I am making numerous runs to this Target. I am amazed at the things I didn't need in my old house, I now need in my new house.   Best of all, they have a spot where you can take a selfie with the Target Dog. My big city store didn't have that. Small town Targets, rock.   When: Very Often  Why: New home owner, I need stuff.

Do you like your cookies soft and moist or dry and crunchy? If you like them like I do, soft and moist, you'll enjoy Insomnia Cookies. They are hot, fresh, chewy  and they have cold milk too.   You may ask, it they're made the way I like them, then why only 3 Stars? It is because of the unfriendly staff who are more concerned about conversing amongst themselves then providing top notch customer service. Another reason for only 3 Stars, is the offering of ice cream. They boosted that they had Prairie Farms ice cream, as if it were a gourmet ice cream. Don't get me wrong, I like PF. I was raised on a dairy farm and we use to sell our milk to PF. It's local, which is great, but I can get PF at my local grocery store. Give me something like Blue Bell that is unique to ST Louis.   Good cookies, poor customer service, but your sweet tooth will be satisfied.

PAGG is a pizza parlor that serves pizza and only pizza. They do one thing and they do it right. The only other thing on their menu is soda. Majority of their customers do what I do and that is carryout. They do not offer delivery and table sitting is limited. Which makes it a true neighborhood pizza joint.   They only offer two sizes Small which is 12" and Large 15" and their prices are lower then the major pizza chains. What is weird is their hours, they are open 4-9PM Sunday - Thursday and 4-10PM Friday and Saturday. Then of all days they are closed on Wednesday. Guess they like having hump day off.   Their dough is hand tossed so while waiting for your order you will always be treated to a show. Love how they give the pizza a nice crisp bottom. We like the Special which gives us; sausage, pepperoni, mushroom, green pepper & onion.   PAGG can not be compared to Good Pie, Dewey's or PI. They are in a different class of pizzas parlors. In my hood PAGG is the better choice over Domino's, Cecil's and Papa John's.

Okay this place is winning me over, I tried it again and my second pizza was pretty damn good. I ordered a sausage and pepperoni and the sausage pieces were big and meaty. The sausage was  excellent, but I wasn't  wild about their pepperoni, so next time it will be sausage and onion.  I can already assume that one will be a winner. Also, the sauce and cheese impressed me more this time then on my first visit.   I've gotten so use to St Louis thin crust, that I'm enjoying having the crust around the edge when I order from Pizza-A-Go-Go. I know my dogs enjoy the crispy crust, they think it's a special treat made just for them.   Keep in mind if you visit this parlor, that it is bare bones. If offers pizza and soda and that  completes the menu. I guess you can bring your own beer or wine in because I saw a table with bottles of Budweiser while I waited for my carryout.

I do not Vape, but I enjoy hot sauce. If it were not for an article in RiverFront Times, I would have never known about this delightful little store. It is two retail shops in one location. One catering to those who vape and the other for those of us who love their food/spices "HOT".   I'll never shop for my "hot sauces" at the grocery store again. The variety of spice and intensity of heat here at Saucy-One are good enough to keep my burn'n love a burn'n. In fact I may need to keep some extra Tums or Alka-Seltzer Heartburn Relief Chews on hand.  Not only do I have a love for a variety of hot sauces, but my family does too. So discovering Saucy-One at the holiday season was perfect. Several of my gift boxes, are being filled out with goodies from their shelves.   The sales associate working (forgot name) was friendly and very knowledgeable of the product. Pointed out his favorites and shared secrets on how he used them (recipes).   Will I return? - I'm always in need of hot sauce.   When: November 30, 2017 Why: Shopping Local

Great old school, mom and pop watch and clock repair shop. Best place to get your watch battery replaced. While we wait, browse the antique clocks for sale and the large variety of cuckoo clocks.   Service is fast, efficient and they know what they are doing. I'd bring my watch here for a new battery, before I'd ever trust one of those young kids working the watch kiosk at the mall.

Yummy Yummy Yummy, I've got Gooey Butter Cake in my tummy.  Like another reviewer, I live fairly close to Gooey Louie and drove by frequently. My waist line regrets that I finally stopped by.....lol. This is little bakery is fantastic - it offers the best gooey butter cakes in the city that is know for Gooey Butter Cakes.  I've taken these to work, family functions and just home for us and everyone loves them. They are moist and bursting with flavor. The original is best by far, followed closely by Chocolate Raspberry and Chocolate Chippewa.  When craving Gooey Butter Cake, go to Gooey Louie for the best.

Best Happy Hour when you are wanting an Mexican theme. The Top Shelf Margaritas are one of the best if not the best in the city, we buy them by the pitcher...lol. Their chips and regular salsa are a great compliment to the Margaritas. (I'm glad you can get them at your local grocer) I sneak off to the bar and get cups of the other two salsa they have available as a bonus. My favorite entree is the Wet Burrito it rocks with flavor.  I hope they re-cycle the little cups the salsa come in.

I enjoy shopping, dinning and going to a movie here at Plaza Frontenac. Typically I'm not a mall shopper, but I love the selection of stores here.  I basically shop the home stores, Bissinger's, Louis Vuitton and enjoy a cocktail or two at Cardwell's.  I have shopped here in bummy jeans and unshaven and have gotten the same quality type of service when I am dressed to the nines.

Tucker's by far is the best steak value in the city. A 10 oz. Sirloin, side salad and a baked potato for $13.85 is a bargain to me. Add the Yelp check-in free appetizer to your meal and you've got a full belly.   My steak is always seasoned well and cooked to my request temperature. The side salad my primarily be iceberg lettuce, but with the red onion, bacon bits and their Lemon Pepper house dressing it is a perfect lead in to my juicy steak. Then there is the huge baked potato that I can never finish. It's a baked potato, but it's so good. I take the other half home and make my own American Fries for breakfast.   The friendly service and relaxed atmosphere makes for an enjoyable steak dinner.

Gaslight is a new fun place to to meet your friends for a cocktail. It's not just a bar. It's a recording studio, music school and lounge all combined into one venue. It's an interesting combination and they make it work.    There is a floor to ceiling window between the lounge and recording studio. How cool is that? I haven't been there during a recording session, but I can't wait to see one in action. It will be fun to experience a live feed from the acton in the studio.   I was impressed with the masterfully created cocktails. My current favorite is the Crystal Palace. Being a fan of vodka, I was immediately drawn to this one. It's Mastermind Vodka, Orchard Creme de Violette, Lemon Juice - Sparkling White topper. It is served up and the violet color reminds you of Liz Taylor's eyes.   A big bonus for drinking here, is that Cha Cha Chow the famous food truck has a kitchen next door. You can order from their amazing menu and they'll bring it over to you in the lounge area.   Drink - Eat - Music & Be Merry @ Gaslight  When: March 22, 2016 Why: Needed a Cocktail

The staff is great and friendly. While waiting for a carryout they engage you in their conversation.  Location is tucked away like a well kept secret.   How do I fell about the pizza, I'm not really sure. My partner really liked it, we ordered "the special". My first reaction was where's the toppings, they were hidden under a large amount of "real" cheese. The amount of toppings were minimal compared to other pizza parlors and the pizza sauce had minimal flavor.   It's close to home, my other half likes them so I'll give them a second chance. Once I do, I'll post again.

We've grabbed lunch here several times, and it has always been good. I enjoy the fact that they offer some of their menu items, "naked". Which is nice for those days when you are watching your weight. Which I should be doing everyday.   I love their tortilla chips! They toss them with lime and kosher salt,  which makes them a step above some of the local non-fast food Mexican restaurants.   Today when I stopped by after visiting the AT&T store next door, I just wanted some Grilled Chicken Nachos to snack on while working around the house. The young man working the front line provided great customer service. He asked me if I wanted my chips on the side? Being me, I asked "why?". Since my order was to go, he explained the chips may be limp by the time I got home. I would have never thought of that. He put my toppings in a bowl and the chips in bag. What a great afternoon snack, it was like having a layered dip.   I have used the Qdoba catering before and it was a major hit.   My only wish is that Qdoba offered Margaritas.
Good selection and prices for sterling silver. You can find something for every age, and sex.  May not be in a blue box, but this store is still great for gift giving.

At first I thought they were a local business, then I found out they are actually a chain.  Weird that they only have two items on their menu and that they close at 8 PM. These tacos would be a great post bar treat.   I enjoyed my taco, but was surprised to see that it was a puffy fried shell. It's bigger then most fast food tacos and so is the price. It's simple fare, seasoned beef, tomato, lettuce and cheese. The combo with two tacos and a soda was more then enough for a weekday lunch.   The location is off the beaten path, but I guess with the near by industrial parks that they do a brisk lunch business. They're not near my hood, but if I am craving a quick taco when heading to Brentwood, I may just pull in and give them another try.

Cheap fried chicken done right and done simple. You'll have no extra sides to choose from, they only offer one and it is crinkle cut fries. Your order will then be placed in a plain white box with a flip lid. They focus on flavorful chicken, not presentation. Your boxed lunch can be a 1/4 or 1/2 chicken and be mixed, all dark or my favorite all white.   The pieces are above average in size and seasoned with a peppery coating. Pieces may be a little greasy, but the box absorbs it up so it really is not an issue. They also offer burgers and from what I've heard, great milk shakes. I need to expand my experiences here, but every time I walk up to the window, I order chicken.   Keep in mind that there is no where to eat here, it is take out only. You'll walk up to a window that is outside, place your order and go enjoy your meal elsewhere. No ambiance, keeps the chicken cheap.   Yes, this is the same Fast Eddie as Fast Eddie Bon Air. If you enjoy him at the Bon Air, check out his chicken.

Smoking is allowed at The Famous Bar and you'll know that the moment you enter the door. The smell of smoke immediately hits your sense of smell. However, it doesn't take long for your to realize the smell of smoke is really the smell of fun. Okay,  it is a smokey smell and your clothes will smell like smoke when you get home, but all of that can be overlooked because of all the fun you will have while drinking in this classic dive bar.   The bartenders know their craft and produce some amazing cocktails in a comfortable, unpretentious atmosphere. The original tin ceiling is a you must see for its beauty. Let your hair down, be adventurous and come have some fun in a smoke filled dive bar.

Bigger then my regular Office Depot, but being bigger didn't make it better. Good thing I am fairly self efficient when shopping. I knew what I needed, and with the good signage in the store I was able to navigate my way directly to the office supplies I needed. I easily found an orange three ring binder and highlighter to keep me organized on my quest to visit all the 250 Birthday Cakes in the Cakeway to the West.  What I found sad, is that there were 6 sales associates in the store working and not one of them offered assistance. How could they? They were all gathered up front talking amongst themselves. My previous career was retail and this store would have been a shoplifters dream with all the employees clustered together.   Great variety and selection in a bigger store, but I will continue to shop my smaller city store that offers superior customer service.

Next time you are preparing an Italian dinner, get out of the pasta aisle at your favorite grocer and take yourself to J. Viviano & Sons on The Hill.  You will be amazed at the variety of ingredients to help you create a truly authentic Italian meal. They've got it all and at prices you will not want to resist.   I have always been a fan of their typical ingredients; tomato sauce, paste, spices, fresh cheese and etc. etc., but this last visit I experienced something totally new. I tried their frozen ravioli and was shocked how well it went with our awesome homemade sauce. They are made and frozen in house, so it is almost like you made the pasta yourself.  I'll keep it a secret, if you do.   The staff is always friendly and helpful. If you have questions, do not  hesitate to ask, they'll give you ideas on that masterful meal.   As we were leaving, at a perfect time. A huge charter bus pulled up in front and droves of little cute silver haired ladies headed to the front entrance. I had no idea, Viviano's was a tourist stop.

I live near Stellina and never visited until a couple weeks ago, and I kick myself for not visiting sooner. It taught me to never judge a restaurant from the curb. It may not look like much from the outside, but the food is incredible. My first visit was a house salad and Lasagna, the portion of lasagna was large enough for me to save some for lunch the next day at work. I was so impressed, three days later I ordered carryout for lunch. My partner and I had the Braised Beef and South Side Smoke. Both sandwiches were large and full of flavor. Stellina Pasta is big flavor in a small cafe.
This Einstein Bros was a disappointment.   Unfriendly staff - flavorless sandwiches - weak tea.   I'll stick with my Einstein Bros in the city.

"Grease" is the word. Greasiest fried chicken I have ever experienced. All the food here taste the same, like old "grease" that is long over due for a change. The cole slaw is flavorless, the crinkle french fries are mush, and Mrs. Paul makes a better onion ring. Why people think this is the best fried chicken in St. Louis is beyond me.

So glad to see that on my last shopping experience that they have totally raised the level of their customer service. We were greeted as we entered the store and when we had questions an associate was available to assist.   I love this time of year when they have the pumpkin mixes for quick bread and waffles. They make a delightful fall breakfast.   As stated by the infamous Patt C. they have some impressive cookbooks. I should know, in our house there are over 200 cookbooks so I think I know a good one when I see one.   Glad I was able to raise your stars, WS.  You deserved it.

I will always prefer to shop at a Target over an Wal-Mart and I am lucky to have one this good in my neighborhood. I use to be a fan of the one on Brentwood, but since this location did a complete renovation a couple years back....wow.  The store is clean, the selection is great and the customer service is top notch for a major discount store.  The parking is easy, plenty of space on a private lot and a parking garage. It is so cool they have a escalator for your shopping cart so you don't have to carry all your bags down to your car.  I've never walked out of here empty handed, I usually walk out with more then I went in for.

If you're a gourmet chef or if you just play one at home, Chef's Shoppe is a place you gotta check out. Seriously, they have everything you will ever need for your kitchen and then some. You'll feel like you are shopping at Sur La Table, Williams-Sonoma or Bed, Bath and Beyond, but you'll be shopping LOCAL.   Being a old farm boy, I love their selection of Lodge Cast Iron cookware. Nothing beats a nice big skillet to fix up some Sunday Fried Chicken. I also like the large selection of hot sauces and spices. It has assisted me in creating several gift baskets for friends and family who like things on the spicy side.   If you're a popcorn addict, they have an awesome popcorn shoppe within the store. They offer a wide variety of flavors and tins to make gift giving easy. Or just buy yourself a couple bags for your next Netflix marathon.   Next time you need gadgets and gizmos for the kitchen, remember to shop local and remember Chef's Shoppe.

I stand corrected. This is not a chain as I was originally informed. My internet searches were misleading and the site I visited has been corrected. So eating here, you are supporting a local business.

The Erker's have brought fashionable, unique and affordable optics back to the CWE. Their selection is cutting edge and fun. If you're like me, I like a couple frames I can change into depending on my mood or attire. With the prices available here at Eye Roc, you'll be able to have a pair for dress/work and a pair for casual/playtime.   The staff was extremely friendly and knowledgeable. I'm due for new frames later this summer and I'll be shopping at Eye Roc.

Decor is over the top, but it adds to the fun time you'll have at Amigo Joe's. Their top shelf Margarita's are fantastic, be careful they can sneak up on you. The salsa is thick and spicy a nice compliment to the chips. For the price point offered at Amigo Joe's, the food is well worth the price and beyond.
