I've done both dine in and carry-out and have been pleased with both. The staff is witty, friendly and very helpful.

I absolutely love this store. Once again, so many of my Christmas gifts came from here. Each of the ladies on my gift list got something from the GB and I even found something for one of the guys. The holiday has passed, so I can tell you each gift received great praise when it was opened.  This store kinda reminds me of Pottery Barn or Williams-Sonoma Home, without the high prices and snobby attitudes. The staff is always friendly and goes out of the way to assist and accommodate you.   If you are looking for unique items to decorate your home, or an unusual gift for that hard to pleased friend - this is the place to shop. So the next time you are in Edwardsville, be sure to make time and stop here to shop local.   Chances of returning: You can bet money on it.  When: Three times within a 10 day period in December Why: Holiday Shopping

If you like Restoration Hardware, Pottery Barn and Williams Sonoma Home. You're going to love Gingham Buffalo and you'll be shopping local as well.   Your creative juices will start to flow as soon as you enter the store. You'll see how a few simple accessories can jazz up a room and make it feel new again. As I shopped, I wanted to curl up on the sofa with a glass of wine and a good book. Then I saw a bedroom staging and was ready to snuggle up for a nap. Each staging had me wishing it were in my home.   They have so many unique and unusual gifts that no one would dare think of returning or exchanging them. They'd be cherished for years to come. Take your time shopping and notice all the details. You'll be delighted at what you'll find to make your home more beautiful and enjoyable.   If you have questions or need some basic decorating suggestions, ask the staff on duty. They are eager to assist you at any level. This store is a definite stop for me every time I am in Edwardsville.

If you love Gin, or if you are wanting to learn about Gin, then you've got to have a cocktail at; The Gin Room. I stopped by the other day with a friend to enjoy a cocktail. Ms Norma had told me how knowledgeable Natasha was and she wasn't kidding. Natasha knows her, Gin and she'll share that knowledge with you as she makes your cocktail.  I'm a vodka drinker and love Moscow Mule's and when I shared that with "The Gin Girl", Natasha made me a, "Gin Gin Mule". It simply is a mule made with a high-end Gin. I was amazed how more flavorful the mule was with Hendrick's Gin.  If you're hanging out with friends on S. Grand, I highly recommend that you stop by The Gin Room.

Great neighborhood coffee shop. Great location making it easy to stop by on your way to work or while you are out running errands.   They have several tables in a small dining area that is brightly light by a large window and colorful walls. Making it a great place for a morning meeting with a coworker or business associate and gossiping with BFF.   I didn't see much of pastries available, but I stopped by early afternoon for a holiday flavored Latte. However, I did see a menu offering soups and salads for lunchtime fare. I hope they get a website up soon so we can see their menu at all times.   They use one of the most popular roasters in Saint Louis, Kaldi's for their coffee so you know it will be a good brew.  Also, they have a frequent drinkers card that you get punched and after 7 lattes or 7 cups of coffee the 8th one is FREE. Who doesn't like a free cup of morning Joe? A nice touch to a neighborhood shop.   When walking the dog(s), this will be my reward.

Great news, this ancient grocery store is getting a remodel. As with any remodel where the store remains open, there are obstructions to maneuver around. Shoppers may have a little inconvenience now, but it is well worth it. The areas that have already had their face lifts, are looking fabulous.   This is my before work grocer, I pick up supplies for the office and on occasion lunch items. I have found this staff to be, small town friendly. They give new meaning to the friendliest stores in town. They are so excited about their remodel, they take real pride in their store. So with a remodel and energetic employees, I am bumping them up a star. They deserve it.

Is this place heaven or a warehouse store for booze? I absolutely drool from their selection of Vodka. How am I ever going to have enough time to try them all? Cucumber Martini was a refreshing summer treat.  To visit the beer selection pull out your passport, its a trip around the world in 80 brews. I love the fact that they separate by country, it makes the selection process so much easier. Got a holiday parties? Let Randall's help you stock-up the staff is helpful and they know booze. Their wine selections will make great hostess gifts.

Poor customer service, the staff was too busy standing around and talking to each other, then assisting shoppers. I'm going to assume they were holiday help and not the regular staff.   I found what I needed, but could have probably bought more if someone would have approached me and done suggestive selling. (For every $50 you spent you got a $10 coupon)  You would think that they'd turn it up a notch for someone who is carrying a competitors bag from the other end of the mall.  Wouldn't you want to try to make that person a loyal customer to you?   When I went to check out the ladies at the register turned on the charm but, it was too late. They should have had them on the sales floor and those who just wanted to stand working the register.  It would have been nice to have gotten a $10 coupon, but they didn't deserve my $50.

According to Webster's dictionary A-OK means, excellent, fine, in working order, ect. : a generalized term of commendation. So for me to say that my hometown airport is A-Ok is a good compliment.   Is the best airport I have flown in or out of? No, it is dated and needs a major face-lift to bring it up to the same level of other major cities. However, it is easy to navigate, TSA lines move quickly and it is kept clean. I do prefer the East Terminal over the Main Terminal, but that could be that I fly Southwest more often then other airlines.   When it is time to fly out of the Lou, Lambert is A-OK and that is a good thing. So go explore other cities and get Yelping.

Not only does Lesher's do incredible floral work, but their customer service is outstanding. They truly go beyond the call of duty. I recently needed flowers delivered to a friend who works from home and it required a little more details in the delivery. This friends schedule is sporadic, she is in and out of her home office often. I asked Lesher's to call and make sure she was home before delivering and they said that was no problem. Flowers were delivered to rave reviews from my friend.   Lesher's is on speed dial with my younger cousin who now lives in Little Rock, AR. As he started to reignite a relationship with a girlfriend here in Saint Louis he called his older Yelp cousin for a florist recommendation. He has now used them multiple times, stopped in to meet them when he was in town for a Blues game and is truly on first name basis with the staff. The joys of a Ma and Pa shop with good solid local roots. Oh, the girlfriend Kyndall has loved all the bouquets from Lesher's.   If you need flowers, use Lesher's.

Love, it! Love, it!   I am so glad Craft Beer Cellar opened an additional location in South City. They made great use of an old car repair shop. The retail area is compact and well organized. They offer a good variety and it is all priced individually, or as a six-pack and case.   To be honest, what makes this location better then it's sister location in Clayton is the bar area. It's larger and offers more craft beers on draft. You can sit at the bar and chat with the bartender, or you can sit at one of the tables with a group of friends. There's no kitchen, but if you need something to munch as you sip a craft beer, they don't mind if you bring your own.   If your not sure what you want or you're wanting to try something new, talk with the sales professionals, they'll give you good guidance. The staff is friendly and are true lovers of craft beer.   A bonus - In the mornings, the bar area is a coffee shop - The Living Room.   I'll be back? - I'm confident I'll be a regular, here.   When: July 19, 2018 Why: Grand Opening Party

Great little boutique jewelry store. Love their sterling silver - hence "The Silver Lady". They have fantastic pieces at  a variety of price points.  The sales professionals are suggestive and not over bearing in their approach.   Recommend this place for any holiday or special occasion that deserves a gift.

Shhhh.....we gotta keep this a secret. The Happy Hour, at Bartolino's Osteria, is top notch. They celebrate HH, 3-6 PM, every Monday thru Wednesday. On Thursday, they celebrate Happy Hour 3- Close in the bar and on the patio. Now that is how HH should be scheduled.   In addition to discounted adult beverages, they have a special bar menu offering super deals on a variety of finger foods. Some of the most popular are; Toasted Ravioli, Pizza Fries, Crab Cake, Lobster Rangoon, Mini Cheeseburger and a One Topping Pizza.   The bartenders are old school. They free-pour their creations, making them extra strong. Many of the patrons sitting around the bar are regulars. It's almost shades of Cheers. They all greet each other by name as they position themselves on a bar stool. Don't worry if you're not a regular, they're all extremely friendly and welcoming.   Will I return? - Yep, I love a good strong cocktail.   When: July 2, 2020 Why: HH - Out running errands and day drinking with a friend.

This Sonic is off the beaten path. It is tucked away in an area that resembles an industrial park for fast food restaurants. It sets so far off the main road, you could miss it if you did not know where to find it.   Work was over, I was headed home and the chocolate cravings begun to sneak up on me. I wanted a cool refreshing chocolate malt for the drive home. So veered off the main drag and into fast food lane, to satisfy my craving.   Pulling up to the Drive-Thru menu I was meet with instant disappointment. Sonic does not sell malts. I couldn't wait to get back into St Louis to stop at my neighborhood Steak-n-Shake, so I lowered my expectations and ordered a shake. It was chocolate, it was thick and creamy. It just lacked that malt flavoring I wanted oh so bad.   The drive-thru service was nice and pleasant. No scratchy speaker voice, it was crisp and clear. Was hoping to see a carhop on skates, but no such luck today. Perhaps another day when I craze one of those slushy icy drinks for the drive home.

It was my friends and she love tequila. So selecting her gift was easy, I'll get her tequila. The only problem, I don't drink tequila the way she does. I only drink it in a Margarita. So I was going to need help.   Randall's is usually my go to for booze and since it was on the way to the party, I stopped by to get her gift. Being clueless, I stood in the tequila aisle totally confused. One of the sales associates came over and asked if I needed help. Lucky for me, he was a tequila drinker himself. He showed me several bottles and shared which ones he liked. I asked him about one that was in a gift tin and he pointed out its high rating. It had a 94 out of 100 from the Ultimate Wine Challenge. Best of all, it was on sale. My gift was the hit of the gift table.   Thanks, Randall's for making shopping for a birthday gift easy.   I'll be back? - Yes, I drink.   When: March 13, 2019 Why: Birthday Gift Shopping

This restaurant has absolutely no ambiance, but that is ok. Why is it, okay? You're not here for the decor, you're here for comfort food. Comfort food that is prepared in good ole homestyle fashion.   Being new to the area, I am on a constant search for a good breakfast place. Having breakfast out is one of my favorite things. I swung by Village Inn on the recommendation of a Chicago Yelper. Yes, a out-of-towner turned me on to a diner in my new neighborhood. She loved their pancakes and she's a pancake snob.   So, I went with one of their Wipe Board Specials. I choose, the Pancake Combo. It was a huge amount of food. Not only did I get two pancakes, I also enjoyed 2 eggs scrambled, 2 sausage links and 2 strips of bacon. Next time, I'm just going for the pancakes and a side of bacon. For me, it will be enough.  Service was attentive, my coffee cup was constantly warmed up. They were friendly and you could tell who the regulars were, they greeted them by name.   Will I return? - Good pancakes always bring me back.   When: November 3, 2020 Why: Breakfast

Disclaimer: I've never eaten here, but I have done a lot of carry-out.   I am totally in love with their Bartolino's Special Salad. I have loved this salad, since they were at the old location down Hampton Avenue. So it has been ordered as my entire meal for a night and as a salad to accompany a steak grilled in the backyard. I've called ahead and it is always waiting for me and living 5 minutes away, I have just driven up and ordered when I arrived.   It's basically a simple salad; lettuce, choice of turkey or salami (my favorite is turkey), tossed with provel cheese, pepperoncini, kalamatra olives, artichoke hearts and tomatoes in their famous house dressing. It never disappoints us.   3 Stars is a good rating for carry-out. If I enjoyed the salad in the actual restaurant, I'm sure it would be a 4 Star review.

I am slowly transitioning over to this Schnucks from the one on Hampton. Why? Customer service. The staff here is so much friendlier and professional. This location also seems to always have enough cashiers working, so the lines are not insanely long.   It has taken me awhile to adapt to the different lay-out. I'm now favoring the shorter aisles, that are cut in half with a center aisle dividing them in the middle of the store. Which means more end-caps to display those sale items and implies items we should all avoid.   I'm finding the same fresh produce,  quality meats and regular grocery items that I need and want. The frozen foods section is laid out and organized much better.  Plus, with the superior customer service, it is a no brainer to shop here over my previous favorite.   Hope they get a remodel soon. They deserve it.  Chances of returning: It's a work in progress When: January 17, 2019 Why: Grocery Shopping

When I told friends I was going to Rosie's they polietly told me, "you know that is a dive bar".  Like that was going to stop me. I told them I was aware of the "type" of bar I was going to and as long as they had vodka things would be A-OK.  The drinks are cheap and the bartender gives a healthy pour. So it is real easy to get your buzz on. The decor is simple; bar, stools, high top tables and a juke box.   It is a true neighborhood bar, with a good cast of regular drinkers. It was fun to watch as each new arrival entered the dive. There would be waves , handshakes and hugs from the other drinkers. A true "Cheers" bar, "Where everyone knows your name". Which is a good thing, because I think some drinkers there might need a little reminder of who they are before the night was over.   When visiting Rosie's just beware, you may run into someone you know and just like Vegas, what happens at Rosie's stays at Rosie's.

A Kolache is better then any biscuit or McMuffin from any fast food place.   Their freshly baked pastries are stuffed with a variety of hearty ingredients making them a perfect breakfast or light lunch.   Get there early for the freshest, and keep in mind they close at 2 p m.   Wish they were closer, but they're an extra treat when we are in the Brentwood area.

Let's Party!  Simply said, Party City is the place to go for party supplies. They literally have it all. You'll find every color imaginable, special occasions and themed party supplies at affordable prices. It's also a great place to go for balloons, greeting cards and gift bags. I may not shop here often, but when I need certain party supplies, this is the place to go.  What ever you're celebrating, Party City can help you celebrate it in style.   I'll be back? - When it's party time.   When - April 23, 2018 Why - Party goodies

I love this store. I bought several holiday gifts here. What gave me a chuckle this year is, I received many gifts from here as well. I've talked so much about how cool this store is and the unique selection of home furnishings, that my family finally listened and shopped local for me this year.   The store is beautifully merchandised. Having worked a number of years in retail and home furnishing, I can honestly say this is a top-notch store. Others in reviews have commented that the prices are on the high side. I take the other road and say they are extremely reasonable. Many of the items are unique, but others that I have found at a competitors store are less expensive here at GB.   The staff is always available for questions and when the owners are present, they are totally approachable as well. In fact, they are eager to assist all the shoppers. They make shopping at GB a fun & pleasant experience.   Will I return - I stop by overtime I'm in Edwardsville  When: August 31, November 8, 2017 Why: I'm a Shop-a-holic

The menu selections are few, but the sandwiches are big in flavor. I choose the Sloppy Joe and it was the best Sloppy Joe I have ever had. It was topped with my favorite cheese, Pepper Jack and pickled Brussels Sprouts/Kale. I would have never thought of pickling brussels sprouts, let alone putting them on top of a sandwich. Wow - they really added to the flavor of this Joe.   Your sandwich comes with your choice of chip or drink. It was a beautiful day, so I choose chips and added a Schlafly beer to my order. I enjoyed my sandwich outside on one of their picnic tables, creating the perfect ambiance.   This was Bolyard's first time making Ian Froeb's STL 100 List and it is well deserved. They may only serve sandwiches, but they are top notch. Stop by and experience the deliciousness of Bolyard's.   Well I return? Yes.   When: March 8, 2017 Why: Lunch - Ian Froeb's STL 100 2017

Warning: You will not see Jack, Janet or Chrissy sitting at the bar and Jack will not be working the kitchen. This is a hometown sports bar that is all about cold craft beer and good pub food.   It's a great place to gather with friends, or as in my case cousins. The variety of beers is vast and it is always served in a frosted glass.   They serve up some better then average pub food. Their burgers are thick and juicy and the variety of pizzas available can put some pizza restaurants to shame.   If you are in the Alton or Godfrey area and want a bar to have a fun time with your friends or family, I highly recommend the Regal Beagle.

Attending a private party at Smashburger was a blast! I enjoyed my food so much, I couldn't go home to my SO empty handed. I ordered an Ultimate Cheeseburger, Smash Fries and a Gooey Butter Cake Shake to go.    The staff that made our party so special, was equally as nice when preparing my to go order. They truly provide service with a smile.   Being a city dweller, I was concerned about the long drive back into the city with a carry out order. No problem, it was still warm and the shake was awesome.  Actually I was hoping to get the shake, but no such luck. For once the SO's sweet tooth was as sweet as mine.   As the SO devoured the burger & fries, they received rave reviews just as I raved about the ones at the party. We both talked about wanting to revisit Smashburger but dreaded the long drive to St. Charles. To our surprise, we learned a new one is opening in Chesterfield very soon and that drive we can deal with.   Five Guys, Smashburger has you beat.

Great service without the attitude. This is a top notch hair salon, that provides great cuts, and from I have observed fantastic color and highlights.  I love the fact that my stylist actually runs on time, my experience  with other salons, is that you have to wait almost as long as you do at a doctor's office - but not here.  Everyone is friendly and greets you as you walk through the salon.  Another review commented on the noise, I actually love the hustle and bustle - it adds to the atmosphere and conversation. A bonus of coming here is I get to shop at Crate & Barrel before or after my cut - like I need an excuse to shop...lol.

We drove a little further to get lunch the other day and I am glad we did. It was my first visit to Sweetie Pie's and for the life of me I can figure out why it took me so long to get here. Let me first comment on the "ladies" of Sweetie Pie's, they are amazing, so friendly and down home. They make you feel as if you are dining at your favorite Aunt or grandma's house. I had the fried chicken wings and two sides. Don't know where they get their chickens , but I think they are on steroids. The wings were huge, biggest wings I've ever seen. My sides were Mac-n-Cheese, which reminded  me of my favorite Aunt's and Green Beans that were equal to my Grandma's.  The servings were so down-home plentiful, I had lunch for the next day.  I'm going back and on my next visit, I'm dining in so I can experience the true experience of Sweetie Pie's.

This place came to my rescue, so I'm a fan. I had visited several shoe stores looking for shoelaces to replace a pair in one of my favorite work shoes. None of them had the type I needed. How can  a shoe store sell you a shoe with laces and not have the replacement laces when you need them? Finally a sales clerk at one of the stores I visited referred me to Hampton Shoe Repair. (That was excellent customer service.) What a shock, the store is in my neighborhood and I never thought of going there. I was pleased with the selection of laces, and they had the exact one I needed for my shoes. I was also amazed at the selection of work boots. I don't need the boots for work, but they look great with jeans and flannel when you are going for that outdoorsy look.  After reading Kelly B's review I'm taking a pair of loafers in for a sole-lift.

I am so glad that someone has bought and brought the Three Dog Bakery franchise back to St. Louis.   The location is further out in West County, but well worth the drive. It's located in the new Town & Country Crossing. You can shop Whole Foods, have lunch at Five Guys and pick treats for your favorite K-9.   They have all the fabulous cookies you remember from the previous Ladue location and many new ones as well. When I returned home with a bag full of mini bones, Fire Hydrant Cookies, Cranberry Cookies and Dottie Spots, I was greeted with 4 wagging tales.   In addition to all the yummy dog treats, they an excellent selection of doggie accessories and necessities.   Check their website for special events, sales and promotions.   My Four Dogs are glad Three Dog is back in the Lou.

Love having a great neighborhood park like Tilles. The city keeps it well maintained and the locals do their part to keep it beautiful.  I love the walking paths, as much as my dogs do. It's amazing how many dog walkers you see in the mornings and evenings.  Tilles is just the perfect size.

Their recent commercials got me to stop by and try their new, Reese's Outrageous Blizzard. It's a blend of vanilla custard, Reese's Pieces, broken up Reese's Peanut Butter Cups and Caramel. Sounds delicious, right? Yes, if you have a serious, sweet tooth. For me, it was too overly sweet.  I admit, I've been known to order a Blizzard with Reese's Pieces in it or one with their Peanut Butter Cups. Alone, each of those made for a good blizzard. However, mixing the two and adding caramel as a third ingredient, made for an overly sweet treat. Next time, I enjoy a simpler Blizzard with only one ingredient or may-be two at the most.   In closing, I'll say the staff is always friendly and professional. This location is truly a neighborhood DQ.   Will I be back? - Their commercials for a new Blizzard always catch my eye.   When: August 21, 2018 Why: Outrageous Blizzard

My first visit here was for Abby's Farewell, and I will return for the true Latitude experience.  I got enough of a tease to know it will be amazing.  It may sound weird, but I judge a Mexican restaurant by its Margaritas, chips and salsa and queso.  If they can pull those three things off,  you've got me hooked.  The staff was extremely friendly and made us feel as if we were attending a private party in someone's home.  I'm sure I'll raise my stars after I experience a full meal.

I am a big fan of Costco and this GFS has impressed me. It is restaurant quality, you can still buy in bulk and no membership is required. They had many name brands on some items and their house brand GFS. Just imagine a Costco or Sam's with only the food section and you've created GFS.   They also had an aisle with party supplies. Who needs Party City when you can pick up your plates, cups, catering trays, napkins and table cloths at the same store you're picking up your party food.   The pricing was very comparable to the warehouse clubs and on some items it was even lower. The staff was upbeat, helpful and walked us directly to various items when we requested them. Just like the warehouse stores, they had a sample lady who was passing out goodies.   I think Jenny S. hit the nail on the head, GFS is the baby of Sam's and Aldi's.

Had to revisit the very next day after my first visit. We ate all our gifts, and thought of others who would enjoy these fabulous chocolate treats.  Today the customer service was incredible. Everyone there had their A-Game on which made for a pleasant shopping experience.   I made my purchase and as I was leaving, hand on the door knob they spoke of the Egg Nog Truffles that were just coming out. I turned and said, "did I hear Egg Nog?".  I love Egg Nog, and these Truffles are bursting with flavor.   Chocolate lovers you've got to go visit this place, it is amazing.

Simple update - I am a fan of their "Garden Mix" which is a mixture of top soil, mulch and just a small amount of sand.  Perfect for planter boxes.  We recently used it to top off an area of our front yard to start new growth. We're starting with a clean slate and a good foundation of "Garden Mix'.

Bentley's is a great new addition to the many pet boutiques in St. Louis. It has an incredible selection to top rated foods for my fur-babies. They also have grain free and made in the USA treats. I was particularly impressed with the bulk section, because they offered a variety of flavors and sizes in treats. They also have a selection of dog beds, toys and of course collars and leashes.   On my first visit, the service was friendly and helpful. Being a first time shopper, I got a goodie bag with coupons, sample of dry dog food and a couple of treats.   When shopping Lucky's, or Stien Mart or dining at The Slider House or Katie's Pizza, Bentley's will also be on the itinerary when I'm in the Rock Hill hood.   Will I come back? YES!  When: October 12, 2016 Why: New pet boutique

Forget a co-workers birthday? Can't get out of the office to get a cake for the celebration? Don't worry, Hot Box Cookies will be your hero. They deliver and they even brought a small ballon, for the birthday honoree.   Our box of cookies were still warm when they delivered them. Being a true Yelper, I had to block my co-workers from grabbing the delicious cookies, so I could get a photo first. We had a great variety, Peanut Butter, M&M, Chocolate Chunk, Oatmeal and White Chocolate Macadamia. There was something for everyone.   I was amazed how fast they delivered after we placed our order. I wish my pizzas or Chinese could be delivered this fast. The delivery girl was perky and made our birthday girl feel special.   Will I return? Only have had delivery, gotta go check out the shop.  When: February 22, 2017 Why: Birthday Celebration at work

Let's talk some dirt. I mean some serious dirt, the kind that will make your garden, flowers and landscaping grow.  I never knew there could be such a large variety of mulch and dirt. Their staff knows the dirt and will be able to tell you which one is best for you.   With spring finally here, and our green thumbs looking to get dirty this is the place to shop for dirt. As pointed out by Ms. Sarah S., they do have a high delivery fee for those of us who do not drive a pick-up truck. So I highly recommend that you find a friend who does.   Now let's get out there and get dirty in the dirt.

I am going to make this one short and sweet.   I love the salsas, jellies and spreads form Harry & David. The Jalapeno jelly is one of my favorites.   On my last visit they had Chicken Pot Pies on sale for half price. What a deal, how could I pass on this opportunity to try something new.  It made for an easy dinner that night and we were impressed. The pie had lots of vegetables and white breast meat. It was large enough to feed 5 adults, or in our case lunch the next day.   The customer service was friendly and extremely helpful. When I asked about one of the spreads, they went to the back and brought out an opened jar for sampling. What a nice touch.   Be sure to sign up for their email list so you will be informed of sales and on occasion they send you coupons and we all like coupons.

This DQ has grown on me. They've recently turned their game up. I think they've done it as a corporation and as a franchise. I don't stop by that frequently, but when I do, I'm not disappointed. A soft serve cone or a Blizzard can always satisfy a sweet tooth craving.   What motivated me to stop yesterday, was seeing a poster promoting a Dipped Strawberry Blizzard. How could I resist a blizzard with one of my favorite fruits, strawberries and Ghirardelli chocolate. It's so cool how they turn it upside down when presenting it to you. If they don't, your next one is free. My blizzard was rich, creamy and tasted just like a Chocolate Dipped Strawberry. I ordered a small. It was so delicious, I wished I had ordered a larger size, but thankful that I didn't.   The staff was friendly and the kitchen area in view was clean.   I'll be back? - Sure, don't know how quickly, but I'll return. Can't control my cravings.   When: February 4, 2018 Why: Dipped Strawberry Blizzard

Three Dog Bakery, made the holidays a howling success for my Fur-Babies. My dogs will celebrate any holiday if there is a cookie involved and TDB has them all.  They have celebrated Hanukkah, Winter Solstice, Christmas and Kwanzaa with delightful and tasty treats. One of our Shelties even celebrated a 10th birthday this week with a TDB cookie. With all the holiday treats I didn't order a cake, but will be getting one for Big Gracie's birthday in February.   I even picked up some great little bags of treats to give to our cousin dogs and neighborhood dogs making us the cats meow.....LOL.   Keep in mind Three Dog is not just a bakery, they also have a large variety of dog accessories and their own line of premium dog food.   Also,  the staff here gives exceptional customer service. They not only remember my name and call it out when I enter the store, but they remember what breed of dogs I have too.

Bigger and better then the Huck's close to my home and they offer gas too. It's like a mini U-Gas. Great selection of fountain drinks and convenience mart type items. They even had a small area of table and chairs for those who want to sit and grab a bite to eat.   What makes Huck's special is the fact that they are employee owned. When the one waiting on you is part owner, you know you'll be getting good customer service. If I lived in Kirkwood, this would be my convenience mart and gas station of choice.

The produce and sea food departments alone get this Whole Foods a 5 star rating. The fresh vegetables and fruits are perfect for starting the new year eating right. Eating right sounds so much better then dieting.   The counter person in seafood was so friendly and helpful that he had me laughing while making my selection.  Excellent customer service.   The cashier is the last image you have of a shopping experience and it needs to be positive. Mine wasn't, but I did not let that effect my star rating. My cashier said the same exact thing to me as she did the two customers before me - come on change it up. The most annoying thing to me was the young lady's style of chewing gum. She chewed it like a cow chewing it's cud. Not only did she chew aggressively, but she made it snap and pop.  I must be old, I remember the days when people in retail or food service were not allowed to chew gum while working.

My mama told me, you better shop around Oh yeah, you better shop around. When Smokey Robinson sang those words years ago, it was about love. Recently, I learned it is also true about rocks. Who would have ever though the price of rock would differ so greatly, but they did. What amazed us most was that the larger and furthest businesses from the city were the most expensive.   After "shopping around", we found the best price for Iowa Rainbow to be at Brentwood Material. Being novices at buying rock they showed us how to figure out the amount we'd need to fill in a 2 1/2' x 13' area. After moving 3/4 of a ton of rock, I can tell you it is a gym workout. However, never having to mow that small area between our house and sidewalk is a win.   Good Pricing and Good Customer Service has Brentwood Material Co. leading the pack.

Pizza delivery be gone, I no longer need you. I will gladly order my pizza and salads from Station Pizzeria and go pick them up myself.  I want quality over the convenience of delivery.   Tonight we dined on their house salad with house dressing.  A good mixture of iceberg, romaine, onion, pimento, provel and Parmesan.  As stated n my previous review, I like that the pieces are actual bite size and do not need to be re-cut to enjoy.  Their house dressing is a Italian vinaigrette, which adds the perfect touch to the salad.   Our pizza was The Godfather, a flavorful mixture of sausage, pepperoni, mushroom, green pepper and onion. For an extra kick we had them add jalapeno. With or without the jalapeno peppers this is an excellent pizza. It's a traditional St. Louis thin crust, but is cut into pie shaped pieces, not squares.   If you love pizza and have not had one from here yet, you do not know what you are missing. I suggest that you correct that situation as soon as possible.

Excellent breakfast! With Eclipse being attached to a hotel, going in I was a little concerned about the quality.  My experience with restaurants attached to hotels has not been good in the past, but Eclipse has totally changed my opinion.   Our breakfast started out with a spicy and flavorful Bloody Mary. I enjoyed a Three Egg Omelet with bacon, onion and pepper jack cheese. I'm trying to go low carb, so our server was very accommodating and allowed me to substitute my side of hash browns with asparagus. My omelet was fluffy, filled with the bacon and onion and had the cheese melted and poured on top. It was a delightful twist, to the typical cheese inside.   My dining partner enjoyed Eggs Benedict with asparagus and a side of Hash Browns.  For a hotel and only $9, this was an impressive Eggs Benedict. We both enjoyed the asparagus, it was done to perfection. Butter, a dash of salt and steamed to a perfect snap. The Hash Browns were served crispy, my favorite way. I had to be strong and stay low-carb.   Good friendly service, great food and free valet parking makes Eclipse worthy of my Breakfast,Bloody Mary and Benedict list.

For me this AC does a good job.   I primarily use them for my shirts and slacks. I'll admit when it comes to my clothes, I'm high maintenance. I separate my shirts in separate piles, for different starch levels and those shirts I want dry cleaned. They've never gotten them mixed up and they are always done well.  I also bring in all of my dress and casual slacks. On occasion, I have brought in jeans to have them heavily starched. As I've stated before, I wish they'd do a light starch on my Docker's. When needed, they've also done an excellent job on my suits and sport coats.   AC use to only take cash or check and now they take debit and credit cards. To be honest, this use to be the only place I wrote checks. Being someone who does a lot of dry cleaning, I am thankful they send out coupons on the regular. If I run out, I can also print them out on the company website.   I'll be back? - Almost every 10 days.   When: Way to often.  Why: Gotta look good.

A great mom & pop donut shop. Staff is friendly and the coffee is strong and fresh. When visiting a new donut shop I judge them on two basic donuts, Chocolate Long John and Glazed Donut Holes and Mister Donut does them right. The LJ was moist and the chocolate icing was perfectly smeared end to end. I've been a sucker for holes since I was a child. I really love them now, eating a couple holes satisfies my cravings for an entire donut.   I noticed they offer other breakfast items as well, especially Biscuits and Gravy. I may have to leave for work a little extra early some day and see if they are worthy of being on my Biscuits and Gravy List.

I can not believe it, no one has written a review for this great co-op boutique. I was here for a Halloween party before their opening and just now got back to actually shop. I am now remorseful for not returning sooner.   There are about 40+ vendors offering all sorts of goodies. Ranging from clothing for women and men, to hand made soaps, posters, candies, candles and so much more. One vendor offers some very creative and tasteful stationary. I'm a sucker for note cards and thank you cards.   Next time you are downtown, make it a point to stop by and shop this "Collective" boutique. Chances are you will find something to your liking. I did. I love my new poster/map that shows all the neighborhoods in Saint Louis. Now I know where all the Yelp Dukedoms are located. Also, the Milk Chocolate Triple Dipped Malt Balls from, Oh Lolli Lolli melted in my mouth. Yes I am dieting, but I can still have a treat and these malt balls were truly a treat.

I arrived extremely early for a dinner with friends at Preston's, so I popped in at The Chase Club for a cocktail. I arrived the same time as a huge group of Wells Fargo sales representatives were arriving for a conference. I thought it would take forever to get a drink, with this large group all descending on the bar at once. To my surprise, the bartenders hustled and had us all enjoying our drinks in a timely fashion.   I'm normally a vodka man, but recently I have fallen in love with Manhattan's. A Manhattan is a classic cocktail. Like a martini it is strong, so I sip it and enjoy it for a longer period of time. The Chase Club makes their Manhattan's with Marker's Mark. I watched my bartender make my Manhattan and I was pleased to see he stirred it. I prefer my martini's to be shaken, but I like my Manhattan's stirred. Trust me it makes a difference.  As a bar for Happy Hour, I'd say the Chase Club is A-OK. It's a great hotel lobby bar.   When: June 6, 2016 Why: Happy Hour - Manhattan

Great service and Great food! Our last visit was a simple meal, salads and mussels and if anyone knows me, they know I love "mussels".   The SO enjoyed a Beet Salad with Goat Cheese and I had the Caesar Salad. Both were very good, but the Beet Salad was the best. I loved the large thick slices, topped with Goat Cheese. The Romaine Lettuce in my Caesar Salad was diced and cut into bite size pieces and coated in the appropriate amount of dressing.   We both took advantage of the nightly special of, Prince Edward Island Mussels. They were so good, we easily could have ordered a third bowl to share. PEI Mussels in a White Wine and Garlic broth is always a winner for me.   Everyone who works here is friendly and attentive to the diners needs. We always feel welcomed here with their warm hospitality. Once again, I am so glad Mathew's is in my neighborhood.

Pop's Blue Moon is the Grandaddy of all dive bars. The decor is tacky, the building is in need of renovation and plaster is falling from the ceiling. All of that makes for a dive bar full of charm, warmth and coziness.   They offer cheap beer, of course Blue Moon and I was pleased they offered Schlafly's APA on draft. I was also impressed with the selection of brand names that you could call for your liquor drinks. Some regular bars don't offer the selection that Pop's has.   Our bartender was friendly and personable. I thought he looked like one I would see at Bad Dog or JJ's Clubhouse. The other patrons come and go, some stay to themselves and others will enjoy conversation with newbies. I had a fun time and would love to go back and enjoy some live music.   Remember, Pop's only takes cash. So don't leave home without it, because there's no  ATM to save your ass.

My skin crawled when I walked into this new Hobby Lobby. However, I realized sometimes you have to put political choices & opinions aside when you are shopping for specific items for your DIY art project.   I will admit that HL does have some great items for all sorts of DIY projects. However, I will also admit, their store is poorly organized and laid out. Also, it could use some serious signage to make it easier to find the items you are shopping for. None of the aisles were tagged as to what is in them. I had to search up and down until  I found one item on my project list. I had to search long and hard to find it.  While browsing the store looking for my creative tools, I did find some great future gifts for friends and family. I also saw some decorative items that just may find their way into my home.  Customer service on the sales floor and from the cashier was lacking. I can only imagine what I may have spent if I actually had gotten assistance and was made welcome in the store.   When: June 22, 2016 Why: Big Creative Art Project.

Andy,   I will never cheat on you with another custard stand. You are by far my favorite custard in STL. In the past I have had brief love affairs with a Wizard and a Ted, but neither of them satisfied my sweet tooth and ice cream (custard) craving like you do. You're consistently rich and creamy. Also, your portion of mixers are always the right amount and are blended throughly thru out the concrete.   I live smack dab in the middle of your Richmond Heights and Kirkwood locations. So if I do cheat on you, it will be with another Andy's. Living so close to two of your custard shops, is a curse to my waistline, but it is a curse I am willing to live with. I just need to enjoy your decadence in moderation.   Love ya,  StevenB  Will I return? You bet, I will.   When: August 11, 2017 (Friday) Why: Love Affair with Andy

I wish I had children so I could take them to the City Museum. It is such a fun place to play. It can bring out the inner child in all of us, so I guess I could go alone and just have fun.   Recently the Oscar Road Trip made a stop at City Museum and it was the perfect place for all of us movie buffs to have our fantasies come true of winning an Oscar. Or at least hold it for a brief moment and pretend that it is ours.   Come and play, everything is okay at the City Museum. It's a fun place for kids of all ages.

Alton Restaurant Week   Enjoyed their lunch special during ARW.  I enjoyed it so much, I'll definitely will be returning.  I enjoyed a, Beef Tenderloin Mushroom Melt with au jus and French Fries. It was marinated beef tenderloin tips topped with sautéed wild mushrooms and Swiss cheese, served on toasted French bread.   The sandwich was a good portion and the fries were crisp. It was a very filling lunch. Personally, I would have preferred, Provolone cheese on my sandwich, but the Swiss was fine. During this pandemic, I would have preferred the ketchup to have been served in a "little cup", but they did wipe down the bottles between diners.   The restaurant is in a space that was previously a store in a strip center, so it is a very vast space. Being a large open space, there's an echo, but not so much to disrupt your conversation.   The staff was doing a good job following CDC guidelines, making sure all guest were maintaining social distance and wearing mask. They also, did  a through job sanitizing when guest left.  In addition to providing, friendly and attentive service.   When: January 23, 2021 Why: Lunch - Alton Restaurant Week Jan-2021

Michaels you are so much better then Hobby Lobby. Your aisles are marked, making it so easy to shop your store. I was able to find what I needed for my DIY art project. I even found items to take it up an additional notch.   Your staff was helpful on the floor and your cashier made small talk that complemented my selections. Not being a crafter, I left your store feeling like a top designer and an established artist. Look out world, here I come.   When: June 22,2016 Why: Craft Project

I was so excited when Stein Mart opened a store closer to the city, I hated the drive out to Ballwin to get my SM fix. For those of you who are not familiar with SM it is a TJ Max and Home Goods in one store. When I shop SM my focus is the Men's Dept. and occasionally I wander into the home accessories. In the Men's Dept. I can always find a bargain. I start out with the sale racks, and work my out to the regular priced racked. You can find many designer names and some of SM name brands are just as good. Trust me I know, I am a clothes horse.   The sales clerks are friendly and helpful. On my last visit they were doing a floor change, and they informed me of the sale they were sitting up. Love 30% off already low prices.

Kohl's is better then TJ Max, Marshall's and even Stein Mart. I just wish they were at a better location so I'd remember to shop them more often. This location is not on my normal path for shopping so I have to make this a destination store.   Great for men's casual clothes and accessories. The home goods are pretty impressive as well.  I have gotten  several good deals on pots and pans and other kitchen goodies. Their prices were lower then BB&B.   Only downside is the customer service, it is bare bones. If you need assistance on the floor, good luck on finding someone.  The cashiers are perky and cheerful, just a shame they do not have the same type of associates on the sales floor. It pretty much is a self serve, self find department store.   Small warning to those who are claustrophobic, this store is cluttered. Very cluttered, they pack in as many racks and tables full of merchandise as they possibly can and that is why you save big $'s on your purchases.

Have you ever left home, going the opposite direction of your favorite gas station and realize you are down to two bars on your gas gage. Two bars is the danger zone and time to fill up. You're pressed for time and cannot turn around to go get gas at your normal station.  As you ponder your dilemma, you see a 7-11 ahead and it's one that has a gas station. My ass has just been saved.   For connivence it is a pay at the pump, so I am not tempted by that big Slurpee machine inside. I slide my card into the slot, answered all the questions and filled my CRV with gas. To my surprise it was the same price on credit, as I would have paid for paying with cash at my regular spot.  The lot where the gas pumps are located was litter free and the computer prompts were courteous. I was in and out with self service and that is the way I like it at 7-11.

I love their selection of HIGH quality pet foods. My fur-babies eat grain free food and FMP has an excellent selection of these type of foods and their prices fit my budget. Plus, they have a frequent buyers program.   Shelby finally made it in to select her new collar and leash, but her first choice was out of her size. They offered to add it to an order they just placed, what great customer service. However, Shelby declined the offer and went with her second choice. The apple doesn't fall from the tree, like her daddy she wanted instant gratification.   Again, I gotta give a shout out for their great customer service. They always insist on carrying my dog food out to the car for me. I decline the offer, but it is always nice to hear. Great friendly service.

Been here, shopped here and did a return here. I am not impressed.  I am not a craft-er, but I can appreciate a craft store and this one did not make the cut. The location is good, so most likely I will return when the need arrives and that is why I am giving them a 3.

Great little shop for the Fur-Babies. I was down the street picking up a Gooey Butter cake and knew I couldn't go home without treats for the children.   While selecting the treats, I also browsed their selection of collars. I'll be re-visiting soon with Shelby so she can select a new collar.  They also have a great selection of toys and quality foods.   The staff was friendly and provided excellent customer service.

I'm not a fan of the Queen. I find her soft serve ice cream to be bland. Even when it is twisted in a cone and you have vanilla & chocolate combined together. To show you how bad, after two bites/licks I tossed my small cone in the trash. When a pudgy boy tosses a cone in the trash, you know it is bad. I've also tried their Blizzard and once again, even adding my favorite M&M's it comes out with no pizazz.   For me I'd give DQ a 2, but my SO likes their Chicken Tenders that  are served with milk gravy so I'll give them a 3. When he is sick, these Tenders are his "comfort" food. There is something about dipping tenders into milk gravy that makes him feel better.  I've sampled them and like their ice cream, it's not for me.   This DQ has recently had a major remodel and does look good sitting on the corner of Hampton and Eichelberger.

Their Reuben is truly Best of The Best. It is, Corned Beef with Kraut, 1000 Island Dressing, Swiss Cheese, Grilled and Served on Marble Rye Bread. It is huge, it is so big that I only ate half of my sandwich and took the remaining half home for dinner. I may have had the same thing for lunch and dinner that day, but it is was totally amazing.   It is a small sandwich shop, with the ambiance of a dive bar. It is dark, has a mixture of hightop tables and video games. In addition to the sandwiches, they offer a variety of chips and bottled soda. I was here mid afternoon and the place still had at least a dozen folks enjoying a late lunch. The lone man working was outgoing and very personable. Why anyone would choose Subway or Jimmy John's over S&S is beyond me. We shop local, now is the time to eat local as well.   I can't wait to go back and try their Pastrami and Pig on Wing. Even if I am not hungry, I will stop and get a sandwich to go and enjoy it later.

A local company that serves the nation via their website.   Who knew there could be so many puzzles. The variety and selection was mind blowing.  My reason for shopping here wasn't for a puzzle, it was for a Christmas Trivia game. My cousin and I wanted to add some fun to the, "Rob your Neighbor" gift exchange at the Christmas gathering. They had a clever little deck of Christmas Trivia Cards that did just the trick. We had so much fun reading the questions, that we continued after the gift exchange was over.   Will I return? - When I need a gift for a puzzle fan.  When: December 20, 2017 Why: Trivia Game

Four Muddy Paws is a solid 5 Stars, even during the Covid-19 pandemic. They're offering #curbsidepickup and free same day delivery within a 20 mile radius from their store. That not only is top notch customer service, it is taking care of our community. As we continually hear, "we're all is this together" and FMP is doing their part to help us care for the fur-babies.   I've used the curbside pick-up several times. Each time their amazing staff has made it so easy. I've used this service when I needed my regular 20 lb. bag of dry food and a re-stocking of the treat jars. They even helped me pull together Easter gifts for my Shelties and gifts for a couple of friends dogs as well.   During a pandemic or not, when I need something for my fur-babies, I'll be shopping at Four Muddy Paws. Inside the store, or curbside, they've got my business.

I walked in with seven old coins with face value of $3.08 and a sterling silver necklace and walked out with $152.  How do you like them $'s. Of course, Patt C.'s sister would say, "why bother".  If she'd clean out her coin purse, she might be singing a different song.   Check out those old coins and jewelry you've tossed in to a drawer they may be able to provide you with a night on the town or give you some extra money for the holidays.   The staff is knowledgeable and friendly, making your transaction fun.

PTC, saved my ass. I am one of those peps who drives until their gas tank needle is so close to  E, it is scary.   Actually, I forgot to get gas when I left work, I was in the zone to get home. Working in IL, once I'm on 255 and merge on to 70 to come back home to STL, there's no exit with a gas station until you see PTC. I was down to one bar, I couldn't risk continuing my drive across the bridge. I needed to get gas.   My experience is only at the "pump", but I'd say the customer service was spot on. The pump even asked me if I wanted a receipt. The area around the gas pumps well maintained and free of clutter and litter.  This PTC offers a Taco Bell and Subway for those who are hungry. I'll be honest, I miss the old days when a truck stop had a huge glorified diner. The food back then was good ole comfort food and not fast food.   I'll be back? - If I'm leaving IL and down to one bar again.   When: June 3, 2019 Why: I was outta gas.

Saw the commercials for the new Tacos at Burger King and thought I'd give them a try. I've tried the Impossible Whopper and enjoyed it, so I thought may-be the taco would be good, too. It wasn't. I put it on the same level as Jack in the Box. If you've got the I've been drinking munchies, it may satisfy you. If you're sober and wanting lunch, I'd order a burger instead.   I can not for the life of me, figure out why businesses just don't continue to focus on what they do best and what they are known for, instead of trying to expand their menu. Do something well, instead of serving mediocre everything.   Another reason to lower the star rating is the customer service here is on the decline again. There's not interaction between the staff and customer. They take your order and that is it.......if you get a thank-you you're doing good.

Great place to enjoy a cocktail before and after The Fox. Or, get a group of friends together to enjoy their Happy Hour and amazing view of downtown STL.    If you go for Happy Hour be sure to arrive between the hours of 2-6 PM. That way you'll be able to enjoy special prices on select cocktails, wine and local beers. You'll also be able to enjoy some tasty appetizers at a reduced price.   The service at the bar and tables are both attentive and friendly. If the weather is permitting, I highly recommend that you get outside and enjoy the terrace with a view.   I'll be back? - Absolutely.   When: A couple of times. Why: Happy Hour

I know there are some Yelpers who do not want us to review fast-food restaurants, but they still get our business and need to be rated.   I visited BK simply because we were lazy, needed dinner and had received a coupon in the mail. Our coupon in-titled us to; two Whoppers, two small fries and two small beverages for only $6.99.   We enjoyed the Whoppers, they were big sloppy burgers with all the toppings. The French Fries were awful, why would anyone want to eat the fries at Burger King. Our beverages I filled with no ice - we had ice at home.   The customer service was better then any thing I have received at a McDonald's or any other fast food. I have to be honest, I'll only be back with a coupon.

This vet is awesome!!! Everyone here is friendly and totally professional. I love their approach to holistic care.  They even give followup calls, to make sure everything is okay after a change in treatment. Totally recommend this vet, and we have a family of four dogs.

Need a spice for a new recipe? If so, get out of that spice aisle at your local grocer and get yourself over to Penzeys Spices in Maplewood. Once you have arrived, you will realize that you have arrived in the "mecca" of the spice world.  The large selection of your "typical" spices and the very "unique" spices will have you amazed. I love the fact that you can buy spices in a variety of sizes, to fit your immediate needs. They offer a great selection of gift boxes that make perfect holiday gifts for your "foodie" friends or a house warming gift for those who can afford to buy now.  While visiting Penzeys, drop by Vom Fass down the street for a "mecca" of oils and vinegars.

Only recently have I become a fan of Aldi's. I've learned that it is the place to go when you are wanting to fill the pantry. You will not see your typical brands that you do at the mainstream stores, but the quality of the brands sold at Aldi's will be the same quality.   Before I discovered this location, I was a regular at the Maplewood. That location filled my needs, but this location is like - WOW! The selection of merchandise is more vast, especially the produce and meats. It even has a larger variety of the non-food merchandise. I'm always amazed at the good buys I can find for my garden, kitchen gadgets or something for the tool box.   What also makes this location better then other Aldi's, is the lay-out. The aisles are wider and the coolers and cases for merchandising their products are newer. It makes a big difference in the presentation. Another big plus, is the friendly and fast cashiers.   I'll be back? - It's my Aldi of choice now.   When: May 17, 2019 Why: Weekly Grocery Shopping

I have to agree with, Kevin W.. All Aldi's are not the same. This Aldi's is way better then some of the other stores I have shopped. It's bigger, cleaner, merchandised better and seems to have a better selection of products.   When I receive the Monday sales fliers, I'll be honest, Aldi's is the first one I glance through. I then compare the prices of sale items to the other two major grocers in STL. Most times if they all have similar products on sale, Aldi will have the lower price. Especially on fruits and veggies and all the produce at Aldi is "organic".   Most of the brands you see on the shelves at Aldi's may not be the national brands you are familiar with, but the quality is equal and the prices are lower.   The staff is friendly and those working as cashiers, are fast and efficient.  This has become my favorite Aldi's and slowly is becoming one of my main grocery stores.   When: January 8, 2020 Why: Shopping with a friend and picking up items for myself.

They had me the moment I saw their Red Velvet Ice Cream. I quickly asked for a sample and it was a winner, so I ordered a scoop. The friendly associate asked me which topping I wanted and I said none. He was a champion salesman, informing me that my first topping was free. When I still said no thank you, he told me most people blend brownies with the RV. He even gave me a sample of the brownie to help me make up my mind. I gave in and enjoyed my Red Velvet Cake Ice Cream blended with a brownie.   For me Maggiemoo is better then Cold Stone. On a revisit, I blended white chocolate chips and for me that was a better topping then the brownie.   Also, keep in mind that Maggiemoo's offers  Yelp Deals.

Fresh Thyme is a great addition to the CWE. The other grocery stories in the neighborhood should be shaking in their boots, with this new kid in the hood.   I have always been a fan of the FT in Kirkwood and this one totally blows them away. The produce and meat departments were very impressive, they were making my inner chef want to buy one of everything.   The lay-out of the store flows well and the aisles are wide enough for a smooth flow of two-way traffic. I was also impressed with how they used end-caps on each of the aisles to feature and promote "local" products. Fresh Thyme may be a national chain, but they still care about the local vendors.   Be sure to also check out, Iron Drop Biscuits and Beyond. I'll just say, they are mind blowing for this ole farm boy.   Only thing that I saw as a negative, is no cashiers. It was all self check-out, which I am not a fan of, but it is the way of the future and I am learning to go with the flow.   When: November 10, 2021 Why: Grand Opening

Nothing attracts me faster to a big thick burger,  then the addition of Jalapeños. If you add Pepper Jack Cheese, my favorite cheese, you totally have a winner in my eyes.   Hardee's may be a fast food joint, but it has created a winner with its' new El Diablo Thick Burger. The couple, okay several El Diablo burgers I have had, have all been sit down restaurant quality. They not only serve it with sliced Jalapeños, but they add Cheesy Jalapeño Poppers as well. Double Jalapeños, now that is a winner. Then to really top it off, they use Pepper Jack Cheese, add bacon and a Fiery Habanero Sauce.  The customer service at this location at times is lacking and service may be slower then most fast food joints. However, I am able to overlook the poor service, when I am served a Jalapeño burger.

Beer! They've got it all, draft, bottled and can. They've got local, regional and out of state craft beers. They've even got the boring major brewery beers for those who like that type of brew.   To be honest, I accidentally found ITAP. I wasn't paying attention to the entrance as I was going to Epic Pizza. It was a Monday and when I pulled on Epic's door it was locked (they don't open till 5 PM). Not paying attention as I stated, I tried the door to the left and presto, I was in beer heaven.   Once the bartender explained to me that I was in a different biz, I was impressed with knowledge of beer. She answered questions and got us set up with a couple of chilled draft beers. Then she made my night, telling me Epic will deliver to us here at ITAP.   We enjoyed some beers on the side patio. Then we went next door ordered pizza and wings and continued to enjoy more beers on the patio. With or without the pizza, ITAP is a great place to enjoy a cold one.

Even being on a busy street like Bemiston in Clayton, I still enjoyed a relaxing lunch on their patio. The traffic was not loud or distracting and at lunch time there was enough shade to make it comfortable. If the weather is permitting, I'd highly recommend dining outside.   When at a wine bar, of course I had to have a glass of Pinot Grigio. Mine was; Stemmari. It's an Italian wine from Sicily. It was a perfect accompaniment to the Bronzed Mahi Mahi. It was served with Shrimp and top of a bed of Green French Lentils. It was a perfect healthy lunch and I'm glad that it was. Because, it made up for me cheating on my diet and enjoying the incredibly delicious Bruschetta & Tapenade basket.   My only disappointment was that after enjoying the bruschetta and Mahi Mahi, I was too full to enjoy their famous Bread Pudding for dessert. Oh, well that gives me another excuse to come back in the near future.

Great gift and souvenir shop on Decatur Street. It's larger, cleaner and more organized then some of the shops closer to Bourbon Street. I also, found the prices to be a little bit less expensive. So walk a little further and enjoy a cheaper price and larger selection of product.   They lured me in with a display that was close to the main street entrance. It was a couple of racks with dog related plaques and magnets. Being a Sheltie lover and having to find a gift for my pet sitter who also loves the breed, it was perfection.   The staff was friendly and personable. As I was being rung out, they asked about my dogs, which for me is like asking about my kids. You ask, I will gladly show you a picture or two.   Great selection, service and prices. I'd shop here again.   When: August 29, 2016 Why: Sheltie Merchandise

I'm going to make this one short, sweet and direct. When alcoholics dream, they dream of Total Wine & More. TWM has is all....if you want booze, they've got it. It you want it at a reasonable price, they've got that too.   Stocking up the bar for the holiday parties? Shop Total Wine & More.

Very friendly staff, they provide excellent customer service.  It is a very cute and comfortable shop. It's cozy like a neighborhood coffee shop be.   What attracted me to visit Park Avenue Coffee was the fact they were featured on the Food Network and won the best Gooey Butter Cake competition. Not sure who did the actual judging, but they made a bad call. I was not impressed, nor were my friends who I shared the original cake with. Other bakeries and grocery stores do a much better gooey butter then the one I got from PAC.   Visit PAC for the coffee, ambiance and good friends - not the GBC.

I thought for sure my experience was going to be dreadful, but it actually was fast and easy. First I went to the wrong office and it had a huge line. Luckily a cheerful and helpful lady came over and made sure everyone was in the "right" place. When I explained my situation, she informed me I just needed to go to the Collector of Revenue and they'd have my tax bill on file.   When I arrived, the line was short and only one person was ahead of me. When it was my turn, I told the young lady my story/problem. I had lost my personal property tax bill. Only thing I could figure out is that it fell into the recycling and got thrown out.  When I told my story she giggled, smiled and quickly printed me a new copy. Best thing, I didn't have to pay the penalty for being late. Now that is great custom service.

Books and a Beautiful Building, who can ask for anything more.   The Grand Hall is absolutely gorgeous and I enjoyed the displays of local history.  They had the bell from the KMOV-TV show Cookie & The Captain, which I got to ring when my Cub Scout Troop were the audience for one of the shows. Oh, the flashback of memories.   Great quiet spaces to study and do work projects, with an endless amount of references available at your fingertips. If you need a computer, they have that too.   If I lived downtown, I'd be a regular here and perhaps the Duke.

Best cookie trays in the area. I can go to a party and spot a Cose Doci cookie tray in an instant. They're beautifully presented and the cookies themselves burst in flavor. I just want to get a cup of coffee or a glass of milk and totally indulge myself.    If you need cookies for a party - this is the place and it is totally worth the drive to Ferguson. While there get yourself some rugelach and stash it away for yourself. It is so good it's not worth sharing.

What? That is the attitude I had when my co-worker told me she ordered the cake for our managers baby shower from Wal-Mart. I was even in more shock, when she told me she also ordered the tray of sandwiches from them. The shock went deeper, when she said it was from the Maplewood Commons location. I told her that location was on my "Terrible Two's" list on Yelp. See admitted it was a rough store, but assured me it would be okay.   She was right, they did a great job on the cake. I was surprised how flavorful it was and smooth and beautiful the icing was. The sandwiches were just average. In fact they forgot about them and didn't have them ready when she went to pick our order up. However, they quickly prepared them and discounted our order by 10%. In the rush, several of the dollar sized sandwiches missed the cheese. Oh well, at least they hustled and tried to make it right.   Congratulations Wal-Mart, I'm removing you from my Terrible Two's List.

Meet West County friends here for happy hour and it was a pleasant experience. However, I must say being in a strip center with multiple businesses, parking is a pain and we got there at 5 p.m..  Appetizers were half price till 6 p.m. which was a great deal. We had chicken wings, quesadilla and Black Angus Sliders. We also had an order of french fries and a Crispy Chicken Salad.  We were pleased with all the food.  The service was very good, the waitress was friendly and provided top notch service. I have been here several times before, the clientele has changed and it just doesn't have that festive fun feeling anymore. I'll come back, hopefully it was just a Tuesday crowd that wasn't in a party mind set.

When: February 25 Why: Late Night Dinner After Work  We've ordered a Chicago Original Deluxe a couple more times and have enjoyed each and every one.   This time I ordered the daily special off the kitchen calendar. Oh, guess I better explain "kitchen calendar" before I go further. It is a monthly calendar they place on top of your pizza box that has different special offerings each day. The night I ordered it was a two topping large pizza (St. Louis Style), a house salad (big enough for two) and an appetizer of your choice (we choose chicken wings) for $19.99.  Our pizza was sausage with pepperoni and it was damn good. This place I am learning, can do both Chicago and St. Louis very well   On one of our future orders we are trying Chicago Style with the sauce on top and our wings extremely hot.

21 custom colors of M&M's need I say more?  Multiple flavors of Jelly Belly's, including one of my favorites, Popcorn in bulk or pre wrapped. Wall full of unique and candies of days gone by. This place is what tooth fairies dream of. A heaven for those who truly have a sweet tooth.   This candy boutique is the perfect place for creating little gift bags full of candy treats for a child's birthday party or in my case a 60 year old. I was able to snag candies from yesteryear and create a gift bag that will have the memories flowing.   The customer service is cheerful and helpful. The young lady assisting me made me feel welcome and I could really tell she appreciated my business. I rarely need a place like this, but when I do Miss M's will be my destination.

It's been over a year, so it is time to do an update.  I am still a fan of their Chicago Style Pizza. I love the original Deluxe which has White Chicken Meat, Spinach, Bacon and Tomato. They give you the choice of sauce on top or bottom. We bounce back and forth, but usually go with bottom. Chicken and Spinach on a pizza to me makes it healthy. (lol)  Add a House Salad and you've got a meal for three or next days lunch for two.   Fast and friendly delivery.

If you join Louie's email club, you a free appetizer for your birthday. All you need to do is buy a small pizza and you can get one of their many tasty appetizers at no cost to you. You may have to buy something to get your gift, but I was happy with an order of Hot Chicken Wings as a gift. Combining a small pizza and the wings made for a perfect lunch as we did our house chores.    The staff here is friendly and when picking up my order, they always engage me in witty banter.

Great independent hardware store, with exceptional customer service. We're always greeted when we enter and when inquiring about a particular item, a sales associate always takes us directly to the item. On my last visit, I got distracted by a display (I'm fun to shop with)  and stopped following the associate.  He came back to  me with item in hand and closed the sale. The display also closed a sale, with the power of merchandising.   For a hardware store, they've got some great plants and accessories for the yard and garden.   I have stock in a big box hardware store and I shop here whenever I can.

We all see things differently - I find the VG staff to be friendly & outgoing. They listen to your likes and dislikes in wine and guide you to new & exciting experiences. As for the class on Thursday night, I found it to be informative. I found the talking patron to be rude. There are no excuses for bad behavior.  The "you'll impress...." comment, I found it to be a humorous opening. If she lost you after that comment, perhaps you're ADD. I have shopped multiple wine shops in the St Louis area and find this staff to be the most friendly and knowledgeable.  *This was my first Yelp Review

The Chicago was so good the other night, that we went back for the St. Louis Original Deluxe. How can you go wrong when your pizza is topped with the following:  Sausage, pepperoni, hamburger, bacon, chicken, anchovies, onion, mushroom, green pepper, black olive, green olive, tomato, jalapeno, pineapple, spinach and minced garlic.  As we were chowing down,  literally we both looked at each other and said, "this is the best pizza ever".  Yes we were extremely hungry, but still for a delivery pizza it was one of the "best".   Again, we ordered the House Salad as a side making it a complete meal.   Louie's is now a 5 Star pizza in my tummy.

I need to start traveling more, because I found the best luggage store in St. Louis. They have it all; day packs, back packs, duffel's and traditional suitcases.  In addition to fantastic suitcases, they have messenger bags and top of the line briefcases.   The Tumi store at Plaza Frontenac is crisp, clean and merchandised well. There is no clutter, each style and type are grouped together in focal groups. Their sales professionals provide excellent service, they listen to your needs and wants then guide you to an appropriate item in the store.   I've got my eye one two bags, so I guess I better plan a trip too.

Let's start out with some positive points:  1. I liked the movie I saw. 2. Great old theater and the architecture is incredible.  3. Good location, close to the true city and in a neighborhood that is alive      with activity. Which makes for a fun-filled day or date night.  4. Well maintained and I love the fact that all the movie poster on display have a St. Louis connection.  Now for the negatives:  1. Stale old popcorn and we were attending the first matinee of the day.  2. Prices were very high for a matinee show. 3. Young man selling tickets and working concession stand was not friendly. He was also wearing aviator sunglasses inside, I hope it was for a medical reason. If not, it was not cool. I like to have eye contact with the person I am conducting business with.   I've been spoiled by other art houses for film, but the Tivoli Theatre is a St. Louis tradition. I remember it when it was a single screen, so I will be back to give them another opportunity. One bad experience is not going to keep me away from a St Louis Landmark.

Pretty, oh so pretty, but not worth the price tag.   We're getting ready to redecorate our main seating room and are shopping for three matching club type chairs. Before shopping at Whole Foods, we thought we'd pop into Arhaus and see what they had to offer. We did see a couple chairs that we liked, but once we examined them closer, we were shocked at the poor construction of these chairs. They were wanting $1,000+ and when you gripped the arm rest, you could feel the wood frame. If I am going to pay over a thousand $ for a chair, I want to feel the padding that is going to give me comfort while I relax in my new chair.   The sales staff was friendly and helpful, I just was not impressed with the quality of the merchandise for the price of  they were asking.

My first visit was only appetizers and cocktails at the bar and I am already impressed. I was shocked to see their cocktail menu featured some classic cocktails; Manhattan and Old Fashioned. To my surprise, they were masterfully made and refreshing accompaniments to my appetizers.   I started out with Salt Cod Rangoon. They were not folded like a typical rangoon. These were rolled more like a cigar or fat cigarette. The flavor was intense - I actually liked it better then crab. My second app was the, Shu Mai Dumplings. It was a serving of four dumplings, perfect for two to share and almost enough for one to eat as a entree. They were delicious.   The service was attentive and friendly. Other reviews have commented on serving size and price point, I thought they were spot on. Prices were reasonable and the serving size matched the price point for the quality of food.   I'll be back? - Yes, I'm a fan of scallops and I want to try theirs.   When: May 23, 2018 Why: Dinner

It's a Walgreens, just like all other Walgreens. The only thing that sets this one apart from all the other Walgreens is that there is no customer service. More then once, we've been given the, "talk to the hand" gesture. There's another Walgreens in the next block and that is where you'll see my $'s spent.

We all know Cracker Barrel is good for breakfast and good  southern comfort food, but do you know what else they are good for?  Christmas decorations. Most of my Christmas ornaments, garland, tree topper and other holiday decorations came from CB. When guest are visiting and ask where I got my festive and unique decorations, they are shocked and amazed that they came from Cracker Barrel. The prices are affordable and they look as if they came from a pricey boutique.  So next time you are feasting at CB, stop in the Country Store and shop.

An historical train station in the heart of Kirkwood.  This station is well kept and staffed by energetic volunteers who assist Amtrak passengers who leave and arrive on four trains that pass through. This station gives you the true feeling of days gone by, so I highly recommend you stop by for at least a quick visit next time your shopping or dinning on the main drag in Kirkwood. It will give you something to talk about the next time you visit grandpa or grandma.   Keith D. was looking for Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye to show up and sing White Christmas. I was watching out for the Andrew Sisters, to sing Bugle Bugle Boy from Company B.

I am so glad that Treats Unleashed has opened a location in Creve Coeur. My fur-babies vet is in Creve Coeur, so this will be a great place to stop and reward them for being good little doggies while visiting the vet. Also, so many times I'm out running errands and stop at other TU locations and they never get to be with me, now it will be all about them.   In addition to the made in house treats, they offer an excellent variety of premium dog foods. They also offer a very fashion forward selection of dog collar and leashes and a multitude of toys.   As with all Treats Unleashed locations, they are always dog friendly and the staff is knowledgeable and friendly. This location is offering grooming as well.   My fur-babies are now looking forward to their next vet appointment.   When: April 19, 2016 Why: Shelby went to the vet

Total disappointment - it was the most flavorless breakfast I have ever had. How they can mess up fried eggs & hash browns is beyond me. Over easy eggs were over cooked and the hash browns under cooked. The bacon & sausage were done well. Our side of biscuits and gravy had no flavor. Thank God, salt and pepper were on the table. Service was friendly, but minimal. The server took our order and delivered the food, period. Which was sad, considering there were only three tables being served.

A testimonial update from the holiday purchase:  The  Ghost Pepper Powder is fantastic. We have made chili, taco soup and a couple other dishes with this spicy addition and each had their recipe improved with the addition of the powder.    Nothing beats a fresh ghost pepper, but when you don't have one handy, this is a great substitution.  Thanks, OTSS for making it available.

Oh, Happy Day. Murphy, my Fur-Baby is so excited about this new Treats Unleashed location.  His pet stylist is just around the corner (Little House of Dogs). So now he can come here and shop for treats after being groomed. I like the convenience, too.
