Murphy gets car sick, so he doesn't get to go for that many car rides, so this allows him to two outings in one.   I love that all the treats are freshly made in house and they offer a great variety of quality dog foods. Their offerings of toys, collars & leashes and other pet accessories are top notch.   The staff is always friendly, knowledgeable and when your dog is with you, they make them feel as if they're the best doggie in the world.   For those who are DYI folks, this location has a bathing/grooming room. Appointed very nicely.   Will I return? Yes, Murphy and I will be stopping by every time he is groomed.   When: July 18, 2017 Why: Shopping with Murphy

When: March 6 & 13 Why: Sunday Brunch  This is a great place to get a kick start to your Sunday. The service is always top notch. They have great Bloody Mary's, Mimosas and a specially created brunch drink by Chad the bar-master.   Then there is the food, the Eggs Benedict are by far the best in St. Louis. The hollandaise sauce, has an extra kick due to the whole grain mustard. You can make the Croque Madame a true breakfast delight by adding an egg to the top. Each Sunday they also have a special Quiche, I experienced; spinach, bacon, chicken and roasted potato. It was served with a side salad which made it a light fulfilling meal.   Let's talk potatoes, Brasserie does some great approaches; The Oven Roasted Red Potatoes are better then Hash Browns and I love me some Hash Browns. Then their fries/ frites, if a hamburger joint could only come close to matching the quality.

As their website says, "The White Rabbit - A Vintage Chic Boutique".    What a great boutique to find unique and original gifts. When you enter the store you know you have found a #shoplocal #shopsmall store that will help you finish your holiday shopping. I found so many amazing gifts for those hard to buy for cousins. There were vintage items, that took me back to our childhood memories and I cannot wait for them to open their gifts and have the same flashbacks as I did shopping.   I got a chuckle out of the candy jar for well behaved children. It's a shame they don't have one for well behaved adults as well.   Would I come back? Yes, when I need a unique gift that you can't find anywhere else.   When: December 11, 2016 Why: Gift Shopping #shoplocal

Ross is a weird version of TJ Max, Marshall's and Stein Mart. It actually reminded me of Marshall's in the old days. Their racks of clothes really had no organization, except for the fact that they were separated by size. The sales associate who assisted us informed us they get trucks daily, so since they didn't have what we wanted today to check back because the inventory and offering change daily. Wow, rocket science in the world of retail.   I didn't find anything to add to my closet, but they had some great offering on gadgets and gizmo's for my tool box. The housewares department was rather small, but offered some good bargains. They also had some great gift baskets with sweet and salty treats for the holiday gift exchange. Some of them were even labeled gluten free.  The employees were friendly, but the check out system moved rather slow.  Even though I found the store to be disorganized, I think I'll return. After all, they get trucks everyday which means it will be a new shopping experience.

Meet my first Yelp friend Norma here for Happy Hour. Having my first golf lesson later tonight (6Jun), I couldn't stay long, but I did make time for a Bubble Bath (Erin G. recommendation). A Bubble Bath is three glasses with 3oz pours of champagne. I love the place-mats that the pours are presented on, it makes for easy notes and knowing what to buy by the bottle when you fall in love with one as I did.   All three were incredibly good, but the NV "J" Brut Rose, took my breath away. If I didn't have a golf lesson, I could have stayed and nursed a bottle till it was gone.   The bartender Frank and the wait staff all dressed up in fun t-shirts were top notch. I will make sure my next visit does not need to be cut short due to a golf lesson, I want  to experience the true Robust.

The other day when I was driving to work, I noticed Hardee's had changed their marque. When I read "Fried Bologna Velvetta Biscuit," I threw my hands in the air and said, "Jesus take the wheel". He immediately took the wheel and guided thru the drive-thru to a magical box that asked me, "Do you want to try out new Fried Bologna and Velvetta Cheese Biscuit?" Instantly I said, "YES!"  This biscuit was a throw back to my childhood, when I use to enjoy a fried bologna with a Kraft American Cheese slice on Wonder bread sandwich. However, this version kicked it up a notch being on a Hardee's freshly made biscuit. As most of Hardee's featured items, this is not a healthy entree. It may not be healthy, but it will have you singing the Oscar Mayer song about your bologna.   If you are a fan of bologna, you've got to give this biscuit a try, at least once.

I can see clearly now, my eyes have been examined by Dr. Michael Antoine.   Sometimes the convenience of having a doctor of Optometry office attached to eye glasses boutique is to your advantage. Okay, calling Lenscrafter a eye glass boutique is a stretch, but still having the two next to each other is a big plus.   I finally found a pair of frames I liked at Lenscrafter and Nerea my sales associate was able to get me a walk in appointment with Antoine Eye Care. Extra bonus points, they took my vision insurance so it was no money out of pocket for me.   Dr. Antoine was friendly, explained each test and questioned my computer use to make sure he put me in the right lens. When it is time for the next eye exam, I will not procrastinate like I did this time. I will call Antoine Eye Care and get it done.

Hello Hardee's,    I am not sure if you have noticed the construction next to you where the old car wash use to be, but it's that little red headed girl named Wendy. If I were you, I'd be scared.  With another fast food burger joint right next door you need to improve your customer service.   I'm a fan of your Turkey Burgers, Tacos and Chicken Tenders, but your customer service is on the down slide.  My last couple of visits, the cashier and other front counter staff have been just down right rude. Then on my last visit,  I understood why. A Manager was assisting with the front counter passing out orders and he was equally as rude as his employees. I guess his staff was just following his lead.   I think your TV commercials are sexist, but you do put out a good "heart stopping" burger. Improve your customer service or I'll be getting baked potatoes, chili, frosty and a square burger from Wedny when she opens.

Great nonsmoking soccer bar. They offer a good beer selection which goes well with the food you can order next door at The Dam. If you're not a beer drinker, they're a  sports bar and will mix you up a simple bar drink too.   The ambiance is definitely soccer. This is the place to be seen watching a World Cup or any soccer game for that matter. Our bartender Matt, was friendly and attentive. He told us about the patio expansion which is going to be great for this coming spring and summer.   The Amsterdam has always been a great little bar and now with The Dam next door, it just got better.   When: 30 Jan 2014 Why: Enjoying a burger from The Dam

Every time my dogs go to the doggie spa up the street we have to stop here. Honest to God, the last time I was pressed for time and passed TU. My boy dog started to bark and he never barks when traveling. He was telling me, I missed the turn off for TU. I circled the block and we went to TU, so I could have peace at home. Murphy was a happy K-9.   My dogs are big fans of the soft bites. Their favorites are peanut butter or blueberry. They are so healthy and all the treats are baked in house. It cannot get any fresher then that.   For special occasions like birthdays or gotcha days, they can personalize a cake or cookie with your dogs name. At my house, we're happy with the ones that say, Princess or Prince. After all, my fur-babies are royalty, at least in my eyes.   The staff is always friendly and as I stated in my previous review, they always make your dog(s) feel welcomed and special.   Chances of returning: It's a guarantee when the dogs get groomed.  When: Every six weeks at least if not sooner.  Why: Treats of course.

Got a birthday dog in your family? If so, you need to come to TU and get them a special cookie. You can buy one of the generic Happy Birthdays or they'll personalize one for you. Today, I just went with a generic one, but I added some extra smaller cookies to make it extra special.   I also grabbed a couple of cookies for the Cardinals opening day.  Love the staff here, it is becoming my go to of all the TU's in the area.  Shop local!   I'll be back? - My dogs insist on it.   When: March 30, 2019 Why: Murphy's 7th birthday

We were at Deer Creek shopping at GFS and thought we should walk around to check out the other stores as well. We are so glad that we did, because we found some good bargains. Here at Ross Dress For Less, we found a pair of Nautica khaki shorts for $4.99. That is an insanely low price! That is yard sale or Goodwill pricing. You have to be patient and flip throughout the racks, but you can dress for less at Ross.

When I checked in my Yelp App today at the City of St. Louis Collector of Revenue office, it told me I had 4 check-ins and if I kept it up I could be a regular. Seriously? Who wants to be a regular or the Duke of an office that collects taxes? Visiting once a year is enough for me. I don't need to be a regular.   However, I will say this office is no way similar to the local DVM. The ladies that work here are polite, professional, friendly and fast. I was in out, in a flash. With the great service I'd be tempted to come back more often, but paying personal property tax and real estate tax once a year is enough for me.

This PAC may be off the beaten path, but you still get some of the best roasted coffee in the city. In fact you may not find it any fresher, since it is roasted right on site.  What I love about Park Avenue Coffee - The Hill:  Best Black Coffee in the city  Almond Milk is offered for Lattes  Yummy Gooey Butter Cake  Powered by Solar Energy  Earth friendly, they recycle and use reclaimed materials in their decor.   Frequent Buyers Club  Friendly Staff who provide top notch customer service  Need coffee and a relaxing place to work on the laptop? Skip Starbucks and find your way over to Park Avenue Coffee on Columbia Avenue.

It's always scary when you have to visit the "collector of revenue", but it doesn't need to be that way. These ladies have seen and heard it all. They could probably write an Emmy winning sitcom from all the bs they have heard from the citizens of the Lou.   What I thought was a major problem, was a speck in the whole picture. I didn't even have to write a check to correct my problem.

The envelope, please and the winner of best Fish Fry of Lent Season 2019 is, Edibles & Essentials. At least in my opinion it is.   Every Friday during Lent, E&E had their food truck, Essentially Fries parked out front serving up the absolute best fries and fried fish. With a food truck that specializes in fries, you already know the fries are going to be good. Well, let me tell you they can also fry up some crispy, flakey and flavorful fish. I had a lot of fish this Lent season and even though this was my last on Good Friday, it was also the best. I wish they'd do this at least once a month. If they did, I'd be here.   After ordering from the food truck and paying at the food truck, you could go inside and enjoy your meal. I enjoyed mine with a couple glasses of white wine.   The staff here is always so friendly and engaging. It may be order at the counter and take a table marker, but the service is still top notch and attentive.   I'll be back? - Absolutely!   When: April 19, 2019 Why: Lent - Good Friday - Fish Fry

I admit, I strayed away from Lucky's for awhile, but I am back now as a dedicated shopper.   Now that I am eating healthier, Lucky's produce department is becoming part of my new life. Especially on Wednesday when their sales brochures overlap. Their sales fliers always have good deals on veggies, fruits and great deals from the butcher case.    Shopping LM is similar to shopping at WF and Aldi's. You'll see brands that you haven't seen before at the local major grocers in town. However, once you have tried them, you'll realize they're basically the same quality. In some cases, better.   The staff is friendly. Those woking in produce and the meat departments have always been extremely helpful when I have had questions.   I'll be back? - Yep, give me those veggies   When: April 17, 2019 Why: Stocking up on fresh produce

I admit, I am a closeted Craver. It's not that I am embarrassed that I enjoy these steamed burgers cooked on a bed of onions and served on a steamed bun as well. It's just that some non-cravers just do not understand the love for these tiny burgers. After all, they were the first fast food hamburger back in 1921. OMG! in 6 years they'll be celebrating their centennial.   My favorite slider now is the Jalapeño. Instead of the regular American cheese, they top the beef patty with an American cheese flavored with pieces of Jalapeño. The mix of the grilled onions and the Jalapeño cheese, just makes the heartburn so much more enjoyable. The fries may be frozen, but they serve the crinkle cut, hot and crisp.   I'm glad that WC is a Coke restaurant and that they keep the fountain soda lines clean. I can personally tell the difference between freshly cleaned lines and those that have been neglected. A clean line, always makes the soda more refreshing.   The staff here is at times a little scattered brain, but I have never had a mistake in my order, I've just had a long wait.

Pointer's is a solid, A-OK above average fast order pizza joint. What makes it stand out from other fast-food pizza, is their New York style.   I was on my home from a Happy Hour in Clayton and needed dinner. As I drove down Big Bend, I started to crave pizza and Pointer's came to mind. My go to pizza toppings are sausage and jalapeño and that is what I ordered. They were not stingy with toppings and they do not use provel - win, win. My 12" pizza was enough for two meals.   The service at the counter was friendly and fast. I was surprised, just stopping and ordering my pizza had me in and out in 12 minutes. I'd recommend Pointer's over Domino's.   Will I return? - If in the area and I need a pizza.   When: October 19, 2017 Why: Dinner

I love me some Home Goods, but this location is not one of the better ones.  When I shop here, I am kinda lost and confused. The store lay-out and merchandising is totally different then my regular HG stores that I shop.   I can still find a treasure or two here when I shop, but the selection seems to be far less then what I typically find at the Kirkwood and Edwardsville stores.   Also, the staff is less engaging than the other stores.   I'll still frequent and shop this store when I'm in the area, but it's not one of my favorites. Hopefully I'll find a true treasurer some day and have exceptional service and I can raise their score.   When: August 7, 2021 Why: Accessories for the home.

I am not a fan of Indian food, but I was impressed here at Himalayan Hut. I came with a group of friends. Our little group meets monthly as, International Supper Club and they help me push my taste buds to explore and discover new things.   Even though we call it, "supper" club on this day we did a lunch. We came to HH for their lunch buffet. The spread was small, but had plenty of offerings for lunch. I'm not normally a buffet person, but all the food was fresh and at a good temperature. I liked it because, I was able to sample a variety of entrees and different sides. It was a great way to educate my taste buds about Indian cuisine.   The service was professional. Even with it being a buffet, they made sure we always had full water glasses and the baskets had plenty of pita bread.   I'll be back? - I actually think I will.   When: February 16, 2019 Why: Lunch with friends

Sweet EM's is just what Dogtown needed times two. Dogtown was in need of a coffee shop and a ice cream parlor and Sweet EM's gives them both all rolled into one cute little shop.   I discovered Sweet EM's while I was sitting in my car waiting for one of the frame shops to open. I was craving a coffee and was wishing Dogtown had a coffee shop. I finally saw someone crossing the intersection and then I saw them recross with a coffee in hand. I immediately jumped out of my car and went in the direction I had seen them go. To my surprise I found Sweet EM's.   I not only was impressed with my simple black coffee and muffin, but was also impressed with their curbside service during COVID. They were offering service through a walk-up window from the front sidewalk. The young lady working was perky and friendly.   Next time I have dinner in Dogtown, I'm definitely saving room for dessert. That way I can come here and try the ice cream.   Will I be back? - I scream for ice cream.   When - October 29, 2020 Why - Needed Coffee

What in the hell is going on? I have no excuse for why I haven't written a review for, The Bug Store. Honestly, it is one of my favorite stores to shop for the yard and unique fun gifts for friends and family. I even take out of town guest here for the experience.   All I can say is, if you haven't been, you've got to go now. You will find the most fabulous items for your home decor and garden. The staff is helpful and friendly making for a pleasant shopping experience.   Just a heads-up, they do not sell bugs.   When: Countless times Why: My garden and gifts

We went Saturday around 11 am, one of us had breakfast and the other did a lunch fare. Both were very good, with the lunch fare being the best. Don't get me wrong, the breakfast was still very good, the club sandwich was just better. The parking is plentiful, but beware of the senior drivers who pull-up to drop or pick-up their friends. Which is fine, I have no problem with that happening. However, while I was there they were lined up like they were waiting for valet parking, and we had to wait to back out of our parking space. It gave us a good chuckle, knowing that would proubly be us in the future. Recommend | Not helpful

I had been in STL partying with friends and just needed some finger food to munch on the drive home. So as I drove pass this WC, I pulled in and ordered my favorite, which is Combo #2. I also wanted a small order of onion rings, but they were sold out, so I tried the Mozzarella Sticks instead.   The Combo #2 is; two Double Cheese Sliders, fries and a drink. For my drink, I choose a Diet Coke. Having a diet soda balances out the calories and carbs from the combo meal. My burgers were hot and gooey, just like a slider should be. The fries (Crinkle Cut) were hot, as were the cheese sticks.   The young lady taking the order over the intercom and my money at the window was polite and efficient. I was through the drive-thru in nothing flat and back on the road to IL, with a tummy filling snack.   I rounded up for some charity, but I don't remember which one. I'm a sucker for round-ups.   When: August 4, 2021 Why: Snack for Road Trip - cutting the booze

I am totally a fan of Treats Unleashed and I love this CWE location. It is such a  convenient location. It is close to some of my favorite restaurants, making it easy for me to stop by a grab a few treats for my fur-babies.   As all locations, they have an amazing selection of freshly made in house treats. In addition, they have top quality dry and canned foods for K-9's. They also have a huge selection of plush toys, that can make any dog do the zoomies with excitement.   Staff is friendly, it's obvious they love dogs. It's also nice that this location offers grooming. Dogs need a spa day, too.   I'll be back? - When I dine in the area, I'll be there.   When: December 13, 2019 Why: Treats for my Fur-Babies.

I was attracted to this donut shop by all the raving 5 Star reviews.  Sorry to say, for me it's just an average donut shop that is no better then a donut from the QT.   The shop itself is cluttered, poorly organized and dingy. Everyone raved about the friendly staff, they must be off on Wednesday. The lady working this morning was surly and rather rude. There was no greeting and no thank-you. All she said, "What do you want?" and "That's 95¢"  I have too many donut shops near me to make the trek here for just an average donut and below average service. I'll pass on this donut shop, but for those who love it, I wish them well.   I'll be back? - No.   When: October 17, 2018 Why: Raving Reviews

This location use to be The Barking Lot and is now Little House of Dogs.  The original owner lost her battle against cancer, but some of the staff have kept the business going under a new name.   You are still going to receive the same high quality pet styling your had  under the TBL name. I wouldn't trust my three dogs to any other grooming shop. The entire staff here are truly pet people and pet professionals.   The building may be "little", but the service you receive is HUGE.

My love - hate relationship with this store continues. I was struggling finding various decretive items for this holiday season. The pandemic has everyone getting into the spirit of things and most stores are sold out. Not Home Goods, they had me checking everything off my list and I didn't even have to check it twice. I even found things that I didn't even know I needed.   This HG use to be practically in my backyard. Now that I have moved out of the city and state of Missouri, I miss my quick trips here to find little and big treasurers to make my house a home. Now, I need to plan my trips here, but they are still well worth the travel miles and time.   If you have a new home or need to give your current one a face lift. Shop here and you'll save dollars.   Will I return? - I can guarantee it.   When: December 15, 2020 Why: Christmas Decorations

My Shelties have been coming here for years and they'll continue to come here. It doesn't matter that I have moved to IL and it is now a 45 minuet drive. I like the quality of work they do and my dogs love Cathy, their stylist. The pricing of their grooming is also, very reasonable and affordable.   In addition to Cathy, the rest of the staff that I have encountered are friendly and it is obvious they love dogs. A good way to judge a grooming salon is by the way your dog acts arriving and leaving. My two are spoiled little daddies dogs, but the do not hesitate to go with Cathy with I drop them off.   I highly recommend, Little House of Dogs to anyone who lives in Kirkwood and an area close by. Or if you're like me and don't mind the drive, you'll be pleased that you made the trip.   Oh, I too still see my STL hair stylist, so I schedule our appointments on the same day. It's our spa day in the big city.

Another great shopping day at Costco.  Was out in West County running errands and picking up a special ordered item from another retailer and thought we'd swing by for some household staples that we were out of.   The Customer Service is always top notch. It is amazing how the staff keeps a positive attitude with the volume of shoppers they handle.

Some my say that Lafayette Park is the Red Headed step-child to Forest Park, but it is not. It is the petite and prettier little sister. It is also proof that size does not matter. It may be smaller, but it has all the amenities and beauty of FB without all the traffic congestion of the tourist attractions.   It is a great park to stroll before or after enjoying dinner at one of the many restaurants on Park Avenue. Also, it's a paradise for a photographer. That is why you see so many weddings being photographed within the well manicured grounds. I'd say don't stop with weddings, do your engagement, senior and family portraits as well. Heck, bring you camera or smartphone and take a couple of cool pictures of just the natural beauty and landscaping.   We are so lucky to have so many beautiful and well maintained parks in Saint Louis.  Get out and enjoy them today.

I'll admit my dogs are spoiled, very spoiled. They are my children and I take very good care of them.  I watch their diets very closely and would never feed them a dog food I could buy a grocery store. TU carries some of the best dog foods available, many of them are highly recommended by Whole Dog Journal.  The staff is very knowledgeable in all the foods and can recommend for your dog based on its health, age and size. However, lets not forget about the freshly baked treats, after all "treats" is in their name. My dogs love all flavors of the Soft Bites, and Peanut Butter Barkers too. (Next door is a Fannie Mae so you can get a treat for yourself.)

Kelly B has the right idea, "Get the bread" and she is right about loving it.  My advice is shop early, get fresh. Their bread is their best seller.   I've tried the Parsley, Dill and Rosemary and it made great sandwiches with turkey and bacon. Going back to try the Hot Pepper & Parmesan and gotta get me some Irish Soda Bread.   Tried the mini chocolate chip cookies and was disappointed. They looked so cute in the case, but lacked in flavor. I also tried a Red Velvet Cupcake, moist and good flavor. However, it's appearance was lacking. I think places like The Cup and Jilly's have spoiled us on cupcakes.   Parking can be a pain, but I just park at the empty business next door and walk over.   I want them to succeed, so I will be back for bread and promise to be open to trying other pastry items.

Love this place!! I have had a couple of lunches and Sunday Brunch and all have been excellent. The staff is extremely friendly and attentive. Their service makes you feel as if you are at a friends home.  Sunday Brunch is a bargain at it's price which includes your first Bloody Mary or Mimosa. A huge variety of food which makes it hard to decide where to start and when to say stop. The Nachos are better then any Mexican restaurant, the ribs are a notch above Pappy's  and the chicken wings are crispy and offer a different twist to the typical restaurant wing. Love the Patty Melt when offered as a daily special. My only nay, is the Cuban sandwich is a little over done and dry. Visit this place, you'll love it!

II am not sure if it was the prayers to the Shopping Cart Gods or if it was the coin I tossed into the Wishing Well, but Schnucks finally has gotten new shopping carts.   We shop like New Yorkers, only buying for one or two meals at a time. So those big bulky carts are way to big and those plastic hand held baskets are way to small. As Goldilocks would say, "These two tier small shopping carts are just right".   Thanks Schnucks for making my shopping experience easier and more enjoyable by offering a shopping cart that meets my needs.

If you are a knowledgeable wine drinker, do not shop here. This wine shop caters primarly  to inexperienced young women who are drawn to "cute labels" and no substance.  Their selection of quality wines is small and limited. You are better off shopping at another local wine store where your selection of "good" wines are a smorgasbord.  It's a shame that a prime location and presentation are wasted on such a selection of wines.

Big disappointment. I try to use local businesses and those near my home to keep our neighborhood strong. However, when I tried to purchase a full set of tires at Auto TIre their customer service went flat. I wanted to use AT, because I could walk back home & be productive. Who wants to sit in a tire store waiting area?  When I stopped by, they informed me they'd have to order my tires. That was no problem, I could come back easily. I told them my next day off and they assured me they'd have the tires. When I arrived on the scheduled date, a manager with the look of a deer in your headlights informed me he forgot to order my tires. Being a busy professional like most of us, I took my business elsewhere that day. They lost a $700 sale.  I do give them an extra star for being totally honest.

Three Monkeys has gotten three strikes and they are no longer a favorite place to visit. I do not know what has happened, but they need to fix it and fix it fast. The problem is not front of the house, they still have some of the friendliest and best service in town. The problem is in the kitchen, they are not up to the quality they once were. Did they change Executive Chefs? We  had a carry-out that was a BIG disappointment, during a birthday celebration with multiple friends we had entrees sent back and then the final was a Sunday Brunch that had us walking out saying, "WTF happened here?" Please fix the problem, I want to be a fan again.

I recently bought new accent tables for my living room, that had tops made with natural tile blocks. I loved the look they provided, but wanted to protect the tiles with glass tops. I knew I needed to protect those beautiful tiles from pesky cocktails rings.  Immediately I thought of Kirkwood Glass, because they had done a great job rehanging my huge bathroom mirror when it became detached from the wall. Ordering the table tops was easy and within a week they were ready for me to pick-up. Now I can entertain, serve cocktails and not worry about my beautiful titles being ruined.   Jocelyn at the store when I ordered my table tops and Adam who came out to my house to hang the mirror, both were extremely friendly and professional. If I ever need a windshield replaced, I will consider them for this service as well.

The Top Ten Reasons to Love Carl's Drive-In  10. Fries and Onion Rings from a bag. 9.  Soft Grilled Buns. 8.  Counter Seating Only - Small & Cozy 7.  Biodegradable China 6.  Prompt Service with Attitude 5.  Nostalgic Ambiance 4.  Milkshakes in only two flavors 3.  Foot long Hot Dogs 2.  House-made Root Beer in Frosted Mugs  And the number 1 Reason:  The Best Flat Grilled Burgers in Saint Louis!!!

Give me the keys to the bulldozer, I'll drive. This shopping mecca should have been leveled years ago. There is no reason to come here, unless you are a "mall walker".   How Sears survives is beyond me.   Amanda Z., I don't think Ikea could even bring this place back to life, it is dead.

It's not the New York store. It's not even like the Michigan Avenue store in Chicago. However,  we do have a Tiffany's  in St Louis and it lives up to the experience. The selection of sterling silver jewelry is classic & fashionable for both women and men. They offer a large variety of price points so everyone can find a bobble within their budget.  As for diamonds, you will not find more sparkle for your $. The sales professionals are truly professional. They'll educate you on the importance of the 4 C's. Bigger is not always better, you've got to take the color, clarity and cut into consideration.  Two other categories you need to check out are the pearls and watches. Every woman needs pearls & not Barbara Bush pearls. A classic single strand or a 60" strand that can be looped for a strong fashion statement.  As stated in my profile I'm a watchaholic and love my two Tiffany watches. Everyone deserves a gift in a Blue Box.

I have boosted before that Pint Size Bakery has the best scones in Saint Louis and this morning they once again proved me right.  My savory scone this morning was Sweet Potato Bacon, what a winning combination. Then the sweet scone made me weak in knees it was so good. The apple and caramel made me feel like I was eating a slice of apple pie for breakfast. Both were so good, they made me wish I were not sharing them and had the entire scone to myself.   If you have not experienced Pint Size Bakery yet, you need to get yourself there now and try their scones. You can also try their; cookies, brownies, muffins, cupcakes and more. Whatever you enjoy, you'll be back for more.

I have always loved this bookstore, the selection is overwhelming. I love the fact that they open at 11 AM. on Sunday. It makes for a great shopping experience after breakfast. You'll always find a good read for a lazy afternoon.   I think one of my good traits is that when I'm dumb, I can openly admit it. In fact, sometimes it gives me a good laugh and that happened Sunday when I visited Left Bank Books. I had no idea there was an entire lower level of used books. I was amazed at the variety of selection and quantity. Next time I'm in a store and see a staircase, I'm taking the adventure and following the steps to see where they lead me.   Cat allergy alert - they have a house cat who is very friendly and loving.

I can get spoiled shopping @ Culinaria. Downtown dwellers have it so good. If I lived closer, this would be my grocer of choice.   I work downtown, so this is a great place to pick-up lunch/dinner from their prepared foods section. I love the way the staff sell and describe the daily offerings. They do it as if they were waiters at a trendy cafe.   I've also gone in and picked up some non-perishable items on my lunch hour and have drooled over the extra selection of items available to the Culinaria stores. It still isn't Whole Foods, but damn close.   The staff is friendly, almost beyond believable. They must have selected the best of all their stores and transfered them to this location.

Lee's may be a chain, but they offer up some good friend chicken. My favorite is their crispy and I always order the Breast Meal. It includes one very large breast, with a biscuit and as my sides  I choose mashed potatoes with brown gravy (they give you a choice here) and cole slaw.  For a beverage,  I always go with their Sweet Iced Tea. It is done in a true Southern style.   My advice to you is do not turn your nose up at Lee's because it is a chain. Give them a chance, they do chicken right. This location is always extremely clean and the staff is courteous and friendly.  I never do fried chicken at home, it is the one meal I always let someone else make.

I love my watches from Tiffany's and it was time for one of them to get a new battery. Taking your watch in for maintenance can be dangerous, because it gives you time to browse and browsing can lead to shopping. This time I discovered some new crystal pieces that I want personally and others that will be great for upcoming weddings. A Blue Tiffany Box with that White Tiffany Bow on a bridal gift table, makes a statement and gets noticed by all.   Besides weddings, I also use Tiffany's for baby gifts. Why not help your friends child be born with that silver spoon. I also help them start saving for their first Tiffany purchase with a bone china piggy bank in blue or pink.   My watch is being sent to the mother ship in New York, to have it's battery changed and to be cleaned as well. When it comes back to the Lou, I'll be able to do some more browsing and shopping when I go to pick it up.   The customer service and sales professionals here are always top notch. They are the high standards which you'd expect from the brand Tiffany's.

Fresh, warm, soft and delicious. Better yet, they'll deliver these scrumptious cookies to your work or residence. Reward your staff for a job well done, or chase the blues away at home with a box (eco-friendly) of these insanely delicious cookies.   Their traditional flavors; Chocolate Chunk, M&M, Sugar and Peanut Butter Chip are only the beginning. More traditional flavors like, White Chocolate Macadamia Nut and Oatmeal Raisin will have you coming back for more. Do I dare tell you about my favorite Deluxe Flavor - Chocolate Peanut Butter Cup? Give me a gallon of milk and a dozen of these and I'll be doing a happy dance.   Great location on Washington, but you're to close to my work - be gone satan. However, I do love you. It guess without saying, I'll be back and so will all of my co-workers. Customer service has always been spot on, glad I didn't have the trouble Kate did.   When: November 25, 2016 Why: I am a Cookie Monster

Oysters, mussels and wine make for a perfect evening. Add fabulous ambiance and attentive service, you've created DeMun Oyster Bar. It is the perfect place for a romantic evening of two or a fun place for a group of friends. Our recent visit was the latter, a group of friends and we had a blast. Our server was so attentive to our needs, he made each of feel as if we were royalty.   Words can not begin to explain how luscious our food was. After 3 different oysters, I would be hard pressed to say which one was my favorite. I might even have to say, I liked the steamed mussels or poached salmon better. Not to mention the Pomme Frites and the Sweet Chips we munched on as well. Oh, I can not forget the Beignets we used to soak up the incredible broth from the steamed mussels.  It was a night to remember, even after three bottles of wine.   If you're an Oyster lover, treat yourself soon to the magic of DeMun Oyster Bar.

I've always been a fan of TU, as stated in my previous review. They carry the best of the premium dog foods and this weekend they saved my ass. I shop local and try to support businesses within my "hood".  However, my usual dog food store got shorted on my brand and size and I was disparate. I quickly called TU and they had Now Senior in stock and I was a happy dog daddy.   When I arrived, it was great to see they held my bag behind the counter. My dogs not only got the premium food they enjoy, but bags of wheat free treats as well. If your dog has wheat allergies, come here for treats.   The customer service is always great, they're friendly and true dog lovers.

Major Kudos to Schnucks for being Proactive and having their store appropriately staffed for all the snow storm shoppers. I was shocked to see every check out lane open and each one had their own bagger. The check out process was smooth, easy and the cashiers kept a positive attitude. Which was amazing, lines for each check out wined down the closest aisle of items.   Also, a big shout out to my fellow city residents. You were all in good spirits, you were not fighting over something meaningless or being bitchy about the approaching storm.   This is my closest Schnucks to home and I'll admit at times I get frustrated with them, but today you had an A-Game.  Today I would have given them a 5 star if they still had rock salt while I was shopping. Shame they had to lose a star over salt.

Congratulations Autotire, you are off my Terrible Two's List.   One of the tires on my roommates CRV kept needing air added to it. When adding air the last time he noticed the culprit, a nail. He was adding air at U Gas, so he just drove over to Autotire which is close to our home.   The current staff was friendly and professional. Living close, he just dropped the car off to have the tire patched. They called later, to let him know the nail was too close to the sidewall to be patched. He bought a new tire and got an alignment. With the alignment, he claims his ride is riding better then when he bought it.   Thanks, Floyd and Bill for the good customer service and making my Terrible Two's List shorter.   When: 13 JAN 2014 Why: Fix a flat tire

This place is a friends favorite restaurant so we took her there for a birthday celebration - a group of ten. The service was great, they made her and our group feel special. However, I can not say the same for the food. Every entree was poorly presented and looked bland. The rest of us chatted after the dinner, except for the honoree, no one in our group was impressed.
Flavorless BBQ and the meat was dried out. I've given them two tries and both times were a total disappointment. No need for the third strike, I'm done.

FREE Wi-Fi is available at Diner's Delight and that is the most positive point about this diner. With the majority of the reviews on Yelp being 5 Stars, I was expecting to be blown away with some down home cooking. Instead, I was served food that made me wish I was bulimic.  All the food was overcooked and flavorless. Yet it left a horrible aftertaste in my mouth. I couldn't get home fast enough to brush my teeth to rid myself of the terrible taste in my mouth.   We had two Chicken Dinners with two sides, two ice teas and 1 Peach Cobbler with Ice Cream. Total cost of lunch $27 with tip. No alcohol, poor service and bad food. I think I've been robbed. I would not recommend this place to a homeless person.

Who knew shipping could be so easy? I sure in the hell didn't.   I have U-Verse for my TV service and love it. When doing a major redecorating of one of our rooms we decided to eliminate a television from our service. Three TV's for a household of two and three dogs seemed to be a little obsessive.   I was instructed to take the third receiver and the power cord to a UPS Store, along with my account number. Being anal retentive, I typed up a form with my account number, the serial number of the receiver and my confirmation number of downgrading my service. I thought I was being a good boy scout and being prepared. When I arrived to the UPS Store, the associate tossed it aside, asked me a few questions and presto a better form was printed out for my return. It was so easy peasy.   The staff was friendly, professional and if I need to ship anything in the future, I will return

I just discovered Gelato Di Riso and I am already a fan. I love their Salted Caramel.  I also tried their Cherry ____(drawing a blank) and it was rich and creamy. I was almost tempted to order it, but I love Caramel too much. I also tried the BF's Tiramisu and it was tasty too.   I will be coming to Gelato Di Riso and buying Gelato by the pint and quart in the future. I'm sure I'll be enjoying a cone on the drive home. Why it took me so long to discover this cute little Gelato shop on The Hill is beyond me.

Cheap, Cheap, Pizza, Pizza.  Can not beat the price. This was my first experience of Little Caesars and we tried the Deep Dish with pepperoni. The sauce was flavorful, they topped it with plenty of pepperoni and cheese. I know it was deep dish, but it was still too much dough for me. Next time we'll save $3 and order the regular pizza.   We also tried their chicken wings, the pieces were kind of small, but the flavor big for the price. They offer 7 different flavors, we choose traditional "spicy".   When funds are low, or you're in a hurry Little Caesars can provide you a quick good meal for the price.

White Castle to the rescue.   Sometimes when you're out having a good time and you drink too much, you need a good ole belly bomber. Yes, the best treatment for over drinking is a combo meal from White Castle.   My go to combo is the #2. It includes, two double cheese, a small french fry and a small soda. I just love the double cheese, especially with the jalapeño cheese. Also, I'm a big fan of crinkle cut fries. They may come  from a frozen bag at WC, but they're always crisp and satisfying.  If the dining room is open, I always go inside. I am not a fan of drive-thru's at any fast food establishment. The staff here was friendly. I was shocked at the amount of plexiglass that they were secured behind. At least WC has their safety in mind. Even with a barrier of plexi between us, the service was warm and personable.   I'll be back? - If in the area and hit by "the crave" I'll stop by.   When: January 5, 2018 Why: Drank too much

I live close to this Schnucks and want it to be my favorite grocer, but it just misses the mark. I do shop here a lot because of the closeness, but they need to improve the two most important departments.  Those would be produce and meats, they are just average compared to other grocery stores  near The Hill. Please work on improving these areas, I can not be loyal to a grocer based on canned and frozen goods.   The staff is great, they are friendly and extremely helpful while you are shopping.

Impressive Quik Trip.   I stopped by in the early AM and could not believe how busy it was. I needed gas and almost pump was in use. After filling my tank, I pulled forward and parked to go inside for some lunch supplies at work. Again, I was shocked at how busy it was. I grabbed my Gold Peak Ice Tea, a donut and a bag of chips. I was tempted to get something from their kitchen that prepares food fresh. May-be next time.   When I went to pay, there was only one cashier and the line was long. I took my place at the end and was impressed how fast the young lady checked everyone out. She worked that line and quality customer service did not suffer. She still talked to her regulars and thanked everyone for their business. QT needs to promote her to corporate training.   I'll be back? - It's close to my work exit/entrance on 255.   When: August 12, 2019 Why: Down to Two Bars on the Gas Gage

After being introduced to a St. Paul Sandwich while attending a UYE, I am now trying to experience them at my regular Chinese restaurants. Fortune Express did not disappoint me, it does a St. Paul as well as it does the rest of their menu. I never thought I'd see the day that I would enjoy a sandwich placed between two slices of Wonder Bread.   Egg Drop Soup, a St. Paul Sandwich (chicken) and an Egg Roll makes a nice little lunch.

This is a great little park/garden that honors Robert Pershing Wadlow, who is known as  "The Gentle Giant".  Other names he has be known to be called, are Alton Giant and Giant of Illinois. He was born in Alton, IL Feb. 22, 1918 and passed away at an early age of 22 on July 15, 1940. When he died he was an amazing 8' 11.1" tall and weighed an astounding 485 lbs.  He achieved this great height due to hypertrophy of his pituitary gland which results in an abnormally high level of human growth hormone.   In the park you will find a life size statue of Robert and also a life size statue of a  chair that was made especially for his large size. Next time you are in Alton, watching the eagles, passing through to Grafton or getting your drink on at Fast Eddies, stop by the park it only needs to be a short visit.  Then you can stand next to The Gentle Giants statue and just see how small of a man you really are. Then have a seat in his big chair for a good chuckle.  Best of all it is "free".

Jessica C. has called this one out right. This is by far the best Costco in the St. Louis area.   The selection here is superior to the other locations. When they say, "location, location, location"  makes a difference I guess it helps to be located in West County.  They have products and brands you will not find at the other two locations.   I will drive the extra miles to shop here and I'll miss my Culver's lunch which was a treat when I shopped the South County location.

The service is friendly and fast.   The food was fast Mexican food fast.   Our beers and margaritas were ice cold. I'm fond on traditional margaritas, but my cousin had a mango one that was fantastic.   She also, had the best entree which was grilled shrimp and fresh vegetables (forget the name on the menu).   Atmosphere, drinks, good customer service and above average Mexican food make this a good place for an inexpensive meal.

Friendly staff gets them 3 Stars, the weak coffee gets them a  2.   I ordered Buddy The Elf Mocha and it was the most flavorless and bland coffee drink I have ever drank. How can an espresso drink with steamed milk, dark chocolate sauce and maple spice syrup topped with whipping cream have no flavor? Not one of those flavors came through the entire drink. They either forgot to add ingredients, or they were using old stale ingredients.   There are many other places to get a latte or mocha on Manchester, so I suggest you stroll up or down the road and get your caffeine fix elsewhere.

Great little neighborhood liquor store. As stated by Kelly B, the store has no merchandising sense, but the inventory is unbelievable and they know where everything is located.   I got turned on to this place a few years ago when I was searching for the new Espresso Vodka by Van Gogh. None of the major booze retailers had it, but would order it and I'd have to wait several days. HHL had it in stock and gave me instant gratification. They may be small, cluttered and a little dusty, but they are cutting edge and have always provided me with good service and good prices.   CJ H. get serious, when you are buying booze at a liquor store at 10:30 am with the wino's you kinda gotta expect bad behavior. Unfortunately  when you shop at Arena or Randall's you'll see the same thing and the owners are helpless. It's sad, but true. Next time call the police and file a complaint of a flasher.

When I crave Chinese (Carryout), Fortune Express will now be my destination. I have been favoring the other Chinese restaurant east of Hampton on Chippewa and needed a change. I am so glad we used the coupon that came in the mail.   Our dinner menu included; Crab Rangoon, Egg Rolls, Chicken with Broccoli, Kung Pao Chicken, Ham Fried Rice and Egg Drop Soup.   The Crab Rangoon and Egg Rolls were great. I was impressed that they were not over deep fried as many places do. My broccoli was crisp, not limp and wimpy. Seasoning in both main entrees, were spot on.  Egg Drop Soup was flavorful and one of the best EDS I have had.   Yes, I will be back.

Great neighborhood bar. They live up to their name and offer some great martini's. I love  a good dirty martini.   Their bar menu is typical, I've enjoyed a couple of the St. Louis style pizzas that were impressive. Yes they have provel on them, but you're in St. Louis deal with it and enjoy a slice.   I gotta get back and enjoy a breakfast and trivia night.

You've heard of the "Never Ending Story", well Dunaway Books is the never ending bookstore. There are bookcases after bookcases on the first floor and mezzanine. As if that weren't enough for you to browse through, the basement is full of more treasured reads.   Each bookcase or section is plainly labeled to make your search easy. They also have little maps like at an amusement park stating, "you are here" and showing you where you need to go for the type of book you have on your shopping list.   When shopping most used bookstores, they feel musty and dusty to me, but not here at Dunaway. It is well organized and very well kept. The salesman with his British accent made me feel like I was in an old 40's black and white movie and he was the shopkeeper.   I didn't find the two books I was searching for, but this place impressed me just the same and I am now a fan. I recommend this bookstore to any avid reader aka bookworm. It will totally give them a readers orgasm if there is such a thing.

That perky little red head Wendy is back in town and she is totally changing the game of fast food burgers. She is giving you an upscale contemporary dining room with fireplace, flat screen TV, high tech coke machine and a bakery case equal to Starbucks.  I've never seen a fast food restaurant look this good.   Her Value Menu can not be beat, all the items are 99¢. For a small lunch or late night snack you can not go wrong. When the burger urge hits, I now know where I will be going. In addition to the square burger, I'll be enjoying a cup of chili and Frosty. To my surprise Frosty is now available in vanilla. I remember the early days of Wendy when it's only flavor was chocolate.   The staff is friendly and I hope they can keep the positive attitudes beyond their Grand Opening.

Great neighborhood nursery.   They offer a good selection of perennials and shrubs. All of my hanging baskets come from here each year and they survive the entire season.   Their staff is very knowledgeable. When I bought plants at a competitor and they got sick, the staff still coached me into saving my plant.   Best prices on stepping stones and garden statues.

Definitely the best of our three Whole Foods stores. The salad and hot food bars are going to be a big draw for the employees of the Barnes and Cortex campuses. It is easily accessible from all areas of the CWE and the parking garage eliminates the nightmares of the parking lot at the Brentwood store.   This location has the same high quality meat and seafood departments as the other locations. The produce selection outshines any of the other grocery stores within the CWE neighborhood as well. It's obvious they took the width of the aisle into consideration when designing this store. They are much wider and easier to navigate with shopping carts.   As with all WF stores, the staff is eager to offer friendly and professional assistance.   Whole Foods is a great addition to the Central West End. My future shopping trips to WF will be done here.   When: May 25, 2016 Why: Grand Opening

Great store!  I discovered Batteries Plus earlier this year out in Creve Coeur and immediately look for one closer to home. I love the fact that they recycle batteries and light bulbs for you. Which helps protect our environment, something to keep in mind as Earth Day approaches.   This store is older then the West County store, but that gives it some rustic charm. However, the customer service is the same having a knowledgeable and friendly staff.   This is my store of choice for batteries and light bulbs.

Five Below is a fun store and gives new meaning to the $ store. Instead of everything being a dollar, it can be any dollar amount up to 5.   It is a great store to shop for things you really do not need or want at bargain prices.  If you've got a young child to buy for, this is a fun store. We grabbed a couple of goodies for the little girl next door and she loved it.   They've got travel size toiletries, school supplies, DVDs, toys, hair accessories and so much more. If you are on budget, Five Below may be able to help you stretch those $'s.

If you are on, The Hill and need a cup of Joe to keep you going or to start your day, Shaw's is the place to go. They are by far the absolute best coffee shop on The Hill. I myself have been known to stop by for an iced coffee, just simply because I am in the neighborhood.   They've been serving, The Hill and STL community for over 20 years. What I like best is that they do their own roasting and do it multiple times during the week so the coffee is always super fresh.   The Baristas also help with the weekly roasting, so they have a true love and knowledge of the coffee bean. A good barista is like a good bartender, so be sure to tip accordingly.   When: March 5, 2021 Why: A morning cup of coffee.

If I could turn back time, if I could turn back time If I could turn back time, oh baby -  I'd be setting at the bar at Tick Tock Tavern, having a drink with you And munching on a Hot Dog from Steve's next door  TTT is a dive bar that is stuck in a time warp, with class. The drinks are good, strong and cheap. Not only is the staff friendly, they're eager to know your name and make you feel like a regular. Each of the bartenders introduced themselves to us and asked us our names. I found that to be a real nice personalized touch.   A bonus to TTT, is the fact that a side door inside connects the dive bar to Steve's Hot Dogs new location. This is a perfect set up. You can slam down a couple of beers, order hot dogs from Steve and watch your favorite home town sports team on TV. What really kicks ass is the staff from Steve's will bring it over to you when its ready.  Tick Tock Tavern, you're my new favorite dive bar.

Cute and simple cafe. Not only do they offer hand brewed coffee, but you can get a shrub cocktail or a mimosa to start your day.   I was impressed with the pour over, Chemex preparation of my coffee. They use Perc Coffee which is out of Savannah, GA. It's a decent coffee, but with all the great coffee roaster here in STL, I wish they supported another local business.   As of now, the pastry offering are minimal. However, I must say they are very good. I was surprised to find out they are done in house. I devoured a Spinach & Feta Croissant and thought it was from a popular French bakery out in West County. It was that good.   The only negative I will comment on, is the service. The staff was not friendly or engaging.  In fact as I watched them during my visit, they hardly smiled. They almost were robot like.  Smile, engage and encourage me to return. It's a great place, if they kick up the customer service.   Will I return? - Yes, I'll give them another try.   When: November 2, 2017 Why: Morning Coffee

I've been shopping here for 4 years and can say, the service has consistently been top notch.  The staff may have changed time to time, but the friendliness and professionalism has always been the same. Light bulbs and batteries aren't like they use to be, they are getting more and more specialized and at times you need guidance to make sure you are making the right purchase.   Being an avid recycler, I do recycle everything that I possibly can. I've been a recycler since, the first Earth Day back in the 1970's. As stated in my previous review, recycling is one of the services they provide here at Batteries Plus Bulbs. When you come in to purchase your new bulbs, you can drop off the old ones and they'll make sure they are disposed of properly, so our environment is protected.   I said it before, this is my store of choice for batteries and light bulbs. They're items that I don't need that often, but when I do - this is my store.   When: September 23, 2016 Why: Batteries and Bulbs

I was craving cheap Chinese for lunch, so I headed over to Fortune Express. It was a simple lunch, I went with a Half Order of Beef Fried RIce, a single Eggroll and an order of Crab Rangoon.   As always, I had to have an Egg Roll with my Chinese food. FE does a good ER, so my craving was satisfied. I was also craving some Crab Rangoon. I know it really isn't Chinese, but it's American Chinese and when you're hungry, it's okay. However, today it wasn't okay and that is why I need to take a star away from Fortune Express. The pockets holding the filling, barely had anything in them. I was so disappointed.  My main dish, the Beef Fried RIce was excellent. It had plenty of beef and a half order was more then enough. With the two appetizers, I could only eat half of the half order.   It's a small family business, so the service is friendly and personable.   Would I return? - When I have a craving.   When: July 24, 2019 Why: Craving inexpensive Chinese

Sometimes I am attracted to a business by a rant rather then a rave and that was the case with Everest Cafe. After my visit I could not find anything to rant about, all I found was things to rave about.   I will start out with their customer service, it was friendly and full of true hospitality. As our large group of 14 were dining, they made sure each diner felt like a VIP.   My meal begun with Miso Soup which had organic spinach and was by far the best Miso Soup I have ever had. I followed it up with Lamb Tarkari with Organic Vegetables.  It was so nice to see that the vegetables they serve are all organic.   I gotta get back and try their lunch buffet. I heard it is better then their dinner and their dinner was totally satisfying.

Since my last review, I have now moved on to the east side of the river and this Friar Tuck is now the closest, "Big box" liquor store to my new home.  Since I now live on this side of the river, Friar Tuck is satisfying one of my vices by keeping me stocked with craft beers and whiskey.  On my recent visit, I was searching for mini bottles. I needed them for swag bags for a party I hosting. To my surprise they had an over-whelming selection. To my disappointment, they  did not have the quantity I needed in the brand I choose. However, the sales associate checked the back stock and provided top notch service. She even gave me a lead of where I might find what I was looking for.   Don't worry, she did not lose a sale. I still bought some craft beer and a couple of canned cocktails. The sale was just smaller and I am sure future sales will make up for the shortage on this visit. After all, the holidays are approaching.   When: October 20, 2021 Why: Shopping for mini bottles

Steve nailed it with this new location in Tower Grove. Locating next door to a dive bar like Tick Tock Tavern was a smart move.  Having them connected by a secret hallway, is the true winner. The hallway is not a secret, we all know it is there. If you don't, you are missing out on some good hot dogs to enjoy with your beer or cocktail.   I enjoy your Hot Dogs Steve, but I just cannot get into your buns. I understand they're your creation with Vitales Bakery, but they are just too chewy for my taste. However, it's your dogs that are the star. Your toppings are plentiful and some of your combinations are creative, unusual and totally out of this world. I had wieners in my mac-n-cheese as a child and I love bacon as an adult. Now I can chow down with those toppings on one of your hot dogs.   Cute little shop with great service. Delivering next door to Tick Tock Tavern is excellent customer service. I just wish I liked your buns (it cost you a star), but I'll get over it because your dogs are so good.

I do not know what possessed me, but one day I returned here and gave them another try for breakfast and was pleasantly surprised.  The Sausage, Egg and Cheese on a bun was actually enjoyable and no heartburn after wards.  Not a fan of the tater tots/hash browns, so when I want a side I just order the regular fries.   The staff is friendly and always have a positive attitude which is good to see at a fast food business.   Like Dunkin Donuts, I am becoming a fan of their open your eyes dark coffee. Wish they offered it in Keurig K Cups for a quick cup at home.

I loved this store when I lived in STL. My hood was Lindenwood Park, which is close to the South Hampton area. Being that close, made it easy to shop at Southside Hardware.   When I was preparing my house for sale and getting the occupancy permit, the inspector had me get new fire and carbon dioxide alarms. Mine were connected to my alarm system and if the purchaser did not continue the service, they did not have alarms. Really didn't want the expense, but I understood.   So off I went to Southside Hardware and as with any visit here, as soon as I entered an associate asked me what I was looking for. I explained my needs and he showed me what he had in stock. I was able to get 3 smoke detectors and also one combination with carbon dioxide. I was in and out of the store within 10 minutes, top customer service.   Gotta love a mom and pop shop. The customer service is so much better then that of a big-box store.   When: October 8, 2020 Why: Smoke Alarms

It is that time of year when some folks get excited about all the local Friday Fish Fry's.  The only sad thing is, they are only on Fridays and at selected churches. During this same time of the year, White Castle brings back their Clam Strips and they're available everyday. These Clam Strips are equally as good as those you'd get at Captain D's or Long John Silver's. Pair them up with a side of Crinkle Cut Fries and a soda and you've made the perfect "fish" lunch or dinner during Lent. They offer them in three sizes, to fulfill the various hunger levels.

What was I thinking? I wasn't thinking is the problem. You must have a stomach of steel to eat here.   It was early morning (5:30 AM), I'm on my way to work and I need breakfast. Normally I stop at the QT or McDonald's, but this morning I just wasn't feeling their love and wanted something different. Boy did I get something different.   I over shoot my work location searching for a new experience and saw WC. Knowing that they had added breakfast sandwiches to their menu, I gave them a try. I ordered a Sausage with Egg & Cheese and one with Bacon. I had the same side effects that their sliders give me when I'm sober, HEARTBURN.  I swear the only time to eat WC is when you are F***ing drunk.  I will say, the coffee was eye opening and the service was extremely friendly for that early in the morning. I have now stocked my locker at work with breakfast items I can prepare in the microwave for the mornings when I'm just not loving QT or McDonald's.

This place has decent Chinese food at reasonable to cheap prices.  The location has been multiple places and was most recently a vegetarian Indian establishment.  You can easily drive past this restaurant and not even notice it.  There has only been one person working the front of house during all my visits and it hasn't ever been crowded during lunch so this has been a quick lunch spot.  It's a pretty bare bones and basic place without a lot of atmosphere but that seems to be reflected in their affordable prices.

Ahhh it is ok but nowhere near the ambiance of Cafe du Monde.  I've never seen this place crowded so you do get super fast service.  I really don't care for beignets but they have those here too and it is all very similar to Cafe du Monde EXCEPT they also have a decent small menu of some New Orleans classic dishes so I would say the dining options here are far superior to Cafe du Monde (but a terrible location in a strip mall).

This is a small bar with a large gangster theme.  I really like the tommy gun decor but I wish they offered it with some bullets and a range to go along with it.  This is a nice spot to grab a quick drink right off Bourbon Street when you are on your way to or from dinner or some other activity in the Quarter.  I've never seen it unpleasantly crowded here so it seems to be a reliable spot to have an enjoyable experience with breathing room and a sound level appropriate to have a proper conversation.

It is connected to the original Galatoire's and so in some ways this is sort of just extra space for the original restaurant but they do offer a different menu.  The steak is good and the service is professional.  The downstairs bar here is large and comfortable so it might be a good place to drink if the upstairs bar at original Galatoire's is full.  Generally I would prefer dining in the original Galatorie's but if it was full I wouldn't mind eating here again.  You can also access Galatorie's 33 from the upstairs bar at Galatorie's.  The dress code here is more relaxed than the original so if you find yourself in a more business casual mood then this might be a better choice than the original Galatorie's.

This is a spacious place for watching live music and other NOLA events (I also usually end up here for MOM's Halloween Ball most years).  The bar has developed a clever system of using number cards that you have to show when you run a tab as it can get very loud when music is playing so that makes it easier to get your order in.  I've always had great service and the crowd has always been interesting.  They have adequate bathroom faculties for men but I've seen some shorter lines form outside the women's before.  They are usually very good about stamping you and letting you go in and out as you please.  The have a "set" behind the stage that has several "houses" giving it the look of a New Orleans neighborhood so that gives it a unique NOLA spin.  As with many things in the area it can be challenging to find parking at times so plan accordingly.

This is probably the least interesting putt putt golf course I've ever played but its the only putt putt in the city.  They do have some nice New Orleans specific learning information and icons for kiddos.  I just like my putt putt with more crazy stuff like whirling windmills and other such obstacles.  They have a few interesting water hazards and a few trick shots you can attempt but most of the holes are pretty basic.  I wanted the Mr. Bingle and other figures to be part of the actual course play and not just static decorations.

This is a very authentic Mexican and not Tex-Mex restaurant.  With that being said the majority of the stuff is the same old tired Mexican theme of things wrapped in tortillas.  They have decent tacos and have the great authentic Mexican spicy green sauce that burns so hot and tingly.  They do have some sandwiches and other assorted items not found in the typical NOLA Mexican place.  The area where this restaurant shines is in its selection of soups.  They have a large selection of many types of soups and stews that you just won't easily find anywhere else in the area.  The caldo de pollo (they recently have cut back on making this) and caldo de camarones are two of my favorites here but they also offer lots of other meats and different combinations.  The prices are generally a decent value and they have a large selection of Mexican beverages (but no booze).  A decent stop for a quick meal before heading next door to Brocato's for a bit of dessert.

This is a nice little indoor snowball spot where you can sit and eat at a table if you want.  They specialize in stuffing their snowballs with cheesecake here and have come up with some really interesting combinations.  They use a Snowizard machine so the ice isn't quite as fine as Hansen's but the cheesecake addition and the creative flavoring twists make this a worthy place to grab a treat at.

This is a good place for bread and desserts but the sandwiches are just NOT so good.  I'm not a big carb person and prefer the protein parts of my meal the most with lots of veggies on the side so this place isn't my optimal feeding spot.  Better to grab some bread to go and work your own magic on it.  They also offer some traditional Jewish breads that you might not find anywhere else in the area.  I never tried any of the Jewish breads and don't have any point of comparison to know if they are good or not but they looked nice.  The desserts here look pretty tasty and I had a cherry mini-pie that was pretty decent.  Overall I just wasn't that impressed and haven't been back for a long while now.

I used to have lots of friends that were members here and I would visit this venue often.  This can be a fun place with its Asian theme and lots of nooks and crannies to hide away in.  They have some nice wooden carvings of naked ladies in here that are cool.  This place is alright but there are certainly better private clubs in NOLA.   As time passed most of the people I know realized that they really didn't get a lot of value out of their memberships so they dropped out.  Personally I prefer being on the ground floor for shows at House of Blues and I really don't like being stuck up in the balcony area.

I've rarely have had a fun time at the bar here but there have been a few moments that were enjoyable.  The food here used to be much better and they once had a great turkey burger BUT the food has gone WAY downhill and now I just refuse to eat here.  The last terrible meal I ate here was around Mardi Gras and two of the cooks got into a huge fight that spilled out into the street and there was all sorts of great blood and gore everywhere (this is probably an extra star for sheer entertainment).  Of course due to the fight it took three hours for us to get our food.

Decent snowball joint where you can drive through for your chill fix.  They are heavy on the syrup pour and the sizes are large and cheap.  The ice consistency just wasn't my cup of tea and it seemed more like a snow cone instead of a snowball but that might have been due to the very heavy syrup pour.

I discovered this super hidden bar during an adventure to the Homedale Inn with a group of friends.  This bar is further down behind Homedale Inn and we just saw it as we were turning around and decided we had to check it out.  We came in here and there were only around two people in the entire place so it seemed a bit spooky.  It looks like a place that only people that live in the immediate area would even know about or go to.  I've never met anybody else that has even heard of this place or been here.  It looks like a decent place to hang out but it is just very far off the beaten path.  If there were more people here and I would have stayed for longer than one drink this might actually have been a fantastic place but from my short visit there wasn't much going on here.

Beer was drinkable but probably doesn't inspire me to want to drink much of it.  The biggest challenge here is that the interior warehouse space gets very hot and uncomfortable.  So far this is probably my least favorite brewery experience in the NOLA area.

This is a much nicer park than I expected and a lot of time has been taken with the decorative foliage planting.  The view of the river isn't as nice as other spots along the river as there is a fence blocking access.  This park is all shiny and new and certainly doesn't look like your typical New Orleans riverside venue.  The access bridge could be a challenge for some but it is also one of the best places to train running up and down a significant elevation in NOLA.  The biggest downside is this park closes relatively early and they lock everything down so no later night running which during the Summer months is the better way to go in our heat.

This is just a place to drink as the food is completely overpriced for the boring and typical Tex-Mex crap wrapped in a tortilla of some type.  Tex-Mex isn't complicated and nothing in it is very expensive so there is no way the outrageous prices this place charges for their food can ever be justified other than  they must get a lot of tourists and locals who don't know better so they just rip those clueless folks off.  Why even bother with the overpriced mediocre food here anyway when you can just go eat awesome food right across the street at Lola's!  The owners are nice people but what they charge for a freaking taco is insulting.  Do yourself and your wallet a favor and just booze it up here but never eat.

This is a great locally owned and operated sporting goods store that focuses primarily on hunting and fishing.  They have a limited selection of clothing items and frequently offer great sales on Colombia fishing shirts.  If you need anything in the area of firearms or fishing equipment this place often has items that are difficult or impossible to find at other area stores.

The food consists of small appetizer portions and really didn't impress me that much.  Don't come here expecting to be able to eat a full meal as it is just snack size portions.  Nothing I ate really appealed to me and I won't be eating here again.  The beer selection was small, overpriced and not very impressive (seriously no Abita Amber).  They do have a large selection of cocktails.  The bowling alley portion is nice enough but the overall experience just doesn't rate a return visit and I'm sticking to Rock and Bowl for my bowling excursions as it is FAR superior in every way to this venue.  Tip:  You can bring children here so for those with kids this can be a spot where you can drink adult beverages with the offspring in tow.

Convenience store with a Vietnamese restaurant inside that also does traditional NOLA po boys along with banh mi and NOLA's own yaka mein (aka "old sober").  The chicken pho is a flavorful version in a a good size bowl that is not too small or too large.  There is a dining area in the front with tables and chairs and then a lot of folks get things to go here.   Prices are quite affordable for many things and a good value for what you get for some items and less so for others.

They give you large snowball sizes for little money.  They have a selection of ice cream, hot tamales, burgers, hot dogs etc. in addition to just snowballs.  The ordering is very quick but then you often have a very long wait to get your order as many people are ordering for MANY people and get a big box full of snowballs.  Overall its a good snowball at a value price for the larger sizes they offer along with a good flavor selection.

I had great times at old Pravda and liked that joint.  This new incarnation has nothing in common with the bar formerly known as Pravda and I don't like it.  Another fancy cocktail bar that ignores the needs of beer drinkers with a very limited selection of overpriced beers.  There is nothing Russian or Slavic about this joint so the name makes absolutely no sense.  I have absolutely no reason to return to this establishment.

This is a convenient location for me as it is near my home.  They have some of the most flavorful chicken meat in their chicken pho here.  Generally the food here is decent to good but it doesn't seem to always be as good as their other two locations in terms of service and consistency of food.  In this area I generally prefer Pho Cam Ly, Lilly's and Mint Modern over this place but you can certainly satisfy your Vietnamese cravings here.  They don't seem to stay open late here usually and tend to close right at 10pm or earlier.

I've been in this store a handful of times and it has a much better selection than the Breaux Mart I'm much more familiar with on Magazine.  The location is a bit problematic depending on which way on Severn you need to go as the traffic is almost always terrible.  This grocery is very near Whole Foods so if you need items not carried there you can add Breaux Mart to your itinerary and complete your shopping in a more timely manner but items here are often more expensive than at Rouses.  They often have great prices and specials on beer.

This is the seafood market side of Harbor Seafood & Oyster Bar restaurant.  They sell boiled crawfish, shrimp and crabs along with fresh and frozen of the same along with fish.  I eat at Harbor Seafood & Oyster Bar all the time and it stays open later than the market side but if you want something boiled to go or to take home and cook yourself the market can provide you with most of the seafood items you can eat on the restaurant side along with quite a few they don't.

This is a pretty nifty bar for watching live music and they also have a kitchen putting out some decent food.  The people that run the place all seem very nice and they want to run a quality place and seem to constantly work on improving it.  I'm really happy that this is a non-smoking venue so I can actually breath oxygen instead of poison and even smell something other than smoke.  The main problem here is that parking is a bit tight in the area and Mid-City tow trucks are always on the prowl these days.  They have a very long bar but when it gets crowded they seem to need more bartenders to cover the area so it sometimes can take a bit longer than I like to get a drink but usually they do a good job.  They have a really cool small courtyard area that is "hidden" away that you might miss if you don't know to look for it.  They often get bands and music that you won't see elsewhere in the area.  This place is always a great place to check out as they always seem to have something interesting going on.

I've been to a few events here but other than that this place never seems to have many people in it.  Overall its a decent place to grab a drink and watch a game but the food is inconsistent so I probably wouldn't eat here.  This is a good place to host an event as you can easily do a block party as there is usually not much traffic in this area.

They have "Ghetto Punch" (AKA Red Drank) what more can you ask?  17 flavors of wings, crab cakes, chicken tenders, fish strips and crawfish balls.  Where else in the world but New Orleans would you find such a place?  Let me tell ya:  NOWHERE!  Go Ghetto and go to Wing Snack Express!  Take out ONLY!

This bar looks really new but the staff seem very experienced like they have been doing it for years.  Tall boy cans seems to be the order of the day here and they have tall boys for beers I have never seen tall boys for before.  The bartenders were really great, friendly, attentive, provided fast service and remembered my name every time I ordered.
