They have a small little patio on the side that was mostly filled with the smokers.  This seems to be more of a sports bar vibe than anything else and they also have a decent menu but I had already eaten so I didn't sample any of the food.  The parking lot was a bit small and was full but it was easy to find street parking a block away.  Overall this seems like a cool little spot to enjoy some sports... now if they would just play the only real sport RUGBY!!!  Really nice folks, fair prices and nice comfortable venue so just a good spot to be if you're in the area.

This is a Chinese Restaurant with some Vietnamese dishes.  I usually just get the chicken pho here which is pretty good but probably the most expensive pho in the whole New Orleans metro area.  The other dishes I've had here are decent for the most part with the sauces being not the most flavorful to me.  They seem to give good portion sizes and the service has always been good.  My biggest negative for this place is I really find their hot & sour soup to be the worst example of that dish I've ever had and I just don't find it edible. The location is very convenient to where I live and the nearest place to get my pho fix (for now but I've seen TWO new pho places opening on Magazine so huzzah!!!)  When new pho options appear I doubt I shall be returning very often if at all...

Gambino's is famous for their Doberge, Red Velvet, Wedding, Birthday and King Cakes.  They are also noted for their French bread and muffuletta bread.  In addition to their cakes and breads they have great pies, cookies, petit fours, cake balls, cannoli, pastries and all sorts of other delicacies.  The one thing they've really dropped the ball with is that with their olive salad they don't use 100% olive oil and they dilute the mix with cheaper vegetable oil.  They have a great website where you can order many of their products and have them shipped all over.

They actually do have watermelon here along with watermelon punch, Obama punch, and Michelle punch (but for some reason no Ray Nagin chocolate punch).  This is mainly a chicken wing focused joint with the addition of chicken gizzards, red beans, jalapeno bombers, fries and the namesake watermelon.  They also offer the infamous 100 piece chicken.  Cash only!

Really nice folks run this place and while they have some good food they just don't seem able to produce a good brisket.  Unfortunately this is one of the worst examples of brisket currently in the area.  They do have a nice selection of sauces and quite a variety of sides.  They have some creative ideas and do a lot of things here with pickles, sides, sandwiches and entrees.  If you only want chicken or pork BBQ they seem to be far more proficient in that area of BBQ skills.  Overall this is probably a three star joint but the seriously lacking brisket is a vital component of any BBQ place outside of Alabama and the Carolinas.  McClures went to brisket school and improved their brisket offering so I would suggest a good brisket course would drastically improve the results here also.

This is a good bar to hide away from the nearby madness on Bourbon Street that is far enough away to be an escape but near enough to return if you need to.  They also seem to have several tour groups that use this bar as a meet up spot.  Flanagan's serves food and although I've never eaten here what I've seen other folks eat looks decent.  There typically seems to be a mix of tourists and locals here but during tour times the place can get really crowded with tourists and the line for food often gets long at those times.

This is a nice dive bar that caters a lot to the tourists taking the swamp tours in the area from the nearby dock.  This is also right next to the Westwego Shrimp Lot so you can hope they are serving some good fresh seafood and you would be right.  During crawfish season they have a boil going nearly everyday it seems.  Nice folks working here and they always seem to be having a good time.  Best bar I've ever been to in Westwego so far!

This is the closest location of this local area chain to my house and the one I've been to the most often.  The food is "ok" here but it definitely isn't anywhere close to my preferred pizza spot.  They have other items like sandwiches that are also passable but once again not my favorite.  My main attraction to this place is that on Monday & Tuesday they have super cheap $2 pitchers of beer and on Wednesdays $10 bottles of wine!  Without the drink specials I would NEVER come here.

This is theoretically a fine dining restaurant but they are very lax about enforcing any type of dress code.  The service is often much slower than I'm accustomed to at other similar restaurants in the area.  The ambiance is nice enough while seeming more modern than many of the other creole restaurants in town and personally I tend to like the more old fashioned environments.  The food is generally good but I think many other area restaurants are better and the seafood gumbo here is especially disappointing.  The blood orange margarita is a nice drink special they sometimes have at lunch.  Generally it is a decent place to grab a meal but for the price I much prefer most of the other creole restaurants in the area.

Excellent Service!!!  I had a lot of problems with my Jeep Grand Cherokee and the security interlock that shuts down the engine stopped recognizing my keys and would shut my engine down and make it very difficult to start along with frequently locking the key and steering wheel.  I took the vehicle to numerous Jeep dealerships and other repair shops but NOBODY was able to fix what I thought was a pretty basic problem.  What I needed was a WOMAN running things just like the owner of EFI Services does.  She immediately knew what the problem was and fixed it FAST.  Every other place I had taken my vehicle to took WEEKS and still didn't fix anything.  I returned for many other repair issues after this and EFI Services was always fast and fair.  They know what they are doing here and don't give you the run around of incompetence that I found at every other place I went.

The seats in the theater seem a bit older and more worn than the AMC locations on the Eastbank.  If you are on the Westbank and want to watch a movie this will certainly work.  Personally I think I like the Elmwood AMC better as it seems everything is in better shape generally along with having a few more screens of options to choose from.  Prytania Theatre is always more fun to me than any of the AMC's but they are local and local is always better.

This is a great locally owned old school grocery that has lots of fantastic classic New Orleans food!  Their prepared foods and deli are great, the bakery is amazing, the meats are high quality and they have a wonderful cheese selection.  They also have one of the best wine and liquor selections in the area and carry things you won't find at any other local stores with great prices to boot!  This is one of the best grocery stores in the entire metro area.

The prices are a bit higher and the portions a bit smaller than I would like but they sling out some generally healthier than average food here.  Mostly this is a simple sandwich, salad and soup spot that offers lunch and breakfast.  They are located in one of the more interesting buildings in the CBD so its fun to visit just to see how everything fits inside.    Everything I've had here has been pretty good but the seafood gumbo is on the bland side for my taste.  Vegetarians and Vegans will find their strange and quirky ways catered to but they also offer some good old fashioned omniivore options.  This is generally a nice spot to grab a quick meal as it is far enough way that most tourists never find it.

This place has good po boys, entrees, and daily specials at decent prices.  They are only open for lunch and cash only which makes it very inconvenient.  They seem to have a deal with a quite a few tour operators as many tour groups seem to end up inside here so if you time it wrong you might end up in a LONG line.  Overall it is a decent place to grab lunch when there isn't a tour group ahead of you and the building has a nice old school ambiance with lots of seating.  I like the fact that the owner seems to always be there and has a hands on approach to running his business.  They would make a whole lot more money here if they stayed open later and took credit cards and I know I would eat here often in the evenings if they were open so maybe one day they will get better hours and finally take credit cards.

I used to have a weekly meeting that met at Zachary's on Oak Street before these folks moved to this current incarnation of their restaurant and renamed it Li'l Dizzy's so I got VERY well acquainted with the food here.  The fried chicken is fantastic and some of the best in the area.  The Sunday brunch is nice but way to expensive for what you get.  The gumbo is just full of lots and lots of sausage so I've never really liked that as it is very greasy.  There isn't much healthy for you among the choices here but this place is certainly worthy of at least one visit.  Personally I've eaten here enough to last a lifetime but I could still have some more of that mighty fine fried chicken.

$5 for a pint and a slice is one of the best deals in the city!!!  I would rank them higher except they have recently been inconsistent with their closing times.  This used to always be my go to place for some late night food but of late they have been closing much earlier so it is hard to judge when they may or may not be serving later at night.  They do tasty pizza, lasagna, and everything else I've had has been very good.  Not my favorite pizza in the area but at $5 for a pint and slice you are losing money if you don't eat your slice!!!

Andrea's advertises itself as "Northern Italian" to distinguish itself from the largely Southern Sicilian tradition that is prevalent in New Orleans.  The advertisement, however, doesn't seem to translate into the actual food as the dishes seem very similar to other NOLA area restaurants.    For full disclosure I need to admit I've only eaten here at lunch so dinner could be a different story.  The food is good basic Italian and the chef has always been making the rounds in the dining room and has always asked me how my food was (so extra kudos for that).  I've always had good service and the food has been consistently good (just not outstanding).  If you are in the area and craving some Italian food this is a good place to sample.

I rarely get to this Rouse's but they seem to more actively do more crawfish boiling and BBQing in their parking lot than other Rouses locations.  During my visits here this place has always been really crowded and the check out has often taken longer than I would like.  They seem to always be improving their selection and every visit I've made here I've seen marked improvements to the interior and the selection.    This Rouse's has also recently added a nice snowball stand with an exterior window or you can order from inside the store.  They have some unusual flavors like "dill pickle" and "wine cooler" along with some more expected selections.  I was actually pleasantly surprised at the quality of the snowball they make here.  It definitely isn't Hansen's or Plum Street but it can give many of the other snowball joints in the city a run for their money!

This is a very popular spot and its both a nice bar and restaurant.  They have a really nice ambiance along with very large TVs above the bar for sports fans.  The chicken pho here was the most generous with the meat of any pho I've ever had!  The food here is among the top Vietnamese in this area of the city while the service could be a bit better.  The prices are slightly higher than some of the other Vietnamese places but they do seem to earn their money by providing more bang for the buck.  Their pho bowls have a little cup indentation in the bottom, unlike any other pho bowl I've ever seen, that concentrates the last of your broth goodness down into a little extra treat.  There is often a line for tables but you can usually get a seat at the bar.

This place was crazy happening and busy on a Thursday night when they run a great 2 for 1 drink special.  They have a really smart system I have seen a few bars use where they give you a token for your second drink so they don't just throw two drinks down at you so one gets hot.  Their food looks interesting but leaning a bit on the overpriced side for what you get and I had already eaten so I never got to sample any food.  I really had a great fun time hanging out at the bar and there were a lot of other folks also having a great time.  The bartenders were probably some of the most professional, calm and collected I have ever seen dealing with such a large crowd.  I was impressed at how quickly the bartenders were able to quickly serve me and still provide polite, friendly and professional service the entire time on such a crowded night.  This place was right next to my hotel and was an awesome place to have so nearby.

For historical significance alone it gets 4 stars along with being one of the best ways to see the Mighty Mississippi as our ancestors did.  The steamboat trip is a slow journey that can be a relaxing experience as you watch and hear the repetitive cycling of the steamboat paddle churning through the water.  You can easily imagine a time not far gone when "Mark Twain" would be yelled and inspire Samuel Clemens onto adventures and writing.  This is more than just a journey down the river but a journey in time to experience what travel was like just a few lifetimes ago.  The loud blaring whistle may awaken you to the fact that you're back in the present for a moment but you can swiftly find yourself drifting back into a slower time as you watch the banks of the river drift past.  Yes the Steamboat Natchez is more than just a steamboat as its also a time machine.

I've been to brunch here several times along with a few visits for lunch and dinner.  For brunch I've always opted for their great drink special with bottomless sangria, mimosas, and Bloody Marys for $15.  I've had a bit of a delay getting my drink refilled when sitting at a table but when sitting at the bar it has always been extremely rapid and the bartenders are fun to banter with (my last brunch visit they even gave us full go cups of our chosen beverage).  I don't really like breakfast food at brunch and lean more towards the lunch side of things and they have a limited offering of these choices so I usually opt for either the grillades and grits or the steak and eggs.  For lunch and dinner they have a nice selection of items with some good lasagna, po boys, and pizza (with the pizza probably the thing they do best).  It is frequently crowded here so it is best to get here earlier and snag a seat at the bar for the best service.

This Italian Creole restaurant is tucked away a bit further upriver on Jefferson Hwy than a lot of people from New Orleans venture.  They have some good Italian and seafood dishes here with a strong New Orleans creole influence.  They have some very tasty gumbo and a good selection of daily changing lunch and dinner specials.  They have quite a respectable lasagna and most of the other pasta dishes I've had here have also been well done.  I was first introduced to this restaurant many years ago as a meeting space (they have a large private meeting room) and I have attended many events since then and I enjoyed the food enough to return occasionally for lunch whenever I'm in the area.  I have noticed that the food and service can be a bit inconsistent at times but generally it has always been a good experience for me.

The main time I end up in this joint is during the Krewe of Kringle and they generally have kegs for us before we begin our "march."  This is a decently cool bar with a nice little courtyard in the back.  I've heard talk that they are going to ruin this place and try to make it some swanky cocktail bar and ruin the great ambiance by beginning to go all high dollar and run the locals off.  They are alleged to have plans to transform this place into a "rum bar" which means they will probably be killing off the Russian theme.  Will it be transformed into yet another overpriced and pretentious cocktail/gastropub place I don't frequent because they have a crappy selection of beer?  We shall see...

The front of house was excellent and all were very friendly and took great care of me.  The sushi menu wasn't very inspiring and the three rolls I had were small with little fish and rather mediocre in flavor.  The only item that seemed different from other sushi options in the area is they offered "Scottish salmon" which I'm not sure if it really is from Scotland or just how they describe it as it tasted like all other salmon I've had.  This might be the only sushi restaurant in the area to only have a regular bar and not even have a sushi bar.  I think they might want to give up on the sushi idea and focus on other seafood dishes.  This would be on the bottom of my list for sushi in the area and while it's not bad it just isn't as good as the other options.  The lagniappe grilled oyster I was given was the best thing I ate and it was well executed.

This is probably the best option in Orleans Parish other than their location Uptown on Tchop.  They usually have some supplies but not always a full selection of supplies but far better than the St. Charles Ave. location that seems to usually be out of many things.  This location rarely seems overly busy so you can usually get in and out in a reasonable amount of time.

This place gets three stars for three for one drinks!  They also have a mechanical bull and I've seen more women show their tits riding that thing than I've ever seen on Bourbon Street!  The bartenderesses can be a bit short tempered and grumpy but with three for one drinks they probably are worn out from making so many drinks.  As far as cheesy Bourbon Street bars go this is probably one of the best and I end up in here more than most others as it is directly across from the Old Absinthe House where many local folks congregate but we prefer to take advantage of the three for one drinks here instead of paying the high dollar prices inside Old Absinthe.

This is a pretty great spot for people watching as the restaurant is surrounded by full length windows.  They have some good specials and do some decent seafood.  The burger seems to be made from a pre-formed patty and while it isn't inedible there are far better burgers to be had in NOLA and this one also seems an over priced poor value.  Generally I would probably stick to the specials and entree menu items here while skipping the burger.  Breakfast and brunch are also offered here and because they are a part of the Blake Hotel they are also open during holidays when many other places might be closed.  They also have a nice happy hour here with good drink specials.  The combination of a great people watching spot along with good happy hour prices makes this an interesting spot to check out.

This is an old bridge that shakes, rattles, and I'm afraid its going to roll over into the river.  The lanes are scary narrow and you always have the feeling somebody is going to ram into you that they are so near to you in the other lane.  If you didn't have to use complete Jedi force focus to stay within the centimeters tolerance you get for your narrow lane to avert disaster you could enjoy the nice view of the Mississippi River and the East and West banks of the river while you cross the bridge but leave that for when you're a passenger and not a driver as I don't want you ramming into me while you look at scenery.

This is a decent TexMex place with one of the larger menus in the area.  The interior is nicer than you might expect from the outside and its often quite crowded.  You get two dips brought out with your complimentary chips and its good to have the selection.  They have some combo platters that let you sample a good range of their offerings.  Nothing is really great here and all the sauces seem to end up tasting very similar with most things being covered in gooey melted cheese.  The service is usually adequate to a bit slower to get drink refills with larger groups.  You get what you pay for here and the combo plates will definitely leave you full.  This is a consistently good spot to get average TexMex in the soulless suburban strip mall sprawl of Veteran's.

Decent Middle Eastern food located in a strip mall in a former Chinese restaurant.  The chicken shawarma and lamb were good for the entree plates.  The menu specifically makes note that all of their meats are halal and there is also a nearby halal meat shop.  Overall it is a decent spot for a quick meal but it isn't my favorite Middle Eastern place in the area and I find for a similar price I get a bit more food at other places.

This truck seems to have become a regular fixture at the Rusty Nail so I gave them a try during a recent Saints game.  I had the double cheese burger, lamb meat pie, and fries.  The food was all good and the fries are nicely done while the burger was really more of a slider size than full burger size.  One of my friends ordered the poutine debris fries and they were really tasty.  For the quantity of food you get the prices are on the high side and really I think the tiny burger should just come with fries.  I would certainly eat here again but probably only later at night if nothing else in the area is open as it's expensive for what you get.

This dive joint is the basement/ground level of a house right across from Rouse's on Tchop.  This place sometimes has music and often has other events going on.  It is a relatively generous space and has a decent sized bar.  This place will often get crowded during a big show at Tipitina's when folks will walk back forth between here and there and then hang out here after the Tip's show.  This generally seems to be a cool bar except for the times when it gets too smokey and I'm not a fan of smoke or dumb ass smokers that always seem to accidentally bump into you and burn you with their cigarettes.  This place seems to almost always be open so I'm not even sure what there hours are if they aren't 24/7.

I really like Pal's and I love the "special" wallpaper in the men's restroom here.  They often have cheap and free food specials.  They have outstanding bartenders that always make sure you have a good time.  They have a security officer at the front door and you have to get buzzed in by the bartender (as the neighborhood used to be a lot more shady and might still have some shady characters occasionally but it seems to be getting better and better around the area all the time).  I've never had any problems in this area and I've been here at ALL hours.  I've always had a fantastic time in this bar and they are always making some very creative cocktails.  They also have all sorts of fun games in the back and an awesome jukebox.  I wish this place was closer to my house and I would be here even more than I already am.

The music is good but the lack of drinks is terrible.  It can get very hot in here during Summer and when its both hot and crowded this isn't a place I go.  The seating is very tight so it quickly gets crowded in here.  Really the only time I end up here is when I've got folks from out of town that want to check it out.  Without drinks this just isn't a place you end up staying for very long and the show only lasts 40 minutes anyway so usually your money is better spent on Frenchmen St.  If you've never been this is worthy of at least one visit.

Great dive venue with some interesting characters frequenting it.  They sometimes have some good music and always cheap drinks.  I've rarely been here when it has been crowded but it is ALWAYS smokey (which I'm not a smoker and find smoke disgusting but almost everybody in this joint seems to be a chain smoker).  I can only endure this place in limited visits due to the intense smokiness so it isn't on my regular rotation but I still end up here several times a year.

This is a really tasty Middle Eastern restaurant specializing in Greek and Lebanese cuisine.  They have some very generous helpings on their entree plates and they have some nice combinations not offered by similar restaurants in the area.  The food is delicious and the service is excellent.  On my last visit my drink was kept full even though the restaurant was packed to capacity and there was a line of people placing take out orders so that says a lot!  Keeping my drink full doesn't seem like a big deal but some restaurants really seem to have service problems with waitstaff just doing that basic task to actually earn their tips but Albasha took excellent care of me in that regard and these days that impresses me.  I was also asked multiple times how my food was and my order was delivered very rapidly.  This is a thoroughly experienced and professionally run restaurant that does good quality so even though they are a local chain they perform where it matters.

This place seems more like a bar that serves Mexican than a full blown restaurant.  They have a nice daily happy hour from 3pm to 7pm with $2 tacos, $2 domestic beer, $4 margaritas and half off chips with salsa, guacamole or queso.  The tacos were larger than those you get at Rum House or Tacos and Beer.  The margarita was alright but I found it small.  Overall a decent place to sit at the bar and eat some tacos.

The seafood gumbo wasn't really anything overly impressive flavorwise but it was alright basic gumbo with enough shrimp and oyster in it.  The shrimp and oyster platter had some very impressive sized oysters on it and probably the largest fried oysters I've ever been served.  The service was friendly and efficient and I was asked by multiple staff multiple times how my meal was and if everything was alright so kudos for the extra attentive service.  I was disappointed the only fish offered was catfish as I'm just not that into catfish.  I also found myself wishing they would've used some Tony Chachere's or other spice mix more heavily into the food to give it a bit more kick.  The french fries were probably the best thing I had surprisingly and they were really excellent with perfect crunch on the outside.  Overall it seems like a decent spot to grab a quick meal in this little spot in Metry.

This is overall a pretty decent military surplus and outdoor store with a good selection of several items.  It is a decent sized store for military surplus and they have most of the basic items.  Sadly you just don't find large quantities of cool WWII stuff very often in stores like this anymore and I miss the days of my childhood when that stuff was everywhere in places like this.  They still have a good supply of more contemporary items and you certainly can find all sorts of things that can be multi-tasked for various uses.  One item of particular importance for those of us that like to attend outdoor festivals is they have a good selection of military boonie hats which are some of the best hats you can possibly wear during outdoor festivals in NOLA in my experienced opinion as they work great for protecting you from sun and rain.

This Rouse's location has recently added a nice snowball/snack "stand" which is actually an exterior sliding window you can order from or you can order from inside the store.  They have some unusual flavors like "dill pickle" and "wine cooler" along with some more expected selections.  I was actually pleasantly surprised at the quality of the snowball they make here as I had really low expectations for a grocery store snowball but Rouse's generally does things well.  It definitely isn't Hansen's or Plum Street but it can give many of the other snowball joints in the city a run for their money!  They have all sorts of other snack and dessert items here but I've only tried the snowball so far.

Decent sushi place in a Metairie strip mall on Airline.  They offer some affordable lunch specials and the rolls are decently sized.  The ambiance is a bit on the basic side but it is clean.  It's right next to Rouse's so you can grab a meal before making groceries.  Probably not one of my top spots for sushi but one of my friends lives nearby and loves it.

Hipsters and assorted other grimy folks were stumbling about in here.  It was dark dank and smokey but they do sling food pretty late.  The prices were not good with overpriced $5 Yuengling so this seems to be a bar for those that don't know that this is overpriced as all they probably drink is that gross PBR poison.  The smoke fumes really left a short threshold of being able to survive in this place so I had to get out pretty fast.  Maybe I can check it out again if they ever clear the smoke out but otherwise I probably wouldn't go back.

This is quite an interesting dining option in the area now.  The vibe reminds one of a techno dance club or stripper joint when you first walk in so you aren't quite sure if you are in the right place but you are.  They have a really extensive menu with a nearly overwhelming and sometimes confusing array of choices including à la carte along with all you can eat lunch and dinner options.  Regardless of the ultimate choice you make it is highly unlikely you will leave this establishment hungry and most likely you will be bloated to maximum capacity.  You get unlimited banchan and the serving portions of the main dishes are all generous.  The experience is one of the best for the Korean BBQ concept in the area currently.

I was a member of the New Orleans Energy Club that was briefly at this location prior to Katrina and I enjoyed that place.  I wasn't all that thrilled when Zea's took over this spot but Zea's has some pretty solid rotisserie meats and some interesting sides that are not very common at other restaurants in the area.  They are a bit pricey for what they offer.  Zea has very consistently good (but not great) meat and seafood.  I generally avoid chain places like the plague but this is a local operation and has quality far and above most other "chain" type operations.  I will go for the meat maybe about twice a year.

Yet another mediocre Mexican place on Magazine where there are already too many Mexican places adding to the already overly crowded number of mediocre Mexican restaurants in the area.  The interior is interesting and they have done a unique theme inside while their tables are more form than function being a bit slippery on top but highly decorated.  The menu continued the theme of form over function as the print the menu was written in literally stabbed my eyes and was painful to read so it was hard to decipher what the offerings were. Their enchilada was not at all what you usually expect from an enchilada while their tacos were nice with generous slices of avocado.  The salsa that comes with the chips is very thin and watery along with the fact it could definitely use some spice kick. For the prices there are just many better places to go.  I'd stick with the taco happy hour and before or after that still just stick with the tacos.

This is a great location overlooking City Park.  I've been to a few private events here and many dinners.  The ambiance and location are my favorite things about Ralph's and it is a very relaxing spot to enjoy fine dining.  I've always enjoyed the food, service, and atmosphere of this place.  They often have different specials throughout the year.  They currently have lunch Wed-Fri with brunch on Sunday and dinner 7 nights a week.  They also have a nice bar here that can be enjoyable just to hang out at.

This place has breakfast and lunch but no dinner.  I don't care for breakfast so I never eat that stuff.  The only thing I generally eat here are the large and tasty burgers.  They have good, large, basic burgers here and while they aren't anything special they are solid burgers that are above average in size while being better quality than many other places.  The service is often slow and not always up to standards.  There can sometimes be a wait to be seated and it gets crowded during the weekends.  I rarely end up here anymore, as I hate to wait, and I usually can only get the time to eat here on the weekends.

I'm not really the coffee shop type of person and I rarely drink coffee as I much prefer beer.  Despite my tendency to avoid such places as this I've had to end up here for various reasons and I've always found this to be a pleasant but small place.  They have often had very nice folks working here that add to the experience.  If I have to get dragged to a coffee shop this is certainly one of the better ones.  The biggest problem here is that this is such a nifty little spot it is almost always crowded and that takes away from what could be a much better experience.

A nice little neighborhood grocery market that also has a decent deli with meat and three plates.  They actually have parking which makes it easy to do some quick shopping for needed items.  Martin's BBQ is also has one of their locations right next door so you can combine a grocery shop and BBQ stop all in one.

This space has gone through several restaurants over the years and so I felt compelled to sample the latest development.  I'm quite a fan of Thai food so I was excited to sample some of their offerings.  I started with the Tom Yum soup and got Pad Thai as my entree.  The food wasn't the best I've had but it was tasty.  The interior of this establishment hasn't changed much from the previous tenants but it is a very nice and comfortably designed space with a fantastic location on Maple Street.  I would probably choose La Thai, Basil Leaf, or Sukho Thai over the food here but if you're in the area this place can certainly satisfy your Thai craving.

They have a plumbing supply business and also a retail display store with bathtubs, sinks, faucets, lighting and other associated home decor items.  They seem to mainly carry higher end items in the retail store but some things can be ordered in a cheaper configuration.  They want you to sign in when you first walk in the retail store and the wait for a salesperson can be a much longer time than you would expect so they use the sign in list to determine who gets the next available salesperson.  The plumbing supply business can get really busy especially in the morning as they carry one of the largest selections of plumbing supplies in the area.  I have been given some incorrect parts before but they have always been easy to work with to exchange them.

The Fly is a bit of a locals secret that sees far less tourists than many other areas of the city.  Being hidden back behind the zoo also makes it more fun as you get to get high up on the levee and look down on the zoo below.  There is a good amount of open grassy space to play games, picnic, throw a Frisbee, let your dog go for a good game of fetch or otherwise enjoy a bit more open space than a lot of other areas in the city.  It is also a great space just to get a bit of sun or watch the Mississippi River pass by as you sip on a daiquiri or some beers.  This is a very relaxing spot or a great spot for activity depending on your mood.  Unfortunately they keep building more and more stuff out here taking away from the open space and natural beauty of the area and that development has drawn enough complaints that it seems they have at least paused most additional development for the time being.  Overall this is one of the nicest spots to kick back and have fun outside in the Uptown area.

Perlis is one of the better clothing stores in New Orleans.  They primarily focus on men's clothing but they do have some women's and boy's items also.  The Perlis brand is most famous for their crawfish logo items and you will see many local folks proudly wearing these clothes.  In addition to crawfish logo items they also specialize in fleur-de-lis and Mardi Gras items.  Perlis is also noted for their selection of suits, ties, and shirts with the suits coming with their offer of free lifetime alterations.  The prices often do seem a bit expensive but they do often have some good sales and also have things you can't find anywhere else in the area.  They will also special order items and will really go out of their way to search for things for you.  I have several of the Perlis polo shirts and I like them "ok" I just wish they fit more like Brooks Brother's which I find more comfortable.  They thing they provide better than just about any other area clothing store is service!

I've got a special place in my heart for this old joint that was Bruno's for most of its existence as I attended many a good rugby party here and did nude Zulu Warrior ceremonial jogs around the block on multiple occasions.  Things have certainly changed since this place got nastier when this bar became Rocco's and now waaay too calm and grey haired as Redd's.  I think we need to bring a rugby party back to this joint and reclaim our old bar!

This is one of the few meat and three places in New Orleans except in New Orleans it is almost always a meat and two which is the case here but you can add a third.  They have nice vegetables and their meats are good along with having a rotating selection of daily specials.  They offer a quick meal at a good value that will satisfy your appetite.  Service is traditional meat and three cafeteria style.  They only offer breakfast and lunch and close by 2pm so unfortunately don't plan at having dinner here and they are also closed on the weekends so if you can't make it for the weekday you are out of luck (which is really unfortunate for folks that don't work downtown or have the flexibility to make it here during the weekday).    Overall this spot offers a hearty lunch for a good value and their changing daily specials keep things interesting.

This is still a really new place and they definitely have some kinks to work out with service and keeping the buffet stocked.  It was taking upwards of 20 minutes for items that had run out on the buffet to get restocked so certainly that is an area for improvement.  The service was also very inconsistent and it took quite a while to get a drink refill.  The food was very well spiced and at a generally higher level of spice than the other area Indian food restaurants in the area.    Overall I enjoyed the food but for the moment I would advise to order off of the menu if you are in any kind of hurry.

This is a chain and some really clever people came up with the idea for this chain.  Every time I drive past this joint it seems to have some folks inside and even later in the night/early morning.  They serve WARM cookies, warm milk and cookie ice cream sandwiches.  Apparently their cookies and milk recipe is pure genius as the college kids seem to be addicted to it like crack.  I generally don't go out of my way to go to chain joints but I was right across the street at Bruno's so I gave in to my curiosity and had to check what all this hype was about.  I got a cookie and I wasn't expecting it to be all hot and fresh like right out of the oven deliciousness which it most certainly was... the warm milk, usually not my preferred option, but with the warm cookie ohhh nice... the finale with the ice cream cookie mmmm ahhhh yeahhhh.  Ok so they ARE serving crack here and it is VERY dangerous so be VERY cautious if you choose to sample their goods as you will NEED more sooner than later.

NOSH is in the space that used to be Tommy's Wine Bar and they offer a daily happy hour.  Most of the food items on offer for their happy hour menu are pathetically small and a waste of time and money to even order while the main decent special they offer would be the 50 cent raw oysters.  The service is really slow and mediocre at best.  The drinks are ok but their happy hour prices are not all that happy and still seem overpriced.  The crowd usually seems that it isn't a very friendly or happy gathering type so this place just lacks the usual happy friendly vibe most NOLA establishments generally offer.  The bar itself has a nice ambiance and very comfortable seating which is unchanged since before Katrina and still works quite well.  Overall without the 50 cent oysters there would really be no need to even visit here and even with the oyster special Superior Seafood offers a more enjoyable friendly crowd along with their 50 cent oyster special which also offers much better drink specials.

The ice doesn't compare to Hansen's or Plum Street and the flavors taste like the commercially made ones.  This is about the only game in town along this stretch of Jefferson Highway so unless you're willing to travel about three miles further in either direction you won't find another snowball treat.  I've only ended up here due to the fact that a Concentra drug testing lab is next door where yippee ki-yay I get to pee in cups for drug tests due to the line of work I'm in so after I pee I saunter over to this joint to get a snowball.  The good thing about the remoteness of this place is I've never had to stand in a long line or seen a long line here but that could be due to my timing.

This is a very casual spot with a warehouse/barn type construction with a large open seating plan.  They offer a pretty respectable seafood buffet here which is a bit pricey but its the only one I've ever seen that has soft shell crabs on it.  The seafood here has lots of fried options with some boiled choices.  If you choose to order off of the menu they have a good selection of typical Louisiana seafood dishes and some chicken and beef choices along with po boys and burgers.  The gumbo includes sausage so it isn't a pure seafood version like I prefer.  They also have some non-local seafood like snowcrab and some unique items like their Mardi Gras rolls. The service is a bit slow sometimes but generally acceptable.    This is certainly a good place to chow down on lots of good local seafood and your biggest issue will be choosing between the buffet here or the all you can eat boiled options at the nearby Salvo's.

The downstairs bar and lobby area along with the restaurant space are quite impressive.  The Three Keys "intimate music venue" is quite a unique spot to watch live music as the crowds swirl past among the bars between the restaurant, Josephine Estelle, and the lobby bar.  I never made it up to the rooftop pool and garden space, Alto, where there is another bar and restaurant but the YLC Wednesday on the Square after party is there so I'm sure I will get there soon.  The prices for drinks outside of happy hour seem too rich for my taste and the beer selection seems to be lacking my preferred options.  This is certainly one of the trendiest  and happening spots right now in NOLA.

This place has some of the best vegetables of anyplace in NOLA.  I really love the mashed sweet potatoes, the creole okra with shrimp, the collard greens, and the green beans.  I used to work across the street from here before Katrina and I ate lunch here everyday so this place really does hold a special meaning to me.    I really like the daily specials (with a choice of yummy veggies) which are pretty much the same goodness as they have been but the new training format they have started since Katrina has resulted in substantially decreased and consistently bad service (where before Katrina I always had great service).  If you can't get here by well before 11:30 then you should expect a very long wait generally to complete your meal.  I understand that this is a training ground but the training used to be much better and they need to institute more discipline and control to get this ship running right again.

This is causal restaurant with some fine dining options that has been displaying a vigorous lunch crowd and more relaxed dinner scene.  They have a decent private back room for meetings or events.  The location in a strip mall on Metairie Road leaves a lot to be desired aesthetically but provides ample parking.  This is definitely a vast improvement from the last restaurant in this space, Zeke's Restaurant, that even Gordon Ramsay couldn't save.

I was here during Christmas time and they really do a nice job of adding a lot of holiday fun, decorations and add in Santa being available for kids.  This is a nice space and I really found it far more pleasant than the Gaylord Resort at National Harbor I had recently visited prior to this one.  This is also located at the famous Grand Ole Oprey and right next to a large shopping mall (pro tip: you can park at the mall for free then take a free shuttle bus to the Convention Center).  This is a very large space with a great deal to see so make sure to schedule a pretty large chunk of time to fully explore this space.  The convention center is also very nice and this is one of the best places to attend a conference that I've ever experienced.

They have some wacky flavors in this place and just their chocolate flavors take up an entire corner.  There is almost always a line to be served here and they offer free tastings of their many and varied flavors.  I'm all old fashioned and mainly just stick to my strawberry but I sometimes mix it up with one of their chocolate flavors or anything else that might catch my eye.  The only big negative about this place, other than the sometimes long lines, is that they only take cash.  They also have the infamous Tchoupitoulas Sundae challenge, that consists of 8 scoops of ice cream and then a huge onslaught of toppings, and completion of this challenge gets your name on the wall (I've never achieved this accolade but I could certainly eat the eight scoops but all those toppings just gross me out).

They have a plumbing supply business and also a retail display store with bathtubs, sinks, faucets, lighting and other associated home decor items.  They seem to mainly carry higher end items but some things can be ordered in a cheaper configuration.  They want you to sign in when you first walk in and the wait for a salesperson can be a much longer time than you would expect so they use the sign in list to determine who gets the next available salesperson.

This is more than just a mere Po Boy shop as it is far more of an actual restaurant as they offer an impressive selection of entrees with the rare and elusive country fried steak that is actually a made from a steak (a ribeye steak properly served with brown gravy instead of that nasty white gravy).  They have a nice selection of breakfast, daily specials, steaks, seafood, pastas and desserts.  They are not scared to give big portions and the roast beef po boy reminds me a bit of the meat used at R&O's. The exterior is pretty much all black & gold so this is a big time Saints and LSU business.  There is a lot of seating inside and you simply just order at the cash register then get your number and take your seat and place your number in the designated holder and the food is quickly brought to your table.

Blah boring chain burger place that's slightly higher quality than McD's.  A much better restaurant is deserving of this prime location and this place would be better served next to some other fast food places.  I really could do without the steel cage basket they serve things in.  Maybe this place will do ok as there isn't any other fast food joint within eye shot of this place other than Subway but I think a local joint would have done better business and fit in much better with the neighborhood.  Personally I could do without it and probably won't be back as there are much better burgers for a similar price nearby in the bars.  I guess this would be a good spot to bring kids.

Puckett's is a local Tennessee chain with locations in some pretty cool spots.  This location in Franklin is often SUPER BUSY especially on weekends with generally about an hour plus wait to get in but you do often get live music to go with your meal.  They have a really great and really large selection of some pretty dang tasty food and this is one of those rare places you could probably eat at everyday of the week for a few weeks and never get bored with the food.  The service is also friendly and attentive with focusing on the finer details of keeping folks happy.  For a place so busy and with so many food options they still somehow manage to put out a good BBQ brisket along with their own house BBQ sauces which is pretty impressive with all the other things on their menu.  The only item I'm not really a fan of is the skillet pecan cobbler but some folks might love it.  Overall I might just eat here everyday for a couple of weeks if it wasn't for the crazy wait times.

The upstairs balcony view is an enjoyable space when the weather is nice.  The food was inconsistent on my initial visit with the gumbo having undercooked okra but overcooked shrimp while my trout was alright.  The crawfish au gratin tasted exactly like au gratin potatoes with crawfish added which is far better than plain potatoes but could have been kicked up a bit more.  Overall it is a decent spot and still seems to be getting the engine up and running at full speed.  I will have to give it another try in a few months and see how they have progressed.

This is a great little park in the CBD that is host to YLC Wednesday on the Square and the Harvest the Music series of events.  Many other festivals and events are held here and this is a great location for such celebrations.  When events aren't going on this is just a nice park spot just to enjoy a picnic or anything else you might want some green space for such as frisbee etc.

So for the same price as just an oil change at most other places you can also get your car washed and vacuumed here.  There is usually a bit of a wait but they have a pleasant enough waiting area with some creatures and magazines to read.  You don't always get the best car wash and interior vacuum but if you're getting your oil changed anyway its not a bad deal.

I feel so utterly betrayed as the recent law, requring disclosure of the origin of seafood from restaurants has gone into effect now, has revealed a dark truth I would never have wanted to accept.  The current menu at Slim Goodies reveals their crawfish are sourced from foreign lands even though they are literally across from the amazing seafood distributor of Big Fisherman.  I feel utterly betrayed over my patronage of this business over the years as they have proven to favor China over local Louisiana... so so heartbreaking....

This is a pretty solid diner with good quality diner level food.  I'm not big into breakfast but occasionally I will grab the crawfish etouffee omelet here.  They also have some pretty solid sandwiches and other menu items are also good.  They also have a really great back patio that a lot of people don't ever check out that looks like a wild jungle!!!  They open really early so they are among a handful of places in the Garden District to grab something to eat at 6am.  Update:  1) Good, they finally take credit cards!!!  2) Bad, sadly like many places service has declined and isn't as good as it used to be.

Brought to us by the same folks that gave us Slim Goodies this is a bit more of a nicer restaurant feel as compared to Slim Goodies casual diner concept.  The food is pretty similar and some dishes are exactly the same and actually the menu is consistently larger at Slim Goodies while Horn's varies between breakfast, lunch and dinner.  Horn's also offers quite a selection of cocktails to enjoy along with your food.  Service is a bit lackadaisical so don't think your drink will get refilled quickly or often.  Overall its a nice spot for a meal in a slightly bit of off the tourist path location.

This is a nice new addition to the expanding Vietnamese restaurant scene of Magazine.  I'm getting a bit concerned about the sheer saturation of Asian and Mexican joints on Magazine Street but this place is affordable and I liked their pho.  They also offer a crazy giant pho challenge that consists of a huge bowl with 2 pounds of meat and 2 pounds of noodles that you have to eat within one hour.

This is a grocery store that has a nice deli and bakery along with a good selection of typical grocery store items including a large alcohol selection.  They seem to be well noted for their seafood enchiladas, king cakes and making a lot of popular sausages.  Their deli and bakery should certainly be investigated as they have some good hot food and nice looking desserts.  If you find yourself in Belle Chasse this is certainly a place you should visit and see for yourself.

This is one of my secret hide aways that I like to go to for cheap but great raw oysters and good seafood options.  They do good boiled seafood and grilled fish (or you get several other options on how you want it cooked).  The po boys are good yet smaller than I like but that leaves room for some of the other good options (like the delicious fried seafood appetizer, gumbo, or turtle soup).  Sunday through Wednesday ALL DAY they have 50 cent oysters (used to be 25 cent until BP) so I like my $6 a dozen deal.    This place can get crazy crowded with a substantial wait on the oyster special days so there might be a line out the door waiting to be seated sometimes.  I've always had great service and I prefer to sit at the bar to enjoy my food.  There are always some interesting characters in here and this is certainly a great spot to see and hear things that you are hard pressed to find elsewhere.  I find the oyster size more consistent at Luke but generally more interesting people here.

This is a pretty solid diner with good quality diner level food.  I'm not big into breakfast but occasionally I will grab the crawfish etouffee omelet here.  They also have some pretty solid sandwiches and other menu items are also good.  I've always had just outstanding and very friendly service here that is completely 5 Stars I just don't think diner type food can be more than 3 Stars generally in my ranking bias.  They also have a really great back patio that a lot of people don't ever check out that looks like a wild jungle!!!  I don't get here very often and when I do I usually forget that it is cash only so remember to bring your cash.  They open really early so they are among a handful of places in the Garden District to grab something to eat at 6am.

Typically long lines and the food just doesn't have a whole lot of flavor to me.  The tortillas are very "gummy" and just don't have a very good consistency to me while at the same time being too dry and often falling apart.  I'm just not a fan of "better" fast food that takes a cafeteria line approach and then just doesn't taste as good as Taco Bell.  For the same price I can go to an actual Mexican restaurant and get better food with actual service while actually being able to enjoy my dining experience.

This is definitely an interesting and uniquely New Orleans type of diner experience.   There are several Dot's Diners around but this is the only one I've ever stepped into.  The place is always open so that does take away from the cleanliness factor but I've seen far worse.  The service staff are very friendly and engaging  and they seem  to always have folks inside.  I'm not a big breakfast fan but they have all sorts of other offerings and I got the sliders which were actually rather large for sliders and very filling.  It definitely isn't the best or most tasty food I've had and "greasy spoon" definitely sums up most of what is dished up here but they are always open.  It wouldn't ever be my first choice for a meal but if it were really late/very early and nothing else was open I'd probably venture here again if I was stuck in the area.

A nice little neighborhood grocery market that also has a decent deli with meat and three plates.  They actually have parking which makes it easy to do some quick shopping for needed items.  Martin's BBQ also has one of their locations right next door so you can combine making groceries  and a BBQ stop all in one.

I've eaten here many times and had many private events here.  I have always had a great time with outstanding service and food.  Muriel's has some amazing gumbo and they usually have a special for around $30 for a 3 course meal.  Some people don't know you can usually get a drink downstairs and go and enjoy the balcony upstairs and this is one of the best places to people watch all the interesting things going on down around Jackson Square below.  They also have an interesting "Egyptian" themed room upstairs. Always a great place to go with a group, book an event, or just eat by yourself at the bar.

This is a pretty cool bar which is right next to Smoked BBQ which offers some nice meat.  There seems to be quite a few locals that frequent this place and it is the perfect location to grab some good BBQ then go hang out at My Brother's Bar after.  Overall this is a nice neighborhood joint with some friendly folks and good bartenders.

I just stopped in here to drink a few brews and I had not yet had a chance  to try the food but as the burgers here do look nice I decided to sample one.  Looking at the menu I decided on the mushroom Swiss burger with a side of slaw... with the results that the burger was sadly mediocre but I have had worse while the slaw was absolutely not to my liking at all and I couldn't eat it (first time EVER I have met a slaw I couldn't eat). They have some nice outdoor seating and the indoor seating is a larger space than many bars offer so this has more of a restaurant vibe than bar but they still have a nice long bar to sit at as well.  The service was friendly and attentive along with telling you what their favorite beers of the moment were.  This is a pretty popular spot in this neighborhood and seems like a generally fun spot to be and I would return for the beer but not the burgers or slaw.

This is a nice addition to the expanding Vietnamese restaurant scene of Magazine that I have been eating at for several years now.  This is a nice spot for a quick and delicious meal with their offerings of a variety of rice dishes, noodle dishes, spring rolls, pho, Vietnamese po boys/banh mi, Vietnamese tacos/sliders/banh gap and many other delicious items.  Their stir fried beef banh mi is one of the best beef po boys in the city!  My video review of Pho Cam Ly is here:  https://youtu.be/E2TfP_bLwBg

This is an old Italian place that  was in Bucktown for years (and the Quarter before that) and had to relocate to the West End due to the Corps of Engineers work on our levee system.  Their new location is a lot nicer with better space than their old cramped space so the move has been a blessing for them.  I've only eaten lunch here and they have a good selection of local seafood dishes, po boys, and the usual Italian options.  The seafood gumbo is ok but the rue is a bit thin for my taste.  They have a pretty decent lasagna here and the prices are reasonable.  I rarely ate here when they were in Bucktown because R&O's was right across the street and really the only time I ended up at Two Tony's was when the line was too long at R&O's.  This is still a good place to grab some decent Italian for lunch and it might be nice for dinner too but I've yet to experience their dinner menu.

This is causal restaurant with some fine dining options which has been displaying a vigorous lunch crowd and more relaxed dinner scene.  Generally Porter & Luke's averages a bit over a 3.5 star mainly due to consistency issues as they absolutely can put out some four and five star food when they are firing on all cylinders but they seem to often have misfires.  They have a decent LARGE private back room and smaller private side room for meetings, events or other private dining groups.  The location is in a strip mall on Metairie Road which leaves a lot to be desired aesthetically but provides ample parking.  This is definitely a vast improvement from the last restaurant in this space, Zeke's Restaurant, that even Gordon Ramsay couldn't save.  My most recent visit was during St. Patrick's and the special was corned beef and cabbage and the corned beef was on the tougher side and certainly could have been better while the gumbo I also got was good.  Overall this is USUALLY a nice spot to get a good lunch or dinner and I've been to some good events here.  My video review of Porter & Luke's is here:  https://youtu.be/uLEkT9jOf28

So I've kept a deep dark secret that I sometimes get a craving for a big bag of Krystal burgers and I had long heard White Castle was a very similar burger so I ended up staying in a hotel very near this White Castle which seemed like the perfect opportunity to finally lose my White Castle virginity. So on getting my food I certainly noticed the similarity to Krystal but I have to say that overall I just didn't find the experience anywhere nearly as pleasing as my deep secret sin I very rarely engage in with Krystal usually is.  The flavors of White Castle were simply not quite as flavorful and nice a flavor fix as I gain to my taste buds with a big bag orgy of Krystals.  White Castle just didn't provide me the same naughty pleasure swerve that my long affair with Krystal has always succeeded with inducing.

I had the enchiladas and they were exceptionally bland.  Everything just seemed very disorganized and while the place only had a handful of tables with patrons there seemed to be more than enough staff it took a very long time to have my order taken.  After that waitress brought my food out very fast she quickly disappeared for quite a long while.    I had initially been planning on going for a second trip to sample the tacos to see if those might redeem the place but when I never got a single drink refill on my iced tea I was done with the place.  There were literally four staff members sitting at or behind the bar just doing NOTHING and nobody managed to pay attention to me and get me a refill on my drink (and I was sitting at the bar).  Until I started waving around my credit card to pay while making plenty of noise and run out of the place I received no attention after my food was delivered.  Too many better places at better price points with better service to deal with buffonry like this.

In more civilized days when individual HONOR had meaning and men were willing to put their lives on the line for it, other than just in warfare, this area of City Park was very frequently used for duels.  Originally there were two dueling oaks but unfortunately one was destroyed by a hurricane in 1949 so we have the last remaining and singular dueling oak standing.  There is a commemorative plaque explaining the historical significance of this oak and the area around it (at least until Maoist Mitch and the rest of of his Cultural Marxist Red Guard continue their destruction of history spree and remove it and cut down the tree).  We sorely need to re-legalize dueling in City Park and I would be happy to meet all the honorless Cultural Marxists in duels under the dueling tree at such time.  They would lose in a simple battle of wits as they lack logic and facts to justify their destruction of history.

If your looking for a quality smaller gun store with a reliable and straight shooting owner that knows what he is talking about then this is the place for you.  Meplat Group is an FFL with a small but notable stock of firearms and is happy to do do transfers for $20.  They buy, sell, trade, and transfer firearms of all kinds including Class III weapons like machine guns, silencers, short barrelled rifles and shotguns.  They also provide training through their NRA certified instructors and give a great level of service and knowledgeable advice to help customers in the selection and acquisition of firearms that meet their needs.  The owner, Kenneth Bossetta, is an attorney and can also set up NFA trusts to assist with the process of acquiring NFA items.  Mr. Bossetta is also a great person to do business with and is definitely a step up from your average gun store interaction.

I was at Ole Miss when the very first McAlister's came into existence (initially it was Checker's but a burger joint already had that name taken so they changed it to McAlister's to franchise it out). It's really just a boring bland franchise chain now so in the land of delicious po boys I just don't find myself eating here.  The sandwich quality seems to have declined with the franchising but the iced tea is still great so I mainly stop at this location for iced tea as its near my office.

This place is a solid three star 24/7 dive bar with very comfortable bar stools with bonus points for the 24/7 part.  Metry still allows smoking in the bars so that will drive me out of a place really fast but fortunately on my last visit nobody was committing smoke suicide.  This is also a spot where you can get your bartender to cook you a burger and I had a discount coupon so I took a chance and tried the burger and I probably would never get the burger again unless it was 4am and there were no other options but there usually are better options even then so I would choose those.  So just come here to drink drinks and play some chess or something like that.

I've only been to the CAC for parties, bands, and events.  Honestly I've never found most of the art here very interesting but I'm not really into modern/contemporary art as I much prefer the more classical approach.  This place is a great party and event venue and I've had lots of good times here.  Admission:  $5 General Admission $3 for Students & Seniors FREE to CAC Members

Fresh local produce along with boiled peanuts, tamales and other assorted treats so what's not to like?  They take credit cards and actually have pretty good parking around the building.  If you want some local Louisiana love or need to satisfy that boiled peanut craving this is a great place to do it and it's probably the nicest and best Becnel's produce option out of the several out there.

This place has a great selection of some of the most amazingly fresh produce, meats, and seafood anywhere in the area.  They also have many Asian fruits and vegetables that are difficult or impossible to find elsewhere.  They have a large selection of products and prepared food items from across Asia.  They even carry a decent selection of cookware.  The prices here are generally very affordable and they have some great values.  They also have a deli where they make some good things with most people seeming to focus on the banh mi.  They do have a few things missing that I like to get from Asain stores but other than those they have nearly everything else I've ever looked for.

This establishment is a coffee house that does some baked goods, desserts and sandwiches.  I was really leaning towards two stars as I HATE the hours this place keeps.  I made it in here once, right after they opened, and they were sold out of everything.  After about 20 more attempts I finally made it here before their posted closing time of 6pm but they stop serving sandwiches at 5pm.  Holy Batman I was getting frustrated BUT the owner saved the day and one star by stepping up and making one last sandwich for the day.  While I was waiting for my French Dip roast beef sandwich I also ordered an apricot raspberry pistachio bar which was pretty good.  The sandwich was pretty good too with rare roast beef on real French bread with a dipping sauce that seemed to be French Onion Soup.  The food was good but a bit overpriced and this seems to mainly be a breakfast and lunch joint.  I would like this place a lot more if it were open late as I'm a night owl and have to work during the day.

The Colombian style arepas sandwiches here are definitely a unique experience in the New Orleans dining scene.  I had the chicken and avocado which seemed very filling while being very healthy.  I really only got the taste of avocado and didn't notice a whole lot of chicken which with most sandwiches would make me grumpy but somehow the whole was greater than the parts.  I've been able to sample most of the other arepas and they have all been tasty and their liquor drinks are all done decently.  I've made several attempts to eat here when they are not yet open for their posted times so plan accordingly that they will often open late and close early.  Expect to have a much slower pace of most everything while here.

The ambiance inside this place is nearly non-existent and doesn't encourage dining inside.  This place is generally very fast but it really isn't one of the better po boy joints in the city.  You do get a free drink with your po boy but they only have Pepsi products and no fresh brewed iced tea.  The roast beef po boy here is the sliced variety with no real gravy but it does have some green pepper and onion coating that gives it a bit better flavor than just plain sliced roast.  Unfortunately they also don't have creole mustard here.  If you're in a hurry or its late at night and want a mediocre po boy this place will work but there are far better places to go.  Its also cash only so be prepared.

This is probably the most comprehensive grocery store in the entire French Quarter while most of the other options are more convenience stores with limited grocery items.  This Rouse's is surprisingly larger than you would think it was from the outside but still smaller than most other Rouse's locations.  They pack in a lot of items for the space and it is a well stocked grocery for the Quarter.  There are frequently gutter punks that hang out in the area that will hassle you but if you ignore them they usually leave you alone.

This is a really cool independent movie venue that focuses on local area films.  They have mainly relied on word of mouth thus far and the nearly secret location is inside an old Wash-Dry-Fold laundromat.  The brother and sister team that run this place, Will and Hayley, are very passionate about independent local films along with wanting their patrons to have a great experience.    Tickets are only $5 and half of that goes to the filmmaker.  They have a few basic snacks available and its also BYOB so you can have quite an entertaining time.  They have very comfortable chairs set up and this seems like it could develop into a great and unique venue for films you just don't get to watch anywhere else.

This is a bar with games that also frequently hosts events like comedy nights etc.  They have bottle and can beers and a limited selection of other types of booze.  It's an alright place with a decent vibe but it rarely seems to be hopping outside of their events.  This is generally a pretty laid back and low key joint to duck into for a few beverages and maybe to play a few games when events aren't happening.

I typically only end up here when I decide to take out of town friends on an adventure on the Algier's Ferry and this usually ends up being our first stop where we grab some food and drinks as it is the closest bar to the ferry.  From here we usually continue to the Crown & Anchor and Old Point Bar.  This is a good sized space and they usually have a decent selection of food with some of it being pretty good but most of it is just "ok" for the most part.  I've rarely seen it crowded but it does seem to draw a fairly steady stream of tourists who decide to go on the Algier's ferry adventure as well.

This is one of the best hotels in New Orleans and is home to fantastic pieces of NOLA history and legend like the Sazerac Bar.  This hotel would often donate food to the place I worked prior to Katrina so I often got to take the elevator deep down into the bowels of the lower levels of this place which was fascinating as there are many functioning antiques down there that still keep this place going.  I've been to many Mardi Gras balls and other fun events here over the years and it was a sad time after Katrina when it was closed for so long.  It was a happy day when they finally reopened and added even more new restaurants and reinvigorated many of the traditional spots.  The most special time here is during Christmas and they do some serious decorating above and beyond nearly any other location in the city and it is a definite destination during that time of year!

This is a cool little Oriental store that has a lot of things you might not even find at Hong Kong market.  They have herbal remedies I like such as ginsing with royal jelly.  The prices are a bit more expensive and this place is more of a convenience sized store but they pack a lot of items for the space.  This is one of the few places where you can find many Asian items in Metairie.

The vast majority of seating here is an outside covered patio so that comes with the benefits and risks of the NOLA outdoors.  There is also a great deal of hookah smoking so that is an additional element to consider if you're gong to eat here.  The food is decent but not as good as most of the other Middle Eastern restaurants in NOLA and Mona's would give you a better experience.  The service really was unacceptably slow at many points and it seems the staff have a lot of distractions.  This is probably a spot best reserved for those that are looking to smoke a hookah and if you're just in the mood to eat you will probably be happier elsewhere but the patio could be nice.

This place is just "ok" BBQ and they are similar to but slightly below Corky's for a BBQ experience.  They give you a very good portion of meat on their plate specials BUT they dole out their BBQ sauce, like it is liquid gold, and you only get a tiny little cup of it that isn't nearly enough to go with your meal.  The brisket is very similar to that at Corky's but it isn't the moistest and is more on the dry side so it certainly needs some sauce.  They also only give you ONE napkin and I'm always suspicious of any BBQ that doesn't take multiple napkins to eat.  They do have some of the most FANTASTIC vinegar cole slaw I've ever had and I've rarely enjoyed eating such marvelous fresh and crunchy stuff as this with such amazing flavor.   Besides the slaw I would probably not return here again as it is so similar to Corky's and the location is far out of my way.

This is a cool dive Italian restaurant in the usual Metairie strip mall.  The place is just old and kind of dirty the way you expect a dive joint to be.  The food is much better than I would have expected and it is some of the best  casual Italian food in the area that its in.  They even managed to surprise me as they serve their lasagna with a side of angel hair pasta and that's something I just haven't seen anywhere else at the local Italian places.  In addition to their pasta entrees they also have pizza and po boys. Overall I like both the dive ambiance and the food here along with the fact it is a great place to grab a quick lunch at a good value.

This location has had several bar and grills located inside it and so far the current one is the best.  They provide really good and friendly service along with some decent to good food.  It does seem to draw a mix of tourists and locals from the area and it actually has quite a spacious interior that can accomodate larger groups.

One of the oldest Yacht Clubs in the USA the SYC has a long and distinguished history in the annals of yachting.  This is the epicenter of sailing for the NOLA area and the club has some fantastic programs.  They have a nice pool area with a smaller kid friendly splash pool.  The clubhouse has nice facilities overlooking Lake Pontchartrain and the food is generally good to excellent depending on what you order.  This spot is always a hub of activity and it is certainly a popular venue for many events and activities.

This is the bar of New York Pizza.  I like this place for the fact they offer a $5 pint and a slice special which is a pretty awesome deal.  There isn't a limit on this special and you can just keep eating and drinking as many $5 slice/pints as you want.  They also offer the full menu of New York Pizza usually so you can get some good options here if you don't feel like pizza.  Some nights they stay open late and other nights they just close when they want to close.  The inconsistent hours is the main thing that irks me about this place but generally its a good place to grab a quick slice of pizza and a pint of beer.

Probably the best Little Tokyo location I've been to so far.  Larger portions and better service seem to characterize this spot.  The ambiance doesn't really scream sushi joint and is more generic restaurant.  Quick and easy spot to grab some food at a decent price and all day happy hour on Sundays.

This is the nearest sushi joint to my office and I eat here occasionally when I'm in a hurry.  I much prefer Kanno in Fat City but they have some strange hours sometimes and close for extended periods so this is a decent backup place when the need for sushi arises.  I also like Shogun but I hate dealing with Veteran's traffic not that Causeway is much better but this place is much closer to my office.  They generally have good selection and quality at decent prices.

This is a good basic bar with a dedicated local following.  It is like stepping back into the New Orleans of old as the place is actually in good repair while still having a vintage feel (so yes hipsters love to come here and attempt to absorb all the vintage they can).  The crowd is like many other NOLA neighborhood bars with a mix of young, old, dirty, clean, blue collar, white collar and just plain weird.  The prices are decent and they have good TVs for game days.  They have some bar grub and often will have crawfish during the season.  The parking can be a bit challenging sometimes as this area often seems to get crowded as there are several other attractions in the area.  My main complaint with this joint is that it can get too smokey for my tolerance.  Overall a decent place to hang out and enjoy some drinks among interesting folks.

The food here is very well prepared and has a nice balance of flavors with balanced spices.  This certainly ranks among the best Indian food I've ever eaten and it is also the most expensive I've ever eaten.  This is also the only Indian restaurant I've ever seen beef served and the sacred cow was divinely delicious.    The entrees here seem to vary widely in proportion so you should discuss this with your server prior to ordering.  The scallop dish seems to be one of the smaller entrees while the beef special ranked as one of the largest servings I've seen here.  The curried gumbo is really great and provides a marvelous Indian fusion spice up to a NOLA staple.  I was a bit disappointed in the small serving of naan that comes in an order when compared to the very generous portion you get at Nirvana.  The vegetable sides are quite pricey and the desserts are very over priced considering the very small portion size.  Generally I would stick to the entrees and specials along with a selection of the starters, such as the phenomenal gumbo, and skip the sides and desserts.

The owners went on some insane rampage and fired all the long time staff in this once great joint.  The burger seems to have really slipped in quality and the meat portion has gotten smaller.  Everybody that knew what they were doing seems to be gone so the once fantastic burger seems to have died with the departing of the long term staff.  Another great thing that just ain't there no more :(

It pretty much seems just like Phil's Grill but now a bit more expensive.  It isn't really bad but then it isn't really fantastic either.
