The cost of the food makes it a poor value for just a burger and I spent $20 for just a burger, cheese fries and iced tea.  At that price point I don't see any return visits.

This is a cool little music festival at the Mint and its FREE.  They used to hold it in conjunction with the Seafood Festival but that fest has grown too large and has branched off into its own big event so that has decreased the food options at this fest.  The Creole Tomato Fest is also going on at the same time as this event so you can check that out also.  They have some good music and this is a good opportunity to have a good time but the heat can make it a real challenge.

This is a Rouses on steroids.  They have an exotic meat section where they sell Vietnamese python meat.  The layout of the store takes a little getting used to as they have crammed so much stuff into a smaller space.  They have a lot going on in this place so it will probably take a few visits to take it all in so just grill some python, relax, and plan your next grocery shopping trip.  Although I'm not sure why we can't just get some of that giant invasive python from the Everglades to keep it local...

Hummm I'd have to rate this as one of the less good Chinese joints on the Carroltton corridor.  I've eaten inside which is a bit of a stark prospect and not a very enjoyable dining experience.  The food while not terrible isn't the most tasty and tends more towards the blah.  I'm probably not going to be tempted to ever make another visit here.

One of the best burgers in NOLA by far!!!  Huge sides that could be a meal in themselves.  One of the most unique selections of burgers anywhere I've ever seen in the area.  This is where I go when I'm craving a really good huge burger.  It also lets you enjoy your food in classic NOLA dive bar French Quarter style with attentive bar staff that keep your drinks full and keep things interesting.  I love the Bull Fighter Burger, Blue Cheese Burger, Chili Chedder Burger, and most of the others....   Those are some tasty burgers!!!  They could make them even better with some custom made buns.

Its still quite a popular mall but it seems to frequently have stores "disappear" from closing.  I rarely venture into this space as the parking seems insanely busy all the time.  This is really the only remaining true shopping mall experience with a large selection of stores and sizable food court left in the New Orleans area.  Now if only Banana Republic still had a Jeep coming out of their window and still sold Gurkha shorts I would be in 80's bliss!

I've been to all of these since they first started and I've still yet to get a po boy at the fest.  They always seem to run out of most things by the afternoon and there are almost always really long lines.  The problem I have is I hate lines and standing in line for a regular po boy I can get all the time in NOLA isn't going to cut it and I only want the "special" po boys you generally can only get at this fest.  The challenge is the "special" po boys sell out fast and rapidly develop long lines.  I arrived right as the fest was opening last year and there were already lines!  Ahhhh standing in line for a sandwich I just can't take it...  The crowds are also completely out of control packed and make it a misery to attempt to walk down Oak Street.  They really need to extend this fest to more days or to a larger area.

Another new place that has jumped on the recent rolled ice cream fad.  They have a much shorter line and slightly better prices than the very popular rolled ice cream joint in the Bywater.  They have a decent selection of flavors and quite a lot of seating inside.  This is definitely a very family friendly place and it seems quite popular with kids in the area.  The service seems to be faster than I've seen at other rolled ice cream joints in the greater New Orleans area as well.  They have an interesting space here and seem to have invested some time with doing some decorating of the place in bright and cheerful tones.

This is the best Academy in the GNO area and probably the all around best place to shop for your sporting gear.  They consistently have the best selection of firearms and maintain the largest selection of ammo of just about any other sporting goods or firearms dealer in the area.  The prices on their firearms are generally significantly lower than any other local competitors.  They have a nice selection of local team fan gear for both professional and college levels.  They often have nice surprises in the sale racks.  The fishing, hunting, sports and fitness sections are well stocked as are their clothing and shoe areas.  This is generally the best place to start when looking for something you need in the sports and outdoors genre.  Academy also sells hunting and fishing licenses for those that might need them at the last minute.

This venue has a small bar space downstairs with the majority of the venue being upstairs.  They have two large bar areas upstairs along with a nice outdoor patio with some nice comfy patio furniture.  I find the drink prices at night to be a bit too expensive, as many places in the Quarter are, and I'm not sure if they ever do drink specials or have a happy hour as I've never been in early enough to discover that.  I've also only been here for crowded events so I'm not sure what its like on less crowded nights.  The ambiance is quite nice and they have made a really nice space here.  It is more of a fancy club scene with VIP options which isn't really my favorite type of venue as I prefer just a plain old bar or live music venue and I hate DJs.  Most of the bartenders here are really nice but I have run into one surly grumpy one before.  This place does attract quite a horde of very nice looking ladies but it does seem to attract a much younger crowd generally.

This is a pretty cool bar and one of the best places to watch jazz.  They also have a nice second floor.  The cover charge can be a bit steep sometimes by Frenchmen St. standards.  This place can also be very touristy and some of the folks here want a concert hall type atmosphere instead of a bar atmosphere and will shush you.  I'm generally more into being all fun and rowdy and not being seated all quietly so I don't end up here much as I get shushed a lot.  I appreciate jazz as a great music and it was largely developed in the famous Storyville brothels of New Orleans where you didn't ever get shushed.  I enjoy New Orleans Jazz the way it was meant to be experienced.

Wow this place has nearly totally collapsed from what it used to be at its prime.  This used to be a really amazing mall and had lots of fantastic stores.  Unfortunately this place has been on hard times for a long while now.  I never go to this mall anymore and I rarely did before as its waaay out in the suburbs.  I was really shocked at how deserted its gotten when I made my last visit out here.  Back in its prime it did have a lot of hot ladies dressed to impress which it certainly doesn't seem to have anymore but I guess the same can be said of the bygone glory days of Canal Street...

This is probably the best Middle Eastern/Kosher restaurant in Metairie.  They have different lunch specials daily and a solid regular menu.  I've enjoyed everything I've eaten here and they have several dishes that generally are not found at other Middle Eastern restaurants in the area.  The prices usually seem a bit more expensive than other restaurants of a similar type but you also seem to often get a bit healthier portions depending on what you order.  While it is located in the typical Metairie ugly strip mall hell they do their best to redeem the interior with an atmosphere that is one of the most intricately decorated among restaurants of this type.

This is a small little bar located (and connected to) directly behind the Azalea Grill.  They have a nice side patio that's actually larger than the interior of the bar.  They have crawfish boils every Friday (during the season), ladies night on Wednesday and other specials along with occasional live music.  The patio definitely seems like an awesome hidden away spot to enjoy a nice day.  This is certainly one of the cooler bars on Jeff Hwy and I will certainly be returning to enjoy the patio.  They only have a Facebook page and no direct website so Yelp won't let me enter that for the address so you will just have to use Google to find that page.

They have a parking lot but currently almost all of it is filled with picnic tables (perhaps in preperation for Gretna Fest) so parking can be a bit of a challenge as this is a very popular lunch spot.  They have some cute and friendly waitresses here that generally take good care of you.  The roast beef po boy is decent and is of the pulled variety but they only have a small size and the bread I had mine served on was toasted way too hard and crunchy.  The burger is a better choice here but they also have a wide variety of items to select from on the menu.  This is one of the better bars in Gretna and I usually only end up here during Gretna Fest but will occassionally stop in for lunch when I'm in the area.  My biggest complaint about this place is they don't serve fresh brewed iced tea and use the aborrent fountain type instead.

Mr. Santos has always been quick, pretty affordable and even downright cheap for lots of things I've needed a tailor for.  I've had many pants hemmed by him and well as things taken up and let out.  He has also gotten me out of some embarrassing jams like one time when I had a zipper on my fly rip off during a conference in Metairie he was able to get a new one sewn on in about 10 minutes and save me a drive back to Uptown to change into a new pair of pants.  Numerous times he has sewn buttons on for free for me.  Mr. Santos has always done efficient and quality work and I would certainly recommend him for your tailoring needs.

I really want to like Herbsaint, as it has a fantastic location and great ambiance, but I've just never been excited by the food here.  I've eaten here many times and I've always been left HUNGRY as the portions are always too small for me (and I doubt I will eat here again without some major temptation).  They do make fantastic drinks and the bar, although very small, can be fun at times (especially during Wednesdays on the Square to beat the heat and enjoy the A/C).  The service has always been excellent and the bartenders are usually on top of their game.  For the portion size and what you get I generally find the food is just is a poor value and my money is much better spent elsewhere to eat but this is a good place to drink.

Decent food for a tourist trap with slightly inflated prices due to the location.  They have acceptable boiled shrimp and crawfish.  The seafood gumbo is good and the fried items have a nice spice to them.  The ambiance isn't very spectacular and the bathrooms are upstairs which could be problematic for some folks.  The food is brought out pretty haphazardly with some people getting served quickly and others at the same table still waiting for their food 15 minutes later.  The servers do their best to keep things flowing well but it often gets crowded so that causes challenges.

This place was really more like a 2.5 star overall.  The staff were really nice but they were a bit slow on refilling my iced tea even though there were very few people in the restaurant.  The building and atmosphere were nice and much nicer than I thought they would be.  The food really disappointed me as it was served in really small dainty portions and the flavors were not very impressive.  I got the Gulf fish and it was a really small portion that made it a very poor value and only a snack with both the fish and watermelon/olive accompaniment being a bit bland.  My friend got the goat tacos and I got to eat one of those and I found it very tough and dry without a lot of flavor.  The dessert I had was probably the best thing I ate and it was a zucchini bread served with peaches and a blueberry syrup.  Overall I'm not sure I would have a great deal of motivation to return as I'm not into dainty small portions and bland flavor but the ingredients all seemed to be quality and fresh so there is certainly potential for a better experience.

I've been going to Tips for many years and I've seen many shows.  I've had friends in bands and gotten to hang out backstage.  I've been to many a New Year's Party and more special events here than I can even begin to count.  I've even seen midget wrestling here.  Ultimately Tips is just a fantastic venue and has some fantastic bartenders.  They often have shows that will run until dawn so make sure to pay attention to the music schedule.  The bathrooms can get nasty as there are some nasty people out there but thankfully it is now non-smoking and you can breath fresh air in here.  This is a place to dance, drink, and enjoy yourself in a crowd so don't think you will be sitting down and having lots of personal space to yourself.

This is one of the better spots to watch some music on Frenchmen and they often don't have a cover.  The crowd can be pretty variable in here and it can be hit or miss a lot of times depending on what other bands are playing in the area.  I've always had relatively quick service here with some above average issues with my order being wrong as the bar is so close to the band that it is often hard to communicate or hear anything.  When on Frenchmen it is certainly one of the main venues to investigate.

The lasagna here has the most meat of any lasagna I've ever had and they also offer it in an Alfredo sauce version if you prefer (I couldn't finish the full size version so the half size lunch portion might be the best choice).  The roast beef po boy here probably has the most meat on it of any roast beef po boy I've ever eaten so plan accordingly as it is also quite nice and sloppy.  They have very large burgers and will often do daily special burgers.  The seafood gumbo here is quite respectable and is usually of the hard gumbo crab with shrimp variety.  They offer a lot of bang for the buck here and portions are huge.  Service is fast and friendly here and they have some nice specials.  The only downside is the location and parking make it a bit dangerous to get in and out of the tight space on the angled road that doesn't have the best viability.

This is a nifty boutique chocolate store that has some very interesting and often local themed confections.  This is a great place to get a tasty gift for those who love all things chocolate.  I personally ate about 100 pieces of their chocolate this past Christmas so I might possibly have sampled almost every "flavor" of chocolate that they offer (including the blue frog... yes they really have a blue frog chocolate).  Every time I've visited this store they seem to have something new and interesting so it is always a great place to check out.

If you grew up watching the Dukes of Hazzard like I did then there is only one way to review this place.  In summary:  KICK ASS!!!  This place is fantastic for all things about those Duke Boys and sometimes ole Cooter himself is around to further kick this place up to Infinite KICK ASS levels of AWESOMENESS!!!  I'm going to go shoot my bow now (obviously with some arrows attached to dynamite) before I call it a day so I can then start hitting up some of Uncle Jesse's special distilled magic and just wait for Daisy to show up and demo some wrastlin moves with me before we take a romantic ride off in the General Lee to ramp off some dirt embankments.

For my 1000th review I want to give a big loving Yelp hug to my neighborhood.  Yelp gimped up my 1000th review and put it under a place it did not belong in its quest to associate everything with a business but this is a neighborhood not a business.  I had to delete that review and yet again add my neighborhood.  The Garden District is my home and where I live.  This is one of the most beautiful areas of New Orleans and has some of the most amazing architecture.  There are amazing restaurants and fun bars.  This is a prime place to catch Carnival Parades and St. Patrick's events.  There isn't anywhere else like this neighborhood in the world and I love living here!

This place is a bit different from your typical Tex-Mex joint and offers some things most of the other area Mexican type places don't as the Honduran owners put their own slightly different spin to some things.  They have their "cebollitas" grilled green onion appetizer that is tasty.  They offer the usual taco, burrito, and other options wrapped in some type of tortilla like most Mexican joints do.  I usually opt for one of the entree platters to get a selection of several different things.  This is one of the few places to offer beef tongue as a meat option to stuff your taco or other tortilla wrapped entity.  This place does frequently get crowded and nearby parking is at a premium so it can be more challenging to get here than the usual restaurants in this area so if driving be prepared to park further away and walk a bit.

DBA is probably the bar I like the best on Frenchmen as they have a great beer selection and they usually have some of the best music.  I think their beers are overpriced for New Orleans but other than that I've usually had a good time here.  There is usually a good crowd in here but it is rarely so crazy crowded that you can't get a good spot to watch the band.  The bartenders are usually pretty quick and efficient and I've rarely had bad service.  Always a good mix of locals and tourists so there is almost always the opportunity to meet new and interesting people.  I'm also really happy they have gone smoke free!!!

This is quite an interesting venue that has a vintage ambiance with a hint of rustic to it.  They host a variety of events here from art exhibits to pop up restaurants.  I attended the Mosquito Supper Club's fais do do brunch here and it was like being transported out into the bayou to a Cajun house party.  There was not a lot of table space for eating and the chairs were quite small and uncomfortable as they want you to hurry up and eat to get out on the dance floor  as quick as possible.  Overall this space provided a good environment for a fun event in an unique space that fit it perfectly.

I've been eating in this place since they were on Vet's in Metairie and now they have moved into my neighborhood and are much more convenient for me to access.  The food here is generally good and they have some Korean style noodle soups that are decent.  They have both a "Chinese" and "American" menu but many of the items are the same on both menus with some notable exceptions.  This place has always been easy to get in and out of and I've never had to wait to eat.  They did irk me a bit the last time I ate there on St. Patrick's night when I ordered a dinner special and they then didn't bring me anything but the entree and said I just ordered that when I had POINTED on the menu to the "Dinner Special" that came with soup and egg roll. If you are in the area and need a quick and good meal this place will meet your needs.

Ahhh the food is ok and the ambiance is not my style at all.  There are usually some decent looking women in this place but it is always so loud that any attempts at conversation are usually futile.  It also can take unacceptably long times to get your food here and often service is extremely SLOW with everything.  I have literally sat for an hour waiting for my completed sushi order ticket to be taken and longer still for my drink to be delivered and that was at the sushi bar.  The food here is consistent but nothing that has ever excited me as it has always just been... ok.  It is very rare I ever go here and usually only when I'm with other people that want to go here.

This place is located in a small little snack stand of a structure and you can only order Mexican food to go at the walk up window.  It has tiny little tacos just like the kind you get out of a real Mexican taco truck except they are less good than most I've ever had out of those trucks.  I got the chicken tacos and they were way more dry and flavorless than most any other I've had.  I think the tacos at Taqueria Guerrero are much better for this "authentic" style of Mexican taco.  I've only had the tacos and usually the only time I'm in this area I'm heading to 9 Roses for some pho so given the choice between these tacos and pho I will go pho nearly every time.  Pho sure!

Mid-City's attempt at a New York style/Pizza Delicious style pie.  While the size is comparable the pizza flavor and quality is not.  Its an "ok" pizza but the crust is very chewy and if you attempt to eat it the next day it will be very tough and hard.  For the price I would much prefer Theo's in Mid-City.

Dear Tips,  Raising the price of Abita Amber to $5 and the for real imports to $6 is just a rip off and pure greed!  I can go to Maple Leaf and most places Uptown and on Frenchmen and get cheaper beer and watch great music.  I simply can't afford to pay cover and then shell out $5 for a beer that I can buy for $13 a 12 pack or go to Ms. Mae's up the street and get for $2.50.  I've been a VERY good customer for years but I'm not paying that much for a LOCAL beer!  I might show up for a few shows but far fewer than in the past and I will be doing all my drinking at Ms. Mae's and not at Tip's during those shows.  Maybe if I smoked weed it wouldn't matter so much but I don't and I only like my beer.  Y'all have the freedom in our great country to charge whatever you like but the market dictates to me that you are way out of line with the value of what you're selling so I ain't buying no more.  $5 for Yuengling is outrageous!!!

This place gets really crowded for games and it can get a bit sardine can style packed at times.  The bartenders at not the fastest and some of them seem pretty surly and grumpy to even be there.  The crowd at my last visit was way too hipster for my preference as hipsters love to spread their miserable angst ridden ways to everybody as they hate joyful mirth.  I have to say that the nearby Von Elrod's Beer Hall and the Germantown Pub are just a much more pleasant and fun environments during game time.

This is a Metry dive bar (on that lovely strip mall hell known as Veterans Memorial Blvd) that pushes their Swamp Burger.  I've only been here a handful of times and it was always to eat.  I've only stopped in as I've been driving past the bar and see their sign that it even comes to mind that I should stop in for a Swamp Burger.  It is a nice sized meaty burger just not as big as I was expecting from all the hype they give it.  There are a few other things on the menu but I've never tried them but all the prices seem pretty reasonable.  The ambiance is your usual Metairie dive  bar with sports paraphernalia everywhere and it seems it usually has female bartenders that range from sweet to a bit gruff.  One of my visits ended up being on lingerie night (where women just walk around and "model" lingerie) so that definitely made the burger taste better for that trip.  If you're in the area it is worth a visit to sample the burger but I wouldn't make a special trip.

The most comfortable bar in a greenhouse I've yet been to.  It was pretty cold outside on my last visit but a nice fire was going outside keeping it nice and then inside was all toasty warm as well.  The beer prices were quite fair and the service was friendly and efficient.  This spot in Green Hills also makes do as a decent sports bar as they have a good number of TVs about the place to watch your preferred event.  I saw mostly preppy SEC type folks in here and hardly any hipsters so hopefully that is the normal crowd in here for college games as nobody likes nasty surly hipsters not even other nasty surly hipsters.  Decent crowd of folks seem to frequent this place with a focus just on having fun making this just an easy spot to kick back and enjoy yourself.    Overall this is certainly a unique place with a great laid back vibe where it is natural just to have fun like a plant growing in the sun.  Tip:  Don't eat or drink the fertilizer that's for plants not humans.

Dear Tips,  Raising the price of Abita Amber to $5 and the for real imports to $6 is just a rip off and pure greed!  I can go to Maple Leaf and most places Uptown and on Frenchmen and get cheaper beer and watch great music.  I simply can't afford to pay cover and then shell out $5 for a beer that I can buy for $13 a 12 pack or go to Ms. Mae's up the street and get for $2.50.  I've been a VERY good customer for years but I'm not paying that much for a LOCAL beer!  I might show up for a few shows but far fewer than in the past and I will be doing all my drinking at Ms. Mae's and not at Tip's during those shows.  Maybe if I smoked weed it wouldn't matter so much but I don't and I only like my beer.  Y'all have the freedom in our great country to charge whatever you like but the market dictates to me that you are way out of line with the value of what you're selling so I ain't buying no more.

I used to hang out here all the time before Katrina when it was Moonlight and it seems they have made many improvements in the space with each of the restaurants that have followed and developed into the current Down the Hatch (they just recently added an improved patio in the back).  They advertised a night time happy hour from 11pm til 2am one time when I was there but then they didn't have it when I returned so that made me a bit unhappy (along with the fact they were OUT of roast beef for the roast beef po boy).  They do have some mighty tasty burgers here and I really do enjoy eating those here.  They have bison and lamb burgers available sometimes as well.  I would like to sample the roast beef po boy but I as I mentioned before I was foiled in my attempt.  This place is usually open til 2am so it is a great late spot to grab a tasty burger or sample some of the other things on their menu.

This is a nicer bar with a wine focus that comes with a nice courtyard and indoor seating.  The owners are the same folks that own Tropical Isle and they are often in here and they seem like very nice people.  I've yet to eat in here but the menu looks to have some good things available and I plan on sampling the food soon.  I've enjoyed several drinks here and this is definitely a nice spot to escape the madness of Bourbon street and certainly a step above most of the dive bars in the Quarter.

It's a big corporate chain but at least they are offering healthy organic products.  They probably offer the best soft corn tortillas I've had in NOLA and you get a huge amount of food for substantially less than most other options.  I'm usually not a fan of chains and fast food but Chipotle offers a fresh and healthy alternative that dominates their niche.

This place offers a decent selection of entrees and sandwiches in the Elmwood area.  I was a bit disappointed that they only offer one size of po boy and don't give you the option for a half or whole and honestly I found the size they offer is on the half size which left me a bit hungry still.  They do some traditional NOLA dishes with a bit of a unique spin so this is certainly a spot to check out for  a quick meal with some more unique choices than offered in many other places in this price range.

This is a VERY popular ice cream joint and people stand in quite long lines to get their fix.  I drove past this location several times on several trips to Nashville when the lines were just longer than I was going to deal with and after many attempts I finally scored a good time with no line outside.  There was still a line inside so I waited for my time to get up to order and finally got to see the different options available and I also got to see it also is on the expensive side for a small serving.  I made my choice and sat down to enjoy my ice cream and it was alright but I have certainly had better so I'm not really sure what the hype is all about that rates standing in line so long but these days in Nashville there seem to be lines all over the place for all sorts of things.

They have an upstairs to go along with their downstairs and usually have some good live music.  This is generally one of the main spots to stop in and check out during a visit to Frenchmen.  Usually there is no cover and the crowd is always a decent size while usually not getting overcrowded.  The only thing I'm not the biggest fan of is that their drinks are more expensive than Blue Nile and DBA.

It's like Nirvana but on Metairie Road!  That would be Nirvana Indian Restaurant not the actual state of "Nirvana" because the same folks that own Nirvana also own this place but you might still find your actual Nirvana here if you love Indian food.  I've been eating here for many years and they have the same type of buffet deal as Nirvana.  The food choices are a bit different and the set up is much smaller but it is still some decent Indian food and one of the two choices you have in Metairie for Indian other than Tandori Chicken.  The parking lot here is really crazy, tight, and you have to park at a really weird angle so getting out can be a challenge if you aren't used to it.

The lunch specials are really not very impressive to me and I don't find them to be a good value.  In fact I would NEVER eat the Monday special of the Cuban steak ever again.  Perhaps the other items on the menu are far better but after sampling several of the lunch specials I'm just not impressed.  They do provide very rapid turn around on your order and the specials are served within minutes of ordering them.  Service is non-existent here and you just order at the counter and they put your food out on the counter when its ready.  Pho Orchid is a block away from here and I much prefer lunch there.  I will return to sample the dinner menu at some point and see if that brings some greater love to the disappointment I've experienced here so far.

This is just a great old school honky tonk music hall with a lot of history.  The beers are cold and the music is fantastic.  It was mostly older folks cutting a rug out on the dance floor but they have far better moves than most young folks I've seen so I enjoyed watching their skillful dancing along with the great music.  This is a nice spot to catch some great music for the price of what you pay for your drinks. Friendly folks, great bartenders, great music and just a great time along with very easy parking.

This is a HUGE space accompanied with a mega sports bar with lots of TVs and generally it's quite a nice ambiance.  I still must profess I prefer the original location in Metairie which might be among the handful of times I prefer Metairie to the city limits.  While this is an amazing spot where you can get the fantastic charbroiled oysters and other Drago's signature items just like at the original location it seems to cater to a majority tourist crowd so I favor the more local feel of the original.  You still can have some great food and fun times here so if you've never had a Drago's charbroiled oyster there is no time like NOW!  Overall I prefer the lower prices, better service and usually better food at the original Fat City location in Metairie but I'm always up for some oysters.

P & J is a New Orleans institution that has been around for generations!  Almost all the best restaurants get their oysters from P & J.  The BP oil spill hit them hard but they're back up and roaring.  These are generally among the highest quality oysters available anywhere in the area.

This place took some adventuring for me to locate and it looked rather scary on the outside but the staff was very accommodating and friendly on the inside.  The atmosphere is definitely that of a run down dive restaurant but they certainly are not going to let you go hungry in here.  I ordered the chicken parmesan and what I was served might be the largest example of that dish I've ever been served.  The food was certainly not the best I've ever eaten but they definitely give you value for your money here.

This is pretty basic and overall pretty bland Mexican food located at the small corner of a strip mall.  The service is nice but you had certainly better point to the exact item on the menu you want or you might get something else.  This is the kind of Mexican food that makes me not such a big fan of Mexican food as most of the selections are just something rolled up into a tortilla of some kind and in the end most things end up tasting exactly the same as each other.  They do have some decent combos and you can get some items not rolled into a tortilla.  Overall basic and very bland Mexican that will please the most New England spice hater.  The Margaritas will work some special magic on you sometimes though and then if you check out the patio it might turn into a fiesta.

I tried this place out for lunch and Chef Ron was there to greet us and he took our order.  He explained that everything was made fresh from the best ingredients and sourced locally whenever possible.  He also explained that it might take a little longer to get our food since everything was prepared fresh but I found the timing to be very fast and efficient.  The gumbo was ok but didn't seem to have very much seafood in it and was a bit bland for my taste.  The roast beef po boy is pretty good and it was a sliced style with a thinner gravy.  It wasn't my favorite gumbo or roast beef po boy but it was "ok" and it is close to my office so I will probably give it a few more tries as they do have some good looking things on the menu and Chef Ron seems like a real stand up guy.

This is one of several of this chain of hispanic markets that offers a wide range of Latin American groceries.  They also have a very busy deli and bakery offering an impressive array of items in impressive serving sizes for comparatively miniscule prices.  They have many Latin American things that your typical grocery will typically not have.  For just the deli and bakery this place is worth a visit.

The Cabildo is part of the Louisiana State Museum and features exhibits about the history and heritage of Louisiana.  The building features Spanish and French architecture and has served many functions during its history with most of them being governmental.  This building was the site of the Louisiana Purchase transfer ceremonies in 1803.  If you're looking at the front of St. Louis Cathedral the Cabildo is to the left of the church.    Admission price:  Adults  $6 Students, Senior Citizens, Active Military  $5 Children 12 and under  Free Groups of 15 or more w/ reservations  20% discount School groups w/ reservations  Free Purchase tickets for two or more museums  20% discount AAA membership discount, with card  10% discount

This is a cool little bar that is part of a house right in the middle of a residential neighborhood.  I recently discovered this joint during my adventures along the Metairie Road St. Patrick's parade.  It is a long rectangular building with a long bar that covers most of the length of the structure.  We had a cute bartendress, that is also a nurse, and she took good care of us during our visit.  We learned that they frequently have free food here and that this is a popular spot in the area to watch Saints games.  During my visit they had some sausage pasta and mac n' cheese.  There were some serious smokers in here so I really didn't enjoy that aspect of this establishment.  I met some interesting characters in here and I even got invited to go on a  fishing trip to Grand Isle.  This seems like a nice secret spot to go and grab a few drinks and there are certainly some friendly and interesting people in here.

This is a really great Italian joint in Rivertown that offers a lot of bang for your buck.  There was another Italian restaurant right next door to this one several years ago that wasn't such a hit so if you are recalling hearing about less than good Italian in Rivertown it will be that now closed establishment and not this great spot.  The space is pleasing with classic Italian themed music and attentive service.  The huge meatballs here with their very affordable and amazing "Meatball Gendusa" appetizer being one of the stars of the show will certainly please the largest of appetites.  The po boys are very nice here and priced at a great value.  The pizza is done very well and they have really nice roasted garlic as one of their toppings that will cure what craving you might need in the hunger and flavor department along with a more than fair price.    Overall this is fantastic food at a fantastic price in a nice restaurant in the cool area of Rivertown.

This is an interesting joint that has the unique offering of serving several wild game options.  Since I'm an old mean animal killing hunter carnivore I do like to eat some wild game so obviously I was just like a moth to flame here.  They really do have an extensive menu here and even if the thought of wild game terrifies you and your Vegan soul demands non-animal protein grub they will still likely have something here you can stuff your face with.  I really liked the interior decor which was lots of taxidermy meets old wooden shack aesthetic and just made me feel right at home.  The food was nothing outstanding but it was solid descent food that trended more to the bland side for my taste but since I live in New Orleans I'm used to a large degree more spice kick than the average diner.  Overall I would certainly never hesitate to grab a meal here and they really provide a cool environment along with some unique food items not easily found in most restaurants.

This is an Italian food and po boy joint located in a mini strip mall on Veteran's (aka strip mall hell).  The food is ok here and they offer the only version of a "seafood muffaletta" I've seen other than at Johnny's Po Boy's.  They have a few other specials and pasta dishes in addition to their large po boy selection.  The service is usually rapid and the lines still seem much shorter than they were before Katrina.  This is always a good place for a quick lunch but sometimes the portions are a bit small for my appetite.

This bakery puts out very hearty loaves made with as much locally sourced grain as possible and in fact the owner is leading a movement to establish more local sources for grains.  Personally I am not a fan of white bread and like my bread dark and full of whole grains and the Bellegarde breads certainly deliver in the hearty strong category and blow the weak white bread options away.  The bread is so hearty and many varieties so chewy I find them not always the best suited for sandwiches and some varieties are better used in other applications or just stand well on their own.  My favorite Bellegarde bread so far is the Country Rye.

Looks like a really cool dive bar from the outside but when you go inside ouch it is waaaay too smokey.  This was the smokiest place I encountered during my whole visit to Nashville and it was even more smokey than Santa's Pub.  I couldn't stand being turned into a ham so I had to get outta there as fast as I could and instead planted myself next door at nice and smoke free Tenn Sixteen.

Ahhh Drago's charbroiled oysters are a beautiful thing to see, smell, and slurp a few dozen down like the addict to them I am!!!  What's better than getting 3 dozen grilled and another dozen or two raw???  The downside is nothing is exactly cheap at Drago's but it is cheaper at this location than their new space at the Hilton.  I'm also rather disappointed in the portion size of their fish lunch specials as you get about three times as much fish at nearby Acropolis for a much lower price.    They have a lot of great seafood options and are one of the few local places that offers lobster as a consistent special on their lunch menu.  The other menu options are very good and they also offer a good selection of po boys.  They have some really good gumbo and lots of changing daily seafood specials.  Did I mention the oysters and how you just have to eat those charbroiled oysters.  Excuse me I have to go somewhere... must have oysters now!!!

Honestly in the world of national chain fast food sandwiches I think Subway does a better sandwich.  Why would you even want to eat at this option when you could get a locally made po boy from a local business that would keep more money in the local economy?  This store seems generally well run and clean along with keeping a pretty good volume of business so I guess they are doing something right but it just isn't my cup of tea.

This is a really great Italian joint in Rivertown that offers a lot of bang for your buck.  There was another Italian restaurant right next door to this one several years ago that wasn't such a hit so if you are recalling hearing about less than good Italian in Rivertown it will be that now closed establishment and not this great spot.  The space is pleasing with classic Italian themed music and attentive service.  The huge meatballs here with their very affordable and amazing "Meatball Gendusa" appetizer being one of the stars of the show will certainly please the largest of appetites.  The po boys are very nice here and priced at a great value.  The pizza is done very well and they have really nice roasted garlic as one of their toppings that will cure what craving you might need in the hunger and flavor department along with a more than fair price.    Overall this is fantastic food at a fantastic price in a nice restaurant in the cool area of Rivertown.  Gendusa's Italian Market video review:  https://youtu.be/a8Q-y4jAXIk

This seems to be a very popular coffee shop for the night time study crowd.  They also have a nice board with upcoming music shows and other events posted.  The coffee was not the best to me but it was not the worst either.  The tables seem too small to me for comfortable studying but I guess I'm old and used to books and notebooks instead of all electronic all the time but I still need to write things down myself to really help my memory take them up but maybe that is my outdated brainwashing from my ancient schooling jading my opinion (except for the research that proves otherwise).

New Orleans Ice Cream Company has some pretty nifty local themed and often sourced flavors of premium ice cream.  This brand can be a bit of a challenge to find and so far I have only seen it at local groceries like Rouse's, Zara's, Langenstein's, Dorignac's, Breaux Mart, Fresh Market, Winn-Dixie and Whole Foods.  Their Po Boy Ice Cream sandwich is probably the finest ice cream sandwich I have ever had and I believe Parkway Bakery offers those also.  I first tried their ice cream at a Yelp event and I have been a fan ever since.  This stuff has to be really good to occasionally break me away from my normal Creole Creamery and Angelo Brocato's addiction.

The gumbo here is a 2 star and most of the sandwiches hover between a 2 and 3 for me.  I find the BBQ shrimp po boy alright but it is probably one of my least favorite versions of it in the NOLA area.  The "Breathtaking Beef" roast beef po boy has always disappointed me as it sounds fantastic but tastes bland and I've never been able to taste any horseradish on it.  The garlic oyster po boy and the Reuben are probably the best sandwiches made here.  The seafood platters and shrimp remoulade are also good as are some of the daily specials.  The ambiance of this place is the biggest redeeming factor as it is a complete and total classic New Orleans dive with lots of character and characters that can be seen here.

This is one of the best po boy joints in the area.  They excel in everything from roast beef to seafood (both grilled and fried).  Unfortunately they close before dinner so this is mainly a lunch spot and there is limited seating.  The biggest issues here are that they only take cash (which is always a huge hassle) and it is usually slow (which if you're getting quality I don't mind and usually you do here).  Rumor says they have the best shrimp po boy in the city and I probably can't argue that point.  The roast beef is also among my top choices and is very multiple napkin worthy.  This is a classic New Orleans po boy joint atmosphere and a unique local experience that everybody should sample.

I checked this place out for their opening weekend.  It will be a cool place to enjoy a German style beer garden.  The main food options are almost totally pork based with even the no-pork options seeming to be stuffed with some kind of sausage or pork item.  I am disappointed they only had a pork schnitzel as I love some veal, chicken, beef and venison schnitzel.  They have some appetizer snacks like pretzels and such and actually had a small but decent dessert menu.  Overall this should be a good addition to the neighborhood but I really hope they expand the schnitzel offerings for those of us that don't eat that pig meat.  *Update: they have added chicken schnitzel.

This appears to be a simple spaghetti or pizza place from the outside but when you walk inside you discover it is actually an intimate restaurant doing Northern Italian in a fine dining atmosphere.  Even though the restaurant's atmosphere seems to be fine dining most of the customers seem to be dressed causally.  This might be one of the smallest restaurants in the entire city but there always appear to be people sitting outside enjoying themselves at the sidewalk tables.  From memory the servers recite the longest and most deliciously detailed descriptions of their daily specials that I've ever heard at any restaurant.  The menu has a good selection of other options if by some improbable chance the specials don't entice you.  My biggest disappointment here is that I'm not a fan of their lasagna and I would certainly recommend steering clear of that.  The pasta prices are rather expensive for pasta and I think the meat and seafood entrees are often better choices if you don't go with the specials.

The most dive of dive bars and it is ALWAYS Christmas!!!  The dedicated don't even go til 4am but happy hour is 9pm-Midnight.  It is a glorious dream & dank nightmare that blurs and melds into an alcohol induced numbness of sensation that both terrifies and fascinates all at once (damn that tiny evil Santa!).  Always an interesting crowd and the most unusual things to see and hear going on.  Usually some pretty good music being played by the bartenders and somehow shots (usually Jager or Jamison) always end up being put in front of you whether you ordered them, want them, or even run from them.  I've seen & experienced some very strange things in this filthy glorious place but I don't recommend sitting on the couch just from what I've seen.  Sadly when the sun comes up they kick everybody out and make them go home (or to Ms. Mae's or Brother's Three but that is another story).

How strange I used to have a review for this establishment but yet AGAIN somehow YELP has made it disappear???  Gordon Biersch has some good beers they brew and good food.  Out of all the various restaurants operating in the Harrah's Casino sphere this is probably one of the best.  They have some decent deals on beer samplers and offer some decent specials for their happy hour.  When it is nice outside they also have one of the better outdoor dining areas/beer gardens in this area as well.  As an army vet I also want to give an extra THANKS to Gordon Biersch for offering military veterans a free meal on Veterans Day and I would really like to offer my great appreciation for this fantastic gesture they offer to vets.  Overall this is one of the better spots for good and affordable food and drink in the immediate area, although it is a national chain that won't give you the local NOLA flavor like you can at some of the other spots nearby, this establishment is the only brewery in the Harrah's area so that is something to consider.

I've eaten at the original Parran's Poboys in Metairie many times but this was my first experience in this location.  It was a bit bittersweet to me coming here as I was a big fan of the sushi joint that was here previously and it was really strange to me seeing how much of the space had been moved around and changed.  I certainly felt a bit like a fish out of water and a man out of time with how so much had changed in here.  Of course I ordered a poboy combo and as it has always been in the past Parran's put out a good product and I enjoyed my poboys.  I don't know if I will ever quite get used to this being a Parrran's instead of my long time sushi joint but it is a nice addition to this area.  Overall Parran's has a long history of doing good food but I still think there is more character at their original location in Metairie while the food is good at both locations.  My video review of Parran's Poboys Uptown is here: https://youtu.be/Vc7HhfiMI98

This is one of the best po'boy joints in the New Orleans area.  They excel in everything from roast beef to seafood (both grilled and fried).  Unfortunately they close before dinner so this is mainly a lunch spot and there is limited seating. Rumor says they have the best shrimp po'boy in the city and I probably can't argue that point.  The roast beef is also among my top choices for a sliced style roast beef and is very multiple napkin worthy.  If you don't want a po'boy they also have some great listed daily specials on the menu along with chalkboard specials that are also fantastic choices which have included gumbo, oyster artichoke soup, shrimp stew etc. etc. which give you more options of deliciousness! Overall this is a classic New Orleans po'boy joint atmosphere and a unique local experience that everybody should sample.    My video review of Guy's Po'Boys is here: https://youtu.be/asgRGYpUcgg

I LOVE Deutches Haus so much I joined and became a member!  I'm German on both sides of my family so it just seemed like the natural thing to do.  It was a very sad loss when the old Mid-City location got "taken" by the hospital development that still isn't developing.  The current temporary location of the Haus in Metairie is certainly not as much fun as the historic location BUT the new location is going to be AWESOME and is right next to the Fairgrounds.  The Haus is renowned for Oktoberfest but they have MANY events and festivals throughout the year.  They also run the Haus like a bar from Wed-Sat so you can just stop in for some awesome German beer.  I think Deutches Haus is a fantastic organization and I highly recommend anyone that is of German ancestry, interested in German culture, or just interested in having fun check it out and consider becoming a member.

Leni's Café is one of the most affordable restaurants for New Orleans breakfast and lunch in the Warehouse District.  Many locals say it is their choice for the best value for a New Orleans breakfast restaurant in the area. Leni's Café is a popular neighborhood spot for the residents and workers in the Warehouse District. Leni's Café has become noted for their affordable daily plate lunch specials that feature a lot of great New Orleans and Southern food. This is a great spot for breakfast and lunch with daily specials, burgers, po-boys and other traditional New Orleans food.  Overall this place offers some great value on good food.  My video review of Leni's Restaurant is here:  https://youtu.be/C3NY-U-x-l4

I'm not a coffee shop person as I would rather have beer than coffee.  If you find yourself in need of a coffee shop this is a beautiful location in an old bank.  They have a large downstairs, sidewalk seating and a cool upstairs so you can find the perfect nook to use your computer, study, read, stalk the other coffee shop patrons or whatever it is that people do in coffee shops.  I've stopped in here a few times to use the WiFi and it seems like it usually has decent connectivity and speed.  You should keep in mind that this joint is frequently very crowded and they only take cash.  The coffee isn't anything outstanding and cost more than coffee should and in this area I would rather go to Cooter Brown's to use their WiFi and drink beer.

The Ogden museum is five floors and they have a rooftop patio at the top.  This museum showcases all aspects of Southern culture with permanent collections and rotating exhibits and includes a weekly event known as "Ogden After Hours" featuring the best of the diverse talents in Southern music. Ogden After Hours takes place every Thursday (excluding holidays) from 6-8 PM and is quite a popular and fun event.  Admission:  Free Members $10 Adults  $8 Seniors, 65 and over  $8 Students (with current i.d.)  $5 Children 5-17 Free UNO Students, Faculty, Staff (with current i.d.) except special events (i.e. Ogden After Hours - $5). Please note other special event prices may vary. Free Children under 5 Free LA Residents Thursdays 10 a.m. - 5 p.m.  Adult group tours are $8 per person with a minimum of 10 adults.

This is a really cool museum that would appeal to younger children.  I've only been here for events and parties and this is a fantastic location for fun times.  I've never been here when there were actually children in the museum but they have some really cool interactive displays that I have to assume most kids would find fascinating as I still find many of them to be interesting.  Admission:  $8.00 per person, adults and children. LCM members and children under the age of one are admitted FREE. Adults must accompany children under 16 years.

This is an ok seafood spot on Magazine famous for their tile interior and decent to great oysters.  The main drawbacks to this place are that they close for the Summer (usually from May-September) and they only take cash so it can be a bit of a hassle.  They are a bit unique in New Orleans for not using French bread on their oyster loaf and instead use some stuff akin to Texas Toast they call "Pan Bread" (I also get irked that they seem to eternally be out of creole mustard as that is what I like on mine).  It has seemed more inconsistent in quality over the last few years and there are certainly better places at better prices but it's unique tiled interior makes it worthy of a visit just to see a classic New Orleans oyster bar.

This is probably the worst and most expensive movie experience in the area.  The seats are not comfortable to me and the screens appear smaller than any other venue.  They do have servers that will bring you food and alcohol for a premium price but the food isn't that great.  This place is dead last of any theater I would want to watch a movie at.  I appreciate the concept and I've seen it executed very well in other cities but it is not done well here.  I would far prefer going to Prytania or one of the AMC locations for a cheaper ticket price, easier parking and far better experience.

For Metairie this is ok Thai food but really I think I've had some better Pad Thai at some Vietnamese places.  The lunch portion is very much on the light side of a serving size for the price.  I would far rather go to any of the Thai places in Orleans Parish but if you are trapped in Metairie this is one of your few options for Thai.  The parking is also pretty limited and challenging so be prepared for that.

For the NOLA area this is good Mexican food but it is WAY overpriced for what it is.  Surprisingly the menu selection is quite limited.  This place is attempting to be fancy fine dining in a very Metry kind of way which doesn't work for the peasant food that Mexican food is.  Nothing here is awe inspiring or must have and I was slightly excited by the prickly pear margarita but it didn't impress so the only decent one in the area is still at Rivershack Tavern.  They do some things with lobster that might interest some people.  I seriously doubt I will be returning as this place just doesn't work for me but it might work for some out in the burbs.  At the price point of this place there are hundreds of other places I would much rather go to with far superior food.  I'm sure there are lots of people that will love this place and it should do well but it just isn't my style.

They have expanded their offerings and I was able to get a great plain flavored kombucha tea and a great green smoothie.  They have a lot more products and menu items available now and this a great place for some healthy items that you aren't going to find anywhere else in the area.  For such a small place they pack a lot of punch and they take credit cards.

This is probably the worst and most expensive movie experience in the area. The seats are not comfortable to me and the screens appear smaller than any other venue other than the Broad. They do have servers that will bring you food and alcohol for a premium price but the food isn't that great. This place is dead last of any theater I would want to watch a movie at. I appreciate the concept and I've seen it executed very well in other cities but it is not done well here. I would far prefer going to Prytania, Broad or one of the AMC locations for a cheaper ticket price, easier parking and far better experience.

Yes its a tourist trap and they sling those crazy Hand Grenade and Horny Gator drinks that will eat the polish off your shoes but you can have fun here as a local because they actually get some decent music here.  The Tropical Isle's are all best experienced in great moderation just like the Hand Grenades so make sure you pace yourself.

This Acme is typically a lot easier to get into than the one in the French Quarter and the food is exactly the same because this place has pretty much become a chain.  The raw oysters are always good and the fried seafood and po boys are typically the things they do the best at.  The gumbo is terrible and I would just skip it.  The prices are expensive for what you get and I think there are many better places with better prices.

I stop at this Rouse's location pretty often as its on my way home from work.  What I like most about this location is that they always seem to have a quick check out process compared to other locations I go to.  They also seem to always have a better selection of seafood and have a higher quality choice of cooked seafood items than any other Rouse's in the area.  This place is always busy but the wait at the deli counter for sandwich meat is usually significantly faster than at the Tchoupitoulas location.  I like the efficiency of this store.

This is a decent Ethiopian restaurant with a nice ambiance inside.  They have a small courtyard in the back that still seems to be in the process of getting finished.  The food here seems less flavorful than you would expect and the portion sizes are less than I've had at other Ethiopian places. The flavor and portion sizes are both superior a bit further down Magazine at Café Abyssinia.  They will actually give you silverware here if you want it.  Overall its really about a 2.5 star experience.

Debbie Does Doberge has a new location that is open late and slings some amazing desserts.  On my several visits now there has always been a good crowd of folks enjoying the desserts.  They also have other food but so far I've only had the desserts.  Lots of folks seem to like to grab their treats to go and take them down to enjoy at Courtyard Brewery.

This is one of my least favorite festivals.  In past years this festival has been held in  in a really small and cramped space with too much crammed into the tiny area but this year they moved into a larger nicer spot in Armstrong Park.  There is some GOOD music and that is the only redeeming factor to this event other than the move to a larger space.  Even though the space isn't as small the line for drinks is usually LONG.  Unfortunately a lot of the food is disappointing here and very sadly many of the gumbos are AWFUL!  There are still some good things to eat but this festival has among the highest level of disappointing food options of any festival currently held in New Orleans.

This place seems a lot cleaner since the new ownership took over.  The food is still about the same "ok" quality as it always was but the menu is a bit different than the old one.  The service is absolutely HORRIBLE and you have to make substantial effort to get anybody's attention after they initially take your order.  I would suggest sitting at the bar and you will probably get slightly better service as compared to hardly any service at the tables.  The only awesome five star thing about this place is that it really is 24/7 so you can always get something to eat here.  If the service wasn't so very bad it would be a three star joint and it also seems they cleaned out a bit of the character that used to be here... or at least a lot of the characters that used to always be eating in here.

This restaurant is a fun NOLA anomaly because the vast majority of locals will look at you really intently if  you DARE call the streetcar a "trolley" and they will quickly correct you and say "you mean streetcar!"  That being said this is a great little spot for breakfast, lunch, and dinner food.  This place has a bit of a diner feel but with classic New Orleans dishes available early and open late.  They used to be 24 hours all the time but now they seem to only be 24 hours on certain days which are usually around the weekend even though they advertise being open 24/7.  I've always gotten really great and friendly service in classic NOLA style with the waitress calling me darl'n, sweetheart, and luv.  The food is a good value and this is a favorite spot of NOPD who seem to have largely abandoned St. Charles Tavern for here.

It looks a lot more like a New Orleans seafood joint than a Chinese joint from the outside.  The food was alright but really heavy on the pork and light on the shrimp in the shrimp fried rice.  I probably wouldn't make a special trip out here just to eat here and I would probably end up at one of the other restaurants in the area before eating here.  Inside was nice and clean with attentive staff.  The food at dinner might perhaps be better than the lunch experience I had as I just found my food on the bland side.  If I lived in Lakeview I would probably stop in to eat here when I needed some Chinese and they do seem to have some decent lunch specials along with a lot of parking.  It is very hard to tempt me in here though with Russel's Marina Grill and Two Tony's so VERY near.

This is just a magic Willy Wonka candyland!!!  They have some fantastically decorated desserts and sweet treats in here that are nearly too pretty to eat but they taste mighty good when you do!    They generally have a nice selection of good but not fantastic gelato (as several of the flavors are very mild and if you were blindfolded you might have problems discerning some of the flavors from the others).  I'm also not the biggest fan of their espresso (I much prefer Angelo Brocato's).  Sucre is also a bit pricey for what you get but they do give very large scoops for even their smallest size of gelato.    It is hard to find anywhere else that has such beautiful presentation and artistically crafted deserts along with the fact they stay open very late (especially on weekends) so just for that they rank 5 stars.  They recently added alcoholic concoctions and I haven't yet sampled any of those so that is an adventure still to be had.

Their hot & sour chicken soup is 5 stars but everything else is around a 3 and sometimes a 4.  I always get an extra large bowl of the soup; as I do love that lovely velvety like texture of it (equally as good as La Thai's version just not as much stuff in it with a bit of a different flavor profile).  They have had some good seafood specials that I've experienced here and the curries are decent but not anything special.  They have recently added a sushi bar which seems a bit out of place in the manner in which they have installed it; so I'm still not sure what to think about that and I don't plan on ordering sushi here anytime soon as I come here for the Thai (really mainly the SOUP).  This place has certainly always been consistently good and their seafood specials have always seemed to be the things I've been most impressed with (other than the SOUP and I will come here often just to eat that!!!).  So in summary I think you can agree I think you should really try the hot & sour chicken soup.

This is probably the worst Middle Eastern food I've eaten in the entire Greater New Orleans area.  The few times I've eaten here it seems to be run only by a husband that does the cooking and his wife that is the only waitress/cashier/hostess.  I have found the portion sizes to be extremely small for the price and the flavors are very lacking as compared to all other Middle Eastern food I've ever had.  I've never had bad Middle Eastern food before so I gave this place several chances over the years and I hate to report that every visit was a disappointing one.  This place has always been very deserted during my visits and I've only seen at most 2 other people dining here (which unfortunately is probably a good measure of the quality of the food).  The family seems nice enough but the food just doesn't really merit a return visit from me ever again.

This is probably the most dive like Thai place in the NOLA area.  Before Katrina I used to frequent this place several times a week for their lunch buffet.  I don't believe they ever brought the buffet back after Katrina as I haven't seen it since.  It was never the best buffet and the food I've ordered at dinner is also not the best example of Thai food I ever had but it is always tasty and filling.  This usually isn't my first choice for Thai but if I'm in Cooter Browns and want some Thai this is the place to go.  The best thing about this place is they usually have the cutest actual Thai waitresses working and they are very nice people that give great recommendations.

This is one of the most massive convention centers around.  I first came here way back during the 1984 World's Fair as a wee child and it has grown more than I have since then.  In its current incarnation this huge venue hosts various events like conventions, like the Comic Con I've attended, and numerous Carnival Balls I've danced my way through.  I don't suggest eating here as there are too many far superior options in a city like New Orleans noted for its excellent food culture.  The one continuing issue I've had with events here is they frequently don't post the actual location of the event and with such a huge facility you need to know exactly where you're going to as otherwise you could spend a very long time walking around so you might have to call the convention center to confirm the location.

My friend recently expanded his catering business to include a retail restaurant.  NOLA Boils offers boiled and fried seafood options along with po boys, grilled oysters and daily plate lunch specials.  The fried shrimp and oysters are among the largest I've seen at any restaurant while the prices are a substantially better value than other nearby places like The Galley (which I find quite expensive).  The dining room is small but nicer than many other joints and they also have a few tables outside.  I only wish they had fresh brewed iced tea instead of fountain drink tea and also offered seafood gumbo in addition to their chicken and sausage gumbo.  For a brand new establishment they are doing great food at a fair price and I'm sure they will continue to improve all aspects of their operation going forward as they expand their restaurant based on their extensive catering experience.

Consistent good results can be expected and this is probably one of the better fast food chain joints for burgers.  They load you down with a lot of french fries here and the service is typically fast and efficient.  With so many options available to customize their burgers they have always gotten my burger correct which isn't the case with most other fast food joints.

This is the best and most flavorful Chinese I've had in a long while!  They use plenty of wood ear fungus (which is very healthy for you) in their tasty hot and sour soup and other Chinese places have been so stingy with this ingredient I was beginning to think it was an endangered species or something.  The freshness of the ingredients is evident and there isn't any evidence that they're using pre-made frozen stuff they're just reheating like a lot of the lazier Chinese places have gotten.  They have really good specials and have many things on their menu that are authentic Chinese along with Americanized dishes.     I'm really unhappy that I got charged for an entire extra soup when I asked to substitute hot and sour for the egg drop with the lunch special when the two soups are EXACTLY the same price!   So I might not eat lunch here again and pout for awhile before I return for dinner.

I had the crawfish bread and that was really great and then their cheesecake was also very nice. Unfortunately I was very unimpressed with the BBQ and would probably skip that from this point forward.  They had a much larger menu with several great looking items outside of the BBQ realm that were more NOLA style food.   Overall they should probably focus on their other food and give up on being a BBQ place as they don't come near The Joint, Central City BBQ or even Frey or Blue Oak.  The service was really friendly and they took great care of all the folks.  I would say you should certainly visit for the food but definitely not the BBQ part of the menu.

This is a solid Italian bistro with a small and intimate atmosphere.  Lunch is  a good value here with a nice selection of specials that rotate Monday through Friday along with an affordable selection of their regular entrees.  Dinner is a bit more formal and offers a much larger and nicer selection of items on the menu.  I've enjoyed everything I've ever eaten here and it has been consistently good while nothing has ever just blown me away.  This isn't really a fine dining atmosphere but it does attract an older crowd for dinner that tends to dress more formally.  Lunch generally draws a business crowd and business casual would be the typical attire.  Overall this is a great place for lunch and an affordable dinner option if you're in the mood for Italian.

I love the concept but the execution often falls short and when demand is high the system often breaks down and wait times can get very excessive.  The actual streetcars themselves are fantastic and I live right off the St. Charles streetcar line.  For me its usually a very convenient way to get around except during special events and until after Midnight when the streetcars seem to get much more rare than their published schedule would indicate.  You need a $1.25 so have it ready and get ready for a rambling ride through history.

I've been nearly every year and this year was by far the worst.  The bathroom situation was out of control bad.  I've always gotten a 3 day pass or 3 day VIP pass.  I had such a bad time this year I gave my armband away and didn't return after Friday.  The single day tickets have gotten outrageous and when a festival costs more than Jazz Fest you're losing most of your locals.  Hardly any of my friends went this year and the line up was terrible other than the local bands (and I get to hear them often and for far less than what the prices at this fest are).  They had freaking carnival rides this year and it just was totally out of place along with what seemed like very diminished crowds.  I'm not buying a pass for next year and I will need to hear about substantial changes to return again which is very unfortunate as this is the best weather of any fest in NOLA.

Mardi Gras is one of the things that New Orleans is famous for and arguably something that New Orleans does better than anywhere else.  Mardi Gras strictly refers to Fat Tuesday but in common usage it often refers to the entire Carnival Season which starts after Twelfth Night, on Epiphany (Jan. 6th). It is a season of parades, balls, and king cakes.  Celebrations are concentrated for about two weeks before and through Fat Tuesday (Mardi Gras in French), the day before Ash Wednesday.  There is generally at least one major parade each day and many days have several large parades. The biggest parades take place during the final five days of the season. For the last week of Carnival events occur EVERYWHERE in New Orleans and the surrounding area.  Parades in New Orleans are organized by Carnival krewes and the Krewe float riders toss "throws" to the crowds.  Throws include beads, doubloons, plastic cups, and toys.  Living in New Orleans and experiencing an entire Carnival Season is an unmatched experience and makes life anywhere else during that time painfully dull!

The food is decent except when they run out of things or haven't defrosted things which has happened on every visit.  The service is just unacceptable and its a miracle if you can get your drink refilled.  I hope I don't have to ever come back to this joint and I would far rather go to the City Diner next door or Tic Tock Cafe across the street for much better food, much better prices and light years better service.

Inconsistent seems to be the best way to describe this place.  They seem to attempt to be all things to all people and don't do all things well.  I've had some good dishes here and then I've also had terrible food served to me.  They also do sushi here which can be variable from good to less so.  They just have such an ambitious menu covering so many things that it is hard for them to execute everything well.  The building and interior of this place are modern and clean which are aspects that don't always exactly blend in that well with St. Charles Ave. but it is tolerable for what it is.  The best thing about this place is that gets them an extra star bump is that they have later hours so you can find something to eat when many other places are closed.  Tolerably average is the best way to sum this place up.

A great spot for a picnic and a very tight squeeze for festivals.  The French Quarter Fest and other events are held here and it can get really crowded very fast in this narrow strip of land.  I love fests but I also appreciate this area when it is calm and you can enjoy looking out at the Mississippi River and have a long lazy picnic as the world on the water slowly drifts past.

Its a holiday that I get the day off for that folks in other parts of the country have no real clue about.  This is the end of long and amazing Carnival season that really distinguishes New Orleans from the rest of the United States and most of the world.  Being virtually anywhere else on Mardi Gras day but New Orleans is a terrible idea as this is the center of an amazing celebration that is roaring to its conclusion until next year.  There are so many activities, king cakes, parades, events, balls, parties, dinners, lunches, snacks, excessive costumes, total lack of clothing, elegance, decadence and sheer exuberance.  There is just nothing else like it!

Kyoto is the closest GOOD sushi restaurant to my house so if I'm in need of a quick sushi fix this is where I will head.  I really like the area that this establishment is located and there are several great places to eat clustered nearby.  They have a lot of interesting rolls that are unique to them and they are generally very fast with getting your food out.  The Poke salad is probably one of the most outstanding things they make here and many of the cooked items from the kitchen are often overlooked but still very tasty.    * Quick Tip: If you sit at the sushi bar you get a free bowl of miso soup.                            ALWAYS sit at the sushi bar!!!  It often does get crazy crowded here at night (and especially on weekends) but it has always been a quick lunch spot (if you sit at the sushi bar).  Parking can be problematic at times (and I miss the days before Katrina when they wouldn't hassle you about parking in the strip mall parking lot across the street).  It is also really nice that you can run to Creole Creamery next door for dessert.

They have really improved the fish selection here and offer a menu that details both the local selections then those that come from Japan.  I find the sushi bar here to be better than many of the kitchen items generally.  I have found many of the rolls are often not rolled tightly enough and come apart easily.  In the sushi restaurants selection of the Metairie area I would place this location of Little Tokyo at around third place with Kanno being #1 then Shogun at #2.

This is a bit of a hidden away space where you might want to sneak into if you determine your quest necessitates you to escape the crowds of Bourbon Street.  This is a very concise venue with some craft cocktails to encourage some higher prices.  The ambiance leans towards a bit of a tiki bar theme.  The target audience seems to be the hipster folk.  It could be an alright place for a few drinks but I don't think it would ever rate on my regular rotation.

Good boiled crawfish and shrimp at decent prices.  The crawfish pie is one of the pre-made varieties and not made at the store.  The shrimp was  properly boiled and not over cooked which seems to be a hard thing to find these days.  They also offer Banh Mi style po boys, fried seafood and some Vietnamese and other Asian options which are also nice.  This establishment is run by a very nice Vietnamese family that takes good care of you.

To me a snowball is mostly about the ice and ice here just doesn't inspire my love like Hansen's does but it's better than some other joints and they have definitely improved the quality of it of late.  They have a nice selection of flavors and they also expand beyond just snowballs to offering other food items which might be part of their problem.  The places that seem to be the most awesome snowball places tend to specialize in just doing snowballs.  This place does offer a great value as you can get a very large snowball for not a lot of money.  The wait is usually significantly less here than many other popular snowball purveyors in the area.  This place is alright but when compared to the nearby Hansen's it just doesn't compare as Hansen's snowballs totally blows them away except if you're in a hurry and can't wait in line at Hansen's this will do in a pinch.

I avoided this place for awhile as I didn't know they had an inside but then my waitress from Mona's defected so I had to try it out.  This place has some of the most tender and tasty lamb I've ever had!!!  I've been several times and enjoyed everything except the giant burger, which I found was too much bun and not enough meat.  I recently went with a group of people and we got the giant combo kabob platter and that was a LOT of food for the price and we all enjoyed it so much that even though we were full we got more food as the meat was just so tasty.    Nice people running the place and the owner has very high standards for his food and wants to get fresh organic produce whenever possible.

The really standout thing about this place is their fantastic backyard and patio area which is one of the largest and most amazing of any in NOLA!  They have bananas growing on their trees ready to eat along with an amazing cabana and bar area ready for a party.  The interior of the hotel is nice but some of the rooms are quite small so be specific about what you need when booking a room as there is some variation.  Hotel Storyville definitely has more of a friendly hostel feeling to it than a fancy hotel.
