Maybe the limited selection here is just their dedication to their highly limited and exclusive high standards of only serving the freshest and best but unfortunately for whatever reason that leaves them far behind the other choices for tasty sweet treats in the area.

Food and drinks are like every other Felipe's I've visited in the area so the quality is consistent.  Service at the bar was a bit slow and disorganized and seemed one of the bartenders was not familiar with the menu or how to enter a combo into the register.  In general Felipe's taco portions are just so small I always end up having to order more here and somehow end up spending more than I do  at other Mexican joints and even then I still seem to be a bit hungry afterwards.  I do like the little salsa and topping bar they have as you get to really sauce up your food and that is my main attraction to this joint as I'm a saucy salsa freak.

I used to really love Ninja and they used to be one of the best sushi joints in town.  My last many visits though have just really disappointed me.  Some of my rolls have just tasted bad and they have often just fallen apart into a crumbled mess.  I have just found that I really no longer have a desire to go there and when I want sushi I really just greatly prefer Kanno.

I just was really turned off by the ambiance and the menu really seemed overpriced especially for the fish entrees.  Things started bad when they were out of the first thing I ordered. I then got a turtle soup and burger.  The turtle soup was actually good but I was never offered any Sherry so what's the point at that point so that was just an epic fail.  The burger was not up to par and especially for the amount they charged ($15) as it really didn't have much flavor and it lacked on all levels.  The shoestring fries served with the burger did not please me.  The service was inadequate as it took far too long to get drink refills.  So for around the same price as a fantastic lunch at Commander's Palace or Mandina's I got a mediocre burger and turtle soup with no Sherry offered with it.  So many better burgers in NOLA I can't see ever getting another burger here and  I just don't think this is making my rotation or even worthy of a return visit.

5 stars for the Tuesday night $2 beer pitcher special but other than that I'm really not a big fan of the food here.  There are much better pizza, pasta and sandwich options in the city.  I wish I liked the food here better as I really like the $2 beer pitcher special and I would love to support a local chain but I just really like so many other pizza joints so much better I just really never choose this place.  I only ended up at this location as it was one of the few places open during the recent ice storm around where one of my friends lives.  This location is probably about the most modern, hip and trendy of any that they have and I'm not a big fan of modern, hip and trendy most of the time so the ambiance here pretty much goes against my whole grain.  If not for the $2 pitchers of beer I would never have even allowed myself to be dragged inside this joint but hooray and 5 stars for the beer!

The food was around three stars and they keep expanding their menu and adding new items but they need a better organized menu.  This location is alright but nothing outstanding about the ambiance or architecture and it doesn't even manage any dive dank credibility so very three star there too.  The pricing  seems way out of line for the quantity of food you get and honestly I could make a better sandwich for a lot less coin.  For the price point here there are lots of better sandwiches and po boys in the area I'd rather eat.  Overall this place just doesn't float my boat but for those obsessed with high dollar grilled cheese I reckon you can find your bliss here but I also hear the grilled cheese at Delachaise is better.

This is a solidly consistent place to grab some good food.  I rotate in here probably once every two years or so, as it usually isn't at the top of my list of places to go with all the other great options in the area, but I've brought a few out of town folks here when other places were super crowded and it has always been easy to access.  The service has always been pleasant and the interior space is much nicer than you might think from just driving past and looking at the exterior.  I've never had anything that disappointed me here but I've also never had anything that excited me either so this place is definitely a solid three star A-Ok in my book with potential to reach higher.

This is one of the nicest spots in the Warehouse district and I've always enjoyed myself here.  As the name implies they have a nice selection of wines while also offering a good choice in beer and spirits.  They have a comfortable bar along with table seating.  If your looking to escape the normal bar scene and want a more sophisticated and civilized location then this is your place.

The best offering here for my money is the fish and chips and that is also the largest serving offered on the menu and is in fact so large you could probably split it with someone.  The rest of the offerings on the menu run far more on the smaller side of things so you might need to order more than one of those other dishes to make a meal.  The service is usually adequate and friendly and the ambiance is alright with a tad much hipster vibe for my taste.  Booty's might just have the best and most authentic British version of fish and chips in the city currently.

This is a good spot for a quick lunch that also seems to serve as a neighborhood bar that probably would be nice for sports watching.  They have a limited daily menu of lunch specials.  The sandwiches I've had so far were a bit light on the meat portion while the lasagna was very good and other entrees decent sized.  They are right behind the post office and you just order directly at the bar before getting a number and sitting down so this is a great place if you need to do some postal business and then grab a quick lunch before going back to work.

I've been to several events here and it seems like a unique spot set off in the middle of a giant parking lot.  They have a nice patio in the back and the interior is spacious with a large bar.  I'm repulsed by hip hop music so that gets to be a big problem for me in this joint sometimes.  Friday is probably the most popular time for this bar as they usually offer free food.

This is a national chain that caters to the niche of higher end men's barber shop that also offers a substantial selection of shaving items.  They offer all the tools, accessories and needed items associated with straight razors and safety razors.  They offer their own shaving products that include pure essential oils.  Their menu of options is as follows:  Royal Shave $55 Traditional Shave $35 Hair Cut $40 Head Shave $35 Beard/Moustache Trim $35 Royal Shave & Harcut $80 Traditional Shave & Haircut $65 Royal Shave & Head Shave $75 Traditional Shave & Head Shave $55  I've gotten shaves at many barber shops over the years and never paid such high prices so I might purchase some shaving tools and products here but I doubt I would find value with their barber services.

Lee's is a local Louisiana chain that has locations on the North Shore, Metairie, and Kenner.  Lee's makes some decent fast food burgers with a thick piece of meat compared to most other fast food joints that earns them a third star.  The fries usually aren't the best and their onion rings are usually a much better choice.  The burger is definitely the star of their offerings here and is probably one of the better one's you can get at a fast food joint.

I had been meaning to try this joint for many years but it never worked out over many attempts in the past but I finally forced the hand of fate to comply with my need to sample their food.  I was sorely tempted to try some of their goat dishes but instead I went with sampling their chicken pho and their example certainly passed the test with flying colors being very flavorful and satisfying.  It is an inconvenient drive from my work or home to get here so it will take some planning and luck for my next visit but I do plan on some goat here soon.

Tal's has a small little menu to match its small little space.  They only have bottled drinks, free water and iced coffee but no iced tea.  I really prefer Mona's and Lebanon over this place as they have a better selection of items and serve iced tea at those joints.  This place can work for a quick lunch spot and they have puffy pita's more like what I've had at Turkish places.  It's a little bit different than most of the other Middle Eastern style restaurants in town so if you are in the mood for that then this might fit the bill.

Jamila's is epically known worldwide for their excellent food they have been providing the hungry hordes for many years during Jazz Fest.  Less well known but even more delicious is what they prepare in their restaurant proper.  The Tunisian food here has influences that will bring memories of food from the Middle East and France while producing some remarkably unique and wonderful flavors all its own.    The hospitality here is legendary and offered in abundance by the husband and wife team that run this establishment.  The husband is frequently found to be sitting at the tables jovially conversing with customers while his wife will occasionally tell him to stop bothering people and, all the while, making it seem very much like you are part of their family as they go into great detail explaining the many wonders they have on offer for your dining delight (along with the best drinks to accompany each selection).  This is a truly enjoyable place to dine, drink, enjoy wonderful food, as you experience wonderful hospitality.

The Lakeview Pearl has a nice selection of specialty rolls here that are a bit different than other sushi joints in town.  The menu also offers a good selection of other non-sushi items for those that like to mix it up or don't want sushi.  The location is a bit strange as there are other businesses in the building with their signs facing Harrison but the Lakeview Pearl is the only one with their sign facing Canal Blvd. so it took a bit to figure out how to get inside.  The service was attentive and professional with drinks being refilled consistently.  This is the best sushi place in Lakeview so if you are in the area and craving sushi this is the place to go.

This is one of the best values on all you can eat shrimp, crawfish and crabs.  They have an extensive and affordable menu with a selection that will probably satisfy most people.  Seating is at large picnic style tables and it can get loud in here when its crowded.  Even though this place is on the Westbank its a really quick trip from the city and from Uptown its really faster to access than most restaurants in the French Quarter or Bucktown.  The biggest criticisms I have are that the shrimp are sometimes over cooked and when it gets busy service can sometimes take longer than I would like.    Overall this is a great casual seafood spot that is mostly a locals joint that will give you a lot of bang for your buck.

This place is much nicer on the inside than you would assume from its drab old strip mall exterior.  The food trends more on the expensive side for what it is with basic sandwiches, salads, soups, pastas and steaks.  They have a good burger that is nice sized but it comes with potato chips and fries are an up charge.  Cafe Fresca also has changing daily specials but many of them don't seem like good values.  The best value here is probably the 2 can dine for $20 deal and that's definitely the way to go if you plan on eating here.

This is a really great space and you can really just hang out in here like its a bar.  They have decent beer prices here that are far better than many other Warehouse district locations and it doesn't seem to draw the same crowd of douchebags and randos like some other bar locations in the area have.  The Phil's burgers are generally very nice and I like this location a lot more than their original Metairie space.  I never would've guessed it would've been so nice and actually so comfortable a place to just hang out and drink beer so I would suggest giving it a try.

This place has some of the most perfectly seasoned and spiced Thai food I've ever eaten.  Their Coconut Soup is the best version of that dish I've ever experienced and one of the best flavor experiences I've had in quite a long time.  Even better is that I had ordered a small cup of the soup but the kitchen made a mistake and they gave me a large bowel so that I was able to even more fully enjoy and lengthen my ecstatic gastronomic pleasure with that wonderful Coconut Soup.  I have really enjoyed every meal I've eaten here with the Tom Yum soup being very nice, the basil shrimp having great flavor and the noodle dishes all making my taste buds very happy.  This is DEFINITELY a place to eat at ASAP if you are a fan of spice, flavor, seasonings and awesome service which is all done at an amazing value for the great quality.

I've got some out of town friends that love this place... they love it so much that they demand to go here non-stop the entire time they are here regardless of what else is going on.  It can be Jazz Fest, Greek Fest, French Quarter Fest and all they want to do is go here.  From being dragged here incessantly I've grown to not like this place very much as I like my fests a lot more and I can only take Bourbon St. locations like this in very limited doses.  The big thing that really gets on my nerves and pisses me off after a few minutes in here is that the damn shot girls won't leave you alone and try to shove test tube shots down your throat no matter how many times you tell them no.

I've eaten here many times over the years and the food has just never impressed me and has never surpassed being simply average.  I'm sure this would be a fine establishment in most other places but we're very spoiled in NOLA and can demand more.  This can be a fun place to eat with a group and have a few drinks but this is probably one of the most mediocre pizza, sandwich, sort-of-Italian  places in the area.  The service is usually provided by Tulane or Loyola co-eds that provide varying levels of service and attractiveness that can add or distract from the quality of the dining experience.  The food is two stars while as a drinking establishment it  ranks around a three.

NOLA BBQEAUX works out of a food trailer and typically can be found at the Westbank Flea-market lot in Harvey.  They have some good brisket and very nice burnt ends served here with a tasty selection of three sauce options (regular, spicy and tangy).  Their sides are typical decent standard bbq joint fare with beans, slaw, grits and mac 'n cheese.  The BBQ reminds me a lot of Chef Ron's (formerly of many places but lastly of Central City BBQ) with the burnt ends being especially similar to his.  The folks running this place are very nice and you typically get your food very fast.  There is plenty of seating to be had around the area and lots of other food options to explore.

I usually just stop in here on way back from the Shooter's Club to grab a quick meal.  They have a decent menu selection and generally have good service that is sometimes a bit slow.  The food is typically good and they offer good value for their portion sizes.  They have good sandwiches, pasta, burgers and the seafood is typically prepared well.  I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here but it is a decent family restaurant if you find yourself in this part of town.

The food is decent and pretty authentic.  They don't have iced tea and I tried to get a Topo Chico water but they just gave me a plastic bottled water instead.  Sunday is a bad day to go here as they have VERY loud Mexican music blaring to the point you have to yell to understand the person right next to you.  The loudness of the music makes this place intolerable and unbearable on Sunday or any other day they choose to do it.  For just the food it is worth giving it a try but if you hear the loud music skip it.

Decent spot for some seafood or burgers.  They really like their fried catfish here but I'm not really a fan of most catfish and prefer trout and other fish for a seafood platter.  The seafood gumbo had quite a respectable amount of seafood in it and the fried shrimp were good.  I was rather confused over the lack of any hot sauce on the tables and wondered if I had been magically transported outta Louisiana?  The service was attentive and kept the drinks filled.  They close right at 9pm so that is a bit early for my taste but maybe it is what works in Westwego.

How strange I used to have a review for this establishment but AGAIN somehow YELP has made it disappear?    Golden Corral is a buffet joint and as is expected a lot of the food is of mediocre quality like most buffets.  Their grilled steak is probably the best item on the menu and is of a good quality that is above most other buffet joints items.  The biggest thing that makes this establishment a real winner is that they have a free dinner for military vets every year for Veteran's Day so as an army vet I would like to offer a sincere THANKS to Golden Corral for doing such a fantastic thing for vets.

When this place first opened it was AWESOME!!! Sadly they have been in a long, slow, steady, decline ever since.  The quality of nearly everything has gotten to be seriously lacking.  They now have a very poor selection of sushi and so many of the other items have just gotten plain gross as they are either prepared with such little care or are of such low quality.  I'm so sad as I used to so enjoy my time here but unless radical changes are made my time here is at and end :(

So the only other Kilwins I've been to is in Franklin,Tennessee and that one just fooled you into thinking it was a local gem while this location unfortunately reeks of corporate chain.  The service here was less than usually expected and really it just wasn't very friendly.  The atmosphere inside this location of Kilwins definitely doesn't invite you to order your treats and then kick back and stay awhile to eat them as the only seating is a very tiny area in a corner.  Overall I just likely will never return as I would rather go to Angelo Brocato's or Creole Creamery for a better experience other than the fudge they do have really good selection of fudge here.

China Doll serves some really large sized portions on their lunch specials so you get good value for your money here.  The ambiance is old school Chinese restaurant in a strip mall with attentive service.  The food in addition to being abundant is also rather tasty as well.  They do a large carry out business so you often need to walk past a lot of folks standing in the front waiting for their orders to get to the hostess for seating.  Overall this is a decent spot for some good and fast Chinese food on the Westbank at a decent price.

This was my first visit to this location of the growing local pizza chain of Theo's and they are certainly one of my favorite pizza joints around the area.  The thin crispy crust makes me a very happy eater.  I enjoy the wide range of interesting combinations they offer.  The Eccentric & the Spicy Mexican are two of my favorites but my usual fix is the Hippy with either chicken or meatballs added.  I always get a side of their tasty marinara to dip my crust into; although often it isn't needed I still love the sauce and will just drink it!  I also really like their meatball sub which is what I ate at this location and it was consistent with my good experiences at their other locations.

The Historic New Orleans Collection is many things and they describe themselves on their website as, "a museum, research center, and publisher dedicated to preserving the history and culture of New Orleans and the Gulf South."  The seven building complex has some good exhibits and often features interesting speakers on various historical topics.  The best thing about this attraction is that it's FREE.  They seem to do a good job with constantly changing the focus to different themes here touching on different aspects of history to ensure that future visits can be a different entertainment and educational experience than past ones.  They have a lot going on here and you never know what might be scheduled in the near or far future so you should check out their website frequently to see what is in the works.

This is a really nice looking space inside and half the space is dedicated to private events.  Much of the food seems to be very pork-centric so it was challenging to find items that left the pig fat out here.  For a distillery they also surprisingly seemed pretty stingy on their liquor pours and ALL the drinks my party sampled were what NOLA folks would call "watered down" and they just were not all that flavorful generally.  The food also was pretty bland and blah so again generally mediocre.  Service was also rather forgetful and inattentive.  There was decent live music so there was that.  There likely is a low chance I would return here unless they bam it up and add some actual flavor to things.

This is a nice easy spot to grab some great beers and decent food.  I like it more for the beer than food and they also have some good drink specials they run.  The crowd is a bit variable and it often seems to be more of a restaurant crowd than bar crowd a lot of the time but sometimes it does get more of a bar atmosphere.  They have a nice little patio out front that is nice to see the world of 12 South pass by. Overall this is definitely a pleasant spot to grab some great beer and have a good time.

$12.04 for a brisket plate with 2 sides and an iced tea is a great value.  Brisket was not so good while all the sides were great.  Among the best mac 'n cheese and cole slaws of the bbq joints in the area along with a very nice selection of different items that gives more choices than other local BBQ places

This is a comfortable coffee joint in Germantown that has a decent amount of both indoor and outdoor seating.  They have some food options here too but I only sampled the crack... I mean caffeine beverages and for those that care about such things they also make those fancy little latte art decorations in some of the beverages. When the weather is nice the outdoor area is a nice spot to enjoy some caffeine and get some work done or just enjoy the view.  There are some other business around here but you still get free parking around the area at the moment but things keep changing and growing so hopefully the free parking stays around.

This is a good Middle Eastern restaurant but it is the one that I eat at the least of any in the area.  This place is very often quite crowded and parking isn't always the easiest in the area so I usually opt for places that are easier to grab a quick meal like Pyramid's, Mona's, or Courtyard Grill.  The main factor impeding my eating here more often is the problem of its location in proximity to Jamila's, which is so close I will ALWAYS opt for that as my first choice over here, as I enjoy Jamila's so very much.  This place has a a nice ambiance and the energy level of the crowd usually seems to be high.  I think Lebanon and here probably seem to have some of the most jovial crowds having fun while they eat of any of the area Middle Eastern restaurants I've been to.  I've found all of the food to be good and I've always had great service.

Ok so they have repaired and put the giant mug back up and it is once again working.  They have brought back the signature Frostop root beer and use real glass mugs to serve it in.  They seemed to have gotten much more pleasant staff and the super bad attitude employee was not there.  The food is still the same and a bit overpriced for the fast food quality that it clearly is with a few local flavor and breakfast options that kick it up a bit.  They had a gross roof/ceiling leak dripping all over the place when I was there so they still have some work to do.  I hope they continue with their repairs and get this place back to the classic place it has the potential to be.

This is a combo candy store and wedding store.  I was just browsing the selection here as I was waiting for my tailor to finish something next door so I don't know anything about their wedding services. They have several types of candy available (with most of the focus being on chocolate) and offer fancy gift packaging.  They have a retail area with lots of gift and wedding items.  Overall it looks like a decent place to grab a gift or have some sweets wrapped up for a nice presentation and they have a lot of Louisiana and NOLA spin offerings.

Pretty generic as expected typical Mexican fare.  The food was on the more bland side and the salsa was more sweet with no spice.  The service was alright and they kept the drinks full.  They have a large parking lot and that's about all there is to say.

Sadly this formerly fantastic chain has been in a long slow decline and I believe this is the last one left standing in New Orleans (I think there is still a GOOD one in LaPlace http://www.laplace-frostop.com/index.htm).  The food and service have been on a drastic slide down ever since Katrina.  There is one employee that is just beyond any type of bad attitude and rudeness I've EVER seen anywhere.  They have some unique New Orleans and breakfast options available in addition what you might expect from their fast food burger selection.  They used to make their own famously great root beer served in a frosty mug but now all you get is Barq's in a styrofoam cup (I did hear they have recently started serving the old formula again but I haven't been back to confirm).  The last time I drove past it looked like they had even removed the long standing, upside down, giant, rootbeer mug.  I used to really enjoy the unique experience of eating here but after many attempts with all bad experiences since Katrina I just can't see going back to the miserable place it has become.

This is definitely a bird of another feather compared to the other spots on Broadway.  I first tried to visit on a Wednesday at 10pm and it was already closed so that really blew my mind and I'm still confused about that???  It seems more like a bar than a restaurant but with that early of a closing time is this place really more of a restaurant?  They have a fantastic view of the river from their rooftop and then each floor has a different "theme" of what is going on with food and drink.  It certainly seems to be leaning more towards the tourist trap destination while still attracting a fair number of locals.  It is overall a really awesome ambiance while the prices are a bit on the expensive side.  It is certainly a place that needs to be experienced and I will most certainly visit again.  I still have a lot to learn about the ins and outs of this joint as it is so complicated with all of the different things going on so maybe I shall come to appreciate more of the quirks of this place to enjoy it more.

This is usually my go to place for boiled crawfish, crabs, and shrimp.  They have the best boiled shrimp anywhere!!!  The crawfish is usually great depending on how and when in the season is they can be a bit small sometimes and I prefer to get the larger "select" premium ones when available.  They also usually have some great crawfish pies available.  They also have a good selection of other fresh & frozen seafood, gator, and turtle you can take home to cook yourself.    This is a market and they don't have anywhere to eat it once you buy it.  I used to always go across the street to eat my feast on the Bulldog patio but a recent change of rules has stopped that and I'm not happy about that!  You can still grab some drinks at Breaux Mart and go the park behind the grocery to chow down.

This is the spot I had my first taste of Middle Eastern food and I've been a fan ever since.  The combo kabob plate is huge and really enough for two people.  The inside and outside of the building doesn't really have any nice New Orleans "character" about it but they have done a nice job painting and decorating the space with a kooky Middle Eastern theme that makes it a much more fun space.  Many people bring their own wine to drink here (and I don't believe they have a corkage fee).  Service can range from excellent to terrible based on what waitress you get and how crowded it is and, as most of the servers are college aged females, they have a pretty high turnover.  Parking is also a bit tight in the area so you might have to find a spot a bit further away but it is very convenient to the streetcar.  I've always been very happy with my food here and it is certainly one of the best Middle Eastern places in the area.

I usually only end up here after all the other groceries are closed as this is a bit of a longer trip from my house than most of the other markets.  This is a nice sized store and they have a good selection of items but don't seem to have as many local products as Rouse's.  They have a nice booze, wine and beer selection.  They're also big on using your Winn Dixie card and you can save some money if you get one and remember to use it.  They have later hours than any other grocery in the area so that really gives them convenience points. I do appreciate their later hours but I still miss the 24 hour grocery shopping we had in the area before Katrina.  What's a night owl to do these days at 3am when a sudden need to make groceries arises?

This place has been getting lots of hype of late.  Popeyes has nothing to fear from this chicken.  The biscuits are better than Popeyes though.  They have an interesting menu and concept but the food just is not all that great.  I've actually had far superior gas station chicken in many spots.  I might sample some other items eventually but I am not left with any strong motivations from the rather bland flavor of the chicken to hurry back.

Old school NOLA style eating establishment with traditional NOLA lunch items and traditional breakfast foods mixed up with some Louisiana accents.  They still offer a good value for your money here and you get your food fast.  The setup is a cafeteria style system where you go through the line of items on the buffet to select or make an order from the menu before paying at the register and then they call out your menu ordered items when ready.  The burger here is ok but certainly not in the top ranks of NOLA burgers so the po boys, daily specials and breakfast items are better selections.  The seafood gumbo is decent with generous amounts of crab and they do offer small and large options.  The seating is a bit tight and it can get crowded in here but it is a unique and interesting space worthy of a visit.  The main downside is this place is only open Monday through Friday from 7am til 2:30pm so if you don't work in the CBD it is rare you can eat here.

Mardi Gras World is an exhibit of the works and magic of Blaine Kern Studios who build the majority of the floats used in carnival parades.  This is both an actual workshop where they build Mardi Gras floats and an exhibit of the process and final results.  The Kern's are nice folks and they have put together a nice venue which is a  fantastic space for a party or event.  One of my favorite party areas is the cool-fake-Southern-plantation-garden room which is just entertaining to no end for some reason to me.  There are frequently fun events occurring here so make sure to check out the website and see what else besides just the tour is going on here.  Admission:  Adults: $19.95 Seniors (65+): $15.95 Children (2-12): $12.95

Sadly another dive bar that has raised the price of Abita Amber above what I'm going to pay for it.  The quality of the food service has been slipping and it just doesn't seem to bring in the crowds it used to so the ambiance has dropped.  Higher prices, less people and less fun...  Times are changing fast and not for the better in the bar industry of NOLA.  At least they still have the St. Patrick's day events but other than that I just don't find myself coming here anymore.

They did a nice job here and everything looks shiny and new so maybe too nice of job as we like our old school dive look in NOLA.  Unfortunately like most new places opening these days their drink prices are overpriced and I really didn't find the beer prices competitive to other places on Frenchmen.  They do have quite a selection of food so you can find something to satisfy your hunger here.  They have a nice upstairs with a balcony that can be entertaining for people watching as the crowds go past on Frenchmen.  Speaking of crowds there wasn't one here while the rest of the establishments on Frenchmen seemed to be jam packed this place was very sparsely populated which I would guess is due to their overpriced drinks not being competitive.

Edley's Bar-B-Que is really expanding all over while they seem to also be maintaining good BBQ quality at all their locations I've tried.  So far I've most frequently visited and enjoyed their 12 South location then I've also been to their Chattanooga location along with this one in Sylvan Park.  I didn't eat any BBQ here and I randomly ended up here simply due to the fact they stayed open later than the other joints in the area so after spending some time at McCabe Pub and Neighbors I closed out my night here.  Edley's certainly seems to have the largest selection of draft of all the spots I visited in Sylvan Park and there were quite a lot of folks in here enjoying themselves at a later time.  Overall I enjoyed myself here and Edley's has shown themselves to consistently be a great place to enjoy some fun times with good drinks along with good BBQ.

Junction is a dive bar that makes a good burger at a decent price.  They have a nice selection of options to kick the burger level up a few degrees.  They also do quite a very nice job on their fries here too.  The staff seemed to be enjoying themselves at work and took good care to make sure drinks were filled.  I actually still think the burger at Kukhnya in Siberia is a bit better though while the fries at Junction would win that throwdown.

I want an Abita Amber and I can't get one here it seems.  I loved the Bridge Lounge's mojitos but I can't get that either anymore.  I liked the Bridge Lounge's unisex bathrooms but now equality of bathroom rights has become segregated.  I miss the Bridge Lounge's dog obsessed atmosphere but that just is all gone.  The music volume is way out of control here and its hard to have a conversation inside its so very loud.  I'm always a fan of dead animals on the wall and animal hide rugs so that's an improvement.  There is more space but the new seating is far less comfortable than before.  Maybe I will grow to like this new place but until they add Abita Amber at a decent price it has slim chances of being a spot I frequent.

This is a decent medium sized grocery that has some nice prepared foods.  They have most of the things you need at prices higher than you would sometimes expect.  They often have some surprising items here that you wouldn't expect along with typically good produce.  The parking is a bit limited for the location and getting in and out from Claiborne can be tedious.  Due to the location I rarely visit this place but before Katrina I used to really be a fan of the Robert's prepared food at their location in the LGD on Annunciation... so if they would just reopen that location I would probably be a more frequent customer of theirs.

This is a great dive bar with some amazing daily specials!  They have a great Monday night special with two lobsters and then steak night on Wednesday and Fridays.  Their regular menu food is also great bar food with huge burgers and flavorful tamales.  The drinks are reasonably priced and there seems to usually be a decent crowd of folks here.  Overall this is a cool spot with some great bar food and they serve later than many other spots.  My video review of Sportsbeat Pub & Cafe is here: https://youtu.be/TveQyQYthXc

Jack's Bar-B-Que has three locations in Nashville and this is pretty good BBQ for a local chain joint.  There was quite a line of folks waiting and the inside was packed full of hungry people during my lunch time visit so this certainly seems to be the case at all of the BBQ joints I've visited in Nashville so far.  I got a brisket plate and it was some good brisket although I certainly have had far better this is definitely some of the better brisket I've had in Tennessee.  For sides I had mashed sweet potatoes and turnip greens which were both delicious. I'm always VERY happy when a place has mashed sweet potatoes and the turnip greens are also a great side to my taste buds.  Overall this was a great spot to grab a decently quick lunch even with the line and although it was more of a fast food type environment as you just order at the counter and then you take care of yourself the staff were very nice.

This place is actually a great little French Bistro that also does pizza.  They would get a higher ranking except they make things very inconvenient by only taking cash/check and that greatly reduces my ability to enjoy this place.  I just don't like to carry lots of cash around, as although this place isn't terribly expensive it would take a bit to have a nice meal and drink some good wine for a couple here, so they really lose out on money I would spend if I could use my debit card.  The atmosphere here is very cozy and it is a great spot to bring a date.  I've enjoyed everything I've eaten here and I've always had decent if a tad slow service.  I would frequent this place much more but for the large inconvenience of them not taking credit/debit cards.

I had lunch here and sampled the Tom Yum soup with chicken and the spicy basil with shrimp.  Unfortunately both of these dishes were my least favorite examples of these Thai classics that I've had anywhere in the area as I found them very bland.  The food was fresh and well prepared but it just lacked any kick whatsover and was blander than mild.  I honestly don't see myself returning here as the other Thai restaurants in New Orleans are so much better than what I experienced at lunch.  The service was generally good until the end when I had to wait way too long to get my bill.  The clam appetizer sounds interesting so maybe I will return for that but overall it was just too bland an experience for me.

The Par 3 didn't quite live up to my par expectations for my Chicken Parm so I probably wouldn't get that item again but the fried seafood and burger seem to be OK.  Service was spotty during my last visit and often disappeared for long periods of time which led to a much longer time sitting around than in most other restaurants in the area.  For what it is the place is alright but there are definitely better joints in the area to eat with much better service and service is a very important part of a business like this.

It is an EVIL chain restaurant and I HATE chains!!! That said of my STRONG aversion they do have some of the best food of about any soul sucking chain out there and they run a very strict establishment.  They have a fantastic prime rib and I love their apple cobbler dessert.  The service is ALWAYS outstanding and the food and establishment are always in first rate shape.  I've been to many locations of Houston's just for these consistent facts alone.  If they weren't a big chain they would get 4 Stars but minus 1 Star for being a national chain with absolutely ZERO local flavor or charm!!!    You can eat this food almost anywhere in America so I would never take anybody here but if I'm in a hurry it will fit the bill for a decent meal.    Please don't tell anyone but I mainly just sneak off here to snack on the apple cobbler...

This is a decent little bar that also serves food. I ordered "The Redux Burger" which has a  menu description which says it has Creole mustard and horseradish but I didn't taste or see either of those condiments on mine so not sure what was going on with that?  There is always an interesting crowd in this joint and it never seems to be the same environment when I visit as the music and people seem to shift depending on the day and time you visit which for me have always been very different and quite spaced out.  Overall this is an interesting little bar with a lot of character but I still wanted a whole lot more Creole mustard and horseradish on my burger.

This was a nice event with drinks and snacks.  I hadn't been to the venue in several years so it was nice to check it out again and even better I got to sample some new cocktails here as on my past visits I just had wine.  Good times seemed to be had by all the Yelpers and it was a lot of fun to have some awards distributed to some hard Yelping folks.  Overall this was a great time at a nice spot that made for plenty of good cheer!

This place looks like a dive from the outside and a bit form the inside but they put a lot of energy where it really counts in putting out some flavorful food.  I usually stick with some standard simple dishes when exploring a new Thai place and they delivered with a nice coconut soup and decently spiced drunken noodles.  The service was adequate and they kept my drink filled.  Overall it was some decent Thai food at around the current price point most of the other places are running.  Overall it is a decent place on the Wank to grab some Thai food.

Junction is a dive bar that offers over 40 beers on tap along with plenty of other beers in cans and bottles.  Junction also makes a good burger at a decent price and they also are one of the few spots you can get a good fish & chips in the city.  They have a nice selection of options to kick the burger level up a few degrees.  They also do quite a very nice job on their fries here too.  The staff seemed to be enjoying themselves at work and took good care to make sure drinks were filled.  I actually still think the burger at The Green Room Kukhnya  is a bit better though while the fries at Junction would win that throwdown.  My video review of Junction Bar & Grill is here:  https://youtu.be/Zwzu3XQR0RI

This is a very cool looking bar & restaurant that looked like it had opened not too long ago.  It seems more restaurant than bar but they have a great selection of draft beer.  They also have a great patio here and they have taken a lot of effort to make a really fun space here. During my visit they had some great music and I really enjoyed my visit.  They had great bartenders that took good care of me and were happy to chat and tell me more about the business.  I had noticed this place had been packed several times during my stay in Nashville but by the time I got around to visiting it was pretty laid back and calm but the good music, nice service and cold beer certainly give me plenty of reasons to linger on for quite awhile and enjoy the hospitality here.

Guillory's Deli & Tamales is located inside a residential neighborhood in Metairie where it originally opened as a grocery store in 1972 where they then developed their now famous tamales in 1998. Guillory's offers a a lot of great food in the small package of their deli.  Some of the great things I've enjoyed include their po'boys, daily specials and obviously their tamales. The only thing I'm not happy with here is they don't have fresh brewed iced tea. Guillory's is a very popular lunch spot and they offer a lot of options that they put a lot of effort into making which has paid off for them as all that work has made this a very popular spot with people from the surrounding neighborhood.   Link to my video review of Guillory's Deli & Tamales is here:  https://youtu.be/gbVIk9kOFW4

I've eaten here for many years and it's one of the better Chinese options Uptown.  Before Katrina I ate here very often but I rarely end up eating here anymore as there are so many new Vietnamese places that have opened nearer my house that I end up at those more often.  They have a decent selection of Asian items beyond just the expected Americanized Chinese offerings.  The prices are decent for the quantity you get and the service is generally adequate.

This is the largest Asian market on the Eastbank and they have a good selection of items and fresh produce.  This definitely isn't on the scale of Honk Kong Market on the Westbank but they do offer more than I expected.  I was disappointed I couldn't find my ginsing with royal jelly liquid herb supplement that I like but they had quite a impressive selection of Asian snack foods.  This space used to be Oki Nago and I had really loved that place and was sad to see how it declined and then died but this is a great addition to the area while offering some much needed variety compared to the normal American grocery store selection.

I have been to several Cavender's previously in Texas so I was curious if this one would equal my past experiences and I was pleased that it did.  They have the best selection of Western items and boots in the area along with some decent prices and good sale items.  The staff were friendly and I seemed to be the only person even in the store so I hope they usually get more traffic than during the time I was there.

I've attempted to eat at Yang's several times only to be disappointed that they had closed earlier than their posted hours.  I finally got the opportunity to sample an oyster/shrimp combo prior to Isaac making landfall.  The bread was less appealing than that I've had at many other places and the breading on the shrimp and oyster was a bit less crisp with a hint of mushiness to it.  It was a decent po boy but it wasn't in the same class as my favorite po boys.  The owner was very friendly and the staff was very quick at filling my order.  Overall I'd say this is a decent place to grab a quick po boy but the quality of the preparation is a bit less than some of my other favorite spots.  I will return to sample the roast beef.

This is the fastest rock ding repair I've ever had on my windshield.  They did a great job and you can barely tell where the damage was.  They literally had me in and out within about 5 minutes!  The last place I went to it ended up taking a good hour of time to get the process done and it didn't turn out very well.  For speed and quality of service I was very impressed with the service I received here.

This museum hosts one of the largest displays of Confederate artifacts from The War of Northern Aggression in the world.  They house a display of actual uniforms, swords, pistols, long arms, canons, flags and other artifacts used in the war.  They also have related items that put  some men like Jefferson Davis in a further context with items from their life and their families lives.  They also have soldier reenactors that will be present at times that can give even more context and explain in more detail the equipment and life of the typical soldier of the time.  There is also a small gift store with many affordable items and books.  The entrance fee is quite reasonable and if you're a history buff you will really enjoy this museum while if you're not a history buff you should educate yourself and start becoming one.

It's sort of like Commander's Palace except way too modern and with much worse service.  It really is quite a disappointment in many ways if you're used to the other Brennan restaurants.  This is more of a very casual establishment certainly designed to cater more to the tourists in the hotel than the locals.  I would certainly steer most people that want to experience a traditional NOLA fine dining experience to other spots but for those people that want to wear their sloppy velour tracksuits, shorts and blue jeans please come to Cafe Adelaide instead of ruining the locals fine dining traditions at Commander's Palace.  There are times and places to be casual and there are times and places for dressing up and we do like our traditions in NOLA that set us apart from the rest of the all casual all the time world outside our civilization.

This is one of the few fine dining restaurants in the Lakeview area and the only steakhouse.  The ambiance leaves a lot to be desired and the space itself is a long narrow stretch.  The food is usually good and the service is typically excellent.  This is a pretty good value for a nicer restaurant but they certainly could use some work in the interior to make it a bit nicer.

I found my pho here to be on the light side in the meat and noodle department.  Instead of basil I got salad greens.  The ambiance of the restaurant is a bit off as sound echos inside it and they have televisions on that create a weird acoustic sensation as the noise bounces all over.  The service was very good and the broth was very flavorful but I was actually still hungry after completing my bowl of pho which has never happened before in my long experience of eating this Vietnamese delicacy.  I was actually able to consume 2 spring rolls, 2 cookies, a snowball, a small "Korean" melon and a rambutan fruit immediately after which would have been impossible with every other bowl of pho I've ever eaten.

No more 3 for 1 drinks and instead it's pay double price for 1 beer apparently.  I was charged $8 for one Abita Amber so since that's more than a six pack at the grocery so... I won't be returning here.  This location is far off the tourist path of Bourbon and should be catering more to locals but as a local I'm not paying such ridiculous prices.

This place is just a long narrow space with a long narrow bar.  You can play pool, listen to the jukebox, and drink cheap drinks.  The color scheme is red just like the door... well maybe more of a deep burgundy but that's just splitting hairs.  There ALWAYS seem to be people in this joint and I think it might stay open 24/7.  I've never done more than grab a few drinks in here when eating at one of the several area restaurants but service has always been good and it seems like a decent place to just hang out.

So just the facts:  Buffet here is darn good but not the best Indian buffet I've ever had.  Menu is pretty awesome and I love the "Nirvana Special" most especially!!!  I have had terrible service here a few times but usually it is decent.  Buffet is everyday at lunch they are open and then on Thursday and Sunday nights (you can also get a FREE sample on Sundays at Rendezvous Bar).  Don't believe anything vegetarians tell you about this place as they have brain damage from a lack of meat protein and too many carbs :)

The people of France gave the golden bronze statue of Joan of Arc to the City of New Orleans in 1959.  Unfortunately New Orleans was unable to find a way to pay the  expense to erect the statue so it wasted away in storage for eight years. Fortunately private funding was secured and the statue was was finally placed on a 17 foot pedestal in front of the International Trade Market at the foot of Canal Street.  When Harrah's Casino was constructed in 1999 the statue had to be moved to its present location of the "Place De France" on Decatur Street in the French Quarter next to the French Market on Decatur Street.  This statue is an exact copy of the 1880 Emmanuel Fremiet equestrian statue of Joan located at Place des Pyramides, Paris.    The inscription on the pedestal of St. Joan of Arc's statue reads as follows:  JOAN OF ARC  MAID OF ORLEANS  1412 - 1431  Gift of the People of France  There is an annual parade in the French Quarter honoring Joan of Arc on her birthday every January 6th which also happens to coincide with Twelfth Night which is the official beginning of the Carnival Season.

This place when it first opened wasn't that good.  Over the last few years they had really stepped up their game and were doing much better food than the nearby Oki Nago that has been in decline.  On my most recent visit this place seems to have experienced a serious decline as well.  I'm afraid they are seriously letting the quality of their food go down.  The difference between my lunch today and my last visit several months ago was astounding.  The selection and quality just were nowhere near what they had been and most of the food just wasn't very good.

This is a pretty nifty place to go and sample many wines and then if you find one you like they will be happy to sell you a bottle or case.  They also have a decent beer and cheese selection.  I've been to a few events and birthday parties here and it is a pretty laid back place to enjoy yourself.  They have nifty Enomatic machines (AKA wine on tap) that you get a card (rechargeable with money) to use for sampling various amounts of wine in increasing volumes (that are consistent) for increasing prices (that vary by wine).  So (C = V x P/B) or the state of NOLA Crunk equals the volume of wine times price divided by your budget.

So after many years of missed opportunities I finally ended up having brunch at the original Rugby Slipper location.  I'm not a big breakfast food person but I do love some veal grillades which they didn't have those so skipping to the lunch items...  The "Gulf Fish St. Peter" (drum on the last visit) was done well while the grit cake was really large and the spinach was nice but I really would've liked it served with a biscuit or toast of some sort.  I was also left looking for a steak and eggs which I didn't see...  The Reuben sandwich is a nice option along with a selection of a few other sandwiches and the shrimp omelette can peak my palette.   Overall it's a decent brunch and lunch spot with some good drinks and fairly priced beer.  The Sunday brunch line moved faster than the brunch wait at Katie's but I find I prefer the food at Katie's more.  For a causal brunch spot that can get you seated within a reasonable time this is a good choice.

I'm a big fan of La Petite Grocery and their new restaurant, Balise, doesn't disappoint.  They have done a major renovation of this former dive bar space and significantly elevated the character of the space while still maintaining a NOLA feel to it.  The burger is almost as good as Lat Petite Grocery's but doesn't quite reach the same level while the fries are better.  Beyond the burger the menu is quite distinct from La Petite's while still keeping the noted quality that I've come to expect.  This location also has a beautiful bar that makes it quite a pleasant spot to enjoy happy hour and is framed by the stuffed head of a waterbuck and also sports a goat skull under glass (any bar with animal head trophies on display is a win in my carnivore book).  Overall this is a nice addition to the area and the NOLA restaurant scene.

This place will often have a line out the door but don't let that deter you as often these are folks that are ordering "to go" and you can scoot right past them for dining room service.  They have pretty good food here that defies the expectations you might have from the really rough looking exterior.  They absolutely have the largest, greasiest, and most extraordinary eggroll I've ever seen anywhere.  This is very Americanized Chinese that more specifically seems to cater to Southerners love of deep fried foods so many menu items here are really greasy.  I once bit into one of these monstrous eggrolls and grease from it spewed all over my shirt and it took many months of washings to finally get all that waterproof grease out (if it is that hard to wash out God knows what it does to your arteries).  I think the two "healthiest" things I've ever eaten here are the Moo Goo Gai Pan and the shrimp in lobster sauce.  If nothing else I think you should sample their eggroll at least once in your life.

I've eaten here a few times and the restaurant is a nice little spot off of Carrollton.  They have an open kitchen and its nice to sit at the bar and watch the food being cooked.  They offer some standard NOLA dishes with their own unique spin along with some things that veer off into the very creative.  The food ranges from average to excellent depending on the dish and when you visit.  This is generally a very casual restaurant with food that trends more towards fine dining.  Its certainly a very intimate space and one of the smaller restaurants in New Orleans so, even though I've never been here when it was crowded, reservations are probably the safe way to go here.  This establishment is certainly worthy of a visit for lunch or dinner.

This is the bar of Antoine's and they offer their own menu (with some limited offerings from Antoine's).  This is a great space and they make great drinks.  I've always enjoyed myself here and it is a great place for a quick lunch (or a long one).  My only complaint would be they are a bit haphazard with what you can and can't order off of the Antoine's menu.  If you want to sample some of Antoine's food without the full formal dining experience (but that is a big part of the experience!!!) then this will be a good introduction.  This is a great place for couples and groups.

The food is decent here but nothing outstanding.  They seem to always have a pretty respectable rotation of daily specials. Portions are very small for the price and the biggest irritant to me is that they only sell bottled iced tea and don't make their own.  I really don't trust any restaurant that won't take the time to brew their own iced tea!   Every meal I've had here has left me lacking in the fullness department so I've always had to get something else to eat relatively soon after eating here.  The small portions coupled with the lack of iced tea multiplied by the prices have resulted in me probably never returning here.

Just like their original location in the Warehouse District this joint has an awesome daily happy hour with great food specials and OK drink specials.  The margaritas aren't my favorite here so I'm usually going to stick with the beer.  If you deviate from the happy hour specials and order something special such as adding cheese it will increase the cost of the taco quite a bit.  I like this location far more than their original location as it has much more space and I just like this part of town far better than the Warehouse District.

So I finally got around to sampling the BBQ brisket after numerous aborted attempts.  The brisket is ok but they are damn skimpy with the sauce and that always incites some grumpy feelings in me!  The real stars are the sides in this joint as they really get creative and interesting with some of the stuff they do.  Definitely not the best BBQ and doesn't come close to the Joint but still a cool dive bar in an absolute nightmare scary location!

Bad news: No lunch!  Before Katrina I really enjoyed eating lunch here but after Katrina they have never brought lunch back and only do Brunch on the weekends now.    There is a pop up BBQ restaurant that operates out of this space M-F for lunch and Tuesday nights for dinner.  Good news: They have certainly stepped up the culinary level!  They always seem to be featuring as many local and very fresh options as possible and the food is always excellent here.  They have a nice courtyard and it is a very enjoyable place (especially at lunch so please bring lunch back!!!).  The parking can be a bit challenging but other than that I've always had a great time here and the service has always been fantastic.  I'm not a big breakfast person so I've yet to eat brunch here but the food is so good that it is probably just a matter of time before I get here (the next time someone forces me to awaken at some horribly early hour on the weekend).

This review is for their website and their actual hours.  The website of this place says they are open until 5pm during the week but when you get to the actual location they actually close at 3pm.  Their Saturday hours listed on the website are until 5pm but in actuality they close at 3pm and then Noon on Sunday.  I've made several trips attempting to try this place out but they are closed every time I get there.  Working a regular 8 to 5 job makes it very hard to ever get to this place and I've nearly given up being able to ever find this place open.

The interior of this place seemed vaguely similar to Balise as I walked in.  They have a main dining area with a bar for drinking and another separate bar seating area for eating.  It was much larger than I thought it would be inside so they made good use of the available space.  I didn't know they had started lunch service and just happened to driving past around lunch by chance when I noticed they were open so I decided to give it a try.  They offer a lunch special menu along with their regular menu and I decided to go with the lunch special fish, which was a drum.  The fish was well prepared and a fair portion size for the price.  The only issues I have is that the service wasn't that attentive and my server didn't have a good knowledge of the menu.  The prices also seem a bit too expensive for the neighborhood.  Overall I enjoyed my time here and could see returning if the service improved just a bit.

This place is brought to you by the same family that has R&O's.  This seems to be going for a bit more of an upscale move up from the more family dive joint atmosphere of R&O's but not too much as it still seems more sports bar in a lot of ways.  The food definitely has fancier options available and the interior and furniture are also certainly nicer.  Their gumbo and roast beef po boy are alright but I still prefer R&O's personally.  I probably wouldn't get the po boy again here and would just stick with the entrees as they just seem to provide better quality and price for what you get.  They do have some really good fish dish options here.  This is probably the nicest restaurant currently in the Elmwood area.  I will rate it four stars for the Elmwood area but for the NOLA area overall it is more of a three star joint to me.  I think they can really get this place chugging along well and seem to have the ability to put out some really good food here but still seem to have some inconsistencies and need to work on improving many dishes.

Nothing really stands out here to me but everything is decent to good.  The ambiance of this place seems a bit blah and could use more  feng shui or something to give it some more character and flow.  For the Bywater this joint is alright but I'm not sure it would make it in another part of town without some tweaks.    The big draw of this joint is that it offers food later into the night so for that aspect it really shines and provides a much needed service for the area.  I really appreciate that they seem to care about using quality local ingredients and putting out good food here but the flavors seemed a bit bland in some dishes for my taste while others seemed to have had a lot of attention to being spiced and flavored well. They could really kick it up by adding more consistent spice, herbs and seasonings to all the dishes to give the food more life but then the flavor explosion might scare away the large Bywater population of fake ass hipsters that infest this area.

I really had higher expectations for a private venue and overall I just wasn't very impressed with this space.  I found it quite unacceptable that no entrance was allowed from the back door and the staff required you to do a long walk around to enter via the "front" door that really really felt more like a back door.  Personally I think this is definitely on the bottom tier of event spaces in NOLA and there are MANY far better spaces that offer a lot more quality, charm and old NOLA ambiance than this space.  This space could be anywhere blah else strip mall America.

This chain really just doesn't even close to measuring up to the local Middle Eastern options.  Lebanon Cafe, Mona's, Pyramid, Shwarma to Go etc. are all significantly better at around the same price point along with providing table service.  The music was turned up so loud it was challenging to communicate my order in further complicated by the fact the guy taking my order was a Spanish speaker that didn't seem to be very good with English.  I got a combo plate and tried to add the hummus and flafal as sides but that was not comprehended so I had to go back and reorder when an English speaker arrived.  The iced tea was also left with no lemons.    Overall I ended up spending more money here for a lower quality product and inferior service to all other Middle Eastern options I have eaten at in the NOLA area.  This place sort of reminded me of Chipotle except Chipotle has a good quality product at a great value.  I don't see any reason to return to one of these Halal Guys chain locations again.

I haven't stayed in the hotel and I've just visited the upstairs bar and downstairs cafe & bar but I did tour the public spaces.  Overall it seems to be a rather well appointed hotel placed within a small footprint.  The location is a bit away from the hustle and bustle of the French Quarter while being near enough to still go to enjoy it if one were on a tourist adventure.  It is still quite a new space so I'm sure it still has some time to develop its character and we shall see how it fits into the overall landscape of NOLA.

This is an "ok" time but is more shopping than festival focused.  They have started imposing all sorts of rules and have started selling wine instead of giving it away free like they had always done in the past.  Too much political interference is really causing a drag on this event!

Ambiance is kind of nice with the old house feel but it can be a bit tight in the seating areas.  The service is adequate but the food is very slow in coming.  The food was nothing outstanding and there are plenty of better Italian pasta and pizza places around town doing better food.  The food isn't bad it just isn't nearly as good as most of the other pizza and pasta around town to my taste.  On my last visit I also got charged 50 cents for a tiny little cup of marinara sauce to eat with my pizza.  They do have a good drink special here on Tuesdays with $5 pitchers of beer and half off bottles of wine.  They also have a nice patio area for when its nice outside.  I would probably only come here on a Tuesday but it is crowded due to the special so plan ahead.  They might get up to three stars with some of their food but so far all my visits have been two star experiences.

This is a cool and laid back fest that is mostly local folks.  The crowd is never crowded and is very manageable which makes for a very relaxing and enjoyable vibe at this event.  There is a good selection of food vendors and they have a lot of arts and craft vendors.  This is a great time and best of all its FREE!!!

This is one of the few places in the immediate area to get live bait shrimp and that's the primary business I've engaged in with this establishment.  They also offer dry dock storage, cleaning services, maintenance services and all sorts of other things related to keeping your boat in good working condition.  The ship store is where you get live bait shrimp and it also offers fishing tackle and accessories along with the important things like snacks, ice, drinks and beer.

A small restaurant in a Metairie strip mall but this strip mall is actually hidden away and you can easily drive past it and never notice it so it could be the most secret strip mall in the NOLA metro area so you get the added bonus of "mystery."    The pizza here is decent while the space is small but it does have a little side courtyard.  The lasagna here tastes like the frozen type you buy in the grocery and cook in the oven so I'm not sure if they make their own our outsource for the pre-made but I've certainly had better tasting but I've also had worse.  The main thing I don't like about this place is the bathroom situation is rather limited and really needs to be improved.  They seem to have a good stream of regulars here for lunch and it seems like a popular spot in the area.  The pizza seems to be the best choice here and they do have it available by the slice in limited topping options.

I'm a big fan of the fact they use the excellent and Louisiana local Smith Creamery dairy products in making their tasty treats.  I'm often much less a fan of many of their flavors of gelato.  I'm often just in the mood for plain strawberry and I respect the fact they attempt to use things that are locally in season but even when strawberries are in season they usually don't have just a plain strawberry.  I can appreciate their wild and whacky combinations but sometimes I just want plain strawberry.

I've seen some good bands here but the experiences have definitely seemed to have been consistently declining with every event I attend here.  The vending prices here have grown as outrageous as the Superdome (so I just refuse to partake of any food or drink in this rip off price gouging pure highway robbery of a racket).  The parking NAZIs are in full effect around here so you either end up getting trapped in the long vehicle lines to get into the venue and have to pay for parking or you try to park off site and walk but then they find a way to tow you unlike in the past when there was free parking at UNO.  The security just seems to be ready to jump on people for the smallest of infractions that would merit just a verbal warning in most other places.  My past multiple experiences here have been so increasingly BLAH I'm about ready to just call it quits and say I won't return unless the Beatles reunite and play or Elvis rises from the dead for a show.

I don't really like buttermilk drops as they taste pretty much like doughnuts to me and I don't like doughnuts.  Most of the desserts here focus on doughnut shop type items which don't appeal to me.  They do have some brownies, cookies, cakes and pies that are quite nice.  They also serve hamburgers and po boys in here but I haven't had a chance to try the real food yet.  This would be a good breakfast spot for those that love doughnut shop type fare and then a good lunch spot for folks like me that don't.

Da Wabbit sign is probably the coolest thing about this place as it is some 1950's style pink Bugs Bunny.  The menu has a selection of diner/New Orleans dishes and the place is divided into a bar and dining area.  The food here kind of reminds me of Joey K's but maybe a bit better.  The inside actually is far nicer than you would think from looking at the outside and very comfortable.  They have a choice of different lunch specials that rotate through the week.  The seafood gumbo does not disappoint as, unlike many places these days, they load it down with shrimp and oysters.  They also have a respectable turtle soup here that has very large chunks of turle in it. They serve very healthy portion sizes and the service has always been very friendly and quick.  The food is good for what it is and this place draws a large crowd of dedicated regulars.

This bar has an upstairs and a downstairs and it seems to have different things going on in each respective level.  The downstairs is more of a bar area while upstairs is where they usually have live music and serve tapas.  The tapas I've eaten here has been among my least favorite tapas in New Orleans (except for possibly that frightful stuff that Salu puts out).  I've been yelled at a couple of times in here by random people for "not being from the Marigny" and because I "dress like somebody from Uptown" which I guess means I engage in personal hygiene while refusing to wear douche bag skinny jeans and dressing like some smelly hipster (I would imagine these were fresh transplants as most local NOLA people are having too much fun to do stupid things like that).  I've also spotted several random celebrities eating in here late night as it is one of the few late night spots to grab some food in the area.  This is an alright late night spot if you're in the area as there is usually a decent crowd of interesting people in here.

This is a great little Italian place and I've eaten here for many years.  I especially enjoy lunch when they give you FREE martinis but dinner is a great time as well.  The corn and crab bisque in the bread "bowl" is a must and they always give you some great garlic/cheese bread to kick off your meal.  EVERYTHING I've ever had here has been outstanding and the service has always been above all expectations.  I really can't recommend this place enough and you have to eat both lunch and dinner here ASAP!!!

I've had days where I've been working on a home repair project and had to visit this store up to 10 times in a single day.  I've had last minute plumbing emergencies where I've made it with literally seconds before they close to acquire the items I needed.  I've generally not enjoyed my visits here and I've often grown frustrated with often having to make so many visits here but I'm glad it is here and not far off in the burbs when I have a need for it.  The joy of owning a historic shotgun home in New Orleans is the never ending stream of repairs that happen which are also multiplied when its a shotgun double so you get double duty of repairs.  I dread my next mandatory visit but I love the fact that at least it isn't too far away from my home.

They have some good Latin and Caribbean food here along a few random food items like pizza thrown in.  Live music and no cover charge usually makes this a main stop on any tour of Frenchmen Street.  They have more expensive drinks than DBA or Blue Nile so I guess they incorporate a cover charge with their increased drink prices.  There is generally a good crowd here with an energetic vibe so a fun spot to check out typically.

I really loved the prior That restaurant here, Basil Leaf Thai, and I'm sad its gone as their hot and sour soup was one of my favorite things in the city.  This new Thai spot also has a good hot and sour soup but its much more similar to La Thai's (which is also one of my favorites).  The food here is generally pretty good and it is certainly one of the top Thai spots in the area.  The service can be inconsistent but is usually adequate.  I've heard good things about their lunch specials and wish I could get into the area to try them but in the meantime I've had some enjoyable dinners here.

This is a large consignment store that has a great number of very interesting things.  The prices range all over the place so you have to shop around and really look at lots of things.  I've seen things here I've never seen anywhere else so this is really a great place if you're looking for a unique piece of furniture or household decoration.  Definitely one of the more interesting places to shop for home goods.

This is the best local place to purchase your "official" Saints and LSU gear.  They have a huge collection of nearly anything you could imagine with a Saints theme.  They also carry a much smaller assortment of Hornets paraphernalia.  The crowds can get crazy sometimes and the parking is often a nightmare so going during the off season is your best strategy.  They also often have good sales on older Saints T-Shirts for around $5 along with some other sale items.

They have some nifty T-shirts in here and a lot of unique items that can only be found here.  They specialize in New Orleans and Louisiana (and also now Austin, TX) themed shirts.  They have a collection of Saints shirts that are a bit more original than the standard NFL issue ones you might find everywhere else.  They have some other stuff engineered to peak the fancy of women so be careful about getting dragged in here with females as they will find hours of entertainment while men can usually complete a satisfactory search in about ten minutes.  They also have a website that works far better for those who really don't want to endure the pain of a "shopping" trip (except there are usually some nice looking ladies shopping here so that can make the experience more bearable).

Sometimes I space out and miss the exit I need to take to get on the Expressway when I work out of my Wank office.  I then get to travel through this scary tunnel!  Your radio signal goes dead as you descend into the bowls of the Earth until you see the glimmer of light at the end of the tunnel and rush towards the light!  I'm always really glad to get out of this tunnel!  I don't trust tunnels under canals!

I live really nearby this tourist mecca and there always seem to be a lot of folks interested in this historic cemetery.  Lafayette Cemetery No. 1 is the oldest of the seven city operated cemeteries in New Orleans.  You can easily make a trip out of visiting the cemetery and eating at Commander's Palace across the street.    You do have to wonder though how they control the smell of decaying bodies with the way the above ground crypts and vaults are laid out as it seems that there would be a terrible smell in the neighborhood from decaying flesh.  They seal the burials in a few ways depending on the "internment vehicle"  so that seems to control any odor problems and I've never personally smelled anything foul or heard of anyone that did.  To learn more check this website out:  http://lafayettecemetery.org/

This is an ok seafood place.  I've frequently had the crawfish here as this is usually the place to grab it for parties during Jazz Fest.  I've also bought decent raw oysters here.  They have a selection of po boys and fried seafood platters that are usually good.  This place often has a great aroma of cooking seafood and is probably the best spot in Mid-City to grab boiled seafood but I prefer the crawfish and shrimp at Big Fisherman on Magazine.

This is a small pasta joint to the rear of The Tasting Room where you order at the counter from their small menu of freshly made pastas and sauces along with a few appetizers.  The pasta and sauces are all good and seem decently priced except I find the quantity to be a bit smaller than I would like as I'm used to much larger servings of pasta in most restaurants in the area.   Word is definitely getting out about this place as the few tables in the courtyard seating area stayed mostly full during my last visit.  If they continue to do well rumor has it that they might move to a larger and more established location.  In conjunction with some wine from The Tasting Room in the front you can certainly make an enjoyable and affordable evening meal of wine and pasta at this location.

The Bad:  Cash only.... it's the 21st Century... groan...   You have to request ice as the drink machine doesn't dispense it.  Ketchup available as a condiment but not mustard?  Give me my mustard as I hate ketchup!!!!  I thought Ben's was "better" than Bud's and I don't taste a difference and it doesn't taste that great sober.  With ATM fees my meal cost $9 and change for a #4 burger, chili cheese fries and small drink so not a good value and way better burgers available at that price point.  The Good:  Open 24/7 and in Metry that's hard to find.  Serves beer!  They do offer a wheat bun option.  Has video poker so more money can be sucked out of suckers to increase tax revenue.  Overall I think this place is best regulated to late night eating to sober up and see no reason to ever eat here again sober.

Ok it is getting to be a real painful pattern that Oak is ALWAYS running out of beer.  Last night they were out of Abita Amber by 9pm.  It is just a bad repeating incident that they keep selling out of beer nearly every time I go.  How much trouble is it to keep some extra in stock?  It has gotten incredibly frustrating and really has led me to skip many happy hours with friends that frequent this place at this point.
