The triple cheese was grilled with a buttery crust which gave it a bit of chew and goo that makes for a fine sandwich.  And the smoked tomato bisque I ordered as an additional side added great depth to the meal.  Besides the smokiness, there was a taste of oregano (I think) that kept the soup from tasting like something out of a can.  Tasty!  Good food and service made for an enjoyable lunch.  Review #181

I recently returned to campus to explore their impressive collection of public art.  Having been a graduate of the university back in 1980, I was amazed at the transformation the grounds of the school had undergone.  Back then, most of the art was confined to the classrooms and to exhibits that were put on by the art department.  Now, there are green ways and a water installation as well as nearly two dozen art installations.   As a fan of bringing art to the masses, I believe the school should be commended for its devotion to the arts.  Only the campus of IUPUI has a more expansive collection than this private school.  In fact, U of I has published a walking tour of the numerous pieces.     If you are a fan of art, plan a trip to visit this campus to appreciate the creativity and artistic expression on campus.  Review #158

Although the number of vendors wasn't large, there were quite a few items that I purchased on my visit.   I found a number of cheeses from Shipshewana.  There were cobblers and pies from Generations Pie Company in Fishers.  I also picked up a loaf of fresh sourdough bread from Circle City Sweets located inside the Indy City Market.  It didn't take long to browse through the place to see what was there, and because of that, the lines were short as people were coming and going the entire time.  That made parking available too.    If you are looking for local products, but don't want to spend all morning doing it, give the winter market a try.  Review #2018

As proud as I am of the city Indianapolis has become in my over forty years living here, I must admit I am humbled by the City's namesake ship and the men who will always be connected with the ship.  While many have heard of the horrendous tale of the sailors who first survived a submarine attack only to fall prey to denizens of the sea, there was also a mission that was completed.  The USS Indianapolis delivered the atomic bomb successfully to a location that was within bombing range of Japan.  That mission, though devastating in its own purpose, saved an estimated 2 million lives that would have died if an invasion of the islands were needed to end the War.  Because of the secrecy of the mission, radio silence prevented immediate help to the damaged (soon sunken) ship.  For five days, men survived as best they could without food, water, and cover from the sun, and shark attacks from below.  The memorial, somewhat shaped like the vessel, includes panels describing the ship on the north side, and the tale of survival on the south.  There is also an etching of the ship on the north side.  Review #1611

This shop has an eclectic mix of gifts, toys, and women's clothing.  Located along Washington Street, there is street parking out front and a shared lot behind the row of businesses.    I found the variety to be more unique than most gift shops I've been to, but familiar enough to be appealing.  Although the shop is relatively small, I didn't feel like it was overstocked and restrictive for movement.  Though I didn't have anything in mind when browsing, I did stumble upon something I had been planning to buy and at a price that was very affordable.  Double win!!  The staff was friendly and checkout was quick and easy.    Review #1121

I enjoy going to Pier 1, especially at the holiday season.  Everything is marked down and the store if filled with Christmas accessories throughout.  Beyond the candles, runners, dishes, and stuffed items, they still have some of their furniture and household items making up the remainder of the store.  The staff was friendly and advised me of a further discount I had missed seeing.  Good salesmanship and good savings for me!  Review #1924

After lunch in Broad Ripple, I looked across the street and saw Nicey Treat.  I recalled several of the Yelpers I follow/befriended had given it great ratings, so I headed over to give it a try.  They have a variety of uncommonly flavored popsicles that can be dipped in milk chocolate or dark chocolate for an additional charge.  I chose to splurge and go with the Strawberry Cream and have it dipped in dark chocolate.    The flavor was quite good.  I believe the dark chocolate has a coconut oil added that helps it solidify.  I could definitely taste the coconut flavor in my treat which surprised me that it was nearly as strong a flavor as the chocolate and strawberry.  Fortunately, I like coconut and the flavors I chose paired well with it. I mention it only for those who choose one of the more exotic flavors that may not pair well.    All in all, it was good, and probably a lower calorie treat than nearby Brics or Graeters.  Unfortunately, I devoured it much quicker than one of the competitor's much larger scoops.  So, for the price, I personally prefer the cone over the stick.  Review #111

This was a nice collection of booths and rooms for browsing.  It isn't as big as some of the mega antique malls I've visited, but it does have a nice variety of items, including furniture, inside its walls.  I was greeted as I entered and did see some things of interest, but didn't make any purchases this day.  It was a a little odd seeing several antiques that I remember having in our home as I was growing up in the 60's...items that were considered old even then.  A bit of nostalgia may have influenced my opinion, but I liked stopping by.  Review #1911

This is a nice shop that carries most of the supplies your pet would need.  What I noticed right away is that it seemed like everything was on sale.  However, what I figured out later (and isn't really mentioned on their website) is that if you become a "member" on their website (sign up for member emails), you get the lower price.   If you don't, you pay full price.  I don't live in the area and there isn't one near me, so I didn't want to give out my email address for a one time purchase.  So, all the items that I thought might be at a really good price were no better than I could get at lots of other places.  If it's convenient and you want to join their club, you will probably like this place.  Otherwise, it's not worth going out of your way for.  Review #2137

I usually dine at the Jockamo's in Greenwood, but decided to travel to the east side today and grab lunch at this one instead.  The place has a front and rear (parking lot) entrance and is divided into several rooms including the main ordering counter/dining room, and a large bar area to the west.  Since I was dining by myself, I opted for the no waiting seating in the bar where they have some 4 top tables besides the chairs at the bar counter.  I was greeted and had good service throughout the meal.  I went with a lunch special since I wanted pizza (I usually get sandwiches in Greenwood) but not an entire pie.  The daily special was a tasty bacon cheddar slice that was really good.  Because it's thin crust, I was able to fold it, but did have trouble keeping the chopped tomatoes in the fold.  Still, the flavors were nicely balanced and when combined with a small side salad, made for a filling lunch.  Checkout was quick and easy and almost made me wish I didn't have to worry about calories since they have a great assortment of sandwiches and whole pizzas.  Review #2287

I stopped in and enjoyed the three house brews I sampled in my flight.  Being a micro brewery, less than half of their taps were house options.  Since I am not an IPA fan, I went with three house and one guest tap, the Breakfast Magpie by New Day Meadery.  The Dry Hopped Blonde called "Han Shot 1st" was hoppier than most blonde ales (5.2%).  The Scotch Ale was dark and rich (6.3%).  The Gose (4%) was tart and would pair well with some of the food options they offer.  They do have Cuban food available, but since we ate before arriving, we didn't sample it.    There is plenty of free parking in the lot on the south end of the building  (2200 block of east 46th street).  The entrance to the Brewery is on the south east corner.  A ramp is available as well as stairs.  Review #299

For those looking for the Museum at the Soldiers and Sailors Monument (middle of Monument Circle) to find this museum, you are looking in the wrong place.  Back in 2018, the collection was moved to the Indiana World War Monument (431 N Meridian) to provide more display space and to do repair work under the Soldiers and Sailors Monument.  As of the time of this review, the collection has been moved for over a year and my thoughts are part of the review listed on that location.  According to the staff working in the Soldiers and Sailors gift shop (located on the south side of the monument at the top of the steps), something new will occupy the space under the monument once repairs have been completed.  It has not been released what will go in the space.  Review #2581

In the basement of the building just north of Litre House, there is a delightful collection of antiques, vintage clothing, house wares/decor, and vinyl.  The space is very inviting and the owners, including the house Pug will greet you when you arrive.    There are numerous open booths where you may find some beautiful furniture or crystal.  There may be china sets or old toys that you haven't seen in years.    If you are in the area, you can find free parking on the north side of the building.  Fun place to check out!  Review #2157

I was pleasantly surprised at the amount of items this place had.  There were lots of hobbies represented here.  I think it unfairly categorized by some as a guy's place, but guys definitely can find a lot of interests covered.    Since I am not into all these hobbies, I can't say if the selection is the best, but at least they have items on hand and may be able to help you track down what you are looking for.    I was also glad to see they carried board games and supplies/tools for working on assorted hobbies.  A nice place to browse around and to get ideas if you are looking for starting something new!  Review #1925

Nice little restaurant on the first block north of the underpass on Meridian.  Though a little bit of a hike for folks working on the circle, it is still close enough to catch some of those customers as well as those visiting the Convention Center.  I stopped in for lunch and they have appropriately sized portions for about $6 which includes sides and complementary chips.  I ordered the Classic Chimichanga with Ground Beef, but was surprised when it came with shredded chicken.  My waitress didn't stop by until after I had decided to go ahead and eat it, so I didn't bother complaining.  The chimi was about 6" which when combined with the beans and rice, was plenty for me.  Good taste and the chicken was moist and tender.  Just enough spice for flavor, but not much heat.  Decent food for a good price (especially for downtown).  Just need to get the staff to check in on customers more frequently.  Review #2583

If you like Caesar Salad, then I highly recommend the Grilled Chicken Caesar Wrap!  Great grilled flavor of the chicken paired really well with the mini salad (including a few croutons!) inside the wrap.  And the portion was generous too!  If you need more than this, they do have some sides, but I haven't tried those yet.  Located in the south east corner of City Market, there is an order window with some of the entrees written out on small black boards.  They also have printed menus on the right of those.  When it is your turn to order, they take your payment, give you a number, and then you wait for it to be called.  I grabbed one of the bar stools nearby that looks like it is from an unused kitchen (maybe they have classes or demonstrations there.)  For dining, you either take your selection to go or haul it up the stairs to the seating that overlooks the market.  This is a place I would gladly return!  Review #2297

I stopped in at Crown Liquors while out shopping in Fishers.  I wanted to get a bottle of Hendricks Gin as a present as well as check on different flavored mixes for frozen cocktails.  This corner store has its own lot and was easy to get into and out of.  Inside, there is a lot of space and I was able to quickly identify the sections I needed.    Not only did they have two sizes of his favorite, they also had a limited edition with more botanicals that was an option.    I also found some flavors of mixes that my local stores didn't offer.  Checkout was quick and smooth.  I don't buy frequently enough to say how their pricing compares to other stores, but I liked the variety and service.  Review #3441

Here is another nice park for the folks in Broad Ripple.  This one features tennis and volleyball courts, a splash park, a playground for kids, and a small swing playground for toddlers.  There is a shelter with picnic tables but I didn't see a grill.  There are restrooms and a water fountain available during park season.  There is shade for adults who might not be participating in the splash park.    Note:  I thought the tennis courts looked like they were in really good condition compared to many I've visited.  Review #595

My wife loves this store (I like it, but not as enthusiastically).  She loves browsing through the items and enjoys seeing how they make arrangements so that she can take some of their ideas and use them at home.  On this stop, she noted some table lamps and a couple paintings that she is keeping an eye on.  She's a smart shopper and knows that there will likely be a sale soon, so she wants to go back in the near future.  I enjoy seeing the variety of items and if our home was larger, things I would add to my den/computer room/workout room.    We will be return!  Review #1953

In a state with 50+ covered bridges that are over 130 years old, it makes sense that the State Fair should have one of its own.  But since moving one of these treasured bridges is too expensive (and may cause some hard feelings), the state built a new one back in 2008.  The placement and function are perfect as it spans 90 feet over the west entrance to the infield of the fairgrounds.  Not only does it serve as a road, but it has also been setup as the entrance to events like the Chinese Lantern Festival back in 2017.    The cool thing about covered bridges is that as you walk through, you can see the intricate design and woodwork needed to support the structure.  This burr arch truss style bridge is one of the most common in the area.  I like that this bridge also has windows that let you look out as you cross.  Just another thing to take note of when you visit the fair.  Review #2857

While out shopping with my wife, we stopped into this Broad Ripple Shop that sits high above street level along Cornell (I forgot to check if there is an easier access from their parking lot on the west side of the building.) After climbing the stairs to the front porch, we entered into the shop.  To the left of the shop is a row of dressing rooms for visitors to try on the women's clothing offered within the shop.  To the right are several rows of clothing that extend to the back of the shop.  To the immediate right of the doorway are accessories, party games, greeting cards, and other small gift items.  Based upon my wife's opinion, the clothing seemed to be high quality but also came with a higher price tag than what she was used to paying.  She found a gorgeous necklace almost immediately, but the nearly $400 price tag scared her off.    The ladies working were welcoming and offered to help find something if needed.  Review #3329

I am so glad I stopped by this shop on Small Business Saturday.  It is filled with so many cool toys and collectibles that it was hard to keep from smiling as I explored.    The shop is located in a shopping plaza on the southeast corner of the intersection.  The entrance faces Madison and is set back from the road quite a bit.  But there is plenty of free parking in the lot which lets you browse as long as you like.  The main entrance is filled with action figures, pops, and so many toys/collectibles that I remembered buying for our kids when they were little.  There were even some that went far back enough that they were something I had too.    The north section of the shop (a separate room) is filled with Lego pieces and kits.  I wasn't into those as a kid, but the place is packed, so if you are a fan, you need to check this place out.  Now that I am old(er), it is a little easier to resist making large purchases, but if you want to see your kids smile, bring your wallet when you bring them in.  It's like Christmas!  Review #3373

Greenwood finally has one of these tasty bundt cake bakeries of its own!  Just like the other locations around town, they sell a variety of bundt cakes in three sizes to meet your personal or party needs.  The shop can be found in the outlot north of the Home Depot.  It is a little tricky getting into and out of this lot because of the medians along Smith Valley Road and SR 135, but if you are patient, you can get here...it's worth the wait!  Not only do they have bundt cakes, but they also have some gift ideas on display as well.  And be sure to try the free samples they have...you may find a new favorite.  I found the cakes to be moist and light with just enough icing to pair with the cake flavors.  Even the smallest of the cakes is shareable, but not so large that you will feel like any is being wasted.  I picked up a Lemon Cake and a Carrot Cake variety.  Really good cakes that you can now get on the south side without having a long drive.  Review #3616

Even though I live in Mooresville, I was the Duke of the Zionsville home location of this business.  So, when I heard that a second location was opening on the south side inside the Greenwood Park Mall, I was thrilled!    My Sugar Pie sells pies, scones, and other baked items in small sizes, and even whole pies!  I usually just pick out individual slices so that I can sample lots of flavors since I don't have a favorite.  On this trip, I picked up a Peach Lattice, a Cherry Lattice, and a Mixed Berry.  I've had them all before so I knew I would be happy with these selections.  The shop is located near the entrance of the mall by the outdoor shops across from the Thai Ice Cream place.    This location also has round tables for friends to sit at while enjoying their selections.  There is also a wall of merchandise to browse while you are there.  I didn't see any beverages for sale, but I am not certain about that.  But because of the way the slices are packaged, there isn't any concern about transporting them.  If you like pies, make a point of stopping by!  Review #2181

Despite being downtown often, I had never stopped in for gas at this place.  I like that you can access this spot from both West Street and Kentucky Avenue.  There are lots of bays that are stacked 2-deep and the roof that covers the filling bays reaches all the way to the convenience store so you don't have to get rained on when you need to run inside.  The equipment seemed to work very well.  I had no issues at my pump and was able to get a receipt.  The other bays seemed to be nearly full too, so I guess that means they were working as well.  Out front, they carry ricks of fire wood, windshield washer, and I think I recall seeing ice (no propane tanks though.)  Since I don't buy things at gas station, I can't comment on customer service.  The only negative I have is that the space is packed, so there isn't a lot of room to turn around your vehicle when the place is busy, especially if you have one of the outer bays.  Review #3758

After discovering a new pocket park on the near east side, I stopped in at KIB to find out more about the park.  Did you know they have about 200 projects per year?  Inside their lobby, there are sign up sheets for projects that are being planned right now!    When I was working, my company planted over 40,000 trees in the Indy area.  KIB was right along side our volunteers.  We would often have to clean up areas before planting so that the trees would have the best opportunity to thrive.  Overall, it felt good to volunteer on these projects to see how much better a bare lot could look cleaned up and newly planted.  For a list of opportunities that you can become involved with, check out the KIB website.  Review #2304

This small shop on Main Street is part furniture store and part home decor (there seems to be items on just about every surface in the place!)  It has a farm house style for a lot of the items; there's even a mounted deer's head on the wall.    It has a different sense of space than most home decor places.  There are definitely lots of furniture pieces that take up most of the floor space.  But if you decorate in this style, it pays to look at all the shelves since they are loaded with goodies that you don't see in the big box places.  Note:  If you stop by, there are some cool historic photos of old Plainfield on the walls.  Pleasant shop with friendly service that doesn't bother you while you browse.  Review #2601

Everyone who is old enough to remember their feelings on that horrible day in 2001 will have some connection to this landmark along Indy's canal.  Though the location is surrounded by traffic (both vehicles and people), there is a sense of peace and quiet, of reverance, here.  The park was dedicated on the 10th anniversary of the event.  The memorial was designed by Bill Cotterman.  The eagle that is perched atop one of the beams was made by local firefighter/artist Ryan Feeney.  If you have an interest in the story behind the scenes, let me direct you to Wanda's review.  It is a fascinating read.  Review #1188

Not your traditional florists:  this place is filled with live plants and accessories for the plants and your home.  I couldn't get over how many live plants, all tastefully hanging or arranged, there were.   And they also had displays of stationery, artisan products, and an area that had macrame that could be used for supporting your purchases.  Small space, but with free street parking along the cross streets, and such a nice assortment, it is worth stopping by to see what might fit your own home.  Review #3369

Although this was my first visit to this location of Jockamo, I knew from my visits to the other locations in town that there was a good chance of finding something really tasty to eat!  I chose to bypass a small pizza and opted for the Italian Beef.   I don't know if it is the most authentic, but it sure is delicious.  Not only does it come with a thicker dipping sauce than most restaurants, but inside the sandwich were peppadew peppers that added another burst of flavor with each bite.  Really good.  My wife enjoyed her side salad and an order of breadsticks (3) that came with parmesan dipping sauce.    Review #3968

One of the newest places to eat inside the AMP is the latest expansion ofCaplinger's fresh catch seafood.  I Was there briefly to order their special  of fish and chips along with a side.  My favorite side is the collard greens.  It seemed the breading on the fish wasn't quite as crispy as l had desired.  The breading seemed more crumby and so I rate this location lower than some of the sites.   Seating is plentiful inside the AMPs food court.  Parking is still random while the garage is under construction.   For a change of pace from fast food lunches stop by here.Review #3981

This park is going to be so cool when it grows up.  Developed in 2017, the park has a new Amphitheater, paved walkways, two bridges that span Pleasant Creek which now handles more water (it's deeper and wider), a firehouse themed playground, and a gazebo.  Parking is conveniently located on the south.  From there, you can walk down the broad steps to the main level of the park or take a slight detour to the paved sloped trails which lead from the west end of the parking area.    The only knock I have is that the grass and the plantings aren't ready for all the activities the city wants to put on here.  I hope that whenever they have festivals and activities, that the plants will hold up to the foot traffic of all those who don't stay on the paved paths.  But once the plants get established, this should be a beautiful addition to the city's park and trail offerings.  Review #776

Although a lot of the park is open green space and lacks much character, I love the look of the playground and main pavilion area.  If I was a little kid again, this is the kind of playground I would have totally enjoyed.  Instead of the run of the mill playground like most parks, this place features "rocks" and sand trails.  I loved climbing and digging as a kid.  When you add the hidden surprises formed into the rock piles, I couldn't help but start searching for more (and there are plenty!)  The pavilion is large and has lots of shaded area and tables to relax while the kids play close by.  The grounds looked well maintained and the parking lot was just a few steps away if you needed to get something from the car.   Review #740

This 16 acre park is located on the east side of Carmel on Main St, nestling back into a neighborhood.  The front of the park has a lot of open space which turns out to be a mini disc golf course.  It has only 9 holes and the distances are on the short side compared to other area parks.  (Kid Sized?)  The entry road has parking spaces all along the way as it bends around the splash park, the large shelter, and back towards the woods where a small playground tower is nestled in the trees.  One side of the tower has wind chimes that vibrated along the rails of the tower while I was there.  Nice touch!    You could take a short hike through the woods, but because of the small size, you are within viewing distance of the nearby houses behind the park.  If you are looking for hiking, I would suggest other parks would offer more enjoyment.  The park seems to be well maintained and looks like a fun place for kids during the summer.  Otherwise, it's kind of limited.  Review #741

After lunch, I made a few stops and found myself in the neighborhood of this family owned business. (They own a shop in Florida as well.)  They are located between the Starbuck's and the McAlister's on SR 135, so there is plenty of convenient parking.  I was surprised at how many options were available for customers.  They have a wall display that shows the options.  They have pre-assigned scoop amounts for the different sized cups and cones.  Since I had already eaten and was only interest in a single scoop, the server suggested the "kiddie" size bowl which worked out fine!  I really like ice cream, but ever since Cafe Nonna closed in Fountain Square, I have been looking for a place to get gelato.  Ta da!!!  I was able to get a Cinnamon Apple Pie Gelato and was I happy!  Saturated flavor with a nice balance of cinnamon and apple flavors.  Nice texture that didn't melt before I could finish it.  Delicious!  And all their servings come with an animal cracker on top just to make it fun.  I got a lion, so hear me roar!  This is good!!!  Review #396

The former Northeastway Park shares an entrance with the golf course/driving range on the east side of the road.  The main feature of the park is the 20 year old aquatic center which has two sizes of swimming pools, a spray park, a large water slide, and a zero depth entry pool.  Outside of the summer attraction, there are numerous shelters, tennis courts, basketball, sand volleyball, and a playground.    Although there have been some reviews that refer to this park as "little", the park has over 85 acres which is enough for a disc golf course and some wooded hiking/running trails.  Parking is spread over a great length of the park, so you don't have to park far from where your main interest lies.  Review #735

Note:  Review is for the mural on the outside of the building  One of the keys to having a successful business is getting people/customers to notice you are in business.  What better way than to put a bright and colorful mural on the side of your building which is clearly visible from a main thoroughfare like Keystone Avenue?    In 2016, the business owners commissioned the FAB Crew (Fantastic Aerosol Brothers) to create a full sized mural for their location.  Done in deep colors of purples, oranges, and greens, the mural has a huge face with lots of swirling shapes and highlights that seem to have an electric quality to their appearance.  I'm not very good at determining if the shapes are meant to be letters and spell out words, I guess I spent too many years being a dull accountant to be able to pick the letters out correctly, but if I had to guess, I would say that the symbols spell out "smoke" and "vape" based on the nature of the business.  Or, I could be totally wrong. Oh well!  Review #1585

I stopped in for lunch on Tuesday and ordered the special of the day: fish and chips.  Prompt service and a meal that was exactly what I was looking forward to.  The quantity of food was just right for lunch and the price.  The fish was lightly breaded and fried enough to have a nice crunch while staying moist inside.  The fries were equally impressive.  Nice and crisp on the outside and steaming hot inside.  The fish was slender in profile, so it was fine as finger food not requiring utensils to cut it first.  With a pickle spear on the side, I had plenty to eat for under $10 (excl tip).  At lunch hour, there was a flow of patrons stopping in, but sitting in the bar near the entrance did not get too loud.  Overall, I enjoyed my meal and the ambiance of the state's oldest bar.  Review #203

Whether your dog is big or little, you are sure to find something here that will allow you to spoil your buddy with something special.  Maybe it will be one of the in-house baked goods.  Maybe it will be one of the myriad of rawhides.  Maybe it's a packet of training snacks or new toy from the wall of colorful items.  I picked up some smaller treats from the baked goods counter I my dogs devoured them.  Just wish I would have picked up some more for the next day.  The folks who work there were friendly and seem like they are dog lovers too!    If you are in the old town village, stop by and pickup something for your special pooch!  Review #2217

This is the 2nd Festival of Trees I've been to at the Indiana Historical Society.  Each year, they seem to add more trees and encourage you to explore the IHS while you look at the trees.  They have both conventional and unusual trees decorated by local businesses, organizations, and societies on display on the ground level, 2nd floor, 4th floor, and canal level.  Some are absolutely beautiful.  Others make you scratch your head and wonder "What were they thinking?"  Overall, I felt the festival in 2016 had a bigger "Wow" Factor than this season's.  Some of my favorites were #24 Bumbles Bounce, #36 Visions of the Sugar Plum Fairy, #52 A Traditional English Christmas Tea, and #41 Yelp, Actually!  Nice job!!  For those who have trouble with stairs, they have an elevator right across from the coat check/closet area.    If you park in the IHS lot, be sure to have your parking ticket validated at the time you buy your ticket.  It's free to park when validated.  Review #1858

Leonard Park has a wide variety of things to do for children, big and small, and adults too!  There is a really nice playground with lots of climbing equipment and a smaller version for little folks.  There are also two baseball parks, several tennis courts, lots of horse shoe pits, and paved walking paths.    For those who want to have "get togethers", there are a couple nice sized shelters and a permanent restroom building.  There are lots of shade trees throughout the park.  I also found parking on the east end as well as along the street.  Not sure if there was parking on the opposite end by the second ball field.  There were a quite a few benches around the playground for adults to relax on including several under the blue shade tarps to escape the sun.  Note that the playground is in full sun, but only a short distance from places to take a break in the shade.  The park was clean and maintained during my visit.  Generally, it looked like a fun place to get some outdoor time.  Review #1373

I was hoping there would be a lot to find in this over-sized warehouse, but I found the place to be congested and messy with the quality of items you might find at a garage sale, not an antique store.  Lots of booths were in disarray, over packing their space with everything they could instead of trying to showcase their best stuff.  I walked through the entire building (except for the food and electronics places on the periphery) and felt there was little stop and look at.  I did notice that the back and east side of the floor space seems to feature more large pieces of furniture if that is of interest to you.  I probably won't return.  Review #2055

About midway along the CCIC is a small, but very cool gift shop for those looking for items locally produced and affordably priced to give as gifts.  I have been by a number of times, but hadn't stopped in until today.  The shop itself is has a small area for items on display (though there is an open area in the back with tables..not certain what that is used for.)  But in the display space, they manage to arrange a nice collection of items plants in cool pottery, small prints, incense and CBD items, DIY embroidery kits, and jewelry.  Just lots of stuff to browse through in a small space.    My advice is to go during the week when crowds might be smaller so that you can take your time without bumping into other shoppers.  Review #1944

This small shop has a variety of baked goods with focus on cupcakes and chocolate covered items.  Along the sides of the shop are packaged items that are priced individually like chocolate covered oreos decorated in themes like superheroes or winter.    There is also a display case at the order counter where you can see a variety of cupcakes, some cookie options, and more chocolate options.  The staff were patient and helpful and we were soon able to make our selections.  It isn't the widest variety of baked goods around.  I didn't see a lot of pastries here.    Also, at the time of my visit, there were only a couple of each type of cupcake on display.  Don't worry, they have plenty in the back if you want more of a specific type.  If you have a sweet tooth, stop on by to see what may grab your interest.  They are located in a stripmall so there is plenty of parking available close by.  Review #3497

"I don't fly often, but when I do, I use Indianapolis International Airport."  That may sound a bit over used, but it's true.  I get that this isn't a major hub and that because of its size, everything is easy to reach.  It also helps that it was planned from day one instead of being put together as a series of expansions.  All that helps to make it such an easy airport to get around.  What impresses me is that compared to other markets, how much I noticed how well Indy did.  Arrival and check in was easy.  A short stroll through the central concourse filled with food and shopping options led to going through security which was the fastest we encountered on the round trip.  And the waiting areas in the secure areas/terminals had enough to do that we weren't hungry or bored while waiting for our plane.    If I knew flying was this easy, I might have gone on my vacations!  Great job, IND.  Keep it up!  Review #2392

This large warehouse is pet friendly and has plenty of room in the aisles to let you browse for your pet needs.  They also have a mini pet hospital, grooming area, and adoption center inside the store, but I haven't used those.  I have spent time looking through the wide variety of options they have for toys, healthy snacks, and items meant to make my pet's life better.    Note that they often let animal rescues to set up inside the store or on the large sidewalk/parking lot out front.  I won't get into the debate about where the pets come from...every pet should have a home.  I've seen lots of mutts available here, so I have a good feeling about it.  On my last visit, there were a number of greyhounds that were needing homes.  Overall, when I am in the area, I like to stop by and see if there is something I can pick up for my two dogs.  Review #1955

Indy has a new park (Fall 2018) that opened on the south side of the City-County Building on Washington Street.  The plaza is a makeover of the former concrete sidewalk/patio that was boring and unattractive.  Now, the out buildings have information about the city's history.  There are colorful pastel tables and chairs for those wishing to bring their lunches.  There are even bench swings on the west end for those who wish to spend their time having a little more fun than the rest!  The old sculpture that was on the corner didn't survive relocation, but a new art installation has been added.    The plaza is supposed to hold up to 1500 people for gatherings downtown.  Looks like just one more perk for folks who don't want to feel chained to their desks at lunch time!  Review #1752

I'm not sure why this place is getting such a good rating.  It is difficult to get into if you are westbound on 82nd, it looked a bit picked over, and even though my wife and I were the only ones in the shop, the two clerks were busy eating (3 in the afternoon) and didn't speak to us or even acknowledge us as we browsed through the store.  There were some witty little pieces, some animal slippers, and most items seemed reasonably priced.  But they have arrows that encourage you to look in the restroom for savings and they have a large display of candles that aren't for sale.  What???    After having dealt with businesses earlier in the day that made sure to offer help and thanked us for coming in, we both agreed that this place won't be a place we will return.  Good day, Sir!  Review #2050

Wow!  I really enjoyed my lunch here!  I am not very familiar with Korean food having only had it maybe three times before today.  I love that with my basic lunch order of Bulgogi (shredded beef in a somewhat sweet sauce), I got an entire bento box of rice, cooked veggies, and two pieces of avocado sushi.  AND on the side I got four more dishes that I'm guessing were sprouts, somewhat sweet cucumbers, potatoes (in a thick Teryaki type sauce), and chopped white radish (Dongchimi?) that wasn't spicy.  Add to that a side salad with a mild ginger dressing and a small bowl of fruit pieces for after dinner, and I was a happy camper!  Oh, and the cup of Green tea was probably about 24 ounces!  Nice flavor with little bitterness.    The greeter and the server were both friendly and did a great job of clearing my used plates, offering me a fork since I am a dork with chopsticks (would probably starve with anything requiring actual skill), and bringing out the bill and processing it when I was ready.  Highly recommended for anyone who wants a great meal to get introduced to Korean cuisine!  Review #2083

Although the majority of the business has a variety of items for purchase (quite a few vintage), in the back is an ice cream parlor which drew me in.    With a few small tables for customers to dine inside, the parlor has large display cases filled with two dozen varieties of ice cream.  After sampling a couple varieties, I settled on a Key Lime Pie ice cream.  The flavor was quite good and the scoop even had bits of graham cracker to add the flavor of a crumb crust.    The parlor also sells a few other items like hot dogs and nachos.  The staff/owner was very pleasant and helpful, as well.  Review #868

I stopped in for a quick cup of coffee late in the afternoon and was very pleased.  Not only did the shop have plenty of free parking outside their door, but inside, the place looked inviting and well kept.  Very quiet vibe so that if you wanted to spend a little time working here, it seemed like you could go undisturbed.    Although they offer a lot of pastries (and sandwiches until 3 pm), I simply wanted a nice black coffee that was drinkable without burning my tongue or tasting bitter.  I received a really fine tasting coffee that was hot, but ready to drink and I was happy!  The man behind the counter was friendly and we chatted while he got my coffee for me.  So nice to have baristas who can make a customer feel welcome.  If you are in the Geist area, make this your quick stop for a good cup of coffee.  Review #3672

From the pleasant phone call to schedule the glass repair to the moment I drove off with the repair completed, I found the experience of dealing with this business very positive and affordable.  Since I took my car in before the windshield started to "spiderweb", I didn't need the full windshield replacement.  In less than a half hour, the repair was completed.  I really liked that they advised me that if for some unforeseen reason the window cracks or I am dissatisfied with the appearance, they would apply the cost of the chip repair towards the installation of a full window replacement.   After leaving, I went out and got my car washed with confidence.    Review #579

My wife and I decided to head to the near north side for lunch one Friday in February.  We appreciated the free parking in the lot north of the restaurant.    The atmosphere was clean and a colorful with a long row of tables by the windows and a huge amount of seats next to the bar counter.  We were seated promptly at a table.  After looking over the menu, I decided to go with the Hoosier sandwich (pork patty, apple, arugula, smoked gouda, and hickory dijon) and Yucca fries.  The sandwich flavor was excellent!  I highly recommend this to anyone who is a first time customer.  The yucca fries came with a dipping sauce, were huge in portion, but without the sauce, were rather bland.  I probably wouldn't order them again.  My wife and I decided to share the white chocolate & raspberry bread pudding.  This was a tasty item as well.  This is a place I would definitely return to.  Review #57

This place must be doing something right.  I stopped in around 2 on a Friday and the place was packed!  Some folks were working on their devices, but most seemed to be chatting with friends, both seated and standing.    I was able to stop in for a quick cup of black coffee and grab a spot off to the side.  I like to try something simple when I try a new coffee shop since  it's a good way to see how the base ingredient tastes.  I found the drip coffee to be full flavored without too much bitterness.  And I love that they serve it at drinking temperature so I didn't have to waste too much time waiting for it to cool or burn my tongue.    The staff was friendly and got my coffee right away.  Note:  This spot is a self busing place with a bin for your dishes/mugs right by the door as you exit.  Review #2088

After a morning of hiking around downtown, I decided to quench my thirst at YoguLatte.  It was Sunday morning, so the business was open but only had a few other customers. I was able to place my order directly at the counter: Italian Cream Soda with whipped cream on top.  There were eight flavors to choose from, so I opted for Raspberry.    The beverage started with a bit of cream soda in the bottom, then ice was added and cream to augment the bubbling nature of the soda.  The whipped cream was added to the top.  I only ordered a small serving, so I was able to hit the bottom quickly.  Well, bottom is a relative term.  There was plenty of ice and whipped cream left inside.    So, overall, the flavor was really good, but since the ice didn't do much other than act as a filler (okay, there was some chilling that occurred), I find it hard to give a 5 star rating.  The next time, I will have to try one of the frozen custards.  Review #122

I think this is a park that targets younger children while offering a quieter setting than Hummel Park down the street.  There were lots of stand alone pieces for kids with imagination or those who can't resist climbing on things.  Lots of the equipment was made to look like something else like an ant, a wagon, etc.  They also have a younger kids/toddler playground separate from the bigger kid equipment, yet close enough for a parent to see both.  There is a shelter and the side street (which has a sign making you think it is a utility road) has angled parking in the shade so that your car doesn't get too hot while you're visiting.  There is a school across the side street, so I'm not sure if the ball fields are part of the park or school, but even if they aren't for the park, there is still a lot of room to run around beyond the playgrounds.  Review #614

When I lived in Greenwood, I made it north of the County Line regularly to visit Michaels.  Back then, I used to like it more than the Hobby Lobby next door; more things I liked and less crowded.  I always used to find lots of stocking stuffers for the grandkids during the holidays.  I also used their framing for posters or shadow boxes.  And they had lots of fun crafts for the grandkids to work on when they came over to visit.  But upon this visit, the place just looked different.  It was brighter, but seemed somewhat empty.  Maybe I should have stopped by earlier in the Christmas rush (like October or early November), but just two weeks out from Christmas, there just didn't seem to be that much to choose from.    They still had the framing station in the back and quite a bit of craft related items, but it seemed like there wasn't much that caught my attention like in the past.  Review #1930

After some research by my wife, she found this was the nearest location for us to receive our booster shot for Covid 19 and although the processes was a little confusing   because we had three insurance companies for the pharm tech to sort through, She managed to keep the line moving.  When it was time to get our shots, we were able to get our booster AND our Flu shot  in  a single injection which was very convenient.  Like a lot of places these days,  it seems they could use a bit more  help around lunch hour when demand is high.  Review #3979

What a trip through my musical past!  This two room shop has used vinyl and books at reasonable prices.  The albums are grouped by genre and then alphabetically within that grouping.  Most of the ones I looked at were in the $5 to $10 range.  There was a wide variety of artists as well, though they didn't have complete discographies.  Still, any place that has Mountain's "Nantucket Sleighride", "Ten Years After Recorded Live", and lots of early Genesis (with and without Peter Gabriel) is okay in my opinion.  There were a lot of books too, but I didn't see any clear markings on the shelves indicating the categories like I did on the albums.  There was a general order to the books, but I found it confusing to find anything specific on my own.     I appreciated that I had the opportunity to browse even though I currently don't have a record player.  But walking through here made me consider it might be fun to pick one up.  The sound playing on their system was so much better than what I have now.  Ah, the good ole' days!  Review #1122

This delightful shop on the southwest corner of Audubon and Bonna Streets is laid out like a house where you wander from room to room, each with its own sense of style.  So, just because you see something in the front room where the host is seated, you may find something quite different as you wander on back and around.    I went towards the end of the year, so there were lots of holiday items on sale.  There also were lots of knick knacks, some jewelry, pottery, unique ornaments, and even an autoharp!  It's an eclectic gathering of items so take your time to browse.  You never know what cool thing you will find next.  Review #1989

Great ingredients are necessary for great sandwiches.  At Sub 16, the ingredients are both fresh and full of flavor.  I ordered the roast beef which was served medium rare and had a moderate amount of seasoning.  The Swiss cheese I ordered was sliced from a block of cheese while I waited.  They have a number of size options and allow you to select your toppings and condiments.  I like that they offered toasting for the sandwich for that extra bit of crunch and aroma.  And the taste was so good!    Review #451

This is another store my wife and I frequent when browsing Perry Crossing.  They always have some cool items to check out (even if you didn't think you needed it!)  Most of the items are smaller and could find room in your home, but I noticed they are carrying some larger items like chairs, so that will be interesting to keep an eye on.  They have a lot of holiday merchandise as well as their assortment of home decor.  Prices are typical for mall franchises, but not unreasonable.  And they often seem to have sales to help with that.  Staff usually lets you browse but seem helpful if you ask.  Most of them are running the cash registers since this place always seems busy.  Review #1950

This review is strictly for the exterior garden and art.  I have not taken classes here.  On a beautiful afternoon in August, I had the time to wander about the gardens of IAC.  There are numerous terraces & gardens, a mural, and many large installations of outdoor art placed around the paths as I wandered.    In addition to all the art and nature trails, there is a scenic overlook of the White River that comes equipped with a ramp so that anyone can enjoy the view.    Overall, the tranquil setting allows for individual contemplation on what was the artist of each piece trying to convey.  So glad I was able to find time to return to this pocket paradise along the Monon in Broad Ripple.  Review #110  FYI: For a more complete list of Public Art in Indianapolis go to the following website:  http://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/

This full service bakery has a large variety of pastries, both Mexican and traditional American.  There is plenty of parking in the lot for this business at the end of a strip.  Once you walk in, you will see walls of display cases filled with assorted pastries and cookies that don't run out early.  Making selections is self-serve, so you should pick up a large metal platter and pair of tongs near the entrance to take with you as you move around the store.    I picked up a mix including double flavored danish, strudels, churros, and some crispy versions of twists and elephant ears.  My wife loves the crispy styles and is already planning our next visit.  When I made my selections, I took them to the central counter and was pleasantly surprised how affordable they were.  The staff was friendly and had offered to help if I had any questions.    If I could make any suggestions, it would be to maintain the labels on the display cases.   Review #501

Nice little shop for all your sweet cravings when visiting the marina/Geist Reservoir.  Tucked away on the north side of the reservoir in a small strip mall filled with mostly restaurants, this is the place to pick out your hand dipped ice cream, get house baked cookies, and some packaged items like honey, popcorn, or some candies.  The staff was helpful giving tastings before purchase if you are debating between flavors.  I went with a Dark Chocolate Raspberry Ripple which had a deep flavor.    There is convenient dining both inside and out (weather permitting) for enjoying your purchases.  Parking is shared with other businesses in the strip.  They don't have the largest selection of flavors in the metro area, but all in my group seemed to enjoy their choices.  Review #3637

Although there is some stiff competition for top ice cream spot in Broad Ripple, I believe Wyliepalooza is right near the top!  The shop is small, but has a great location on 54th at the Monon.  Though small in size, they  have big flavors and I recommend the Banana Cream Pie Ice Cream.   Plenty of creamy texture and such delicious flavor!    They have some lawn chairs out front for relaxing and a few area lots will let you park and go.  If you haven't been here yet, make it a point to check it out the next time you're in Broad Ripple!  Review #2800

They have lots of options for caffeine and and non-caffeine drinks, smoothies, juices, and even some pastries.  Honestly, as someone who usually just drinks a straight black coffee, the options are seemingly endless.  Still, the staff behind the counter was patient and took their time to make sure I knew all the options available when I decided to try one of their specialty lattes.      The drink itself was pretty tasty.  I also enjoyed the Coffee Cake muffin which was reasonably priced at $2.50.  Service was fast and helpful.  They have drive-up service too.  Review #496

Pleasantly surprising food from this little corner shop of City Market.  Although I arrived after five, I ordered from the posted lunch menu:  small tomato basil soup and half a sage aioli chicken salad on french bread.  All for only six bucks!  Service was quick and they offered a choice of a slice of french bread or corn bread as well.  The soup had a lot of flavor with a slightly salty leaning.  Although it was good, I found the basil was only a minor flavor leaving a mostly tomato taste.  The chicken salad was generous in size and was fresh and moist.  I liked that they added pistachios to the salad for a bit of crunch.  The sage was very subtle like most of the flavors.  Not exactly bland, but not screaming with flavor either.    Overall, a quick and satisfying meal for a low price.  Review #183

If you are looking for a variety of options for breakfast/brunch, stop in at this location of this family owned and operated restaurant.  I ordered the Eggs Benedict with a side of hash browns and found them to be quite good.  The coffee was also good; not too bitter, not too hot.  The only place they could do a bit better is on the service.  Although there is no sign about waiting, there isn't a sign saying to seat yourself either.  So, I waited even though one of the cleanup staff saw me without thinking to mention it to the the wait staff who were back by the kitchen counter.  Eventually, someone in the back saw me and mentioned it.  Once I was seated, I had pretty good service though my waitress wasn't the most efficient I've had.  With a little more awareness (keeping coffee filled, watching the front), the service could be really good.  Review #3617

While my traveling companions stood in long line at that "coffee chain", I walked over to Shapiro's and grabbed a bacon, egg, and cheese bagel and a cup of coffee.  The sandwich was made to order except for the bagels which were offered in a variety of flavors.  I finished my yummy breakfast just as my companions were getting their frothy beverages.  I think my choice suited me better for a day of travel than theirs.    They are on the pricey side being located at the airport but I got that impression from all the businesses.  The only negative I had was that I was going to get the sausage instead of the bacon but they were out at 7:30 in the morning.  You can't let that happen at a breakfast place.  Review #2353

I really like browsing through Williams-Sonoma.  The store is arranged into groupings of food and kitchen related items.  I can't help myself from picking up a utensil that I've never seen before or some food item "starter" or additive.  In fact, if they weren't charging mall prices on everything, I would probably buy more gadgets.  Over the years, I have picked up a number of items and they all seemed to have high quality.    On my most recent visit, they had samples of barbecue sauces with some freshly cooked meatballs for dipping.  End result?  I ended up buying a sauce that I had never heard of before and probably wouldn't be able to find anywhere else.  (I ended up making dinner that night with the sauce as a key ingredient.) And that's the point.  Williams-Sonoma is a place to find quality products that can either make your home food preparation more simple or add to the flavor profile.  Fight the routine!  Try something new.  Stop in at W-S for a change!  Review #332

Unlike most big box hardware stores, this True Value is part of an existing building.  The good news is that it is convenient for downtown residents and visitors who need to find something that they just don't find elsewhere.  The bad news is that they are limited in space, so the aisles are narrower and the stacks of inventory aren't as high.   This place does have a paint department as well as most of the items you would shop for at a hardware store.  I was looking for a smaller watering can than the one I have.  I was able to find them in three sizes at reasonable prices, so I gladly made my purchase.  Another benefit of having a smaller store is that if you have any questions, it isn't hard to find someone to help.  I was directed to the specific aisles right after being greeted when I entered.  If you like having service as well as supplies, then consider stopping here when downtown.  Review #3755

On the south wall of the Central Ace Hardware building, local artist Carl Leck has created a giant mural (2012) that ties directly to the hardware store.  The wall features a giant screw and screwdriver that are painted with 3D shading to make them look real.  Behind them, the background has vertical shades of gray with white silhouettes of other hardware items routinely found inside the store.  This is one of Leck's earliest public art murals.  He has done both commercial and independently themed pieces around town, including several for the "46 for XLVI" Superbowl project downtown.  Review #1344

I like that Plainfield has created a series of parks that target different needs and has connected many of them with trails.  For visitors who want a tranquil place without the long hikes of a nature park or the bustling of little kids at a splash park/playground, Friendship Gardens has numerous benches and some gazebos to sit and enjoy the outdoors, maybe to even reflect and remember.  As you go through the park, you will see a lot of dedication plaques.  Some are by trees.  Some are by fountains.  Some are on benches.  I am not certain who determines what gets a plaque, but it is a sign that people wanted to create a place where visitors are encouraged to appreciate the beauty of the space.  There are several larger memorials.  One is to honor those who served in the military.  Another sculpture called "American Family" (Connie Scott 2003) depicts a bronze family (even a dog!) that honors "family values" and their importance in the community.  Review #615

This is a very nice neighborhood playground/park.  Set in an area with mature trees, the park has two playgrounds (toddlers and older kids), and a shelter with a picnic table and a grill.  The play area has drainage to avoid puddling which is good since the playground uses recycled rubber to soften the footing.  There is also a water fountain and a lending library too!  On the negative side, there is no designated parking, but the street parking is free in the neighborhood.  I also did not see any restroom facilities.  Review #513

Although the place was packed when I arrived, I was greeted and seated promptly.  I took advantage of their low priced lunch options getting free salsa & chips, and a lunch sized Chimichanga with lots of options for $5.99.  I liked that the Chimi came with my choice of soft or fired tortilla, with beans or rice, and I could add cheese sauce or red sauce.  The Chimi was definitely smaller than most places, but since I knew it would be, I was fine with that.  (My waistline probably is too!)    The salsa was a little bit spicy and has nice veggie chunks.  Very nice!   The service was prompt and even check out was quick too.  (You can have the staff run your payment like a regular restaurant or take your bill up to the front and pay yourself.)   The only negative was that there wasn't much visual appeal to the meal or setting.  The sour cream was mostly liquid and the the interior of the place looked rather dated and broken into lots of small areas.     But the food tasted quite good and is worth stopping for.  Review #495

If you are looking for a quiet place, or a local place to get a good workout from hiking, then Glenns Valley is a place for you.  They have a parking lot at the entrance.  From there you can head in several directions on unpaved trails that have numerous branches.  I was surprised at how steep the assent was on some of the paths and really got my heart pounding!  There is a mix of evergreens and deciduous trees along the way and lots of wildlife could be heard scurrying about.  With so many winding trails, I will need to return to explore more of the paths.  Note:  There are now signs posted that sledding is prohibited in the park.  Review #688

This mammoth store has large sections devoted to flower arrangements, fabric, hobbies, and Christmas items.  In the middle, you can find baskets, knick knacks, small furniture pieces, and plenty of other things for your home.  The stuff isn't of the high end quality, but they do have some neat items that you don't see elsewhere.  And if you are trying to decorate on a budget, then it may be your favorite place to start.  Still closed on Sundays, so plan accordingly.  Review #1931

For a park without much space and limited access to the nearby river, this park is amazing.  There are festivals and concerts here.  There is a state museum, a sports museum (NCAA), a western museum (Eiteljorg), a zoo and botanical garden, and a former pedestrian bridge that now hosts temporary art installations.  Oh, and there is a beautiful canal that wanders through it designed for handling lots of folks using different modes of transportation.  It has a large underground parking facility and is just a short walk from the IUPUI campus, the convention center, Victory Field, and downtown.  Could there be a better location for this place?  The only negative I have is that it doesn't really promote itself as being a collective park.  There are lots of things to do here or very close by, but I don't see a lot of promotion saying "come to White River State Park".  But people still come here for all the individual activities.  Imagine if these activities/events all coordinated instead of doing their own thing.  This could be a next level event!  Review #1616

I've stopped in twice recently and enjoyed my meals both times.  On my most recent visit, I stopped in to try the Burger of the Month:  Nice Burger.  The Nice was a juicy half pound burger (even when served medium-well!) and topped with Brie, shaved apples, fig aioli, and caramelized onions.  The flavor was sweet and savory.  The burger also came with Truffle Tots which were crisp and crunchy.  Nice flavor on both.  The bartender was very personable and let me sample a couple tastes of brews on tap before I settled on a seasonal pumpkin spice brew.  Also, the burger was ready right away so I didn't have much of a wait.  Overall, it has a great location with the outdoor seating, but because it was cold outside, I finally dined inside for the first time.  There is plenty of room but it did feel like the ceiling was a little low.  Maybe it's just me, but I guess I'm used to a lot of pubs/restaurants with higher ceilings than here.  It wasn't claustrophobic, but noticeable.    Tip:  If you park in the garage just off Senate, they will validate your parking for you!  Rev #39

I was pleasantly surprised at the size and selection in this two story antique store in the middle of the Main Street shops.  The store is arranged with orderly booths with plenty of room to pass.  There are lots of collections including furniture, books, table settings, comics, vinyl, coins, and just about anything else you can think of.  Towards the back, there is a large staircase that leads upstairs to even more items.  Cool selection well worth checking out.  Review #2100

My wife seems to enjoy looking at jewelry and estate items, especially when they are displayed as nicely as they are here.  The shop is laid out like an "L" and has both estate items as well as new that cover a wide range of collectibles, jewelry, and watches.  The staff was very helpful and assisted my wife who was checking out the watches on the west end of the shop.  While she was engaged, I browsed the store and couldn't help but notice the beautiful furniture and decor used inside.  There's a grandfathers clock, an ornate display cabinet, and even a beautifully maintained salt water fish tank that make the place seem special.  My wife says the prices are good to great for the items she checked out.   That's a good enough recommendation for me!  Review #2213

There is a lot to like about Flat 12.  They have a wide variety of beers to choose from.  They have a large patio with plenty of spots to sit in sun or shade.  They share a space with Hoagies & Hops, so you can get really good sandwiches without having to bring it with you or wait for a delivery.  There are lots of televisions to catch the latest games/events too.  Basically, it has about all you would want for a relaxing location to sip a beer and enjoy being with friends.  I won't say it is my favorite brewery, but I definitely enjoy coming here.  Like a lot of places, parking is somewhat limited to street parking.    Note:  Dorman is one way northbound, so head east on New York St to get here.  Review #984

We don't have a Trader Joe's on our side of town, so it isn't practical to shop for perishable foods here.  But when I am in the area, it is a place I stop by to see what food items are out there that I hadn't discovered yet.  In some cases, when I am about finished with my business on the north side, I actually make purchases that I can trust to stay fresh on the drive home.    Such was the case on my most recent visit.  The vibe was inviting and friendly,  not like the big box stores that have every item you need and more that you never will.    Here they have variety and that in itself is interesting.  And the prices, while maybe not the same as the giants, is reasonable and worth the quality.    Now that Marsh has closed its doors, I wish we had a Trader Joe's on our side of town to find those items that the big stores don't carry.  Review #329

The Small Mall is a single story shop that has relocated its collection of furniture, antiques, and home decor from the former Mass Ave location to the one in the strip mall off 62nd near Binford.  There is a lot of furniture that seemed reasonably priced to me within the shop.  I also found a bunch of cool home decor items like paintings, wall hangings, mirrors, and some antique knick knacks.    There are some arrangements that help you visualize what a room might look like with the piece you are interested in.  There are also open spaces that have been setup as rooms, but without the walls.  Traversing the length of the shop is easy with plenty of wide and clear aisles to pass along.  The quality of the pieces appeared to be on the nicer end, not flea market stuff.  The person behind the central desk was friendly and greeted me when I entered and offered to help if I was looking for something specific.  Overall, I enjoyed looking through the shop though I didn't make any purchases on that day.  Review #2140

Pretty much a "to go" only coffee place with just a couple small tables outside during nicer weather days.  Didn't see any indoor seating.  The place seems like it is a beverage only shop as well since I didn't see anything on the menu to munch on.  I simply got my standard black drip coffee and it was okay, not fantastic.  It was served right on the edge of being to hot to drink, but I managed to not burn my tongue, so they get a good rating for that!  Friendly and quick service around lunch time, so good ratings for that too!  Review #2584

I've been to several UPS stores in the area and based upon the amount of services and supplies this location has, I would say that it warrants an average rating.  It doesn't seem to have as much to offer as the Greenwood location, but is laid out better and offers more than the Mooresville location.  So maybe  3.5 star?    I do like the layout with the counter area to the right which allows people to come in and move about without waiting in a long line by the door.  However, the amount of supplies for shipping on display near the front seemed somewhat limited.  Still, if you have your items already boxed and ready to go, the staff seemed to be intent on getting everyone helped.  Review #3482

What I like about Crate & Barrel is that they have items for your kitchen AND your living space.  With so many open kitchens, sometimes it's better to be able to match colors, patterns, styles from room to room, so when I pick up something that may sit out on the counter or be visible, it's nice to know how it will look.  But even if you aren't coordinating, the staff was quite friendly and wanted to point out that they've added a kids section and a design section to the store.  Most of the downstairs seemed to concentrate on the kitchen items while the upstairs was for the living spaces.  I like when a shop arranges their furniture in groupings with accessories...it's great for ideas and possibilities I hadn't thought of.    The store has a lot of space and was uncluttered making for easy browsing.  That also allows them to have a large variety in store that you just don't see at some of the smaller boutiques.    Overall, I enjoyed my visit to the store and dealing with the employees.  Review #2189

I found this Michaels to be arranged very similar to the one in Castleton, so I assume this is the standard layout for most of the franchises.  (I think the one on the south side is a little different, but similar.)  So, I was able to find my way around the store to the areas of interest quickly.    I was also pleased that this location had lots of staff working the floor during my visit, so if I had any questions, there were plenty of people to ask.  The staff here wasn't as outwardly friendly as the Castleton location, but there wasn't anything negative in my visit.  The store was clean, orderly, and well stocked...pretty much what you would want from a hobby and craft store.  Review #3682

I really enjoyed my first visit to Boyden's.  I'm more of a pie than a cake guy, so seeing a large variety of fruit Danish right as I entered the door was great sign.  The staff was friendly and I was able to get my order promptly.  They have a nice variety of pastry options and have a limited amount of coffee available too.  The Danish have a light texture and the icing is very sweet.  They also have a fair amount of fruit filling, more than I have found in most bakeries.  Review #1972

This garden center nursery has been a staple on the south east side of Indy for a long time.  Although it is quite a distance from our home, my wife and I were on a road trip and were searching for some specific plants to grow along our new trellis.    The folks here had a great supply of plants and were quite pleasant.  Not only did they have a wide assortment of colors and types of plants for my wife to choose from, but she was also able to pick up some bird seed and some top soil which the staff helped her load (she knew I could unload it once I got home!)    Good selection and good service makes for a good rating.  It has easy access off Emerson to the Interstate (465) so even though the distance was a little farther than we would normally consider, the drive was easy and pleasant (as long as you avoid rush hour.)  Review #3769

I've been here a few times, and though I haven't shopped here on a "regular" shopping day, I have stopped in when in the area and picked up a few things so that I wouldn't have to make a special stop elsewhere.  They have convenient parking (rare near Mass Ave) for up to 2 hours.    Inside, they have most of the departments that the big box stores have for groceries:  Deli, cheese, sushi, produce, salad bar, and the standard boxed goods.  Note that there is also a small pastry shop on the Alabama Street side where you can get some additional goodies/lunch.  I just needed a couple items and so I was able to quickly find those and go through the self checkout.  It wasn't too hard to figure out and soon I was on my way.  They don't have all the options that the giant stores have, but they have the basics covered here and for most things, you can pick them up without having to go to the suburbs.  It will be interesting to see how this franchise fares now that there are more options popping up downtown.  Review #3756

Although I didn't make a purchase on my visit, I was pleased with the quality of home decor and furniture I saw in the store.  There was no hassle but plenty of staff on hand if I had a question.  The store was set up with many "rooms" of arrangements and then shelves of accessories along the side walls.  I liked the openness of the store which allowed me to wander without feeling like I was tripping over displays or other customers.  Review #2187

This is a nicely organized shop with primarily consignment furniture.  They do have some accessories like lamps and wall hangings, but the majority of space is furniture.  Like most furniture places, the items are packed pretty close together but with a little effort, you can get to all of them.  The shop is on the end of a strip mall, so there is lots of free parking and the site makes it easy to load any purchases you wish to take with you.  The staff were all busy helping shoppers, some making purchases, some loading stuff in their vehicles.  Seems like everyone was focused on the customers.  They do have several business spaces connected with the main purchase desk on the far west end.  Note that they encourage folks to browse and have free popcorn in the back in the show area behind the counter.  Review #2089

I can't believe this was my first visit to this little shop on Madison.  I've been across the street at least a half dozen times, but had never made it in here.  I won't make that mistake again.  The business was a two-story house turned into a florists and home decor shop.  The front door is kept locked, so be sure you go around to the north side of the building to enter.  The main parts of the building within your sight lines is filled with home decor.  At the holidays, there was Christmas stuff from top to bottom!  Even upstairs they have a room with more items.  Behind the stairs is the cooler area for fresh flowers and to the left of the counter (seen as you enter) is more space for the employees to put together arrangements.  I decided to pass on fresh flowers and instead found a seasonal spray hanging on the wall with lots of festive ribbon and greenery.  It looks nice on my front door.  Very pleasant people to work with and a nice variety of items (and colors) to help you decorate.  Review #1912

Having tried the Noblesville location, I thought I'd swing by the City Market's version even though it was getting later in the day.  Fortunately, they still had about nine varieties of doughnuts and bismarks available.  If you've not had their pastries, then you're in for a treat.  These are big donuts!    I will be the first to admit that I am not the biggest donut fan, but I've still eaten my fair share.  So when I tried their Boston Cream, I was impressed!    Some places are really skimpy when it comes to the cream in the middle.  Not here!  The Boston had just the right balance of chocolate icing on top and cream in the center.  Really nice flavor too!  I know it's called Rebellion Doughnuts, but I have to admit I would would love to see more bismark options, or maybe Danish.  But that's just me.  The flavors are really good.  Review #2346

I enjoyed browsing through the shop.  It's filled with art, jewelry, clothing (both serious and whimsical), and an eclectic mix of items for you and your home.  There are several rooms on each floor that have their own unique collection of items.  The shop has its own parking on the east side of the building.  It does have it's challenges if you aren't okay with steep stairs, but other than that, the space is laid out well.  The staff was friendly and welcoming.  If you are looking for something unique for a gift (for yourself or others), stop by and give this place a try!  Review #2087

This shop has women's clothing and accessories, primarily for younger women who want clothing that looks both professional and fun.  The shop is much larger than it appears from the front since it extends across the entire block.  There is plenty of room for the merchandise to be displayed and there are nice dressing rooms about 2/3 of the way back.  The woman working at the desk was friendly and seemed to manage several customers at once.    Note that there is a small floor level change for those who have mobility challenges.  Review #2215

This brand new addition to "the Yard" in Fishers was a pleasant discovery.  After parking in front of the building on the east side of the north-south access road, I entered the shop portion of this meat shop.  There was a rack of food items by the door.  There is a U-shaped meat counter with multiple staff available to assist.  In the center, a 2-sided cooler has packaged meets and food items.  I decided to get some bulk Mild Italian Sausage, some sliced Jalapeno Colby Jack cheese, and after getting a free sample of their house made Ham Salad, decided to get a pound of that.  The ham salad was fantastic and I've already tried some on crackers with the cheese. Yum!  Very friendly, helpful, and timely assistance from the staff.  I wish I lived closer.  I could see becoming a regular customer here.  Review #3409

I stopped by on a cool Sunday morning just after they opened. Free parking on Indiana Avenue (love the free weekends!) for a short walk down the stairs to the canal side location.  No lines!  I ordered a half Italian Beef sandwich and added the pay options of Mozzarella Cheese and Giardiniera.  I also liked that they let me select how I wanted my au jus.  I got it in a cup instead of drenched over the top.  I can't stand a sandwich too soggy to be picked up, so this option with the cup wide enough to dip the bread was appreciated.  The standard side is a bag of chips.    My sandwich arrived in minutes and was loaded with flavor.  Their beef is finely shredded instead of sliced, so a few globs managed to drop into my serving basket.  The beef stayed moist and seemed evenly balanced throughout the sandwich.    The location is great (as long as you don't mind the stairs) and they offer pizzas and dessert options as well.  It is worth noting this is a seasonal location from April through the end of summer. Then, the business transfers back to the original Lockerbie location.  Review #280

I don't buy a lot of athletic wear, so I can't really say how this shop compares to the big box places.  But what I do know is that they provide a service to Avon and the neighboring community when it comes to personalizing band/athletic clothing.  My wife has a lot of sewing equipment at home, but even she prefers to come here when it comes to having our grandsons' letter jackets embroidered.  She can get the jackets in the school colors here, and have them embroidered with the school name (official logo) and personalized with our boys' names.
