And as they earn patches for competitions they perform in, my wife is able to have them added to the jackets in a reasonable time frame.  It isn't a cheap place, but it is done well and looks professionally done.  Our oldest grandson's jacket has held up well and we haven't had any problems with the patches becoming loose.  We recently picked up our next grandson's new jacket and it turned out great.  We are looking forward to continued service from this business as our grandchildren progress.  Review #3363

Once again, my wife and I enjoyed ice cream at this wonderful old depot on the Monon Trail.  This time, I went with the Broad Ripple Blackberry ice cream in a dish.  We sat out on the deck beneath the table umbrella to watch folks go by on the trail.  While we sat, the server brought out water to help quench our thirst since it was nearing 90 degrees.  It was a nice touch that wasn't expected....just good customer service.  Some places get it...some don't.  Rev #5

After dining at one of the upscale restaurants in Broad Ripple, the group of friends I was with headed over to Brics to enjoy an ice cream dessert (6-2-16).  It was a great night to sit out on the patio and people watch the folks and pets on the Monon Trail.  I ordered an Apple Crisp ice cream (single serving) in a waffle cone.  It was huge!  After having dinner, I was glad I didn't splurge on a double dip....can't really get a to go box for ice cream! :)  Excellent flavor.  Generous portions.  Great location for people watching.  This is a really great place to go for a dip!  Review #7

I used to live in Greenwood, so I was a regular customer for ten years.  A few years ago, I moved to another town, but find myself returning to this location for my oil change.  I really like that they keep my maintenance history on their computer so that I can see what is recommended due to mileage.  It gives me confidence that I am only paying for needed services.    I know some people feel places are pushy and try to sell them new equipment.  I find that simply saying "no" and not making a big deal about it has worked when I am asked.  Having been a customer for over 15 years, I have always been treated with respect and never noticed any pressure to purchase on me or others who are getting vehicle service while I am there.  I trust this place to do the work quickly and correctly.    I think there are other places that have cheaper prices, but with the money I have invested in my vehicle, I don't want to go to some fly by night shop or have to leave my car all day just for fifteen minutes of work.    Review #437

What a fun place to hang out to grab a fix for your sweet tooth!  This brightly colored shop is staffed with folks who seemed to enjoy their job and were really glad to engage with the customers.  They have a nice variety of cookies, brownies, and similar treats that looked as appealing as they taste.  There are teas and coffee type beverages and even some alcohol based options too.  Though it is located on the outside corner of a group of shops, you can park in the lot behind the shop and enter through a back entrance.  Note that the entrance didn't seem to have a large sign to call your attention to it, but if you pick the door near the corner, you can walk right in.)  These aren't your mass produced store bought cookies, so expect to pay more.  I think they compare favorably with a number confectionery shops around town.  Good quality.  Friendly staff.  Flavor worth the calories.  Review #449

Just a few blocks west of Keystone (around 73rd) is a 11.6 acre park that is mostly open fields used for soccer and lacrosse.  However, in the southwest corner, there is a splash park and playground for smaller kids.  Conveniently, there is parking right near the children's area.  There are a few trees for shade and a single shelter.  During the "season" for Indy Parks, there is a permanent restroom on site with water fountains on the outside.  If you have small kids and live in the area, this could be a really nice park.  Otherwise, there isn't much to draw you in.  Review #734

First, let me say that having a Martinsville address for this location is very misleading since it is north of SR144 between Mooresville and the Center Grove section of Greenwood.  (Much closer to Indy).  I stopped in for lunch and enjoyed looking at the overload of memorabilia of "days gone by" that cover the interior of the restaurant.  I ordered the grilled tenderloin sandwich which was pretty tasty.    Service was okay and the food was enjoyable, but there wasn't much about this restaurant to distinguish it from other restaurants beyond the decoration.  Pretty much a standard menu of items.  Review #42

I get that they have a lot of state brews that are hard to find around Indy.  And the service was fine and helpful.  There's just something about a bar with only one wall that left me with an odd feeling about the place.  It gave me the impression of the type of gathering at a wedding reception of a bunch of people sitting around talking in an open area.  There is a historic building, but other than being old, not much to see there.  Maybe it would have felt different sitting at the small bar, but if you sit just a short distance away, you might as well find a cafeteria to sit in for ambiance on par with this.  I like a bar to have character.  This comes off as rather bland.  I do appreciate that it was convenient to be able to grab a beer after ordering something to eat downstairs.  But if I wasn't already at the market, I probably would head somewhere else.  Review #184

Note:  I've never ordered flowers here.  This review is based upon the home decorations.  My wife and I love coming into McNamara Florist.  The store is like a showroom for decorating ideas and always carries something unique that I've not seen in other stores or online.  I'm not talking about country style knickknacks.  I mean beautiful accessories for the home, often seasonal, as well as candles, lighting fixtures, live plants, and elegant pieces you would be proud to set out.  And when it comes to seasonal, they have a Christmas celebration the first weekend of November.   That is when they have finished decorating the entire store and if you don't mind crowds, it is like walking through a Winter Wonderland.  Truly amazing things to see and grab a cookie or two!  Sure, the prices are relatively higher than other south side shops, but the quality is top notch....and I find you usually get what you pay for.  Don't be afraid to stop by and look.  You may just find something you didn't know you needed!   Review #1437

Nice variety of cakes, cupcakes, cheesecakes, and mini-pies.  There are even quite a few large cookies!  They have convenient parking in their lot on the east side of the building.  You can even order special event cakes, but I strictly stopped by for something sweet to eat right away!  The cupcakes were running about $3.75 each, while the pies and cheesecakes were a bit higher.  It's not cheap, but it isn't standard grocery store baked good either.  Good and fresh with lots of flavor.  The adage "You get what you pay for" applies here.  The service was friendly and efficient and the store was spotlessly clean.  Review #1703

I really liked this park.  There is a private parking lot (paved) that is an easy stroll to childrens' swings and two playgrounds, to a pavilion, and to adult swings, as well.  There are two shelters on the west side of the park and lots of mature trees for shade.  There are paved walking paths and for older kids, there is a climbing rock that has "fossil" imprints made in the surface.  The park is nicely spaced with nothing seeming too far away, but allowing the features to have their own space.  There is an elementary school as a neighbor of the park, so that offers even more greenspace to the setting.    Review #573

Downtown Mooresville has a beautiful shop on Main Street, Bud & Bloom Florist.  I was walking by today and was surprised at all the items I could see through the window besides flower arrangements, so I stopped in.  The shop is tastefully arranged with live plants on the right near the entrance, and the rest of the shop with zones for different themed home decor accessories.  There's even a table area with seating if you need to rest while shopping.  The arrangement counter is in the back so if you need help with picking out something in the front part of the shop, or need an arrangement put together, head on to the back to be helped.  Review #1935

This shop is filled with items to spruce up your home.  Whether it's colorful candles, or original paintings, or maybe stones or table top items, there is a lot to check out.  Although it is located on 54th, they have a small parking lot in front of the building which makes it pretty easy to stop by.  Inside, it looks like an older building that had log columns in a previous use that are now mostly covered by a softer appearance, with a few columns left for support and visual interest.  My wife and I browsed the store, enjoyed our conversation with the clerk, and found quite a few items that would work well in our home.  We ended up picking up a candle in a colorful watercolor style jar.  Very cool!  The items I found here are familiar, but still unique to this shop.  And if you are interested in local art, they feature artists Kyle Ragsdale and Nathan Foxton (check out more of their works at the Harrison Art Center at 15th and Delaware.)  Review #2158

I could ramble on about how tasty the freshly made to order sandwiches were that I had.  Or get into detail how I really liked the tubs of side salads they carry in their coolers.  I could even mention that they had lots of local food items that many folks saw at the recent Yelp's Totally Bazaar.  But let me just get to the point that if you want to get something to eat that you can count on quality, freshness, and tastiness, come to R2Go!  They have some free parking on the south side of the building and I was helped right away by Chef and the staff.    So glad I found this place!  Review #473

I stopped in for lunch and what a difference I noticed.  In my earlier review from opening day, the noise was overwhelming.  This time, the sound was at very acceptable levels while I waited for my "to go" order.    The hostess directed me to the pay counter to place my order and then after paying, I was encouraged to have a seat over near the "chef's" bar.  The staff was very friendly and put together my meal in about ten minutes.  And what a delicious option!  I ordered the Roasted Chicken Salad with an upgrade to the fresh fruit side.  First, the Chicken was so good!  I could taste the roasted flavor of the chicken along with the curry, roasted almonds, balsamic reduction, and julienned apples served on sliced cereal bread.  It also comes with a small greenhouse green salad that was tasty too.  The fresh fruit was truly that...a wide variety of berries and melons served in small bite pieces that were ripe and colorful.     If you are looking for good tasting food and want something different from the generic options served elsewhere, give Rize a try!  Rev #29

Let's see...they had everything I was looking for, they offer a 10% discount for 1st time Yelpers, they gave free advice on planting and care of my purchases, and they have a pair of mini donkeys out back!  Expectations exceeded!  The garden center is easy to find on 71st near Michigan Road.  The parking lot is gravel and out front, they have a lot of outdoor plants and a couple green houses. There is a large building for gardening supplies and a smaller building (climate controlled) for all their house plants and accessories.    Out back, there is a small barn with a couple mini donkeys and a quiet, shaded area with a gazebo and a small creek running by.  Very quiet and relaxing when you want to take a break from your daily routine.  I had some questions about house plants and about best times and conditions for planting some perennials.  The owner and the staff working were all pleasant to deal with and I left confident that even I could make the plant grow!  (Wish me luck!)  A very positive, personal experience that you just don't find at the big warehouse garden shops.    Review #2906

Instead of telling you all the details about parking and ordering, I'm simply telling you that this is great ice cream with wonderful flavor options.  I first tried Graeter's eight years ago and it is my favorite chain of ice cream shops....also it's available at my grocery store.  If you have put off trying this, that's okay.  It just leaves more for me!  Review #1722

Like many antique malls throughout the metro area, this shop is much larger than it appears from the outside and the amount of enjoyment you get shopping here will probably depend upon how your personal search lines up with the booths inside.  I did find that a number of the products seemed to have a decent quality though pricing is always subjective.  The owner of the shop greeted us as we entered, but otherwise let us browse on our own.  There are numerous small rooms towards the back of the mall, but otherwise, there is a long room with booths on the left, glass displays on the right.  Some of the rooms seem to have themes, like books, or clothing.  Note that the building shares space with a fireplace shop on the south side of the building, but they are separated inside by a wall.  They share a common lobby, but that's it.  Review #2201

Each Wednesday during the "summer" months, there is a pop-up event where vendors block off Market Street between Delaware and Alabama Streets.  Some of the vendors are farmers with fresh produce.  The majority are selling anything from flowers to soaps, to sweets.  Just about anything they can sell from a tent and table, it's here.  What surprised me was the different approaches taken by the vendors.  Some were greeting folks as the passed.  Others were buried face first into their phones.  Guess which ones were attracting customers!  Seriously, if you aren't going to engage potential customers, why show up?    Look, you can find this stuff at your local grocery or on line, but if you want to change your routine and are anywhere close to the downtown event on Wednesdays, swing by and check it out.  You might find a fresher quality item or find something that you haven't noticed before.    Review #2682

When I lived in Greenwood, I used to frequent this place often.  But now that I live elsewhere, I was glad to see that the place has maintained the quality that used to draw me in.   The aisles are clean and orderly and generally, are labeled to assist you.  However, I didn't see anything specifically called "shelving", so I took a guess and headed back to the interior lumber area.  Success!  I like shopping in the digital age, because when I found a board I thought ideal for my new shelf, it didn't have a label on it.  So, I simply took a photo of the bin label and had it handy at checkout.  Easy peasy!  They also measured the board since it was priced by the linear foot.  Also easy!  I grabbed some support brackets from the facing aisle of the wood and was pleased that the man who worked the checkout counter was pleasant and efficient.    It looked like there was plenty of staff on the floor as well as at the customer service and checkouts.  I hate going to some hardware stores where you can't find anyone to help.  Looks like Home Depot understands!  Review #3703

What a wonderful spot to pop in for a savory pot pie or to grab a fruit pie/slice to go!  They have a different pot pie each day (some days have vegan options) and the fruit pies and galettes available every day they are open.  Half the business is the bakery which can be seen through the front window or the cut out wall that separates the customer side of the business that features a handful of seats for those who wish to eat immediately without having to wait.  I ordered a slice of Apple Crumble pie and the Sugar Creme Brulee pie as well.  Tasty crusts.  Yummy fillings.  And you don't have to make a mess in your kitchen trying to get something this fresh.  (They do all the hard stuff for you!)  I will have to stop by more regularly now that I know where they are!  Note:  There is limited parking in front, but an empty lot across College is easy enough to use.  Review #2102

I've been meaning to stop by here, but always seemed to drive by on days they were closed.  Today, I made a point of stopping in and I'm glad I did.  The shop is small and has a display case with a few types of cupcakes, cake "balls" which are wrapped in chocolate, brownies, cookies and Hello Dolly treats.  I picked up a variety and all had really good flavor.   The cupcake was a little dry, but the icing was perfect...not too sweet, no greasy aftertaste, just lots of tasty flavor.  The chocolate wrapping on the strawberry ball reminded me of the texture you get when eating a cordial.  The strawberry cake inside was great!  The service was friendly and kept up with the steady flow of customers.  I look forward to my next visit!  Review #1934

The library was a steady source of reading, audio, and video entertainment when I lived in Greenwood.  The staff are very helpful and I have gotten to know several on a first name basis.  Even after moving to Mooresville, I maintained my membership even though I now have to pay an annual fee.  In addition to the stock of materials on hand in the local branch, they can transfer materials from any of the JCPL branches at no additional cost.  I also use the digital download Hoopla to borrow electronic media without leaving my home.    Finally, I can reserve upcoming new releases so that I don't miss any of the entertainment that is of interest.  Review #63

This was the first time we used FastPark and it was great.  My wife knew it would get busy around spring break, so she reserved a space.  Then, on the day of our departure, she drove up, used the email image on her phone to get in, and was told which spot to park in.  The ticket they gave her had the space location AND the instructions for where to go when at the airport to be retrieved.  Fair price, great convenience.  The shuttles are numerous and run frequently.  Highly recommended.  Review 2389

Short and sweet review:  An independent coffee shop is conveniently located at Perry Crossing that serves a tasty black house blend at a temperature that is hot, but doesn't scald.  So, you can drink it right away!  The shop has convenient parking out front, but if those are taken, there are spaces in the larger lots beyond the main drag.  Inside, the shop is spacious and bright with a large central seating area, but with a couple nooks toward the front.  One has a large checkerboard set up and the other is a mini library.  The counter is towards the rear on the left.  There are the usual coffee options as well as sandwiches and sweets.  Bottled beverages are chilled too.  On the right is an assortment of Popcornopolis popcorn is available as well.  And the service?  Just a friendly man who had a lot of personality and seemed glad to have customers coming in.  He greeted everyone with a smile and a positive attitude.  I wish all coffee shops would do that.    The next time I am at Perry Crossing, this will be the spot I go to for coffee.  Review #2849

The shop has a convenient drive up window, but it's the inside that makes this coffee house worth stopping by.  There is a lot of space, but it feels like it is warm and cozy inside.  They have a variety of beverages here, but are somewhat limited when it comes to finding something to eat.  They receive their pastries from another company, so depending upon the deliveries, they can have a swing in available options.  One thing I like is that the plain black coffee has a rich flavor and is served at a drinkable temperature without having to wait for it to cool down.  Another was that the barista was friendly and got the orders ready promptly.  While I sat at the counter with my coffee, I noticed he kept the line to a minimum so that folks could go about their business.  Review #2000

Having been to several Mexican restaurants this week, I feel I have a good perspective on what's available for lunch in the market.  If I had been the only diner on this trip, I would have probably given a 5th star because the flavor for my lunch sized Chicken Burrito was delicious!  Nice portion and it came with Pico and sour cream without an upcharge.  Just really tender chicken that was full of flavor.  My wife's ground beef burrito came with plenty of stuff on the side (incl. beans), but the entree was very dry inside.  Overcooked beef and not much seasoning.  The portion was generous (she brought some home) but will probably add some more sauce or flavoring.  So, I had to take a star off for the disappointing beef.  Didn't see steak offered as an option, just the chicken or ground beef.  They had some beers incl. Mexican and some local, but I passed on the choices.     Plenty of parking outside and a large lot behind the restaurant too.  all free. Review #3928

My wife and I stopped by for a  tasty lunch earlier in the week.although there was plenty of parking but limited spots to transfer from the lot to the sidewalk. No automatic doors either.  Fortunately, we were able to get my wheel chair in and situated at one of the dining room tables.it seemed chilly since the outside air was unobstructed-from the dining room.   You place our order at the counter and help yourself to  utensils and napkins.  There are many-options  iicl. soups FYI Bigger spoons would be be helpful, salads, lots of appetizers and sushi options.entrees  are diverse and several proteins are available.  Rev #3985

It's too bad that I'm watching my weight for the holidays.  There were so many kinds of candy and soda in here, that I was really tempted.  Whether its some old fashioned candies like salt water taffy (bins of them) or candy cigarettes (yes, that is a real thing!), or chocolate covered malt balls, there was a sense of nostalgia and childhood memories regained.  And the sodas were mostly small company brands with names that made you wonder what the manufacturers were thinking!  Although they don't have every type of candy that I remember, I will say that if you grew up a half century ago, you will probably find something to bring back pleasant memories.  And if you are younger, you can find something for the first time to try.  Review #1975

In 2016, this local eye care business hired artist Justin Olson to create a colorful mural on the outside of the business.  The artist depicted the face of an eye glass wearing person on three sides of the building.  To fill out the rest of the space, vibrant colors are swirled including silhouettes of eyes.  As you drive by this place on Shelby, the colors draw your attention to the building...that is if your vision is good enough.  If you have trouble seeing it, maybe you should stop in....and maybe somebody else should drive! ;)  Review #1890

Although this place may not appeal to everyone, it must certainly be a favorite of those who are looking for uniforms and costumes.  I got a chance to chat with the owner who says that some of his pieces are used in plays, events, and even some museums in Chicago because of their condition.  There are some antiques like gramophones and oil lamps, even some antique guns/rifles.  But the mainstay of this place is the availability of clothing and hats that fit specific themes.    Oh, and if this sort of thing interests you, I got a tip that they may only be around another few months before moving (and taking their collection) to Canada.  If you are interested in uniforms and related military items, get here soon!  Review #1937

In preparation for Super Bowl XLVI, the Arts Council of Indianapolis commissioned artists to create a lasting tribute to the celebration and to Indianapolis called "46 for XLVI".  Hoosier artist Pamela Bliss was selected to paint this mural back in 2011 (she did touch up in late 2016).  The mural is officially called "My Affair with Kurt Vonnegut".  Bliss has been a key contributor to the public art scene in Wayne County (Richmond area) by holding a series of annual mural contests which brought public art to every town in the county.  This mural was made from a composite of photographs of the author and faces northwest.    Vonnegut was an author born in 1922 who wrote such famous works as "Slaughterhouse Five", "Cat's Cradle", and "Breakfast of Champions".  Many of his books mention Indianapolis which Vonnegut had a deep connection to.  For more about public art in the Indy metro area, see the Arts Council of Indianapolis Public Art Directory (PAD): https://www.indyartsguide.org/public-art/my-affair-with-kurt-vonnegut/  For more about the artist, see her Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/pg/PamelaBlissArt/posts/?ref=page_internal  Review #1172

Nice variety of cakes, cupcakes, cheesecakes, and mini-pies.  There are even quite a few large cookies!  They have convenient parking in their lot on the east side of the building.  You can even order special event cakes, but I strictly stopped by for something sweet to eat right away!  The cupcakes were running about $3.75 each, while the pies and cheesecakes were a bit higher.  It's not cheap, but it isn't standard grocery store baked good either.  Good and fresh with lots of flavor.  The adage "You get what you pay for" applies here.  The service was friendly and efficient and the store was spotlessly clean.  Review #1705

Rusted Window is tucked away in the corner of a strip mall a half block east of the roundabout of Rangeline Rd and Carmel Drive.  I had a bit of trouble finding it, but was glad I did.   The shop has a little bit of everything.  Home Decor?  Candles? Just Pop in! popcorn? Women's Clothing?  Floral arrangements? Yes to all!  I will say I was surprised that there wasn't more floor space since it looks rather roomy from the parking lot.  But once inside, there are basically two rooms for shopping while the rest of the space is storage area behind the counter.  The staff was friendly and offered to assist in finding something.  The space was organized and arranged so that it presented the items in groupings that made sense, not cluttered like some spaces.  Review #2098

I've been meaning to stop in here for awhile, so I finally made a plan to make it a destination one Wednesday(4-6-16) for lunch.  I was able to find street parking reasonably close and the lunch time crowd wasn't too packed, I didn't have to wait in line to place my order at the counter.  I decided to try the Turkey, avocado, bacon, and cheese on a croissant with a side of cole slaw.   Excellent choice.  The croissant was what I had hoped it would be on texture and flavor.  The rest of the ingredients were fresh and generous without being over the top.  Just an all around good sandwich.  I also stopped at the bakery counter to get some bread to go.    It's a shame it takes me nearly an hour to get to Broad Ripple.  This is a sandwich worth stopping back in for!  Review #36

Although not a official city park, the Opti Park (Optimist Club) does have the standard playground features that small kids seem to enjoy.  There is also a parking lot (gravel), a baseball field with a backstop, a small shelter, and some shaded seating.  The best part about the park is that it has a great location that allows you to park here, play and relax, and then if you wish, to stroll over to the Arts Center (on the north end) or along the Monon to some shops and restaurants.  So, as long as you don't mind walking, it's a great place.  Otherwise, the park is what you get just about anywhere in the metro area.  Review #1176

My wife and I stopped in after seeing their colorful decor on the back porch/yard of this shop in Greenwood.  Since it was a fall day, all the unique items fit perfectly with the season.  From rustic to fancy, this place has a bit of everything.  My wife was drawn to the nice selection of clever plaques touting the wonders of being a Grandma!  I liked the varieties of yard flags and pot pourri. Lots of holiday items too!  The staff was very friendly and welcoming.  They shared info about when the open house would be in November for converting their entire store from fall to Christmas items.  They even mentioned to watch their Facebook page for updates on sales and promotions.  Sure, lots of places do that, but I liked that the staff had such enthusiasm for the place.  It was like an invitation to join the fun!  We will definitely be back, and for me, it is a lot closer than driving to Nashville/Brown County.  Review #147

I had heard good things about Santorini, so I met a friend for lunch (3-24-16).  I decided to go with one of the daily specials.  The food was generous in proportion, but frankly, didn't make much of an impression on me.  The dining area is a spacious room and the service was okay.  No complaints...just nothing that makes me desire to return.  Review #39

I went here in March, so none of the water park was in use, but even without having access to that large portion of the park, I can see this park has a lot to offer.  First the park has a lot of paved parking and instead of making it some giant rectangle, it is separated by outcroppings of natural plantings.  There are also paved paths to a number of the activity centers in the park.  There are quite a few activity centers:  a skate park near the entrance, a full court basketball area, a playground is located right next to a splash park with a shelter (concession stand?) with restrooms within easy range of both.  There are shelters that can be reserved and an expanse of open space that includes a hill which can be a challenging uphill run or a thrilling sled down when there is snow.  It was clean and seemed in fine condition (a park and rec worker was there even in March taking care of the place.)  Overall, it felt like a place I would gladly return to.  Review #644

There are so many cool items in this shop that I was surprised!  Not only do they carry greeting cards, but they have collectibles including Disney, Dept 56, and Possible Dreams.  They carry puzzles, stuffed animals, Colts logo items, and lots of gift items.  There is even a women's fashion area called Simply Noelle to the left of the entrance.  On the right is a room dedicated to Dept 56 with several diorama's of village setups including Halloween, a New England Village, and a Dicken's Christmas Carol.  I must have shopped and browsed for ten minutes checking out the store and none of the three people working acknowledged me while I was there.  I liked being able to browse without being hassled, but at the Greenwood Hallmark, I was greeted and told that if I needed any help, to just ask.  That would be nice to hear from this one.  Review #2084

Plain and simple review:  If you want a delicious bundt cake (various sizes and about a dozen flavors available), then this is your 5-star place to go!  However, if you want something else, there isn't much else available to eat.  They do have some birthday candles, coffee mugs, and other little knickknacks you can by, but this is a chain that says let's do the best bundt cakes we can.  And they do.  I liked that they had a sample of the day where you can taste a bite-sized amount of one of their flavors.  I liked the sample (white chocolate raspberry) and bought one of their Bundtlettes of that kind as well as a Lemon.  Both cakes were really moist and have a light and sweet icing ribbing on them.  Very reasonable prices too since each one of the cakes was shareable in size.  Review #1713

While browsing around Zionsville, my wife and I stopped into this boutique on the south side of Pine Street.  The shop is nicely decorated around the perimeter and features free standing racks of women's clothing in the middle.  The target age of the clothing is probably younger woman and from what we could see, targets smaller/athletic fits.  The woman behind the counter was friendly and offered to help find something, but it didn't seem the type of clothing my wife could see herself wearing.  From a neutral observers point of view, I did find the simple racks looking a bit out of place from the rest of the store which was spaced nicely and decorative.  The racks just looked a bit cluttered and not as fine as the rest of the shop.  Review #2212

I avoided all the drama by simply pulling in to the pumps and filling up with gas.  I liked that they had the squeegee and towels to clean my windows actually in working condition.  However, the pump I chose ran out of paper and directed me inside.  I didn't need a paper receipt and simply used my phone to take a picture of the amount.  No need to go inside.  No drama.  Review #2900

This large shop has a variety of sections including a canned goods grocery, home decor, and a seasonal holiday section.  The place was crowded with shoppers and the aisles got a little congested, but most were plowing through the Christmas stuff.  The rest of the shop seemed pretty easy to get around.    They don't carry the high end brands, but the items are serviceable.  So, there can be some savings if you are willing to take the time to work your way through.  Review #1932

I hadn't been to Canterbury Park for about ten years, but it has been maintained well.  I like that it has restrooms and a water fountain (great place to know about if you are running the Monon Trail next to the park!) There are swings and climbing & sliding equipment for the kids.  There is shade, a volleyball court (no equipment, just a location), and a shelter with picnic tables and a grill.  Considering the size of the place, it has enough to make it useful and fun without feeling crowded.  Review #594

Although I haven't purchased any pianos or instruments here, I have been to their showroom and have attended two concerts in the performance hall.  Such was the case for my most recent visit.  After browsing through their rows of grands and uprights, I entered the large room to listen to the performances of a pair of pianists that were brought in by the business to entertain.  The pair alternated in short sets and really displayed the range of sounds and emotions that an artist can extract from the equipment.  It really makes a difference when someone that talented plays an instrument that you might be considering.  I did notice that for the performance, nobody from the business made a point of introducing the artists.  They had to introduce themselves which seem like an oversight.  If they are going to continue providing concerts, surely someone could be available to do the introductions.  If you are interested in purchasing a piano or guitar, there is a large selection here and the arrangement of them seems conducive to "test driving" them before you purchase.  They also offer lessons and additional accessories to enhance your skill and enjoyment of the purchase.  Review #2498

I decided to stop by Best Buy since I had been having some audio problems with my computer's sound system.  I was pretty sure it I had a short in my old system, so I started browsing the options inside the computer section of the store.  Before long, one of the "blue shirts" asked if I was doing okay or needed any assistance.    Long story short:  He answered all my questions, even demonstrated the sound quality I could get from the system, and then answered some more questions about another item.  When done, he made sure I knew to ask any of the blue shirts if I had any more questions.    This is the third Best Buy I've been to in a month and each one has done a much better job of being customer friendly than I had remembered from years passed.  Yes, they still offer a "buyer's insurance" warranty on almost everything, but I don't have a problem of saying no on the lower end items that are more disposable.  The new system was easy to install and the sound is really good.  No more short!    Review #3698

Now that I'm retired, I don't wear as much high end clothing as I did.  So, I mainly shop here when my wife is looking for something.  I like the direction the stores are taking with emphasis on customer service.  My wife was greeted and ended up making a purchase in record time.  I also like the atmosphere in the store.  During the holidays, the pianist was playing holiday music near the escalator, surrounded by a Christmas tree and lots of decorations.  It seemed more festive than the other stores.  Sure, the pricing is higher than most of the other mall stores, but that is pretty well known by the shoppers who are looking for that something special.  There also seems to be plenty of room to move around in the store and enough staff to handle the daily shopping customers.  Review #1905

Don't be fooled by the small storefront.  The mall not only has that space, but the building to the east which also has a basement to browse through.  There a many booths (though some are not clearly defined spaces) of items with a wide variety of items.  I saw a lot of dishes and because it is December, lots of holiday items for sale.  I wouldn't say that it was an antique mall so much as a mix of antiques and lots of collectible items that may have some age, but not the value that bargain hunters may be looking for.  The staff was friendly and helpful.  Review #1936

This location, just north of the the SR 267 exit on I-70, is a convenient spot to pick up a wide variety of beverages and mixes.  I was directed here by the Cardinal Spirits website as a place to find their products.  Although Discount Liquors doesn't carry the full line, they were able to help me find the Bramble Vodka that I was looking for.  I like when local products are available to purchase conveniently.  This location also carries local wines and beers as well.  Of course, they still carry most of the big name options as well, but this store is smaller in size than the big warehouse type liquor stores.  Still, I like supporting the independent and smaller businesses when I can, so I recommend giving this shop a try.  Review #2119

While waiting at the hospital, I decided to a grab some breakfast.  As I was heading to the cafeteria, I happened to notice this restaurant.  Near the entrance, there were several stations with table seating beyond them.  Along the wall was a pastry station and a salad/chilled item cooler at a right angle.  A soup island with several varieties was placed between the pastry wall and a breakfast/sandwich counter.  Cashier stations were to the left with a self serve coffee station beyond that.  I grabbed a cinnamon roll while waiting for my order of "the Good Egg" to be prepared.  I also grabbed a small Hazelnut coffee.  After paying, I enjoyed my meal in house.  The sandwich was really good.  The bun was toasted and the eggs, spinach, tomato, avocado, and aioli were ripe/fresh and tasty.  The cinnamon roll was glazed with icing and had a slight taste of citrus along with the cinnamon.  The center had a slightly doughy texture.  The coffee was full flavored and though served hot, did not scald.  Good food and a smooth system for getting served quickly.  Review #3411

My wife treated me to the newest addition to the Fundae's franchise which just opened in Speedway.  I was pleasantly surprised at how friendly the staff was, encouraging us to sample any flavors of ice cream we had questions about.  There were about two dozen flavors, a wide variety of flavored cones dipped in chocolates, and lots of toppings to add if you were inclined to do so.  I'm probably not their target customer preferring a simple, but creamily delicious, cup of ice cream.  I sampled a tasty lemon poppy seed flavor before settling on a divine Raspberry Rhapsody.  Creamy cold smoothness with raspberry swirls and chocolate coated raspberries to offer a little texture.  My wife went with the Caramel Chaos ice cream that was equally as creamy.  The place was spotlessly clean and though we were not rushed, we were through the line quickly and enjoyed our ice cream in the small dining area.    Parking was free along the street, but there is also a free parking garage nearby (for up to 3 hours).  Once the word gets out, I can see this being a very popular spot this summer.  Review #2848

Twenty five months ago, I gave my very first Yelp review: the Loft at Traders Point.  I have been there a few times and usually get dinner and wander around the place, enjoying the experience seeing the cows and the dairy production.  I just realized when I was looking for a place to get ice cream that I had never reviewed the Creamery.  So after crossing the one lane bridge on Moore Rd, I turned into the private parking lot (gravel) and saw the Dairy Bar was open.  This small "shack" sits in front of the first floor entrance into the shop where Traders Point Creamery products are sold as "to go" items.  Inside, there are varieties of cheese and yogurt and just about anything dairy that can be made on the premises.  But today I was just hunting ice cream (also made here).  They don't have  infinite flavors, just some of the most popular.  I went with a single scoop (actually 3 small scoops) of chocolate chip mint ice cream that was delicious and perfect on a hot day.    Review #1115

I can't say how good the food is here since I had just finished eating across the street when I noticed this place.  I decided to try one of their smoothies.  No matter what flavor you order, they give you the option of making it juice or yogurt based.    The staff was prompt on taking my order (at the counter) and my wait was short as they finished someone else order before making mine.  The interior is small and cozy though it didn't get too loud.  Most folks were dining and managing their voice levels so that it seemed like if you found a spot, you could do a little work while consuming your purchase.  Review #3167

A new home decor shop opened in Mooresville that has a variety of arrangements, accessories, pottery, knick knacks, and furniture.  They sell oils and narrative plaques.  Just a wide variety of items.  The general character of the shop is rural/comfortable living.  The shop is located in the shopping center where the local cinema can be found. It faces SR67, but you have to enter at the light and then drive to your right to get here.  Once you drive to the storefront, there is plenty of parking.  The shop has a lot of room to grow.  There was space at the back, and even in the middle of the shop, there is plenty of space between the aisles.  There were two people working when I entered and they greeted me even though they were still working on arrangements.    If you are looking for someplace new to get ideas for your home, why not stop by!  Review #2145

Behind the town hall in Avon, there is a beautiful park with lots of open space for hiking and disc golf.  To the east of the town hall is a playground, a remote control car course (bring your own), a pair of outdoor ping pong tables, and a twin set of shelters.  Behind the town hall is a large pond that allows fishing and makes for a pleasant view while hiking around it.  The pond also has a couple art pieces along the trail.  "200 Years" was commissioned for the Bicentennial while "Angel of Hope" is a secluded monument area for parents who have lost children.  Behind the pond is a huge disc golf area that has quite a bit of elevation to it.  There is plenty of space on the east and west wings of the park that are great for hiking too.  Overall, it is a well maintained park with plenty of parking at the front and easy access from US 36.  Review #724

This sprawling nature park (188 acres!) has a lot of modern conveniences to make for a fun day at the park.  There is a 2.5 mile paved trail that goes throughout the developed parts of the park.  The winding access road through the park goes by each of the numerous shelters and provides parking so that you don't have to lug your picnic very far.  There are a couple playgrounds located near the shelters as well.  But for those who like to bike and hike, the trail is the reason to come.  And if that isn't enough, there are unpaved trails through the woods for getting back to nature.  The park seems well maintained and attendance seems light compared to some of the other large nature parks around Indy.  Consider this park if you want to explore something new on a staycation.  Review #675

Although my latest visit was on a cold winter day, I've been here in the summer when the park is shaded by mature trees and is filled with the sound of the central fountain.  The park is in the center of a roundabout a couple blocks south of Washington Street at the intersection of Audubon and University.  The location is where Butler University used to be located before relocating to its current campus.  The park also features a bust of Washington Irving, a famous American author at the beginning of the 19th century.  Irving is commonly known by his works including "Rip Van Winkle" and "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow".  I didn't find why the author from New York was memorialized here other than the similarity between his last name and the name of the community.  There aren't any other amenities like a playground, shelter, or restrooms due to the lack of space.  But the location is a nice addition to the neighborhood, offering a gathering place for the community as well as a quiet place for individuals.  Review #554

Excellent chocolates with as much visual appeal as they have taste.  As much as 98% of the candies are made in house and the variety I sampled were really good!  Lots of varieties coming in milk, dark, and white chocolate flavors.  Chocolates are sold in packages or by the piece.  The only negative is that the pricing is quite a bit higher than house chocolates I've had in Zionsville and Greenwood.  If money is no object, then you can let your tastebuds and imagination go wild!  I recommend the Ganache (Raspberry).  Review #453

My wife gets a lot of her sewing supplies through Joann Fabrics.  I usually tag along and so this is the third one I've been in.  While the one in Bloomington has the greatest collection of fabric (by far!), this one has a nice mix of fabric and crafts, with a fair amount of room for seasonal items.    One thing I've learned is that you are going to overpay if you don't have the JOANN app on your phone.  They always, and I mean ALWAYS, have coupons that will save you double digit percents (I've seen 60%) off your purchases.  The staff has been helpful when we've made purchases, but they do get slammed on weekends at the cutting counter.  I always encourage my wife to go during the week to avoid the delay.  Review #1933

I would have loved this place as a kid/teenager, especially if I had any money!  As a fan of comics growing up (and now movies), I would have enjoyed looking through the collectibles (like statues) and t-shirts.  They have a lot of things that I've not seen elsewhere too, so points for that!  The space was a little crowded by the routing of customers around the counter, but once I got passed that, I was able to move about fairly easily.  Prices on some stuff seemed quite reasonable considering the store is located in a mall.  Fun place to browse if your interest runs in this direction.  Review #1908

Embroidery and Cross Stitching supplies are what you will find in this delightful shop.  There is a rainbow of colorful threads that greet you as you enter.  Patterns and supplies are found throughout the two stories of shop.  The woman working was very helpful in explaining the differences and showed a number of completed examples to make it easier to understand.  Upstairs, there are a couple long tables where it looks like you might be able to get some training/guidance on how to do the craft.  Overall, I found the place to be a one stop shop for pursuing your interest in this type of hobby.  Review #2198

I have to admit I was impressed with this place.  Not only is it huge, it has a lot of items that you wouldn't normally think of in a bookstore.  It seems they realize that people who read books might also like board games, of collectibles, or gifts for folks who read, and a cafe for enjoying your newest purchase.  On the day we went, there was an organization providing gift wrapping for the holidays.  Very cool and convenient.  And of course, they have all the latest books and if they don't, they can track it down for you.  The staff we dealt with were helpful and friendly.  Great experience!  Review #1949

After trying out another new restaurant on Mass Avenue, my wife and I stopped in three nearby gift shops.  This was our favorite.  There are small items from around the world that range from jewelry and clothing, to food items, to art projects, and Christmas ornaments.  There were spices and hand made greeting cards.  Each item also tells you which country the crafter was from.    It was mentioned by several of the staff that the artisans are paid a "fair wage" for their goods.  I'm not sure who determines that wage, but it sounds like more than most places do.  Anyway, we saw a number of items that interested us enough to make purchases.  It was fairly busy, but the place didn't seem too crowded, so that was also a plus.  Review #1833

My timing was fortunate, but not optimal as I caught this place just minutes before closing on a Saturday afternoon.  So, they didn't have any black drip coffee available, but suggested an Americano as an alternative.  I also grabbed a twist tie coordinated blueberry muffin (they have a mini chart to help you identify the flavors by twist tie).  The server was friendly and helpful and I was planning to get my coffee to go anyway, so I didn't have a lot of opportunity to check out for ambiance though I will say that the seating area looked inviting.   The American was just a bit too hot to enjoy right away, but had a good taste and was a useful alternative to standard drip coffee.   The muffin, though not huge, was very filling.  I am not sure how long it had been there.  The blueberries had a bit of a raisin texture to them.  It didn't affect the taste, but it was a bit unusual compared to other muffins in my experience.  Good food, service, and setting.  I like it!  Review #2869

This is one of my favorite music stores to browse.  They have lots of music on both cd and vinyl.  Not just inventory, but lots of really good records to choose from.  There are listening stations for cd's and a play area if you need to let your kids play while you browse.  The prices for vinyl were running in the $20-40 range for most of the classic albums I was looking at.  I also liked the friendly greeting when I arrived.  Review #2866

My wife and I stopped in during a day trip to explore Broad Ripple.  This shop is located next to "The Corner" at Guilford and Westfield.  It is filled with jewelry, home decor/gifts, and appears to do custom framing too.  The shop is small but is filled with a lot of high quality items.  My wife kept finding many cool things to look at.  The items seemed unique and well made which explains why they are on the pricey side.  If you like looking for a special gift, for either yourself or a friend, check this place out.  Review #2156

In the wedge neighborhood formed by the intersection of Virginia and Shelby Streets in Fountain Square, a small playground was added on a corner lot of Grove and Elm.  The playground is fenced and has a mulch base throughout the entire play area.  Slides and swings are the main source of entertainment/activity for the park.    The park has no dedicated parking and does not have running water or restroom facilities, so plan a visit accordingly.  Review #538

The Antique Emporium surprised me with the number of large pieces of furniture that I saw in this double spaced strip mall shop.  Though the shop looks small from the front, having the second area to the west doubles the space making it possible for large pieces to fit in, often as cabinets, with loads of small items.  There are collections of vinyl albums, vintage clothing, dishes, coins, books, and just about anything you can think of.  Not the largest collection, but decent quality pieces.  Review #2019

This location of BBW is one that contains the White Barn candle section in the back half of the store towards the checkout counter.  There are lots of sales, especially during the holiday season.  My wife also enjoys the foaming soap products while I prefer the candle section.  Plenty of room to move about without feeling crowded too!  Review #1926

Good food and cocktails.  Good service too!  Basically, it is what you would expect from a lounge under the St Elmo's brand.  But like the steak house, it gets too crowded.  (Visit the one in Fishers for comparison.)  They offer a nice variety of cocktails.  I went with the French 75 that is based upon an old recipe from Harry's Bar in Paris.  Nice flavor with a hint of lemon and splash of champagne.  I also tried the Sesame Seared Sashimi Tuna served over a mound of rice.  Excellent flavor when combined with the dipping sauce on the side.  But understand that you have to climb a flight of stairs to get here and the lounge is kept very dark with a bit of a reddish lighting.  It isn't exactly welcoming to older folks who may have trouble seeing the menu or have mobility problems.  (I didn't ask if they have an elevator in St Elmo's, but there wasn't any visible from the lounge.)  And because of the tight quarters, it can get loud.  If those things don't affect your experience, then you may give it a 5 star rating.  Prices are comparable to St Elmo's.  Review #3424

The ice cream and gelato we ordered were okay.  Pretty standard for homemade ice cream shops.  Although the service was prompt, when they asked if we wanted the homemade waffle cones (which were fresh and crisp), they made no mention that they were $2.50 per cone (without the ice cream!).  My bill (with tax) for two cones (one single, one double) was over $16!  I had seen the photos on Yelp and in those photos, the cones were only $1 or $1.25 extra.  Be advised to look at the prices before you order.    The shop was clean and had a lot of room for visitors.  Parking is limited to the available street parking.  Review #1032

This park is primarily a sports park with numerous baseball fields.  The good news is that there is a lot of paved parking for when there isn't a game on.  There park has a couple shelters and there are playgrounds near each.  Some of the equipment is unique with playground pieces that look like trees, or the stages of a butterfly, or a bee.    The park also has tennis and volleyball courts on the west end of the park.  Perk:  The park is within easy walking distance of Mrs Curls Ice Cream shop!  The park definitely has a lot of features, but doesn't have any "wow" features of some of the more modern parks in central Indiana.  Review #777

My wife and I were looking for a new dining table and chair set, so we stopped by to see what they had.  We were greeted by one of the salespeople who let us know to come see her if we had any questions.  We browsed for a bit, but didn't really see anything on the floor like we wanted.  Too bad I hadn't read Dylan's review that mentions they have an online catalog available.  Also too bad for the salesperson that she didn't mention it either.    They did have some nice pieces, but nothing jumped out as being a piece we wanted for our home.  I guess we will continue looking.  If we are in the area (it's about a 50 minute drive for us), I wouldn't mind using their online system.  Review #2049

Although I have read reviews of the YMCA, none of them talked about the cool park and trail system just north of the facility.  The park has paved trails for hikers and bikers that allow options for one mile and 5K distances.  Inside the northern loop, there are soccer fields, a baseball diamond, and a beach volleyball court.  Along the south side of the loop is a shelter with picnic tables inside.  On the west side of the park is a wooded area that is undeveloped with trails, but not blocked off by fencing.  On the east side is a community garden for locals to plant their own gardens.  There are also loops of trails which run down each side of the campus towards US 36 for the extra hiking distance.    The park looks to be pretty well maintained as well and is free to use without the gym membership.  Parking is available in the lots for the YMCA.  Review #723

I've tried stopping by here several times and always seem too early for their lunch hours  or dinner hours, but I finally arrived later in the day closer to dinner and picked up a large NY style slice of pepperoni that I found to be delicious.  No wonder when the proteins are locally sourced from Turchetti's Salumeria. Delicious!  My only problem was that I didn't want an entire pie, so I settled for a slice which I had no idea how long it had been sitting there.  The flavor was fantastic!, but the crust had become tough and chewier than I prefer.  But that didn't deter me from devouring the slice.  I'll need to return with a group so that we can order an entire pie fresh to see how well this place measures up with other favorites.     I hope they can get enough staff to offer longer & earlier hours.  Pizza for lunch sounds good, but it hast o fit my lunch schedule.  If you like NY Style pizza that is full of flavor, stop by Frankie's.  I t is located along the back wall on he north end of the AMP.  Enjoy!  Review #3950

After several years of being hard to find unless you frequent Farmers Markets or the Circle City Industrial Complex, it's nice to see the sisters behind the delicious ice cream company Lick land a spot in the new Bottleworks Garage.    All the same flavors and all the things you like about the ice cream itself, but now located where you can grab a meal from one of the other vendors in the garage.  All the ice cream is made completely free of artificial ingredients, even food coloring. So, not as wide a range of colors, but pure, fresh flavor all the same.   Although the production part of the business is likely to stay at the previous location at the CCIC,  a new, more accessible store front went into the Bottleworks Garage (Just north of 9th Street).  I ordered a small bowl of champagne cherry ice cream and was thrilled with the flavor!  Make this a must visit place when you visit the Garage.  p.s. I can't resist throwing in that the business got started when one of the sisters got an ice cream maker for a wedding gift....Now that was a useful gift put to good use!  Rev #57

While in Irvington for breakfast Our first,choice-place, was Closed due to a lack of staffing.  Fortunately I remembered that Lincoln square offered complete meals just down the street and had their own lot.  inside had plenty of room though it wasn't as accessible as I had-hoped.  normally I order  Eggs Benedict when out for breakfast,  I changed selection to the Indiana Benedict.   Instead of the light and   and rich Hollanddaisese..the meat was more like a burger patty than Canadian bacon for breakfast   The breakfast wtopped with gravy which was much heavier than the usual Hollanddaise too,I would suggest   The Standard option.  Review#3946  .

Although this theater shows second run films, they have somehow managed to keep the place in good shape and are an affordable option for anyone who wants the big screen experience without going broke.  I recently returned to catch a film I missed during the avalanche of movies released trying to be considered for Oscar nominations.  The check in process was easy and the common areas appeared clean.  The actual theater was huge with two aisles splitting the seating into three areas.  I grabbed a seat closer to the front to get the "big picture" effect and was able to pick any seat I wished.  The picture and sound quality were okay.  Not the best, but good enough to be enjoyed.  The seating was the old fashioned kind that you sit in...not recline/nap in.    They appeared to have a variety of concession items and a few activities in a game room just off the lobby.  My only real negative is that the hallways outside the theater are quite dark.  Even a my noon time viewing, it felt like walking down a darkened city street.  A few simple lighting modifications could make the area much more inviting.  Review #491

Krannert is another one of the better Indy Parks.  This is one with a very nice pond and shaded shelters/playgrounds.  There is a large family rec center and an aquatic center.  In the outlying areas of the park, there are sports fields/courts for the bigger kids.    For those who like hiking, there are two options with paved pathways.  Although the park & rec center are showing some age, I did see the parks department had workers attending the outdoor swimming pool.  I hope the maintenance continues to keep the park at a high quality.  Review #662

Mofoco is a nice choice if you are near the Monon in Broad Ripple.  They have a variety of taco options, but on my visit, I decided to try the Chicken Club Wrap.  Really solid choice.  The wrap is stuffed with lots of meat and veggies and flavored with smoked gouda and chipotle aioli.  Very nice flavor.  Although the chicken was a little chewy, the other ingredients kept it moist.    I also ordered the seasoned fries as a side and upgraded with the basil aioli for dipping.  Very tasty combo that went well with the wrap.    Service was prompt and courteous.  I appreciated that the check was dropped off while I was still eating which allowed me time to ask for a "to go" box for the other half of my wrap.  Overall, a very pleasant experience.  Review #345

This neighborhood park has historical significance for Indy as well as providing a nice playground for kids.  Camp Morton was a training ground for soldiers preparing for the civil war on what was once the state fairgrounds.  Later, the site became a Confederate prison from 1862-5.  Now, this raised park (wheel chair accessible) has good drainage and paved walkways with numerous picnic tables and trash bins to help keep the park clean.  Leashed pets are welcome and doggie bags can be obtained from a dispenser on site.  The playground has a central climbing piece with slides.  To the east, a set of swings and a spring animal for riding have been added.  A shelter occupies the south east corner of the park.  There is no designated parking for the location and I did not see any water fountains/restrooms on site.  Still, with a bit of planning, the park looks like a fun place to gather where families can grab a table and watch as the kids have fun.  Review #517

Just north of the Mile Square between the Central Indianapolis Library and the Veteran's Memorial Plaza is a two block park that is nestled between the American Legion National Headquarters (on the east) and the Indiana American Legion Headquarters (on the west).    Since the Indiana World War Memorial is located two blocks to the south to honor veterans of World War I, additional memorials were set up on this mall to honor World War II, Korean War, and Vietnam War veterans.  These monuments were created between 1996 and 1998 by sculptor Patrick Brunner.  In the center of the north end of the mall is a cenotaph (empty tomb dedicated to veterans) with four columns topped with golden eagles built in 1931.  The middle of the south block is a sunken garden/lawn that raises to street level and is edged by the street level war monuments.  The park is a great location for hosting events downtown or for strolling along when the weather cooperates.  Review #1862

Generally, I am not a mall shopper.  I don't go for big crowds and hate waiting in line.  But now that I am retired and since it is the Christmas season as I write, I was pleasantly surprised at the condition of this place and that I didn't have to deal with the flocks of young people who can sometimes take over a mall.  The mall was clean and in good condition.  The holiday decorations,  including a place for Santa, seemed appropriate, but not over the top.  I saw a number of newer food options, and a number of new stores that I hadn't seen on my last visit.  New is good and can help keep the interest of shoppers.  Review #1900

This park has a very accessible location, lots of parking, and some amenities that aren't as common at the area parks:  a full aquatic center and an ice rink.  There are ball fields, tennis courts, basketball, shelter, playground and plenty of room to hike around.  However, from recent news that persistent ice troubles forced the rink to close during the youth hockey league, the park must do lots of work to have the rink repaired by fall of 2018.  As the last park ice rink in the city, this was very disruptive.  So, I applaud that the park is trying to fix the problem...I just hope it has better luck than with Ellenberger Park.  Review #687

If you are an adult, this neighborhood park may be more appealing than the Shawn Grove Park.  This park has no playground, just a central fountain and mature trees.  There are several areas that separated by shrubs and distance so that even if someone else is there while you are, you can still relax on one of the benches or in the gazebo.  There is a special section designated for sensory appreciation for visually impaired visitors.  Unfortunately, the sign is written in English only and could have added braille.  I guess they figured someone without eyesight would need to bring them here at least the first time.   The park does have a water fountain but no restroom facilities and no designated parking.  Street parking is free but dependent upon the time of day and occasion for how accessible it can be.  Review #514

Nice smoothie chain based in Dallas with good flavor and service.  I stopped in while shopping for a boost.  After finding some free parking out front, I entered and placed my order and paying at the counter. I left my name for the order and stood to the side.  In just a few minutes, my smoothie was ready.  I got a 20 oz. Banana Boat that was delicious.  I passed on the added peanut butter option which may have been even more tasty.  The staff was friendly and kept busy so I was on my way quickly.  Review #3442

I usually don't go out for tacos, but when I realized this franchised taco shop was locally based, I decided to give it a try.  I really liked that they had a variety of tacos available including a chili ground beef soft taco and a chicken soft taco.  I loaded them with what ever toppings they had and selected the 2nd of five heat sauces since I wanted some heat and flavor, but not too much that might override the taste.  The ingredients were fresh and the taco shells were sturdy enough to stay together while loaded.    The amount of chili on the chili taco was minimal and was a bit disappointing.  The chicken version had a lot more meat, but it seemed like standard chicken deli meat, not seasoned like I might find at some other Mexican restaurants.    The staff was friendly and fairly quick on building my meal, but they have very limited interaction other than calling your name when your order is ready.    No tipping or busing of the tables by the staff seemed apparent.  Plenty of parking in the common lot of the strip mall.  Review #1985

This park has a wide variety of activities and plenty of room for enjoying the park.  There was an aquatic center with a splash park, pool, and water slide.  There were basketball and sports fields.  There was a long hiking trail around the park and another that goes to the south around a farmer's field.  There are several shelters with grills and a playground with a nice variety of equipment for sliding, swinging, and climbing.  One of the negatives is that the park doesn't have adequate drainage along the trails, so I noticed several places where water was standing across the paved paths.  I don't appreciate getting my shoes and socks wet while on a long hike and that would discourage me from using the trails unless we had a dry spell.    Otherwise, the park seemed in pretty good shape with plenty of parking.  Review #611

I was surprised when I checked in that Claire's hadn't been reviewed before.  Like almost every mall in Central Indiana, Perry Crossing/Metropolis was no exception to having one of these small accessory shops.  Here you can get your ears pierced, pick up earrings and head bands, a few toys, and holiday novelty items.  During the week, the crowd was small so it was fairly easy to get around.  The only negative was that when my wife was ready to pay for some festive earrings, the only clerk was busy with an indecisive boy about getting his ear pierced.  (He didn't.)  So, depending upon your situation, you may or may not be helped promptly.    Like most malls, parking is limited in front of the store with free lots about a block away from the store front.  Review #3446

One of Indy's older parks (1909), the park has plenty of room for hiking, two playgrounds, a shelter, swimming pool, and indoor ice rink.  The park is lined with numerous mature trees offering shade to visitors and shelter for lots of neighborhood animals.  The only real negative I'm aware of is the limited availability of the single shelter.  For a park having 42 acres, it seems a shame that there wasn't planning for another shelter to facilitate family gatherings.  The park has had its problems (some are financial based) with the pool and ice rink staying open.  Hopefully, those issues are behind them as the warmer weather approaches.  Review #555

I can't say how good this store is throughout the year, but during the holidays, they have a wide variety of accessories that my wife wanted to check out.  Conveniently located near the front of the store, there were loads of colorful earrings and small gifts or stocking stuffers.  She picked out a pair during our visit and had a quick checkout process.  Everything seemed to be working well today!  Review #1901

I stopped by for a quick lunch at this Irish Pub/sports bar located on the end of a strip mall on the south east side.  Inside, there's a sign to wait to be seated for the dining room.  Although I was dining by myself, I chose not to sit in the bar that was behind a short wall beyond the dining area.  I was taken to a 2-top table with a bench seat on one side.  Silent sports television was playing on the numerous screens.  I went with the Classic Reuben and fries for my meal.  The Reuben has thick sliced grilled corned beef, a sauerkraut that was a bit more sour than most, Swiss cheese, 1000 Island dressing, and grilled rye.  The fries had a crispy exterior like they were fried in duck fat (not sure what they used.)  Both sandwich and fries were good and I'd recommend them.  My waitress did a good job of keeping my lunch on track in case I had a limited amount of time.  She checked on water refills and processed my check timely.  Overall, a good place to stop for a meal!  Review #2644

Every time I enter a record shop, I debate within my mind whether to get back into vinyl or simply stay with cd's or streaming.  It's nice to know that at Luna Music, you don't have to choose between cd's or vinyl...they have both!  And the collection here isn't just the pop stars of the moment.  They had a wide variety of artists here...maybe not every record in the discography, but a solid representation of the artist's work.  Most of the previously unused (I find it hard to call a 40 year old record "New") vinyl that I checked out were running in the mid $20s range.  The used items, which are separated (yea!) are considerably lower.  It looks like this place stays in touch with the local music scene as well, so that's another bonus for stopping by.  Parking is a little hit or miss with reliance upon street parking (south side of 52nd to the west of College is where I found free parking.)  You can turn around on one of the side streets to head the right direction if needed.  Friendly greeting but otherwise, you are free to browse without hovering.  Review #3639

Tucked away in a strip mall, this two roomed Mexican restaurant provided a quick and tasty lunch.  Upon entering the restaurant, the lobby has two doors.  The one on the left appears to be more overflow seating while the one on the right, which I chose, allowed me to be greeted and seated upon entering.  Service was good throughout the meal as I was quickly brought my water and utensils and had my order taken.    Complementary salsa and chips were provided.  The bowl of salsa was wide so that the large chips could easily scoop the salsa.  The salsa was smooth in texture but still had a nice flavor.  The chips were fresh and crisp.  After a short wait, my Burrito de Chile Colorado arrived with my choice of rice (beans also available.)  The cubed beef tips were tender and covered in a special sauce and cheese.  Really good!  The rice was also tasty, not dry like some places.  When finished, I was brought my check and paid at the front counter.  Review #3641

This is one of the newest CVS pharmacies in the city.  Located on the corner of South and Delaware, you can park on the north side of the building (off Delaware) or pull into the drive thru (off South).  Note that current construction on South Street limits you to pulling in from westbound only.  The entrance is on the northeast side of the building.  Inside, the space is clean and filled with rows of pharmacy items as well as some convenience store items where you can pick up seasonal items (yes, both Christmas and Halloween items are on display).  There are grocery items as well including breakfast cereal that I hadn't seen elsewhere.  I didn't use the pharmacy, so I can't really comment on that.  I assume they are comparable to other CVS locations.  One thing of fun to be aware of if you visit is that there are a couple cool murals on the outside of the building (see separate reviews for details).  One is an instagram worthy butterfly wings on the east side while there is a shadowbox of giant butterflies on the south side.  Review #3314

I've been by this place many times but it always seemed to be closed.  I finally noticed it open on a Saturday afternoon and decided to stop by.    The place is smaller than I expected with the space being divided into a front and back room with the purchase counter about midway in the store.  What made an immediate impression was that there was a lot of glassware/ceramics in the front end of the shop.  There were also some ornate furniture, but just a few pieces.  The back half of the store was more of an assortment of items, with pricing seeming a bit high for the condition of the items.  The clerk was engaged in a general conversation with one of the other customers during my visit, so I can't say that there was any interaction during my visit.    Like a lot of antique places, if they have what you are looking for, you will have a higher affinity for the place than if they don't.  I didn't see anything that jumped out at me to consider making a purchase.  Review #3293

This place seems to appeal to some people, and to others, not so much.  They did have some unique items and there seemed to be plenty of room to browse for items as well.    I guess the problem is that I found a number of their items to be crass.  Okay, I get an unexpected comment that is off color can have some humor.  But this place is loaded with items that use sexual references or bathroom "humor" to be funny.  I outgrew that about half a lifetime ago, so I didn't see anything I would want to give as a gift to anyone I wanted to keep as a friend.  What is a shame is that it was scattered throughout the store, so it wasn't like I could avoid it.  There were some nice items that I might have considered buying, but didn't on my visit.    Review #1835

My wife and I are fans of McNamara since we find many unique items (especially around holidays) in addition to the floral arrangements.  This shop in the Geist area is much smaller than the other McNamaras I have visited.    Though it has a bounty of beautiful bouquets and arrangements, there isn't room to carry as many home decor items that we search for.  But even though the shop is smaller, I can't tell you how much I enjoyed stepping into a room full of color and floral scents...it felt like springtime!  The woman who greeted me was friendly and let me know to take as much time to browse as I wanted and that she would be there to assist if I had any questions.  Nice!  Although smaller, this is still a fine addition to the McNamara name.  Review #3673

Come for the free water.  Come back for the cool park to the west of the Artesian Well.  Seriously, I didn't know what to expect at this place as I pulled up.  I had seen the small white building with a few benches while driving by, but had not noticed the shelter and the trail that leads into a wooded area where Cool Creek meanders in an ever changing path.  The path is paved until it reaches a bridge that spans the creek where it bends back on itself.  But once you cross the span, the path is natural and not as friendly for anyone who is physically challenged.  The path wanders in a loop around the trees.  Inside the small white building, there is a circular area where a pipe comes up from the ground and distributes the water to four elbow pipes where you can fill your own containers with the water.  The water currently flows at about 15 gallons per minute.  It's a nice park for relaxing and taking a stroll in the shade.  And remember to bring your own jug!  Review #739

I stopped in for dinner on a Saturday afternoon (4-23-16) on my way home from Brownsburg.  I had enjoyed a dinner at the Dawson's on Main a year or two ago, so I thought I would give this extension a try.  The restaurant is part of a strip mall, so there is plenty of parking.  I chose to sit inside and was taken back into the restaurant.  I noticed that there were some art pieces on the wall, but the atmosphere of the restaurant was stark and rather drab.  It didn't feel like an inviting place to dine.  I ordered a craft beer and the Grilled Shrimp Parmesan with a Ciabatta roll.  The shrimp were large and seemed to be prepared well.  The pasta was okay, but forgettable.  So, I doubt if I would go out of my way to return when I can go to the original Dawson's on Main which is much closer for me.  Review #23

Although this side of town has seen a stretch of economic downturn, there seems to be a new energy as the city is focusing on redeveloping the area and entrepreneurs open new businesses near the park.  So, it should come as no surprise that this park should see an upturn in interest as more people discover it.  On the west end of the park, new public art installations are adding visual interest to visitors who stroll along this long and narrow park.  To the east of the artworks, there is a playground and shelter/gazebo portion of the park.  The rest of the park has numerous mature trees that line Pogue's Run as it flows southwest towards the White River.   Review #558

I stopped by for lunch after hearing good things about this family run cafe.  I was able to find street parking just around the corner and took a seat in the front part of this shotgun style building.    I have heard good things about the soups (I will have to try them on another day), but I was intrigued by the Hawaiian Grill sandwich:  croissant (that's my hook!) with ham and cheddar, pineapple, and honey mustard.
