I went with the standard chips (soup and side salad are options for an extra $1.50)  Although all the ingredients were fresh and tasty, the pineapple was a bit too dominant/sweet for the rest of the sandwich....maybe a spicy brown mustard instead of the sweet honey mustard would have been a better match to add flavor depth.    The cafe is eclectic in decor with a comfortable feel.  There is a sense of humor to some of the signs and a definite link to canine appreciation.    I plan on returning to try some soup and investigate their bar options.  Review #45

They have a really nice lunch special.  I ordered the Broccoli Beef and it came with soup (I went with Egg Drop), an egg roll, and steamed rice (about a cup sized serving).  All of this for only $8 plus tax and tip.    There was a private lot and seemed to be a lot of tables available on the inside.      I had a couple waits that seemed awkwardly long during my visit:  No one greeted me when I entered and when I was finished, the two staff members were engaged in a conversation without either watching the dining area.  So, I simply got up and walked over to check out.      I liked my food, but wouldn't say it was any better than a number of other places around town.  I'll give them a pass on the delays, because most reviews seem to praise the service....maybe it was just an off day.  Review #599

I have to give this McNamara's the benefit of the doubt because they are trying to move the last of their Christmas items with a big sale, because I imagine in a week or two they will have all kinds of new items to explore in the showroom part of the store.  During my visit, the pieces they still had were classy, just not what I was looking for. The store is laid out nicely and was easy to get around.  Like the other McNamara's, they have a cooled room that they keep their fresh flowers in to prolong their beauty.  I normally shop/browse the Greenwood store and this one seems quite a bit smaller in floor space and shelf space, so they just won't be able to show as many cool items.    As I browsed, both of the staff working this afternoon let me know that they would gladly help me if I needed anything or had any questions.  I like that!  Review #2085

This was my third visit to Amelia's, a bakery located next to Bluebeard, along the Cultural Trail on Virginia Avenue in Fletcher Place.  I would probably have stopped by more often if they had more parking, but it is hit or miss finding a spot close by.  Just plan on stopping while in the area for one of the bars, distilleries, or restaurants.  Although this was only my third time, I have been fortunate to have tasted Amelia's bread upon many occasions since they supply breads to quite a few restaurants in Indy. Always tasty.  On this Friday afternoon, I selected a Semolina bread.  The staff was friendly and attentive and offered to slice the bread at no extra charge.  On the wall opposite the counter and bread racks are a number of items that may compliment a sandwich or a picnic dinner.  I have selected tomato jam and rumesca (garlic-y sauce) on prior visits.  Good quality foods!  Review #92

This park has a lot of the standard features (shelter, playground, parking lot) of most parks, but also has a great nature trail (about a half mile) through the woods that winds along a creek.  The trails are easy to follow and in most places, stays relatively dry so that you don't have to get muddy just to walk.  There are also some open areas for active sports and additional picnic tables by the east end woods.  There is also a sturdy bridge that spans the creek if you wish to enter the park from the south side of the woods.  Review #769

This Lowes doesn't seem quite as good as it was 10 years ago when I was a more frequent customer.  It also doesn't seem as large as the one I now frequent.  Lots of staff behind the counter, but not many out in the aisles when you need assistance.  This one has most of the seasonal items in a separate area between the yard and the main building.  Review #3407

Although I've seen larger fabric stores and quilt shops, this one has a solid inventory of fabric, quilting machines, threads, patterns, and accessories.    I browsed around noting that most of the fabric and threads were sorted by color palate.  There was a section for holiday quilts/runners including an advent calendar; a section for baby/small kids with whimsical prints; and many types of quilts for everyday interiors or for those quilters who like a challenge.  And that challenge is what made my wife make purchases here.  She wanted to find something beyond the basic squares and triangles.  Not only did they have some finished quilts on display matching her needs, they also had accessories that made it easier to be precise while doing the odd shapes.  The staff was very helpful and even pointed out somethings that my wife might have her sewing group make for fund raising ideas.  Review #3489

I stopped in for a quick lunch and was very pleased with the quality and service.  They have daily lunch specials, so I ordered the Sun King Beer Battered Chicken Strips and chose the homemade coleslaw.  The chicken had a tasty seasoning and was moist and tender inside the crunch of batter.  The coleslaw was crisp and sweet.  I sat at the bar and the bartenders were friendly and efficient at getting my order in.  Ten minutes was all it took from the time I ordered to the time I was eating!  Great local spot to stop by during a lunch hour.    Review #1328

I haven't been here during the warmer months, so I probably haven't been able to appreciate the full beauty of the place.  But even in the winter, I could see the elegance of the design of the park.  There are plenty of picnic tables within a short distance of the ample parking on the north side of the garden.  The small pond has a fountain and koi fish.  The park sits next to the Monon and makes a nice stopping point for travelers to relax.  Review #2017

Although I've only had limited transactions here, I have to say that service I received was prompt and accurate.  Although my wife bought her computer while we were at the Best Buy on the north side, when we learned having the start up (adding all the software & antivirus) would take several hours (up to 24), we found that we could take the computer to the store closest to us and avoid having to make the long drive again.  So, we dropped off the computer and a few hours later, it was ready.  I went to pick up the computer, and after showing ID, was able to pick up the computer for my wife (who had made the purchase).  It only took a couple minutes for the tech to bring it out, and launch the computer to demonstrate it worked.  No mess, no fuss.  I was soon on my way.  I see some negative reviews, but I honestly can't think of any other store I would take the purchase of a new computer to in the metro area.  Review #3679

I've lost count of the number of times I've driven by Bungalow, so I decided to pull into their convenient parking lot and stop in.  I was greeted by the staff and a friendly pup that welcomed me.  The shop, though somewhat small, had a nice selection of clothing, both serious and whimsical (think fancy socks!), mugs, books, and home decor items.  I didn't really think of this as a furniture place that you might guess by the image of the polka dotted mural on the east side of the building.  But it was a cool gift shop sort of place that I could see finding something unique, often humorous, for someone.  Definitely worth checking out the next time you are near the canal!  Review #2104

I've been to a lot of craft and hobby stores, including several other Michaels in the area, and I have to say this is one of my favorites!  Not only did the store have a tidy appearance, but it was well stocked with the types of items I expect.  Sure, there are some other places that are even larger and have items like furniture and faux antiques, but I wouldn't buy those types of things anyway.  Here, they have rows of crafts, florals, accessories, and a few other items like toys.  Basically, they had what we were looking for.  When we had a little trouble finding a specific item in the craft section, one of the employees brought us directly to the item.  And checkout was prompt, even opening another register to help us through.    I wish the Michaels closer to home were as well managed and operated as this one.  Review #3652

I really enjoy finding places that fit their neighborhood, and in this case, are a gathering place for locals.  Inside, the folks who volunteer here were all welcoming and upbeat.  And the coffee was fresh, tasty, and ready to drink without a long wait to cool.    In addition to the coffee, there are some baked goods to grab if you're hungry.  And did I mention that a small coffee is only $1?  What a deal!  The space is simply decorated with a huge dining area/gathering space that has a pool table, a communal table made from a wooden door, and there's a laundry available (I don't know the specifics of that).    I was also able to buy some fresh ground coffee that is a special blend made just for Lincoln Lane.  If you like what you try and can't get here often, just do like I did and buy a bag to go!  Review #2609

Location! Location! Location!  If you like walking through a wooded space along a river, this place is for you!  This 62 acre mature park has a lot of options for visitors of all ages.  A family center, swimming pool and spray park, a dog park (requires a pass from the family center showing your dog has its shots and fees are associated), large playground, shelters (can be rented, but otherwise are first come/first served), and sports fields are here with plenty of space between them.  There are lots of events held here too, so check out their website for a list.  Fun fact #1:  This park used to be the site of the carousel that is in the Children's Museum during the 1920's.    Fun fact #2:  This park used to have the steam locomotive that is is at the Transportation Museum in Noblesville.  Review #588

I'm not sure why this place is so popular with the other reviews.  I have been to a lot of furniture and consignment places in the past few months and I found the inventory small, random, and not really anything that grabbed my attention.  I think I spent more time trying to find the place than shopping.  Once you climb the stairs near loading dock 10, the front area looks promising.  It seems coordinated and decorated with cohesive pieces.  But once you enter the warehouse with its concrete floors and walls, you realize that the majority of the space is "employees only" and you can only shop a long single aisle.  Very little as far as wall decor was on display compared to other places.  If I am going to take the time to get out and shop, I think I would go to some other places around the metro area where they have more of a selection.  Review #2090

I enjoyed my visit to Insomnia Cookies.  I saw that they offer something called a Cookiewich:  your choice of two warm cookies with your choice of ice cream in between.  They serve it on a small plate with a plastic spoon.  The flavor was great with the chocolate chip in the cookie being somewhat melted and the Moose Tracks ice cream juxtaposed with its cool crunch.    The only problem is eating it.  The cookiewich was to thick to get a proper bite and the plastic spoons aren't sharp enough to cut through.  I ended up deconstructing the treat eating the cookie by hand (you WILL need napkins) and ice cream by spoon.    Very friendly gal behind the counter who was very helpful and even asked if there was enough ice cream.    Lots of flavors of cookies are available individually or in groups.  Ice cream too!  Or you can make combos by adding ice cream or frosting to your cookies.  Not cheap, but this is more about serving that immediate craving rather than getting full.    Review #2703

This was my first visit to Beasley's Orchards and I must say that I was very pleased with my visit.  Not only do they have an orchard, but there was a decent sized parking area, a play area and corn maze (both require a fee), and a store.  The store has a sampling of apples and garden vegetables, honeys, jellies, apple slushies and cider, and a bakery that makes pies and cobbler.  Outside, pumpkins and mums are for sale too.   All the store and outside purchases use the same checkout line, so the line can get quite long on weekends.  Review #1371

The shop is much more than just a bakery for dogs treats.  You can find dog beds, apparel for humans, kerchiefs for the dogs, and assorted dog related items.  There is also a section of wall dedicated to flavored dog biscuits which are kind of ordinary looking.  Then you head toward the counter and see the colorfully displayed hand made dog treats.  Some are big, some are small.  Most have a colorful icing applied for visual appeal.  Some are cut out in shapes like bones, trees, and others.    I picked up a couple large ones which were decorated to celebrate the Indy 500.  I also got some small ones including pastel colors and others with sprinkles!  Most of what I ordered had a peanut butter base.    When I got them home, my dogs were a little skeptical, but once they played with it a bit, they devoured them!    The prices are not cheap, but if you've ever tried making these type of things on your own, then you will appreciate how much time it takes to decorate even something that seems simple.  My dogs enjoyed their treats.  I enjoyed the service and dog friendly space.  Review #2600

Although I don't shop here regularly, I like that the grocery has a nice location that isn't too far off SR 37(eventually to be I-69) along Southport Road.  They carry all the brands you see in the larger Krogers and have a pharmacy on site.  They also have a floral area, a bakery, a produce section, and a deli.  They have a decent sized area for wine, liquor and beer, including a few local craft brews.  I was a little surprised that only half the self serve stations were open.  I get that they don't need all the check out lanes staffed, but why not have the self check lanes open?    The store was clean and seemed like the produce and deli sections were filled with fresh items (no fishy smell like at some groceries.)  Seems like a great place for "one stop shopping" for those in the area.  Review #3619

This is our go to pharmacy.  I guess that sums it up in that we use them when needed and generally, have success and good experiences dealing with the pharmacy and the general store staff.  I like that even though they aren't 24/7, they generally are open when I am in need of something.  Their prices are usually okay if you have insurance, but it doesn't hurt to use a price checking app like GoodRx to see if you can get a better deal elsewhere.  But I like the convenience of this place being close and their past service has earned our trust.  One point I want to mention is that for a small store, they have a nice variety of stocking stuffers in the seasonal aisle each Christmas season.  Although it looked a little smaller this year, I always pick up something for the grandkids when I stop by.  Review #1768

This is a pretty good place if you are looking for some fried chicken to go.  Not much atmosphere in the limited dining space they have, but they have an easy to read menu of chicken items on display that helps you get individual amounts or larger family/party sizes.  The chicken breading here is more salty and less peppery than that national brand.  Not too salty, but it is definitely the strongest taste in the coating.    The chicken was nice a crispy on the outside, but just a bit over cooked on the white meat.  The biscuit was a little on the dry side too, but that may be due to the early afternoon timing of my visit.  Pricing was very affordable and I was in and out so fast that I really didn't get much chance to look over what other items they have on their menu.  Review #1913

While out exploring, I remember my wife had mentioned some items that we needed and I figured that Walgreens might carry those items.  This store is located on the northeast corner of Madison and County Line so there are medians to deal with getting here, but the entrances to their parking lot are far enough away from the intersection to not be much of a problem getting in and out (except for rush hour).    The store is a fairly good size, though maybe not as large as the one in my hometown.  As you enter, the checkout counter is on your right with the pharmacy in far left corner, separated from the shopping by a little distance which affords a bit more privacy.  The aisles were clear and well spaced.  A Seasonal aisle is centrally located on the counter side of the store.    Although there was a delay at the counter, another employee saw that I was ready to check out and opened up her register so that I could proceed.  Very nice!  Review #3429

Just west of Allisonville Road on 116th is this pet store located in the same shopping plaza as the Kroger.  There is plenty of parking nearby and the store was generally clean and orderly (though someone left one of those large ladders blocking one of the aisles.)  The franchise out of Michigan isn't the largest pet store, but seems to carry a fair supply of healthy dog and cat foods, supplies for those pets and also sell birds, fish, and a few other critters.  In the back is a dog washing room for those who like self serve, but prefer to not do it at home.  I did notice that when I checked out, the Yelp discount seemed to show up as being expired.  Fortunately, the clerk went ahead and gave me the 10% discount which I appreciated.  Seems like the manager should look into that.  Overall, I had a positive shopping experience and would recommend this place to people who care about their pet's.  Review #3688

I stopped at Walgreens in hopes of seeing the new ELF Villain's collection. Sometimes Walgreens gets them before the holidays. Sometimes they don't. This particular one doesn't ever get them according to their cosmetics person. SAD. Really sad. I suppose I'll have to skulk other Walgreens to find them.

I love shopping at Ross Stores. I stop at every one I come across. Yes, much of the merchandise is the same, but once in a while, you find a gem. It really is a treasure hunt.   They carry a selection of "as seen on Tv" stuff, a slew of Jr's clothing, a decent selection of ladies and missy, but they generally fail at plus, men's and petite.  These markets are woefully represented. Sure they have a men's section, but looking through the stuff, it's crappy t shirts and fubu jeans. Hardly anything the men in my life would wear.  This particular store's selection of lingerie/under garments is sad. They don't have a good variety of lingerie other than bras and panties.  Their home goods is very nicely situated as are their bed and bath items ... and their shoes!! My goodnes, their shoes are to die for!  One rhing I've noticed recently is that they are carrying many more high end designers: Michael Kors, Calvin Klein, and others at decent prices. So it does pay to shop at Ross.

Tried a Flat White for the first time on the recommendation of a friend (Thanks Amy P!) The first location I went to said no, I couldn't because they were out of whole milk. This location though, they were more than happy to oblige. The service was quick and efficient. The barista was both bubbly and sweet as she made my drink order.   The drink itself was tasty, not sweet but rich on the tongue. Next time I get this, I'll see if they can add vanilla to it.

It was whispered this was some of the best Ice Cream out there. I can NOT dispute this fact.  I splurged and got myself a single scoop of Mint Chip. The scoop was HUGE. I mean -HUGE- The flavor was delicious and it was so creamy! It was a delight in my mouth!  I also ordered a large cappuccino. While it wasn't the perfect cuppa, it was a decent cup of rich java, and that's just what I wanted with my ice cream. I would reccomend this place to anyone.

It's been a while since I've visited BayWalk... that I call it BayWalk tells you just how long it's been.  Re-branded the Sundial, it city center has undergone an overhaul and is quite lovely! From its open air design, to its stunning sundial sculpture with dolphins surrounding it's base, you can tell that there's been a small fortune sunk into the over haul and its well worth it.   High end shops line the promenade, A lot of restaurants have decided to populate this popular destination and of course Locale Market has finally opened, this means more foot traffic! This it certainly is a good thing for Down Town St. Pete.

Ice creamery outside of the Cobb theatres at Countryside.  I'm giving this a 3 because the girl who tended, Sarah, us was good but she was left to flounder due to poor scheduling. She was in the weeds. I felt bad for her.   The ice cream was good, especially when she blended in the toppings I requested. But there was a line building up and there was only one girl, a new menu and she was new there. She kept her cool and di just fine with us.

Had dinner with a friend here, before going out shopping.    The service was quick, efficient and friendly. I ordered a pick two of French Onion Soup and a 1/2 salad.  I asked for extra croutons and dressing on the side. My requests were easily made and cheerfully done.  My friend ordered a special sandwich on white bread.  They did that for her as well. We were quite pleased.

Tasty, tasty, tasty!   For a fast food option, they're relatively healthy. The pulled pork was delicious and moist. The black beans were delightful, but the salad was over dressed. I'll come back when I get the chance, since it's on the way to work, but now I know it's a great choice for protien.

Lunch after a massage is always something that I crave. So since this was in the same plaza as the massage envy I go to, I stopped in for a bite.   The locale is large, it's spacious with nice seating. I was even greeted by the company dog outside.  Once inside, I realised I was the only person there on a Monday Afternoon. Sad really..   I placed an order for water and a small pizza, this way I could take most of it home and eat it later.  I ended up getting the margharita pizza, and it came out rather quickly. The ingredients were fresh, large slices of tomato topping it with lots of basil and some garlic and oil. Tasty. But a touch underdone.   I'd go again.

We saw Jessi at one of the most derelict events I've ever been to. I only say this because I've been to a few and My husbeast and I were the only people who weren't vendors at the Glorifying Women's Expo, that Say's something.   I'd seen Jessi and her Product on Monday at the Moonlight Bazzar at Red Rockstar Bar, but since I don't like hot things, I had avoided her. HOWEVER.. This time I had the Husbeast. and he is an avid consumer of all things HOT and spicy.  This was a good match. Jessi was awesome. She allowed him to sample each sauce, telling him about the components behind them and even offered some to me. Sharing with  me a brownie bite that was decadent and made with her blueberry ginger sauce.   In the end, we liked them So much that we bought all 6 flavors. Yes, You read that right all six bottles now have homes in my kitchen. We will certainly be new customers as long as she's making these delicious condiments.

In a food truck food court, one food truck stood out in stark contrast above the others, it was Twisted Iron. Why? they had a line.  We were at the front of this line and I was happy for that, because it was chilly under the Bridge at Pierce street market.   Both the husbeast and I got Chicken & Waffles. The wait time was short but the food portions were large. 3 juicy pieces of chicken atop a large waffle, a serving of smuckers breakfast syrup and I THINK It was honey Mustard, but since I don't use it, I gave that to the husband.   The chicken was good. VERY VERY GOOD. it had a nice flavour and was perfectly cooked.  THe only thing about the waffle I can say negative is that it wasn't light. it was very heavy and dense, and that's not the way I prefer my waffles. Bt the flavour was spot on and yum to my mouth!   I ate all the chicken and 1/4 the waffle. The husbeastie was a member of the clean plate club!

The husbeast is working from this building for a while, as his new company is setting up shop off of 60.  The lobby is clean, neat and the bathrooms are kept spotless.  The only issue is that their wifi isn't strong. Le Sigh.

I LOVE me some Zaxby's Zalads.  Their House Zalad is fantastic, with cucumber, tomato and crispy onion, it makes for 2 delicious meals. Add to that some zesty fried mushrooms and life is good!   The seasoning on their fries is perhaps the best around - though I've noticed that Universal uses something very similar!

Totally a gorgeous venue, if you're looking for a place to have your wedding or other special event. What is not to love about floor to ceiling windows draped in diaphanous curtains, or marble floors that are originals to the building. The Vault is steeped in History, and will make your event something so very memorable.

I've never seen a "super center" that is this small.  It lacks a cohesive plus size clothing center - heck what used to be their plus wear is mostly clearance now.  They do have a decent electronics department, if you have an Iphone. A fairly OK selection of Health & Beauty.  But this is mostly a Walmart if you need to quick stop. There's a real super center 20 minutes away on SR54 or JUST up the road on Alderman.

Long drive home and I needed sustenance... I don't generally care for fast food, and since Steak 'n shake is a step above most places, I opted to stop there.  Where else can you get a triple patty steak burger and fries for $4 bucks?   In general, the food is good, the burgers are fresh, even if the service is NOT the fastest.

I remember when these apartments were horrid.   Now they're kind of passable. I had to drop a friend off here after she stayed the weekend with me. Gated entry and exits keep this from being the suitcase city of old.  (and yes, way back when, I used to .. well not live here exactly, but spend a LOT of time with my then boyfriend, now ex husband - ahh good ole college days..AHEM)  They've done a lot to clean up the place, given it a complete over haul, even though the apartments still look like boxes on the inside.

The burgers take time to come out because they're made fresh. The fries weren't as hot as tthey could have been, but the food was made to my specs and I didn't have a problem with that.  The diet coke was a good mix and all in all, II'd come back.

If EVER there was a store that had -too- much, Bed, Bath and beyond is the perfect example of that store.  They have floor to rafter and just about every square inch of floor space - save that what you would call isles filled with merchandise.   And given that this is Christmas shopping season, well, it's doubly so! Yes, if you've seen it on TV, you can find it there. Do you want the Veg-o-matic Spaghetti maker? They have it.  Do you want Poo-Pouri?Its there too, and in multiple scents. The sweeping craze of Adult Colouring is big as is STAR WARS. Oh lard, lets talk about Star Wars. If it's got Kylo Ren or the Chrome Storm Trooper on it, its there.   They have pillows and comforters, they have everything you need. It's packed floor to beam with everything and more. I don't enjoy the pace, or the place, but it is what it is, and they will print you out a Gift receipt if you forget to ask for one when they're ringing things up.

Contrary to other reviews, this is NOT the worst Ross out there. Sure it has it's issues, and yes, like any other major discount retailers, the clothing is a bit jumbled and discombobulated. But for the most part it's an OK shopping experience.   The Loss Prevention person hangs out near the door, is more like a Walmart greeter, if you ask me. Yes, their presence is seen, but what do they actually do? Not a lot, really. Nothing they CAN do, honestly.  Since the holiday hours have been extended, they're currently open til 12:30 am or 1:30 am on any given night. This means, no long waiting lines to check out.   Heck! I walked away with 4 new dresses last night, all of them looked great.  I'll continue to shop here when I can!

Stopped here for lunch. It wasn't busy at all, so our food was made very quickly.   This location is not at all like the other location I've visited in Tampa, but it is quite nice. The food came out hot and fresh.

I've been meaning to come here since they opened. Today afforded the opportunity.   I've been to Oahu, I've had Mac Nut Pancakes and I've been craving them ever since.. and today, I had them again. they were Ono Grinds! The weather was perfect for sitting outside on the patio deck, listening to the conversations that flowed around me while I ate my food, and sipped my tea.   The service was attentive and the food was fresh. The menu was a bit daunting for a dyed in the wool omnivore like myself, but if you're a vegetarian or are health conscious, visit Ohana Cafe, Give a little Aloha and Mahalo to the wait staff.  I will be back!

I'm not a huge fan of Chick-fil-A, but I will say that they are always courteous, quick and the food is always good, if you order one of their value meals. You certianly can't beat the waffle cut fries or their grilled nuggets. Seriously, if you've not tried the grilled nuggets, do so, they're the tastiest thing on the menu!

I went all afternoon without eating. This is a dumb move, so finally after my trip to Kohl's was done, I stopped in at Tijuana Flats fo fill my neglected tummy.   This is a new store, the windows really provide for a very bright, airy feeling to what are usually dark venues. The bright "comic book" style art on the walls always makes me smile. This store's, in particular was crisp and fresh, even the ceiling, which was not yet tiled in painted tiles, had ones that were neatly done.   The Manager, himself waited on me, he was polite and funny and made sure i got just what I wanted, including the Diet coke, topped with cherry coke for sweetness. *grin*  He came out to check on me a few times to make sure that everything was ok, and that I really enjoyed things.  And I did. His competency was excellent. He was really personable and told me about how the training of the stores were done, how quickly the stores are growing and how they manage to keep quality even across the board.

Popped in to Hot Wax but briefly last night. I didn't get a chance to do more than just peruse while my friend was on a call out side.   The store is beautiful, well lit and kept very clean. The staff seems friendly and knowledgable. I love that there's a glass blower right there making pipes right in front of you. That's so neat.

Honestly, I'd normally skip this place because of the way it looks like. But as the adage goes, don't judge a book by the cover. Once inside, I placed the order for a Margarita pizza and took a seat outside with my friend.    Our pizza was delivered shortly, it was topped with fresh tomato, LOTS of fresh basil and garlic, and a white sauce. THe crust was perfection, toasty and tasted wonderful. Everything was just right.   We had discussed knots but in the end decided not to order them, imagine my surprise when an gratis order was delivered to us. You can bet that we will be back here again. Perhaps not to eat in, but certainly for carry out. I really want to try their wings.

I was meeting a friend here because I remembered the last time I was here, they had a coffee shop attached.  It wasn't busy, but lawdy, Clearwater was sure hopping. After fighting for a parking spot, I finally gave up and paid a pretty penny $10, for a spot behind CVS across the street and walked to the destination.  As I said, it wasn't busy and that was good. My friend and I placed our orders, I got the Steakhouse burger - sauces on the side, and He got the All American burger. We upgraded to the combo for $3 more, and got a drink (Soda for me, coffee for him) and a side, rings and fries respectively. I paid the $27 and we got our buzzer and took our seats.   Five minutes later, we were called up and our food was given. They were good sized burgers, however, i took the bun off of mine. They weren't over done, they were cooked just over medium. The toppings were done too. The rings and fries were tasty.   I'd come back.

Crockett's towing was the service that the FHP used when my mom was in her accident. At first, we had no idea where her car was at, so it took a little detective work on my end, but we found it.   The people there were awesome, caring and understanding. There was a hold on our car and the others involved in the multi-car accident so I had to wait to get the important things out of our car.  Those things included the hearing aids that she was wearing when the airbags went off. So for a week she was deaf as a door nail. Ah well.   When we were able to retrieve things, the Crockett's team was there to help me with getting the license plate off, made sure I had what I needed. All in all, they did a great job with helping me.

Stopped here because there was an ETSY craft show.  The only other time I'd ever been to the Coliseum was a Cat show nigh on 20 years ago. Nothing had change except what they were showing. The floors are still lovely wood and highly polished, The accoustics are great and the stage calls to me.   This particular show was set up as any craft show is, with rows and rows of people selling things, the Venue itself was selling hot dogs for a buck and they were tasty.   The only complaint I had was that parking was scarce and hard to use.

During Third Friday I decided I just NEEDED to stop in. They have such great displays that I wanted to see what else they might have. Lo and behold, they had a picnic basket just outisde the door, and it was a whopping $5. I bought that! It will make a fantastic Ren Faire basket.   Inside, its a bit cluttered, there's a lot to look at, a lot to browse, and you can't forget to look up at the walls near the ceiling, as there's stuff up there too! The prices are reasonable, and all in all, its a fun afternoon to poke around.

A Tampa classic.   I've stopped in here so many times. It's odd that I've never given them a review.  I find them best for late night bites and cups of coffee, when you want to linger with the person you're with, but don't want to deal with Denney's or Village Inn.   Their food is damned good, and the waitresses work hard to get you what you want.

Came here with a friend of mine before doing a salt float. We chose it because it was close and our original destination was closed because it was a holiday.   Chili's wasn't busy, and we were seated rather quickly. Both of us perused the new menu, neither of us saw what we really wanted but did notice that there was a lunch menu that offered relatively cheap food for a low price.    The server was concientious and quick, but the food was mediocre at best. My friend opted for the fajitas on the lunch menu with the side of rice and beans - Cadillac style, and was disappointed to find out that the rice was hard, as if it was old and had set out and dried.

I found this shop completely by accident! I love spice shops, I love the way they smell, I love the way they have their displays.  This store was special in the way that they will let you taste the blends as well as smell thing. I've never encountered that before.   Service was impeccable. The gentleman running the store too an interest in what I was needing, how It could be used, and showed me some recipes I might be interested in.  He even had a powdered chili pepper that my husband would love.  I will -certainly- be back.

Took a class here, so this is only for the Meeting room.  The staff was friendly enough, and directed me to the large room where the CPR class was being held. The room had one small issue, the AC was either too hot or too cold, there didn't seem to be a happy medium. I would certainly take a class here again.

Date night, Apparently there are 2 locations in Oldsmar and I was at one while the beau was at another. While I waited for him to join me at this location, I ordered my hot chai Tea. Jonah was absolutely wonderful. He was personable and friendly and exceptionally warm. We chatted about how our names are different (my alternate Id) and how we don't often hear them, though mine is growing popular due to Anime.   Once my order was placed, it took only a few minutes to have it in my hands so I could wait for Bruce to join me. I'd come back.

Friday night is a busy night... and when it's cold outside, it's even busier since they can't use their outside seating.   The food is -good-, VERY good.  The husband and I decided to try a little something from every column.  We tried the Caprese salad, two different kind of wings: The fire side and the Garlic/parmesan wings and a small margharita pie.   Everything was delivered relatively quickly, the caprese salad was very fresh with nice big leaves of basil. The wings were tasty, but the garlic/parm wings were missing something.. salt.   And the pizza.. THE PIZZA was delicious! Absolutely tasty. Would certainly come back for that any day.

After going to the Neiman's in San Fran, I was So hoping to find that they too carried a great selection in bras.  Sadly, they do not.  They have a fabulous collection of clothing, great designers and what have you, but their foundation selection is paltry and very slim. I am saddened by this. I mean, really! There were no bras over a DD cup even offered. THIS.. just is not acceptable.

Not your typical chili.  Don't expect beef & beans, don't expect your typical taste. This is more of a meat sauce than Chili con carne, but it's still flavourful, it still have a good texture, and you can add beans if you so choose.   I like the cinnamon taste to it, It's very Greek to me.   This isn't an everyday place to go to, it's a guilty pleasure, a once in a while kind of location to go to, and since my Father in Law is from Maysville, Indiana, we go here every so often. For me, it's either a chili dog or Dogs in a bowl. For the husbeast it's a burrito, and the father in law gets the Chili 5 ways.     Anyway you serve it, it all tastes like home.

The chocolate covered strawberries are what called my name, but I didn't end up getting them. Sadly the service was terribly slow and I didn't want to wait. They are always busy!  There's a reason for that though! Godiva chocolate is GOOD chocolate and people want that stuff!

The name is no longer Holiday inn, but rather Tampa Stadium Hotel. I showed up because a friend let me know about an Estate stale that was going on here.   The hotel itself is in need of some repair, and the little out building smelled of mold.  But the sale was decent, I was able to pick up some much needed things. And some wanted things.

After a comedy show fund raiser for a friend, I needed to grab a quick bite. But it's Monday, it's after 10 and it's Tampa. Very little is open this Late. What to do, what to do?  We high tailed it to IHOP and got our food on.  The waitress was surley, but the food was tasty. Other than the service being minimal, I really can't complain.

Due to the size of this hotel, the Old Hickory Grill is the only option for food on site, except for the bar, but they get their food from Old Hickory, too.   When I visited the first time, there was only one other couple in the place, so I was sat RIGHT in the middle of the eatery, the 2nd time, pretty much the same.. Always dead center of the room.  My first meal was the Meatball and a wedge salad, an actually reasonably priced meal for $16 total. Filling too since I wasn't sharing it with anyone.    The 2nd time I ate there We had 4 people in our group, so there were several things ordered, nothing complicated, but the Apps didn't come out ahead of time, not that it really mattered, but it's the little things you notice. Our glasses of water were allowed to go empty.   I eventually opted to go out side of the hotel by Lyft driver.

After a -really- long day, the husbeastie and I decided we'd stop for a treat.. We've waited to visit the Twistee Treat because there's -always- a long line.  The line today was not terrible, but it still existed in the drive thru.   Our order was simple, A dish of Strawberry and a medium vanilla dipped in chocolate cone.  We were both surprised at how large the servings were. Sadly the cone had alredy started to melt when they handed it out to me. *le sigh*   The ice cream was delicious, very smooth and creamy. I will certainly have it again, Diet permitting.

I really don't like to shop at WD. Their stores are generally .. dirty in appearance, but I stopped in because they were running this wicked sale on Keurig K Cups. How can you beat -any- variety of KCup for $5.99  but if you bought 4 or more packs, they came down to $4.99. YOU know I ended up buying 8 boxes. A nice variety of diferent flavours!    I won't give up my publix shopping, but if they run sales like that, I'll be back.

Brand new location. They are new and there are growing pains. I will re-evaluate them later, but for now, they're solid at a three. Why? 15 minutes in the drive through with only one car ahead of me.  I placed my order at 2:55 pm and it wasn't handed to me until 3:10, it really should not take that long.   However, the service was polite, the food was good, and the value was pretty ok. I enjoy Zaxby's and am happy to have one closer to Tarpon, than all the way out off of Waters or Hillsboro/Dale Mabry.

I go here one Wednesday a month. I meet with a chapter of friends and hang out with them. We're all of like minds and when we get here, we have the best service, We have a great time.  The food? It's ok. It's not stellar, but it is filling. Their omlettes are good, as long as you get the grits with real butter. :)

it's IHOP. It was late at night on GRAY Thursday/ Early Morning Black Friday. I really did expect it to be busier than it was. But when Mom and I walked in, there were 3 groups. One group of giggling teens, one group of 30 somethings and Us.   The service was amazingly fast, our waitress was very polite and courteous. She knew her menu in and out. Answered any question we had without reservation and delivered our food very quickly.   The food was Ok. Again, it's IHOP ,so it was nothing special, but it was tasty and inexpensive. It's chain food, a little better than fast food.

Stopped here for a lunch date with a friend.   Hadn't been to this particular VI in forever, but the food was all the same.  It wasn't a wednesday so no Free pie for us. *sad*  Our waitress was amazing and she was handling a huge section all alone. How she did it, I don't know, but she did and she did it with a smile. WAY TO GO.   We both ordered off the VIB menu,  I got the cheese omelet, bacon, 1/2 a waffle and coffee. My friend got the same but opted for the pancakes. OMG the food was tasty

I -wish- it was non smoking.  The moment you hit the door you can smell the smoke and the stuff they use to cover up the odor. It was rather.. strong.   Inside though, the light is phased out and the bells and whistles of the machines come up, There is an odd sense of euphoria that seems to weigh over you as you approach and you sit down at the slots.  I played the $0.02 machines (Really more like $0.40 -$0.80 machines based on the bets you have to play) and did fairly ok.   The one thing I can say that I do not like is the inconsideration of the staff when they stand RIGHT behind you, quite literally nearly touching you when they're helping someone out. This happened twice to me. It makes me very nervous and very .. uncomfortable.

Other than the service - which I found  touch lacking. Everything was AMAZING.   After watching a play at the Studio@620, the paramour and I walked down to Cask & Ale, and while they weren't busy, we had to actually place our orders at the bar vs any sort of table service, this was kind of irritating but other than that, what we found out was that we were VERY pleased with what we ordered.   I ordered the spring fling (I think that's what it was called) and the Paramour ordered a Maple old fashioned. To eat we ordered their bacon mac and cheese. When everything came to the table, EVERYTHING was absolutely amazing. My drink was light and fresh, the lover's was sweet and tasty. But the mac & cheese? The Mac & cheese was in-freaking-credible.  I have to say it's probably the best that I've ever had.   I will come back.

All Target stores seem to have an "entrance fee" for me of at least $50 these days.  What I mean by this is that when I enter one, I will not spend less than that before I leave.    This Target has recently renovated and put in a Starbucks!  The scent of coffee fills the air where once there was only go backs and customer service issues.

Located at the corner of Us 19 and Tarpon Ave/Main street, you'll find this Subway.  It's a nice, clean store with some of the most complicated parking.  Inside, the employees are friendly, the store is neat and the baking bread smells great.   We arrived at noonish on Friday afternoon. I was quite surprised that it wasn't overly busy, we were able to place our orders for a 6" BLT and a Foot long BMT very quickly. Since we were on our way over to the theme parks I'd thought we were getting them to go, but the husbeast decided to eat in store.   All in all a fine place to eat if you want a quick sandwich either in store or to go.

Came here on a date with my Darkness. We opted because it was nearby where we were staying.  It was close to closing when we walked in, so it was quiet and not at all heavily occupied.    We were seated and our waitress was over almost immediately.  We perused the menu and the chips and salsa were laid down. I have to admit I LOVED the sampler but the best part was the black bean dip, that was my ultimate favorite.   We weren't terribly hungry, so we ordered the Nacho Appetizer, the Guacamole and the steak tacos.  We'd share it. We had NO idea how big the Nachos were.. LAWDY! That was such a huge portion, we didn't finish it. The Guacamole was Delicious, especially topped with the roasted corn.  The only thing we were disappointed with was the steak taco, and that was because of the masa shell. Took that off and the flavor returned.   The service was perfect, the food was great and the company was better than anything else.  We will most certainly return.

For her birthday, Mom got a new mailbox. She needed to have numbers for the side and that's something she was lacking. Sure we could have painted them on the side, but neither one of our handwriting is the greatest.  So what we needed to do was go get those 3" tall sticky letters...  Home Depot had it all, our numbers were hidden on isle 13, buried down near the mail boxes and sundry. A pack of 26 numbers was less than $3.  SCORE!

First visit in, and my impression is pretty good.   I needed a new battery for my cartridges, the one I have wasn't giving me enough of a draw.  Their selection for that wasn't huge but they did have what I needed, even encouraged me to try it to see what the output was. Pretty cool.   They have a guy there who works, who's a glass blower, he's done many of the pipes there, his work is really nice.   They sell tobacco, they sell water pipes and they even say on the door that they sell drug (weed) related products, so if you're offended, don't go in.   Prices are competitive and reasonable.

Typical Wendys.  I used the drive through on my way home, and grabbed their 4 for $4 with the Crispy BLT Chicken Sandwich, nuggets, fries and a drink.  I asked for the crispy chicken BLT to have no mayo. When I got my order, the fries were not hot - not cold, more of a kinda UH.. not tasty and there was Mayo on the chicken. Meh.

The ultimate men's playground.   Even for men like my husband who's not truly Home repair inclined.   We went, looking for some wire so I can make costume wings, and ended up getting a much needed 8' ladder, some window cling film, new sprinkler heads...   What should have been a quick and inexpensive trip, turned into a fun shopping trip that cost a small fortune - and one that the husbeastie actually ENJOYED!

The heart of the Tarpon Springs sponge docks holds Hellas' bakery and Restaurant. It's a great place to dine, to people watch and to grab a cup of coffee and a slab of bakalava. There really isn't anything better to do on a Saturday afternoon, than sit at one of the outside tables, sipping your java and licking honey off your finger tips. The food is fantastic! Opa!

I enjoy banking at FCU's. I find them safer and more friendly than your average National Bank.   GTE FCU is no exception.  This location is always friendly and quick with their service. I'm glad that they're close by!

Stopped at Newks as we needed to get to Target to pick up something I needed for my up coming trip.   We ordered their get two options, I ordered the salad and pizza, teh husbeastie got himself a sandwich and soup.  The pizza was tasty, but the portions were still too much for me.   They were woefully understaffed at my visit. People who were prepping food had to leave their job doing that to handle the register, or were cleaning the eatery after people had eaten. I saw Three people working, possilby four at 2 in the afternoon on a Saturday.

This is a Tampa Icon, and sadly it is soon to be closing it's doors forever!  A comprehensive costume house, Features offers you the ability to rent or buy costumes that run the gamut from your most basic tunic and fabric shoulder piece for your Christmas padgent as a wise man to the most ornate Lady in Waiting to a Queen.  Each costume is marked with a rental/purchase price and all are fair.   There is a HUGE makeup selection, wig and accessories are all available. The customer service is always helpful and friendly.   If you're looking for a good sale, right now absolutely EVERYTHING is 50% off while they liquidate their inventory. I suggest if you're looking for theatrical makeup, you go and invest in some quality Ben Nye product! Their lipsticks DO NOT MOVE, not even through eating fatty pork! I know, I tried it this weekend!

Stopped in to get myself my usual Carmel swirl latte... I was told that the Caramel was on recall. Funny, the next one down the road didn't have that issue. I dislike being lied to. REALLY dislike it. Consider that I won't stop at this particular location.

Not too crowded, the place was designed to look 1950's retro. I have to admit I liked the decor.   Coming to the theater on a Wednesday afternoon had it's perks. There were no kids, no crowds and no lines.  It was the perfect time to see a new release!    The movie itself - Insidious chapter 2 - was almost a private showing, with 2 other small groups of people, who all had the same idea, cluster in the center of the theater for the best seats.    I'd come here again if it were nearby!

Stopped in this new Starbucks for a coffee after visiting my niece. The starbucks is easy in, easy out, and the people that work there are just fine. I ordered a vanilla latte iced, it took about the time I placed the order until I got to the window to pay for my drink to be ready.

I usually attend the Holiday, Fl Location, but since my Beau lives more closely there, we meet here to work out after work.   This gym is well lit, with a large work out area filled with an assortment of machines.  There are areas for Abs, free weights and the 30 minute circuit as well as the Ropes area.   The Lifestyle machines for weights are well kept and everyone wipes them down between their usage.   Depending on your level of membership, you can tan or even get an aquassage (a massage table that uses controlled jets of massage to relax you) or use a massage chair.   It's a really nice facility.

I needed a drink, that's all. The drive through was efficient. I ordered a medium Pepsi. I waited in line for about a minute and forty seconds and paid money, got drink with a smile from a guy covered in tattoos.  All in all a fair exchange.
Friends of mine were hosting a small bazzar to give back to a community of cafts people in developing worlds.  The place allowed them to do so on their patio. That gets big marks from me.

I've driven past here many times but since I was with a friend and we were looking for things to do, I figured why not.   The place is bright and clean, but older. They aren't brand new and have been serving the area for a while, but that's ok. They serve the community with love.   My friend and I walked in and were seated immediately. We had a very friendly waitress, and our order for Coffee and water, as well as a Reuben and a Hamburger club were taken right away.   The food came out quickly as the place wasn't terribly busy at 1:45 pm, and what came out was HOT and delicious. My Hamburger club was delectable, It was tasty and fresh, the bacon really added a lot of flavor.    The only "complaint" I have is that there were too many fries.  How is that even possible? It was, but that's not a complaint, it's really a good thing. Keep up the good work, I'll be back.

Large WalMart, got what I needed and got out.  I dislike this walmart because on Thanksgiving 3 years ago, someone tried to use our "Credit Cards" while we were out of town. We don't know how they got our numbers, but they used them here.  Not the cleanest store.

Needed Gas on the way to my MOM's house before leaving for my trip to Alabama. The price was right at $1.69.  This racetrack is neat on the outside and neat on the inside with quick service and clean pumps.    If you can avoid the Pasco County yahoos who drive through here as a cut through to avoid the light at 19/fox hollow, you'll do just fine. Otherwise, someone might try to take your bumper off.

Stopped here for breakfast as i was headed out to Spring Hill to go get my Mom's car.    It was a sit anywhere kind of place, and the service was beyond good, it was by far some of the best I've ever had. The waitress was wonderful. I told her I hadn't had any sleep the night before, so she took the small coffee cup off the table and replaced it with a big mug.   She took my order, and within minutes it came out. The food was DELICIOUS. I ordered the ham and cheese omelette, with breakfast potatoes and an English Muffin. I think I age just about every scrap. Ok, so I was hungry.   When I asked for my check, my waitress asked if i needed a coffee to go, I said yes, and she came back with her largest cup to go.  She was AWESOMESAUCE.

I drive past this place frequently and finally decided to stop in.  They have La Segunda Bread. That's some damn fine Cuban bread!   Feed the cows! For a small price, they will give you a helping of veggies they've cut up for the bovines out back and you and your littles can go feed them. They will thank you, your kids will thank you and you, might just enjoy the break from being on the computer.   Get some local produce, fruits and veggies, some herbs and meat too.  THey've got hives now, so Honey is there as well.   This is a nice agribusiness!

Located near the up and coming area of Trinity, FL this Goodwill is huge.   I came here specifically for old luggage. There were a few newer pieces but nothing like what I needed, and that's OK. They did have a varied and clean assortment of just about anything you could possibly nwantnor need.  They even had a new section. I've seen this at other locations. I'm not sure when this started, but it's kind of cool.

An adorable little shop on Main street Safety Harbor that calls to you with it's uniqueness.   We came inside while at Third Friday in December 2018. The weather was rotten, but the store was nice and inviting and smelled divine.   Inside the store there is a selection of unique gift items, spa & resort clothing (With the attached price tag - soft pants that were $169 ?? Really?) Hand bags, jewelry and other accessories.  It was a very, perfectly lovely store that you could find that perfect gift for someone in.

My family and I stopped here to see the lights during their annual Christmas display.   We arrived too late for the 8:00pm display but on the center stage they were still entertaining with dancers from a local dance studio. Scenes from A NutCracker seemed to be going on. The kids did a great job. Some very promising young dancers out there!  The Shops is an open air Mall, with some fantastic anchor stores like Barnes & Noble, JcPenney and Nordstroms & Macys.  There are plenty of specialty shops too, so if you're looking for SOMETHING special, you're likely to find it there.   There's plenty of parking, lots of parking lots and even in front of shop parking too, so please be careful when crossing the street and make sure to look both ways.

Publix is my choice for grocery shopping bar none.   You have -everything- you need in one shop. Bakery, deli and one of the best produce selections around outside of a farmer's market.   The staff is always friendly, always asking if you need help and most importantly seem to genuinely like their jobs.

The husbeast is going to Washington, to make a presentation. He has to look nice! Since he's a large man, buying clothing can be a challenge. It used to be that Men's sizes were easy, now they're leaning towards some vanity sizing as well.    We were able to find the pants and vest, 2 shirts and 2 ties he needed for a 2 night stay in the DC area, and yes, it wasn't cheap. For some reason clothing manufacturers believe that larger clothing needs to be higher priced. It really doesn't. Especially Tees and polos. There isn't that much more fabric.   The store was clean and well maintained, save for the bathroom which had a lack of a working towel dispenser or toilet paper holder, both were just rolls set on top of things. Stay classy Tampa.   The store is necessary. Yes, They carry Big and Tall sizes, Emphasize on the TALL. They seem to have a LOT in that category.

Solid eatery.   Dinner choice of my friend while she visited and we were dapperfied.    I'm sad they got rid of pork nachos, but the food is still good, still fresh. I ordered the cajun chicken nachos. The chips were fresh. There wasn't a lot of chicken on there but the other toppings were plentiful.  The drinks never stopped flowing .

The host hotel for the Legendary Haunt Tour. My room was up on the 5th floor, the quiet floor. It was for the most part.  The bed was comfortable, the shower was nice, but there were a few housekeeping issues, such as: a few stray hairs on the tile of the shower floor.  Odd things on the carpet that were missed by the vacuum - like food or something. Not sure what they were. One coffee mug was NOT clean, but had been "Wiped out and put back."

HUGE. This facility is one of the newer Goodwill stores recently built within the last 5 years. Their floor plans are open and they even have new merchandise, not everything is donated. During Halloween they have a full zone of new merchandise that has never been opened or used. I suspect it is previous years overstock from the "big halloween stores".    There is the usual merchandise as well, the stuff people have donated and it's kind of hard to find things by size since it all gets jumbled when things get put back. Sadly the plus sized stuff is almost non-existant, and hard to find.   Shoes at this particular location were amazing. I have a feeling a Drag queen off loaded her heels because I found MANY amazing pair of heels in size 13. They were So PHENOMENAL! I wished I could wear them, ALMOST, but then again I can't wear heels any more.

Chick-Fil-A, I love the food, but hate the politics.    That being said, when I want something that can be ALMOST healthy (The naked nuggets and the grilled chicken breast sandwich are the best on the menu) and those waffle cut fries, this is where I head to.   They are always friendly at the drive through and I've yet to get the wrong order unlike at other drive thru services.

Fellow Yelper, Stacy Z recommended that I stop in and check this place out. She wasn't wrong.   First thing out of the box is this store is clean, it smells good and they have a huge selection of merchandise.   They have all the tobacco for all your smoking needs. There's a respectable sized humidor with a good selection of varied sizes/style and quality of cigars.   They have all your assorted smoking parephenalia, from rolling papers to lighters to the occasional (or more frequent) water pipe.  Their selection is quite nice.   They also carry CDB and Kratom at this time.   Join the VIP program and get 10% off your purchases each time you come in  -simply mention it.

We were driving down to Sarasota and since we didn't nosh before we left the house we really needed to pick up something to eat on the way.  The idea was to grab food before we crossed the Skyway, so we stopped in Pinellas Park.   There were a lot of selections, but seeing I'd never had a Jersey Mike's sub We opted for it.  I perused their menu and saw they offered Cheese steaks and that made me happy. I chose the BIG Kahuna! So a cheese steak with extra onions, mushrooms and cheese. It was delicious, I got a size regular, with chips and a soda.   Everything was delicious, the service was quick and friendly.   I'd come back again.

After trying out a disappointing cupcakery in Orlando, I was happy to find this little shop in the strip mall near where I was eating lunch.  The cup cakes were fresh and lovely in her display case, each one marked with a Heart, noted a filled one. All cup cakes were $1.50 save for the canolli cup cake and that was $1.75 because it was real canolli filling and a bit more expensive to make.   The shop smells wonderful upon entering. It is a bit no frills but over all, that's fine. It's the product that you're looking for. The cup cakes are small, but GOOD. Moist cake, good icing, not too sweet but very tasty. The husbeast had the blueberry filled one, and he said it was amazing, I opted for the Salted Caramel cupcake and it was DELICIOUS.   I will come back when I'm by this way again. This is the kind of place that needs to be heard about. They're a little off the beaten path, but well worth the journey.

The crown jewel of Tarpon Springs.   If you're coming to the sponge docks, make time to visit Hellas too. The food and service are genuinely impeccable. The gyro's are flavourful, the souvlaki is tender and the flaming cheese is, well, in a word  HOT!  You can get all your Greek cuisine favorites like: Skordilla, stuffed grape leaves, Avgolemono soup, spanokipita,Horiatiki Salad, Greek Salad, a broiled octopus and even a whole fish that is then deboned at your table side.   And while you're there, don't forget to visit the bakery for even more absolutely decadent treats, the bakalava is some of the very best you'll ever eat.   OPA!

A town and country institution. I've driven by this place a thousand times and never once gone in.  So one Sunday morning, after staying at the Beau's home, we opted to go here for breakfast.  He apparently used to go here when he was a kid.   Opening the door was like stepping back in time. It is most certainly a greasy spoon, but that's fine.  The place hasn't been updated in 30 years but the food is good and the service is amazing.   We both had breakfast food, I ordered their skillet and ate nearly every bite of it except for the potatoes, the man ordered eggs, bacon and french toast.  Mind you, it said 3 pieces of french toast. Most places that'd get you three triangles, right? Nope here, it was 3 whole pieces of french toast and that stuff was amazing.   The coffee was kept full and hot.   Will I be back? You know I will.

The name caught my attention, more than the color of the building, so I knew I had to go check it out.    It makes me REALLY happy to see that this is a great thrift shop that supports the LGBTQ community and offers FREE HIV testing.   Inside is well laid out, lots of clothing to choose from, lots of bric-a-brac and furniture too.  They had a great selection! But honestly, what I liked best was their imagnative window displays. Their manequins were well done.

I've driven past this Marshall's a few times in the recent past, so I decided to pop in on the way home. The asiles were wide and clean, and yes, it's filled with Christmas merchandise already, but what a fabulous collection.   I found KT Tape - something I didn't think I'd find there. I found Hawaiian Black & red salt, a cool journal that will make a neat gift for a friend, and a few other things. Over all a productive trip shopping.

I'll admit, I've not stopped in here before because I wasn't sure how it would be. I was skeptical, because it looked sketchy to me.  But the beau was craving BBQ and we agreed, it sounded good and was pretty close to home.   We arrived around noon on Saturday, we sat and our waitress was there quickly. She was friendly and welcoming.  We took a few minutes to look over the menu and when we were ready, we placed our order - All of us getting the brisket and each of us choosing a different 2nd meat: I got the chicken quarter, there was pulled pork and sausage.  Sides ranged from Okra to cole slaw, Mac and cheese to green beans.   When we were done, there wasn't Anything left. We consumed it like locusts. It was THAT good. Everything had so much flavor, good texture and the sauces were really good too.    Now that we've tried it, we'll certainly come back. The guys didn't get to try the amberjack spread, and they're really wanting to.

Largest of the Ollies I've been too. Product repeats in different sections of the store says there's too much space, not enough product for the location, but I suppose that means they can always get more stuff in.   We went before Phase 3 opened, so they were still social distancing, they were still wearing masks (And should be still). Their book section was HUGE and well spaced out. They have lots of coloring books and reader glasses, if you're the type who doesn't want the stigma of always wearing specs.   Toys were prevalent, we saw they had the teenage mutant ninja turtles, a whole set, but one of them was boxed wrong so it looked like you'd have gotten 2 Raphaels, but you would have actually gotten them all. A collectors gaffe. We didn't buy it.   The store was disorganize but fun.

I honestly thought this was a new shop, but according to the owner, Miss Merrie, they've been in that location for 13 years! Huh. You'd think I'd pay attention to my home town a bit more. *chuckles*  I wandered in because it reminded me of Rocket Fizz, only with a better more cohesive selection.  What I noticed is that they had more imported candies, like licorice from Norway (including these awesome licorice pipes) and a whole LOT of Gummy bears from Harribo. There were turkish taffies and all manner of different candies from all over the world.   If you're looking for something unique, stop in this quaint and clean shop. You won't be upset.  THe prices are fair and much less than the $12.99 a pound shops you find in the mall.
I stopped to fill my tank and get a slurpee. I sent my guy inside to get me the frozen concocotion, while I pumped the gas at a clean pump.

Typical walgreens. Had to stop here on the way home from the shopping extravaganza with mom to pick up some pain reliever for the niece. Poor thing couldn't figure out the dosage on the kids ibuprophen all because "she wasn't 11" I did explain that being over 11 meant that was the "adult" dosage. *chuckles*  Clean and fair priced. I'd stop here again.

I can't tell you how many times I've driven by this place but I've never stopped in. Well that changed when the husbeastie and I decided we needed a change of pace.   We stopped in and were seated immediately.  It has a nice ambience for a former Burger King.  It was busy and there was one waitress for the entire dining room, so wait time was a bit high but not unacceptable.  We perused the menu which was quite extensive but settled on the Sushi Dinner and the Shrimp Tempura to get an idea of what they made the best.   Their miso soup and salad were delicious, I especially love the ginger dressing, it's so good.  Infact that's what I opt to have as the dipping sauce for my shrimp tempura.   The meals came out and the sushi dinner looked and smelled fresh. The husbeastie devoured it, so I assume it was good.  My meal had plump, juicy shrimp and several different veggies and a side of sushi rice.  I ate the proteins but split the veggies with the husbeastie.    All in all, a very pleasant experience.

I'd heard some good things about this place.  They had a Huge selection of goth and steam punk wear, and I was thoroughly impressed with what I saw.    That is until I saw on their re-sale rack an Alter-ego Corset.  Alter Ego Corsets are lovely pieces of leather that are now available under a different name.  What bothered me about this is that the price was tagged at $150.00. NOT a bad price for a leather, steel boned corset, until you realize that when they sold this item on Ebay (their main sales option back in the early 2000's) They sold for new between $100-130.   This left a really bad taste in my mouth.   Otherwise, they've got a great selection of clothing, in a variety of sizes, from a variety of manufacturers: Hellbunny, leg avenue, Tripp, the whole gamut is offered up. Go check them out, you won't be disappointed.
As of this writing, the new location on Main St in Tarpon has closed. It is sad to see this happen.

Came here to work on one or two of the artists as a massage therapist and then got some ink for myself. My artist was Matt.  Matt was extremely professional. We consulted over what I wanted, and he drew it up, presented it and got to work.   It'd been a decade since I've had any ink done so I was a little apprehensive, but I didn't have to be. He was gentle and made sure I knew exactly what he was doing, what needle he was using and everything else.   He made sure to check in with me, to see how I was handling things and when it was done, I was incredibly pleased. I now have the Lotus I wanted! It's delicate and the ink work is incredibly fine. I can't wait to get more ink soon!

My guy and I were looking for a place to eat last Saturday night, and we wound up in Dunedin. We were going to do Mexican, but our usual spot seemed too crowded in the age of Covid, so we saw the D-Town and stopped in.   It's very nicely decorated, the staff is really friendly and they do adhere to social distancing and masks.   We placed an order for an appetizer (rare for us) of stuffed potato skins, thinking they be like the yukon gold potatoes, small. Boy howdy we were wrong. These were idaho russets, large and stuffed with bacon, cheese & chives. They were delicious.   For our mains, my guy got the steak special and I ordered wings. The steak was nicely cooked, with a good seat to it. It came with a salad and a baked potato.   The parmesan garlic wings were a savory delight. I wish we'd had room for dessert, but alas, a cream puff was not to be.   We'll be visiting again.

Nice looking gift shop in the new condos on Main Street.  Absolutely adorable shop with gifts for every age range.   I LOVED the Turtle pillows and mermaid items which were right out in the front of the store.    There was a large selection of toys and childs clothing as well. And while I was there, I found out it has a new owner too! Apparently a woman came in to buy something and wound up buying the store.   In any case, the store is well kept and the people are friendly. Stop in and see if there's something you want.

McDonalds that butts up against Fivay High School, it's in nice condition, the store is clean and the double drive thrus are extremely efficient and friendly.   I placed a special order (Fish Fillet without cheese, extra tarter) med fry & med coke, and was pleased that the order was right, the fries were hot and my coke was upsized (Thanks!)  Service was quick and they even gave me a shout out on Twitter when I checked in.   Will be back when I'm in the Hudson area.

This joanne's is located in NPR, and is usually a disorganized mess. They're always getting ready for one holiday while the other one is in the middle of a clearance or still in full swing. Honestly i've seen Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas and Valentines day up all together. Talk about a mish mosh.   But when you come in looking for fabric or jewelry findings, they have it. They'll ahve what you need and it's easy to locate. Their associates are easy to deal with and friendly too.

This is actually for the "old Fashioned Christmas"  I had wanted to go shopping in Dunedin, but when I arrived I noticed that there were cars EVERYWHERE. Oh NO.. Something was going on. When we started walking down the street.. well what do you know, there's a parade going on! I stood there and watched a good 50 floats/groups going by, and that was just up to #73, with more to come.    It was staring to get cold so I wandered away, but I can tell you that they were planing on having an excellent event with snow and vendors, it looked like it was going to be a heck of a time.

With the Covid-19 outbreak many stores have decreased their hours, so I was stuck going here instead of Publix.  I was NOT disappointed.   I sent my boyfriend in to the store to pick up a few essentials, and he said the store was fairly well stocked, even a half hour before closing. That the fruits and vegetables appeared fresh and that the store staff was friendly, right up until 5 minutes before closing when they stationed an employee at the door to dissuade any further people from coming in.   We were able to get the milk, bread and other sundry items we came for at cheaper than I expected.  If I had to,I'd certainly shop there again.

A quaint, little park near the street car line's last stop that serves as a place to hold the Saturday market, Free Pt, and a few other things.   Lovely chickens roam through the area at their will and there is often parking available around the area if one is inclined to make their way to the park.
My mom's 2nd home, or so it feels like.   I can't tell you how often I've brought a sewing machine here to be repaired or just serviced. They're always nice folks.

Had a lovely lunch here with my friend Amy.   We had not seen each other in some while and were looking for a place that would allow her and I to both eat happily. She's a pescatarian and I'm an omnivore.   Poblano's menu was very flexible and customizable with what proteins you wanted. The service was good, friendly and prompt. Our glasses never went empty.    The Portion sizes were quite large as both of us had take home boxes. We were quite happy and both would recommend the place to others.

I popped into Clothes Mentor after getting a massage just down the way. I've been in once before, but it'd been a while so I thought I'd check to see what was going on now.   They carry all sizes, including Plus, but their selection for anything over a large isn't huge. I looked through the racks and shrugged, I found a few things but it wasn't until I found the back wall that I was happy.   On the back wall they had Lularoe items. Many of them were Unworn and new. I helped myself to 2 pair of new leggings at $10 a pair (vs $25 new) and a necklace which was marked $0.99 but came up $6.95, they corrected it, but that was still annoying.   Over all, I'd come here again, but I wasn't terribly impressed.

My 1000th Review!  I waited too long to eat. I'd been sitting in my stylist's chair and my tummy was getting angry with me, so that when I finally was able to get food I was grumbly and moody. I opted to head to the international mall and decided to try The Earl.   I'm sad they don't have combos, so everything turns out to be really expensive, but the food is very good. I had a bowl of soup and a buffalo chicken wrap, of which I ended up only eating half - see if there was a combo that allowed 1/2 a sandwich and a cup of soup, it would have been better and I wouldn't have wasted money!  Though I did end up getting a better deal on a drink, since they were out of small cups, they had to give me the big cup for the price of a small.   Service was quick, the food was good, I'd give them another chance.

Tonight, after a hideous day, I just needed some comfort food, and Orchid's was on the menu.  The maternal unit, the husbeast and myself headed the handful of blocks from Mom's place to their store front, only to find them packed!  We only waited a little bit of time as they cleaned up a table and sat us.  Our waitress was amazing, she took our order, looking rather shocked when my husband ordered his meal Thai Hot.  Seriously, he means it. He wants to cry and sweat when he eats his soup. Me, i can't handle it... but I digress, she put the order in and brought out the pepper tray too.   I ordered the Chicken Sateh, Mom ordered the Sampler platter and the Husbeast ordered the Noodle soup with beef and meatballs, we had an order of fried rice for the table. Everything was absolutely fresh and delicious. The food came out quick and hot and nothing was left on our plates in the end.  If you like Thai desserts, I suggest you try the Mango Sticky Rice. It's Delicious!

We dropped by after attending a Spooky themed night at the Cuban club.  The decor is the perfect cross between Addams Family Lush and Goth Library plush. It's perfect.    My guy helped himself the the Kavatender's knowledge and ended up with a drink that made him happy and mellow and kept him awake all night long. That was some really good stuff there.

Stopped because gas was 2.88 for regular unleaded, 11 cents cheaper than surrounding locations.   Pumps were clean, but the trash cans needed emptying. There were windshield buckets missing and although they request that you use towels to dispense your gas, none were provided and no hand sanitizer.

I'm a massage therapist. So what do I do when I need a rub down and can't do a trade with a friend? I utilize my membership at Massage Envy at the Fountains.   In truth, I've been coming here since just before I got my license. They have some damn fine therapists that work there! My favorites are Tony, Karen and Diane. Each of these therapists are going to listen to what you need, do what they know your body needs and leave you feeling rejuvinated.  There are some draw backs, though: It's a membership place. Some people don't like that.  They up charge $10 for Bio-Freeze (WHY? it's $16 a bottle retail), $10 for Aroma therapy (most oils, even special blended oils don't cost that much) and $16 for a foot scrub... yeah.   There are some pluses: They're open from 9 am to 9 pm, they have a lot of locations and a lot of different therapists to suit your needs, weather you like it gentle or are like me and need a little tough love.    Either way, I'll be back at least once a month, because I work hard, and I deserve some touch therapy. SO DO YOU!

We'd been in Tampa proper and needed to eat. Out of Nostalgia, because ABC Pizza's were once everywhere, we stopped in. It was like stepping back in time. We loved it.   We were seated and our waitress was wonderfully fast. We ordered a large Cheese pie and a salad, and I swear our food was out in record time.  The cheese pie was perfect! I wish the one by me was still an ABC at times.

Daniel from Fluent in NPR recommended this and another dispensary as his favorites.  Since I'd been down south, and this was on the way home I opted to make the stop.
